_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea what this game was about. I knew it was a survival horror game, but that was pretty much it. I read the praise it got for being an indie game and then decided to give it a go. What a wonderful game it ended up being! Easily one of the best ones I have played this year. I loved the setting, trapped in a hotel resembling the shining situation, with many clever puzzles around to advance and some enemies to tackle. It takes many things from resident evil 7 (item management, saving mechanics, chest to drop items, weapons, art...), the story is interesting and pretty long, easily around 12-15 h in your first gameplay. It also has many rewarding secrets and some backtracking. The puzzles are challenging, reminded me of tormented souls kind of puzzles, you really have to think hard to solve some of them and look at your notes or documents to get the hints. The last part of the game was a bit more boring imo, but still pretty good. The only thing I did not like was the combat, felt clunky, harsh and a bit unfair: you can get stuck in narrow path with enemies and get killed because you cannot shoot at them and cannot run away from them. Otherwise, it is a must have if you like horror games and well-thought satisfying to resolve puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, we have another Game that I didn't expect too much from and it still managed to surprise me positively.Fobia - St.Dinfna Hotel is a AA (I don't think this counts as indie) 1st person Survival "Horror" Game in the vein of Resident Evil 7/8 just jankier.I just want to do a brainstormy review instead of a structured one, so let's start and get my thoughts out of the way. There are many things to like about Fobia but also many things to dislike.The translation of the Game is relatively bad but that's fine since the developers probably speak brazilian portuguese as their main language.Even though the Team is relatively small, there are many options in the options menu, especially for accessibility. When you turn in the Game it feels a little awkward (at least with 90FOV) because you see your whole body and shoulders, but after a while you don't really pay attention to that.The English Voice Acting was not got...at all. I mean it's serviceable, but it's still kind of bad.Graphically the Game looks good enough for an AA FPS "Horror" Shooter, uses the Unreal Engine.Fobia has a RE7 style inventory, but it feels a little clunkier to use.Everything from movement to shooting and strangely placed invisible walls feels just a little janky and not 100% on point, but I can overlook that easily.Also there were a few bugs, for example: a) many times after a loading screen you have to move your character before you are allowed to look around/gain full control of your character.b) the lighting was kind of buggy. When I went through the Game there was a preeeetty dark area and you didn't have a flashlight in that area. When I then exited the Game and came back to it later, after I reloaded the save, suddenly everything was bright and all the lights were on.c) in some areas were soundbugs. Not everywhere but in a few rooms you couldn't hear your own footsteps anymore, only when you left those areas.d) Sometimes there were prompts missing. (Example: A few collectibles/memories didn't show that I could take it and without a walkthrough I would've missed them.)Using stairs in the Game could be kind of slow sometimes.We got saveroom music!The AI is pretty stupid and enemies can be hard to hit in their actually kind of big weakpoints.The human "models" look terrible.Almost no enemy variety.Some references to the RE Games and even Metal Gear Solid.Never had ammo problems, in the beginning it was all kind of sparse but it accumulated over time. Also there is an accessibility option in the settings where the game gives you ammo for bosses when you should be out but I never used it.So now on to another big thing that I have to get off my chest. 30% of the Game I played blind. But then I kind of had the feeling that I was missing optional content and I didn't really take note of every area where I thought there could be something that I either have to come back to, to progress the story or optional stuff for achievements.So I decided to check a walkthrough. And what ended up happening: I used it for the rest of the Game. So I pretty much robbed myself of a blind playthrough experience.Let me say that Combat is super easy, so are the bosses. But some puzzles can stump you. Even though most of them, I still figured out on my own but there are also some that are kind of obscure to get.The thing with me using the walkthrough mainly, is because there are so many items that I just overlooked, even though I am pretty thorough in my Games. And this - for me- is the Games biggest fault. Items are not highlighted enough.Some Items are in random corners and they are also super small, so they are easy to miss in all the rubble lying around. And I don't mean that I need yellow paint everywhere to highlight things, I just needed a little more "glow" or visual clarity in all the cluttered environments to make out items that you can actually pick up. So yeah, either check every corner and every table 10 times over or use a walkthrough.This really is my main gripe with the Game. And since I started using the walkthrough 30% in, I of course missed out on some items for achievements. But that's okay.Many things I wrote sound quite negative but it is still a solid and competent game in what it does especially when you consider it is not a AAA Game.The puzzles are actually kind of clever and fun, I think they are even better than the puzzles in RE7/RE8.There were also a few (under a handful, but still) jumpscares that got me and the story is also competent enough that you want to see the ending. It is by no means great, but it keeps you going anyways.Fobia also has New Game + after completing and just like in the RE Games you can achieve different ranks (C-S+++). So it has replayability. If you are an achievement hunter you have to start a new game anyway. There are achievements for playing and not getting hit or maxing out all your weapons.But I didn't care that much for this Game that I would do that.Verdict: Even though it has a few drawbacks, I still think for fans of RE7/RE8 this is a must play. I just hope you can live with a little bit of jank here and there.Also don't be like me and get a walkthrough early on. You will probably miss out on items anyway even if you are thorough...

_childDocuments_.review: Fobia is a pretty solid game with plenty of references to previous horror games/franchises and although having finished, it ultimately didn't capture the survival horror formula I was looking for... The game is far more focused on a puzzle-solving narrative, and much of the core game play is tied to this as you navigate through the levels, and whilst the puzzles themselves were executed quite well I did end up often getting frustrated because I missed a really obscure hint hidden away somewhere, or I had forgotten there was a locked room/item somewhere. (there is no map in this game, so you're required to make mental notes). The story, whilst I won't give anything away really wasn't captivating in my view and honestly by the end of the game I really didn't care or know what exactly was going on. In terms of "scares" there is nothing here, at no given point throughout my playtime was I dreading going into an area, or caught off guard except the horrible flashing screen effects. Where the game really falls short is the combat... there are just TWO enemy types in this game, a generic looking zombie and an insect/bug, with the exception of two mini-bosses that pose absolutely no threat or induce any type of fear or anticipation as you navigate through the game, to the extent where I didn't die the whole game, had an absurd amount of ammo and heals, topped off with an incredibly anti-climatic end boss fight with an end cut-scene ripped out the Kojima playbook... (still waiting for an indie studio to get this right).Fobia might be for you if you like to take your time and study every nook and cranny in a room and become absorbed in puzzles, but if you're looking for something more akin to your classic Resident Evil/Silent Hill then you're better off looking elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I expect a horror/survival horror game, got a hidden object/escape room game.It starts out not so well - The game feels cheap and unpolished, the prologue happens in a prison, with no cutscene at all, then the player starts to search items. In the first chapter the player wakes up in a hotel room, starts to scavenge random items without knowing what they do in identical hotel rooms. There's no map other than maps stuck on the wall, but all the rooms are identical, I had to explore blindly and try my luck to see if I'm on the right path. The camera is both a night version and a tool to open supernatural path,  but the entire game lacks proper instruction and story, I feel tedious fast and decided not to torture myself any longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Makes pretty much all of the mistakes you can in a first indie-dev horror game. Extremely dark gamma that's hard to see through, "jump" scares all over the place and the character you play as doing things that, in-game, make zero sense. Also tons of pointless cutscenes. Has you backtracking in the first chapter for absolutely no reason. Look. If you want to make a good horror game (or any game for that matter), you need to give compelling reasons for the players to do things or else its just a ton of obvious padding. I did not, in fact, need to take a key from a door, to a cabinet, back to THE SAME DOOR in order to progress the game. That's wasting everyone's time. If I plead anything to developers, please play games in the genre you're making for and learn from them about what does and doesn't work.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Fobia is a puzzle game with a horror theme. That's fine if you're into puzzle games but I was under the assumption from the tags that this was a survival horror experience with actual gameplay and not a glorified walking sim with an emphasis on puzzle solving. In the two hours I played I solved a dozen puzzles and didn't fight a single enemy. To me that's tedious and very boring. It also doesn't help that said puzzles are illogical with solutions that rely on you getting lucky and spotting a small detail that's easily miss-able. Here's an example, you need to open chest drawers in a particular sequence that is only known by looking at a random painting on a separate floor. Yeah.. that's not good game design. While Fobia tries to emulate it's contemporaries like Resident Evil or Silent Hill it falls short in the sense that the pacing is completely off. In RE I'm not solving hours of puzzles chained back to back. I'm navigating a dangerous world of monsters with puzzles thrown in to add variety not make up the entire experience. So yeah if you go in expecting classic survival horror you'll be disappointed, if you go in with the idea this is a puzzler first and foremost then you might get some enjoyment out of Fobia. For me though this is a hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was pretty good. Has some decent spooks, fun puzzles, and the like. There are so many things that point to there being three endings, from the achievement for beating the game three times to a secret room that shows scenes of the first two endings alongside what could be a third. _childDocuments_.review: (booking tips - ask for a knife)St. Dinfna Hotel has a lot, a lot of puzzles. It's the safe codes, hidden in notes. It's invisible hints, revealed only via camera. It's a special key, which you assemble gradually and then backtrack to unlock multiple boxes. And more!Solving the above is rewarding, as you get upgrade points, rare ammo and in other cases pressing correct keys is a requirement to advance a story.What does this game have in common with RE? Rare saving stations. Inventory, which you can expand. Scarce ammo and shaking enemies. Aforementioned puzzles. There's even an item box, where you can store unwanted things. Furthermore, say hello to a local chaser. Not as tough as Nemesis or Mr X, but its appearances (often after important story episodes), may disturb you.By difficulty, it's more forgiving. Multiple mechanics (camera, puzzles, new blockages) play out well. In the end you may have more questions than answers, but for me it was well worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: A great quest with action elements. The combat is not overwhelming, though, I died quite a few times - but just because I spent ammo lavishly and was low on ammo during some boss fights.The mystery... well, it kept me hooked throughout the game, but I can't say it all became clear in the end (even though I did collect the notes meticulously). Actually, I am still confused when it comes to the bigger picture. Could it be by devs intention? Maybe they plan to have part 2, idk.One annoying thing is that there is no personal map, where you could see locked doors/unsolved puzzles. The hotel is rather big, and you have to run back and forth a lot (and switch between camera and no camera mode), so such map would make total sense.I would also like to complain (and warn you if you're reading this) - there is this thing, called "memories". In order to collect them, you need to interact with it, and then left-click again, not right-click! Otherwise, you'd just be putting them back. I missed several memories by just putting them back after inspecting.All in all I enjoyed the game, even though I was annoyed at some poins.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice indie survival horror for fans of the genre.Could have been way better but game is still good (personal score is at the bottom)+ The Hotel is amazing, the detail and level design in it are great! Leaves u rly wanting more of it (this is probably the strongest and best part of the game, luckily hotel is ~70% of the game)- Sadly the Lab area is not like that and even tho it seems big it isn't :/- 2 Main areas only (hotel/lab)- Overall game is not 2 short but def should have been longer- 2 Walking simulator sequences. On 1st play they are even interesting but later just plain boring and repetitive + the 1st time the "walk sim" section came I was super excited to continue exploring the hotel and it rly put my excitement to continue down+- Camera mechanics is a great addition but they should have used it for more rooms/puzzles (almost all the time when u need the camera for the clue it was in the same room)+ Inventory management done right! (think early RE and RE7)- "Ambient" sound is nonexisten, you can hear some sounds if u turn the volume up but there is no background music or anything.. The boss fight/chase sequence sound is great+ Even tho there is no ambient sound the atmosphere is still nice and keeps u on your toes cos u never know what will be in the same hall you passed few times already- Overall game is 2 easy and u will never be low on resources unless u miss them (specially after the 1st boss)- Enemies are kinda meh the main ones have a nice rush attack/mode but overall they are not a threat (would be better if they used the rush more often or the surroundings were not against them)- 2nd boss is rly bad and way 2 easy, if he were more aggressive and jumped around faster and more often it would have been a worthy boss+ Great puzzles! More pls!+ Very nice secrets/easter eggs (some are optional but a true gamer will want 2 do them at least once)- To get 2 achivs you will have to beat the game 3 times (for the upgrade weapons one u will have to do at 2-3 plays collecting all/almost all upgrade items so u won't even be able to just rush the main story even tho once you beat the game u can rush a ~100% game in less then 3h)+- Graphics are nice altho the lighting (specially with raytracing) can rly be off. I started with raytrace but reflections were just disrupting my gameplay so I turned it off ~mid gameConclusion:Might be my high expectations after playing the demo (or even after seeing the trailer which makes the game seem longer than it is, i.e. from trailer u will think "Mines" will be a nice playable area while its a 1min walking sim) but I do feel the game had much more potential and could have been waaaay betterPersonally would give it 7/10Game is good and I had my fun with it, but it is missing a few important things that would have made it an easy 9 or 10 out of 10

Why are bugs traumatizing me by jumpingscaring my screen and my heartrate? Why does it take my guy 10 million years to switch from Camera to gun and flashlight and viceversa? _childDocuments_.review: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel : By Triple F"Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel", an indie psychological horror game, is a harrowing journey into the depths of fear, anxiety, and the unknown. Developed by a small team of dedicated creators, this game offers a hauntingly unique experience that pushes the boundaries of what horror games can achieve. Prepare to be psychologically challenged and emotionally drained as you navigate the eerie halls of the St. Dinfna Hotel in this unforgettable adventure.The game presents an atmospheric masterpiece that's as terrifying as it is visually stunning. The graphics are a testament to the developers' commitment to detail. The dilapidated hotel, shrouded in darkness, is rendered with impeccable realism. The use of lighting and shadows is particularly praiseworthy, as it effectively sets the tone of impending dread. Every flickering light bulb, rusted pipe, and bloodstain on the walls contributes to the oppressive ambiance that constantly envelops you.Character and monster design are equally impressive, showcasing grotesque and unsettling creatures that fit seamlessly into the eerie atmosphere. The game's art style leans toward a nightmarish surrealism, making encounters with these entities all the more unsettling. The attention to detail extends to the protagonist's character model and animations, adding depth to the immersive experience.I found it quite interesting, the way "Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel" takes a more minimalist approach in terms of game-play, emphasizing atmosphere and storytelling over action-packed sequences. You'll find yourself navigating through a series of puzzles and riddles, each progressively more complex. These puzzles are cleverly designed and are closely tied to the narrative, making them feel integral to the story rather than mere obstacles.While playing, you'll find that the game relies quite heavily on exploration, encouraging players to scrutinize every corner of the hotel for clues and items. This approach adds to the tension as you never know what unsettling revelation may await you in the next room. The lack of combat mechanics might disappoint some, but it aligns perfectly with the game's theme of vulnerability and powerlessness."Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel" also greatly excels in creating a relentlessly oppressive atmosphere that permeates every aspect of the game. The narrative is delivered through fragmented notes, diary entries, and cryptic messages left by previous occupants of the hotel. This method of storytelling keeps you engaged as you piece together the dark history of St. Dinfna.The story is deeply psychological, delving into themes of guilt, trauma, and the human psyche. It leaves you questioning not only the reality of the hotel but also your own sanity. The game masterfully employs a sense of cosmic horror, reminiscent of H.P. Lovecraft's work, where the true horror lies in the unknown and the incomprehensible.Sound plays a pivotal role in "Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel", adding a layer of terror that is hard to shake off. The soundtrack, consisting of hauntingly beautiful compositions, perfectly complements the game's atmosphere. It knows when to be subtle, letting silence do the heavy lifting, and when to crescendo to heighten tension.Sound effects are meticulously crafted to induce anxiety. Creaking floorboards, distant whispers, and the eerie echoes of your footsteps all contribute to the sense of dread. The voice acting, although limited, is suitably eerie and adds depth to the narrative.In terms of replay-ability, some players might find "Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel" to be limiting, as it primarily relies on its narrative. Once you've unraveled the mysteries and experienced the story's twists and turns, there might be less incentive to revisit the game. However, it's worth replaying to fully appreciate the intricacies of the narrative and uncover hidden details that may have eluded you on the first play-through.To finish off the review, I believe "Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel" is a masterclass in atmospheric horror that deserves recognition for its exceptional artistry and storytelling. It's not a game for the faint of heart, but for those willing to confront their deepest fears and delve into the darkest corners of the human psyche, it offers a uniquely terrifying and emotionally resonant experience. This game sets a high bar for indie horror titles and is a must-play for horror enthusiasts seeking a genuinely unsettling and thought-provoking experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a HUGE survival horror fan! The genre is actually why I got more into gaming. Seeing the screen shots of this game I had to give it a shot and I am glad I did. There are puzzles on puzzles on puzzles. Some main, most side. So it is up to you to solve them. To be fair, a good number are just locating a code, but sometimes they are hidden pretty well. Still, it felt good using my brain to solve some of these. Gun play is serviceable. Only thing I would like is the handgun/revolver to sound a bit beefier. Enemy variety is lacking to be fair, but the design of what we got is pretty good. Also, the game isn't the longest. So I did not mind too much. These are small issues compared to the whole though. Is it scary? Honestly, not really. However, I do not scare easy, so mileage may vary depending on the person. That being said, there were a few times the game got me. Atmosphere is top notch. Graphics are clean. Story is taken seriously. Music fits nicely. These guys knew exactly what they wanted to make and in my opinion, accomplished with flying colors. Issues I Ran IntoPersonal journal does not save last visited page. So any new entry, you go down memory lane to get there. There isn't a million entries, so it isn't too bad. Honestly, any bugs all came from the last visited location of the game. This included, footsteps muted, safe not allowing me access, getting stuck between two unlocked doors, weapon swap or draw not allowed. Granted, a quick load fixed all of it. But for someone doing a speed run, or forgot to save, this could be a huge issue. Only suggestion I have for this game is adding an echo after shots depending on location. It gives it that extra oomph I'm looking for when shooting. Again, what we got is fine. Just a suggestion if possible. All that being said, I gotta say, I love finding these indie games that just go off swinging. Blows my mind to see what hard work and determination can do. No way making a game is easy. Especially a game like this. I truly hope to see more from Pulsatrix. We need more fighting survival horror. I know it doesn't pull COD numbers, but to me, on a cold Winter night, snow outside, lights turned off, Astro A40s blasting in my ears, nothing beats it. Great job! I truly say go for it! The game is a great addition to my collection.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10A really good horror game that takes a lot of inspiration from RE 7, 8 and the recent remakes of 2 and 3.Fobia is a game where you play a journalist called Roberto that is invited to investigate the occurrences that happened in the city of Treze Trilhas (or Thirteen Trails), staying in the St. Dinfna Hotel, where strange things start to happen and he soon finds himself in the middle of a ruined hotel filled with monsters.The game largely plays like recent RE games: explore, find items necessary to progress, solve puzzles, fight monsters. Combat involves the use of guns where standing still improves the accuracy, trying to land shots in monsters' weak spots. Upgrades and more inventory slots can be found along the way. The inspiration on RE games is very clear throughout the entire game, from the gameplay to the plot and the ambientation.It isn't a perfect game, but it has potential. It's also worth mentioning that the devs are listening to player feedback and working on patches to fix some things in the game.The good:The neutral:The bad:Despite the issues, I had a lot of fun with the game and I'm currently waiting for future patches to play it again.Easy recommended for any fans of horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, my feelings are insanely mixed about this game. The puzzles are excellent, the movement and inventory/interactions are fantastic, the story is complicated enough to be interesting without being so cryptic you can't follow it, and the atmosphere is really wonderful, unique, and well done.However... The lack of a map solely serves to extend gameplay totally needlessly. The game really overstays its welcome when you're wandering around aimlessly, knowing you have all the key items you need, but unsure of what door you need to get to in order to proceed. There's at least one section where I was pretty sure I softlocked because I was missing a VERY minor prompt to get to the next area. I wandered around for probably a full hour before finally ending up where I needed to be. The lack of a map doesn't even make sense in the context of the game universe because your character has a journal. You'd really think that the first time we see a map we'd jot it down in the journal so we could at least reference where we were and what rooms we haven't entered. In this regard, it's downright frustrating at points with how obtuse the destinations are. I can guarantee this game would be 2-3 hours shorter in average playtime if the devs chose to include a map.There are also some other quality of life issues. Camera bob is pretty infuriating, but I did eventually get over it. The gunplay is awful, this game would almost do better with no guns and just the threat of enemies that you need to dodge/run away from (keeping in mind, the enemy AI is so potato they'll whiff most attack attempts.) The headcrab/facehugger guys will chain attack you and pretty much just serve as an infrequent jumpscare. They don't feel very well programmed and the 2 canned animations you'll get, usually in a combo with no possible reaction time, will ruin the jumpscare effect pretty quickly. You'll end the game with so much surplus ammo you could do a whole other playthrough with just your current inventory, and that's WITHOUT the accessibility option to add more ammo throughout the game.So.. it's good, and I can recommend it, and it's both directly and indirectly referencing a bunch of survival horror franchises in some of the best ways but man, this game has some segments that either shouldn't exist or should be far more linear than they are. I'm into exploration and even backtracking, but spending so much time aimlessly wandering just isn't fun and it really impedes the pace of the game.And as a final note, cutscenes should be skippable. Maybe not on a first playthrough, but at least in the NG+ playthrough or as a toggle-able option in the settings. I'm not trying to sit through 10-15 minutes of pointless "waking up" cutscenes on a second or third playthrough, and the information gained through cutscenes isn't even that valuable compared to the information gained in-game through documents and phone calls.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of mixed feelings about this game. The atmosphere, sound design and graphics are all top tier, the St Dinfna hotel genuinely seems like a living breathing place that people actually inhabited before the plot kicked off. However this sort of trails off once you leave the hotel and get to the final act of the game, where it seems empty and video gamey.The gameplay is fine, some of the animations are a little bit stiff and lengthy, but Its not enough to pull me out of the game. Fobia pretty clearly wears it's inspiration on its sleeve, coming from the same breed of survival horror as resident evil 7 and 8, and borrowing aspects from Resident Evil 2 and 3 with the occasional large monster popping up to give chase. My one criticism is that sometimes ammo can be a little tighter than usual, leading to softlocks in some boss fights, but as long as you have half decent aim, that shouldn't happen.The story is a little confusing to follow, involving "temporal anomalies" (aka time travel) and everything that usually comes with that sort of plot, but I was able to figure it out mostly, and the notes are decently interesting to realise.My biggest criticism of the game is that the hotel itself can be very confusing to navigate, and there's no map (other than a few for certain wings on certain floors of the hotel) this could be rectified by having a map of the floor, or even a floor number next to the stairs on all he floors. Overall though, If you are a fan of survival horror games like Dead Space or especially the newer resident evil games and remakes, I can recommend picking this up, though I do believe that £24 is a little steep, so perhaps wait for a sale

But it all culminates very confusingly and vaguely, so much so that the game can't explain it, and not that it chooses to keep it vaguel.  The game never bothers to even try to mesh the concepts together.It greatly saddens me to say the game was just boring, too easy, the monsters were just inconvenient, and the story was void.Even the banner and mascot of the game is a generic gas mask girl.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this game! It's a survival horror with a big emphasis on puzzles. The puzzles are fun and not too testing, although I did find the number based puzzle on the cube a bit more tricky.  You can get sidetracked with optional puzzles to complete and you'll gain ammo and upgrades. There's a lot of backtracking which is only made worse by some floors being partially blocked and having to take the stairs from floors above or below to gain access to other parts of the hotel. It never annoyed me too much but it does make it very confusing as to where you are and I did get stuck a few times not knowing where to go. Still, it is rewarding once you've figured it out. I like the design of the enemies and at first, they appear to be very slow, slower and clumsier than your average zombie but they can suddenly dash at you and I got caught out a few times whilst being super cocky. Overall though, they are quite easy to fend off, depending on how lucky your shots are. There are upgrades to weapons but I didn't find upgrading the accuracy much of a difference really. Some shots are visibly off centre but enemies still went down with a single shot, then on other occasions, it took 4 dead centre shots to take them down. I've encountered two bosses so far and although they are tanky, they're easy enough to defeat which might disappoint hardcore survivalists. I'll update once complete but I think it's great.Update: So, after finishing the game I encountered a few bugs. One of them was game breaking which allowed me to leave Christopher's chapter at the house early without obtaining all the parts of the key for a subsequent chapter. Rather than waiting for a fix, I ended up reloading a previous save. I still think this is a great game. I just hope some of the bugs can be ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Great psychological horror that falls short with overwhelming puzzles and clunky combat mechanics, frustrating unbalanced boss fights and a very confusing story. The game FOBIA could be so much more, it is trying to do too much and be everything while failing at the basic mechanics all at the same time. To start it off the monsters in this game have a dash and dive attack, while your character is slow and clunky does not have the mobility to dodge or move out of the way quick enough to respond to the animation, it's a glaring issue in the game and it is one that comes up often. The ammo and bandages in the game are very limited it is the most frustrating thing in the game you need "ALLOT" of ammo to kill bosses over time, through the game you use most of your ammo on other mobs that sponge the shots take forever to take down, you won't have any to finish a boss fights. In short FOBIA is incredibly unbalanced it has the ability to do better they have the monsters and the psychological horror factor but they lack balance and story compared to other horror games out there. _childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Resident Evil, I really want to like this game. However, I can't even bring myself to finish it. What Fobia attempts to do is replicate the same feeling of the survival horror oriented RE's (most of the internet would like to think it's an homage to 7, I'd say 2). It brings to the table:1. A consolidated area for most of the game. Think the RC Police Station in RE2, but it's a hotel now.2. A Mr. X that stalks you, although it's in certain areas so maybe it's more like Nemesis from RE3.3. Creepy enemies that are bullet sponges.4. Puzzles to unlock things.I could list a few more, but I'd be here longer than I want to be. What Fobia does wrong is that it mimics RE at only a surface level. Yes, it checks off most of the boxes, but the execution is just all wrong. Let's list why...1. The hotel is extremely boring and they don't give you a map. How am I supposed to keep track of things?2. The Mr. X/Nemesis knock off segments are too short. I would've appreciated it if it was a constant presence, maybe. 3. The enemies are simply bullet sponges and *only* that. Even the bosses! RE gave you a knife as a way to at least get enemies off of you and to do some damage, but not Fobia. Relying only on firearms and then not giving the player any ammo is not fun in my opinion. 4. The puzzles just aren't fun and there are too many of them in order to just progress a little. Plus, the lack of any map whatsoever is just rubbing salt in the wound.I can tell the love for the genre is there, but please do better next time.

It's annoying but it's not deal breaking level so you can still have a fun time.I really hate the head bobbing and you can't turn it off in this game. The control is very clunky as well. Switching between the camera and guns is soooo slooooo Like, please speed up the animation 3 times. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It took you 3-4 seconds to switch from a gun to the camera and back. And in this game, you need to do that almost constantly. Going through that was a horrible experience. Also, the black out mechanic is almost useless and annoying. The screen sometimes go black because of some paranormal activities, but that's it. There is nothing else to it. And it happens many time as well. Imagine trying to proceed but you have to stop for 5-10 seconds to wait for the light to come back up, several times! Make it once or twice is acceptable (for atmospheric reason) but doing it again and again and again is not.Pros:Fun survival horrorFun puzzlesDecent lengthGood atmosphereGood graphicsBug-free experience (personally)Cons:Very clunky controlCan't turn off head bobbingHave to ♥♥♥♥ gun everytimeBad voice actingHorrible flashlight Few variety of guns + enemies are too easy7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks VERY polished at first, but it soon becomes apparent that the polish is unevenly applied. Great environments, great atmosphere, good puzzles, but the combat system and enemy designs feel phoned in. They're mostly generically creepy flesh monsters, and while I'm usually a fan of a good flesh monster, these ones just seem to lack any sense of place or purpose. They stand perfectly still or shuffle around randomly until they spot you, at which point they do nothing but charge and try to eat your face...assuming they don't get snagged on a doorframe or stuck in a corner. There aren't very many enemies to be found, either, and most of them go from being a thrill to being a chore after only one or two encounters. The boss fights, especially, feel like a slog. You get locked in a room with a big scary thing and have to put a billion bullets into it before you can return to exploring. The game gives you ammo drops in every boss arena that quietly refresh when you turn your back, so you can't get locked in an unwinnable fight, but being handed bottomless resources takes a lot of the sting out of the "survival" aspect of survival horror. It's one thing when a survival horror game decides not to emphasise combat, but if that's what you're doing, you can't also force your combat system into the limelight so much. Even the game's otherwise excellent atmosphere starts to suffer when you realize that these stumbling flesh-clowns are responsible for 90% of the actual peril you'll face. There's a lot to love about this game, really. If they'd focused more on fleshing out combat, or de-emphasized it, it could have earned my recommendation. I hope to see another offering from this team in the future that gets it right.

_childDocuments_.review: I've decided to re-write this review as I think last time I was salty about losing progress. I've since 100%'d the game and got all the achievements which just goes to show how great a game it is. A few cons I would point out, is that the first one (or two if you go back in) times through the game, it's very easy to get lost. The game would really benefit from a map feature, like Silent Hill, that updates as you go, that would be fantastic. I still maintain that the archaic save system isn't the best. Not that the game should quick save every three feet, but getting the achievement for a damage-less run had a few hair pulling moments with the spiders popping out from the shadows and needing to replay like 20-30 minutes over is not tension, it's tedium. Also, the story is tragic. I have played through this game 3 times now, and seen both endings and I'm still not really sure what the plot is about. It's like the plot to a porno, not important and if anything just gets in the way of the action. One thing that I really have to commend the devs for, is the sense of exploration. There were a fair few puzzles I completely missed on my first run, even though I was trying to search every nook. There are collectables in the game in the form of upgrade points and memories, which really do help with getting you to search the whole map. The puzzles were also well thought out, there were a few in there that had me scratching my head for a little while, so they're not like baby's first adventure game by any means! All-in-all, if you're a fan of survival horror games that this game is clearly playing homage to, you will certainly enjoy your time with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the worst indie horror game, but not very good either. Awkward voice acting, very basic enemy designs and AI, a lot of cheap jumpscare attempts, and player model is a bit weird. Doesn't feel like there's a good enough utilization of the camera mechanic. The flashlight is horrendous, doesn't light up very well in many scenarios, the entire light beam gets blocked by high railings, and when it's on you're unable to see highlights on interactable puzzle elements and such. The objectives can be pretty vague and easy to get lost in at times due to inconsistent guidance. There's also the issue of the player speed is really slow, makes for some painful backtracking or going through the flashback chapters as well as can make it impossible to dodge enemy attacks if you aren't already out of the way. There were two or three points where I was starting to believe the game was bugged. As for good things, the guns work well, and the chase segments are cool especially the music for it. _childDocuments_.review: Fobia St. Dinfna Hotel is a new horror game that revolves around a mysterious hotel where things aren’t always what they seem. You mainly play the game as Roberto Lopes, who is staying at the St. Dinfna Hotel to write a story about the strange occurrences that are happening there.You are supposed to meet your friend Stephanie, who is going to help you with your article, but she is nowhere to be found. After a week of no progress, you decide to hop in the shower to relax but are swallowed up by some sort of time-bending black hole.You awake 50 years into the future and the hotel is crumbling around you. You find a new lens for your camera that allows you to see a different dimensional version of your surroundings, and you must discover what has happened. While this synopsis might seem a little “out there”, things become much clearer as you play on. The hotel is definitely a great environment, there is just something that is eerie about the whole thing. There is cultist activity, flashbacks to the distant past, time-travel, and mutant research subjects. It is filled with puzzles, limited ammo, and mysteries in every corner.As such, the gameplay reminds me of the original Resident Evil games, but in first person. As you progress, you will gain access to a few different weapons that you can upgrade by spending points that you accrue by collecting tesseracts. For example, these upgrades can increase the gun’s damage, recoil, and magazine size. While the controls can be a bit stiff with the guns, everything works well enough.Another great thing about the game are the puzzles and sense of exploration. You do come across items that will help you access that were previously unreachable. I would highly recommend keeping a notepad to jot down locations of things like safes and locked rooms to help yourself remember all of these additional areas. The rewards are usually worth going for since things like ammo and upgrade points are fairly limited.The boss encounters in the game are pretty standard and the enemy variation leaves room for improvement. It reminds me of how Deadly Premonition added combat to help sell the game and make it more interesting to a wider range of people.This is highlighted by the “clunky” weapon controls and lack of responsiveness. It’s not terrible, but certainly not very fluid. Even with max upgrades for recoil and aiming of certain weapons, they still lack precision. I guess you could chalk this up to Roberto being just a journalist, but combined with limited ammo, it can be a chore.Other than that minor complaint, there is a lot to enjoy with Fobia! Technically, the game runs well. Environments are nicely detailed, character models are serviceable, monster design (while limited) is well done.I also did enjoy the story overall and the two endings. After you complete the game for the first time you unlock New Game + which allows you to try and max out your weapon upgrades and also aim for a higher ranking.To complete my play through, it took around 10 hours and I only managed to complete 44% of the puzzles and found 82% of the documents hidden in the hotel. There is quite a bit of value and fun to be had with Fobia – St. Dinfna Hotel and I hope you give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: "Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel" has some janky character animations and funny glitches, BUT it is a really nice game. Yes, it is overly ambitious for its low budget, but it delivers on so many fronts that I can forgive the rough edges. The most important things are well done: the map layout, the puzzles (of which there is a sh*t ton), the suspense. The combat is serviceable at best, but that's perhaps more acceptable in a survival horror game than in most genres. I also don't like the main stalker enemy, but he's got only a few appearances, so it's tolerable. The appeal of "Fobia" is really the titular hotel and the exploration of its many rooms and corridors. Pretty good atmosphere, too. An easy recommendation for fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty competent spiritual relative of the old-school tank control survival horror games blended with a lot of the new wave of survival horror: very old Resident Evil meets old Silent Hill at times meets Resident Evil 7. The story is pretty decent (though a couple beats feel kind of rushed and contrived), the gunplay is competent if not a bit repetitive in the latter chapters and the puzzles, while maybe too numerous, are for the most part pretty creative. Big complaint: there are some bits of the game where, seemingly to pad out length, (in a couple cases to artificially add tension) the level design pisses you around and makes you take overly circuitous routes around contrived obstacles. This could be fixed in the future by rewarding exploration with ways to re-open or clear new shortcuts. Overall, a pretty competent and fun indie horror with good puzzling and a decent story (though the ending is a bit abrupt and disappointing).

_childDocuments_.review: Fobia offers a unique gaming experience. The sound design, graphics, and storyline are its strong points. The immersive sound effects and the detailed graphics enhance the overall gaming experience, making each moment in the game feel real and intense.  There were barely any instances of characters appearing visually, but the game still manages to engage you with the voice acting and the lore. The storyline is well-crafted with a great build-up that keeps you hooked. The lore is intriguing and adds depth to the game world with the several documents and items of interest. _childDocuments_.review: ------------------ UPDATED ---------------------------I will say as of the recent patch the performance issues are, as far as I can tell, completely resolved. Now that I can play the game, and it seems alright, it feels wrong to leave the negative review up even though I haven't finished the game yet and can't put my full thoughts here. I will address what I can post patch now that I have had a chance to play a bit though. To clarify, pre-patch I couldn't run it even on low settings and now I can run it on high settings with no issues. The movement still feels a little clunky in spots, but without the hitching it is far more tolerable as to not really be an issue for me. If you can live with the kind of movement in games like RE7 you'll be fine here even if it's a little rough in spots.Now that I can play past the first area the lighting/coloration is still a bit annoying, but you do get a bit used to it, especially if you remove the vignette. Basically just look at the store screenshots and judge for yourself if it's a problem for you. I originally thought the lighting was off because it was a staged screenshot for the store until I bought it, but it does just have that somewhat washed out look. Some areas in game look alright despite it, others less so. It seems like they used very colorful lights in the levels then washed it out in their color balancing to make it look more grounded, so areas with those kinds of colors look alright and areas without a lot of color built in look less than good. Sound-wise I'm not noticing as much harsh higher pitched noise, I'm not sure if it was balanced in the patch, or if I just got the in-game settings just right, but if it's a problem for you on starting then it means it is fixable by fiddling. As to what I've played of the game itself it seems decent so far, some neat monster designs, plenty of RE style puzzles if you like that sort of thing. As mentioned above I haven't finished it yet, but as I write I am looking forward to playing more. I appreciate the work the dev team put into getting a patch out relatively quickly.------------------ PRE-PATCH --------------------------Spent 30 minutes messing around with various settings. Can't really speak much about the gameplay or the story because various technical issues were just too frustrating to deal with. Let me preface the rest of this review with saying my computer specs are decent, I have an i-7 cpu, 24gb of ram, and a GEForce 1080. Not top of the line but not even remotely low end.The performance of the game is awful. Standing still you can usually get a steady framerate, but looking around, moving, or hell, even looking at the floor sometimes will cause the game to chug and stutter for a second or more. I tried turning just about everything down to low, but to no avail, the game still will sporadically chug every 4 or 5 seconds while playing. Tried leaving the initial area until I got to the hotel lobby to ensure it wasn't just a particular room, but both areas had this problem *as well as* the connecting cutscene between them.Another technical issue seems to be the color and gamma correction, possibly also the lighting. No matter what I set my gamma to or what graphics settings I modified, the game looks washed out. At the initial mid gamma the game looks uniformly grey/black, with even bright lights blending in. Higher settings make things more visible, sort of, but it everything is just washed in light grey instead, conversely at low gamma settings the game is just a uniform black. The game just feels desaturated, and lacking contrast, shadows don't really seem to exist unless you make the whole game a shadow. It felt like the game practically had a film or a deep vignette over the screen and it was just frustrating, like my eyes could never adjust.Sound-wise just about anything higher pitched is going to hurt your ears unless you turn the game way the hell down. For example the menu sound that plays when opening your inventory in the first area ends with a brief high pitched metal noise and even setting the menu sounds down to the point where I could barely hear any other menu noises I still would somewhat wince when opening the inventory. Not sure if this is a balancing issue in some of the actual sound files or a sound design issue or what, but it's not very pleasant.Finally, other reviews have mentioned the insane head-bob, the lurchy control, and I can kind of respect it in that it does make your character and movement feel weighty, but given everything above it's just another thing you have to put up with. The performance especially interacts badly with this design choice as when the character is lurching back and forth, the game chugging and stuttering just makes it feel horrible.At the time of writing I would avoid this game, largely for technical reasons. Would love to give it another go if it got a technical/performance pass as it seems like there was some care put it into, it's just too rough to love at the moment though unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel's best efforts to emulate the horror of Resident Evil 7, it ultimately fell short of expectations, leaving players feeling disappointed and unfulfilled. The lack of terror and suspense in the game only served to highlight the emptiness and loneliness that players felt as they navigated through the dark and desolate world. The game's graphics and storyline may have been impressive, but they could not make up for the sense of dread and fear that was conspicuously absent. It was a sad reminder of the frailty of human hopes and expectations, and how easily they can be dashed by circumstances beyond our control. Despite its good gameplay mechanics, the game's lack of horror elements was a missed opportunity that left many players feeling unsatisfied. However, the spooky girl with the gas mask managed to steal the show with her eerie presence and memorable gashion sense, providing a glimmer of intrigue and fascination amidst an otherwise lackluster experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is unfortunately not a good game. I'm down for survival horror - that's what I bought the game for, after all - but this game is not good survival horror. Another review said "Good escape room, but bad survival horror." I'm inclined to agree, but I question even its quality as something akin to an escape room game. This game is primarily puzzles. Puzzles, puzzles, everywhere, halting progress near constantly. I'm not averse to some good puzzles, but these puzzles are often rather obtuse. Sure, some are pretty good, some are the super easy kind that a child could figure out - those are fine. What's not fine is running around for ages trying to figure out what the game wants you to find or do to solve its newest roadblock.A better game would utilise the fact that it has combat to break up the pace of having the player constantly solve puzzles or find codes or what have you. This game is quite light on combat, however, though frankly, perhaps this is a blessing in disguise? The game gives you paltry amounts of ammunition, and while I could kill the enemies in front of me with it, it never felt like I was engaging in any kind of good decision making process when expending it, especially when the enemies are just tanky as all hell, the pistol is inaccurate, even with a focused shot, and it doesn't sound good to shoot. There's no real enemy variety, either. Enemies block your path. Kill them. They have a weak spot in the center of their chest, but it doesn't really matter. The weak spot is so small, the pistol is so inherently inaccurate and the enemies' animations are so odd that it sincerely comes off more like a matter of RNG as to whether you'll hit it. I'm not sure I ever did. Maybe it's just visual and they don't react to being shot there. The game doesn't give me enough feedback to know.So we have a survival horror game where engaging with enemies is tedious rather than scary, and where exploration is halted *constantly* by something that will take you a while to figure out. Not off to a good start. I wish I could say the plot is engaging, but it isn't in the slightest, not helped by the absolutely amateur English voice acting. It's impossible to take these characters seriously when the delivery is this stiff and half-hearted. Perhaps its better in Portuguese. I likewise can't even speak too highly on the game's atmosphere - this is where it feels most like an escape room, and less like a survival horror game. It's got solid enough background noise, especially with the rain, to feel sort of lonely and quiet. It has nothing else going on most of the time, however, that would unsettle you and keep you on edge. Even when enemies appear, they aren't intimidating to listen to, music doesn't perk up to imply a sense of danger, it's just business as usual.I suppose if I can compliment anything, it's that the game's visuals are generally pretty good, so long as you don't look too closely at anything to see the low-resolution textures. It makes good use of shaders to give a look that's at least to some extent reminiscent of something like PT or Resident Evil 7. While I tire of horror games trying to go for this visual style, it's at least competently accomplished here. The big issue, however, is that the game is *dark*. A lot of the time, it feels like you can barely see a damn thing, with the flashlight providing such a paltry amount of light that it barely matters unless you're bumping up against something. The game's worst enemy is just garbage visibility. The camera the game gives you that can see into the past makes things even *darker*, which is a real pain in the ass considering you'll be using the camera relatively often to find items as well as hints and solutions to puzzles. Just rubbing salt into the wound, the default black levels are washed out and just hideous to look at, prompting me to have to turn the brightness down until black was actually black. You'd think turning the brightness down would make it even harder to see, but it didn't - it just made the opaque greys into opaque blacks. So the game's a mess. It's poorly paced, obtuse, hard to see, doesn't have a thick atmosphere, fails to scare the player, and has writing and voice acting too poor to at least present an engaging tale. If the game were free, I'd be more forgiving, but tell you that the game wastes your time too much to bother with. The fact that they're asking $30 for this, however, is just not acceptable for the quality of the game itself, especially since the game has no replay value. An extra $10 nets you Resident Evil 2 Remake. $10 less gets you Resident Evil 7, which is a game I have plenty of misgivings about, but it's a far better game than this is in nearly every respect. Signalis and Tormented Souls are both $20. Hell, Nightmare of Decay is a game I don't care much for, but it's a better game with more replay value and only costs $5. The value proposition here, I feel, is just insulting.All that being said, the developer is currently trying to raise funds for a second game. More power to them. I hope their next game takes lessons learned from this one to make something special.

I abandoned it after 5 hours.There's literally not enough ammo in the game to kill all the enemies it throws at you, even if you don't waste any ammo on the unkillable boss enemy chasing you around, and even if you are scrounging around for the small 1-3 pistol bullets hidden in random dark places. You will frequently find additional inventory slots, which is great, but it doesn't solve the annoyance of every single room key, tool, quest item, ammo type, even your flashlight and even your camera each take their own inventory slots! _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for February 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before March 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A PS2-era horror game, right down to the graphics.Fobia isn’t your typical horror game, it doesn’t seem like it’s trying to jump out and scare you, at least not in what I saw, and I’ll be honest, I probably didn’t see as much as I should have.  I got stuck three times in this game in the first hour and needed to use a guide twice because I couldn’t make progress.  In all three situations, I didn’t notice something that probably should have been obvious.  Make sure you look low to the ground, I’ll just say that. The thing is Fobia though feels like a key hunting simulator.  Much of the game is hunting for items.  There are puzzles, inventory management, and eventually combat apparently, but the first section is a couple of puzzles where there are not a lot of hints.  There is a great mechanic where you use a camera to somehow transfer between two time periods, but also… well I mean I’m showing this scene because my god, the character models look straight out of the PS2 era. Pick this up if you’re a die-hard Silent Hill or early Resident Evil fan and want to pretend this came out back then.  It came out last year, but man it feels so dated.  Honestly, the graphics and gameplay here are really what makes me not enjoy this game, it’s not really that scary or horrific. There are so many key hunts, it feels like a really bad version of an Escape room game, but instead of a short experience that’s only the first section of it. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: To begin with, a video reviewReview of Fobia — St. Dinfna Hotel. A copycat of Resident Evil, which in many ways surpassed the originalStorylineThe town of Tresi-Trilias is considered a strange place for a reason - what the hell has not happened here. Researchers have found suspicious artifacts. Under unclear circumstances miners were killed. Residents have complained of an unusual ghost: a child allegedly running around in a gas mask. Also, many things in these parts are run by a sect called the Sacred Trail.The protagonist is an aspiring journalist who has decided to solve the mysteries of Trezi-Trilias. In addition, a local resident has promised to assist. Alas, as soon as the guy checked into the St. Dinfna Hotel, everything did not go according to plan: the receptionist behaved suspiciously, the assistant never showed up, and all the clues led to a dead end. That, however, was only the beginning.When the journalist planned to abandon the investigation and go home, there appeared a rift in the bathroom, from which flew out the very same child ghost in a gas mask. After that, the hero lost consciousness and woke up practically in hell: the hotel is destroyed, there is not a soul around, and creepy monsters roam the corridors. What happened? How much time had passed? How to escape? These are the questions you will have to answer.On the whole, the story came out decent. The writers skillfully intrigue, reveal the creepy town's past and tell curious stories about ghosts and monsters. It is most interesting to read the tapes and listen to the audiotapes that the survivors left behind. The poor people tried to save themselves to the last and willingly described their misfortunes - some stories give you goosebumps.The investigation process is fascinating, and the narrative is often served not through cutscenes or notes, but directly through gameplay. Gamers will be allowed to take control of different characters and look at what is happening through their eyes. This approach perfectly immerses you in the story.If we believe the page on Steam, the game does not have the Russian language - but in fact subtitles are availableIf you believe the Steam, there is no Russian in the game, but in fact there are subtitles in the gameHowever, you should turn a blind eye to the doubtful finale, because most of the passage of Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel cool intrigues and skillfully immerses into the atmosphere. The journey to the truth itself turned out to be interesting.GameplayIf you compare Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel with other games, it reminds Resident Evil 7 the most. First-person camera, similar animations, camera locations and a constant sense of menace. Even some of the enemies look like mold, and the hero is hunted by a local version of Jack Baker. You shouldn't compare the stalker to Tyrant, though - the creature from St. Dinfna Hotel prefers to follow scripts rather than walk around freely.True, the developers have shifted the emphasis from action to research and solving puzzles - the shooting in Fobia is times less than in Biohazard. For example, the gun comes into the protagonist's hands only after about 1.5 hours after the game starts. Before that the poor guy has to wander around the ruined hotel and shake with fear.But you still have to shoot, because there are huge cockroaches, dangerous mutants and even bosses waiting on your way. Of course, bossfights can't be called outstanding, but they keep you in suspense perfectly. Thanks to the eerie surroundings and oppressive atmosphere you go to the important battle as if you were going to the executioner. It's a shame that the devil isn't usually as scary as you make him out to be.Pros of the gameExploring the world is fun;Awesome puzzles;An engaging narrative.Cons of the gameSimplistic shooting;Lots of backtracking;Weak ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played dozens of horror games, and I can confidently claim that it is the best one of all.This game has no annoying stuff you usually find in horror games. Always sufficient light, sufficient bullets (you can even choose your favourite weapon and just go with it through the whole game), mostly sufficient inventory (to the point its fun that its scarce rather than annoying), memorisable location (at times hard, but more than possible), comfortable walkthrough (rarely hard puzzles), a lot of checkpoints (that are always available to use), understandable and great story (at times too many names, but the story is unique and eerie), there are objectives (you mostly always know what to do), no bugs (literally none, except from rare AI that stucks that must be killed, so doesn't matter), magnificent graphics (you really feel like in antique hotel).Although it is a horror game, I found it more in the sense of an immersion. It has horror aspects, i.e. scary spiders, scary writings, scary story etc etc, but its not like most cheap horror games that base off screamers. It is just full immersion that never lets you down. There are only two potential downsides. Firstly, items are indeed scattered across the map. When you need an item to open a door, this item can lie anywhere in the hotel. So you will have to check and re-check every corner of the hotel to find this lost item. Can get boring (only sometimes, the game itself is fascinating), but this aspect is not too extreme. Secondly, I found the camera annoying. Basically it shows you hidden objects, i.e. like alternative reality. At times feels unnecessary and only hurts immersion.Generally, I would more than suggest it. It took me 17 hours, but its mainly because I was motivated to look in every corner. If you do it fast, I guess you can manage it in 12-14 hours. I got the game on sale, but even without it, it is worth every penny. Fully suggesting it!

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 - Classic Survivor Horror: Unlock, Upgrade, Backtrack. Scavenge. Survive. I think most survival horror fans will like this game, but I could see casual players being on the fence about this game. Lots of backtracking, decent puzzles and a tension filled creepy atmosphere. The enemies are pretty basic B!the'z and the combat takes a backseat to the environment navigation. But the boss fights and common enemy encounters we at the least entertaining, though a lil easy. There were a few sections that I thought were outstanding, where i'd had made a lot of progress, opened locked areas and found new items. It was a stretch where there were no save points, meaning if i died all my time would be lost and i'd have to go back and do it all again. It also was set up so backtracking and finding a previous save point was too much of a hassle. I remember feeling incredibly anxious and tense during the whole exploration just to be met with a "run for you life" scenario which really added to the tension of needing to find a save point. Immediately after that sequence I thought what an amazing job the devs did with that section. If I had died at any point i would have lost my sh!t. I don't think this games for everyone and its got some flaws, but overall its one of the few games I played recently that I thought was worth my time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish neutral was an option for recommendation. It has some really cool ideas, good monster and set design, decent enough voice acting, some tense moments, a few really fun puzzles and a lot of notes and collectables. It felt like a blend of older and newer survival horror and that worked for a good portion of the game. On the other hand the movement felt very janky at times, the combat wasn't good, the story is very convoluted and messy and the endings are really bad (like no spoilers but both of them just suck).If you like survival horror games that try some different things and have promise then I'd say pick this up (preferably on sale) but prepare for very little to actually make sense, otherwise just avoid.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly competent addition to the Survival Horror genre. Fobia feels like a darling love letter to Resident Evil and Silent Hill. More specifically, RE7 and PT. Taking place in a hotel, I was rather impressed with the use of the aesthetic. Although I found that far too few of the rooms were utilized, I believe this was probably for the better. It is already a pretty long game clocking at about 10 hours. The horrors are somewhat stilted I found, the creepy aspect was there certainly, especially in the early hours where you are unarmed with psychological spooks really carrying weight. However as you proceed you find yourself getting more and more well equipped, and unfortunately the psychological scares start to give away to attempts at cheap spooks and musical stings. This isn't entirely helped by the enemy variety. The two single enemy types are extremely easy to deal with, with a fairly easy to juke AI. Ammo eventually becomes a total non-issue; I had ammo enough for miles before the final boss with a little bit of rationing and dodging a few enemies. Health items are also plenty, however the healing charge mechanic behind the items does make using them far more risky in combat.The bosses are fairly alright, the first of three especially, as you are limited in ammo and power. however the other two are pretty well and easy. especially with the harder hitting weapons.The camera mechanic was fairly well utilized across the game, although its entirely used for puzzles and some traversal. I was a bit disappointed that it was not once used in combat; outside of fleeing the Red Light.The puzzles are relatively well designed, many of which could be solved with the things nearby, but the many that spanned the game meant that a certain level of inventory management felt necessary. My main major complaint would be in the level design itself.While the puzzles are well done, I found traversal through the hotel to be a painful endeavor. with only one elevator, in which you only slowly amass floors for, I would have hoped that it would be consistent. However, every time the pursuing Red Light appears, he breaks some of the levels in some way, making wide open areas long jogs with enemies that sometimes respawned (with ammo not being as kind), removing pathways through floors you've been wandering through, forcing you to make detours, and even breaking the call buttons on some floors permanently. This never was anything more than an major inconvenience to the design, especially when most of the back and forth puzzles explicitly required travelling down to these now longer and inconvenient floors. I'd say 3 hours of my gameplay was just looping around floor 1 and the rat maze that is floors 4-6 to find one or two items I missed or a puzzle I finally found the item for.Past the gameplay, I found the world building to be fun in itself. Although a bit confused. it feels inexplicable why there are monsters roaming the halls of the hotel until the very end, which only brings more questions to hand. Are the monsters created from the survivors? Did they spawn from the darkness? Is it an apocalypse? Some Silent Hill hell world? Was it resident evil **SCIENCE**?? I still don't know. The game felt like it was having more fun confusing the player than it did letting us make sense of the game world. I cant say this is good or bad.At first it feels like the hotel was a psychological eldritch horror in itself with the monsters being entities, and than later into the game, a lab shows up and it feels like the whole genre swapped from Silent Hill to Resident Evil on the fly. Overall, in spite of the drawbacks, and confused, writing that I can't decide is smartly confusing, or just genuinely stupid. I enjoyed my romp through the game! Although I still feel like this thing needs far more polish, and maybe a patch or two. 7/10 Why the ♥♥♥♥ is there an Overclock Energy Drink as a health item? This is set in 2009 ffs

_childDocuments_.review: To the Point=================A solid survival horror experience that is somewhat bogged down by a few poor design choices. Still a great addition for fans of the genreGood Stuff================- The Hotel really is a character all its own and it's a joy to explore it. Seeing the various levels of ruin and weirdness around takes what could have been a boring design and really breathes life into it.- The puzzles are tough but generally fair (especially if I could figure them out), provided you are willing to look around and reference your notes extensively- There's a lot of content here, though not all of it stellar the game felt almost perfectly spaced out.- The voice acting straddles this fine line between the camp this genre is known for without being completely absurd- The story is explained in depth via the pickups in game so it makes hunting around worthwhile- Personally, I quite like all the monster designs, well excluding the main pursuer enemy who looks like he's doing his laundry.Bad Stuff================- The save points in this game were put in place by a mad man. They are nonsensically placed and many times you are put into situations where you are encountering a pursuer type enemy with no save room in sight. Also there are MANY save spots that do not have item boxes directly next to them which is such a bizarre choice. I know we're a bit spoiled with something like RE where there are frequent auto saves but this swings too far in the opposite direction.- Enemies in this game are brick walls, meaning that if avoiding them is worse then it needs to be. To expand in RE and other FPS horror, if you get hit by an enemy there's usually a brief grace period where you can push past them but Fobia chose not to do that so if an enemy pins you up against a wall, well you better hope you have enough bullets, which reminds me...- Apparently there used to be too much ammo in earlier versions of the game, now there's really not too much. I feel like this game uses RE's Difficulty adjustment system, where the drops get worse/enemies get harder the better you play so you can go for long stints where every bullet pickup is one or two bullets. It seemed to even out by endgame but the early and middle parts were rough.- You can skip NOTHING in this game, not cutscenes, not scripted events etc. you need to watch the whole thing every time. This can suck especially bad if you run afoul of the bad save point problem I mentioned earlier then die and go back 20-30 minutes.- This is a weird one but there are many times in the game where you get F.E.A.R. style slowdowns and, I assume, something creepy is supposed to happen. This occurs all the time but I think I only ever saw something once or twice, not sure what the triggers were but it could just be an oversight.- The spiders, one of the stupidest enemies ever. They make nearly no noise, crawl on all surfaces, ceilings included, are nearly impossible to see if you don't hear them, and will chain jumpscare you since their only attack is them crawling in your face. Thankfully they do little damage and you insta kill them once they bite you but still what a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying enemy.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of really great things about this game, but unfortunately the combat situation made the game unplayable.  Its a real shame because this game has some great puzzles and the setting and lore is pretty good.   I am still recommending it and I will explain why: you can mod the game to be playable.  Honestly, was getting ready to uninstall it after dying multiple times in the second boss because the game does not give you enough ammo to actually defeat the boss.  But that isnt even the worst part.  Let me give you a break down of why the combat is soo soo bad.  1. Lack of ammo and healing items to be found.  2. enemies (even the basics) take multiple bullets to kill, like four or five (but you dont find enough ammo!).   3.  the game doesn't seem to register about half of your hits.  So you really need like 6-8 bullets per enemy.  4. The enemy attacks are poorly - well, everything.  Some dont seem to notice you for a good 5-10 seconds.  Others attack you as you enter a room so fast off to the side, you didn't even have time to see them.  They all do a lot of damage.  And due to the lack of healing items, this is frustrating.   They move way way faster than your character can turn or aim when they actually do start towards you.  There is no dodge.  You cant seem to shoot them when they are right up on you.  Multiple times the gun would not come out as I was being attacked or the game would not let me aim to shoot.My second gripe.  Inventory management.  You can only carry a few items with you at a time.  Because of this,  you cant just carry all of your guns hoping that all together you have some decent ammo level.  Also, there are a lot of puzzles in the game that require items. And lots of doors that require key cards and keys. I constantly found myself running back and forth to find storage boxes to move stuff in and out.  It was exhausting.Early in the game there is a lack of save points.  They become more numerous later and closer in location.  I sort of felt like the early part of the game needed more save points.  Minor gripe though. Like I said,  I was going to uninstall this game early on because it seemed impossible to kill the spider (2nd boss) because most hits didn't register and the damage done to my character was heavy and out of proportion to it being early in the game.  I found the game on we-mod program/app and it let me modify the game.  I changed it to endless ammo, full health always, and faster running speed (though the running speed didnt always stick after each save).  The game was then pretty decent and I really liked it.   It also partially fixed the inventory issue as I then just carried the shotgun, no healing items, no ammo.  No other weapons.  The choice to do "full health always" was mostly due to the demand on my inventory for puzzle items.  I would have liked to still have a little bit of a combat challenge in the game.  But its all or nothing with this one. It had so much potential.  I do not know why the devs decided to make one difficulty level and set it so high.  Especially since the game was so narrative rich and a focus on the puzzles.  Why then make the combat so impossible and frustrating?  People who generally like strong narrative puzzle games dont like hard difficulty combat.  We want to get on with the story!I really liked the hotel setting.  I thought the black hole thing was creepy.  The monster design was pretty good and original.  Art style was very nice.  There were some plot holes and the final conclusion wasn't as explanatory as I would have liked but still good story.  The game is well made.... but. Whoever made the decisions on the combat did a bad job though. I still recommend but only if you get the we-mod for this game.  Its basically unplayable without it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fobia - St. Dinfna Hotel

_childDocuments_.review: Do not get confused by the trailer or the marketing material, this is not a survival horror game, it's more of an escape room style puzzle game with the occasional shooting section. Sadly, the puzzles are almost exclusively "find the key or numlock for the next room" It was just so boring to run around the hotel with clumsy movement system to find a clue for a room you visited 40 minutes ago. The horror element is there and the hotel looks nice, but the constant backtracking, incredibly tiny FOV and slow movement made most of my experience just overly long and dull. This isn't really about building tension, since the horror happens really early on. I think it's an ideal game if you find Resident Evil like games too difficult, or you are looking for a horror themed escape room game. Just know, the puzzles aren't interesting and solving them does not make you clever. The story is... there. I was not intrigued by it, but it facilitates the setting, so I guess it's functional.It's not my type of game, but it's definitely well put together, so I have to give it a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! Great gameplay and no performance issues!A haunted big hotel with puzzles to solve to progress, with zombie to kill every once and a while- a few bosses too.
