_childDocuments_.review: Upon hearing of Red Barrels and their attempts at making an online Outlast, post Outlast 2, I'd been a little timid to the idea for what Outlast 2 had laid out with the new mechanics it'd introduced in how one interacts with the environments in Outlast 2. I felt like in a way Outlast 2 had innovated enough but fell short in the narrative department due to the focus being pushed too much elsewhere. Despite this, Outlast 2 had felt familiar, over feeling like more of the same, but its story was just... trying very hard to be a bit cryptic? And all over the place.Upon actually PLAYING Trials though, I can confidently say my expectations were and even still are rather subverted, in the best way possible. They cut the fat, some unnecessary manners of traversal, and doubled down on the gameplay-focus by introducing the ability to actually 'fight back', buying yourself a window to react to approaching enemies by throwing bottles, bricks, even utilizing certain special tools in the form of 'Rigs' which you can build in a way that's to your style of gameplay. Let that be being more stealthy, more quick, more defensive. The variety of perks and what you can utilize with Rigs is rather contained yet robust.The overall level designs of the escape rooms in this game are very labyrinth-y yet pretty congested, with a wide diversity of environments to get lost in while you tediously task-work your way out of the games variety of trials, which they continue to add with each passing update. The 'named' enemies inhabiting the levels are also rather interesting characters, which the game allows you to learn more about thru its various lore documents you can find on occasion. The worldbuilding is interesting, the premise of what Murkoff is doing to those that wander into its grasp keeps you questioning ethics and what exactly Murkoff has to gain. Funny enough, this game is very anti-authority and isn't shy about showing that, despite you being a lab rat.My largest complaint with this game, which I hope Red Barrels can shed the need of, is the AI disclaimer. I abhor the usage of AI art in any content medium, and I'm doing all I can to not let that cloud my judgment of this game, but it's very hard to not be critical of it. In their disclaimer and I quote; "...Throughout the development of our game, we may leverage AI-based tools to assist our team in content creation..." which to me says either -- A) They're using datasets in order to create reference art to then create their own work off of -- B) They're gathering their own images and such to feed an AI machine to train a dataset that'll help them curate work to litter around levels -- or the unfortunate latter -- C) They're simply posting AI imagery around and simply polishing turds.It's a bit too ambiguous for me, for which I quote again in the latter of their statement; "...Please rest assured that what you see in the game reflects the creativity and hard work of our team. Examples may include pictures and/or posters used in some of our environments..."I hope it does, Red Barrels. I'm honestly being optimistic for your sake. You know if you ever want to abandon AI and find references for your work you can always look to the community that truly loves your games, being the found-footage/snuff/horror analyst community that has a TROVE of YouTube content for you to inspire yourselves with. It's hard to want to give any form of AI that isn't helping an NPC pathfind or something even an inch, knowing that much of it began off of stealing from others. Despite my rather glaring, personal gripe with a tool they may use, they are at least transparent about it and I feel could be further transparent, and it luckily doesn't bear an impact on any of the games other assets, for the game does have a visual identity luckily, and has a lot of care going into its variety of decals and signage, really selling you on the timeframe the game inhabits. Outlast Trials is great with friends, or even by yourself. It will test your patience at times, but the reward is worth the tussle, and the game is pretty generous in how it levels you up, unlocking more and more tools for you to toy with amidst its trials and tribulations. Honestly, I'm keeping my review at a solid thumbs up since Steam lacks a mixed button of sorts, but the AI disclaimer truly worries me. I will continue to timidly enjoy this game until I see something I deem too blatant and lazy on Red Barrels behalf to warrant supporting this game further. Continue to be as transparent as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a reminder to the rest of the gaming industry; Good development pays off, humility earns trust, and listening to your general playerbase (not your top 10%) makes for a much happier audience.This game is optimized, runs fantastically at max settings (I have a 3070, and I get ~130fps at 1080p), and only takes up ~34GB of hard drive space. The download itself is ~18GB at the time of this review. It's such a breath of fresh air that my friends who have slower internet can finally download a modern game in the span of a day instead of an entire weekend, and that I'm not choking out 10% of my monthly internet cap just to download a single game.Oh, and the bugs? What bugs? I've played for 14 hours, and haven't encountered a single bug that was noticeable. The polish is phenomenal. The only issue I even have with the game is that some of the auditory jumpscares (steam bursting from pipes, broken lights sparking) are a little too frequent, but considering that's the sole issue I have, that speaks volumes about the rest of the game.As for the gameplay itself, I'm a big fan of the "figure it out from environmental cues" structure. Missions only tell you where you need to go if you're already closing on the location, otherwise you'll need to look for indicators such as signs/mannequins pointing you the right way, light cues, or even things like wires or pipes running along the ground that lead you to your objective. The game never tells you any of this directly, and lets the player figure it out for themselves. It's both incredibly immersive, and greatly refreshing compared to other modern titles that put a giant objective marker in your face and draw you a path directly to it. I feel rewarded for using my intuition to approach new tasks instead of punished for not doing a brain-dead sprint toward a giant marker.Progression is solid, and lets you feel more empowered as you advance. Core mechanics such as effective door bashing, sliding, and saving yourself quickly from being pinned are quick to acquire, and are permanently unlocked upon acquisition. No need to pick between which quality-of-life perks you'd like to keep, you get to use them all. The only loadout options you have to choose between are ones that modify gameplay in ways that don't necessarily give you a huge advantage.Rigs, for example, are the equippable gear slot, which allows you to have a healing fog, or a throwable stun grenade, or even tactical vision to see enemies through walls for a duration. These all serve the same purpose, which is to help you avoid or mend damage from the enemies. Because of this, no Rig is necessarily better than the others, and they all have upgrade paths to let you improve your favorite.Speaking of other gameplay mechanics, Red Barrels has had their ear close to the forums and surveys, making adjustments to gameplay in response to feedback. Solo was too hard? They added infinite respawns for solo players (with a grade penalty for each respawn), and made enemies not linger around objectives so hard for solo-play. Running from some enemies was complicated due to limited stamina? They adjusted the base stamina value to make it a little more even. They even took some of the unlockable perks in the game, such as the ability to kick enemies off of your fellow players, and made them base-kit, while adjusting the perks to remove the stamina cost for doing so. If it sounds like they're just "making the game easier," they aren't. They still offer modifier-packed missions that'll amp up the difficulty immensely, these adjustments just help new players stand a better chance when matched up with fully-perked players who want to do harder missions while still giving progression a noticeable edge above base-kit, and a reason to invest into your progression trees.I don't know what else to say about this game, it's beautiful, it runs great, and it's probably some of the funnest co-op gameplay I've had since Phasmophobia's original release.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is an adrenaline-fueled roller coaster ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. This latest installment in the Outlast series takes the horror genre to new heights, delivering an unforgettable experience that will leave you gasping for breath. While the game might have given me multiple gruesome deaths (including one that involved 10,000 volts to the nipples), it only added to the exhilaration and excitement of the gameplay.First and foremost, the atmosphere in Outlast Trials is masterfully crafted. The hauntingly detailed environments, combined with the eerie sound design, create an immersive world that truly feels alive with terror. From the flickering lights in the abandoned asylum to the bloodcurdling screams echoing through the halls, every moment is filled with an intense sense of dread that grips you tightly.The gameplay mechanics in Outlast Trials are equally impressive. The stealth-based approach forces you to tiptoe through the shadows, desperately avoiding the clutches of your deranged pursuers. The tension builds with each step, and the constant fear of being discovered adds a layer of urgency and suspense. The game's variety of puzzles and challenges keeps you constantly engaged, while the cleverly designed levels provide ample opportunities for both strategizing and sheer survival instinct.The graphics in Outlast Trials are stunning, showcasing the grotesque and macabre nature of the game's world. The grotesque imagery, while disturbing, is a testament to the game's commitment to delivering an authentic horror experience. The attention to detail in character design and environmental elements adds an extra layer of immersion, making every encounter feel all the more real.Despite the many gruesome deaths I encountered, including the infamous 10,000-volt nipple incident, the game always managed to draw me back in. The shock value of these moments, while intense, serves as a reminder of the high stakes and unforgiving nature of the game. Each death only fueled my determination to survive and push through the challenges ahead.The Outlast Trials also shines in its narrative. The story is well-crafted, with intriguing plot twists and well-developed characters that add depth to the overall experience. The game's immersive storytelling keeps you invested throughout, and the sense of mystery and suspense will keep you guessing until the very end.In conclusion, the Outlast Trials is a truly unforgettable horror experience that pushes the boundaries of the genre. Despite the many gruesome deaths I endured, the game's atmosphere, gameplay mechanics, graphics, and narrative all come together to create an intense and rewarding adventure. If you have a taste for heart-pounding terror and a strong stomach, I highly recommend diving into the twisted world of Outlast Trials and testing your survival skills against its horrors. Just be prepared to face some shocking moments along the way!

_childDocuments_.review: I have managed to reach the end of content in just under 30 hours, that includes replaying some segments for no reason other than to get better at it. It is my estimation that you'll have seen everything in this game in under 4 to 6 hours minus the final mission and the rebirth cycle scenes. Between hour 6 and hour 30, you'll be replaying content you've seen before with different modifiers or you'll be playing the few challenge modes that the game offers, where you'll further explore the game's 3 core gameplay loops, namely; "Find Item, Bring to X", "Follow Wire" and "Find Keys." Any challenge mode may have any or all of these loops included, sprinkled with the Outlast horror that people are familiar with.It's interesting how this game is set up to replayed again and again, yet the trials lack replay value. Most importantly this is because there are no skip buttons, no quick replay options, and no significant differences in how you can approach the trial each time. It is good fun, but it's not as good as it could be. That's the caveat of Early Access players, I suppose. Regardless, one should expect the horror aspect to last no more than 2 to 4 hours. After that you'll have seen every enemy, jumpscare and trap the game has to throw at you. Once you're past the initial scare, which happens once you're familiar with what each audio cue means, the game mellows out to be an edgier Dead by Daylight, or Left for Dead without guns and zombies.It's not currently worth the price £25 tag, but it is fun. I hope we will see more trials soon to justify the game's cost. The Locker Hag will give you a rough reach-around for half that cost, and Mrs. Doubtfire will give you a lobotomy for free.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished The Outlast Trials a couple of hours ago and I can confidently say that this is one of the most fun online games I've played in a very long time. Quite innovative and fresh in every aspect. Considering I love Outlast 1 and 2 I was already quite familiar with the gameplay but I gotta say, the changes they made really made the gameplay fresh for me, too, which was a very welcome surprise. If I had to break it down and simplify it, the gameplay is essentially pretty much like Outlast 2, except you get to upgrade your character in every aspect. You get a rig, which is pretty much your power. You can get a stun grenade, x-ray, a mine and you can get a healing gas. All of those have their own "skill-tree" as I'd like to call it, even tho it's not really one. Each of those rigs you can upgrade to your liking with great benefits which genuinely help you in-game. Everytime you buy an upgrade you'll never feel like you just wasted your points. Then there's the normal skill tree. You can get general upgrades like more stamina etc. and it always feels good to upgrade your character. Later on, once you reach a certain level, you unlock amps. They basically give you a special passive power such as not making a sound when you walk through glass. Believe it or not, but that amp significantly made the game easier to play. Upgrades aside, I gotta mention the general gameplay. The gameplay is pretty much just run/ walk/ crouch around, find an object and then bring it to where you're supposed to. Sounds pretty boring right? Wrong. Even though this seems like it'd get tedious after a while, it really really does not. I've played the first map at least 10 times and I still enjoy playing on it. The gameplay loop is thankfully satisfying and fun enough to actually make you WANT to play another match, instead of feeling like quitting. The level system also greatly improves the quality of life of the game. Thankfully, the game got some RNG layouts, such as the secret room, which grants you a lot of goodies such as health increase, stamina increase etc. The rooms spawn is entirely RNG, from what I could tell, which is awesome considering you can't just run to the same room every match expecting you get OP stuff. Sadly, the RNG aspect is also kinda hurting the game in some aspects. For example: The enemy AI. Now I know that the enemy AI is not entirely RNG, which seems pretty obvious considering they immediately switch targets once a player starts to do the main objective. That is not bad per se, but it can and really does get annoying once you play a little solo. The overall game I think was structured to be played duo minimum, because some of the maps really are not as enjoyable solo as they are with friends. Doing the objective and therefore alerting countless enemies to your location can get very frustrating especially when they just decide to stick around and you gotta lead them away. The AI generally I don't think is something memorable. They're not really bad, but not really something that stands out, which is kinda sad really. I wish they decided to go for more memorable characters with smart and learning AI like in Alien Isolation. That I believe would've been a better step, but overall, the AI not being great doesn't take anything away from the game. Another thing that bothers me personally is that I always feel like all enemies know where you are. Whenever you decide to lead one enemy away, they never just start to look around in an area with no player, they just always stay in the proximity of a player and look for them there, even if you don't make a sound. I do realize that this is to make it more intense but after a while it can get really frustrating when you just wanna take in the atmosphere and try to look around. The Co-Op factor is easily the strongest aspect of the game. It's incredibly fun to look around with your friends or even randoms and hide and outsmart the enemy. Speaking of randoms, I've gotta mention that for some reason every random I've encountered so far was pretty great at the game. They always were very helpful and vocal, whether it was through the pinging system in the game or through the proximity chat. Those two aspects I'll talk about later however. When you play with your friends and you get attacked, your friend can save you from either getting incapacitated or even executed, which is really fun and feels satisfying, I love that aspect of the game. Overall it starts to really be obvious that this game was designed for multiplayer considering half the skills you can unlock are to save your friends in some shape or form. That is not a bad thing in my eyes, because this game was pretty much built around being multiplayer and being able to play it solo is just a bonus for all those who don't like to play with others. Proximity chat and the ping system are a MUST in this game. I genuinely believe that without those two aspects the game wouldn't be as fun as it is now. The proximity chat, if you decide to go with the open mic, is always fun to use. The only thing that I've noticed is that sometimes the things you say either arrive delayed or not at all? Partially the reason why I mention this is because as you stray away from your teammate, you obviously become quieter. After a certain distance you start to talk over a walkie-talkie. However, if you're next to them in a room you don't talk to them through the walkie-talkie, you talk to them normally, which can lead to very frustrating moments where your partner can't properly hear you 'cause you're very muffled. This rarely ever happens but I did want to mention it as it did get annoying at times. Now, if you're the quiet type and you don't really like talking, you can just use the in-game ping system. This is a great addition due to the nature of the game. You can ping objects and you can even straight up use voice commands. If you can't picture anything in your head right now think of the Left 4 Dead 1/2 vocals. They're exactly like that. Gameplay, AI and Co-Op aside, I obviously have to talk about the meat of the game. The story is very bare-bones, I'm pretty sure everybody knew that going into the game. However, I'd like to say that the atmosphere and the design of each level exceeds what they've done in the previous games. This game feels like the love child of a SAW game and an Outlast game. I can really dig that. You see all these fabricated locations and you can just feel that these places and houses were built by sick people to test you. When you walk around and look up you don't see the sky, you see that you are trapped in some warehouse. That realization when you walk around really hits. It feels very oppressing, scary and dark in the best way possible. I mean, think about it for a second. Think about the people who built these trials. That thought alone made the atmosphere of the game phenomenal in my eyes. The atmosphere in the game is awesome. It's not as scary as the first two, in fact, I personally don't think its very scary at all, but the level design is so good it really makes up for all of it. That being said, you do get scared. I can't begin to describe the amount of times I screamed when I decided to leave a room and suddenly run into some naked giant in the hallway. The game is scary at times! It just doesn't have scripted jumpscares, which I think was a good choice. I also quickly wanted to add that this game runs as smooth as butter. This game is really well optimized, you should give it a shot!Overall I'd say this game turned out really well. I'd give it a solid 8/10. Only things I'd love to see in the future would be new objectives on new maps. I'd love to see new maps with more traps too, and please not just with the regular door traps and such. Please give us actual traps reminiscant of SAW or something. Give us fun traps you gotta solve for the objective or you lose a finger or something, be creative!

The plot, in turn, has become quite compressed and has acquired the appearance of the dictionary with lore notes. Nevertheless, the location and character design, scene staging and voice acting remain of tremendous quality and astonishing esteem for players. This is only enhanced once again by superb optimization and eye-pleasing graphics that don't overwhelm the computer's processing power. This kick-ass combination of details is transformed into an addictive gameplay that will keep you entertained for more than a dozen hours. That's why I highly recommend to try out this game even without friends, considering most of the playerbase is talkative and friendly. WP, Red Barrels!

_childDocuments_.review: Goofy early 2000's torture porn edgelord vibes taken to the point of comedy.Played solo, this is very much akin to the previous games, just in enclosed maps aka trials instead of an ongoing storyline campaign. Tense, creepy, horror game where you alternate between sneaking, running and hiding. Trials can have modifiers when played at higher difficulties or during weekly challenges or bigger seasonal events. Maps have randomised elements on what items are available where, as well as doors being locked that force you to take extreme detours and really alter the working layout of the map.While there's no full story mode, there's a background narrative that does build a little as you play, with several evolving endings when you complete the equivalent of a prestige system. Levelling up unlocks the ability to buy more permanent buffs (pharmaceuticals), upgrade your rig (power), and unlock more switchable perks (amps) giving you things to work towards as well as cosmetic options.Multiplayer is a riot. It's the same content but enemy numbers and objectives are scaled up for more players, and it becomes a Benny Hill comedy sketch as everyone runs several enemies around like crazy screaming as they go.It's far from perfect, with some very frustrating bugs, enemy AI can cause them to just stand right in front of an objective for minutes at a time, some of the combinations of modifiers are just plain unfair and/or unfun, etc. But as someone who frowned on hearing the next Outlast would be a multiplayer game, I was pleasantly surprised, and now I'm hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is a case study in how cooperative horror games should be designed. The synergy of every structure in place from a gameplay standpoint is phenomenally fun and terrifying. It continues to give players reasons to play via an incredible progression system that ensures players will always have something to work towards as they continually torture themselves in the name of psychoscience. On top of this, trials feel distinct and personalized to each "prime asset"--charismatic serial killers that stalk the players alongside normal enemies in every trial environment, offering a certain level of charm and distinctness I haven't felt in a co-op horror game in some time. The game also offers incredible acting performances, coupled with some fascinatingly well-written and disturbing dialogue and narrative. You very well may find yourself getting lost in this game's lore, just as equally as you will find yourself disturbed at the well-represented forms of psychological abuse and manipulation your character will undergo in-game. This however won't ever be on your mind for long, as you'll be having too much fun with friends to be focusing on the atrocities committed before your eyes. On harder difficulties, you and your teammates will likely be too focused on completing your tasks safely to even realize how evil what you're doing is--creating a synergistic relationship between player and protagonist in a way that only a game can. Both you and your reagent will be completely desensitized to violence in the name of completing trials efficiently and safely, which intentional or not, is brilliant.This title is not without its flaws however. Some trials and MK-Challenges find themselves being considerably more tedious and poorly designed than others. One has you attempting to slowly carry dangerous buckets of acid through maze-like level design with constantly changing paths that shift on a timer, and another has players attempting to power generators in a dark building filled with awkward paths, unconventional routes, and confusing objective placements. These undoubtedly will be grating to many players, coupled with a bizarre usage of incredibly obvious AI artwork that only serves to make the games presentation come off as trashy and childish at times compared to its usually incredible appreciation for creativity and originality.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, the devs keep iterating on the difficulty scaling and enemy ai, which for me have been the biggest problems since starting the game, and the current state as time of writing is pretty good in my opinion. The problem of the first mission being too hard for new players got fixed by adding easier mode, while we also received the psychosurgery difficulty. Combined with the mentioned ai tweaks the game now has a mode that lets even experienced players feels some challenge.The environments are the best part of the game for me. Each chapter has a unique theme and a main mission. Then the just as detailed but less visited parts of the map get used by setting additional mini challenges at those places. Going higher in difficulty, the maps that previously have been buildings open to exploration and free movement turn into mazes, that reward the therapy subject for becoming familiar with the layout, and being able to quickly think of all the possible paths to their destination.The monetization is extremely user friendly - all the new content so far besides a few cosmetic bundles has been free, which on one hand is good, but on the other makes me worry about how viable that system is for the longevity of the game after being used to other companies squeezing their player base dry.I can't escape the comparison of this game with Payday 3. Both are games I wish to succeed as a long term services. The difference is one feels like it's doing what it can to wrest the money out of me, while Outlast Trials feels like it's even afraid to ask for it after the initial purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead, murdered by my brother-in-law Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, Hank came to me with a rather, shocking proposition. He asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using his connections in the drug world. Connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Gustavo Fring, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn.Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Fring flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Fring was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my criminal activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.If you got this far, then you probably really care about the game so here's my real input. The game is actually really good, has its moments of fright, and is one of the best CO-OP horror games on the market right now. It's got a good amount of content with multiple trials and more challenges. It's also got the reborn system with even more content. Having friends to play with is ideal, but there's a ton of people in matchmaking for the trials so there's no worry. I think we can all agree that the arm wrestling is the best part of the game

_childDocuments_.review: I reached freedom on my first reagent and i'm halfway to freeing my 2nd one which is a cool little prestiege like system they added and I feel like i can confidently recommend the game. In essence, this game excels at what  a lot of modern games fail at such as the following:Red barrels absolutely nailed the level design and themes in this game. Each program (which is a collection of individual trials) has its own distinct unique theme. After playing through all the trials multiple times trying to level my account up, I still get amazed at all the little details and sounds they put in the levels. This game can be used as standard for A+ level design.Another massive critique we see in modern gaming is badly coded or low-effort AI in the game environment. The enemies in The Outlast Trials are not only unique in their game play functions, but they all have different distinct personalities and characteristics. Sgt.Coyle is a great main antagonist for the police station level and is a great example of taking an extreme law & order personality and placing it into a psychotic killer. Mother Gooseberry is hands down one of the best video game antagonists you can play against. The voice acting is absolutely top notch and worthy of receiving awards itself. The amount of work into this character is so great the point where she will hold ENTIRE CONVERSATIONS with her puppet while she randomly walks around the map looking for and also has unique voice lines for whenever something happens in the game environment.Game is really fun in 2-4 player coop and i think they nailed it as a coop game. This game is definitely more intense doing the trials solo but the game design doesn't translate to it really (although it is still fun). The final tests for the initial 3 programs (referred to as exams in game) are fairly easy and can be beaten solo or in coop starting at around level(s) 8-10 as long as you are not just holding your W key the whole trial. The final program (Referred to as Program X) has 10 trials that use maps from the first 3 trials but have multiple modifiers that make the game play much more difficult, intense and enjoyable. I am interested to see what future programs are going to be added into the game and want to see what other environmental themes they put into the game.Was they game worth all the delays? yes it was. What is in the game is very high quality and there are very few bugs I have encountered in 20 hours played in 3 days. Red Barrels have a strong foundation, hopefully they knock the future game play updates out of the park like they did with the original Outlast.

_childDocuments_.review: The best stealth horror game I've yet to play.Solid stealth mechanics, amazing environments and atmosphere. While the mechanics are fun, they are not deep which hurts replayability. The maps also have a type of Warframe generation system where there are RNG pathing on how to get to objectives. All in all, I got a solid 50 - 70 hours before I played everything and then started playing just for the game and atmosphere.They raised the price to $40 which I do think is just barely reasonable. This is a high quality product, but just falls short of having the seemingly endless replayability like Deep Rock Galactic.If stealth and horror is something you want to try, then this is a solid buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Outlast Trials, the latest installment in the renowned horror franchise, is a chilling masterpiece that pushes the boundaries of survival horror gaming. As I dove into the dark and twisted world of Outlast Trials, I found myself captivated by its terrifying atmosphere, engaging gameplay mechanics, and captivating narrative. Allow me to take you through the haunting journey that is Outlast Trials.At its core, Outlast Trials excels in creating an unnerving and oppressive atmosphere that constantly keeps players on the edge of their seats. The game's meticulously crafted environments are hauntingly detailed, with every flickering light and creaking floorboard adding to the sense of dread and suspense. The ambient soundscape and eerie musical score perfectly complement the gameplay, further immersing players in a world of terror and paranoia.One of the standout features of Outlast Trials is its intelligent and challenging gameplay mechanics. As a helpless test subject trapped in a sinister experiment, you must rely on your wits, stealth, and limited resources to survive the relentless pursuit of deranged enemies. The game strikes a perfect balance between tension-building exploration and heart-pounding chase sequences, keeping players constantly on their toes. The intuitive controls and responsive character movement enhance the gameplay experience, allowing for seamless immersion into the nightmarish world of Outlast Trials.The narrative in Outlast Trials is another compelling aspect of the game. The intriguing storyline draws players deeper into a web of conspiracy, fear, and psychological torment. As you unravel the dark secrets behind the experiment, you'll encounter a cast of complex and memorable characters, each with their own motivations and dark pasts. The game's well-crafted narrative hooks you from the beginning and keeps you engaged until the very end, leaving you craving more answers and revelations.Visually, Outlast Trials is a stunning achievement. The meticulously designed environments are filled with atmospheric details, from flickering lights casting eerie shadows to gruesome scenes that send shivers down your spine. The character models and animations are impeccably rendered, showcasing the grotesque and twisted nature of the game's inhabitants. The attention to detail and visual fidelity heighten the sense of immersion, making every moment in Outlast Trials a visually striking and unsettling experience.Furthermore, the game's optimization and performance deserve applause. With smooth framerates and minimal technical issues, Outlast Trials ensures that players can fully immerse themselves in the horrifying atmosphere without any distractions or interruptions.In conclusion, Outlast Trials is a shining example of what a survival horror game should aspire to be. Its unnerving atmosphere, engaging gameplay mechanics, captivating narrative, stunning visuals, and exceptional optimization come together to create an unforgettable and chilling experience. If you have a taste for fear and a desire to be truly terrified, Outlast Trials is an absolute must-play for any horror aficionado. Brace yourself for an unforgettable journey into the depths of horror.

_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a great Co-op Horror game, look no further! I play this game not only with my personal friends, but with randoms and enjoy every bit of it. As someone who is a fan of the Outlast Series, I had high expectations, especially with the co-op aspect going into it. I myself got the chance to sign up for the closed beta, and was impressed from what little I got to play from that. I highly recommend this game and still play it in my free time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: Played 34 hours (including beta) and can say it's extremely fun to play with friends. I admit the solo aspect is not as strong as the previous outlasts but I came into this one expecting a multiplayer experience, which for me was a big upside. The gameplay is smooth as butter and the AI isn't stupid enough for you to be able to hide in a closet all game (cause some people just enjoy doing so for some reason), and not annoying enough to never loose chase if you turn a corner and try to use stealth. The only aspect that could be improved on are the progression levels and the items you can get by doing so, which I believe will be worked upon full release, so I'm not too worried about that. The game's replay value isn't insane right now, but it's a decent 15 hour game for those who aren't addicted.All in all, if you expect an outlast1/2 type of game, don't buy it. I believe the multiplayer aspect enriches the experience and while it's not as scary, it's also more enjoyable and a chase game that actually feels satisfying to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the single best cooperative horror game I've ever gotten my hands on. Repeatable, atmospheric trials that with the right company can make for a genuinely fun and scary experience. My only gripe is the scares get old fairly quickly in this kind of system. I hope to see more intense scares or a more thrilling atmosphere in the future. The Root Canal is an incredibly unnerving and terrifying location regardless of the amount of players in the trial. The addition of some skills was a fun goal to work towards, and they don't feel *too* out of place for the feel of the game. Thankfully none of the skills feel like they change the game fundamentally, and regardless of if I have more stamina or not, chases feel intense. Constantly looking over my shoulder in case of an ambush, or accidentally stepping too close to a psycho in the trial, even realising I have an unexpected third player in my trial was always a thrill. Giving the player a voice that actually can talk feels really neat, and I'd like to have slightly more talking in the final product for that extra bit of flavour to the game. Nothing crazy, just little things like groaning out an "Oh god..." when searching for the keys in their...containers, or other one or two word lines for various other actions. Peeking from hiding places, getting jumped by psychos, being downed, things like that could benefit from the occasional comment from the player character.TL;DR the game's a 10 out of 10 for me as it is right now, and it remains the single most incredible early access game I've played. Aside from personal wishes for greater scares and locations, or some added atmosphere to your player, I can see nothing that could make this game better than it already is. Obviously more maps and scares are coming, so grab it now while the early access price is still cheap!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: Completely ridiculous in the best ways. I have played both solo and with groups of strangers AND both experiences have been a lot of fun so far. It is a pretty challenging game and it can take a bit to understand how the game works, but it is very satisfying when you succeed. The mechanics feel a lot more varied than the previous Outlast games. What's even more exciting is that the team clearly cares a lot about the state of the game and has already made changes to enhance it based on player feedback. I can't wait to see what's next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for the game and still do. As an Outlast fan I was really looking forward to this game. But as it stands it seems like playing on single player is nigh impossible with the high difficulty level of the trials and no way to adjust the difficulty settings. It seems like it is more adjusted to playing multiplayer rendering playing on single player frustrating and unfun and more of a chore than a fun game. Since the game is in early access I hope the devs will tweak this to make it more single player friendly. I understand it was primarily meant to focus more on playing together but thats not the best when none of your friends play or want to play. Please either make a difficulty setting level that can be changed of adjust the game to be better adjusted and scale to single player.

_childDocuments_.review: As an Outlast veteran, I can say this is one of the best multiplayer games to date. Super immersive visuals, shocking levels of gore, and audio that really lets you into the messed up trials Murkoff puts you in. There is extensive amount of replayability in this game due to randomized parts of the trials, and the massive free updates Red Barrels puts out is something you don't get to see too often.There are a few issues with this game which include heavy lag even when playing solo. The really long cutscenes and loading times before/after a trial make it tedious to want to play over and over again.All in all, I give this game a 9.5/10, I've never had so much fun or been this immersed in a multiplayer game before. The astonishing level of detail continues to surprise me and I'm glad Red Barrels continues to deliver top notch material.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast TrialsFor the first time in years i played a game that i had insane amounts of fun at. The game is being selled for €39.99 and i love the fact that Red Barrels didn't add any way of transactions in this game for cosmetics or anything at all, the only way to get good at this game and get cosmetics such as Cell Decorations, clothing and skins for your character is simply done throught grinding the game, leveling up and completing new Trials or even ones you've already completed which will still reward you with xp, Murkoff Dollars and level up rewards.Lore: The Outlast Trials take place in the year 1959 aka a couple years before the events of Outlast 1 and 2. The Murkoff Corporation conducts group experiments for CIA program MKUltra. You are a drug addict that lives in the streets and is one that the society wouldn't mind losing, so one day you find a poster/invitation to join the Murkoff Corporation Industry but why? When you join the doctors will make experiments on your body to change who u are to pretty much change society's point of view on yourself because they will understand that they lost someone important, and that someone is you.Gameplay: In my opinion this game finally brings something fresh to the gaming industry after so many years and tears of companies ripping off eachother and releasing the same broken games over and over (Battle Royales, Arena Shooters and much more). The game comes with a great Coop mode which i would say is honestly one of the best we've seen in any Coop title. You can partner up with up to 4 people forming a squad and taking on the Challenge of the Trials together. The game came out 18th of May this year and since then they've added new in-game holiday events such as a Halloween and a christmas event and on top of that brand new trials for people to grind. As of right now the game features 4 different and unique Programs with their own and different Trials and Program X which you can beat to earn your freedom (won't touch upon this Program due to spoilers). When grinding this game you can unlock different cosmetics, Amps which are small abbilities that you either Sprint for longer, bash through doors while running, slide while running, make no noise when you step on broken glass that would otherwise make noise to alert enemies of your location and many more that even can't think of cause we'd be here for hours. There is a feature called Rig's, there are 4 of them and each one has it's unique abbility for every playstyle aka Solo or Squaded up. Rig 1: Is a device called "STUN" which whenever you hit an enemy with it you temporarely stun them and disorient them. Rig 2: is a Mine you place on the ground that when is stepped on by an enemy releases a "BLINDING SMOKE" that makes any enemy type blind for a duration of time. Rig 3: is a "HEALING CANISTER" that releases a healing cloud around you for yourself and your teammates if they are close to you. Rig 4: is called "X-RAY" and makes it so you can see enemies through walls and ping them for you teammates or is also really good if you are planning to go solo in the trials. I'm not gonna touch upon what missions you do in the trials cause that is gonna spoil the fun.Characters and Maps: The Outlast Trials offer a huge variety of enemies, some more memorable than other but it is what it is, The First Trial you'll be mainly hunted down by "THE COP" who has a really cool design in my opinion and has a shock stick so he better not catch you roaming around. And the other one is "THE MOTHER" she is my favorite one easily, her voice actor did a great job and her design and lore is just pretty sick, her abbility is that she has a little puppet on her left arm with a drill in it's mouth so if she catches you then yeah. her lore is that she loves to skin people's faces and put them on Manekins and too be fair after you play Program 2 and 3 you'll realise that it's not only faces she likes to skin, super freaky and insanely cool at the same time. All of the Maps in the game are just way too good and really well designed to be honest, the game thus far has only four maps but even more trials so it's not one trials per map. this game has more content than what meets the eye at first. First we have the "Police Station", "The Fun Park", "The Orphanage" and finally "The Courthouse" until they realese more ofcourse.Soundtrack: The soundtrack and Score of this game is just way too based and knows exactly what it wants to be without it trying to be a certain way it can't. Huge congrats on the guy who made the entire Soundtrack and the orchestra.Verdict: The Outlast trials is as of right now on sale due to the holydays for about €21.99 and it's normal price is €29.99. In my opinion if you are a long time Dead By Daylight fan and you are looking for something new and more fresh of a horror experince, The Outlast Trials will do you just that favor. It's an amazing Coop game and even if you play Solo and have no friend you can still matchmake and find people to play with so you can make yourself friends and meet new people. This game is an insanely fun ride to go through even Solo or with friends and trust me, with friends? it's on another level cause this game is actually scary.I love the games that are paid and don't have a battle pass system or any in-game purchases at all because that's how games should be, because it also ruins all the fun. Someone could grind their ass off to get a certain cosmetic and someone else is just gonna buy it with real money to just flex it which really shouldn't be the way and i love that this game is this way.I'll give this game 10 because it knows what it's trying to be and the devs clearly know what they are doing, and let's not forget that the dev team is roughly around 100 people and when they made Outlast 2 they were around 20 people and just shows you what type of insane quality a team can put on a project if they are willing and passionate about it, Thank You Red Barrels.The Outlast Trials: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: "The Outlast Trials" is a harrowing journey into the heart of darkness, and while it left me mentally exhausted, there's no denying its ability to deliver a chilling and immersive horror experience.From the moment I stepped into the sinister world of Cold War-era experiments gone awry, I knew I was in for a psychological rollercoaster that would test my nerves and sanity. The game's setting, with its grimy and foreboding atmosphere, creates a sense of claustrophobic dread that's hard to shake. The developers have masterfully crafted a world where every corner hides a new terror, and every step forward feels like a step into the unknown.The core gameplay in "The Outlast Trials" remains true to the series' roots. You are powerless, armed only with a camera to capture the horrors that unfold. The need to navigate pitch-black corridors, evade deranged enemies, and solve puzzles while grappling with your own fear keeps the tension at a constant high.One of the standout features is the co-op mode, which allows you to experience the horrors alongside other players. This addition introduces a new layer of paranoia and teamwork as you and your comrades try to survive together, never knowing who you can truly trust. It's a welcome twist on the traditional Outlast formula.The character development in the game is a testament to the survival instinct. As you uncover the secrets of the experiment, you'll be forced to make morally ambiguous decisions that can lead to both salvation and despair. It's a reminder that in a world devoid of hope, the line between right and wrong can become disturbingly blurred."The Outlast Trials" doesn't shy away from visceral horror. The game is a relentless assault on the senses, with gruesome imagery and unsettling audio design that will haunt your nightmares. It's not a game for the faint of heart or those seeking a casual horror experience.In conclusion, "The Outlast Trials" is a game that doesn't pull its punches when it comes to delivering bone-chilling terror. It's a wearying, nerve-wracking experience that leaves you emotionally drained, but that's precisely what makes it effective. If you're a fan of the horror genre and enjoy being pushed to your limits, this game will test your mettle and leave you with an indelible sense of unease long after you've put down the controller.

Meaningful upgrades that make traversing trials easier but not a cakewalk. Will continue to play for the foreseeable future as I cannot recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun. Reminds me of indie coop horror games of yesterdecade, but much more atmospheric (hence the Outlast series), polished and fun. Enemy AI is good and pretty relentless. Proximity voice chat is good. Performance-wise game is great even with RT enabled on ultrawide 1440p (though with it disabled game behaves more stable and RAM/VRAM usage can spike to enormous levels with RT). Chase OST is good as the music in general.Cons: tuning FOV requires editing .ini file, no ingame slider. LFG system is somewhat clunky (but functional).I recommend it to outlast fans and other gamer who want to have some COOP fun. Also, game is GOAT with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so proud of you, Red Barrels. You had an idea many years ago and made it happen, and every second of development was worth it. Where to even start? It's Outlast! Another person who reviewed had said that this doesn't feel like an outlast game but that it feels like a cheap copy of Dead By Daylight. While this game does have DBD aspects, it's still the Outlast I know and love. Another review had also said that the horror was eliminated completely compared to other outlast games and that it was all about the difficulty. I can say with full confidence that is also false. In fact, this is the scariest installment yet and the best part is you get to experience it with your friends! I think Red Barrels made a very smart decision placing this game in Early Access. I don't think the game is broken by any means, but unlike other game devs they came prepared. This game is seriously insane and the fact that it is this good in an early access state is huge, as an Outlast fan this means everything. I've been huge on Outlast for years, and I'm so pleased to report that The Outlast Trials just may be the next big horror game for people of all kind, whether it's playing with your friends, just having fun, play competitive or casually, or just in it for the scare, you've come to the right place because this game absolutely has it all. I recommend this game fully, and besides me being actually loving the Outlast genre and sounding like a fanboy, with that all aside it's seriously refreshing to see an actual finished game as good as this in 2023, especially in an early access state. All the more reason to get the game, you'll get your money's worth and you won't regret it:)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the multiplayer horror game of your dreams. PROS: The enemies in this game have all there own unique way of chasing or searching which keeps the game different depending on who you are going against. The difficulty of this game is mastered to perfection where the more you learn the game the harder the levels that you do will be. Even on the easiest difficulty the game will not make you fall asleep ever due to its quick 0 to 60 moments as you get chased. The leveling up system is amazing making you want to play more to unlock more things.CONS: The only cons are that the Fake Player always knows where you are so you cant escape him except through hiding in Lockers or Barrels which is not fun when he is around. There is way to much gore in this game, making you desensitized to it just on the first level you play. As it is still in BETA the enemies may glitch around.Summery: If you are a fan of Horror Games and want to have fun with friends and actually feel scared  this game is for you. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I believe this is by far one of the most bang-for-your-buck-game out there. **DISCLAIMER** I will say the things that I enjoy:1.Progression in the game is very linear.2. Creative styles to the game making you find your preference in play style. (Aggro, Defensive & Variable) 3. The increasing in speed as you learn new maneuvers, shortcuts and preservation of resources. The things I do not enjoy:1. What I found after achieving rebirth 6 times is the mundane and redundant aspect to the game. You definitely begin to hit a brick wall in this game for sure.2. The development of the Antagonists is slightly incorrectly tuned, leaving us getting poor interactions and false hits. An example: When hit by a Grunt, if you are overlapping the Grunt you inadvertently become stuck between them and can sometimes die in one fell swoop.3. Everything becomes so painfully repetitive. Yes, you're doing previous trials to become successful in Program X, but there is no real difference in Program X and leaves me feeling like "Ah, so they quickly worked something to kind of was our throats down with something.ALL AND ALL: I enjoyed the come up of this game, having a full week of free time and an appetite to continue on with this game, my friends and I successfully beat the game in a week. There is plenty of content, definitely worth every penny! I would totally try and play this COOP and NOT alone! It's very doable alone, but COOP makes it so much more fun and faster!Very well done  Red Barrel, I've enjoyed all of the Outlast games growing up, hopefully there's more to come and this isn't just a nostalgia game like the rest!

_childDocuments_.review: This Feels Like a Full GameUsually i fall for the trap of buying early access games and they just remain incomplete for eternity. This game feels like a fully completed and polished AAA game. This is a fun escape room coop game with the vibes of a Saw + Outlast lovechild.Progression is what you expect, complete missions and your performance effects your XP gains. Levelling up gives you tokens to redeem for perks but you also get money from performance to buy cosmetics. Cosmetics include character customisation and room customisation as well! So far i think theres only 4 levels with 3 sub levels to each of them, as well as hard modes for every level as well. (This may be the early access part as 4 levels is a bit low)Graphics for this game are great and it runs super smooth! With a Ryzen 9 3950x, RTX 4080 i was running this game MAX settings including MAX Ray Tracing settings as well. Hitting minimum of 120 FPS throughout all of my game time. For reference Star Wars Jedi Survivor sits well below 100 FPS between 60-90 on Max settings.So far i give it a minimum of 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It amazes me how every other AAA developer somehow produces the most unoptimized pile of UE4 crap BUT FINALLY a competant developer!Game looks stunning and runs flawlessly.Movement is seamless and all mechanics including upgrades are so useful. The progression system is super fun and replayable.I would ask the intro sequences were skipable because they are so looooong and also do some better level reward scaling. Currently as the game is, playing the hardest difficulty offers very little in regards to rewards both cosmetic and level-wise. I would expect at least 4-5 blue tokens and maybe 5 green tokens to reward the player for fighting through the high enemy spawns, faster enemy movement and scarce loot spawns. Instead though, you are given the same rewards as you would mid difficulty which doesn't encourage me and my buddy to replay the hardest levels. So those two fixes would be greatly appreciated. That and maybe some more shoe outfits, my guys got his dawgs out and I only have one leg cosmetic that gives my man shoes.

_childDocuments_.review: So, my final opinion on the early access version of the game, i've rebirthed three times [which is this game's version of a new game+ and regeneration system mixed in] (You don't lose progress from rebirthing btw) and have been in countless sessions and missions, got to say? Extremely good game, even for early access, i can't wait to see what red barrels bring to the table for the full release.The community is also really nice and friendly from what i've seen so don't be afraid to matchmake for randoms if your friends are unavailable or don't own the game yet, hey, you can make some new friends too along the way!Of course the game has its bugs and glitches here and there, and while they can [and have] been annoying, they aren't completely dealbreakers or game breaking in any sense, which for early access makes it look very polished.Whatever you decide to do, take on the trials with friends or make new ones along the way by matchmaking with randoms, the game is really good fun and i absolutely 100% recommend you try it.TL:DR | Game is really polished and good for an early access game, and is tons of fun

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a lengthy review but I couldn't help myself!I played the beta back when it was available, and while we only had the first trial it was an absolute blast. Red Barrels really went all out with approaching Outlast from a multiplayer perspective and even with a full group of four players it is terrifying. I'm torn between absolutely loving the enemy designs and being utterly terrified of them, and they made sure to add all the small details that really bring these enemies to life unlike so many other horror games I've played in the past.Coyle checking the locker next to the one I'm hiding in, only to get visibly frustrated, leave the room and just when I thought it was safe I hear two light taps and he slowly opens the door behind me, or when Psycho (as I like to call him, gas mask guy) appears with his wonderfully maniacal laughter if you hit him twice with throwing objects he will go: "Alright alright you got me!" and scurry back to the 'spawn closet' instead of chasing you. Coyle obviously being aware that you are nearby but instead of searching he decides to take a smoke break while tapping on a glass door right next to your hiding spot. (This next one is during the beta) The big lumbering giant guy (I dont know what his name is) chasing us only for us to lose him between a hallway, rounding that hallway being chased by Coyle we spot him searching a tiny drawer for us and with all the commotion he gets startled and confused at how we got there, and then proceeds to join the chase.Its small moments like these that really bring to life these characters and you can see personalities within them that go further than just their voicelines and general demeanor. A really good example is with Psycho, who is very aware that he is playing this role of an 'enemy' in these trials, designed specifically to challenge the progress of the player. He clearly relishes in it, and when he comes onto the playing field so to speak he always opens with maniacal laughter. Its his time to shine and he is out there living it. Being that you get to know these enemies quite quickly throughout the typically long initial runs you gain this sense of cruel intimacy, you learn their patterns and behavior and you pick up on cues with how they behave, I mean Coyle can go on long rants about pistachios (yes, really.) and the bible and if hes into it enough you can sneak right past him without concern! While it is clear that the main 'big bads' of the enemy roster have a lot more work and detail put into them than some of the lesser knife or machete wielding enemies most if not all of them have little quirks or habits which, were probably so unnecessary for the developers to implement but in doing so, makes them feel so much more alive.You can really take advantage of the AI with the right tools, get out there experimenting! Same goes for any in world traps that have been placed, a good brick can fix most problems.I don't have the most insane pc rig, but its not super low end either, with a fairly aged 1060 6gb and an i7k processor (SSD + 16gb ram included) I managed to get a steady unwavering 60 fps (I only have 60hz monitors) on default graphics settings (which I believe is medium). For me these settings were comfortable enough that I did not need to change them, and somehow out of all games I actually need motion blur on or I get a headache, take that as you will.Small section but I really wanted to happily mention that I absolutely adore how they really gave every enemy true vision (as I'd like to call it). No weird can't-see-through-windows McGee here, standing in the light behind two layers of slightly frosted glass and you move an inch? They'll spot you, because you are still pretty visible, silhouette and all, even if they aren't entirely sure they still gotta check it out. Darkness is your friend in Outlast and playing between shadows and taking your time can help completely outsmart your opponent (as long as he isn't wearing his own pair of night-vision goggles...The map design is incredible, its very easy to get lost if you are panicked and they leave so many nooks and small passageways that you can escape to (or from, as enemies can follow depending on their size). Each of the 3 core Trials currently available all have their own stories, with 3 separate difficulties and two unique side-stories that you can also do. The replayability is strong in this regard. The 3 total separate 'stories' for each one also use different routes and might open or close areas you have and haven't been to, it really feels like a stage where they set it all up before hand real quick. I don't really want to spoil much about these and I've only played the initial difficulty of the three in the session I had before writing this review, perhaps I'll update it further as I put in more time.Back in the beta we didn't really get to modify much, and if we did I don't ever remember seeing it. However, the skill progression in Outlast Trials feels pretty solid, its a little weird having to spend a 'skill point' on being able to slide after sprinting, but as far as progression goes it does not feel out of place and comfortably scales the strength of your character with each unique unlock.As far as the 'classes' go, which are more so just tools, each one has their own upgrade path with some seemingly a little overpowered the further down the upgrade tree you go, however as I spent all of my points on the former skill tree section I have not experimented with any of the tools other than the one I chose as my first.From what I encountered? None, however I did run into a few janky movement issues but that could have been from the fact I was repeatedly cornered by a tall naked man in a bathroom stall (while in pure panic mode mind you).In the end if you are a fan of horror games, have been a previous fan of the last two Outlast games that Red Barrels released in the past or are simply looking for a unique experience you can't exactly find then I strongly recommend you give it a shot. It fits comfortably for solo play and really scales up the chaos with 3 more. The thirty dollar price tag feels reasonable for what content there is to offer and they will continue to add more Trials as development progresses. I've been on the bad end of previous early access title releases (where I've bought into EA on their release, which unfortunately would go sour), and despite my now innate uneasiness with trusting a lot of new EA titles I had genuine faith that Red Barrels would be able to deliver on a fun, engaging and outright terrifying new take on the Outlast formula, especially after getting a taste of it with the beta, and was more than happy to buy into whatever little ball of chaos this game is.I was about to give this some sort of #/10 but I've not played enough yet must play more so just yes for now.

_childDocuments_.review: The foundation of the game is strong with a solid ambience that contributes to the overall horror elements of the game. For the new player, it is one hell of an experience that had me scared enough to mute my friends on a discord call.I just despise the way they went about adding smaller missions. Crappy small segment maps with not much thought put into it. Didn't really commit to the theme of the main missions they follow, and really just seemed like a way for developers to boast about adding new "maps" and "content" to the game.It was most certainly fun at first, but as you level up, the game just gets easier removing elements of "team-play" as you essentially become self-sufficient enough to just blitz through most if not all objectives. Wait for a sale or buy it while 3 other friends are just getting into it to get the most out of it, otherwise, don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: As a guy that is bad at direction, Outlast trials is slightly a challenging game for me when it comes to locating objectives and collectibles. Good thing is that I have friends to play so they can handle other objectives lol.One part that i love in this game is the chase sequence with lots of ways to maneuver and hide in the dark. Objectives are randomly placed in each map. Locating them depends on players ability. Sometimes it takes around an hour to finish a session, if you have an experience maybe it might take 30 minutes to 45 minutes. The costumes are given through a reward in Catalogs (banners/seasonal pass/warbond). Also they are free to get and only need to grind some trials in game.Overall definitely a recommend game. If you can handle some gores, horrors, and jumpscares this game is right in your alley, Also it's fun with your friends..

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good contrast of being jump-scared, yet still having to be aware and strategic. There is a good gore and horror element to it with the introduction to every trial being unique and scary to its own, as well as every single trial having its perks. Every single character in the game that is hunting you down has its own scary features, and every trial has different aspects of gore and horror such as cutting limbs off, or searching for a key in a corpse. I also really love the feature of being able to decorate your room as well as customize your characters, but I would like to see more character customization features in the future such as outfits and hats. _childDocuments_.review: Outlast Trials had a solid structure during EA. You had base programs that prepare you for the endgame content: Program X and Rebirth. The whole point of this was to make it difficult and give players an incentive to play the hardest mode. Now with 1.0, not only did they make Program X infinitely easier, but the whole reborn system is just horrible. Genesis is pretty much the base programs and you can get the same amount of tokens there as you would with the harder difficulties. I'm not against the idea of giving everyone a chance to rebirth freely, but it should be earned like it was before. Genesis tokens should be a one time thing and you should have to play Program X or Ultra to get the tokens. Like I said earlier you can play the easiest trials with 0 enemies and get the same rewards as you would on the higher difficulties. If they don't plan to revert this change they can make it better by doubling or tripling the amount of tokens you get from X/Ultra. The fact that you can complete all of Program X and still not have enough tokens to rebirth is insane. There's no reason for most people to play X/Ultra if the rewards are the same anyways, and this will actually kill the player count too. I've already seen people spamming sabotage the lockdown 20 times to rebirth and complain the game is boring and repetitive. If more people hop on this train, give it a month or two and the player count will be lower than it was in EA except for the new content releases.At this time I've been reborn 361 times and I don't plan on continuing the grind towards 1000. Don't get me wrong, the game is still great but it feels miserable for people grinding reborns.

_childDocuments_.review: I mostly played this with friends, and I've gotta say that the challenges this game provides can bring about some fun (albeit frustrating) trials.Like in the previous Outlast games, you need to go to point A and retrieve stuff while simultaneously trying to avoid killers. That changes a little bit here. Think of the SAW movies, and then mix it into a kind of gameshow-esque kinda setting. It even brought back its charming weirdness, like full-on public nudity. Penises are abound here, along with decaying tits stapled to nuns. Yeah, it's Outlast alright. ._.The Perks you can unlock and upgrade as you level up are great uses, and having a squad that can come in with different equipment can help you as you try and beat each game. There are unlockables you can use for your own little room to show off your own personal flair, but they're not really super satisfying to unlock. You can unlock some desk unique items for completing certain map challenges, but that's really about it when it comes to the cosmetics.It's fun for a good while, but after you play through all the maps through all their difficulties so many times, you kinda lose interest as it gets a little easier to do every time. But I'd say the biggest letdown of this game is that there's far too little content to keep gauging my interest. It was fun, but in the end the $30 I spent on this game doesnt seem all that worth it when I only have 22 hours on this game.I know we're only in 5 months on this game so far, but I feel like there 'should' be more, but there just isn't. And that's the biggest letdown of them all. I'd give it a thumbs up, but the above reasons are just why I can't. I'll come back to this game in a couple months to see if new content drops.

_childDocuments_.review: Outlast Trials is an outstanding cooperative horror game that exceeds expectations, offering approximately 15 hours of thrilling content in its current state. With engaging gameplay, a terrifying atmosphere, challenging stealth mechanics, immersive sound design, and impressive visuals, it successfully delivers a memorable and adrenaline-pumping experience. Whether playing cooperatively or solo, players can immerse themselves in the heart-pounding world of the Cold War-era research facility.While the game showcases many strengths, it's important to address a few areas that could benefit from improvement. The limited variety of enemies encountered throughout the game could be expanded upon to provide more surprises and challenges. Additionally, incorporating more incentives for exploration, such as hidden collectibles or optional objectives, could enhance the overall depth and engagement. Furthermore, introducing more complex puzzles that require creative problem-solving would add an extra layer of satisfaction for players seeking a greater challenge.It's worth mentioning that future updates and expansions have the potential to significantly change the content and gameplay experience, further extending the game's value and replayability. Despite these critiques, Outlast Trials remains a must-play for horror enthusiasts and fans of the series, offering an exceptional cooperative horror adventure that keeps players on the edge of their seats. Prepare yourself for a gripping and unforgettable journey into the heart of terror, whether you choose to face it with friends or brave it alone.

_childDocuments_.review: *The Outlast Trials* attempts to bring the intensity of survival horror into a multiplayer setting, but unfortunately, the experiment falls short of capturing what made the original *Outlast* games so terrifying. The shift from a single-player horror experience to an online co-op format weakens much of the suspense and isolation that were central to the series’ success. Instead of the tense, solitary atmosphere that *Outlast* fans expect, *The Outlast Trials* often feels more chaotic than creepy.The gameplay, while retaining some elements of classic *Outlast* mechanics, lacks the polish and depth to make it feel truly satisfying. Objectives and tasks are repetitive, and much of the tension dissipates with multiple players sharing the horror. This setup could work if balanced carefully, but here, it undermines the fear factor, making it hard to fully immerse in the horror when you’re constantly coordinating with other players. What was once a game of careful stealth and spine-chilling scares feels more like a generic team-based horror that struggles to keep its footing.Graphically, the game maintains the dark, gritty aesthetic of the series, but the visuals can’t compensate for the lack of atmosphere. Moments that would otherwise be terrifying lose impact with the multiplayer format, and the overall quality of gameplay feels underwhelming, especially for longtime fans expecting the same quality of horror.In short, *The Outlast Trials* is a disappointing attempt to bring *Outlast* into the online realm. While the concept had potential, the execution leaves much to be desired, and the game struggles to deliver the quality and intensity that made the original games stand out. As a survival horror, it simply doesn’t live up to expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 4/5Outlast Trials, the latest installment in the Outlast series, takes a bold step into cooperative horror and delivers a spine-chilling experience that will have you gripping your controller tightly. Developed by Red Barrels, this game successfully introduces cooperative gameplay while maintaining the series' trademark atmospheric terror.The standout feature of Outlast Trials is undoubtedly its co-op gameplay. Whether you choose to face the horrors alone or team up with friends, the game excels at creating a truly immersive and terrifying cooperative experience. Working together to overcome the twisted challenges and survival scenarios adds an exciting layer of strategy and camaraderie. The cooperative mechanics are well-implemented, ensuring a seamless and enjoyable multiplayer adventure.The game's atmosphere is incredibly tense and unsettling. From the dark and claustrophobic environments to the haunting sound design, Outlast Trials knows how to play with your fears. The psychological horror elements and well-timed jump scares keep you constantly on the edge of your seat. The narrative, although not reaching the heights of its predecessors, still manages to engage players with its mysterious and twisted storyline.Visually, Outlast Trials is a treat for horror enthusiasts. The graphics are crisp and detailed, bringing the terrifying world to life. The character models and environments are meticulously crafted, effectively enhancing the sense of horror and despair. While there are occasional technical glitches, they are minor and don't significantly detract from the overall experience.One area where Outlast Trials falls slightly short is in its replay value. Once you've completed the main campaign and explored the different paths and outcomes, there's not much incentive to go back and replay it. Some additional content or modes would have added more longevity and replayability to keep players engaged beyond the initial playthrough.In summary, Outlast Trials successfully delivers a terrifying co-op horror experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat. The cooperative gameplay mechanics, intense atmosphere, and solid visuals make it a must-play for horror fans. Despite a few minor technical issues and limited replay value, Outlast Trials remains a chilling addition to the franchise, showcasing Red Barrels' commitment to delivering scares and thrills.
