_childDocuments_.review: You have to be genuinely impressed how the developers are continuously making new content and updating their game for bascially no monetization and no financial incentive. The aesthetics of this game is breathtaking. The attention to detail meticulous. The game combines gruesome gorey imagery and environments in eerie settings with beautifully rendered assets and character design. Yes, it is true that the missions is quite repetitive overtime, but keep in mind this is a multiplayer optional game, and as a PVE game it still offers alot of replayability and the playtime definitely justifies its price. Even when Ive replayed levels for 50 times, I still manage to discover new things everytime I play. The maps design is ingenious and the procedural generation makes every playthrough a fresh experience. I hope the dev team continue to make more challenging modifiers for veterans, and new objectives for the existing maps. The maps contain so much detail it should be very easy to create novelty missions on them for the future. There should also be custom modes where you can add any modifiers to any exisiting missions, and a pool where you can access any previous missions outside of time limited events.The only negative I have with the game is how little you are rewarded for your achievements. Its easy to max out in levels and there isnt much reward for you to repeatedly grind the game and strive for A+ evaluation on each mission, which in itself should be an end goal in the game. Lack of rewards greatly dissuades people from wanting to dedicate more time to the game after the initial playthrough.Overall the game is amazing and deserves to be experienced and cherished by any fans of the horror genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon watching IGN’s  and, yet again,  review for this game, which is a highly expected and predictable deed from this particular company, I thought it would be much more beneficial for incoming players to have an honest declaration of appreciation for the game from one of the already playing players themselves rather than some incompetent video game reviewer.Beforehand, I recommend playing the game  co-op with a few friends if you want to have a playthrough filled with stress and panic rather than fear since trying to solo the entire game will have a deeply felt burden on you as the player, both psychological and physical. Psychological in the sense that it  exerts  fear and horror like no other on you up until the mid stages of the game as you are left to face the levels all alone. Physical in the sense that you have to do everything on your own while having a distribution of tasks might really ease this burden. There are certain objectives in the game like pushing the stool of a snitch in the first program where you will really feel the abscence of fellow players. Additional players will also cause the agro of the npcs to be distributed among the players which will also give you some  time to breathe.I will abstain from giving the game a certain score, but rather will lay out what striked my eye as overwhelmingly positive  features of the game during my playthrough:-: Even in this more objective oriented entry of the Outlast Franchise, horror as an element is executed right on point. The game is horrifying, not mainly because of its jumpscares and atmosphere,  but becuase of how it forces the player to complete the objectives while giving full attention to the environment with its roaming enemies and many variations of traps. There is also a very fitting word in the english dictionary to describe the overall atmosphere  of the game: morbid. The game takes place at morbid locations and is filled with morbid characters conducting morbid actions. Gore is obviously the main reason of this morbidity. You will come across dissected and beheaded bodies, their organs being out in the open, and get chased by giant npcs with their brains and genitals hanging out. What a freakshow!  Another aspect that adds up to the game’s horror is the fact that you are left weaponless and defenless. Your only weapon is your ability to work together ,your ability to run and hide, and your ability to make use of miscelleanous items such as bricks and bottles.-: Overall, the current levels and the environment of the game is very well-polished. Beside the aforementioned body parts laying out it is safe to say that a lot of effort has gone into making the maps seem real to the eye. Every level you will play on is detailed down to its inches. What really struck me when I completed the first level is that the different segments of the level become more  inter-connected the more you play, giving you an impression of free roam.-: In comparison to previous entries a new progression system has been implemented into the game which, in fact, serves its purpose  perfectly. Your character level progresses as you go through the levels, making way for new tactics and strategies on, for example, how you approach a certain objective or how you run and hide from an enemy. The amount of variety in existing player movement and class perks (rigs as they are called in-game) is sufficient to cause a clear distinction between players and to allow different playstyles. Such a progression system also adds replayability as you will definitely want to try out your newly unlocked attributes in previous levels.-: yet another differentiation from previous entries, the co-existince of co-op and solo modes for the same level has been executed with perfection. Both modes have their own merits and takeaways. As mentioned above if you choose to solo the game you will experience the fear of loneliness (as in Outlast 1 and 2) but will have a lot less work to do. Contrastingly if you prefer going in with friends wou will be left with the confidence of solidarity rather than loneliness but you will have more sub-objectives for the completion of a main objective and additional enemies that roam around. (But do bear in mind that the game was meant to be played co-operatively and has always been advertised as a multiplayer game.)

_childDocuments_.review: **SPOILER WARNING**TO PREFACE: I did not attempt to play this game solo, as I played the entire game as a trio. This was the general consensus of the three of us after simultaneously completing.TL;DR-Game extremely well made, worth picking up, but definitely leaves some to be desired. 7/10-Very fun cooperative experiences, especially towards the beginning. It was an absolute blast to play the first trials and learn the flow of the game.-Division of labor between multiple people seems fair, never did I feel overwhelmed with tasks when playing as a group. -Environment, enemy and general art is fantastic, reminiscent of the previous Outlast (for obvious reasons), but I would even say they stepped up the grotesqueness of this game compared to the previous (somehow). -The mini-trials using the same "realm" as the main trials adds a level of connectivity, which I appreciate. We would begin trials with an epiphany of sorts, recognizing the area and how to loop enemies. -The FIRST time you view the cinematics, they were amazing. The approach of no "screen-locking" cut scenes was a great decision, as watching live cinematic while being able to walk around is a fantastic touch. The initial start of the trial was also interesting, although a vote-skip button should be added when replaying levels.-The voice acting and audio design in general was very polished and well done. I could almost always detect enemies using audio. The voice acting really helped to bring these characters to life, which is reminiscent of the original Outlast .-Great progression system, leveling up feels satisfying.-Cosmetics and room decor was fun to play with.-Arm wrestling.-The leader-board in the main area I enjoyed, nice touches like this are appreciated.-The tutorial was absolutely fantastic, as I was quite literally ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ my pants playing through it.-Spare for occasional frame drops, the game runs amazing. -Character customization could be improved, ex: rig customization feels lacking, along with not being able to switch a helmet and hair.-Game play loop CAN feel extremely mundane and repetitive, as only three trials are the backbone of the  entire game at this moment. You find yourself doing the same trial with the same objective upwards of three times. Note: I understand that more content is likely coming, I am merely speaking on the CURRENT state of the game.-Enemies can occasionally feel unfair and too abundant, especially on the harder difficulties. It began to feel quite frustrating as we got to levels with the "high density of enemies" label. Especially when some enemies will blatantly camp the final objective, like at the end of kill the snitch for example. My group found themselves being mercilessly camped and bum rushed by enemies whose entire pattern was to circle the final objective. In my opinion that is not good game design, just frustrating and artificially boosted the "difficulty" and time of the trial.-Towards the end, the lack of tension building began to backfire on the game-play loop. As again, frustration crept up as enemies will mercilessly surround the objective or any general area the player is in.-The final trial was the real summation of almost all of the gripes listed above, as simply four objectives took upwards of an hour to complete, enemies felt unfair and simple tasks felt arduous. -In my opinion, solo play is almost an afterthought, as the solo-experience is obviously under-cooked to say the least. Relegating the objectives to solo play undermines the cooperative aspect of distributing the work.Final Consensus:The cooperative experience is this games' bread and butter, if you are looking for a game to play with your friends, this is a fantastic choice even at this current "under cooked" stage. If you are looking for a comprehensive, narrative driven game, or enjoy a solo horror experience, then this game simply isn't for you. This is a enjoyable game at its core however, and the frameworks are well-defined and simply fun. The sour aftertaste of some lackluster levels shouldn't deter you from trying this out.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is pretty incredible for an early access game. Red Barrels has proven with their two previous Outlast games that they're completely capable of a unique gut wrenching, morbidly disgusting, horrific & gorey yet intriguing, thought-provoking and eye-catching cinematic experience. The world of Outlast highlighting genuine insanity to the max is extraordinary to me because of how it's portrayed & executed. I applaud the imagitive people who help create the scenarios and characters they feature within their stories. The perks, the customization options, the abilities, the collections, the badges & the trials themselves..EVERYTHING, is admirable. I thoroughly enjoy this game!However, at the time I am writing my review, I've completed every single trial a multitude of times & was reborn just a single time back a few months ago. I'm able to solo queue the trials without trouble because I'm pretty familiar with each and every trial & enemy that is currently avaliable to face. I'm ready and eagerly waiting for new content.DEVS, please continue updating your game! Little by little is perfectly fine. But, please, don't abandon your works (I'm not implying that that's the case, though). There's INSANE amounts of amazing potential for you to delve into! I'm excited to witness your visions for this game within the next few months to a year from now.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and engaging survival horror game. Not very scary after a while, but the first Trial solo can be exciting. My favorite part is how satisfying the animations of everything are. Your character pops open a bottle of meds, takes a pill out into the palm of their hand, and swallows. Adrenaline shots are first stabbed into the arm and then the bottle is squeezed like toothpaste. Sliding, moving, jumping and hurdling over obstacles is smooth and satisfying. Your nightvision is simple and easy on the eyes. My only gripes are how excessive the "spooky" factor is put up. Eventually all of the blood and gore and evil capitalism vibes just get a bit much and no longer become scary but rather just gross and uncreative. I would love to see future Trials centered less around blood and guts and more on the psychological horror elements on their own. I don't need to see a guy getting chopped up to be afraid of the idea of going insane.

_childDocuments_.review: Outlast trials is good.Well designed levels with multiple approaches to multiple situations. Everything feels dynamic because it is. There are enough trials to play for about 40 hours id say as a casual player, that + trying to get good grades for every stage which might add a couple hundred more. ( not very casual at that point ). I do hope they add more enemy types and programs ( programs are basically locations ) Currently there are a few enemy types with some differences, some they could add include a ranged enemy and a crawling enemy that grabs players from holes or something like that.On the horror side of things its Outlast, not much to it than that. If you were scared of Outlast 1 or 2 you will be scared of this one, maybe even more scared. Enemies are ruthless and will hear you from quite far away, luckily there is a sound for detection so you aren't completely clueless.The game does a lot to overwhelm the player, there are constant threats with little to no downtime. You will not get a good grade from your first few trials, but it does feel rewarding once you do.In terms of difficulty, as i just stated the game is hard. Way harder than the previous titles. You might think playing in COOP makes it easier but its actually well balanced. While you have more shortcuts and ways to approach situations in COOP, you will also have more objectives and longer animations. Solo you cant do risky plays, but you have faster animations and less objectives which lets you do things slower without sacrificing time.Customization is OK, you unlock more options the more you play which is a good thing since it rewards clean runs and more runs. Acting is some of the best, i love Leland Coyle ( dont know the actor ). All the side characters the grunts and stuff are extremely well acted aswell.The game is great, get it if you like horror games / coop games / challenging games.

_childDocuments_.review: After so many new co-op games being announced and then turning out to be generic Live service games with RPG elements, incremental progression, battlepasses and in general various strategies to ensure you will only be playing one game forever, Outlast Trials is a breath of fresh air and I can recommend it just because it is something different and incredibly fun. Hopefully this statement will not age poorly as the game leaves Early Access.To sum it up quickly, tense stealth horror game with satisfying progression. With a higher player count and more gameplay hours in, the scare aspect upon being caught quickly becomes replaced with pure chaos.For those on the fence, the tutorial showcases the core gameplay and almost the worst it will throw at you horror wise, I strongly recommend to buy, try (should take around 20 minutes) and decide whether you want to keep going or refund.After the tutorial you are put into a lobby with other players, where you can select the main missions of the game.These missions have slight randomization for the replayability aspect, certain doorways will be locked, items will be changed around, different hiding spots will be blocked off, however objectives and the general route will pretty much stay the same.In the same lobby you are also introduced to the game's progression systems, personal customization and the  arm wrestling minigame.The actual gameplay varies as in the first hours of the game, the horror aspect of the game will be heavily present as you get used to the game, the way it messes with you via the multiplayer aspect. You will be familiarizing yourself with the traps, the enemies and in general will take it slow and careful.10 hours in and with a high enough playercount however, the horror aspect wears off and the game becomes something akin to first person , The careful tense stealth gameplay now becomes a prelude to the chaos that happens when somebody gets caught, as all the players will start running away from the enemies, possibly into the traps, saving eachother from being attacked all while scrambling to complete the objective.

_childDocuments_.review: This game throws you in and gives you a quick moment of ice water when the tutorial is a solo, first person, spooky treasure hunt; it does well to teach you mechanics and rules without ruining the atmosphere or general nerves it's created. It has a pretty mundane character customisation screen, -but- you can access it throughout your time between trials, as well as unlocking cosmetics and room customisation options. The programs the game currently has are repeated with different "difficulty" modifiers, which is usually the game just loading in 50 extra enemies into the instance and calling it a day, however, some of the modifiers make the game super interesting like removing survival items like health restores and night vision chargers. All players can pick from different "rigs" that facilitate different play-styles and bring out different players strengths; as well as picking from "mods" and other add-ons to "sneak in" to your trials. Honestly, if you enjoy taking your time with the survival side of the horror genre, this is an excellent game; since stamina is limited and you need to think strategically to hide from enemies and collect objectives, both in multiplayer and single-player, this isn't your game if you prefer a fast paced FPS game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outlast Trials

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 8/10Optimisation: 9.5/10Combat: 7.5/10Movement: 8.5/10Ease of use: 9/10Audio: 6/10 (bit buggy and not special overall)Map design: 8.5/10Content quantity: 4/10 (basically finished the unique missions in 4 hours)Overall: 7.5First and foremost, the game is verrrrrry well optimised. I haven't gotten this many frames on max graphics + ray tracing in ages, it feels really good. The movement is nice although the toggle sprint is a bit awkward sometimes because of the fairly low stamina. There is a lot of room to try different playstyles, although if you care about the rating at the end of a trial, you will be disappointed if you are hoping to get a good rating and play aggressively (I personally like playing more aggressively but it is virtually impossible to get a high rating without high tier upgrades). Speaking of, the upgrade system is very straightforward and easy to understand for the average Joe, yet the upgrades themselves feel very impactful while maintaining good balance. The game can be fairly difficult if you are not experienced in fast paces first person games or games that require good mobility, unless you want to just resort to hiding a lot (again, lots of room for varying playstyles). Overall, game is a solid 7.5/10, with my main issue being the lack of content, which I wouldn't expect to be an issue at the $40 CAD price tag. There are only 3 levels and variations of these levels, each of which only takes 30-40 min to complete on average, maybe longer if you are having trouble or play very quietly to preserve your stealth.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outlast Trials is a horror movie in reverse, in ways both good and bad. Instead of screaming in terror when something jumps out at you or stabs your character in the face, you usually just laugh as your friends make fun of you from their hiding spots. Instead of a clueless group of protagonists who get picked off one by one, the enemies hunting you and your teammates are the ones with the hilariously poor decision-making skills. While the early access version of this cooperative horror game proves the concept and has a couple of very memorable maps, it’s not one of those games that’s sprung into being almost fully formed. Expected bugs and general lack of polish aside, there’s just not much content yet. Even so, I had an overall good time with this silly, gory, and uneven slaughterfest even in these early stages.The Outlast Trials throws you and up to four of your friends into insane and improbable Saw-like “death games” in which you must work together to overcome the gory terrors that await. What little story there is so far doesn’t amount to much: you’re abducted by an evil corporation and kept in a prison under the guise of rehabilitation, but instead are subjected to a seemingly random series of murder playgrounds. You can glean some mildly interesting bits of lore by collecting compromising evidence that immoral company men apparently left lying around its death courses, but it’s not exactly mesmerizing stuff. And that’s okay! You’re playing The Outlast Trials because you want to see a crazy lady use a sock puppet to drill a guy’s face off, and there’s certainly an abundance of that.That said, even when treated with the unseriousness and gore-filled levity that I think The Outlast Trials is going for, the over-the-top violence, deeply unsexy lechery, and extremely on-the-nose subject matter can be a bit much sometimes. One level features a maniacal police officer who enjoys tasering his own genitals and rattles off nonsense like “I don’t recognize this country anymore,” while in another you’re repeatedly shown a bunch of penises for seemingly no reason at all, and then forced to recreate a crucifixion for an audience of school children. I get that shock and gratuitous violence is sorta the whole point, but it often feels like they’re trying so hard to be gross and extreme or make some kind of unsubtle statement that I just shook my head at the tactless, edgelordian overkill. At least when South Park does it it’s usually funny.Each of the three maps in the early access version has its own bizarre and twisted objectives that must be completed before your untimely death, like one where you’re forced to turn an impure orphanage into a malevolent religious establishment by replacing all the secular materials with unholy profanity. There’s another where you have to punish a group of wicked animatronic children by shoving them into a meat grinder, working around various obstacles as you slowly push the cart of misbehaving dolls toward their demise. Of course, the absurdly macabre goals you’re presented with merely serve as complicated and unavoidably noisy chores that you’re expected to perform as numerous psychopaths hunt you, drawn to the sound of your actions. While it’s not particularly exhilarating to, for example, fill a generator with gas and turn it on, the fact that you have to do so while being hunted by murderers and under great duress goes a long way to making things extremely chaotic and panic-inducing.Where would you *least* enjoy being hunted by stupid but bloodthirsty murderers?Did I mention that you don’t have any weapons? Certainly nothing that will turn the hunters into the hunted, at least. Instead, you must rely on stealth by creeping in darkness, hiding in closets or barrels and under beds, and occasionally using thrown bottles and bricks to distract or temporarily stun enemies when you’re stuck in a tight spot. When everything works as intended, your inability to face the enemy head on creates some delectable dramatic tension that aptly recreates those iconic horror film moments where the protagonist tries to hold her breath while the monster lurks just a few feet away. Other times, though, the enemy AI bugs out and the murderer just stares right at the barrel you’re hiding in, indefinitely, until you decide to blow your cover and risk making a break for it. That makes that game of cat and mouse feel janky and unfair.One of the awesome ways enemies mess with you is by inflicting psychosis on you via poisonous gas. It leaks out from some level traps and enemy attacks, and if you’re exposed to it you’ll see hallucinations like creepy Michael Meyers-esque mirages or Skinner Man, an imagined enemy who can do you real harm if you’re drained of your sanity. This results in some amazing social moments where you shout out a warning about a monster your friends don’t see, and begin to doubt your own eyes and ears. (Only a few games, like Dead Space 3, have dabbled in this kind of co-op trickery.) You’ll also encounter doppelgangers of your teammates who, if you miss the slight differences in their player name, will shank you if you get too close. That’s a fantastic curveball that makes you question whether you can even trust your own comrades.While you can play The Outlast Trials alone, contending with evil twins is just one example of why working with friends to survive each stage and help one another out of jams is undeniably a better experience, though also usually more tumultuous and less atmospheric. As you add up to four players to any given trial, the objectives you’re asked to complete become more complex to offset the advantages granted by having friends, which usually results in less stealth and more frantic running around as you and your buddies accidentally set off four times as many traps, get hunted down by all manner of grotesque horrors, and fight over the best hiding spots. (Remember: you don’t have to be faster than the bear, just faster than your slowest companion.) But when your crew is coordinating well, staying on task, and have had a chance to get familiar with the level, operations can feel much more controlled and tense. Either method can definitely be fun and earn you victory, but only the latter will earn you a good grade from your sadist overseers, which grants more better cosmetic unlockables and XP.The Outlast Trials Early Access ScreenshotsThat XP can be spent to permanently unlock a fair selection of upgrades that make the going easier in each level. One of those is your rig: a special ability that lets you do things like stun an enemy with a thrown bomb or see items and enemies through walls with X-ray vision, all of which operate via cooldowns and lend some much-needed identity and role-based dynamics to your cooperative squad. There’s also a number of appealing and helpful passive abilities that can be purchased which let you do things like slide when sprinting into a crouch or automatically slip free of lesser enemies who manage to grab you. None of these unlockables gets around the fact that you’ll be repeating the same trials over and over again as you grind to obtain them, but they definitely make the optional tougher versions of each level more doable and give you more interesting options with which to tackle them.The Outlast Trials is a unique cooperative horror game with a fantastic premise and some really memorable scenarios, but while the early access version proves the concept there’s a lot of work to be done to make those ideas pay off. Running around with friends as you hide from murderous killers and complete utterly insane (and sometimes too edgy for their own good) death games is paradoxically tense and hilarious, but the fact that the enemy AI is about as effective as a concrete parachute and two of the three levels share too much of the same DNA certainly leaves a lot of room to grow on. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a positive review full of negativity at the end, because I really enjoy this game HOWEVER it has pain points that I would love to see the developers handle. Let's start with the good (and some VERY good things).The good:Performance is great for a good looking modern game, I'm glad red barrels have ignored the status quo set by the AAA industry and have decided to not use DLSS as a crutch for a poor performing title. The game looks good and runs well for most people. I run the game at the highest settings which by most games standards means high framerate with terrible 1% lows as it hitches all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time; not a single hitch in all my hours. Add to that the game install is small by modern standards, doesn't need to be put on SSD, the technicals of this game are spot on.The game is gorgeous. I'm not talking graphics I'm talking art direction. While some enemy designs are a bit uninspired and a lot of the shock is a bit played out, the locations feel detailed and "lived in", making them feel plausible with just the right amount of "game-y" shortcuts and stuff jto make them actual levels. Bar the second mission, the levels are pretty spot on with a great feeling of escalation of challenge brought by the map design.Multiplayer is 90% quiet people having fun, with a good amount of talkative and NICE people having fun. As unlike a certain other multiplayer horror game with a lot of running away, working together is incredibly beneficial and the levels also work to give a mix of encouraging you to split up and encouraging you to stay close but ALWAYS to work as a team. The story and atmospher are well crafted and work with the gameplay on a meta level. I never thought a live-service style of game would be able to come along and make me enjoy the story it tells AND work it into the structure of the gameplay but they did. It's not some subtle masterpiece, but it's very enjoyable.The bad:The worst issue is the loadouts, there is no variety. You get a choice of 4 rigs, 16(I think) pharmacy drugs and 3 amps. The 16 pharmacy drugs (basically skills) can all be unlocked by the time you finish the story so they aren't really a choice, but they do really empower you by the end game and mostly work well with the co-op aspect so whatever. The amps just seem to be less meaningful than the skills even though they cost more to unlock and you can't equip as many.To extend upon the previous points, the 4 rigs (active skills) are horrifically balanced:-Stun: Reliable staple good for clutching objectives. It sounds good, it's even better than it sounds. Stun enemies, they stop moving, easy peasy.-Heal: Reliable free resource generation for you and your team. Unlike stun it's strength is very non-interactive and impossible to go wrong with. All it really ends up doing is letting you know you can waste limited resources. Perhaps a necessary evil at the top difficulties where even basic enemies can two shot.These two rigs are incredibly strong and are LITERALLY the only rigs you will see or should get. The following two are comparatively awful and never seen.-X-ray: I have seen one player use it and that player is me. It lets you see through walls for a short time when un-upgraded and the upgrades give it some incredible uptime while also regenerating your night vision. Sadly night vision is already very easy to keep topped up and the game already gives you sound queues for nearby enemies. It's good for finding posters, avoiding wasting lockpicks on trash like batteries, finding important loot in a clutch and doing stealthy plays. Posters just give XP, no loot behind locks is essential, loot in general is a bit meaningless other than antidotes and stealth only is a sub-optimal play style that you use situationally between running away. It's honestly not that bad but compared to stun and health it's just mediocre, without any benefit to multiple people coming with it unlike stun or heal.-Blind: I have never seen it, not even once. I have beaten the game and never seen this used by a single player. I might update this review when I finish levelling my amps and inevitably go for blind after because I like funky play-styles.A lot of the horror between the levels relies on the same topics to get a reaction. Partially this ties into the story . However I still found that within my initial play through of each level there weren't many moments that made me go "Wow that's incredibly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and creative" and I'm not a horror guy either. It relies on a lot of  it just needs some more variety. This sort of ties into the environments being fairly expected horror locations but bar the second level the flavour that the game and story bring tends to elevate these fairly expected environments.Certain enemy types such as the imposters or whatever the ♥♥♥♥ that disguise as you have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up AI that seems to follow you in the dark frequently despite your stealth, they suck and are also easy to spot so never end up catching you off guard in the intended way. Worse than that are the screamers. They stun you borderline randomly, sometimes not stunning others in the exact same situation. Screamers are awful and need to be made consistent as they are currently an un-fun gamble on whether they will even trigger and whether the trigger will end up even stunning you. To make things worse they can also often stun even when you can't even hear the scream or see them.Finally, the final level. I will try to avoid spoiling it but cannot do so entirely. I was one of the first 200 or so to clear this and I wish I wasn't so I could rely on some tutorial to cheese it. You are forced to play the tutorial level backwards alone on a server (so you can't pause), in my case with X-ray which sucks balls, with a randomly generated object you have to find that can be in some very weird locations and with randomly generated resources that can sometimes make the layout incredibly hard. Also if you start again you have to start from the beginning, no checkpoints, watch all the animations again. It plays differently from the rest of the game in the worst way, with its cramped linear layout, unclear objectives, horrid patrol paths, RNG and lack of co-op aspects. If I have to complete this level again to "prestige" for the second time I'm just not doing it, it's miserable and frustrating. By the way, the open area with the night vision guy that's hard to hide from is easiest to complete if you bait him back to the light and dodge the door camera instead of stealthing as the devs want you to.To sum up, the game is very good with a few big pain points that are possible to iron out with patches mostly around the balance. The flaws aren't fundamental but they do hamper an otherwise great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "Furry Sex" transports players to an imaginative world where anthropomorphic characters and adult themes combine to create a unique, interactive experience. The game caters to a niche audience, skillfully blending elements of fantasy, intimacy, and storytelling.Gameplay & MechanicsThe gameplay is surprisingly dynamic for its genre. Rather than a passive experience, "Furry Sex" encourages players to make choices that impact character relationships and outcomes. This level of engagement, combined with character-specific backstories and personalities, adds layers of depth to what might otherwise be a straightforward simulation. The choice-based mechanics ensure that each playthrough feels fresh and personalized, appealing to players who value narrative-driven interactions.Art & Character Design"Furry Sex" excels in its art style, with high-quality visuals that bring each character to life. The anthropomorphic designs are carefully crafted, striking a balance between cartoonish charm and sensual allure. Each character’s design reflects their personality traits, making interactions feel more immersive and enjoyable. From expressive eyes to meticulously detailed fur, the visuals convey a surprising amount of warmth and intimacy.Storytelling & World-BuildingThe storyline in "Furry Sex" is more developed than one might expect. Characters have histories, personalities, and unique motivations that add richness to the game world. This added depth encourages players to explore and invest emotionally in each character’s journey. The writing is tasteful and playful, with witty dialogues that elevate the experience beyond mere physical interaction.

_childDocuments_.review: Great experience overall. For those who want to mainly play solo as I have, this game is still definitely worth buying. I feel like there's some nice mechanical improvements from the previous Outlast games while also still respecting their visions; the general feel of it resembles the original in a lot of ways which was great and  perhaps surprising given the length of time between this RB release and the first game (over a decade, so potential for many changes within the structure of the Red Barrels creative teams).The loop and progression is satisfying enough without being addictive. Familiarity, but plenty of new things to adjust to. If you loved poring over the documents in the first two games, the new ones that you discover throughout trials may help you connect a few dots from those in the first two games.The trial environments are super interesting in their own right, and I've really enjoyed learning how to progress through each one so far. They can get mildly repetitive, but you would be surprised what the modification of objectives and other parameters can do to give the environments a new feeling of life. They have clearly made a conscious effort to ensure variety, and this success varies but is generally acceptable from my experience.To summarise and keep the review (kinda) short: If you love Outlast, I think you'll love this. It's a bit of old and a bit of new and the result is quite impressive. Bring your friends into the mix and the possibilities for mayhem and fun grow even further with clear intent for cooperative playstyles baked into the gameplay. I have to say as well - being able to experience Outlast-style gameplay outside of the main instalments, but with changing environments, objectives and modifiers, is fantastic. Love the gameplay of the former titles, but say it's been too soon since your last story playthrough? Boot up this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this game up while looking for a fun co-op game with friends and was not disappointed. I haven't really played the single player Outlast games, but you don't need to. Even in Early Access, the game is very polished and easily has 20+ hours of content even if you try to blaze through the missions currently available. The grind can seem a bit brutal at first, but once you start unlocking some of the 'prescriptions' the gameplay feels very smooth and enjoyable.The core gameplay loop involves navigating a scary environment infested with enemies in first-person, attempting to solve various puzzles while collecting helpful items and avoiding or outrunning enemies. Beginner players will resort to hiding more often, but the game is perfectly enjoyable without having to stall by hiding in the same spot and instead outmaneuver enemies stealthily. Enemy AI is currently more forgiving than not, and once players get a feel of how enemies work, they shouldn't have trouble using the items and environment to their advantage.You can play this game by yourself but playing it with friends is recommended, and even solo queuing up with randoms can be a lot of fun. The game has a strong and healthy community and most experienced players seem to be supportive of helping newer players learn the ropes. The game also provides a really helpful emote system if you prefer not to use voice, but being on voice with friends is a LOT of chaotic fun.Absolutely recommended, especially if you're looking for another multiplayer horror game or trying to take a break from one (e.g. Dead by Daylight).

_childDocuments_.review: Manage to release a Reagent (prestige) at the 38 hour mark.This new Outlast, which is a prequel of the first games, is a nice change of scenario, however there is some lack of terror with clumsy “jumpscares” and usually not very frightening events. One should think, as a game before the events of the first games in the series, the change to heavy survival horror and cooperative was needed to build it. It still remains within the Outlast lore where violence and crazed up enemies are present, only from another era.In every trial you must complete a set of objectives with different gameplay factors, some better suited for up to four players. Singleplayer is still an option but when it comes to primary trials, doing those with teammates is a must. As a guinea pig you must tread with caution, observe the enemies around, and do the best to outmaneuver their movements. Of course, there is special bosses who move and attack faster and harder than your regular foe. Stealth remains as a loyal companion but eventually you have to run and hide.What it surprised me is that you actually can defend yourself (finally!) by throwing bottles and bricks, and using special equipment that stun your enemy population. No longer one has to depend on heavy stealth and shutting doors to stop anyone. Although if you don’t have nothing on you, or the boss is on your tail (as they’re only stagger by projectiles, but still vulnerable to Riggs), they become a decent option. Vaulting remains here and you can also slide while running. Jumping through windows and breaking doors while running remain available, but you have to watch for the noise you make, or someone nearby may listen.Featuring coop moves such as rolling gates, barricaded ones, and also reviving are some of the features in the Trials. There are more items to use than Outlast 2 and you can share them. Everyone will have to take care of themselves as it remains the core of the whole game: don’t get hit, don’t die. It will seem selfish, but because even when reviving and healing, Murkoff will know someone died and it will have an impact on the group score after the trial. Triggering loud traps, getting hit, knocked out and executed, will lower your personal score. And that’s all there’s to it. You can buy cosmetics and better gear, but at this point there isn’t much to do, other than playing timed chess at the lobby. For a title still on early access, there is some fun and can be quite teaching to help new players, but it will get quite repetitive and for that I won’t be playing it soon until new stuff is released. It’s still quite addictive if you want to do what I did.So goodbye for now, and don’t let the doctor teach you about dental hygiene.Edit: Nominated for Steam Awards 2023 - Better with Friends!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great game, great performance at a great price, recommend purchase as the price will increase over time. Terrifyingly well executed 9/10My take:Full graphics settings, RTX on, dlss on Hybrid, very good performance and consistent frame times. Very well put together and for once, a very polished experience. This game could be released as a full game if they wanted to. Lots of content and great game play. Lots of FREE customization items for your rooms and person (Things they easily could of slapped a $ in front of).Game has a well designed "Hub" area where you can customize your person or room. You can also arm wrestle with other captives while you wait for your friends to finish customizing their load outs with the engineer, this nurse lady that sells you drugs, and one other character that sells you other upgrades. You have a set that you can equip that ranging from giving you the ability to stun enemies or heal nearby teammates (there are other ones).Game play is fun. Sometimes is stressful and it seems like there is no way you could ever finish a challenge then all of the sudden its like "oh theres the gas can!". You can ping things to teammates and hand/drop things to your teammates. Communication is vital, and the game scales the difficultly depending on how many people you are playing with. Runs can take anywhere from 25 minutes to an hour depending on the experience of the players and if you have played on that level before. All the levels have more challenges and "quests" to do on another run through. The faster you complete the tasks the better. Avoid taking damage, and get the hell out as soon as you can. You are graded at the end of every run, affecting your XP turnout.The level design and challenges are incredible. Each puzzle and mini games are well crafted and have some overall purpose to the level you are on (each of them are kind of unique per level). Music and sound design are pretty good too. Voice lines and sound effects are great. Music is intense when appropriate. Nothing to really praise but well executed.The only issues i have is that the AI tends to get really fascinated about specific spots in the map and just hover there yelling about how mad they are for not finding you.Other than that, great coop game to play. _childDocuments_.review: Outlast Trials is a fun multiplayer Puzzle / Maze based survival horror that does keep you on your toes with the map and enemy design as you both have to keep your attention at your environment to not trigger traps and sound devices, and avoid hostile people who are patrolling or chasing you around!That part is not unlike your previous Outlast games, pretty much the same if maybe a bit easier since it is less scripted and you have more tools at your disposal to get rid of your chasers!It isn't that hard to get away if you trigger an enemy and it might seem a bit "cheap" how you can slam doors at their faces and then hide away - but the difficulty of the game isn't in the aspect of running away or just surviving but staying stealthy and completing the maps and the stage fast and easy to keep your final score high ( since the game has an evaluation system )--------------Just like any AI based game most of them can be memorized and so that can be a little bit boring once you learn the game more but that still requires 2-3 runs of the same program and each of them take  around 20-30 minutes or more depending on how experienced are the people you play with. Yes, your team will drastically change the experience from smooth game to the worst possible struggle based on how good everyone is ^^So far though there is at least 3 programs ( big maps ) and 4 scenarios at least I think for each of them so if we take what I said about each staying 100% fresh for 2-3 runs and then get a bit more repetitive or familiar due to the same objectives or map layouts :That is still around 18 hours of fresh content Outlast Trials offers currently and there will be more maps and scenarios available!If you enjoy stealth / puzzles and perfecting your runs and games - this will offer many many hours above that especially that there is a PROGRESSION SYSTEM available to level up with and 4 different classes to maximize and try out their unique tools.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game; great atmosphere, visuals, sound and a potentially amazing coop experience, but the game has a major issue that destroys the very core of the experience. No surprises here; it's the enemy pursuer AI.AI for game like this, where much of the time is spent in an elaborate game of hide and seek, is a balancing act between two possible extremes; extremely dumb and omniscient. In The Outlast Trials it leans heavily toward the latter. The enemies in this game just KNOW; know where you're hiding, know where you're heading, and relentlessly camp objectives you need to complete. It feels extremely cheap and artificial, and it isn't fun or exciting to compete against.If the devs can find that balance, this could be great. Until then, I'm out.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I'm sure kids are gonna have fun with it but I dont get it.  Its the noisiest, most unpleasant "stealth" game I've ever played.  I like horror movies but Im not much of a horror gamer.  I dont get scared at most horror games and I dont say that as an attempt to sound like a tough guy.  It's just my taste.  I enjoy horror films and while I dont get scared the way a child would where I'm losing sleep and all, I do get in suspense when I'm part of a short, say two hour experience thats been specifically curated to  be experienced from my point of view.  Horror games... they happen with or without you. You dont matter. Youre small, weak, insignificant, always running while trying to solve some sort of problem.   I'm sure some of you dig the vibes but it's not my thing at all.  There's rare exceptions, but this aint it.  I just find games like this unpleasant and boring.  Just nasty ugly images and sounds to accompany boring monotonous gameplay.  Go fetch this, sneak around this guy, distract him. If you screw up take ten minutes to reset the process and do it again. Just... not my thing at all.  You cant like...hit anyone which sure ok thats the game but for a game that encourages stealth based approach all it does is throw ugly distracting noises and images at you. None of it is frightening and I cant see how anyone would find it immersive.  Intense? I guess if you get into it. My first impressions watching it were that it would be intense but once I played it, yea its just another "fetch this, cross chores off your list while someone screams in your ear the entire time" that confuses uncomfort-ability with suspense.  Now I'll stick up for it a tiny bit in a few areas.  For one, it deserves success for reasons we'll get into.  It's not some rip-off cash grab.  If it looks like it appeals to you because games like this do... I'd say it's a reasonable bet you could enjoy this where I did not.  Also, obviously the community are making comparisons to DBD and while my initial reaction was "it's DBD but actually scary" I was wrong on both counts hahaha.  While I found it tedious I think those of you who get into this sort of thing would find the tighter maps and stealth based pve approach to be quite thrilling and not at all like the gameplay DBD offers.  I also think its very unique.  Theres a few DBD-esque trappings like a terror radius and all but it really is its own unique experience for better or worse.  Another plus that should be discussed for it being in early access is it's technical finish is already apparent and very well done.  The sounds are awful and gut-churning.  Dissonant music and blood-curdling screams and hair-turning cries.  But they are crisp as it gets with my nice headphones on AND with the crappy earbuds.  And the visuals are extremely well polished.  This doesnt feel like some cheap-o rush job this is very well crafted thus far.  I can not stress this enough: this is NOT a bad game even in my dismayed opinion.  So those things said, I dont think the current asking price of $30 is unfair.  But I cant recommend a game I am almost certain to never want to touch again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm ordinarily not huge on horror games - initially I was a bit skittish on this game because I have a pretty bad needle phobia, but the consumables are a Revive (on death) and Speed, so I haven't had to interact with them and have managed to play just fine. But, ordinarily, I'm a huge scaredycat for horror games, and I avoid them like the plague - but figured I'd strike out on a limb here. And I'm pretty glad I did!It's not that it's not terrifying - it bloody well is, atmosphere is extremely tense and gets to me, but in a quite enjoyable way. It being co-op takes the edge off that fear of course, because yeah, co-op games will dull the fear factor, but in this case it makes it quite a bit more accessible for my group of absolute pissbabies. I've even done a solo excursion or two but that gives an extremely different vibe - and having just me and one other person also raises the tension.But that's my personal experience. The game; audio design bangs, it does rely on jumpscare tension here and there of environmentals going off (gas bursting, lights popping, etc), but hearing enemies trample around, the groans and tells of each different type, the tension of when the game alerts you you're on the hook and you've gotta run, it's all quite good. My only complaint is that enemies are a bit too chatty; a lot of the time their lines overlap and there's no "dead time" between lines, making it a cacophony of insults and noise that lessens the tension somewhat. But the lines and audio itself is good - it just needs to be used more sparsely.The level design, likewise, is quite excellent. Claustrophobic and dark, mazelike, easy to get lost in in your panicked fleeing from enemies. It's designed to keep you on your toes, alert if you want to avoid environment traps and the like, and very willing to force you to panic and get you lost in said levels. (Will finish this later, was writing this while waiting for a pal and he's back. :) )

_childDocuments_.review: Whatever the Navajo told you... it's just one possible solution derived by Cipher. My will is different. I've known you since your time at Langley. I've long been the other side of your coin. 1964, Soviet territory. FOX's first mission. Any mess you made, I was there to clean up. You completed your task - and admirably. The 'information' you returned was far more than enough to fill our pockets. With it, our futures became - more or less - set in stone. And then the major came to me with an idea. 'Washington doesn't know how to spend money,' he said. 'I'd like to... redirect it'. His goal was an organisation dedicated solely - covertly - to supporting America. Cipher. You know the rest. To him, it was mourning - the loss of his friend. Or rather, an act of revenge. On the world, but America most of all. America is a country of liberty. A meeting of immigrants. Instead of simply assimilating, its citizens live along side others. Their roots are varied. Diverse. America's never been made up of just one people. But he tried to forge a single consciousness. For it, and from it. The idea that every citizen would use free will to unite behind their country... Unilateralism like that can't be entrusted to any one individual. So the major sought a system which used information, words, to control the 'subconscious'. To unite America and the entire world. The major thought this was his friend's will. But I think he never understood what she wanted. Before he ever walked, or cried - even before he was born - his mother tongue was English. He doesn't know the pain of losing his own language. Not yet. He cannot understand her will. I do. I was born in a small village. I was still a child when we were raided by soldiers. Foreign soldiers. Torn from my elders, I was made to speak their language. With each new post, my masters changed, along with the words they made me speak. Words are... peculiar. With each change, I changed too. My thoughts, personality, how I saw right and wrong... War changed me - and not only my visage. Words can kill. I was invaded by words, burrowing and breeding inside me. A philosopher once said, 'It is no nation we inhabit, but a language.' 'Make no mistake, our native tongue is our true fatherland.' My fatherland - my truth was stolen from me. And so was my past. All that's left is the future. And mine is revenge. On those who'd leech off the words of their fellow man. This is what I learned from the major. And then it hit me. It was he who should feel my wrath. He and the code he chose as basis for control. Language codes, information codes - beamed all around us - genetic codes spanning history. By controlling the codes, Cipher... Zero intends to unify the world. Codes implanted into our heads, sucking our minds dry as it spreads from one host to the next. A parasite upon the earth. That is what Zero is. As one born into this world, he's afflicted. I hold him responsible for killing my freedom. Killing all traces of my past... Killing any promise of a future... We are all but dead men forced to walk upon this earth. A world reduced to Zero. Cipher plans to use its codes to control the world. They think they can. And the 'mother tongue' of all those codes is English. The word became flesh. The final parasite. It knows English. An English strain of the vocal cord parasite. I will exterminate the English language. With this, I'll rid the world of infestation. All men will breathe free again - reclaim their past, present, and future. This is no ethnic cleanser. It is a 'liberator,' to free the world from Zero. Let the world be. Sans lingua franca, the world will be torn asunder. And then, it shall be free. People will suffer, of course - a phantom pain. The world will need a new common tongue. A language of nukes. My Metal Gears shall be the thread by which all countries are bound together, in equality. No words will be needed. Every man will be forced to recognise his neighbour. People will swallow their pain. They will link lost hands. And the world will become one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's single-player mode is definitely not suitable since you are constantly being chased by numerous enemies every 10 seconds. This game mechanic is incredibly frustrating and fails to deliver any sense of horror.I would appreciate it if the game could provide a better balance, allowing me to truly experience the horror atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: Trials 1, 3, and 4 are the same objective in the same area just more difficult each consecutive level. The game can be a lot of fun but that is just way too much repetition. More varied areas and a wider range of objectives would make it better but even then there's only 4 main trial areas at the moment. I get that it's early access and it's going to improve but the repetition is the main thing holding it back from being great for me. Unless you're a die hard Outlast fan or are just looking for a horror themed game to play with some friends, I would personally wait a bit and see what some updates bring. On the bright side, the game runs surprisingly well. It's not exremely demanding by any means and while there is some micro-stutter here and there, it could be a lot worse. To summarize, it's a pretty fun game that is reasonably optimized but is held back by repetitive trials and objectives.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this since the early access release, and familiar with the Outlast franchise since the beginning. The short of it is: yes. Now that 1.0 is finally here, I can recommend this adrenaline rush of a game.Movement and traversal is at it's best here in the franchise, with the ability to slide, jump, hide and smash/close doors in snappier, more refined way over the singleplayer games. The obtuse storytelling that veterans expect is still here, with players needing to look at visual storytelling and read documents to put the narrative together.But what most might be interested in -- how are the scares? With most co-op horror games, the fright factor will only take you so far. With Outlast Trials, I think, with all things considered, it does a great job of terrifying or (in the case of The Toy Factory) mortifying people rather well. Will it frighten you as much as Outlast 1? No. Will it frighten you /despite/ being a co-op game? Absolutely. And that's where others in the genre usually fail.Once you've seen all the trials, the scare factor might wane, but that is where another factor comes into play. When you're ready to tackle the harder modes, stress and adrenaline become the moving factors. There is a level of intensity to pushing through the harder modifiers that you need to experience with your friends. You'll sweat bullets.Audio is quite literally the best in the business when it comes to horror-based audio design. There is no comparison. The lightning is extremely good for this genre, speaking as someone who knows how to use Unreal Engine myself. If you have a good PC and can run with raytracing, Outlast Trials is a beautiful yet horrifying set upon the eyes.So what are you waiting for? Your "voluntary" therapy awaits. Let's get better together.

_childDocuments_.review: A strong showing for an Early access title. The gameplay is excellent. I particularly love the setting, and think that the concept, art design, and voice acting all mesh together perfectly to sell the very weird world of the Trials. Being early access, here are the things I hope are improved/changed1) Many meta upgrades should not be locked behind meta-currency, and should just be a part of the base game. Sliding is just a game mechanic, not an upgrade. Kicking enemies to free team mates is something you assume is built in, but surprise, go unlock it first. Holding E to use an item instead of picking it up is NOT something that should have to be unlocked 2) More content. At the moment I have gotten an A- or higher on all available missions, probably took about 10 hours of gameplay. I believe they are going for a GTFO kind of rundown system where the set of missions will change over time, but not 100% sure. At the current moment there are only 2 boss-type enemies (The Cop, and Gooseberry) across 3 maps. All were excellent, and can't wait to see more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Very awesome game. I find playing with friends makes the game more fun. You can search by random, or trial, or program. Depending on what you search for, is how long it may take to find people. The official outlast trials discord is also a great place to find players. Gameplay is great for the most part. I don't really like the new changes (nerfing rigs and bricks don't have multiple uses when hitting enemies anymore), but I'm sure I'll get used to it and make it work. Enemies are really cool and powerful, with a good balance of being annoying and dumb. I really love the specials and weekly challenges. It doesn't feel like a dead end game. There seems to always be new stuff being planned and in the works. The Geiser and Winter specials were really enjoyable. Cosmetics and room decoration are also a huge plus, along with arm wrestling and chess in the waiting room.What I am hoping for in the future are more rigs with different specials, possibly a "create your own" trial where you can choose the variators and how difficult (or easy) you want to make it. Another thing that would be cool, is possibly a 2v2 type of game, where two teams of two compete against each other in a trial to see who finishes their tasks first. The team who doesn't finish first gets gassed to death or something lol. Also, for the love of cosmetics, please bring us hats that have hair. I'm tired of being shave headed with a receding hairline when i want to wear a hat accessory. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Amazing game, great fun, i recommend you buy it, the most enjoyable horror coop game i've played in a long while. My one note is that the xp system could be slightly better as it promotes one playstyle - sneaking everywhere. Needs to implement a player kick from group system too :)  9/10 gameBefore I get to my very small complaint, I want to say the game is awesome, everything from the gameplay, sound design, the environments, moods just every single inch of this game is stunning. I will leave my original unedited complaint at the bottom.-Visually it's incredible and sometimes horrible to look at, graphically it's pretty flawless. The atmosphere is really heavy in a lot of places and the enemy design is so fitting for the world, everything from inside the trials and outside the environment really builds upon the world in an amazing way.-The game is in an amazing working state, I have had next to no issues with gameplay or the ai, only one minor incident with the Cop AI struggling with pathfinding around a door but it was funny you know? The gameplay loop it's self is engaging enough and i can see it being a formula that will allow for new maps and trials to come in the future which is really exciting.-I love how the customisation works, it's nice and simple and the way stuff unlocks is fun, you don't know what all the cosmetics are so just randomly getting them after trials is always enjoyable to see!-The sound and music in the game is super tense at points, with general atmospheric music as you explore the trials really adding a sense of dread and unease. On top of this the voicelines of the enemies are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious sometimes, they're really well done and they add some quirks to the characters and bring them to life more. Every interactable object has a really satisfying sound to accompany it.-The Hub (Sleep Room) is really simple, not overcomplicated or anything and it is honestly perfect, it's really well designed. From the being able to see everyone's rooms, the 2 shops for upgrades, the arm wrestling table to pass some time quickly waiting for people and the design of the whole area, i couldn't imagine it being any other way.Now here is my unedited original complaint with the xp system.Games really fun, it's a good laugh to play with mates, however the levelling system is annoying and favours only one play-style. I am doing 75% of the objectives and taking enemy aggro away from friends which means i'm setting off traps and getting hit, so i'm walking out of every trial with a D- rank and my friends are B and above. I wouldn't be bothered about the grades as i'm having fun if it wasn't directly levelling me slower, my friends with less hours have now surpassed me in level and it's a quite annoying being punished for playing a certain way, a way that i find enjoyable and i'm contributing most of the workload, while my friends are crouching in corners.Update - i think a kick system is needed for the game as I was playing with 2 other friends and we got a random to join so we were a 4. We noticed halfway through the trial that this 4th was hiding in the main area, letting us do all the work, we assume so he can get a good grade. So we stopped doing objectives and have been sat in this game for about an hour and a half. none of us doing anything, we can't get him and this has gone on too long that we can't leave. So I am currently leaving for food and I'll see if he's left by the time we are back. Would be very nice to kick this person, so they aren't getting free +A grades for being a ♥♥♥♥. <3Update - He left, we won!

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much to say about this literal masterpiece of a nightmare. Whether you've played the original single-player Outlast games before this or not is irrelevant. Outlast Trials stands above every horror game in the genre. The team at Red Barrels takes the coop horror experience everyone knows and brings it to the highest levels possible in terms of pure adrenaline-inducing horror, excellent animations & attention to the worlds detail, along with masterful audio that I swear will have you screaming wherever you play this.  So what do you do in this game? You are a patient (taken against your will) to essentially an MK-Ultra style mind control facility where the powers that be force you to undergo "Trials" that are meant to harden you and make you stronger in the face of pure horror & this game has so much of it. Each trial is a different location that has been turned into a grotesque extreme vision of whatever is being portrayed. Your job once inside is to do what Murkoff tells you & then get the hell out. Or die trying. Each character or enemy you encounter is intensely scary and satirical depending on who you get (I'm looking at you Coyle) with what I think is some of the best voice acting in the industry along with truly scary enemies physically as well.Nothing is scarier after running room to room and being sliced up with everything wanting to hurt you in some way and you finally find a moment of "safety" hiding in a barrel or bathroom stall and you hear Mother Gooseberry's singing muffled on the other side of the wall getting closer to you. Or hearing your friends screams over the radio as you hear them get brutally assaulted by "the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ man" as he chases them attacking the whole time. This game really is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. But in the best ways.If you want a truly horrific coop experience that looks so damn good you'll wonder why other games in the genre aren't even close, with sounds that are so realistic you'll be holding your breath to not miss what's coming around the corner, enemies that are so completely terrifying you'll literally be screaming running for your in-game life like it's real life, with levels that immerse you in every way so much so you'll think you can ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ smell it as the lighting, sound, darkness, and all of the wonderfully done set pieces and assets blend together into what I swear is an experience you have to see to understand. It is the scariest game I have ever played and in the genre it's the best there is. Are there some negatives to note? Yes. Quickly I'll say this game is the best to play with a friend or several (4 in total). Having your friends there, or even matchmaking while dealing with all this game throws at you is the most intense juggling act, and keeping everyone alive is so not easy. So if you're someone who solos games alone, although I believe you'll still have an amazing time it will not be easy and you'll come out of it like someone who was lost in the woods for 10 years trying to escape. Are there bugs? Some, but it's been less than 5 in the 60 hours I have played. Some were graphical and I think we had audio issues maybe once. I know some people might complain there's a lack of variety in the levels but dig this: there are I think 5 main levels currently (with the 6th coming in a month) but the replayability comes with the fact that they take those 5 maps and when they add new trials they'll reconfigure these maps and change them in totally different ways, sometimes unrecognizable with new enemies, different layouts, different objectives and for me the content has not ever lacked.Some stuff I didn't touch on that's still amazing about this game: The lobby where you choose your trial you get your own cell/room that can be customized with all sorts of awesome decorations/cosmetics from good looking to guts on the night stand (your choice) kinda like the Sims in Hell. All of the cosmetics are unlocked by playing the game. Each trial rewards you X amount of cash + rewards like clothing cosmetics which are great. In the same lobby you can also play mini-games like arm wrestling & speed chess (which happens to be like the best 3D chess game on the market for some reason?). I'm sure I missed plenty of good, and maybe even some bad but with this game coming out of early access soon it's already the most polished horror experience on the market next to something like RE: Biohazard but because this is a coop experience also based in reality I think this stands above that as well. It's so well done and I love everything Red Barrels has made here. Completely recommend this experience & I can't wait to play the Toy Factory level when the game goes out from early access which is soon. "The Goose is on the loose, the Goose is on the loose..."

name: Lost Ruins
detailed_description: A young girl wakes up in a dimly lit dungeon without any of her memories. Surrounded by horrible, bloodthirsty monsters, she is rescued by a mysterious magician, Beatrice. With Beatrice’s help, the girl goes on a perilous journey to find answers and unlock the secrets of the Lost Ruins. Engage in Combat Combat in Lost Ruins is both strategic and methodical. Slash away at enemies, burn them to a crisp, or even deflect their projectiles back at them. Arm yourself with a variety of swords, axes and other assorted medieval weaponry, and hack monsters to pieces. Master Spells For those with an affinity for magic, Lost Ruins allows you to cast a variety of spells through wands, tonics, and scrolls. Burn monsters, freeze bosses, and heal yourself when in danger. Choose what works for your playstyle and make a magic casting character that’s totally your own. Choose Your Accessories The world of Lost Ruins is a dangerous one and being armed to the teeth with awesome weaponry is sometimes not enough. That’s where accessories come in. Accessories are unique pieces of equipment with all manner of effects. One accessory might protect you against fire, while another might heal you when you’re poisoned. The right combination of accessories can create different strategic options for your adventure. Make Use of the Environment As you explore the depths of Lost Ruin’s dimly lit dungeons, you will find that while everything around you might bring about your death, you can also use the environment around you to your advantage. Elements within the world will react with other elements realistically. Flammable liquids will be set ablaze when in contact with lit lanterns. Ice magic will freeze bodies of water, making them dangerously cold. The more you understand the environment and how to use it to your advantage, the more dangerous you will become. Main Character A young school girl who wakes up in a dangerous underground maze with no memory of her past. Desperate to find answers to who she is and how she ended up in this place, she begins exploring the ruins. Beatrice A mysterious woman with incredible magical ability, Beatrice acts as the main character's guide through the lost ruins. She seems to be hiding something, however. Goblin Merchant This helpful little guy works for Beatrice, and appears throughout the game to assist the main character. Sora & Mingie These two girls aren't just zombies, they're also big fans of pop music idols, evidenced by the glow sticks they carry wherever they go.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a bit of a mold-breaker. It's a metroidvania, but it's not at all about fluid movement or interconnected backtracks or rpg-style progression. It's slow and weighty. Your hitpoints melt in just a few attacks. You have no i-frames on hit, and can get juggled by single attack strings from bosses. You swap your gear frequently, but few items are strict upgrades---just situationally relevant sidegrades.The tone is almost closer to survival horror, with a focus on resource management and proper equipment, except the game is so punishing that you sort of have to cheese it to win.Unlike other metroidvanias, which have added a souls style stamina bar as a way to manage attack pressure, Lost Ruins just makes its attack times long. You hit your attack, freeze in place, your animation slowly begins, and if you're lucky and your spacing was perfect and the enemy doesn't suddenly shuffle a pace to the left, then your attack lands.There's ways you can mitigate this, but even the fastest weapons feel slow. Spells take forever. Dodges have a few warmup frames during which you're not invulnerable, and a bunch of similar cooldown frames at the end. A lot of the time you have to dodge before an attack starts, not as it starts, which makes the dodge sort of useless as an evasion tool instead of a spacing one.Despite all of this---and despite the fact that I went in expecting Momodora and got this instead---I genuinely liked the game.It's got a lot that could put people off. Between the slow controls, the extremely dark story, and the weirdly voyeuristic "defeat a boss and gather their underwear" progression, I can't fault anyone for bouncing off it. But the difficulty was satisfying, and learning to cheese the game's mechanics felt fun.If you're willing to try a slower-paced survival platformer and don't mind a probably-too-much-anime aesthetic, give this a shot.Also, despite what some online stuff is saying, you can get a good ending without doing a hardcore no deaths run. There's a tiny bit more context that the hardcore no deaths run gives you, but it's like two frames of animation. Just follow the obvious instructions that the unlikeable character gives you and you'll be fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Having passed the point where I can refund this game, I can safely say this game is a gem.Yes, there's a lot of cute girls. Hell, one of the bosses is a giant slime girl in an area partially inhabited by normal sized slime girls. But push all that aside for a second and just listen to me.This game is a metroidvania that punishes you for trying to play it like most others. Your dodge ability is slow and clunky. You character is fragile and can die fairly quickly. Your weapons are either slow to swing or lacking in range. The game is stacked against you in every possible way; fighting foes face-to-face is INCREDIBLY dangerous. I've often said people overhype the difficulty of Dark Souls, but this game somehow manages to live up to the hype of a completely different series by being every bit as brutally punishing as FromSoft's work is hyped up to be.However, this game is not unbeatable. It is a thinking man's metroidvania. Don't think through problems; think around them. The game gives you ample resources; I've actually found myself using things like consumable wands, thrown items and spells very frequently to avoid direct confrontation, and whenever I was forced into a face-to-face fight, I used proper spacing to maximize distance between me and my opponent so that once I landed a hit, I could escape before they could retaliate. You're a scared, confused schoolgirl, not a trained warrior. Once you understand how the game is meant to be played and pick up on the way it encourages you to approach situations, it becomes a blast.Let me give an example. The second boss's arena has cages with goblins inside. These cages can and will be knocked down during your battle, but the goblins just stand there and cower. During phase 2, the boss will eat these goblins to heal itself; in my first couple of fights, I made the mistake of ignoring that and ran out of resources quickly and died. However, there is a finite number of these goblins. So I decided to just hit it once, back off, let it heal, then rinse and repeat; then, once it was out of healing resources, I used my consumable buffs and spells to steamroll the boss.This is the beauty of Lost Ruins. It deserves every ounce of the praise it has received and then some. I can absolutely see myself running the game on a higher difficulty once I beat it.And for those of you intimidated by the game, there is an Accessible difficulty; I'm not someone who believes hard games NEED easy modes per se, but if a developer wishes to implement one, it's always appreciated.Try the game! And I hope you enjoy it as much as I am.
