_childDocuments_.review: The monsters are cute girls.  The bosses are cute girls.  The ghosts are cute girls.  The deity haunting the castle is a big ol' cute girl.  You, yes  are a cute girl!  This here is one of the best  money can buy, with methodical roll 'n' slash 'n' cast combat in which  offensive has its windup.  People actually complain about that, believe it or not, then turn right around and act like a whirlytwirlfest like  is the second coming.  The combat in  is just great, if you ask me, a lot more rewarding, a lot less frustrating, a lot more  than in that other thing I just mentioned.  This is slower and more thoughtful than , another notable girlvania -- but maybe that's the very thing with the complainers!  They want this to be another  instead of its own thing (and if they'll just wait a long minute, there's another  coming down the pipe.  I'll be there, too.)  The jumping, running, and dodge-rolling execute immediately, but the sword-swinging and magic-slinging as I've said, do not -- and that's just fine!  I like it like , too!  It makes things interesting.  Because as you proceed, you'll constantly have to ask yourself:  which of these million-billion weapons am I going to use in this room, taking into consideration the speed and behavior of the (likely cute girl-centric) enemies present?  But within each encounter there's still a lot of leeway for creativity -- a  of it.  Yes, for a short game, it sure gives you a ton of ways to be a cute, ditzy manga girl killing cute manga girl-things (and the occasional green orc, and I think they're included because they imply a certain bestial lust despite not doing anything lustful to Heroine at all -- something to do with the overall manga/anime/ecchi meta).I didn't know the game played so well, or I would've gotten it sooner; I only bought it because I thought (and still think) it was just so pretty, weird, and cute.  Well-drawn.  Shiny.  Sparkly.  I'm a crow!  I saw clips of the carnivorous pooch-bellied maniac, Rosie, babbling and throwing a goblin hock at Heroine, and I saw Heroine's silly idle animation, and I said, "Hell, just buy it already."  A good decision on my part!  Much to my surprise, Boss Mode isn't a boss rush at all . . . but a whole new campaign (and story) about three of the game's bosses being reincarnated into one body and forced to fight their way through the Lost Ruins -- as Heroine did before them!  It's kind of like ; you switch between the girls to use their various abilities.  This playthrough is much quicker since you rely on a relatively limited weapon set and don't need to go around gathering new tools.  I find it as fun as the main game!  Another point in 's favor!(Heh!  The story is a load of  nonsense (yet still more coherent than !), but the dialog is often clever and every artistic element is so consistent that the game doesn't really  a tight story -- the art and atmospheric touches twine together and crisscross thickly enough to make a strong springy seat for the "it's a dream-story in a dream-world with its own dream-logic" excuse to sit comfortably.)

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals in this game should be shown to aspiring artists taking game design classes.The combat should be shown to aspiring game designers on how not to do combat.This game has so much potential but the clunkyness of the combat is abysmal. Metroidvanias are my all time favorite game genre and this game is devoid of the understanding behind how Metroidvanias should play. - There's no reason for your weapons to swing as slow as they do so much so that even "fast" attacking weapons with their respective equipment enhancing item get out-paced by enemies spamming attacks at mach10 speed or backpeddling faster than your weapon can swing- There is no reason as to why you lose momentum when attacking in mid-air - A lot of the "equipment" should've been relinquished to passive items (i.e the air dodge boots) some of the descriptions on items are unclear (i.e the winged boots not mentioning that they enable air dodge or the Magic Rune saying that it nullifies spell damage but the necromancer boss's spells still hurt you?)- There are so many vendors and items to buy but almost nothing drops gold???- Why would you use two different save methods to act as your checkpoints??? The computers let you hard save and the many green statues act as auto-save checkpoints but cannot be triggered a second time? So if you auto-save before a boss get ready to have to re-configure all your gear if you die every single time.- Speaking of green statues why don't they refill your HP/MP? I get the whole "survival" aspect but when gold is non-existent having to buy any kind of consumables is a chore and a half.- The dodge roll is atleast 50 recovery frames too long, some enemies just straight up attack faster than you can after dodging their initial attack so rolling seems kind of pointless other than abusing I-frames.- Because there is no XP/leveling system actually fighting and killings mobs is made kind of pointless other than to watch the nice sprites do cool things.Hopefully the devs can update the game to fix these glaring issues but until then its a fat NO from me which is a real shame because I was looking forward to this game based on the art alone but that's all it has going for it at the moment. I'd be more than happy to help in any way I can to address some of these issues with the devs but if you're in the market for an incredibly solid Metroidvania experience check out Unworthy or Blasphemous, those two games are way more polished and Unworthy was a one man job.Edit: To clarify because a lot of the comments have pointed to this particular point as a way to discredit the review, I'm not saying that the game absolutely NEEDS a leveling system. What I'm pointing out is that there is no reward for killing enemies apart from some drops. Towards the end of the game, I found that it was a lot more worthwhile to spam the invisibility spell with mana regen equipment to just bypass enemies. Because of how clunky the combat is, especially if you're playing on the harder difficulties you waste more resources fighting than just bypassing which isn't particularly good game design. I want to have a reason to kill enemies beyond getting another arrow bundle for a bow I won't ever use.Clearly some people have very strong opinions about this review and are very vocal in the comments, we can agree to disagree on the state of this game but for the 20 ish dollar price tag I feel there are currently better options on the market and the game being tagged with the "Metroidvania" tag might be misleading to some and I hope this review can give them a clear picture about MY experience with the game compared to the many other Metroidvania games I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a really good time with Lost Ruins. Looking at the store page the most striking thing is the artwork: especially the characters and bosses but when actually playing the game you'll see that the backdrops are also really pretty too, and the weather, particle, and magic effects are also beautifully executed. As impressive as the aesthetics are I think there's a risk that they might misdirect potential buyers into thinking this is just another basic lewd anime game, leading them to either dismiss it or to dive into the community hub looking for information about a R18 patch. This game isn't that kind of thing at all - sure, the boobs jiggle a bit here and there and some of the characters show a lot of skin but there's no explicit content at all and it's all the better for it. Instead it's a short but perfectly formed metroidvania that tells an interesting story complimented by a surprisingly deep system of weapons, spells, and artefacts that give a really outstanding variety of build possibilities. It's also surprisingly humorous in places, with quirky characters and situations and references to other games and memes - shout out to Lusty the lizard maid who just wants to get her sausage back. You'll spend plenty of time working out how to fill your limited accessory slots to create interesting synergies and overcome tough opponents - you can be a frost mage that lays runic traps to freeze enemies, or a deadly gladiator that heals by attacking, or a sneaky invisible assassin, or a lunatic in a hockey mask exploiting bleed mechanics, or one of many, many others. It's even possible to build a class around spending most of your time on fire. You can change these builds on the fly to adapt to the various interesting situations you find yourself in - you'll want to be careful about throwing lightning around if you're knee deep in water, for example. This flexibility is important, as each fight presents different problems to solve and your enemies are varied and interesting. The environment doesn't just exist as a hazard either, but as a resource to be exploited - for instance, clever use of a fire bow might make short work of that horde of goblins hanging around underneath those flasks of oil. In places the mechanics reminded of games like Terraria or Noita - environmental destruction is limited to props in the foreground but I was still impressed by the possible interactions between elements. I've seen people criticise the pace of the combat and especially the slow swing speed of the weapons, but personally I didn't find any issues with this. Most enemies are strong enough to kill you if you mindlessly take them head-on, but there's nothing that's impossible to overcome if you ruthlessly exploit all the available resources, items, and mechanics and have a plan before you initiate the fight - you just have to think strategically and not treat it as a fighting game. The complexity available to you but not to your the enemies is your best weapon. This is especially true for the multi-stage boss fights that increase in lethality as you near victory and will really require your pattern recognition and build choice to be spot on. It's a game in which the execution of the little things adds up. A perfect example of this is the map, which is absolutely excellent: it populates itself, automatically marks when you encounter a locked door or a chest, shows all the possible entrances and exits in each room, and highlights portals, vendors, and NPCs clearly. So many games do a poor job of such a simple thing but Lost Ruins handles it perfectly. There's also excellent replay value - in addition to the 3 initial difficulty settings, there are 3 extra modes unlocked at the end of the game. In the first you are limited to a skirmishing assassin build and in another you are a magically-powerful but fragile witch, but the highlight of these is an expansion of the story where you play as 3 vanquished bosses from the main game who are surprised to find themselves alive but trapped in one body after the story ends. This mode completely changes the way you navigate the world and the perspective you play from and it's a really nice addition if you finish the game and want more. Overall it's a fantastic package and easy for me to recommend to fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but I can't help but feel it was misrepresented on the store page.The trailer does not do a good job of presenting how the combat actually is.   At first, I thought it was just me, but the "fastest" are still incredibility slow.  I got the kitchen knife weapon and it was going the speed I would expect of the long sword.  All weapons need to be sped up by a level.  For example, give the speed of fastest to fast.I know it's the "design" and that the game wants the player to manage their resources.  However,  having to open the inventory every 10 seconds is rough.  It feels really bad.  Especially when it's what you'll be doing most of the time.Also, no one should call this game a "hack and slash."  After all, the design of the game punishes that approach.  This is NOT a hack and slash.  You will die if you treat it like one.  The store page may say "Slash away at enemies," but this is not what you will be doing.  Using "side-scrolling survival action game" is also a bit ridiculous since that describes every 2D game with a health bar.   My opinion would be improved if the store page didn't use phrases like those.The resource management of the game's combat needs to be front and center.  The trailer should also show a minute of unbroken combat gameplay.  Meaning no cuts, not flashy video transitions.  Also with HUD displaying so the viewer can see the resource management taking place.That or a demo should be available.  Honestly if there was a demo, I think it would nullify any of my complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty interesting 2D side-scroller. I've only played through once and on normal difficulty for reference.The story is basically what the description if the game says. Not much else except a few side stories. There are 3 multiple endings you can get but I've only gotten 1 so far, but it was decent. Nothing crazy or really engaging but okay enough to keep me playing.The gameplay is relatively easy and simple. Enemies follow basic and repetitive attack patterns. Most bosses took me 2-4 tries. The final boss was really disappointing, super easy and only a few attacks. There's a large variety of different weapons and magic to fight with. I will say that I didn't delve too much into the magic aspect of combat as I mainly used a weapon and shield. The shield is incredibly OP in this game. It blocks like 80-90% of attacks in the game and you can just infinitely block.The art is fantastic and the soundtrack was good. The art is probably a big reason this game gained some traction. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 6/10. A reasonably challenging and fun Metroidvania that has good replay value thanks to additional difficulties and game modes. It's short and sweet. Definitely worth a try.I'll start with the critiques first:- Air combat sucks. You will drop straight down if you try to attack midair, making it largely unusable. - Magic dominates. Magic quickly scales above the other fight methods and becomes absolutely broken. .- No I-Frames. You will take hits, and immediately get juggled with additional hits. Worse on higher difficulty.Now to some positives:- The game has charming visuals and a good soundtrack.- So much cute stuff to go around, I almost feel guilty having to kill them.- Dodging and blocking are very reliable, and most of the time you can tell which will work and where.- The different game modes are exciting and encourages repeat playthroughs. .- Set items that allows you to experiment with different builds.- The game is challenging, but more often than not fair to the player.- Multiple endings. While not major, still a nice touch and satisfying.Perhaps what the game lacks is the ability to chat with NPCs who inhabit the world. Shopkeepers will not say anything to you once their scripted dialogue is over and only offer services. It felt like a missed opportunity to flesh them out along with the world.The gallery you unlock is on the smaller side and you quickly unlock it all. I would have liked to see more artwork of the different designs for the enemies and locations. As it is now, it's underwhelming. Made worse by the fact that a few artworks are just rearrangements of each other, which feels pretty lazy.Some plot beats seem to go unfinished, which makes me wonder if the game was rushed of the writers just didn't care.  It just feels like a dead end and is disappointing.Similarly, the game lies to you in one area that I don't know if it's a glitch, oversight, or intended design.  So that's weird.Boss Mode feels quite a bit shorter than the main modes.  It's still fun and an absolute cherry on top to the existing story.However, none of this kills the enjoyment for me. I've already binged the game to satisfaction and I see myself picking this up again to try and beat the other game modes I've not tried yet. I recommend this to anyone who likes the Metroidvania genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot going for it, particularly the visuals.  The lighting effects and animations are particularly impressive.  But the gameplay has some very significant issues that I have a hard time getting past.  The combat is slow, and ponderous, and at first this seemed like a good design choice and I was enjoying the different pace.  But as I played more, and got through a few bosses, I started seeing that the combat was actually problematic.  It feels like you're fighting in quicksand, with every action taking far loo many frames to complete.  When you combine that with the fact that every hit staggers you, and that there are actually ZERO iframes in the game, you find yourself facing frustrating death after frustrating death at the hands of a single hit that started a chain reaction of further hits that you have no ability to avoid.  It feels like a juggle-heavy fighting game, where getting hit with a single punch can lead into a 20 second long air juggle that ultimately takes 90% of your health before you get to control your character again.There is magic in the game, and the spells are very powerful, but you don't recover health or mana when you hit a save point or safe room (like SotN or most other Metroidvanias), so you don't get to cast but 2 or 3 spells and then you have to wait until you find another mana potion or something to enable another spell or two.  It's too bad, because incorporating spells would make the combat less of a trudge.  The same thing goes for items.  There are throwing items like knives and bottles, but they are extremely finite.  It's not based on an energy system or anything replenishable like most Metroidvanias, they are literally - you find 3 knives.  You can throw three times and then they are gone forever.  You also only get two items you can equip at a time, which includes your melee weapon and shield if you want one.  So, you can choose to have a sword and shield equipped, but that is it.  No throwing knives, bottles, arrows, etc.  If you want to use one of those limited number items, you have to forego a shield, which is insanity since everything in the game can easily kill you.  All in all, there are some good things in here but ultimately the combat killed it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it! Just finished the initial play through and for me it delivered exactly what I was looking for.I will admit, at first I thought the combat system was clunky and unresponsive but when I actually learned how to play I realized that it's actually brilliantly designed. It encourages the player to be very thoughtful about which weapons they use and when to use them. This helps avoid a button bashing frenzy and actually makes the combat experience much more thoughtful and sophisticated.Some people might be disappointed at the games length, but to be honest, I'm a busy guy with a lot of games I've never finished. I much prefer a shorter high quality experience instead of one that is padded out with filler content.I bought it on sale but at it's regular price its absolutely worth every penny. Well done devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this off by stating one key detail about this game: It is not, by any means, a metroidvania nor souls-like - although the tags and some online reviews may suggest it is. It's best described as a 2D survival sidescroller with RPG elements. I originally wrote a negative review, but the sole reason for that was because I judged it from a metroidvania point of view.I really love the artwork, OST, sound-design, dialogue and characters (Sigh... yes, booba included). The gameplay mechanics, however, are quite clunky to say the least. Stationary attacks, no combos, lackluster movement and way too much menuing (ESPECIALLY if you're using magic). The shield literally breaks some of the bosses and so do the invisibility options. Playing without the shield, however, is near impossible when you're up against multiple enemies because the mechanics are too slow to allow you to have any sort of control.The boss fights are nothing spectacular although still fun (except for Rosie, I hate Rosie and the fact that her entire phase 1 is irrelevant due to shields while phase 2 is bugged in the sense that her jump attack deals contact damage while she's still on the ground/preparing to jump). Generally speaking, the game is somewhat challenging on veteran difficulty - IF you're reckless, that is. The devs reward a methodical approach and if you use everything you have at your disposal, then you shouldn't have too hard of a time. Some of the items have really cool synergies, too.Now, let's get to the main question at hand: Would I recommend "Lost Ruins"?It depends. If you're the type of player who values fluid gameplay and a good combat system... No. If you can look past that, then I'd give it a shot. 16€ is somewhat high for such a short playtime, but it makes sense when you see the pixel art and artworks.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Full stop -- this game is not a Metroidvania.It is, as the devs put it, "2D side-scrolling survival action." You will hate this game if you expect classic Metroidvania with upgrading abilities and progression.This game is pure exploration and depth of weapons/magic(that are also almost always damage spells).This game is also a little clunky (by design), your attacks, dodges, and spell casts will be heavily punished if you don't act with intent (think old school Castlevania). You will probably die a lot, also by design.It's a punishing game, but not terribly difficult. You just have to understand what you're playing.+100 if you enjoy monster girls

It's fun!+ Multiple game mode that offers wide variety replayability and high hour play+ Great art+ WaifuBad:- Control can be janky for first-timer- No music- Nobody drops money so it can be a little grindy if you want to buy something

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Korean metroidvania with a monster girl theme and some survival/ryona undertones.The game has beautiful visuals, with smooth and detailed pixel art animations, as well as slick and sexy character portraits. It's worth getting just for the art alone, but the gameplay is also very enjoyable, provided you don't mind a challenge.For whatever reason, the trope of a cute high school girl being put in some extreme life-and-death situation is very popular in Korea, and this game is no exception. The combat is difficult, the protagonist is slow and clumsy, even the fastest weapons take a bit to wind up, and you have to commit to animations. Moreover, there are numerous status effects, you can be poisoned, electrified, frostbitten, lacerated, set on fire etc etc. Suffice to say, it's very easy to die in just a few seconds. An enemy spits some poisonous liquid on the ground, your overhead swing catches a light fixture, and boom, the room is on fire and you're rapidly losing HP unless you can stop the burning status. It sounds awful, but it's actually very fun and to be honest quite refreshing compared to all those cookie cutter metroidvanias where you just zip around the map spamming attack mindlessly.Having said that, while the game is punishing, it's not meant to be frustrating, e.g. the save points are quite common, but they do not restore your HP/MP. Instead you have to rely on consumables, which the game has tons of. Some of them restore HP/MP, others deal with status effects or provide temporary buffs. The environment is very interactive and as a result the combat can be quite creative. For example, the first boss is very difficult to take head on. But the boss arena is filled with shallow water, and you can just equip a rubber swimsuit and spam shock spells for an easy win.The progression is more similar to , as in you don't unlock any new abilities. The initial moveset is exactly what you get, there won't be a double jump upgrade later on. There are no level ups either, you'll be just as fragile by the end of the game. The diversity instead comes from the massive selection of weapons, spells and equipment. You can use knives, axes, swords, bows, hammers, various throwables etc. You can cast an invisibility spell, sneak up on an enemy and execute a sneak attack for an easy one shot with gore chunks flying everywhere.As for mitigating damage, there's the usual dodge roll as well as shields. Shields block virtually all damage and can stagger smaller opponents, whereas the roll is useful for getting behind enemies and dodging bullet hell patterns during boss fights. Oh, and the game doesn't have any contact damage which is really cool.Story wise, there's about a dozen NPC questlines, providing both comedy and fanservice. Notably, the Lusty Argonian Maid from  makes a guest appearance. The localization is quite decent for a Korean game, the dialog flows naturally, there aren't any typos or mistranslations.My only nitpick would be the excessive inventory management. Sadly, there's no way to save gear presets (like in ), so e.g. switching from a melee build to a bow build would require re-equipping all your gear to respec into ranged damage.A single playthrough will take about 8 hours, but there are multiple endings, as well as bonus modes. One of the bonus modes lets you play as a trio of characters, just like in .
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I didn't expected this to be an anime pixel art souls-like Metroidvenia game but here we are.As the art itself may have you confused about what this game actually is. The game literally explain itself right at the start that it's a survivor games that you have to use items you can find to help with your journey (and it's true.)The combat is pretty much what you can expected from souls game. It's all about find your comfortable range, spacing, dodging, flanking, and type of weapon that is right for you. It slow but weighty. It's clunky but satisfying. Every enemies are meaningful in the term of they can kill you in the matter of seconds if you don't have strategy. You have to learn not only offensive but also defensive and using environment to your advantage real fast. And expected to die a lot to because you will learn something new from it every time it happens (again, just like souls.)Arts are vibrant and beautiful. Animation is smooth and compliment the combat nicely. It also has a unique type of anime story telling which might not be everybody's cup of tea. But It's a really solid package for it's price nonetheless.A bit of a surprise? Of course, but a welcome one.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, this is rough.The game has really pretty pixel art, visually Lost Ruins is great, but on the gameplay side it's just not fun.Your attacks are slow and even the largest weapons barely have enough reach to hit an enemy before they are able to get our their *much* faster attacks.Also almost every enemy in this game will apply some sort of debuff onto you, like bleed or poison damage, which can last up to 30 seconds for certain enemies, dealing 1 damage per second, when that's more than your total HP.But hey, there's a ton of consumables that let you heal a tiny bit and remove such status effects.That however means you constantly have to go in and out of your inventory, looking for the right consumable to get rid of effects every time you get hit by an enemy.And again, enemies get much quicker attack animations than you, so the chance of getting hit isn't exactly low.And what do you get for defeating enemies?Well since there's no XP system or anything like that, if you're lucky they may drop another consumable...Sometimes, but only rarely will enemies drop some coins you can use to buy equipment at vendors.But prices are super high and the amount of gold dropped by enemies is tiny.Like a piece of equipment may cost you like 150G, but every 5 or so enemies you may get 5 gold to drop.To keep it short, gameplay isn't fun at all.Sadly, the story and characters are just as bad.It's already weird enough to see all these girls running around in japanese schoolgirl outfits in a dark fantasy setting, but the story revolving around summoning girls from another world for some sacrifice is just extremely threadbare.The main character, merely named "Heroine" is as milquetoast as they get.She never has a single interesting thing to say in dialogue nor does she react to things like characters getting straight up killed in front of her.There's a small handful of other characters here, mainly they're the bosses, but their writing is just as terrible.It's such a shame, since the they really seemed to have put a lot of work in the pixel art for Lost Ruins, but everything beside the visuals, this is terrible.Wouldn't recommend this at all sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I would've liked this game more if it doesn't turn into "opening inventory simulator". This game offers you the versatility to use anything towards your enemies, whether they're swords, magic attacks, or environment interactions like setting up oil on fire or freezing enemies inside water. The problem with this is, there is no presets for you to make to quickly switch from one to another; you have to open your inventory to switch to the weapon or magic you want to use in that situation, and then switch back to whatever you're using before because it's a playstyle you're comfortable with. Perhaps you see water on the floor and you don't want to be electrocuted or be frozen, so you open your inventory to equip the swimsuit. Or perhaps you encounter enemies that does bleed damage, so you open inventory to consume bleed removal foods or wear armor that negates bleed debuff. Or perhaps you're just low on HP, you open your inventory to consume foods.All of this makes the pacing very slow, on top of the combat being slow already in the first place. I don't mind if I have to commit to the slow sword swinging animations, but what I don't like is having to constantly pause the game to switch stuff around. Sure, I can just stick to one type of build all the time, but in a game where the game can be very punishing because of the character's low HP, no i-frames upon getting hit, and HP and MP are not replenished unless you consume foods, it's better to try and take advantage of the situation you're in.After all, this game has a popup at the beginning of the run that says the game wants the player to think to solve problems they encounter. I want to do that, but the constant pausing to switch stuff around due to lack of preset options is ruining the experience. The unfortunate part about this game is, there is a bonus mode that fixes this problem, but you have to beat the game first.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I wanted to wait a bit before I made this review because while I was going through my first run of the game I was checking the reviews and I wanted to see if I would have a different opinion after beating the game or going through another run. I'll say that even after beating the game for the second time and now currently on witch mode, I still believe this game is just as great as during my first run. To preface this, I played the game on veteran difficulty for my first run and the second run I played was boss rush mode.I'm going to touch on the art style just a bit, as I think it's already been said enough but it's really good and fits the whole anime style they were going for. So there's not to much to say on the end of art for the game but I will give praise for the sprites and how you're able to get a good feel for the characters. Now let's move onto the gameplay, which has had very polarizing out look on it. I gotta say, I haven't had as much fun with a lot of games I've been recently playing in comparison to this game which I've been having a blast on. As I mentioned earlier, I played this game on veteran mode, so it was especially challenging and it caused me to die quite a lot. Though it was really only at the beginning where I felt like some of the deaths was the games part. In the beginning of the game there are a few enemies that have attacks you just can't punish without taking damage if you didn't get the right equipment but it's pretty easy to avoid those enemies. It won't be long until you are able to come back and kill them anyway because those enemies become quite easy to beat once you get either the spells, weapons, and/or artifact to deal with them. That's where the fun comes in, I was able to play the game how I wanted. There are a bunch of kits in the game where you can cheese out the enemies but there's a lot of customization you can go through to fit your playstyle. When I came back to face those difficult enemies, I wasn't trapped using a certain kit because I had other options. Not every customization is going to be good for an area but you will never be limited to just one kit. This is reinforced with the spells in the game around the mid game you're able to get artifacts and a weapon that grants you mana, so you won't have to use mp potions as often. This means you can just go wild with certain spells and have a blast using them. You feel like one of bosses made the game into a bullet hell just use a spell and don't have to worry about the projectiles anymore or maybe you feel like the enemies ranged attacks are going to fast there's a spell for that too.  The only real issue I had with the gameplay and this is more of a personal one is the hitbox for specific weapons like the hatchet and the Cursed Scythe feel very small and inconsistent at times. This was really annoying to deal with as I would lose all my stacks and begin to take bleeding damage when I thought they were in the hitbox for the Cursed Scythe. The combat in the game is the reason why I wanted to make this review in the first place. It was really fun doing what I wanted to do, even if it wasn't the most optimal I could still mess around with it. Late game I had a blast using invis with full stacks on cursed scythe and just one shot most enemies. This ties in with what I believe with games like this, if I can do what I want to do and still feel pleasure in doing so then it's a great game. I recommend this game 100% and if I had to give a rating for this game I would definitely give it 4.99/5 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Plays like a 2d Dark Souls but more focused on survival. You don't get an Estus Flask you have to use the healing items you find or buy some from merchants. Combat is somewhat slow and tactical. Referencing Dark Souls again, you will think about your spacing between yourself and the enemy, when to roll and attack etc.There are lots of status effects to cleanse with items, as well as apply to your enemies. Magic is very fun albeit a little bit overpowered towards mid to late game. There's so many items and weapons to augment your character you can absolutely break the game if you want to. On that note, there are difficulties to challenge you even if you go for a cheesy overpowered build. The hardcore mode is especially fun. You have a limited number of deaths and after that your save is wiped.I might be making the game sound too difficult. There are plenty of difficulty settings. If you are terrible at this kind of game you can bottom out the difficulty and the game will become much easier to handle. If you want a challenge, the options for it are there.The story is barebones and just exists to service the gameplay. It's a very gameplay focused game, and the gameplay is what makes me recommend the game. You won't find anything amazing in the plot. The characters are very nice looking, if you like anime style visuals you'll be happy with this.Overall if you like Dark Souls 2 and don't care much about the story then this is a very fun and entertaining game. There is a lot of build variety and the game has a lot of difficulty options to make multiple playthroughs entertaining. Some of the difficulty settings are actually new game modes, for example there is a mode where you can only use magic and it changes what items you come across and what items you start with. Another limits you to daggers and projectiles. You can easily get 2-3 playthroughs out of the game or more.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Took about 8 hrs on veteran to get through the story once. Don't think I'll be going back for achievements.Combat doesn't feel as clunky to me as others have indicated, it is for sure not smooth and sexy but it is consistent and dependable.Most enemies also don't have contact damage, which I think is really cool. I've always enjoyed that in games.I mostly avoided magic because MP restoration items don't come for a while if you do quests so not many comments on magic. Shields will block like 70%+ of the attacks in the game, including magic, so if you're willing to turtle your way through you'll go a bit slower but may have a less stressful time overall.I'd probably say this was worth $10 to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I like anime tiddies lol.Joking aside, this is an incredibly fun game, with several engaging boss battles and is very difficult. The combat itself requires a good amount of strategy based on the environment and also reoeatedky dying to learn attack patterns.HP and MP doesn't regenerate naturally, making them yet another resource to be carefully managed which is a unique aspect of the game. Whilst people find it annoying and time consuming to keep entering the inventory mid combat to use an item or swap to a different load out, i believe it just leads to a different kind of gameplay that some my enjoy while others don't, but isn't necessarily a bad thing, in fact i quite like it.Finally, the art is absolutely phenomenal (especially the animations), to put it simply, the game is worth it even for just the art. The fact that it's a game makes it even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: It amuses me how many people are complaining that a schoolgirl can't swing a broadsword faster than a battle-hardened orc.That aside, here are some things you need to know:-- This ain't your daddy's Metroidvania. It's tough as nails and will torture you if you're expecting a mash-happy slash-fest.-- Combat is clunky and messy, and it's by design. It's supposed to be punishing and brutal, and it's entirely fine if you avoid it. -- Even if you avoid combat, you're still gonna die a lot. Poison, bleeding, freezing, and being set on fire will kill you faster and more often than an axe to the noggin will.-- Recovery items are sparse. If you do find any, this game is a hoarder's worst nightmare, as most fights you get into in the early game will force you to use something. Don't think you can rely on checkpoints to get your HP/MP back either! -- Money is hard to get at first (I often got it by selling items). There are lots of items, spells, and weapons to buy but you won't be able to afford many of them at first. Recovery items are a luxury. If you want them, you must sacrifice things to be able to buy them. -- The game really makes you think about what items you're equipping. You won't have an all-purpose build. You need to think about what enemies you're going up against and plan accordingly.-- Graphically, this is one of the most gorgeous games you'll ever play. Truly enchanting pixel art.-- If I had a complaint, it'd be that I'd like to be able to refresh checkpoints with updated equipment. Checkpoints only become usable again after every third one you activate, and if I die at a boss with the wrong equipment loadout I have to keep remembering to switch to something else each time I die.edit: I was asked about time to completion. There's a good bit of content in this game. It'll take you probably 8-10 hours on your first playthrough, and then you unlock three (yes, three) new gameplay modes, each with a different way to play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of Midnoria, but this game is better.I went in with 0 expectations and was impressed. The weapons, items, and spells are the highlight. They can be combined in many ways to play however you want and set your own difficulty (it is easy to make a game-breaking combo).The bosses are better than average, but I'd still like more variety and organic difficulty. The story is what you expect: predictable and unmemorable.---One of the top reviews complains about the combat. This game doesn't have perfect combat, but they didn't experiment enough. If the game is hard, just try something different. It is a game, have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The combat felt slow and sluggish in the best way possible. It forces you to think each encounter rather than just steamrolling through the game.Magic is a bit op, but not enough to be issue. Melee is pretty weak, but I beat the game using mainly a sword and I am bad in video games, so it is possible.Also, get shield of life as soon as possible, it's the most OP thing in this game ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: There's not a Metroidvania in recent memory that I've enjoyed as much as Lost Ruins. Blasphemous is a little tight for me personally, and Dead cells relied too much on random chance and grinding to really experiment with "the" set I would decide I want to use.Lost Ruins achieves what both of those systems went a little overboard to really do. The combat is tight crisp, but not in a way that punishes you for not reacting in 0.2 seconds, and the equipment system allows you to experiment with what you want to do without the worry of losing it all. A lot of people say that the game encourages you to cheese it, and I cannot stress this enough. When I found the combination of spells types and items I beat the final boss with just over a little more than halfway into the game, I could've sworn I'd found an exploit. And I'm confident that in any other game, it would've been. In Lost Ruins, however, I found that I'd only begun what that particular build was, eventually finding multiple upgrades to it that completed the kit and turned me into a professional buzzsaw impersonator by the end of the game. The best part about it? It was sub-optimal for most situations. There's no all-round "good" build, or perfect meta. Some are better than others, yes, but some flourish in situations that others flounder in.Lost ruins is a Metroidvania with no direct upgrades or "You can now magically double jump" powerups, only sidegrades. You can run straight to the first boss without much hassle, but it'll probably kick your trash if you don't have either the item that lets you move freely in it's arena or the item that  on the type of floor the boss arena is covered in. Nothing makes the game itself free, but plenty of things can make specific situations free, or pretty close if you puzzle out how what you're dealing with interacts with what you're using. Using a life drain spell as a crutch? Better find something else if you're dealing with skeletons that don't have any life to drain. The main criticism I see of this game is that "you swing slow". That's done intentionally. Most of the enemies in the game have  simple (read: the same, single attack) patterns, allowing you to hit them if you plan around it, and learn when to swing. Hell, I did a lot of the game with the 2-handed greatsword who's absurd damage output was only matched by it's range and time it took to swing. Lost Ruins isn't so much a twitchy fast-paced combat like Dead Cells or Blasphemous, and trying to talk ♥♥♥♥ to enemies like it is will hit you with a rather steep difficulty curve. Not an impossible one, but one that's more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ than genuine learning, especially early on.Sadly, it is fairly short. I've finished the main game on the recommended difficulty and the "boss mode" campaign in only 9 hours, but I do see myself coming back to this game still for the harder difficulties and to poke around in new playstyles to see what else I can make busted. Speaking of, here's my personal recipe: Overall, Lost Ruins is a nice case study in the art of sidegrades. There's always something else for you to try, with the only thing stopping you from blasting to the end of it all being your build-solving skills and how well you can put them into practice.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Be prepared to struggle-bus through segments of the game. There are some sections that can be particularly punishing, and there's no leveling system in this game, so you can't just power through on stats in a fight that's close, but you keep failing.The game also seems to be set up to discourage grinding, but it also seems to be necessary to progress at times. Honestly, the fact that this game lacks an estus flask, or bonfires to easily refill HP and MP kind of highlight why those design choices keep showing up in so many games. It's way too easy to use some of your healing items on a bad attempt to clear a zone or a boss, then not have any for subsequent attempts.It's still pretty good though.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I only have good things to say about this game:+ Incredible art and visuals, especially for those of us that really enjoy pixel/8-bit style games+ Fun dungeon and bossfight mechanics+ Normal difficulty was challenging in a great way, perfect balanced at least for the difficulty I desired (imho)+ Story wasn't by any means complex, but it was fun and kept my attention!+ The choices of weapons and spells was pretty extensive, lots of interesting options to choose from to defeat your foes+ Usage of special items to gain more power and the upper hand in fights (&/or looks, in the case of the maid outfit/etc)Definitely worth every minute played, easy 5/5!
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Survival Tips for those looking to pick up this game - Speed is always better than power, because stun locks make everything one-sided. This also applies to you.  - The healing amulet is your friend - The shield is your good friend - The roll is your best friend.- Healing amulet + Belt is the game's internal easy mode as it means you can't die unless you're really bad at dodging.  - Combat for stronger enemies is the really boring process of roll-attack-repeat. This is probably what's causing people's complaints for this game. It's slow. Especially when it comes to area hazards where you have to burn them away, and then wait for the fire to die down. There are trinkets to counter this, but, until you get them, its a lot of waiting. - I managed to beat the game fairly quickly once I switched my build to shield + dagger. The shield is great and even works on bosses in ways that make them stupid easy. The dagger's speed lets you get in hits without getting countered, but the range means you'll have to space and time your rolls so you're close enough for a hit. - If you want to use magic, you can...but only if you like constantly going into menus to restore your MP or swap to another consumable wand. Magic Sucks. Get the Knife.Overall, the game is okay, but I wouldn't call it great or even very good. Its short, its simple, its awkward, and its the kind of game where you're constantly looking for the quick kill on otherwise mundane enemies and bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Re-doing my review, now that I have properly finished a run of the main game, at around 90% completion.I respect Lost Ruins on the basis that I understand it. The designers behind this, you and I are not so different. We like the same thing- cute, sometimes a little ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, anime monster girls. That is what this game is- a tour of and/or an excuse to meet a healthy cast of anime monster girls. And for that, I can say that I enjoyed my time with Lost Ruins. I will likely take some amount of effort to keep an eye on the artists behind this to see what else they do, simply because I liked the monster girls so much.But, unfortunately, that's where my enjoyment basically comes to an end. The actual video game that's built around this monster girl tour... wasn't that great, really. Normally I enjoy these kinds of anime 2D metroidvanias. However, I think the blend of "survival" elements, and what I would consider the removal of real "metroidvania" elements really just did not vibe with me.Without going into too many details, I would say that all of the elements in this game felt watered down in some way. The combat? Simple, slow, and honestly pretty clunky. Magic? Uninteresting, save for maybe the magic only run that has additional modifiers to make magic actually useful before the 3rd boss. Equipment? Mostly useless, didn't even get the maid outfit until the last 30 minutes of the game. Exploration? Painfully simple. Enemies respawn, and you don't ever get any additions to your moveset. What you have when you spawn in is what you get, and while that fits in with the Survival elements, it made me wholly uninterested in exploring.The bosses, while designed very well of course, ultimately were a drag. Either painfully frustrating or pathetically easy. I beat the final boss on my 3rd try using the same strats as every other boss- hit her with a big weapon before she kills you. I can't say much since there aren't any real standout elements that I think are bad, persay, but it equally did not have any standout elements that were good.The story is also pretty much nonexistent. It came off to me that the text here was translated, because it all felt a bit flat. But, I don't hold that against the game as I'm not one to harp on stories anyway. As I said previously this was a tour of cute monster girls, and the plot just facilitated our continued progress along that tour.The only thing I'll say that genuinely upset me was locking the "true" ending behind the highest difficulty, without any indication that that's the case. I don't mind jumping through a few hoops to get the best ending (The "Don't open any chests until the last zone" quest is stupid, but I digress), but I have ZERO intentions of playing through the entire game again, even harder than before (Having cleared on "Recommended" previously), just for some extra dialog at the end. The unique game modes after the initial completion are interesting, especially the "Boss mode" which I briefly took a look at, but it just being a beat for beat run through the entire game again but with various restrictions just feels more like padding than actually interesting.I will give this game a thumbs up, as I would not want to negatively affect the review score for this game. I will, however, say that if you do not find the idea of touring cute monster girl sprites interesting enough for you, then this probably isn't the experience for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is an interesting Metoridvania. It's slow paced and heavily gear focused. There's not as much focus on dodging attacks as there is building your gear the correct way for a fight. There are also additional modes that can be played. The main game is ~7 hours. Each subsequent playthrough tends to be shorter, as you know what works.The Good:- good aesthetic/effects- cool weapons- variety in how to play- well animated/designed bosses- music- Assassin Mode is a blast- Spells interact with the world.- If you want to, you can break the game (Oil spell plus+4 fire damage makes a fiery oil ball).The just okay:- Witch Mode- Weapon selection- Has a story- Bosses need more variety in design. "Giant Waifu" only goes so farThe Bad:- Boss Mode (feels like you're playing 3 pretty crappy characters)- Waiting for stuff to refill (MP/HP)- Inverse Difficulty curve. As you play, you get gear. Gear lets you defeat bosses easier. So, the first boss tends to be the roughest (or the ice one if you're unprepared).- Good ending locked behind hard mode and doing things a certain way (or so I hear).
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly short, mildly challenging action-platformer, with a more tactical focus than running straight into every enemy mindlessly. You will be punished if you try to do this. I was lead to believe that this game was going to be unforgiving. My experience, even on the "Recommended" Difficulty was hardly that. I died, sure, but never enough times to want to pull my hair out or quit playing altogether. That said, I didn't find it as challenging or as difficult as some reviews led me to believe, but the game is not an easy one either. They warn you outright upon starting a new game that this is not meant to be a quick "run and gun" experience. The Heroine, swings melee weapons slowly. Timing is important. Traps are appropriately dangerous, but relatively rare. Figuring out when to dodge is likewise, very important. Nothing particularly new here. I found a wide variety of weapons available, mostly swords, axes, daggers, and hammers. I never encountered any spears, as far as I am aware of. Ranged options are mostly down to various throwing weapons (both traditional and, uniquely, some throwing bottles), a few bows, and casting spells. It took me some time to encounter a bow, so if that's your preferred playstyle, be wary of that. You may not acquire one till an hour or more in. I like the interactions between various mechanics. Casting a Lightning spell while soaking wet is, obviously, a bad idea, and a quick way to kill yourself. Finding means to solve these moment to moment problems is definitely a treat. However, I want to preface that previous statement with confirmation that you will be doing quite a bit of inventory management. If you're suffering bleed stacks, you can die quickly. So you will find yourself going into the inventory very often to resolve various issues. Casting a fire spell, while covered in Oil is likewise, a bad idea. Also, if you do find yourself changing your routine to fight against a boss. The Green "Angel" Checkpoints will only store whatever version of your equipment you had as you passed them. So you will have to reset your equipment should you be stuck at a boss. I didn't find it annoying as other people did, but I can see why it would get frustrating. So I will also mention that here. All in all, I found it a fun, and occationally challenging experience that lasted a handful of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy is this game a mixed bag! Let’s start with the first thing though: this game is NOT a metroidvania in any stretch of the imagination. It’s a pretty straightforward action-adventure game. Now that said let’s just skip to some of the problems and even dealbreakers with this game. Problems. 1. The combat is stiff and very clunky. Now you may like this so it really depends but I would have liked it to be much more fluid and smooth. For me it took some time and many deaths before a learned it and in the end I can somewhat appreciate it. 2. There’s save points and check points. Now at a save point you can obviously save your progress (logic) and the check points are there to restart you when you die. But here’s the problem. You can only activate a check point once and if you choose to go back and save and then pass the check point again it won’t activate! You now restart from your save point. Now to  the real issue, let’s say you activate a check point and then you fight a boss. You may have a different setup for some bosses (different weapons, different magic you get what I mean) so you change your setup before that boss fight. And now you die and you go back to retry (from the check point) and you notice the all the changes you have made is reseted to what you had before so you have to do the same changes EVERY TIME after you die. The only way to save the changes is at a save point. This is infuriating to say the least. 3. The achievements are totally broken! I mean they straight up doesn’t work! If this is important to you move this to the “deal breaker” section. The deal breaker! Now this last one is an absolutely deal breaker for me. You see I started playing this game on my Steam Deck and I was planning on finishing the game on my PC once I got back home. But no such luck, the cloud saves doesn’t work. And I’ve tried everything under the sun the game refuses to sync up to my PC. This is the one thing that tipped me over for: “it’s a ok adventure game I can recommend to some people” to “nope! That’s one more technical issue I won’t accept”! So if any of my complaints is a deal breaker to you just stay away from this game or at least wait to a sale and/or an update…..maybe it’ll be good game in a couple of months who knows?

_childDocuments_.review: I should start by saying that I really don't want to write a negative review of this game, because parts of it are very good. The Art, which everyone has already touched on is one of the best uses of particle effects and lighting that I've seen in a 2D game, and the level design is, for what it is, actually very good. I did enjoy myself when exploring, both while going through the first time, and when going back for all the chests that I skipped (There's a reason to do so, it's explained in game). Unfortunately, I can't say the same about the combat, and for a game that is so heavily based around it, it's a deal breaker. To put it simply, it feels as though the players move-set and the enemies where designed for different games. The player has a simple move-set, with slow weapon swings even on fast weapons and a dodge that has I-frames but also a very long recovery, which indicate that the game is one based primarily around spacing and avoiding enemies with similarly long windups and cool-downs. Many of the enemies however didn't seem to get the memo, and attack so fast that in the time it takes for some of the player's slower weapons to swing, they can finish the recovery on their last attack, start up a new one, and finish it before the player can hit them. This more or less results in a combat system that encourages not skill, but finding the cheesiest possible strategy and then spamming it regardless of how boring it is to play, and make no mistake, standing out of range of enemies, hiding behind a shield while the enemies get killed by spinning swords isn't fun.Perhaps this kind of clunky combat would work if the game was based primarily around avoiding enemies, and indeed many horror games achieve success in this way quite well, but this game is a different beast, as it has fairly involved 2 or 3 stage boss fights, in which the sub-par combat is left to fend for itself, devoid of any good level design to hide behind.To compound this, the game has a fairly significant number of smaller design issues that make it quite frequently a chore to play. On that front, the rest of this review is just going to be list of my more minor issues and some of my ideas on how they might be resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to recommend. I don't usually review games I haven't beat it, neither for games I refunded, however, if the first few hours of the game doesn't hook you in, it's a bit hard to continue playing...This is specially the case with Lost Ruins. A game that visually looks incredible, reminding me of the Momodora series by Bombservice. Despite the great looking visuals, the biggest problem of this game is the pace. I'm talking about "constant open inventory" kind of games.In this game, there are a lot of things you have to be aware of, environmental things that can damage you, healing items that heal or cure effects, and so on. You can also use different weapons that vary your attack speed and things like that. Some enemies work better with certain weapons, while others are best approached with complete different playstyles.The game does not have any sort of preset switcher or ways to quickly switch things, as pointed out in other reviews that have beat the game. I stopped playing the game after my first hour or so, those hours were mostly going into the inventory screen to change gear and stuff, not much about actually playing the game. Every time that I had to do something on the inventory screen made the game feel incredibly slow.Some of the items I unlocked seems like they could simply be passive items instead of items you have to equip to have that effect applied to you. One of those items can be easily exploited, being a Ring that reduces your Max Health, but regens your health upon wearing it. I think there's also another negative upon wearing it that I forgot what it does now.Lost your health? Well, you can go to the inventory screen once again, equip that Ring, return to the game, wait for the health regen, go back to the inventory yet again, equip an item with a better bonus (since you won't be needing the Ring while at full health), advance a little to the room before you get damaged to something that you would prefer to get damaged instead of relying with constant inventory opening for every little thing in this game (as there's many different environmental damage types toward your adventure). Repeat the process.Even if you don't constant switch to this Ring (either play without it or play with it equipped at all times), you will still need to be constantly using your inventory screen to use specific spells to deal with specific things blocking your path, to defeat enemies easier, to heal yourself, and so on. No matter your playstyle, you will have to rely heavily on the inventory screen in this game, and with no way to quickly switch things, and no preset-loadouts, it's really hard to get the pace of this game flowing. The great visuals stop being your focus, and the letters of your inventory screen ends up being what's shown on screen most of the time, sadly.Your attack speed, depending on the weapon you equip, is also pretty slow. Your character goes into a complete halt when attacking. I wouldn't mind this very much if it wasn't for the constant menu-ing in this game. I really want to like this game, I really do, specially because of those great looking visuals, but it's really hard to continue playing after you realize what you'll be doing in the entire game:Opening the inventory screen every few seconds or so.The enemies are also unforgiving, as they can quickly drain your health due to the lack (or very little) invincibility frames. Combine this with things I have previously mentioned, you want to rely the maximum with your current arsenal, and the things you have obtained. Healing yourself with the Ring is a huge bonus and it's hard to overlook when so many things in this game can damage you in either fair or unfair ways.So yeah, this is one of those reviews that the writer wants to like the game, but just can't. I really really want to like this game, but, it doesn't feel like I'm playing a game when I'm constantly switching my arsenal instead of doing anything on it.There are also a few other nitpicks I want to bring up:- There's no way to disable voices in the game. These are tied to Sound Effects volume slider (you can disable Music and Sound Effects separately). This game doesn't have voice acting for dialogue, but your character will shout things when doing certain things like getting hit, being killed, blocking, etc., and it can get annoying after a while. I wish I didn't had to turn off all sounds to get rid of the voices / grunts that my character does when doing action X, Y, Z.- You can equip a shield that, upon successfully blocking, the character uses the same voice line when you take damage. This feels pretty weird, to be honest. It should either have a different voice clip or no voice at all. Just a loud "blocking" noise would be sufficient in this case.

_childDocuments_.review: In this action adventure we play a young girl who has been teleported to a castle. In the process, we have completely lost our memory. The castle is full of skeletons of other people who, according to the messages on their cell phones (with rather long-running batteries...), seem to have been teleported to this world just like us and tried (unsuccessfully) to find a way out. Besides goblins and aggresive animals that want to kill us, we also meet the sorceress Beatrice in the castle, who helps us find our way around. Soon we cross a fantasy realm full of monsters and hard-to-conquer bosses to find out how to get back to our old world.Lost Ruins is a 2D action adventure game in pixel style, in which we can attack our enemies with a variety of swords, axes and other medieval weapons. Soon we'll also learn spells to burn enemies or heal ourselves. The game teaches us to use the environment to achieve our objectives. Flammable liquids burst into flames when they come into contact with burning lanterns or fireballs, ice magic freezes waters. The game's focus is less on frantic jumping passages and more on combat and managing life,magic points, and our inventory. Cute characters, fluid movement animations, lots of items to collect (clothes, food, weapons, spells), an automatically drawn map and portals for fast travel make Lost Ruins a fantastic 2D action adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like MetroidVanias this will be neither Groundbreaking nor Mediocre. Its cruelly short however, at 20 hours I had completed both the Normal and "Boss Mode" difficulty options. And personally, I really wanted more of this clueless and naive protagonist but with all that said, in summary 'Lost Ruins' is a brisk romp of a MetroidVania that's fun whether you're new or at home in the genre. I'd suggest starting on 'Veteran' difficulty as there is something added onto the tail end of the game not present in 'Recommended' and 'Accessible' difficulties. As well as 'Veteran' feeling like the intended experience for such a comparatively brief MV. Grab it on sale if the length is a concern for you, otherwise I find the price and game itself perfect for what the developers intentions clearly were! Loved it c: <3

_childDocuments_.review: This review is going to make me a hypocrite. But hey, we’re all hypocritical once in a while, right? Oh well, here we go.This metroidvania is pretty heavy on the “-vania”: there are some really heavy RPG elements that, depending on your level of enjoyment of those mechanics, will make or break this game. Elemental damage and status effects abound here and only the right combination of equipment will make life easier for the player. Depending on the player’s gear, a puddle of oil on the floor can either lead to a quick death to the player or a helpful weapon against any baddies standing in the middle of it. At first, this caused me some really aggravating deaths until I started to get a better grasp of the system. Also, it might be worth noting that the menuing can be a little annoying as the player switches equipment in and out for different obstacles, but all-in-all it’s really fun.The story is pretty silly, despite some twists here and there. But the characters you meet along the way are pretty great. The psychotic butcher schoolgirl, the zombie fangirls, the katana-wielding goblin slayer: they’re all fantastic. On top of that, the enemies the player faces are memorable as well and each poses a different threat while being vulnerable to different damage types. This game constantly mixes things up and keeps things interesting.Where this game makes me a hypocrite is that it’s very linear – which is precisely the same reason why I didn’t like  and why I didn’t recommend that one. Any real exploration is locked behind sidequests, so if the player isn’t paying attention to those, there is no real reason to roam around the world. On top of that, items needed to complete those quests are marked on the map, eliminating any need to do any real searching. The thing that makes this game more interesting than  is that the limited exploration usually leads to a unique piece of equipment or a new spell or something. In , exploration lead to either a health pick-up, a stamina pick-up, or (eventually useless) money, and that’s pretty much it.  does it better, is what I’m trying to say.In the end, I really had a blast with this game. From the characters, to the maps, to the combat, everything came together to make this one a memorable stand-out. If you’re willing to muscle your way through this often-challenging game, you’re likely to find something you like in here. I know I did!

_childDocuments_.review: At first I loved this game, as I'm a fan of 2D souls-likes... that said, after a while it feels like a lot of cheap & unfair game play keeps coming up. For example, you might do some tricky platforming only to be killed by a fireball from off screen while the devs clearly planned for you to be in a position where you can't avoid it, all after you just spent several minutes getting to that point finally! I'm okay dying repeatedly in a game so long as it feels fair, but this game subs clever design for cheap shots...Update: I've also noticed quite a few bugs related to button remapping. some labels don't update correctly for "back" if you remap the B button, for example. This sucks because the default layout is bad; it uses triggers for map and menu nav and bumpers for combat stuff... what?! So backwards. I tried to give it another chance today but now my L trigger brings up map even though it is clearly remapped for secondary attack in settings and reflects that on screen... So it says press LT equip but when I do the map opens. This sort of thing might be acceptable if the devs were updating the game and fixing issues, but it appears they abandoned supporting this game after a series of patches post-release and zero updates or community communication since.

The combat is very stiff but fair — every attack locks you in place for the entire duration, even completely negating any horizontal movement during the jump. There are lots of options for one-handed or two-handed melee weapons and different ranged and magic attacks. In addition to weapons, you can equip various items that provide huge bonuses to completely alter your build on the spot (or even between different phases of a boss fight).The first playthrough takes about 6-7 hours to complete. After that, you unlock additional difficulty levels, challenge runs (magic only and daggers only), and a Nier: Automata-like additional mini-campaign in which you play as three bosses from the main campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: I think i want to like this game more than i did. I keep thinking ‘i like it but…’It's high point is definitely it's art. Fantastic pixel art and a good mix of nice lighting, effects and particles that are notably different resolutions but that still work together to be clearly readable in gameplay,  It dose lean a bit fan servicey in a similar vein as the shanty games for the bosses. Has a nice map to explore, with simple but enjoyable puzzles to break up the platforming and combat. An ok story, bit tropey but dint hate it.Gameplay it's a slow paced castlevania with sprinklings of souls like systems. It's core movement and combat felt good to me and i had a fun time playing it. Weapons each felt different and satisfying to use. A Solid variety of enemies to fight, simple but enjoyable bosses. The Magic spells you got were neat and the elemental effects looked nice and would have environmental effects. But it feels like it layers too many unneeded or unbalanced systems on top of this. I think it's health system is largely pointless as most damage you take means you die in two or three hits on normal anyway. With the items to heal largely being either heal for a useless amount or over a useless amount of time. so you have a good chance of insta-gibbing as soon as you leave the frustrating long item list menu regardless of the items you spamed. This also is similar to the equipment system, too many largely useless bits of gear, some that i think are broken or have wrong item translation descriptions.  with too few slots so i ended up just using the same items most of the game as it wasnt worth touching the system.It's save system also feels messy, with two different saves. A manual save point but also statues that auto-save when you walk past but you have no control over. Also it's unclear when these ones reset to be reusable. Meaning it can lead to frustrating repetition in sections with only the auto-statues as you cant control its use well. Also with death coming to you so swiftly i found the time to re-load is also frustratingly long too, i just felt like i wanted instant respawn/reload not what felt agonisingly long from death slowdown and wait for the prompt that your dead and want to re-load.I still enjoyed it over all apart from those issues. My first playthrough on normal was a solid 6-7 hours and it unlocked a bunch of modes on completion. Also seems like there are multiple endings and ways to play through, so it's got replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: Wannabe H-game that confuses challenge with frustration.Story: 2/10Absolutely nothing compelling. You appear in a strange world, you fight bosses to find a way out. Very little is explained beyond surface details, and uh oh surprise twist except you definitely see it coming after playing the game for 5 minutes.Oh, by the way, you won't be able to see the real ending unless you beat it on Veteran mode. So yeah, have fun with that. Super fun and rewarding game design. Characters: 4/10 (9/10 for the heroine, 2/10 for just about everyone else) The main character is charming, but almost every single other character is dripping with the kind of art style you expect to see in adult-themed games. I recognize the talent, but it's also a bit ... gross. Some characters have interesting personalities, but you get a total of about 60 seconds worth of time for each of them.Three of the bosses are giant women that take up your entire screen, have massive and fully animated breasts, and "get embarrassed" when you do enough damage. Almost every other boss transforms to a second stage "party city skanky costume" form. How horny was the dude that made this? Good lord.Music: 3/10What music? There's maybe 7 tracks in this whole game. Some are okay, the rest are just ambient background noise.Sound: 7/10"Clunk! CLANK! CLANK! Clunk! Clunk! Clunk! Clunk! CLANK!"It's fine, but more variety would be nice. Some of the character noises are fun, though.Gameplay: 3/10Definitely my least favorite part of the game, and it's basically all there is to the game. To call this game "challenging" is inaccurate. It's intentionally designed to frustrate you. - If you attack in mid-air, you stop forward momentum. - Attack animations take forever to execute and recover from, while enemies attack with lightning speed and have massive windows for hitting you. - You don't get i-frames if you're hit, so some enemies can one shot you, by actually hitting you 5+ times in rapid succession. All you have to do is get hit that first time. - HP and MP don't regenerate unless you use items. There's no camp to restore HP and MP. You'll be able to cast a spell twice, and then have to spend money on items to cast again.- Status affects (which stack in higher difficulties) are overtly brutal, so you can play this game two ways: - - 1. Spend most of your time menu-ing to apply heals and cures.- - 2. Actually play the game, and just die. And then sit through all the cutscenes again.- When you die, the game makes you wait 5 seconds in slow-mo before letting you continue. Why? Because screw you, that's why.Graphics: I don't usually grade on this, and I won't start now, but...- The pixel graphics are very pretty.- The lighting effects are neat.If this game's for you, hey, that's great. But ultimately I'm just frustrated and disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Great metroidvania that even if it's somewhat short, has good survival mechanics that tests the player's creativity and skills.Lost Ruins, even though it's a metroidvania, it's sold as a survival experience, and as such, it should be tackled with a bit of patience. I see some people complaining about how the combat is slow, heavy and clunky, but I personally like it because you can feel the weight of the weapon you're trying to use, and it was done purposely so you build your character around such "flaws", like equipping a accessory that increases the attack speed of heavy weapons, or cast speed and/or cost of spells, and the game gives the player freedom to do any kind of build, as long you have the equipment to make it work. Early on that might be a problem tho, since you have to either buy the equipment or find it around the map.You can't grind out of any situation in the game or increases the stats of your character through items, like other games in the genre do, because it doesn't have a level up system, but the game has lots of checkpoints and save points, so it doesn't ending up being too frustrating and whatnot. I personally think there's way too many checkpoints in the game tho. I just think that the existence of shields somewhat broke the difficulty down a lot, which enables you to defend yourself virtually against anything, but it's not just aimlessly guarding, since you have to time the guard action correctly to defend (which has a pretty forgivable timing window), and elemental attacks usually pierce the shield (which you can mitigate or nullify completely with the right accessory), so it involves a bit of skill.Visual wise, Lost Ruins is beautiful. Every area has its own design and particularities, and the use of simulated pixels it's a shown of its own. I like how there's no reuse of enemy design, and how each enemy race suits the area which you encounter them perfectly, without feeling like out of place. The boss design is superb. A bit fanservicey, but it's great. I really like it.Replay wise, it offers quite a bit of content actually. The main campaign, which is divided into 4 difficulty modes, has two endings, and 3 extra modes are unlocked after finishing it for the first time, which may not contain anything new per se, it offers diversified gameplay and more challenges.Anyway, I really recommend Lost Ruins to the fans of the metroidvania genre. It may be somewhat slower early on, but keep pushing. It's really fun. It really is what I've expected, and a bit more.
