_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is an excellent metroidvania, side scroller game.  Now this is the part where I talk about the story a little bit, but this is one of those games that talking about the story may spoil it for you so I'll just say it's about a young girl who has been teleported into a strange castle.Okay then the likes, the story is really good at first I thought it was your simple stop the bad guy story but had plenty of twists and turns and well-written characters that just made the story phenomenal, especially when you play the game a second time and everything in the story just seems to click together.The gameplay is really good it has a bit of a Dark Souls like feel to it, but with metroidvania-styled gameplay, it's tough but fair and when you die it is mostly your fault. It also has a nice balance of weapons and spells you can play with, you can also customize your character with different items to give them more strength or more durability or certain abilities. The weapons and spells are really good each one with their own unique look and power, some weapons and spells are better than others so this game gives incentive to mix and match to figure out which character build works for you. The pixel graphics are really beautiful, very well done with plenty of detail and nice little touches to it, I also love the character portraits it has a nice anime feel to it. The levels in the game are really good quite diverse with plenty of interesting locations to look at and explore, like a sewer to a castle to even a crypt, all of it well designed that makes you want to stop and stare at certain places in the level.The characters are really good very well written even NPC characters with little dialogue are quite interesting. I really like the main character because she's generally a very nice, very caring and considerate person, I also like this demon Merchant she's also really cool character and generally very sweet and caring, also I really like this Dragon maid she's super adorable looking.The enemies and bosses are really good each one with their own unique design and skill that keeps you on your toes, especially when playing a more harder difficulties. The music is really good with plenty of great tracks to listen to, that fits the game really well especially at the last level.The game also has quests by certain characters you meet which can give you better weapons or access to areas you couldn't get to before. Now the best things in the game is the multiple endings and different modes to play, basically after you beat the game for the first time you are given different modes like which mode, assassin mode and boss mode both the witch and assassin mode basically makes you play with a certain type of build. While boss mode where you get to play as three bosses you defeated and in that mode we get a completely different story which I found it quite good especially with the interactions of the three bosses. There's also different endings in the game which encourages you to play the game multiple times to get everything.There's also plenty of great references not just to other video games, but to anime and manga like in one scene it makes references to paper RPGs and berserk. The notes in this game I absolutely love as you know I like notes in video games as it can help build a story and these notes are very good they help build the world; these notes give insight to different characters and the villain of the game.Okay then the dislikes, alright there is not really anything to dislike about this game, okay there are some things but really they're just so small compared to how great the game is, but here are just some small complaints I have.The platforming can be a little bit frustrating sometimes like you could miss a platform after jumpping even though you were very close to it the platform. The final boss is a bit of a letdown I mean don't get me wrong the final boss has a cool design and she can be a bit tough, but I thought she'd have a second form like all the other bosses but no she doesn't even, not even on more harder difficulties she's still the same, like I said I found that to be a bit underwhelming and a little bit of a letdown. I also wish the game had some DLC to buy because I think it would do really well to have a soundtrack, pc wallpaper and art book for the game especially pc wallpaper.Alright now that I told you all this stuff, Lost Ruins is an excellent metroidvania, side scroller game. With a really good story, really good gameplay and really good characters and just so much more to love so I highly recommend this game if you like metroidvania games I recommend this game to you.

_childDocuments_.review: This might look like a simple pixel-art indie game at first. But, surprisingly, this game offers a lot more, and it totally took me by surprise of its unexpected great quality.For the game art, it really blows me away! The game will definitely please fans of cute anime art style with its awesome 2D illustrations of the characters. Aside, the pixel art looks pretty great, too. The characters, the monsters are pretty distinguishable and attractive. The graphic elements of the boss fights are top-notch for pixel-art game standards. The only downside, I think, is the environment design. It might get bored after a while, and some details and parts of the environment are hard to see.For the gameplay, it really challenges you with lots of traps, combos from monsters and bosses. The overall enemy AI is great, and it surely gives you a hard time battling through. The platformer elements and puzzles of the game is solid, yet somewhat easy at times.I also particularly love how the game offers you a variety of play styles, You can beat the game through brute force of weapons, or cunningly cheese the enemies from afar with bows, or backstabbing them with daggers, or wisely defeat them with a variety of spells that counter their weaknesses. Overall, the game has a great replay value. Finally, watch out for multiple endings of the game (3 of them, as I read online). So, if you are into cute girls with cute anime style, with a bit of a metroidvania and survival-style game, Lost Ruins is definitely a must-try!! Hats off to only 2 developers of this wonderful game!

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and fun game but has a very steep learning curve and punishing early game. There are a couple of achievements/endings locked behind playing on "hardcore" mode in which you lose your save file when you die and cannot manually save during the game (autosaves only). There is also an optional quest you have to complete to get an ending that makes the game much harder if you decide to complete it. I don't know if I will come back to the game to complete these.One playthrough is actually fairly short all things considered, maybe 5-10 hours if you are thorough, and only a couple hours if you speed through. Even so, the various obstacles, items, equipment, and magic that you encounter keep it a fresh experience to the point that no matter how far you get or how many items you have, if you use the wrong ones against the enemies you're fighting, you'll have an impossible time. Similarly, if you choose them well, a fight that seems very difficult will be a walk in the park. Some people have commented that the attack speed on weapons is very slow, but this is also a matter of choosing the right approach for the task at hand.You'll also unlock a few extra game modes after completing your first playthrough. I haven't tried these yet, but if you really liked your first playthrough this will probably keep things fresh for you and give you a chance to tackle the game from a new approach.Overall I would recommend this due to the interesting and engaging combat implementation (and some puzzle solving too) plus the cute characters and great artwork. The current price of $20 is definitely as high as I would go on it though. Ideally I think maybe $10-15 is a good price point (and I picked it up on sale myself). Still though, you'll definitely know if it's a game for you within 2 hours of playing, so you might as well give it a try if it looks interesting and refund it if it doesn't end up agreeing with you. I enjoyed it overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting take on a Metroidvania.It diverges from the norm in a few ways:- You do not heal at save points or checkpoints. You have to rely on consumable items, or gear you find later.- Enemies don't respawn. Except when they do. Not really sure what the criteria is here, but it isn't screen transitions or hitting a save point.- You do not gain new traversal abilities at any point. Walk, jump, and roll is all you get.None of this is necessarily bad, just unusual.Games had top-notch pixel art, is relatively difficulty, and pretty short at around 6 hours for a first playthrough.Sound is a bit lacking - the sound effects are serviceable, but even having just finished the game I couldn't tell you if it even had music. Definitely no voice acting.Gameplay is a little bit rough, but solid.Decent 7/10 game. Worth checking out, but not likely to amaze you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this, but Jesus is death so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. For as fast you respawn after death, you'd think the game would autosave your inventory whenever you change it. You're constantly swapping items from room to room;Okay, goblins in here, switch to the Shaman mask for 50% damage against goblins) This room is covered in water in, lets switch to the swimsuit so we can move through water normally.Lightning-weak boss, let's switch to lightning weapons, etc.Well, whenever you die, your inventory gets swapped back to whatever you were wearing prior. And since the autosave statues only autosave the FIRST TIME YOU ENCOUNTER THEM you never have a chance to resave your new loadout. So with each death comes having to switch all your ♥♥♥♥ again. And again. And again... if you suck like I do.Imagine if everytime died in Dark Souls you appeared at the bonfire with whatever you were wearing the LAST TIME YOU VISITED IT. It's infuriating! The best part about these types of games is running at the obstacle over and over until you figure it out or force your way through it. Most of the obstacles in this game come with a pause just to swap out your loadout every single time.Still. Great art, I'm digging the story. Just a little butthurt. If you like metroidvanias and anime you'll dig this.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky weapon animations that feel like they are out of a flash game while the enemies attack smoothly and quickly, a health pool that has no reliable way to recover outside of consumables, an overabundance of damage-over-time status effects until it basically feels like two hits will kill you, checkpoints that you cannot retrigger if you go pick up a new ability and come back, a combat system that forces you to go into the menu and unequip your weapon in order to break walls or remove hazards, an amnesiac isekai plot that looks to be trying to subvert tropes by being tongue in cheek about it but just ends up feeling shallow, and all of this compounded by a half-crash bug that has apparently been around for years and has not been fixed.Maybe this gets good later on, but when I get my second game-freezing crash in less than a half hour (right after I finally got done dealing with a really obnoxious set of rooms that killed me a dozen or so times), I simply can't bring myself to play anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Garbage. Just complete garbage. It's obnoxiously difficult not for any challenging reason but because every weapon has such a huge windup and delay to it that actually hitting enemies is the hardest part. Every enemy can attack faster than you can so for literally every encounter you have memorize how many seconds before they reach you, you should have pressed attack. The game has ranged options: Spells where you have to use a consumable every 2-3 casts because you ran out of mana and mana doesn't regenerate on its own... ever. Or you can use the bow that renders every enemy in the game trival... except for the lack of arrows. The store has a limited amount and if you run out that's it. Boss enemies are instead much much easier than the normal fights because since they fill the screen you can just attack anywhere and be sure to hit it. In fact the slimboss first phase where she is human sized is harder than the 2nd phase where she is just a naked goo monster. And while hp seems like an issue, since you can just open your menu and eat as much as you want at all times you hp is more of a quick time event where your reflexes are tested more than anything. Which is why its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that you have no I-frames and as such wave attacks by magic casters can hit you multiple times from the same attack. The game is labeled a metroidvania which is an insult to the genre. The map looks like a metroidvania map but you don't gain any new abilties or items that would let you access new areas. Instead obtain a key to open a door and that's it. You also just linear progress through it unless you missed a secret and desperately want to go back for it. And then there's the "story" or rather anime trope collection. You play as a girl in school uniform and the only item you can equip that changes your appearance is a swimsuit...

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is fun in some cases.  The storyline is a bit meh, and the exploration tends to actually be held back by the game mechanics itself.  There appears to be some basic concepts that I thought was a bit out of place for a dungeon/exploration/platforming game.I do think that the direct "drop" of the character while in mid air attacking plays in a cheap way to increase the difficulty.  The character should dedicate herself to the jump and while I think the jumps are sufficient, the attacks to bring a 90deg drop and wallstop mid air is an artificial cheap way of making this game harder.I also find another artificial difficulty in this game where there's very little money to buy items to assist.  This tends to create this "hoarding" type mentality and I don't actually use items or tools to help when it's too consumable.  I'll farm for items like chicken, and the difficult part is that I gotta teleport to respawn items.  This tends to get in the way of progress and also delays what is suppose to be just straight exploration.There are just straight forward game design flaws in this game, and at full price I would have never bought this game.  I do love the art style and I do love the characters, but the artificial difficulty bumps that are just due to bad and lazy level design is quite "annoying" to play through.  I will complete this game, but so far after maybe 5 hours of it -- it's a little uninspiring with the game mechanics. boss battles are fun at least, but the artificial handicaps get in the way.  The only saving grace is that respawns are close items are recovered when death occurs (eg it just reloads your auto save).Controller configuration gets annoying, I don't understand why the button configs on the controller changes the movement of the tabs?  This is a good example of lazy programming and not putting an extra routine in to properly map buttons to separate the way buttons map between menu and actual game play.(eg. I don't like spells on left or right buttons, so I move it to right button and right trigger, but now the TABS on the menu are mapped to left button and left trigger -- this is plain lazy for a game developer)I hope this gets properly patched and the devs look into making some of the gameplay mechanics better so that we don't get stalled by bad fetch quests and bad mechanics that artificially make the game longer and harder. One other item that bothers me is the lack of MP heal drops.  enemies tend to drop more health than mana recovery drops.  I tend to not even use spells if MP is used up since there's no way to heal and with the lack of resources (being unable to properly buy items without farming for hours) there's no reason for me to stick around and do anything or even look at vending machines.  MP heal drops should be a bit more often if you want players to use spells, also larger mp pool would be nicer considering you have spells that cost 12MP given a 20pt pool.  this is not even good if you don't allow for HP/MP recovery at autosave spots (which is also another artificial difficulty bump). Better planning and more enemy placements in a room would be nice - large empty room with 1-2 mobs with platforming is too little.  Even with no XP gains, it would be nice to just be able to do more.  Makes the inclusive fetch quests a bit more entertaining.  Also RESPAWNS, I gotta warp out and back to do a respawn, this is just meh.

_childDocuments_.review: The art is beautiful and the character designs are modest! That is all it has going for it though. The gameplay is super frustrating. I wanted to like it but it keeps making the experience feel cheap and unfair in most situations. I love souls-like, metrovania-style gameplay but this needs a new set of developers or someone from the Metroid series to help them design the gameplay. You will go through a level where you have studied the enemy movement and counted the pixels so you can come out unscathed, only to be killed by an off-screen magic attack that had no business coming into the screen. There is no real tutorial or any "lube" build-up in the gameplay. They just straight-up raw-dog and throw you into the hardest difficulty without learning proper weapon or magic management. Mind you, I played on "Normal". I cannot imagine the hardest difficulty. For normal, you already get hit once or twice and you are dead. I'm a Dark Souls fan but FromSofware are at least fair with their deaths. This studio feels like they are purposely trolling us.The controls are clunky and agitating when you cannot change the directional buttons to "W". It is non-existent to play.I highly recommend buying this game at a discount, which I did, thankfully. Or free for that matter. I'm going to keep playing only just because I spent money on it but keep in mind, you will get frustrated playing on "Normal".

_childDocuments_.review: Although the crux of the game is lol anime titties there is a decent metroidvania in here somewhere. The art clearly has a ton of work put into it and is well done, and the music and sound design is pretty great too. However, the gameplay itself is absolutely frustrating - even on the easiest difficulty, some mobs can barely touch you, while others have instant death attacks, even at full health with stacked resists. This is made even more frustrating because there is zero sense of speed to the movement and attacks - you feel like you're moving in molasses the entire time even with the fastest things equipped, and as a result the combat feels super clunky and drags on. Magic is super over powered and I felt like many bosses (especially the last few) basically required a certain spell load out to spam in order to beat, rather than finding my own way to victory. Overall there's a lot done well, but it was too frustrating in the end to be able to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a Metroidvania. It is a "open menu every 5 seconds of combat to change the entire set of spells and weapons + use 3 different potions to remove the debuffs" type of game that is trying to be an action platformer. The story is linear and you don't have to take any detours, at least not in my experience on the expert difficulty.- The mechanics? Suck.- iFrame on dodge? Yes, sometimes it works as intended. But you cannot cancel any animations with it (super fun when fighting bosses, of course).- Story? Generic with 1 twist at the end. Speaking of the end... Man, it was awful, really. You expect something after *a certain conversation*, a final showdown, but no, they just roll the credits.- Cute high school girls? For whatever reason, yes. Also, you collect their clothes after defeating them (like taking their panties as their corpses disintegrate, nothing indecent).It was a bit of fun for the ~7 hours, but I know not everyone will like this game. It really is frustrating at times. Oh, and the achievements don't work most of the time. I'd only recommend getting it on sale (paid about $2 or $3, but it was free on GOG).

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game.  Story is predictable, archetypical, japaneesie, boring.  The characters are stupid and basic.  The character portraits are sexualized as usual and also stupid.   The weapons are almost all boring and possess no individual noteworthy qualities,  Most of the magic sucks, as does casting it until the game is basically over.  Now for the good.  Thank god they didn't try to voice act this.  I do not like the grating voices these types of games assign to their characters.  The fact that it was text based meant I could stand to actually read the cutscenes instead of feverishly searching for a skip button.  There actually is a skip button, and you're not missing much by enjoying its use.  The bosses and enemies are all pretty fun to fight but the bosses can be cheesed really easily.  Like the spider archer lady is completely negated by a shield and summon swords and the ice lady by the fire sword and summonable fire orbs.  The visuals are very nice.  Pretty good pixel art.  Cool looking bosses.  To complete the map isn't too arduous and "how do I get over there" to get a treasure chest isn't a huge time sink for the most part.  Load up your favorite magical teleporting christmas throwing ham and... uhh, go ham on some demons!  Without elaborating much, the only real complaint I didn't already know I was going to have coming into this game was the magic system.  There are equippable accessories that give you constant MP regen you find very late in the game.  Otherwise, your MP NEVER regenerates at all unless you use restorative items which tend to be expensive to buy and somewhat rare to pick up.  The basic (lousy) spells give you up to 4 casts to exhaust your entire magic bar, and the useful ones as few as one or two casts. That's it.  The spells are almost all terrible.  Once you've gotten the two accessories that make magic use practical, magic becomes almost overpowered, one shotting just about any enemy and doing around 1/5th of a boss's health bar per charge if you exploit elemental weaknesses. I don't have a quick and easy solution for this problem.  It just feels like the game developers got lost trying to come up with the magic system, and it's not very good as a result.  You find new spells constantly throughout the game, but it never feels practical to use them at all outside of necessity to open a door or something until you find the items that regenerate your MP.  It would have been nice if there was a scaling up system where spells were either much more useful in the early game when casting them was extremely expensive, there was a very slow regeneration of MP by default, or even a system that regenerates MP for killing enemies so that the player would feel welcome to use it offensively.  Maybe this bothered other people less than it bothered me.  7 hours to 100% the map and beat all bosses with copious amounts of screwing around in the process.  Definitely worth the 8 bucks I paid for the game on sale. Conveniently, I'd give it a score of 8/10 as well due to the combination of length, cost, and enjoyment factor.  It's a pleasant game that, if you like to get-off looking at cartoon characters with comically inappropriate wardrobes, you'll enjoy even more than I did.  If the story in every anime you've watched or JRPG you've played has blown your mind, then you will love this game because it does not deviate even slightly from the common tropes of that genre.  At 10 bucks, it'd be a solid 7/10.  It is not worth 20 dollars.  Unless you're looking for your waifu or whatever the hell that means, wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: + lots of variety in weapons, armor, builds+ really nice soundtrack and sound design+ animations and pixel art graphics are great+ large world with multiple distinct areas- punishingly difficult until you get in the groove- poor difficulty pacing and balancing- lots of tools at disposal but most of them impracticalLost Ruins was advertised to me as a metroidvania but I never really got that feel. You don't gain new abilities or skills that open up previously inaccessible areas, the game's pretty open from the start and instead relies on puzzles and exploration to unlock new areas. The main idea of the game, is that you're criminally underpowered at the start and really don't know anything about the world. And you don't really learn much by playing: besides some cute and funny dialog, the story is really of no consequence and shouldn't be a reason to grab the game. It's a hard game, but only really near the start. From the beginning to the first boss, you'll struggle to make progress as you only have one equipment slot and your equipment selection is slim. Enemies hit hard and you lack many means to heal. After the first boss but before the second, it gets a lot easier, especially since you gain an extra equipment slot and can get a passive heal equipment. Shortly after you get a passive magic point regen item which is where the game starts to become trivial.Some of the later bosses I could do on first try without any difficulty because the tools at your disposal are so plentiful and powerful when paired with passive HP/MP regen: it's difficult to lose. Even the final boss, you could stand still and just regen and use up curatives to stay alive and deal damage without need for dodging or evading attacks. It really does get that easy.You have many weapons, spells, and equipment to choose from, but it's clear from the very start that speed is the name of the game, as enemies will stagger or be pushed back when hit. All enemies I could find could be stun locked, although the window for some of them is very slim, like the skeletons with shields. For the whole game I used daggers and a shield, and the shield honestly wasn't necessary. Using swords or hammers can be fun, but it's way too slow to really be effective unfortunately. But that's the whole shtick of the game, that attacks take time and need to be timed as an exercise of risk vs. reward.The soundtrack is quite nice. It's very muted, subdued, but very effective in setting tone. Each of the world's locations have their own track which repeats, but it's seamless and fits the locations well. The sound design in general is very nice: I noticed if I was on the left side of the screen, audio from my left speaker was more pronounced, being able to hear water dripping or footsteps clearer, and as I moved to the right side of the screen, the sound traveled with me, migrating to the right speaker. It's a neat use of spatial audio here.It took me a couple of hours to really get into Lost Ruins but I'm glad I stuck with it. It is extremely challenging in the beginning but you quickly get into the flow of things. I did a couple playthroughs and it took me 9 hours but I was thorough and did some achievement hunting, too. There's additional modes that unlock on game end which give you specific builds or restrictions which can make for interesting second or third playthroughs. I think the value is here, it just might not be for everyone. It's a cute game with clear love in it, but the difficulty can scare some away.Setting the Deck to 7w max TDP ensures a 60fps experience throughout. 5w is good enough for 95% of the game, but there are a handful of areas where the lighting or particle effects bog things down a touch. Experience on Deck is great, but cloud saves do not work properly. Your save data will not be available on both PC and Deck, only the system you started it on.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a beautiful game that captures a stotic since of tranquility in is playtime, offers challenging metrovania combat and a cast of strong female characters, that makes this game ultimately one that I would recommend. Earnestly, I actually didn't mind this and even enjoyed it since so many times in games Consumables felt kind of worthless, but in this game they might be the difference between saving your life or needing to restart back to your last checkpoint.The story is what I call "enviromental" much of the story is told through the pixel art on the screen,  and through your own imagination. There are words that fuel the flames of creativity but, if you take just the story that you're told, the words on the screen, it's a bit lackluster.When buying this game ask yourself: Do I want to play a game where I am a cute school girl fighting through a castle against other cute, deadly creatures that both look like they want a headpat and want to rip my neck off? If the answer is yes, then this game is for you! But if you don't think the concept of playing as a school girl with a variety of spells and weapons is enough to carry a game, maybe find something else.But if you're reading this review then obviously it's captured your interest. My recommendation is go ahead and buy it- but only if you're prepared to die a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Good example of a very fun game with a thousand flaws.The characters and bosses are all very stylish and the whole thing is a joy to look at.  The plot is predictable and not very memorable but it stands fine without it.  Exploring is a lot of fun due to the wild assortment of weapons, items, and accessories you can find.  You'll never feel like the game is wasting your time, because often what you'll discover is extremely useful for what is up ahead.  The huge assortment of practical collectibles and boss rewards gives a real sense of wonder and adds a lot of variety.The downside to this is that it leads to a lot of menuing.  When you have a hundred weapons and accessories with specific uses, you'll feel obligated to swap them constantly to be gaining full advantage.  There is no restriction on this, meaning you can literally hit an enemy with a DPS setup and then swap to a defensive one during an attack phase.  It slows the gameplay to a crawl.Additionally, there is a real problem with the combat in this game, in that weapon speed is far too overpowered.  The increased action delay on using a heavy weapon leaves you wide open, often getting your attacks interrupted completely since enemies tend to attack quickly.  Due to your very low health pool and relatively limited consumables, this is disastrous.  On top of this, faster weapons are better dps anyway, and you can often just stagger enemies and use your shield and counter, rather than trying to secure a larger opening.  It often feels like the optimal strategy is to force a boss into a corner and dagger them to death while spamming food.  The spell to slow projectiles also completely breaks half the bosses.I should mention that upon completing the game, you unlock a game mode that removes weapons entirely and gives you a Castlevania 3 (or more recently, Curse of the Moon) setup with well-defined characters you swap between.  This actually removes the issue of having to menu weapons, and since the combat didn't make good use of the weapon selection anyway,  the game just feels much smoother.  Menuing accessories and food is still a problem, but it's better.  I wish that the game had been built with this as the main mode instead.Despite all of this, the game is just fun.  A thorough playthrough probably runs 10 hours or so, but boss mode was fun enough for me to sink in another several.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I thought this was gonna be some Castlevania/Momodora hybrid but as time went on it started to feel more Shantae. And this is mostly due the writing and the enemy variety which I'm sure has been a huge inspiration.I'd argue that the early part plays like I mentioned, then turns into Shantae up until you reach the late stage (think clock tower) when it goes back to being your typical Metroidvania because this is when difficultly really ramps up. And like Shantae there is no way to level up, meaning you have to rely on your gear, spells, upgrades and most importantly your wits.If you know what you're getting yourself into and can deal with the difficulty (spikes) then the game is about 6-8 hours depending on how fast you rush it like skipping achievements or not, going for optimal builds or not. You can definitely do it in half the time if you so choose, but I choose to cheese half the game due to some glaring issues. Did I mention you get the option to cheese your way quite early on? You'd think that wouldn't the case but it is. It's so powerful in fact that it can easily carry you for 80% of the game once you realize it. It's bad game design no doubt considering everything else at your disposal and makes the game quite trivial and boring if you choose to use it. But that's what I did during my first playthrough. There's a few issues with spells and certain equipment later on as well which makes the game quite trivial to the point were weapons are kinda useless (other than for achievements). Normally you aren't really expected to be carried by magic often being a limited resource, but you can go ham quite literally if you so choose at a certain point. Often if not always you have to rely on some weapon build but it's kinda pointless and sad considering the arsenal at hand. A missed opportunity for sure. As for the the weapons themselves, you'd think they cause staggered damage of some kind in this game, but nope... you have your debuffs and that's it, while it's magic that does everything else. And oddly enough it's the opposite for enemies since they are all mostly melee while having longer range. Technically everything an enemy does will make you stagger and fall through platforms whenever possible.And now unto said glaring issues if you ask me at least, which can make this quite a bad experience if you aren't prepared, namely:- Konami/Capcom/Tecmo NES era enemy placement. Although not as bad you can get chain staggered by enemies which can lead to cheap deaths if you're not careful. So plan accordingly (if/when possible).- Infamous From Software animation locks and delays. I still think this is one of the biggest banes to game design since it crept into everything imaginable where it shouldn't have been in the first place. Weapons and spells in general have an overly long windup time which is slower than the enemy, and even with certain gear it becomes very tedious to the point where you can just match up to the enemy by deflecting them, i.e arrow vs arrow which is just bad game design overall. I'd treat the exploration part more as a stealth game, especially when you have access to spells and health/mana regen. Learn the animation cycles instead of relying on brute force unless you can of course towards the end.You'd think that after 35 years (Ninja Gaiden) that meleeing certain ranged enemies would be just as easy if not easier, but think again. Thanks to "brilliant" From Garbageware it now is the exact opposite instead. Jumping and stabbing, slashing or even shooting might as well not exist as a feature unless you like 100% vulnerability because potato. There are no iframes or forms of block unless you use a shield and then only a shield, because when you attack you are animation locked for that duration regardless if you hit something or not, tried casting a spell or not. You can by no means swap from attacking to blocking (even with a short delay) like in something "modern" like for example Ninja Gaiden from 2004 or Sekiro from 2019 which means that even if you hit an enemy you will mostly likely get staggered even if they die in one hit, because remember, they are faster than you and have longer range. Even older/other metroidvania titles have some form of evade ability like backwards step which was at least useful overall wheras the roll here is only useful for evading certain traps, boss attacks and finding secrets. And the best of all, even if we had that you still wouldn't be able to use it as intended due to said animation locks.Imagine if this timeline would've gone with Capcom or even Team Ninja instead. I'd love to see a DMC or modern Ninja Gaiden platformer but that'll never happen now. So thanks From Garbageware for making gaming worse once again.- The checkpoint system is EXTREMELY half-baked. Normal savepoints work as expected but the checkpoints are really bad because you can't run to the same one again after using it, which means if you did a loop of some area (which this game has A LOT of), you now have to travel further, often twice as long (even though we're talking seconds at most (but this adds up over time) just to use the next checkpoint. I'd almost argue they should've been removed or if you can then avoid them until you cleared the area, but then you end up in a catch 42 because you don't know what's ahead until you do which makes said checkpoint useless on your first run, unless you're really struggling or not saving that often..? if you're going for a second run on Veteran or any of the Modes then they make a lot more sense because you kinda know what to expect by then, but this is obviously not the case for first time players. If this game was stage-based then I wouldn't have complained but it isn't, it's a metroidvania. And if you have checkpoints you expect them to work all the time.It's not about being hard or anything but it's very tedious because you might die due to cheap death on the next room, AND EVEN IF YOU PASSED SAID CHECKPOINT, you now have to rerun the entire area even though you passed the checkpoint twice. And since the game has story bits it can mean rerunning the same part a couple of times which happens the closer you get to the midpoint. At least savepoints are placed next to boss rooms like you'd expect unlike some games which makes you rerun the entire thing to waste your time because reasons. Overconfidence can definitely kill your mood for the game if you end up in some deathloop because you're skipping mobs or forget about some traps when skipping about.To give a better example; time is limited (shocking I know!), so if every death costs about 1min, over time that can be (over) an hour lost simply due to having to rerun the place you just visited. And trust me, this will happen A LOT unless you go at a snails place. In worse games you get punished for simply sneezing because for some reason you can't pause the game whenever which can lead to a death. Why pause could exist 35 years ago, because I need to visit the bathroom or anything other urgent at any given point and not now is anyone's guess. Oh but thankfully you can pause whenever unlike some company's insistence on not letting you do so which is somehow a feature and quite widespread because potato? Thanks said company for making gaming worse! And if you think this was a great idea then I have a bridge to sell you.Music is okay and fits the game. A bit too atmospheric for my taste and nothing to write home about but considering the length (and price) does the job well enough.There's a few other things I'd love to mention but these would fit more unto a guide other than the things I really had to mention here. But for the asking price I still think it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential from the art style and exploration elements, but there are a lot of things that set this game back. The game moves at an abhorrently slow pace, especially evident in the combat. Enemies tend to attack too fast for your slow attack animations to counter. Unlike most metroidvania which allow you to keep your forward or backward movement while jumping, here you get locked into place until the animation finishes, no jump cancelling allowed. Also if you play this game on a controller (like I did), the game uses controller rumble in response to every miniscule action you do, from picking up an item, to saving at a savepoint, to even landing after a f*cking jump. All this combined lead to me dropping the game after a mere 8 minutes, probably the fastest I've ever gave up on a game...ever. Let this be a warning to anyone hoping to get another fun, fast-paced, combat-forward metroidvania, just look anywhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly player-hostile design, and not in a hard-but fair Hollow Knight way. The game features slow, clunky movement  affected by barely visible surface effects (like slimy, oily, or simply wet floors), and a useless dodge roll with a painfully long recovery that leaves you wide open. The combat is built for maximum frustration, with even the “fastest” weapons being painfully slow. Anything that deals any kind of damage takes a comically long time to deliver a blow, while enemies have no trouble spamming projectiles and lightning-quick attacks.Aside from some charming and well-animated sprites, the visuals are murky and hard to discern, so you often aren't even sure what hurt you. The game doesn't give you any way to heal or replenish MP early on, leaving you to scavenge a menagerie of borderline useless items that heal you a couple of HP at a time.And then there are abnormal status effects. Every, and I mean EVERY enemy gives you abnormal status with their attacks. Got hit by an insect - poison! Got hit by a goblin - bleed! Stepped into a barely visible puddle of water - wet (enjoy that 50% movement speed reduction for the next 5 seconds in a middle of a fight). All effects are unavoidable and instant, and all of them will absolutely kill you in seconds if you don't pause the game, open inventory, scroll to items tab, scroll down through a long list of confusing junk, and find the exact thing that heals this particular status effect. Close menu and get a new status effect right away.Despite how frustratingly difficult and un-rewarding the “normal” mode is, the game doesn't even deem it pertinent to give you an ending, as, you see – you only get endings if you play on “veteran” or higher. On top of it all, the game is confusingly horny, to the point where I feel like it was originally meant to be an H-game that got neutered for wider release.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm reluctant to admit that I enjoyed this game since it was obviously made for weeboos, what with you playing as a short skirted schoolgirl that can find a swimsuit as an alternate costume, fighting other girls as big titted bosses (some of which are completely naked) in pretty generic dungeons with generic dark fantasy enemies. Not to mention, the generic amnesiac main protagonist seems to lack a moral compass as they go around slaughtering enemies while acting all kiddy and innocent. Ultimately, the game really doesn't even have an interesting story so I definitely think catering to weeboos was a central draw to it's presentation.Mechanically, the game shines with pretty solid effects and animations. The base combat consisting of your girl swinging swords in an arc of various timings based on the kinds of weapons you use adds some strategy to combat by forcing you to get the timings right, which can be a lot of fun, and there's neat gimmicks like pretty well done fire physics, all apparently done in the Unity engine. I'm not a big fan of all the status effects you can incur from so many enemies' attacks, and it's got that "Symphony of the Night" problem where it's not long before you find a sword that's guaranteed to be your preference over others, trivialising other loot you find which is the game's only real progress draw, what with the lack of a levelling system (which I also like). Being a Metroidvania game, I also inevitably came to points where I got lost, which is where I'm at now in the game. Lacking a real interesting story or characters that aren't terribly written under-aged waifus, I can't say I'm that motivated to move forward either. The smooth animations and pixel graphics do look pretty good, but the game might've been optimised terribly, as it bricked the computer played it on before I got the one I'm typing on now. 6/10 - I would play it again, and even recommend it to some, but there's likely better Metroidvanias that don't rely on schoolgirls as their draw, so thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: I like and also don't like this game. It's hard to explain, so I'll be simple about it.You attack really slowly, so you have to plan your attacks in advance. Only problem with this is that you encounter new enemies pretty fast and their attack patterns are so fast that you can't react right away. Some have multi-hit attacks. For instance, I encountered some slime girls, and they were easy enough to figure out, but then I found a blue one and immediately expected something different, but wasn't expecting it to be a close range activated attack that hit SIX TIMES while I was in the air and could do nothing about it. At that point I decided that playing this game wasn't worth the effort, there are other, better games that do similar things, so I'll just play those. But that's not all the issues I saw.Second most egregious issue I found was that checkpoints and save points don't heal you - at all. You collect plenty of health resources and all from killing monsters and exploration, but... The items aren't very good. It's not forgiving at all. Even Dark Souls' campfires healed you, so what's the deal?Third strike for me was the fact that most traps aren't obvious at all. I could see where the spikes come up from the ground all over the place except one, and when I hit it, I almost threw up from how bad that design is.Ways this way could be better? Make those checkpoints HEAL you. Have mana replenish itself slowly automatically. What's the point of having fireballs if I can't use them on flying enemies when I need to? The enemies attack faster than you do, rhythmically. Either increase our attack speed, or reduce theirs. Heavy weapons suck and have arguably 0 use case, since they're insanely slow to use for all the power they've got, resulting in them being lesser picks.The only thing I liked about this game really was the artwork and atmosphere. Should have gone with Ender Lillies or something.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a fantastic atmosphere. Whenever I boot it up, the title screen music just makes me feel like I'm in a dream. The art-style is on point, along with the OST and animations. Some bosses are out-of-this-world beautiful.The gameplay is very refined. You get to choose from a number of weapons that differ in size, speed and additional effects. Different weapons are not just slightly stronger reskins of each other, they are meaningfully different. I've seen people complain that the swing animation is too slow, but that is not a valid criticism: there are quick weapons with which you can outpace certain opponents, and there are slow weapons, which, granted, can't outpace some enemies but have some other advantage like range or healing or bleed. On top of that you have a bunch of magical spells, items and equipment that can help you deal with foes that do not go down easy to your usual build of choice.I want to point out separately that there are various ways to bend the environment to one's advantage, be that setting floor on fire or poisoning water. There is a lot of variability to how you can approach any encounter. There are also shields, and magic sticks, and veils and floaty boots and a lot of other stuff. And there are other very curious interactions that you should try and find for yourself.Exploration is quite good too. You don't have to visit every nook and cranny of the labyrinth to complete the game, but it will let you find: side stroies, interesting puzzles,  special weapons, special enemies and bosses, new scenery.  The game map does not feel empty in the slightest.The story is nothing special, but I did find it charming. The dialogues communicate the characters'personalities very well and the characters themselves usually have some nuance to them. Reading small pieces of lore lying about and talking to side characters made me feel connected to the world.The game does not waste your time. Save points are located in a balanced manner, they neither trivialize nor amplify the difficulty, there is a substantial challenge in getting from one save point to another and yet there is never an annoyingly long stretch of no save points.The game is also filled to the brim with content. After completing it once, you can replay it in hardcore mode or try for a different ending, or play a new story with different mechanic, or play it again with some restrictions. There are also a lot of secrets scattered around and a gallery to view your achievments.This game is quite amazing, I love it.

There's a whole system where liquids like oil, poison, or water can spill on the ground and react with fire or electricity, but aside from certain traps, this whole system doesn't come into play too often. _childDocuments_.review: Fairly short game that some have called a Metroidvania. It feels like more of a puzzler at the beginning, but then you get equipment that can cheese bosses. As I am pretty low skill level, this was nice. Due to the low hp of your character, it seems intended that your repeatedly die and retry.Scaling: The game starts out quite hard, but then gets relatively easy. The hp scaling of enemies is too flat. While you can still die from a single enemy, the regular enemy battles are still pretty quick. Weapons/Spells: I like the variety. There's a multitude of ways you can get through the game after you've run the past the first area. However, there are significant issues the speed variation in the weapons make many weapons next to useless unless you really like handicapping yourself to hone your skills. The enemy reactions make many slower weapons unusable.  While it's intended that you use specific weapons/spells for different areas of the game, you can eventually cheese through with 3 or 4 after the first half of the game, especially if you pick ranged weapons. Bosses: I do like most of the bosses, and definitely died the first try on most phases, but felt some satisfaction in getting the timing down. It's weird that they have the order of the items from the bosses that they do. It definitely could have done with more balancing, but was still worth playing.

Not worth your time unless you have nothing left to play. Instead of going into every issue I have with Lost Ruins I'll summarize it overall. The game isn't broken but it puts forth the minimum effort to make just about every aspect barely passable. This genre is too competitive for these kind of entrants to be positive recommendations.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty well made for the content it gives, but the additional endings are pretty difficult. As for the 'clunk', the combat is slow but people are assuming it was made poorly or badly, just like many other games some weapons swing faster than others. The game becomes a joke when you use utilize magic as it just shreds bosses, and that is where the endings come in, aside from the free chest in the catacombs you have to beat the game without opening gold chests until a certain point. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This is game is just a joy.  The area, level design, and enemy mechanics work together perfectly.  For the first time in, maybe years, I never felt the need to check a wiki or a guide or google mechanics.  You just kind of experiment and progress.  It's a good time and a callback to the best the genre has to offer.The 'good ending' is even spelled out fairly early.  No hidden mechanics, no easily missable requirements, the game just tells you "Don't do X" and if you don't you're on the right track to the good end.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: The inventory is a pain in the a** to use, and you have to use it a lot. It's great that spells and weapons feel different, and that different enemies are susceptible to certain effects, and you can even cleverly use the environment. But the slow weapon selection takes all joy out of this, and the same goes for consumables and armor pieces. If the items were at least sorted by the effects they cause! Why there are two different mechanisms for saving is beyond me. There are  which let you save your progress permanently, and you can even manage multiple savegames for some weird reason. But then there are also these  that only act as a temporary checkpoint mid game. And they can only be activated once! So if you pass the same checkpoint again, your progress until then will not be saved! So when you die you often find yourself in the position of having to do a lot of busywork like talking to a character or picking up items again and again. It's just a frustrating experience.There's also no real sense of progression or accomplishment. There is no levelling (which doesn't have to be bad in and of itself, but it is in this case) and most items are utterly boring and don't have any advantage over the stuff you already have. Buying items is also almost completely useless. I could go on about graphics, combat, and other silly design choices, but these are the biggest deal breakers for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I liked the game.Clearing quests helps a lot with sustainability of HP and MP (f.e. that one bunny-like weapon, that regenerates MP when you hit it).Gameplay-wise it is entertaining. Encouters may be challenging depending on how quick you adapt to each new type of enemy and boss. Visuals are pleasant to the eye, that is if you don't mind pixelated anime-like style. I also enjoyed some of the OSTs throughout the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't qualify that game as a Metroidvania, as the platforming elements, or the backtracking isn't complicated in any form.What makes up for it are the graphics and the "survival" elements in the usage of weapons, traps and environments that encourage the player to try, die and retry lots of different strategies.Game is quite short, but a completionist can close the tale in under 40 hours

_childDocuments_.review: surprisingly decent game but many small issues, rock paper scissor gameplay with the right weapon combat is trivialized and using wrong weapon will put you at massive disadvantage, art and animations are nice, the game is a lil sus do not let anyone saw you playing this, map design is pretty good but can be confusing to traverse due to lack of detail in map, puzzles are janky and no much explanation making a small mistake irreversible forcing you to reset the puzzle by leaving the area, you need to manage save files to make the game easier otherwise you may have to do things all over again and to manually save you need to travel to a nearby computer making it a little tedious at times.overall a pretty good game with several janks, a fun experience nonetheless

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game! The magic and environment interactions are surprisingly deep for a kickstarter metroidvania. The art is great and bosses are all memorable, music is great as well. Not a great balance between punishing normal difficulty or face-roll accessible mode for your first playthrough, but once you get the hang of the mechanics and rolling behind enemies it's not so bad and gear selection for the area/boss you're in is vital. Pretty short but extended with special modes after beating the game, witch mode, assassin mode, and play as the bosses mode, and 3 endings. Hidden gem and quite a unique experience all together.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommended this game, but give a warning.  Accessible (easy)  is too easy and the other difficulties start off too hard.  The difficulty curve is very steep and doesn't level out until after you gain a few items that give you enough health and mana to deal with the combat. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: It's unfortunate that this game has been left in a buggy state, as it seems very enjoyable and relevant to my interests. Lost Ruin is a very difficult action adventure game that doesn't give the player the advantage of being able to level up. The player character is limited to the items and spells that she finds as she explores the castle she wakes up in. I got about 40% through before the frequent crashes became too much for me to bear. The achievements were also apparently broken, popping up on the Steam overlay several times as if I had completed them when I was no where close (popping the award for beating all the bosses after beating the first boss). I thought i could at least get past the crashes in compatibility mode, but I just got hit with another freeze. I'd be interested in coming back to this and pushing past the difficult game play, but not while having to deal with so many technical issues as well.e: I wound up returning to this game to give it one last try, and while it did crash on me one more time I was charmed enough by the gameplay the press on. I don't know that I can recommend the game at full price with its current bugs, but I don't think it's fair to negatively review a game that captivated me enough to pull me past numerous barriers.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: People say this is a very hard souls like on even recommended difficulty and I have to disagree. While the initial difficulty is quite high, once you unlock a few accessories and find better weapons then the game is pretty easily doable in the 4 hours it took me to reach one ending. It seems there's a myriad of different modes and difficulties, so I'll explore them. But it really isn't that hard to get into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Item/equipment management was pretty bad. Could have used an easy item swap mechanic ala dark souls. Game is technically a metroidvania but is kind of a hybrid and once you focus less on the combat/action and start playing it like a survival horror it takes off and you have an aha moment. The first 20% of the game is extremely hard for some reason. Early on it is more about item management than combat until a good chunk of the game is completed then it becomes pretty easy once you are able to equip a certain type of item which I wont spoil. There is lots of options for builds which I really truly enjoyed as each one presented different challenges and strategies for gameplay and were different enough to have much enjoyment from changing up my build every so often for fun. Straight playthrough probably 12-15 hours to complete if you do most of the content. I 100% the castle and defeated all the bosses and completed all the quests but didnt get all the items because you would have to grind for money to buy them all tbh. Some of the bosses are pretty easy near the end as well. I got this game on sale and I would play through again if I didnt have 1253125 games in my backlog. But it gets points for originality because it doesnt try to be castlevanaia it kind of does its own thing which is really cool. Also some clever design ideas and tricks are thrown in here and there that put a smile on your face like the designers were being pretty creative. (more games like this and less games that just try to copy older games) =) 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good game, it's very short (i finish it 9 hours, but im sure u can finish it in less time) but when u want to play a good metroidvania with very smooth animations and and beautiful art (and a lot of waifus) this is your game.Also have re-play modes, and didnt try it but they are very interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

Hope to see similar titles in the future.* Several difficulty options to cater the different palettes. * Soulslike simple to learn but hard to master combat.* Weapons have different animations and unique abilities.* Equipment, spells and items with interesting modifiers.* Weapon, item and equipment synergies leading to different builds.* Anime girls all around. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game. Unique mechanics and design choices. Cute art. Not too difficult. And for those who are looking at this game specifically because of the metroidvania tag let me tell you that this is not a typical metroidvania in the sense that there is zero backtracking required in this game. This for me is a good thing because that is the one feature of metroidvania that I find a little tedious. This game is more accurately described as a mild action platformer. Everything in this game requires more thought and planning. If you think things through and use your items generously, then combat becomes pretty trivial. However, if you go in without a plan, don't use your items, or start button mashing, then you will die immediately. Definitely worth it on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, it's a very good experience. Kinda hard and unforgiving even in recommended difficulty but it's really fun. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a solid metroidvania that seems too difficult at first, but once you play it for a bit and get used to weapon timing and enemy attack patterns, then it feels more balanced.  The game doesn't have the special moves or enemy soul collecting of similar titles, but what's there works well and the game is worth playing through a couple of times to see the different endings.  This has one of the more enjoyable boss modes that I can recall.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet, to the point. The game play is just good enough to get you through to the end of the game. Story was mediocre but good enough to get to the end. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This game commits many "sins" of 2D action platformers/metroidvanias:-HP/MP does not regenerate naturally, even at a save point-Attacks are clunky, slow and have poor hitboxes-Movement and dodging is slow and deliberate-No i-frames at all after being hit, leading to getting juggled by enemies-Air attacks stop all forward momentum-Checkpoints are single-use (until you hit another checkpoint)-Status ailments everywhereDespite all of these things, the game is actually great. It's designed to be playable with all these "downsides" so enemies are clunky and slow themselves, healing items are plentiful, and hard saves are frequent. You can eventually find items and spells that will allow you to consistently heal your HP/MP as well as deal some decent damage. The story is pretty good and it doesn't overstay its welcomeThe main character's idle animation is ridiculous though.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a beautiful anime metroidvaniaRating: 8/10The anime art is really beautiful with a fitting soundtrack and some action. I might try 100% in the future but I'm not sure.It's pretty skill dependent and also you can choose the difficulty if the game is too hard but it was quite easy and linear compared to some other games.Pros:Beautiful anime artGreat soundtrackGreat entry level for people who never tried this genreShort gameCons:Nothing reallyNeutral: Replayability is to be desired but most of the time game like this you just come back out of nowhere and play it again.

_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely clunky controls, but once I learned that combat should be avoided and slow weapons are impossible to use, I managed to stick it out to the end. Nothing particularly interesting story or gameplay-wise, but the art is pretty cute. I'll point out the things that I found particularly egregious though. You lose all momentum when you attack, so I got killed or fell a lot by dropping like a rock straight into a pit until I got used to that. Items can get lost in the background art sometimes. Usually, it's just unimportant enemy drops, but I spent an hour unable to progress because a boss dropped a key and I didn't see it because it blended in and you have to pick up items manually for some reason. Finally, there are no I-frames when getting hit, so certain enemies can just wombo-combo you to death if you're not careful and that never feels good. Also the inventory menus are hard to read if you're colorblind.It's not the best game I've ever played, but aside from the rough edges, it's passable if you have ~5 hours to kill.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. _childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Stylistically unique, tad short but interesting game. Combat is very janky, sadly simple as that. If you approach it expecting just another standard metroidvania only with fun pixel art style, you're gonna get disappointed and/or annoyed.Worth checking out still, I had fun with it and am willing to spend more time to complete higher difficulty and other game modes. _childDocuments_.review: Reading some of the reviews I thought I was going to get filtered hard but I think the game on "Recommended" has the perfect difficulty, you just have to be careful, consider your items and use them, I'm one of those who hoards items and barely pays any attention to status, bonus modifiers and such yet I was constantly looking forward and gearing for the next challenge, I hit some walls ofc but checkpoints are plentiful as long as you prevail you will make it, if I did I'm sure you will. _childDocuments_.review: This is a metroidvania with souls like mechanics and quirky anime girls you may or may not care about. There are outfits and items you collect that benefit you (such as  a swimsuit so you can cast shock while standing in water without dying and oven mitts that protect you from fire). You start off with low hp (20 total). You recover your hp by using items that work like estus flasks, so you can die while healing. There are status debuffs, such as bleeds, that can instantly kill you.The level of difficulty and the time spent playing this game is mainly reliant on which difficulty you are playing (there are a bunch of them). IF you are playing on the default difficulty, be prepared to basically die all the time. the game is not "short". It's the same length as your typical metroidvania, and said length is based off game mode/skill/ familiarity.Having never played this before, I just downed the first boss and made it to the second boss in just under 2.5 hours. Most of this time was spent dying constantly.Fun game. A bit quirky with it's themes, but fun none the less.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. A little brutal at first but once you get the hang of the combat and how to use the correct weapon/spells the game seems to unlock. Attacks are queued similar to souls games. I went into this game thinking it would be more of a platformer but once it clicked with me I started to enjoy it more and more. _childDocuments_.review: Bought the game around launch but it slipped down my list of games to play, I should have played it sooner because I had a lot of fun with it. Decent story, fun characters, plenty of different skills and weapons to mess around with.Game is a little short but the extra modes you unlock on beating it made up for this.

_childDocuments_.review: there just isnt enough clairvoincy.  flys for example, flout just above were your projectiles go, they lob their attacks and you have to prep your attacks because frame reaction time is so slow, even on weapons labled "fast".    the consumables are the only way to regain health and mage abilities, most of these are fount after killing enemies, however some can be found in rooms they are always dangerous. there doesnt appear to be a enemy spawn rate. thats cool, but i  mosty try to kill them all and it seems as though that is a bad decision, you might be able to get away with avoiding most enemies. the progression is slow and i havent seen any new arias yet after an our of play

_childDocuments_.review: What could I say about this game? To start with I got my first ending during 1 sitting. Game is a little bit on the short side. This is a plus for me cause of shallowness of gameplay. Almost every mechanic is accessible from the start and there is a little variety to that so 5 hours is a good sweetspot between engaging gameplay and exhaustion. You just simply have no time to get exhausted. Bosses have clear counterplay and telegraph their attacks very openly. To touch a little bit more on bosses, I simply love their pixel art (and that they are all female ^^). In the comment section is  easy to see some comments about high difficulty level of this game.  This is simply not true.  When you know what to use, the game is just easy (if you want easy gameplay stack life regeneration). But there is some place for artifically increasing the difficulty by playing build that cannot facetank like 90% attacks in game.I like the variety of weapons, spells and artifacts provided by the game. Everybody can find something that they enjoy using. The combat feels very heavy and clumsy. It may be considered as a minus but when you think about it for a little bit longer you can find some plus that comes out of that. Namely when you design this clumsy system every slice or spell feels like it was turn based. You have pretty capable dash with some iframes so you can find analogy to every single souls-like system of: you slice - end your turn - enemy turn starts- enemy slices you back/you dash- your turn starts. Overall I moderately like this game. If you do not get it for cheap its just not worth. But for a humble inclusion the game holds its own.I would give it 5/10 but for quality pixelart anime tiddies the score is raised to 6/10. Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost Ruins

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a masterpiece on the level of Hollow Knight or anything, but definitely was a fun way to spend a weekend for me! _childDocuments_.review: I got this game as part of a Metroidvania bundle, but having played it for a while now I would consider it a worthwhile purchase even at full price. There's a bit of a learning curve but not so much it's frustrating, and a single playthrough is long enough to be fun but not so long that you'll hate playing multiple times to clear the extra game modes and get all the endings.Side note: I could have done with a little less breast jiggle on the characters whose sprites are large enough to animate that way, but it just felt silly and unnecessary rather than actually off-putting.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't necessarily all this a metroidvania.  It's more of a souls-like platformer.It's very fun and exploration isn't clunky.  Some enemies are a little cheap and can stunlock you into oblivion.  After you beat the game once you can play a secondary mode as three of the bosses which is very fun.Combat is fun and rewarding once you get the hang of it.  There's really no "gun's blazing" strats that work and all of your attacks are fairly slow and lock you in place for the duration.  The boss mode fixes that issue with one of the characters.There's virtually no ability gating.  Some treasures are locked behind abilities but the whole map is accessible without any extra abilities.My biggest gripe is that free Healing is virtually non-existent.  When you die you are teleported back to the last save point with the amount of HP you had when you saved.  so if you saved with 1 HP, you're SOL until you find food to heal with.  Healing potions are expensive and the a lot of the food that drops  applies healing over time so in the middle of combat it's not usually viable.  The best way I found to heal for free was to equip the purifier and stand in the water at one of the portals you find.  But even then it's only 1HP/sec so you'll be standing for at most 40ish seconds for a full heal.  Once you get the staff, MP becomes a lot more manageable too.Overall I give this a 6.5/10.  Good platforming soulslike, bad metroidvania.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ruins is a metroidvania with methodical combat that emphasises adapting your equipment and weapons to suit the situation. It introduces small yet meaningful changes to its genre, but the tedious UI hampers its execution.  The most apparent aspect of Lost Ruins is its visuals — a contrast of clean, anime-styled characters in a grimy, somewhat realistic environment. It’s a compelling aesthetic for those who like both styles. With its pretty pixel art and portraits in gameplay and dialogue, if you like what you see on the store page, you’ll like what you see in-game.  Lost Ruins also has adequate character animations overall — both in visual appeal and for gameplay purposes. The main character’s idle animation is incredibly animated, in two senses of the word. Environmental lighting is also subtly animated, giving everything a glow that makes enemies and your character easy to distinguish from the background. Most enemies have the appropriate wind up before they attack, giving you a fair chance to dodge and counterattack all but the fastest enemies.  However, similar to older metroidvanias, the main character’s attack feels janky. Every weapon has the same overhead swing at a constant speed, based on their speed stat, so there’s a lacking sense of heft in the heavier weapons.  In spite of its combat animations, combat is still interesting enough to engage in. While the weapon swing and movement are simple, the equipment you obtain over time are diverse and situationally useful. It’s a game that rewards adaptability; swapping to the appropriate equipment according to the environment and enemies you encounter will make fights easier. Whether wading through water or killing fast monsters, there is probably an item that will make obstacles easier to surmount.  As you get further in the game, overpowered combinations of equipment become available and I love it. After cautiously navigating every encounter up to that point, there was an incredible relief in simply rolling over every enemy that once gave me grief.  The need to frequently swap equipment, however, also means you have to navigate the inventory often. It’s cumbersome.  You have to press ‘down’ and ‘up’ to trudge through your extensive lists of items. Even though these are partitioned in helpful categories, these categories are each a single, long vertical column. Most of the items you’ll frequently equip or consume are in 4 categories: weapons, spells, items, and equipment.  You cannot skip ahead by jumping several items at a time. You cannot use your mouse. The only QoL in inventory navigation is the ability to change the sorting order and marking items as “favourites”. Though it’s better than nothing, the “favourites” feature simply keeps your items at the top of each long list, and still requires many button presses since you’ll likely want to keep several “favourites” (maybe six per category). Furthermore, when you want to try new items, it’ll take a while to find.  It’s a small frustration that grates on you as you keep playing on.  Fortunately, the game took me about 10 hrs to beat — including all side objectives, some frivolous achievements, and grinding for equipment and healing items.  Expanding on gameplay a little more, there’s the matter of difficulty. Having beat the game on “Recommended”, I would say I had a comfortably tense experience.  You can pause to heal in the middle of battle, but these are two key limitations that hinder such boring brute force. Firstly, the most common healing items regenerate 1 HP per second. Secondly, instant heals are expensive and tedious to obtain in large quantities. Not impossible, but tedious.  On the first encounter with a new enemy, you are given room to fight it on its own, allowing you to learn its behaviour and abilities. You are then continually introduced to new combinations of enemies, each addition a compounding threat to your life. Fast enemies allow slow ones to attack. Some hinder your movements. Nearly every enemy can kill you if you carelessly swing at them.   If you die, you lose your progress up to your last save point. In a strangely refreshing way, this classic way of handling death works well. Given the increasing prevalence of ‘running to your corpse to take back your money’ in newer games, I think I like restarting with all your money and items still on you. The consumables you spent before death will return, so you don’t have to worry about making subsequent retries unnecessarily difficult. Put in combination with the autosave point right before boss fights, I never felt unduly punished for messing up.  There is a hardcore mode, and new challenge modes unlock after beating the game, but I have not played them, so I cannot comment on those.  All in all, it’s rather . Lost Ruins’ most interesting feature as a metroidvania is that it rewards the player’s adaptability just as much as their skill with the controls. Yet, this very selling point is hindered by tedious menu navigation as you frequently swap out your equipment.  Its difficulty is well paced. Its visuals are as you see on the store page.  It’s not a must-buy, but you might like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Biggest personal peeve has to be the slow respawn time after each death.
