_childDocuments_.review: Every great idea is hindered by its execution.The combat is fast and furious, but shallow and repetitive, and the controls feel too loose. Hack and slash games live and die by their combat, and this feels like a floaty Ys game with weird timing for counters and no special moves to add any flavor to it.Turning into a raven and flying from encounter to encounter with hidden secrets along the way is a great spin on the StS model, but turning into a raven requires standing on a raven shrine, but icons for shrines and encounters only show when you are in raven mode and not a humanoid walking around, so if you lose track of where a shrine is, you're stuck walking until you find one.The card system is a neat idea, with new equipment and power ups needing mana to "play," but mana is exceptionally hard to find, coming in chests that are not marked by different icons than gear.There is potential here, but as a version 1.0 and no early access, it may be too late in development to expect the changes it needs. $30 is also a very big ask for a game of this genre, with most in its class going for $20 or less.I can't recommend it at its price point and its current state. Maybe at $15 on sale, but not for $30.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay seems to be mostly OK, tho the fact that you don't have full control over what you will play is not great.Also, moving around map in raven form feels nice, but only being able to change into said raven form from a few spots is not so great and seems like a pointless limitation.However, the reason why I can't recommend this game is poor optimization. It will often run at 80-60 FPS, but then will dip to 30 FPS for no apparent reason at all, including in the middle of the combat. Oddly once you are done with the run (die essentially) and go to a selection of menus, then one of them will have around 37 FPS (collectibles or sth) while others are 90 FPS, 200 FPS, 60 FPS on average (don't remember order, not important tho). Like why?Changing graphic settings doesn't seem to be doing much to help with this.So unless those devs fix this, I don't think this is worth picking up, even if you have decent rig and play other games with better graphics and no problems with FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: The core way you fight any enemy barely changes between runs. You are still going to try and perfect dodge then perfect block until frenzy wears off, and repeat. Bosses give you little to no openings to use charged attacks so the devolve into spamming light or heavy attack depending on what weapon you use.If this played at the speed of a souls game rather than 4 times faster it could be a niche but amazing game. but as is you are better of playing hades or dead cells for better roguellight gameplay, or devilmaycry or nier for better hack and slash combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun and feels like it has a lot of potential. However, the expansive world with all of its climbable tall objects feels pretty bereft of reasons to explore anything that isn't highlighted with a marker. There's a ton of open space, which I can spend tons of time exploring, all for no reason. Not even a few extra coins or anything else to reward my efforts to scale a massive tower.I have also encountered a pretty run-ending bug. I accepted a quest to clear a nearby group of enemies (Utlagi, in this case) only to find that they were nowhere to be found. The game still thought they were there, because the chest at the camp read "enemies nearby," but there were none present. Not only that, but accepting the quest removed the Utlagi from the other neighboring camps. too. Given that I was fairly early in the run and not equipped for harder fights, removing all of the easy ones from an entire area and preventing my quest completion killed the run.Grade for now? C.Fixing the bug and/or populating this vast world with more interesting things will definitely result in an amended review.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: I think this could be a good game at some point but after reading through all the cards the game has too offer for changing game play there is virtually nothing other then just different weapon types with different attacks. Every card does a very similar thing, your character doesn't cast magic or have access too anything else other then essentially a very easy parry and dodge system. I could see this game being fun for someone who only cares about melee attacking for 20 hours straight but the card system needs to be way more varied then "your parry now freezes, or poisons, etc. Or now you just have more health and more armor. There is something here but it needs way more too do and change about yourself for a action rogue like coming out in 2023. Also I was able to make it too and almost kill the second main boss with virtually no gear and zero effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenbound

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Game isn't trash, people expect too much. If you find an interest, give it a shot. People seem to forget that "a game is bad" ≠ "a game is NOT my style/taste."This game is by no means bad. If you're expecting a fully fleshed out open world, with hours and hours of "varied" filler content, this is not it. But, what you will get, is a world that was clearly crafted with passion and a game that's vision is so niche that it either works or it doesn't. You'll get a satisfying, challenging and engaging combat experience, wrapped in a roguelite package with light RPG elements (build crafting, traits etc) and a beautiful world to play in. If you watch the trailers and do some research, and in any way think to yourself "Hmmm, that looks interesting...", I say it's worth the try. Worst case, return it under 2 hours. A vast majority of the negative reviews I see on here list CORE FUNDAMENTAL GAMEPLAY FEATURES as cons/problems with the game. Does not mean the game is bad, just means you do not like the game. There is a difference :)

_childDocuments_.review: This one needs a few months worth of updates before it'll be a satisfying, balanced proposition. First few hours may feel good, but then the frustrating and bad gamedesign choices start sticking out more and more.So far my issues with the game are : - Not enough variety in potential builds, even after unlocking more than 70% of the total available cards, and that leads to a lack of surprise or interest from run to run. - Way too many tempting chests and camps everywhere, which would be great if the game wasn't about going for the very minimum of looting in order to survive (The main roguelite game mechanic is that looting makes elites and bosses become stronger the more you open chests and draw cards from enemy fragments). So you're constantly holding yourself back from wanting to fight and loot more. Why such a wide openworld full of enemy camps then ? - Not enough ways to earn mana, leading to a constant feeling of being low on mana. That leads to more temptation to loot camps for mana, even if you know it'll only make you increasingly suffer for that, making the whole experience more frustating than rewarding even if you manage to win every fight without taking damage. Maybe they should reward battle performance by being able to remove hatred from chests depending on how well you cleared the camp ? - There's also money in the game that you can use to heal or trade some gear. Not a bad idea, but there's so little ways to make money in the game : either open chests and hope for a money card, or go for the ONE AND ONLY quest of each main area (and that'll reward you 100 coins = 2 heals = 1 random weapon or armor or relic), I think they should have provided more quests in each area, cause if you're gonna mana-starve your players (and you need mana to use more powerful gear and relics, except from the gear you buy at the forge), at least give them ways to risk their run from fighting to earn more money and buy 0-mana cost gear with it. - I also had quite a few crashes, and some weird glitches here and there, making it feel more like an early access than a full game. + On the plus side, traversal as a raven feel great + Graphics aren't mindblowing but they're really ok + Fight animations are suprisingly smooth, and combat mechanics are actually decent (although a bit too much of a spam-fest, really).I'd like to see this game improve and challenge its own gamedesign choices to provide a more balanced, rewarding and thrilling combat and progression system.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an unfortunate missed opportunity. The concept is amazing and has so much potential but right now it is not worth your $30. This should still be in early access, devs please turn this into what it could and should be! The game systems need some serious tweaking to make the game playable without, and add more game play mechanics and featuresPros:- Cool concept- Flying crow anywhere is enjoyable- Very responsive combat and movementMain Cons: - Too much RNG: Nearly all aspects of the game are RNG and yet they expect you to build a strong character and enjoy their empty world of just fighting and doing the same 2 tasks every boss? If you even make it that far without maxing hatred.- Hatred system: Completely makes no sense and extremely limits the run to rinse and repeat tasks that are always the same. On top of that, there are so many chests to get but 99% are hatred chests and no benefit from opening it just makes the final boss and elites stronger??- Mana system: So difficult to get the mana you need to even use the cards you get which is all RNG-based on which camps spawn with mana chests or cards you get. Would be far more enjoyable if you could actually get mana more reliably.- No active healing system: There isn't one!? Compared to how much fighting you do, aka all you do, the only way to heal is a RNG card (which requires mana to use) or to purchase some healing from a town (which requires gold, and only way to get gold is RNG card or a single town quest for 100 gold)- Bugs and crashes: Mine constantly crashes during fights and the NPCs in town glitch and are invisible often.I could go on but these are the main issues I see currently. I hope they make some major adjustments to bring this game to a level of playable and more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've been playing this game for a few days.  While it's a unique concept there is a lot to be desired and honestly a lot of ♥♥♥♥ that needs to be fixed.  First, there are so many bugs that it just breaks some of the game.  Graphical bugs are an issue. _childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly one of the biggest disappointments I've had with gaming in a few years. It's like you took nothing but good ideas and the executions were just failed at every step of the way.The game looks nice, but has insanely unoptimized issues that are consistent and reproducible. OC'd 5800x, OC'd 6800XT, and 32gb of 3200mhz ram, all running at 1440p. The game runs around 90fps/140fps on ultra/medium settings, except anytime there's actually something going on. You lose 30fps on the regular with 5 or so enemies, and even more when any enemies have a transparency effect like smoke. Every time a fight ends you have the fragments on the ground to pick up, which causes FPS drops of 140 to sub 60. It's horrendous.The world is huge and offers a lot of places to go, but the world is bland and empty. All you ever come across are camps with normal, hard, or elite mobs. In between camps there is basically absolutely nothing. The game has a travel system that allows you to turn into a crow and fly around fast to navigate it. Except it requires you to walk across a certain "shrine" that turns you into the crow. These points are tedious to reach and the whole concept is pointless and made to do nothing but pad out game length. If you were able to turn into a crow at will, you'd be cutting out probably 30-40% of your game time. After every fight, you have like a 10-30 second run to get to the shrine that turns you into the crow, just to fly to another enemy camp. Other camps are JUST far enough away that it's 30 seconds faster to run to the shrine and fly as a crow, even if that shrine is in the complete opposite direction of the enemy camp.It's such a bland and lifeless world that has the experience padded extremely heavily by needless back tracking to turn into a crow, instead of it having an action to turn into it at will.The onboarding/tutorial are severely lacking. You have TWO systems (hatred) but one of them is permanent(ish) and can only be slightly reduced by beating the zone boss, and the other entirely cleared. They have the same name, which is wildly confusing, and it doesn't clearly explain what reduces which one and by how much. Needlessly confusing when all they needed to do was give them 2 different names. The game doesn't explain any status effects and requires you to read the codex, which is fine. If it were consistently so, or even if it told you READ MORE IN THE CODEX. It gives you explanations of systems like in the tutorial that require no need, like duh, press space to jump, wasd to move, but completely ignores things like the status effect system, and most importantly the luck system.The wardens (zone bosses) are the exact same each time, there's no variety and the boss fights are just boring. Just iframe dodge 2-5 times in a row and then attack while they are on cooldown between attack animations. That's it, nothing else at all. The first boss has like 3 attack patterns in total.Some weapon types are utterly worthless. Hammers and most 2h weapons are really slow and have a lot of windup on even the first swing, so they become almost useless in boss fights. Most attack animations the boss will swing at you about 4 times then retreat on the last attack and opening up a gap between you and them. With 1h or dual wield weapons this isnt a big deal as you can get in quick hits before you weave the next attack animation from the boss. With 2h weapons sometimes no matter how quick you are as the boss enters their cooldown phase, you flat out cant both close the gap AND get a hit off consistently. It doesn't make the boss difficult, it makes it wildly tedious and boring.This gets EXCEPTIONALLY worse with certain world mobs who have movement patterns where every time you approach them, they dodge back. It makes getting consistent hits in with slow weapons rare and just makes it a boring game of whack a mole.The gameworld is huge and lush, and gives you like 50-100 different enemy camps you can choose to attack, except the hatred system (the primary game mechanic) actively dissuades you from fighting them. The reward for fighting enemy camps, is that you kill them to get fragments, you collect 3 of these and "empower" them to get passive/active cards that increase/decrease damage in a myriad of ways. The empowering system causes the permanent hatred I mentioned earlier, so the more you get the harder bosses become, this is all well and fine in concept, but it just disincentivizes you to explore and fight lest you make the boss kill you in a handful of hits.The second reward are chests, these are "hatred" chests as well, meaning 1/3 cards pulled is a negative one such as increasing your non permanent hatred level (does the same thing of making bosses more difficult, but gets cleared completely upon moving to the next zone....see how needlessly confusing this is), stealing coins, stealing mana (needed to "use" your cards") or make merchants in the game (your primary way of healing) 25% more expensive EVERY time you draw one.The game definitely needs a balance to how powerful it can let you get by pulling cards, vs how difficult the boss will be, but they do not have the correct balance. And even if they did, it still prevents you from wanting to explore the game world.I got this game at 20% off and I still feel like I wasted money. They have so many interesting concepts or mechanics that are slightly off from being good, that overall it gives you a bad game. It's like if you found someone who you think looks like a perfect 10/10, but if their nose was slightly too big, that's fine they are still really good looking.But if their nose is slightly too bog, their eyes just a little too far apart, ears slightly too small, and so on, you end up with someone really not very attractive. The best way to describe the games design and how it goes from good to bad, would be death by a thousand cuts.They needed better QA testers, or people further away from the project who could give criticism from an unbiased perspective. Lastly, I tried to refund it basically the next day, but I played 4 hours (hoping the game would get deeper) and steam denied me due to exceeding the 2hr limit. The game is just meh, not worth a buy. Maybe at like 50-60% off.

_childDocuments_.review: This has the beginnings of a great action Roguelike but as many others have stated it's just not all there yet.  The worlds are vast and beautiful but practically empty. The flying mechanic is very satisfying but necessary as to keep you from having to walk forever across the vast, empty worlds. The combat is okay, not great but not terrible, very button mashy. Even with a dodge and block mechanic that would lead you to believe timing and precision were needed to be successful in combat I find mashing away at the attack buttons and randomly dodging (a lot of dodging) or blocking to be adequate. Graphics are great, art style is very cool, music is enjoyable. I've not experienced any of the bugs, glitches or crashes others are reporting though so that's a plus. More needs to be added to the worlds, I get it's a roguelite and you're not supposed to endlessly wander the worlds but are supposed to move through them kinda quickly, it puts you in that "one more run" mind set, which I enjoy but more needs to be different in each run and in each world. I've got ideas on this but I won't go into them in a quick Steam review, maybe the devs will get a hold of me...lol!For me $30 is a half price game so I really had no reservations spending the dough. Right now 6/10 with potential to be 8.5/10 or higher.

_childDocuments_.review: This MAY become a good game eventually, but even for an early access game, there is too much stuff missing here. I am no game developer, so I am not sure whether I am on the right track, but I would think that if you start selling your combat-heavy, difficult game in EA, you wanna make sure that the combat actually is precise enough to deal with the difficulty. I feel like the very basis, the combat required for the type of game this is, is not there yet. The combat feels floaty and wonky, and I feel that the fact that most camps always have 3 enemies is like a kind of an artificial difficulty. You deal with three guys with an odd AI (they sometimes get stuck, sometimes they run, sometimes they actually try to flank you), and while you focus on one, it's tough to keep the camera positioned to keep an eye on the other two. Also, and that's the first dealbreaker: If you make your game difficult, make sure your combat is precise. It isn't. Example: The grapplehook is assigned to x on the controller. I had several situations in game where I fought (with the shoulder buttons) with my thumb being all off the X, Y, A, B buttons... and suddenly, my character would use his grapple hook. Which means something is wrong about the controls. I wasn't even CLOSE to the button and all of a sudden my char attempts to grapple and gets hit. The world looks nice (the characters look a bit like they're from a 10 year old game though), but it's rather empty. There are camps there, but they are repetitive and feel like a lot of copy and paste. Not enough mana to use the cards you get and gaining hatred makes the bosses stronger, so you get punished for getting loot and trying to build up your character. Now, I LIKE the basic concept of the game, but the execution is lackluster for now. I know it's EA, but I'm not talking about the amount of content. IMO, right now, the very basis, the combat, is not good enough, not precise enough, and the card and hatred systems suffer from bad balancing... not enough mana, too much punishment when you do get hatred. I will surely check back in a couple of months, and I hope the devs will improve this. So far, I am disappointed because even for something in early access, this seems too raw, too empty and not unique enough, sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: I can definitely NOT agree with most of the negative reviews so far.The game does only offer fairly repetitive content so far, yes.But what it offers is great.Keep this in mind when buying it but also don't forget that the game just came out and there will be updates.The Graphics are nice, for that it runs fairly well and the movement and combat (only played with controller so far) feels as smooth as ever.The game is well balanced by a "hatred" mechanic, which buffs the enemies if activated.This prevents you from becoming too overpowered, oneshotting everything in your path.As someone who sucks at Souls like games i don't find it too hard it's a nice balance between Souls like and casual.The one and only bug/crash i have encountered so far was with the twin axe class at a specific camp.After that my game never crashed again.The game does not have a map!and to be fair it doesn't really need one.You have markers all over your screen to navigate and you will find your destination on the first try 90% of time.Now to adress the third party account creation.the account creation itself is SUPER EASY.It's just typing in a Display name, your Email adress and the password and then confirm your Email.You can also chose not to receive promotional emails, which i did and i haven't received a single one so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Ravenbound has a lot to offer as an open-world Roguelite. There are a few areas that could see some improvement, but its core foundation is sound and polished. I'm a big fan of this genre so to put it into an open-world environment is a refreshing take.So far, I have found the game relatively simple, which, I expect to change as I continue to play. Some of the movement is a little clunky (especially around jumps and the grappling hook), but the parry and dodge system operates in the traditional industry-format, giving you a lot of utility even if you don't have an "over-powered" run. The game is pretty straightforward. You goal each life is to cleanse the area, access the chests that don't give hatred, defeat the warden, repeat. I honestly love the hatred + card/mana system used here to level up your character each life. I understand the desire to just "run in, get items, get buffed", but this puts a little more strategy around it. You can "manipulate" the cards you get by focusing on certain camps which can cater towards a particular build that you want. Want to be a 100% crit chance swordsman, go for it, want to be a fire-guy, you can do that too. With its limits comes freedom of build that isn't seen in other games in the genre like Binding of Isaac and Risk of Rain 2.I will be updating this review as I play on, but my first impressions of the game are great! I'm excited to try out different builds, find secrets, and attempt to make the strongest Vessel possible!

_childDocuments_.review: I only bought this recently, so I missed out on all the issues with launch, all of which seem to have been eliminated or at least improved. No more always-online component, which would've been a deal-breaker for me. The Hatred system still locks you out of one aspect of in-run progression, but doesn't completely halt it as it used to., the game is simple but beautiful, thanks to the fun (and draw distance) of flying as a raven. The world isn't visually unique; it's fairly standard fantasy fare. But it still looks good and never breaks immersion. Motion is a big part of any action game, and this one does it quite well; while flying as a raven, you can really feel the speed when you dive, seeing the world speed past you in a blur. In combat, animations are good quality and just weighty enough (though there are occasional times when basic attacks feel a little lackluster).The  is entirely melee-focused, but fun and varied. It's definitely too reliant on the player getting perfect parry & dodge; the best way to maximize damage is to trigger a defensive move (perfect dodge), and that seems unintuitive. Still, there's enough variance in weapon and enemy types to keep it fresh, and it's entirely possible to do very well without ever using defensive timing techniques; it just takes longer.The  is both vertical (power increase) and horizontal (more options). What this means is entirely subjective, as some roguelike fans hate vertical meta-progression, while others find it essential. Personally, I think it strikes a very good balance between the two, giving in equal measures new things to play with and power upgrades, without allowing you to overpower yourself and trivialize the combat.I haven't gotten very far into the , but after completing the first zone, I find myself moderately immersed. It could really benefit from some more voice acting, as it's not always clear when dialogue will begin, and it's easy to miss unvoiced subtitles that appear unexpectedly during gameplay. Still, the story is compelling and the motivation for the player makes sense, which is more than most roguelites can say., I recommend it. The devs have been very responsive to player feedback and the game has very strong bones. It may have released from Early Access a little too soon, but it's still very much worth a purchase (when on sale).

_childDocuments_.review: The game overall is pretty solid, but it still requires some additional work.Now, let's discuss character progression, as it's a crucial aspect of rogue-lite games. The best rogue-lite games are those, which offer multiple reasons to replay them. Every game inherently has a primary reason for players to beat it, but I feel this game lacks an additional incentive. The progression and customization in each run are quite bland. The entire progression system can be summarized as "gain more stats," lacking exciting synergies or unique classes that entice players to experiment. There is an attempt to spice things up with status effects, but I don't think they really work well enough. Comparatively, games like "Skull the Hero Slayer" (another amazing rogue-lite game) provide not only stat-boosting items but also random classes in each run, leading to insane synergies. Even after defeating the final boss in that game, I continued playing because I wanted to explore different classes at maximum level and experiment with various builds and synergies. Unfortunately, this game lacks that kind of enticing experience.Given that this is a fantasy game, I believe the developers should explore more innovative possibilities for weapons and items. They could introduce cool upgrade systems where players can infuse weapons with different elements and maybe later even have the change to merge different types or discover unique weapons during runs that evolve and change their movesets on each level. A progression system that makes players curious about new combinations and the potential of different weapons would greatly enhance the overall enjoyment. Simply offering sword/axe + one-handed/two-handed weapon types is not enough; it lacks excitement and fails to offer players something to strive for during runs.

_childDocuments_.review: The demo for this game was my favorite game I tried during Steam Next Fest.  1 hour isn't enough time to really get in to this game.  I spent most of the time just wandering around fighting camps and never even completed the first main quest.  I really enjoy the combat in this game.  Perfect dodging and blocking feels awesome and the timing on these is fairly forgiving.  My only real complaint was that mana seemed really hard to come by so I could rarely afford any of the relics I was finding.I jumped in again when they reset the 1 hour timer on the demo a few weeks later and bee-lined it for the blue marker.  This is clearly the correct choice as you get a nice boost of mana right away.  Still hit mana issues fairly soon after.Fast forward to release and they have made some nice changes.  For one the default control scheme on controller is better when in raven form.  It felt off before, but moving accelerate/decelerate to the triggers feels much more natural. Mana feels plentiful now.  In my first run I had 9 mana in the first 20 minutes.  I'm was now gated by relic slots which feels much better, and there is a reason to unlock more relic slots.  I also like that raven vision or whatever it is called when on foot isn't a toggle anymore and is more of a one time pulse, revealing nearby camps or raven .  During the demo I'd often forget I was in raven vision.If you played the demo and really didn't like the gameplay, it probably isn't for you.  But if like me, you enjoyed the gameplay but had some technical issues and never had enough mana to use relics, it's worth it to jump back in.I haven't had any crashes yet and performance seems great.  I did have some crashes in the demo.  All in all I feel the game is in a better place than during the demo.  Defeated my first warden and looking forward to playing more.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing you need to know is that the majority of negative reviews refer to the early access version of the game, which has been vastly reworked, rebalanced, and polished since then. So, mixed reviews don't do justice to Ravenbound.Gameplay offers a unique blend of soulslike battles, roguelite progression, a deckbuilding equipment system, and an open-world environment. Sounds like a crazy mash-up, but does it work together? Yes, it works well, albeit not perfectly.Battles are fun: fighting different enemies requires different approaches, so you never get the feeling that opponents are just reskins of a single enemy type. To my liking, combats are too fast-paced, though, especially when the enemies are numerous; occasionally, there is little time for thoughtful planning, and combats turn into a chaotic flurry of blood and steel. The card-based loot system is an unexpected idea for the soulslike aspect of the game, but it feels totally organic for its roguelite side. The downside is that you have a limited number of attempts to loot equipment before negative effects start stacking, so if you have an unlucky day, you may fail to find equipment suitable for your build. Ravenbound is designed to be played in relatively short runs, though, so an occasional series of bad loot is not a game-changer.The world of Avalt looks gorgeous, urging you to explore it. And that's where my biggest gripe with the game lies: the world is painfully static and lifeless. It's just a huge map with a number of locations, where mobs are standing still, waiting for you to come and fight. Majestic ruins and monuments, mysterious caves and shipwrecks, settlements, and abandoned camps are abundant, but they lack a life-bringing narrative behind them. Like a beautiful stage scenery but with no play to enjoy. What a shame! Making things worse, the game mechanics discourage exploration: the more you loot slain enemies, the stronger mobs become. A workaround could be leaving loot untouched, but that would disable your character's progression, leaving you with little to do but roam and fight enemies for the sake of fighting.I can't help but mention a fun feature — flying around in a raven form. Essentially, just a creative realization of fast travel, but it's so much fun! I enjoy it so much that for me, Ravenbound is a 2-in-1 game: a soulslike roguelite battler and a flying simulator.To sum up, Ravenbound is a good game, but it could have been a lot more. If the devs added depth to the lore and made the game more exploration-friendly, we'd get a Skyrim-lite. But even regardless of that, the game is very enjoyable. And the developers deserve praise for having the courage to try something new and, after trial and error, polishing the game to a point where it's playable and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: DONT LISTEN TO THESE NEGATIVE REVIEWS!!! *heres why*First off, this game is amazing. From the concept, to the execution. Does it have its bugs after launch, yes. But what game doesnt, and most are near unplayable. As for the complaints and negative reviews... ask yourself this. Would that negative review also apply to games like HADES or other 2D games in the genre? Most of the issues relayed in these reviews are  not even that much of an issue.For example, the game crashing... again day 2 drop guys (at time of writing this). Let me ask you this, how many roguelike games have you played that crashed mid run only to lose all progress in that run? This game keeps you at the nearest safe point, keeping your progress and allows you to jump right back to it.The game being online to play even if its single player? I could go on about that but the list would be to tremendous to put on here.Complaints on the raven shrines and not being able to transform "willy-nilly"? Bruh, its meant that way, just as the grapple hook is meant to be a means of climbing small distances and not as a means of travel. Another complaint from the community. This is to allow for a break in between the combat. For those who havent made it to higher tiers of the game yet, Its either that or Pause cause your hands can and will get tired whether you're on KB or Controller.That is to say, This game is quite the experience. Again, from Graphics to concept, I am amazed with the flow of the game-play. The combat I'm sure will have reworks, but it flows very well considering late game you could be fighting 8+ things at once that are all elite. That being said, i will say there are ways to cheese the combat when you are fighting an enemy without SUPER abilities to stagger lock, however you can and will be punished if you slip up and get hit LOLFinally, i would give this game a good 7.5 out of 10 with the capabilities of being a 10 in the near future with a few tweaks. Would recommend to this genres gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: I think after 7 and a half hours of playing this game, I am actually qualified to give a valid review unlike these other squares lol.I'm not sure why or how other people are having astronomical issues, but the game has run pretty smoothly for me with a modern gaming desktop as well as the crashes have been minimal and have no major effect on the gameplay as you often are just brought back into the game on login about 5 seconds back.The graphics are considerably A+ Tier, the only shame is my OBS hates it for some reason, but it still ran perfectly fine on my computer nonetheless. Maybe frame capping could help some people with issues, since there is no button for that. The combat seems to take a lot of inspiration from Souls like games but made a lot snappier and fluid like Sekiro mixed with Outward. The enemy encampments are actually a valid part of the gameplay  as they constantly change between every run as well as upgrade when you beat a warden for the first time to get to tier 2 world state. Of course there will be quite a bit of dead space when you focus all encounters into these camps, but there are also hidden POIs that i'm sure most people will probably not find for quite a bit if they only go to the camps. (ie Caves, and such)Disclaimer: This game is rough, you will get punished for doing silly stuff and there is no natural healing (at least in the early game as that is where i've basically left off. You have to buy your healing with gold or get a card to heal yourself with mana. Basically the resources are relevant all the time and its rare that you aren't lacking at least one of them. For people who complain about signing up for their third party website, its literally so a game mechanic can be performed which is the other players gravestones, unfortunate for offline players obviously, but it is what it is. If thats a deal breaker thats on the company and I can't back them up on that choice. My only hope is that there is future DLC or major updates, whether paid or Added into the game over time that get people to come back or pick up the game later on during a sale or something. Maybe challenge modes (if they aren't already in could help with this as well as new cards, characters, and weapons).8/10 for now

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just good enough to bait you into thinking it's worth not refunding.  Notice how every video on display is beautifully edited, hiding the fact that the camera is incapable of clearly tracking the 3-10 enemy packs you will be engaging.The combat is repetitive in a fun but frustrating way.  It lacks consistency, as you will be hit by attacks that shouldn't have, and dodge or block ones that you shouldn't.  It's just part of the RNG.  Made more frustrating by the camera.Damage you deal in combat is similarly RNG, from crits to normal attacks a weapon's listed damage is a lottery.  Enemies in my runs regularly survived with no health.    Crashes happen frequently, which are frustrating but ultimately not a problem as I've never lost progress due to a crash.The UI will never get enough flak, for how seemingly simple it appears, it feels and functions extremely poorly.Finally, there is some audio glitch in the post run summary screen that sounds like quiet static that persists until you disable audio or leave the screen.  All things considered I'm not convinced Systemic Reaction isn't some kind of research company designing 'gameplay' experiments designed to needle users in order to test just how obnoxiously a game can be designed and still sell units.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR : wait for a big sale.the game is very fun, roguelites are naturally appealing imo and this one doesn't bank only on the character building fun but actually has great combat, quite a bit of enemy diversity, and good boss battles. it's at its core a really good game.BUT it's janky af :bugs, lots of them, including but not limited to : enemies stuck in decor sometimes preventing you from getting the rewards you get after camp clear altogether, or making you lose time to try and clip the mob through walls if possible (while the game is timed, you get bonus rewards after each boss if you got there fast enough), got myself stuck inside some decor once, had to abandon run. sometimes cards you play just don't take effect, wasting both the card and your mana for nothing. can happen for buffs you play or the rainbow card that leads you to a pot of gold. had an instance where the pot of gold spawned below ground too, with no cave nearby, wasting both the card and the mana too.random freezes. and i've got a powerful rig so that's not the issue. the freezes don't even stop what's happening entirely, quite a few times an enemy would prepare an attack --> game freeze --> instant hit when game unfreezes.perfect parry randomly stops giving temporary invulnerability.tear not being cleansed when enemies around it have been defeated.by the way, the more you play during a single session, the more bugs you get, the best way to proceed imo is to restart the game in between each run.some more jank : the camera is absolutely terrible, steer clear of any walls / decor the camera might get stuck behind it, the lock on camera isn't nearly reactive enough, and the camera is probably too close to the character for what the game throws at you, especially during the last boss fight where combat effects can regularly block your vision. overall the action lacks visibility because of the camera, even though you can get used to it / there are ways to work around it.worth mentioning the game is pretty short too, took me 14 (steam) hours to complete and from there it's just more of the same, although i feel like the game has a lot of replayability since it has a pretty decent item pool and the combat is good/fun.so yeah overall i'd definitely recommend playing this game if you like roguelites and/or action games, but the amount of jank and the amount of content doesn't justify the asking price imho. wait for a sale :)

_childDocuments_.review: Experienced a couple of crashes (which I submitted reports for when prompted) so hopefully that's just some early issues that can be fixed. I love the concept for this game so much but it falls short because of its main appeal: the flying.I don't know if I'm missing something but the flying doesn't work how I thought it would. Once you start flying its at a constant speed. If you change it, it doesn't gradually change your flight speed, it feels more like an all or nothing situation, it would be nice instead if you accelerated so there was a range of speed instead of just fast and super slow. This would especially nice when diving so you don't lose control of the speed so easily, for instance holding lightly on the trigger (assuming you're using controller) then it would control the dive speed so you didn't just speed past everything.I haven't played too much because of the crashes but I quite like the play style of this, I like rougelike games and from the little I played it was enjoyable!A few other things I noticed:• Flickering glitch where you get mana from the Hatred Pillar things (it was the blue mana crystal flickering)• I was in combat with a group of 3 enemies and the final one seemed to be invincible for like a minute so I kept attacking and eventually its health started to go down properly• Dialogue boxes disappear too fast, at least for my liking - I would suggest making the player press a button for them to disappear and maybe adding a setting you can change if you do want them to disappear automatically or maybe just extend the timer• The account creation (as others have pointed out) is unnecessary, it shouldn't be there and neither should the "always online" part of the game, especially since it is single playerI didn't want to be too negative because this game is really promising, I think the criticism I provided is constructive but here's a few positives:• The landscapes are gorgeous, flying around as the raven is enjoyable for the views alone, even if the speed control is not what I would like it to be• The combat is satisfying when you get the timing right for dodges• The visual style is still gorgeous up close when you are fighting in vessel form• The overall concept of the game is very unique

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Ravenbound for more then a few hours now and overall I've had a pretty fun experience playing it. The game provides a pretty unique take on the rogue-lite genre, featuring easy to get into combat and game mechanics. I love the concept of playing as an immortal raven, possessing different vessels each run. Every time you die and re-progress you learn from your past mistakes- creating better builds each time.While I've had a blast playing the game exploring its vast world and combat I cant ignore the polishing/content it lacks.- The map is huge and flying through different environments looks visually stunning. However, while the landscapes change the enemy variety is generally the same and starts to feel repetitive. I'd love to see greater variety between different enemies, maybe even different objectives between each camp. Currently, its kill an enemy, get a chest, repeat, for a big portion of the game.- The build variety with all the unique cards definitely adds a sense of refreshment between each run.- Unfortunately, the in-game quests are pretty bland and repetitive with no varying rewards.Overall, while you can have tons of fun playing the game alot of the content isn't as fleshed out as it could be. I'm excited to see what updates are to come in the future but the game does not feel like a 1.0 release as of yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit surprised by all the negativity, and that's what prompted me to write this review.I've only ever played a few rogue-like games, and have never really been a fan, but the open world concept really appealed to me. I was on the fence after the bad reviews, but watching some game play sold me, and so far I'm really liking it.The Good:- The whole game looks great. I wish there was a photo mode because flying above the landscape as the raven would make for some awesome desktop photos.- Combat is quick and punishing. I've only played sword and shield so far, but I really like darting back and forth between enemies, blocking and reacting, though it's quite easy to get cocky, thinking you can't be touched, only to be smashed into the ground over and over and lose half of your health in a second or two.- I really like the progression. There are a lot of folks complaining that the flow of mana, and therefore the flow of upgrades, is too slow. Having not played many games like this before, I see no issue with it. I had my first character for over an hour, and had him fully geared with relics (which require mana) in 45 minutes. If mana was easier to find, I'd be fully geared too quick, and that would leave little incentive to continue.- I have had zero performance issues at 1440p with everything on max. No crashes, no stutters, nothing. Ryzen 5 3600 and 5700XT.The Neutral:- The world could be more alive. 90% of the time you're going from camp to camp to clear out a few enemies and open a chest. Roaming bands of enemies, world bosses, or other things to do would be awesome. I have found a few unmarked locations that had enemies and loot though, so that's a good start.- Always online is a bit of a bummer. While I get giving players the opportunity to find the graves of other players and gain some of their cards, that's not much of a positive given the servers could crash at any moment.- Creating a separate account doesn't bother me, but it also feels unnecessary. So many companies think that people just can't wait to receive email updates about what they're doing, but I'm willing to bet most people don't really care.The Bad:- I can see this getting repetitious relatively quick. I'm guessing that that's kinda par for the course with these types of games, but it would be nice to have more quests or activities to vary up the game play.Overall, I really like this idea. It feels like a mix of a few different genres that come together to make something unique. I hope they continue to add more and more to make it a real gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Ravenbound does not make a good first impression. Post tutorial, you'll realize that you will regularly be rushed by multiple enemies with poorly telegraphed attacks and large health bars. You're given the ability to do a perfect dodge and parry, but with multiple enemies rushing in at all times, this creates a mashy, hard-to-read mess. And you can't kite single enemies away from a group.To make matters worse, because the combat is typically group combat, the only way for the game to accommodate so much spammy, jumpy, slidey awkwardness is to place it in large, mostly flat arenas. That flattens (literally) the environmental design of most combat encounters (or at least the early ones). Regardless, I can't imagine wanting to play tens of hours of this combat when the basic mechanics are this loose.Finally, this game is bizarrely online-only. The devs say that this is because they want to have social features. But Nioh and other Souls-like games have social features and also an offline mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the game at $29.99. Although..Pros:*The music is really nice. *Graphics are nice. Runs well locked at 60fps, max settings.*Combat feels nice enough. Raven flight mechanics are great. *Controls actually feel pretty responsive to me (I read some other reviews). I'm using a PS5 controller and have been since I started playing. Cons:*Making that Apex Connect account almost made me ask for a refund. Knowing that the game requires a constant internet connection despite being a single-player rogue-lite makes me question the developers. I read their statement online regarding this and I personally don't think it justifies the decision. *Should have been released into early access, nevertheless, there are balancing issues. Specifically with the loop of mana RNG from chests, and gold acquisition. I'd suggest these two be more streamlined.*The currency used to purchase traits after a run is nice, but feels 80% useless. Sure, getting the axe boy or dual swords is cool but I'm sure they aren't much different than the other three and I'll probably go back to longsword anyhow. *The cards I get don't excite me. Maybe one or two that increase my raw damage or give me mana / gold(because I'm usually starved of one of these two). *Status Effects are useless and it doesn't feel like it adds more fun to the game to pursue a build around them. Devs could make the different vessels have elements attached to them (fire, ice, whatever) and use cards in a run to augment / enhance this. *In-game sound needs to be improved. _childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game, I'm not very good at it but it is fun. It is an open world roguelike game where the world is kind of static but the enemies in it are randomly generated every time. The gameplay loop is basically choosing a character with a certain weapon type and random trait, going into the world, defeating some camps of enemies, upgrading your character with the loot from those camps and finally confronting a boss, rinse, repeat. The metagame is unlocking more races, traits and equipment based on thing you do during a run - a sort of an achievement system that gives you more gameplay options, or by spending scrolls that are rewarded for defeating enemies and bosses or for doing certain weekly or daily missions. So far I haven't done a single mission and I have amassed quite a number of those so your progression is not time-gated in any way.The upgrade system is based on cards that you randomly find or rather draw by either defeating a number of enemy camps and combining the fragments of loot you find from them or opening a chest. Drawing cards can also empower the bosses you meet so it is a balancing act between what you need to upgrade your character and how powerful you want the bosses to be. The gist of the system is that the more cards you draw more fragment slots will get locked by "hatred", additionally opening most chests require you to temporarily fill one of the fragment slots with hatred in order to obtain the loot in them. When you combine 3 fragments each of the slots that is locked by or filled with hatred increases the damage and health of the bosses by 5% instead of giving you an option of a card to choose. Eventually all of your fragment slots will get locked at which point there is no point in further exploration in the area and you would be kind of forced to confront the boss to progress further.The cards you find usually give you mana or require mana to use. The cards that require mana are gear, gear upgrades, talismans or gold. You can also find cards that unlock the amount of talismans you can have equipped at the same time. The gear is generally in two camps - weapons and armor. The weapons give you damage, armor reduce the damage you take. Both can also have secondary utility effects that either increase some of your stats, provide bonus effects on certain actions or give you bonuses against certain types of enemies. Gear upgrades upgrade the primary stats of your gear, nothing really interesting except that they are not transferable when you change your weapons and armor so you should have your final gear chosen before choosing to upgrade. Talismans provide more of those utility effects that some armor and weapons provide but they are even more varied and give you the ability to specialize on a certain playstyle even more. Gold can be used to heal, buy certain items at the blacksmith that do not require mana to equip, buy random item draws or unlock more talisman slots.Probably the most significant choice at the start is the choice of a weapon. So far the selection is sword and board, twin axes, twin swords, two-handed axe and two-handed sword. Each of the weapons have light and heavy attack combos, empowered(held) light and heavy attacks, dodge light and heavy attacks and air light and heavy attacks. The execution of those is the same for all weapons but the feel and usage of those attacks even between weapons that kind of look the same on the surface is different. Two consecutive long runs with the same weapon type though feel kind of samey and although it is possible for them to play differently through choosing specific equipment during the run it is not guaranteed because of the random nature of the beast.The second most-important choice is the race. The races do not give you additional actions but rather change how you progress during your run by giving you different resources for discarding cards you do not want to use. Humans get gold for discarding cards, elk-people get mana and wolf-people get 10% permanent damage bonus. So far I think the wolf-people bonus is overpowered but that might be just me. Oh, wolves also have a faster out of combat sprint that is pretty convenient for getting around on foot.Enemy variety is pretty decent for the beta - there are normal humanoid camps where you basically fight bandits from the playable races, goblin camps, where there is a horde of weaker enemies, also a few types of undead, spirits, spellcasters, trolls and treants. There might be other enemy types that I haven't seen as well but those seem to be the general ones. Each type of enemy can exist in normal, hard or very hard camps on the map that are marked with different icons depending on the enemy type and difficulty. The zone bosses are basically larger humanoid dark knight figures with different player-available weapon types and you can unlock the player weapon types by defeating them. Based on the room where you choose which boss to go after there are more boss/weapon types planned for the future.Except combat and scraping up a build I would not say that Ravenbound does a lot. There is some very rudimentary platforming with a grappling hook that you get but it doesn't really feel all that great and you could not really say that it is a challenge as you can become a raven almost at will and fly anywhere you were not able to jump or grapple on. The flying can be fun especially with the gain of speed for dipping downwards but it is more of a fast-travel mechanic than an actual gameplay element. There are some snippets of lore in the world to find but so far I've seen nothing all that interesting from those.Edit: Finally killed the final boss, the fight is pretty similar to the other weapon-based bosses but it has a few phases during which the weapons change. Each of the enemy types has a specific boss with an arena in the open world which you can fight and those bosses are kind of more fun than the normal level-based bosses. I hope the game gets more content in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of good here, my hopes are that with some updates this will be a very strong title.Combat is fun albeit repetitive.  Different weapons don't change much of the experience since your success is moreso dependent on timing your shield and dodges.  Some enemies and upgrades will incentivize different playstyles but not by as much as I'd like to see.While I do appreciate a game that doesn't hold your hand, there are a few quality of life changes that I think would benefit the core experience.  The big two are a mini-map that indicates locations for camps and towns, and more consistent ways of getting coins and mana.Meta-progression is poorly realized.  You gain access to more powerful upgrades, yet also fill your deck with cards that more often than not will not work with your build.  I'm also not crazy about the RNG characters when it's already so easy for RNG to mana-block or coin-block a run.  The player needs to have SOME access to consistency.I occasionally have some performance issues (especially during Warden fights) which not only cause very dramatic frame-drops, but also make the game unresponsive.  This may just be a hardware issue on my end, but I'm able to run much more hardware intensive games without issue so maybe this is something worth looking into.  There are also occasional issues with crashing and npcs not loading in.  Fortunately, the save states are very forgiving.  I also had a bug where I briefly lost access to my upgrade menu and missed out on getting an upgrade card.It's good, but maybe not worth $30 in its current state.  Could be great with updates.

_childDocuments_.review: In the spirit of an ancient Norse skald, I shall recount the tale of "Ravenbound," a game where the spirits of valiant warriors and the echoes of mythic tales meet. Let us embark on this saga, soaring through the skies of a world both wondrous and perilous.Behold, "Ravenbound," with its canvas painted in the deep hues of the old sagas. The lands are vast, and each vista tells a story, etched in the artistry of the ancients. The graphics, while not at the forefront of modern sorcery, capture the essence of the Norse world in a way that would make Odin nod in approval.The heart of "Ravenbound" lies in its combat and exploration, akin to the trials of a Viking on a quest for glory. The mechanics are robust, offering challenges worthy of a warrior's skill. Yet, in its quest for authenticity, the game sometimes treads too close to the well-worn paths of yore, lacking the innovative spark of Mjolnir's lightning.The melodies of "Ravenbound" are as haunting as a skald's song under the moonlit sky. The soundtrack, infused with the spirit of the north, complements the saga perfectly. The clang of steel and the rustle of the woods breathe life into this world, making every moment in the game feel like a verse in an epic poem.In "Ravenbound," the narrative weaves through your journey like the threads of fate spun by the Norns. The game does not merely tell a tale; it invites you to live it. The lore is deep, the world immersive, and the sense of being part of a grand Norse saga is ever-present.To master "Ravenbound" is to prove oneself worthy of Valhalla. The learning curve is steep, a true test of one's warrior spirit. The game demands not just skill but the wisdom to navigate its complexities. It is a journey for the brave, not the faint of heart."Ravenbound" is a saga that captures the essence of Norse mythology and wraps it in a cloak of solid gameplay and storytelling. While it may falter in places, the journey it offers is one that resonates with the spirit of the old tales. For those who seek to walk in the footsteps of the gods and heroes of old, "Ravenbound" is a quest worth undertaking.

_childDocuments_.review: My most anticipated game of the year so far. The core loop and game systems resonate so strongly with me it's ridiculous. To put it short, it' a rogue-lite 3rd person RPG where you run fast and hit hard. You have an open-world without any of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (cutscenes, endless dialogue, other fluff that makes games less of a game). You go from encounter to encounter, pick your upgrades and get increasingly more cursed. The graphics are decent, the scenery is beautiful, the UI is minimal during play but very polished when you open up menus.However it's also mind-boggling how little the devs have listened to the feedback for their demo and somehow made the game worse too. As much as it pains me I can understand the current bad review score.GRIPE 1: I personally don't mind the login itself that much. HOWEVER, the fact that the devs chose to make it mandatory even after the massive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ they received for it in the demo makes me question whether they have brains. The massive complaints were not addressed and the devs act as if their actions have no consequences. Now look at the game's health.GRIPE 2: They also did not address the second largest complaint. The stupid camera acceleration when playing on gamepad. GIVE US AN OPTION TO DISABLE IT.Apart from these unaddressed glaring issues in the demo, somehow the devs also managed to introduce two new ones:GRIPE 3: I can't point my finger on it but it feels like there is a new input lag. Maybe the acceleration-loving dev put acceleration on the first 0.5s of the running animation. NOT EVERYTHING IS A CAR. This game needs snappy controls. Or maybe the game needs to talk to a server on every input. If this turns out to be the case I will make sure to change my review to negative as well.GRIPE 4: My first run which included the tutorial lasted 16 minutes. I died literally on the first fight after the tutorial. I was awarded with a high-score of OVER 9 MILLION????!!! On subsequent runs the numbers were orders of magnitudes smaller but still absurdly large (300k +) even though they lasted only 5 minutes each. Completely broken score system.I still recommend it, I think the game is totally awesome and bad-ass. Devs just need to get their ♥♥♥♥ together and listen.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey there! I just finished playing this game and let me tell you, it was quite the rollercoaster ride. The exploration that seemed pointless at first turned out to be incredibly useful. It's true that many players have criticized the game for being too punishing, but I found it to be just challenging enough to keep me hooked.In fact, I was able to take down the betrayer, one of the toughest bosses in the game, with the help of some of the strongest gear available. Even then, the fight was almost unbeatable, and I had to rely on my wits and skills to emerge victorious.All in all, this is a roguelike and open-world game that requires both brains and brawn to succeed. It may be insanely difficult, but it's also incredibly rewarding. So if you're up for a challenge and want to explore a rich and immersive world, this game is definitely worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Since the last update, camps are no longer spawning enemies. Not all, but most. This whole great open world that you want to explore but cant because you get punished by the hatred system. If i was only supposed to go to 5 camps per stage, why are all the camps 500 meters from each other with nothing but emptiness inbetween. _childDocuments_.review: The one thing I think some people may have an issue with is how the controls feel. Movement and combat is very fluid and kind of floaty. _childDocuments_.review: DON'T LET THESE "BAD" REVIEWS FOOL YOU.  Ravenbound feels like a special game with a lot of potential upside.  The combat is fun, but it does have some minor oddities, like extremely brief timing windows for perfect dodge/block, and the responsiveness of the player inputs has the slightest but noticeable delay, so that also impacts the timing windows.  But once you get used to the game being this way, the combat starts to become more fluid.  I enjoy the way this game handles the rogue-light aspect, and the card system feels right (I am anxious to unlock more cards and traits through the achievements).  The look and feel of the world is great, and the flying while in Raven form handles wonderfully.  The game itself feels very stable (speaking from perspective of a gamer with latest gen PC).  The only performance issue I had was sometimes at the end of a run in which I die and the screen comes up to show what I earned, the game would crash at times on that screen.  I wonder if this is in fact due to the online aspect of the game, which for a single-player rogue-light experience, there is simply ZERO reason to have to make an account and always play online.  Ridiculous, pointless, dumb decision there.  Other than those things, the game is a lot of fun so far, maybe slightly more on the simple side of things, but that's not always a negative.  Oh, I also forgot that this game has excellent background music, but there are moments when you are traveling as a raven where it seems to reset and start over (depending on crossing regions?)  Game needs a few tweaks and cleaning up for sure, but it's not by any means broken or bad.

However I did not start playing until April 1st, so maybe issues others were experiencing have been patched out.I enjoy Ravenbound and recommend it.*Full disclosure I received this game for free because of my beta testing input.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game could use some polishing I find it very fun overall. I keep coming back to it each day to see how far I can get and enjoy doing so, so you guys are doing a good job.I feel like if certain things were addressed there would be a lot less complaining. Tears and Hatred need some kind of balancing, either add 1-2 more tears that activate when you enter the next region or perhaps make the tears harder but make them cleanse all the chests or warrior gravestone withing the area. Maybe for chests you can summon some enemies to fight to clear the hatred and for gravestones we could fight an undead version the the character that fell fell therre with their equipment.Quests and Healing could also use some improvement. There's only three ways to heal; either spending two mana on a potion if your lucky enough to find one and can afford to take it over other loot, spending 50 gold in a town, or beating a Warden. Also only 4 ways to gather gold; via the one village quest per region, getting lucky with loot (which still takes mana to use the  card), break pots for chump change, or be a human and scrap cards. An easy fix could be offering more than one quest per village. I understand why you would limit healing in a roguelite but it really sucks losing a run because you just couldn't afford to heal because there's almost no resources because you didn't choose the right race or get lucky with loot.Thanks for making a fun game, can't wait to see what future patched/updates hold for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Not even an hour in an I can see both all its potentially and all of its core flaws.1. Animations (especially for Raven Claw) are very rough and need a complete overhaul, if you attempt to use Raven Claw and turn during the animation, it simply does a 360* making you look like a stop motion figure getting turned around mid throw.2. Movement is not as free form as it seems it wants to be and ends up making it feel sluggish over all.Example: Attempting to Slide Jump completely stops all momentum the second you jumpin fact most movement options kill momentum whenever you transition between them.3. The Lack of a mantle feature also hinders the movement system as well4. The reason my playtime is so low is because my game crashed and I immediately began to make this review5. Combat feels very unresponsive enemy attack animations blend to much into regular movement and a lack of attack indicators (i.e the arkham series or spider-man) leaves you getting hit by many off screen attacks which leads me into my next point6. That you might not even notice you've been hit because other then your health going down there is no indication of being hit unless you get staggered.7. Enemies getting staggered is very random and hard to predict, most times you'll just be landing light blows and your enemy will suddenly fall over which often makes the lock on change targets despite their yellow stance meters not being filled.8. The lack of enemy attack cool downs makes landing hits without ground slamming a group of enemies near impossible because the hordes you have to fight just spam attacks simultaneously leaving no openings to actually engage.9. The Hatred system discourages exploration to an uncomfortable degree, essentially if you decide to get any of your rewards by the time you get to the boss they will have over a 50% increase in stats and that includes elites as well, not to mention 10% is often permanent for the run, it seems like a better idea to get 2-3 encounters hope to get armor or a weapon then fight the boss immediately or just immediately restart the run.10. The lack of a character creator in favor of the randomized vessel system takes away one of the core experiences of a rogue likes which is permanent upgrades or appearances outside of runs and instead also makes your starting kit randomized and makes you spend in game currency just to re-roll these vessels ( which frankly all end up looking really ugly which I also disliked)11. My last gripe is having to go to raven towers to transform, it just feels bad to be honest, most of the world is completely empty with encounters spotted between so having to go from 1 encounter just to run back to a raven tower again is super tedious.But these flaws are not so core to the experience that they are unchangeable, while I did not enjoy my experience I definitely feel like I could given the right game directions and updates, however I will be refunding for the time being as it does not feel worth the price currently

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: August 2 2024 - Score changed from 5/10 to 8/10. See edits denoted by Asterisk (**) below.Beautiful game for a rogue. Combat is very fluid, impactful, and engaging. Gameplay loop will sustain you for a fair amount of hours, and you'll enjoy the sense of power progression. I did not experience any FPS drops whatsoever, and load times were good. The freedom to explore the absolutely gigantic map is awesome. However...Progression is heavily hindered by an extremely unforgiving resource system. You may spend half an hour attempting to farm said resource - which has an extremely low drop chance. Meanwhile you are completely unable to upgrade your character because you lack that resource, and while you farm in hopes of obtaining the resource required for upgrades, the enemies passively grow stronger. So your character remains stagnant while the game increases in difficulty. **This is still an issue, but it is not as bad as it was before. The simple solution is be conservative with your resource, and kill everything in sight.**And then...You finally upgrade your character, venture out into the wilds to test your might, and the quest tells you to kill these guys over at this camp - but you get to the camp and none of the guys have spawned. So you fly away and return in an attempt to force the game to reload the assets - you get excited when you see the enemies have spawned. You kill them. You fly back to the quest giver and guess what - he failed to load into the game as well.**This is no longer an issue.**So you fly away and return in an attempt to force the game to reload the assets - and as soon as you land at the newly spawned quest giver your game crashes to desktop.**This is no longer an issue.**You restart, and to your astonishment you haven't lost any progress and you're standing where you were before you crashed. Cool. But 15 minutes later you go for a killing blow on an enemy and crash to desktop again. **This is no longer an issue.**Great game - but it's in a terrible state mechanically/functionally and I would highly suggest holding off until they patch and address the mana/resource starvation.**Great game, it is in a very good state mechanically and functionally. The combat is INCREDIBLY impactful and satisfying. The new tutorial slides you into the main game without you even realizing you are in the main game, it's awesome. Boss fights are SICK. They have added new combat mechanics, resource mechanics, and fixed most of the issues I stated in 2023. Free roam /raven flight is super smooth, the zones are massive, and it's satisfying to play. Enemies can be unforgiving if you slack off, and health regen is just like any other Rogue, so be careful.8/10 Recommended. Not a 10/10 because I still think resource gain should be increased so you can purchase upgrades sooner than later. The entire game revolves around this resource, and with it being such a massive world way bigger than a typical rogue, you have to spend a LOT of time gaining the resource to stay powerful enough to take down bosses. Not like a top down roguelite where every 5-10 minutes you get a massive upgrade. This one is a little slower, and it risks making players bored because of the resource gain being so low. At a minimum, you should receive at LEAST 1 mana when you clear an area or open a chest - or at least every 3-5 clears/chests. As it stands, you collect tons of upgrades but have no mana to use/purchase them. Whats the point in having all these upgrades if the resource you need to use them is so hard to gain? In the meantime, I am having a blast revisiting this game after all the updates.**

_childDocuments_.review: If you see a "Best played on a controller" suggestion for a PC game.just refund it.Ironically, this game plays BAD with a keyboard and mouse, and it's even WORSE on the controller.[+]>>Some special attacks are fun to execute.>>Flying over the world is spectacular and graphically impressive.>>Idea is good, but, unfortunately, not executed properly.[-]>>Flying>The flying mechanic has a joystick "pitch control" and you cannot even reverse/change it in the settings.  Flying mechanic is both the most annoying and the most impressive thing in this game.  It's a shame the devs did not think it through.>Funny thing is, devs suggest playing on the controller, but it's even worse there. Maybe they confused joystick with a controller...>>Mobs>The difficulty of this game is that mobs surround you and attack you all at once or from behind.  If you confront them or bosses one on one, the fight suddenly become very easy.>>Randomness>Randomness is the only challenging/punishing aspect the game. If you do not have good cards, you are screwed, just restart and don't waste time>>Imbalance>When you realize what cards you need for your weapon type, you just need to get lucky to get them.  And when you get them, you can either one-shot mobs and bosses, or kill bosses within 10-15 seconds.  It took me 15 seconds to kill the last boss with a proper set of cards.>>Copy-paste locations>All locations are just a copy-paste. No unique places. And that is huge missed opportunity.  This game lets you fly and see from the sky different interesting places, like castles,  but when you go there you realize it's the same one as you saw previously.>>Static objects>The most annoying thing of each locations is that every single one of them is made of static objects.  You cannot destroy anything (except vases, those are the only things you can break),  you cannot enter houses/castles, well, any interesting-looking location.>>Copy paste bosses>All bosses are the same: same mechanics, almost the same models, same boss pits, nothing unique at all.>>Rogue-likeness>Rogue-like type killed this game.  It would be much-much better if it was a single experience.>>Pointless locations.>Some locations, like World Bosses are pointless and just a waste of time and effort.There are even more minuses...Conclusion: 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a $9.99 DLC that adds a roguelite mode to an existing game. Discarding 99% of the content of the main game to focus on procedurally-generated mini-questlines to build power and go for a boss rush.It doesn't feel like a full game, and it reinforces my hatred of roguelike/roguelite mechanics in games.I feel like I'm wasting my time in a game world that ignores all of its good aspects in favor of the roguelite "loop."Well, the loop isn't fun for me.The combat is decently serviceable. It has a good hack'n'slash foundation. Dodging feels good with generous iframes and no stamina management.Because the game was released after 2019, it has a  style deflect. We'll be dealing with that in games for the next decade at least, I'm sure. But at least the parry is pretty generous in this game.The main problem is all the enemy spam the game throws at the player. Most enemies have two main attacks they use, but timing dodges or parries is very difficult with 4-10 enemies attacking at a time.Would be great to balance all of that in a game that doesn't strictly punish mistakes by starting the game over again.It must be incredibly easy to create open worlds in the Avalanche Apex Engine. This is a very large world with a lot of little towns, mines, settlements, caves, canyons, and more. And it has a lot of visual variety in biomes.Too bad that each run wastes 99% of those locations, requiring you to go to a handful of them before heading off to the boss.Exploration is a risky endeavor, as dying requires starting over, and the reward isn't very good. Maybe a card you could use, maybe a bunch you can't.The raven basically uses traversal mechanics from the  series, but you don't take any damage by running into the side of a cliff. The raven just flies above it.There's no fall damage. Great!Controlling the raven took a little getting used to, but it's pretty smooth overall. Flying close to the ground or soaring high above the world, you'll see a lot of cool locations that have absolutely no point in your current run.The bosses are hard. Not because they have a lot of intricate moves, but because they'll spam 4-6 hit combos with inconsistent timings, even for the same attack animation.The bigger problem is that, even by the second boss, you'll be doing minuscule amounts of damage. No matter what weapon cards I found, they didn't increase my damage enough to outlast the second boss, who spammed attacks.I wish Systemic Reaction would turn this into a real game.  was a fun game.  was also fun, for as long as it lasted.This game seems to have a -like foundation, and turning into Avalanche's version of that game would have made this much better. Hell, I'd take a game that was just Bethesda style radiant quests, but in this world.Anyway, I don't like that I hate this game. I keep trying to play it, enjoying a lot of it, and then getting annoyed so little of the game is fleshed out.I guess that's a roguelite, though. And I don't like them.
