_childDocuments_.review: Despite me having most of my hours in GRID 2 of all the GRID games, I undeniably love GRID as a franchise. GRID 1 with it's oddball cars and fleshed out gameplay, GRID 2 with its flawed but still fun take on the game (and modification system which allows you to make cars punch up at tiers above them) and GRID Autosport with a basically more revamped identity that sets it apart from GRID 2. The point is that despite all the previous games flaws, they still are fun to play and master.GRID Legends is not fun to play. The cars are simply not fun to drive. I turn all the assists off and the cars drive like normal. I slam the brakes with no ABS on and instead of the car locking up and skidding, it simply slows down to a stop. I take a turn as sharp as possible and what would've sent me into either an uncontrollable skid or the drift of all time on GRID 2 would just make my car lazily point towards the corner in this game. It's pathetic.I really REALLY wanted to like this game. The car roster from an outside perspective seems amazing and the graphical fidelity on this particular game is stunning to look at too. All of this sadly does not excuse the poor gameplay and soulless feel of the cars.

_childDocuments_.review: Might as well be an alpha release.I'll start with the cons.1. The player lobby is stupid. You can't adjust settings if you're in a lobby, you can't adjust settings after a race, you can't adjust settings other than during a race, waiting for it to start, you have 15 seconds. But then you wait 30-60 seconds on the results screens for no reason at all. Like come on, everyone saw their time, pressed A/X and are ready to move on. 2. There's vehicle upgrades for multiplayer that you earn from playing career mode. You can run the most perfect lap ever and people with upgrades will beat your time by 4-12 seconds just from extra speed on the straight, faster shifting, etc. And since every car can be upgraded, the stock car runs like a piece of garbage. 1st-3rd gear is great, 4th is just enough then you hit 5th and have no power. I find myself constantly switching back and forth through 4-5 just to take the S's at Suzuka(as 1 example.) Stay in 4th you're redlining. Stay in 5th you're slow. I'd be okay with it if there was an option to turn them off for the lobby. Oh wait, there is! but IT DOESN'T WORK. If you want upgrades you have to buy the car in game, but to earn money you have to grind more than Old School Runescape. 3. No Multiplayer features. No championships, no racing stats(unless you use their racenet website, and even then it's the bare minimum), no online replays to save, no option to pass lobby leadership, vote to kick someone.. Like all but one of those was a feature in the original GRID from 2008.4. If you use a wheel, force feedback is absolute dogsh*t. They advertised logitech TrueForce for GRID Legends back in August 2021 on Twitter and it's not available on release. Even GRID 2019 has it.5. The racing AI is some of the worst I've ever seen. Doesn't matter what level you put them at, on Easy they're 20mph faster on the straight then come to a crawl around the corners. On Legend they cut you off even if you're not they're "nemesis" , block the racing line completely. You can turn them off in multiplayer, except in the one game mode where literally everyone wants the AI gone, time trial. Good luck setting a fast lap with AI hogging the racing line in the corners.6. Audio mix is just awful. No matter how you adjust the audio sliders, EVERYTHING drowns out your revs, especially with the dash cam. If you use manual gearbox you'll find yourself redlining gears out of a corner because you can't even hear that you are. There's commentary during each race and it's not bad but the only way you hear it is by driving by a pole with a speaker on it. You make the most arcade racer ever but go full sim mode with that? And to add to that, the GLARE during afternoon races is blinding. You can't see a thing. There's a car with a carbon fiber dash and honestly all I could see was the reflection of carbon fiber on the windshield. Wtf is that. Guess we'll just run overcast races only guys sorry. Too many cons to mention. - There's so many more things wrong with this game and it's frustrating it's been out a week and there hasn't been a patch for anything. I will gladly change my review if they fix/add these things. These are the bare minimum expectation for racing games. I don't see how this was made and approved for release.Pros (if I HAD to give some. 1. Story mode can be fun. It's different. It's real actors for the cutscenes but the writing is a little over the top. Like F1s drive to survive on steroids level. They definitely put most of their work into story mode which is fine. 2. You can hop into some races that have already started. That's a great feature I wish every racing game had.3. Graphics are pretty good. Not groundbreaking, but good.4. Many cars of different classes to choose from. That's GRID though, they should have more in each class with an option to nearly equalize their performance. They put cars that are insanely slower than another car in the  class. I don't get it. GRID 2008 had different cars but it really was up to which cars handling you preferred.5. It can be fun with friends, and it's crossplay which I hope every racing game from EA/Codemasters is, especially F1 2022. No voice/text or quick chat, But with the right cars(usually the classes with 1 car to choose from) and good settings you can have some close racing. All in all I can't recommend this game at the moment. I just expected so much more.. As I have with every GRID since 2008, just remaster that. Please fix this game, I'm sure so many people feel cheated as well, this should've been 20 bucks. As of March 4th, 2022, RIP GRID series in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: As a professional sim racer, i can say that the racing game market is over-saturated with unfun sims that prioritize realism over anything else. I have an $800+ racing sim, and playing this games campaign was one of the most positive experiences i've had on it, and it can be said with certainty that this game scratches all the racing itches that sims like AC, RaceRoom, Rfactor, and iRacing can't. The cars in grid legends handle fantastically, and you'll frequently find yourself pushing the limits of your vehicle in order to gain positions, but never overstepping and flying into the gravel. _childDocuments_.review: Finished Driven to Glory and played a small bit of the career mode, here's my thoughts:THE GOOD:- The writing is impressive, especially for a racing game story. Whoever came up with the idea of making it a parody of Drive To Survive deserves a raise. - The game was surprisingly smooth for a 2022 game. Was able to run on High quite comfortably, only experiencing frame drops in rainy/snowy races due to the intensity of the effects. Graphics are also beautiful.- The handling model, while not as good as 2008's Race Driver: GRID, is up there as my 2nd favourite behind the original. It has a very rewarding feedback to nailing corners that not many racing games have.- The music is... incredible. Seriously, even if you don't play the game, give the soundtrack a listen. So much emotion and you can tell that the composers and everyone involved with the audio put their heart into it.THE BAD:- Driven To Glory does drag a bit, with a couple of moments where a race doesn't feel awfully relevant, especially near the beginning of the game.- There's a bug with Driven To Glory's Chapter "The Perfect Recipe" that hasn't been fixed for two years, and probably won't get fixed for the forseeable future. The fix is to play on Hard or lower to complete the race, but its still frustrating nevertheless as I was able to beat the rest of the game on Expert.EVIDENCE: - Team Names are still bugged. "Player Team" appears in the career mode's standings menu, and teams in general (to rant) don't have that much impact. Fixed car sticker sponsors instead of the selected one, mid liveries and overall a pretty shallow experience compared to the 2008 original.THE VERDICT:GRID: Legends is a good homage to its original game, while bringing a well-written story and satisfying handling with incredible graphics to the next generation of player. The customisation is weak, even compared to other games in Codemasters' catalogue (F1 and WRC have a livery editor, with WRC having a much better one.)SCORE: 7/10Great game and sorely underrated, has some issues but they're far from enough to stop me and most players from enjoying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: That said... I would recommend this game... but with a caveat. It's incredibly easy if you're a seasoned racing game enthusiast.GRID Legends is an amazing looking hands down arcade racing game lifting on the back of the Drive to Survive series on Netflix, following F1 drivers. In GRID Legends'  storymode, you play the role of Driver 22 embarking on the quest of becoming GRID World Champion. The story isn't anything ground breaking, but as someone who got bored from Drive to Survive after 2 seasons, I was actually excited playing through a similar story as myself. And to be fair: The Drive to Survive narrative lends itself exceptionally well for GRID's agressive gameplay, and playing through this was actually really fun, potentially the most fun part of GRID Legends.Aside from the Story mode and the extra smaller stories, there is the career mode, in which you set up your own team.  The difficulty doesn't ramp up there, but it's fun building your own team and driving your own races without the narrative.Gameplay-wise. Racing is great, but you need to get used to the forgiving, but a little awkward handling at times. Cars feel decently weighty and all feel different depending on what you drive. Older cars are slower, a little more sluggish to handle than sleek supercars, which in their turn are very twitchy all over, especially over kerbs and bumps.The nemesis system is back, but lasts through multiple races in your career as well as through the campaign. I felt the effects of it through races, but it isn't that unforgiving that all the nemesi (?) sideswipe you at every oppertunity (except for Nathan McKane, that guy's just a prick.), but will peek their noses up at every oppertunity, even if you can be sure it isn't going to be fruitful, of defend incredibly hard up until the point they will lose lots of distance with the cars in front. It's actually fun navigating through their antics to be fair.I've played through the career and campaign with the Legendary difficulty, manual shifting, and TC set to 1 (I don't like playing my arcade racers as sims, so I accept a little forgiveness in the handling, especially because it's that arcady to begin with.), and I have to say. It's an average difficulty if you have played a lot of racing games on higher difficulties.For comparison, WRC 10 is on 140% with moderate challenge, played GRID Autosport on highest difficulty with some challenge and played the F1 games with an above average difficulty, all on controller. GRID Legend is easy all throughout. GRID Legends is a fun game with a fun story to play through. Be aware, if you're an enthusiast you might find this easy, but playing through the story in about 5 hours is a great experience. Pick up while on sale and you should have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Alrighty, let me yap for a bit.Do I enjoy this game? Yes!Would I recommend it? Yes!Would I recommend it over other simulation games? Not really.Grid Legends is an amazing game in an of itself but its style really isn't for me. The graphics are amazing and the car models are impressive and detailed.My problem comes with how the car feels (I play on keyboard and wheel). The slightest movement sends the car so far either left or right and there is a lack of any sense of downforce. Some of the track layouts aren't thought out well and could use some work. I've said a lot of negative, so let's talk about positives! The live-action cutscenes are unconventional for the genre, and it works! It really gets you into the game. The only issue with them are when there are scenes of real people with the "fake" cars, it just seems out of place. The acting by some actors is questionable, but it's a racing game company, not Hollywood. The DLC's are generally worth it, though it forces you to race some uncomfortable races to advance through the campaign ( i dont like the stadium trucks, sorry y'all). This was all opinion, let's go facts:The menu isn't exactly aesthetically pleasing to the eye and feels like an outdated game- not in a good way. Would I recommend buying the game? Only when it is on sale. I got the Deluxe edition for $15.99 and it was worth it. Would I pay $79.99 for it? No. Even the Base game, $59.99? No. The Graphics are next-level, the actual content, is not, really. Ultimately, it's up to you. Look up gameplay and see how you think it feels. It is a different unconventional type of racing, it feels "tighter" than other racing games. It is very beginner friendly and runs well and looks amazing. It is NOT a hardcore sim but is fun and was worth the 16 dollars I spent.Thanks for reading this. I spent more time on this than I did on college applications. Priorities amirite?

_childDocuments_.review: If you don’t know EA decided to pull a Titanfall 2 and release the game at the worst possible time. It was released between Elden Ring and Gran Turismo 7. It’s like they don’t want the game to succeed and I bet they are gonna blame the game’s small release player count on other games like Forza and Gran Turismo. Small rant aside the game is better than Grid 2019 in every possible way. The new addition that is the story mode had me captivated the entire time I was playing. The acting was well done and I had no complaints about the plot. The only thing that I did not like was the fact that it was a little bit too short (I finished the story in 5 hours!). Physics in this game are mostly arcade, you are gonna get used to them very easily, I consider them an improvement from Grid 2019 (drift physics are a little wonky though, so don’t buy this game if you’re expecting a drift simulation type of game). The sense of speed in this game is really good thanks to the camera shake, motion blur, and the upbeat soundtrack (the cockpit view has an even better sense of speed). The cars themselves are detailed and sound good. Graphics, even though I see some people complaining about them, I find them to be good, maps, weather and the overall lighting are fine. The only complaint I have about this game is that the career mode can be a little bit too grindy. You don’t get a lot of money and XP for races and I don’t like the mileage requirement for races and upgrades. So all that being said, I consider Grid Legends to be a good follow-up game from Grid 2019. Such a shame EA decided to botch the release date.

_childDocuments_.review: The hackneyed idea that racing is just about circling the track is trying to change the arcade racing Grid Legends.In the thirty-six races of the basic campaign, you will drive the cars of the underdog Seneca team, and in the classic story about supposed "losers" who, despite adversity, will eventually win, you will sit behind the wheel as the mysterious driver with serial number 22.I didn't expect anything from the story, and maybe that's why it surprised me very pleasantly. The exposition between the races is arranged by great animated films, which give your efforts a different meaning than the pursuit of the first place. The scenes are completely dominated by your arch-rival, the black-clad Nate McKane. The Bond-like evil, arrogant ace of the Ravenwest Motorsport stable will be your arch nemesis on the way to the championship title.Relationships transfer from the cutscenes to the asphalt. Antipathy towards the villain will bubble to the surface every time you pass Nate's vehicle. You will rarely forgive yourself for a vicious stilt or a push into the barriers from the tires. When the five-time champion emerges from the wreckage in last place, it warms the heart beautifully.But what I resent the creators a little is that the scenario does not respect your position in the championship races. Everyone treats you like some kind of amateur who is happy to get off the starting line without the engine blowing up. At the same time, even on the hardest difficulty, I won the vast majority of races with a huge margin.Immersion in the story is fundamentally disturbed when your stablemate is raving about how amazingly fast she is and, above all, get out of her way and don't interfere too much when she overtakes you. But she can only say that to your rear spoiler, because you give it (and everyone else) an incredible amount of trouble in every race.This addition to the world of car racing is a competent game with a robust career, but it lacks too much to be perfect and rank among the top racing games.

There's also too many niche racing categories thrown at you, especially stadium truck races which take place way too frequently for how awful they steer ingame. My experience improved significantly once I finished the story and moved on to career mode where I was able to  buy & customise new cars, level up my teammate and pick the races I want to do. In terms of actual gameplay, you have to tune manually most of the cars as by default the are very slippery even on dry asphalt. Once you do that the game is quite fun. There's one thing that the game does amazingly well and that's the presentation. Hearing "Razors Edge" playing in the background while you fight for first position in a GT1 car at night, in the middle of a storm is peak GRID moment.Overall, I do recommend the game if you can get it on a sale, it has some flaws but can also provide moments of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The EA Play trial version is a paid demo. 6 story chapters only. They patched the workaround too. Seriously, EA? It also looks like no other review has really touched on the story so far, so if you're interested in that, or at least in Ravenwest, then read on.The good:* Dynamic music is back! I'm pretty sure Ian Livingstone of GRID (2008) and old F1 fame is the one who did the score for this game, and it shows. Just wish the tracks didn't play in every single story event as it somewhat cheapens their impact compared to the old GRID where they were basically boss battle themes.* Performance-wise, the game seems pretty well optimized (runs much better than its 2019 predecessor) and is not particularly large. Given that the game still has Denuvo, that's a solid accomplishment by CM's standards.The so-so:* The handling is better than in 2019, but not by much. I get the feeling that a lot of people playing this game on a controller with no assists will be really frustrated by the Super Trucks, as they're a perfect example of the sort of weirdness I'm talking about here. It's heavy, but weirdly rally-like, with the steering in particular being very reliant on hard initial turning and relying on slip angle to carry you through. With some cars you'll have no choice as the technique is simply too fast not to use and too easy to induce even by accident, regardless of whether or not you change your setup.* Legend difficulty is a touch harder this time around, but in the story mode in particular there's a small element of rubberbanding that makes AIs you don't outright need to beat much faster than they otherwise should be. That element stands no chance against what I said in the previous point though.The bad:* The story, for people who haven't played TOCA Race Driver 1. It's the game's main selling point and understandably a good majority of people won't care about it. You know what's really bad though? Those who do care about it will just be let down. If you're expecting even something as good as F1 2021's Braking Point, then forget it. The DTS approach works well in theory, but in practice this story makes far less sense and is a lot less compelling despite being longer. At least it has a good variety of events.The absurdly ugly:* The story, for people who HAVE played TOCA Race Driver 1. Yes, I'm bringing this up again. Are you one of those people who never played that game? Good. I'm happy for you. I honestly mean that, because I have played it. I know what that game's protagonist, Ryan McKane, is supposed to be like. I've also played all the past GRID games and know all about Ravenwest's "class act" image. As such, as someone who knows about the "lore" of the "extended" series (insert your favorite GRID Cinematic Universe (TM) joke here), I can only describe Legends' story as a vitriolic insult from Codemasters not just to their own past games, but to those games' fans.Verdict:If the EA Play trial will eventually let you play through the entire story, then pay those 4 euros and go through the story mode if what I said hasn't deterred you by now. If you don't care about that part of the game though, then don't bother. Multiplayer is very likely to be dead on arrival and the regular career mode does not provide nearly enough content to make the game worth what it is at anything less than 25% of its price.

_childDocuments_.review: GRID Legends really surprised me.As someone who has played the first two GRID games, they really didn't click with me. Something about the gameplay, handling, and other aspects just didn't intrigue me to continue playing. They aren't bad games, but I guess just not for me. Yet, GRID Legends on the other hand just clicked for me right from the start. It certainly is not perfect, and there is still room to improve things. However, its definitely worth checking out.Firstly, this game looks great, and runs great as well. Seriously, the EGO engine is so damn good, and it really blows the garbage DiRT 5 engine out of the water. Its even an improvement over the visuals of GRID (2019).Secondly, there is a story here. Honestly, from the trailers it looked a lot cringier than how it is in game. I'm actually getting invested in the story where I at least give somewhat of a ♥♥♥♥ about it. I can't say that for many, many other racing games...Thirdly, the car handling. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the handling so satisfying. Its much gripper than any of the GRID games I've played. In the other games, it felt like I could power through corners easier by sliding, instead of taking the time to slow down, to get that optimal racing line. Yet, in Legends, if you end up sliding, you will most likely over steer. That intense feeling of keeping the car from over steering is just not in the other games. There is a certain risk, reward factor, plus a feeling of absolute control in this handling that makes it leagues above any of the handling models in the previous games.Fourthly, its also the small details that really make a big impact on why this game is so much better than GRID (2019).-Music in races: Having a dynamic soundtrack play both in singleplayer and multiplayer just makes the racing way more exciting. Racing games feel blank without music, and since GRID Legends is not try to be a simulation game, its a welcome addition that was missing in all the other GRIDs.-Good sense of speed: Seeing this stiff, lifeless camera in many modern racing games made me appreciate the developers on making the camera way more dynamic. Something about how it sways, shakes, and shifts in and out when braking, makes it feel like I'm actually going fast. Seriously a set up from the lazy camera of GRID (2019).-Boost: The electric car events introduced a boost mechanic, which can be turned on in single and online races. The boost is works like a powershot, which means you get a huge speed increase when you use it. You feel on the edge of control when using boost. Its so damn exhilarating!-Jumps: The trophy trucks introduced ramps on to the track. Just like with boost, they be turned on in single and online races. I can not tell you the chaos I had with a friend when he enabled the ramps. Its just stupid arcade action!-Crossplay: Admittedly, this game didn't do well, so finding people online can be tough. However, it has crossplay which means console players can play with PC players. Thats a huge plus in my books.However, the most striking negative about this game is that it is buggy. Its not completely broken like some other games, but you can tell its not as polished as GRID (2019). Issues that I and my friends had include: ---Trouble connecting to online games.-The game crashing in photomode.-The main menu completely going black.-Race creator options resetting.-Unable to start race creator events online.-Game refusing to load.NOTE: Strikethrough means the issue has been fixed. Will keep this list updated.Since the game is still being updated for the time being, this is what I would like to see:-Splitscreen multiplayer-Give us more slots for race creator- and drags.-Add back the removed Silverstone Speedway that was in GRID (2019).-A less aggressive motion blur that doesn't blur the environment as much.-Please add in Lamborghinis. Its weird to see them missing, especially with Ferraris-Restore the car audio to match GRID (2019). Legends cars feel more toned down in comparison, which is a shame.-More anti-aliasing options. SMAA and Checkboard AA are options hidden in the game files, so why isn't it in the menus?-Expand the car classes. Some only have one vehicle or two vehicles, which is just bad.Overall, I think GRID Legends is worth your time and money. It may not be as iconic or great as the previous titles, but this game is just damn fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "Yes i recommend it, but..." review.First of all, I want to say that I love Grid. I played Grid 1 one of the ps3 back in the day, and have since played every installation in the series on PC. I enjoy the arcade racing and being able to jump into some mindless car fun for a while.What i found really interesting about Grid Legends when it released was the story mode. The story was fun, and I think the actors in the cutscenes did a really good job of making everything feel important. I thought the acting was good and it felt really authentic and engaging. I really felt like a participant and not a spectator.My biggest issue so far is with the DLCs. Yes I've had similiar progression bugs as a lot of other reviews are mentioning, but for me it never stopped me from actually progressing. The issue I have now is that the sponsors are reset and all my career events have 0% despite me having gold medal and almost all of them. What I really want to talk about is the DLC's.Valentin's Classic Car-Nage:This DLC is okay if you like Demolition derby but not worth the 10 euros, in my opinion. The story was okay, the cutscenes were funny, and I like Valentin Manzi's character. I want to specify that I don't personally enjoy the demolition derby gamemode. It has been a part of the Grid franchise for a long time, so I guess it made sense to have a DLC for it, but I think it should've been free.Enduring Sprint:This fresh new DLC offers... nothing new. The "story" mode felt almost non-existant, there were like 3 short cutscenes with the actors. I didnt feel any connection or any sense of importance to any of the events. Half of the events in the story championship are not even Endurance races. They have a couple truck races and electic races as well as normal circuit races. On top of all that, the actual Endurance mode itself offers no new experience other than a time limit. No pitstops, no tyre degredation, both of which are essential elements of actual endurance racing. Disappointing, considering the price point for this DLC is also 10 euros. Should've been free in my opinion.Overall, I like the game. I think it looks and performs really well, and it has a great selection of cars. The DLCs are OK at best, but both should've been free in my opinion. I would buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: First, this is an ARCADE game.  As such, if you do not enjoy power sliding your corners, move on to a simulation title.  And, this game DOES work on most wheels at the time of release (unlike the travesty of Dirt 5). Second, there are so many bugs in Grid Legends that it is hard to recommend it.  Game breaking bugs include the automatic application of hard braking as soon as you lift off the throttle with certain wheels and pedals.  Lesser bugs include the failure to get credit for getting a gold trophy on all championship races in any given series.Notwithstanding all of that, if you have the right controller setup, this game can be a lot of fun.  On my Accuforce Pro V2 direct drive wheel with clubsport V3 pedals, TH8a shifter, fanatec handbrake and Next Level Ratcing Motion cockpit V3, everything worked fine once I tweaked a few things in the ini files.  And, unlike many others, I can state that Codies (now EA) have done a very good job distinguishing how each type of car handles as well as how weather effects modify same.  To be clear, at least with my controller setup, there is a huge difference in handling between open wheel cars, vintage cars, electric cars, stadium trucks, etc.Highlights:  Tuner cars, Muscle cars, Vintage cars, Electric Cars and all trucks except stadium trucks.Lowlights:  Open wheel cars (whose front wheels barely turn kinda like all F1 titles), stadium trucks which (to be fair) don't really belong on asphalt. and drift cars (which cannot be skipped if you attempt to work all the way through the carreer path).  For several of these cars, I found it helpful to radically reduce my reported steering range.  Most cars ran well from 540-900 degrees.  But, open wheel cars needed much quicker steering so they were happiest between 350-450 degrees.   ADDENDUM;  The problem with open wheel racing was as a result of a poor speed sensitivity setting.  If using a wheel, make sure this is at 50 percent or below.  As for drifting with a wheel, it is obviously much improved when you turn off/lower traction control and stability control in the menus.  In addition, there is a counter-steering aid specifically for drifting which I found immensely helpful.  End result, I am actually enjoying the drifting and open wheelers now.Graphics are perfectly acceptable running on a 2080ti in 4k..  Not jaw dropping in any way... just good enough to work.  There are graphical bugs like inverse mirror reflections and reportedly bad LOD but on balance, graphics were a non issue to me.  AI difficulty starts out way too easy but does get harder as you go along.  My suggestion is to start on Hard AI mode with 2x race distance set in the game option menus. In summary, Grid Legends, is an honest arcade game, whose closest competitor is probably Project Cars 3.   Grid Legends has more bugs than Project Cars 3 (even after multiple patches).  Project Cars 3 has far better graphics as well as VR, but I still got quite a bit more enjoyment out of Grid Legends.  (At this point, I have more than a hundred hours in the game.  I hve finished Story mode as well as the Rookie, Semi-Pro, Pro and Gauntlet carreer challenges.)I recommend this game as long as the wheel you choose is fully supported.  I can offer no recommendations for those still using xbox style controllers other than to suggest saving for a wheel and pedals.  The transition from an xbox controller to actual steering is likely to be difficult but ultimately worth it.

_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said this is a repackaged GRID 2019 with a cringe story line. It does have some slight improvements such as the base car selection and the game has more structure instead of a big grid of races. The driving physics are slightly improved but that isn't a difficult feat from GRID 2019.The AI seems to have gone backwards from 2019, even on the hard difficulty its easy to win as they brake way too early and bunch up into corners. The AI also seems to sometimes have a complete lack of awareness of where the player is and it's not uncommon to get sideswiped while racing along side them.The drifting physics feel like a complete copy and paste of the drifting physics from racedriver grid from 2008 which were not great and haven't aged well at all.With the added upgrades and boosts i can't tell if they were going for arcade or lite sim, either way whatever they were going for it completely missed the mark. I really wanted this to be a good game but with all the issues it's just stale not fun at all.
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: this ruined forza horizon 5 for me! i mean yeah i know forza is an open world game and this is a closed track one so its like comparing apples and oranges, but hey both are healthy and rich with vitamins arent they ;) what i mean is both forza and grid are great arcade racers and while a sim racing fan myself i find myself wanting to just chill on the couch and enjoy a nice arcadish racing experience with amy controller, NFS is nice and all but its handling model and physics are just weird, Grid meanwhile have the greatest most intuitive and fun physics and handling model in any arcade racer! its just so much fun and just masterfully walks the fine line between too simple and too hard; you what they say about easy to learn hard to master, yeah thats grid for ya! and this handling model and physics are adjustable to your liking with plethora of options, grid great driving model made forza horizon 5 feel too generic for me even tho forza have a lot of car customization and modifications but still unlike grid all cars drive almost the same in forza and generic which is why im saying grid ruined forza for me!the campaign stories and cut scenes while admittedly cheesy and satirical but fun and good for a laugh nevertheless, career is not exactly the best but its not too shabby, at least they reduced the repetitiveness of previous grid titles careers to a minimum.graphics, sound and optimization are what you would come to expect from a codemasters title, which means it sounds great; looks great and runs great on the vast majority of systems with great optimization and fps even on midrange and low end PC's.TL:DR if you are into a fun arcade racer with fun arcade physics and handling model that runs and looks great on your PC or laptop, look no farther than grid legends, highly recomended.

_childDocuments_.review: If it's on sale, it's a pretty fun way to spend (in my case) over 90 hours of your time. Story mode and a careermode with alot of different cars, tracks and locations.It looks great, the cars handle like you would expect, the weather actually impacts the griplevels to some degree, and different drivetrains handle differently. Upgrades are basic, and so is the tuning, but at least you can change the characteristics of the car.The AI is pretty basic, they want to race on the racingline and will sometimes act a bit weird if you're on it. The griplevels of the AI is off the charts, if you accidentally bump into them, their car doesn't react and your car will sometimes lose all grip and spin out. Their spatial awareness is the complete opposite, most of the time they won't see you (even when in front), and will take you out.But all in all, a lot more fun than Dirt 5
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: So what is GRID Legends? Well, it's exactly the same as GRID 2019, except instead of learning from '19's mistakes, it doubles down and keeps them and adds some more. Legends keeps the gorgeous visuals, accurate car models, slick handling, and wonderful sense of speed of the previous GRID games, and then shatters all of it with grinding, an awkward story, bugs, and abysmal AI. I'll get to the part that bugs me the most. This game is a COMPLETE AND TOTAL GRIND FEST. Making money in this game is so slow in fact that I presume they went to the Asphalt Mobile school of economy progression. Several cars in the game cost over $150,000, and on average I was making about $3,000 per race. Because here's the silver platter: you LOSE money at the end of every race based on any crashes or scrapes your car took. With an income of $10,000 per race roughly and losing sometimes $6,000 of it to minor scrapes or suspension bumps that come from normal track driving, there's most of your income gone. Makes no sense for a game that is trying to be as arcade-y as possible yet include a punishing economy. Not to mention, this game has encrypted memory, so good luck trying to use Cheat Engine. The story does not interest me at all and has the only effect of filing the loading screen with awkward close ups of creepy old men with beards. Yes, that's totally what I care about in a racing game. Not the cars, just creepy close ups.  I've had several bugs in just three hours. These included the Pause Menu header being stuck covering the top of my screen during a race. Another is that in ultrawide, after using the rewind feature, the pillarboxes remain on the sides of the screen until you pause and unpause the race. And the worst bug is an glitched loading screen that lasted for two minutes and when the game finished loading it was locked to 24 FPS. Mmmm, cinematic.  Somehow, they've managed to make the AI even worse from GRID 2019. Not only are they just as immovable as before, but they spin you out even easier and we still have the mortal sin from GRID 1, that being your teammate AI has an impact on your finances at the end of a race. I do not want to babysit an AI at the back of a pack of cars and tell them to overtake, they should be able to race on their own and NOT cost me money. On top of that we have much fewer races than '19 and fewer cars leading me overall just to have lost interest in a few hours. If you absolutely must pick this up, wait for a sale. Codemasters are increasingly moving away from the classic formula that made their games iconic and unique. Perhaps this is the fault of their new publisher, but for now let us keep that wound closed.FINAL SCORE: 4/10IN A NUTSHELL: OBVIOUSLY TAKES INSPIRATION FROM RAID: SHADOW LEGENDS IN MORE THAN JUST ITS NAME.
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not bad - it's just not as good as the other games in the Grid series. The graphics are nice but the driving is not as engaging as previous titles. The story mode is pretty good for a while, and there is a separate championship mode with lots of disciplines to race, so there is plenty of game here. I do not like that you have no option to qualify and always start at the back in the Championship mode. After completing the story and playing the championship mode for a while, I booted up Grid Autosport. The driving was so much better and there was the option to practice and qualify for the races. I ended up uninstalling this and going back to Autosport in the end.My recommendation - buy Grid Autosport if you don't have it - if you do have that, don't bother with this.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't like when reviews start out with "I wanted to like this, BUT..." Well, I wanted to like this, BUT the game requires a lot of grinding in Career mode. It's just a way to artificially inflate the game's overall game length. I finished the Story Mode and I thought it was great. Figured I would jump into Career Mode next. There are 5 different levels and each level has races. Each race is split into different cups and disciplines. I did the first two for Ginetta Cup fine enough, then the game says "Unlock Ginetta Cup level 2 to access this stage." Ok, so I go to Google and ask "how to unlock Ginetta Cup Level 2" and I find a thread that says I have to repeat the same races until I finally drive the required amount of miles, and I think it's 25 miles. The elimination race only gives me 6 miles while the cup gives me around 10 miles. This is dumb! And it's the same for every single cup. I looked and there is that option for every cup in Career mode. Just requiring the player to repeat the same stages over and over is an artificial way to inflate the game's length. It's a shame because I had planned on beating Career Mode and then buying the Season Pass for the other 4 Story Mode chapters, but, nah. This is terrible game design. Codemasters never would have done something this grindy before selling out to EA.EDIT at the 31 hour mark: Yeah, this game is complete trash. I STILL haven't even been able to knock out the Rookie level of races in this game. I finished everything, but there are sponsors that I don't even have access to after unlocking Pro level races. The game just doesn't want me to finish ANYTHING! For reference, I finished the ENTIRE career mode of Grid 2019 in under 25 hours. I'm over 36 hours here and I only have 2 completed disciplines in the Semi-Pro level, and there are 4 levels: Rookie, Semi-Pro, Pro and Grid Finale. Having a fully upgraded car is a complete waste too, because the AI of the other 21 racers is on rubber bands. They zoom off at the start, passing me with ease even though I have a fully upgraded car with the highest power and acceleration in available to me at the race. My car magnetizes to other cars when trying to pass, I'll either rearend them or sideswipe them and I am fully tilting the stick the opposite way of them to get around them. The game doesn't care. The game doesn't care at all about any car stats, it's all just superficial fluff. You're just battling the game's rubberbanding AI the entire time. And since that is the case, WHY DOES THE GAME REQUIRE ME TO GRIND OUT 35 MILES TO GET ACCESS TO THE CUPS?! If the upgrades mean NOTHING (and they don't because I stopped upgrading cars to save money after realizing the upgrades are USELESS!), then why force me to grind races to some arbitrary number?! And it is a grind. Every race gives around 5 miles, and each cup usually has 3 races. The first race doesn't even give you miles because you are "borrowing" the car. And there is NO option to buy a car for the discipline before the race. You are FORCED to use their car, so you get no credit for it. But you can go back and repeat the first race after you own the car, right? NOPE! The game gatekeeps ALL the first races of every cup to "borrowed" vehicles, even if you already own the car you are racing. Everything in this game is just trash. I don't grind this much in JRPGs or MMORPGs. And it's such a boring grind. The racing isn't fun. There is no music (which sucks because the music in Story Mode was great and was a mix of Metal Gear meets The Matrix). This is a complete trash game and even if they pull a Ubisoft in the future and release it for $1.00 (like Ubi is doing at the time of this writing with The Crew 2), it's not worth it. Codemasters sold their souls to EA and it shows! Dead developer. Dead franchise. I'm leaving comments on with this review. Please tell me why this game is good. Because it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: A huge step up in every department over GRID 2019.The car handling is definitely more arcade-like but the cars are much more planted. 2019s cars oversteered all over the place, so much so that an average racer like me had to keep traction and stability settings at 3 of 5 at all times. Here? I could switch both off and was still comfortable. This is not a sim, it's very much an arcade racer. And I'm perfectly fine with that.Graphics and optimisation are excellent. Game ran ultra smoothly with everything at its highest. Everything looks sharper and more detailed than in GRID 2019. Wet weather and snow effects are stunningly beautiful.I've only completed the Story mode so far but it's so much fun and I did it all in one sitting, start to finish. Brilliant production values, some genuinely decent enough acting and they don't overstay their welcome. They do what they have to do and get out of the way, leaving you straight into the racing again. Very well done.Career mode and multiplayer modes are there and other reviewers suggest they work well but I have not played either modes at the time of this review.If I had to make any complaints? The AI is very unbalanced, a bit like in GRID 2019. I played on a mix of Hard and Expert AI levels and found that the AI were either crazy fast that they were practically unbeatable on some tracks or they were so far behind that they offered little to no competition. Only a handful of my races on Expert finished closely. The rest were easily won or lost. The nemesis system returns here too but it doesn't really offer much in my view, same implementation as in GRID 2019.Overall though, at 5 hours in (the time it took me to beat the Story mode), I've had a great time already and can't wait to continue with this over the coming weeks and months. Everything in here feels more refined, like the game GRID 2019 should have been (I still enjoyed that game a lot).That's a "Recommended" from me!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a first glance review for all who don't know if they want to spend the money.When I was buying Grid Legends I really really hoped to get the sequel to Grid 2. I loved the story of the world series, the handling was alright for the time and I really dont need yet another racing game where I am driving "real motorsport". But THE most important thing was for me the story. So yes after 1h playing this game: this has it all. The story is just phenomal. Even though its very linear. But hey its like watching a netflix series. But dont expect yourself being a part of it. No chance to decide anything. The car pool is great. From some Ferrari, to old group c Porsches, to old DTM and British Touring Car until you finally reach the newest cars. Obviously the old Fernando Alonso licenced F1 car is not missing. Graphics are insane. Really looking awesome. Missing a bit cool looking ray tracing. But hey the rest is just stunning. Sound is okaish. That's the real first down side in this game. Motorsport is all about the sound and the atmosphere. Seems like CM didn't understand that yet. Bugs ... lets dont talk about it. There is a hidden swarm and the come with features. Like the replay function is not working yet. But you can drive while being in the replay :D Actually funny, but its one major bug I would expect them to find before releasing. But also this is codemasters. Buying a CM game on day 1 means borderline love, missing knowledge or living in a fanatasy world. This game does not redefine racing games. But it's what it should be years ago. A perfect follow up game for all who loved Grid 2.If you are short on money or you hate driving around bugs. Wait a month.

_childDocuments_.review: OG Codemaster Grid:- a million tracks- plenty of cars- a whole ass car ebay- ravenwest scoring ungodly amounts of points- no DLC's- no stewards to wine about you going slightly off the track- tons of campaign races to do- every car had your same livery for simplicity- you buy the cars you need to race- amazing body damage- easily can spend 1000's of hours onBetacuck EA Grid Legends:- confusing ass menu- forces you to always drive forward in races- gotta be 10s ahead of 2nd so the stewards ♥♥♥♥♥ ass doesn't penalize you into 2nd place- GotTa BuY ThIS DLc tO PlaY DeMO DeRBy Hrrrrr- cars are just given to you after 1 or two loan races making buying cars have little meaning- body damage is not really good- the damn car liveries don't even transfer to any new cars even when you select the choice that says "apply to all owned cars" - uses racetracks from the original Grid and Grid 2 games, just with a reskin- Fairly small campaign it looks like, but I haven't played it a bunch- why the ♥♥♥♥ are the bots driving cinder blocks how the hell do they spin me out when I barely move them- if you're even a slightly aggressive driver after about 10h of racing almost every driver will be your nemesis- only 13h in and I've seen a lot of random bugs, like invisible walls making you go from 100-0 instantly, random parts of cars falling off, which for some reason are weightless, even a visual bug or two========================EA has once again ruined a once amazing game, I remember playing the og Grid as a child, and it was one of my favorite racing games, it was such a quality game, it had an amazing amount of customization, with both your team, and your vehicles, it had a huge amount of races, a big selection of tracks, amazing visuals for its time, even the damn intro gave me chills for how good it was, I poured my heart and soul into that game, and seeing now how EA had apparently at some point bought Codemasters or something just made me very sad.. I blame EA for everything that was done wrong, they ruined what was once a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a progression, track-based racing game with a lot of different race types, cars, circuit locations,  that's easy to play then, Grid Legends is the game for you. I like it because it doesn't try to be the most realistic racing simulator out there, where you have to spend a huge amount of time tweaking your settings to get a decent result in a race. Instead,  you can just jump into a race and do fairly well right from the start. At the same time, as you get good at it you can progressively tweak it to become even more challenging. Another thing I like is that you get 4 seasons worth of story content,  along with a number of race cars that racing-series fans and gear heads will recognize (i.e. IMSA, Formula-E, NASCAR truck series, supercars, muscle cars and more).As part of their latest season launch, they dropped the price to about $20 for the game plus all seasons -or- $11 just for the base game. It was too good of an offer to pass up.I highly recommended it regardless of price.

Even for driving on the line, you will get points and they pop up every second. Furthermore, in comparison to Gran Turismo 7, the environment and music is very pleasant. The exciting music in the background, the lighting and the fireworks. It all add up to the fun arcade driving experience, which is very fun and immersive!I make use of a Thrustmaster t300 RS and the experience using a wheel in this game is absolutely fun!

_childDocuments_.review: edit: As an update to the review below, I got the complete edition for $15ish. The DLCs are.... really lame and short. The drifting one (winter, the last one) sucks snowballs.________________________(Note: Played via a 99 cent EA Play subscription trial- obviously any fart of a game might be worth it within that context, so let's just pretend I paid a normal sale price of like $20 for it. I really enjoyed it and will probably get it on sale at some point. edit months later: I did find the deluxe/complete edition on sale for about $15, worth it but the DLCs are pretty lame and repetitive, nothing up to the quality of the main story)I completed the story mode. Well, the first of 3 stories- the second two are locked behind DLC. I see alot of reviews knocking the story-- maybe I'm just a simpleton, but I liked it. Very well acted (for the most part), and while it feels kind of 'uhhh hey what?' when the game changes the results a little bit to fit the pre-scripted narrative,I'm not expecting a visual novel branching path here, and neither should you. Actually dramatic and I kind of cared about the characters. Graphics are absolutely lovely. When it's really raining hard it is quite difficult to see due to the drops on the "camera/windshield"; at first this really bothered me but I adjusted and actually came to appreciate how it made me change my focus. For the drifting events and such I turned down the difficulty a bit (because I suck at that stuff, other than basic racing), but for most of the game I was on Hard and pretty easily won 1st in most. I'm usually an easy/medium mode player. The music is very much to my taste, but I suspect I might be in the minority there. It's often a mix of orchestral and something akin to chiptunes, and it really fits the arcade driving for me (note: Yes, this is an arcade racer, not a sim. _childDocuments_.review: This game is much more fun than I was expecting. Closer to arcade handling, but still a challenge and the AI is programmed well enough to make it plenty interesting. Lighting and track modeling is gorgeous; driving beneath awnings and through tunnels with the exterior lights flooding into the cabin looks amazing. Fighting your way through the smoke of a limping car ahead of you. Dodging loose tires and spinning wrecks. The imaginary city tracks are all gorgeous and technically challenging. Track facilities, cityscapes, mountainsides all feel imposing and loom over you as you drive by. Somehow cars crashing out in this game feels much more significant than most other racing games; whenever you see someone ahead start spinning out you know its about to get interesting. So many little things done well here. Even the drift competitions, which I normally don't get much enjoyment from, I find to be fun and challenging here. I'm coming from hundreds of hours on wreckfest and Horizon looking for something a bit more challenging and race oriented (for gamepad racing), and this game is it and more. So happy I picked it up, hope to see the player count grow.

This means either you repeat a few of the events over or make it up with a few quick races or online. Either way I don't think it's optimal or streamlined. 2x is far too long for every single race, especially with this AI issue, just makes it a huge slog when you have 7 laps left 10 seconds out in lead.' _childDocuments_.review: GRID Legends is a simcade racing game, where you race in different racing categories with your teammate or alone to win them all, get cars and upgrade them and go against others on the track or in the leaderboards.The game looks better and it’s better to play with, than GRID 2019 in my opinion. Also, the career and story mode makes the offline game more interesting, than the previously mentioned game. GRID Legends is actually trying to focus on the story and connect the GRID and TOCA games’ story, which doesn’t sound much, but I genuinely enjoyed these moments, but maybe I’m just too invested in these games' story. There are some good amount of cars and tracks in the game, also there are a few interesting race types too. I have to praise the story soundtrack in GRID Legends, it’s awesome. Just listen to it, you won’t regret it!I would love to say that GRID Legends is the game that we should have gotten years ago, but it’s far from perfect. There are progression bugs here or there, the notorious career eraser bug, which makes your progression 0% in the mode, which is already a grind fest to do and also this is the only mode to get cars for the multiplayer. There are sponsor objective tracking issues, where sometimes the game can’t register if you did a progression or in my case, the game randomly completes objectives, which I never completed in any of my previous races. There are some sponsor goals, which if you complete early without tracking the objective, you won’t be able to complete it ever in the game. The DLCs for this game are not the greatest, the Classic Car-nage DLC which has the derby game mode and cars it’s horrendous and stupid, the Enduring Spirits is just boring, but atleast the new track is all right, however both of the DLCs’ sponsor objectives are either broken or almost impossible to complete. Atleast the Rise of Ravenwest is not too bad in my opinion, thanks to the additional backstory of Ravenwest, but if you don’t like the story in the game, you might not like this more, than the Enduring Spirits. The Winter Bash was not too special with the types of races, however I enjoyed the different environment and some of the fast cars. Also, you can drift on Okutama, so that's something to mention. However what really annoys me in the game, is the connection between upgrades and the multiplayer. If you want to play an online game without doing any career race, you will find yourself with not many cars to go with, plus with zero upgrades on them. There are not many players in the multiplayer, however those who are still in the game have maxed out cars, which are somewhat impossible to beat, if you don’t unlock cars and get the mileage for their upgrades AND buy those. So you have to start playing the career (which is not the same as playing the Story mode by the way) and grind your way up, which takes atleast 50 - 60 hours just to be competitive in the multiplayer. And sure, you can loan a car for multiplayer too, but again, you still have no upgrades and you are not gonna finish high up, because the game forces you to do the career slug west.GRID Legends looks good on paper, hell I even think it’s a better game than GRID 2019, but the devs just misused some ideas and can’t really fix their own mess. However, I can still recommend this game over the previously mentioned GRID title, but only if you can get it for around 10-15€ for the base game, the Deluxe Edition might be worth around 20-25 I think.I just hope that this won’t be the last GRID we ever see, and maybe next time we are going to get a more polished game.

_childDocuments_.review: SUMMARY:GRID Legends is a fun arcade racing game in an age where arcade racers have gone the way of the Dodo bird. The cars feel unique and fun to drive, the tracks are as gorgeous as always, and the gameplay is comparable to other arcade racers on and off the track. Overall a decent, new addition to my library of arcade racing games.BREAKDOWN:+ Driving is accessible and fun on controller with adjustments to sensitivity (i use 100 sensitivity and 4 linearity)+ Weather effects look visually stunning+ Every vehicle feels unique on track+ The team logo creator from F1 comes to GRID to help give your team more of an identity in Career Mode+ The selection of cars and disciplines is varied without choice overload problems- The game still has some bugs that, at this stage of release, are somewhat unforgiveable (super low quality textures on the driver car sometimes, occasional softlocks in the main menu, audio stuttering/clicking and others)- AI Catchup/rubberbanding isn't strong enough on Legend difficulty (I'm beating the AI by a heaping handful of seconds at the end of a race, which becomes a bigger problem if Career Mode races are set to longer than 1X length)- Drifting physics are underwhelming (the engine bogs down at any significant angle regularly seen at a drifting event, which makes the cars feel like the tire compound is too grippy for the engine's power output)- The gameplay outside of the on-track action feels one-dimensional, especially when compared to the first GRID's in-depth team and sponsor management.SHOULD YOU BUY IT?I think this game is a great purchase when it's on sale. The incredibly high standards set by the first GRID game have yet to be matched by the latest Codemasters team, but compared to other arcade racing games released at the same time, it's a solid addition to my library. This game isn't quite where it needs to be to recapture the sheer level of immersion and replayability the original GRID had, but it's a great start towards achieving and hopefully surpassing those standards.

_childDocuments_.review: Grid Legends is much better than the previous Grid titles, but it's still missing features and Race-types from the original Grid. (I AM BEGGING YOU CODEMASTERS TO BRING BACK TOUGE & ENDURANCE RACES!).I found it interesting that, even though Codemasters is now a part of EA, you don't need to download Origin to play the game, you just need to log in with your Origin account if you want to play online.Grid Legends builds on Grid (2019), and the handling is almost the same as in all the other Grid games, which is not a bad thing at all.The Game is good, but when it starts raining it looks gorgeous. On top of the improved graphics, the game also runs better than its predecessor. With my R5 1600X, 16GB ram, and RTX 2060 S I achieved a solid 60FPS even on my ultrawide 1440p monitor.The best thing about Grid Legends is adding a Story, complete with cutscenes and everything. It is a basic Story but it isn't as unpleasent and cringy as the Story in other racing games, looking at you NFS.Another thing I like is that more Race modes were added, in comparison to the last Grid game, but the selection still feels basic and overall worse than Grid and Grid 2. In addition to the Circut, Sprint, and time trials there are now Drift and Elimination.Sadly there are also some bad aspects to the game, some smaller some bigger.One small flaw I noticed is that no matter how good you race the story will go on and on about how the main antagonist has to be cheating to be so good, yet I managed to beat him with a distance of 10 seconds between us. I would have liked it if the game was so difficult that you can't beat him or have the game acknowledge that you have beaten him.I played the game on hard difficulty and yet the Story mode was still insultingly easy, simply because you don't need to win at all, except in the Final Race, in most races you just need to finish at about 7th place. I overall recommend this game, its a solid entry in the Grid franchise and is fun to play, but the Story is a bit on the short side and it feels like a big chunk of the game is locked behind DLC, I would recommend that you pick up the Deluxe Edition when it hits a price point of about 30€.

_childDocuments_.review: Grid Legends is a solid racing game that has a few achievements of its own making it stand out, but there are some hiccups when compared with Grid 2 from 2013, which is the last game I played in the franchise.It is not a high bar, as the racing genre is notoriously plagued with bad and forgettable stories, so it is quite refreshing to see a story that is well-engineered and well-acted as a fake documentary on the imaginary Grid racing series.It has nothing groundbreaking, and the plot is actually very one-dimensional, but the story has a stake and characters have some personalities, making players care about their fates and cheer for their success. Simple as it is, it already outperforms other racing games in being intriguing and by hiring some actually competent actors, it also excels in presentation.The game also has the best racing music I’ve heard, which keeps reminding me of Devil May Cry because of the strong angelic and demonic themes and vibes, and it makes racing extra exhilarating.Notably, the story and music quality take a dive after the main campaign: there are hardly any stories in the rest four small campaigns and the music becomes quite forgettable, but the humor did put a smile on my face.Grid Legends has basically every type of race that is held on paved roads: open wheels (formula racing), sports car (including different classes of grand tourer and prototype), stock car, touring car, production car, and one-make, only with drag race missing, but it has trophy truck, racing truck, and drifting as additions. There is also an event type called Derby Demolition, which is basically car smashing each other.The 10-to-13-hour or so (depending on skills and difficulty) story mode introduces players to various race types and modes (time attack, elimination, endurance, etc.), where players can grab a taste of everything.However, the story mode doesn’t do well in introducing tracks, as many are missing in the main campaign because they were added after. Also, you can’t choose your car in story mode, which takes away more excitement than expected.Besides the story, there is a career mode that is significantly more time-consuming for it has more races, with some having certain requirements to unlock. You can choose what vehicles to use and who you compete with, as the game allows you to play offline against AI or hold online sessions to race with and against other players. This is the mode that caters to sweaty gamers and those carving for more game.Most race types are very fun, with the exception of drifting, trophy truck racing and Derby Demolition.Derby Demolition is the game’s fancy word for car fight and it has one dedicated small campaign that is painful to go through, as I don’t think the physics is meant for it.In this event, racing is not important, which defeats the purpose of the racing genre. Instead, players are required to chase up other vehicles to smash out as much damage as possible. However, because the hitbox is small, inaccurate and weirdly placed, more often than not you get totalled before doing enough damage, resulting in lots of chaos, frustration and simply unfun.Drifting remains my least favorite event, but it actually feels fine. What makes it unpleasant for me is the game’s obsession with putting drifting events in tracks that are easy to break the drift chain, like Okutama which has lots of narrow straights in the middle session. This is the only event I always lowered difficulty to save myself from frustration.As for the trophy truck, it is one motherfxxker to handle for the soft suspension and high gravity center. It exposes an issue in car physics, that a slightly fast deceleration or downshift is enough to cause front wheels to lock on, resulting in the car spinning out, which just feels unrealistic.On the subject of car physics, Grid 2 is my main comparison and it has great car physics that is on the oversteering side. For Grid Legends, it is neither understeering nor oversteering. Of course, it varies for each individual car, but the general neutral physics is still highly enjoyable and also makes the game more accessible to audiences, compared to Grid 2, in which oversteering physics is a bit challenging to master. Grid Legends also provides robust accessibility settings from ABS, stability control to traction control, drift control etc., to make driving more accessible.Physics change makes Grid Legends more accessible but also makes it less exciting. Grid 2 feels like a mix of car sim and arcade racing, because driving feels raw, unfiltered and dangerous, though not to the degree of pure simulation, Grid Legends is pure arcade racing. While, unlike Need for Speed, it doesn’t introduce the unenjoyable artificial tractions, it does feel like lots of information is filtered out for the sake of making it easy to drive, even with every accessibility setting off.Each track used to feel very different to drive on in Grid 2, but possibly as a result of the physics change, most of them (many returned tracks) feel identical to drive on despite the different designs and layouts.But those are just nitpicking, the one solid criticism I have of physics is how easily the car spins out, which has been talked about in the trophy truck session. However, trophy truck is just one prominent example. It varies from car to car, but for some, one not-very-fast downshift, one not-very-sharp turn, one small bump in the corner, or even a gentle braking on the straights with no steering, is enough for the car to spin out. A large part of the battle about driving has become trying not to spin out, which even with accessibility settings off, still feels highly unrealistic to spin out that easy.In Grid 2, AI is bad for its unpredictable racing lines, tendency to block and brake check, aggressive driving and unfair speed in certain races. I am happy that AI became much less aggressive and more tolerable with no cheating, but they still drive like those a-holes who brake excessively and don’t look at the rear mirrors when changing lanes. And when collisions happen, it feels so hard to break away like the car is somehow glued together, which is very unpleasant.As for sponsor objectives, in Grid 2 they mean ugly stickers across the chassis, but the actual requirements are easy and usually complete themselves without notice. But in Grid Legends, they become such a big deal to prolong the game that takes players extra effort and time and many purposely built races to finish, to unlock exclusive races and cars. Sponsor objectives is already grindy and a handful, to make matters worse, the game won’t track completion unless objectives are activated (only one sponsor at a time), meaning lots of extra repetitive work to be done. Furthermore, tracking does not always work correctly and progression has a chance to bug out and reset itself, which happens to me and many people.People play the game differently and some don’t care about these objectives, but for me who has OCD, MY GOD, it is a thorn in my side. I care about finishing them so much it starts to strip the fun away. Part of me was actually glad the progression reset itself so that I could just give up. ://No game is 100% perfect, so as far as everything goes, Grid Legends is a pretty good game that is safe to recommend to everyone. I wish the sponsor objectives to be completely gone, and physics and AI to be better, but in the grand scheme of things, they might not matter to most people. I am just glad I bought the game at 90% off and it is worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not deserve anything more than 'Mostly Positive' reviews. While it is definitely a step-up in comparison to GRID 2019, it still has a lot of problems.- The opponents' cars are just brick walls. You can't spin them out or inflict damage on them, but they can absolutely destroy you.- The damage is tuned down by a lot. I understand that visual damage is not as spectacular as in GRID 2008 for licensing reasons, but why do I need to launch a nuke in order to actually damage the steering of the car?- A lot of bugs seriously affecting the gameplay. For example, if you create an Endurance race in the Race Creator mode, the starting grid will be sorted by teams' names (from my observations) no matter which option you chose in the settings before. Another example would be a very bad calculation of estimated time to finish the race for bots. Sometimes in normal races and every single time in Time Attack mode the game does a very poor job estimating when a bot will finish the race, which often results in you appearing at the bottom of the standings when you clearly finished first and were the fastest on the track all the time. - The DLC content is pure garbage. It is clear that those packs were made just to fulfill the Season Pass obligations. Each of those packs is undercooked to say the least. Carnage DLC makes no sense with the physics this game has (See point 1). Endurance DLC adds Fuji Speedway, when Le Mans would make much more sense. And on top of that the devs again did not give a s**t about the game, so when you participate in a lower car class and win the race in your class, you will not get a gold medal for the event, because overall you were like 10th. Excuse me, how am I supposed to win in my Bentley GT3 against BMW V12 LMR? Ravenwest DLC was ok, but nothing to write home about. Winter Bash DLC is another piece of garbage. No new tracks and only 3 cars. They added new weather conditions and modes like drifting to existing tracks, but guess what? You can't use them in the Race Creator mode. They are only available in those 10 sh***y career events. And the cherry on top is that all those cool liveries like in Ravenwest DLC can't be used on your own car. Why? Because the devs didn't give a s**t about the game. - Sponsor objectives. Absolute horror for completionists. They make you grind utterly stupid objectives like make 10 barrel rolls. Are we doing official racing or clown show? You might think that after hours spent on each sponsor you get something cool, but no. You just unlock another soulless event in the career mode. Instead of just adopting the GRID 2008 sponsor system, they decided to reinvent the bicycle. - Teammates. As a tradition, your teammates will do everything they can to hinder you and your team. They (Yume and Valentin) are slow and unreliable. I would gladly fire them and hire someone with demonic speed like Jamie Christopher or Rick Scott, but we are not playing a 15-year old GRID 2008, are we? In 2022 we evolved from cool mechanics and now we make simplified cr*p, because who cares?As a result, the devs got what they deserved. While I am sad that this is most probably the end of GRID franchise, I will never tolerate a bad product in hopes that the next one will be better. Now, I'll go play GRID 2008 with Xtra mod and enjoy it much more than the GRID games released after that.P.S. Don't get me wrong. There is still fun to be had in this game, as reflected by my hour count, but I simply cannot overlook all the game breaking issues. That being said, I'd definitely recommend buying it at a 90% discount.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting some time into the game's story, I have to say I enjoy the game more than I was expecting. The story is very compelling, albeit flawed. What I mean by that is this; the game's story is interesting in that it follows you, a rookie driver, trying to build their way to becoming a racing legend. A pretty solid premise, if a bit generic. However, the game continuously sets you up as being the support driver for Yume, the other driver for Seneca (your team) and thus your teammate. Following this premise of you being a support for Yume, the game sets realistic objectives for you, ones that typically would involve you staying behind Yume's position. The problem with this premise is that the game doesn't really care how well you do, in practice. So long as you enter the position specified each race, whether you come in first or tenth, the game plays out all the same. So you form this disconnect between the cutscene version of you, and the you who's in control - you can dominate in every race, always ending up first place despite playing the game on hard difficulties (the AI drivers are pushovers even on the hardest of difficulties) and while intuitively I can understand why that is, it still makes winning feel kind of pointless. Why strive for first place if the game will, in the grand scheme of things, always treat me the same as it would if I was hanging back and playing it safe?While it certainly doesn't ruin the game, by all means it's still thrilling to go up against the likes of Nathan McKane who's always breathing down your neck no matter how fast you are, I feel that it does make the story a bit frustrating to watch. Cutscenes where your team is struggling, when in reality you should be thrashing the competition in every race? Story-related frustrations aside, the game's audio is fantastic. The many various engine-sounds all sound great, even the electric cars. The ambience is great too. I don't much care for the music - even with dynamic music on, I find the music in the story races very repetitive and I find myself muting the music more than anything. The graphics look exquisite too, and the choice of full-motion video for story sequences really adds a level of realism to it all, especially given how well the actors perform. The cast is small, sure, but they're all talented actors and I find myself watching each and every cutscene to the end, which I normally don't bother doing in racing games. All in all, I really do enjoy this game. I had some issues with the game at first, but a reinstall fixed my problems and I was able to go online just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade racers with real cars are a bit of a thinning genre these days. But in the midst of Elden Ring's launch and the lead-up to the long-awaited Gran Turismo 7, GRID Legends kinda just... came out with little fanfare. And you know what? I like it. I like it quite a bit. After spending some time playing the game, both on the Xbox Series S and on various PCs, I've found that it really didn't deserve the lack of coverage it got on release.GRID Legends is a game of two halves: the story and the career mode. I'll dive into the career mode first as I can sum it up pretty quickly. As a whole, the career mode isn't  per se - it's just poorly structured. It's a bit all over the place, which is pretty weird, especially given that you'll have to grind races to even unlock a car that you'll be racing in anyways. There's a fair bit of backtracking involved in the career mode. The career mode really needed more structure, but at least it's very hop-in-and-play-friendly, which is quite handy when you don't have a lot of time to play a game.The story mode, on the other hand... The main story takes a different approach to telling its story compared to how most other games do it. While the basic structure is the typical "rise up from the bottom to win the most elite challenge" structure you see in every other racing game, the narrative is essentially told in the perspective of a dramatized documentary. You are Driver 22, an otherwise nameless and faceless backup driver for the Seneca racing team. You and your teammate push through the GRID World Series to beat Ravenwest in the final race to win the World Series. The cutscenes are surprisingly well-acted and flow pretty well with the rest of the game. My only real criticism of the base story is that it's short -  short. The main story only takes about 5-6 hours to beat, which isn't a long time. At least that means the story doesn't drag on, which isn't a bad thing. The DLC stories are relatively short and mostly decent. Valentin's Classic Car-nage kinda drags on and repeats itself far too much, but Enduring Spirit and Winter Bash are both pretty fun and reasonably challenging in their own right. Rise of Ravenwest, while the easiest of the four DLCs, was also the best DLC, at least to me. It leans into what the base game does best - story telling, and actually tries to contextualize the story a bit more. All of them add vehicles and tracks to the game.In terms of the actual racing experience in this game, as I mentioned earlier, it's an arcade racer. It doesn't really try to be that realistic - it's a GRID game, after all. But I really enjoy the handling model in here. It's one that has actual weight and feel to it, but one that isn't brutally punishing to wrangle. At the same time, the game's difficulty settings  you to make the game more difficult to play if turning off all driving assists is your thing. The cars themselves also look excellent and sound as good as the models look in here. It's certainly a major step up from both Gran Turismo and Forza in this regard.Visually speaking, I like it a lot. It's not pushing the bleeding edge of technology, so you won't get advanced ray-tracing in here. But its Xbox One and PS4-optimized roots doesn't mean that the game looks bad - far from it. It's been a long time since I've played a racing game that really leans into using a brighter and more visually striking color palette to sell its visual makeup rather than aiming for raw realism. The color grading of the game combined with a very nice lighting pass, high quality cars and tracks (with plenty of detail to boot outside of the main driving area), a high-quality post-processing pass and a good sense of speed makes for a visually attractive and cohesive game. That being said, if you're trying to run this at 3840x2160, make sure you have a beefy GPU. The game becomes quite a lot more demanding past 1440p, as a lot of the post-processing pipeline, as well as stuff like lighting, operates at full-res. Otherwise, at lower resolutions, it's not that heavy, even at higher settings. It's an Ego engine game, and if you have a Radeon Vega 8 iGPU in your laptop, you can play this game at a decent frame rate.Overall, I quite enjoyed GRID Legends! I wished I had actually played it when I first bought it on Steam, rather than only starting to play it when I tried it out on Game Pass to see what my Series S can do. It's a thoroughly enjoyable arcade racer that goes on sale quite often. And for the $20 or so I paid for it a few months back, I definitely felt like I got my money's worth out of it.
