_childDocuments_.review: One note right up front: If a good-looking arcade racer is what you're looking for, this game fits the bill (although certainly not for $60, wait for it go on sale). Big mean rich guys beat up on underdogs and underdogs win, heard of that one before?Driving Experience: Most cars feel like driving boats. Weather visually exists but doesn't change driving characteristics at all. Opponent cars lose parts at random and crash in almost every race, although dodging crashes is somewhat fun. Drifting is not fun, almost feels like a different game's physics engine. The difficulty scaling between races is awful.Cars: Same models, same body kits, same liveries except for a few new cars. No customization, which is standard for GRID but still sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: While there some aspects from GRID 1 & 2 that I like more (such as the sense of speed with the camera, and some aspects of the presentation), Legends is not only a step up from GRID 2019 but an innovation in certain aspects that I didn't expect, and it has to do with the online multiplayer. The hop-in-hop-out system is amazing, I played a custom race and was about to hit someone on the second lap... before I realized the AI had turned into a real player. It's something I've never seen before and it's fantastic. It also means there's little loading and waiting to race online.As for the rest of the game, the new story mode is quite cool with the documentary-style cutscenes. I much prefer the FMVs over in-game (or in-engine) animation. The car handling is more akin to Project Gotham Racing 4 than the older GRID titles, as there's much more heft to the cars along with more reliance on the handbrake. Once I got used to it, it was really good. The car list is probably the best of any GRID game - but I wish they would bring back as many cars from the old games as possible before adding a bunch a new ones. I'd like the cars to just carry over and be in one place - think Smash Ultimate. The presentation is much better than GRID 2019, along with the music. But I think some aspects of the presentation can look "cheap" - such as the race finish animation and the animation when the podium winners form. It's much better than 2019's, but the game when it comes to camera angles, UI design, etc. looks very cheap compared to the Xbox 360/PS3 era Codemasters games. But that's the case for every title they've made (other than DiRT Rally 1 or 2.0) since they ditched the 3D menus - I really want them back. They made the games feel very unique, and looked way cooler than any other racing game back then, and even now.However, GRID Legends is a smaller title in terms of content and scope, just like every other GRID title. I recommend the game, but I would recommend waiting until it's at most $40. It's quite an enjoyable experience but in my opinion it isn't worth a full $60 asking price. That's not a fault of the game though.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Really solid - 8.5Overall feels like a much improved version of 2019. Driving feels like a more grippy, forgiving version of the previous title but still much better than the rip handbrake/brake to drift handling NFS has nowadays. Still need skill to hit your braking points and lines. Every car feels different and unique - Shelby Cobra 289 feels like a nimble, well balanced 60s sports car ; Ferrari 599XX feels like a high downforce car whose tires barely handle the absurd horsepower.Car and class variety is great. I'd say as close to Autosport/ToCA 3. However not many real life circuits right now (hopefully more added post launch). Fictional city and racetracks are as good as ever.Car damage is pretty much a non-factor - you can see it and what is there is good but it takes some really bad driving to get anything significant.Storylines is meh at best - not too long and it does show off most of the types of cars/tracks the game has but doesn't do much otherwise. The guy playing Nathan McKane is fun to watch as the overall douchebag villain but thats about it, everyone else is straight out of the EA diversity box with zero character traits. Doesn't detract too much from the game but doesn't add much either.Career is similar to 2019. Sponsors aren't nearly as complex as the 2008 game - just select one and get some set targets (drive x amount of km in specific car) and you can't change your teammate. You can upgrade his skills, and once fully upgraded they seem to listen to orders better. The "Nemesis" system that was introduced in 2019 is back and improved - once you piss off other AI drivers they will stay mad and rough you up in future races.AI overall is good, but has some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. They weave a bit too much during braking making clean overtakes hard. They also often check up when close to each other because they seem to have been coded to really avoid any contact and will brake midcorner if they come to close to your or each other. However if they have speed they will go for overtakes and they don't drive as if your car doesn't exist so that's better than a lot of other racers.Multiplayer needs some work. The drop in midrace and replace AI car is a great idea, love that. However, there are two fairly big issues - one is inability to run series of races. Second issue is that car upgrades make a massive difference - and you unlock the upgrades by just putting down km/miles with that car. So that means you will get destroyed online by people that have played more of the singleplayer than you. The option to disable upgrades in multiplayer is there - but it seems bugged as of the time of writing this and seems like something most people would miss when starting up lobbies.Good racer overall. I'd say if you enjoyed the core gameplay and varied content of the previous GRIDs except for GRID 2 you will like this. If you enjoyed stuff like Forza Motorsport/Gran Turismo and can deal with the lack of car customization you will find an enjoyable pickup and play racer.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better Grid games in recent years, particularly a good upgrade in terms of graphics, types of races, car selection and general features than Grid 2019. I'd still recommend waiting for a sale to purchase the game though. The story mode and the 4 DLCs that are part of the season pass offer around 15-20 hours of content (about 75 different races/episodes) and are really enjoyable to play through. You can drive on a large variety of tracks (I think there's about 20 locations, each with multiple routes) with many different cars and types of races (traditional lap races, elimination, time attack, drift, overtake challenges to name a few) as well as a variety of weather conditions. The race creator is also nice, allowing you to setup single or multiplayer races using a wide range of customizable settings.Two things really let the game down for me though and they are:1)  The lack of new locations compared to returning tracks. I'd say that 2/3rds of all locations in the game have been in previous grid games, which is rather repetitive. 2) Career mode seems shallow in terms of variety of content compared to the story mode.And the sponsor/team/mechanic upgrades systems are rather pointless for the benefits they provide. Getting extra money from events or faster upgrades or things like that really doesn't matter, you get all of the upgrades and cars you want without having to specifically grind for them.

_childDocuments_.review: GRID Legends has rediscovered the forward momentum that the franchise has been missing in recent years. With a concise and simple off-track narrative, the racing is well connected in the story mode. The on-track action is good too, with adequate variety, good AI competitors, and a decent track roster. Despite having a lot of recycled tracks, the racing is generally exciting due to dramatic accidents and tight encounters. There are more memorable races in just a few hours of driving than could be found in the entirety of the previous two games combined. And the online portion is fairly strong, despite some unnecessarily long waits. GRID Legends might not be the best in the series but it makes me excited to see what will happen next.

The story is so bad, you call the game Legends whereas it has none. I'm only 3 hours in and I can bet you there is not gonna be a single cameo from any driving legend, probably not even a brief shot of a Max Verstappen interview pulled from an amateur YouTube channel and y'all can only afford to have Nathan on the spotlight??? no Rick Scott?The best thing y'all could've done is make a prequel to GRID, the point before McKane became the big scary guy you're faced in the first game and work it into a sequel/remake of the first game because apparently y'all can't make the same gameplay mechanics with the SAME engine, is it really that bad? Did you delete all the old assets or something?But even then the way the cutscenes are shot a la The Office but cringy in a bad way makes me want to skip the whole game. You cannot have candid camera and invisible movie camera being the same!Since you're using actors anyway, there was so much potential to generate slightly different scenes depending on how the driving goes. Pushing Yame too hard? She quits and joins Raven or if you drive too aggressively you get recruited by Raven, leading to the "bad" ending. Having the player being "number 22" is so generic it pains me how you'd think that would make the player care about self-insertion if you have already set up a whole universe of characters. Give us a name, even Ryan Cooper would be a cool for how as many legal loops you'd have to deal with EA as that may be, a face, something!Marcus is so bad as the team manager, he's too green. I don't care about his African roots, tell me something about his own racing career and make that interesting! For something like The Office you'd need a comedy troupe and these folks have chemistry of a Need For Speed cutscene. For experienced people in racing they sound horribly amateurish. The whole aesthetic is such a bland copy of ProStreet, trying to be all kewl for teh kidz. That shxx is mid AF. You already had that feel with the first game, then you went all minimalistic white stripes and now you're adding random kool graphics here and there, it doesn't fit the whole 'lets be professional' aesthetic, does it now?Just on story alone makes this game unbearable, imagine my gripes with the damn gameplay!Driving is a tenth Grid 1 and nine tenths Need For Speed. It's so stiff I don't think any level of in-game settings are gonna get you to that first game feel. That looseness the steering has was something unparalleled to any other game and a shame its never been back. I'm almost sure they sacrificed such beautiful DEFAULT steering for more peripheral compatibility. And the handbrake, holy shxxxxxxxxxxxxx. If you know, you know. I never figured it would be near-impossible to drift on a front-drive car with even spamming the handbrake button. Unforgivable.As for variety, trucks? Really? Were the devs playing DiRT while making this game? Weeeeee really bad suspension weeeeee i feel like a carmageddon powerup hit me weeee and why do i have the feeling that we're not gonna get a LeMans? I got that within the first hour of the first game, sheesh.Speaking of carmageddon, and i'm talking the second one, why can't you make an AI that have personalities? Not just a  spectrum between aggressiveness, control, bladibla but like Carma have them toggle between 'sulking' and 'racing' and 'looking for trouble'. Perhaps even build up a preferences list like getting -10 driving at midnight touge or rainy circuits, aside from the standard weaknesses. Same can be applied to strengths too!Penalties that MAY be applied by stewarts have to be seen immediately, its kinda dumb for a SIMCADE game to have limits on the tracks.And the graphics... looks like they skimped on the cockpit cam again, the mirrors are barely rendered even at everything maxed out. Y'all be playing on DX12 yet no Ray Tracing, huge miss. The settings are pretty bland too, resolution rendering dependent on 30/60 fps? cuhringe.This game boils down to CM wanting to make a NFS game, failing at it and I regret getting this even on a 60 percent sale. Unless this is 80 percent off and you like turning your brain off too, don't get it. This smells like a cash grab and such a huge waste of talent, I'd honestly rather have written a review in how rehashed this was and too samey to the first game than this mess. My ache recently for racing made me buy this and next time i will just reinstall the first game. Lesson learned.

_childDocuments_.review: GRID Legends is a serviceable arcade racer but ultimately is too simplistic and bland. The driving physics even for a arcade style racer is far too forgiving the car is pretty much glued to the track, way too much grip. The handling overall just feels bad and even with all the assists turned off it's like the car is driving itself. The "Story" mode campaign features a campy but entertaining cast of live action sequences which I enjoyed, but even during the short runtime of the 4 seasons of that you could tell the game lacks depth. I did really appreciate the attempt to add some drama but it's kinda lame. The actually career mode is very bland and grindy and has a poor sense of progression. You always have to grind for upgrades before entering the finale event in a series it ruins the pacing and discourages trying new cars. The car list is decent but has some huge holes, the track list is average at best but they look nice. The visuals are beautiful especially the weather effects are superb and the performance is mostly great. The game has a few different race modes which is nice but the career doesn't use them enough. No qualifying or tire wear/fuel consumption even on so called "endurance" races. I thought this game was more of a middle ground between Sim and Arcade like Grid series use to be but it's not at all. The AI on one hand is great because they make mistakes and actually crash but they are stupidly easy even on Hard difficulty and they don't seem to be able to see the player and just run straight into you. The engine/exhaust sounds are pretty good but i've heard much better but I do like the commentators they did a good job but the lines get repetitive quickly. It's a very casual game and easy to pick-up and play which is great if that's what you want and on sale is still worth while if you enough racing games, just don't expect anything spectacular. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Codemasters is my second favorite racing game developer, after Papyrus. I played the heck out of the TOCA touring game games in the 90's. Although I love my sim racing, their blend of sim/arcade can be so enjoyable without being stressful, and also very accommodating to those using joystick/game controllers. Unfortunately, their last several efforts have been disappointing. While the car physics are still quite good, the experience has gotten far more arcade-like than sim. The worst, and the primary reason for the thumbs down, is the poor AI. To me, if it feels as though the AI has not improved over their past several games. They have marginal positional awareness, adhering to their racing lines, which waaaay too often results in being punted from behind or the sides. The weird physics that does not allow you to turn the car when there is another stuck to the side of you is still present, and incredibly frustrating. I've played almost 3 hours and that is enough to know that I'll never play again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game got a lot of stick just like old TRD1 (Toca/Pro Race Driver) and I honestly don’t see much of an issue. Its kind of the same level as TRD1 for me.Game has all the content that GRID 2019 had including its DLC’s plus new tracks/cars and old favourite locations from Grid 2, the game looks just as good if not better and the handling model has been refined again to be less realistic as GRID 2019 and to be a tad more arcadey in my opinion but not as much as GRID 1 or 2 and its good feeling I think. The game has a story mode that includes Ryan McKanes return that are acted out with real actors, a bit cringe but I loved it to be honest. Theres 4 DLC’s, only 2 of them being any worth playing. The first and last DLC’s are just lame: first being destruction derby, which should be fun, but isn’t designed properly and the last one is just a mash of game modes that isn’t anything to shout about. DLC’s 2 and 3 cover endurance racing at new track Fuji and the history of Ravenwest team which does some nice callbacks to the older GRID games.Post story there’s a non story career mode which is unfortunately about as grindy as GRID 2019’s. It has a lot of events but each event uses a wider variety of tracks and weather combinations to keep it quite fresh. The grind comes in sponsor objectives and getting into the final league of the mode where you have to master every car discipline but every finale race of the disciplines require a fully upgraded car which can only be unlocked from driving 25 miles with the car - but in most cases the game only gives you 2 events to use with the car. So you end up having to make single races grinding out mileage on the car for an upgrade which is dumb, the game is long enough it didn’t need that.  On the track the AI is much better than the last game and opponents cars can just get critical malfunctions out of nowhere which just adds more action to the race, plus the soundtrack that plays in story mode makes the races hyped up. Some race characters are also complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and really ram into you if you try to pass them. The team driver AI also can be upgraded to let you pass, etc bringing a bit more depth to them but you cant hire anyone it has to be one person which doesn’t bother me. You can also upgrade the mechanic (who isnt as annoyingly repetitive as the last game) to give you money off cars and upgrades, etc which is okay.The games flaws as far as I see it are: DLC 1, the grindy career mode, the tacked on drift mode (which can be mostly avoided) and the simplistic tuning options. All in all the game isn’t as good as GRID 1 I don’t think any racer ever will be again but it’s a decent game that has learned from its past mistakes. I think many that are heavily low rating this game are mostly nostalgia salty that they don’t have GRID 1 again.

_childDocuments_.review: It took until now to finally get a GRID game that feels as good as the original, and in some ways surpasses it, even if it still has some flaws the series has been dragging around for over a decade. It addresses just about every shortcoming from the previous game to the point it renders it obsolete - more environments, more cars, more event types, much better career progression, and tighter handling.Ironically, the game's weakest aspect is the much touted story mode. The script itself is fine (it's just a fairly standard underdog story) - the issue is that there's no attempts to connect your actual performance with the plot to the point it undermines your own contributions to the team. It's clear Codemasters had a very specific tale they wanted to tell and the only way it works is if you assume you canonically finish races at the bare minimum needed to move on to the next event.My other issue is more about how Ravenwest, especially Nathan McKane, are now portrayed more or less as cartoon villains when previous games showed them more like when Audi was dominating LeMans about a decade ago - just a well funded racing team with the best drivers in the league. Still, this is basically just nitpicking on my part - besides, the real highlight of the game is its career mode.Instead of the incredibly dull and linear career mode of GRID 2019, we now have one that will encourage (and sometimes force) you to constantly switch around disciplines to break up the monotony. You will have to master racing touring cars, open wheel, drifting, stadium trucks, electric hypercars (with a new boost mechanics), and everything in between. You can easily spend 50 hours to be able to see everything it has to offer.The nemesis system is also now more meaningful since it carries over not just through events in career mode but will also impact how they will act in free play mode. By the time I reached the final race I'm pretty sure that half the drivers hated me and races were turning into a bloodbath. You will grow to hate them as much as they hate you when you find yourself eating a wall when one of them nudges you during a corner. The only gripe I have with the feature is that they don't understand context, so you can instantly piss someone off if you hit them after they spin out and there's no way to avoid them.There's also a new upgrade system that doesn't work very well in practice. Upgrades are unlocked by getting mileage on your cars and then paying for the upgrades themselves, but the issue is that every car has the exact same thresholds, so it takes longer to unlock them on, say, a Volkswagen Beetle than in a Mazda 787B. This creates two problems in career mode - in the early stages you'll be grinding for mileage to make progress, but in the later stages upgrades become very expensive so you'll have to save up money to be able to do the fully upgraded events.Your teammate is now a fixed character that you will gradually invest on to make him more competent and will eventually protect you against all the nemeses you've gained through your career. It makes your teammate a lot more useful than they were in older entries, but it's odd that it's a preset driver since he does not have any voice lines like teammates had in the first game. Still, it's an overall improvement.On a minor note, you will no longer get slowed down like a tethered electric go-kart when you're caught cutting corners; instead you will now get a warning if it wasn't too egregious, or get a time penalty that can affect your final position and a cash penalty.Unfortunately, the game still holds the long standing tradition of giving the AI drivers different physics than the one players get. Human drivers will lose in just about every collision scenario you can imagine - if you rear end someone, you will spin out and the AI will be fine; if they rear end you, you will spin out. It doesn't make the game unplayable by any means but it's disappointing to lose a race just because physics are against you when an accident occurs.Still, even if it's not as extravagant as Gran Turismo 7 or as accessible as Forza Horizon 5, GRID Legends is still a solid racing game that fills its niche of being one of the few racers with arcade physics using a track based setting. I would recommend it at full price if it weren't for the fact it's already being sold with a 34% discount as of this writing, and I wouldn't be surprised if you can get it for 50% off by the next big sale.

_childDocuments_.review: GRID Legends is quite a great improvement on prior GRID games! I've played them all but didn't really feel addicted beyond completing them. This one is resonating with me more - there's just a smidge more of everything here: more Driveclub-esque stunning weather effects that just make you want to stay in the car lap after lap, more oomph to the handling model (which was always Fun, but now it's Fun edging into Intriguing), more tracks that cross weird lines in my brain (is this a gorgeous sprint track through beautiful scenery, or is a circuit race? OH SNAP IT'S BOTH AND I CAN LOOP IT INFINITELY), more personality in the campaign that was just the right level of personality and camp (much on the grounded side as opposed to like an NFS 2015, as much as I loved that too).I beat the story and am now doing campaign - there's quite a few hours of things to do - and hope to make it to some multiplayer events while there's still a healthy community, love the crossplay and drop-in MP - really smart for a game in this genre.I also wanted to say, I have a severe injury to my right leg that lost me my ability to drive with a clutch, and thought If this is what EA + Codies be like, well sure, sign me right up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a clear negative or positive review. If neutral was an option, I would've picked that. This game is a bit complicated. I'll lump it into categories.1. The driving.The driving is very stiff and difficult, and practically unplayable on a controller. This is not purely an arcade racer, nor is it purely a sim, far from it. If you have a decent force-feedback wheel, you'll have an easier time playing this game, but that doesn't make it easy overall. It's past paced, easy to mess up, but really rewarding once you get the hang of it. Fun? hardly, driving is a complete chore in this game, but it's a step up from 2019. PS: I recommend setting the springs and dampening to max firmness in every event. I could hardly turn a corner if I didn't do that.2. The story.The story actually positively surprised me, despite really having some issues regarding pacing. But not to spoil anything, I won't elaborate too much further, other than to say that it seems the vast majority of development time has gone into the story and the events within, despite there both being a somewhat lack of variety and identity, AND it simultaneously manages to feel a bit drab towards the end, not to mention the ending, which.. spoiler alert, . But overall, I really enjoyed the story, and it's one I think I'll remember for some time.3. The career.Well. This is where it falls a bit short. When I learned that this game would have a career mode separate from the story mode, I got really excited. Fast forward to now, and I'm  I thought they would've learned their lesson after 2019, but alas, only very minor improvements. This game is basically GRID 2019 with a storymode added onto it, and some tacky car performance and perk trees that you can buy upgrades in for in-game currency, which don't feel fitting at all in a grid game. 4. Performance and graphics.It looks good.  even. And it runs just fine on my outdated hardware on high graphics with consistent frames above 60. Though I'm hearing it doesn't really utilize the full potential of newer, more powerful hardware, and has a hard time reaching 120+, so take from that what you will. I think it performs overall more than acceptable.5 Bugs.Didn't find many in my relatively short time with the game. Sometimes the opponents would do their spectacular spin-outs and rolls, but  in front of me, and it was clear the in-game director didn't take my position in relation to the affected car into consideration, when choosing to make Claire Fox suddenly turn their car 90° and start barrel-rolling down the track, in less than a second, just a few meters in front of me. It's cool, sure, but it's a bit on the nose when it's so obvious about it. And well, that's about it, really.6. Connection to other GRID games.Seeing Ravenwest back, and even getting to see a portrayal of Nathan McKane is really awesome. As a long-time GRID fan, the story really tickled me in a lot of right ways. Many of the old track layouts like Chicago, San Francisco, and especially Yokohama docks is particularly awesome. Even the spin on Okutama is really nice. Good tracks all around, no complaints there. I even spotted Euro Rand at some point, though I don't remember where exactly. If you're a GRID fan like me, there's a lot you might recognize.7. Verdict.There's two sides to this. On one hand, the story is really cool and well done and all, but the story is also the best the game has to offer, and it only takes about 5 and half hours to complete. I really hope they add a lot more content similar to the story, especially considering I blew 80 euros on the deluxe edition, practically just praying it'll be worth it. And on the other hand... it's just GRID 2019 with a slight update. All the meat of the game, all the cars, custom events, all that, is in the career and online. And well.. that's just 2019, with a little bit more variety, and a fresh coat of paint.So is it worth the money? .. I can't bring myself to say yes. Don't get me wrong, you can do a lot worse, but that's more of a testiment to how absolutely repulsive and sickening the current state of the triple-A gaming industry is. Though, I had a good time with the story, but I'm not touching the excuse for a career mode. For that itch, I'm booting up GRID (2008).

_childDocuments_.review: I feel I've put in enough time to leave a review. If I could vote mixed, I would... but honestly I'm leaning more "no." Especially if you've played the original Race Driver GRID from 2008.For a game that was basically a redux of Grid 2019 to resolve all of that titles problems, why does this game still lack several features from a title that came out 14 years before it? Why can't I choose a spoken name to be used by my pit crew? Why can't I change my teammate and hire new options based on a performance wheel? Why are sponsors on my car fixed to vinyls instead of being fully customizable with bonus rewards depending on my performance in every race? Why is the car damage model still not able to replicate what we had in GRID 2008? Where's the truly dynamic music that changes depending on whether you're idle, racing, or on the last lap? Why is there seemingly no music in Career mode? That's just the tip of what I've come across in my 10+ hours of game time. I don't understand how a modern title can't keep up with features found not only in GRID 2008, but also Colin McRae's DiRT 2. Codemasters was on top of the world during the late 2000s, yet can't seem to replicate what I'd call a brief but stellar golden era.And sweet baby Jesus, what on earth did Codemasters do to Ravenwest in this game? I'd call it character assassination, but that's underselling just how badly they butchered Ryan and Nathan McKane. I'm not gonna spoil it, but if you're a fan of TOCA Race Driver or GRID 2008, you'll hate what they've done to these two just as much as me.
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: Where Grid 2019 felt like a good racer that lacked spice and content, Grid Legends packs a punch. Way more tracks(beautifully designed), BGM during races that make for that extra adrenaline kick, wayyyy more cars and actual flavor during the career mode. The biggest improvement is the handling imo. It's still arcade and no match for a Sim racer but it feels perfect on the controller.(sth that bothered me A LOT) in Grid 2019.The addition of the story is also a treat. Sure, this ain't a high production value netflix drama, but it does achieve that it gives a purpose to drive and a nice theme to the whole thing. Definetly wanna see this in other upcoming racing games.It might take about 3-4hrs to finish but it's an appetizer to the bigger career mode that comes after and is filled with content.I'd say if u got bored of Forza Horizon(i kinda got) and just want straight up action packed track racing with stunning visuals, sound effects and a really good AI that feels quite alive, look no further. This is Grid coming back to glory. It doesn't have the same impact as the OG Grid back then, but there is,no denying that this is the best Grid-like racer you can buy for money these days.Sth maybe worth adding, depending on who cares: Flawless optimization right out of the box. No fps drops, bugs, crashes etc. And very moderate requirements.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:👍 Excellent AAA Graphics.👍 Perfectly optimized. Game runs so smooth for the high end visuals.👍 Loads of vehicles.👍 Physics are top quality arcade, with excellent feel on a steering wheel.👍 Very realistic audio.👍 The AI isn't too bad.👍 Weather affects are very good.👍 Progression is steady, without too much grind.👍 One of the only non-VR racing games that looks great in Cockpit view without giving you a visual disadvantage.👍 Plug-and-Play - No tweaking settings for this game. It runs perfect as it is. (The only thing I did was turn off Stability Control)Cons:👎 Honestly haven't came across any Cons yet. At first I thought the steering had an unwanted Deadzone, but turns out to be loose steering for that particular vehicle, which fits into the Arcade style of physics.Summary:This is exactly what a modern arcade game should feel like. _childDocuments_.review: Grid Legends might be the game where they tried the best to have a personality but I felt this was the least Grid experience after playing all the others Grid games.This is not the first racing game using real life actors and probably won't be the last. Sports games do it and it can be a hit or miss. I felt it was mostly well done but I feel it's hard to have a proper story with racing games and if you're like me, you just want to race and not caring for a vendetta, taking revenge or becoming the underdog. I just want to race.And when it comes to racing there's plenty to game on. This is the third time I play Grid Legends story (on 3 different platforms, hence why the short play time on Steam since I just went for the story). The different racing categories are all over the place and nobody knows why exactly. From circuit races to a drift events, followed by elimination races and also racing in a truck while trying not to destroy the Minis on the track. Once again, if you just want to race you'll enjoy the story but if you're looking a specific categories only, then there's quite a fine selection of championships to go as well specific special events. Sound design felt solid and this is a good opportunity to say that soundtrack can be hit or miss. Often I felt I was like in an action movie where the hero saves the day in the last second before defusing a bomb. I could see a different type of soundtrack but I understand such decision could mean music licensing and a higher budget. Physics felt okay if you look at Grid Legends strictly as an arace race. Trying to bring sim expectations will leave you disappointed because it's far from it, especially collisions with other races.Completing the story and all the races will rob you some decent time so you'll be busy for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's my bad and uninformed opinion from someone who only recently got into racing games:- The story mode is just a series of different racing events interspersed with cheesy live action cutscenes. They feel very heavy and have a lot of grip for some reason. Some cars are also way more sluggish than they should be, almost as if the speedometer is inaccurate. - Good god I can already see a lot of unnecessary grind. You need credits to purchase new vehicles (not too out of the ordinary), but then you also need to put miles on those cars to unlock the privilege of purchasing upgrades for those cars. I  hate that kind of padding.I did have a bit of fun with it at times but I don't think I'd pay $60 for it.

_childDocuments_.review: "On track, But Missing the Apex"Long time fans of the TOCA and GRID series will find themselves wanting after experiencing what GRID Legends has to offer. The game packs a punch in the graphics and sound department, with beautiful engine notes complimenting the striking visuals. When raytracing gets involved, it has a beauty that is unmatched and colorful. These many improvements are thanks to refinements to Codemasters' Ego engine. However, the beauty of this game is simply a mask covering up it's faults and blemishes. The gameplay, while fast and arcadey, doesn't handle well and never feels like the successful GRID predecessors. With that said, it does seems to address many of the complaints raised about the handling of GRID (2019), but still feels off when compared to early games in the series, that hooked users with wonderful physics and driving mechanics.  The core systems of owning a team, managing expenses, and advancing through a career don't make an appearance in this title which adds to the lists of disappointments and continues the trend of GRID (2019) frustrations. To add, the reward of advancement is absent, which tends to make the player feel a disinterest in furthering the pursuit for late game content. Over the top of the lackluster career, there is a menu system that will make you hate having to use it. Unintuitive seem to be a common theme through out all parts of this game's  processes and the UI is no exception. A new edition to this year's title is a story mode, that even though cheesy, can be a fun way for new players to experience the GRID series because of the recent successes with Netflix's Drive to Survive. The only issue with this game mode, is that if you win, there is no adaptive story arch that is created, which is a huge oversight from the development team. Changes in scenario have been addressed by many franchises in the past five years and so has adaptive storytelling. Team objectives are great, but any racer will tell you that they want to win, otherwise there is no point in racing.With everything out of the way, we are onto my final thoughts. Now that the story mode has been done, it is time to move on from this concept. The originality is good, but it was a waste of resources that could have been applied elsewhere. Handling definitely needs to be worked on, it did not even reach the lowest expectations, when compared to successful titles in the series. The career mode desperately needs a rework and following the template from Racedriver GRID, with improvements is the answer to remedy this folly. If I was in charge of this project, I would have made it so. To add, with the wonderful games that Codemasters has created over the years they have all the tools to make the World Series Racing, truly a world series of events. Track, drift, and rally, are all in the repertoire of the wonderful development team at Codemasters and deserve a seat at this table, or at least in consideration for a seat in the WSR discussion. As long as these issues go unchanged, this series will miss the apex and continue to find the gravel on exit. If you have made it this far, thank you for reading my review, I hope that this helps you in your decision on your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute comeback of a game compared to what happened to Grid 2019. 5 well-written and engaging story modes allow you to enjoy bits of the lore behind the Grid World Series across the entire franchise, as well as help you build funds to kickstart your Career, which is pretty long but has you explore the entire car roster it has to offer.The Hop-In multiplayer system makes it so much more fun by putting you in scenarios similar to the prologues of ToCA Race Driver 2 and 3, as you try to discover how far up you can finish in the usually small time frames given.Physics are enjoyable enough for a not-so-simcade racer.My only complaints are that kerbs often curse you with spin-outs, the stats menu hinted that probably more events would be added after the DLCs but that didn't really happen, there is a typo in one of the derby event objectives, and the upgrade that has your teammate let you pass him while nearby often feels more like a downgrade, with tendencies to either brakecheck you or slow down so much to the point of him dropping a lot of positions. Teammate contract systems from Grid Autosport are sadly missing as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty bad experience right from the start. After first start up of the game, it kept telling me to press 6 to continue but that would never work. I tried everything. Eventually after button mashing for a minute it dumped me right into a race. No chance to set up controls or anything. If you've ever played a racing game before on PC you know that you ALWAYS need to bind controls before it works right, and Grid was no exception. I had no gear shift, FFB was not working, steering felt terrible, etc.After finally finding my way to the main menu, the menu kept spazing out. Wouldn't let me click on things, then when it finally did click it registered a bunch of times and didn't act as expected.At this point I'm just gonna call it a lost cause. Unfortunate, as it looked fun.

The new drifting mode is disappointing and feels awkward to handle cars in it.It's a pretty fun game, but I personally think i'll get bored of it really quick.Graphics are amazing, I have a 1080 GTX and it can still provide 4k quality all settings at ultra. I have a sound issue with this game, I did with GRID 2019 too, where the audio sounds like the CPU is overloaded when it's not. The spectral audio settings make it worse and sound like a bassboosted bad headset, keeping that disables limits the memory leak feel audio.This game was in works before EA acquired Codemasters, so we'll have to see what the future holds for Codemasters, hopefully a completely new Need for Speed game made in works with Criterion.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it. If you like/prefer arcade and simcade racing games on streets and nature tracks in various locations (that eliminate games like Need for Speed which are always set in just one location/one city and are unfortunately ultra repetitive) like Project Gotham Racing 4 and DriveClub, this game is perfect for you, I don't see how you could not like it.Actually, I really I don't understand all the hate the game (and its predecessor) gets. Sure if you swear only by racing sims and what I consider boring tracks (base on real life dull tracks, the same you see in every single racing games like Asseto Corse, Forza Motorsport etc.), this game is definitely not for you, but if you like arcade/simcade racing games on fun tracks streets/nature (juse one, the Alps) closed tracks like Paris, Barcelona, Shanghai, Japan etc. and misss games like Project Gotham Racing, then you'll have a great and fun time with GRID Legends (even GRID 2019).+ Graphics+ Run easily at 4K 90fps on a RTX3080 with all settings on max+ Fun+ Street tracks and plenty of locations (it's like 80% of the tracks)! Paris, Barcelona, Havana, Shanghai, Japan, San Francisco, Chicago etc. a real pleasure+ Unnoficial VR suuport via Reshade VR+ For those who like Project Gotham Racing 4 and DriveClub+ You don't need to launch the EA App to play the game+ Crossplay- A bug with HDR and the EA app makes that when you launch the game and didn't close EA App before, your monitor (at least mine) goes on "no signal" mode and your controlelr is not recognized anymore and you have no other choice that restarting your PC- The grinding to buy new car but it's the same in other racing games; so...- I would have loved a Tokyo race... There Yokohama docks and onein the mountains in Japan, though, but racing i nthe streets of Tokyo would have been amazing.I hate DLCs in games, but I would have been happy to see a DLC with new street and nature tracks (Tokyo, Mexico, Miami, Rio De Janeiro, Seoul, Hong Kong, Roma, India, nature tracks like in DriveClub too)

Also worth to mention racing with the AI is a horrible experience as they are overly agressive / suicidal and doesn't pay attention to the line you are holding and gets in the way a lot.In the story missions their shooting a cinematic 1'st person NFS 2015 like experience casting with real actors. _childDocuments_.review: Grid Legends builds on the 2019 release of Grid, and it does some things fantasticallyand some things dull"ish", what do I mean? In all fairness Codemasters have latelybeen on a roll when it comes to Racing games, from the brilliant F1 series to the Dirt series to (in my opinion) a good reboot of Grid (2019). Grid Legends followsthe path of good racing as seen in the previous installment and improves upon that.While Grid Legends expands on what we saw in Grid (2019) with a ton of cars, more locations with different layouts, and a fun cheesy story mode (totally worth playing), overall it left me wanting a bit more out of the game from the get go..  What do I mean? even though there are more locations than ever with variations, it would have been fun to see even more locations, maybe even take the racing a bit off track for the truck classes that are in the game, we're trying to become Legends after all right?And maybe the other thing that I was left wanting, would have been taking the Nemesis systema bit further.. But I'm not dissapointed at all with the end result. So don't get me wrong. I am totally happy with the amount of things there is to do already in Grid Legends, It will have You and Me still spend plenty of hours to finish everything there is in the game so far, and I'm pretty sure we can expect some more goodies addedas time passes. So for the good things I spoke about ; What you are in for is a bit of a treat overall in all honesty, I said the Story mode istotally worth playing, and I stand behind that.. even if the acting in some sense couldbe called cheesy, it takes a loan from Netflix's drive to survive kind of angles, filmed over shoulder occasionally trying to be sneaky catching a glimt to hear what's saidand the drama between the teams, including of course as anyone would expect plot twistson the way.. So over the course of 36 chapters, you'll be racing for Seneca to become aGrid Legend, and I do think you will find the story mode rather fun once you've finished it.Kudos to Codemasters for putting the story mode into the game, to give additional value to the whole package, I give a thumb up for this service.More good things? Like I said there is a ton of locations and variations of the tracks, and that you will be spending hours upon hours in the career mode to Finish everything.There is a total of 22 Locations, from San Fransisco to London to Yokohama; so you willbe racing practically around the globe, and these tracks do come with a total of 137 variations/layouts (if I counted that correctly with my old head), and from all the classes you can pick from (Electrical, Trucks, Drifting)mentioning the new classes, to all the classic classes that you know about GT, Touring etc.These classes feature more than a 120 different cars so far.. so you are sure to finda car that you love and know..If you want to be more outrageous than what the game offers straight up for you, Legends also comes with a Race Creator so you can mix and match classes layouts locations weatherspecifically up to just as you want it, be it regular Circuit racing or a Elimination race.. you pick, you choose, you race.Before I forget I have to give the music in game, a special mention and a thumbs up. The picks for tracks, got nailed right on the head and normally I do go to the optionsand turn off the music in game, but this time around I felt like nope, I'm going to leave it on as it gave a good feeling and that extra heart bump in the heat of racing. Online is a big part of the game besides the Career, and you can part take in Quick Races, or even a dedicated session with your friends, so you are bound to have some fun momentsin there as well. What I've tried out of the online racing so far, I have not noticedany issues, so that's a good start to things, (me being cynical and thinking aboutusually online modes how they work) but no such voes here. I've been playing the game on PC, and besides 1 odd bug relating to using the rewindfeature in game, I've not come across anything that I would describe as game breaking,not even a crash to windows, so for that I'll give solid points on how the game is built.It is though quite resource heavy, compared to Grid 2019, but that is to be expectedwe are in 2022 after all, and Graphics have gone forward since then.. Playing on an i5-9600k and a Nvidia 3070 (8GB) with 16GB of memory, garnered I wouldsay an average of around 100-110fps in game (Playing at 3440x1440) with HDR enabled.It's a smooth experience, and loading times are fast (assuming you have an NVME ssd)I've included above a plenthora of Screenshots from in game, and the menus to give you an understanding of all the options / choices there are in game.. as well someRacing action. So.. what now? Final word; GRID Legends, is a worthy successor to Grid (2019) with a cheesy storymode, with plenty of locations, cars, multiplayer, A race creator that will give you tons of playability, replayability, onlineability.. Yes, I just did that.And I believe you will have a fun time playing the game. Go and become a Legendit's totally worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game with very accessible simcade style driving. The main campaign is pretty fun, having you drive events in between 'drive to survive' style docu-drama videos, telling a story of a new underdog team rising through the ranks and challenging the cocky champions. It's cool, but unfortunately your actions have very little impact on the story. The only thing is do you meet the requirements for each event, yes then continue, no then you have to do it over. If the requirement is finish at least 11th, but you place 1st? Absolutely no difference, you don't even get a radio message cheering for when you do win, it's just a mild 'well done', same as if you had placed 11th (which was the goal). Still, it's fun for the 5 hours that it lasts.After that you can start your own team in the rookie class and you can work your way up through the ranks in different disciplines. The racing is still a lot of fun, but unfortunately the AI is not very good. I usually drive at 'expert', which only has 'legend' above it. It's way too easy, in most events I'm in first place after a few laps and far ahead by the time we finish. However on legend difficulty, the AI cheats, while they're still bad drivers. They are very slow in the corners, but somehow are still very hard to overtake depending on the track. I've seen people online say they just get really fast on the straights, having higher topspeeds than is possible for you, and this seems true to me. So in corners it's easy to be surprised by how much they brake, making it easy to accidentally slam into them, but even if you can use this to overtake them, they will then roar past you on the straight. And by the time you make it to 3rd or 2nd place, you'll find the number one car has been using that time to get 20 seconds ahead. One other strange aspect of the AI is they will just randomly crash. And I do mean random, they'll be going along a straight and just out of nowhere dive into the barrier... Very odd.The AI is relatively clean driving though. Only if you smash into them a lot they become your nemesis (like when they brake way too much for corners, be ready for that), then they'll be more aggressive, but mostly it's possible to do clean racing with them. Definitely better than Forza Horizon in this regard.One thing I do really like is there is a setting in the difficulty to make races longer. You can set this to 2x to 4x I believe. Unfortunately because of the AI this is less useful than it could be. It was fun at expert when I was still learning the game, but legend level is too annoying to play against so now on expert if I increase the number of laps it just increases the number of laps I am out in front and only ever see backmarkers.The game is a lot of fun to drive though and especially on sale I would recommend it (I got it for €5,99), even if I probably wont stick with it for very much longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Two patches and no fixes for big issues: Race Creator interface is bugged if you try to select boosts or laps, using arrows or the gamepad to interact with those elements makes the options scroll by too fast.Nemesis system is a permanent system with no cool downs. Read the driver names and note that they are forever your enemy, if your position is close to theirs it triggers aggro like you impacted them. These drivers never cool down and you might as well restart if you make a new one by accident.These issues have been reported and do not get resolved. This is a potentially good game marred by flaws.Also, the drifting portion of the game is awkward given how grippy the cars are.

There is a TV like quality like one of those daytime soaps. Looks a bit weird.The biggest letdown is the Nemesis system. The AI drivers are suicidal and constantly getting in the way. To be fair most racing games have terrible AI but this one seems particularly bad. There also aren't a lot of tracks. They advertise 130 tracks but most are just layout variations. There are only 22 tracks in reality. You soon learn them all and the game does get stale. It's 30+ hours of fun though. Well worth it especially when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice arcade racer, physics and handling are much better than in the previous entry in the series (Grid 2). Typical CodeMasters game. The city tracks look better than the closed circuits, and I also find them more fun.Pros:* Racing is fun & looks great.* It has a career mode, and an additional story mode with a story about two competing racing teams that is told through video clips. The story is predictable and a bit cheesy, but somehow I still enjoyed it, haha.* You race with a team mate, and can upgrade them and your mechanic between races with $ you earn. Team management lite. I do prefer racing to team management, so I like the way they implemented this. Upgrades should be cheaper though, so we can get more cars early on.* Lots of cars, classes and tracks. Great quick race creator, you can even drive cars you haven't unlocked yet (loaning for some in-game cash).* Great sense of speed, especially with the prototype cars.* Works will with gamepad (I use Xbox controller, default setup was perfect).Cons:* Not that many. It's a bit too casual for me, but that's a matter of taste.* The races with the trucks are a bit annoying. There aren't that many though.* I own the standard edition, and all menus are filled with options that are shown, but only give a message "Please buy DLC to really be able to access this content.", which feels really bad after buying a game.* A bit too much grinding to unlock cars for my taste. Same goes for upgrades, which require you to drive a certain mileage with the car before you can get them.If you wanted to know that: Yes, Forza Horizon 4 and 5 are both slightly better, I have them as well.I got this for 10€ and would recommend for that price. I do not regret that I did not buy any DLC or the more expensive editions that include more content. I liked the story and started playing a bit of the career, but I am very sure I will be done with this game before I finish the career.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Take some of the realistic aspects of Gran Turismo (5), mix those with the arcade approach of Forza Horizons (4 or 5) and  mix  with some of absurdness found in Burnout Paradise and you'll get a good idea what Grid Legends is all about!I played with all of the titles I mentioned above and while you will  get any "this being better than that" comments from me I  want to state that Grid Legends deserves its place amongst those other titles because it manages to add something which the others don't have...  a  entertaining mixture between simulated and arcade gameplay.For example, the way the AI can make mistakes or worse: completely break down or crash is something you don't see happening in those other titles, not like this. But there's more... what about hitting the curbs too hard and then ending up with your 2 wheels in the air? With a little luck you'll be able to correct yourself, but if you're not careful then this can have some serious results.Another important difference is that races don't always have to be clean, and if there are collissions then things can get really heated up. First the collisions appear a lot more realistic to me, cars can literally spin out of control or get into bigger accidents. But better yet: other AI drivers can actually become mad at you and thus turn into a nemesis; a driver who is out to get you. Meaning that if you approach them they can even move out of their line to try and block you, or worse...  Tick someone off hard enough then this rivalry could even carry onto other races too.The story is simple... team Seneca has a problem because the co-driver for their star, Yume Tanaka, turns out to be a complete doofus who can't even keep their car on the road. So that's where you come in: once you managed to get the attention of the Seneca scout you'll soon be part of the team.You will unlock extra contents as you complete challenges such as making sure finish above a certain position, and you'll also earn credits for doing so. These credits can then be used to buy upgrades or new cars. Apart from story mode you can also follow up on your own career in "Career mode"; this allows you to participate in a wide variety of race types and events. From the classic laps on a circuit, a "point to point" race on a larger track right down to time trials and even demolition derbies! Ever wondered what could happen if you were to combine trucks with open wheel racing cars and then maybe also add some GT racing cars to that mix?  Well, Grid Legends can help you find out ;)Although really entertaining this game does have some issues. For example I've experienced a few sporadic "crashes to desktop" ("CTD") which I cannot explain. But there are also little things... during story mode I manage to score one victory after the other and yet the story keeps pounding over how hard things are for the team and how bad things are going. Making me wonder... "excuse me?", I'm writing up victories and somehow this doesn't affect the team?Speaking of which... things also get a little weird when you start playing with your own team in career mode because one moment you're part of Seneca, the other it's suddenly your own team which prevails.Small things for sure (apart from the sporadic crashes) but weird nonetheless.If you're into racegames then this is most definitely something to consider. A huge selection of cars, a large variety of circuits, tracks and areas to race through and you'll find tons of action here.Ever been in a race where you see your car literally falling apart piece by piece?  Yah, that's another thing which you can experience in Grid Legends.Two thumbs up from me!

_childDocuments_.review: I will update this review once my trial expires.At time of writing this, i've accumulated ~1.2h ingame time.My current rating:Love it- It's an improvement over GRID 2019. I'm here for the career section.Love how they've brought back older maps and updated them.Yet to try drifting. Fingers crossed.Edit #1: Roughly 5 hours of ingame time, here's what I've got to sayThe good:The driving model- Steering response is quick and does not feel sluggish. It doesn't get as boring quick. They've even got the old togue tracks with winter. Oh my lord do they look beautiful.Tuning and upgrades:Upgrades aren't just for Tuning, like they were in Autosport. Here they give you a little performance boost.Tuning is just like in Autosport, I'm assuming the higher the level of part= More fine tuning.Progression:You level ups cars by driving them, which is an interesting approach. _childDocuments_.review: I am a long time fan of the Grid series, and I was really looking forward to this one, and as you can see, I've put in over 60 hours of game-play in it. Alas, I am done trying to justify it and enjoy it in my head. So what's wrong with it?- The core racing mechanics are engaging and fun and have a nice balance between arcade and realism, a signature staple of the Grid series. Check.- Graphics are excellent, even by today's standards (2023), and the game can look gorgeous on mid range PC's as well. Check.- Career mode is an abysmal disgrace from both the game design and the implementation side of things. Game design wise, it is utterly uninspired, bland and just a progression with no investment of any kind. Implementation is frustratingly bugged out, even after a bunch of patches and updates. The system will frequently not detect completed conditions for unlocking next stages of the career progression, effectively leaving you stuck, and sometimes, Tiers that were 100% completed will get the flashing exclamation mark, suddenly marking all of the completed events as new? Gigantic fail.- Story mode is a joke. You get videos that you sit through that are not engaging, amusing, or serve any purpose really, other than to artificially inflate game-play hours. Strip away the useless videos, and you have the same bog standard racing events with absolutely nothing special added to them. Fail.So at its racing core, Grid Legends is a great game, but everything else that was supposed to make use of that awesomeness fails to such a degree, that it is very hard to justify playing or even owning this game. Hard Pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Race Driver: Grid and Grid 2 are some of my favorite arcade racers, so when I saw the newest installment in the series go on sale I was eager to pick it up. If you're expecting it to be like those games, be prepared to be disappointed. Gone is the fun, playful handling model of the old games that makes you feel like a badass as you carve through the pack. Gone are many of the narrow, technical courses that push the limits of your car and your driving ability as you careen through turns at breakneck speeds, one mistake away from a spectacular crash. Gone is the high-risk high-reward style that gave early Grid games that spark of magic.Here's my general overview of the game. The physics feel dull and neutered compared to older Grid games. The AI can race decently well but don't expect any good one-on-one battles. Scripted crashes are frequent and unconvincing, I once found myself in third place on the final lap and by the end of the race both cars in front had spun out and flipped on completely straight sections of the track. The damage model is a major step down from the previous Grid games I've played. The story mode is fine but feels less engaging than previous titles, I found myself skipping past the cutscenes. Career mode is nothing special, and annoyingly it will automatically put you in an online lobby unless you go into the settings menu to disable it. The menu itself is cluttered and confusing, it feels like they were focused on packing in "features" than creating a cohesive gameplay experience. Everything feels shallower and less polished than previous installments in the Grid franchise.The game overall is dull and doesn't do anything particularly well. It doesn't uphold the legacy of the old Grid games, and it ultimately lacks any exciting elements to make it stand out from other new titles in a market full of better racing games.

_childDocuments_.review: -REVIEWED AS A CASUAL SIMRACER WITH A TRIPLE MONITOR SIM RIG-UPDATE: The black bars on the side monitors are still there in the menus and when you rewind, and I also found out that they appear when ever you use rewind. They do STILL cover a majority of the side monitors when they are present. THIS NEEDS TO BE FIXED in the next update. Devs have fixed the problem with the HUD showing up in the far right and left corners of the side monitors when using triples, it now shows up on the center display like it should. After spending several hours comparing the handling of this game to Grid 2019 I can gladly say that this feels a bit better and more intuituve for an arcade racer. Enough to earn it a buy and a positive rating.Another thing that I crave is the option to adjust your seating position in game so that the interior of the car matches your steering wheel IRL. PLEASE CODEMASTERS? OLD NEGATIVE REVIEW: Got 1 month of EA Play just to try this game on my triple monitor sim rig and wow, it's UNPLAYABLE due to the fact that Codemasters for some reason decided to add thick black bars covering most of the side monitors when you are in the game menus. This results in not being able to see all the options for calibrating your wheel and pedals etc. Also the HUD when racing ends up in the far out corners of the side monitors, making them impossible to see without turning your head 90 degrees left or right. Not at all ideal when you just want to glance at the track map and so on.There is also NO OPTION to move the seating position like in Dirt Rally 2.0, and the FOV-slider just doesn't go far enough for me to be able to sync up the ingame cockpit with my sim racing gear. Grid 2019 suffered from the exact same issues, and sadly they haven't been adressed in this iteration of the series either. The developers REALLY need to fix these issues if I'm ever going to be able to play this game again. The driving part of the game seemed alright and rather fun, almost like Grid 2. Sure this is and arcade racer but as it stands right now Codemasters are literally pissing in the face of anyone trying to enjoy their games with a proper sim rig with multiple monitors. They could just copy the code snippets from Dirt Rally 2.0 and voila - problem solved and no more pissing in my face! Right now this isn't (for a sim racer) even worth the 4 dollar fee for EA PLAY. Fix the proper support needed and I will gladly buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: My previous review was very negative because i encountered a critical bug where my Career had reset all progress after 100 hours.I decided to check back now that all the DLC was released, and to my surprise it seems like that bug and others like Sponsor objectives randomly "unchecking" were fixed. Haven't encountered any of those since i returned, which is good, so i decided to change the review to reflect the current state.It was a big shame that i had to write that one, because the game itself is great ( otherwise i wouldn't spend 100 hours, right? ) Yeah.The driving is fantastic with gamepad, very smooth and precise. I think it's the best handling model they have done, even better than GRID Autosport. Drifting is maybe even better than in the first GRID, which is saying something! :) Driving is leaning more on "simcade" side than on full simulation though, so if you are looking for a pure simulation game better look elsewhere.AI is generally pretty good, though sometimes they can be too aggressive on certain tracks and fail to "see you" on the track. In some tracks they are very faster than others, which is a shame that it still happens nowadays, but you can have great battles with them. :)HUGE amount of content on the Career mode, which is the "meat" of the game. Story serves as a preparation for the massive Career ( specially if you play on 2X length or more, you can select up to 5X ) and is nicely done, it's a decent 7-8 hour story ( not counting DLC's ).Optimization is good, i average about 90 fps @1080p High settings with my Ryzen 5600G + RTX 3060 setup, no stuttering of any kind. Graphics are nice, with great lighting, though there are some problems with rendering distance, specially on trees. Cars look and sound awesome, and there are a lot of them even without DLC's.While the game itself is excellent, it could be practically perfect if it had some missing features of real racing, like fuel consumption, tyre degradation, pitstops, flag system. And the ability to setup custom championships. These are things that Race Driver 3 had, which i still consider the best overall driving game since then because of them.Other negative things are the payouts for custom races being much lower than in career, and some sponsor objectives being quite grindy to achieve.

_childDocuments_.review: The GRID series was one of my favorite racing series. No more.The car physics are a complete joke, it is like you're driving on a predefined path and braking is only necessary for 15% of all turns. Everything else you can just drift through, since there is no weight or loss of traction to the cars, even with all driving assists disabled. Talking about drifting: it seems to have been put in as an afterthought, because "fans were screaming for it". You get four boring drift tracks, five drift cars, and a combo system that penalizes you for the slightest collision. Even collisions with the corner markers you're supposed to get as close as possible to. And if you decide to use a Flashback because of a mistake, your entire combo is lost too. Also: You cannot participate in some events because your car is not upgraded. Then you try to upgrade it, and it won't let you because you need to drive it for a certain number of kilometers. TF is up with that? They are putting up deliberate limits like these to artificially lengthen the game. Not player-friendly at all.More issues:- Soundtrack is missing in races outside of story mode.- Race commentary is inaudible (but is supposed to be there, according to subtitles)- When you turn off those annoying notifications about points for anything you do in a race (drafting, overtaking, etc), you also don't get see you score in drifting anymore. So you have to manually put that HUD back on whenever you start a drift race.- Hard difficulty is Easy. - Some of the city tracks have been recycled for multiple generations now. Boring.It hurts to say that the original GRID (2008) is better on so many levels. Car handling, damage models, collision impacts, track selection (mountain roads, Shibuya, Le Mans are heavily missed), demolition derby races; all better in a game that's almost 15 years old.

_childDocuments_.review: Might be weird to other people to say this about a racing game, but I became a GRID fan because of Ian Livingstone's music, and I've been a fan since the first GRID's release in 2008, when I was 7 years old. I do not care about driving mechanics, crash model, story, all that could be the worst thing imaginable, but if it had music composed by Ian Livingstone, it automatically would be a 10 in my book. This isn't to say that any of those things are bad here, I'm just saying it's already absolutely great because Ian made music for it. To be honest, the main motivation behind my purchase of this game was to extract the tracks and make mixes for personal listening, and I think this entry in the franchise has the best music from Ian yet, I would even say that, in my opinion, the Razor's Edge remake that came with Rise of Ravenwest is Ian Livingstone's magnum opus to date. I might be obsessed with the music from this game, because at this point it's the only thing I listen to. aside from GRID 1 and 2's tracks (which are just more Ian Livingstone).I know that Mark Willott also made music for this game, and the tracks are also good, Nate Unbound is one of my non-Ian favorites too, I'm just saying Ian has been here from the beginning, and I'm a fan of GRID because of him, and if Codemasters would drop him for some reason, I would honestly stop buying these games (so please Codies, Ian truly carries this franchise for me, absolutely get him on board for the next entry if there will be one). There's also one track that was made by Ian Livingstone's son, Ethan, and it's one of the best tracks in this entire game, so he also has a seal of quality from me (for all that's worth). For the longest time I thought that I was literally the only one on this planet to think this way about this franchise, but after Legends released now two years ago I discovered that there are more people like me thankfully,I know I'm probably weird for liking a racing game mainly for its music, but you can't disagree that if ranking the racing franchises for its music, GRID would always take the first place. Me becoming emotional over the music is also probably weird, but when I first heard Off the Grid and noticed the GRID 2 theme bit, I legit cried, as I did when Rise of Ravenwest first released and I heard the first game's remixes. So from that 7 year old in 2008 - genuinely thank you for still making these gems, and still having Ian Livingstone make music for them.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a big fan of Codemasters racing games for ages. Was very much looking forward to GRID Legends, despite not so hot reviews. Got the game and finally tried it. Played ~20 hours so far. Here is my take - I want to like it, I really do but I can't. 1. And my first HUGE complain is not even about the game mechanics, it is about UI and usability. After each race  there is a ~15-20 second unskippable timing screen. So, you are forced to sit and wait for 20 seconds after each race looking at some less than useful statistics...  Dear developer who programmed this unskippable timing screen, if you are reading this, please never ever do this again. This "feature" alone makes me regret buying this game.2. There are tons of other small usability complaints, such as racing wheel button 16 is a confirmation on some dialog screens while button 18 is a confirmation on other screens. Sponsor achievement requirements are shown as a scrolling line on a screen before the race but the scroll rate is too slow to see the 3rd requirement in most cases, etc.3. The game crashes once in a while. If you play for 2-3 hours, you will probably experience this. Here is the annoying part: if you are in a 3 stage race and the crash occurs while you are in the 3rd race - you will have to start all over again from the 1st race of the event. The developers haven't quite figured out that saving thing... Or, they really want you to learn some tracks well through endless repetition.Speaking of the devil, here is the racing part:4.  There is WAY too much grip. I've turned stability and traction control off, it did not seem to change anything much. Most cars stick to the road like they are on velcro... Feels quite a bit unnatural.5. Cranking the AI difficulty level seems to turning AI drivers into some aggressive psychopaths, if anything, their race craft becomes much worse. They are mostly ok up to about "High", however, when you change them to "Expert", they become completely psychotic by wildly sideswiping, ramming and driving with extreme level of aggression. The challenge shifts from beating them (which is not hard even on "Expert" level) to avoiding them ramming you of the track. And they are constantly doing it without warning or provocation. When you are driving a regular car, it is sort of ok, typically, you can get punted off the track or into a wall a couple of times and still win the race. The problem becomes unmanageable in open wheel racing. No matter what you do, it is highly likely that the bots will put their front wheel in between your front and rear and the next second you will be flying off the track spinning. And again, if this happens 2-3 times - it is survivable, but when you are coming from the back of the field, on "Expert" level, friendly bots driving will be constantly punting you to the back of the field. I find that above "Hard" AI difficulty, the open wheel racing in this game is no fun at all. It just an exercise in annoyance. The bad news about playing it on "Hard"? Once you passed all the bots (likely way before the end of the 1st lap), you will be bored to death driving the remaining laps trying to entertain yourself with sightseeing or counting spectators, once you are in front, the bots on "Hard" will not be a challenge.6. If you choose "Sequential" gearbox option, the clutch pedal does not work... Why? I have no explanation to this rather than there were times when Codemasters games were made by real car enthusiasts... These times seem to be over now. The consequence of this, if you are driving a slow car and were punted into a wall by bots, and need to reverse and then drive forward again, it will take forever - there is no way to rev up the engine and drop the clutch. 7. Most cars feel very similar. Even cars from different classes. Codemasters used to be great at making different cars handling and sounding differently. See my previous point - These times seem to be over now.8. Time attack issue. Time attack is a kind of racing when you are given 3 laps to set a fastest lap time. In general, because your car is just getting up to speed, the 1st lap is no good, it will be much slower then the rest. And here is the issue: when you go off track or cut a corner in time attack, the game invalidates not only your current lap but also your next one as well (two laps in total). Which means, if you made a mistake on lap two - your entire session is pretty much over - 1st lap is no good, laps 2 and 3 don't count due to your mistake on lap 2. I kind of understand why they did that, this is to prevent you from cheating at the very end of a previous lap (cutting corner) to get an advantage on the next lap. But this is a very lazy way of doing this. Again, car enthusiasts replaced by lazy developers. 9. The tracks. This is another highly disappointing moment. Not only this is about the smallest number of tracks which I've ever seen in a racing game but also all tracks have been lifted from the previous GRID games (did I mention lazy developers already?). I do not remember which game exactly but I've seen most if not all these tracks before. Here is the list by memory: Indianapolis, San Francisco, Chicago, Paris, Barcelona, Shanghai, Moscow, Suzuka (Yes!!!), Okutama, Havana, Red Bull Ring (Yes!), Sepang and Sydney. Pretty much everything else is a variation of the ones above. Conclusion:There are car racing games which have great campaign. There are others which offer good driving feel and plenty of racing tracks. Sadly, GRID Legends offers none of that. It is a shame. I really wanted to like this game.UPDATE:So far I was not able to finish Okayama Sprint race in heavy rain (Track Weapons, career pro). I've tried 6 times, the game crashed every single time. Annoyingly, two of the crashes were AFTER the race while on the timing screen. And, in order to progress with career, I need to finish this race type. Not to mention, every time it crashes, I need to repeat all previously completed races of the event...  Could be just my observation but the game seems to be crashing mostly during the wet races. Very, very disappointing. I'm close to giving up.UPDATE 2:The game is crashing often. Very irritating. Not only you need to re-do the race you were in, but also all previously completed races which are part of this event as well.There is something wrong with the on-screen timer. The timer shows time difference (delta) between you and the next car down. Normally, you'd expect the timer to shrink when you are braking into a hairpin and then stretch as you accelerate from the hairpin while the next car down is breaking into this hairpin, correct? This is called "concertino" effect. Well, the timer does not seem to show any of this. The timer seems to live its own life which only vaguely reflects the delta between you and the next car. Older Codemasters racing games used to be quite famous for communicating traction of various surfaces. If you drive over a patch of sand on tarmac - you would know it instantly as your car would lose traction. Not in Grid Legends. Running over a patch of snow on tarmac makes no difference whatsoever, there is no difference in traction at all.

(in a street circuit LOL) . talking about that, half of the tracks are city circuits.. all the same boring 90 degree corners all the same with little changes if not asthetic from one another... EA or codemasters whatever you prefer didn't even do their work. many car models and some tracks are from project cars or recycled from previous grid games (even the dlcs are actually just recycled content. hilarious).. this game just killed the little hope i had to see a game like toca race driver 2 or 3 happen again... everything about this game feels wrong... don't buy it.
