_childDocuments_.review: So lets get this right up front. This is not a sim racer, and it is very much an arcade racer.While I have given it a thumbs down. I do enjoy arcade racers and this while not amazing is not also that bad. In short its pretty but has lots of grind. Online play will be something to see how long it lasts in 3 months time.Pro's - The game looks very pretty like you should find in all good arcade games. I ran this on a large 4K TV and had no issues on ultra details.  - It allows for extending your campaign races so that you are not just stuck with 3 lap races. Also see Cons - There are some fun tracks. But having an open wheeler jumping street gutters is no something a simulator would allow. - This does allow for Wheels. I have used a Thrustmaster T300. I have not yet tested my Fanatic Wheel's. - You can level up different aspects of your Co Driver and your Mechanic. This might be an initial, wow this is different. Where in a few more weeks of play, it could feel more like a new grind mechanic (which is very very likely). Also note car's have similar upgrade which are only unlocked when you spend time in the car. So yes more Grinds. - The game has a toggle for Cross Play in online mode. - You can race VASTLY different vehicles at the same time. It feels like a gimmick for online play. But even the one offline challenge I entered was incredibly enjoyable. The slower cars start first and the faster cars need to chase them down. Due to my race lap being multiplied by 3, I was required to unlap myself before putting in a series or time trial like laps to chase down these slower racer and hope I could cleanly pass them without slowing the lap times. Con's - The cars all have a similar feel (At this early stage). - The Audio is nothing special. - The surface grips do have some change, but a snow race (yes they have snow) should be very very difficult to maintain grip and speed. I have had the easiest snow and wet race tracks in my 30 year gaming racing experience. - No Virtual Reality. This could really have been fun. - The Story Mode is strange and poorly scripted. And does not seem to have a different script from when you place higher then 10th or when you win the race and beat the so called pro driver on your team. - A good amount of grind mechanics. This actually includes grinding the "mechanic". See Pro's.
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: No qualifying??? Why would they remove such an integral part of a track racing game? Which WAS in the previous title? Career Mode is now Forza levels of grindy because it's now just a matter of how few flashbacks or restarts you have to do until luck is on your side. To add insult to injury, you will also start in 22nd in crucial, must-win races. I could tolerate not having pit stops in Project CARS 3 and the previous game, but no qualifying? Come on.
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: I love my sim racers and I have pretty much all of the obvious usual suspects. But sometimes I want to jump into something more forgiving, something I'm actually half ok at. So I have a few arcade racers to scratch that itch (sometimes it's nice to actually win a race).This is the best arcade racer out there at the moment by a clear mile and, if, say, you like Horizon and want a little more enthralling arcade-style racing that feels a little more engaging, this is it.I run this on a HDR ultrawide and it looks absolutely astonishing. Astonishing enough that I cannot not watch the replays whilst marvelling at how far game graphics have come in such a short space of time. And it is wonderfully optimised.This is a thing of beauty both to play and look at. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: The game improves to its predecessors when it comes to graphics, and car handling - it feels more modern.Much of everything else is worse:- the customisation is poor, it's not one thing or the other, it's not a solid menu where you can customise or something that comes as is like before, every end of race you unlock between 1 and 3 liveries (I suppose), you just don't want to use them and don't care on a GRID game, otherwise I'd be playing NFS.- the difficulty levels don't seem to work on some "finals" or weather conditions (it rains an suddenly they all cruise around).- the nemesis system is a huge pain, the nemesis nudge you with what feels like a tank, and see even though you make nemesis you can't nudge them back - who can nudges a tank - you make nemesis by idiotic things such as when the AI cars break down in the middle of the road (which happens at least once a race) or when they hit you - yes ridiculous - or even when you overtake them without touching them. So they are basically there to spoil the game, make you use playbacks and remove the immersion of the game.- The engineer on the radio is ridiculous, the studio were extremely lazy about that, not exciting like the previous games, he announces that your partner had a crash every 1-2 minutes, sometimes you're staring at the partner and see that it isn't the case.- The steering wheel feedback is good, but feels loose every now and then, and it feels like feedback is at 50% even when it's at 100%.- Money. Really? In GRID? The game seems to try get you interested by awarding you with money and sponsor objectives which seem to make no difference whatsoever, you don't have much to do with money, you could buy cars just when you don't have patience to unlock them, the team management section is laughable - spend $ in improving your partner score in drifting or make them less prone to get in accidents (which obviously makes no difference.)I played career and by the time you done some 10 hours you've played all tracks, racers are the same, no commentary from engineer, no exciting music, to rewarding feeling.The game is all wrong, I feel like going back to GRID 2 or Autosport when you do some precision driving, get excited with the racing, and not get annoyed multiple times in what seems to be the new formula for GRID, chaos and lack originality.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on the original Racedriver Grid, and actually, it was the first game I ever personally played for myself on my own PC. Then when Grid 2 came out, while it felt different, the progression and story were a wonderful trait of that game. Seeing cut scenes with real people talking about your performance was a lot of fun. I spent far too many hours in both the original Grid, and Grid 2, and honestly, I am genuinely excited to do the same in this game.I have been excited about a true successor to Grid 2, and this really feels right. The intro story made me so incredibly happy, and the faces put to the characters and team I have grown up racing and getting competitive with are so well cast, it all feels perfect.As for the racing and graphics, the game handles just how I have gotten used to with the previous games, and is genuinely a ton of fun. The feel of speed is a little different in different camera positions, but was very quick to get used to. The physics is great, as always. And of course, stunning graphics. The races with rain coming down, and the sun peeking out, are unbelievable, and I feel right at home racing around many tracks I grew up perfecting.Overall, I give this game a very positive review, as a very happy player, and cannot wait to hop back into the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked up the Deluxe edition recently. It's a decent arcade racer with plenty of tracks & vehicles to keep you busy for a while. Works fine with an XBOX ONE S controller and the cars are very responsive with the slightest touch of the controls. However, there does seem to be a lack of force feedback & heavy traction on the track with an emphasis on hand braking & drifting through turns.  It feels a bit more loose than I would like but it's playable. As long as you remind yourself that this game is more arcade like than simulation it's acceptable.The game looks really nice & there are various difficulty levels. If you're just a casual player, stick with easy or medium. If you are more hardcore, increase the difficulty level. With that said, the game is enjoyable & offers a more accurate arcade like experience at home than other racers. I'm sure it would be more fun to play with a wheel but I just got it & haven't had the chance to explore all the options.I recommend it if you want a casual arcade racer with both cross play multi-player support and offline capability. You might want to wait for a sale & go for the Deluxe edition which offers a bit more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugs, bugs, bugs and bugs. This game has a lot of them sadly.It's a very unpolished game (in terms of bugs), BUT... the core gameplay is OUTSTANDING! (at least most of the time)This game has at least 100 hours of playtime if you combine the Story and Career mode. The Career mode does get a bit boring at times, but there's enough variety to keep you busy with many different race types and car classes. The story is actually great and very well thought out. The DLCs are a mixed bag, where the weakest one has to be the Enduring Spirit DLC and the strongest one has to be Rise of Ravenwest, where you essentially replay races from TOCA / GRID 2008 with extra narrative and it's executed perfectly. They even put the sepia filter and old UI back for those specific races, which is great attention to detail.My main complaint about this game is the glitches and bugs of course, but another one is the lackluster car customization in terms of livery and colors. Sometimes I wish I had a livery that is just a single color, because I like the look of some cars looking unmodified, but it's a bit of a hassle to achieve the look of a livery-free car, which could easily be fixed if they added a livery preset that has nothing on it.The sponsors in this game are also something that isn't very well executed. Some of their objectives are so specific, you are forced to create custom events for it in order for them to be achievable.Besides that, I wish Endurance events had tyre wear like in GRID Autosport, but I guess they couldn't really implement that, since they would have to do it for each car separately. I also wish Demolition Derby events had more maps, since it's a really fun gamemode, but you can only pick from 2 tracks.All in all, I think this game is insanely underrated and the fact that the player base is record low for a GRID game, makes me worried that the franchise might be dead.Please support the creators, as the game they have created is actually great and I really hope we get to see another GRID game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Although a mere 15 hours in, I can somewhat understand why we have Mostly Positive reviews.GRID Legends is unapologetic. It isn't trying to be the best game ever... in fact, I'd argue to say its not trying to be good at all. I get this undeniable sense it aims for longevity, similar to Need For Speed games of the early/mid 2000's. The racing is easy to pick up and play, and not even hard to master, but it'll be there when you wanna turn your brain off and race while simultaneously looking pretty.Graphics are a 7/10, stunning when firing on all cylinders, but easy to tell where corners were cut in production. Great optimization as well. The multiplayer vaguely reminds me of games like Wreckfest, where you can join an ongoing player created lobby without the stress of matchmaking. My favorite type of multiplayer experience.There's plenty in the way of downsides, like the inability to pause your single-player race, and skipping to continue to the lobby once races/rounds have been completed. Customization is pretty terrible, and aftermarket parts and locked onto each vehicle, whether you like them or not. Damage modeling and crashes are far-fetched from what they were advertised to be, and the game itself lacks too much content. It's seemingly difficult to become a die-hard fan of a game like this.All that being said, its so damn bad, that its pretty damn good. You pick it up, turn your brain off, and whether you win or lose, who cared anyway. Simple games like these are aiming to be played in 10-20 years time and still be enjoyed as if it was just released. Who cares if its bad, because it's not trying to blow you away with handling from Forza, and its not trying to keep you locked to the screen with effects like NFS. Its that halfway point with an indie feel I can wholeheartedly appreciate.Disclaimer: NOT worth $60... get it on ♥♥♥ or when its on sale for no more than $20.

_childDocuments_.review: Mind you this is coming from someone who is a major fan of assetto corsa and project cars 2. However, back when i was on PS3 i used to play Grid 2 all the time, I loved the game. After not following the series for awhile i saw this was being released and became excited. A friend of mine had it on trial and i played it all night on controller and loved doing custom races for fun. I got home and bought it on release and started to play with my steering wheel. I was quickly disappointed with the lack of FOV scaling, force feedback customization, and vehicle tuning. Along with that vehicles were way too twitchy and for some reason turned from the center of the car instead of from the front wheels. So if you only have a controller and want a fun arcade racer then this is for you, but if your planning on having a simcade and fun experience on steering wheel then this is totally not the right game.

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with how the Forza series has changed over the years is what used to be a challenging arcade racing game has ended up turning into an adventure game with cars where the actual racing has taken a backseat to all the bells 'n whistles they added to the game.So how does Grid legends fair when it comes to the racing?Well, when I started the story mode I opted for the hard difficulty and was expecting multiple restarts, close races and pressure.What I found was I won every race in the story mode - easily, no restarts and it was well, no challenge.The racing doesn't give you a sense of "I'm pushing the car to the limit and I'm driving on that fine line of what the car can do on a corner etc".This is what I think is the biggest let down with GRID : Legends which is the racing game play.The real star of the show should always be exciting racing.Onto stars I found the story mode and it's tongue in cheek style fun.Unfortunately, no matter how you perform during the story it isn't relayed at all as you progress.I remember the original NEED for SPEED that came out on the 3DO system and it had full motion video and depending on how you performed during the race determined what video would play and it was good. In other words the story reacted to how you performed and wasn't on rails where your actions largely don't matter like it is in GRID.I read another reviewers post and he stated exactly what I have found regarding the racing which is that the cars are simply too sticky on the track and the driving physics/mechanics etc are just too easy which take the challenge - and thrill of racing - out of the experience.Another example of missed opportunity is their was a race during the story where you are in a truck racing against minis (small cars).What should have been a fun "plow through minis and watch them fly" kinda experience ended up being "hit mini with the truck and get a tink' where the mini barely moved at all reality'. Kinda underwhelming and sad.Another missed opportunity and underwhelming feature is their are races with a turbo boost.The turbo just feels sad. Where is the sense of holding the turbo button down and achieving ludicrous speed and pushing the car, truck or whatever to the edge?It just doesn't convey the thrill of turbo boost at all. The game, like Forza is pretty.The sound is ok'ish.GRID : Legends could have been great if the racing was better implemented.As it is, it feels like Codemasters used a focus group of play testers that aren't gamers and dumbed down the physics etc to the lowest common denominator so be aware of this if considering a purchase. 6/10-1 for truck vs minis sadness.-1 for the underwhelming boost feature-2 for the disappointing racing physics

This really almost made me uninstall it because i have NEVER played a single game where this is the case. At last i am now going for the achievements almost being done. If you are an achievement hunter, be aware. This game is super grindy when it comes to the achievements, and you also need the dlc. The story part of this game is really fun btw.Edit: Easily the worst ai i have ever seen in a racing game. The "nemesis" system is a joke. The ai's behavior is a joke. The difficulty setting is a joke. The race line they take is a joke. The person in charge of the ai should be fired and blacklisted from ever touching a game again, worthless POS.Final edit: Just 100% the achievements. The ai is still the worst i've seen in any racing game. Us not being able to properly drive over curbs (atleast without assists) is also a big fat joke. The rubberbanding from the ai is also a little to much (even to the point that some people are not able to win time attack events because the ai gets unbeatable times sometimes). The achievement list isn't the worst i've seen, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it a time grind. Took me 140 hours to get em all (i did do other things to, if you are extremely efficient you shouldn't need 60 hours for all achievments). Easily the best part about this game is the main story and side story. Also playing with friends is a blast. I do have to say though, even though i do recommend the game, it's barely. _childDocuments_.review: Music: First thing I noticed was that the music was atrocious. I mean like Nokia ringtone level of quality. So I turned off the music and it still plays music in the menus and cut scenes. The loading screens have same “dun dun dun dun” each time it shows the Grid Legends logo. It gets super old after the 4th time, and keeps going and going.Controls: This game had the same problem that Dirt Rally 2.0 had. The controls are A and Z for gas and brake and then , and . for left and right. Why are they still using this scheme? I haven’t seen anything like this since Need for Speed games in 2004. The wheel feels ok but like most arcade racing games I would rather use the keyboard. Not a bad thing just feels like it was a console/controller ported over to PC.Gameplay: You could put the need for speed logo on this and I would be fooled. Not that that’s a bad thing I like Need for Speed but not much seems original. The one thing I did notice that stood out was the gameplay mechanic of  The driving line is actually up there with Forza. It shows you when to brake and accelerate perfectly which is a nice touch. A lot of driving games get this wrong.Storyline: I can’t even describe how cheesy the story is. It has the same feel as F1 2020 games but the cheese is off the charts.  The problem is that they just give you the cars. There is no sense of progression. Like you should start in a touring car and work your way up. Instead it’s just, here you go it’s a super car or an open wheeled car. It’s more about the team building and less about the car. I did like the one part where they  It doesn’t really get much deeper than that. I mean I can’t describe how cheesy it is. Almost like they played it so safe and basically had no story. Every race is max amount of crowd and fireworks etc.. I guess they didn’t want to have so many track states and it was easier and less time consuming than having the crowds build and stuff.Multiplayer: At the time of this review (5 hours after launch) there is no multiplayer. Every time I went to quick race it said, “error joining” and went back to the home tab. To put salt in the wounds every time you switch tab there is like 3 tutorial boxes that come up and explain what that tab is. Oh the online screen lets me play races online? Wow thank you for explaining that. Oh the options menu lets me change in game options? Thank you so much. It must be a console thing where the people are brain dead idiots. _childDocuments_.review: GRID Legends is a stunner from menus and UI to presentation, game content, and certainly technical proficiency.  Play this game on a giant TV with a racing wheel and pedals in surround sound and you basically have a multi-faceted racing simulator.  After a few logos you are greeted by the grid-like menu system with a Home screen offering up curated challenges and special timed events that offer their own unique reward.  While Career mode is still the heart of the content the new “Driven to Glory” Story mode is the game’s soul.  This brilliantly designed component features an immersive story filmed with real actors on real sets telling the story of an up and coming race team, Seneca, trying to make their mark in the world.  The dramatic story bounces around from your own teammates to an egomaniacal opponent and rival team suspected of cheating to an injured teammate that we all end up rooting for in the end.  These FMV HD cinematics are part reality-show, part sit-down interviews mixed with the standard creepy cameraman lurking behind a bush filming a semi-private conversation.  It’s all quite convincing.For detailed game review (based on PS5 content) - For PC tech review and PS5 comparison - For gameplay footage with commentary (PS5 version) - More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if the racing demographic will get this, but GRID Legends is the Ace Combat of racing games, It's cheesy, over the top and with a cast crew-- but I'll be damned if it doesn't make for a wonderful experience.After years of searching-- NFS, Frz Horizon, Frz Motosport-- I finally found the racing game for me. That said, again back to the Ace Combat analogy, don't expect this game to be a simulator of any sort. It's a more of a fun-over-realism racer than anything else. And in a racing game world now dominated by hardcore sims, I'm so glad this got created.Soundtrack, again like Ace Combat, is bloody great. As I write this, it's already in my 'Favourite OSTs' playlist on YouTube.In my honest opinion, the AI is leagues and bounds better than what Forza cooked up in any of its recent releases. It's been a long while since I genuinely fought for the lead place, quite literally on the edge of my seat. A massive plus in that department. I play on a 6 year old rig now-- GTX980ti, i7-5930K, 32GB 2666MHz RAM. The game runs top-notch on medium shadows, high textures, particles medium, volumetric lights off-- so when it comes to optimisation I wouldn't sweat it if you have anything close to me. Straight up 60 with no problems apart from one area where it dips (more on it below).One glaring negative-- the bugs.Upon the new update that released recently, like most people, I get annoying stutters when completing laps. Menus can be odd as well. Since these are true, then I imagine the other bugs are also prevalent. In all honesty, I think ironing them out should be a priority.Seeing what the >100hr reviews said about content outside of the main storyline, the Career mode to be precise, I fully anticipate myself spending many hours after work playing this one.EA-- the release schedule and overall handling of recent GRID games has been odd. If you kill this franchise like with everything else you touch, I will outright boycott all of your games until I drop dead.Not like you actually check the reviews of the games you publish anyway.And yes, I'm only 1 hour in, but I wrote my piece anyway to counterweight the negative reviews.10 pounds/euro on a sale? Absolutely mad. I would happily buy this for its full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Grid is a difficult game to review. The game is not 100% an arcade game, but is also now near being a sim. In short, the game tries to be both, and it fails.The game is in my eyes not worth 60 €. If you love arcade: buy FH5. If you love sim: buy acc or iracing.The graphics in the game are okay. It's the same style as in the other grid games, just a LITTLE bit better.Handling is 100% the same as all the other grid games. The cars feel unrealistic and boring to drive.The tracks in Grid are something in themselves. I can not find out if the tracks actually exist in reality, or if it is something who grid has made. Tbh i think it's a mix. I have seen RedBull Ring as the only track i know. Driving on tracks that you have never heard of is not fun.In short, no. The game is just like the other grid games, so buy one of them if they are cheaper. Grid Legends is in many ways just like PC3. A game that tries to be two things, namely arcade and a sim, but which fails BIG time. I got the game through EA PLAY and do not even bother to play it. There are many car games that are MUCH better than Grid Legends!

_childDocuments_.review: Main thing for me to know was how informative the FFB is on my Wheel (LG G 920). And as expected, it's a complete joke. Incredible weak, set on max it doesn't change a lot. You feel the usual Self Aligning Torque and a little rumbling at collisions - that's it. No tire slip, NOTHING from the surface, nothing when you brake or drive over curbs. No vibrations. This wheel has two vibration motors which are - of course - not used by the game.  If this is what they call FFB - they better just leave it out. Gives about 10% of the information  that your wheel would be able to through FFB. Tried to disable GHUB while playing - didn't change it. Skip it, the times when they made games like Dirt Rally are long gone. Your little son would like playing it with a controller, I guess...

_childDocuments_.review: Is this really the best we can do in a year 202x?Ok, the game is fine. At times it is even great. But it feels like a stagnation, like a regress. It might be the second best Grid game (after the original), but only because it has a lot of content.What has happened that racing games are so s--t nowdays? But ok, let's start with positives. It has the Renault Laguna, so it's a 10/10 game, case closed. The physics are somewhat sketchy, but sometimes they provide massive fun. Some races are quite dramatic. I adore Shelby Cobra tournament, it is pure adrenaline. Another good aspect: it carries a ghost of the Project Gotham Racing series. The tournament based racing games with sim-cade physics are a dying breed, therefore despite all of the frustration with Grid Legends, I will rate it positively.Now, the negatives...The FMV style live action career is pure cringe. It is well produced, ok-ishly played by the actors. But the screenplay is pure trash. I get that they watched the netflix series and wanted to reproduce that drama and montage, but it is just bad. I feel sorry for actors that they had to read those lines. Who needs that? If you want narrative racing game that much, write a good screenplay! Off screen commentators are fine, but often they say something that has nothing to do with what is actually happening on the track. The pre-race commentary is also a bit cringy, but passable.The physics engine is unpolished. Sometimes cars behave weirdly, collisions are sketchy. The damage system is obviously dissappointing, but I get it is a fault of licencing and not Codemasters.Now. The AI. It is bad. The opponents are hyper agressive, even if they are not in the foe mode. They will ram you, pit manouver you. In general, the opponents do not see you, they will go blindly on their line like on tracks and will not react to whatever is going on on the track. The AI is sooo scripted (in a bad way, in a way that you see), sometimes to pump up the drama, which most often will fall flat. And you'll see them suddenly crashing on an empty straight line like in a comedy. It happens very often. They just... crash for no reason in the most improbable way. It looks like they pulled the handbrake for no reason.The other aspects of the game are just mid. Not worth talking about. Engine sounds are pleasant. Some rare cars appear and that is very cool, cars seen only in this game. The car roster is good in general. Quality over quantity with that one, cars fit their categories. Graphics and aesthetics are fine. The UX/UI is not the best, but one can live with it.Overall, it is fine. But you'd think, living in the year 2008, that in 2024 racing games will be mindblowing. They are not, they stagnated and/or regressed. What a pity.

_childDocuments_.review: Grid Legends is an OK Simcade racer that is a big improvement over the Grid game that came before it, in the sense that now the front and back ends of the cars actually feel attached to each other.  The story mode is incredibly cringy (glad I only bought the base game, it would have drove me nuts playing through any more than one season of it) and lord knows how silly it is constantly hearing about how great your team mate is who needs to be levelled up just to finish above 8th, while you're single handedly dominating the championship.  The video sequences are well made using professional actors primarily from UK television.  How would I rate it?  It depends on your tastes, if you are a hard core sim-racer only it won't be for you, the physics aren't precise enough or deep enough for your needs.  It also won't be for out and out arcade racer fanatics for the opposite reasons.  This is for Dirt type fans looking for a tarmac experience, or Forza fans, or if you're an old TOCA fan looking to get back in with something modern you should feel at home with this one.  Oh, and the online mode is quite active with most people on it racing quite cleanly, in my limited experience so far.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: Feels a bit more arcadey compared to the previous grid games.random spin-outs and flips: Quite frustrating when you're having a good dogfight for first place and then they just spin out and flip for no other reason apart from being in front of you. It can be helpful when you're really struggling to get first place in a race, but it genuinely feels more like a letdown to me.The electric car gameplay modes are boring. there's boost gates, which kind of make it more arcadey again like having NOS in a NFS game. In the electric car modes, it's literally down to your braking in corners which isn't very adjustable because the electric cars feel like they still have traction control even though i have it completely turned off. They really refuse to slide round corners, or spin their wheels/lose traction. not sure if that's because of realism, or something else, but electric car racing in this game honestly felt super boring to me.having stories behind the characters was new, it was okay i suppose, but preferred the career mode stuff.Got to the pro stuff, and i genuinely don't see myself playing more of it, everything seems grip based racing and fixed/specific race lines. Did like in the earlier grid games that they'd mix in low powered/same car races in the higher classed races. feel like that's missing in this game.The vibe of grid in general has drastically changed going from Autosport to this.Also, missing mountain passes. I know autosport didn't have them either. but Big Sur was really fun to race on (GRID 2019 or GRID 2 i think had it). loved those types of races.But that's all my opinion. Hope it helps.
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid simcade roster with very good core, but with some rough edges.Pros:- very good driving model for racing, pretty much all cars feel great to drive- good amount of content, solid car roster and track list with lots of variety without overwhelming amounts of random trash (cough forza cough)- looks good, runs great, great car sounds as well and solid soundtrack- "story" mode, basically extended tutorial, that does great job of introducing various trac, event and car types- very good single player career modecons:- the story is NFS 2015 levels of cringe, the story in DLCs is pretty much just as bad- the side activities / special modes - drifting and destruction derby - are pretty bad, the drifting has pretty bad drive model that makes it feel like steering cruise ships and not race cars, and the engine is straight up not vibing with crashing at all even in regular races, much less in DD events, it all feels super flat with 0 impact and weird physics responses- the game economy is way too grindy, outside of story events and some specific career events, you earn basically chump change, and the length of race and dificulty has either no, or very little impact on the reward, so you are basically stuck racing a handful of events over and over to get decent progressConclusion: It's a solid pick at a discount, but the excessive grind can make the game way too frustrating at times for it to be worth AAA price.
_childDocuments_.name: GRID Legends

_childDocuments_.review: i remember GRID 2, GRID Autosport and Dirt 4 having this awful problem of resetting the resolution every time i alt-tabbed, and i just didn't want to deal with that. GRID reboot solved that problem, but the UI and physics i couldn't stand. After my experience of refunding 3 out of 4 of those Codemasters games, i just didn't really care about GRID Legends at the point of its release.That said, i'm happy i eventually decided to give this game a try. No technical issues, not terrible UI, and i quite like the arcade physics that give a sensation of losing grip instead of outright going into a drift.I think its fun and there is a regular career mode in addition to the story mode, so i feel like its worth the time. Multiplayer is alright, don't expect much from it. i do wish there were pit-stops and the strategy that comes with it, just like Codemaster's F1 games, but i also don't know how well it would have worked. COMPLAINTS:  the WIDE iconic GRID font i think is rubbish during gameplay cause it takes time for my brain to process what im looking at, in fact the whole UI takes too much space, and the Player Name isn't even highlighted, i named myself --YOU ARE HERE-- so that i didn't have to compute while im racing. its little things like this that can make a game feel low quality.if you use a wheel for racing, you probably want a game with more depth to it. Skip this series.

Just electronic music that seems to be made specifically for the game.Roads are big and the controls are great for most cars. I liked going fast.Nice easy to use main menu ui.The BadI didn't like having to constantly replay the same maps. I kept giving the game chances but enough was enough. And the thing is, a lot of the maps in this game were from "Grid" but in this game, the levels have better graphics. And having a map be backwards sometimes doesn't help either.Some races had 4+ laps. I can only take 3, to be honest. With how many times I've played the same maps, I just get frustrated doing the same thing over and over again.The elimination mode in the story kinda sucked. I liked that it was different but when you are in first and on medium difficulty, it becomes apparent that the timer takes forever, and this unique mode always overstays it's welcome.Can't turn off vibration.ConclusionI would have continued playing if the game just had different maps for me to play throughout the story.

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of racing games. I really enjoyed Grid Autosport, which is a delight to play even on the mobile port, and I vaguely remember liking Grid 2008, the first one, as it had a cool style and introduced the rewind mechanic. Unfortunately I cannot say the same for Grid Legends.It just comes down to the fact that it is not fun to drive. The car never feels stable, kind of bouncing around. The controls are unpredictable. More forgiving, like many arcade games? Sort of. I honestly just don't know what to expect most of the time, which actually makes it harder rather than easier. I can never figure out when to push and drive the car harder, so I wasn't able to improve much, not that the AI is hard enough to need to usually.Taking off assists, which improves most racers if you're good enough, actually makes it worse because you feel like you have an unrealistic amount of grip one second and then are spinning out the next. I play a lot of simcades and some sims, but I also play a lot of arcade racers. The physics are not a problem because they're not wholly realistic, they're a problem because they're not good. I heard Grid 2019 was much worse in this department, which is surprising because this is very not good, especially when compared to Autosport and Grid 2008.This is a shame, because as far as the content goes, it is fun and appeals to me. I liked the live action career mode which prepares you for the more in depth career mode where you make your own team from scratch. Solid amount of cars, solid amount of creative races types, ok amount of tracks, though they're still recycling tracks from Autosport.But none of it matters if it's not fun to drive in it. I got through the story mode and tried a bunch of ways to improve the driving experience unsuccessfully, then called it a day.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game! There are some significant flaws on Grid Legends, but you can avoid most of them and after I started doing that, this is probably the most fun I have had from a modern racing game!So what are the strengths of the game? Well, the presentation is definitely one them, it is a beautiful and cinematic game, with a lot of colors and epic music (don't forget to enable it on the settings menu). On top of that, it has a great physics simcade model, it is easy enough to keep the car in the track if you are careful, but if you have skills it will be a lot cleaner and faster.I am not an competitive player so I can't judge based on top tier skills, but I did have a lot of fun playing against the AI in single player in the higher difficulties, they gave me trouble at some races and it was a challenge. I do think that they have a problem at the start of the race, when a lot of cars are grouped, this can slow them a lot.The story mode is basically an interactive movie, you will play one race here and there but it is nothing special gameplay wise, but I still had a lot of fun with the story. The bulk of the gameplay in single player is the carrer mode, and it has a lot of content there, with lots of variation also. The carret mode is structured as almost an event list, there are some progression gates here and there, but you can do whatever whenever mostly. You will progress to faster cars by the end of the carrer, but will not buy them, you will be gifted them when you do some events, and buy the upgrades for them as needed.Now, what are the weaknesses of the game? For me at least, I needed to fine tune some things from the game before I had as much fun as I do now. For example, I did not want this game to be a sim (I have DiRT Rally 2.0 for that), and I also think that this game's physics have some flaws that don't help a sim-like experience. Some cars can feel weightless and at certain scenarios you can spin really easily without warning with assists off. So I turned on some light traction and stability assists (level 2, i think), that way I still need some skill, but I can consistently have fun when racing with this setting. This was just an example, but there are some other things like that:If you want music in all events, you need to turn it on in settingsThe nemesis AI system, while a good idea, is mostly an annoyance. But at some events like open wheels, it can be a major problemThe AI will only give you a challenge at the 2 latest difficulties (Expert and Legend), but the default is Medium, which is basically a garanteed win and boring. Maybe the difficulty above, Hard should be the defaultA lot of events in Career mode are boring or frustrating, you need to learn what to avoid as you play. For me, I am avoiding most of the Grid Challenges eventsIt can be boring to play slower cars, and because they use these cars, the rookie category at the early Carrer can be a slog.The game randomly will halve you fps when loading races, you should restart it at these moments.As I said, this game has some pitfalls, but you can avoid them mostly, and if you do, it is a really fun game to play with a lot of content!

_childDocuments_.review: As the last GRID game for me to try I was surprised at how much fun this game is. I'ts probably my favorite one in the series now. I'm sad that EA has killed off this series but they truly went out with a BANG. Only complaints I do have are the AI being unmovable and they will crash you out and the wonky handling/physics of the smaller truck racing with the ramps. Game is also surprisingly well optimized and I've yet to face a stutter in it. The multiplayer is fun, you will get crashed into, you will get spun out so it sometimes feels like Wreckfest but I am completely fine with that.

_childDocuments_.review: Grid Legends is like a rollercoaster ride on four wheels, and just like a rollercoaster, there's a good chance you'll scream, curse, and possibly question your life choices. But hey, that's what makes it fun, right?The graphics are so slick, they make my car look like a sad potato on wheels. It's like the developers borrowed some pixels from the future and sprinkled them on the asphalt. If only real-life road trips were this visually stunning—I might actually enjoy my commute.The gameplay is a blend of precision driving and strategic use of expletives when that rival racer decides to play bumper cars. It's a lesson in anger management with a side of burning rubber. Dodging opponents is like a high-speed dance, and the finish line is the grand finale where your car gets to take a bow.In conclusion, Grid Legends is the game where your driving skills are put to the test, and your vocabulary is expanded with creative vehicular profanity. It's a wild ride that'll have you gripping your controller like a steering wheel and praying your insurance covers virtual crashes. Buckle up, because Grid Legends is not for the faint of heart—or weak of swear word.

_childDocuments_.review: A textbook example of how not to do a story in a racing game... TLDR, the story is, small team challenges big team, only to find out big team is cheating. If you sum it up like that, it actually sounds better than it is. In truth, Grid Legends is flat out insulting. It's a crying shame, as it's coming from the only developers who have made a good grounded racing story (Pro Race Driver 2002), and the only developers who attempted and succeeded in creating a "silent story" (Grid 2008) with the events you partake in telling the story without cut scenes or characters. In fact, the base game and the DLC's draw heavily from these previous entries only to retcon them into oblivion. Ravenwest (The Star Racing Team of Grid 2008) and the McKane family (Pro Race Driver and Grid) have replaced with Generic Evil White Rich Dude #142 and his son, who are both unlikable A-holes with no motivation for their actions other than "we are the best". This is combined with more dislike-able and boring characters who have as much depth to them as paper. It's clear most of them were casted to fill a diversity quota, and most of them although decent actors, are clearly not engaged in the story at all. Nor was I, being known simply as "22". (Yes, the series that pioneered using you're name for a personalized experience, has now has determined you are a mere number who's name isn't worth uttering anymore.) There's this racing series called the Grid World Series, which is a utter cluster of racing organization with you jumping from so many different cars and classes it's honestly annoying, and some dude wants to you race for his underfunded back marker team. (Spoilers here on)After joining and proceeding to win every race by several seconds, the commentators and team treat you like you are a... Well, nothing special, with people talking you down, like you haven't just won the last 15 races and killed Nathan McKane several times over by smashing his car into the nearest inanimate object. After continuing to dominate the series like you're dressed in all leather, McKane attempts to kill your teammate, to which he is only somewhat successful. The Team, who has apparently been spending more money than the US Government can print, suddenly finds itself in financial trouble. (No doubt because of the amount of stupid expensive cars you have to maintain for this racing series) So you have to drive solo, continuing to score points in the championship you should be leading by several million points by now, to keep the team afloat. Finally your teammate comes back, now undeaded, and you take the fight to Ravenwest... Who you find out is cheating...And that's it. You beat them, and nothing else happens worth a crap. On to the Career mode. Oh wait, it's always online and people can jump into you're races and wreck you. Great! (You can take the career mode offline, but it's a semi slog fest that's very linear in nature. Not horrible, but not inspiring either.)And if I still haven't spooked you off, then there is the clear discrepancies between the Environment and the cars, namely the interior of the cars, should. The Environments and the weather effects are jaw droppingly beautiful. However, the inside's of the cars look like something from the earliest Xbox 360 days, with blurry gauges, low quality textures, and no shifting animations. Grid 2008 looked and did it better. However, with all that said, I'm still going to recommend this game for one reason only. Grid is the last of the track based, authentic action arcade racers. Even with it's problems, it's still enjoyable enough, that if you get it for like $20, you'll have a good time. I really hope EA doesn't shelve this franchise like they have Burnout, because the market NEEDS a game like this. Just preferably one that doesn't suck...

_childDocuments_.review: After 104 hours and 90 Achievements I decided to give a review of this game. It’s good. But it’s EA.The racing gameplay itself is nice, typical Grid-Sim-Arcade driving that works fine with a gamepad and steering wheel (Thrustmaster TMX). BUT in order to complete a race series you need to unlock “Stage 3” Upgrades with the car you compete in, which means driving a certain amount of km’s. Driving the first few Events with the car will never unlock stage 3 for you right away so you will always need to “grind” km’s in other useless races to progress the game. Why did they do this? To sell you a “Mechanic Pass” (0,99€) so you don’t need to drive as much to unlock the last stage. The “Teammate” you get is more of a nuisance than actually any help in the game, also voicelines get annoying at some point. You can “customize” cars with a livery that suits your team but they really aren’t that great and you need to wait a long time until you unlock an “okay” livery for your cars. You can’t really customize Ferrari’s and they seem to have the best engine sounds in the game. Makes you think why, huh? *wink*. Also, BMWs can’t be a certain type of pink, but idek why.The graphics look alright with a mediocre damage model and average world graphics.Game Audio is good as far as the cars go, solid engine sounds. Commentators spew a lot of bs while they announce “what a move on the outside” while you’re the only one left in the race just grinding km’s. Team mechanic announces “your teammate just had a crash and lost positions” while they’re either not involved in anything, just overtook someone or have been out of the race for many minutes now. Voicelines repeat themselves a lot and get annoying after 40+ hours but you can just turn them off and listen to music. Now there is a short story with real life cutscenes, which aren’t too cringy. A great start to get you going. After the short story there is the “career” tab, which is just one race event after another without any context or story at all, where you need to progress from Rookie through Semi-Pro and Pro until you compete in “The Gauntlet”.There are a couple of DLC for this game I’ll go through quickly. Every DLC has a short story with real life cutscenes that are alright. Winter Bash has 3 new vehicles and a few new drift tracks. Classic Carnage brings a Demolition Derby experience with 5 cars and 4 tracks. Game mechanics are the worst I have seen yet because you barely do any damage, cars are slow and the overall fun I had in this was -15. Do Not Buy. Seneca & Ravenwest pack delivers 4 new cars and liveries, that are not worth it in my opinion. Enduring spirit brings 4 new cars and an Endurance mode, plus another short story. Overall, a great DLC. Rise of Ravenwest brings 4 new cars and a short backstory of the antagonist team “Ravenwest”.Now is this game worth it?If you’re looking for many hours of driving fun on a great engine and don’t care about achievements, wait for a sale and invest the extra 0,99€ into the Mechanic Pass so you don’t grind yourself to death.If you really want to grind through all the 90 Achievements, you will need all the DLC, so wait for a sale and get the deluxe edition right away, which also includes the Mechanic Pass. The rest is pretty achievable in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: -ENG-"First of all, let me just say, after I finished the first story, I was absolutely furious and just had to write this article. The game is simply stunning. The graphics, driving mechanics, and acting are all top-notch. However, the way the story unfolds is enough to drive anyone insane. If I wanted to play a simulation game, I would've opted for games like Assetto Corsa or iRacing. I'm playing this game for its story, but it feels like they're mocking us. They refer to your character as "22" right from the start. Oh, how difficult it must have been to record voice-overs for different names. I guess this was their way of solving that problem. As a result, you're practically nonexistent in the story. Sure, there's a team, but you're just a vacant seat that they had to force into relevance. I get it, I really do.I played the game with all assists turned off and set it to the highest difficulty possible. And you know what? In every single race so far, I either won or finished way ahead of the competition. Yet, they completely overlook Yume, the other pilot on the team, as if she's some kind of racing goddess. It's as if your victories don't even matter. No, Yume was the star pilot, the one who was exceptionally skilled. Okay, I can accept that too, but here's the kicker—they expect you to win races where 22 vehicles are cramped on tiny tracks, going at 300 km/h, and constantly crashing into each other. If you're lucky enough to avoid getting rear-ended at 250 km/h, the track limits punish you and throw you to the back of the pack. Oh, and let's not forget the story spoilers conveniently placed right below the cover photos. They give away what's going to happen in the story, even before you start that race. So much for suspense!After enduring those nightmarish moments, the final race arrives, and we find out that the racer with the best car, boasting 5 championships, has been cheating all along. Oh, how delightful! And instead of voicing our concerns about this cheater, we're simply told that our pilots can beat him on the track. Really? This guy won 5 championships by cheating! And to add insult to injury, in the last cutscene, right after you become the champion, you're told, "I'm proud of you," as if you don't even exist. Meanwhile, your teammate has had a leg amputated, and yet you're left to fight alone against 20 racers from 10 other teams, leading your team to the finals and becoming the champion. It was truly a delightful experience, right until the very end.Please, developers, spare us from any future story-based games. Stick to simulation games, where you clearly excel."-TR-Öncelikle ilk hikayeyi bitirdikten sonra bir hışımla gelip bu yazıyı yazmak zorunda kaldım. Oyun çok güzel. Grafikler, sürüş mekanikleri, oyunculuklar vs. Ama hikayenin akışı sizi çıldırtıyor. Simulasyon oyunu oynamak istesem açar asetto corsa, i-racing oynarım. Ben bu oyunu hikayesi için oynuyorum ve bizimle adeta dalga geçiyorlar. İlk bölümden itibaren isminize "22" diyorlar. Tamam kabul her bir isim için seslendirme yapmak zorunuza gitmiş ve böyle bir yola başvurmuşsunuz. Hikayede adeta yok sayılıyorsunuz. E işte bir takım varmış da koltuğu boş kalıyormuş ve size mecbur kalıyorlarmış. Tamam güzel anlarım. Oyunu tüm asistler kapalı ve olabildiğince yüksek zorlukla oynadım ve bu bölümden itibaren tüm yarışları ya kazandım ya da limitin çok üzerinde bitirdim. Buna rağmen takımın diğer pilotu Yume'yi tanrıça gibi gösterip siz yarış kazanmamışsınız gibi yok sayıyorlar. Yok takımın birinci pilotuymuş da çok iyiymiş de. Hadi bunu da anlarım ama küçücük pistlerde 300 KMH ile giden araçlardan 22 tane koyup bu araçların birbirini parçalaması sırasında yarış kazanmanızı istiyorlar. Şanslıysanız ve kimse siz 250 KMH hızla arkadan vurmadıysa da pist limitleri sizi son sıraya atıyor. Hikaylerin kapak fotoğraflarının hemen altında, hikayenin sonunda ne yaşanacağı açık şekilde anlatılıyor ve siz o yarışa başlarken o hikayeyi baştan biliyorsunuz. Kabus gibi anların sonunda son yarışa geliniyor ve 5 şampiyonluğu olan en iyi araca sahip yarışçının hile yaptığı anlaşılıyor. Aman canım benim pilotlarım bunu pistte de yener denilerek bu adam şikayet edilmiyor. Adamın hile ile alınmış 5 şampiyonluğu varmış ! Şampiyon olduktan hemen sonra son ara sahnenin sonunda, bize hitaben "seninle gurur duyuyorum" deniliyor ve bunun dışında sanki yokmuşuz gibi muamele görüyorsunuz. Üstelik sezonun sonuna kadar takım arkadaşınızın bacağı ampüte edildiği için diğer 10 takımın 20 yarışçısına karşı tek başınıza mücadele verip takımınızı finallere taşıyıp bir de şampiyon oluyorsunuz. Gerçekten oyunun sonuna kadar acı verici bir deneyimdi. Ne olur siz bir daha hikayeli oyun falan yapmayın. Simulasyon kafasında devam.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I wanted to write good review for the game. Since the driving model is actually not bad, it is one of best in arcade games. But after the last DLC (that is also the final patch) I’ve changed my mind.Let’s start with positives:Good driving modelDrift (everywhere except Okutama Point-to-point Drift Routes)Decent graphics (especially rain)Interesting truck selection (especially street trucks)Eliminator races (finally done right, how they are supposed to be done)Multi-class racesUnfortunately, all these positives are completely eliminated with the worst implementation possible. The game is full of bugs, that even after the final update manage to ruin (zeroize) progress.Menu navigation is just awfully uncomfortable, and you cannot reassign a lot of necessary keys (like photo mode keys).A lot of cars and trucks are just recycled from older GRID games or even form one DLC into another, and some are recycled with bugs.The story mode has a couple of good race stories, but most part of the it are just detached random races. You just race, and the story goes it own way. In many cases it is just comments from same “talking heads”. There is just no connection with the player.The worst part, is that the game was made so beautiful, but you cannot see the beauty just because the devs didn’t bother to make a good replay camera. It is just side track always or standard race cameras. There are no more cinematic replays like in old GRID games, that made that games so attractive.Derby (Car-Nage), why do at all it was brought back?! When Wreck fest is still in the market, adding such a bad implementation of derby in the game is a joke.Endurance races are just another variant of multi class. There is no point in such implementation of endurance races, if you don’t have pit stops and car components degradation.Rise of Ravenwest DLC is the only good DLC.Winter Bash is the worst. It brought only one new car - Bugatti Bolide. All other content is just a recycled content from the base game or previous DLCs.Verdict – don’t buy this game. Play older GRID titles they are much better.

This results in constant grind by repeating same races over again just to unlock  new events. Game has one story, all others are, you guessed it, a paid DLC. To put cherry on top, after latest update game crashes after completing a race. So ♥♥♥♥ you EA. I regret every cent I gave for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that my crashing issue somehow fixed itself, I can give a more proper review. If you are among those who have been a GRID fan since the first game, you might like its car list, which is probably what holds this game up still. There are some really nice additions returning from TOCA games like the BTCC cars and GT cars like the M3 and Astra V8, which are great additions imo. Career mode could be better, it's a bit too repetitive but when you play them in short bursts, they don't bore you as much. Now the negatives. I think connecting career mode to the main story might make sense canonically, but not being able to change your driver number in career mode makes no sense at all. You just don't feel in charge of the team since you can't even change your engineer and teammate unlike in the original game, when you felt like you had all the control you want. This might be the realistic way, but the original game engaged the player more on management stuff, which was still fun.Overall, it's not perfect, but a good game with lovely variety of cars and categories, which keeps the game alive and still engaging. However, knowing Codemasters, it still could've been better. I think you should get it on sale and enjoy some simcade driving with especially those BTCC cars!

_childDocuments_.review: I hate car simulations, I prefer arcade games. Grid 1 is still a reference, unfortunately Grid 2 is not sold on Steam. Grid Legends is much easier to play with low graphical details (than medium or high) since FPS is far better (on a GPU like mine, a GTX 1060 6 GB Ram) but the game remains beautiful despite low details. Using a Microsoft pad is great (no need to change the default settings). I advise to purchase the game with all DLCs. I just regret I am stuck in a DLC (Ravenwest story) because I cannot drift (I do not have access to the rest of the story al long as I do not complete this horrible level). I am playing on three 27 inches screen at 7680*1440, interior view is great. The standard races out of stories are fun to play (the possibility to upgrade the vehicle or the capabilities of your teammate are a nice addition compared to Grid 1). For those who just want to have fun without having headaches on simulation, it is perfect, the game works out of the box, no parameter to change of any kind. Explanations to setup our own races would have been welcomed (in Grid 1 we have a dedicated menu allowing to race any class car on any circuit, thing we do not have here, our tailor-made races are here limited to four, we have to change options ourselves, for this aspect Grid 1 was best). I keep playing Grid 1 and Grid Legends, they both meet my expectations of casual driver using a PC dating 6 years now. Pay attention that you can be easily addicted to the game especially in story mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Grid game finally after Grid 2. Great physics, handles good, performs better than Grid 2019 on my same old pc, sounds are good, story mode is good, multiplayer can be improved but still better, I spend hours making insane drift combos just like I used to in Race Driver: Grid 2007, good car selections.Only thing it lacks is a proper career mode. Main reason : Career mode and story mode are separate and you dont "set a path" for your team by selecting the type of races you get into, or what cars you buy for team. Grid 2007 was like a simi race career simulator introducing various real racing aspects to kids/teens which still no other game has. This Grid, again, only comes close to it. It is still very much a Grid game in every other aspect and trying new things that are not Grid 2019. But I must add that it lacks quantity in content although quality is of content is good.Step in right direction...probably a bridge between Grid 2007 and the ultimate Grid sequel game we and this series deserve. Underrated racing game. I tried this with EA Play sub but I might consider buying it, heck I think I should have bought it day 1 'cos multiplayer is....not very populated these days. Imagine a full lobby race in this game oof.There never will be a Grid game like the Race Driver: Grid, some games like that are too great to be out done.

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited so long before buying this game.I've tried it, i wasn't convinced and i didn't wanted to spend 60$ for something "meh".Now, i've gained for 10$ and here we are:+ gameplay is impressively fun, sim-cade like the good old TOCA Race Driver+ Graphic is polished and clean, looks like a previous-gen game with more details+ Audio is fantastic, Codemasters always know how to nails it+ Soundtrack is dynamic+ There is a story mode, a career, a multiplayer section, a quick race section... i mean, you have a lot to do+ you can join all your friends whenever you like to+ fine selection of modern cars and classic cars (finally an almost complete Supertouring car grid)+ tracks are detailed and funny, day/night, sun/rain/snow/sandstorm... you have everything at your disposalBUT- Story mode is a Drive To Survive wannabe, with stereotypes, cheeky characters and nothing more than that- Too few racetracks, and that's a real shame for a racing game like this one- the dynamic multiplayer is cool but you'll never use it unless you want to make disasters in lobbies- MyTeam section is questionable (especially liveries and sponsor mechanisms)- Your teammate is useless- there are still AI unbalances in time attack events- the AI sometimes is quiet but sometimes acts like you've insulted its grandma, every driver will avoid you or will crash you- multiplayer section is average and you don't have an integrated chat system- Could become boring quickly- Damage system has improved but could have been better easily7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Are we finally going to get a  GRID game again? + Handling model across all game modes+ Loads of content+ Has many cars not usually seen in an arcade racer+ Works great on a lower-spec gaming PC+ Story mode is a nice extra layer+ Career events can be played in co-op multiplayer+ Energetic background music (mostly in story mode)+ Race creator has pretty much zero boundaries to it+ Only takes up roughly 30 GB on your HDD+ Does not require Origin unlike most EA games on Steam - Tons of technical glitches, many of them months old without a fix- AI is unfairly and artificially overpowered on the highest difficulty- Many objectives require you to grind certain cars or events- Overpriced DLCs for what they offer (I guess to push the Deluxe Edition)- Way more cars than tracks (though there's many layouts to choose from)- Game gives you zero information about how to unlock certain items This game could have easily been on par with the original GRID. The background music, the car list, the event types and most importantly, the car handling are all on point. However, there's a lot of technical issues with the game and certainly not all of them have been fixed. EA/Codemasters keep adding new content, sometimes they patch the game as well, but they are still far from making it work properly. I'm worried they'll give up on the game after the last DLC gets released, leaving us with these unresolved issues. While I'm yet to run into something truly game-breaking, many people already report stuff like this. Always make sure to back up your saves! For now, I'll keep playing what I believe is the best GRID game ever since the first one. 7/10 |

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I always find myself coming back to and I just don't know why. Having played the first RACEDRIVER: GRID from 2008 and the 2019 GRID reboot. Not only do I recommend this Game to any racing game fanatic, but I would go as far as say that it is the best GRID game since the original. Not only do we see legendary GRID antagonist Nathan Makane in the flesh for the first time, when racing I could sense some of the long lost, fun and arcade-like DNA from the Original had returned. Drifting and Demolition Derbies also return from the older games which make for a good laugh. I'll admit that there are some negative points I still have about this game, but with the current state of the racing genre it's just whats expected these days. Forza Horizon 5 is considered by some as Horizon 4.5, but a lot of people keep coming back to it. Overall this is a great game that make racing 'FUN' again. It's a Racing 'Game' after all isn't it? CODEMASTERS, WELL DONE!!!PROS:- Pick up and play physics with Nostalgic feel.- Wide Variety of Racing Categories.- Open Wheel 'POD/Halo camera' ripped from the F1 games.- Cross-Play with PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S.CONS:-Race Creator not paying more for longer races.Did/Survived 99 laps of Demo Derby and got the same as 1 lap of Indianapolis Motor Speedway. ~4400 Credits.Possible Solution: More Mileage = More Credits + Existing Position Bonus

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll be honest, I bought this for the touring car aspect. Particularly since the Renault Laguna was making a surprise return!I’m not too experienced with the GRID brand. I tried various titles in the past, and for one reason or other, I just never got on with them. I am however familiar with the rest of the ToCA series. More specifically, GRID’s predecessors: ToCA Touring Car Championship from 1997 on the PS1, and ToCA 2 from 1998. I lost interest when ToCA World Touring Cars came along in 2000. But those first two games I played to death!I had to check out this latest addition to the series, and I’m glad I did. I’m aware that GRID titles have always seemed to be a bit “hit and miss” in their reception and popularity. But after watching a few gameplay videos online, I was convinced I had to try it.There is a story mode, and while parts of it certainly had my full attention, there are definitely other parts which are either uninteresting or irrelevant to the game. The cutscenes are produced in Extended Reality (XR) using real actors. There’s no CGI or motion capture here. Initially, I felt that this would be more of a huge step backward to those crudely filmed cutscenes in games of yesteryear, but I was actually quite impressed with how well it had been executed. Those of you familiar with Sex Education on Netflix may be surprised to find Ncuti Gatwa (Eric) playing the part of Valentin Manzi, one of the lead characters.Visuals are awesome, especially in 4k. I play on a native 1080 display (due for replacement soon), but even so, the colours, lighting and environments still look amazing. The fireworks constantly going off at various points around some circuits look brilliant too, but they seem like a cheap trick to make the racing feel more intense and dramatic. Something which isn’t really needed.Audio is epic, but it has its nuances. If I’m playing with a headset on, I have to turn off spatial/surround sound to be able to hear anything from my engineer during a race. I’m not sure why this is, but hopefully it will be addressed in a later patch. The trackside commentary becomes annoying and repetitive quickly too. The most common things I hear are  and  Occasionally you’ll get  It’s always at the same points around the circuit too, so you’ll hear them each time you go round regardless of what’s happening on the track.The cars handle as if they are on rails for the most part, but they do lose traction if you push them too far, especially in the rain. Turning off the assists can make the handling more realistic in some cases, but you’ll need to work harder to make progress through the pack if you want to win.AI drivers actually seem half human compared to some other racing games. They make mistakes! You’ll see them spin, slide, nudge, crash and even roll over. You’ll also see them suffer terminal damage, with smoke billowing from their cars as they slow down and retire from the race. It’s great to see this level of attention to detail on AI cars, something I’m not used to seeing in racing games.Damage modelling is really good. If you’ve had a shunt at the start of a race, you might see parts falling/flying off your car a few laps later. But surface damage looks the way it should too, with dents, tyre scuffs and scrapes all appearing exactly as you would expect. If your car has fibreglass panels or bumpers, expect to see them cracked and broken. Watch for tyres blowing out too!The so-called Livery Customisation Suite is a joke. It basically consists of three steps:1 – Choose a preset design pattern.2 – Choose colours for said pattern from a fairly limited palette.3 – Remove sponsor decals if you wish.And… that’s it. There’s no way to fully customise your own personal livery. You can’t colour your wheels, put your name on the car, nothing. It sucks. Hopefully modding will deal with this in due course.I found that car handling took some getting used to with a controller. While it’s definitely more of an arcade racer, it does do sim racing quite well in my opinion. That said, you’ll run into a few minor issues when using a wheel and pedals for the first time. Read this for an example…Overall, one of my favourite titles from the last year. It seems to be leaps and bounds ahead of the rest of the GRID series, if other online reviews are anything to go by. For me personally, VR support would be the icing on the cake. Cockpit racing just isn’t the same without it. Even so, I can’t recommend this title highly enough.If I think of anything else, I’ll add it to this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, not great. TLDR - an absolute steal on discount but not worth full price.Grid is a fantastic series. An arcade engine pushed to its limits giving the cars some of the character of real sims without the limitations sims impose. The concept works very well. This is one of the weaker entries - a fairly decent game on its own but doesn't hold a candle to some of the older renditions like Grid 2. It's still head and shoulders above The Crew.Full motion video cutscenes and story helps a ton. It feels a little short, perhaps could have had more audio and races to extend the FMV story section. Still definitely a strong point. The cars are very different, the tracks largely the same as before but they're good.But you don't feel like a team owner, nothing feels of consequence like managing the team in Grid 1. The sponsorship system is flat bad. The car setup is a good idea but poor execution - Grid Autosport did it best but Dirt 3 before the Grid series was another great try. The range of cars is fantastic  but I'd prefer them to have slightly more options in fewer categories - sometimes you feel forced into a car you don't like.Overall it just seems to lack the passion the first 3 games had, and the 2019 attempted severely lacked. But for the discounted price the short length isn't a factor and you're left focusing on the good without noticing the bad. I'm hoping for a future Grid, just a little more time could bring the series back to the glory days of Grid 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Aight' look, this game made me feel happy things, almost made me feel like a teen playing GRID (2008) again.Far as I can tell they tried to recreate 2008 and I think they did a pretty good Job. While the story isn't groundbreaking, it's perfectly serviceable and by racing game standards quite alright... It's pretty girthy at 30+ races, even if it feels padded at times. The first two story races are a bit underwhelming, but it really gets going a few races in.MOST IMPORTANTLY, try starting on the "expert" setting, it turns off all assists but ABS (low). In my opinion most of the assists make the cars handle worse and feel sluggish. See if you can do well enough in the story mode on expert, if you're significantly overshooting the story objectives try putting the AI up to legend, or vice verca if it's a bit hard.Looks pretty amazing when the weather effects are in force and during the night races. Oh, and the soundtrack is amazing if that matters to you, does to me.I ain't no reviewer but I felt the need to give this a thumbs up, I really am loving this game.Ps: Devs please release the soundtrack in some form, pretty please?

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. I wanted to like it, but there are reasons why not many people is talking about this game.~ Depending on the type of person you are, you may find the story mode cringy, or actually decent. The story is what you expected for a motorsport game, and given the record of racing games with their inability to develop a good story mode other than involving cops and street racing, I'd say it's one of the decent ones.- Career is still the same thing as GRID 2019, except it is much more boring. They become tedious once you start doing Semi-Pro season or Pro season. Each discipline feels the same with the difference is you drive fast or slow cars, unlike in Autosport where they try to make some disciplines unique by making the player drive road cars on city tracks while GT3 cars drive on real world tracks.~ Handling is now manageable for a controller, except it still keeps the drift nature to be faster from 2019. Also, cars have way too much grip now it feels jarring to drive if you're used to driving some of the tracks from other racing games.- Multiplayer is dead for a new game. Only one session with 10+ players in it, it's expected given that it's a $60 game and EA is committing another Titanfall 2 release again.- Customization for cars are still piss poor. You can only do basic tuning (which is good for those who don't want to spend time learning how to tune, and bad because if a car handles poorly, there's no way you can tweak it to be better) and you can only customize liveries from a selection of preset liveries. I don't think anyone really liked the level of customization GRID 2019 offered, and yet they still brought it into this game.- Vehicle upgrade system seems like a last minute decision to make progression feels different compared to GRID 2019. You have to drive a car for a set amount of distance and it ONLY unlocks the upgrades for that car. This makes it tedious to drive cars in each class so that you can be competitive in multiplayer should the host enabled car upgrades.+ Sounds are still good as ever, but it is not as loud as what it used to be from GRID 2019.+ Graphics are the same as to GRID 2019, which doesn't look bad.~ If you disliked the AI from GRID 2019, you'll definitely not gonna like this one too. They still has the same behavior of braking way too early before a corner, and never take any line other than the inside line around a corner. Higher difficulties are difficult only because the AI cheats on straights. The only great thing about the AI in this game is they don't drive perfectly like other games used to do, sometimes you get to see them making mistakes or suffer from mechanical damage.Just wait for this game to go on a sale before you buy it. $60 isn't worth for essentially a GRID 2019 v2.0.

_childDocuments_.review: Return to form for GRID series! While I enjoyed GRID 2019, this is much more polished and complete package. It comes with story mode, career and many multiplayer options with crossplay. I am enjoying story mode so far, its a good starter and has some decent performances.Driving feels even better than before. I'm playing on a wheel and I like the feedback, its actually quite good for simcade game. Cars don't spin out as much as in GRID 2019 or even Project Cars 3. I feel like AI got improved as well, although its still a bit uneven, sometimes I'm unable to catch a lead other times I get like 6 seconds advantage over 2nd place.One of the biggest improvements is game's performance. GRID Legends looks fantastic and runs beautifully, I'm getting over 70 FPS, 1440p all maxed out on GTX1070. I'm getting much better framerates than in GRID 2019. I only wish there were some options to adjust specific post processing effects like motion blur, depth of field or lens flare, for now I adjusted these in config file.I recommend buying GRID Legends to any racing fan out there, whether you play on controller or a wheel. Of course, its not a game for hardcore sim fans, it never tried to be, it is however a great game for simcade players. If you enjoyed previous GRID games, Forza Motorsport 7 or Project Cars games, you should find a lot to like here. Its a very polished and robust package. It has much more to offer than GRID 2019 or Autosport and I spent around 60 hours in both of those games, so I'd say I'm getting my money's worth out of GRID Legends.UPDATE 23.06.2022 - GRID Legends had its biggest bugs fixed with the latest patch, so I'm reverting to positive review. There are still plenty of bugs and weird design decisions, but nothing game breaking and the base game is very enjoyable nonetheless

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Grid 2019, and no this is not a sim. Feels like a Cross between dirt rally and the F1 games, however those games are are superior to this.This games performs well, and for single player feels to have enough content, however the multiplayer is going to be hit or miss depending how well its received. I would not suggest this as replacement to Forza or GT, but it does fill a nice gap while waiting for updates or new titles to drop.
