name: FORECLOSED
detailed_description: Resist the System Join the Discord! About the Game FORECLOSED is a narrative-driven action-adventure set in a Cyberpunk world filled with action, suspense, and experimental augmentations. Follow the story of Evan Kapnos, his identity recently Foreclosed, stripped of his job, his brain implants and his access to the city Block-chain, he must now escape before his identity and implants are auctioned off. An Interactive Graphic Novel and Immersive Narrative FORECLOSED combines the playability of video games with the sleek visual aesthetic of comic books. Everything from game-play to cinematics are experienced within the stylistic framework of a graphic novel. Full screen and comic panel perspectives are seamlessly blended as you move throughout FORECLOSED's Cyberpunk city, uncovering a gripping conspiracy story. Cutscenes are also interactive and transition smoothly between alternative game-play styles. Hi-Tech Combat Discover and unlock new abilities with an RPG-like skill system. Upgrade your weapon's potential with futuristic modifications like the Explosive or Machine-Gun Rounds mods, enhance your brain with experimental augmentations and fight back against your enemies. Learn to control your new abilities, fight opponents, and manipulate your surroundings. Acquire superhero-like abilities such as telekinesis to launch your enemies into the air or hurl huge objects at groups. Hack into different systems to create traps or even overheat the implants in your enemies’ heads. Features Overview Slick Cyberpunk Action – FORECLOSED is a narrative-driven action-adventure set in a Cyberpunk world filled with action, suspense, and experimental augmentations. Interactive Comic Book - Everything from gameplay to cinematics are experienced within the stylistic framework of a graphic novel to make you truly feel like a comic book hero. Immersive Narrative - Follow the story of Evan Kapnos, his identity recently Foreclosed, stripped of his job, brain implants and access to the city Blockchain. He must now escape the city before his identity and implants are auctioned off… Hi-tech Combat - Modify your Symbiotic Pistol with an assortment of customisations that can be swapped out or even combined. Augmentation Upgrades - Discover and unlock brain implant abilities with an RPG-like skill system If you like these games, FORECLOSED is for you: Max Payne Liberated Deus Ex series (Human Revolution, Mankind Divided, Invisible War) Cloudpunk

short_description: FORECLOSED is a narrative-driven action-adventure set in a Cyberpunk world filled with action, suspense, and experimental augmentations. Follow the story of Evan Kapnos in this sleek comic book styled game as he unravels the conspiracy behind his identity foreclosure. Who is responsible and why?

_childDocuments_.review: Foreclosed is a narrative driven cyberpunk shooter set in the style of a graphic novel.Evan Kapnos awakes to the news that the company who owns his identity have gone bankrupt and his account has been foreclosed. He has lost his job, his implants and access to areas around the city.As per regulations he has until 4pm to attend the court and witness the auction of his identity to the highest bidder.After leaving his apartment he gets shot at, and it becomes obvious that someone is trying to kill him. The question is who and why?Gameplay consists of combat, stealth and puzzles.You have a gun with six upgrade slots and up to six implants can be used during combat. There is no ammo shortage and you can fire to your heart’s content but if your gun has upgrades then it will heat up and need cooling before use again.Shooting enemies is your main objective whilst trying to make your way to the Court.You can crouch behind cover or use objects to hide behind. When you press the trigger of your gun you will immediately stand up and when you finish shooting you will go back to crouching again. There are no mechanics to lean around corners or stick to walls in a cover position. It is all quite loose and free but works nonetheless.There are a few different enemy types differentiated by the armor they wear. Some have no armor, some have helmets and some have energy shields, or a combination of the three. Each enemy has its own pattern which they will follow religiously; If you die, you will know their movements and what to expect next time.Enemies with helmets and shields are much harder to kill and require certain upgrades to deal with effectively. Enemies can be seen through walls by their red silhouette which gives you a bit of preparation time whilst others will jump out without warning.Increase your shooting rate; exploding bullets; armor and helmet penetrating bullets; energy shield penetrating bullets; use telekinesis to propel bullets; and reduce implant heating are the six upgrades you can equip. You can only equip three upgrades at a time. Create a mind shield; create a health draining shield; cage an enemy; cause an explosion; lift enemies; and slam enemies into the ground are the six implant upgrades.Four of these can be assigned and mapped.Acquiring upgrades costs experience points which you gain from killing enemies or finding hidden signals.Using implant powers causes your microchip to heat up. If it gets too hot it will incapacitate you for a few seconds and leave you vulnerable to attack.You also have the ability of telekinesis and can make certain objects fly into enemies, either killing them or removing their armor.There are a few dedicated stealth sections but stealth plays a big part in the game. Each enemy has a viewing zone and if you are detected for too long will trigger the alarm and all operatives will engage.You can crouch and approach enemies slowly and quietly and then perform a stealth kill. This doesn’t attract any attention and is a good way of eliminating enemies without being discovered.There are very light puzzle elements in the game mainly involving moving objects to create pathways. Occasionally, your path will be blocked and you may have to find an alternative route by finding air ducts and navigating through them to bypass the area.Now and again, you have to perform some very crude hacking mechanics to open doors by repeating directional combinations within a time frame.The game has a nice narrative running through and you will have dialogue choices to perform when meeting various characters.I’m a big cyberpunk fan and I loved the atmosphere the game created. It had a futuristic feel with a dystopian underbelly.The comic book aesthetics displaying different scenes on one screen looked nice and give the game that graphic novel feel. The art direction was very attractive and imaginative and made moving between scenes a lot more interesting than normal. Main characters were drawn well and environments felt like they had been ripped out of a comic book. It was effective.What a wonderful soundtrack! I loved the cyberpunk vibes it created and it injected drama and excitement into proceedings very well. I thought the voice acting was very good too. In true comic book style, the villains sounded like stereotypical villains and the hero was downtrodden and out for revenge. It was marvelously over the top.Although the story was intriguing to begin with it eventually petered out and didn’t amount to much. I don’t think the game was long enough to really develop a strong narrative but it held my interest until the end. It should take between five or six hours to complete. The dialogue choices are pointless as they have no bearing on the story whatsoever; Each answer results in the same reply. This is a shame because some of the choices were difficult and I spent a while deciding which answer to pick.Gameplay was a little trial and error. Enemy AI was nonexistent as they would behave exactly the same each time and once you knew their strategy it was easy to formulate a plan.Earning XP to upgrade your gun and implants came quite easy, especially if you take the time to locate the signals, but I didn’t mind this as it made gameplay more interesting, if not a little too easy.Some implants and gun upgrades are better than others and you’ll find your favorites and stick with them. Most of the time I would use the lift enemy and slam enemy, which made it really easy to pick them off from behind cover, and the armor piercing rounds were essential too. This sort of made the other upgrades obsolete.I tried to mix things up by using telekinesis on objects and perform stealth kills just because it made it more interesting. Combat can become a little stale and easy if you let it.One annoying feature was that your upgrades were removed after you die so that you had to add them again. Sometimes, I forgot to do this and shooting becomes much harder without them.The variety of enemies was disappointing. There were no bosses and only three different types of opponents. I was expecting an advanced cyborg to appear or something a bit more imaginative but it never happened.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: Foreclosed is one of those games that you just hope that the developer learns from and gets a chance to make another game in the future, as potential is here with the interesting presentation style and different story camera angles, but it fails to deliver in the core experience of the game. You see potential at certain points and can see what the developer was going for: but a lack of polish and an overall lack of execution of the design fails the game in the end.The strongest thing about the game is it's visual presentation, which can have some great moments of wonder as you are put into the core of the cyberpunk city. The comic book aesthetic combined with the unique camera angles while still playing the game (even if at times the views can be awkward) can lead to some cool moments, even if the story is a generic cyberpunk story that you've read before. It does not help that the writing here is obviously translated for English audiences, as there's awkward dialogue that feels just short of being google translated. There are weird decisions for visual cues for the game (nacho face), but overall it's not what makes you want to stop playing.Sadly, it's the gameplay that fails to deliver. Stealth is frustrating: I mean, enemy AI isn't smart at all, but you really have no clue when an enemy can see you or not until you get into a trouble point, and that can lead to massive frustration. It doesn't help with those different camera angles the games give: trying to understand distance and things that can be seen, especially at various item heights, is a frustration in futility. The gunplay isn't any better, as the AI can easily be cheesed and while yes headshots really count, the lack of real scariness of enemies means that you're just firing like your pistol is a minigun. The skills help to vary things up a bit, but the game is also glitchy as hell and you'll find ways to get stuck or even softlock yourself.Overall, a game that just needed a bit more to it in order to really warrant a purchase, or your time. Skip for now.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: There's a thing I really admire about Foreclosed, and that's its story. Not so much the minute to minute writing - at one point a character describes a warehouse as forlorn and abandoned, "just like me" - but the big picture. Most modern cyberpunk takes a cheeky, sometimes sardonic, usually just flat out C-rate comedy approach to a nightmare corporate dystopia. Even the corpos get in on the gags! Dark, edgy humor about sharp dressed people with even sharper skills ruining lives for the average person!Not so in Foreclosed. Foreclosed, more akin to the early entries in the genre like Neuromancer and Blade Runner, presents a future where regular people are pinned between governing bodies and the megacorps that control them. Postmodern life defined by earnings and profits. Like, for example, the life of our protagonist Mr. Kapnos, which is very abruptly complicated when the company that employs him goes bankrupt and liquidates all assets in an instant. Assets including Kapnos himself, disconnected from the omnipresent blockchain and fully separated from so much as recognizing the people around him. Something his company left in his head has attracted the attention of the wrong elements - his only friend isn't on their side, but she doesn't seem to be on his either. It's a race to make things right before Kapnos' suddenly liminal state from his itemized identity becomes more permanent. Despite how fond I am of the tone this game takes, a cure to years of cyberpunk that's all cyber, no punk, you've probably noticed this is a negative review. That setting is wrapped around some of the worst third person shooting I've played since the Nintendo 64, punctuated by puzzle sequences of such narrow breadth and ambition that they feel included as nothing more than padding for this brief game which would, ironically, have been better for being briefer if the alternative is a mindnumbing isometric stealth sequence to open some doors and immediately engage in combat anyways. It ends as so many games bafflingly do not by saying anything or doing anything with its premise, but giving a choice to the player that results in a vague finale of riding off into the sunset. A disappointment, considering the strength of the setup, as well as the accomplished aesthetic that does the comic book look better than any game I've played since XIII some decades past. Maybe worth checking out on deep discount - otherwise it's all the more frustrating for the scant handful of things it does right.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, certainly not. It is still an interesting cyberpunk adventure with some shooting, stealth and hacking.In the near future, everyone wears an implant in the head, but your implant is different. It has been modified without your knowledge, and it seems that someone wants to kill you because of that. You have been working as an unimportant employee at Securtech, and you obviously got this experimental chip as a guinea pig. All your colleagues who also got the experimental implant have already been eliminated. What a nice coincidence that the person who designed the experimental chip, the busted CEO of Securtech, also has a little problem atm, and needs your help. Maybe you two can help each other?Guided by the ex-CEO, you infiltrate Securtech and sneak around, killing guards and avoiding detection. Your experimental implant enables you to hack devices or (at close range) overheat the chip of your foes, leading to their demise. Since all firearms are usable only by their owner, you need to find a handgun hardcoded to your implant. There should be an experimental handgun somewhere in the company's testing grounds... but the shooting parts are the worst parts of the game. Dumb AI and technical problems when using the mouse to aim led me to finish those sequences as fast as possible.The game is played in a third person perspective, but the camera is quite close to the character which makes orientation difficult. It does switch to different panels like a comic book sometimes, which is a nice effect. Using a gamepad works fine, but during the shooting sequences you might want to use a mouse (which sometimes leads to the visuals endlessly spinning around you). You enhance your implant with new abilities, upgrade your gun and hunt for the ones responsible for your problems.Short, visually interesting cyberpunk thriller with good story but weak action sequences.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: The little things add up... and unfortunately they are bad in this game.  It's a simple game, which isn't bad, but what doesn't work well is the controls.  Especially if you're using a 60% keyboard, you will have to alternate between using WASD and the arrow keys.  WASD is for movement, and  the arrow keys are for "hacking" the doors.  You will have to switch back and forth between the keys in order to do so, and it is a very annoying thing to do.  Also, the game's desire to make you use backspace in order to back out, instead of allowing the universal use of ESC drives me up the wall.  Also, you can't even leave the inventory menu unless you press "i" again.  It's super annoying.  Second... the volume control is awful.  You can lower the volume to the lowest setting, and even then it doesn't do much.  Also, the game will completely ignore your settings when some things such as voiceovers will blast through your speakers still.  Right now, I can't recommend this game.  I'm going to continue playing it, but what I mentioned has annoyed me so much that I have to give a negative review for now
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: The game features a lot a different gameplay mechanics and none of them really feel great. The worst it probably the shooting, which is a pretty big part of the game. The cyberpunk world and story is nice with some good intrigue, but the voice acting leaves a lot to be desired. Overall I have to recommend you pass on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: If looking for a graphic novel with some action elements Foreclosed can be a good fit. Even then, the gunplay aspects are too simple and repetitive. The art direction is pretty good but the underlying game mechanics fall too simple in my opinion. Also the voice acting is very subpar. It tries to resemble the Max Payne 1 type of dramatic voice acting style however it sounds again too simple and takes you away from the game due to lack of emotions in the voice or incompatible emotion in the voice acting compared to what is supposed to be.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from the comic-book style visuals and different story camera angles, the game is decent at best, but probably bad if you want to spend 20 euros on it and get your money worth. I couldn't even find the story interesting, especially when the voice acting was unbearable at times (at least for me) and as for the shooter experience, it felt clunky and not very satisfying. Even when you reach higher levels and unlock new abilities it doesn't feel like you made much progress combat-wise. Would give it a go, but not at the original price.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: Final review after 3.8h and finished the game.I was wondering why I was levelling up so fast. That's because the game is so short. I love the comic book, cell shading stuff, the story is good. voice acting is also good. Shooting mechanic is plain bad. upgrading your gun seems like it does nothing. no key remap so you are all over the keyboard, tried with a controller it made the shooting even worse. some mechanic like moving a container with a crane something a million game have done is not even well implemented you would think that pushing A to move the crate to the left would work to always push left? Silly you, no because the view is angled, A is now down for the second move. Dialogue choices are nice but they all lead to the same conclusion. The worse offender is the camera. getting close to wall cuase it to zoom in so you can't see your character anymore, crawling along a wall can cause the camera to jump in and out of zoom giving you headaches. being close to an enemy may not activate the frying brain function if he's not perfectly in the line of sight. Causing you to be seen or dancing around to trigger the event. Being behind a wall also cause your shooting menu to not appear. preventing you from using the slam (best superpower) or the mind shield (completely useless btw). dying means restart at the beginning of a section even with the unskippable cut scenes and dialogue (is it 2021?). You also have to reacquire all the collectable you found and re-equip all your guns upgrade because they were all reset! The sound menu refuse to lower the volume of the music and puts it back to 100% everytime I start the game. There is also no mention of the backspace button being the back key for menus. not worth your short time.Original reviewSo far: graphic (cell shade reminiscence of XIII), and story is great and that's what keeps me going for my review. But the gun play is terrible, you can (and the enemies) shoot through walls. The camera movement is giving me headaches. It constantly changes from zoom in out depending if you are close to a wall or in a tunnel. You can't see the fry chip pop up over an enemy's head if he's behind a pillar and you don't have line of sight, you need to rotate the camera and expose yourself which defeat the purpose of that function. The use of arrows to change shoulder view is a bad idea when you are in a middle of a fight. I put some upgrade on the guns but they don't seem to do much more damage. Not recommended at this time. It need some fixing.to not see your shooting menu
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mixture of good and bad where the potentially good weighs slightly more. The story is ok, the graphics and the story telling are quite nice, especially if you liked XIII. The mixture of hacking, stealth and combat works for me (mostly). Without doubt the game has its generous share of issues: It is bad in conveying its intentions, so especially in the beginning you are not sure what to do. The keymapping is bad and cannot changed for the way you interact with the menus. The sensitivity of the mouse is your main obstacle in havin fun with the shooting. The save points usually make you replay unnecessary parts of the game like cut scenes. But most of these issues could be fixed within a few hours work while the substance is fine. Well, with one exception, the writing and the voice of the main character could use some work (while the other voices are fine) too. Nevertheless, this is a nice little indie game 70/100
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: Several audio glitches and a clear lack of experience with how to guide players smoothly through a linear experience. It's got great visuals and music, no question there. However, if I spend ten minutes standing in a box wondering what I'm supposed to do with no signposting or clear communication of what I'm supposed to do, then you've lost me. A game this linear simply can't afford to be opaque less than a half hour in. It's very clear the presentation weirder abilities you get later in the game were the priority over the brass tacks stuff that you need to nail out of the gate. Such a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 3rd person action without any interesting ideas. Definitely not worth playing. Another game where comic should be a comic - not a game. Like a Liberated. But even there, gameplay was better.Here I have just one thing to praise - art direction. Here feel dynamic and style. Period. If that's enough for you and I persuaded you buying it - my condolences. Because this game doesn't deserve of your time. It's tasteless and hollow.Art style is good, but graphics aren't. Low poly textures spoil everything. Stylized effects can't hide obvious shortcomings. Animations are a very rare event here. You can hit 15 times in a head of your enemy and observe just one animation of death. Thanks, dudes, you created it, at least. And yes, you can perform more than 10 headshots in a guy before he dies. Game mechanics look ugly. Shameful shooting. You don't already want to do it again after 2nd killing. The most boring shooting range. As minigames too. Match-two-similar-objects and link this and that. The story doesn't deserve to be told. "High tech, low live" setting with big greedy corrupted corps where everything isn't fair, and your life is irrelevant. And this is not about "what" here. It's more about "how". And the answer is "bad". Seriously, boring game deserves boring review. Better play cyberpunk in 101 time. Because FORECLOSED isn't the future we've wanted.P.s. You can find all my short reviews .
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: Story and art style are great. I love walking through those comic pages. A lot of love went into the level and character design. As a few other players, I also got stuck at the beginning of the game. I couldn't figure out how to hack doors. A quick tutorial would have been nice. The shooting mechanic is alright, but I was missing a cover system. You die pretty easily in the game, and it is a pain in the butt to go behind cover. In some sections of the game, the camera is also placed in terrible positions and will result in you dying a lot.Even though there are a few negative points, I still had a great time playing the game and will probably play it again in a few months.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: FORECLOSED is a third-person action game. It takes place in a cyberpunk world. When I first saw the game on Steam, the graphics peaked my interest. The comic book style narration and gameplay is great. You know, when reading a comic book, you play out the scenes in your mind. Playing FORECLOSED feels exactly like that. It's an interactive comic book. The story is classic corporate/secret experiments stuff, there'S nothing to talk about. It gets the job done. The gameplay is both action and stealth oriented. You can play some of the sections of the game stealthily if you want or you can go in guns blazing. You have an implant, with this implant you can do cool things. You can sneak up on enemies and overload their implants. You can lift them in the air and slam them to the ground. With your telekinesis power you can throw heavy objects at enemies to kill them. You gain XP as you kill enemies and unlock new upgrades. Although the gunplay is weak, using your powers is really satisfying. The game is enjoyable to play in general, but it has a major downside. It is too short. I finished it under 3 hours. Being short is not a bad thing, but I think FORECLOSED is too short. I got used to the gameplay, I got new upgrades and unlocked new stuff, I was blasting enemies left and right and I was expecting some plot-twist to increase the length of the game but the game suddenly ended. It left me wanting more. Well, at least I enjoyed my time playing FORECLOSED. I bought for the unique aesthetic, and it didn't disappoint. If you are looking for a game that you can finish in one sitting, FORECLOSED is your game.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game really blew my mind. I wishlisted it before it came out but never got around to it until now. I have to say it was not what I expected, the comic book visuals went much deeper than I thought with some very creative camera work to realize interactive vignettes at time. I really appreciate this but at the same time am glad that it only used on some portions of the game, while the majority of it was from behind the shoulder 3rd person prerspective. This game is a short linear experience however there is a surprising amount of game mechanics going on:shooting, stealth, weapon upgrades, abilities, kinetic object manipulation, arrow input puzzles (I really loved these), blockchain transaction puzzles, signal tracking, spatial puzzles, mazes... admittedly none of the mechanics are too deep but it is so much more than you'd expect for such a small experience.The shooting is alright, it feels a bit weak at first however with the explosive bullets, armor piercing and shield piercing upgrades it starts feeling a lot punchier and more satisfying. The stealth was cool, as bit hit and miss at times but once you figure out the paths it's fun to go through them.My only complaints are 1. the dialogue options don't really make any difference, 2. your equipped upgrades only persist if you complete a section with them equiped but if you equip them and die then you have to re equip them and 3. a lot of encounters/stealth sections are trial and error so you tend to die a few times until you memorize them.I really enjoyed this game and and hope the developers do well enough to create something larger and more polished in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a really awesome look to it.  Some of the puzzle parts are frustrating due to the camera angles.  This game could have potential if given more time to work out a more complex and choice driven story line, and work out some of the gameplay kinks mentioned by other reviewers.  Looked great on my 4K monitor, and it definitely a fun 3 hour romp.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and thoroughly enjoyed the overall experience. The game is was just over 3 hours long, which felt like the right amount of time for the story being told. The execution of the story, narratively and visually (using the interactive comic book frames) was excellent!Despite being 3 hours long, there is actually a rich variety in the gameplay. You can approach combat situations the way you choose (using powers, or an upgraded pistol) and the environmental puzzles are a fun distraction, and never frustrating.FORECLOSED is a  cool, short cyberpunk story with some cool visuals and moves along at an enjoyable pace before it concludes. My biggest criticism is the inability to customise your controls on either gamepad or keyboard, and the defaults won't be suitable for everyone. Hopefully they can fix this soon.
_childDocuments_.name: FORECLOSED

_childDocuments_.review: STORY :Evan Kapnos wakes up in his apartment to find a "Foreclosure" Notice since his employer Securetech INC. went bankrupt. His ID has been suspended, his implants useless, he cannot leave the city, his service weapon dissociated & he needs to reach the court before 16:00 or else he will be considered 'Non-Compliant'. However, Evan realizes his life is in danger. Guided by a 'founder of Securtech' - and motivated by vengeance he needs to unravel the truth behind his Foreclosure.GRAPHICS :The game flaunts a live-action 'comic book panels' style cinematics where you control the character movement. This reminded me of an android game named "FRAMED".True to the cyberpunk genre, the color palette potrays a neon, blue, purple, and hot pink shades. The art-style borrows heavily from Frank Miller's "HARD BOILED" graphics novel.GAMEPLAY:Think of Watch Dogs & Deus Ex meets Control. The symbiotic weapon definitely reminds me of Control's weapon mechanic, the Camera manipulation of Watch Dogs, and the augmentations of Deus Ex - brain implants that are a reminescent of a skill system in an RPG with simple yet interesting puzzles. You can hack devices, stealth kill by overheating implants, possess Telekinesis, create a shield, drain energy, lift and slam enemies & much more. Its really fun.MUSIC :Faithful to the visual and literary genre of Cyberpunk, "Foreclosed" attributes it harmony to techno, industrial,  and futuristic punk rock. The dialogue delivery and voice acting is compelling and praise worthy. Walking into a disco & danger looming around, with your foot-steps synced with the beats never felt better.CONS:Aiming seems to be a bit stiff and its visible in the character's movement.Invisible walls around the corners sometimes mar the experience.Enemies do not take cover and this may break the immersion during combat.VERDICT:"Foreclosed" is one of the best games of 2021 so far. With an amazing, engaging story sunk into a Cyberpunk genre married to an immersive ambience, satisfactory combat, futuristic synth beats, through the eyes of a comic book reader & structured with love and care, "Foreclosed" is a rare combination of style with substance. A must buy. Strongly recommended.Video Review :

_childDocuments_.review:
FORECLOSED is a narrative-driven action-shooter set in a Cyberpunk world filled with action, suspense, and experimental augmentations. Follow the story of Evan Kapnos, his identity recently Foreclosed, stripped of his job, his brain implants and his access to the city Block-chain, he must now escape before his identity and implants are auctioned off.

An Interactive Graphic Novel and Immersive Narrative

FORECLOSED combines the playability of video games with the sleek visual aesthetic of comic books. Everything from game-play to cinematics are experienced within the stylistic framework of a graphic novel. Full screen and comic panel perspectives are seamlessly blended as you move throughout FORECLOSED's Cyberpunk city, uncovering a gripping conspiracy story. Cutscenes are also interactive and transition smoothly between alternative game-play styles.

Firmware Upgrades

Discover and unlock new abilities with an RPG-like skill system. Upgrade your weapon's potential with futuristic customisations and enhance your brain with implants which provide almost super-human abilities!

Hi-Tech Combat

Utilize experimental augmentations, weapons and tech to fight back against your enemies. Modify your Symbiotic Pistol with Explosive Rounds for maximum damage, or, go silent and equip the Stealth Bullets mod. Learn to control your augmentations to fight opponents and manipulate your surroundings. Acquire superhero-like abilities such as telekinesis to launch your enemies into the air or hurl huge objects at groups. Hack into different systems to create traps or even overload the implants in your enemies heads.

name: Bears In Space
detailed_description: Get ready to unleash your inner bear in Bears in Space, the over-the-top bullet-hell FPS that's bound to have you ROARING with excitement! Dive headfirst into hordes of oil-thirsty robots as you embody Maxwell Atoms, a Spacetronaut turned extraterrestrial castaway, whose DNA has been merged with Beartana, the She-Bear. Embark on a zany and humorous out-of-this-world adventure that'll have you blasting your way across exciting and varied locations, from wastelands to space carnivals to ancient hidden temples and more as you quest to find your way back to earth and if there’s time, save your crew. Fast-paced Mayhem Bears In Space offers non-stop, high-energy gameplay. Fight your way through waves of fiendish robots using an arsenal of outrageous weaponry and gadgets. Double jump, dash, and dodge enemy attacks in the tradition of the best old-school shooters. Mighty As A Bear Consume elusive honey pots and unleash your Ursine rage, transforming into a bear! Use your unique DNA fusion to your advantage, carving up robot enemies with your mighty bear powers and masterful knowledge of the ancient art of Bear Fu and the fabled Kuma No Ken. Upgrade Your Arsenal Complete challenges and break open loot crates to purchase guns, choosing from a diverse range of over 25 weapons! Most weapons upgrade, with each kill gaining your equipped weapon XP until it evolves into its next evolution tier! So, get out there and let the lasers fly! Varied Gameplay Venture beyond the ordinary FPS experience and discover Substories, secrets and collectibles across every level! Learn how to bake a cake, investigate a crime scene, battle a Rock God, play a round of Basketcube and even bust some ghosts! All while meeting a colourful cast of characters with their own quirks and stories to tell. Completing these exciting optional encounters brings with it a hefty loot pay off, making these encounters even more rewarding to search out as you save up for your next weapon! Choose your difficulty and play the game your way! Modify your difficulty with independent sliders for incoming and outgoing damage. You can also engage our Platform Helper mode, making all platforming segments of our game significantly easier to conquer! Perfect for kids or gamers new to the FPS genre! Whether you're a seasoned gamer looking for a blast from the past or a casual player seeking a fun-filled adventure, Bears in Space promises a fun and absurd, action packed time. Get ready to shoot, chuckle, and unleash your inner bear in this one-of-a-kind bullet-hell FPS adventure that’s truly out of this world!

_childDocuments_.review: Bears In Space is, for want of a smarter phrase, a video-ass game. Like, the kind of game that had me grinning and nodding and saying to no one in particular, "Man. Video games, right?  Yeah!"Does that make sense?Movement is . It handles well. Really fun and easy to run all over the map.I understand but do not at all share the complaints with the writing. The story is just dumb gag after dumb gag after dumb gag and I loved it the whole way through. I hope this doesn't come off as a backhanded compliment or anything, but I feel like you could adjust the difficulty to make the game as easy as possible and it would still be worth playing as a good, funny walking sim with action and exploration sequences.Not great for extended or back-to-back play sessions for reasons I'm not sure I'm smart enough to pin down. I found myself not exactly burnt out but thinking "Oh, wow, I still have a lot of game left, don't I?" at about the one-third mark. In retrospect, I probably could have given myself more time to breathe after every mission or two.I want more video-ass games like Bears In Space.

I played it for almost 40 hours and would love to play more in form of DLC or other titles.That's it from mePeace

_childDocuments_.review: A quirky game that unfortunately runs into tedium VERY quickly. Think of Bears in Space as a kid version of High on Life and you'll get the idea very quickly on what to expect. Its more comedy show than actual shooter, but the shooting here is pretty decent with some great feedback from weapons. The issue is the game never really adapts enough to keep interest and the jokes are so stale. One joke had me wait 5 minutes for an elevator to slowly arrive then break when i get on it. Another had me wait through a long chain of unskippable dialogue before moving forward. The combat is another issue. While i like the shooting the game's enemy variety is extremely basic and the bullet hell tag seems be because enemies will spray 100's of orbs everywhere you go. Damage is frequent and unavoidable, lacking any sort of skill other than running around and spraying back. I'm not going to say this is a bad game. A few extremely devoted people spent 7 years developing this game and had a clear idea in mind. The music is awesome, the theme is great, and i've encountered 0 bugs or issues. I recognize the comedy isn't my cup of tea and the combat isnt deep enough to keep me going. I respect the grind and will recommend it to people with this taste in comedy, but i'm tapping out. $20 is fair and the OST slaps if you want to support the devs further.
_childDocuments_.name: Bears In Space

_childDocuments_.review: To be fair, you have to have a very high IQ to understand Bears in Space. The humour is extremely subtle, and without a solid grasp of theoretical physics most of the jokes will go over a typical viewer's head. There's also Beartana's masochistic outlook, which is deftly woven into her characterisation- her personal philosophy draws heavily from Delueze literature, for instance. The fans understand this stuff; they have the intellectual capacity to truly appreciate the depths of these jokes, to realise that they're not just funny- they say something deep about LIFE. As a consequence people who dislike Bears in Space truly ARE idiots- of course they wouldn't appreciate, for instance, the humour in Maxwell's existential catchphrase "...." which itself is a cryptic reference to something. I'm smirking right now just imagining one of those addlepated simpletons scratching their heads in confusion as broadside game's genius wit unfolds itself on their pc screens. What fools.. how I pity them. 😂And yes, by the way, i DO have a "SPEND" tattoo. And no, you cannot see it. It's for the ladies' eyes only- and even then they have to demonstrate that they're within 5 IQ points of my own (preferably lower) beforehand. Nothin personnel kid 😎All jokes aside, this game is brilliant.

_childDocuments_.review: I am sorry, the gameplay is fine, not amazing, but genuinely, I cannot stand this writing. The writing for me never stops with endless joke after joke after joke, never ever once letting it breathe. While the gameplay is plenty fun on it's own I genuinely did not care for the story as far as I played. From dealing with Beartona and her chain smoker voice not ever stopping her endless banter with a silent protagonist in a world with no straight man in the comedy to play off of, a myriad of distractions that feel absolutely pointless other than for cash, but constant need to distract from any story at all with whatever came to mind just making the gameplay feel more like filler till you go from set piece to set piece. Ultimately if you want this kind of gameplay you have options out there that can do what this game does but frankly feel like they have more substance: Postal brain damaged, Doom Eternal, High on Life, Incision, Wrath Aeon of Ruin (the levels can be abit long), Dusk, and frankly more. Which is why when the biggest pull for the game is the comedy, I am sorry but I am frankly not to keen on this style of comedy as it never feels really funny, more like someone constantly forcing a joke over and over wanting you to laugh with all the references they pull when the most they might get from me is the odd "heh, I get that" then silence. I know comedy is subjective, I am not gonna ignore that, but I feel that the primary flaw in this type of writing is the same as what is going on with Borderlands, everyone is the  wild and crazy character, but no one is the straight man to bounce the joke off, making the jokes just fly, but never feel like they land as the main character literally has no personality of his own, just Beartana whom frankly never ever shuts up. No hate on the VA but I feel like you never have a minute away from another "Bear rule #who cares: the thing that just happened is totally a rule", which is a joke that gets old when in the less than half hour, I have heard it about 8 times or more and genuinely stopped laughing after the second time.TLDR: Not a bad game, but the writing is essentially High on Life but with more dad jokes and even less room between the jokes so as to make them feel even more bland.
_childDocuments_.name: Bears In Space

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for *purely* old-school shooter gameplay that takes itself very seriously, then there are plenty of other options. This game is just FUN, and goofy and lighthearted and I think it's a refreshing take on the genre that's usually filled with gritty and grim aesthetics.It reminded me of classic Ratchet n Clank/Jak and Daxter type platformers in their adventurous, cartoony world. Bears in Space is FILLED with detail and it's kind of overwhelming to think this was done with primarily just 3 devs. My only real criticisms are that perhaps it does *too* much humorous fluff if you're just interested in shooter gameplay, but it also has SO much variety that it's always entertaining. Also, there really doesn't feel like there are any stakes, storywise, and as much as the silliness is fun I'd appreciate if there was a bit more of a reason for everything that's happening.Also pls add more steps to the sensitivity bar, it only goes by 0.5!

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. it was really well made and enjoyable from beginning to ending...but there are a few problems i have with it1. the levelling up the guns system is cool and inviting but it takes so long to level up 1 gun, and there are plenty of different weapons to try and use, now i understand if the developers want people to grind and replay but theirs no real reward other than steam achievements - woo.2. The enemies were fun and different but some areas the enemies are overwhelming and you just get wrecked,3. The level design and biomes were perfect, they go through so many different places and eras, or fantasy places that its inviting every time.4. The bear got annoying. To much aggression and KILL KILL KILL, you never really could say no to what the bear wanted. The honey drops or rampage mode was fun but again seemed to go on for a long time.5. The challenges were good and different, but I'm not really a 100% achiever seeker, so doing them doesn't really interest me.I would play this game again, do a second play through if there was a new game plus, or if there was a secret level or area you unlock after finishing the main game.All in all 8/10, highly recommend it for something different and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel pretty mixed on this game but I'd still recommend it cause I think it's overall a good package. Maybe a 7/10. There's a good variety of enemies that keep encounters engaging. Sometimes it can get too chaotic. At it's best I think the action and graphics blend to enhance the silly cartoony fun of the game. Often you're well stocked for encounters and will be given respawning resources just in case so you can go buck wild kicking bot booty. Now and then there are too many bullets and enemies to keep track of which makes some encounters a slog to get through.The gun play is pretty fun and there's a couple decent mobility options to use to keep you on your toes. Weapons can vary from complete jokes to gimmicky but effective to complete utility. Its too bad most of them aren't bound to keys so if you want to regularly use the bulk of your arsenal you'll need to repeatedly spend 5 - 10 seconds mid combat trying to navigate the multiple weapon wheels to find what you want. Really dampens the flow of combat if you want to involve the whole arsenal. If not, that's fine because the weapons that are bound to keys are fairly good but weapon progression is entirely too grindy. I think I maxed out one of the main weapons. Which was fun maxed out. It's too bad I don't want to put in the time to see the others maxed out. Which I think is my biggest criticism of the game. Like a bad joke, it overstayed its welcome. Sometimes a good secret would get me invested again but marathoning the game left me pretty exhausted. I don't think this game really needed hour long levels. And maybe they aren't so long if you're skipping secrets, but the secrets seem to be where a bulk of the games personality lies. Honestly I don't know how much better it would be only doing the main objective but I definitely wouldn't recommend that for a first playthrough because then the progression will be even worse.I will say the game is very consistent with its strong aesthetics. Artistically and writing-wise the game did a good job capturing a cheesy, goofy, B-movie sci-fi vibe. Visually the game was never disappointing, it was a pleasant ride all the way through. Some of the jokes didn't quite land for me but most of them did. Would've preferred less cutscenes but that's not a huge issue with the game.The music is surprisingly good. Took me a while to notice but there are a couple really good rock songs in the game to really get you invested in a fight. Heck, honestly just go listen to it on it's own on bandcamp. Phenomenal. One more bonus for the game. Gianni Matragrano voices about 90% of the cast. That's how you know its a quality modern boom shoot.But seriously, it's got some good highs, some annoying lows. If you're interested give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Bear in mind that this game not only bears a ton of fun in it. I was bearly ready for the intricacies of the story and moving character development embearasses most "over their head" big names. You'll bear a lot of fire arms which all feel responsive, pleasant and goofy AF to use. Be prebeared for an adventure of lifetime as you clubber some worthless robots... bear punNow SPEND!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. Lately a lot of games I played felt like made from people who did not really want to make a game. This is the complete opposite. You can feel the love and passion these devs have for gaming, movies and so on. Those lovely, adorable environments, the wide and crazy weapon variety, the movie and game references and most of all the gameplay. So fast, fluent and smooth, just incredible fun. You have to prioritize enemies and choose your weapons accordingly unless you want combat to be a hassle - as it should be in every good fps. Beartana's voice acting is excellent, she sounds so adorable. One problem: I want more!!! No idea what the plans are, but it screams for some sort of survival/endless/horde mode or even a second part. The story would allow for that, since you left everything open. Oh yeah and if possible: Make a "Last used weapon" option available please! Highly recommended even for full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Bears In Space

_childDocuments_.review: This shooter is a passion project through and through. It has a great choice of upgradeable weapons which want to be used strategically and without remorse against those pesky robots. Additionally many grenade types complete the roster of destruction.On top of that you'll get a bunch of tools to complete puzzles and find easter eggs.  The gameplay loop of shooting enemies, platforming, exploring the world to fulfill side tasks, unlocking new stuff, and laughing your ass off from the great humor is well done.It took me almost 38 hours to 100% the game and it was a great joy. There is sommuch content in the many levels which are filled with creativity in world design, cultural references, humor, subversion, and genre-bending.One of the later levels called  seemed to have more jokes and creative ideas packed into it then some whole AAA games nowadays.The graphics are stylized, cool, and you'll discover neat things in almost every corner. Be warned though if you are allergeic to invisible walls. There are quite a few wide open levels  that protect you with thise invisible walls from getting lost. THe developers even aknowledeg that with an ingame sign.It's also really accessible. You can (de-)activate and adjust multiple settings to get the challenge you want. Or modify them at the end to get those last remaining achievements a bit faster. This allows the game to be fun for lesser experienced kids as well."Bears in Space" is an all-around fun game with lots of content and absolutely worth its asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Bears in space is some combination of Doom, Ratchet & Clank, Borderlands, and the more recent High on Life but doesn’t do any of its influences all that well.Gameplay is very doom/bullet hell inspired and while fun at the start, quickly becomes repetitive and more of a nuisance than anything. Guns and their upgrades are directly influenced by R&C but ultimately feel barebones at best in comparison. It takes forever to get the gun upgrades and with dozens of them it would be a massive time sink to try. Enemies are really generic and most just have a variation on laser ball attack pattern. It’s not the worst gunplay I’ve ever felt but it certainly won’t be bringing you back. Also, I hope you like destroying purple boxes because that is one of the pillars of this game (yet even in this area it feel less satisfying than R&C).Story/characters are…rough. The ultimate main story is a bit of a meme the whole way through and feels extremely disjointed at times. It also drags on for way too long for what it is trying to tell and ends up feeling like a chore that never ends. One level after another that feel repetitive and derivative. The characters while there are a few bright moments, are mostly annoying to listen to and frankly uninteresting. It’s just joke after joke after joke and it devalues them the more the game goes on. This is compounded by the terrible voice acting of the main characters’ partner and various other NPCs you meet along the way. They don’t do a good job of selling the stereotypes they are trying to poke fun at and have a pretty underwhelming delivery. I know this was made by a small team but it doesn’t change the fact that it is still bad.The world levels themselves are varied at least but are again too large, empty, and bland. It feels like you are going through a game still in alpha and most of the visual clutter has yet to be added. Lighting feels really washed out too with a weird low contrast haze look. It’s not fun to look around most of the time and if you don’t care about the little secrets scattered around, would probably prefer to just run through most of it. Those secrets can be fun but most of them are just on the nose 2 second jokes that honestly feel pretty lazy.As for performance it ran fine for me on a 7800x3d and 2080ti but was surprisingly maxing my gpu, odd for a game of this low visual fidelity. There are some major performance dips when a bunch of small enemies are killed in succession. Overall I would most likely give this game a mixed rating if there was one because I can see some people enjoying enough about it but I’m going to err on the side of don’t recommend. It just doesn’t do all that much well and feels like a watered down soup of multiple other games. Maybe pick this up on a deep sale and give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really ever leave reviews but this game was so much fun I feel obligated to.About a week ago I saw a vid about Bears in Space pop up on youtube, part way through that video I saw what was obviously a Chron-o-John, I immediately turned off the video and bought the game and have hardly been able to put it down since. Bears in Space is in many ways the game Serious Sam 2 should have, could have been in a perfect world, and then made it 10x better. At least that's the most direct comparison I can think of for the overall feeling of the game, but there's so much more. The weapons are fun and creative, there's a ton of them and they are really satisfying to upgrade the next version. The rocket launcher is downright amazing it feels perfect. There is a ton of side stuff, secrets, eastereggs, and even some mini games, all of which I really enjoyed and even though there is a lot, it never felt like anything was 'getting in the way' The gameplay is really fun, the enemies are good and there is no 'super annoying one' at all, your character moves and jumps and shoots just right and there is nice variety between the different levels.I loved the story and characters, they are funny without having to rely on being foul or edgy or overly self aware, its just nice solid comedy very much in the style of the classic Lucas Arts adventures, which the game contains several great references to, among many many other things.My biggest fear while playing was that it was going to be too short because I was having so much fun but thankfully it went on just long enough to hit that sweet spot before feeling like anything was dragging on. I will be going through to replay it and find the rest of the secrets, and there are some very nice features to make replaying levels enjoyable: enemy multipliers, weapon upgrades you would probably not have gotten to the first time around (there are a BUNCH of weapons) and of course the secretsThe secret locator item you can buy at the ingame shops on each level gives a little light up beeping when you are close to a secret, enough to be helpful without that feeling of shame that comes from looking one up or getting a hint. Really really really one of the nicest features in a game like this is on the Level Select screen there are different checkpoints you can start the level from and it actually shows which secrets/collectibles are obtainable from that checkpoint on.(Ex: If you are missing Trading Card #5 and you mouse over checkpoint 1 or 2 it will show you can get it from there, but when you mouse over checkpoint 3 the Card #5 will be red, meaning you've gone too far, so if you just need to collect that one you can start at checkpoint 2 to get to it quickly) If I had to find a gripe with something it would be that it uses checkpoints instead of quicksaves, and there are some limitations in backtracking, but it is definitely designed with replayability in mind so thats more of a directional choice than a flaw, and maybe one of the reasons I had so much fun was because I didn't get caught up in quickloading over and over to save myself 1 extra rocket and a little health for the next area.Bears in Space is great, really great, definitely buy it, can't recommend highly enough. It's pure magic and I hope they make more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's impressive how much a small team was able to accomplish.  The scope of what they tried to do is huge, but the level of polish on the final product is low.The game can be boiled down to two things: FPS arena fights, and secrets that mostly take the form of little comedy skits.  Some of the comedy lands, and some of it doesn't.  It's a toothless brand of comedy that aims to be wacky without poking fun at anyone or anything in particular.  There's joy to be had in exploring a level and discovering these details, but that joy is severely tampered by levels filled with invisible walls, and arbitrary one-way gates that prevent you from traveling backwards.  Will going down that path take you to the next secret?  Will it be an invisible wall?  Will it take you to a one-way door that stop you from secret hunting?  It's a gamble every time.The only way to get back to secrets you missed it to replay part of a level, which is a chore, because the shooting isn't very good.  The game features about 15 guns, which is 10 more than it needs, and each arena is an exercise of moving methodically from health pickup to health pickup, clearing out spammy enemies as they tick down your health.There's effort and creativity on display here.  I hope that the team involved keeps at it, learns from what worked and what didn't, and takes on another project of a more manageable scope.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd much prefer to be excited about Bears in Space given the 'small team many years' disclaimer the game starts with, but it is just a passable boomer shooter where secrets in each generically-themed level come with a tangential bit of lukewarm comedy.Bears in Space isn't particularly funny. A lot of the humor stems from short, spontaneous jokes or zany character introductions. When it tries to subvert gaming tropes, the bit is done predictably. Very few of the jokes are diegetic, which misses the unique potential of comedy in an interactive medium. Bears in Space is also very happy with how funny it thinks it is. Comedy is of course subjective, but if you've found yourself wincing at the meta and self-congratulatory humor in Borderlands or High on Life, well, this is the same domain. Bears in Space isn't particularly fun. It's a skeleton of a boomer shooter. There’s a double-jump and air-dash. Melee on 1, pistol on 2, shotgun on 3, SMG on 4, etc. You've played this before. The weapons, even the assortment of barely functional comedy guns, feel slippery and lack impact. The basic guns have crazy bullet-spread problems. Enemy types are generally homogeneous alterations of gumball machines and the smattering of tiny projectiles that fill firefights is visually unappealing and moves unpredictably.Within the narrative of Bears in Space, there isn’t any interesting stakes or build-up or comedic continuity or reason for the things you do. The only recurring characters of significance are the twelve-packs-a-day bear in your head and the merchant. It’s no surprise then that the lack of structure leads to throwaway “well that was something” scenarios that break the pacing of gameplay and sabotage the integrity of the comedy.In the end, the comedy doesn't carry the game well enough to justify putting up with the gameplay and vice versa. Unless the genre's basics are enough to get you going or you're a tuber looking for some easy riffs, Bears in Space isn't worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: For all the love and personality that's baked into Bears In Space, the actual gameplay experience leaves me with two elephants in the room that are keeping me from recommending it. First and foremost, this game is in dire need of optimization. I'm not normally a stickler for performance, but in a genre like FPS, every frame counts and there were several places with a lot going on that made my computer chug. I was often struggling to stream this at 720p on low settings and I don't think it helped that a game of this scope was a 20 GB download. Second, even when things were running smoothly, enemy hordes were often super messy. Between enemy movement and shot volume/spread, it was just too much for me to deal with on normal difficulty. Maybe with some extra tuning, this could be a great game, but for now, as much as I want to praise what's good about it, I'd approach with caution.

_childDocuments_.review: Bang for your buck Boom Shoot goodness with at least 100% more Bears. Bears in Space is a Retro FPS that combines both faced paced FPS gameplay mixed with Bullet Hell qualities and a large humorous tone. Created mostly by 3 people in the Unreal Engine 4, it follows the story of Maxwell Atoms as he's one day from retirement on a boring prison ship until they're attacked and in the chaos fused? with a talkative bear called Beartana or BT for short. From there they go on a absolute wacky, robot slaying, adventure all across over the place on a quest to get back to Earth. It's such a nothing plot but has so much rich heart and humor that you're just happy to be on the ride to see what's next! Gameplay of Bears in Space follows a more linear style with having arenas for combat and platforming and miscellaneous segments between the arenas. The shooting is pretty solid a good variety of enemies with various attack patterns, movement options, and a absolutely absurd amount of weapons. Like there's so many weapons that you need 2 weapon wheels to even see all of them. They range form the workforce FPS weapons like Shotguns, and Rocket Launchers, to novelty weapons like a Anvil and Rubberband launcher, a almost useless Carp Spraybottle, and Basketcube Launchers to name a few. The amazing part, is that all of these weapons are useful in one way or another. While yes, the sheer amount does mean the game has a large weapons bloat, I think it does a decent job separating the workforce and novelty weapons. Like for example the Gamma Launcher which is basically your rocket launcher is more useful but the Tri-Shoot can be a replacement if you run out of ammo. As going the sheer variety of robots is insane even by Episode 3 you're still getting introduced to new robots that have different attack patterns along with the earlier ones. Futhermore all of these weapons are upgradeable, which are tracked by getting kills with each respective weapon that has a upgrade tree unless stated otherwise. While the upgrades are nice to make your early game weapons still useful, the grind to get them can be a bit long such as the one for the pistol.Now the level design is one so notable it needs more elaboration. As stated earlier Bears in Space's levels for the most part are mostly linear hallways connected to arenas or set pieces with secrets spread out inbetween with a handful of exceptions. The difference of this compared to what you normally hear when a Retro FPS has linear level is the absolute sheer length of these levels. With few exceptions most of the levels can take 20+ minutes to beat and they're typically stuffed will with combat encounters, moments featuring humor, variety or both, or just normal secrets. Throughout these levels are a currency known as Vicbucks which you spend at Vic's. A robot who is more than glad to sell you new weapons, along with things like health, armor, and ammo refills as well as a really useful secret detector. You're also given a handful of Tool "Weapons" which effect either your movement options or affect the environment during platforming segments inbetween fights. It's a notable enough mechanic that you even have a weapon wheel for it. As for all the side modes to provide variety, they often take the form of idea adjacent to FPS gameplay, like becoming a Light Gun shooter, Basketball, or other minigames in the FPS style. Otherwise it's either themed arenas or simply jokes. It's a amazing blend that also helps that the humor is pretty consistent. Often making jokes at FPS game tropes, general pop culture references, and just humor that rarely becomes annoying through a full playthrough. There are also Trading Cards hidden around like these humorous secrets but they kinda are just there as a collectable rather than being something interesting. As the story is really just an excuse to go on this wacky adventure, I'd rather take a look at the style. As Bears in Space has a wonderful Retro Spaceage-like style. From the colorful environments, to the design of the robots and weapons, the game absolutely nails it's visual style. Even for me who had to roll back on some of the fancier effects for performance the game still looks and runs mostly great!  This is even more notable with how big the game is. As assets are reused very rarely, and when reused are often for a specific callback to a joke or fitting within a different level's theme. It can be jank at times but still consider that all of this was mostly made by just 3 people. The music also really well done, having a variety of themes for each level as well as music made during combat to really amp things up. Overall, Bears in Space is an incredibly unique FPS game that's stuffed full with content. You can easily get around roughly 15~ hours on a normal playthrough and it's not that particularly hard to get 100% so you could easily get up to 20+. Really the most annoying parts about 100% is that, due to the way the levels are constructed, you have to rely on specific checkpoints when revisiting levels. Which can be tedious if you have a secret that's hidden between these warps. As other than general grind-ness for two other achievements, I'd highly recommend going for that 100% as you'll get to see everything the game has to offer. As a whole it's a great game that's easily worth the full price of 20$ for how much content you get, that is something I cannot say often for most games!

_childDocuments_.review: Do not be fooled by the game's presentation.It's "DOOM in stupid" with tons of side events to shake things up.Enemies can (and will) destroy you by flooding the entire combat area with bullets and explosions.It is genuinely challenging on medium difficulty.As for the jokes, humor is obviously subjective.Most of them didn't land for me, but moments like "We got ourselves a little security" and then showing a tiny bouncer did get a chuckle out of me. It's dumb, it's on-the-nose, and the game knows it. My only gripe is the projectile-based combat. It takes quite a bit of time for your bullets to actually reach the enemy. And they move around a lot. It feels like more than half your shots end up missing because of it, making for a very unsatisfying experience. I highly recommend enabling a small amount of aim assist in the options menu to give each bullet a little bit of "magnetism" (yes, even if you're using a mouse). It makes a world of a difference.Like so many other games, it's seems impossible to get a solid 120+ fps out of this one (usually an engine/optimization issue).Once things start exploding, it can drop all the way down to the 60s.Therefore, I have to lock the game to 60 and use frame generation software to at least have it look like a 120 fps game.If you're a 60 fps person, this does not concern you.

_childDocuments_.review: If the devs are reading this, just want to add that I was blown away by how good the writing is, it's truly great comedy. My advice would be to understand why all these reviews liked Bears in Space more than High on Life and build on that (keep doing what you're doing, and embrace/widen the gap between the competitors)When I played High on Life a couple months ago the jokes were a bit too edgy and crass in that game. I would often get annoyed by the humour in High on Life, or cringe at it, or both. Bears in Space is a lot more modest with it's jokes in a smarter way, even if the jokes themselves are really silly and goofy fun. To put it into perspective, Bears in Space has a wide range of humour but it particularly has more old-fashioned 90's/00's type of humour (think Leslie Nielsen's parody movies like Airplane/Scary Movie) relative to high on life being strictly more ultra-contemporary (rick and morty, etc.). I think Bears in Space will age a lot better because of that alone. Bears in Space had me actually laughing out loud more times then I can count. My only 1 single negative/criticism is that the game was too long (22hrs, could have been 30 on higher difficulty setting and exploring more). It's great value for money, but the issue is that it certainly risked the humour getting dry and old. Some jokes/sequences were repeated a few too many times. Personally, I didn't mind, I actually thought it was funny to see the repetition, but I could see how others may have grown a little tired of it. Putting the humour aside, the gameplay also got a little tiring- not a lot, just a little! But a small part of me was glad the game was over when it finished, the robots and gun noises and all the ADHD chaos just gets physically tiring. Short and sweet is a virtue in game design in general, and in comedy too. The gameplay itself is still very fun and relaxing to play in general though. Despite complaining about the game length, the devs did such a great job at adding in new guns, gameplay, new mini games, it really was phenomenal and I have huge respect for them. It's a solid 9.5/10, a genuine GOTY contender for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Let the records show I almost never write reviews for games. While that probably doesn't really hold any weight to you I hope it at least communicates that I was impressed with Bears in Space. I don't think I've ever played a game from such a small study with so much heart and polish, and I honestly think it will be a difficult challenge for it to be knocked out of my top 5 games of the year. THE STORY:BIS's most standout characteristic is its incredibly funny and smart writing. Almost every cutscene and joke brought a smile to my face and several even made me laugh out loud and had me thinking about them even when I wasn't playing the game... at least the first time I saw them (I will elaborate later). The over arching story doesn't really matter, which is brought up several times, because BiS is really about enjoying the moment. Its story is kind of a sketch, comedy game  filled with tons of pop culture references both recent and older. Every secret is more or less just a bit that rewards you with Vic bucks to upgrade weapons, but most of them are very creative and some have ridiculous amounts of efforts put into them. BiS is absurdist humor, think Dear Sister or Aunty Donna, at its peak.GAMEPLAY:BiS is a very competent modern, boomer shooter/Bullet Hell most of the time. You have a double jump and dash and enemies all fire large amounts of projectiles in unique patterns. BiS features a VERY large enemy roster, and it truly astounds me how every one manages to be unique and many use the bullet hell formula in very fun and creative ways especially the late game ones. These projectiles also deals large amounts of damage. I played on the highest difficulty and it is possible to get mowed down from Max health and shields to dead in a couple seconds. That being said health is pretty abundant the difficult is staying alive to get to the health. However, to be honest I'm no shooter god, and I probably averaged only 2-3 death every level (which are usually about an hour in length). To combat the large enemy roster you have a similarly large arsenal, 25 guns and several grenade types, and many of the weapons can be significantly upgraded by getting kills with them. Are all of the weapons good? No. A few of them are gag weapons that do at worst decent damage, but they all have their own fun or interesting quirks, and I enjoyed switching to at least one of them in every fight or so. Completing secrets and destroying boxes around the map will give you money to buy weapons, ammo, armor, etc. You may have noticed I said BiS is only a shooter most of the time. Several of the secrets and gameplay sections will totally shake up the gameplay style changing to be like Mike Tyson's Punch-Out, Galaga, House of the Dead and more. As I said early it truly astounds me how much work and love this small team was able to put into this game.THE BAD:I think BiS really only has one flaw, which I hinted at earlier, and that is seemingly padding out its run time when it is already a decently long game. The smallest way this is apparent is in the number of kills required to uipgrade guns. The main arsenal takes around 1,500-2,000 kills with each weapon to fully level them. While there are a lot of enemies in the game, there is not nearly enough to upgrade them all in a single playthrough if you're are also working on your special arsenal. This is especially frustrating, because if you die the kills from your previous life are not saved. Even if the weapon upgrades in a fight it will revert back if you die. This seems to me to be an intentional choice, because there are certain things like secrets that will save progress when you die. Now to combat this you can go back and replay level with your current arsenal to get any secrets you missed and grind kills. However, this brings me to the MOST egregious example of padding playtime. Cutscenes are mostly unskippable. You can slowly "skip" some of the dialogue in most cutscenes, line by line, but it is not uncommon for them to have entirely unskippable segments.  If you replay a level you will have to watch these each time. To make it even worse checkpoints are almost always BEFORE them, so if you die you will have to watch them again. Checkpoints are also often far-ish apart meaning you can actually have to watch two or three cutscenes again if you die. The absolute worst example of this in my playthrough was a cutscene where a guard walks a ridiculously long distance to set off the alarm. I died in the fight after it 2 times, so I had to watch that guard walk the ridiculously long distance 3 times, and let me tell you the first time it was pretty funny, the second wasn't funny and the third was very annoying. Broadside if for some reason you're reading this, please for the love of Vic at the very least just put the checkpoints at the start of fights.FINAL THOUGHTS:Like I said I absolutely think Bears in Space is worth anyone's time, but I think it's probably best played just to enjoy the ride. Play on the normal or easy difficulty, and don't sweat trying to get every collectible and secret your first time. That is the exact opposite of how I usually play games, but I still loved my time and after taking a break I truly look forward to coming back to finish up what I missed. The game was clearly made with an unbelievable amount of heart from a small, team that is made of truly talented writers and game designers. I genuinely can't wait for what they do next.

_childDocuments_.review: People are absolutely sleeping on this one. I have not beaten the game as of writing, but I have played to the "Carnival" level, which seems to be at least halfway to completion by my best guess.To start, the humor is not for everyone, its not edgy, but clever about how dumb its being like something out of "The Naked Gun" or "Airplane!" with alot of sight gags and reference humor. It is far more subdued with how often they crack jokes compared to something like "High on Life" where they would throw 30 jokes at you a minute with like 1-5 of them landing. Its dumb in a tasteful way for lack of a better term, though if you don't like getting riffed at by a bear woman who sounds like she smoked 40 packs a day since conception, maybe turn the voice slider down.That being said, the gameplay is fantastic. Movement is fast and responsive, and the level design encourages a lot of platforming and out maneuvering your foes who are primarily various types of robots. They all gib satisfyingly into multiple pieces upon death, spilling oil and bolts everywhere. I've encountered about 8 enemy types so far (not including bosses) and the only one I actively dislike fighting are the small ankle biter robots who come at you in swarms (They're very fast, but you can outrun them).Now where this game shines is in the weapon variety, level design, and quality of life features that encourage replayability. Maybe I'm misreading inspiration here, but Bears in Space seems heavily influenced by the older Ratchet & Clank titles. You're given access to a staggering amount of weapons. I'm talikng 20+ unique firearms, melee weapons, and throwables, and not a one feels out of place. Every weapon ends up being useful in different situations, however there is at least one weapon that seems like it was placed there as a joke. Also a legally distinct Unreal Flak Cannon is in there. That is the only one I'm gonna spoil, because they are all a treat to discover. Continuing with the Ratchet & Clank comparisons, 90% of your arsenal has an experience bar that fills on kills. When filled, your weapon evolves. These evolutions are all accompanied by a physical change to the model, as well as an additional firing mode or enhanced weapon statistics (Damage, rate of fire, projectile size). The last 10% of weapons do not upgrade, but are usually found in secret areas on levels and can be missable.Missable weapons are not too big of a deal to me simply because this game has several quality of life functions that make hunting for secrets painless. Your overall character, his arsenal, and any relevant gadgets for level traversal you find are ALL saved to your profile, and level select is unlocked from the very start of the game. This effectively acts as a New Game Plus mode that is always on. You could play for 10 hours, decide to start over from a level of your choice, and keep your entire progress. That includes Arsenal, upgrades, and level traversal gadgets. It's such a breath of fresh air from having to redo an entire game just to get to a fight you wanted to replay with your new toys.And the levels are all fantastic, 20 minutes long at minimum with tons of side objectives and secrets that actually give you permanent additions to your character. It doesn't go as far as Ratchet & Clank did with how expansive the side paths are, but often you'll often leave the critical path to find a mini level of its own off to the side. This is also where most of the reference humor tends to be.I don't want this to get too much longer, so I'll end with this. This game feels like a true labor of love. A shooter with the speed and precision of modern standards, harboring the soul of a game from the mid 2000's. It's fast, fluid, clever, and well designed. A hidden gem that shines so bright, I'm floored that it doesn't have 10x the amount of reviews it currently does. Broadside Games has crafted something truly special here, and I wish them nothing but success in the future.
