_childDocuments_.review: This is now one of my favorite games. The characters and friendships in it resonated with me so much that I just instantly fell in love and just couldn't stop loving every single scene in the game. Game play is basic choose your own adventure respond to conversation stuff. Though sometimes they have small twists to show your characters mental state like stuff jumping around. Even though the choices don't exactly line up with what Fang says they always show what she is feeling when she says through both the text and effects surrounding it. I almost never felt like she went to far from what I wanted. You can also choose specific things like some lyrics to the songs or what your band logo and posters look like which felt super nice. The other major part of the game play is a rhythm game music sequences which were always so fun. They felt like a nice level of challenging where they never felt like to much and I was still able to pay attention to the visuals in the background of what the characters were doing. You can make this easier in the options. The visuals are lovely and the animations are so nice. I love the designs and the emotions the characters make throughout the whole game. Enhancing it too is the lovely soundtrack and music throughout the game which just kept me in touch with the emotions of every scene. Story is great with fantastic characters, each one felt nice and engaging. I loved going through each of their highs and lows. The pacing was fantastic and I was hooked on the story the entire way through. I ended up loving this game a ton and it really is difficult to say Goodbye to Volcano High.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start this review by saying that this is an amazing coming of age story, with fantastic music, great character writing, and a super pleasing to the eye art style. This is a great game that if you like visual novels and good music, you should buy this. It is worth the cost of the game and more at full price. I do want to say though that around the end, it really feels like the game gives you dialogue options but doesn't account for the different conversation paths in the final scenes. I was a very supportive friend to someone who seemed (without naming names or spoiling) to be scatterbrained, refused to give what was important to my character much thought, was constantly disregarding my character's exciting events and attempts at making the band a bigger thing, but the game siloed me into dialogue trees that made it sound like I was the one who was constantly messing up and being rude to them instead, when I explicitly kept picking the nicest path with them over and over again. So amazing game, I'll definitely be playing it multiple times, but the devs should definitely put more thought into how their different conversation paths can take people and account for them better. Also don't be a loser who cares if sweet baby inc helped make a game or not, if you're at all concerned about that, I invite you to grow up and find some real problems In life.

_childDocuments_.review: really good lil vn, I appreciate my time with it and the effort put into it, particularly with the music, animations and the designswith regards to the story, it's hard not to feel stuff about it; I have a bit of a tough shell, but as as someone who pursues creation as something more than a hobby, as someone who's had their own complicated journey with identity, as someone who's messed up more than a few of their own relationships with their own bullheadedness, and of course, as someone who has to deal with all this in the face of everything ending (just like everyone else), it's difficult not to relate to Fang's messinesslooking at the art, I'm usually pretty annoyed at the presence of animations in vn as I feel they trend towards being a lil iffy and usually represent wasted effort, but the animations here find a  nice space where they can genuinely add something but without compromising on the benefits of asset reuse that vns allow, it comes together in a really nice way.When I had the auto play option enabled, things animated together really naturally without kicking me outta that flow state vns put me into, so I really like it for thatcan't comment too much on the music as I'm not a music person and can't tell bath salts from dishwater, but I really liked its implementation and vibed with it a bunchthe setting was also really fun, there's something about using furries/scalies/dinosaurs for the cast that adds a sense of hyper reality that sort of makes the structure of 'highschool game' more workable; it  generally doesn't hitch itself on the same dialogue issues that stuff like life is strange does, cause when it's not trying to be believable, you don't really think that much about whether or not line deliveries sound 'cringe'I also really like how the dialogue ui is animated together, it's a small thing, but it adds a lot and it's genuinely a crime that only ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cage games ever seem to be interested in trying that, so I'm very glad to see it hereI think the only issue that I truly have with this game is the major external problem of the internet not letting us have nice things.I won't get into the issues with four channers ripping people's art exclusively to defecate on their identities and their hard work, but like...it really really REALLY sucks knowing that even though I enjoy this game, I won't be able to talk about it publicly or enjoy fanworks about it cause the stink cloud that hangs over this game, that other people have created, is feccing impenetrable. things like this shouldn't be ruined just because jerks on the internet have a problem with them simply existing.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think there's much for me to say about this game. It's great. The visuals are amazing, the game direction is excellent, and you really feel like the experience was meticulously crafted by the developers. Perhaps it's because I barely play these type of games, but the dialogues syncing up with the animations in between scenes really sold it for me. I felt more engaged and involved that way, as if I was watching a show at my own pace. If I were to nitpick the game, I'd say the D&D inspired scenes were a bit lackluster and boring, especially since it barely had any voiced dialogues. It would've been nice if they spent a little bit more effort in actually making some form of mechanic for those scenes. Also, aside from that, the narrative is not the best out there, possibly due to how short it is. I thought that the premise and ideas of the writers were noteworthy but how they executed it felt rushed and not cohesive. Additionally, I think it would've helped if they added a chapter select for more dedicated players. Overall, it's a good VN game and is definitely worth a try. I enjoyed the time I spent in the game, however short it was.

_childDocuments_.review: Believable relatable story. I had the impression that it's been well-written. It's dramatic, it's cute, it's wholesome and sometimes even dreadful. There are things that look a little rough around the edges. Timing during scenes is sometimes a bit off, and I think some lines could have been delivered a bit better.By the end you are invested into the characters, or at least I was, and I think the question of "what do you DO, if you know the world is going to ♥♥♥♥?" was well explored. What if you are never allowed to reap the fruits of your labour? Or if you never had the courage to do what you wanted the most? Or if everything you thought was meaningful to you stops being a part of you?If you are ok with the characters being silly dinosaurs, you should give this game a go. It's food for thought. I do like to remind myself what being human is all about, these days, so this was a very welcome experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't lie, this game made me cry. Like.. A lot. I found myself relating to Fang in so many aspects. It kinda hurts but in a good way. I think that's pretty amazing.The game is very story-driven, it focuses more on narrative choices, rather than the rhythm sections. Those sections add a lot of immersion to the game, though, and I love them. They aren't too difficult, in my opinion.I also like how the dialog options actually have an effect on your relationships. They're impactful and meaningful. The songs are all beautiful and well written, I love all of them so much. I even listen to them on Spotify frequently. You can tell the team put a lot of passion and love into making the music, as well as the artwork. Every scene, every frame is so beautiful. I think my total playtime was closer to 7ish hours rather than 8, I afk'd for a bit, so it's not a super long game by any means. But the story is definitely worth it. If you like little rhythm mini games and a story about friendships, how your actions and words have an affect on them, and even a little bit of DnD (in their case, LnL), then this is a game for you. I honestly can't recommend it enough. Not many games can put me in my feels like this one did.

_childDocuments_.review: A terrific way to start the year. A wonderful experience overall. I haven’t played many visual novels, but the ones I’ve played weren’t fully animated and voiced like this one is. I’m pretty sure that this isn’t common at all in the genre, and I believe it’s worth trying out for that reason alone. In terms of its presentation, it’s more an interactive animated show rather than a traditional visual novel.I found the story and characters to be wonderfully written. It really nails the very online sense of humor, but it’s never snarky nor mean. It’s a very heartfelt story, and even though nostalgia, growing up and the end of the world are key themes it’s never a bummer nor does it lean on despair. In terms of its gameplay, the few rhythm sections are solid and fun to play through, and the decision making feels consequential enough to be consistently engaging.The soundtrack is on another level altogether. Banger after banger of original soft indie rock songs accompanied by some beautiful background music. The album is already on my Spotify rotation.I don’t really have much to say about it, it’s a short, very wholesome, very unique, experience that I’m happy to have played through.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short and sweet experience, with some brilliant design decisions punctuated with occasional technical hiccups.Despite what the game insists, you CAN play this game on Mouse and Keyboard.  I didn't have a controller on me so I was forced to play this way.  Its honestly not bad.  I can't speak for if the game is significantly easier or better experienced with a controller but it didn't really ruin or affect my experience at all.This is more of a story-based choice game than a rhythm game.  It has the two molded in, but it leans a lot more into the former.  Think the band jam sequences in Night In The Woods, on a smaller game and a bit more frequent.As spoiler free as possible; there is a looming astronomical threat to the entire world, and you play as a high school teen trying to kick off her band.  That's it.  You spend your time learning about Fang, the protagonist in this game, and their relationships with their friends and schoolmates.  There's enough threads to string you along for their stories.  Some of the major themes is coming to terms with an uncertain or even grim future, and it utilizes this well, both as the physical plot device of the Meteor becomes a larger and larger threat, and as you participate in Fang's story.The game is entirely serviceable and well made from a design perspective.  Animation and character designs are gorgeous, but the animations are frequently reused and it can get easy to notice.  I never found that necessarily distracting however, it was just a mental note that popped in and just kinda faded off as I got invested into it.The game plays similarly to any other choice game of its genre; more of a movie punctuated by choice options to play things out in a different direction or to respond to things differently.If you're here for the short version: Its a six hour experience; it demands little time, and little investment.  You won't get Mass Effect levels of carrying choices but you'll get specialized content and its not a waste to try another run if you're interested in seeing more of what the game offers.  I think them main thing that will scare people off is the price: its rather expensive for the amount of game you get, but if you're okay with spending a bit more than usual for it, this is for sure the game for you.  I don't give number scores because I'm based.  Just make up your own mind about it.----LONG VERSION:First thing I wanna gush about is something I think all choice games should utilize way more; UI design on choices.  Most choice games of its time would usually have a highlight on some options that summarize what you're gonna say and thats it.  However, this can lead to confusion about intent if its not clearly written, or its tone reads differently then what you thought.  In this regard, GVH expertly and impressively circumvents this issue, by giving each choice option specific visual effects depending on the mood and intent of the option is to Fang.  If Fang is HEATED about something, the option will be a giant flame.  If they're provocative, positively or negatively, it'll have sparks and electricity.  If its optimistic, it'll have a soft glow with particles floating on it.  There's at least a dozen of these effects that really help grasp the tone that the choice in particular is trying to send, which is something I *have* to gush about because its an expert tactic to circumvent the common issue of choice games like this that have difficulty discerning its intent to the audience.The effects I've been able to identify are as follows:- Fire = Heated, Angry, Furious.- Electricity = Provocative- Sharp = Mean spirited.- Wiggling = Lying.  Unsure of self.- Rippling = Anxious.- Wavy = Powerless.  Regretful.- Severed = Broken.- Glow = Optimistic, friendly.- Pulsate = Heart pumping.  Nerves.  Adrenaline.There's a ton.  And again, I have to gush because this is such smart design for one of the major flaws I see in games like this.  This is punctuated even further by the Resistant Choice system.  If you're about to do a choice that Fang may not be thrilled to take, or may be the 'unsafe' option at the time, Fang will subconsciously 'resist' the choice.  You may have to select one multiple times, you may have to input multiple buttons to commit, the choices can be scrambled and randomized, or the choices just blank out if you don't select it fast enough or hesitate, due to Fang overthinking it.  Its a cool feature that happens infrequently enough to not be annoying while also demonstrating the head space Fang is in, and lets you further immerse yourself AS Fang rather than playing as them.  This, combined with the tones I mentioned above, really allows you to make far more informed choices than if every choice was just neutral, without even having to use more words.  You can read the tone and mood you want to give your dialogue before you commit to it, and that is simply brilliant design.However, the Resistant Choice system begins one of my gripes with the game at a technical level, and the only one that really annoyed me and took me out of the experience when I encountered the issue.  Some Resistant Choices require you to input (on keyboard) the Left Shift and Right Shift at the same time while holding the choice.   I had no problem with this physically, but for some reason, either because of the game or because of something with my computer, GVH would just NOT register me holding both shift keys.  In order to get past this Resistant Choice, you have to hold both down for a small period before it lets you commit... Fortunately I was able to disable the feature and actually progress, but if you're playing on keyboard, be aware you may encounter this issue.Other technical gripes include dialogue cutting off, dialogue spoken not shown in the game or on subtitles, and other small things like that.  The dialogue is mostly okay, and when it happens you notice it but its not frequent enough to take me out of the experience.Speaking of dialogue, voice acting is great.  Some voice actors are better than others but the main cast is serviceable in almost all scenes, downright fantastic in others.  Some one-offs sound odd but nothing to get upset about.The characters themselves, I adored almost every single one.  I had my favorites, but the entire cast does well in doing their role.  Naomi puts on a good performance as the super-prep science tryhard.  Fang is a great protagonist character who feels like their own despite our control of choices; everything about them feels like it would be a choice THEY would make, or have a spin on it that makes sense for their character.  Nasar is funny and a good brother character, and I ended up caring about him more as the game went on.  Reed I thought I wouldn't like at first but you get a few good moments with him.  Sage is just hilarious and adorable.  Stella is the friend-mom we all need.  Trish is a great best friend and one of the core conflicts in the game.  Rosa was a bit... lately introduced for me to have an opinion on her to be honest?  I think she's one of the weaker ones in terms of her entire role... Extended content in the flashback showcase some good stuff about her and Sage.  Though I never got high affinity with her to find her extended content neither.Since I'm running out of space, I'll wrap up by saying that the game got me to care about all the characters, which is vital.  A few things I wish the game had: A couple more hours of extra content.  I'd love to see more about Fang's relationship with their parents, but sadly we only got a couple scenes, at least in my playthrough... and it would make the final scene even more powerful.  Same with Naomi, I wish we got more time to simmer in her romance if you decide to romance her.Overall, good game.  Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually not too fond of visual novels but i found myself pleasantly surprised with goodbye volcano high.The characters feel fun, generally well written and relatable and their design is expressive to boot.Both the feeling of Fang's (the protagonist) personal struggles and coming to terms with change as well as the looming impending feeling of doom as the end is growing ever nearer.. its quite a cocktail of emotions that gripped me.Its rare i find a story where i feel so invested in the characters, i just wish there was more of it to experience.Due to the rather short nature of the game (about 5 hours of content) the pricepoint is pretty steep but for a visual novel it certainly delivers a lot on the visual part as the game plays more like an interactive movie rather then just a picturebook.Last but not least the music and voiceacting, the voiceacting can be a bit choppy on the technical side but the deliviries of the actors hits well and are expressive like one would hope, it also helps to give a lot of character to the characters beyond visuals and story.The music is not particularly my type of genre but i found myself enjoying it plenty, the vocals and instrumental bits meld well together and i was looking forward to the next song each time.Gameplay wise.. well its a visual novel, i'm afraid that the little bits and pieces of gameplay won't be satisfying any gamer needs though the central minigame for the performances works well and is a unique spin on the rhythm game format that i found far more enjoyable then the usual "hit key when the colored thingy lines up" though its not too far from that.. don't play this game for the gameplay itself.I would hearthily reccomend this game to anyone that enjoys a good story with some emotional baggage to boot, oh and i want to congratulate the game on portraying queer people the way it does, its relieving to see it put in a light that isn't just a token character in a bethesda game or something.But even if you're not all about the gay, queer, trans whatever stuff the characters are plenty relatable taking that aside, it might even give you some insights to think about!Conclusion: 8.5/10, wish it was longer but i enjoyed the time i did play it a lot!

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely incredible game with phenomenal characters, story, and progression. Every character you interact with is written in such an incredible way that it is impossible to disregard even one part of their personality. They have nailed the dialogue, interactions, emotion, feel and weight behind every little thing in the heart-wrenching story of "Goodbye Volcano High." I cannot give the writers and developers enough praise for the masterpiece of a visual novel they have made, and I cannot stress enough how much it has touched me on such a deep level. There are multiple paths to tread and methods to try, with every action you make culminating into how you react to the characters, and how they will react to you. Several story lines are present and while I wasn't able to chase all of them in a single playthrough, I will absolutely be back to try it again. I will admit though, it would be nice to be able to manually select chapters to play or have a "story tree" where I can pick and choose moments to replay. It would definitely make it easier for me to keep track of what I've already done.I know it's impossible, but I've been left wanting much more of Fang and her wonderful group of friends. There won't be another performance from Worm Drama. There unfortunately never will be, and it only makes my heart ache even more for the characters, but I will avidly wait to see what this talented team will create next.This game is truly a unique and memorable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and I have a lot to talk about, so if you're interested in a specific topic, feel free to skip to it!TL;DR: A little overpriced, but the game can surely touch your heart, worth it with a discount!Gameplay: To start things up, GVH is meant to be much more of a story than a game, having really few gaming aspects, and if you're not the person who can handle a slow pace, this game is not for you, you need patience to get everything that the game has to offer, and you may get a little confused with the lore if you rush it too hard.Graphics: The artistic approach of the game is stunning, bringing to the player's eyes lots of vibrant colors, marvelous backgrounds and great character designs, which together, are able to create a great environment capable of concretizing memorable moments and saving some neat wallpapers. The game also uses a lot of dynamic animating, where the sprites are drawn separately, and then called depending on the situation or moment. This is a great way to make the game's expressions look more "organic", but it can also give a bad impression because, sometimes, the switching may cause small flickers on the process. But with a little polish, this problem can be easily solveable.Characters: Adding up to the point above, the game's characters have great designs, being unique on their ways and avoiding any types of stereotypes that many games fail to do, each one of them has different vibrant colors for skin and clothing that combos into a great palette for them. The ideia of making anthro dinossaurs is also pretty creative, letting the creators to make a much more diverse set of characters that colors your screen with a variety of cheerful colors that helps to pass out the game's vibe. Lore: I personally think that the game ROCKED with the choice of time and space: Passing through the last year of highschool, where everyone gets anxious when needing to choose your future definitely, in union with the fear of everything ending suddenly with the threath of a supermassive asteroid possibly hitting the Earth. With all of that, you can really see the characters' feelings and see how they react differently to what the future may or may not bring, at the same time that they do everything they can to continue together, no matter what. My only problem with the progression was the huge absence of time indicators between chapters, you can't really know if a day, a week or a month passed since the last events that occurred, and that might make you a little confused with the timeline and its pauses between key events.Soundtrack: I NEED to say that I entered the game expecting a good OST, but I finished it with ABSOLUTE BANGERS IN MY HEAD. Really one of if not the BEST OST that I've ever heard in my life. The game offers a great variety of tracks, ranging from usual band songs, to calm ambiences, to even epic RPG medleys! One of the main characteristics of the game is the presence of music, and it makes everything more magical, usually including lyrics that may sound like something at first, but as you near the game's ending, you get to find out what the song was really meant to represent. And to wrap this up, the performances (parts where you play the songs), are really well thought, I've never played a rhythm game with a multitasking system so well made, needing to pay attention to the entire screen at the same time makes you able to play well while enjoying the videoclip on the background AT THE SAME TIME. The design of these parts are marvelous, making this one of the best rhythm game systems I've ever played with.Replayability: I NEEDED to bring this theme on the table, because this is one of the game's BIGGEST PROBLEMS: GVH presents two main playing buttons, New game and Continue, not a single way to play the game again from a certain chapter, and with a game that has 8, needing to play the game from scratch multiple times just to see the characters' backstory would be REALLY time consuming and boring at some point, which is why I'm not 100%ing this game right now. Other visual novels have this feature, and for me, it is a MUST to extract the game's full potential. Another thing that breaks my heart is not having a way to replay the game's performances, the videoclips are gorgeous, and the rhythm features of multitasking makes me LOVE them, having a way to play them separately would make me re-enter the game every other week to experience this game's bangers.Overall: As a senior high school student, GVH was really relatable for me, even without impending doom and the VAST LGBTQ+ presence on my life, the game made me wake up and notice that this is my last chance to make my adolescense unforgetable before turning into an adult. Time never comes back  once it ends, and that's why we need to live, live like the world would turn upside down at any moment, live enough to leave a mark on the world AND on ourselves. Goodbye Volcano High tells an incredible narrative around this theme, which can inspire you in many ways, making this, a one of a kind experience for me, and maybe, for you, you should definitely try it out!Worm Drama Forever!

_childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews Video Review: High school poses undeniable challenges, a sentiment shared by most. The uncertainties of the future, the daunting decisions about courses and careers can make it feel like the end of the World. Yet, the cool kids of Volcano High seemed more intellectually prepared than I was at the time, perhaps forged by their life experiences and drama associated with the impact of an asteroid, draped with a sense of “do it today, or it may never happen.”Goodbye Volcano High immerses players in a visual novel, chronicling the life of Fang, a non-binary pterodactyl, navigating through their final year of high school alongside their tight-knit group of friends, Trish and Reed. Together, they form the band Worm Drama, which recently secured a spot in the Battle of The Bands, a gateway to performing at Caldera Fest in front of thousands. Fang’s sole certainty is music; their future unfolds within the confines of a band van, with dreams of playing at countless festivals.Unfortunately, the future is shrouded in uncertainty, extending beyond academics. The world grapples with the looming threat of an asteroid collision, a concept that can lead to various reactions. Amidst this uncertainty, the residents of Volcano High stand out for their unwavering support and understanding of one another, transcending, sometimes, their convictions and internal debates. A highlight of this adventure is the exceptional voice acting, which impeccably reflects the characters’ personalities.The story explores significant societal issues, embracing themes of inclusivity, trauma, and friendship. Fang, as a non-binary, navigates the complexities of their relationship with parents who struggle to understand but are willing to change. Trans characters are also featured, highlighting the generational gap in attitudes toward diversity and acceptance, bridging the gap between the virtual world and our own lives outside the realm of video games.As expected in a visual novel, dialogue choices serve as the primary gameplay mechanic in Goodbye Volcano High. However, rather than choosing options based on correctness, the choices that I had were made to match the vibe of the moment. Yet, it is still possible to opt for either the good or bad Fang’s mood, even though there are no cookies on the latter!The game introduces rhythm sequences between chapters, while not overly challenging, they demand attention. Additionally, there are geeky moments like the incorporation of Dungeons & Dragons, reimagined as L&L, which will undoubtedly delight board game and storytelling enthusiasts. The music seamlessly complements the narrative and is available on all major streaming platforms.The diverse cast of characters, even those in the background, is captivating. Though the backgrounds may often remain static, they are rich and engaging, providing a vivid canvas that enhances every line of text and character interaction. The animations are visually stunning, to the point where I would actually watch a Volcano High animated series.Throughout my 7-hour-ish journey to complete the story, I encountered no graphical or performance issues, save for a few instances where I couldn’t read or see character interactions on a specific slide due to automatic advancement. While not revolutionary, Goodbye Volcano High solidifies its place in storytelling games. It made me laugh, feel melancholic, and, as such, it’s challenging for me not to recommend this title.

_childDocuments_.review: A game I had uncertain expectations for, but nevertheless blew me out of the water by far succeeding them. A tense and beautiful story packed full of so many emotions, lovable but complex characters (that occasionally frustrated me but I really grew attached to) with fantastic voice acting, surprisingly stellar sound & music designs (one of its best qualities), and with gameplay & rhythm mechanics that make for a genuinely immersive and often overwhelmingly emotional experience (those pre & post show nerves go crazy... also, y'know, the threat of inevitable heat-death). I went into this game with little in mind, and came out of completely different. It's rare for me to find a game that can have me so far on the edge of my seat in anticipation, even if I already sort of knew what was coming, so I'm very glad I stuck around to play GVH on release. An instant addition to my favorites and a proper brain rot that led to several re-playthroughs to see everything the game had to offer. My only complaint being the difficulty of achievement hunting without any save slots or chapter select! Also not being able to see what photos you already got/missed... I'm missing four for the achievement and I think I'm out of steam playing through the entire game just to still not get the ones I need. But regardless, I'm very proud of the team that stuck with and gave this game the love it needed to become what it is, despite the challenges. You folks have created a wonderfully profound experience, one that'll absolutely be sticking with me, just as I'm sure it will for many others.

_childDocuments_.review: What an Incredibly heartwarming and simultaneously heartbreaking story, oh my god. The music and writing of this game inspires me to create my own stuff, which is the single best thing a work of art like this game can do in my book.I also can't explain how upset it makes me that people would harass the devs and community of this game just because of a trans character. This is one of the only pieces of media that I can think of with a trans person as the lead, and we should have more of that. This kind of representation is *so* important to normalise things like queerness and being trans, so that this kind of harassment and hate and anger happens less and less. Especially because this isn't a game about Fang being trans/non-binary -- while that is an important aspect of her character, it doesn't define the game. The game is about a group of friends, their memories, their dreams, their relationships, and how they choose to spend their time with each other during their final days. Fang being non-binary is important *because* it's not that important to the story. It normalises having queer characters in 'normal' stories, it makes it a less foreign concept to some people who might not be educated in what that means or have misconceptions about being queer as a whole.Anyway thanks for coming to my ted talk, go buy the damn game

_childDocuments_.review: i'd give Goodbye Volcano High an 8/10 -- it's absolutely one to make time for this year!PROS+ fantastic voice acting: the direction for every line was so good and there's so much vulnerability in the acting. every character feels perfectly cast and there really is just this wonderful degree of warmth to each voice+ fabulous music: this is such a good soundtrack. the rhythm mini-game is fun and actually quite challenging at times, especially because i just wanted to focus on the bops playing+ delightful character writing: i LOVE when games get teen dialogue right and GVH absolutely nails it. every character has layers and is lovable. comedic timing is impeccable, emotional scenes mostly land, one -- just a conversation between friends -- even made me tear up a bit because these characters were so well-written+ fun rhythm mini-game: already mentioned that it's quite fun!CONS- plot writing: i think we could have been shown how life changes after a certain point in the game more, it would have added a lot to the narrative and the weight behind the emotional scenes that occur afterwards. there are also three lengthy D&D sections that feel like they really overstay their welcome. they don't contribute much to the character relationships and that time feels like it could have been used on something else. i do think the subplot ends powerfully, at least- a few technical hiccups: some dialogue seemed to follow a conversation branch i hadn't chosen, mouths not moving while dialogue is being spoken, things popping in etc -- nothing that can't be smoothed over!overall, just so full of heart. you can tell everyone who worked on this put a piece of themselves into this game. this game is so eager to wear its heart on its sleeve and be vulnerable and revel in the joy of love and friendship. such a very lovely story.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't express how good this game is. Genuinely, the only issue i have with the game is that it's ever so slightly buggy, if you minimize the game without pausing sometimes it will ♥♥♥♥ up the animations. The characters are so deep and thought out, their interactions make them feel like actual people. there are arguments, and disagreements, and things get rough, but they turn around. even just looking at dialogue options builds the character. if they're too anxious or lack the confidence to say something, then even if you select it it'll go staticy and not let you choose it. and options that take a lot of confidence to say, you have to hold multiple buttons down in order to say it. it's really a very unique system, and i haven't seen something like it anywhere else.This game, despite taking place at the end of the world, is still hopeful. but it still feels real. there's a palpable dread in the way the characters talk. _childDocuments_.review: I'm really confused by some reviews here saying how amazing this game is... I agree that it does have some really amazing parts, but did we really play the same game? Obviously, I recommend you to play this game, it's rather unique and offers a proper gameplay experience. How to actually talk about this game without spoiling the whole feel of it? From beginning to end, it follows the idea of personal growth, acceptance and the strength of community when things go downhill. The story in Goodbye Volcano High contains several main elements: music, an asteroid, friendship and dreams. What should be emphasized is that everything is interconnected and no element is deprived. It is very impressive how the game follows the cycle of day and night, how we have real conversations on social networks, we get to know in detail almost all the main characters and those essential to the story, and it is fascinating how the developers managed to place all of this in one fantastic world which makes sense. What the game offered us the best were the relationships between the characters themselves, their friendships, families and backstories. We all know what happened to the dinosaurs (that's why I mentioned the asteroid earlier) and all the time we have that doomsday feeling that is inevitable. Our characters are high school students, there are moments in which we can find ourselves in them; the drama, the worries of everything, the different experiences, but this also made the overall feeling of the gameplay perceive like the truest exploration of high school life in one game.What should be highlighted first is the music. The music was truly superb, it doesn't matter what genre you prefer, we can all listen to this kind of music. In addition, the voice acting added special charm to this game, each character had their own voice and the tone was also very good. Furthermore, the text that is shown below while someone is talking or while something is being shown to us is also unique; it is visible and well bolded, compared to some other visual novels. The graphics and visuals were beautiful; whoever illustrated the scenography and interiors had the right idea and plan on how best to do this. However, for a game that consists entirely of animated sequences and stylistic choices, there were a lot of odd pauses between dialogue, characters starting at an empty space, animations felt a bit off as things occasionally didn't load at the same time as everything else or seemed slow, the lip syncing during the music segments was good, but outside of that it often happened that the characters would simply skip the text or not speak in rhythm with the words we hear. However, the amount of effort that was clearly put into the music, animation and character work was very evident.As for the gameplay mechanics, this title almost always offers us the possibility to choose what we want, that is, we are offered several dialog boxes and menus. Sometimes that system is playing with us and make us click exactly what we want while time is running to keep us focused, and there was also randomly changing choices during some stressful situations. Sometimes you'll have to be quick in determining what's right, and sometimes you'll have some leeway to do so. Your choices are very important, they affect your relationships with other characters, whether you will argue with them or try to understand their situation and why they are telling you this. Goodbye Volcano High also offers us a system of memories, images, and relationships/affinities with other characters, i.e. how close you've become to some of them, which means it unlocks special decisions or parts of the story that you might not have at the end if you went the other way. Other than that, the game lacks a bit more honest conversations, sometimes it was all about having to forgive each other anyway, imagine what life would be like where you lose your best friends on purpose?What needs to be pointed out is that this title lacks replayability, specifically certain segments or even the ability to save, which hurts the replayability quite a bit. On the other hand, committing to replaying the game just to take a different path is too time-consuming, especially since there's no going back if you choose the “wrong” option and end up on a side you might not have wanted.What can definitely be a problem for fans of rhythm games is that this whole mechanic in this game doesn't really make much sense. We have three types of rhythm control, the first is the middle circle which is the most important, where you are simply not allowed to make mistakes and affects your final performance, and it fills up when you turn exactly on the side where circles are coming from. The second is the WASD keys that come from time to time and have to be timed, and the third is the two down arrows that represent some highlight of the beat or song. You can completely ignore those two rhythmic systems because they do not affect the final performance. In addition, the rhythm in Goodbye Volcano High has no relation to the song at all, that is, the rhythmic playing is never in tune with the music, but it forces you to look exactly what is coming first and when so you can time it with your eyes and not your ears. What can also irritate are sudden zooms in and out of the frame, and its sudden changes. I will subjectively say that I don't understand why this mechanic was added in the first place, which is actually not difficult to master, you pretty much always get 90% score, and it doesn't matter if you made a mistake or not.The characters themselves are well written and defined. You will definitely develop some of your preferences, for example, how much Trish will get on your nerves or how much you will like Reed, and this is just proof that each character has their own mind within the game. However, as mentioned earlier, as players we would like to be able to talk to other characters more in private, get deeper into their heads, ask them what they think about this or that. One playthrough can last between 5 and 10 hours, depending on whether you skip some parts or not, and it's clear that we don't have enough time to get to know such a large number of characters. In particular, the romance between Fang and Naomi was really rushed. What if it was, right? It is understandable that not everything can be squeezed into the game, but the inability to connect more deeply with the other characters is still annoying.Finally, as for the ending, everyone will have their own thinking and preference, however, it must be admitted that the ending somewhat ruined the story that was going on all along. In fact, the ending even makes sense, but everything just suddenly disappears, and all the drama that happened the day before means nothing anymore, as if the game introduces us to the fact that we will all die one day and what we have done during our life will also dissapear. Honestly, I definitely recommend that you play this title, not only is it unique in its approach to narrative games, but the overall impression at the end remains positive due to the very high quality of the music and graphics. In fact, this game could have gotten an even better rating if only some features were better designed and planned.

_childDocuments_.review: 12 years ago, in 10th grade I read an article about FF7: Crisis Core on psp that opened with the words "From the beginning of the story, you know how it ends". And so it is with this game. In an Era where the greatest achievements are finishing a game  or a show, and learning how it ends, KO_OP decided that the journey was more important than the destination. And what a journey it was. GVH made me cry, yes but not because the game was emotional (though it absolutely was), but because it, and it's soundtrack ask so many questions, and honestly, some of the answers I came to were hard. More games need to remember that sometimes, getting to the end isn't as important as how we got there, and reflect that in their storytelling. Now it wasn't perfect. There were a few visual bugs in my first playthrough, and a few janky moments where dialogue cut off, or characters talked over each other, minor annoyances, nothing that ruined the game for me. That said, the devs are quite active in the discord community, and 1 week in have shipped an update fixing a lot of the things players have been reporting. If you have a bug, seriously, go report it in the discord, chances are they'll fix it. Thank you for coming to my TED Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough last night.I'll start by mentioning that I was surprisingly  for Volcano High. I haven't been following it for very long, discovering it by coming across the teaser trailer. I fell in love with the music, the character design, the concept. Teen melodrama, but they're all gay dinos and it's the end of the world? Hell yeah, sign me the ♥♥♥♥ up. I was ready to cry until my eyes are sore.For the most part, I think I got what I was hoping for.Volcano High has an amazing concept to work with. I can't be the only one who's (day)dreamed about an apocalypse scenario - the sadness in accepting it, struggling to make the most of the time you left, taking the last chance you have to do something you've been holding back for so long. The game is well positioned for an incredibly emotional tearjerker of a story.That said, it took playing through about half of the story before I got properly emotionally invested. That's about the point at which the characters start treating the approaching cataclysm as all but a certainty, and the emotional intensity ramps up accordingly.Starting off where the game does, I found the musical minigame surprisingly good. It's not too difficult but they ramp up in difficulty as the game progresses, dividing your attention with multiple incoming "notes" to increase the pressure.While I got all the 90% achievements, I did struggle to get them perfect. I kinda wish there was a practice mode for the minigame, andit was easier to pay attention to the animations and montages behind the prompts. I'll admit to resetting after screwing up one of the performances, though for the most part I took them as they came. After all, being rushed and only having one shot to get it right does fit thematically. I definitely felt the pressure to perform well, so if that was intentional, kudos to the developers.It's cute that you get to contribute lyrics to the songs but it wasn't initially clear to me that the lines weren't gonna be one after the other.This is also the first visual novel I've played after Life is Strange that is fully animated, and that was a pleasant surprise. Great character design along with the animation works really well. There were a couple of times where I wish the characters were a bit more dynamic, e.g. when you (Fang) are chatting to a couple of characters, and one of them is talking to you, they both keep staring at you rather than the person talking. That felt a bit unnatural when I noticed it.The characters themselves are reasonably well-written and well-defined, though some of the side characters can feel a little shallow and stereotypical as a result. I definitely have my preferences like . Anyway, personally all of the main cast are believable and I got a good sense of them from a single playthrough. They're all casted and performed excellently. A couple of lines could have made a bit more energetic to really make it melodramatic but might just be me.I will echo other complaints about pacing from other reviewers. I have a good idea of what and how each of the main cast are feeling towards the end. Even so, I wish I got to chat more, dig into their heads, ask them what they think about this or that. The game insists several characters are in my "inner circle" by the end, but I still don't feel like I know what makes them tick by the end of the 8 hours playtime. There's such a large cast that not enough time is given to each to flesh them out, especially the side characters. They're cute, and  in all it's a reasonable size for a friend group, but again, too many to squeeze into 8 hours alongside the plot.Running out of time is part of the whole concept, however, months fly by in-game, but you get to see a tiny number of conversations during all of that.In particular the . Again I understand there's only so much you can squeeze in, but it still hurts to not be able to connect as deeply with these characters not because of the story, but because of the game's budget.Maybe another playthrough will give me a chance to explore the characters and decisions that could have been. I might do that before searching up route guides. But this is something that I struggle with visual novel style games: you sometimes aren't given the tools to speed through the bits you've already played through to get to the paths you haven't explored. That does seem to be the case in Volcano High due to the simple save system and some unskippable dialogue.When it comes to the end, I personally thought it fit perfectly. I didn't see ambiguity like another reviewer suggested. .For the record .I'd definitely recommend Goodbye Volcano High, especially if you're in the mood for a cry. Nothing'll do that better than a teen melodrama with a dash of imminent doom.

_childDocuments_.review: To be quite honest, they had me at "Dinosaur high school".Writing and voice acting are great, appear very lifelike; just maybe a little too enthusiastic. It is all very emotionally affecting, easily among the top three media measured by that, right up there with Fry's dog.The animations could be better, especially the singing; that appears to be a hard problem others failed at before. But, they do the job just fine.I've played a couple of narrative heavy games before, but no 'proper' visual novel style one (you know, big character sprites, mostly talking, gameplay mostly dialog choices). So not much to compare it to in that regard. I played through once, don't intend to replay anytime soon; I'm not too interested to see what happens with other choices. But I do get the impression that the big story events are fixed and can only be altered in small details by your choices. That would be a negative for some, I guess. But given the big theme, that may be the point.Yeah, I have only nitpick complaints. They could have done more with them all being dinosaurs. A little more pop culture. Where is their version of the fight between Kirk and the Gorn? (Maybe I did not pay enough attention, mind) They have chairs clearly not made with big, long tails in mind. And why do pterodactyls drive cars? It's not like their wings became useless when they evolved that second pair of arms. Also, that second pair of arms bugs me a little.

Not really.I mean, obviously it's not something for everyone unfortunately but hopefully things would change with time.Back to it, first: Colorful talking dinosaurs! And singing/playing music even! Hell yeah!The animations! And the soundtrack! Can't say no to that!But considering the whole "Snoot Game" incident I was a bit worried, and it turned out pretty good actually.It has some bugs, like broken animations, textures slowly loading or not doing it at all. And the weirdest ones where during the songs, being zoomed in and out resulting in VERY PIXELATED textures and leaving barely some space for the buttons.I wish the devs fix most of these if not all and we get later some more content because the story was beautiful and I loved every second of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Strong narrative, great characters, unique setting.This game inspires wholesomeness and dread, with its slice of life atmosphere slowly getting darker and darker as the story progresses. Exceptional soundtrack.Cons:Sometimes the dialogue can feel a bit "what's up my fellow kids".Jokes can run on a bit long. Art direction seems to be a matter of personal taste (I personally love it).The OST was so good that I wish we had more rhythm sections </3Overall, if you're into games like Life is Strange or just slice of life content with a bit of "impending doom" spice; I believe this might be right up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really good. Beautiful art style, the story is heartwarming. I liked the gameplay for the songs, but you miss a lot if you want to see what is actually happening on the screen. The game NEVER is clear when you can pause to save and return later. _childDocuments_.review: The mix of visual novel and rhythm game serves GVH well. The rhythm game: the mix of directional arrows controlled by analog stick with the face button inputs scattered across the screen is inspired. You really feel like you are doing two things at once without it being overwhelming. Plus the music is really good!The visual novel stuff is really good too. This is a game where the dialogue button's text does not match up what the character actually says, which annoyed me, but it makes some sense when there's supposed to be subversion in how the game presents dialogue options. There's a few tricks, like options cycling around to represent Fang's uncertainty. And the game will lock you out of some choices if you hover over them but then move away, representing Fang's hesitancy (this is something you can turn off through the options menu).In the end this is a story game. And the story is kinda great. There's a chunk of it that's a little weak because the meteor stuff is pushed to the back and it feels like the drama could come from any YA fiction but eventually shows its teeth and the drama becomes gutwrenching but also very human and affirming. It's worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: This made me laugh and cry. I absolutely loved it. One should not expect to have a nice experience if they act like a jerk , since there are choices that may negatively impact how things unfold, luckily that is not how i played and my ride was wonderful (but sad, but wonderful). If you play with your heart, the game will make you feel.The gorgeous artstyle , music and voice acting , and generally the execution complements this perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: As a queer person who seen their senior year get wrecked by a natural disaster, I touched deeply with Fang and the crew from Goodbye Volcano High. The story was beautiful and very emotional, the rhythm aspects were fun, the characters both design and personality were really enjoyable, and I’m likely gonna replay this a few times in the future. Some technical issues were present, like visual pop in when a scene transitioned; lines of dialogue being cut short, and I think I seen the beginning of a romance scene with Stella after I already was with Naomi, and some kind of relatability/retry menu would be nice for the chapters/music performances, but these are all things that can be added with an update. That being said, absolutely buy and play this game!! Go Worm Drama 💜💜
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely so beautiful. Sure, there are some bugs that need to be ironed out, and a few choppy transitions, but the writing hits so close to home. The characters are fleshed out, and you can feel the emotion in their lines & voices. My favorite part about it is that even when making all the "right" choices, Fang still has their feelings. You can't deny that, the other characters will have their own complex feelings too, both good and bad. It's their story together. The game doesn't try to blow things off and gives it to you straight. This game is down to Earth (no pun intended) and that's what makes it even more special. Definitely worth your time and support.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: Right so, just finished game. For me clocked in at 6 and half hours. So what do you get out of it?You play as Fang, a (taradactal? been awhile since dino class) Teen aspiring to have a Music Career and go on tour with her friends. But, first she needs to survive Senior year. Oh and their may or may not be a world ending event about to transpire. So you know, no pressure.Gameplay wise, its a Visual Noval, you pick dialogue options and you even get to do a rythum mini game like 5 or 6 times everytime Fang and the Band have a song to play. Some of them are NOT EASY, your gonna get a mental work out trying to keep up that hand eye coordinaiton.A color cast of characters, a bit of drama, a bit of sadness, Fun times.If their is one message you take away from this game, let it be this "Live everyday like its your last", and hold on to your Friends, Family. You never know, ya know. Hope you enjoy the game as much as i did.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: Some great ideas exceptional art and well designed characters. However this game leaves almost no room to breathe as you are moving from one event to the next. It doesn't really feel like there's any time to stop or take a break. The story also ends on a rather abrupt note without much finality. A lot of things in the narrative don't make any sense if you look at it a little closer but for the most part a lot of the character driven interactions were well done and interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet (Beat in about 5 hours). I can see the comparisons to Night in the Woods and they are justified, similar edgy teen slice-of-life tone and also has rhythm game sections with a few songs. Speaking of songs, I do like that you can choose your own lyrics, although I still think the replay value here is somewhat limited as the player's choices don't seem to have a huge impact on the story otherwise. I think the main problem is that the game simply wasn't long enough for me to create bonds with the characters. There's a big cast here, so I find it faces a similar problem to Mass Effect 2 in that there's all these great characters but barely any actual dialogue with them to get to know them further. I do also feel the LGBT elements were ramped up a little too high, while I'm supportive of the community, this does come across as a little in your face. I heard others mention technical issues, but I didn't find it much of a problem. A couple freezes but nothing serious. I enjoyed the L&L sessions most (potential future dlc?), and while this game definitely isn't for everyone, I quite enjoyed my brief time with it. But I'm not sure it's worth the asking price considering how short it is though and the aforementioned lack of replayability.  If you like these types of games and can enjoy the unique tone it's worth picking up though.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable if bittersweet experience. Was thoroughly amazed by the amount and quality of voice acting and the polish of the art and story. Not to mention the music, that stands in a league of its own and enriched the entire rest of the experience. Definitely recommend if you're a fan of stories about friendship and life purpose.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: A bit rough around the edges but overall a really good experience. _childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't follow the development of this game, just added it to my wishlist a few months ago when I caught a trailer on Twitter and I'm glad I did. Going into this, I figured I would enjoy it well enough, but this game exceeded my expectations. I know the story leaves some to be desired, and I do wish the game were a bit longer, but the characters and music made it a thoroughly enjoyable experience. Despite its flaws, I am still thinking about GBVH days after finishing and a melancholic feeling comes up whenever I do. The character designs are great, and Fang's is probably one of my favorite of all time. And don't get me started on the amazing soundtrack, Dabu, Brigette Nagger, and Lachlan Watson (not to mention everyone else who worked on these songs) did an incredible job and most of them have ended up in my permanent playlists.This game made me grow attached to a bunch of dinosaur teenagers, and despite knowing what the ending would be, it left me hoping that this wouldn't be true to history. I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys visual novels and games like Night in the Woods & Life is Strange as I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Does this game have technical problems? YesDoes this game have overall problems with writing and character development? YesDo your choices really matter? You should already know an answer to this question based on how many games have used that phrase in the pastIs it worth playing? If you are not discouraged by the questions and answers above, then go for it, you will not regret it.There are some technical issues, I am not gonna list all of them, since other people did that. There were two things that bothered me the most. First, some dialogues are skipped, I needed to check if I have not accidentally pressed a button on the keyboard. Second, something went wrong in the process of audio mix for most of the dialogues, often when characters stop speaking it sounds as they have not given the track time to naturally fade away but just cut it right in the moment when the line ends.The only real struggle I have with the story is the ending, which stands against the message that this game wants to tell. Overall, story is not perfect. But it does not need to be, it is still enjoyable and emotional and left me in this sad/empty state after finishing it. 30$ for a 7 hour experience is a bit much, but honestly I had much more fun than in other AAA titles which take waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaay more hours to complete and this game reminded me of what I love about short games. It was not the best and most perfect, but still it was a great ride for me and I will go for it again, after the devs will patch it up. Although, if you cannot ignore some inconsistencies or flaws with storytelling and it bothers you, I would say skip this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When first seeing the announcement trailer I knew I had to play this game since I'm a big fan of narrative / decision based games like Life is Strange, any of the games Telltale has been making etc.I didn't watch any of the following trailers since I try to keep going in as blind as I can into games that interest me and having said that a lot of the narrative in Goodbye Volcano high is treading known paths of stories that deal with similar situations.But even if the game goes through very similar story beats as other stories in that genre I had a great time from start to finish. The characters felt earnest and the voice performances where great across the board.There was a lot of charm and love crammed into this project at every opportunity. There were a lot of small animation details that surprised me. For example the different animations when Fang is texting with their friends on the phone added a lot of personality. And those small details are everywhere.The first time you'll see the credits is around the average length I'd say for games in this genre (5-6 hours)and while I ended up wanting more when I saw the credits it wasn't because I felt the game was incomplete but because I loved the cast and wanted to spend more time in that world.But when it comes to what is in the game. Well it delivers an at least to me emotional story with a great cast.(Sorry for not going into detail here but I want to keep it spoiler free)When it comes to downsides for this game. I ran into a couple of bugs where sound wouldn't play (fixed it with restarting the game) or sometimes inputs wouldn't work. Though that was fixed with changing between fullscreen and borderless window in the options menu.As someone who played a lot of rhythm games some of the input prompts felt weirdly clumsy and unresponsive. But since the focus is more on the narrative I didn't really bother me that much. I had 1-2 instances where I reload a safe cause I though the input for one the prompts wasn't really working. (When you have to push both analog sticks down at the same time) But after getting a feel for the required timing it was fine.Overall I feel I can safely recommend this game to people who enjoy games like Life is Strange or telltale games and I am really exited to see what the team behind this Goodbye Volcano High does next.

_childDocuments_.review: Goodbye Volcano High is a sweet mix of a VN / Rhythm game with wonderful characters / visuals, and a compelling story that intrigues the player as the passage of time goes on with the impending event behind everything. Truly a wonderful a game in its own volition with memorable characters / setting. Must play for a nice story!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! I loved it. Great dialog, fantastic voice acting and downright incredible production value, to the point it felt at times like I was playing an animated TV show. The story is moving and carefully crafted so you don't hate the characters even if they argue or make dumb choices. There are a surprising number of fun creative choices you get to make in this game, alongside the usual 'communicate your feelings' dialog choices you would expect. Also, the music rules. The length of the game is 6-7 hours, which I think is the right length for a story like this one but keep it in mind if that is a factor before you buy.The only negatives I have are small missing features or technical problems:The game sometimes hangs for too long between shots. This can lead to awkward pauses in the dialog.There is also sometimes pop-in when the game switches shots, causing a background element or character to show up a few frames later than everything else in the shot.Finally, there was one instance where I paused the game and audio broke, which I fixed by quitting to desktop and reloading my save.Speaking of saves, this game has no save slots, or manual saving at all. Not even a chapter select screen. You just have one autosave and that's it. Very odd.Overall: The story idea and characters alone warrant an 8/10. Voice acting, music, and stylistic flourishes bump it all the way up to a 9.5/10. The minor technical issues and lack of save options hold it back just a little, but hopefully the devs will fix these problems with a patch.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game at a 75% only because i had a few problems with it. But i will say none of the problems took away from the awesome but sad Story. It hit so many marks with me, from how i used to feel growing up, to how i feel today. I did a play through all in one sitting and took a little under 7 hours to beat, There isn't much of replay other than to get 100% the songs for the Achievements. In all the game makes you connect with the main dude. If you used to be a no one, someone who cast aside, Didn't follow in the footsteps of there parents, the game will speak to you just, like it does with me.But for what i would say would break the game for some people, -I had it skip over dialogue on it own some times mid way through or right at the start and jump to the next. and there is no way to look back to see what was missed.-The Animation was either slow not synced right or just not there for talking, moving, etc.-There are many times when the game just loses all back ground sound, You'll be talking to someone with music in the background and then it just disappears and its all gone. leaving to a very awkward conversation between you and the NPC.-The biggest thing i have a problem with. There is not a single point where you are given a moment to pause to put the game down, not after days or in between what is going on in the world. It just goes and doesn't start from the beginning to the end. -There is no Save file meaning. if you mess up on a song mid way through the game and what all the achievements you have to restart the whole game over again just to get said achievement. That goes the same with all the in game choices (IMO you shouldn't go back to change a choice and you should play it all in one go. but i know people can't do that).

_childDocuments_.review: Now that it's been almost a year since the release, and I've had time to play through this completely as well as with friends and get new people into the game, I feel like I can leave a better review.Goodbye Volcano High isn't for everyone, both good (just not a fan of the gameplay style) and bad (queerphobic), but I HEAVILY recommend giving this game a shot. It doesn't try to be some grand story, it doesn't glamorize its characters or fit them into a cheap box, there isn't some attempt to make every single line a standing ovation. KO_OP treats its characters like they would any real person. I won't spoil much about the story, as it's something that loses some of its impact (pun intended) if you already know a lot of the story beats.They don't always talk with absolute clarity, their motivations can be confusing, and some things they say or do don't always make sense. But they're not an oversight in this case. They're an integral part of the story and the characters, and the dialogue and delivery are both much more like what you'd hear from actual people. Despite all being dinosaurs, they're all very human.There's also no big, crazy story going on beyond the asteroid that's hinted at in the demo and the middle chapters, just Fang and their two closest friends trying to win the Battle of the Bands before summer while figuratively making it through in one piece.There's more focus on the characters and how the little details can get in the way of being friends sometimes, and it doesn't portray anyone as perfect. Not even Fang, the character you play as. The people who call them selfish or a jerk tend to miss the point that this is part of the overarching story and Fang's character arc, and they don't always see that for different reasons.And besides the art direction being really unique, offering an almost 3D style done completely with 2D art and an entire system for both movement and characters talking, the music and sound direction are incredible. It's worth listening to the soundtrack alone from this game, especially if you're a fan of genres like Shoegaze (which seems to be the main inspiration). You'll also find some familiarity if you've ever played games like Dwarf Fortress, as its soundtrack is made by the same person, Dabu.For the voice acting, despite feeling a lot more human and personal, there's still some real talent behind everything. It doesn't sound like 90s high school movies, where the actors and actresses are more obviously in their late 20s to early 30s; I personally forgot these were even adults doing the voice acting. Especially Fang's voice actor, Lachlan Watson (They / Them), someone who's appeared in the Sabrina the Teenage Witch reboot and the Chucky TV series. You get to hear their singing voice in the soundtrack too, which they NAIL. Brigitte Naggar's singing isn't anything to scoff at either, though!There's also Allegra Clark, someone you might recognize from Apex Legends and Jujutsu Kaisen; Ozioma Akagha, known for some live action shows like Delilah; Mark Whitten, a voice in Spider-Man 2 (the PlayStation game) and the Demon Slayer movie from 2020; Sarah Elmaleh, someone you might recognize from Hi-Fi Rush; and more, such as Abe Bueno-Jallad, Dee Revilla, Jensen Trani, and Dahlia Salem, the last of which was an actress in Paul Blart: Mall Cop of all things. (The last part isn't important, just funny to mention.)(If you are just here for Goodbye Volcano High itself, this next part may not be relevant to you, but I still recommend reading it.)The last thing I'll mention is this: If you have any amount of respect for queer people, regardless of what group or if you are in that group yourself, I recommend staying VERY FAR away from both "Snoot Game" and "I Wani Hug That Gator!", as both of them are by the same person: Cavemanon, a common 4chan user (the kind you hear about on the news, not the kind that stopped the cat killer) much like almost everyone on his team.The first game was made completely as an anti fan-game, started and ultimately released years before this game was much more than its reveal trailers, containing some really vile content that doesn't just include very blatant transphobia. All of its endings are centered around the transphobia, though, and one of the "downer endings" specifically turns Fang into a literal school shooter (in a FULL SCENE, graphics and all) just for not being detransitioned. The other "downer ending" is not nearly as graphic, but is still based on not being detransitioned. The other game does not have much of this, likely because Cavemanon and the people he worked with knew it would likely not fly a second time, but the beliefs, views, and even outright hatred is still a part of its design.Cavemanon himself, and by extension a lot of his fans, are - for lack of a better description - exactly what you'd expect from the "bad side" of 4chan. In particular, they're quite fine and adamant to dox certain people over Goodbye Volcano High (especially Wolf Nanaki), and Cavemanon has made multiple long-winded post about his "traditionalism" and how Snoot Game is explicitly MEANT to be as queerphobic as it is.When it comes to "I Wani Hug That Gator!", there's a certain chance that artists who make content surrounding it (especially art) may not know these things about the previous game and Cavemanon, and you may have some luck warning artists about said content. But when it comes to Snoot Game, I would almost not even bother due to how blatant it all is. Which is a shame, as there is a very large and disappointing amount of queer people who are fans (or "fans") of these games, not knowing or caring that the creator very publicly despises them for who they are.If you're all the way down here, and you read all of this, I'm glad you took the time for it. If you're all the way down here and DIDN'T read all this, imagine I'm throwing bean bags at you.Worms Forever,Dreamless

_childDocuments_.review:
In times of change, what do we owe each other? 

Goodbye Volcano High, a cinematic, choice-based narrative game set in the final year of school for a bunch of dinosaur teens, on the cusp of graduation and the rest of their lives.

You will follow them as they struggle to make their mark on the world, figure out who they're going to be, and try to find love, all before time runs out and they're thrust into the world of adulthood. But what they don't know yet is that time might be about to run out for real. In a time where we're all feeling a little lost and scared, and not sure what happens next, we're hoping that the story resonates with people.
_childDocuments_.name: Goodbye Volcano High

name: Alone in the Dark
detailed_description: Alone in the Dark weaves a chilling tapestry of psychological horror and Southern Gothic charm, reimagining the iconic game that set the benchmark for the genre. We invite you to join us on a journey into madness, where each encounter could be your last. With each step you take closer to unravelling Derceto's mystery, the eyes that watch from the darkness grow hungrier. Every bullet means the difference between survival and an unthinkable end. The next door you unlock could lead to a nightmarish realm offering nothing but slashing claws, grasping tentacles, and frayed sanity. Journey to interbellum Louisiana, where an era of decadence hides a darker tale - of escape from past traumas and an intolerant society, into the waiting grasp of something darker, something that has patiently lurked for impossible eons. This is Alone in the Dark as you've never seen it - a skillfully-woven narrative of Southern Gothic elegance and eldritch madness that pays homage to its legendary origins while taking the next step forward in survival horror storytelling. A Haunting Tale of Mystery and Madness Step inside Derceto Manor, an asylum shrouded in intrigue, guarding a terrible secret. Client Emily Hartwood and private investigator Edward Carnby embark on a harrowing quest for answers; Emily to the mystery of her missing uncle, Edward to the toughest case he will ever face, and both to questions they dare not ask themselves. This re-envisioned classic invites you to explore an unforgettable single player adventure rich with suspense, frights, and revelations that will test the limits of your imagination. Featuring Hollywood Talent Experience some of the greatest acting survival horror has ever seen through the performances of award-winning actors Jodie Comer (Killing Eve, Free Guy) and David Harbour (Stranger Things, Black Widow) in their first videogame roles. Jodie and David’s immaculately captured likenesses breathe life into Emily Hartwood and Edward Carnby, lending a deeply personal aspect to Alone in the Dark’s story that demands it be played twice to get the full experience. A Tribute to Horror Pioneers Rediscover the essence of psychological horror in a game that respectfully nods to its 1992 origin, the game that established the survival horror genre. Alone in the Dark is your gateway to an experience steeped in the atmospheric dread of classic horror, with next-generation storytelling and gameplay. A must-play for fans of twisted tales, nerve-wracking exploration, and desperate combat. A Story That Challenges Reality Envisioned by Mikael Hedberg, acclaimed writer behind modern horror classics “SOMA” and “Amnesia”, Alone in the Dark’s intricate web of mystery delves into themes of trauma, faith, evil, and abandonment. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an enjoyable survival horror experience with good enemy design and level design. The game also has pretty good feeling combat as some of it its strengths. However constant visual stuttering and bugs plagued my first play through. Whenever I entered a new room I would experience noticeable visual stuttering. I would suggest you setup a frame counter to determine your lows and then cap your frames to that minimum in Adrenaline or NVIDIA control panel. This game has really nice looking graphics, featuring highly detailed textures and great looking character design. Props to the voice acting and dialogue as well. I will say that solving the puzzles in this game is too tedious to be fun though. Finding the correct combination/code requires serious effort as you have to back track to find key items and search through files for clues. Compared to the joy I get from puzzles in Resident Evil games, this game simply can't compete.The combat feels good in this game and the gun play feels fairly accurate. Ammo and healing items are fairly sparse which fits nicely with the survival horror genre. However it is worth mentioning you will probably get stuck on objects throughout your play through and have to re-load your save to get unstuck.  I wish they would fix these bugs as it really ruins the experience. All in all I'd say it's worth a play through, but maybe wait until it's on sale. I really don't approve of this game selling for the price of a triple A game.
