_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic AA horror game, albeit with some flaws. The game is 100% overpriced and should not be $60, especially with the ridiculous performance issues and multitude of bugs. I also can't justify that price with the lack of unlockable content. $40 would've been the perfect price for this game.(AN EDIT: The game has been patched to remove a lot of the bugs, and the shader cache issue has been addressed. Please take this into account - I appreciate their devotion to making the experience better.)Moving on from those criticisms, I wholeheartedly loved this game. The story is fantastic, classic Lovecraftian fare with a delightfully confusing story that feels rewarding to unwrap and digest. The characters are fun and well-acted - David Harbour particularly breathes a lot of life into Edward Carnby. The combat isn't fantastic or super engaging, but it's serviceable - combat is not typically what I go into survival horror for, so if it's functional I'm alright with it.(Silent Hill 2's combat is pretty bad, after all. And that's a perfect game in spite of it.)The atmosphere and tone are also fantastic. The soundtrack is perfect, and I found myself very immersed throughout the game - Derceto becomes very atmospheric once we approach night-time, and I adored the atmosphere and oppressive mood of the French Quarter, Hateful Mound, Cemetary, and Sunken Temple areas. Spoilers ahead.Some nitpicks: I wish the Dark Man were more present as a gameplay enemy, as I enjoyed the gimmick of him draining your health in the Toroella level. He could've been a lot scarier if he showed up more often outside of cutscenes.I also am mixed on the Ghouls, who aren't too differentiated from each other and all have the same "bones, gore, and mud" aesthetic. I do wish some more classic Lovecraft-type monsters, like the Deep Ones or the original games' zombie chickens, had appeared in some capacity. I also wish the big ♥♥♥♥♥♥ who appears at the end of Hateful Mound and in Emily's 4th chapter had gotten a proper boss fight.Finally, while I'm not too bothered by it, I do wish both routes had conformed with each other more rather than the Resident Evil 2 Remake style "both routes are their own canon" kind of deal. There are elements of the story that fit each route differently - the Dark Man and the Jeremy cutscenes feel much more natural in Emily's campaign, while Edward's route generally fits the slow reveal of the cult and Grace's character better. Part of me wishes the game had gotten more development time to flesh out each route and present them as "two sides of the same story," rather than "the story but with a different character."Overall this is a great survival horror game if you understand its scope and what you're getting into. I would love it more if they 1) patched out the bugs and frustrating graphical stuttering, and 2) lowered the price to a much more reasonable $40.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first entry to the series, so I'm coming in without nostalgia for the earlier entries.This game feels flat, bland, and overall unpolished in a way that really makes me wonder why it has mostly positive reviews at the time of writing.It oozes Resident Evil clone to its very core, though whether it was because of less funding, a smaller team, or a less experienced team, this just feels like a cheap imitation of what it wants to be while selling itself as an equal.This is a full price game, and price tags set expectations. The general animations in this game are bad, at times the facial animations can look like they were animated by Tim and Eric, the environments range from uninspired to okay, the dialogue is mostly uninteresting, David Harbor's performance is lackluster, his character design looks goofy and he just doesn't fit the role in my opinion. Then there's the combat. The combat is easily the worst aspect of this game.Melee weapons just don't feel satisfying to use. It looks and feels like a unity asset flip where you just float the weapon around rather than swinging it. It doesn't have any sort of weight or impact to the hit. Melee weapons also break very quickly, which in most games mean they are a precious commodity and can be used to stun, break a grapple, or overpower an enemy or two until it breaks. Not here though. It gets worse if you don't have one because aiming at something close to you is so imprecise, making it significantly more difficult to hit than something far away. Even while using a gun, it just doesn't feel satisfying. Compared to Resident Evil where it would throw a decent amount of enemies at you, forcing you to make a quick decision of target priority and stunning with head shots, Alone in the Dark only throws 1-3 at you at a time. Shooting enemies does not stagger them and your dodge lets you evade damage and clip straight through enemies. In fact, combat is rarely, if ever, even mandatory,  leaving it pointless to engage with combat at all.. You truly can just skip fights altogether if you want. When a core aspect of the game is given such little care or attention, it proves that this is not a $60 game.There are a whole bunch of puzzles in this game, and they aren't too bad. Some are really easy, some are frustratingly obtuse, but overall okay. If you select to play on "modern" mode rather than classic, the game will give you hints towards puzzles. Some hints are barely any help at all, others will outright tell you what to do if you haven't solved the puzzle in 3 seconds. Even so, these puzzles are not enough to carry this game.I don't recommend even thinking about picking this up for more than $15.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only chapter 2 but it's already clear this is an excellent survival horror game. The mansion, the keys, the collectibles, the music and presentation, it's all very engrossing and far beyond my low expectations. Also happy to report the game runs well on midrange hardware, beyond the shader stutter which is not as bad as I expected. Performance feels very much like the Dead Space remake. UPDATE -I was only an hour or so away from finishing this enjoyable survival horror game when I saw a subject line in the discussions - "NO NEW GAME PLUS OR UNLOCKABLES??" - and after looking into that and confirming it's true, my enjoyment comes to a full stop. Just shocking that a developer making a survival horror game doesn't understand the element of "here's a toy or two for the second playthrough". Why include 2 playable characters if there weren't reasons to replay.There are a lot of issues with the game I was enjoying as worthwhile symptoms of a lower budget game. The story is interesting enough but some dialog requires a lot of suspension of disbelief, the puzzles are hit and miss and the player is prone to getting stuck. These issues go from charming to infuriating with the understanding that the developer did not bother to include a reason to replay the game. They are just annoying flaws now, not fun quirks to be dealt with as you scour for secrets and unlock goofball stuff in a second or third run.I was on my way to give Alone In The Dark a glowing review but now I am frustrated at my own 40 dollar discounted GMG purchase. Absolutely not worth more than 30 dollars. Shocking disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: [Edward|NG|Normal|Old School][Emily|NG+|Old School]+ The story is quite a bit steeped in Lovecraft mythos, just like the original. I thought it was pretty great, but recommend a first playthrough with Emily for a clearer picture, especially if you're not familiar with Lovecraft lore. Other than that, it's an intriguing mystery encased inside an atmospheric 1920s setting with a gorgeous aesthetic and a great mood and feel. It's mainly what carries the game in spite of some of its flaws. It has some jumpscares here and there, but I wouldn't call it scary overall. It relies on its eerie mood and atmosphere much more than on outright scaring you directly.+ The environments are gorgeous, both Jeremy's memories and the Derceto mansion itself, and the lighting is often stunning. Congrats to the lighting artists for sure, great stuff! The game showcases pretty great usage of Unreal Engine overall, especially for a AA game and talking strictly about the visuals; performance is another matter entirely >.<+ I thought the voice acting was excellent across the board, all fitting with the 1920s era and helping create convincing, mysterious characters.+ Puzzles were pretty great, well balanced in difficulty (at least for me), never frustrating but almost always satisfying to solve.+ I kind of like the decision to not be able to pick up throwable items (bricks, molotov cocktails). It forces you to pay attention to your surroundings, keep their locations in mind and have some spatial awareness of where you need to move to gain an advantage on the enemies. It adds a very slight tactical element to the otherwise generic combat that I appreciated.+ The gunplay is serviceable, guns have decent kick and feel good to use and aiming is snappy.- Melee on the other hand is very janky. There's no impact to your hits, so sometimes it's not even clear if your hit actually connected and the animation work involved really doesn't sell the action.- The final boss has some pretty awkward movement and animations as well. Again, the key word seems to be janky.- Some bugs were encountered in my two playthroughs, small visual issues and the main character getting stuck in collisions occasionally (only once with a reload required). Nothing game-breaking though, and no crashes.- Performance-wise, the game is a stuttering mess. It stuttered constantly across two playthroughs, on sudden camera movements, traversal, and transitions to cut-scenes. It's very likely not only PSO related and, with Unreal being used, it can be quite a number of things, but it's definitely frustrating and negatively impacts the experience (and ruins a jumpscare or two). I'm pretty tolerant to poor performance, for me it did not render the game unplayable, but I could understand how it would for others.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad per say, but it has serious flaws that made me decide not to finish it. Its worse flaw is that it performs absolutely awful. It was literally unplayable for me at launch due to the frequent stuttering, and it's still bad even after the patch. So much so that, when I shoot an enemy, the game freezes because it can't render that basic blood effect apparently (lmao). I can't aim because of the lag, cutscenes are frequently broken, and sometimes my character just disintegrates the fabric of reality. In addition to this, the combat is awful. The revolver Edward gets is so weak that it is practically unviable (I didn't play as Emily, so I don't know if she gets something different), melee is awkward with your character moving with every swing in a way that is sporadic and impossible to control (leading to you circling an enemy rather than hitting it),  and enemies can and will stunlock you in a corner where even dodging won't really get you out. The game genuinely made me sick to play, which is not something any game has ever done to me before. I think it was the bizarre effects the game has, down to subtly moving the camera when zoomed in to a puzzle. Turning off most of those effects allowed me to play the game without getting nauseous, and it may be some sort of problem unique to me. Regardless, I still want to warn any future players about this.The game is very overpriced. It should cost at most 40 USD, but instead the game is as expensive as a AAA game. Get it on sale if at all. Would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The short review:A third person adventure set in the jazz filled streets of 1920's Louisiana, that combines voodoo with the cosmic entities of HP Lovecraft. Mixing melee and shooting with survival horror, exploration and puzzle solving. Passable fun, but so, so, soooo "mid" in every regard bar the quality of its story-telling which is weirdly compelling. And even then it is just more Lovecraftian stuff at a time when Lovecraft is overused and dull. I don't regret my time playing it, but on the other hand there's nothing here that hasn't been done better elsewhere.The long review: Alone In the Dark was one of the earliest examples of survival horror, if not the first to be fully 3d and so give even more tension to the player through that level of immersion. It was one of the inspirations behind the creation of Resident Evil, and ever since that has been its cross to bare. It may have created the genre, or propelled it into gamers awareness. but here is a young upstart that just supercharged those expectations, and then did so again in a different way with Resi 4. From there the likes of The Evil Within and Dead Space took a look at what Resi did, and then said "hold my beer" before super-duper-supercharging the genre.Along the way a barely known game was made called Silent Hill, followed by a hardly remembered sequel of low quality, and bam! Suddenly AITD with its Lovecraftian horror was, like its inspiration, old-hat. In 2008 the series was reborn with the same name, but with a markedly different setting and approach to the horror genre. Personally I think its a very brave (though ultimately a bit wonky) attempt at innovation, and still is, to my mind, the most ambitious AAA horror ever released. Which was a very long-winded way of getting around to this remake, and the slightly disappointing end result when compared to competitors in the genre, or its previous entries that share the same name and legacy.The basis for this 2024 remake / re-imagining is sound;  as a template the mix of combat, exploration and puzzling is as tried and true as ever. Every single one of those horror contemporaries did exactly the same thing. The problem for AITD is that they did it better.What are you hoping for from this game? It's a third-person adventure with melee combat and shooting. The melee and dodging is basic, and weapons break quite quickly. For all its flaws Callisto Protocol did this with a smoother flow to the action, and whilst its technically reasonably sound, at a design level this is no more sophisticated than the playstation 1 days of standing there mindlessly whacking enemies. Do you like shotguns in horror games? I'm sure you do, you know, those shotguns where they obliterate parts of the enemy in a shower of gore and feel super-satisfying to shoot because of that very thing. Well....the shotgun here is sh*t, and the only reason that isn't really disappointing is the fact they eventually give you a tommy gun and that is a beast.Overall the shooting is okay, but nowhere near the slickness or intensity of Dead Space and Resi 4 Remake. Its fun, yet objectively its nowhere near as much fun as them. The narrative and reality-warping set-pieces afforded by cosmic horror are doing a lot of the heavy-lifting here, rather than in the game-play department which is fairly average.Stealth isn't something this game does, even when it does. Its basic and generally so short and easy as to be mere padding. The same can be said for the one vaguely memorable chase sequence that occurs. Again, these are nowhere near other games for intensity or execution, and sadly being pant-sh*tt*ngly terrifying just isn't something the game ever manages.Fun? yes. Weirdly intriguing due to its dreamy story-telling and odd plot? yes. Scary? nope. Thrilling?....??...I guess at around the half-way  point it picks up in intensity, but.....er...noooooo.To me it was a game I mostly enjoyed, yet could never shake off the nagging thought it could have been so much better. A pulse-pounding stealth sequence here (of proper merit, rather than the cheap efforts provided) and  a heart-attack inducing chase sequence there (like Cthulu Dark Corners Of The Earth did around 20 years ago!!!!), and this could have been amazing.Could have, would have, should have, but....uh...didn't. In the end this is a fairly safe reboot, and one that will probably be more appreciated by those unfamiliar with the games it shares its name with. Whilst this is obviously much better technically than the 2008 release, I am 100% sure that precisely none of it will stand out in my memory in years to come the way that games does. I don't want to be too down on it, as I am quite jaded and experienced in many years of horror games, but even now a mere few hours after finishing it I struggled to think of what I could highlight in this review. It's not bad and its slightly better than average (compared to, say, The Suffering or Cold Fear), but a great action game it is not, and it isn't scary or frantic either. Your mileage may vary of course, but even as a genre newbie I can't see this being frightening unless you have a very weak disposition. All that remains is whether the story grabs you, and to be fair that is its strongest element.

_childDocuments_.review: As a developer of another Lovecraftian game, I would say that this is a perfect Survival Horror game (not an Action Horror like many modern games). It involves exploration, puzzle-solving, and survival. The combat isn't perfect, but it's adequate for the genre. The Lovecraftian elements and story are well-executed. Overall, it feels like a return to the roots. Remember, the very first Alone in the Dark (3D) was an inspiration for the Resident Evil series. So, in a way, the cycle has now come full circle. Please also keep in mind that developers have deadlines tied to funding and contracts with publishers. They've done their best to deliver a good product, but it appears there's still a need for optimization and additional QA. Hopefully, Pieces Interactive will fine-tune this, and the game will garner enough sales to become a classic in future. Let's stay positive, as games like these are hard to come by these days.

_childDocuments_.review: It's refreshing to play a title clearly made with love, with respect for the IP it's based on, that comes to you complete with no microtransactions and no in-game store. This is a really fun survival horror game with good writing, great voice acting, and a balance of humor, horror, and fun. It's not a perfect game by any stretch, but it's been a while since I played a single player game that felt as well-paced. Personally, I wish the puzzles had been a bit harder, but I saw some critic reviews saying they were too hard, so I suppose that means they're in a pretty good spot. There's some jank when interacting with the environment, and combat isn't smooth (but that's a survival horror tradition at this point). The game is perhaps a bit pricey for what you get, but still worth a buy now if you love the genre/David Harbour/Jodie Comer. If you don't, once it's on discount it'll 100% be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all releasing this on the same day as Dragon's Dogma 2 and the HZD: Forbidden West PC port while charging 60$ for it is crazy. Makes me think that people in charge of selling, marketing and distributing this game are not qualified for their jobs.With the above out of the way, tldr: Janky lovecraftian "Resident Evil" with less combat and more emphasis on puzzles and story. Just in case you don't know the original AitD come out before RE1 and kinda inspired the whole survival horror genre. - Environments and architecture are pretty great. Post-WW1 art deco aesthetic never fails to be beautiful, the places you visit have a lot of detail and flavor. - Voice acting is good to great. Lots of charming old timey accents. Every written note is voice acted too and even with different voices depending on the author. - Facial animations are the worst aspect of the game's visuals, stiff faces, dead eyes. They are bad even by janky mid-budget game standards which is a shame in such an otherwise moody and atmospheric game. Ironically NPCs seem to have better facial animations than the two playable characters.- Jazzy night club lounge music is very enjoyable and fits the game's aesthetic well. The horror related sound layer is pretty good too, there's almost always something clicking, scurrying and tapping around you during the horror segments, pretty unnerving with headphones. - Story is a fairly standard lovecraftian affair but it's well written and the characters are compelling, creepy and fun even if you don't get to know them that well. The game relies more on atmosphere and tension than gore. - Combat is....fine. Handgun, shotgun and tommygun, what else you do you need, right? There's a flare gun too but it comes late and is barely used. If you play on hard you might need to rely on the environment (throwable objects and such) and melee more or just run past some enemies. There's a dodge move that's pretty spammable and makes it relatively easy to avoid damage. You should get AitD2024 if you: like 1920s southern US decor and mannerisms, like Lovecraft, like puzzles and moody atmospheric experiences. You should avoid AitD2024 if you: hate puzzles, need a high variety of weapons and enemy types, can't stand janky gameplay or animations. AitD is enjoyable but its gameplay systems and produciton value are too thin for 60$, I really think THQ shot themselves (and more importantly the devs) in the knee with the pricing. I mean Resident Evil 4 costs 40$ for ♥♥♥♥'s sake.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with Alone in the Dark, despite having very low expectations due to lukewarm critical reception. Having played through it twice I can say that the reviews were quite unfair, since many compared it to the Resident Evil remakes, which had much bigger budgets and were overall very different games.My favorite thing about Alone in the Dark is its atmosphere and setting. It goes for this jazzy, noir movie feel and pulls it off perfectly. Its not particulary scary, but it did succed in building tension and unease, that reaches a very satisfying climax at the finale.Main marketing point was of course the leading duo with David Harbour as detective Edward Carnby and Jodie Comer as Emily Hartwood, which I considered a waste of budget before game release, but I must admit that their performance greatly adds to the experience. Unfortunately the other characters are a bit underwhelming in comparison as they are not as well rendered and their actors can't match performance of the main characters.I played entire game twice, back to back with both characters to see the differences between the playthroughs. Gameplay differences are minor and each character gets only one, about an hour long sequence unique to them, but the cutscenes and the story perspective are very different. I really enjoyed that, but I wish the gameplay differences were more substantial and if I had to choose, I'd prefer one playable character in a longer game instead.Gameplay wise its pretty standard third person horror with over the shoulder perspective. Moving around feels good, but sneaking and combat are pretty janky. I found stealth to be nearly useless throughout the game as its way too slow and combat animations often got in the way of gameplay, with some weird hitboxes and both me and enemies getting stuck in environment. It didn't happen too often, but it was pretty jarring when it did. Actual shooting feels good and punchy, with strong recoil, which discourages going full auto and makes you consider every shot. Melee on the other hand is just plain bad, with its stiff animations and weird delay between hits. I played on Hard which made enemies more resilient and resources very limited, amplifying the survival aspect in this survival horror.Outside of combat you'll be exploring very nicely rendered and diverse areas, with many puzzles to solve along the way. I did not expect the kind of location variety this game threw at me and I suggest avoiding any spoilers, its really worth experiencing yourself. Puzzles mostly consist of jigsaw puzzles, deciphering codes and finding numbers in environments. They weren't too hard, but I found them satisfying and nice change of pace.Overall I highly recommend Alone in the Dark to any survival horror fan out there. Its criminal that this game didn't get the acclaim it deserved. Sure, its a bit janky and short, but it more than makes up for it with great amosphere, story and level design. Unfortunately Pieces Interactive, the studio making this game is no more, since Alone in the Dark failed to meet sales expectations of the publisher. This is a sad reality of game development, where solid, niche games like this get overshadowed by money making, soulless abominations like First Descendant or Once Human.

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre project that relies on a once-glorious title from the past, back when computer games were crafted by teams of creative geniuses. Overall, this project retains nothing from the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: When you consider how every sequel and reboot of the 1992 classic Alone in the Dark has only been passable at best, it is a thrill to finally have a game that does one the originators of the survival horror genre justice.The story and characters remain engaging throughout, with plenty of great vocal performances throughout, and the remade Derceto (and the other locations you visit) look great. There's also some brilliant period-appropriate music throughout, while the combat is... serviceable, though not a big focus of the game.If I have complaints, I'd say that it's a shame Carnby's and Hartwood's campaigns are almost identical. There are differences in cutscenes and part of chapter 4 plays out differently depending on who you play as, but for the most part the two protagonists tread the same path. Just a minor complaint, as that was also the case in the original and a lot of games that followed in its wake, but it's still slightly disappointing that there isn't more difference between the two.A bigger complaint is the price, which I think is too high for a game that is pretty short and I would consider mid-range. Mind you, with Triple-A games now costing over sixty quid these days, the £45 mark is probably the kind of price we can expect from middle-tier games these days.Still, if you're a fan of survival horror, or you're a fan of Alone in the Dark who's been burned by previous entries, this return to Lovecraftian form is absolutely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: To the point================A criminally overpriced mediocre revival of a beloved horror franchise. Get it on a deep sale or not at all.+ cleared on hard difficulty +Good Stuff==================- Dercetto is a great setting for the game, I really did enjoy exploring it and it game me strong Eternal Darkness and RE7 vibes. It's a shame that they didn't make it a little more 'funhouse' like with secret passages etc. The dreamland environs are also really great looking and atmospheric but they're just too small with one of them being a proverbial straight line.- The soundtrack is very authentic, if not poorly paced. The Jazzy tracks for the cast is very fitting but they have the habit of coming on at very weird times. Like right after spitting in Cthulhu's eye probably isn't the best time for an upbeat mardi gras style song.- I know it's a collect-a-thon but I did like the Lanappe and finding them throughout the environs. The first set you unlock gets you a powerful gun so I was hoping each would give you something neat but 90% of them are just dumb text blurbs, I mean at least give us some upgrades or something.Bad Stuff===================- I know Embracer group will never read this but how on God's green earth do you greedy slimebags get off charging $60 for this game?! I could name a handful of indie survival horrors with more love and attention to detail in the first 30 minutes then this title has in its entire run time. I guess it doesn't matter since you shuttered the studio immediately after the release of this game but you are the sickness killing gaming- The story is truly awful, when looking at an A and B scenario like Resident Evil 2, you can at least say with certainty that while you don't have all the answers after playing a single scenario, that you were compelled to at least try the other. No such drive here, the story barely has time to breathe jumping from one dull and predictable moment to the next which is a shame because I actually liked most of the characters, but everything's is so rushed and jumbled. Why did anything even happen in this story? Who knows or cares?- The combat, at least on hard, is completely terrible. Enemies are bullet and melee sponges and react to your attacks like a brick wall. They also make no sense damage wise as the early enemies take around 5-6 bullets to kill but these small crawler enemies in the end game take 7 or more.- There is a stealth mechanic that teeters between 'completely useless' with you being spotted immediately or 'super broken' walking in front of idling enemies without them even reacting.- The enemy variety is not great. There are roughly 4 humanoid and 2 bug enemies that all move and attack in bear identical fashion. Also having them completely in plain sight near constantly kind of removes any feeling of fear or dread.- The bosses, again on the hard difficulty, seem near unbeatable. I was throwing bricks at the final boss after running out of bullets early. They have obvious weak points but attacking them doesn't seem to do a whole lot more then attacking them normally.-There are just a ton of janky bugs in this game, enemies will sort of slip and slide around while trying to find you, sometimes melee attacks will clip you into walls or, when running from something, you'll run on top of an invisible obstacle and get stuck until the physics engine pushes you off.- This one is particularly brutal : The character movement. You character is painfully slow making exploring the various environs a chore, even worse when trying to evade enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm surprised to see the steam reviews are only mostly positive. I'm going to try to review the game not as a reaction to disagreement, but on its own. I played the game on hard, switching to standard midway through; and played on the "old school" puzzle style. Overall, I really enjoyed the game. It takes inspiration from Resident Evil in exploration and a bit of The Last of Us in combat. The puzzles are solid and very solveable, I only had one that I got caught up on and I did not need to look anything up. The sound design and the lighting were absolutely immaculate. Seriously, the sound design is a huge highlight. Actors did a great job. 99% of all animations were fluid and great. Story was very interesting, lovecraftian spoiler stuff also super cool. . From what I can tell, there are multiple endings and different things for which main character you play, so I'll definitely be doing at least one or two more play-throughs.Below I have some criticisms, but anything not mentioned was pretty great!Bugs: I only encountered minor 2 bugs in the entire game: Water making flashlight light wonky, and getting stuck on some geometry (quickly resolved by messing around or reloading from a rapidly set autosave). Performance was steady and high throughout on maximum settings, but I have a very good PC. PC Portage: Some of the default buttons are weird, and it was a little confusing to figure out what button to heal and switch weapons was at first, since its shown with a D-padCombat: It isn't the focus, but plays an important role to prevent the player from feeling comfortable. It completes that role well, but the combat is a bit lackluster-  the melee combat in particular. I also wish that you could hold a throwable without having to hold Q and move at a snails pace. That said, I found  very satisfying, intense, and generally really cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in the 90´s, Alone 1 and 2 were one of my favorite games. The mechanics were new, intriguing, and the atmosphere was unique! Even with the 3rd game, although the setting wasn't my favorite. But by 2008, I felt it had lost what made the game so appealing. The modern take made it, paradoxically, more like games that were inspired by the first 2 or 3 Alone in the Dark games.All that to say, I am a nostalgic fan of the saga just exited by this game existing.Now after playing it, so far... although I don't have the latest gamer PC, I can play with settings in high mostly, and it runs pretty good. Had to make some minor changes while playing to make things go smoother, but nothing too drastic.My favorite part is that the 1920/1930 atmosphere is back! The attention to detail, and the love for the original games really shows. Also a big fan of David Harbour so that added a bit extra to make this game one of the best remakes I have played... so far.As a nostalgic fan I have to say I am very pleased.

_childDocuments_.review: WE WANT A REMAKE OF THE ORIGINAL - NOT THIS!!OMG... What in hell did you do to one of my favourite games from my childhood!! I played this game the year it release in 1992 and recently replayed it. Still an amazing game with era appropriate levels of jank.THIS "re-imagining" is NOT Alone in the Dark. All they had to do was to make a Resident Evil style remake of the original and expand and improve where needed and you would have had the beginning of a bright future for this franchise - after all, this game quite literally inspired Resident Evil...PROS:- Beautiful Graphics- Jodie Comer made a good EmilyCONS:- NOTHING in this game is remotely scary or provokes even a slight sense of tension or unease- The plot and story were absolutely terrible and made no sense- The entire game should have been set during the night. Light does not = scary...- Decerto kinda looks like Decerto. But not faithful enough to the original- David Harbour is NOT a good choice to play Edward Carnby (where was the moustache!)- Shooting is passable. But melee is atrociously bad...- Throwable implementation was horrible- Enemies were laughably unscary. They didn't even make sense within the story!- Soundtrack missed the mark. Jazz?? In a horror game? Seriously???- Large portion of the game not even set within Decerto. Other dimensional travel WTAF??- Having Decerto as a lived in space instead of a deserted and haunted space was the biggest mistake here. Decerto was supposed to make you feel trapped and Alone in the Dark. Not hanging out with folks for dialogue that never helps develop the plot in any kind of way!I could not even finish this game. Its like Bloober games got their hands on it. So now its all supernatural themes with rooms changing around with a completely nonsensical plot.I am so damn sad that this is where this franchise finally landed. PLEASE someone just remake the original "FAITHFULLY!!!". And in case you wonder what that looks like... HERE:- A Resident Evil style Lovecraftian inspired survival horror experience- Decerto is a COMPLETELY deserted, decrepit, old, evil and horror filled mansion- A story based on the occultist pirate Captain Ezechiel Pregzt who's spirit still haunts the house in search of a new body: namely yours...- 2 Characters only - Edward & Emily.- Arriving at dusk, you become trapped within the mansion! As night closes in you have to find a way to defeat the evil or die Alone in the Dark...- Set the game ONLY during the night.- Puzzle solving and door keys to find of course!- Now use modern graphical technology with ray tracing and make this a gloomy, scary and horror filled experience where Decerto resembles a house that should be condemned. And fill it with scary as hell monsters including the undead crew of Captain Pregzt who still serve their Captain.THAT'S HOW YOU DO ALONE IN THE DARK "THE REMAKE"
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: While the game might not be as polished as Capcom's RE Remake series, from what I've played so far it's been fun. It apparent that they've taken heavy influence from the Resident Evil Remake games,But saying that the original Resident Evil game took heavy influences from Alone in the Dark. The gameplay is very similar to the mentioned Resident Evil games, so if you're a fan of that you'll feel at home with this. This game does take a more investigative approach as to how to solve the puzzleswhere you need to read some of the notes lying around to gather enough informationto form a conclusion to a solution. The game definitely has a more 'Noire' feeling as well. So it doesn't take place just in the mansion. As the story unravels you'll visit different placesbased off of the "memories" of your uncle via a talisman, as he's being potentially possessed by a 'Dark Man' which you'll read know more about throughout the game. And those areas are essentially 'twisted' memories of places that he remembers, but somehow the people he knows appear in those places too, being *Alone in the dark* with otherworldly monsters.The game can be spooky, the audio design's pretty good and the surround sound is nothing to complain about either. A short and sweet review, it's a recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: We should be praising this game. No it isn't perfect and it's not for everyone. HOWEVER!! This is a complete singleplayer game in the day and age where games are never complete. It is a fun and interesting story from start to finish. The gameplay can seem sluggish but it works for what it is and it is nothing more than it is advertised. A genuinely fun game made with love.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my second playthrough with the other character. Overall, the game is good and I personally like the story a lot, even though I still don't understand some of the details.Combat is a bit wonky but good enough to get through. For reference, it is a little bitter than sinking city and not as good as the RE remakes. Paying full price for this game is too much but in my opinion, a $40 or less price would fair for it. First run took me around 7-7.5 hrs and second one took me 5 hrs. Both playthrough were nearly identical in terms of locations with different dialogue so that is a bit disappointing.  Game needed a bit more explanation of the lore and the details in there in my opinion. Sounds design is real good and I really like the sounds as you move throughout the house. Also, menu theme is a new favorite of mine, makes you wanna hear it with a fedora and a trenchcoat.Overall, considering the price point, I give the game a 7/10. Can be an 8/10 with a lower price point. It doesn't break new grounds and it is not amazing but it is good enough for a fun run with an interesting story. If you know your lovecraftian games, you might like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: It really drives that old school survival horror adventure gameplay, with a reality-bending story. It will depend if you enjoy that type of gameplay, yet it stays true to it. Quality story and characters. Explore, investigate and find objects. There's both ranged and melee combat. It's not scary horror, but more an investigating thriller. It brings back an old game to modern standards. I don't have any performance issues with it myself and can run it smoothly at 4K HDR with 120 FPS (Epic settings) when using DLSS (Quality). I have V-SYNC disabled, but am using a G-SYNC monitor. Some people complain about stuttering however on different PC specs, so check your hardware and use the latest graphic card drivers. There was also a patch released right after the game first launched, so update it.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished Carnbys side of the story my verdict is mixed, it's a solid modern survival horror game, however i feel that the game missed several aspects of the original series that made it so unique. This game does not feature any traps like you would run into in the classic games, the varied and unique enemy design has also been foregone for more generic monsters. (RIP to the ballroom ghosts and animated armor displays, they will not be in the game)In the very least they retained the melee system with breakable weapons and plenty variety to choose from.Most of the puzzles i found to be well designed apart from 1 that had me stumped for a little while (It's the warehouse safe, if you know you know)When it comes to the environments they are beautifully crafted and truly a feat to behold, however i also at the same time feel it doesn't quite evoke the same mood as the classic games do, but perhaps that's just not possible with the graphics used. The caves under Derceto are for example not used in this game.I will also make a short note regarding the use of celebrity actors for the main characters, i find that it somewhat detracts from the experience as i can only see the actors and not the character they're supposed to embody, i also wish they had used carnbys classic look redheaded with moustache and all.All in all i do still recommend this game if you enjoy survival horror, but do bear in mind that the "horror" part in survival horror is rather weak in this game, and it is what i would consider rather loosely based on the source material and retains mostly the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a truly impressive reboot, while also remaining faithful to the groundbreaking original. I honestly feel it isn't getting the credit and player-base it deserves.Alone in the Dark follows Edward Carnby and Emily Hartwood as they ominously arrive at Decerto in search of Emily's missing uncle; tell tale signs of dark curse linger over the Hartwood family. The story kept me intrigued throughout; clues such as letters or diaries flesh out the lore, while also being voice acted too. Puzzles and lagniappes further clue the player in on this world but never directly illustrate just what on earth is going on, which keeps the suspense alive. Just like the original, Lovecraftian themes are woven throughout.Now we have talked about the story, what about the graphical might that brings this world to life?I must start off by stating just how well modelled the Decerto mansion is, it oozes atmosphere and I had great fun exploring it. Subtle jazz music plays at points, while each and every room feels believable, it seeps that 1920's/30's Great Depression style. The mansion isn't the only place you will be exploring however, I won't spoil it, but it perfectly varies up the pace and adds variety. In terms of character models, David Harbour and Jodie Comer have been mo-capped in their respective roles; they both look great, unfortunately, it is where the other character models fall down as they definitely do not look as good as the two main protagonists. However, this did not sully my enjoyment because everything else looks honestly top tier.Gameplay wise, you will be solving puzzles with combat sprinkled here and there, where as this ramps up in later chapters. Combat is fine albeit nothing groundbreaking, my main enjoyment of Alone in the Dark came from its narrative and puzzle solving. The length of the game is around 20 hours for absolute full completion, in my personal opinion I have feel I have got my worth but this my vary individually of course.My final verdict is that Pieces Interactive have done a damn fine job and I hope they get to make a sequel and continue the franchise, sales makes games now but Pieces have proven they are passionate about Alone in the Dark.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a very solid game and I enjoyed the experience throughout. Though I never expected it to set the world on fire so to speak (and it doesn't) what we have here is an incredibly faithful, true reimagining of the 1992 classic. Those who have played that game before will clearly see the intricate ways how scenes from the original game have been taken apart and put together in new and exciting ways. It has atmosphere, it has charm, it has quality. It's all very Lovecraftian in the best of ways. As far as downsides go, there is really just the one. The combat really is quite bad. Luckily, for about 95% the game knows where it's strengths lie and uses combat very sparingly and at just the right moments. The only really bad thing about the game is the ending encounter. It is so frustratingly difficult due to the restraints the combat puts on you that it can get increasingly tedious and results in the fun getting sucked right out. I had to resort to changing the difficulty to easy just to stop me from haven an increasingly bad experience. Of course this immediately resulted in the encounter being such a cakewalk I could practically finish it with my eyes closed. Seems like a balancing issue. So, not a good way to end your game, even though the story round up is quite satisfactory.Overall though? It's good. Pick it up if you like survival horror, Lovecraftian adventures and early 20th century sleuthing.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I will echo another reviewer and say how awful it is that all involved in making this game will have no chance to ever improve on it further. There is so much greatness here that just needs some refinement.Back when this released, I was smart enough to watch a gameplay video and was instantly hooked. In my younger years I was an adventure gamer - easily spooked and slow to react, but fascinated with the creepy, the mysterious, the atmospheric. AITD, in all its disturbing and slow-moving glory, appeals to both my younger self and who I am today. I love nothing more than uncovering a story buried in history's annals.Each environment is crafted with so much care and love, right down to the period-accurate push-button light switches. Even with very little to find, the rooms and larger locations give off something so complete that it doesn't feel especially disappointing when you unearth nothing more than a box of 3 shotgun shells. After all, you're in another world, and you don't simply pick up and pocket everything in real life, right?I enjoyed all actors' performances, though I will say that the dialogue could sound extremely anachronistic at times (more on the anachronisms later). Much has been said of the high-profile actors and motion capture being ultimately wasteful - and this may be true - but it contributed something especially absorbing to the cast.On the topic of much being said, I've also seen a lot of theorizing, wondering, and general confusion around the story. To me, that's the perfect sweet spot for a mystery/horror game. I would be disappointed if I were looking to find out who killed Mr Ratchet on the Orient Express, but - we're in a world where nothing makes sense, on purpose. I was so thrilled and fascinated to ponder the little details and obscure facts that I learned; it only made me wish there were more. While I didn't buy the Director's Commentary DLC, I may well do so in the hopes of learning even more.My only real issue here, wrapped as it is around all this amazing experience, is with the combat. On easy mode it's bearable - two or three shots to kill most enemies, and they stand around kind of swaying for a few seconds to give you plenty of time. On New Game+, which I tried for about half an hour, it takes seven shots for a basic enemy; you find boxes with only one bullet in them; a melee weapon will break after killing only ONE basic enemy; the amount of enemies and their speed are increased; and all of this is only emphasized by the awkwardness of movement and the way the hit animations will keep you in some kind of stun lock, unable to aim and sometimes getting stuck on the enemy instead of fleeing. Very quickly I found myself wondering how I should even deal with it - stealth was obviously supposed to take precedence, but what do you do when you have one bullet left and three enemies just burst out at you? The answer is, go back to easy mode.More minor, but just as important for me, are the anachronisms dotted throughout the game. They're mostly in the dialogue, not necessarily in the word choices but just the way characters phrase their thoughts and choose to speak. I wasn't expecting an actual 1930-accurate experience, Mid-Atlantic accent and all, but it was strange to see how well-done the written materials were in comparison to the spoken word. On some occasions, the dialogue even felt vaguely disconnected from itself - I think that may have been on purpose, though, given the themes; the more you go along, the more you feel that everyone else is living in a different world than yours.And also...the music. Striking as it is, evocative as it is, it did not mesh properly with the world of the game. I'm speaking specifically of the "film noir" jazz sprinkled throughout. That style simply did not exist in 1930 (plus, there are so many old records from the 1920s that could have been used for diagetic music instead of random classical pieces). If I may digress:In general, I've found that the 1920s through 1955 or so are compressed by the public consciousness into flappers, fedoras/trilbys, a couple of gangsters saying "see?", Marilyn Monroe, Frank Sinatra, some Casablanca, and WWII-era things like Rosie the Riveter and maybe some pin-up photos. The issue is that all of those icons had their own time, their own era of sorts - flappers in the 20s, that portrayal of gangsters in the early 30s, Marilyn in the early 50s, and so on. Squashing it all together is how we get Henry Mancini scoring a game set in 1930.So: for someone who doesn't know the details of those periods, it's a game with old-fashioned technology, co-starring a detective in an old-fashioned hat, and featuring some cool jazz music because that's what old-fashioned detective movies play. And if you enjoyed it for that reason, then I'm glad - I just turned off the music and had fun playing some of my own. (Plenty of old late 20s records have been digitized, so it's easy to pick songs that don't sound like they'd be in The Shining.)I was lucky enough to not encounter any major glitches, even on my older hardware (on which it runs very well with mostly medium settings and the blessing that is the Pre-Load Shaders setting turned on). There was some stuttering, which I understand is an issue for many players, but it didn't render anything unplayable.Ultimately I was totally captivated by this game, and even without New Game+ I remain so. If you are willing to look past some quirkiness - and maybe even put more effort into the combat than myself - to get a strange, vaguely disturbing and sometimes very thought-provoking experience, then I highly recommend it. Thanks to everyone who worked at Pieces Interactive for putting their hearts into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal story, written by the same writer as Soma, an absolute love letter to the original games, has some great references to the original games. This is not a full survival horror so don't expect some form of deep inventory management, its considerably more on the slow burn side with plenty of complex puzzles that require deep thinking, some are more nonsensical but they are 100% solvable if you pay close attention to the details between the lines.Combat may seem more on the clunky side if you focus too much on the comparisons between Resident Evil 4, You are not Leon S Kennedy, you are Detective Carnby or Emily Hartwood, You don't roundhouse kick zombies and parry chainsaws you fight with the same technique as anyone would just wildly swinging a pipe
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is an enjoyable horror title, notable for its smooth mechanics, interesting setting, and curious mood. While the gameplay won't be surprising to anyone who has played Resident Evil 2, the gameplay consists of a combination of exploring moody mostly-linear environments and puzzling around an ever-changing mansion. There is combat that is shallow, but never annoying, and the focus on a limited selection of melee and ranged options adds tension effectively.The standout feature is the atmosphere and tone of the game, which renders Louisiana of the the early 1900s in a wonderfully swampy fog. The music and writing combine to create a languid feeling of unease, and yet there are moments that are slyly funny, too. Overall, I recommend Alone in the Dark. The experience is more subdued than Resident Evil, which I compared it to earlier, but that difference is not without its charms.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ... ok. That's it. I often heared about it that it is the best Alone in the Dark Game since the very first one.I got to say I haven't played any AitD game before this one, but if this game is the best since then, then go_d damn the series must be bad.So what are my problems with the game:-the game is like never scary, not even close-the story is a confusing mess-combat really isn't great, quite clunky, especially melee-technical problems:   -performance is very unstable, stuttering is quite common   -sound issues-it's barely a survival horror game, you could even argue it's not even a true one which is kinda funny when people often say the og game was the very first survival horror game. So why isn't it really a survival horror game:there is no limited inventory at all; ressources aren't scarce at all; the game does that stupid thing that if you are out of ressources it then gives you so much ressources, but if you are already decently equiped it gives you nothing or almost nothing which means the game rewards bad players and punishs good ones; combat is quite rare (which is probably a good thing considering the mediore combat system), you are basically just doing puzzles after puzzles, there are way too many of themOverall this game is probably a 6 or 7 out of 10 (at best). I wasn't sure if I should recommend it or not. It's something between medicore and all right.Either way this game is not worth 60 bucks, in fact I don't think you should buy it until it gets a 75% sale.

Tricky and enjoyable puzzles, basic but effective combat with sporadic enemy encounters. Map exploration is a blast, characters are top-notch, and the soundtrack is a gem. _childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Love it. Old-school handmade (semi-realistic, but it shows it's handmade and not photogrammetry) graphics, well acted voiceovers, good animations. Great Weird Tales style Lovecraftian atmosphere. Puzzles are easy, so you don't get stuck on them all the time. It's exactly like I like it, an adventure game.It's not a puzzle game, and not a shooter, so if you were hoping for something like RE4 meets Mist, then it is simply not that. It is more like a walking sim where you have to shoot an occasional monster or do a very simple jigsaw-puzzle.As for bugs - got stuck in geometry one time. Thankfully the games autosaves like every 10 meters, so no biggie.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, there is no incredible variety regarding the enemies and there are really few boss fights, but the visuals are great, the puzzles are neat and the story is really intriguing. For me the game was at its strongest when it started shifting between dimensions, leaving me with this major puzzle: trying to piece together what is happening in this place. I for one had a great, yet admittedly short, time with this. Definitely would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game. It's modeled off the remakes of RE2+3 (which those originals were modeling off of AITD, a cool twist). The combat feels good and punchy, but ultimately the enemies aren't very scary and neither is much of anything in the game. Loading screens are minimal. The game does suffer from the occasional stutter. Going through doors when you are trying to backtrack is, sigh, slow - they really should let you barge through doors like in the RE-makes. Also, it feels like there are still a couple of bugs with the map/collections that are annoying, as it is very easy to find yourself locked out of a collectible because it wasn't clear it was required to be collected at a certain point. Then in future chapters, some doors are arbitrarily locked for no other reason than, literally, who knows, so the rooms with remaining items are still inaccessible but very much obvious from your map.But, this game shines with the puzzles. They should have never included a directed mode, as it basically solves every puzzle for you, making the greatest bit of content in the game simply bypassed for the sake of appealing to a wider audience. It is best to just play unassisted, and enjoy the beautiful environments, solve puzzles, and be happy that you finally get to play as Jodie Comer (David Harbour too, I guess...)!I would love to see a sequel with these 2 characters in it!
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks pretty good, both graphics and design, and the sounds and music are very well done as well, but that's it. Way too many problems bring this down to no recommendation level as far as horror is concerned.The story's not very interesting. The way it's told, the premise and the setting somewhat are, but it's really just your standard Lovecraft plot, to keep it spoilerfree. There's a bunch of characters that get introduced and seem interesting at first, but then you barely ever meet them and they end up being mostly irrelevant. It's also kind of sad they apparently blew a lot of budget on two Hollywood actors for the protagonists and then don't give them much to work with. For instance, at no point during the game do they give the impression they think they are in danger or at least somewhat scared. Mild surprise from time to time is the height of emotional reaction you'll see.Which brings us to the main problem with this game: it's simply not scary. It's not missing it by much, because the game is moody and well presented, but it's still missing the mark. Big issue for me was that during your exploration of the mansion, you're never really in danger and you know it. Sure, there are one or two instances in which realities overlap for a short moment, but it's not enough to make you feel unsafe. What the game does instead is that you get teleported to rather linear combat levels somewhere else at fixed moments in the story, but unfortunately, the combat is so poorly done that it's more annoying than intimmidating. What little horror the game manages to build up flies out of the window the moment you need to lift your weapon against a monster for the first time. Those looking rather goofy, doesn't help much, either.The other main aspect of the gameplay are the puzzles. While the puzzle density is adequate, the puzzles themselves never go beyond the type of generic videogame puzzles you've solved a ton of before. In addition to that, the protagonists tell you how to solve them without asking or warning, even with puzzle help turned off in the options.So overall, this game is one missed opportunity after another. It has it's heart in the right place, but never lives up to its potential. You could have an entertaining time with it regardless and enjoy the atmosphere, but the actual game is mediocre at best and especially as a horror game, it is a failure.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Mediocre, Janky. Those are the two things that come in mind after finishing the game with both characters on hard combat difficulty along with old school guidance difficulty. While this is certainly a better game than the memeable disaster from 2008 it feels unpolished and almost unwilling to commit to being a horror game.As mentioned above there are two characters Emily Hartwood and Edward Carnby, after a brief intro scene you get to choose which character you play as but unfortunately the execution here is less than stellar as both of the characters play through the same core storyline and gameplay segments. Although each character offers a slightly different perspective/version of the events through cutscenes along with some minor changes related to their personal storylines and a brief unique gameplay section in the penultimate chapter of the game but around 90% of the gameplay content you experience remains the same regardless of the character.This is also reflected quite heavily in the playtime as for example my first playthrough as Emily took me around 6.5 hours and my 2nd playthrough as Edward took me only 3 hours 18 minutes which included watching all the cutscenes. That being said I very much preferred Emilys version of the story as I felt it worked better with the core narrative and its themes.So what does the game do well? Environments are one of the highlights and there are quite a few areas that are gorgeous, cutscenes are well directed, voice acting across the board is quite good and puzzles managed to strike a good balance between too easy or too tedious although there are a couple exceptions and issues with puzzle repetition.Unfortunately Alone in the Dark really falters on two important fronts combat and horror, former simply feels unpolished due to lack of proper fit feedback, half baked melee system, bad enemy animations and overall boring enemies that pose very little threat. The latter on the other hand suffers from myriad things that prevent you from really getting immersed in to the game: Gameplay flow is often interrupted by cinematics, game often wrestles the control of your character away from you for a brief moment such as to load a scene, dialogue or if it needs you to focus on something etc.In addition to that sound mixing also is of the variety where loud equals scary which I often find to detract from the atmosphere as I personally find it more annoying than scary. This in combination with a recurring looping audio bug where some sound effects stack on top of each other leading to an ear splitting cacophony took me out of the game quite a few times.Aside from that I have to admit that the narrative as a whole did not really work for me, much of it felt derivative and a bit too much of a been there done that especially when it ends up repeating some of the mistakes that many games borrowing a little too much from H.P. Lovecraft do but at the end of the day your mileage may wary and some may find the narrative to be compelling.What about the PC port then? I would say it could be described as functional but with some issues such as traversal/loading stutters and with some oddities like displaying a HUD element with dpad icon when you are playing with KB/M or things such as assigning holding "I" as a shortcut for opening the map instead of using a separate key such as "m" for it. That being said I don't feel like Alone in the Dark is worth recommending at its current price point as it is a short and unpolished experience with little to none replay value. Horror enthusiasts will likely end up playing the game either way at some point as most of us tend to play a lot of horror games regardless of their quality but for those new to the genre you can get a whole lot of actually good horror games for 60€/$ instead of this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: The Puzzles were good, Made you actually think, the combat while clunky (And that's the point as it is a horror game) was fun, The story was a bit short and convoluted, wish there was more "scary parts" in the game the game had no scare factor at least for me. biggest gripe is probably the bugs like getting stuck on objects and the reload the last save not working properly requiring me to re launch game and reload save from main menu, also game has a minor stuttering problem ( I have a 4090 with an I7-13700KF and 64 gigs of DDR5 ram at 6400) so the game should be running smooth but that's not the case, needs some optimization other than that game is a fun little puzzle/semi psychological horror game 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: For me this is the best Alone in the Dark since the first ones (AID 1 &2) in MS-DOSIs a solid game with great storytelling, good decent voice acting, atmosphere and good puzzles (not like the baby puzzles in Hellblade 2)what pisses me off are the performance issues and bugs (hopefully they being fixed and performing patches as you read)
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: It's a little rough around the edges, but overall it's really good. Feels like a bit of a hybrid of Alone in the Dark and Eternal Darkness, with gameplay that is obviously inspired by the RE2 remake, but with some additional mechanics like melee combat. It's the kind of survival horror game that you used to get back in the early 2000s, and IMO it's the best Alone in the Dark game.Now in fairness, some of the mechanics are a little undercooked such as stealth, and combat is... okay, but not great. The weapons sound great and have punchy animation, but enemy hit responses are a bit flat. The puzzles are sometimes a bit rote. These aren't deal-breakers, but they are areas that could be refined.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Alone in the Dark, ending the game with both characters and enjoying some of the bonuses I get to the conclusion that "professional! critics went to hard on this game. It is a good game, with puzzles, the combat while a bit flawed and simple compared to other games of the genre, but enough to be entertaining. In general I think this game have some bugs that could be avoided and some little details that could be polished. In general this is a good game and a very good reimagining of the classic. I got entertained all the way through and the level design was good.  I am glad I gave this one a shot and ignored the critics that really want to standardize the industry rather to consider classic and different experiences fairly. I recommend for all survivor horror fans, it's a decent entry to the Alone in the Dark series and a great improvement from previous games.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the technical issues (stutters and sound issues) I am having a great time with this game. It really shows that it's an homage to the first 3 games. I guess you need to have played the originals to appreciate this one fully. AitD 1 and 3 were some of my favourite games i played as a kid and this one sends strong vibes. Some complain about the combat, I think it's just right, Carnby is an alcoholic, out of shape and Emily is no girl boss so combat is clunky and slow. However you don;t have that many encounters if you want to play on the normal difficulty (there's no point in being masochistic in this game). Story is pretty straightforward, not something to write home about but I like that the characters are well fleshed out, diverse personality wise and everything is voiced (including ingame books and papers). The puzzles are not that difficult and just like the original games, it's mostly about fetching the thing to the other thing to make some other thing work. It's just a relaxed experience you can probably finish within a day and feel entertained, we need this kind of games every now and then.UPDATE: after beating the game, i can safely say that it's a game worth playing. I miss the time when games were made like this, no bull***t, just have fun. No chasing upgrades for weapons, no stats or leveling up to make you grind stuff, no meaningless side-quests, no open world and so on. The game respects your time and you can beat it in under 10 hours on each character if you take it slow. Honestly, for me this is well worth the 60$ price, i don't judge a game on world size or how long it is, I had plenty of fun for that money and that is what a game should be, fun. Really hope for a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this for 22 quid but certainly don't think it's worth it at full price. You can tell most of the budget went on the 2 actors. The other remakes like RE and SH are much better, but this is still a decent game if you want a 10 hr game to fill a hole. Its nothing special but the locations were quite good, puzzles and combat were average. It was spooky but not exactly scary.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I'd heard of this game, but never played it prior. Now there is a remade 2024 version with enhanced graphics, cutscenes, etc.Great atmosphere.  Interesting storyline and characters.  Dark and creepy at times.  Great for puzzle solving and mystery solving with some combat and/or evasion. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a bit janky, overpriced, and short. But you should expect to do 3 playthroughs to get access to all endings.But I think it got a certain charm to it, the voice acting is to me good and the story in the beginning is nice. You do not either want to fight, you be low on ammo and the combat is slow and annoying. But that fits the setting. _childDocuments_.review: I've never played the first game that came out back then, but I do play a lot of similar games like Tormented Soul, Resident Evil, etc. I find the puzzles in this one very basic — you find a key that opens the door next to it. The game is linear in this aspect and doesn't require much thinking. The optimization is terrible ; aside from frequent freezes, I've also encountered bugs where I got stuck in walls and had to reload the previous save. This happened after only 2.4 hours of gameplay. I personally do not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. A very good reimagination of a true classic with a ton of liberty taken with creative aspects.Whilst it is not a true "Survival Horror" experience (tons of ammo even on Hard mode), it is a very enjoyable experience.Cons:- Bugs. Although I did not encounter any game-breaking bugs, there still are plenty (ex: cannot pick up items and need to reload)- Performance is good, but very stuttery at places
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely wonderfull love letter to the atmosphere, themes and ideas from the original series. Lots of easter eggs, absolutely banging soundtrack and atmosphere is to die for. The game FEELS like a slow burn 70s horror movie in the best possible way. The story, the way it is presented and all the notes and lore are very well put together, smartly written and very engaging. If you like story driven games, get it.Yes, there is some jank and bugs, but nothing that would hamper the enjoyment of this lovely, lovely game.The game quicksaves all the time, there are no achievements tied to playing on hard difficulty so it smooths over the fact that the combat is trash and some bugs can clip you into stuff.EDIT: Patches fixed quite a lot of the technical issues the game had.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: FANTASTIC!!!At first I was a bit worried on account of some of the reviews inclining towards the negative, but after buying and playing the game for myself I can confidently say I LOVE THIS GAME. The environments are MESMERIZING, so much that I'm spending way more time in every room and level than the story strictly requires, just for the sake of gazing at the rich and  impressive surroundings.By the way I very much appreciate the "calm step" at which you can walk through the various environments and still speed up if you want with a very realistic looking jogging animation. So much better than those games where you can only run around like a wet hen.The story itself, although somewhat linear (most doors and rooms are locked and cannot be opened until the story has progressed to a certain point), is nevertheless a great combination of gameplay, detective work, storytelling and unexpected twists so it never gets boring and you'll constantly discover and experience new things.  Granted, the combat is somewhat basic and I don't like the fact that the MC pulls out a gun at the most inconvenient moments (this is because drawing weapon is tied to RMB as well as to ordinary UI exit actions which should have been separated, meaning you keep holstering your weapon over and over again, but that aside). Combat is nevertheless satisfying enough not to be disappointing. Gotta say I love those huge gunpowder sparks, nice reload animations and the sounds aren't bad either!!  I do have some doubts about the replayability but since every one of the two characters is said to have their own unique gameplay I'm looking forward to replaying the game from the other perspective as well.Great classic horror game with a wonderful 19th century feel to it, and if you pick it up on sale for let's say 30 bucks you'll have a great time without any regrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first experience with the Alone In The Dark series, and I'm not sure if that would change my views or not, but I was not impressed with this game. It never got as scary as I would have expected. The character's movement was clunky and they didn't react appropriately considering the freaky things happening around them. There is an option to play as one of two people, the stories were the same with small changes in the cute scenes. After plaything through the game twice I don't feel like this game was very good, the packaging wasn't quite there considering the story they had to play with.You can view my entire review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I was introduced to Alone in the Dark during its first remake when they gave Carnby a mullet and I loved it since then, so it was agonizing watching an old beloved get turned inside out over the years. As such, I went into this very skeptically, which pleasantly surprised me, in a good way, but there are a few things that need to be said:- When playing with a controller, the Tommy Gun has WAY too much recoil. This is not too much of a problem for most of the game, but the final boss is nigh impossible to kill with a controller because of the bad gun controls- When new areas get loaded in it's VERY obvious something's about to happen because the game immediately freezes for a few seconds- Cutscene camera work is odd, like the way it's done makes scenes feel like they're starting in the middle, as if like you missed a part of the scene before the characters continued - The story; to avoid spoilers I will simply say the story felt somewhat disjointed at parts; like there are plot points that come and go and feel like they don't connect with anything else happening and the final segment of the game feels like it comes out of nowhere since the game spends all its runtime pointing you in the opposite direction. I get they probably did this on purpose so the final chapter gets you good but the execution was a little lacking. The good: - If, like me, you're someone who has seen this series get dragged through the mud all these years since the first remake, then rejoice that this is a MASSIVE improvement over everything that came past the 2001 remake. - It's not as tense or as scary as that entry, but it has its moments and the team definitely made good use of the story's Eldritch inspirations to draw up some good ideas and create some really nice looking areas. - As is the norm with horror games, there are many puzzles and most of them are really nicely done, requiring you to actually pay attention to documents and clues to get how to solve them. I will admit though, I struggled a little to understand how the talisman you get at the beginning works.- Narration; it's obvious the team put a lot of effort into this one, as while the scene dialogues are a little odd at times, every single document you find in the game is fully narrated for that extra point of immersionOverall, if this was sold at the price of a AAA title, I'd have some issues but even with all the jank, at its current price tag, it is a good deal for the amount of content you're getting. I loved my experience with this, especially since I've been starved for some good Alone in the Dark content.I will update this once I do the other scenario as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the mainstream critics out there are unjustifiably dragging this game through the mud. While it's not a perfect game, it accomplishes the survival horror experience these developers sought to make. This may not be a AAA experience, but resources were put in the right place - engaging story, lore, asymmetric combat, atmosphere, puzzles requiring thought, and environments oozing with meticulous attention to detail. Not to mention several unnerving moments throughout that blend in with the overall story seamlessly. Optimized well with only minor, occasional stuttering and bugs, such as getting stuck on random assets. That said... $59.99 is WAY too steep for an 8-12 hour experience with little replay value, especially when compared to other games such as Alan Wake that launched with a $49.99 price tag. Wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this, but unfortunately it doesn’t really do the original justice at all. Even if I hadn’t grown up with the original, I’m not sure I’d find myself being that impressed. I really do like the art direction and music, but gameplay-wise? This is hardly survival horror. Extremely linear and scripted enemy encounters remove any sense of dread you would normally expect from the genre…Not to mention its almost complete lack of replayability. (Unless you are a completionist, there aren’t any worthwhile reasons for collecting every lagniappe on repeated playthroughs.) It’s a shame, because I was really pulling for this one; however, there are just too many great competitors to really recommend, even when considering the budget.Speaking of which, I also wholeheartedly disagree with the “pretty good for AA” argument. Robocop Rogue City released this year and had great gameplay. Within the genre, games like Crow Country and Signalis prove that you don’t need a huge budget to make a great survival horror experience. Unfortunately I’d say skip it unless you can get it for half the price or lower. I’m hoping we get another reboot attempt - I doubt this one will get a sequel. Maybe one which emphasizes and expands upon what made the original so great and groundbreaking for its time.
