_childDocuments_.review: Sum up  of the game "our gonna need some keys". Its worth playing but I would wait for it to be on sale. It only took me like a day to beat it so it is worth a play through but not $50.00.  It has a lot of silly glitching, nothing that kept you from playing (at least not for me)  but there were some hairdos and  bottles that were doing an Irish jig. The aiming is a bit atrocious but it didn't keep me from moving forward. Meh its a nice game to play when you want a break from other more long term commitment games. I got it cause I needed a break from BG3 and I like the actors they picked as the main characters. All and all it is another entertaining game if your looking for something small and weird. Pro: It actually was a smooth playthrough despite the fact it was a mystery. I notice a lot of mystery/puzzle games make the mistake of getting you lost and confused as to what to do next. You often will end up spending a considerable amount of time retracting steps and spend more time trying to find out what you are supposed to be doing that you can't even enjoy the game. Not the case here, everything was pretty straight forward a even when I had moments of confusion they only lasted a very short time before I figured out exactly what to do and got back to enjoying the game. Cons:....why the hell is this game $50.00? The play time is not there my dudes, and ya it was interesting but like it wasn't something that blew me away with visuals. _childDocuments_.review: There's some bugs, particularly with collision detection, but thankfully very generous checkpoint placement will help you out there.I mean this sincerely: this one is a 9.5/10 for me. The story is so well told. The pacing is superb. It's not just another Resident Evil clone like The New Nightmare or too ambitious beyond its means like Inferno. This is -just right-.I'll be writing up a full video review in the near future, but if you're at all a fan of old school adventure games -and- survival horror? If you miss puzzles actually being cleverly designed in games? If you crave for something that truly feels like it's both a modern title AND something ripped straight out of the 90s in the best ways? Play this. Absolutely make a point to play this. Between the two protagonist's unique stories, solid scenario design, and brilliant performances bolstering an already solid script... a few glitches and a bit easy of a final boss fight are worth overlooking.

_childDocuments_.review: Look. Clunky? Yes. But I gotta admit, the atmosphere, music, acting, and characters hit. I think this is pretty well done. I, like many others, would like a patch or two to clean up some issues. Overall, I got it on sale for 30 bucks. In my opinion, no brainer if you like horror. I am playing on the hardest difficulty and it can provide a challenge in some cases. It gives no hints on what and where to go, less items to scavenge around the levels. Its fun! I do wish the devs came in and cleaned up the stutters when loading a new level or area. You'll most likely see it early on. As the game has gone on, I see it less. Still, kills immersion. I say try it on sale. You got two hours. As long as you're not very slow, you can experience a decent amount to know if you'll like it. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Items disappeared in my inventory in chapter 2 leaving me to run around for hours before I finally googled it and realised that my save is knackered.Some of the puzzles are very abstract, it is very easy to make an early false assumption with the medallion that can leave you stumped for a long time making the wrong connections. Both times that I had to use it I just brute forced it and got lucky, then when finally googling it I realised how it's supposed to work.Game hitches constantly when moving around the mansion, not too bad to be game ruining like my first point but slightly annoying.Overall I don't want to finish this game, and you should get it on a deep sale and be prepared to Google things for some of the abstract puzzles. I don't want hand-holding but for some of the puzzles you do need to make some mental leaps in logic, which is unfortunate. How the medicine bottles look like a snake is beyond me.I also respect the fact that all of the inventory items are voiced, but some of them are so long and read so slowly that I wouldn't be surprised if you start skipping them.I don't recommend this game, but I may not be the target audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly let me tell you guys that no i haven't played the original but i have heard of the game before. Recently i was interested in the game after i saw some Alpha gameplay footage & it made me intrigued as i'm a fan of 3rd person shooter horror games which includes puzzles as well. The lovecraftian tag made it more interesting cause i love the works of H.P. Lovecraft, i have always loved games like Call of Cthulhu, Sinking City, Sherlock Holmes Awakened, etc. Now coming to the game itself it's a good Remake of the original, it reprises the spooky environments, Ghastly enemies and adds a cool detective formula to it. The combat is your regular 3rd person over the shoulder shooter where you use Pistol, Shotgun, Tommy Gun and Melee items to defeat monsters just like Resident Evil but the combat is kinda clunky with the player getting slow due to heavy recoil. We get to solve lots of cool puzzles but it suffers from heavy backtracking.Can be played from two different perspectives who are Edward and Emily with different outcomes but overall the Story and puzzles remain same. People who love horror and solving puzzles with bits of lovecraftian atmosphere this is the game for you.The performance of the game is very good, played for 2 hours and didn't encounter a crash, it suffered from heavy traversal and shader lags but currently they fixed it with the latest 2 GB patch and the game runs great! The graphics itself are pretty ordinary but the character models and lip syncing is top notch! I give it a solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Underrated game in my opinion.Sure, it has its flaws and quirks, and you definitely feel that this isn't a 100+ Million Dollar production. This isn't up to the standards defined by games like the RE2 Remake regarding presentation and overall production value.That said, this game oozes with atmosphere and tells a compelling story, with some mysteries and twists here and there. The general gameplay-loop (consisting of exploration, puzzling, exposition/story/cutscenes, and combat) was highly engaging for me and I basically finished the campaign (played as Emily; 6.9 hours (nice) for my playthrough) in a few sittings. You just want to know what happens next!Graphics are fine, although performance (mostly traversal-stutter) and pop-in surely aren't ideal. There's some good variety in locations and the lighting sometimes really looks spectacular. Of course, there are weak points, like the character models (other than the protagonists, those look actually quite good). All in all I actually think this game looks quite nice and the graphics set the mood perfectly most of the time.This is a slower-paced game, with lots of stuff to read, some dialogue, and quite a lot of puzzles (which are mostly good, but it falls flat for a few). Movement speed and combat are also rather slow, but that's not a bad thing. I should mention that this isn't really survival-horror though, so don't expect to have to deal with inventory management, crafting, and resource-scarcity!If you enjoy a narrative-heavy mystery-horror-thriller and don't need that last bit of polish in your game, I highly recommend this one. Not quite sure why the critics score on both metacritic and opencritic are that low; user scores paint a different and - in my opinion - more fitting picture though.

It's all very traditional in many ways. A great callback to survival horror games. Reminds me a lot of Signalis in that way. Having great fun so far. This is comfort gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would give this a 7/10 off of what I've seen so far. This isn't a REmake2 or 4 quality title, nor is it as scary as them, but it is a solid first step in the right direction for this battered & beaten series.It still offers some good scares & atmosphere, it's southern gothic noire aesthetic helps it stand out, the story is an engaging mystery with replay value & Decerto has been remade with an interesting history & even has some Spencer Mansion DNA. A fitting evolution. However these would be the CONS of the game.. Melee is janky & poorly implemented . The use of real life actors likeness for the leads creates an uncanny valley effect when compared to the rest of the cast which begs the question, why not do that with everyone?. The framerate has a habit of hitching & there's stuttering during transitions. Some people have even reported crashing but thank God for the Manuel save system. $100 (AUD) price tag is too high for what's on offer compared to another rceent THQ Nordic release, Outcast A New Beginning. $60-$70 would have been more fitting.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing the game, especially exploring the different locations and the temple in the middle of the desert. The puzzle that involved redirecting the lights through mirrors was a fun challenge. However, I did notice that the graphics in the cut scenes could have been improved. In my opinion, the in-game graphics looked better than the rendered cut scenes. I'm not sure why the developers didn't spend more time refining the cut scenes, especially when you compare them to games like "A Plague Tale" and "The Quarry". These games have much better skin, hair, and lip sync with the characters. Despite this, I still found the game enjoyable and finished it in about 8 hours. Now, I'll replay it as the female character in the story. Oh, I almost forgot! Every letter and piece of evidence you find is well worth it to read it to its fully extent to connect the fascinating story behind the manor where the story unfolds. Similarly to Alone in the Dark 4: The New Nightmare, the story combines the spiritual beliefs of the locals that used to inhabited the area. Overall, I give it an 8 out of 10. If you can get it at a discounted price, I would recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game! Such a fantastic love letter to the original AITD trilogy with lots of fun callbacks. (I see you, Slaughter Gulch Script.)It's 100% a survival horror game. Action feels a little on the clunky side (which should feel familiar to fans of older games of the genre like the PS1 Resident Evils, the original Alone in the Dark games, Silent Hill 1-4, etc.) I say this with love, but I know this can be a turn-off for some players.While it isn't fast paced, it is a great horror story with some fun twists and layers to the mystery that I fully enjoyed. I plan on playing through at least twice more, as there is lots of content to unlock, and each character can unlock story beats/items for the other character's game. These unlocks and progressing through both stories help you learn the full truth of what has and is happening at Derceto Manor, and your part to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell: It's "We have Alan Wake 2 at home" (but endearingly)This is a solid game with a little jank. A nice psychological horror with less emphasis on dark and dreary environments, jumpscares and gore, and more focused on the bizarre, occult, and atmosphere. Despite having two big celebrities act as the face of the product, the game has a nice personality of its own that I enjoyed. It has a rich 1920s theme across a variety of totally distinct environments and locations, with pleasant music, gorgeous visuals, some interesting characters and a plot I found interesting. Seriously the environment artists knocked it out of the park with this one.There's a fair bit of dialogue going around about how this game flopped and how they should have put the money used to hire Jodie Comer and David Harbour towards more solid gameplay and mechanics. I think there's some merit there but personally I think having these two people act as the main characters is pretty cool. While they are great actors, I feel like they fall a bit flat at voice acting most of the time. I'm not sure if this is just a lack of direction or experience (Acting and Voice Acting are totally different ball games) because there are a few moments where they put on great performances. The other voice actors in the game do alright, but nothing to write home about imo.The gameplay focuses around third person shooting and melee combat with dodging, while including items like bricks and molotovs that you cannot carry, but throw at enemies in close proximity. I think this is a nice system that allows you to conserve resources in a few different ways while not being an inventory-management based game. I felt like the shooting was a little off, but overall works just fine. Melee combat is floaty, lacks weight and was just unsatisfying however. The item throwing is a nice idea that I think works well. I didn't really find myself bored of the combat throughout.I felt the puzzles were pretty straightforward, with a few more puzzling ones in there but I felt those ones were perfectly balanced in their difficulty. I wish that clues and solutions to puzzles could expand beyond the room they are in, especially those that take place in Decerto. This would have shaken them up a bitI'm mostly writing this review because I think this is a quaint little gem of a game and that the studio deserved better. Because they made something good

_childDocuments_.review: i seldom write a review on a game no matter it is good or bad. but this one is really beyond my toleration. I had high hopes for Alone in the Dark due to it was my childhood favorite , but unfortunately, it fell short in almost every aspect.1, Character Control: The character control is incredibly frustrating. It feels clunky and unresponsive, making it difficult to navigate through the environments or execute any kind of strategy during combat.2. Storytelling and Storyline: The storytelling is painfully weak. The plot is disjointed, and the characters are underdeveloped, leaving players with little to invest in the narrative. I found myself losing interest very quickly.3. Combat System: The combat system is a complete disaster. It feels unbalanced and lacks the depth you would expect from a game of this genre, turning battles into tedious experiences rather than engaging challenges.4. Enemy Variety: The enemies are shockingly boring. There’s a lack of creativity in their design and behavior, making combat encounters repetitive and uninspired.5. Bugs: To top it all off, the game is riddled with bugs. I encountered numerous glitches that disrupted gameplay and further added to my frustration.Sadly i couldnt refund, it is a scam of money.  I wouldn't recommend it to anyone looking for a polished and engaging game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love survival horror games but this one is in a rough state.Pros:- Superb voice acting- Interesting story- More than one story line to play through- The game runs smoothly- There are puzzles but none of them are unfair.Cons:- Hit box of the player character. Not as bad as Dark Souls 2, but it's bad.- The combat system as entirety.- Melee system. I like that your melee weapon is not indestructible but, some of these weapons break way too easily. If you die, your melee weapon is swapped to the weakest one on that level, unless you choose to load a manual save.- The "shake the enemy off" system. For whatever reason, this mechanic didn't work on my keyboard no matter if I reset all the controls, but it functioned on my controller just fine.- The last "boss" fight. Whoever came up with the idea of an area boss that fills 80% of that area making the fight super annoying, great job dude. Really original

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have any of the performance issues that many are complaining about, but this game is not very good. It honestly reminds me a bit more of the Frogwares Sherlock Holmes games than anything else. The combat here is also terrible and fairly unnecessary.  I think my biggest issue is that Lovecraftian Horror is not scary or interesting to me.  If anyone has ever read "The Call of Cthulhu" half of that novella is just my guy describing rocks and topography. That isn't spooky. It's boring.Edit: After playing for a few more hours, there are a few very annoying bugs. First, if you die make sure you are playing with a controller because you can't click load or anything afterwards. For some reason David Harbour is sparkly like a Twilight vampire if the camera is looking directly at him from the front. You guys ever want to get stuck on objects for no reason? The game is still stinky - but is now more stinky, especially given the fact that I've almost finished it after 3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the whole game, it was a good game. There's a lot of care in the details of the game. Almost everything that needs to be read has a nice voiceover instead which is cool. The environments are fitting for the era and there's lots of specific details scattered around the environments that definitely adds to the immersion. Fighting monsters can be rough and the stealth sucks but as survival horror games go that tracks. The puzzles are solid. The characters are quirky and memorable, the ending is memorable. It sets itself up for a sequel that we'll unfortunately never see.The biggest disappointment is finding out that given the choice at the beginning of the 2 characters to play, both play out the same stories and sequences. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the Alone in the Dark series. I'm a fan of survival horror. I think both Jodie Comer and David Harbour are great actors. Based on this, the reboot of the series with these two in the lead roles should be a great game, right? Right?Unfortunately, things aren't quite like that. But everything in its own time.Alone in the Dark (2024) is an old-school survival horror game, another installment of the series that actually created this genre back in the distant 1992. Everything that makes games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill hits is present - puzzles to solve, strange places to explore, hordes of nasty enemies to defeat, with your weapons and ammo being more than limited. So far, so good.But here come the small unpleasant details. The game is endlessly linear - until you find the key to room A, you can't proceed. Until you solve the puzzle in room B, you still can't move forward. There's no freedom of action, everything happens in a precisely defined order.The puzzles, which are an important part of games like this, are too easy. In fact, only one puzzle took me more than 10 minutes, mainly because the slightly strange controls didn't allow me to focus the telescope faster. If for some reason you still struggle with the puzzles, the game gives you more than obvious hints.The story is very pleasant, I won't deny that. Starting as a noir from the beginning of the last century, it quickly leads you to a world filled with madness, paranoia, and more than enough references to the works of Lovecraft and Stephen King. If only it were a little more interactive, instead of completely linear. You can also experience it in slightly different ways through the eyes of two main characters (you choose who to play with at the beginning).Which leads to the battles. The shooting itself is done in an extremely clumsy way, and hitting anything is a matter of skill and luck. Adding the limited ammo, the fact that your characters are mega clumsy, and the enemies - quite fast, and the rare healing items, the overall impression is quite unpleasant.The sound is, well... okay, let me put it this way. All the moans, creaks, closing doors, and other sounds that are supposed to create atmosphere are great. Add some dark jazz, totally suitable for New Orleans at the beginning of the 20th century, and it gets even better. The voice acting by the supporting characters is also on point.And here comes the huge surprise - both Jodie and David sound half asleep, without any emotion, and it's more than obvious how much they hurried to get their paycheck and break away from the studio.Bad.Graphically, the game is quite pleasant, from the crumbling psychiatric clinic in New Orleans, to the infectious swamps of Louisiana, through the ancient Egyptian temple to the abandoned Arctic station, everything is beautiful, detailed, and frightening. But, unfortunately, there's still a "but", the expressions of the main characters are just as devoid of emotion as their voices.Regarding the enjoyment of the game, I admit - I enjoyed it. And solving the story room by room and page by page, and solving the puzzles, albeit easy. A few times I jumped out of my chair at well-directed "jump scares". A few times I laughed at the exchange of lines between Jodie and David, albeit spoken with a tired and bored voice.The game is still worth it, especially considering that there hasn't been a new Silent Hill in years, and the Resident Evil games are getting further and further away from the genre's roots with each new installment.But it could have been a lot better with just a bit more...i don't really know what. Time?Rating: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I'm a big fan of older survival horrors like the earlier Resident Evils and Silent Hills, and the 4th Alone in the Dark, although I never played the original. I've been reading through the other reviews and personally I can't say I've had a load of the problems other people have had. I'll agree that the story isn't revolutionary in any way, but I think it's because this type of Lovecraftian setting and story has been done so many times and in so many mediums it's hard to do something new whilst preserving the expected tropes. I've just started reading Lovecraft myself and it's brilliant to see some of the details from the books used in game. I've also found all of his story's so far to be more about building an atmosphere than action so I suppose the game captures that pretty well too. I'd say it's a solid story with a couple of unexpected twists, although the final act does seem to come upon you suddenly. That said Emilys story is the better of the two. The game does nudge you towards playing as Emily first but as I'm more familiar with David Harbour than Jodie Comer, and Carnby was the main character in the first 5 games, I went with Carnby first and it was the wrong decision. Playing as Emily the supporting characters are more forthcoming with information, Emily's unique sections are more interesting and the whole story felt more cohesive. Carnbys story is better with the information you get in Emily's story. Looking at some reviewers play times it looks as if they've only played one half of the game, and the weaker half at that. I'd also say Emily's story has less technical issues than Carnbys. Graphically I think it looks good and runs as at a pretty steady 90fps on my 5800x/2080/32GB rig without any issues, compared to something like Alan Wake 2 which struggled to hit 60fps for the majority of the game.Gameplay wise It's what I want to see from a survival horror; recursive exploration and some decent puzzles without being too action oriented like pretty much every Resident Evil game and remake since 2004.The puzzles vary from very simple pick up item, turn around and place in slot to some that will require cross referencing a couple of different items in the room and one or two documents you've discovered that will have you scratching your head for a few minutes. To counter other reviewers complaints:> Cost Vs time. Every survival horror I've ever played has cos whatever the industry standard was at the time and taken 6-10 hours for your first playthrough (12-20 for two characters) and 2-4 hours for subsequent runs. This game falls squarely into the middle of those brackets based on my own play time. > The aiming works fine. Yes it's a bit slow and if you fire in succession too fast then your character will be affected by recoil and the second shot will go wide. Similarly if you're moving whilst shooting your accuracy goes down. Adjust how you're playing and you won't have any issues. After all you're not some superhero with special forces training, you're a couple of normal people up against the unexplained, CoD level responsiveness and accuracy should not be expected. This was the design philosophy of a lot of older survival horror games and it's nice to see it back again. Anyone else who played those older games should know what to expect. Personally, this is how I want my survival horrors to handle. > If you get headshots on enemies (and you actually land them, see above) weaker enemies go down in 1-4 pistol shots, stronger enemies in 1-2 shotgun shots. Not broken as some have said. > There's actually 8 enemy types in game. Sure they all look similar and it may not be as varied as the original, I don't know, but its not as bad as some people make out. > Getting stuck on objects. I'm pretty thorough with exploring and I only managed to get stuck in the scenery three times in two playthroughs so make of that what you will, but it's nothing a quick save and reload won't fix. > Grapical issues are minor. My GF got some speckling in a few areas on her PC using DLSS to upscale from 720p to 4k, playing it myself at native 1440p I had no issues. There's one cutscene where the character rubber bands for a few seconds right at the start regardless of who you're playing as but other than that I can't think of any problems in 2 and a bit playthroughs. The game could do with a little extra attention here and there as far as graphics and collision detection go but compared to the state a lot of games launch in nowadays it's incredibly minor. All in all I think this is a great start to resurrecting a classic series and hope they do the rest of the series, particularly a remake of New Nightmare given my nostalgia over it, and hopefully eventually a continuation of the series seeing as the 2008 and 2015 games pretty much killed the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Another decade, another attempt to revive Alone in the Dark. I’ve recently replayed and covered all of the previous games in the series (excluding Illumination, because who cares). The inspiring original trilogy that shaped modern action adventures, but aged poorly. A much simpler first reboot The New Nightmare that nonetheless did several incredibly ambitious things. Overly ambitious Alone in the Dark from 2008, that attempted to reinvent the genre but failed miserably. And now we have a third game simply titled Alone in the Dark, except this lacks any ambition of the previous entries.Alone in the Dark from 2024 is a mostly linear horror themed story driven action adventure game. That serves as a new reboot, a “reimagining” of the original game that directly references this fact in its cosmic horror “nobody knows what’s real” plot. But design-wise it is completely unlike any of the previous entries in the franchise focusing far more on said plot than the gameplay.Mechanically, this is another game taking Resident Evil 2 (2019) as a reference. Except, it only covers the controls and combat, while completely ignoring the rest of the gameplay experiences of both new RE2 or the previous games. As a result, this game doesn’t fit the core pillars of survival action (let alone survival horror) and lacks any meaningful exploration, while the rest of the pillars are underserved as well. There’s one central location that you get to revisit between the almost entirely linear levels which pretends to behave like a typical interconnected survival horror spooky mansion. But in reality even the “exploration” of this location is on rails and the game constantly closes and opens paths in such a bold way that even the most egregious examples of this from Fatal Frame look tame in comparison.But hey – not being a survival horror/action isn’t a bad thing and Alone in the Dark doesn’t have to fit the limitations of a genre to be a fun game. This title focuses on being a story driven experience and to give it credit – the writing for the characters and character performances are genuinely impressive. The writing feels as if something that came out of the Lovecraft novel (minus the racism) and some of the cutscenes are really well directed too. Unfortunately, the plot itself is extremely dumb. It gets caught in its own delusions and attempts to be “meta” and in the end loses any sense of direction or point to it. I mean, sure the storyline of the original game wasn’t particularly interesting either, but that game was released in 1992 and also had a lot of other cool things going for it. While the only thing this new game seems to have is the storytelling.The rest of the game aspects range from barely functioning to potentially interesting. Combat is not good, but it’s also not the worst even within the limits of franchise. Plus it tries to spice things up with the throwable objects and Alan Wake dodge, which are fun additions. Puzzles range from exceptionally primitive to obtuse in an unfun way. The idea of unlocking secret endings or scenes via collectibles is curious, but collectibles themselves can be hidden in an unacceptable manner – like in a tiny spot just few steps from an invisible trigger that blocks you from being able to grab it. There is no meaningful resource management and the ammo/health pickups system is incredibly silly in its execution.Then there are also countless bugs and poor design decisions. You will constantly get stuck on decoration objects and it more likely than not will require a reload of the last save. Animations break for characters and enemies. Sound may suddenly break and you will get a cacophony of noise in the background or a character line will be unvoiced. Map breaks all the time adding confusion to the already frustrating pixel hunting, as pickups may not be interactable unless you’re standing at a specific angle. Collectibles and items may reappear when you’ve picked them up already, sometimes infinitely. Occasional interaction spots appear when they shouldn’t. There are several spots where you can completely break the sequence of events without even realizing it, which breaks the script of the game… The game is in a genuinely unacceptable state and some of these issues could’ve been identified and designed around very early in development.Yet, despite all of this during my first playthrough I was relatively positive and hoping that the game will still manage to surprise me in some way. But no there is simply no ambition in this project. No cool systems like in AitD 2008, no non-linearity like in the original, no wild mechanics and plot points like in the AitD 2 and 3. Even The New Nightmare, for how closely it followed the Resident Evil formula of the time, did genuinely inventive things with the flashlight and created two unique playthroughs for its two characters, with unique locations, story and puzzles. While Alone in the Dark 2024 is completely linear, its story is almost exactly the same between characters and there’s just one mostly insignificant and uninteresting location close to the end of the game that differentiates one character from another. There’s nothing inventive here, nothing unique or interesting. Just a rehash of things you’ve seen done better before.So while I originally considered getting all secret endings in the game, I just stopped during my third playthrough. Alone in the Dark from 2024 is short, I was about half-way through, rushing through everything on easy and in just about an hour or so I would’ve been able to see more of those secret things I’ve already unlocked… But then the thoughts of spending even five more minutes with the game became so suffocating that I had to stop. And will most likely never play it again. If it ever gets properly fixed so thousands of its bugs are gone and you see it at a huge discount, maybe it could be worth one playthrough. Just to check the dialogues between characters and have a simple linear walk through this title. But until that happens I would not recommend it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: - The idea of a reboot of the saga is a success.- The game recreates an atmosphere of terror and mystery that keeps you in suspense throughout the game. To be clear, the mansion setting is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.- The story is intriguing and keeps you hooked until the end: if you're a Lovecraft fan, don't miss it.- It's very replayable: it has five different endings, although Edward and Emily's parts are very similar for most of the game they have some differences that make it worth playing with both of them.- It has some really memorable moments.- Levels are well designed and offer a good challenge....... although there is one level in particular where you have to run away because there are infinite enemies and they don't tell you anything: it's a notable design flaw.- They shouldn't have spent money on the roles of Edward Camby and Emily: it would have been better to use that budget to enrich the game and polish it more.- Some of the puzzles are repeated too often, and are somewhat difficult to solve.- The combat system is too basic, and when the enemy gets too close it becomes almost impossible to survive.- It has several bugs, which don't detract too much from the experience, but are not understandable. For example, I got stuck (literally, unable to move the character) several times, forcing me to reload game.Putting on a scale the good things on one side and the bad things on the other, the good things win by far, but unfortunately for some media the bad things usually outweigh the good things, unless you are a fan of a certain saga. It's true, this Alone in the Dark has a clumsy combat system, but its atmosphere is of honours and its story is remarkable, and just for that alone it's worth playing it.- 8/10.The truth is, I don't understand the bad press that the game has had, because I loved it. It's true that it's not at the same level of the greats of the genre, but its budget is much lower. I hope they make a second part.If you're a fan of survival horror you should give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Mitigated.Starting by what made me playing it and enjoying that time. It is splendid.The 2 main qualities of this game are its visuals and its narrative. Despite fabrics are hard as rock, the rest is simply beautiful. With well crafted stages, splendid lights... It is a Call and serve the Mythos without a doubt.Story is just great. Atmosphere is fantastic.It is verbose. A bit too much. You do not have to read except for 2 documents and probably due to a bug since the plethora of other lectures is voiced. Well voiced.But it comes to a point that having to listen without doing anything else breaks the game.I did jump a couple of lectures because I wanted to play instead of listening.I did stop the voice sometimes because it is just faster to read yourself and I wanted to play. Not to listen books after books. notes after notes.It comes with glitches and bugs. Some visual glitches, nothing game breaking but damageable since the game rely a lot on its visual. Especially with lights that may become strange while entering or leaving a space. Some sparks that are appearing in the back of the character.And some bugs that obliged me to restart a save. It happened multiple times. I could not take hatchets that come in boxes. Objects that are for the least mandatory not only for fighting.It brings to the saves. Automated and manual. No limited slots but limited times. For some reasons, you cannot manual save any time you want... And you will reappear at precise points of the map. With all you have done such as already collected stuff but not reappearing where you saved. A bit disappointing, especially the first time.Controls are rough. At least playing with a controller. Not really responsives.  That does not serve the coming point.The worst.What reproduce the game at best from its sibling from the 90's is the combat. It is different but it reminds this feeling while you had to turn on yourself to adjust a shot. Sometime a creature is right in your reticule, you are not moving, you give a shot and you are still able to miss it... Disappointing.It is still acceptable because the game is good and fights are not too punitive. Fights does not require extra action for most of them and when it does, it is manageable.Except there is an ending boss. One that split  offspring, minions. I stopped here. I find this too painful for the moment considering the lack of polish around the controls.Frustrating because it is the actual ending and I would like to see it.This dev choice was definitely not a good idea considering the fighting mechanic quality. On top, it starts with a video that you cannot skip... Expect to watch it a couple of times.That really bores me.This last point by itself makes me wanting to put the thumb down.I keep it up since I really enjoyed the 11h of game before that.I also want to replay it with the second protagonist to see what changes. But without seeing the ending... Not sure how I am going to handle that. A cheat maybe if there is one.Regarding its price, I bought it on sales. I wanted to buy it at day one but when its price came out, I took a step back. Playing the game confirmed it was the right choice. It should have been released with the 34% off proposed today. Because of its length, including the time you have to listen without playing, and its lack of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has common unreal engine 4 shader problem.It will stutter even with rtx 4090,but i am able to fix this with old knowledge.1-You should increase your shader memory to ''unlimited'' under  nvidia 3d settings - or amd control panel or asus rog software etc.2-Delete all files under C:\Users\yourusername\AppData\Local\NVIDIA\GLCache  and DXCache too if it's there.3-Delete all files that can be deleted under C:\Users\yourusername\AppData\Local\Temp4-Delete dx cache via typing ''storage'' to search then select temporary files - tick directx and clean.5-Force game to use dx12 with adding -dx12 to steamlaunch options or game exe.6-Match your fps limit with your display and use vsync.7-These should %90 reduce your stuttering but if you still suffer stuttering ,try using ddu tool and delete  and reistall your graphic drivers when your windows in offline mode.This will temporarily fix your issue with micro stutters,weird trace in air like using DLAA when moving camera (even while it's turned off) and render issues.It's more usefull on cards with big vram but you still need to repeat delete cache steps when your shader cache starting to bloat again.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished playing Alone In the Dark. I was hesitant to purchase this game because of all the bad reviews but I still decided to get it a try. This game was surprisingly good. I think its a great classic Lovecraftian game. I expected OG Alone in the dark, and what I got was unexpected. _childDocuments_.review: Since last year, I have been eagerly waiting to play the new  reimagination. It was initially supposed to come out before my birthday, and it would’ve been a great, spooky season release. But I’m glad to have waited longer because it was worth it!Either playing as Edward Carnby (David Harbour) or Emily Hartwood (Jodie Comer), the story follows them as they head to Derceto Manor. Emily has received a letter from her uncle, Jeremy, telling her to stay away. Avoiding her uncle’s warning, she heads to Derceto and hires private investigator Edward to help her. However, they find her uncle missing when they arrive, and the staff seem reluctant to help them. Where has Jeremy gone? Why are the staff strange? What secrets does Derceto hide within its walls? It’s time for us to be alone in the dark.Before playing this remake, I decided to play through the original 1992 game to get an idea and feel of what I might be getting into. Honestly, I am pleased I did because it helped me appreciate this game even more. Throughout my two playthroughs (Edward and Emily's campaigns, respectively), I could spot the various easter eggs and references from that first game, such as a secret hidden memory in the attic and collectibles or items that look like those found in the original. Furthermore, so much detail was included in this game, and it’s impressive. Graphically, this game is stunning, which is always a plus. The narrative is quite interesting and kept me engaged as I went along; plus, I enjoy Lovecraftian horror. Just like  or , some puzzles aren’t too complicated but do take some real thinking.As I write this, I want to add that the game still has some stuttering issues. It didn’t ruin my experience with the game, as I encountered it minimally, but it is noticeable when it happens. With this being a survival horror-like experience, there are sections of combat. I didn’t hate these portions, but the only critique I would give is that the reload speed felt a little slow to me, although it did seem realistic. I do recommend playing through each character’s campaign as they aren’t entirely the same experience, just playing as different people. Some neat differences exist (unique cutscenes, unique sections, collectibles that can only be found as each character). It is worth playing through a couple times, trust me.This is an excellent game; there is so much to love about it. I really don’t understand the negative reviews. It felt like a true  game. P.S. Loved the casting!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was a solid entry, albeit dotted with some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ here and there. There's a good balance of exploration, solving puzzles and combat. I think the developers got the pacing spot on and I never felt like the experience got repetitive because there's quite a lot of different locations from ancient tombs to murky swamps. It really nails the environments and atmosphere which have a very Lovecraft / Gothic vibe. Apart from exploring the mansion, it is a fairly linear journey and there's not much going off the beaten track but I was OK with this. The combat was satisfying enough for me, not brilliant but not awful either. It does feel very old school in a deliberately awkward way. Lobbing Molotov cocktails could of been designed better - it's very hit and miss if you're not aiming but maybe that was intended. The ammo placements in a few sections weren't very balanced either and there's a level with an unnecessary amount of flare gun ammo prior to a mini boss fight. During this fight, and after you've beaten him, you can't go back to replenish your gun with all that ammo because the path has now been blocked off. The voice acting is really good, as is the modelling of Emily and Edward. The other characters aren't as polished but they still compliment the main protagonists. I can't fault the gloomy jazz music which is perfectly fitting and assists the game's spooky atmosphere. I say spooky, because in general it was quite tame on the horror. The puzzles varied from easy to normal which I mostly found a breeze on 'Old School' mode, although there's one that's not clearly explained which took me a while to figure out. There's some nods to the original AITD series like a sudden switch in camera view and subtle things like the way Emily leans forward to push open  double doors. I just wished the developers had included some comical kicking and slapping which was present in the earlier games. I encountered quite a few bugs. Some interactivity not working properly and mostly getting stuck on objects. It could certainly do with some more play testing but nothing was really game breaking and was a matter of reloading a save.I had a lot of fun with this game, coming in at around 10 hours and I hope there's a sequel but with more improvements. 7/10

There were a few times I got stuck in game geometry and had to reload. Asset loading causes very noticeable stuttering and hitching at times (even on a high end machine and SSD) and combat feels like an afterthought with poor camera control and enemy responsiveness that can lead to you being wombo-combo'd in a corner with no way to heal, which doesn't feel too satisfying.The story, character performances and atmosphere save this game though. I hope the dev team learns from this experience and can build on this base while smoothing out the issues to polish this game and perhaps work on others in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a mixed bag.i enjoyed it thoroughly but there are many aspects in which i am disappointed. firstly the mansion looks incredible. secondly i enjoyed many of the puzzles as simple as they were.i appreciate the setting immensely. the story for what it is, is fine. the characters and delivery are phenomenal.the music is especially noteworthy as it has almost a twin peaks vibe, very lynchian. theirs jazzy notes that are period appropriate but also some synths to pad out and add atmosphere very good stuff.the fact there are 4 endings and 2 characters adds to replay-ability but also lends itself to some issues.the lack of unlockables for beating the game multiple times is SEVERELY disappointing. many old games especially from the era this game hails from have many secret unlockable weapons and even if they didnt they had a lot of variety and the setting lends itself to some really interesting possibilities but theres only 3 weapons (4 if you include the character specific weapons) but there in itself leads to my main critique of the game. there is no real sense of progression. now many people critique modern games having to have skill trees and level ups ect ect but resident evil and evil within had gotten these systems down perfectly and lend themselves to their own criteria- one being realistic and one being fantastical.resident evil gives way to progression by allowing you to find weapon attachments and allowing you to stow resources away creating a satisfying gameplay loop leading to a nice skill ceiling. the evil within allowed you to upgrade your chracters skills and craft ammo leading to a need to scrounge environments.with resident evil 4 and other modern survival horror games: inventory management makes for moment to moment and emergent gameplay.not only does alone in the dark hamper itself with a lack of ANY of these systems refined and easily transferable from a series that has more than 20 years of experience but it actually spits in your face by carefully managing exactly how much ammo it gives you. alan wake 2 did this and it made for a system thats easily game-able. it takes the control out of the player and keeps it in the developers hands. so there are containers everywhere and depending on how much ammo you have it spits out what you need. your Never struggling or surviving. you always have exactly what you need for each scenerio. its predictable and frustrating. the level design is great but as i have said the combat doesnt just stop with the way the systems work with ammo, progression and player agency but it also physically lacks feedback as well as the enemy variety being very lack luster. when you shoot it feels like a pellet gun and the enemies have very poor animations.the combat very quickly loses any fun factor.the gameplay is imo extremely dated whilst also having bad tropes that modern survival horror games seem to persist in. linear levels that look great but lack any need to explore. alan wake 2 suffered from this as well.there are difficulty options but even those are lack luster, one being guided and the other "not" i say not in quotes because even with it off you are told exactly where to go no matter which section and the map literally tells you when your done with a room. in resident evil this is good because of the progression systems which allows the game to be a lot more mechanically driven and difficult. this game stays largely the same throughout. so if im so down on everything involving gameplay why do i still recommend it?because whilst the gameplay is bleak the setting and atmosphere is really good. especially so if you have appreciation for the setting it takes place in, the south.it has a wonderful atmosphere that all but saves the game. the art director did a great job and if it wasnt for him this game would be really bad.the story isnt anything to write home about and can be predictable depending on what ending you like.derceto is phenomenally crafted and interesting, but with the lack of gameplay elements to keep players invested it seems to be a one and done game, unless the story itself supremely interests you. TLDR: game-play is lack luster and mechanics are too simple to be considered a "survival horror" game but, the atmosphere and soundtrack make up a suitably enjoyable overall experience. the story is ok but the ascetics take it home.notesresident evil has got the blueprints down perfectly evil within 2 also perfected the systems a more fantastical survival horror game should have.the reason silent hill gets away with being so poor mechanically is because the atmosphere and story.this game is jsut barely passing the mark.it falls in an awkward space because it doesnt have the mechanics of resident evil and lacks the compelling stories of silent hill 1-4 that has had fans in forums discussing the game for 30 years. the only saving grace is the art direction. is that enough to recommend a game? i dont think so.so in my notes i wills say stay away until a sale.there a lot to like but the gameplay is out of touch and seems to ignore the improvements capcom has strived to make.

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ After her uncle disappeared from the Derceto's mansion, an asylum deep in the Louisiana countryside, Emily Hartwood hired a private detective. As they drove towards their destination, she explained that Jeremy Hartwood was possessed by something or someone that he refers to as the Dark Man, who is constantly watching his movements. She also mentioned that most members of the Hartwood family go mad and kill themselves before their time comes. But Jeremy didn't kill himself; instead, he hoped to find a cure with the new method of the Derceto's mansion owner, Dr Gray. However, in his last letter to Emily, he made some accusations that the entire staff of the asylum were part of some cult, and then he disappeared. It's time to discover the mystery of Alone in the Dark.Alone in the Dark is a third-person Lovecraftian psychological horror adventure game developed by Pieces Interactive and published by THQ Nordic on the 21st of March on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS5 and Xbox One Series X|S.The game has five chapters and will start with a fabulous cinematographic scene. Then it’s time to choose who to play as. Carnby, the private detective, was my choice. If you decide to play as Emily, I understand the game will lead toward the same path but have different commentary and cutscenes. You can play the game with or without hints. If you choose to play without hints, you'll have to figure everything out by yourself. The gameplay and the character's animations are beautifully done and so smooth. All the locations you visit are visually stunning. In almost every area, there will be things to pick up along the way, such as clues regarding the story and puzzles, ammunition for your firearms and objects you can use as melee weapons, such as pipelines and sledgehammers. There will be locked areas and locked chests; you might find a key for them while playing on your current chapter. But, more than once, these areas or chests will be accessible further down the track in upcoming chapters. What impressed me was the voice-over and the atmosphere in the game. You hear sounds in most places giving you the impression that something is there or that something is about to happen. It made me jump several times. I knew that something was building up, but when it happened, it was not where I had expected it to be. I would classify the puzzles as average; while a couple of them got me thinking, most were pretty straightforward. Yes, some puzzles will require additional objects to find within your surroundings, but on several occasions, you won't be able to complete these puzzles straight away as some of the objects won't be available in the current chapter. The puzzles with the medallion are also pretty easy when you gather all the information required. I was slightly disappointed with the fighting and enemies I encountered in this game. There is not a great variety of enemies, and they are easy to dispose of. Even the last two bosses were surprisingly easy to kill. There are objects lying around, such as briks and Molotov cocktails, that you can throw at enemies.  I liked that!  These objects helps damage them significantly, and can also be used to distract them.  You can easily dodge enemy attacks and use the melee weapon if you are close enough. Sure, melee weapons deteriorate pretty quickly, but if you have enough ammunition and keep dodging until you are out of reach, you can turn around and start shooting at them.  For my first experience with a game of this series, I must say that I enjoyed it. I need to go back and play Emily to see the difference between the two characters' perspectives and to finish collecting all the clues. I have been very thorough regarding clues, so I imagine the other collectables will be discovered while playing Emily. The graphics, soundtrack and voice-overs are excellent! The game runs very well, and I haven't experienced any issues apart from the mouse sensitivity at the start of my playthrough, which was an easy fix by adjusting it. You can play the game with a gamepad, or if you are like me, the mouse and keyboard are just fine. The game is translated into 16 languages, but the full audio experience is available in English, French, German and Japanese.  I think the initial release price of $99 AUD is too high for what you get in terms of gameplay.  $69 AUD feels more appropriate.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics and voice-overs+	Well-designed levels (chapters)+	Intriguing story+	Stunning atmosphere all the way through+	Able to play the game through two different characters +	Achievements and trading cardsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Lack of enemy variety-	Combat is far too easy, including bossesAlthough a rather short game with a lack of enemy variety and manageable combat phases, Alone in the Dark has stunning graphics and voice-overs, a chilling atmosphere, well-designed levels, and well-structured storytelling.7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is much better than you probably think. Try it. It might  very well be the best AitD since 2001  or even since the 'classic' era, and, obviously, infinitely better than that 2008 catastrophe.  Admittedly, i remember vividly only the very first game (c'mon, it's been, like, 25 years ago when i last played the old AitD), but this one is very good.You need to understand though, that this is NOT a AAA game, so don't expect Alan Wake 2 or RE Remakes level of presentation or polishing, and it doesn't have the inventory management system - it's more of a adventure\quest type of  game with some combat sequences. And it's not a cheap travesty either, because while playing you actually see that the developers very much cared about the game, and spent the (humble) budget money wisely; don't be fooled by "professional journalists" opinions and the underwhelming PR campaign. So, what CAN you expect?+stellar voice acting and dialogue+enveloping authentic "bookish" atmosphere+solid writing and story +good level design and detailed environment -combat system is janky - this is where the limitations of budget really showing.-the game relies a bit too much on a puzzles of one particular type (when you need to restore a right picture or order of things)note: i've beaten the game once, playing as Edward (as per canon), but planning to make another run as Emily (as per canon, of course).As of now, solid 8\10, or even 10 if you're a fan of the old AitD.

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark was a pretty good surprise and honestly better than I expected.It does have a good variety of environments and those are usually really beautiful. I like the Lovecraft inspiration and the vibes from Louisiana. The story and music are both pretty good and the pacing is actually nice, so I never got bored.It's essentially a mix of survival-horror (especially in Hard mode) and investigation. The mansion isn't as threatening as in the original, but after all this is a re-imagination and not a remake, while still being really respectful to the original material in general. There's a few bugs/issues, and the combat is clunky (shooting is fine, but the rest meh, I didn't like throwing items). I recommend to adjust camera settings because the default ones aren't the best and make the combat even worse imo. It's not an AAA and it's sometimes obvious, the presentation can be a bit rough at times, but it does have a soul.In the end, Pieces Interactive did a good job and it's a pleasant surprise to play an Alone in the Dark that's not only pretty good, but also closer to the first game than whatever we got since AitD 4.

_childDocuments_.review: Changing my review (again, and I promise I'm not bipolar):I've been waiting for this game, LITERALLY, for 32 years. Was the wait worth it?30 minutes into the game and I was absolutely in love. 6 hours later, I'm not in love anymore. And I'm more disappointed than I could imagine. Tho, I finally decide to recommend the title, in order to try to resurrect the franchise.Why this change of heart?The beautiful thing about Steam is democracy in reviews. You can speak the truth about things.This game isn't what I was promised, and that's a huge disappointment. I'm a true fan of the original series from Infogrames. I grew up with those games.What's wrong with this title? It's only halfway of what I expected it to be.The game itself is the remake I could have expected in 2005 to 2010. This game arrives 16 years later.Gameplay is poor; there's not much to do, most of the places you interact with are empty. Why? Door and area discovery feels like a bad copy of Resident Evil, when Resident Evil series are, in fact, a copy of the original AitD. Go to this point to get the key for the other point. I'm missing a lot of puzzles/riddles here.I read some reviews saying the puzzles are easy. That's true. As a hardcore gamer, I've come to realize that the "democratization" of videogames for everybody has made puzzle designers hollow and a little lazy. I'd prefer challenges and things to make you think more, and let bad players check out walkthroughs and videos. Why does everybody have to play at the level of "not very smart" people?Combat system: I understand what they intended to do, but they didn't achieve it. The movements are clunky. Not organic. The characters are considerably slower than they should be. If you have no weapon, you can't use your fists or feet to try and fight, so if you break your melee weapon, you'll be in trouble (just reload the game if the enemy is covering the only exit). It seems they didn't pay attention to this department. 3/10.Enemy AI: It's ironic that in the era of Artificial Intelligence we have to witness enemies with a super simple pattern: run into you and attack you straight forward. There's nothing close to variety or strategy here. The distraction system by using interaction with elements in the environment could have been way better. Not a lot of variety in monsters.I had to put sensitivity at 2 out of 10 because this game seems not to have been balanced for PC gamers. I have to put my mouse sensitivity at the lowest setting because it was close to impossible to aim or move the camera with precision.Graphics are truly fine. 7/10. But visual bugs are killing me (specially clipping).Very good plot/storytelling: Will give it 8/10. Tries to capture the original smell.Derceto is beautifully designed. This is one of the GREAT areas of the game. The art direction is incredible; I have to say this is the best thing. 10/10 for this.Sound design is great. I'll give it a solid 9/10.The music is fine, but it abuses jazz; I think a more "ambient" or "atmospheric" soundtrack would have benefited the game. Or even a revival of the old school games from Infogrames. 6/10.Collectibles feel unnecessary and like a "classic thing" that doesn't suit this game. I guess they realized, upon finishing the adventure, the little it has to offer, so this way they were able to add 40 extra items into an "empty" game.In the bug department:Some clipping issues that should have been solved by the year we are in.You can trap your character in several spots of the terrain. It seems the mapping hasn't been carefully tested.Some game crashes so far (not a lot, but 4 crashes in 6 hours... that's a lot).At the end of the day, my feelings are that this is another nail in the coffin of a great franchise because the games that were released after the original ones have been disappointing one after another. Really average. This franchise deserved a good development time, and it seems this game needed another year of cooking or some extra employees.OVERALL? 6/10 - I guess I'll have to wait another 32 years for a good remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Level design was quite good, with nice graphics and a story that was fairly entertaining, filled with interesting characters.The blending of lovecraftian horror elements, noir detective tropes and the early 20th century ambience ticked all my boxes for a good time.However it's important to notice that the gameplay felt pretty subpar for most of the time, with movement feeling janky at best, sometimes causing me to lose fights out of the sheer difficulty in positioning the player character properly, something that compounds in the often found tight spaces. _childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but with this game, I just had to.Because it`s way better then I expected it to be - the trailer was a little misleading in my opinion, I almost didn`t buy the game, because the trailer didn`t click with me - the game was different than what I expected after the trailer - and in a very good way.The graphics are awesome and stunning at times - the game oozes with atmosphere.Voiceacting, Sound and Soundtrack are great. Puzzels are not too easy but also not too challenging.Fighting mechanics are... ok - not the best, but good enough for this game.The only thing, that REALLY felt underdevelopt, was the "throwing"mechanic - you don`t really need it, so it`s no big issue, but it isn`t the best thought that went into this game.I loved the original Alone in the Dark - back in the day when it came out, and the remake has a kind of similar feeling - it even pays a little "homage" to the original at some point.Its at least a 7,5/10, maybe even a 8,5/10 - maybe it`s not for everyone, maybe it`s not mainstream, but I had a hell of time with it and enjoyed it very much.I would recommend Alone in the Dark - definetly when it`s on sale and even on full price.btw - there are 2 playable characters and as far as I can tell (first playthrough with Edward, now second playthrough with Emely), even if the "basic" gameplay stays the same - you`ll get different cutscenes, depending on with character you`ll choose - different enough, to justify playing the game with both characters.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't ready to be released. Despite it's impressive accessibility settings (including the ability to turn off handholding puzzles hints GoW Ragnarok needed), the game is overall lacking in quality.Melee combat is plain unacceptable. No manual or automatic lock on as you attack enemies, small enemies' hitboxes weren't taken into account when the whole system was designed and maybe one in every 4 swings you would actually hit them.At least 2 achievements are currently broken, optional/alternate objectives don't update/progress due to bugs.What seemed like a lead to an interesting alternate ending/plot point is just taken away from the experience, and if anybody wants to have that experience will have to wait a week or two for this to be fixed.The game feels like it was developed by a team of entirely first time developers and designers. _childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a game developed by Pieces Interactive and published by THQ Nordic and is a modern retelling of the 1992 classic game of the same nameThe game offers some really pretty graphics and a nice aesthetic, although some ugly textures here and there, it is pleasant all the same. The combat however is absolutely horrendous, worse than The Sinking City, in my opinion, and suffers from the usual cliches you find in horror games which throws my immersion right off - if you're looking to be scared or spooked, this isn't the game for youThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game with some repetitive puzzles and boring walking sections but an okay-ish game nonethelessThe story isn't that much interesting and I really tried to enjoy it but just didn't, I must say I preferred the manor sections over the other-world sections, as they didn't heavily rely on the broken, boring and clunky combat unlike the other-world areas and emphasised more on investigating and looking for clues And having the story from two different angles  have been interesting, but rather than actually running with it and making the two different characters experience two different stories, they just did the usual thing of having roughly the same story told just with different cutscenes and dialogue options, not what I wanted when they were marketing it as having two different stories toldAlone in the Dark overall, however, is a okay-ish "horror" game to play in short bursts but if you're expecting a coherent modern retelling to the 1990's classic, this ain't it...

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I used the recommend button, I'm more on the neutral side regarding the game.Yes, the game is a good survival horror, but after playing so many Resident Evil games, it feels a bit outdated.The story is fine, I enjoyed the main characters and every other character from the game. There are a great variety of locations with the mansion being the core one. The design of these locations are beautiful. The graphics are nice. The game is well-optimized I'd say. There were 2-3 times when the game were stuttering a lot, but a PC restart fixes that. Not sure why.Now, for the worst part of the game, the gameplay. The enemies are not that interesting and they are pretty repetitive. There are only two bosses in the game, both at the end of the game, one after another.There are only 4 guns, and you can't upgrade them, but considering the lack of variety of enemies, I think it is fine.Some of the puzzles were nice, but I didn't like that a lot of time the item to solve the puzzle was in the same room as the puzzle. The game is pretty short, you can beat it in under 8 hours, even if you try to collect everything. I played on standard and didn't die even once. You can play with two separate characters. Each character have separate cutscenes, a small exclusive mission and that's it. Basically the story doesn't go in parallel like in RE2. There are just two different stories depending on the character that you choose.I can't say that I didn't enjoy the game, so if you are a survival horrors fan, you should definitely play it.I still look forward for the Alone In The Dark 2 remake, if there will be one.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've gotten to and started chapter 3 which is roughly the halfway point and I have decided to write a short, but hopefully useful, review. First, lets mention performance. My system specs are an i9 7900x CPU, 32Gb RAM,7900xt GPU, NVME storage. I've been running the game at max setting with no upscaling at a native resolution of 3840x2160. The frame rates I have been getting in the game have been 80fps for the most part. However, some ares have seen my frames drop down to around 60fps for no apparent reason. This just shows that some areas of the game need some additional optimisation which I'm sure will happen at some point. The more egregious issue though is stutter. It's not consistent, but it does happen whenever you enter a new area/room and can overstay it's welcome. I have also had to restart a couple of times due to getting stuck on the terrain. All of these things can be fixed with patches, so if any of this will bother you, you should hold off on buying until it's been patched. Now onto graphics and game play. Graphically, the game looks about 5 years old. It is nice overall, with a nice atmosphere but has some very ugly spots and seems to be missing shadows in many places. Reflections look very UE4, which isn't saying much. Character models look basic. I would advise not to compare this game to something like Resident Evil or Alan Wake 2 when it comes to graphics and you'll be happy with the overall look. How the game plays though is where it will definitely be make or break for many. It plays like it's 10 years old. Your walking speed is slightly too slow, but you can jog everywhere. Stealth is just doing a half crouch and moving even slower. Combat has no feeling to it, especially the melee combat. Gun combat feels clumsy. When you look into what the developers were going for, that is a true spiritual recreation of the original Alone in the Dark, then I would say that they nailed it. Unfortunately that's also it's potential downfall, as what has been released feels old and dated, especially if one attempts to compare it to any other game within the horror genre released in the past 10 years or so. I will undoubtedly finish at least one play through of the game because I do think it has something worth playing, but there is no getting around the fact that is does feel and looking rather old and dated. It also feels like it was put together by a small studio with a very limited budget, which when you look, it was. Maybe it all makes sense.

_childDocuments_.review: Before Alone in the Dark became the legacy name it is, it was a video game my 11 year old brother installed on the computer. When the game began, I was so amazed - 3d  MY HOUSE???? The technology at the time was great even though it is quite humble in todays standards, even in the regards of the tech at the time.. BUT, the important thing was the vibe and feeling it created. The game unique in every aspect with the gameplay and the puzzles. I would open the door to a bathroom and suddenly some strange and eldritchian tub monster is killing me, I punch knight armor and now it is alive (I suspected it would). So anyways, nostalgia ramble aside I think the big question is: IS THIS GAME ALONE IN THE DARK, AND DOES IT GET THIS VIBE RIGHT?Well, yes, and greatly so! It currently (mid 2024) full price, and while it doesn't feel like a full price game as far as cinematics and razzle dazzle, the story, characters, gameplay, and puzzles all feel like a full price game. There were moments that scared me, moments where I was eagerly exploring the mansion, moments where I enjoyed the characters.. it was great. 8/10, on the border with a bullseye for what I wanted out of the game. There's new game plus to get the full story you must play both characters as they have their own journeys. All in all, I think users should go in with a A quality expection instead of AAA. This game really is on the exact path it needs to be. I would buy a sequel on launch, and I think the team did a 10/10 job, this franchise has been cursed and it is so nice to see something meaningful and not a name grab. You did it and it is appreciated, it brought me new nostalgia memories.
