_childDocuments_.review: The Good:-Fantastic atmosphere, music, and voice acting!-Many fun references and Easter eggs to the original AITD game and some Lovecraft lore-Puzzles are pretty fun and unique to the game, although a lot of them are fetch quests and keys-Fun gameplay and replayability!-Perfect for fans of AITD, detective noir and pulp stories, and Lovecraftian cosmic horror!The Not-So-Great / Room For Improvement:-Both characters have almost the exact same path to follow in the story save for a small section in Chapter 4 where each of them has a unique plot point. Carnby and Emily are completely different characters with different reasons for being in Derceto and I feel like their paths should've been more personalized, but perhaps this was due to time constraints or budgeting. -There's one default ending for both characters and the only difference is some dialogue. To get all the other endings, the player has to find and complete certain sets of collectibles and sometimes has to perform certain actions in the game AND in actual cutscenes - all of which requires having to do research to even know what needs to be done to achieve these endings; which spoils the surprise. I kind of wish that there were options in the game where players could choose what happens either through dialogue or opening secret doors/performing arcane rituals; this would keep the element of surprise while also adding more replay value for players!-There's a feeling that I'm on a tight track and can't explore very much, I mostly go from A to B.-All of the background characters have wasted potential; they've got such interesting designs and personalities and it was a disappointment that I couldn't interact with them more. Especially Baptiste, Lottie, Ruth, and MacCarfey; they had great potential for being partners. But I suppose the developers wanted to maintain the feeling of suspicion and isolation. -The game is a bit laggy, sometimes movement stutters to a pause and I worry it could cause a crash but thankfully it hasn't ever crashed on me. But I always make a point to save, just in case.++++I remember playing the original AITD back in the early 90s, it's very near and dear to me since I have a lot of memories associated with the game and the blocky 3D graphics, the eerie soundtrack, and the haunted house with so much history and intrigue. The puzzles, the death traps, the zombies and the mole/bear-monster things that could be karate kicked more efficiently than using the rifle with limited ammo...There are many horror games, but THAT game could stand on its own!Granted, these days it is considered very dated and the controls were clunky and hard to use; but it set the tone.I never imagined that it could receive the remake treatment after nearly 32 years, so of course I had to buy it and see how it was reincarnated using modern tech and gameplay standards. I may be biased, because I loved the original Alone In The Dark so much and this newer version is very ambitious, but I really enjoyed playing this game and I've replayed it to experience every single ending - at least five times. Oddly, the game never really got old for me, I do have some parts that I favor more than others, but it's a strangely dark cozy game if that makes sense. I also improved and got faster playing through each time as I started to memorize some of the puzzles and got a better sense of direction. So, this game does reward you for repeated visits. AITD here ticked so many boxes for me; it has a classic detective noir feel to it, with hints of pulp fiction, actual exploration in the Louisiana bayou, The French Quarter, and more! It also has a more tasteful interpretation of a mental hospital/retreat without shaming mental health or traumatizing the player, that's an added bonus. It does have some elements of horror, but it's more of a dread type of horror instead of scares, without actual jumpscares I'm also pleased to report. Another aspect I really enjoyed about the game is the use of a talisman to travel to other locations, it is probably the most authentic and magical feeling of being transported in a Lovecraftian setting I've seen so far!As for action in the game, I'm happy that the developers were able to find a good balance so that it retains that survival horror-like feel without it being an actual shooter type of game. The original game didn't have an emphasis on fighting, it was always about playing it smart and figuring out how to avoid or outrun enemies or disable traps, which might disappoint some action fans. But, hey, you get a cool Tommy Gun!I could go on about the game but I think I've left enough here to give players an idea of what to expect; I don't want to spoil any of the fun surprises!Alone In The Dark is a pretty good game, not perfect, but certainly NOT regrettable! If you're unsure, you can always wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: POST-COMPLETION REVIEW UPDATE: Yeah, I ABSOLUTELY recommend this game. At about 10 hours for Edward's campaign, I didn't feel that it ever overstayed its welcome once. I took my time looking for all of the collectibles in Edward's run, so I feel I will most likely spend about the same time with Emily's. The ending isn't anything that I saw coming at all and was a great climax to what I felt was already a very enjoyable experience. To add on the my original review, if you enjoy Lovecraftian horror, the classic Resident Evil trilogy and Alone in the Dark remake from the early 2000s, you definitely need to play this. I give it an 8.5/10!Probably about 4ish hours in so far and I highly recommend. I don't agree with many of the criticisms about the game other than occasional performance hiccups, personally. I think trying to compare this to a huge title like RE2 Remake or RE4 Remake is doing the game and yourself a disservice. This is a slow-burn horror set in an early-1900s, southern gothic Louisiana setting. It's much more akin to the original remake of Alone in the Dark than it is the remakes of RE2 and RE4. It has a ton of atmosphere, great music, a fever dream story, and has some genuinely tense interactions. The combat isn't horrible, however, I don't think this game's intention is to focus on flashy combat, but to focus on the looming dread in the silence between fighting whatever monster is about to attack Edward or Emily as to make you antsy to shoot or beat it to death as fast as possible before it kills you. If you like the original Resident Evil trilogy and Alone in the Dark titles, I HIGHLY recommend buying this.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I want to say that I think Alone in the Dark was a tough choice of a game to remake. The original AitD is built upon a very cliched concept: it's basically just a straightforward story about a haunted house. It's remembered for being innovative at the time, and for having some pretty memorable puzzles (it was much more of an adventure game, than an action one, after all), but looking at it from 2024, when we've been having a great horror renaissance for a few years now, it's just not that special. Later installments (like AitD2, 3 and eventually The New Nightmare) mostly were just trying to throw more cliches at AitD core to see what sticks (ghost pirates, Weird West, generic curses/witches/talismans, etc.).How do you remake something so basic? Well, I like to say it's not about the core idea, it's about execution. They could've played it straight and just make a horror game about a haunted house, and then try to elevate it with memorable monster designs, good scares, high production quality and, most importantly, doing . Because the main draw of the original AitD games was, really, how they were doing new weird things, offering unique challenges, how there was never a point where you could say "all right, I've figured this game out, I know what to expect now." This is not how things went.Alone in the Dark 2024 offers a pretty basic story about a haunted mental asylum and about madness, with a bit of a Lovecraftian theme. Unfortunately, there's very little depth or elegance to its narrative or presentation. Yes, the game is pretty, and I do like the new Derceto, but ironically, that's not where you spend most of the time. Most of the time you'll be walking through a series of mysterious locations created by the wild imagination of a madman. Well, that doesn't sound too bad, does it? Unfortunately, if upon hearing "imaginary horror worlds" you're expecting a lot of trippy visuals, shifting architecture and mind-bending surprises, you'll likely be disappointed. Instead, you'll travel through a bunch of fairly realistic places, occasionally populated with one of 4 possible enemy variants. It's not  per se, but there's also almost nothing surprising happening.The voice acting is great, and the noire tone permeating dialogue and cutscenes is very well doen and kind of captivating, though, but the story grows more and more confusing as it progresses—and I don't mean "confusing" as in "the protagonist is going mad and you don't know what is real and what isn't", I mean confusing as in "messy and haphazard."The combat is very much "we have Resident Evil at home" (which is ironic, considering the original AitD invented most things that RE1 was). It tries to follow in the steps of the recent RE remakes, but suffers from being extremely basic and a bit clunky on top. All encounters are just "run, point and shoot", with enemies that don't really require any unique tactics (and like I said, there are like only 4 variants). There's awkward stealth (that the in-game tutorial keeps reminding you about), that is very slow and almost never valid. There's also some run-of-the-mill melee combat with quickly deteriorating weapons, and also a lot of throwing things a-la The Last of Us—but  you can't carry the throwables on your person, instead having to throw them immediately upon pickup, which means almost every location in the game is mysteriously littered with rocks and molotovs.There's also a dodge button that I only found out about in the last couple of hours, by checking the controls—the in-game tutorials either don't mention it at all, or do it maybe once (despite always reminding me about sneaking). On top of this all, the movement doesn't feel particularly responsive, and the character can rather easily get stuck or stunlocked by enemies.Oh, and the final boss is basically .Finally, one of the biggest sins of the new Alone in the Dark is that it's just not scary. And yeah, maybe I'm not easily scared by games, but there are plenty that make me nervous or uncomfortable. To be truly scary a game has to surprise you and subvert your expectations, and this just never happens in AitD.Alone in the Dark 2024 is not a terrible game. It's pretty, it tries to do its own things, it feels like a labor of love, it features a lot of references to the older titles. But I cannot in good faith recommend it when we have games like Alisa , SIGNALIS , You Will Die Here Tonight  and many others that, while smaller in scale and budget, just  it.

_childDocuments_.review: The grandfather of all survival horrors is back! It's a bit of a bumpy ride in parts, but it's strengths certainly outweigh the flaws.+ A triumphant return to the setting, feel and themes and of the original game+ Interesting characters and witty writing+ Intriguing story with enough twists and turns to make you want to keep playing+ Fantastic soundtrack and sound design+ Beautiful visuals and varied environments+ Memorable setpiece moments+ A lot of care put in the optional narrative content. Instead of having to read you can have the game read the notes to you n the voices of the characters  - a huge for the visual impaired and something more games should do.- Several puzzles re-use the same mechanics, which becomes repetitive down the line- The item puzzles are very easy- No matter which lead character you choose the campaign is largely the same- The combat lacks depth and strategic options- The scares become predictableDespite all it's shortcomings I think it's definitely a title worth playing. It doesn't revolutionize the survival horror genre, but it doesn't have to. I thoroughly enjoyed the story, setting, the quirky characters and the wonderful soundtrack - so much that I was compelled to finish the game in one sitting - something that I very rarely find myself doing.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the originals but had heard of the games.What caught my attention with this game was an article in the news paper about Jody Comer and David Harbour playing as the main characters.I'm glad this appeared on my radar as its an incredibly well crafted horror game that tips its hat more than once to games from the 90s yet feels incredibly modern in its presentation.Visually the game looks amazing. The characters are a little stiff in their facial performance (but that is most games - it's just something you notice far more here because you are familiar with the actors likeness). The environments are so detailed and so well crafted. It feels very polished in that regard. The sound design is also incredible. Sound in this game adds a rich texture to every environment. You open an old iron gate and you can hear the springs clicking in the lock, or floorboards creek convincingly as you walk through an old house. It's something that really stood out to me in how much attention to detail there was and this combined with the fantastic visuals make this game incredibly immersive and incredibly eerie. It's not a jump scare game (although there are certainly a few moments). More of a slow psychological horror. I found myself just feeling a great sense of dread the deeper i got into the game. I love the backdrop of New Orleans and the time period this is set in. The actors performances are fantastic. The game mechanics revolve around you solviing investigations while exploring areas.The combat has been criticised but as you get into the game you realise it's absolutey fine. You have guns. You can pick up mele weapons that have limited durability. You can dodge. Then there are objects around the level that you can throw but can't carry around easily. This certainly feels a bit awquard until you are used to it - but essntially it means you need to keey your eyes peeled and take note of where these items are. Then when you encouter enemies you can run to one of these items and throw it at the enemy. Since the molotov sets them on fire it becomes an essential tactic. Once you understand it the initial jankiness turns into more of a strategy. I kind of like it. Especially as you get further on int the game and have encounters of multiple enemies at once.You can tell a huge amount of love and effort went into producing this title. For me it's an instant classic. Something i'll go back and replay a few months down the road. There are two main characters and you can do a playthrough with each that offer some differences to the narrative and dialogue.This isn't resident evil and nor is it trying to be. It's something else. Something more approachable and casual. I hope that the developers get a chance to flesh out their ideas and put out a sequel with expanded content and story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is why reviews ♥♥♥♥ out by main stream "game journalists" are not to be taken serious or of useful in any capacity. About 5 hours into the game so far and it is great (as far as I know, the game split into 2 scenarios and each scenario is 7~8 hours in length). Not a masterpiece but something memorable for sure. Not AAA quality but it doesn't feel cheap, definitely a solid AA experience. You can see the effort that the developers put into this game. Atmosphere is creepy. Ambience SFX and creepy BGM are great. The tense BGM everytime you have to sneak past enemies or something is happening or about to happen is just awesome and makes you nervous.The story is very interesting, with lots of voice-acted story notes to pick up. Everyone is doing a great job playing their characters. The pacing is great and it just hooks you into the story of a dark, mysterious and creepy paranormal mansion.Puzzles are not easy but not holding your hand either. They're interesting and do give you a challenge that makes you think before you solve.For a full old school style survival horror, I suggest playing it on the highest difficulty with old school style option (less environmental clues) where the game shines the most. I'm having a great time so far, a very solid AA game.What can make you dislike this game:+Movement & combat: -This game has an old style of survival horror combat feel to it, like 90s and early 2000s. It felt like I was back as a middle school kid playing RE code veronica. -The movement of the character feels pretty heavy like a real human with weigh. When you turn around in modern AAA games, your character is very snappy, like, doing a 180 quick turn and just run. In this game, when you turn, there is a short period of turn animation, plus heavy body moving sfx, so you can feel your character being sluggish. And when you run, your character doesn't burst into a sprint either, they slowly speed up into a run like real human. Many will call this "janky" but I think it's just design choice. I don't hate it but if you're too used to super soldier characters in modern FPS or stuff like RE4 Leon, it may put you off in this game+Game performance:-As of writing this, the game is pretty demanding in the VRAM department. If you have GPUs below 12 GB of VRAM, you will experience fps drop in some scenes. I didn't have fps drop in combat so it's not really a problem. When I don't have fps drop, my frame rate is pretty high and the fps drop episodes are also short (1-2 sec)-There is also something wrong with frame pacing. It doesn't feel smooth even  though my fps is 120. Lower the mouse sensitivity and aim sensitivity really help but there is definitely something weird going on+PricingThis game is great but not $54 great. It has good quality but still at AA level. So if you're buying this full price, you may feel like it's not worth it for the content it offered. This game is about $30~$40 top.

_childDocuments_.review: While being a fairly short game and pretty middling, even mediocre on certain fronts and the price of admission is a fair bit higher than it ought to be for a majority of people. Alone in the Dark is filled with a ton of spirit and passion for the Survival Horror genre and the original game of the same name. It's definitely worth a trip as a survival horror fan but people who aren't as into the genre or setting are not going to find it worth the price point.The story is best left hands off in this review, i will say that it is absolutely critical to the experience. It's a fun little horror story heavily invested into lovecraftian mythology. If you enjoy that sort of thing, it's definitely something you'll have a good time with. The voice acting is pretty solid across the board but rarely you'll find a few blemishes. The main duo of David Harbour as Detective Edward Carnby and Jodie Comer as Emily Hartwood are pretty solid. David in particular feels perfectly cast for a role like this. However what really shines is the setting. Decerto is a really cool place to actually explore and take in the atmosphere, it really does a lot of the heavy lifting of the story at times. It sets itself apart pretty solidly from similar romps into the time period and really adds to the Film Noir sort of vibe it's going for. If you like a sorta Supernatural Horror LA Noir vibe, you'll enjoy it. The game isn't strictly stuck in Decerto and there are some cool places you get to explore that definitely add to a few elements i've talked about before. The music is great as well. I can't get into other specifics without spoiling certain story elements but the game does a really solid job of keeping a mystery going, it just needed the rest of it to be better.This is where i gotta stop with the outstanding praise. I want to emphasis that i like this game, it's got a lot of heart but it doesn't redeem it's flaws. Outside of blemishes that i will talk about shortly, the game is trying to leaning into it being a Survival Horror game of old as opposed to new. If that's intentional or not, i don't know. I played on Hard without Hints. You die really really fast and your weapon aiming isn't consistent, melee combat feels sluggish at times if you don't take care of yourself, at first i thought this was intentional similar to games like Silent Hill or Call of Cthulhu. This isn't the case. The game breaks pretty heavily with excessive use of the dodge button, the iframes you have on the dodge are just too many. Melee Combat at the start feels very desperate but you will barely use it by the end of the game because your arsenal expands to the point that you never truly run out of ammo like you do early on in the game. The game does a good job of at least giving you SOMETHING to work with if you really are swimming without a paddle but this runs counter to Survival Horror as a genre. Ammo should be valued and it is for the most part at the start but by the end, it's just too much. It makes everything much too easy. Alone in the Dark is a very easy game but in equal measures comfy. It's like sitting down in your bed and reading dracula but lacks that gameplay tension that it's inspiration draws from. The original Alone in the Dark was absolutely brutal in it's gameplay and wasn't afraid to kill you on the slightest mistake, it makes sense why it really did work back then. Puzzles. The game has a fair amount of them and without hints they do indeed sometimes lend a cerebral challenge or require investigating what clues you do have but there are just as many that are fairly brainless. Decerto itself feels like a place that gets more and more closed off as you continue on through it's halls, it feels less and less focused as you go on which is a pretty huge detriment. Finally, the playtime. You will all likelihood, beat this in under 9 hours on a first playthrough. There are secrets and story shift to encourage replays on both characters but it's just too little compared to games that do this much better.It's a lack of consistency i have issue with. It doesn't feel consistently challenging the whole way through and gets easier as you go to the point that it completely deflates the tension the game is going for as a horror and then ramps back up with the climax almost to a jarring 0 to 60 in 30 seconds sort of way. It definitely has it's moments, it definitely has parts where it shines but ultimately it makes Alone in the Dark a very mediocre game with regularly glimpses of true promise. I can't recommend this game for most people at this price point unless you're an absolutely diehard survival horror fan, love Alone in the Dark or really want a fun lovecraft story to play through. In that case, it's a recommendation. I wish i had a mixed recommendation option. However if this price was eventually discounted at say £20 to 25. I could absolutely recommend it for even lukewarm fans but the price point is just too damn high.

Along those lines I think I'm one of the few people who always saw Emily as the protagonist and read the intro text. Edward was a snake who called himself "the reptile." _childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying that my experience with the original Alone In The Dark is minimal, so I can't compare this remake to the original. The game has some performance issues in the form of stuttering when loading new areas. I played it on both windows 10 and linux. On windows 10, the stutters were noticeably worse.You play as either Edward Carnby or Emily Hartford and you goal is to find her uncle Jeremy who's in Derceto, a sort of upscale mental institution. The game follows Capcom and Konami's shift into the third person, over the shoulder perspective over the classic tank controls. This game can be divided into two parts that you will switch between. Exploring Derceto gives you the more open, survival horror experience of looking for keys and other items to progress. While in Derceto you will experience little to no combat. Periodically, you will enter a kind of Silent Hill "other world" that is linear and you will encounter monsters. I find this to have a pretty good pace. Exploring Derceto is the most fun, in my opinion, and the "other world" segments don't overstay their welcome so there's a good balance of both. There's no inventory management, however your resources are capped. You can only carry a certain amount of healing items and ammo for each weapon.Now I'll go through some problems. This game has a fair amount of jank. While sprinting, I frequently got stuck on furniture and other items decorating the environments. Sometimes I was able to use the dodge feature to get myself unstuck, and other times I had to reload my save. I experienced a bug with audio glitching and crackling after the game's first update that was solved by loading an earlier save which luckily wasn't very far from my last one. Combat is hit or miss. You have an array of weapons including fire arms and melee weapons. The latter are found frequently as they break after a few hits. There are throwable items like bricks and molotav cocktails. You hold Q to pick them up and aim, otherwise they get thrown instantly. This is a problem as enemies are fairly fast and it's cumbersome to have to slowly turn yourself around to throw things. This is exacerbated by the fact that there is no quick turn. The enemies themselves are very bland and samey. There are four kinds. The first two are humanoid and they're fought the same way and act similarly. The third is a weak, but annoying flying type. The last and worst is a small spider looking thing that takes WAY too much ammo to kill and deal a ton of damage. Finally, the final boss of the game is frustrating. I should mention that I played on hard mode, so this may not be a problem in lower difficulties. The boss is large and it's second phase is inside a decent sized room. It periodically spawns far too many enemies. If you can't kill them quickly, they'll overwhelm you and you will get cornered. Occasionally the boss gets too close and will not allow you to see anything around you.In conclusion, it's an enjoyable game but it's not without its quirks and frustrations. I would recommend it to any fans of survival horror

The beautiful graphics; the thick mystic detective atmosphere reminiscent of Conan-Doyle and Alan Poe; amazing acting performance of everybody, especially the main cast of David Harbour (I wish he could play Carnby at least a few more times), Jodie Comer, Paul Mercier and Glory Joy Rose. In order to get this again, I have to start over entirely and "follow this walk through, step by step" per the game devs. Instead of fixing their game, and one of the most recurring issues this game has seen, we're told to pull up a walk through and follow it step by step to ensure we are doing exactly what they intended we do--meanwhile, the actual prompts from the game don't give any information regarding this and do nothing to guide players to ensure it doesn't happen.I do NOT recommend this unless you genuinely plan to have a walk through up and running for your entire save to ensure you do not accidentally grab an item that was available to grab in chapters 1-2, but you're not supposed to grab until Chapters 3-4 in a specific order, so you don't end up soft locked and having to restart. _childDocuments_.review: This game was given to me as a gift for my Birthday, and frankly - Can't say enough good things about it. Like it so much that I am making a review now just to make sure others see it and give it a shot. SO ! Here is a short Pro and Con list.  Pros:The game FEELS like it should. While the 3rd person movement is not near as clunky as the original Alone in the Dark, there is a small level of jank that makes absolute sense. It belongs and it is not punishing, at least not at the start.The Voice acting with the notes and characters are well done ( minus a minor gripe...Looking at you Hartwood! ) . While its huge and different from the original, it stands on its own as what Alone in the Dark should be. The story driven atmosphere is even more so amazing now as it was years ago. As someone who normally just skims the side lore and goes on his way, I found myself putting down the controller and letting the notes be read to me in cinematic flare. Its not Alone in the Dark A New Nightmare or the crap movie that was made as a cash grab / tax breakThe Music - I could gush on that opening menu theme forever. The games sound and everything just push and pull everything where it needs to be. And when you find a certain tree at the start of the game that beaters of the original game KNOW what the heck it is? The sounds around that are. fuggin. amazing.The Cons:Granted, I am just a 1 hour and change into the game but I can gripe about a few things.The Spirit of the Original game is here but is lost ever so slightly. While the original game had its fixed items in fixed spots and a whole house to explore, it is replaced with random loot locations for ammo and booze ( or nothing at all )  and with some new locations you travel between that will allow you access to other rooms and key items to help you explore the main house. Its a little odd but its minor in the grand scheme of thingsThe character selection intros. Hearing a small quip about the characters ( i say small but it was like a 2 min long voiced dialog the characters voiced themselves )  when I was making my choices just made us understand the characters a little bit more.  Another minor gripe though!Emily Hartwood has no southern drawl! Big ooofsters! In the original game with her intro you could hear that southerner twang, but now she lacks that and since they do a lot more talking this time around I already miss what it could have been. But again, another tiny gripe. Sound Volume: At times when i find an item and your character says something ( In my case Carnby ) its like he is a mile away talking to you, I am unsure if me turning down the master volume did this , but still everything else is at a decent volume and my sound settings are untouched other than the master volume so things should balance out but it seems the speech is just that much quieter.  Final Minor Gripe though!So far, all my cons are just water under the bridge. I havn't had huge frame drops on Epic settings and my PC is far from top of the line, and it runs smooth like buttah! _childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark 2024 is a thrilling return to the classic survival horror genre that delivers an unforgettable experience. From the moment I started playing, I was captivated by its perfect blend of spookiness, challenging puzzles, and compelling storytelling.The atmosphere is incredible, with eerie environments and a haunting soundtrack that kept me on edge throughout the game. The developers have masterfully crafted a world that feels both menacing and immersive, making every shadow and sound a potential threat.The puzzles are well-designed, offering just the right amount of challenge without becoming frustrating. Each puzzle felt like a natural part of the story, enhancing the overall experience rather than detracting from it. The balance between exploration, puzzle-solving and combat kept the gameplay engaging and varied.Story-wise, Alone in the Dark 2024 holds a gripping narrative that unfolds in unexpected ways and shocked me a few times. The characters are well-developed, and their personal stories add depth to the main plot. The game's pacing is excellent, keeping me hooked from start to finish.Overall, Alone in the Dark 2024 is a must-play for fans of the genre. _childDocuments_.review: Alone in The Dark (2024) is a game destined for cult status. It's design is old school, it's rough around the edges but has had clear loved poured into it by a passionate team.Let's go over some important con's:.It's combat is extremely simple, at times I wished that there were just more enemies to feel like a threat..It's pretty jank at times, while I didn't encounter any stuttering or crashes on both my playthroughs, my character got caught on scenery about six times total. Most of the time a few dodges forced me out but most of the time it was a reload..The price point, it's a very pricey game for what it is. Your millage my vary but I'd suggest waiting for a discount.Now with those out of the way, I can now explain why this game has wormed it's way into my brain like the voices of an old god..The atmosphere of both Derecto and the many unique locations you'll explore are second to none, complemented by a fantastic score. Doom Jazz needs to become it's own genre at this point!.Jodie Comer, David Harbor and the rest of the cast put in great performances, but special praise I feel should be given to Jodie Comer playing such a traumatised and broken character in Emily. Her story goes to some dark places that really affected me.The plot goes deep, if your ready to scour the game for documents and clues (each read by the writer), you'll build up a tangled web of lovecraftian horror beneath the surface of this detective story.I'm so happy with this game, with a bit more polish from a clearly talented team, I'm sure we'll see more people enjoying what is a labor of love and reverence for the 1992 original.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of classic survival horror games and can get this game at $30 or less, I think you'll enjoy your time with this game, but it's a very short, limited game with nearly no replay value. My first playthough took about 6 hours with exploration, and I spent another couple hours as the alternate character. I don't want to say much as to spoil the game, but the atmosphere/art design and lovecraftian elements are great, the mansion was well designed, there's a good variety of locations, and the combat has just enough to make it feel more modern while still retaining a clunky feeling(I mean this as a compliment).David Harbour is...fine, if a little flat at times, and if they could've gotten the game's production cost down and lowered the retail price by not hiring him, they should've done that. Once you beat the game, you do unlock a NG+ option(which was added as their last update), but otherwise there are NO unlocklables outside some collectibles that track between every playthrough. No new modes, weapons, costumes, upgrades, filters, anything. This is a HUGE letdown and practically kills this game's longevity. For many, this will be a one-and-done playthrough, as the second character, while having different dialogue and interactions with certain characters, is practically identical.Still, if you're a fan of the genre, and don't mind a journey back to simpler time, this is a well made game, for what it is. Just don't expect a lot of it.

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing similar to the original is the name.  It's a totally different story, a very convoluted one.  The graphics are pretty nice (though VERY unoptimized), the sound quality is really good (quite uneven, some parts of the game/sound effects are arbitrarily louder or quieter than others).  Some of the puzzles have very bad logic and require you to think in a very obscure way.  The exploration is nice and interesting.  The map could have been awesome if they would have made your character in the map menu an arrow, instead of a dot so you could see which direction you're facing, therefore the map is terrible and confusing.Thank God the combat system is secondary, because it is ABYSMAL.  Absolutely God awful combat.  Clunky and awkward, and your character always feels "heavy" like you're trying to run in a pool, where the harder you try, the worse it gets.  Both the controller and M/KB sensitivities are weird and are either too sensitive or not sensitive enough, which makes combat that much more of a chore.  Headshots don't seem to be any different than body shots and picking up a throwable object renders your sensitivity so slow, that if you're not facing the enemy directly when you pick up a throwable, you've left yourself open to getting hit a bunch by the enemy.  You can't put down throwables either.  You either have to use them, or lose them.There is no inventory system, infinite resources, which makes the game lame and doesn't impose caution, or logical thinking, you can just "Rambo" everything and still be rewarded with plenty more ammo.The character models are quite bad, they look VERY dated.  Maybe they should have spent more resources on the game itself instead of the voice actors.  I would much rather have a game with great mechanics and bad voice acting rather than good voice acting with terrible game mechanics, and that's basically what this game is.  No more than a barely playable "Book on tape".

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is an interesting, if a bit shallow, survival horror experience that's missing some conventions of the genre. There's no crafting, no inventory management and the combat is very simplistic. If you're hoping for modern Resident Evil-like experience, you'll probably be disappointed because combat isn't really the focus here. There's a much greater emphasis on exploration and puzzle-solving. What AitD does really well is world-building and atmosphere. Exploring Derceto Manor and interacting with its eccentric inhabitants is a lot of fun and you'll visit a surprising number of locales through your playthrough(s). The story is engaging, if a bit confusing, and won't offer the kind of closure that some people want. However, that's pretty standard for Lovecraftian narratives so it's better to just enjoy the ride and not worry so much about the destination. Playing through as both Edward and Emily will provide more insight into the characters and lore, as each character has unique dialogue, cutscenes and a couple of exclusive levels.Overall, I enjoyed Alone in the Dark, though it almost feels like more of an adventure game than a survival horror game. That said, playing on the highest difficulty does provide a lot of tense moments, as resources are much more scarce and enemies much more dangerous. Either way, if you're into Lovecraft and enjoy creepy adventure games, AitD should be right up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark is a what I would call "Survival Horror Light".There is no item management, no need to conserve ammo or healing items and no need to avoid enemies (at least on Standard difficulty). But with its interesting setting and characters, great environments and awesome sound design Alone in the Dark is still a good game that never gets boring during the 7-8 hour playthrough. I encountered only very minor bugs and stuttering so in this regard I cant complain. Combat is slightly clunky but otherwise fine.My main issue with the game is that its too easy on Standard difficulty. The combat is no challenge and the puzzles are generally rather easy (and too similar), although a few of them are a bit more challenging. There is unfortunately no need to conserve ammo since as soon as you start wasting it, the game spawns ammo everywhere so you will never run out. As I already mentioned, its a "Survival Horror Light" experience , not really comparable to something like RE1 Remake or Tormented Souls. If you are looking for a challenge this is not your game.There is certainly room for improvement but overall I had a fun time during my stay at Derceto Manor and I hope there will be a DLC or even a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an Unreal Engine 4 and there is no shader pre-compilation step. So guess what? Shader compilation stutter, even on high-end hardware. It's minor, but it's all over the place. Considering all the release delays, considering that pretty much every other dev learned to add the pre-compilation step, it's just atrocious. The stutter is very typical: you get it when traversing and coming into a new scene, even if it's very light on graphical detail. You run around, you come back to the same place - no stutter, as the shaders are already compiled (on the fly, which is causing the stutter). You go into a new area - stutter again. I've went from highest to lowest settings, the stutter is there. My specs are way beyond the officially recommended ones, the same PC can run Avatar at 120 FPS and maximum settings. Smooth AF. Needless to say, Avatar looks much better in general.Furthermore, you can run the game at higher frame rates (say, 120), but real-time rendered cutscenes are locked to 60. Not ideal. There is stutter in the cutscenes, too. Not in all of them, but in some for sure.Oh, and here is another horror. It's possible to change keybindings, but they are limited, reflecting the number of buttons on a controller. So, you can switch weapons with 1, 2 and 3, but for the fourth weapon, you have to hold 1 instead of just using 4. Even if remapped, you have to hold the button. Same goes for opening a map: you can't have a separate map button, instead you have to hold the button that opens the "investigation" menu. So little effort went into this port.Just a bit of reminiscing. I've played the original Alone in the Dark in 1992. It was the best game I've ever played at that point. It looked amazing and boasted a game design that I haven't seen in any game before and not in many after. It was very Dark Souls by design: you were dropped in the middle of a horror, and there was not artificial guidance. The game was non-linear and you could finish it in several ways. The puzzles were clever and a lot of the things were missable, making the game fun to replay. I've played the same game many years later, and it still looked and played great, even though low-poly models started to look a bit funny. It was still an immersive and scary experience. The 2024 version is not a remake or a remaster, it's a very loose reimagining. It's also not even close to be as impressive as the 1992 game was back in the day. The design is very limited - you are often locked into a very linear path. Puzzles are a joke. Combat is clunky.Update: just a few hours after the release, there was a patch sized over 2 GB. Didn't fix any of the problems above. You know what it did? Locked away the paid DLC which accidentally slipped into the initial release.Alone in the Dark is priced at EUR 53.99, which includes a temporary release discount of 10% from the EUR 59.99 price. For this money you can get either a brand new better game, and a lot of them are being released around the same time - Dragon's Dogma 2, for example - or a bunch of better older games.OK, Horizon Forbidden West just came out. Priced at EUR 59.99. This game runs at all maximum settings at 4K and 120 FPS. No dips whatsoever. It looks photo-realistic. It's not the best game out there. I've played it on PS5 a while ago and got a bit bored, as I thought the writing too mediocre, but it's definitely the pretiest, that's why I bought it again, this time on PC. So, priced the same as Alone in the Dark, looks several times better, works significantly smoother, has a bigger world and more things to do...

_childDocuments_.review: So, I just finished the game.I really enjoyed it at the beginning, but the more I played, the less I liked it. Let me summarize my impressions, keeping in mind that the game has a AAA price tag of 59.99 Euros. I'll list everything important to me in a game, from top priority to least priority.Story -> 7/10.I can't say it's an exceptional story, but it's good enough. Honestly, it's the only thing that kept me engaged in the last two chapters. Otherwise, I would have dropped the game.Gameplay -> 5/10.Atmosphere & Characters -> 7/10.Technical State & Optimization -> 6/10.I didn’t encounter any bugs, but the controls and combat feel pretty clunky.With an RTX 4070M, 32GB of RAM, and an AMD 7745 8-core processor, I was averaging 40-50 FPS. Honestly, the graphics aren’t impressive. The locations are small, and the graphics are average. I don’t see any reason why the performance should be this poor.Level Design -> 4/10.Graphics -> 5/10.For a AAA game, the graphics are very average.My overall score would be 5.6/10.Unfortunately, I can’t recommend this game at its current price. It feels like a good indie game with a small budget, not a AAA title. Its real value is more in the range of 10-20 Euros.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to see what THQ could bring to the table after the disaster that was Inferno and Illumination, but I think it is safe to say the franchise is at this stage... cursed... or in need of a developer that has a larger budget.The game drops frames rapidly from one room to the next, even with DLSS on, it can drop anything from 30 to 60 fps, and cut-scenes can be a hot mess as it stands on launch. So optimisation is clearly an issue, at least for now, which I'm sure can be patched up in time. Running into my first combat encounter, I ended up trapped down the corridor and had to restart, which was quite annoying as I couldn't simply navigate around the enemy. It does feel like a few mechanics have been added since the initial release of the trailer, and they don't quite fit right, for example, running down the stairs. (you'll see what I mean) The game does look stunning, and it does remind me of a third person Resident Evil 7 set in the 20's, albeit this is essentially a remake of the original game. The sound design is quite nice, some parts reminded me of the early AITD games, and some tones in the music reminded me of the New Nightmare entry which is always a personal favourite. Sadly as it stands, I can't recommend this game with the issues from launch.

_childDocuments_.review: Very mild recommend, the game is split up between exploration and combat zones without much overlap. The sudden transitions between these two can be cool, but overall the combat feels really bad, I'll go into why that is but if you're down for exploring the mansion with light puzzles and a story that has cool concepts with a weak execution, then go for it.I know it's Survival Horror and believe me, my expectations for combat were low, but oh man. The three ways of dealing damage were guns, which work ok despite some astoundingly bad collisions at times, melee, and environmental thrown objects. The melee involves getting close to the enemies and the poor hitboxes aren't exclusive to the gunplay, I would constantly get stuck on enemies or the terrain, exacerbated by the enemies pushing me. There isn't great feedback for a heavy or light hit (the difference is holding the attack button without a clear "fully charged" animation) and I got stunlocked by enemies more than a few times. For the environmental throwables, they're a cool idea that do appreciable damage, the incendiary ones especially, but are positioned oddly. Once you pick them up you're stuck in slow "throwing" state that can only be broken by throwing the object and thus breaking it. The notification for interacting with these is also really particular and there were many occasions where I could not get the prompt to show despite staring an object down. The enemies are also pretty bland, there's either dudes that are straight forward or bugs. The bugs later on have ridiculously high health and I was convinced it was a bug itself.I won't go too far into the story,  but it's psychological and takes a lot of literary inspiration that it doesn't really do much with. I played the Carnby campaign and his backstory really stood out as being a bland take on a predictable formula. The rest of the plot fares better, but has better ideas than execution. On paper, Silent Hill meets pulp horror sounds perfect, but outside of cool environments it doesn't add up to much. Voice acting is hit or miss, though normally the former. The lead 2 actors are a big exception, David Harbour sucks in this and he looks dopey, I didn't like playing as him.My favourite moments were like Song Of Horror lite, if that adventure game-style aspect appeals to you and you're ok appreciating a framework for what it attempted rather than what it amounted to then go for this game, probably on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than I expected. It has a pretty good grasp of survival horror. I expected something that would eventually devolve into a big dumb action game and so far it hasn't done that.There are a few negatives that I think anyone should be aware of.First, the combat is incredibad. I'm not upset that they don't let me blow the enemy away like I'm Rambo. I'm upset that you can't transfer momentum into enemies while moving. So it's not only possible, but common, to get trapped against a wall if you get hit once in a confined area. If things like this had just been re-contextualized (for instance the enemy grapples you or pins you to the wall) it would work really well with the fact that it's a horror game. But since it feels and looks unintentional, and all you can do is sit there and wait to get hit a few more times, it really undermines any dread that could come from those kinds of situations. It's not "Oh my god, if I get hit here I'm done for." it's "Oh my god, I missed. Just kill me already ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."Secondly, some of the puzzles have very ?-pilled design. Without spoiling anything, there are some puzzles that take less time to brute force than it takes to find all the clues to get past them. Like maximum time to brute force of like 90 seconds. 6^3 combinations at a try rate of 3 per second is like ~70 seconds and that's if you have to try literally every possible combination. You can just cycle through them by flicking the dial without even paying attention so it's even possible to just get the answer accidentally without trying. There's no reason to look for the clues. That really doesn't feel intentional.Lastly, this is not a negative for me, but it may be for some people; This game is a goshdarn book. There are alot of documents to read and alot of them are very important. There are voice-overs for all of them if you don't feel like reading but there is like 20 pages of mandatory text in the first 1hr of the game. I like it. but I know that some people may hate it.All-in-all this is a good game. It's much better than I expected or hoped for.Looking forward to more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's talk about it.Pros:- Atmosphere is great- Puzzles are challenging and rewarding- Game looks beautiful- The story is.. very interesting. For sure keeps you playing- Obviously the live actors are awesomeCons:- I have a new gen gpu and this game still runs poorly. Very framey an stutters.- The frames and stutters on the boat level are almost game breaking- The monsters on the boat level phase through walls and can attack you- The controls for combat are pretty clunky. Best not use melee and keep things at a distance.- The controls in general are clunky and hard to get used to.- Price tag for game, considering all above listed issues- There are 3 or 4 total variations of enemiesOverall:This is fun. It is. If you love survival horror and are looking for another title this is exactly that. The atmosphere is cool and the live actors are great. The puzzles are  challenging with not too many clues. I fear, however, if you are not a die hard fan of survival horror, you will not be happy. The reason being, there is A LOT you have to overlook even though this is fun. The poor combat, clunky controls, and constant stuttering is almost too much to deal with. On one level in particular, it got me killed 3 times because enemies were floating and phasing through walls. This, coupled with the lack of variety of enemies, and the full $60 price tag? Would not recommend. The game functions like a $30 game. If this was the price, I would have had no issues. Helldivers 2 was $40, and even though in a completely different genre, the point remains. I cannot see how the price is justified for all the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: (mini-review).Alone in the Dark is a re-imagining of the venerable, 1992 cult horror game.  Set in the early 1940s, against an Art Nouveau, Call of Cthulhu-inspired backdrop, Alone in the Dark uses the threat of foreboding, cosmic cataclysm to generate much of its anxiety and dread.  The game has atmosphere, unsettling monsters, a unique visual style and two well-performed lead protagonists.  The graphics, are good, if albeit plain and the game, while stuttery at times, is, for the most part, stable.  Gun play is good, melee is a bit of a miss and the bosses/puzzles are a combination of both.  Interestingly eerie environments abound.That said, be aware that Carnby's play through covers everything you need to know about the title and Hartwood's own play through not only adds little in the way of new content but it is also filled with woke narratives that detract from the story. Ultimately, the game feels like a AA Resident Evil-inspired remake of a comparable survival horror IP and its 10 hour campaign is well-worth 15-20 dollars. To date, the developer Pieces, has has been shuttered by THQ Nordic.  Don't expect additional content or additional Alone in the Dark remakes any time soon.A nice, solid little diversion in the same vein as the Resident Evil and Silent Hill remakes.7.5/10.Buy on sale.

And the most important... this game has no HORROR inside, it doesn't have screamers, it doesn't have horrific monster design, it doesn't have feeling of the last medkit and last bullet in your weapon.The puzzles are stupid, the fights are stupid, I am stupid that was waiting it so much all this time. _childDocuments_.review: I run a 3070ti with a trash CPU and at 1440p on High settings I've maintained close to 100 fps with minor frame hitching around new areas and cutscenes. Negative performance reviews are overblown. The game is quite polished, playable, enjoyable, graphically sound. The real thing that needs a patch will be object collision, as the player model has a tendency to get stuck on furniture, particularly in combat.Other than those issues, the writing is better than Resident Evil, frankly. This story is just more interesting. The voice acting is really good all around, the puzzles are great. It's shaping up to be short, sweet, and the extra gameplay filters and 8-bit graphical options were frankly worth the cost, I can't wait to replay the game in full 8-bit. In addition, the Southern Gothic charm shines through with an EXCELLENT soundtrack, campy noir, and a fun setting in Decerto Manor. It weaves a tight modern horror game with very obvious retro influences I really enjoy and which do set it apart from other modern action-horror titles.I would have liked more focus on hardcore survival horror, as it is definitely more of that creepy action game (think Alan Wake 2) than a more horror-influenced, Dead Space-esque experience, but I don't think the game loses much as a result.7/10, I personally find it worth the full price, but think if you can snag it in the $39.99 range you'll get the most bang for your buck and it'd justify the purchase outright.

Return to mansion.Puzzles are okay - most of them don't require item finding and just figuring something out on the spot. Wanted to finish the game, but I just could not get motivated to complete it even though I am 80% of the way through. Zero inventory management. Hardly any exploration. _childDocuments_.review: first...the issues. its a bit buggy. i often found myself stuck on object geometry like cars, street carts etc. and unable to move which can only be fixed by death or reloading. Melee weapons often fail to switch and sometimes the game thinks you already have one when trying to pick one up, meaning you need to die, reload or progress to a cutscene to be able to pick another melee weapon up again. Hit registration is questionable at best...Some enemy animations are broken and can create a bit of unfair difficulty (mostly lookin' at you spider/water flea enemy...) Loading into new areas and returning to Derceto causes brief frame rate drops. And lastly, sometimes after reloading a save, items lose their interaction icons but can still be interacted with. this can usually also be fixed by reloading, dying or progressing to a cutscene.In spite of all of that, the game was insanely fun with an interesting and off the wall story, a unique cast of characters and well detailed environments. It's well worth getting into, even with it's existing issues. I had a completion time of about 9 1/2hrs with Carnby on normal and there's still another character for me to play through the game with.TLDR; Game is good,but has some annoying bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: After watching many a negative review on release day i hopped into Alone in the Dark with some worry as to what i might find ahead, but much to my delight Alone in the Dark is an excellent noir/lovecraftian horror which with time i believe will become a beloved cult classic. I completed my first  play through as Detective Carnaby portrayed by David Harbour of stranger things fame and he did a truly excellent job with voice acting and adding some extra quality to the character. The story though short is very well told with engaging characters and some very well designed puzzles. The gameplay is equal parts the evil within, silent hill with a dash of feeling like Indianna Jones in some parts of the game. I did speed through the game a bit clocking in my first character completion at about 6 hours, but this was 6 hours of all killer no filler and i hopped straight in again to check out Emily's perspective who was barely seen during my outing as detective Carnaby.Performance throughout my play was flawless and i thought the game looked beautiful in parts. Enemy encounters is where the game does falter with some janky melee combat and the throwables were very poorly designed in how you utilise them, but as a huge fan of old school games like the silent hill series and games of that era i could let this slide. A great game that i see myself coming back to again and again, particularly one for my fellow horror heads out there.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the 3rd attempt at rebooting the classic Alone in the Dark franchise. In my opinion, this is the best attempt at doing so. The game pulls obvious inspiration from the recent Resident Evil games, which is ironic because those games took inspiration from the original Alone in the Dark. It features 3rd person gameplay that combines exploration, puzzle solving and combat through a large mansion called Decerto in 1930s Louisiana. The story is based on the original Alone In the Dark, but the lore has been heavily expanded upon. The game isn't as polished as the bigger budget Resident Evil games, but that's OK. Overall, I'd recommend this for fans of the Alone in the Dark franchise and survival horror games in general, or those looking for a Resident Evil style game set in the 1930s. I'd also recommend picking this up to support the developers, who shut down due to the game's low sales. This was a game made with a lot of care and attention, and they deserve our support.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I'm really liking this so far. I love the setting and the spooky old mansion. This game oozes ambiance! I also like how apologetically old school it is in it's design and controls. Reminds me of the survival horror games of the past. I'm a firm believer in the maxim that horror games don't always need the best controls (like Silent Hill 2 for example) and this seems to hold true here too. The movement and combat is pretty janky, but that's alright for me so long as the story keeps me entertained... and it is! The acting is actually really good, better than what you usually get in games, suffusing the characters with plenty of, well, character!I'll update this later if my opinion changes, but for now I'm really glad this series finally gets a respectable release.Edit: I'm mostly through the game and I want to update my review. I'm still really liking it, but it's definitely one of those games where some things came out much better than others. First off, the things this game gets really right is it's story & characters, it's graphics, it's setting & mood, and it's voice acting.While graphically, it's not the most advanced game out there, the art design looks great. They particularly succeed in the little details. Every level is packed with little inconsequential details that really add depth to the game. For instance, when I go into a new room in the mansion, I love walking around and seeing all the little stuff they added to help flesh out the characters that live there. Someone really thought about every corner and it shows.As far as the story goes, I'm loving it. It's a wonderful tribute to the Cthulhu Mythos. The writer (who for the record is the same guy who wrote SOMA) really did his research. I particularly loved that he name drops the Unaussprechlichen Kulten, my favorite of all the fictional books that inhabit the Cthulhu world. Furthermore, the character writing is particularly strong. At first I was a bit put off by the changes made to Edward Carnby as I remember him looking more like how he did in the original AitD trilogy, but the voice acting of David Harbour brought me around. As a matter of fact, none of the voice acting for any of the characters are phoned in. They really landed a solid cast.SPOILERS Now, the parts that this game could have improved on... The game itself is pretty basic and I get the feeling that they ran out of time on a lot of stuff. For instance, the first time you run into the Dark Man it's kind of a joke. He just sort of wanders about aimlessly. You can just run right on past him with very little consequence. If you stop moving and just let him look at you, your health starts dropping, but you'd have to intentional mess up to have this happen. I have to figure that they wanted to do something more here because the level design suggests there was to be a game of cat and mouse, but alas they were unable to provide it.There's also a surprising lack of enemy diversity and the enemies that there are get repeated quite often. And they aren't really scary. And they don't really seem to have much to do with the world itself. For a game that so frequently makes use of the Cthulhu Mythos, you'd think they could do a little better here. At least something that resembles a Mi-Go makes an appearance later in the game.Really, it feels like the gameplay design team ran out of time and just had to patch it together at the last moment. This kind of thing is frustrating because you can see the indications of a potentially much more elaborate game, but alas it was not to be. It has me wondering what we could have gotten if the team had another year.All and all, I still strongly recommend this game. Yeah, there's a lot it could have done better, but I can't say that I'm not having fun. Sure, there was clearly a much bigger game planned, but what there is is a still a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: My daughter and I honestly enjoyed the game.  I've always liked David Harbour as an actor and felt, in my opinion, he did a great job with his character.  We didn't think the story was very gripping though.  I wish they would have stuck with the original story of Jeremy Hartwood.  I didn't like how he was actually still alive and how we "chased" him within his own mind.  In the original game, Derceto was built by a pirate named Ezechiel Pregtz who heavily studied the occult and extend his life unnaturally.  He was eventually killed and his spirit lived within a giant tree in a cave beneath the mansion.  Jeremy Hartwood had killed himself in order to prevent Pregzt from possessing him.   From what I remember, Pregzt then targeted Carnby.  I found the original story to be far more interesting.  This remake attempts to be more psychological but at no point did I feel confused as to what was going on nor was I vested in the story.  I finished the game because I just wanted to finish it.  I do definitely recommend the game when its on sale though.  Pretty short.  Only took me 17 hours and I'm not good at these games.  A good player could probably finish it a little quicker.  If you're looking for something to keep you busy for a couple of hours here and there and you're into psychological horror, it's a good choice.

Liked everything else though.

_childDocuments_.review: While I would’ve preferred it fixed camera perspective, there is really a lot here that screams classic survival horror seasoned for the modern pallet.Combat.I personally am enjoying the not quite right feel to the combat. It does a beautiful job of making you feel anxious and unsure of the outcome of Indie individual altercation, which makes you fear even the possibility of an encounter with something dangerous lurking around the corner. I’m working on my camouflage belt in Krav Maga, but even as a white belt, we were introduced to weapons training: firearms, knives and improvised weapons like sticks. I am a brown belt working on black in Brazilian jujitsu, but I still vividly remember how strikes, being spun around or even just falling to the ground were extremely unnerving and would often paralyze. The four human stress responses to new situations are fight, flee, freeze and fawn. Our protagonist are a concerned relative and a private investigator neither of which is going to have extensive fire, arms, training or experience, utilizing them in a stressful situation. Playing as a vulnerable female, it makes perfect sense that she randomly readies her weapon, places her finger on the trigger and uses it for appointing device. The lack of trigger discipline demonstrates a lack of awareness of the four basic rules of firearm safety. I laughed so hard at the beginning of the game when she declares that she hopes he has a gun so that he can wave it around in a psych ward and get coherent answers from people afterward. Somehow, the developers have been able to encapsulate all aspects of the insecurities, apprehensions and incompetency that anyone, even trained, can exhibit under extreme stress.Atmosphere.While creeks, footsteps and closing doors are typical implementations to make a location feel lived in or alive, I can’t sing the praises high enough for the unique implementation of audio logs for individual notes and objectives, and I only wish that all items would be given an audio clip just to make it a complete immersive feature. The difference in feeling and emotional impact between someone involved in the project reading a description or prose and a random gamer, trying to the potential relevance of unfamiliar text which popped up on the screen, is identical to the difference between a professionally recorded audiobook, read by a trained voice actor, and a overwhelmed, novice volunteer reading subject, specific jargon from a college textbooks for a blind student Recording from their living room.Bug:Fortunately, there is a dash or dodge button. My solution to the problem of being able to walk into objects has been to rapidly press the Dodge or Dash button, while spinning the character, a little further clockwise or counterclockwise. I assume this was done to give more of the perception of limitless exploration. It seems like some of the assets have one particular angle that well allow your character to clip into the asset and that same angle has to be found to get out. An extremely minor annoyance yet it is still there and you should be aware of it as well as the cause/solution potentials.I will add to this once I’ve actually finished both campaigns, but Whats here is a definite a full throated, controller clutching recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of the original trilogy and I can happily say that the 2024 version is worth it. It may have some flaws here and there but it is AMAZING.I took my time playing through both campaigns and damn, it was a fantastic experience. Gonna replay it soon to get all the achievements, YES SIR ! The game FEELS like it should. While the 3rd person movement is not near as clunky as the original Alone in the Dark, there is a small level of jank that makes absolute sense.The story is awesome. All the areas from the game are well-detailed.The Voice acting with the notes and characters are well done. David Harbour and Jodie Comer did a fantastic job. The same goes for the other actors as well.While it is huge and different from the original, it stands on its own as what Alone in the Dark should be. The story driven atmosphere is even more so amazing now as it was years ago. As someone who likes to explore and get more of the side lore. I was very pleased and impressed. I found myself putting down the controller and letting the notes be read to me in cinematic flare.It's not Alone in the Dark A New Nightmare or the crap movie that was made as a cash grab / tax break.The Music - BREATHTAKING. _childDocuments_.review: Admittedly I never played the old Alone in the Dark games, or any of the questionable 360/PS3 era games, so was fairly new to me overall playing this bad boy.As a fan of Lovecraftian horror, it's honestly a damn delight, especially with a few key aspects coming straight from the source material, such as entities or creatures. That being said, the game DOES it's own interpretation of some things, namely a lot of the enemies outside of one particular boss, but it's still pretty fun nonetheless.At the time of the review, there ARE some noticeable fps drops at times, I noticed them mostly when the the game was loading in another part of the map, the transitions between the real world and the "nightmare sequences" and some during the boss fight at the very end of the game, but otherwise? Honestly pretty solid launch.Keep in mind, this isn't a triple A budget game. Sometimes stuff looks a little odd, like some of the facial animations, or things like the running and or reloads, but unless you ONLY want to play hardcore polished games like Witcher or Red Dead, might be a bit of a miss for you.One thing to note as well, that in order to get the most content out of the game, similarly to Resident Evil 2, you need to play as both characters, so that's at least two guaranteed playthroughs, with each lasting around 8 or so hours if you don't try and speed run things.Overall, I genuinely enjoyed this, and I can only hope that it performs well enough to either get a DLC, or a sequel at some point down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: All around a good game with great atmosphere. It is very reminiscent of Resident Evil. Very similar style and atmosphere.I notice how others mention stuttering and performance issues. Which I noticed as well at first. But after tinkering with just turning off motion blur, chromatic aberration and enabling v-sync, as well as not enabling FSR. I noticed that the stuttering almost completely stopped. Only very occasionally will I get a hiccup. So still a bit of poor optimization on the dev side.For reference, I have an Intel i7-1200, AMD RX 6800 XT, 32GB RAM, and it’s on a 980 Pro SSD. Runs it at max settings.I can’t say this will fix everyone’s issue with the stuttering as I’d imagine most know what they could tune to resolve the issue. I hope at least. But for me, I have almost no issues after doing the above that I mentioned. Just a very minor hiccup here and there. Nothing too problematic or annoying to break my immersion of the game.Overall, if you’re interested. I think it’s worth it. Considering most games these days are absolute cash grab garbage. I will say this one is a good buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the OG Alone in the Dark games, but I've seen a lot of media talking about it and seeing it's gameplay. I personally think this is a fantastic recreation and modernization of a retro classic. The setting is amazing, the soundtrack is fitting, the entire atmosphere sucks you in and makes you intrigued. The melee feels weak in a way that it just doesn't have a good punchy feel behind it, but I can look past that since you rarely need to engage in combat anyways if you're quick enough and can press dodge - also I mean the guns feel just fine and punchy. The best part of this game though comes down to the world building and it's ability to really make the character feel like they are barely holding on and living a alternate life all of a sudden - fighting the eldritch horrors of the mind while everyone is just spectating. It's a very well done Lovecraftian style horror story imo. This game lands in my top 5 of 2024 easily, and if you need a totem to understand where that is - the other remake isn't on that list.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original game, and are familiar with the various entries into the series after, it's clear the developers took the time to really integrate a lot of the lore. It's a clear re-imagining of the first that does it justice, just without the obnoxious instant death mechanics for things you couldn't know beforehand and that expands on the Lovecraftian lore the first used in its story. The environments are moody and scary and the story is certainly original, if often told in notes found throughout the game.That said, it's not without its flaws. The game practically points you in the directions you're supposed to go with its placing and camera angles after events in Modern mode, aiming with a controller is awkward, and the enemies are more obnoxious than scary. Worse, the lighting is hard to adjust properly depending on your monitor and the environments don't have consistent brightness, so things can go from dark to overly bright near instantly.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait to play through both stories (Emily first, then Edward, though you can do them in any order) before I left a review.First, I love this game. I was lucky enough to not have the bugs that others experienced, my only issues were a few instances of getting stuck on geometry (where, as Emily, I was able to dodge and eventually free myself, and as Edward, luckily had an autosave just prior to reload and replay.)The structure of the game reminds me a fair bit of the Resident Evil 2 remake, in that your map expands as the game progresses and you do not have all the keys at the start. (Also like RE2R, items are "Archived" when no longer necessary.)  If you played both sides of RE2R, you're familiar about how the beginning of Claire & Leon's stories are very similar, but they differ significantly later in the game (with Leon having the Ada story & Claire having the Sherry story.) That is also the case in this game -- the dialogue and cutscenes differ between Emily and Edward in the beginning, but they each have their own story to address as well later in the game.If you enjoy southern gothic aesthetics, this game will be a feast for your eyes. The sickly yellow tones, the iconic buildings with galleries so associated with New Orleans, swampy shacks, it's all here. The environment team did an incredible job, and truly, hats off to them, they nailed the assignment.Also on the "good job you!" front, the audio team. Though not quite as intense as Alien Isolation (but really, what is,) the audio team succeeds at making you feel like doom is imminent. There is excellent tension created just from what you hear.The downsides, which truly are me reaching for complaints, begin with the combat. It is not as fluid as similar games, and the melee combat in particular could have stood to be polished a bit more. There is no "lock on," so you'll be SURE you'll hit the enemy and then stop just shy and GET hit instead. This is made all the more obvious by the fact "opportunity" items like rocks & Molotov cocktails DO have a lock-on system with enemies, even though they are found in-world and you cannot carry them with you.Additionally, the game is fairly short. One playthrough (Emily or Edward) will average about eight hours if you aren't rushing & are actually looking for collectibles (which you should absolutely do, as that does impact your game.) If we go with two playthroughs for a full experience, that's about sixteen hours of playtime. For me, personally, the price was more than worth it because I am a huge southern gothic horror fan & was anxiously awaiting this game since they announced this reimagining in 2022. If the initial $59.99 price tag is more than you'd be willing to pay for 16 hours, perhaps wait for a sale.Overall, this game is everything I wanted it to be and I'm very pleased. I would absolutely love more stories in this beautiful world.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone whose always adored horror story games in old spooky mansions, I'm so glad the genre hasn't died and Alone in the Dark doesn't fail to deliver... At least not yet!Already I'm immersed in the quiet yet pervasive solitude of the manor, opening clues and stocking up on bullets... I have a feeling I'm going to need them! What I like so far is the simplicity of it (I'm not keen on overly complex UI menus), yet I appear to be collecting parts of forbidden knowledge and access to greater things as I advance. I liked at the start, it shows you three samples side by side of a dark shadowy scene, medium and bright scenes - So you can adjust your personal level of brightness and contrast to suit the range of environments you'll be exposed to.Although I do admittedly have a high end PC, I've not come across any performance issues at all so far. The game runs very smoothly and I am enjoying the atmospheric lighting conditions and high end graphics.I did have one clunky sticking point for my character early on (a fallen over plant pot in the first open area), but I managed to get free of it eventually.Lots of locked doors you need to find keys to, lots of clues and as I've mentioned, wholly immersive. I've gotten half way through Chapter 2 now and have had to kill quite a few creatures. I don't like that they just throw you into that - No warm up, no training, no easy first dude... They take quite a few shots to kill and I did die a few times already, mostly because I felt thrown into the deep end a bit.You can creep around a lot of them, or just run away - Means you don't need to fight everything. But go figure out your controls first if you can! The "opportunity" brick you find to distract the enemy - I haven't figured that out yet, or made it work to my advantage and I've been playing a few hours already.I am enjoying the balance between clues, puzzles, exploring and then the world of fighting creatures... It's a nice mix and keeps things interesting! I'll keep playing and return with more!!
