_childDocuments_.review: The haunted house formula has been a mainstay in horror games arguably since Sweet Home (1989), mainly because video games allow for a completely different approach to places than movies or books. In video games, the player is free to explore every nook and cranny - and in turn must always choose to step into the dark basement himself. Whether it is the police station from Resident Evil 2, VtM: Bloodlines' Hallowbrook Hotel or Thief's Shalebridge Cradle: These locations stick with the players, searing their floorplans into the brain. Derceto in the original Alone in the Dark from 1998 stands among the greatest examples of the haunted house, codifying the genre and freeing the way for the aforementioned classics.This game is not an example of that genre, however. Whether or not you will enjoy 2024's Alone in the Dark depends on whether this is a dealbreaker for you or not.The 2024 reboot sends you away from Derceto frequently - and when you are there, you are never really Alone in the Dark. Derceto is the place where the interactions take place, where the story is continued. While the classic haunted house is explored, 2024's Derceto is a rather linear experience, a starting point into other eldritch locations. Locations that simply bleed atmosphere, yes, locations that Lovecraft himself chose for good reason, but this approach takes time and attention away from Derceto itself (here reimagined as an eerie clinic, although it still retains its roots in more than one way). It is a horror game, but not so much a haunted house as a theme park.For my part, I did enjoy this new iteration of Alone in the Dark quite a lot. I had just finished Resident Evil 4's reboot and while gameplay-wise everything about RE4 is better than AitD, the absurdity of the plot made it hard to finish. I will not return for a NG+. Conversely, I finished both playthroughs of AitD within three days, because I loved exploring a new iteration of Derceto, loved the characters, loved the atmosphere, the inclusion of Lovecraft's Cthulhu mythos, the allusions to the 1992 original. From Weird Tales magazines scattered about to a bust of old H.P. in the attic, from finding the old Indian Blanket again to in-jokes about AitD 2 and 3 - this could have been a masterpiece. Sadly, it is held back by other factors.The technical issues, for example, almost made me refund the game. Stuttering during transitions and cutscenes, repeated crashes to desktop - this game is badly optimized and suffers from it. Strangely enough these problems only occured in my Carnby playthrough. Then there is the combat, a clunky affair, more of an annoyance than a challenge. Some of the puzzles add nothing except for stretching game time. And while the story is compelling, its ending is weak and unsatisfying - in fact, I prefer the secret bad endings, because they fit the bleak tone so much better.Do I still recommend it? That depends. Fans of the original or of Lovecraftian horror should definitely give it a try, with the aforementioned tempered expectations. It is a solid Gothic horror tale and the actors - Jodie Comer and David Harbour especially - do a fine job. Get it in a sale, though, because you won't help the developers: Pieces Interactive was shut down after this game did not sell as well as expected.I would have played a sequel, if it ever came to that. I guess that is as much a recommendation as one can give.Final verdict: 7 of 10 Indian blankets.

_childDocuments_.review: Another case of 'I hate leaving negative reviews, but this was an atrocious mess and I want others to save their money.' THIS is why we don't spend an entire dev budget on a pair of actors. A beloved franchise with yet another failed reboot, because somewhere up the chain, someone decided to force a dev team to work with half the resources so that a couple Hollywood B-listers could phone in wooden performances while the game falls apart around them. What started with an interesting premise devolved quickly into an absolute disaster of pacing, storytelling and design. When the game wasn't stuttering (which was rare), it was STILL clunky and unintuitive to control. Every motion--walking, reloading weapons, using weapons and using health items--is done at a snail's pace, and ALL can be animation cancelled easily and accidentally, meaning you can end up taking a solid 10 seconds to reload a gun or drink some health if you aren't careful. Yes, that's right, because these base actions take roughly 5 seconds each to complete. So a slight misclick--or believing the game dropped your input so attempting to redo it (because it happens ALL the time) means you will accidentally interrupt the animation and double it's length. What's more, reloading and drinking health items both cause your character to stop running and slowly strut instead, and if you are forced to dodge or run--you guessed it: animation cancel. I won't get into the story because it was such an absolute mess. I am a firm believer in the 'show, don't tell' school of writing, and while cosmic horror is one of my favorite subgenres, this was an abysmal attempt at knitting together a bunch of unresolved, nonsensical plot points vomited at you in an exposition dump that would put most anime to shame, with the watered-down glue being 'but it's cosmic horror so we don't have to make any of this stuff add up!' Pass denied. Sorry.I was so excited for the first 2 hours of this game, And had zero desire to finish it, let alone do a second character's full playthrough. I am so let down that I will likely not see another Alone in the Dark entry in my lifetime due to this complete flop of a reboot.

_childDocuments_.review: That was fun.Okay, so, I never played the original AitD, so I can't really compare them. The only other game in the series I've played was A New Nightmare, and Emo Carnby was a major turn off to the game, even aside the game breaking bugs I kept running into. THIS Carnby works a LOT better, and I really enjoyed playing as Emily.Gameplay: 6.5/10 paws.* For what it is, this game's gameplay isn't bad. Some of the responsiveness feels sluggish at times because the characters turn more like real people than the whole spinning in place thing a lot of games do. They don't get moving too fast, and they aren't masterful gun-totting badasses. That's actually kind of the point, though. It makes combat feel a lot more like something to be worried about. Still, some of the jank in interactive points is... well... jank.* There are guns, and you will have to use them. Ammunition is sporadic. There are melee weapons, and you had BETTER use them. THERE IS A DODGE BUTTON AND MAY THE HIGH PRIEST CTHULHU HIMSELF INTERVENE IF YOU DON'T USE IT.Sound: 7/10 paws.* Overall I liked the sound design. It was nothing special for a horror game, but it wasn't bad at all. The voice acting was, by and large, pretty good.Story: 7.5/10 paws.* Harder to follow than I expected and on the surface it feels like you are touching on several different stories at once. In a way, I think it _IS_ touching on several things at once. Though it lends to great future setup, and feels right for the what it is, it does give the game a less cohesive narrative. Once you get under the surface all those branches of story start to make a lot more sense, although I do feel that some of it requires some VERY in depth prior knowledge on the players part with Yog Sothothery to grasp some of what's happening.* Something I found fascinating was just how absolutely hardcore they went on getting ...well... who the dark man actually is... RIGHT. And they DID. They got him spot on. It was glorious.* There is a thing at the end of the game. It is absolutely, exactly right. I adored this depiction of it. If you don't know what I am referring to... play the game and remember that dodge button. You're going to need it...Additional note: 12/10 paws.* Game has an option to play as a woman without her just being a re-skin of the male protagonist. I know that's not a big thing for some people, but I have been having to make do with main characters I just cannot step into the shoes of in a lot of big games for so long that when that isn't an option I find myself not bothering with the game at all. I loved it, and I loved Emily's character, and the backstory of hers hiding behind the scenes hit pretty damn hard, and actually did explain a few things. That said, I actually liked this enough that once I go get myself another coffee, I actually am going to go back in and play through as Carnby, because I am actually kind of curious and halfway like the guy already.I went back and played the Prologue too and thoroughly enjoyed the (EXTREMELY) brief stint playing as Grace. I think I'd play a whole game from her dissociative perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not in good faith recommend this game due to the amount of bugs experienced. I am constantly getting stuck on small objects that cause me too load old saves. Getting stuck is exacerbated by the dodge mechanic that will put you in this scenario more than actually dodging. enemies straight up clipping through walls or disappearing all together. every time I rebound the button for the opportunities, the game would bug out and not let me use anything. I do not believe that this game was actually finished on launch, and bugs are not the only problem. there are multiple sounds that just absolutely do not match what you are actually doing. the first time i encountered the sniffer all of the audio came out of the left channel until the cut scene was complete. There was also an area near chapter 4 where you climb down wooden vines, but the game clearly makes metal ladder sounds. On top of all of this the combat is absolutely not finished. the small ground enemies towards the end of the game are almost impossible to hit with melee weapons, resulting in a waist of ammo as they take almost 7 handgun shots to kill. Let`s go with the pros:I loved the game, it is a fun adventure, a fresh look at the classic first Alone in the Dark game. Atmosphere is awesome, music is nice, environments are decent and have the same vibes as original one. At the core moments it held me nervous and engaged. Collecting and reading stuff to make story connection is very well presented and narrated too!!! Puzzles are nice as well, and you really have to think a bit first playthrough. All and all, I hope game gets polished and perhaps gets a DLC or a sequel to make the other two game remakes happen. I haven`t regretted buying this and completed all the achievements.Secret endings are neat little way of having expected outcome that is not very clear to achieve at first glance. Now cons:Combat. Is. OK. Not good, but definitely better than the OG AitD game. But often monsters felt just tedious and clunky, not challenging, and even worse - animation is not often reading what can happen next. Stutters/lags. Still are there, still break immersion, still hope that will be fixed because it made me feel that broken immersion at the times...Collision - hope they fix it, I was mad that randomly stuck on some objects just because I dashed into a magic pixel and could not hop off the object.Animations and transitions - here`s the deal. I understand it is not interactive kino with press button to make choice. But many little things here could be more polished and done better. I had weapons stuck under feet, Emily standing on a book, dorky movements of the sliding monsters... Plain sad. And last, but no least for me, was the chapter 4. It feels so rushed that probably I`m not the only one feeling it. You basically jump into different places, then the boat segment is just a joke, same as the winter one. That`s why I feel that some stuff could be expanded on. OH and now I remember the worst feeling EVER. Since our characters are doing stuff in parallel, I am very sad to see that their scenarios are exactly the same and we get almost zero insight on what the other character did while we were investigating. I hoped that I will visit a bit more different places, or do different stuff, like resident evil 2 A and B scenarios. Lost opportunity if you ask me. Overall I`d say it is a 7/10 experience ruined by lack of QA, bug fixes, animations improvements, stutter removal, and maybe making combat and story feel a bit more rich.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:Finished the game as Emily. Everything stated below still stands as the game was awesome throughout. I will say the combat ended up generally better than I anticipated when I first wrote the review. That being said, it's still not going to be for everyone, especially those looking for action horror.Original Review:I've only played the first few chapters as Emily so far, but I want to take a moment in my review to talk about the impressive art direction and visual design. I am a huge fan of horror movies, and I find that the most effective films have great cinematography, lighting, and sound design. This game has really perfected those three elements so integral to the horror experience. As an example, I recorded a moment during my playthrough that had at least four light sources with different color temperatures that gave the scene a richness and depth never really approached in even the most cinematic games.Additionally the sound design and the soundtrack are both impeccable. The jazz music, ranging from timely to chaotic and creepy (just watch the trailers), and the sounds of insects scurrying from or swarming the light, the creaking of doors and walls and branches, even the sound of footsteps squelching in mud or dully shuffling a floor above all add up to incredible immersion.It's so rare to find a game with both a strong sense of design and the willingness to stick to that design so thoroughly, but I'm glad this game does it. It's the only thing the game does perfectly, but playing it, you find yourself wishing other games would take this approach. How much better would the modern classics of the genre be with this level of style and execution?To that point, this game could also be improved in places. For the most part combat has been adequate, though sometimes excellent. It's occasionally frustrating finding yourself in a corner with no way out and the camera clipping in ways that make you just wait to die and try again. For every moment I've had like that however, there has been a moment of sheer panic, fleeing and spinning frantically to launch a brick or bottle at my pursuer and land a quick headshot or hatchet swing before running for my life toward the next environmental opportunity. That's where the combat shines, and it's certainly how the game is meant to be played, at least by me. That sometimes means dying, at most a couple of times, until you know where the exits and throwables are, but mostly the auto saves have been just before the fights so far.But you should play this game for the atmosphere not the action, since that's what it leans hardest into and where its greatest strength lies. On a 4070 I'm playing it in Cinematic in 4k with HDR on at 60+ fps, and I find myself stopping and taking screenshots or recording video at least twice an hour, because the game is really that beautiful. If atmosphere is important to you in horror games, you owe it to yourself to experience what this game does well, even if that means plodding through a few moments of things you may think it doesn't.

_childDocuments_.review: You're probably aware that this game is sort-of a mixed bag, so giving an opinion is quite risky.I, for one, enjoyed it immensely. The puzzles were great with a handful that do require your full attention, the manor and levels are extremely well designed (and quite diverse as the story progresses), the music and sound design is top-notch and story-wise? If you're looking for a good Lovecraftian game, you're in for a treat! And the lore of HPL is used exceptionally! Combat is passable; at times it feels janky and could use some fine tuning but in all honesty I never found it frustrating.Yes, there are bugs... A lot of them! Surprisingly, in my first run, I didn't experience any, but during my second I actually stumbled upon all of them (clipping issues, audio glitches, getting stuck on objects, missing objectives etc). Stuttering is there and quite persistent, but afaik I'm playing a Unreal Engine game so it kinda comes with the territory; as gamers we don't have to put up with it but it's hardly surprising!I sincerely hope the devs put in the extra effort to polish this game because there's a solid experience to be had despite the techical flaws. It won't break ground (graphically or story-wise) but for those of us who played the originals this is a loving homage not just of the AitD series but for 90's Infogrames games (Shadow of the Comet, Prisoner of Ice). Definitely worth playing!

_childDocuments_.review: "Alone in the Dark" (2023) is a revival of a series that has always held a special place in my heart. As someone who has been a fan since the original 1992 release, I approached this reboot with equal parts excitement and trepidation, hoping it would capture the magic of the early games while updating it for modern audiences.**Story:**The story is where "Alone in the Dark" (2023) truly shines. It stays true to the series' roots with its blend of psychological horror and supernatural mystery. Set in the haunted Derceto Manor, the narrative feels like a love letter to fans of the original games. The plot, filled with twists and chilling moments, captures the eerie atmosphere that made the series iconic. The characters are well-developed, and their backstories are compelling, adding depth to the overall narrative. The dialogue is well-written, with enough nods to the original to satisfy longtime fans while still being accessible to newcomers.**Graphics:**Visually, the game is stunning. The developers have done an incredible job of bringing Derceto Manor to life. The attention to detail in the environment is impressive, with each room and corridor dripping with atmosphere. The lighting effects are particularly noteworthy, playing a crucial role in creating the game’s tense and foreboding mood. Character models are detailed and expressive, adding to the immersion. However, there are occasional issues with frame rates and textures that detract from the experience, but they aren't enough to overshadow the overall visual excellence.**Sound:**Sound design is another area where the game excels. The eerie soundtrack and ambient noises work together to create an unsettling atmosphere that keeps you on edge. The voice acting is strong, with performances that bring the characters to life and enhance the story. The sound effects, from the creak of a door to the distant wail of something unknown, are perfectly executed and contribute significantly to the horror experience.**Gameplay:**Gameplay is where "Alone in the Dark" (2023) stumbles slightly. While it successfully modernizes some mechanics, there are moments where it feels clunky and outdated. The combat system is serviceable but lacks the fluidity seen in other contemporary horror titles. The puzzles, a hallmark of the series, are well-designed and challenging, though occasionally they can be a bit obtuse.**Final Rating:**Overall, "Alone in the Dark" (2023) is a solid return to form for the series, despite some gameplay shortcomings. As a fan, it’s a joy to see this beloved franchise back in the spotlight. I’d give it a solid 8/10. The story, atmosphere, and dedication to the series' legacy make it a must-play for any fan, even if it's not without its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: excellent game in my opinion. I usually don't buy games at release, but this one was worth it even at full price -10% launch discount. people compare it to resident evil, but I think it's its own thing. there is much less combat and more exploration. the locations all have great atmosphere! just make sure to disable all the hints and markers. graphics and story are great too. i couldn't get into resident evil 4 remake at all and had to refund it, but i loved this game.performance is fine for me with a 3080 in 1440p using dlss and everything on epic settings. shader compilation stuttering sucks in the first few minutes and why is this even a thing? can't it precompile the shaders? however, the major problem for me were the lag spikes during combat. if you turn quickly and want to do a melee hit, odds are that the game hitches for half a second. it's not a hard game so you will likely survive and it doesn't happen all the time, but it's annoying. i'm also fine with the game's length. I spent about 10 hours on the guy's campaign. Will do the girl's story next.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it perfect? No.Does it lack some polish? Definitely.Was it fun? Absolutely. Since the game's combat is not as fluid like Resident Evil, my recommendation is to play on 'easy' with all hints turned off. That way you will enjoy the best Alone in the Dark has to offer, while the worst will not be as frustrating. Sincerely hope that this little gem of a game will do well sale-wise, because I believe this studio has enough respect and love for the originals to remake them with the care they deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: During first 3 hours I sh*t my pants few times, not gonna lie. It's very different game from Alone in the Dark: New Nightmare (last game from this franchise which I played). Can not tell if I like this more or not. Story is good so far. Puzzles are sometimes really hard and I can't believed I (or we, since I stream it to my brother) solved all of them so far without any tutorial. Graphics are ok, runs great on my rtx2080, everything set up on epic. Somethimes (when loading I guess) I have fps drops, but nothing what bothers me. Combat is little bit unpleasant, but I count this game as psychological terror, not shooter game. There are only two things bothering me. Facial expressions of characters are really poor and it's perfect example of uncanny walley, which is very sad, because of perfect casting. Second thing is fact, that main character is somehow totally ok with all strange things happening to him. Travel to another dimension? Ok, why should I tell it to someone. Strange monsters? Ok, I will just kill them and keep going. It's little bit strange.... He should at least ask that afroamerican character after first appereance of this anomally, specially after he got warned he is going to have rough night. But who knows why, protagonist is ok with it and keeps going. Anyway game looks good so far. But it's game you play because of story and atmosphere. It's not looter shooter for kids.UPDATE AFTER FINISHING GAME: Ending of this game really sucks... I must admint that I'm sad and only reason for not giving negative review is, that I like the franchise...

_childDocuments_.review: I played Resident Evil 2/3/4, Silent Hill 2, and Alone in Dark in just over a month.  Alone in the Dark was the one I thought was going to be worst, and was the one I loved the most.  The voice acting in this game is excellent, the audio logs I listened to in full. The notebook narrator recapping things as you went along is great.  I loved the focusing to see items/points of interest mechanic. After playing several survival horror titles in a row I appreciated how streamlined this game was in comparison.  There were some rough spots, some visual glitches from time to time, but nothing game breaking or even really distracting. I don't know why this didn't catch on more, or get better reviews, but this is a sleeper hit for 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: Gem of a game, a beautiful love letter to classic, exploration-heavy survival horror with absolutely insane quality of writing and voice acting. Amazing atmosphere, great soundtrack, great puzzles (which are all connected by context and strike a perfect balance between logic and complexity, Capcom should take note), very good exploration, good graphics, servicable combat.It's a bit janky, but what's good about it got me (and three friends watching the stream on Discord) to laugh from joy for solid 5 hours straight and I had to force myself to turn it off because I need to get some sleep.Instant cult classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like writing these reviews, but I was pretty disappointed in this game. A new Alone in the Dark game in the style of the recent Resident Evil games with a story by the guy who wrote SOMA seemed like such a no-brainer and I was really looking forward to it, but in the end it fails to deliver.The game is way too linear and has none of the interesting exploration from RE. When you find a key or important item you use it almost right away. Sometimes in the same room. Neither the story nor characters are particularly interesting. Or rather, they had the potential to be interesting, had they been more fleshed out. The Dark Man is so nebulous as a villian that it's honestly hard to care about Jeremy or his problems. The combat is so close to being good, there are a few encounters where you're juggling melee, ranged and throwable items, and it all comes together in a satisfying way, but the rest just boil down to shooting at enemies walking towards you at a snails pace (or getting stuck on geometry). The graphics and animation are good enough, but for a $60 game that feels like the bare minimum these days.Also it just isn't spooky enough. Where are all the crazy mindscrew moments that made SOMA so memorable? Like half of the levels take place in the daytime. At the start of the game you arrive at the mansion at dusk, but why not have it be at night and raining straight away to set the mood? Alone in the Dark. It's right there in the name. Yeah, I don't know. Maybe this game would be worth it at around $30, but I can't recommend it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Alone in the Dark 2024 may not be the best survival horror game you've seen, but in the current generation, where the genre has become rare, it's something better than nothing, and for sure, it's way better than the newer action Residen Evil games.The story telling has some weaknesses; it's like it's missing so many unanswered questions about the past of characters and their purpose, like why the maid attacked you aggressively with her knife when you wanted to peek into the kitchen?The action gameplay is very simple; you probably won't feel a lack of ammunition, which is the main feature of survival games. You can cross the enemeis or hit them with bricks or molotoves. There are only two bosses near the end of the game, and they are not challenging even on hard difficulty.Some puzzles are great, and some are just straight-forward due to the lazy design of the levels. It's like in many places, you face a locked door or locked safe, but the key to open it is just placed in the same room or the next room.BTW, despite the issues the game has due to the lazy design of the story and levels, it's still a survival horror game and worth getting if you like the genre, so I'm giving the game a  score.
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game! It's the first Alone in the Dark game I've played start to finish so I can't say much about how loyal it is to the franchise but I simply love this game. I played it on easy mode because I was more interested in the story than the fights and let me tell you, I was still on the edge of my seat! Great story telling, art is beautiful, voice acting superb and great replayability...for at least one more time because it really pays out to play both characters!There are many collision, streaming, freezing and visual bugs in this game. I thought I ran into one blocker which only turned out that one thing that was optional so far, was indeed mandatory. I am fine with the amount and kind of bugs in this game though. Nobody is perfect...and it ads to the everlasting feeling of one can never be sure if it's reality or the slow loss of sanity...
_childDocuments_.name: Alone in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who didn't play the original, I found the game to be quite enjoyable. The story is intriguing, and the gameplay is satisfactory. However, one aspect that bothered me was the melee combat mechanics, where you simply have to continuously press a button, leading to a somewhat clunky experience. Despite this, I didn't encounter any significant issues and overall, I thoroughly enjoyed playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review:
Deep in the 1920's south, Emily Hartwood's uncle has gone missing. Together with private investigator Edward Carnby, she embarks on a journey to Derceto Manor to uncover the secrets of this mysterious place and the circumstances of her relative's vanishing. 

Return to Derceto Manor in this reimagination of Alone in the Dark, a love letter to the 90's cult classic horror game. 

Encounter strange residents, nightmarish realms, dangerous monsters and ultimately unveil a plot of rising evil. At the intersection of reality, mystery, and insanity, an adventure waits that will challenge your core beliefs.

Who can you trust, what will you believe, and what will you do next?

name: Embracelet
detailed_description: Are you looking for a heartwarming, relaxing game? Look no further! Exploration, puzzles and an exciting story in a unique setting Embracelet puts you in the role of Jesper, a Norwegian teenager who lives with his mom in the city. One day he is handed an old bracelet by his Grandfather who grew up in a fishing community up north. This bracelet has powers - strange, mysterious powers! Jesper is given the task to unravel the mystery behind the bracelet. Where does it come from? Who does it belong to? And why did his Grandfather leave the island and his old life behind? EXPLORE A BEAUTIFUL, NORTHERN NORWEGIAN ISLAND SOLVE PUZZLES USING THE MAGICAL BRACELET MAKE FRIENDS AND CHOICES THAT CAN AFFECT THE OUTCOME OF THE STORY With its gentle difficulty level, intriguing story and beautiful soundtrack, Embracelet is a game for anyone who enjoys unique, heartwarming video games. Embracelet is made by Mattis Folkestad, one man team behind the award-winning adventure game Milkmaid of the Milky Way. Playtime: 3-6 hours with different endings. Best played with a game controller, like an Xbox one, Dualshock or Nintendo Pro Controller in a sofa or a comfy chair.

short_description: Travel to northern Norway, solve puzzles using a mysterious, magical bracelet and make new friends on your journey to discover the past - and yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: An enchanting adventure game about the coming of age of Jasper.  He visits an island off Northern Norway where his grandfather grew up and meets all kinds of interesting characters.  Along the way, Jasper learns about the ties of family, loss, guilt, love and friendship.  He also finds the owner of a bracelet his grandfather gave him which has 'magical' properties.After a slow start, there is lots of action.  Reminded me of the Famous Five books but with older teens.  There is a bit of violence and sexual innuendo, so not for young children...suitable for pre teens.Achievements are pretty easy to get, but you have to replay the game to get the second ending.  The game took me over 6 hrs to get through, but it still is a bit pricey, so buy on sale.Graphics were simple, music was good, but the controls were clunky.  Controlling the main character on keyboard was a nightmare, but I believe those on controllers has similar experiences.   Puzzles were casual and simple.  There are no stressful areas to overcome, but there is quite a bit of backtracking involved.I loved the environment of the Norwegian island which was lovely and refreshing to see.  Recommend for those who enjoy non-combat adventure with a sweet story.  7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is very chill game. It's a story driven game about a boy who's given a magical bracelet and it give the boy some supernatural powers. He travels to the small fictional island in Norway to find what happened to his grandad and his adventure begins.On the way he finds friends and spends some time with them. There are some humorous scenes, sad moments and even some thrilling action. Nevertheless the game is very relaxing. All the main characters are really lovable but maybe there's not enough time to fully connect with them. I wish I could've spent more time with those two friends to know them better.There are some light puzzles where you need to move some objects or push a button. Mostly gameplay consists of running around, helping people and talking with them. This is how you advance the story. It's a short game with multiple endings. They're not very different though.Running back and forth could be boring sometimes but overall it's an enjoyable experience.Graphically the game is very minimalistic but it has beautiful art-style and even with these low-poly graphics some scenes look stunning.Game runs perfectly well but that shouldn't be surprising considering the graphics. Should run smoothly on any PC.Unfortunately there's no ultrawide support. It could benefit from cinematic aspect ratio. But what can we do...The soundtrack is pretty nice but at some point it starts to get a bit repetitive.There's no voice acting but there's not much to read either. The dialogues are pretty short consisting of two or three lines sometimes extending to several lines.Overall a good and enjoyable game for those who love story driven and relaxing games. Not a masterpiece by any means but it's way above average. It's short but tells an interesting story. Get this on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: *** Recommended ONLY if you have a controller and can deal with platforming ***This is a better glimpse into a North Norwegian coastal community than you could hope to get during an actual vacation (source: I live here), combined with a solid story-driven puzzle adventure revolving around a mysterious, magical bracelet. The solo dev has come a long way since "Milkmaid of the Milkyway", and thankfully he's abandoned his atrocious attempts at rhyming. He's clearly familiar with the northern landscapes, everyday life, joys and struggles that he portrays in a natural and nuanced way. The game is pretty for having low-fi graphics (that I'm generally not a fan of), the soundtrack is good as far as I can tell (unfortunately played with some background noise and without headphones), the puzzles are alright (you use your magical gimmick to fix stuff), difficulty level very casual I'd say so far*. Most importantly for me, the island feels like a real place with real people. It's a mostly chill experience, though I think a content warning for (general content, not essential for the plot afaik) is warranted. I also would have appreciated an option to disable that hip new jumpy text thing that's supposed to express the speaker being emotional. *HOWEVER, this game seems to turn into a surprise platformer towards the end, requiring dexterity with controls and timing. Thanks, I hate it. I guess it's ok if you're used to platformers and have a gamepad, probably still doable though a PITA with a keyboard. My clumsy self tried and failed over and over again before I got too frustrated and abandoned it. What a shame :( TL;DR: If you love puzzles, I don't know if that's reason enough to play this game. If you love story-driven adventures , this is a solid one. If you love Scandinavia and/or the (sub-)Arctic and feel like spending a few hours in Northern Norway, this is probably an excellent choice with a gamepad and platforming skills. * * * I collect chill and story-driven games in my curator .
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved this. I'm a complete sucker for coming-of-age stories. It's the nostalgia of being a teenager and feeling all of these strange over-complicated emotions despite not having to worry about anything all that more complex than school (although, Jesper does experience some loss). But also being able to experience it in the framework of exploring a beautiful Norwegian island, making new friends, rather than, er... walking around an American mall, sipping a smoothie, with friends you don't even like, because hopping on a boat to a remote island wasn't an option. I only wish the island in Embracelet were bigger, that there were more folks to meet, more hangout sessions with your two new friends. All interlaced with even more magic and mystery. Maybe more complex puzzles, although the very light puzzles were fine. I could envision this game being so much more - but it was a chill three hour experience, and I have no real complaints. It was a delight.Also, Jesper is a bit of an environmental terrorist, which made me laugh, but I don't think I was supposed to??

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this. It reminded me a little of Wide Ocean Big Jacket but longer and with some Studio Ghibli feels. The controls are a little clunky for what is essentially a point and click adventure, and there's a side of me that would have preferred fewer puzzle set pieces, which sometimes felt a bit out of place. These are minor quibbles though in what is otherwise a short and heartfelt coming of age tale with some pretty visuals and a lovely soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: A gentle, touching, atmospheric puzzle-adventure with nice writing and music. Fans of games like Night in The Woods and Oxenfree will feel at home, though Embracelet is shorter and less substantial than both. Fans of point-and-click adventures will enjoy it too.For those who are worried about this game having platforming or action game elements: There is no jumping or shooting here (no jump button, even). I don't remember any challenging action sections. I didn't need to use the sprint button unless I simply wanted to move faster. There were no timing-based movement sections where you'd fail or die if you didn't move quickly enough. I was never in danger of dying though slow reactions on my part. In fact, I'm not sure if it's even possible to die in the game. Arguably, using the bracelet itself might feel tricky for some users because it's mildly reaction-based, where you press a single button when two moving circles line up, but there's sufficient build-up beforehand and I only missed a few times. There's no penalty for missing, you just try again immediately. I played with an XBox controller and everything worked smoothly.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Emotional game about growing up and discovering your heritage, set in beautiful Northern Norway.Not a very difficult game, but with light puzzles, nice graphics, good dialog (first game I played with norwegian text), and a fun "magic" mechanic.A worthy followup to the developers first game, Milkmaid of the Milky Way, which you also should play ASAP.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is a narrative driven adventure game about a 17 year old boy discovering the mysteries of a mysterious bracelet on a small island in the North. It's a charming experience made by a one man team. I haven't played their previous game, but as a fan of story driven adventure games I had to give this one a go. Embracelet is longer than your typical indie "walking simulator" taking about 3-5 hrs compared to a typical 1-2, and it uses its time wisely.  For the majority of the experience your left to your own devices discovering mysteries at your own leisure. You can choose to pursue further on particular topics, and solve problems from the handful of island residents. It reminded me a lot of "Boku no Natsuyasumi" (My Summer Vacation) series with how your spending your vacation in a quiet small island with a lot of the sound effects just being the sound of birds or the wind. It being an adventure game there are puzzles and dialog trees to click through and Embracelet does a decent job on both. A majority of the obstacles in the game can be solved by using the power of your bracelet which has the ability to move/push/destroy objects. None of the puzzles are particularly challenging but they do provide some thought to keep things engaging. I do wish there was more to the bracelet with every action being executed with a timing button press. As for the decision making its very simple dialog trees with a majority not changing much of anything, but create some nice flavoring to the main character, Jesper's personality. There are two endings but they seem entirely based on a simple hangout session you may have between one of your friends. Embracelet's biggest problem is it's lack of time cohesion, which sounds silly on the surface, but does create in a sudden jolty narrative experience. Jesper's time on the island is planned to be a week, but the entirety of the first day is a huge chunk of the game with the last third suddenly shifting between days without any awareness. A simple title card or scene of Jesper going to bed would add a lot. The only other issue being that the games narrative swerves into different directions so suddenly. The final outcome of the mystery is interesting but it happens all too fast that it left it feeling a bit too abrupt to my liking, and if you can ignore some silly story beats that require "don't worry about it" you are still left with a solid experience.Overall, I'm really happy I played Embracelet. I couldn't help but be drawn into its charming little world. It's a well written story with a endearing little cast. Despite the hang ups I still recommend the trip out into the quaint little island in the North. PROS+ well written branching dialog+ Fun open ended exploration and puzzle solving + endearing small cast of characters+ Beautiful Soundtrack creates the perfect atmosphere + Satisfying lengthNEUTRAL+/-  The bracelet mechanic is really basic and doesn't ever do anything new CONS- Inconsistent sense of time- The final act happens so suddenly and ends abruptly- Jasper gets stuck on terrain a lot when highlighting objects8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: A Visual novel, that would have benefited from a voiceover if not for the fact that it's a long game with loads of dialog. Love, life, death and regret, and even, you know when boys prefer boys. Sabotage, espionage and vandalism interspersed with a side story all about the threats to our beautiful planet fill out the plot. Something for everyone.  Don't let the simple boxy graphics put you off, very good controls and puzzles.The back story follows multiple young people all trapped in circumstance. You must play a part in telling their story. Sure you have to make choices, and some choices and some objects you interact with change the way the story unfolds, but in the story arc it's pretty classic, twists and turns some predictable others not. Very much about having fun and some fantasy and magic lightens the mood of what is otherwise a deadly serious story. I missed a fair few items in my playthrough, and this may be one of very few games that I have time to play through a second time.If you enjoyed this game, you can find other much like it here
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet commits "the deadly sin" of being an adventure game "day dreaming" of being a platformer, but it doesn't irk me too often. The story is touching and intreaguing. Themes like illness, loss, poverty, centralization and sexuality are handled with care and dignity; without becoming ham-fisted. A trio of one-dimensional, brutish and cartoonish antagonists stands in grinding contrast to the generally nuanced writing, but most of the character relationships feels natural, and the charming, quirky townsfolk are quite familiar for anybody growing up at the  Norwegian countryside. The branching character and story paths feels organic and believable, for the most part (I would have traded an "action-movie cliché" sub-plot for more hi-jinks and bonding moments with the main characters). Embracelet is a sweet game, with a simplistic but endearing artstyle and solid soundtrack. It's not "perfect," but has personality and charm.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely wonderful experience it was playing this game. _childDocuments_.review: Oh my. I loved Milkmaid to bits. So I was highly anticipating Mattis' next title. Pretty early on in development I was really disappointed by the choice of the artstyle and the way this game controls: 3D environments and direct character control instead of beautiful pixel art and a point and click gameplay. Now that I have played it I certainly understand the reasons for this choice, since in some parts it does add to the immersion, but all in all I gotta say, I did not like the graphics all that much. They serve a purpose, but all in all the world feels like big chunks of polygons, without much detail, sadly. And don't get me started on the way the character controls. Early on while playing this I almost dropped the game because the character will walk in a circle and continue to walk for nearly ten seconds on one spot when you simply try to access a hotspot you stand right at a second time. It's infuriating.I also think the story does not make a lot of sense either and to me the explanation for everything in the end felt very lackluster. Still it is engaging enough to make you continue playing and wanting to discover more of the world you're in and how the relations play out.However, I did like this enough to actually finish the game. It has the same magic and spirit that made me love Milkmaid so much and I think I'm falling in love with Norway thanks to Machineboy's games. It's hard to put a finger on what it actually is that makes this game shine despite its flaws, but in the end it doesn't matter: it just shines. Must be the love that has been poured into it from its developer ;)So thanks for another trip into your beautiful world, Mattis. I am looking forward to your next creation.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished *Embracelet* by the developer who did *Milkmaid of the Milky Way* and really liked it.  This is one of those slow paced story games that left me a bit teary at times.  The main game mechanic for actions is clicking/hitting the button as two circles match up, and your can set the difficulty level in Options.  I had mine set right at the middle and only missed when I wasn’t paying attention.  Easy to play with a controller but doesn’t seem like it would be too difficult with keyboard/mouse.    There are things you need to do to move ahead with the story, but there are optional tasks too.  I found I missed one of these, but could get that in another playthrough.  I was going slow and it took me 5 hours to play.  Playing again to experience things I missed and choose a different ending would go faster.  There are three endings.  Only one autosave though so one would need to start over to get all the achievements and the different endings.  I thought the game was just beautiful and was very glad I played it.  I hate to compare games because the stories told are very different, but if you like the pacing and focus on story in games like *To the Moon* or *Last Day of June* you would likely enjoy *Embracelet* very much.  There’s a demo, so no reason not to give it a try.  I highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is a sweet narrative adventure in the vein of Life is Strange. You play a teenager who finds a magical bracelet and heads back to the fishing village where his grandfather grew up to learn more about the family history and discover the origin of the artifact. It's set in Norway, which is not a common location for games, and that makes it feel a bit special. The characters are all kind to one another, and although the bad guys are a bit over-the-top, the obvious villainy gives it a bit of a feeling like a Famous Five story or Tintin or something. You know the baddies will lose and you're going to make it through just fine, which is exactly the way a light adventure yarn should go.The most annoying part of the game is the controls because you cannot control the camera and sometimes it swings around to really inconvenient locations that lead you walking back in the opposite direction you were just walking in. There is an especially egregious section near the end where the camera keeps swinging around and then you fall off the thing you were standing on and have to walk all the way back round and start again, over and over. I almost threw my keyboard out the window, but I'm glad I persevered because aside from the annoyance with the controls the story is warm and comforting. If you're looking for a bit of escapist fun, and like the sound of wandering around an island in the fjords helping people, Embracelet is a good choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is a narrative and expressive 3D adventure in third person view with low poly graphic style. It was developed by Mattis Folkestad, founder of the one man studio Machineboy in Norway; he composed even the soundtrack. It is commendable that an indie author has ventured into the difficult task of developing a narrative and expressive game with few financial and human resources; that’s the reason why the game is worth of our attention. Let me say that the experiment is totally successful. I’m very happy that Mattis submitted a copy of the game to my curator page on Steam; it’s very rare to receive games as good as this one. You can play it also on Nintendo Switch.Embracelet tells the “bildungsroman” of 17 y.o. Jesper living in Oslo with his mother; he has never known his father, who died before Jesper was born. Jesper is in the middle of an adolescential crisis, he is no longer interested in school and has no friends, his beloved grandfather is seriuosly ill and is going to die. Before to die, grandfather gives him a magic bracelet, with the power to manipulate the world around him, and a mission to accomplish: travel to Slepp island where grandfather lived when he was young and unravel the mistery of the magic bracelet. In the past Sleep was a thriving community based on fishing and tourism; now it is almost uninhabited, and voracious oil companies are compromising its delicate ecosystem. In Slepp Jesper will meet Karoline and Hermod and together they will have an unforgettable summer full of incredible adventures, friendship and love that will change their lives forever.Superpowers, adolescence, coming of age story, loss, friendship, love, family, ecology, narrative game… Does it ring the bell? Obviously yes, Embracelet is clearly inspired by Life Is Strange. However they are two completely different games and experiences. It has even something of Oxenfree (adolescence, magic elements and comics ballons) and of Night In The Woods (existential crisis, the decadent town of Possum Spring and comics ballons). Mattis Folkestad could not rely on motion captured actors; he did a great job by animating every single hand drawn character in the hand drawn game world. Mattis worked as cartoons designer in the past, I found on the web one of the project he worked for: Embracelet comes with a lot of divinely animated NPCs; the intense human relationships that the player establishes with the characters are the real strength of the game. Not by chance the title comes from the verb “embrace“. I didn’t think it was possible to get attached to characters and places just sketched in a low poly style; yet at the end of the game there remains a sense of nostalgia for not being able to experience new adventures with your virtual friends in the fascinating low poly world. The hand drawn visuals are magnificent, able to create a contemplative atmosphere and make you forget the low poly graphics or, maybe, just because of the low poly art! The beautiful soundtrack helps to build a pleasant, peaceful, poetic mood. Divinely written texts and multiple choice dialogues help to estabilish strong and empathetic relationships with the characters. As consequence, the absence of acting voices is not a limit: while reading the comic balloons, it seems to hear the voices of the characters!Gameplay comes with a weird feature: you cannot control the camera. Usually we are used to control camera with the right stick in 3D games. Here the camera is programmed to follow your avatar Jesper so that he is always at the center of the frame. Outdoors or in large places, camera is executing programmed “dollies”, following Jesper from behind or from the side, from near or from afar; indoors or in small places, camera position is fixed but it is programmed to rotate for following Jesper. So you cannot rotate the view, visual is determined by programmed camera following your avatar movements. At first I was perplexed by this feature, then I realized it allows the author to determine always the best view, just like directors do in movies; at the same time it integrates with the player’s freedom of movement. In this way the aesthetic beauty of the view remains consistent throughout the game, it’s a good compromise of cinema and game! It helps a lot to build the beautiful contemplative and expressive mood of the experience. You can see the best result of this technique in the “running for love” interactive sequence. Thanks to this technique the game switches seamless between gameplay sequences and cut scenes. Maybe here cut scene is the wrong term; you have sequences where you can control Jesper, and sequences where you cannot control Jesper; transition is highlighted by the upcoming of two horizontal black bars at the top and at the bottom of the screen, just like in movies. However animations are built in game engine, there is no visual difference between interactive sequences and not-interactive sequences. AI moves Jesper from the position where you left him to the position programmed by the author. Everything is so smooth and seamless. To say the truth in some scenes you can still interact, you can select the different options of multiple choice dialogues or use the superpower of the bracelet or do other limited actions; maybe the best term is scripted sequences. I wrote here about the need to find new techniques for managing the camera as result of player’s interactivity and programmed AI such to grant always the best view; and even of the importance of scripted sequences in interactive narrative. Embracelet is a good achievement in the right direction. Some commentators complained about the programmed camera movements; in my opinion the programmed camera works fine, provided that player follows the peaceful and slow mood of the game. If you want to run, go fast and play in a hurry, the slow camera struggles to follow Jesper and place itself in the right point of view in short time. My suggestion is: enjoy the contemplative and peaceful atmosphere of the experience, give time to time.Continue here:

_childDocuments_.review: The Norwegian setting and crude low-poly visuals are mostly charming, and the "teen boy investigating his grandfather's past with a magic bracelet" setup has potential. unfortunately, it seems like most of the game is set on one island, which you're asked to explore without any sort of navigational aids - no objective markers, no fast travel, not even an in-game map - and the island map is already large enough to make backtracking tedious; the fixed camera and awkward controls don't help in orienting yourself, either. maybe I'll give it another shot at some point, but that's enough to turn me off from this game for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is a genuinely endearing game that will win over players with its relatable coming-of-age tale, sweeping cinematics, stunning soundtrack, and glorious use of color, providing a soothing experience that still piques plenty of interest. Those seeking a setting off the beaten path will absolutely find that here in addition to both charm and whimsy abound. Embracelet serves as a comforting reminder that love can allow us to do great things, and that we’re all the more richer with people we care for in our lives. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, chill coming-of-age adventure game set primarily on a northern Norwegian isle. The title follows Jesper, a 17-year-old kid from the city who is gifted a mysterious bracelet by his grandfather shortly before his passing and goes off to his grandfather's childhood home to discover its origins. Along the way he meets and befriends two similarly-aged-youths and explores the secrets of the island and the bracelet's past. Embracelet is an overall chill title, largely being somewhere between a walking simulator and a point-and-click adventure title with no time-intensive or pressuring portions. There are some latter segments that require a small amount of platforming, which while forgiving when making a mistake are a bit frustrating due to the controls not being well-suited to precision movement. Achievements are relatively easy to obtain, though there are ending variations that require another playthrough to acquire. Jesper also does on occasion notably get stuck on the environment and ends up teleporting to his intended pathing destination, which is a little jarring but both infrequent a serviceable solution.The game's narrative, its setting, and its artistic direction, a gorgeous and vibrant low-poly style, are its strongest points. The narrative is much as any coming-of-age title, but Jesper and his interactions with others carry a genuine and realistic weight to them that is appreciable in a genre often decorated by excessive melodrama. In simpler terms, it largely reminds of a very chill and calming young adult novel. The setting is refreshing, taking place in what is very distinctly rural modern-day Norway, and the art style helps provide a simplistically minimalist but vivid and rich depiction of it. The one of the two biggest weakness of the narrative, though, are that there is a distinct lack of time cohesion given that game's plot seems to begin to jump from day to day without abandon or notice at a point despite Jesper only going to sleep once on his week-long trip. The second weakness is that I feel a bit more time could have spent with the various characters of the island, though that is more of a compliment to how I much I want more from the narrative rather than it feeling empty or unfufilling. A bit more structure to the overall narrative and a few additional moments/ interactions/ etc. with the cast would go a long to improving the narrative, but the narrative that is there is strong in and of itself.In the end, Embracelet is a title that is refreshing and enjoyable experience that I have found myself coming back to every now and again (to the point where I have bought it both on Steam and on Switch). It is not a revolutionary title by any means and certainly does hold a few faults of its own, but it is overall a fairly high quality game made by one person and one that I will sooner say positive things about then otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sweet coming-of-age story with nice music and simple but stylish graphics.Among other things, it, strangely, reminded me of the old Final Fantasy VII. _childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, heartwarming, wholesome little game. None of the puzzles were overly difficult, and there were some quirky issues with the camera at time, but these were absolutely minor issues for me, and the characters and relationships you build with them and the world of the game in general absolutely more than made up for any tiny flaws like that. Just a very pleasant experience all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game.  It's kinda cute and has a simple but pretty look to it.  The idea of the puzzles with the bracelets is a fun (albeit not original) concept.Pros:Cute and pretty  game.Story driven, following the main protag visiting his grandfathers home to learn more about a bracelet with powerPuzzles in which completing them can affect the game (I think)Cons:Puzzles are usually painfully obvious and far and few between.The camera doing whatever it wants, which made an end puzzle particularly a frustrating pain.Doesn't show keyboard controls, only controller buttons, even though I dont have a controller plugged in.The forced romantic interest. [It was a challenge to pick the friend route, and still ended up hurting people's feelings]Reasoning behind ability was DUMB, better to leave a mysteryStory is rather slow, and some elements could be summed up in a short cut scene than being forced to play through it in which none of the choices really mattered and was more tedious than entertaining.Glitches:The in dark puzzle, had a glitch to where got locked into a wall and couldn't turn around and was too dark even with 1 second flashes of light to attempt to correct it.  Had to reload a past save.The character walking away but the camera not moving or locking on to a scene so you have to blindly navigate back to the area to try to leave again.Soft locked puzzles that required you to leave and return to reset them.Overall its an okayey game.  I will recommend it if only because its not so bad its unplayable and it is a cute story
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely experience this was, an absolute joy to play! Embracelet is a game about growing up, finding your own way, making your own choices and finding people that you want to keep in your life, and all that wrappeed in a beautiful story about visiting Slepp, a remote Norwegian island. I was genuinely surprised by the amount of gameplay and story (~4 hrs for me) there was, and none of it felt like filler or drawn out content. I also can't believe this whole game was made by one single person; I applaud them for it! Definitely recommended if you're looking for a fun and wholesome game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful, engaging, and fun game which I would recommend to anyone looking for a casual, story driven game that they can get through in one sitting (providing their definition of 'one sitting' is somewhere up to 5 hours, which is about how long it took me to complete).The game has a number of different endings, which is good, but it's not really a game I would consider super replayable, which is less good, because if you want to see the different endings, you have to replay the game.There were a couple of times during my playthough that I had no idea how to advance the game, so I wandered around in circles interacting with everything I could, but I also forgot that there was a button I could press that highlighted objects of interest until I was almost finished with the game, so I can't rule out that it was my fault.Overall, I really enjoyed this game, though. Check it out if you get the chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: The power to control tear ducts is strong with this one!A delightful coming-of-age style adventure as you come into the possession of a magic bracelet with incredible power and journey to a quaint island to discover it's originA small cast of characters with short interactions and yet, nearly all are warm, charming and easy to enjoy the company of really quicklyClocked in at about 4 hours for one playthrough, it's a great length and fits a surprising amount in, while giving a wonderful feeling of open space

_childDocuments_.review: First i would like to say i REALLY enjoyed playing this game.Both the story and atmosphere kept me immersed to the very end.Also the attention to details as querky as they might be made me smile on more than one occasion. Like the "buss for tog", the old coin slot machine, which i guess you need to be of age to remember, the doorbell and not at least the outgoing personality that is so typicals for northeners .Highly reccommended

_childDocuments_.review: A new addition to the growing genre of "teenager visits island", with some kindred feeling to Mutazione and Oxenfree, though stylistically more along the lines of Wide Ocean Big Jacket.It's at its very best when it's just about the atmosphere, people and landscapes of Northern Norway. Less so when it tries for "action scenes", deeper lore, or awkward platforming. Wide Ocean knew to stick to what it does well, whereas some choices here are a bit less fortunate. _childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful solemn game with simple but unique functions that differ from the adventure genre norm. _childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible adventure, full of heart and charm.  Note that a previous reviewer is wrong, this is perfectly playable with a mouse & keyboard (just change in the settings before you start the game).Lovely graphics, a beautiful piano-led orchestral soundtrack, and a rich story with excellent characters.  I will remember this one for a long time.  My only complaint is there are some dodgy camera angles, but you soon get used to this and it doesn't detract at all from what is a superbly directed story and a well-flowing game.  The puzzles are simple - but I like that. I loved this from start to finish, taking around 4 hours total to complete.  Possibly my Game of the Year.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely enchanting! A coming of age drama on an island in northern Norway. With beautifully written characters, a picturesque landscape and a thrilling story (subtitles available)! With just under 4 hours a little on the short side, but there was not one minute of boredom...If you came here and actually took the time to read the reviews, chances are very high that you will like this game a lot. Don't be afraid of the platforming sections , they were pretty easy to master...
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: A very cozy, different and heartfelt game, Embracelet will feel a bit generic and shallow in the beginning (edit: to be clear, I refer to the introduction here, before he reaches the island community and the game really starts), but it's well worth your time. The depiction of Slepp, a remote northern Norwegian island community, feels authentic and helps set the game apart, and the music, which was composed by the developer, helps set the mood, too.The game clearly draws inspiration from Night in the Woods (the speech bubbles are an obvious homage), and manages to capture some of that game's charm and atmosphere, while also exploring the "struggling hometown" theme in its own distinct way, while telling an interesting story along the way. My main story complaint is that the characters could have had more depth and personality, and the dialogue feels a bit stilted at times.The pacing mostly holds up, although there are a couple fetch quests that feel a bit drawn out, and some platforming sections with at times awkward camera angles and tricky controls if you use WASD instead of a gamepad. Most of the puzzles are pretty simple, but there are a couple fun and challenging ones. The game is played in 4-5 hours, about the length of a Life is Strange-episode, and the story is beautiful.If you want a game to relax with, with an interesting story, you should give Embracelet a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Nice story, nice environment and characters.Really casual game, with somewhat engaging gameplay.However, what matters is the feeling of attachement to your character and those around him, you go on an adventure with many different feelings. Even some good jokes in there, maybe especially relatable for those from Northern-Norway.Most people could enjoy this game if they gave themselves time to play through it. Took me 4-5 hours, missing some extra tasks.
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is a story-rich adventure taking place in northern Norway. Jesper's life changes when his grandfather gives him a magical bracelet, capable of changing the world around him. We fell in love with this game immediately because of its atmosphere, emotion, and great writing. Please see my video for my full feelingsThank you
_childDocuments_.name: Embracelet

_childDocuments_.review: Embracelet is an adventure game set in Northern Norway - a unique coming of age story about love, loss, friendship and family - and a magical bracelet with mysterious powers. Embracelet is a puzzle adventure game with a gripping story, gentle and satisfying puzzles, exploration and a beautiful, orchestral soundtrack. You play as Jesper, a Norwegian teenager who lives with his mom in the city. One day he is handed an old bracelet by his Grandfather who grew up in a fishing community up north. This bracelet has powers - strange, mysterious powers. Jesper is given the task to unravel the mystery behind the bracelet. Where does it come from? Who does it belong to? And why did his Grandfather leave the island and his old life behind?

name: Cult of the Lamb
detailed_description: Cult of the Lamb: Unholy Alliance Crusade through dungeons, slay heretics, build your cult, and seek new powers together. But there’s more. As well as the addition of co-op play, the Unholy Alliance expansion also adds new tarot cards, relics, buildings, fleeces, follower traits, follower quests, and other secrets to discover! Double trouble Experience the entire Cult of the Lamb campaign in local co-op, with one player inhabiting the role of the Lamb and the other taking on the mantle of the Goat. Enjoy new 2-player twists on existing minigames like fishing and knucklebones, and choose from a selection of corrupted weapons, tarot cards, curses, and relics as you embark on co-op crusades. Cult of personality Unholy Alliance adds a huge number of new follower traits, making your flock more diverse, unpredictable, and charismatic than ever. Cultists can be insomniacs, bust law-breaking friends out of prison, enter a catatonic state after the trauma of a resurrection, or become afflicted with a curse: and that’s just a tiny handful of the quirks you’ll encounter as your cult grows. Power play Take your crusades to the next level with Unholy Alliance’s godlike selection of new relics and tarot cards—some of which have been designed with co-op in mind. The Lamb and the Goat can swap weapons, deal extra damage when fighting back-to-back, or deal a critical hit if their attacks are in sync. Solo players also get a heap of new powers and abilities to play with. Cult of the Lamb: Sins of the Flesh The Lamb must lead, and Followers must follow in Sins of the Flesh, a free content expansion for Cult of the Lamb. As your followers indulge in worldly pleasures, choose their prideful customizable outfits, and treat them to a gluttony of vacation juice, you might find that life may hatch from an egg. Alongside a new levelling system, new mechanics, new quests, and improved quality-of-life features, the Lamb has uncovered a new combat weapon to blast the heretics of the Old Faith. This power can be yours if you yield to the Sins of the Flesh. Sins and Disciples New progression systems add more depth and complexity to managing the Cult of the Lamb. By following the sinful path, your followers will delight in gluttonous rituals, vain buildings, and wrathful doctrines. Invite your most loyal Followers to the inner circle of Disciples, a revamped levelling system of Follower progression. Better Cult Life Shiny poop, baneful brooms, and bigger, better buildings improve busy Cult life. Shiny poops have special effects, like yielding fruitful crops and adding XP to your broom. Levelling up your broom will make chores faster and more effective. To improve automation, there’s also a new tier for the Janitor Station and the Storage Structures so your Followers will take better care of themselves. Ready, Aim, Fire Blast heretics away with the new Blunderbuss weapon. When loaded, it fires big damage in close quarters to bring a new combat playstyle for your crusades. If you charge it up even more with a heavy attack, you can aim to snipe enemies from long range. Outfits, Options and Offspring! Each of your cultists can flaunt their Follower fashion at the new Tailor building. Once unlocked, each cultist can wear their own outfit, with 23 different styles to choose from. But your Cult is getting even more unique. When two Followers love each other very much, they might find an egg. Nurture the egg for it to hatch, then care for the offspring until they're ready to pledge allegiance to your Cult! Cult of the Lamb x Don't Starve Together Don’t let the Lamb starve in this crossover update with Don’t Starve Together! We’ve cooked up a whole new game mode, new themed decorations, and a new follower form to satisfy your hunger. Survival Mode The ails of mortality plague the Lamb in Penitence mode. Eating. Sleeping. You will learn how your followers struggle to survive. But a simple bed isn’t enough for a great leader. The Leader Tent is the perfect place to get your beauty sleep. An Arachnid’s Allegiance Webber arrives from the world of Don’t Starve Together. Can you unwrap the quest to convert them to your cult? They just don’t starve! New Crossover Decorations From homages to the Deerclops and Pig society, to base necessities like the science machine and alchemy engine, you can customize your cult with a whole set of decorations from Don’t Starve Together. Cult of the Lamb: Relics of the Old Faith The Lamb must keep their Cult flourishing, their Followers faithful, and their power unchallenged as they crusade in this free content expansion, Relics of the Old Faith. It adds brand new ways to spread the gospel of the Cult of the Lamb with powerful new abilities, exciting new characters, and thrilling new challenges. Delve into the shrouded history of the Lands of the Old Faith as the Lamb fights to conquer those who would question their power. New Cult buildings will appease your Followers while new combat abilities will smite opposing heretics. Uncover the secrets of the Old Faith so you can be the God you want to be in this massive content expansion! New Combat The expansion brings a deeper layer to dungeon crawling for new and returning players. With powerful Relic abilities, heavy attacks for each weapon class, and dozens of items to find, the Lamb will unleash delightful devastation. New Postgame Another challenge awaits after completing the main story. Revamped dungeons, mysterious characters and challenging boss encounters are in your new quest as the God of Death. Along the way, you can unlock Follower forms, fleeces, unchosen doctrines and more. New Challenges Put your skills to the test with several new challenge modes for combatively competent Cult leaders. Boss Rush, Permadeath and other unique challenges await after defeating the final boss. About the Game Cult of the Lamb casts players in the role of a possessed lamb saved from annihilation by an ominous stranger, and must repay their debt by building a loyal following in his name. Start your own cult in a land of false prophets, venturing out into diverse and mysterious regions to build a loyal community of woodland Followers and spread your Word to become the one true cult. BUILD YOUR FLOCK Collect and use resources to build new structures, perform dark rituals to appease the gods, and give sermons to reinforce the faith of your flock. DESTROY THE NON-BELIEVERS Explore a sprawling, randomly generated world, fight off hordes of enemies and defeat rival cult leaders in order to absorb their power and assert your cult's dominance. SPREAD YOUR WORD Train your flock and embark on a quest to explore and discover the secrets of four mysterious regions. Cleanse the non-believers, spread enlightenment, and perform mystical rituals on the journey to become the mighty lamb god.
