Especially as some take around 30 seconds and you will see them around 100 - 150 times, each, if you go for one full playthrough. Sort of feels like playing the Sims 1 at times, just worse, way, way worse. .) No mod supportBepInEx enables some modding but in a game where you can literally set yourself to be invincible and still get achievements it's beyond me why there is no proper mod support..) Animations - again!I need to stress again that, especially in the late game, most animations are just a massive waste of time and get immensely annoying. So cheat engine and its speedhack feature are a godsend. Cult of the Lamb can easily run on 5x speed with little to no performance hit, yet the developers seemingly don't care to either implement a proper skip/speedup setting or to enable mods to let modders fix it.Which ultimately is just a big f* you to the customer..) User interfaceIt's just an outdated low-tier design. It does not work well for keyboard/mouse and it does not work well for controllers. Period. Also the lack of any proper management overview tab is a massive oversight.Furthere there is an overlapping UI bug: (left upper corner)And that's a constant, not just one time, all the time, 100% of the time. .) PerformanceCult of the Lamb demands more from your GPU than is reasonable: In your cult area performance especially will take a hit: (and that's still good performance, comparatively).) Game balanceThere is hardly any, just as with most RNG based games. Do whatever and hope for good dice rolls, it is simply not required to think, you’ll get by either way. Higher difficulties almost exclusivly increase the grind and the enemy's health, yay…..) ControlsThere is Diablo, Titan Quest, Grim Dawn, Path of Exile, Sacred and many more. They all work perfectly fine with a mouse and keyboard.Then there is cult of the lamb which recommends you a controller and gives a subpar experience if you play with mouse/keyboard (possibly also on controller) due to a often bugged out targeting system and a few unresponsive skills as well as crappy hitboxes on some enemy types..) CrashesI got one hardlock as a ritual just got stuck and one total game crash in 30h, so one crash every 15 hours, not great...(And no, I have not used cheat engine when either of these happened).) EndgameIt's stale, it's there, it's something, but it's just not good. Especially as progress slows down too fast and the “god tear” slot machine - which gives you the late game stuff - has pathetically slow animations, wasting your time even more. (Unless… cheat engine of course)But none of these issues mean that the game is bad or not worth playing. Especially in the first 20~ or so hours, cult of the lamb will have you hooked, hard. After that it's still enjoyable, just not as much.And for around 20€ paired with still free content updates that is not a bad deal. However the game is not nearly as great as the reviews might lead you to believe as looking at it critically leaves much, just so much to be desired.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is an absolute gem in the indie gaming scene, offering a delightful blend of roguelike elements, base building mechanics, and dark humor that will keep you hooked for hours on end.At its core, the game puts you in the hooves of a cute yet diabolical lamb as you embark on a journey to build and manage your own cult. The premise alone is enough to pique curiosity, but it's the execution that truly shines. From recruiting followers to expanding your cult's influence, every decision feels meaningful and adds layers to the addictive gameplay loop.Visually, is a treat for the eyes. The charming pixel art style is expertly combined with eerie themes, creating a uniquely captivating atmosphere that draws you into its world. Whether you're exploring dark dungeons or customizing your cult's headquarters, the attention to detail is commendable.What truly sets apart is its ability to balance lighthearted moments with darker undertones. The game doesn't shy away from its occult themes, yet it approaches them with a sense of whimsy that makes the experience both engaging and entertaining.The roguelike elements add a layer of challenge and replayability, ensuring that no two playthroughs are ever the same. Each run presents new obstacles to overcome and rewards to uncover, keeping you coming back for more.In conclusion, Cult of the Lamb is a must play for fans of indie games and anyone looking for a unique gaming experience. With its charming aesthetic, addictive gameplay, and darkly humorous tone, it's sure to cult-ivate a dedicated following in no time

_childDocuments_.review: I will give this game a decent recommendation. Quick note, if you've played similar games to this, you might want to play on hard, the game is quite easy. My first death was 12 hours in, and I only died once more after that.The easiest way to describe Cult of the Lamb is sort of a cross between Binding of Isaac and Hades, with some light management elements. The problem is that its core gameplay isn't as engaging as any of those games, and it (currently) has no endgame or much in the way of replayability.Neither the combat nor the managing of the cult are really in depth. It starts off simple and you slowly unlock new elements, and just when you think it's starting to ramp up, you realise that you're at the end, it doesn't get any deeper or more complex.A few design choices are also a bit strange. You can unlock Tarot cards to help you in your dungeon crusading; one of the ways to unlock some of them is through buying them at various stores. Unfortunately, a lot of the ones you can unlock are just not very good at all (such as the one where enemies can drop fish), so you'd to better to just buy the 5 or 6 that are useful, and steer clear of the others. This way you have a much higher chance of getting the helpful ones in a run.Picking a doctrine could also fall under this category. When it's time to unlock a new doctrine, you may pick one of 5 categories, each of these categories can be leveled 4 times. You are given a choice between 2 doctrines every level. You cannot see future doctrines, and your choices are PERMANENT; there is absolutely no way to go back and change it. What this leads to is a huge lack of synergy as you have no knowledge of what you can do or build in the later portions of the game, thus your earlygame choice of doctrine might end up being completed negated or even goes against another doctrine you want to pick later on. Having a possibly expensive way to change these would have been appreciated, even if it's just a late game thing. As it stands you either have to look them up, or just note them down and then pick what you actually want on your next play through. There is no endgame to speak of besides running the dungeons over and over and trying to go as far as you can. But, as mentioned in the beginning of this review, the gameplay isn't quite at the level where I personally would do this for another even 10 or 20 hours after I finish up all the content. I sunk an extra 80 hours into Hades just because I enjoyed the variety and combat. Cult of the Lamb doesn't have that same draw.If you don't care too much for your cult, and try to just beat the game, only occasionally doing some side stuff, you're looking at anywhere between 9-11 hours of gameplay. If you're like me and enjoy doing sidequests, checking on your cult, making your base look nice and leveling up, it'll probably last you 15-16 hours. If you're trying to 100% unlock everything, add 5 or so hours to that.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, but it has too many design flaws to be a satisfying experience worth the price tag. The first couple hours are excellent: you get introduced to this cute art style, interesting combat, and the gameplay systems that make up the cult simulator aspect of the game. But these systems lack player choices so much so that taking care of your cult quickly begins to feel like a chore that detracts from the rest of the gameplay.Note that the game is not a roguelike; it's just inspired by roguelike elements. You're never faced with difficult combat. The game is designed such that you are expected to beat every stretch of combat you face. There is no persistence element to the combat, and the procedurally-generated maps are short and again lack meaningful player choice to make each "run" (which lasts 5-10 minutes...) unique and replayable. Here's what I would want to see before I could recommend this game earnestly:- Fix the design of systems within the cult such that players have the agency to make meaningful choices.- Increase the length of the roguelike and add new weapons, abilities, and choices that give the player agency to make each run different.- As it currently stands, having to babysit the cult seriously detracts from the enjoyment of the roguelike elements. Give players the agency to focus on difficult combat without having to worry about "doing their chores".- The cult gets so boring. Seriously. There needs to be a way to make the cult simulator gameplay less boring after the first 5 hours of babysitting. The cult simulator aspects detract from the roguelike aspects and vice versa. - None of the lamb's outfits provide enticing bonuses. I found myself going back to the original outfit most often. It's not rewarding to unlock a new outfit when the bonuses harm you more than help. - Is there seriously no way of rearranging your buildings? I couldn't find a single way to do it. - Make the different types of weapons and curses feel more exciting. I would always just pick up the axe/hammer over any other weapon regardless of their type because the types don't matter as much as having a high attack weapon does. - Add more secrets and different rooms and rewards to the roguelike runs.

I also really liked the gameplay of Knucklebones! it’s a lot of fun and when you’re good at it you can also get some in-game currency out of it! It’s very fun when you just want to chill around a bit. What also surprised me in a very good way was the end game content. I was scared the game would lose its appeal to me once I reach the end game, BUT the content that awaits one there is surprisingly good and I’m very satisfied to say the least. I can recommend this game to everyone who like a cute but also very catchy setting, good game mechanics and likes the freedom of designing their cult in whatever way they like! There’s also always the opportunity to start a different safe game and all are saved in the cloud- so you can actually also play on different devices, never losing ur progress!!! :D

_childDocuments_.review: So, the review for anyone considering this. It's good. Really good. It is not Binding of Isaac. It is not Hades. It is a pseudo-roguelite, in that there are rogelike elements, but they really don't impact much. You have a cult that is basically Animal Crossing, but with death, disease, sacrifice, and very basic base-building. But it is quite enjoyable. I laugh when people say it's like "Oxygen Not Included" though. There is nowhere NEAR the amount of harebrained management of ONI in this game. But if you want a cute Animal Crossing-style game with dark themes, crisp combat, and some customization, this is the game for you. I'm still playing it, but I really hope they add more variety to the dungeon-crawling aspect and make them longer so your "build" actually makes an impact before you return to your cult in 2-3 fights. Also, if you could just flesh out the tech-trees that would also be very beneficial - if you want this to have more replayability, that is. Maybe have some Doctrine-specific buildings, or require a certain number of cult members believing in a Doctrine (from when you enacted it) for it still to be in effect, and maybe have a ritual to reinforce those specific Doctrines? I'm sure yall will think of something. Great game tho, 9/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I thought I wouldn't like it very much. I decided to give it a try after it went on sale and I saw some gameplay on a Let's Play channel, and I am very glad I did.It's got enough rogue-like elements where dying doesn't feel like you're losing progress (you get to keep 75% of your resources upon death) but there's enough permanent upgrades to give a real sense of progress. One of my favorite things about this is that there's object permanence, in the sense of spawned items remaining as long as you remain on that map (except for your projectile ammunition, but those are a dime a dozen). There's a lot you have to do to take care of your followers and it seems intimidating at first, but I found it fairly simple to build myself into a rhythm. You build up enough upgrades for them to take care of themselves to a degree.Definitely recommend checking out the demo if you're not sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just too much fun. Dare I say, you have to be a little sick and twisted to truly appreciate a game like this. Don't let the cute graphics fool you...this game has blood, gore, death, poop, vomit, supernatural beings, demons, monsters, tarot cards, an upcoming sex update, and decisions that will have you question your sanity. Did I REALLY just murder a follower in the middle of the night for becoming elderly? Yes...yes I did. Your followers are adorable, but don't get attached to them. Some of them may not last long or they will randomly get killed or leave your cult. This game is like Supernatural meets Hello Kitty. I won't spoil the story or the major surprises, so I'll just talk about the gameplay.   The combat is super easy to get used to and the different weapons and curses keep it interesting. I like it when games play different every single time with random dungeon generations, different items, enemies, rewards, etc. The different areas that you can visit are fun and add a nice touch to the game. The boss fights aren't too difficult and if they are, you can scale back the difficulty. I appreciate the fact that this game has a ton of accessibility options, such as auto cook, auto fish, dyslexic friendly texts, and a dark mode option for the main screen. Good on the game devs for keeping everyone in mind, I respect that.   If you like fun beat em ups, supernatural/cult stuff, and making lots of decisions, then I highly recommend this game. If you don't think you can bring yourself to make cute animals kill and eat each other, throw them in prison, or do anything that a cult leader would do to their followers, then maybe skip this title. As for me, I own this on Steam AND Nintendo Switch because I can't get enough of it. Everyone, put your hoods up, light your candles, gather up your bones, and get ready to be a cult leader!!

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant. Just brilliant. Without a doubt this is my game of 2022. It's extremely fun. I guess you have to be a little bit into the whole cult/demons genre for it to really click. Usually I'm not into roguelikes mainly because of the combat. But it doesn't bother me at all in this game, it is fairly fast and accessible after all. The game is set in a really 'cute-ish' world where it lets you make really evil and cruel choices, in which the game reminds me of Frostpunk. The base building and managing reminds me of what would be a really relaxed version of Don't Starve. It offers an brilliant little dice mini game that reminds me of Gwent in The Witcher. The graphics, storytelling, soundtrack and mainly the artwork is of top tier quality. I can recommend everyone to play this with a controller, it trumps the mouse and keyboard for sure. I think this game is exactly what we need in this day and age - where everything is political correct and about social justice.. Well, in this game you can just make your followers eat poop for your own entertainment. Bravo to the developers, well worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been excited for this game since the first trailer, and I'm sad to say it was a big disappointment.This would make sense as maybe a $15 game, certainly not $25I'll start with the pros:• The dice minigame is fun• Some of the NPCs are cute• Good soundtrackOk now the cons:• The gameplay is stupid easy. Like, a children's game easy. The enemies are very easy to counter and I doubt you'll ever lose to a boss, mini or final. There's hardly ever a need to dodge roll so they may as well not even have added it. • Village management is half the game but it's even easier than the combat. All the "threats" to the village are nothing. For hunger you just repeat a boring minigame, disease you just place a couple buildings down and never have to worry about it again, and lack of faith will never be an issue so long as you do the sermons you need to progress anyways. Most of the unlocks in the game are for customizing your village and cult members, but that's pointless. Your cult members die constantly as a function of the game so there's no point in spending time to customize them, and why make the village look pretty if there's no cult member you really care about to enjoy it?• You'll blow through the unlocks. Each region has like 15 and you'll get most of them by the time you reach the boss. You can also just buy them at a cheap price with gold coins, which you'll have far more than you know what to do with. Entire areas of the game are dedicated to selling these items that you would have unlocked anyways playing through a couple levels, so it limits the already low replayability.• The upgrades to your weapons feel unbalanced for progression. You can unlock weapons that kill most enemies in one hit before even killing the first boss if you just spend an in game week tending to your cult• The spells seem pointless compared to just attacking as you have a limited number of uses on them and half of them don't have very good effects.• Not going to say what it is but the game tells you what the big twist is just by viewing your save slot

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good enough that it deserves not to be rated in the abstract but in COMPARISON to others in the incredibly crowded Rogue-like genre. While it isn't particularly innovating any specific aspect of combat, rogue-like upgrades, town management, etc., it has combined them in an exceptionally satisfying way. One particular aspect worthy of note is the obvious care that has been put into the details: Every action, no matter how minor, feels EXTREMELY satisfying and "chunky" in a truly delicious way. If you enjoy the general rogue-like progression mechanics, and you like a little bit of town-building/resource management too, definitely give this a look. Are you going to be like, "omg they reinvented the genre"? No, you aren't. But are you going to be like, "damn, they really nailed almost every single aspect of this"? Yes, you are. Oh also the art is v cute :3

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game, Art and sound design is inspired. Combat is a bit of a learning curve and punishing at times. Which is at odds with the very basic/casual town management. The base management is shallow , and kind of pointless. It takes zero real effort to keep the cult happy. Followers traits may as well not be there for all the impact they have on the game. Rituals are hilarious and fantastic, Combat is a roll of the dice depending on what items and spells you are given each time. ( That's the point? ) There's a lot of room for an expansion or squeal. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, I have to say- I adore this game. I tend not to gravitate to rouge-lites, but this game's mix of dungeon crawling and colony sim had me hooked. I've started multiple saves to try out the different doctrine types, and play with the base set ups.I have to say: If you are looking at this game purely for the rougelite aspect, don't get it. This is a game about balancing your time in the dungeon and your time with your colony. It has the capability for you to simply go through rooms forever (granted you've beaten the area boss) but that really isn't the point, and your cult will suffer for it. Both the dungeon and management systems are a bit more lightweight than games that are focused on one, and that's to the game's benefit and detriment. While you can upgrade weapons and curses to have different variants (freezing or life steal, things like that) there's only 5 base weapon types and a handful of curses that have different patterns. Almost all your set up happens on one run, balancing character enhancements and weapon types as you go rather than before you go into a dungeon (save upgrading the types and strengths of weapons you find on each run, and add ons). These are meant to be quick and efficient, with the ability to go back in for long runs locked behind area bosses and setting up you cult to be fine while you're gone.Your cult management is lightweight in that while you need to manage hunger, faith, and buildings, the variety of things you can do and make your followers do isn't super broad. Farms for food and a few resource types (but not all, as somethings must be found in dungeons), housing, worship, and a few odds and ends aren't too incredibly strenuous to manage. There are decorations, but they are a little limited at times. Crafting your tenants, doing rituals, and leveling cult are some of your main focuses, with building resource needs and followers requesting dungeon specific materials keeping you popping back into dungeons regularly enough.I think if anything, endgame does suffer a bit. If you seek and complete most of the sideline quests before beating the end of the game, your incentive to go back into the dungeons becomes based on resource requests and your own prerogative. I do also wish we had a few more decoration options, or buildings we could make purely to give idle followers something benign to  do. If this game ever gets mod support, I might look into creating assets to dress up the base, or expand it, or even allow buildings to be turned to face the side or the back (honestly my biggest complaint with base building, actually). That being said, if my playtime says anything, it's that I thoroughly enjoyed this game and will continue to do so. One word of warning- if you're thinking of getting the game on switch, wait for like. One or two patches. That thing is so buggy.

_childDocuments_.review: Jultymer was once a lost, frightened pig in Darkwood but all her worries have been chased away when the cult leader saved her and recruited her into his faction. She watched in awe as their small group turned into a very fearsome, powerful, and influential sect that slayed those who opposed the great leader—namely the four Bishops of the Old Faith and The One Who Waits. It wasn't easy and with every new follower indoctrinated, new problems arise and one of them is in a form of an otter from Anchordeep. Jultymer did nothing but obey and worship the cult leader without question, always lowering her head as she is naive and faint-hearted. The compassionate cult leader noticed this and reassured her time after time and when she finally found her voice, someone started hating her for it. Pamerbre, a hot tempered otter noticed the weak Jultymer climbing the ranks and it did not sit well with him so he started making her pay for it. The small arguments escalated into full blown fist fights but none of them were punished. The tolerant and tenderhearted cult leader can only sigh and break off the fight, but this cannot go on. One time, the leader was a little too late to get in between the two of them so Jultymer got injured badly, and while she was healing all she could think about is how to permanently stop Pamerbre's ill doing. She has a plan and all she needs to do is to ask the leader, a fight to the death! A fight pit ritual! This will settle everything once and for all. But the ever benevolent leader have different plans for the two of them. Instead of using violence, the cult leader decided to make them mates. Jultymer is utterly dumbfounded, speechless even and the same can be said for Pamerbre. The poor innocent Unique Corn was damned after he became stupidly drunk thrice just to extract his Sin, something that is needed for the mating ritual that was bound to fail. Oh, it did fail but the cult leader is very persistent so he tried, and tried, and tried again. This time the cult leader has gotten clever in extracting sins and from 0% to to 50% success rate, Jultymer and Pamerbre gave in and produced an offspring. A tiny egg that the cult leader adored. He couldn't leave the settlement for a while since the egg needed to be tended to but he didn't mind, he treated that egg as his own as it fully hatched into a child—a child Jultymer and Pamerbre didn't care for as they pick up where they left and that is to antagonise each other. As Pamerbre continue picking fights despite the cult leader's effort, he had to make a tough decision. A choice to sacrifice Pamerbre to reopen Silk Cradle, and with that, peace and order have returned in the community., , , , , , , , , , , , TL;DR: Two of my followers won't stop fighting so I had an amazing idea of making them mate. I thought it won't work because they are enemies and there's 0% chance to breed. At first at least. I'm nothing if not persistent. Their baby is the first baby in my cult so I was really happy when I manage to pull through. Thank you devs for making my enemies to lovers happen like a fanfic writer LOL

_childDocuments_.review: This is animal crossing if it was a mobile game without cooldowns. You have a home base, and then you go out on raids to bring back new troops and resources. (Sounds like Clash of Clans? The game feels like it).But instead of in game ads bothering you with pop-up sales on gems, your villagers bother you with tedious requests. These worthless villagers are a chore. I’m supposed to feel attached to them since I named and customized their appearances, but I have no love for them. For some of their villagers, I sacrificed them after giving me a quest rather than deal with their pitiful problems. Villager: I need flowers. Not the flowers we’re growing right here on our farm even though there’s only one type of flower in game. No, I need you to go redo the dungeon you already did 4 times, and get me flowers from there. The dungeons are tedious. There’s no variation between them, and they make you do the dungeon from each realm portal at least 4 times. For a roguelite, this seems like nothing, but you seemingly gain nothing from dungeon to dungeon making it feel like a chore. In most roguelites, you go through the dungeon over and over again, attempting to get better at the game. But in this game, the materials that can be obtained from the dungeon can be obtained elsewhere. And usually you do this rather than complete the dungeons again. Because you don’t need to get better at the dungeons in order to progress. Because the weapons are randomly distributed at the start of you entering the dungeon and the combat system requires nothing more than dodging and slashing. The monsters are different between the 4 realm portals, but not necessarily harder. The method of making new realms harder is by lengthening the dungeons by giving more rooms to fight through- the same exact rooms copy and pasted over and over again. While it works in some roguelites, it doesn’t work here. The NPCs look cool, but they’re all superficial. They’re either one-off characters or a running gag. The guide, Ratau, seems significant in the tutorial, but has no dialogue after that. He nor any of the other NPCs in his house so much as acknowledge it after you defeat the end boss which makes the world seem empty. There is no incentive to do anything after the endgame unless you’re trying to complete it for achievements. Once you complete all the commandment stones, I didn’t feel an incentive to level up my villagers anymore. The economy’s cracked. You run out of objects to waste gold on rather quickly. It’s difficult to earn resources in the beginning, but after you’ve gotten your first few farms set up, you’ll never want for anything again. The story’s predictable. The NPCs are constantly warning you about the possible ending, but it’s rubbed in your face so much that when the twist ending happens you’re just like “oh, yeah, that was going to happen.” I personally only ran into one bug which is impressive. When asking to marry me, the quest-giver said “I know you’re already married to —”. While I was married, I wasn’t married to the character the quest-giver named. Usually religious trauma makes for great video games, but this isn’t quite it. For the first 5-6 hours or so I was hooked on this game. The art-style is cute, the music’s nice, the creators put a lot of love into it, and the premise is oh-so-intriguing, which is the reason I bought this game. But the game is bogged down by unrefined mechanics, a clunky combat system and economy. It leaves you wanting more after you start hitting the second half of the game, and you begin looking for more material that isn’t there. If this game ever goes on sale for less than $10, it’s worth it. But there’s not enough content to justify spending over $20.

It's a bit samey sometimes, but it's still fun and not too much.There was one part that was annoying, though. There's this enemy that I couldn't beat at first, and it killed me a lot. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but the different parts feel like they come from different games, and they don't go together very well. There's both a half-baked base building game, and a much better but still incomplete action dungeon crawler in the same game, and they really don't interact with each other very deeply. The game claims randomly generated levels, but it's really a few hand-made arenas with the rocks and enemies shuffled around. There's also no over-arching level, it's a series of small rooms until you reach the end. I'm really disappointed so much great art and music went into a mediocre game.

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet. Looking forward to updates or sequels! Finished everything and collected almost everything in about 17h. Ignore my Steam playtime because I was er, "trying it out" outside of Steam. Thankfully my save carried over.Pros:- Cute art, animations, etc. Plus the whole gore and cult thing.- Start and manage your own cult! Play it like Animal Crossing except you (well, your cult) actually need that stuff you collect to survive!- Soundtrack is decent.Neutral:- Difficulty. I've heard that the game is pretty easy on Normal so I went with Hard. Yeah, I managed to finish the whole game on Hard without dying once, and only retreating only once during a boss fight. I'm no pro gamer AND I've played the whole game on mouse+keyboard, and even Hard is not too hard. IMO Hard offers just the right amount of challenge for regular gamers, while Normal and below are probably good enough for casual gamers.- You can take your Followers with you in the form of demons. Even without them, the game is easy enough as it is. It's up to you to use them or not.- Gameplay is relatively straightforward. You've got different weapons with slightly different effects and damage values, but they're all pretty much the same. Same with the spells/curses. Dodge roll to dodge stuff. The core gameplay doesn't really change much even until the end of the game. It's fun enough to me though.- There are some random elements for every run (starting weapon/curse, tarots, rooms, enemies, etc.), but not enough to consider it a true roguelike experience. On the upside I haven't encountered any run that was extremely unfair, which can happen with roguelikes. It's good enough for the 17-20 hours or so of playtime, but needs additional content for replayability.- Story is decent, but predictable. The lore isn't that deep like say with Cultist Simulator if that's what you're looking for.Cons:- There are still some bugs that I'll need to reset the game. Thankfully, they all happened in my village and not during runs or boss fights.- Some of the Doctrines and Cultist Actions are obviously much better than the other choices.- I wish the game describes effects more accurately, like when turning your followers into demons. I was worried that it might kill them off, but they just transform back to normal (but exhausted) after a run.

The charm is through the roof, the game is beautiful and breathtaking, the visuals are adorable and the music is well crafted and the colony management aspect of the game is pretty well done... But the actual game is just... Not for me... I'd like more a challenge and this game isn't gonna give this to me. it's a massive shame. It was the first game in years I was really damn hyped for. If you looking for an visually pleasing and adorable colony manager game that's actually really well made. Play it, buy it. It's worth it. If you're like me and an avid rogue-like enjoyer that's looking for a true rogue-like experience that enjoys some challenge then skip this one.EDIT:Made the ending statement a bit more positive

_childDocuments_.review: Starting with the good: The game overall is good. Of course the art style is great, the writing is good and makes a believable and unique world. The entire concept is unique and meshes together community building sims with rogue-lite combat and it just all feels... Right, like this is a cult building game that should have been made forever ago. Thinking on it now that kind of sums up the game as a whole, two sides of a coin. Cutesy cartoonish art and character designs in a rather cruel and dark world with murder and sacrifices. A calm and mostly relaxing community managing sim before you go out and murder cultists, eldritch monsters and literal gods. The music is nice and adorable in a strange way with non nondescript singing that then flows into a more intense beat and a deeper chanting. Overall it pulls off this really interesting duality in more ways than one.It does so much right but to be more specific, building the cult and managing your settlement is about 60% of the game while the combat is the other 40% give or take. The settlement aspect is great, it is relatively simple with clear research trees and goals, the mechanics are explained to you well but at the same time you are not being hand held the whole way through and allows you to play and build how YOU want too. the overall management is fun and unlocking things allows for many different decisions to be made with what order you unlock things but also "one or the other" doctrines that unlock community buffs or one of two very different rituals. Customizing and interacting with cult members is fun and doesn't require a ton of micromanaging. However one small gripe with them is later on when you reach closer to 15-20 members there frankly isn't enough work to keep everyone busy and most everyone just ends up defaulting to praying at the shrine. As for the combat, it's good if a tiny bit weaker than the cult management. Again it feels good and is really easy to pick up with only a handful of weapon types but also slight variations on said weapon types, but there is a fair amount of magic as well that does feel like it has more variety. The It does have it's challenges and does have difficulty selection for those that do want it to be easier or harder which is nice considering most other roguelike/rogue-lites don't even give you a selection like this.But now the bad: The sheer amount of bugs still present at release and even afterwards is... frustrating to say the least. The amount of bugs that were locking people out of save files, not unlocking achievements, basically breaking the whole game until you restarted it is absurd. All these bugs also went alongside strange performance issues, nearly everyone I talk too including myself notices a strange mini stutters every few seconds when just playing the game. This performance problem is STILL in the game as well as a whole flood of other bugs. Yes the devs are working on them but it feels like their priorities are just in the completely wrong direction, fixing things that aren't even really the problem. It genuinely feels like the game should have been delayed a little longer to have all these problems looked at and figured out BEFORE release. These bugs were all present in early access copies that content creators got so WHY WAS NOTHING FIXED? It's as though we should coin the term "Cyberpunk effect" where developers either don't test their games before launch or are aware of the problems but actively choose to just release it and say "ah we will fix it later and it will be fine in a few months." To make matters worse, the developers now seem to be prioritizing nerfing things into the dirt in a single player game. Ok yes it wasn't intended for an armor to give the player the ability to one hit bosses, but who is it hurting? Other players?  Oh right it's a singleplayer game, just let people have their fun. Better yet why was this change more important than fixing the games stuttering or the mountain of other bugs? But on a different note, the combat can feel a bit odd at times and just something about how the camera zooms out and how much is happening on screen does make it hard sometimes to keep track of where you are currently at. The weapon types might as well all just be the same with different attack speed and damage numbers besides the gauntlets and hammer which do actually play a bit differently.Honestly I love the game. I guess my problem is with the developers, not the game itself. Yes the game has earned it's million copies milestone and I genuinely am happy it did but a part of me wished the developers and publisher loved it as much as the fans do and had given it some more time in the oven to fix these major problems. Problems they seem to be ignoring whenever we bring them up... I'm really looking forward to content updates and even DLC later down the line but I pray they don't make this mistake again. I don't want to add a "The Ugly" portion to this review later on if they release additional content in the same broken state 1.0 was.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-cute artstyle-soundtrack is nice-the animations feel fluidCons-combat is a bit too basic-it's a bit unclear sometimes whether you have been hit or not-the tarot card upgrades are too boring/simple, they don't fundamentally change the way you fight -the cult upgrades are too simple/boring, don't really change the gameplay that much-you spend more time micromanaging your cult than doing fun things-there's no skip animations for sermons/rituals/etc, it's a bit boring to have to wait through it everytimeOverall, the keyword I'd choose to describe the experience is "shallow", initially the game throws a lot at you but over time you come to realise it has very little depth. _childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is comparable to a hybrid mix of a few different games. - The dungeon crawling of Binding of Issac- The atheistic of Don't Starve- The cute sim/village management game of a darker Animal Crossing.I've seen reviews of game breaking bugs, glitches, issues, lack of play-ability, and lack of difficulty to name a few. I have my own take, and my own experience with these complaints. I've not once came across a game breaking bug that bricked a safe file or crusade run, I've had issues with memory leaks that caused massive stuttering and screen freezing, but it was a simple save and restart that would fix the problem.Glitches? I expected glitches, but so far most of the glitches and issues I'm coming across are yes annoying, but it's not breaking my enjoyment with the game. My only major glitch I even came across was where I tried accepting a request during a day/night transition and it insta-failed me, but with how far along I already was, 35, 45 faith really didn't mean anything as I easily brought it back up with my graves, sermons, bonfires, or just dancing with my people. Yes I've had some glitches where random particle effects would spawn in the village, previously destroyed paths or ground would respawn when I didn't want them to. not a bug or glitch but it's REALLY annoying to move every single individual plot of farmland when you are trying to move things around more efficiently. But again this is a newly launched title that I expected bugs, and it's up to the devs to bring fixes. My biggest fear right now is the issue with lack of play-ability, which I completely agree on. Out of 5 doors, I've finished 2, halfway to finishing the other 2 and I've already unlocked everything aside from tarrot cards, decorations, and follower forms. There's nothing really left for me to work on my village aside from making things pretty and raising the loyalty of my favorite two followers which isn't even necessary at this point. I want more unlocks, I want secret unlocks, I want secret rooms like in Binding of Issac, I want more fishing spots, I don't want to gamble with a bunch of old crazy characters over rolling dice. But even as far in with the game I'm in, I'm still enjoying myself a lot, the music, the sounds, getting through the dungeons and bosses. I'm excited truly, and those who are complaining about lack of difficulty, I'm confused as they must be master Binding of Issac/Hades players, because as someone who can hardly play Dead Cells without the assist mode on, even easy mode has some challenge for me. Even my friend who is a hardcore Dark Souls player and has beaten Dead Cells is finding challenge with the game on normal and has even died a time or two. Challenge isn't an issue, not personally, and I'm glad an easy mode even exists so casual people like me can enjoy something like this. I want to encourage the developers to love what they've created, and continue to improve on it like Hello Games improved No Man's Sky and how MotionTwin has stated that Dead Cells isn't even past its half life yet!!Games can have scary releases, and there's a chance that the game could stay dead on arrival like Banished and Cube World, or flourish like No Man's Sky and Dead Cells. For that reason I don't want to scare away the Devs, I don't want this amazing rough diamond to become abandonware. Cult of the Lamb is not for everyone, and it may not even be for the hardcore roguelike-lite players that it's targeting. Even if you're not a super big fan of rogues, if it's on sale or even had a demo of a single dungeon crawl or maybe a day or two in the village would be a perfect test for people to see if they'd really like this game. Cult of the Lamb is a rough, but good game with good heart, I can tell there was effort, I can tell there was passion. And I don't want to see that passion die out because of it's rough start. It's not game of the year, but it's still a good game that can win many people's hearts.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique rouge-lite's I've ever played. This game has soo much charm and visually it's extremely pleasing to watch. While the game actually has quite a lot of weapon and powerups to choose from that can fit to your play-style, and the combat has a great amount of depth to it, if you're looking for a game that's got a ton of different weapon variety and the more traditional rouge-lite experience, maybe go for a similarly charming game like Voidigo or Enter The Gungeon, as this game places more emphasis on it's base building and resource/follower management than combat, however it is an integral part of the game-play loop. _childDocuments_.review: It's kinda cute in an eldritch kinda way, it's pretty well made all things considered, and the loop is engaging. It's just that it could've been a lot better like bringing in the cult to the rougelike aspects outside of their needs bar being essentially a time limit. You can explore all you like in the rougelike sections and bosses but your cult will die if you don't get back soon enough. However aside from one or two perks you can get that'll let you kill your cultists for power the cult merely exists to unlock weapons/curses and stages. Once everything is unlocked the cult is basically useless. The funnier part with the cult base building is that it's almost entirely self-contained. There are upgrades which can help automate certain parts of upkeep, but nothing that will really elongate the rougelike timer the cult is. There is one structure that can let you bring cultists into dungeons, but that's basically all the cult is. A timer, unlocks things, and maybe bring a little help if you really want to. The rougelike sections themselves aren't that deep either. You got a dodge roll, weapon attacks, ranged curses, and some basic passive upgrades like slightly more damage and situational slightly more damage. The weapons can mostly be boiled down into 2 weapon types, heavy weapons that kill in one or two hits and lighter weapons that you swing a lot and try to kill with multiple slaps. That boils it down a bit, but realistically that's all you need to know about the weapons. If you like the aesthetic it's fine, but compared to other roguelikes it's far from the best. If I had any recommendations for changes it would be to integrate the cult and the dungeons together. Maybe ways to send cooked food from in the dungeon or ways to get power from specific individuals at a shrine or something.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style this game has brought. But that's all it's brought.The flock mechanics is a shell of a system that has barely anything to do within it and barely any management at all. There's no "cult management" that you might expect from it, only effects that are so strong that they obliterate any semblance of a management of the colony. Not only that, there's almost no depth to what you can do with your individuals either. They provide almost nothing in differences between each other than very slight gains in certain areas. Each individual's special conditions are so interchangeable that they're completely forgettable. Did this one like being sick or were they a germophone? Does it matter?The roguelite part of it is... okay. It's a decent system, but there's no depth at all past a certain point. Each modifier does almost nothing to change the way that the game is played and there's little to no semblance of randomness between each run. Not only that, but what should be endless looping mode seems to shut you out at 3 loops maximum. In terms of randomness, the only thing being offered is the different classifications of weapons. Each type of weapon's effect with the single exception of the final tier, which is just noticeably more damage, is completely forgettable. I don't care which variant of a weapon I have, the base weapon the variant is applied upon is the only thing I even notice. The Tarot Card system seems to be their attempt at making each run feel unique but half the time it's just "More HP" or effects that are one-off and don't create fun synergies. There also seems to be no thought put into balancing some of the run modifiers either. One in particular stands out amongst the rest, which is a modifier that gives +10% damage per kill, reset upon taking damage. This is not capped. Why isn't it capped?Lastly, there's the bugs. Wow, there are still so many. I've managed to softlock the game 5 different ways at this point. I have a follower that cannot level and is permanently at maximum Loyalty and so has the glowing eyes effect which I can't get rid of. Sometimes rituals will take minutes to play out because... I think it's trying to find missing villagers to walk in? It really bugs out if you try to perform a ritual after you've just dismissed the flock and half of them have already left the building. Some of these are minor annoyances but some of these require whole game restarts! Which is especially annoying when it happens in the middle of a run and you're forced to give up all progress and resources gained.Overall, I wish this game was more polished. There's no semblance of an endgame and the replayability is almost nil. There should have been more thought put into the flock mechanics and how they're going to keep each run fresh. As it is now, every run feels exactly the same and I've eaten all the game has to offer already...Cute animals though.

_childDocuments_.review: Just over a year ago I played Cult of the Lamb on stream. The game itself looked promising and I was interested in the art style combined with the dark themes and rogue-like mechanics. Whilst the stream itself was enjoyable, with viewers contributing stupid names for members based on food, (the cult was named ‘Burger Cult’) the game lacked challenge.Rogue-likes are most often known for their challenging nature. Cult of the Lamb in the first stages of the game can be quite difficult, maintaining your cult and going out on crusades requires a good balance so that you have enough followers to access certain portions of the game as well as unlocking weapon and curse upgrades.Around the middle part of the main game, I found that despite increasing my difficulty to the highest possible setting, the gameplay eventually became about feeding your cult grass (a popular trait you can give to your cult followers right near the start of the game which makes it really easy to sustain their hunger). The game then shifts to, going to your base, using grass to make dishes, making occasional buildings and upgrades, and going on crusades. Crusades do sometimes provide a challenge although I did wish more features were added to make the base maintenance part of the game more difficult.This changed however, when I re-visited the game 5 days ago. I found that there was a scenario where followers could become corrupt, kill each other, followers could breed for better stats, a new mechanic relating to sin encouraged players to play chaotically, a gauntlet feature encouraging use of fleeces, several new story elements and a GUN. I knew this game was going to be enjoyable when I equipped the ‘Blunderbuss’ and began shooting the faces of demons.I’m saddened to say I wasn’t able to try the co-op mode (if any of my friends are reading this, maybe we can try it out). In the beginning of the run I picked the golden fleece. It allows you to gain a damage boost for each enemy killed, but resets when you’re hit and enemies can also deal double damage to you. I was able to get a Blunderbuss to over 600% and almost one shot every enemy I came across, it was awesome.Special moves are also a fun feature. Relics in combination will allow you to use special abilities. Special moves are stronger attacks of any of the six weapons. My least favourite special move has to be the dagger as it makes the game way too easy. I often found myself avoiding the use of this attack. I also think the developers knew it was overpowered since killing an enemy with it doesn’t increase your golden fleece damage bonus.The sin feature added a lot of interest in maintaining the base. Collecting sins could result in aesthetic upgrades to your church (no easy challenge if you intend on upgrading your base all the way). The fun part was in the decision making where the player could either collect sin slowly by brewing beers, playing drums and allowing other members of the cult to mate OR a player could go ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy making their followers eat each other and wreak havoc upon the cult. I went with the latter option and in many instances a lot of my followers ended up dying. I now had a reason for maintaining my base carefully and also ensuring I had enough followers to make sure I was getting necessary maintenance of my base. There’s also a permadeath mode which I intend on playing on stream (maybe we could even do a speedrun). The Purgatory run (the game’s gauntlet mode which allows the player to use different fleeces) can get a bit repetitive but the game rewards you with a God Tear for really cool and interesting items. When I first played the game, fully upgrading your base would result in devotion turning to money but now it takes much longer to get valuables from devotion (which I’m thankful for). Increases in collectibles are not bad actually. It was a lot of fun collecting every lore tablet and collecting outfits for my cult. If you’re an achievement hunter then I can strongly recommend buying this game. Achievements are much harder to come by the first time around now with new updates and items finally making the challenging parts of the game worth it.Overall this game went from a 6.9 to a 8.5 with the new updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think it was possible, but they did it. They made a botched PC port in the year of our lord 2022. Never before have I bore witness to a botched PC port of an indie game, but alas here it is. Oh boy, where to start? First of all, optimization. This is not a complex game, so naturally you'd expect it wouldn't be very demanding; and in the grand scheme of things, it isn't. Most of the time. I have regular stuttering and frame dips from just regular gameplay, but some screens (namely the upgrade screen) make my PC's GPU skyrocket all the way to 100% usage, and dips the frames to the low TWENTIES. Being my computer is far, far above the specs listed in the "recommended" requirements, this is really bad. Furthermore I know this isn't just my computer as it also tanks my Steam Deck; for which the game is VERIFIED. Same story with the stuttering and frame dips too. This was reported in the forums as far back as the game's release, and still occurs for some users (like me). Second is cloud saves, which have been completely botched. More minorly, the game does not sync data between Windows and Mac versions of the game. While this doesn't affect me personally, I do think it speaks to how little care was put into the PC version of the game. While it's  that the saves aren't compatible between versions, that almost never happens with Unity, so I don't believe that to be the case at all. More majorly, the game does sync graphics configurations onto other devices. How fun! Now the game goes completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when I switch between PC and Deck because of the conflicting resolutions. How nice. This also means if you wanted to play the game on higher settings on one machine and lower settings on another, you don't have that choice since those options sync to the cloud! Not that you'd want to with the game's poor optimization, you really are better off keeping the game at low. This issue, like the prior one, has ALSO been an issue since release! Once again, no effort was made to fix it, even after all the content updates. Very cool.As for critiques for the game itself, and this is very personal taste but I want to keep my review to the rule of 3, I never cared much for the artstyle. And no, I don't mean the weird snout-mouth thing some guys have going on. More I just think the "cute thing go scary" thing is wildly overdone, and this game does not try to set itself apart in any way. It feels like it goes way too hard with the overt edginess both in theming and in dialog, and most of my time playing it that wasn't spent gawking at my poor framerate was spent feeling just kind of turned off by the whole thing. It's super on-the-nose, but not in a funny, self-aware way; it feels like the game feels like the juxtaposition is way more original than it really is. Having the juxtaposed cult theme with a cute artstyle could work super well if the game had some better writing making it clear it knows the trope is overdone, but it doesn't have that, and it just  Cringy? Gross? I don't know how to describe it, but it's some emotion between those three. I don't like it. Bottom line: I don't like it.TL;DR because no one is going to read allat, game's performance is poor and some areas are obviously severely unoptimized, cloud saves were an afterthought that cause more issues than they solve, and the game's general juxtaposed cute-but-scary aesthetic is extremely overdone and the game brings nothing else to the table to make it feel original. Gameplay's fine, but somewhat generic as well and marred by these issues to the point that they really can't be ignored. For the price especially, I really can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: There is really not much more positive you can say about this game that hasn't been said already. It's a lot of concepts thrown together and some how they all come together to work. You are both dungeon diving and running a small village, both end up being important to balance. You really can't dungeon dive without the support and upgrades provided by your village, and you can't get anywhere without the dungeon diving. It creates a fantastic feeling of management. Helped of course by the fact that the game pushes you over time to being an extremely heartless cult leader. I could say more, but the combat is pretty basic for this genre, so you probably already know if you like it or not. If you don't, this would probably be the game to try out, it doesn't get particularly difficult and I died very few times. I'm not good at games either, so I know there are people just dominating the whole thing out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: The theme and art style work so well together that it makes you ignore some of the massive flaws with the gameplay. Very easy combat and bosses with only 5 weapons and a handful of curses. Before I beat the final boss I had fully unlocked everything without even trying to. There are a lot of fun ideas but none of them are fleshed out enough for me to want to play any more than my first run. Also a lot of this would be more acceptable to me if I could get into the base decorating side of the game more, but because of a lame bug I cannot remove paths that I have already placed and so my floor looks like a Jackson Pollock. 5/10 I fully believe this game is on the right path to being a great game, but it is far far from it currently.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, GORGEOUS art style and smooth animations, 10/10. I'd say village management is a mild mix of Oxygen Not Included + Don't Starve. Examples: cult members can get tired, hungry, sick, or lose belief. They must be treated accordingly.You plant stuff like berries and pumpkins to then cook them and feed the cult. You can build toilets for them in order to have a dedicated place to go (otherwise, they go to the edges of the village to do their business, i.e. create manure!). Every individual cult member also needs a dedicated bed to rest or they will be tired and less believing. You also chop wood, mine stone, etc. The game has numerous and at first seemingly overwhelming mechanics with several upgrade trees, each requiring different methods to level (prayer, sermon, sacrifices, commandments).Lastly, the battle gameplay is rather simple (one simple combo depending on weapon + one "spell"), but entertaining. Heavily dodge-oriented. However, "veterans" of the games such as The Binding of Isaac, Enter the Gungeon, Rogue Legacy, Dead Cells, etc. will not find any battle/run-related difficulty in this game.Nevertheless, it is worth every single penny. The game is not challenging but highly entertaining. It is one of those games which make time fly x10 faster. "Well, it's 1:00AM, guess I'll read a sermon and go to sleep... Okay, maybe gather the plants and conduct a ritual of dancing around fire, but that's it." *15 minutes passes* "WTF 4:00AM???"Must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: The Cult of Lamb is a fun, replayable and aesthetically appealing game about making and looking after a cult of inept followers. The main challenge of the game is balancing growing your cult and beating the bosses, since if you go on an adventure for too long your citizens get angry and hungry. While at times this can be annoying, most of the time it's just a quick fix that is kinda like doing a daily chore. It's interesting watching the cult go from a inept to self sufficientThe controls are smooth and everything from the dashing to the combos attacks, the weapon system is simple yet effective in it's execution, making the player choose whether they want a fast weapon with low damage or a slow weapon with high damage was a good decision. It might have been better to give players the choice of a weapon before spawning in and not having it be RNG but it isn't a big issue.The side missions are a bit of a let down in terms of fun factor. The first three you encounter in the game is The juxtaposition between the cutesy art style and the blood and monsters in the game make for a nicely unique experience. It's hard to say that a games art style is unique in this day and age (Exceptions being Cuphead and Faith: The Unholy Trilogy) but this games art style might just qualify as a unique style as it's imagery is both disturbingly detailed and simplistic at the same time.This is easily one of the best indie games to come out of 2020s and it is worth the price. Additionally their response to the Unity controversy was well done and not in poor taste like other indie teams. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely one of the best games I have ever played, it has rouge-like elements with a big emphasis on base building. combine all the good aspects of Hades, Binding of Isaac, animal crossing and don't starve and put it into one game in an amazing package and gameplay loop. the subtle automation in the game with your followers makes the gameplay loop a lot more fun as well. something else to mention is that the twitch integration is the best twitch integration I have ever seen, it is extremely user-friendly, it doesn't have any chat commands or anything you just click on the screen what you want, and you can get your viewers as your cultists, viewers can choose to either ♥♥♥♥ you over or help you and they can use channel points to put towards your cult.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: It is like animal crossing: new horizons but if animal crossing had sacrificing, murder and actual content. Really cute game in contrast with a dark premise really makes this game stand out. the art work is amazing, and this game is just fun. it has a bit of everything for everyone. it has roguelike elements, dungeons, boss fights, colony and base building, pokemon collecting elements, fishing, farming, and more. Despite having a lot of different elements in the game, each part is pretty fleshed out and they dont feel out of place, they mesh well together into a smooth and fluid experience. I am not done the game yet but I feel like I got a good idea of where the game is going, and I am having a blast so far. Highly recommend this game and do not skip out on this experience.

Developed by Massive Monster, this enchanting action-adventure game promises to deliver an unparalleled journey that will leave players eager for more.Cult of the Lamb plunges players into a surreal and enchanting world filled with rich lore and fantastical creatures. As the lamb, players must navigate through treacherous landscapes and lead their cult followers to build a thriving community. This presents a unique blend of city-building and rogue-like gameplay that promises countless hours of engaging content.One of the core mechanics in Cult of the Lamb is the transformation aspect. As players progress, their lamb avatar will unlock various transformations, each with distinct abilities and playstyles. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves the roguelike genre, Cult of the Lamb is conflicting for me. On the positive side, I like both core parts of the gameplay, the roguelike dungeon crawling combat and the cult management. The combat is straightforward and feels good, the bosses are fun and unique, and the randomization of weapons and cards keeps runs interesting. The cult gameplay was a lot more fun than I expected, I personally find the most interesting mechanic to be doctrines, several choices that you make that may significantly alter how your cult works, for example you can choose whether your followers find it a good or bad thing when a follower dies of old age, if you choose for them to see it as a bad thing, you now have to sacrifice old followers before they die of their age, or else the morale of the entire cult will be lowered. Those two core factors of the gameplay combined with several different areas you can visit with quests and minigames makes the game feel very open, and there's so much to do. On the negative side, when you get late into the game all those separate parts begin to lack depth. The game lacks the features present in other roguelikes that make them replayable. Once you've unlocked everything in the cult management part of the game there's really not much to do apart from decorate, the game offers no way to expand your cults territory or any other thing that would allow you to keep going. Similarly, in the dungeon crawl side of the game, once you've beat all the bosses there's really no reason to go back, no challenges or modifiers to up the difficulty. These things are perfectly fine for one playthrough, but for being in a genre that is based around replayability, the fact that this game has almost none is very disappointing.Ultimately, what I have to say about this game is that

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it a lot and adore the idea. With some tweaking, bug fixes and content updates, this can be an amazing game. It's short compared to other roguelikes but I still recommend it for the unique experience it has. It's especially good as someone's first rogue-like, the game doesn't expect you to sink in weeks and replay it several times just to experience everything. It has a nice difficulty curve (alongside difficulty options) instead of killing you at the beginning 50 times 'till you learn enough. This can be downside as well for people who expect this to be a rogue-like similar in difficulty and length as others.I love the game's artstyle, the combination of cute and dark is so great. The fact that they can make sacrificing, death and cannibalism look so normal and not disgusting is impressive. The doctorines you can pick from were sometimes funny to read with how morally grey they can be or how you can make your cult think something that's normally 100% wrong to be completely OK. This game knows what it is and I like it. I just wish there was a bit more flavour text with NPCs or followers.Monster designs are nice and I like the variety of forms your followers can have. Being able to decorate your base also adds more charm to the game, I rarely decorate in games but for once I did. At the time of writing I did have a visual glitch where some of the tiles I placed would briefly be the wrong tile for a second when coming on screen.The music is amazing, there isn't a single song I dislike. The effect that's done on the music when you're hit makes taking damage more impactful. Sound design also is good.I enjoyed my time with it. The combination of going on a rogue-like adventure and building your cult works pretty well. Everything you do while exploring can directly impact what you're gonna do at your cult. You can't spent too much time in both as you need resources for your cult and can't leave your cult alone for too long. It's a good balance.Combat is simple but enjoyable. I did expect a little more weapon variety but the ones that are here do all feel different to use. Room layouts could use a bit more variety. It did become better later on with environmental hazards and having some enemies come from the ceiling (I like it when games that use 2D art in a 3D world do stuff like that). Should also note that I really appreciate there being an arrow sometimes that indicates the direction a monster is attacking towards, makes things not unfair.The base building isn't super complex but that's a good thing for this game 'cus you're not always at your base. Upgrading things to get more automated feels good, not everything can be automated like keeping faith high but that's alright as it gives you some time pressure while crusading. Just seeing everything run well in your base during the final hours of the game is very satisfying.Watching the followers do anything is charming and you feel more powerful as your cult grows. I do wish they had more impactful triats, it's mostly very minimal and doesn't make them too distinguished from each other. It's also not too difficult to keep them satisfied (at least on normal difficulty, can't say for the harder ones yet), I didn't get a single one to turn against me. The random quests they give you are nice, there are a few that aren't worth the effort but others are funny like a follower randomly asking you to let them eat a dish made out of follower meat. I like that some of them have an actual quest line to go through.I do find it weird that there is no penalty for waiting with indoctrinating a new follower. You can just find new ones and let them wait 'till you're ready to have more in your cult or have them replace one who just died. It would be interesting if there was some sort of time limit or downside to letting them wait too long.The game's default difficulty is not as hard as other rogue-likes, it was a pretty smooth and casual experience to me. The game's also a lot shorter than other rogue-likes, no need to replay 50 times to experience most content. Can be both good and bad depending on what you seek in a rogue-like. This game seems ideal for people's first rogue-like or those who seek a more casual rogue-like. I personally enjoyed a more casual rogue-like for once after playing several ones that kill you for taking 1 wrong step. Definitely will replay it on a higher difficulty and try the Twitch intigration as that seems like a good time.Progression is a bit too fast in some regards. I spent a moderate amount of time in my cult and despite keeping my follower count around 7-8, I quickly gained doctorine tablet pieces and levels for the lamb. I got all doctorines before beating the 3rd area and had the lamb fully powered up at the start of the 4th area. Loyalty seems to either be leveled too quickly or the impact of their levels is a bit too much. Having them give a tablet piece each level makes you get them very quickly, perhaps some cap on either loyalty level or doctorine tablets that only gets increased by beating bishops could help.The cult building does have a well-balanced progression as I never felt far ahead in it as the amount of devotion you can get at a time is fixed depending on your general cult level and extra devotion generation from smaller statues and such.Even if I have some criticisms for this game, I really like it despite encountering some bugs. I do think this game has plenty of potential for further content updates, even paid DLC. So I hope they take a similar approach to other indie devs like Motion Twin and Klei with post-launch support and paid DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful game with an amazing foundation just waiting for an extreme number of minor (and a few major) changes and quality of life updates to be perfect. Honestly, I can go on and on about what's good about this game, but the answer is basically everything. So I'm going to focus on the issues since those are going to be the sticking points if you want to get this.1. Roguelite game in the vain of Isaac, but without any of the depth or customizationThis game has a combat system that feels a bit like Isaac, and it is noticeable for those that recognize blue hearts that can't be healed, black hearts that do damage and red hearts that can be healed. But that's a good point of reference really. As far as I can tell there has yet to be a point to having Blue Hearts. If there is, it's not obvious in the way it is for Isaac. The game offers them interchangably so it's not even like Blue hearts are more common, but less useful, and healing is a rarity, so it's not like red hearts are necessarily that much better. There is also no deal with the devil like system, ironic considering what you are, where surviving a floor and taking little to no red heart damage rewards you.Similarly the combat is stellar, but the powers and weapons lack a significant amount of depth which makes the combat feel very shallow after a while. The powers in this game are pretty luke warm at best, with a lot of them having small percentile chances to do something or things like poison damage that don't actually do any damage worth the card or the effort it takes to keep it up.This might seem like a mean complaint. Isaac had years and lots of DLC to expand on combat and really let you go crazy. But this game, while it didn't quite have those years, DID have Isaac and many other Rougelites to study and learn from. This game lacks the crazy luck runs where you get a bunch of amazing powers and are taking down super versions of bosses for interesting rewards or in game challenges and there's no reason for it to lack those things because they exist in most other Roguelites worth writing home about. So it's obvious they should have been here.Do they need to be Isaac + 13 DLCs and 10 years of refinement? No, definitely not. But they definitely needed a little more then what they have.Oh, and the limited green runs combined with the few rooms you get to actually fight and gather resources and the very small paths with very little choices kind of take away from even what is there. It's like slay the spire, but you only get a 1/10th of the options before you're fighting the final boss and you need to spend some of that time gathering resources for a meta game outside the spire, so you actually only get 1/20th the options because half are being devoted elsewhere.2. Survival Management Game in the vein of Oxygen Not Included mixed with Animal Crossing... but lacking the depthI will give this game this. Being able to choose what our people look like? Inspired. The fact that it's kind of part of a demonic ritual to make them join our cult, thus totally explainable in lore as us turning them into these things? Amazing. But there is a lot of small issues to this part. I'll give an example. There exists a power you can get in this game that allows you to get a small tithe from people, and another power that lets you make them more loyal. These are incredibly useful in the early game to the mid game when you have >10 followers. Once you have more though, it's a chore. But there also exists structures you can build, a Tabernacle and an Offering Bowl. Rather then let these automate this function, they instead do something else. Even though Automation is key in games like this where you're not only doing this survival element but another element (crusading), there exists very little automation, and what does exist is lacking. Want to set a follower to a task permanently? You cannot, not unless it's praying. Or if you can that function is buried in the game somewhere that I haven't found. What about the rest? Well, I have yet to find a way to let someone take over cooking, which would be as simple as having a chest similar to the seed bays for the kitchen (at least how to implement it), which means that every time I try and push the combat aspect a bit my allies start starving (we'll get there). Then there's the cultists themselves. I love them in general, but in specific I'm noticing a trend. Bad Traits are VERY common, there is no way to get rid of them or get better traits. And as for the good traits? They are very few in number and honestly not that impactful. That's fine, being small bonuses, but there are barely any good or bad traits. Again, if there IS a way to get new traits (and I'm not talking about the big ones you can get via doctrines, I mean the base ones that followers start with) I'm not seeing it. So this game's cultist system is right up there with combat in lacking depth. And again, there is no reason for it. Games exist with far more intricate systems and while they don't need to go as far as some of them, a bit more depth then what is here is definitely needed.3. The TimeIn this game there is a clock that has time moving forward. This is a great mechanic that really forces you to try and balance things to the best of your ability and work toward as much automation as possible in order to take advantage of certain opportunities. There are ways around even starving if you do it right (though it is a choice you can miss) and that's great.But the time moves a little too fast. Especially with things like Fishing and Crusading. I can understand to a degree, but even in the cult area I find time moving a little too fast. And this might just be a personal preference but if that's the case, then it should actually be a preference option. Slowing the time would lower the difficulty of the survival side of things, yes, but there's a difficulty slider for combat so why not that side? As it stands I spend 3 days in the cult for every 1 day killing things and I'd prefer a more even balance myself.And again, if there's an option for it, I haven't found it. If the difficulty does slow the time down it's either not very noticeable in how much it does that or the harder difficulties have a ridiculously fast clock.Aside from a few minor bugs a lot of my complaints boil down to the same thing. This game is a great, but shallow, experience begging for quite a bit more. Which makes sense given that it is effectively two games in one. And we'll probably get it considering it's popularity. But we'll also probably be paying for it in chunks and that's not really what I'm saying should happen here. At it's base, they have a good foundation and frame for a game, lacking several months of added powers, depth and choices to the combat and functionality to the survival aspect of the game.This is a good start. And I really hope I don't have to pay for everything that should have been in this game on release, but if I do they better be wary of a price point for the DLCs. Either there needs to be a lot of content in them or they need to be small and cheap bundles. Anything where I'm spending ten bucks for 20 cosmetics is going to get this review heavily edited.Oh, and why in the hell can we not use mouse click to designate where we want to put a building when constructing things? I even saw people saying it was necessary BEFORE the games release. Seriously guys. Or why isn't there a bell or function that lets us call specific followers over so we don't have to track them down?All in all, this game is a very good game, with beautiful art and lots of love and effort. I don't even think the bad parts outweigh the good parts. But I'm 12 hours in and starting to feel that lack of depth very hard right now, where as games like Isaac and Oxygen Not Included can have you sinking weeks worth of hours in and finding new stuff or different experiences and challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: This was the funniest game in a good while. Found it very randomly. Not the biggest fan of roguelites so I probably wouldn't have touched it if someone hadn't recommended it. Added to wishlist so that I wouldn't forget about it. Then a friend bought it for me for Yule, and it stole my heart right away.Art style is pure eyefood, OST is full of earworms, combat is very smooth and enjoyable, and the characters are so adorable I'm unable to sacrifice them. Hollow Knight is a good 2nd, but this may be even better.I also love games that let you do stuff and collect remaining achievements even after the last boss. Big thumbs up for difficulty modes.
