_childDocuments_.review: Not a huge fan of games with roguelike elements but cult of the lamb was a real blast to play. The artstyle is amazing, the overall theme very enticing and fresh. The game basically consists of two parts, building and managing your cult and its buildings on one hand, going for dungeon runs on the other. The management part is pretty relaxed and has activities and minigames such as farming, deckbuilding, fishing and miniquests from your followers. The dungeon runs consist of several stages with occasional minibosses throughout and final bosses at the end of the run. you gather ressources here and all sorts of bonus loots plus character abilites. It's fun to go on these runs, even if you're not the biggest fan of this roguelike system.

_childDocuments_.review: Less than an hour in and I already love this game enough to make a review about it. Found out fast that the visual, gameplay, sound, everything is outstanding, it's a very well-put-together game. Hints of other dungeon crawlers, rogue-like and lights, visually adorable yet creepy and pleasing minimalism with the 2D, cute and brutal story at all the same time.Massive Monster nailed it, Devolver picked it up because they know how to please me as a consumer. Reminds me of a lot of different games, and I think they took the best elements of them. A little Binding of Isaac floors, Gungeon like fighting, city building, cute backstory, scary backstory, it has it all. Plus you get to make a cult and recruit followers, who wouldn't like that?

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of the most unique Dungeon Crawler games! Cult of the Lamb has such a unique personality that is hard to describe, you can see that the devs love the game, every animation, text, and update, is made with so much love! The only thing that I think it's bad in the game, it's the management/building aspect. Sometimes it's boring having to handle all that, but at the same time, it's a cool mechanic that punishes you for being too reckless on the Fighting side of the game. And the famous Sex Update! _childDocuments_.review: Can't make myself finish this game. The roguelike part is very barebones without any depth. The cult managing part takes way too much time, because the cult members are too stupid to fulfill even the easiest tasks.Also, the cult member sidequests are really annoying. Half the time they force you to get a material or rescue a brother from a biome you didn't plan to go to. If you decline, your devotion takes a big hit and you need to fix it before going on your next run.You have to do half the farming manually, cooking can't be automated at all. I've had everything unlocked since around the second old god and I swim in resources. There is no motivation to care for your cult at all, because they die quicker than you can resurrect them. At times, I've had trouble to keep the number of members above 20. If at least cooking could be automated, you would have way more time to go on runs. The building that makes your cult members work faster and is basically mandatory for farms needs to be refueled manually. Scarecrow traps need to be emptied manually if they even work as intended. Outhouses need to be emptied manually. I've never seen a cult member use the janitor's hut to clean up a mess themselves. Everything needs to be done manually.Also, please make the cult members stick to their designated task. It's so frustrating to give a farmer a nature necklace only for him to be doing something else when you return from your run.The roguelike/roguelite part itself is way too simple. Combat feels good for the first five to ten runs, but after that becomes repetitive. There is no possibility to reroll your starting weapon, so if you get one you don't like, you have to live with it for basically right before the end of the run or reroll the whole run. Weapon variety is bad. There is 5 different weapons and their poison, necromancer and other variants. The movesets are the same between variants. At least some of the spells are cool. Enemy variety is ok and the biomes feel different enough. The first two bosses were way too easy. The difficulty spikes tremendously at the third and fourth boss. If you die on a run, guess what. Yeah, back to spending 10-15 minutes on preparing your cult for your absence. Oh, you are out of fish? Fishing ritual and 10 mins fishing. This takes about a day, so back to cooking 3 times so your cult has enough to eat for 1 1/2 days. Dang, you are out of meat, so send some members to collect a bit. One of them dies. Too bad you can't just buy cooking ingredients with your 5k coins.All in all, I don't think I have the patience to finish this. I am right at the fourth boss and spent at least half of my playtime on managing the cult. I absolutely despise the preparation it takes for your cult to survive for 2-3 days without risk while you are absent.

_childDocuments_.review: ARGH THAT ENDING WAS SO SATISFYING I BEAT HIS ASS... *ahem*So I somehow went into Cult of the Lamb not realising it was a roguelite/like, simply because I don't pay attention to any gaming news. I thought it was going to be a farming management sim, which... I suppose technically it is. But the roguelike elements are the core of the game and are great fun. You get that real adrenaline rush when you survive something you didn't think you would. The only thing I would say is that the combat feels a little sticky on keyboard and mouse, but the game does explicitly recommend you play it with a controller. The side quests are a complement the main mechanics greatly since they tend to be things you don't have to go out of your way to do. The management part of the game is simple and not overwhelming, and, despite the games' themes, it does allow you to be a... somewhat nice cult leader.The art is incredible, the dev team very clearly had a strong grasp of the aesthetic they wanted. It fluctuates smoothly and naturally between extremely adorable and outright terrifying. Each world is unique and had a different vibe, but all conveying danger. I would say that the bird cultist designs do freak me out a lot more than the monstrous cultists designs because uh... why are their mouths uh... there? Separate from their beaks? On a more serious note, I do found that sometimes the levels/rooms got a little cluttered, causing me to lose health just because I didn't see one tiny thing in the tall grass, which I'm sure is by design but was also incredibly infuriating.The characters are fairly unique in design, but they do kind of meld together in terms of personality, falling into the binary of 'this one won't kill you' and 'this one will'. I don't feel it matters too much though that the characters felt same-y, because the main plot revolves around the Lamb and their mission anyway; the characters who help you SHOULD feel kind of disposable considering what you're setting out to do.Music is fantastic, and so was the sound design. I could very clearly pick out when I'd gotten hit, and I could hear if I'd forgotten to do something at the cult camp before racing off.I'm still coming down from the adrenaline from the final battle, so... Yes. 10/10 game, absolutely would recommend anyone who's even a little bit interested in it to give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: Remember the cave-exploring mini game in Stardew Valley? Now expand it to the full game and add some cult elements then you get Cult Of The Lamb, a hybrid dungeon crawler seasoned with base-building, and of course, cute animals doing questionable things. As a recently sacrificed Lamb, your death is postponed by The One Who Waits for he has another plan for your life -- a servitude of freeing him in exchange for your immortality. Now you must build a cult and smite all the heretics standing in your way. I cannot stress enough how much I love this game. From its cartooney artstyle and bopping soundtrack, to responsive control and balance between two genre, these elements blend together well. The cute-things-doing-horrible-things Happy Tree Friends style is just the cherry on top. The game does have some issues regarding pacing and minot bugs, buy ultimately they do not hinder your enjoyment for this cult classic. I highly recommend it.Again, I really love the art direction and  addicting soundtrack. For a roguelite, I hardly get tired of either one. You just have to experience these kind of feeling yourself.Dungeon-crawling and base-building are inherently different genres of video game. It's nice to see Massive Monster manages to strike a balance between the two, and create a sort of "shifting mind" gameplay. Dungeon-crawling offers tight combat and resource hunt, while Base-building gives you the freedom to customize your cult. If you are tired of combat or simply being frustrated by roguelite element, you can take your time to manage your "insert base name", tending some crops, constructing dome decorations, fulfilling the needs of those little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I mean followers, and conducting various concerning rituals. And vice-versa, if you are itchy for some fighting or running short of some supplies, feel free to throw yourself into the holy crusade for your cult and smite those heretics. I know this isn't a revolutionary idea since almost every MMORPG has some sort of personal quarter or others of similar design, but as a core gameplay loop I think Cult Of The Lamp does a great job.→Those  I mean followers know your love towards them so they keep exploiting it but they are your  I mean followers and you love them so much you will fulfill their needs anyway.→You ever just play Knucklebone so much that you forget that you have a cult to tend to?→Really cute animation.→There is a dedicated "Baa" button.→Interesting and equally questionable side quests.→So many followers' forms for you to choose.→The noise NPCs make, I love them!This is my only issue about the game. It seems like progression and unlockable upgrade system need some rebalance. For my experience, by the time I reach the third dungeon I have already unlocked two-third of the upgrade system for both the base and the arsenal for crusading. I know I did compliment the dev for finding the balance for dungeon-crawling and base-building, but the progress-and-reward ratio need some adjustment. Because I already have most of upgrades unlocked, I find my self replaying later dungeon less than I do with earlier levels. Instead, I focus more on taking care of the cult and other minor stuff, which could be a good thing since there are several things to do outside your cult.→Tarot cards should always draw one offensive and one utility/defensive. I don't need extra resources gain or map reveal when I really need more firepower.→Sometimes, talking to a follower who is in the middle of dropping resource will cause the camera to focus on the follower instead of The Lamb, even when the interaction is over.中文小簡評→你以為這是邪教模擬器？不！這是幼稚園模擬器。你得幫你的信徒煮吃的、把屎把吐、滿足他們一堆詭異的要求。(我全部都做了因為我太愛這群小渾蛋。)→可愛的畫風、可愛的動畫、一聽即上癮的配樂、可愛的東西做可怕的事情。→Roguelite地城探險和家園系統能找到平衡點。→諸多信徒模樣可供你隨意更改。→遊戲節奏似乎掌握得不夠熟練，到第三座地城我已經解鎖三分之二的東西，→希望抽塔羅牌時可以抽一張攻擊型和一張防禦型/功能型來選，有時真的很需要火力加持而不是顯示全圖或資源加成。

_childDocuments_.review: + art direction is unique and consistent+ gameplay is fast paced and super refined+ great soundtrack+ great mix of genres- poor Deck performance despite the graphics and simpler gameplay- latter half of the game is just going through the numbers; you unlock everything too earlyCult of the Lamb is a combination of many genres, including a hack-and-slash roguelite, a town simulator, and personnel management. There isn't really a story in the game, just an overarching objective of building your cult up and going on crusades to defeat your enemies. Besides the introductory scenes and some brief dialogs interspersed within the game, there is nothing really here storywise to motivate you from A to B.The roguelite gameplay is fairly simple: you're given a random weapon and random curse (Cult of the Lamb's magic equivalent) and are tasked with reaching the end of a crusade, a series of connected rooms, each with a "defeat all the enemies before proceeding" objective. Crusades typically last anywhere from 5 to 15 minutes, and you need to complete four of them per world to reach their respective bosses.Sometimes you will encounter other kinds of rooms in your crusade, often giving you bonus materials, new followers, and tarot cards. Tarot cards are mutators to the game, giving you a boon of some type to aid you in your quest. For example, they might give you extra HP, an increase to movement speed, attack speed, and so on. They make every crusade feel unique and the countless permutations of effects you can achieve makes replaying crusades worthwhile.The town simulator part of the game is likewise fairly simple. You can place and upgrade buildings on a grid-like map, along with decorative flourishes you can add to spruce things up. It's very rudimentary with not much to manage other than ensuring you have enough beds, toilets, etc amenities to meet the needs of your cult. You can also place buildings that allow your followers to collect materials to further build more.What was most interesting to me was the personnel management part of the game: finding new followers and customizing them was really fun, and each new follower typically has a few beneficial (and sometimes detrimental) trait which influences not only their behavior and personality but how well they gel with your cult at large.Part of what ties the game together is the gameplay loop of going into crusades to collect materials, followers, inch closer to the boss, meanwhile managing your town to your cult's satisfaction. You can apply new policies or doctrines to shape how this pans out, as well as perform rituals to build up your cult further. You're always on the move, trying to improve your town.The game's graphics are a mix of simple hand-drawn animal sprites but also some richly detailed backgrounds that can be disturbing to look at. It's a mix of really striking Lovecraftian inspired occult imagery, but with a cute animals aesthetic. You'd think these ideas would clash but they go together quite well. It's not particularly gory or violent, it's as if it was Lovecraft as seen through the lens of cute animals.I think the game is great, especially at holding your attention. There's always something to do, there's always pressure to improve your base or cult members, it's very seldom you have a minute to think that couldn't be better served within the game. I haven't been this absorbed in a game for a long time and that's because the systems gel together very well, even if some of them individually are not so impressive.As of writing, performance is not good. While at first glance it appears you can hit 60fps irrespective of settings, when actually playing the game, there's constant microstuttering. At low or high, anticipate 50~60fps but it's very jittery and consistently fluctuating. Sometimes there's spikes that dip down even further, making 40hz mode also jittery.Settings are stored in the cloud save, so if you go from PC to Deck and vice-versa, you'll need to adjust settings each time. When using on a new device, resolution will be at lowest and needs to be iteratively scrolled to reach 800p, going through several resolution changes in the process.Text is legible usually but there is little consistency in text sizing, sometimes even in the same text box. At times it's very legible and then the next moment it becomes very hard to read. There is a text size accessibility option, but changing from default sometimes makes text appear outside of frame. The game is also quite zoomed out: the right stick is otherwise unused, it would have been nice to have this control zoom level.It's playable on Deck, but it's not a good experience. It's annoying being a dual PC-Deck user and going back-and-forth between them, and performance is not particularly good. I would advise passing if you planned to spend any meaningful time with Cult of the Lamb on Deck.The game supports ultrawide and it's a great implementation. UI elements move to edges of the screen to avoid cluttering center frame. Seeing more of your base is appreciated and one of the great perks of playing this game in ultrawide. There is no FOV slider because it's not really necessary, although at 3440x1440 on a 32in screen, the game is awfully zoomed out.On my R5 5600X, 32gb DDR4, RTX3080 system, performance is not particularly good. My monitor will cap at 112fps and it can keep this usually but then there are very frequent spikes of stuttering. Sometimes these spikes last over a second, where the game will just completely standstill. For a game like this, I can't fathom why it would be so demanding of my hardware. That said, it's still at my framerate ceiling 90% of the time, it's just these stutters really take you out of the game with their frequency.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for an perfect 2 player game, this is it. Quite honestly the most fun I have had with a game in a LONG time.  (some light spoilers)It has almost perfect grind that feels satisfying and rewarding. Every resource has a purpose, and a use. Finding  a fine line in managing your "resources" ( food, materials, money, and even followers ect ) is so much fun. Too many followers and you may not have enough food to feed them. Not enough, causes your devotion earnings to be slowed. Do you kill some followers now to save your cult from famine? Or brainwash them for undying love for 3 days, in exchange for their health later on. Everything has a risk/reward and learning new game mechanics and even lore feels well deserved and hard earned. I played this game solo prior, and with the multiplayer update played an additional almost 50 hours in a new game with my husband. I never felt bored with the game or that anything  felt tedious to earn. So many new games often hide collectibles behind hard paywalls, that often takes you out of the game as you don't earn enough. This game gives you an incredible selections of content just in its base and it's amazingly refreshing to see. Entering the hardest difficulty was a huge step up that I was not prepared for at first. It feels amazing to cull the heretics that previously martyred you, making your followers loose faith in you! This cant often end up causing them to dissent the player, following some funny interactions!Great grind, skills to earn, management, animations, lore, fighting and follower interactions and so so much more. The world feels very alive and pulls you into each interaction. I often found myself hanging around just to look at the background, because they were so wonderfully animated. It once lead me to starve and loose my world because of it! There are some additional DLC packs, quite moderately priced for what they give to game play and base building. You don't need them but I do recommend getting them, if only to support this developer and this gameIf I had to give a game a perfect score this would be one of the only games I can honestly say wholeheartedly, deserves a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, It's way overhyped and overrated. It can surely use a negative counterbalance. If you are looking for a casual game get an actual casual game like Stardew Valley etc. If you are looking for a roguelike then get a roguelike with good combat like idk, Dead Cells or Isaac etc.This game is a mix of taking care of your "cult" (more like daycare for cute anthropomorphic creatures) but your followers can't be left alone for longer than literally 5 min until you get the rituals to extend it to like 20. What do you do with that free 20 min? You mostly go into the dungeons to fight but the combat is very mid. Some enemies telegraph projectiles some don't, most weapons feel the same with fast attack weapons being FAR better than the slower ones. btw, you can only go through 4 stages at maximum, after that it's just going back home.btw, difficulty levels are there but those also affect the cult so if you want your cuties to b**ch even more often than usual you can do that but it's just adding more busywork not real difficulty. In combat difficulty is just the usual HP bloat. Honestly after playing on hard for like 20h I switched to easy and never looked back.imo if you want this just get it on sale and don't expect anything spectacular because the edgy cult stuff wears off fast and what you are left with is just 20 toddler-minded followers to babysit and doing mid dungeons on your breaks.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: "Cult of the Lamb: A Divine Blend of Cute and Quirky"Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)Step into the enchanting world of Cult of the Lamb, where adorable creatures, cultish endeavors, and a quirky sense of humor come together in a delightfully bizarre package. This roguelike action-adventure from Massive Monster manages to strike a balance between challenge and charm, earning its stripes in the indie gaming realm.The game introduces players to an unexpected protagonist—an adorable lamb who finds themselves at the center of an eccentric cult. The premise alone sets the stage for the kind of quirky adventure you didn't know you needed. The pixel art style, combined with whimsical characters, creates an atmosphere that's both cute and strangely captivating.Gameplay in Cult of the Lamb is where the magic truly happens. The roguelike elements ensure that each run feels fresh, challenging players to navigate through procedurally generated dungeons while mastering the art of combat. The combination of precision and strategy keeps you on your toes, making each playthrough a delightful dance between chaos and control.Now, let's address the cheeky suggestion of a "Sex Update" that could allegedly elevate the rating to a mythical 6/5 stars. While the idea adds a humorous twist to the review, it's important to appreciate that Cult of the Lamb's charm lies in its quirky, family-friendly appeal. However the idea of a "Sex Update" would definitely be an addition that would have players enjoying themselves for hours longer with their Cult Followers especially if including the Twitch Integration with your followers and viewers on Twitch.In conclusion, Cult of the Lamb earns a solid five-star rating for its imaginative concept, engaging gameplay, and the sheer joy it brings to the indie gaming scene. While the idea of a "Sex Update" might be tongue-in-cheek, it's essential to recognize and celebrate the game's existing strengths without veering into territories that could compromise its wholesome charm. So, whether you're a seasoned gamer or just looking for a dose of cute chaos, Cult of the Lamb is a divine experience that's worth every pixel.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR --> A great base-building game with some roguelite elements, cute and detailed art, bizarre humor and multiple secrets that will give you quality entertainment for ~20h. Do not expect replayability value though.-------------------------While I had a great time with this game, I kinda wished I had more information about it beforehand so I knew what kind of game I was exactly playing, so here it goes: Cult of the Lamb (COTL from now on) is a base-building animal crossing-ish game with some roguelite elements set in a bizarre, cute but satanic world where you establish your evil cult in a quest of imposing over different heretics. You do so by growing your cult with members (workers), resources and expeditions. The order I described COTL is relevant. When I purchased it, I expected some roguelite game with a base-building feature that would define my perma-upgrades. Instead, it works the other way around: this game is 80-90% base building and is complemented by some basic roguelite mechanics. It did not sabotage my experience at all but if you're expecting to find a next roguelite to dig into, this might not be the best option.In terms of base building content, COTL has become my small addiction for the past week or two. Progression is well constructed and you constantly feel the urge to keep doing stuff to slowly but steadily improve your cult. In general, resources are connected to the strength of your cult, and at the same time, a stronger cult will deliver more amount and faster resources. These are all connected to the game's cultist nature, since you strengthen your cult by raising loyalty, reciting sermons, doing rituals, and such. Other resources are related to new members, basic crafting materials, farm materials, etc. The game also features strategy and risk/reward situations by having potential negative outcomes (e.g. disseases, death by aging, members revelling, etc) and forcing you to mind your resource management better.In terms of roguelite elements, it has a bit of everything but the overall presentation is extremely simplistic. Layouts resemble the ones in The Binding of Isaac, being rectangle-ish, but with much less variety. Floor structure resemble the one in Slay the Spire or Inscryption, but without the same weight. Upgrades during runs resemble Hades in the shape of a multiple choice scenario, but options are much more limited. Combat follows a quite basic structure of a hack-n-slash where you spend most of the time rolling and attacking, while using magic (aka Curse) here and there. Compared to the entertainment value of the base building concept, these expeditions felt very generic and not very interesting, as runs felt very similar one another. But yet again, do not think of it as a roguelite.As a final warning for that, keep in mind that the game presents very little incentive for replayability. While progression of your cult is very solid for the most part, you quickly step up during the second half of the game and you eventually reach maximum stats without much trouble, with no way of getting stronger. At that point, you will complete the game and won't touch that savefile ever again.Overall, if you are not really looking for a roguelite game as a core and simply look for an entertaining game with funny, bizarre elements, great visuals and a length of ~20h, COTL is definitely your game. Despite not having replayability value, it gave me good quality content and it surely deserves a shot :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a nearly perfect combination between base management gameplay and a roguelike isometric dungeon crawler with a creative aesthetic style that mixes cute animal critters with cosmic horror. This clash of gameplay styles and thematic elements work surprisingly well together to create a highly addictive experience which alternates between fast-paced and brutal combat, and a relaxing farm/cult management element. Cult of the Lamb is best summarized as a love child of Hades and Stardew Valley with a bit of Happy Tree Friends thrown in. It does not have the same depth of gameplay as other dedicated games in either category, but it still offers a unique and memorable spin on the formula by making these two gameplay styles work together seamlessly. On that basis, the game is worthy of being played and experienced.HOWEVER, sadly I am unable to recommend this otherwise good game because the PC optimization is just SO AWFUL. Without hyperbole, I have witnessed this game (running on a quad-core 3.7 ghz i7 processor and 16gb ram, no less) regularly drop to 10fps at scene transitions, at crucial moments during the aforementioned very fast-paced and brutal combat, and occasionally for no reason at all. Given that it is the rough graphical equivalent of Yoshi's Island and has been out for some time now, there is no excuse for this other than laziness on the part of the development team. Bugs and glitches are incredibly frequent too, although not usually to a game-breaking degree. Either way, the stuttering degrades the overall experience significantly and occasionally makes it completely unplayable. I thought that this was limited to my computer, but from what people are saying online, it unfortunately appears to be the rule rather than the exception. At a bare minimum, if you are going to sell the game at full price to PC gamers you should make sure you actually FINISH it first. In summary, it's an promising and interesting concept executed well, but handicapped by the laziness of its developer in fixing its core problems. I definitely cannot recommend to PC gamers, but others should certainly give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is a chaotic blend of roguelike dungeon crawling and farm management/farming. The game is like combination of Stardew Valley and Hedes but in an unholy; at the same time, cute way. Your journey starts as a sacrificed lamb, returning back to the world to build a cult devoted to The One Who Waits.By going on crusades (rouglike runs), you are able to gather resources and find followers for your cult. Upon returning back to the main base, where you grow your cult, the game becomes a very chill farming game. Except you farm devotion and prayers from followers. Although you can still farm normal food to feed your people.As for the visuals, they are as charming as they are unsettling, with a cartoonish style that covers the whole darkness of the game. With a combination of smooth animations and beautiful music, the game's visuals are nothing less than perfect.Combat is very smooth and pleasant; you'll dodge and weave through enemies, unleashing curses and summoning unholy powers. Each run is unique, with randomly generated dungeons and weapons.Harvesting resources, constructing shrines, and brainwashing indoctrinating your followers is oddly compelling. You'll need to balance their needs with your own thirst for power, and the game allows you to interact with your followers in many different ways. Despite a dark story, the game is very silly and fun. The creators made sure to add a little bit humor and cuteness here and there to maximise the experience.I really haven't seen any negative points about the game and there are rarely any bugs. So there isn't much to talk about the cons.Overall, Cult of the Lamb is certainly a unique game that makes sure the fun never ends for the player. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: ***************************************************** IT RUNS ON WINDOWS 7 *****************************************************This game has charm, I have to say. The graphics might be simplistic at first reminding people of shows like Gumball but the clash between the cute, the grotesque and the putrid (more on that later) doesn't feel that bad, it somewhat works. Gameplay wise - the 'core' of the game are not the Binding Of Issac/Zelda segments but instead the cult management which will absorb most of your time. The building scheme is similar to that of Don't Starve - so diagonal grid for what looks like a flat plane, which makes fitting some of the buildings tricky. The cultists don't automate tasks until you build a building that does that, meaning that you will have a lot of daily grind to do, especially the farming pretty early on. Cooking on the other hand on all on you so don't expect followers to cook for themselves. Overall that aspect is OKAYISH. Oh and important thing - you CAN edit the buildings by going into building menu and selecting the edit mode. Nothing mentioned that in the tutorials.The cult management aspect is maintaining your faith which breaks down into seremons, adding doctrines and upgrading the lambs capabilities and this is perhaps the least complex part of the entire show - some of the doctrines are passive boosts, some unlock rituals, honestly I haven't found much use in many of these rituals except the ones that raise faith but I might have not unlock the 'right ones' just yet. Now the dungeon crawling/exploration aspect is where people thought the game's meat is... and no - other than the usual Binding of Issac room to room with rewards, Tarot Cards to boost your abilities (Another BoI carry-over) and weapon switching what those segments are are grinds for resources using in the first two segments. The enemy variety is wonderful and so is their design but the problem is that the clock is ticking when you go on these 'crusades'. So if you don't provide enough for your cult they will starve or rebel while you're away. Which means speed IS the key, which again proves to make resource gathering harder. There are also side actions you can take such as - fishing, dice etc. The extensive amount of merchants and NPCs you meet provide more meat and story to the setting but honestly - the lore is very simple to figure out. There is no grand design here. It's nice to meet these NPCs but overall they just fill a hole for those that want a bit more fluff. And the last thing I didn't really want to touch about - one of the things that made me uncomfortable playing Binding Of Issac was the amount of poop and blood around. When I started playing CotL I was relieved to find none of that during the Crusade segments... until I started looking at the followers traits. There's a distressingly huge amount of people that either want to eat excrement (Some of which demand it!) or think that making others eat it is a good prank. I'm scratching my head about this one. Either way - would I recommend it with a solid 7.5/10. The developer already declared free updates to the game and for its price it's a completely servicable game. Mind you Binding of Issac or Zelda veterans should start the game on HARD, otherwise it might just be too easy.

_childDocuments_.review: There should be a yes, but wait for a sale button. That's where I stand with Cult of the Lamb. It's a good game, but not a great game. Fundamentally, it lacks depth, so I can't recommend it at full price.Cult of the Lamb is conceptually half roguelite, half colony sim. I'll start with the colony sim part, as it takes up probably around 80% of your time in practice. First of all, your followers are actually brain dead, like vegetable level brain dead. They will make no attempt to save themselves from starvation, nor will they go to bed when they are sick. This means you have to babysit them, or they will die. Your followers also age like fine milk. Once they're elderly, they're almost completely useless. Unfortunately, they age faster than you can kill them, unless you pick a specific route of doctrines. They should age like half as fast as they currently do.It kinda takes a while to automate basic base functions like cleaning up after themselves, farming, or cooking. These quality of life upgrades are locked behind what I will call the mid-game. The way the upgrade trees work is you have to buy a certain number of upgrades before you can buy the next tier, and then you have to buy the next tier to unlock all the upgrades above the line that was previously blocking them. This can take a while, but you might not notice because you're too busy farming or cleaning up poop, or cooking, or repairing the low level beds you gave them early on, etc. This might get irritating after a short while.Now for the reason you have a colony or base or whatever at all. You're the cult leader. Your word is law, and the cultists are here to give you power. Never forget that they are expendable. In practice this means that you can level up your combat tree with sermons, declare doctrines that affect how the base will function, or perform rituals which give a temporary or immediate effect. Unfortunately, you have to commit to whichever choices you make with the doctrines, as there's no going back to pick the other choice without reloading a save, so you might need to do research on the wiki... or you can just wing it and see what happens like I did. There's not much risk in that. The doctrines are either inconsequential, or there is a clearly, obviously, objectively better choice. This kinda leads to there being no reason to replay the game because nothing would change the second time around.Finally, the roguelite elements. Your objective in the game requires you to enter randomly generated dungeons and kill the end bosses in them. This is fine when you get time to do it, but time still passes normally, so you can't really make an extended or thorough run in a dungeon without having a way to deal with faith, hunger, and sickness, which are the 3 gauges you have to maintain in your colony. Because of this, you're probably going to get all the relevant upgrades in your skill tree before you're halfway done with the dungeons. Let's say you've stabilized your colony and can do a dungeon dive... there are still problems in the design of this part of the game. You start off each run with a weapon and a spell. It's not really worth going into detail, because they all fight about the same save for the detail that some weapons are fast and do light damage, while others are slow and hit hard. It's actually quite balanced... maybe a little too balanced for a roguelite. Enemies do what they do in all games - either come up and hit you or shoot some projectiles for you to dodge. There's not a lot of variety in how these things happen. The difficulty setting doesn't really do much except make the numbers more or less favorable for you. There's no advancement in the enemy AI. The bosses aren't really any better in this regard, and they aren't really all that difficult to kill.Most of my problems with the game come down to the limitations of its design. It tries to be a hybrid of roguelite and colony sim, but it does neither of these particularly well. As such, it just feels a bit shallow. I got a bored of it before finishing. I'll probably go back and finish it eventually, but it's not something I am stoked to do.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely shallow game with little replay value regarding both its major gameplay aspects: base-management and rogue-lite.  For example, the first time you can build a shelter for your followers that does not collapse is at the penultimate level of advancement for your base.  Most of the rogue-lite gameplay is chance-based, so there’s a minimal sense of advancement or improvement each time you venture forth.  Great art style and atmosphere but little else of interest beyond the first few hours of gameplay.  Overall, this game felt to me like it was two separate games that were being developed for the mobile platform that they ended up combining because they didn’t have enough substance to fully market either, and they somehow got the idea that they could pass off the amalgamation as a full-on indie PC game.  I purchased it on sale with DLC (it just adds cosmetics) for around $17, and I still feel that the price was unjustified after having played it through.  Might be worth a couple of dollars, but, honestly, there are so many better games deserving of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the full price currently. I have no idea if there will be any sort of update to add depth to the game, but it desperately needs it. Each tree of upgrades is remarkably shallow and leaves no room for customization. The doctrines are superficial and have no real impact on how your cult functions (save for the grass eating one, which just breaks the food system outright). The dungeon crawling is something out of a browser game. Upgrades with no real weight to them, limited variance on weapons/curses, simple and uninspired layouts, and all but one of the bosses is a cakewalk. On top of this, the extended runs after beating a boss in each zone are more punishing than rewarding, as the cult requires near constant supervision to be fully useful. Spend too long away from the cult and come back to people starving and dissenting.Cult management almost gives you the power to automate the food/currency/waste systems, but ends up falling short and you realize each "upgrade" is just another object that requires regular player interaction to be useful. The game also lacks a central management interface for your cultists, making it impossible to tell how many cultists are prioritizing each job, which ones are the hungriest/closest to dissenting, etc. A fun game with cute art, but shallow as a puddle and completely lacking in build variety/depth. I would hesitate to even call it a roguelite, as many games of that genre have infinitely more replay value at a more reasonable price. It's fun for maybe 4 hours, then becomes monotonous as you grasp for something to keep you interested, only to finish the game and be left with a bitter taste. Overall, a 3/10. Its strengths, while entirely aesthetic, are done well. The art is bubbly and sharp, very distinct. The music is apt for each zone and fun to listen to, and the voice acting for each of the NPCs is great, specifically the prawn who sounds like a cowboy. But the core gameplay lacks meaning and won't garner any investment from the average roguelite fan. It's a fun, zany tamagachi manager with an added dungeon crawl minigame. Sadly forgettable, could have been much more. I would add that my playtime as of the review has about 15 hours of idling, so you can expect about 20-25 hours out of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Note : when recommending, I say . However, I personally did not like the gameplay.When would I recommend :- When it's on sale. / When it receives any major update (that is NOT a cosmetic DLC)- If you are OK with repeated gameplay.- If you are OK with minimalistic mechanics, with a random chance of being curbstomped by RNG.Even though my Cons list is weighty : keep in mind that all of these appeared in lategame, when, unfortunately, the seams are really starting to become visible.Let's check the Pros :- Amazing visuals on all front : characters, environment, decorations, UI. - Fitting tunes.- An interesting spin on the cultist-ish genre.- Simple mechanics which won't overwhelm you.- While the Cult takes a much, MUCH larger role than the Roguelite aspect, the Rogue parts can be done quickly enough so the cult you left alone don't starve or dissent before you return.Aaand about the Cons :- ...be late with one more day and they will.- While the mechanics are simple, they are also sometimes feel bare and unpolished.- The weapons and abilities are all the same from start to finish : the only thing Upgrading does is upping Damage Numbers and give Status Modifiers (chance to Heal/Crit/Possess/Poison/etc.). No major mechanic additions or modifications at all.- At each start of the run you get a random weapon and power. If you suck using those, you might as well just Alt-F4 out of it and hope for a better roll. No "basic starter" weapons.- Rolling is good in the initial stages, but lategame turns either into a patience game (as your weapon will deal a rather low amount of damage despite being maxed out), or a bullet hell where you hope you won't roll into another enemy's attack, or an environment hazard.- You will roll into enemy attacks and environment hazard lategame, as end rooms can be filled to the brim with them.- The visual is a blessing and a curse - I suffered more than once when I could not make a difference between visual and legit attacks, often ending up dying to falsely judged patterns.Enemies obscured by other enemies or terrain is another thing - while Tall Grass is a neat tactical obscurity, I suffered more than once when a summoner enemy summoned a minion "behind" them... only to immediately attack me as soon as the summoning circle appeared. No "summoning sickness" here, sir, they will kill you on first frame.- Lategame will hinge on your cult - if you do not have enough Sermons and Sacrifices, your power will become miserable. So you better lick their butts clean in order to keep up Faith and Loyalty, or face the consequences of literally not being able to viably play the roguelite part.- The game says that the Cult is for you - no sir. You will always be a servant. Refuse one poop quest or "murder prank" and you will be witch-hunted. Because every sidequest decline leads to losing 1/3 Faith.Granted, you can always replace a cultist, or restore faith when poop is devoured - but this ultimately crushes the expectation that -YOU- are the leader of this kindergarten. Bad news : you are the kindergarten teacher, not a dictator.Final words :The overall vibe and feeling of the game is pretty neat, but becomes ultimately (and literally) smeared by the endgame, which feels much more lackluster, especially as the Roguelite aspect becomes irrelevant (due to Cult doing more resources) and an RNG-prayer for the appropriate weapons (as the Cult provides none).This is one of those few cases where I really, REALLY like the entire world of the game, its wacky lore, and its design - but I'm unlikely to revisit the game itself again.

_childDocuments_.review: A game where I came for its roguelite elements, but actually stayed for the management part of the game.Cult of the Lamb is a very charming game. The premise of creating a cult, the game's art style, character designs, sound design and music are all superb, and is what initially got me interested in the game as soon as I saw the first trailers. But after finding out that this game was also half roguelite, it shot my excitement through the roof. But after completing the game, it lacks the replayability than any other roguelite/roguelike that I have ever played. This just comes through a lack of different weapons, curses, room layouts, enemies, or game changing upgrades that could make each run through its dungeons unique and fresh for hundreds of hours. It feels good just to go through the dungeons the minimum amount of times before moving onto the next, but every run just seems to blend together. If you're worried about getting bored after your second run through a dungeon, you don't have to. I found the time I spent in the dungeons fun and rewarding for the effects it has on the second half of its game, but I don't think this game is worth picking up for its roguelite gameplay alone.However, the real reason I absolutely loved the game is its cult management gameplay, and this is where Massive Monster really knocked it out of the park. Each cult member is a mind for you to mould into one of your own. They work, eat, starve,   poop, vomit, revolt, complain, and pray all due to your actions, and its your job to keep them your own without them dying or leaving the cult entirely. It's super fun to design, plan, and eventually build up to your expectations of your cult doing everything for you. I would tell you everything that you can do for and against your members, but that would spoil the fun. Let's just say that if it wasn't for the artstyle of this game, with its cute cult members, I would not feel just for doing the things that I did in this game.With a super fun management game with decent roguelite elements, this game isn't suppose to be replayable as other roguelites, and I'm totally fine with that. Some roguelites you might scratch the surface about get the hang of its mechanics maybe 20 hours into it, and that time investment might turn people off from its gameplay. Cult of the Lamb doesn't require this time investment though, and it knocked it out of the park with what it was trying to accomplish with its premise, cult management gameplay, style, and music. So in the end, I think it was worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, it isn't terrible, just not good enough. I guess Hades destroyed the whole genre for me.To be more specific, there's no strategy. All items are random, and they keep getting more and more random as you add new items to the list, for there is not a single way to direct, even by a little bit, the possibilities presented to you. Just roll with it. And the building part is far to simple to be of any interest. There are way more decorations than useful buildings, which is way too uninspired, in my opinion. Kinda "just throw a lot of options and people won't even notice they're useless".I find myself close to the end of the main story, and yet it feels more like a chore than fun to keep on playing. Which is quite sad, since the game had a lot of potential. The idea of mixing two diferent styles is good, albeit risky. The art fits well with the theme, making it light instead of dreadful. It really makes me want to enjoy the game.But I can't. It just doesn't feel fun. Go play Hades instead. I know i will.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for 4h, I have mixed feelings of this game.I like how there's a lot elements to the game, like going on crusades, fighting enemies, collecting loot, and on the other hand you have a lot of stuff to do at the base like taking care of your followers, growing food, making cermons and so on...The main problem for me is its too much stuff to do, and on a too short period of time -  the day counter is too quick, and it feels like you ALWAYS have chores to do, and it makes the gameplay more stressful than it should be, and not fun.   I wanna go out on crusades and chill and improve my skills,  but everytime i do that and get back to my base,  theres too many unwanted chores to do - collect devotion from followers,  give each one a blessing manually, grow food and nourish it,  chopping wood and mine,  order workers,  find out who is the naughty one who rebels, making cermons, rituals...  and theres so much more to do in a very short period of time before a new day starts and you have to repeat these actions.  and everytime you get back from crusade, its like you're back on square one  and nothing that you did  merely 15 minutes ago mattered -  everyone is upset and you need to take care of it from scratch -  not fun.   dont recommend unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Poor roguelike + mediocre base building + cute = Cult of the Lamb, only recommend people who would enjoy the base building part more than the roguelike part which is totally a lazy design. In total, this game is not completely bad, but also don't deserve to a overwhelming positive game, so I would give the game a negative shot,About the roguelike, it's bad. Only 4 areas you can explore and all of them look very similar except a color design, most spawning enemy are same in every area, few weapons and a meaning less RNG feature. To complete each area, you have to finish the area 4 times, and each run's bosses are the bigger version of the normal enemy except the final run's boss. That's painfully repetitive and disappointing.About the base building, it's fine. As growing your base, not only you'll get various choices to upgrade your base but also level up your character which is more rewarding part than the roguelike part. About the difficulty, you can choose 4 difficulty. I would strongly recommend the hardest one. Other difficulties would be easier and quicker to finish the roguelike part and feels like less rewarding from the base building part.To complete the main part, it should be over 15 hours playing if you choose the hardest difficulty. Also there is additional features after beat the main part though, it's super grinding and repetitive so I wouldn't recommend. However if you really don't mind grinding then the total play time should be over 30 hours so the game would be worth even if the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't that good. It's more of a micro managing game than a roguelike. You spend more time trying to make sure your flock is happy instead of exploring dungeons. This would be fine if the managing section of the game would actually be engaging. Once playing the game you will quickly find the game is shallow in the sense that every single facet of the game is half baked without much thought. They put tremendous effort into making this game feature rich but the features aren't good whatsoever. Where this game shines is in the art design and animations. You'll find yourself gawking at just how good everything looks. The animations are however also a problem in this game. At times I would become dizzy during boss fights as the camera would frantically move in varying directions.I would wait until this game gets further updates from Massive Monster before picking it up. They have promised to add in more content in the future and this game sorely needs it.All in all I give this game a 5.5/10. There are worse things you can do with your time I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: After buying Cult of the Lamb about a year ago, I think it's time for a review. I liked it when I bought it, but something just didn't click with me. I like games with light management, dungeon crawling, and base building. But the game just wasn't there yet.With Sins of the Flesh, the free update, the game feels right. The management is coming together later in the game and I think there are even more necklaces and blueprints for me to find. The dungeon crawling feels better. Hits seem to land more accurately and the blunderbuss is a fun addition to the arsenal. The base building is expanded with the new sin mechanic letting followers be even more self-serving and beneficial.Cult of the Lamb is certainly worth your time when on sale, but even at full price it's a fun, entertaining game. The combat isn't super deep, but it is rewarding. Collecting the right cards and finding a great setup feels good. Changing fleeces and discovering what works for you makes runs so enjoyable.If you like managing villagers, though, Cult of the Lamb is a must-buy. You can collect them, get rid of them if you don't like their perks, breed them, dress them, and care for them. It wasn't quite there at release, but now the game is so much fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Cult of the Lamb is a very grim yet charming entry in the "roguelite" genre.You take the role of the Lamb, a creature tasked with operating a cult for an elder god being.A very fun mix of town building, resource managing and dungeon crawling awaits. It never gets too much, with the "rogue" parts of the game being bite sized and taking about 10 minutes to complete (with an option to extend them, should you wish to do so.)The game operates on a day-night cycle that can sometimes get a little repetitive with tasks that you should be performing every day, such as holding sermons and greeting your cult members, however it never got to the point where I would skip these tasks on purpose, as they don't take very long and give you nice perks.As your cult grows you gain access to more difficult areas and a wider variety of decorations and functional buildings, as well as unlocking perks for your members and new rituals to perform.Should you want to switch up the gameplay a little, the game allows you to change the Lamb's pelt, which gives them different buffs/nerfs, such as stronger attacks in exchange for taking more damage.The story is simple yet engaging, and there is a lot of post-game content to keep you glued to your screen.The developers have an update roadmap available, so there's always new features to look forward to. The mythical "sex update" is on the way at the time of writing. I can't wait~.All in all, a very fun game and worth the pick up both on and off sale.Also, there is a fishing minigame. Also also, you can, in fact, pet the dog.
_childDocuments_.name: Cult of the Lamb

_childDocuments_.review: Start your own cult in a land of false prophets, venturing out into diverse and mysterious regions to build a loyal community of woodland worshippers and spread your Word to become the one true cult. BUILD YOUR FLOCK. Collect and use resources to build new structures, perform dark rituals to appease the gods, and give sermons to reinforce the faith of your flock. DESTROY THE NON-BELIEVERS. Explore a sprawling, randomly generated world, fight off hordes of enemies and defeat rival cult leaders in order to absorb their power and assert your cult's dominance. SPREAD YOUR WORD. Train your flock and embark on a quest to explore and discover the secrets of five mysterious regions. Cleanse the non-believers, spread enlightenment and perform mystical rituals on the journey to become the mighty lamb god.

name: Achilles: Legends Untold
detailed_description: 𝐆𝐀𝐌𝐄 𝐅𝐄𝐀𝐓𝐔𝐑𝐄𝐒 Arena Style Co-Op. Action RPG with souls-like combat style. A variety of enemies to battle, each with a distinct combat pattern. Weapons, items, and skills that offer a unique playstyle. An open world ready for exploration. Over 20 hours of gameplay. A proprietary GAIA (Group AI Action) system that governs AI cooperation within the environment. Achilles: Legends Untold is an action RPG featuring souls-like combat mechanics, set in the mythical world of ancient Greece, where you assume the role of the fearless warrior, Achilles. For the best gameplay experience, we recommend playing with a controller. FIGHT AND LEARN Dive into a world where mastering combat, from defense tactics like blocking and evading to a wide array of attacks, is the key to success. _childDocuments_.review: The bar wasn't set too high regarding gameplay depth but basically everything is very well executed. For less than 20 bucks, this is a very good game. It's basically Wolves of Midgard in Greece.+ Fully voice acted, some lines are lackluster and some are repeated over and over, but overall very good+ Great soundtrack+ Decent graphics and awesome performance (levels load in 1 second)+ Different weapons for different fighting styles (swords, axes, two-handers, spear + shield)0 Pretty simple and repetitive combat system but the sound and the gore make it fun- Some items and equipment stats need a lot of tweaking/balancing in my opinion. Most throwing weapons are completely useless at the moment. On the other hand, two-handed sprint attack ("wirlwind") just plows through everything and makes the game too easy.- Simple, slow (and boring) skill progression systemCoop is only for dungeons at the moment but it works well. Coop for the whole game would be AWESOME.

_childDocuments_.review: Get up young princeDon't let a stone take my glory. There are no pacts between LIONS and men. You will wander the under world deaf, dumb, and blind, as the fool who thought he killed ACHILLES. HECTOR! HECTOR!! HECTOR!!Man Troy is one of my all time favorite movies from the 2000’s. Glad they made a game based off Brad Pitt.Before that Skyrim guard took an arrow in the knee, there was Achilles, the man who took an axe to the heel!It truly feels like a tougher and more badass Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance.My wife’s boyfriend says it’s like if Diablo II, Champions of Norath, Baldurs Gate Dark Alliance, and Titan Quest had a love child named Achilles. Achilles is a fun challenging arpg, with a great skill tree, crafting, and storyline. The game is a lot of fun. I thoroughly enjoyed it. There is plenty of action, as well as lots of places to explore. Enemies will give you the challenge you're looking for. The game is STUPID addictive once you understand the mechanics and know what to expect. Playing in the hardest mode makes it challaging and rewarding. The movesets are basic and the armors are not amazing but the story and the gameplay are great. Soundtrack is badass. I love games that have a good soundtrack and this game definitely delivers on that. Kinda reminds me of the first time I played Hades. Achilles will not have a million things to do… but the things it has, it's extremely good at.I loved the Diablo fused with Dark Souls type gameplay.  Brutal (souls-like) and forgiving (wide open world means you can kite the hell out of strong enemies and get really surgical with your strikes) at the same time. Loved the various weapons, as well. Especially the 2H sword, and the spear+shield playstyles. There’s also enough loot to keep me engaged but it’s not overbearing like Nioh. The lack of armor is only a slight negative as you can still obtain armor just not on a “loot” based system.The combat is awesome. Violent, brutal, and gore-ish but definitely not spammy. The combat style is almost entirely melee, but totally fluid and rewarding. Each weapon style has its moveset, and on top there's a few assignable "skills". The in game weapon system is simple. It’s scale based like Dark Souls. If you know Dark Souls this should be easy. The element system is also like any other souls game where Divine damage is better against “evil” or “Undead” and Dark damage is good against the opposite. Enemy variety is good enough for the stretch of the game. I was hoping to encounter a few more other Greek mythology creatures (like Gorgons, and Pegasus) but it’s still great nonetheless.Overall for me it's a very enjoyable game. You'll get overwhelmed at first with the amount of mobs you encounter but once you understand the mechanics of those mobs and know how to deal with them you’ll find it so fun. So far this game has been a blast to play. Great visuals, great skill tree, ancient Greek mythology... what's not to like? If you're looking for a fantastic action RPG adventure with a touch of souls-like gameplay then this is the game for you! Homer Would Approve.Finally, you can pet cats! Brad Pitt would be proud.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No. You are Achilles. You came to Troy to raze and plunder it. Many ships arrive on the shore, with hundreds of your soldiers. You jump on the shore - and you are alone. All alone. Sometimes you see a dead body on the ground, and sometimes you encounter a single enemy, or two. Later a bit more, but that's it. You fight them. And this is the core gameplay. Close quarter fights against small groups of enemies. Center on an enemy, attack him with 2 different attacks, use your shield, dash... and not too much more. Learn a few new skills later, throw a grenade. Enemies just attack you on sight. You have to watch your stamina, and the game plays a bit like a soulslike... So you kill a few enemies, sneak into Troy, and get killed by Paris. And here the story starts, because the god of the underworld, Hades, asks a few little favors from you, or he will let you rot in Tartarus forever. So you agree, and you are sent back to the land of the living. Or wherever you are sent, because the first enemies are a lot of clumsy skeletons. Rest at shrines (bonfires) to get healed, and most enemies get revived. When you die, you are revived at the last shrine. Collect enough fate (experience) to unlock some new skills at a shrine. Die and collect your fate before you die again or it is lost forever. The sourroundings are looking nice, but you can interact with nearly nothing. You cannot destroy anything, there is not much interesting stuff to loot (some healing potions...), not many secrets to find, and even small obstacles cannot be pushed away/destroyed/climbed... sometimes you find a ladder to climb or a door to open. That's it. More or less. A bit... boring. Furthermore, you see your sourroundings in an isometric view, but unfortunately you don't see very far. This is fine for the close combat, but awful for exploring. You maybe see 10 meters in all directions, so you can run past nearly everything that is close to you, just because you do not see it. Only at fixed points the camera switches to a more panoramic view to show you a bit of the sourroundings.The game is in Early Access. What is here already works... but it ends after Chapter 1. Chapter 1! I mean, huh? Where is the rest of the game? You have to wait another year for it and may get it then, if you are lucky. Ok, maybe they will release the planned missing four chapters as soon as they finish them. I am not against Early Access, but in the last months I saw a lot of Early Access releases which did not contain a lot of content. You may get lucky and receive a large game in the end, like it happened in King Arthur: Knight's Tale. Or you may have an unfinished trainwreck after the devs abandoned the game. Is this worth paying a little less than the finished game will cost? Your choice. I was close to downvoting the game, but I think that this would be a bit harsh because it works fine and as long as you enjoy the fights, it is fun. It can become a good hack and slash game if it receives the planned updates. The conversations are fully voiced and have subtitles. The subtitles are often different from the spoken dialogue, though. Gamepad works fine, my PlayStation Dualshock 4 controller even shows the correct buttons on screen. Ultrawidescreen is supported.Classic hack and slash game in Early Access. Contains chapter 1 (of 5 planned)...

_childDocuments_.review: First of all who the hell comes up with this 'souls-like' nonsense, I've seen it time and time again in many different games but the only 'souls-like' mechanic is portal/checkpoint/bonfire where you can level up and where you can rest and reset all enemies. That sure as hell isn't definition of 'souls-like' but whatever I just wanted to address that.About Achilles ... is it a shovelware? No! Is it awesome arpg? No! It's actually fine enough game which is actually kind of a unrefined gem where the first thorough playthrough takes about 20-25 hours- music fits nicely the setting- it's UE4 so it looks nice- every line is voiced even though the delivery might be janky and whoever voiced Achilles tried to do Aldo Raine impression (and tbh it's not a bad thing)- there's fair environment variability (2 big maps and 3 small ones+some cellars and dungeons)- good weapon and overall equip variety- variety of enemies is also good enough for a game with this price tagThinking about it I don't really have something really bad to say about this game, yes it crashed on me once but that's about it. Story is fine, combat is fine, there's couple of bosses that have well visible attacks unlike Lillith in Diablo 4 and the game (depending on chosen difficulty) will most likely hold you by your nuts until you find a blacksmith but after you level up a bit and upgrade your equip you get from mostly 1v1 fighting to aggroing whole groups of enemies and cutting through them like hot knife through butter.So good job devs, you've delivered a game with fair price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Achilles: Legends Untold is like a narrowed down version of Titan Quest with some souls-like elements. Don't expect this to be Diablo. It's still pretty fun! Also pretty clunky.+ Best part of the game is the hack and slash combat. Lots of different weapons to pick your favourite playstyle: swords, axes, 2-handers, spears, shields, you can even dual wield! Special attacks, parries and dodge rolls give a nice flow to fights.+ Inventory and crafting is pretty nice, you don't need to think about managing anything. You get to take a limited number of items with you, the rest is automatically moved to an invisible stash and you can replenish items at bonfires. Too bad the throwing weapons are not all that useful.+ Map design is pretty nice, but the graphics look a bit dated.+ The game boasts an "intelligent group AI system". I noticed that sometimes one soldier with a shield will kneel and then another soldier does a leap attack off his back, that is really cool! Still, enemies still have very predictable movement patterns, making it easy to time hits as they approach you.- My current build is completely overpowered, an upgraded 2-hander that can drop every enemy in a spin-to-win attack, which makes other items and skills useless. I recommend playing the highest difficulty.- Sometimes the aim is off and your swing misses an enemy completely, which is annoying because animations are pretty long and it increases the risk of getting swarmed.- You can get stunlocked by a group every now and then, but you'll learn to move around it.- The "skill tree" is pretty low effort: it's mostly stat points with a few abilities here and there, no way to build a unique character with it.- The voice acting is mediocre and the dialogue is just dumb.- I was hoping for more enemy variety and monsters from Greek mythology, not just random dark fantasy creatures.I had a hack & slash itch that needed scratching, this game does a decent job at it.It's not amazing, but at this price point it certainly is entertaining.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this at the beginning because I think that there is no element in this game that is done simply well, but I still wouldn't want this comment to be misunderstood as negative. My goal is to identify areas that require improvement in the context of future productions (which I strongly count on)◉ ➝ When I only fought 2 bosses on the first day (playing for over 4 hours), and most of the time I was an errand boy, bringing item after item, while being sent back to some corner of the world each time, the level of frustration kept increasing, and I questioned whether the game is actually worth playing/finishing at this point. ➝ An important element of souls-like games is the  Here, unfortunately, there was no separation of areas and quests into specific sections, that would end with an encounter. I was wandering around aimlessly for most of the game, and towards the end of the game I suddenly had boss after boss, making the entire experience a complete mess.➝ Unfortunately, there is also a , which in my opinion are the most important element of the souls-like genre. Outside of the fight with the chimera, these are rather bland. There are no fireworks or more advanced attacks, that would require specific behavior from the player. Unluckily, nothing happens in these fights, and the whole thing is devoid of challenge. I had the impression, that I could close my eyes, and repeat a sequence of random attack and dodge, and I would still finish this fight without any major problems.◉  A huge part of the game is unpleasant and unnecessary running, which constantly forces you to fight the same opponents that you see hundreds of times. I would definitely prefer to see smaller, but more refined locations. This is a very big problem for this game, because it negatively affects all important elements, and I assume that a lot of hours, which went into making that ,could have been spent on many other elements.◉ There was definitely a  here. I collected several of them, which looked rather poorly, and actually took away the dynamics in combat, due to their laborious animations. A game based on Greek mythology has a huge potential. Without messing with the plot too much, we could consider adding non-equippable items/perks, that would give us different abilities, often associated with different gods and, consequently, the elements associated with them. I think that many players would like to see an attack related to Zeus' lightning, rather than some basic dash-pierce spear sequence, without any "flavor"/effect on it.◉ Visually, the game is basically decent.  This makes the entire game look a bit slurry. Some locations also need to stand out a bit more. Too often I had the impression, that I was looking at the same thing over and over again, but with some post-processing added in the form of a red or blue tint.◉  It seems to me, that the game unnecessarily switched between simply distributing base statistics, and perks that modify the gameplay in some way. I would prefer it to be either a simple statistics-based system, or, if you actually wish, statistics with a lot more modification options than you've made.   Apart from the fragment of the constellation, that introduced changes and bonuses for the usage of a shield, we basically had a few, single, insignificant perks that were part of that system. An interesting idea, but unfortunately it doesn't look very good, if it is only implemented in such a small part.◉ The player controller still requires some polishing. Combat can be clunky and a bit annoying◉ Rift clearing definitely too long and with too many mobs. It introduced an almost irritating "level of difficulty", i.e. running and kiting several dozen opponents, one after the other◉ Boxes blocked with the requirement to destroy 3 rune-stones are crazy. A concept that's good for once, maybe twice. Hiding basically half of the crates behind it is some sort of gameplay paranoia, that constantly calls into question the point of exploration. Not to mention, that many of these runes required the use of a shield (which, let me remind you, is not a mandatory element of the equipment)◉ I think that in a game of this scale, randomizing the items found in the chests is rather unnecessary. I would prefer it to be something planned by designers (items placed in specific places)◉ Selling items individually... well, I believe it's some kind of oversight, because I don't know how to comment on it :DAfter playing for 1 hour, I could say I've seen it all. During the remaining 11 hours, I did not experience any changes that would offset the sense of fatigue I was experiencing. Other soulslike creations do not turn their systems on their heads, but because they don't have to due to attaching importance to: With these things, they are able to keep the player's attention and not cause a feeling of monotony throughout the entire playthrough.--Not sure if any developer is gonna read it. Sorry for being such a pain in the ass, but I hope that these can help you in your upcoming games.

_childDocuments_.review: Devs have done a lot of major patches since my original review, and even reached out to me to let me know, so I think that's really awesome and shows the hard work they've put in this little gem. So please give this game a chance, and I'm definitely excited to see what they come up with next! <3   I'll be honest, I played the first 15 minutes or so, put the controller down and said it wasn't for me, even though I LOVE Greek mythology (which was what drew me to the game in the first place). I actually opted in to refund the game, unknowing that I'd had it over the time period limit. And let me tell you, I am THANKFUL that I didn't commit to the refund. I thought hell, I've already paid for it, I may as well play more of it, so I did. Following this tale of Achilles was well worth it, and the length of the game is also decent, too.  Look, there are some little things here and there that make it janky. The voice acting isn't AAA, but it's not a AAA game (and I'm pretty sure the same dude did the majority of the voices). Sometimes the shield doesn't aim the way you want it, so I'd use my keyboard instead when necessary. But overall, the game was definitely worth the hours of play. The world itself is gorgeous, as to be expected with anything Ancient Greece. The range of enemy types as well as weapons is good, too. I'm so thankful that I didn't end up getting my refund, because once I gave it a chance and let the story progress, I wanted to see it through til the end. It was a little hidden gem with a pretty damn good price tag to it, too. I had a lot of fun, loved the writing of the story, and enjoyed the fighting style. Really well done. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not recommending this game for two reasons. 1. The player is easily stun locked, by swarms of enemies (anything more than two). It's not like a souls game where you get one enemy to deal with. IMO being able to be stun locked as a player is the dumbest mechanic on the planet. 2. The stamina pool and regeneration rate is way way way too low (even maxed out) you'll find yourself with out any stamina to attack or doge. So on top of getting stun locked the player can find themselves in situations where their surrounded by enemies, and unable to move away (either by stun or lack of stamina; or even worse getting stuck on the environment) Areas of less of concern but still annoying terms of game mechanics, The enemies have this attack which the player cannot block, which they are quite fond of using it aaaaa lot. The wolves use it as their opening attack and you won't see the notification icon until it too late. The wolves also don't stick around to fight either, they circle you like a wolf would. However the players walking pace is too slow to catch them and running uses stamina, which you'll run out off instantly. The attack animation will get interrupted, but attack speed isn't a parameter which can be upgraded or made player aware in the weapons menu. Aside from that, the graphics and animations are pretty good, the story is a little meh; but good enough to keep you engaged. The camera, especially for a isometric game, is pretty good. However those game play mechanics makes the game very very frustrating at times; enough to make you want to find a trainer and cheat.
