_childDocuments_.review: I've tried to like this game, but is just not worth it. I've spent 14 hours more than anyone should because i am one to usually end a game before giving it a review, but Achilles: Legends Untold doesn't deserve this just like i don't deserve to keep suffering needlessly by playing this dissapointment of a game;The premise of the game is simple: you are Achilles and you died at the Trojan War but were given a second chance, resurfacing in Greece 10 years after the end of the War to find everything is bad.The gameplay is a mixture of ARPG with Souls-like, with a stamina bar for rolls and attacks along with a "fury" bar for your weapon skills. The game tries to do a lot of different things, but none is particularly deep so there's a very limited crafting system, with some enemies dropping resources needed for some one-use items. Later on there will be some "rifts" that you can choose to close, but they are basically very small arenas. There will also be this big monsters from another dimension that you can hunt down to get skill points, but they are all the same. Achilles  also has a Star-sign attribute system (something which reminds me a little of Grim Dawn), but it is horrible: the star signs used in the game are neither the classic >GREEK< ones, nor something interesting (like the 12 tasks of Herakles/Hercules).The game have some pretty sites, but they are few and far between, most of the time just being some sort of "generic Greek ruin" or another. Enemy design is very dull and repetitive, and after the first few hours (3-4) you will have seen most of what the game has to offer. The enemies are divided in: human (different kinds of soldiers), then wolves,dogs, and lions (just reskins), Cyclops and Gryphons (these two are the only two Mythological monsters you will be facing), then Big Soldier Statue, skeleton, Big Skeleton, plant, Big plant, Bug, giant scorpion. The enemies might have different skins, but mostly just behave the same.The story of the game is dull and manage to be even worse than the gameplay, with atrocious voice acting from most of the cast, forgetful characters, uninspiring design and too much "not now, i will explain this later" going on. If anyone knows what "foreshadowing" means, well, this game doesn't understand the concept of the word, making everything too obvious all of the time.Not every game has to have a great story, and that's fine, but the fact that Achilles TRIES TO make it all that much worse. It even tries to give you some choices by letting you decide to either execute or spare some boss enemies.I think one of the greatest disappointments of the game is that it tries everything, accomplishing nothing. If you want a Greek Tragedy, Greek mythology enemies or anything remotely connected to that, you WON'T find it here. If you want a weak, but serviceable story also, you won't find it here, instead you will find something written by a 14 year old boy who skipped History lessons and never managed to grab a book, with all the male characters trying to force some deep, rough voices and a very buffed, not crippled Hephaestus.The "GAIA AI", which is supposed to make the enemies interact between each other in interesting ways (one of the major selling points of the game) rarely shows and, more often than not, it's poorly implemented.I see this game got a lot of positive reviews, but i also noticed by all of the VERY RARE ACHIEVEMENTS that i got from the game, and that are just mostly story progression, that most people didn't even manage to finish the first part of the game.Keep your distance or check this game some years from now. Achilles has a lot of cool ideas that are just VERY, VERY POORLY implemented.One of the good things about all of this is that i did manage to get a lot of friends from removing this game from their wishlists, because no one deserves to throw their money away at this poor attempt at a game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were to ask someone what the greatest story ever told was, you are very likely to get a whole slew of answers, ranging from the classics like Moby ♥♥♥♥ and Huckleberry Finn to modern day classics like The Cat in the Hat...  Hey don’t hate Dr. Seuss got a lot of people through their childhood.. Giving us things like Green Eggs and Ham, and The Grinch..  Sure he also had some questionable beliefs and may or may not have created some questionable drawings for his books, but most of them are still classics..  Anyway, getting back on track, one of the best stories ever told will surely be the Iliad and the Odyssey, two books interlinked with each other and written by the same man..  Homer.. Not the slightly below average intelligence Safety inspector who chokes his son, but the man responsible for all those great movies we watched about the Trojen war..  One of the main characters of the story Achilles.  A conflicted hero of the Greek army considered to be one of the greatest warriors of all time.. Slayer of Hector, the Trojan Prince and greatest Trojan Warrior..  Also slayer of numerous other notable Trojan soldiers..  Done in by Paris and his lucky arrow..  Forever to be associated with your heel..  This story -  takes the tale of what happens after Achilles stops being polite and starts being real... Ok, that’s totally not what happens, he dies and strikes a deal to work for Hades (yes that Hades) back from the dead and ready to reap souls, collect some scraps.. kill a bunch of stuff,, chew bubble gum, cash checks and crack necks.. Achilles wants to drive a range rover... (ok not really) Not to mention slay some legendary heroes or not if you’re feeling generous..   Gameplay - Achilles legend untold models itself after the Souls series, although not nearly as difficult or polished.  The combat features the things you’d expect from a souls like, blocking, dodging, light and heavy striking.  The game also has a co-op option, which I didn’t partake in before writing this review so I’ll abstain from commenting one way or the other on that aspect..Pro’s  Playing as Achilles is something I never knew I needed to doDecent graphicsFairly fluid and smooth movements Difficulty was fairly good, although needs to be tweakedCon’sHad some issues with Fatal exceptions, seemingly fixed with the latest patchno achievements or trading cards, although game is early accessSome minor graphical and sound issues although it’s early access so...Conclusion The games price of entry is 19.99, a fairly reasonable price for the content delivered, with the game being in early access it could be a doubled edged sword like other games in the past, ALTHOUGH, this game seems to have lots of bells and whistles which aren’t normally included in games which sputter out in early access,, but the potential is there like with all early access titles.  That’s one thing to be weary of when making your decision... BUT the game itself is fully functional with only minor bugs here and there, nothing too concerning.. Things that would be nice to see in future updates, aside from additional content, achievements (we love to show off hits), trading cards (Achilles, Hades, Hector, Paris, Trojan trading cards,, yes please).   So I’d recommend picking this game up, giving it a whirl, and enjoying a game which will have you coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an isometric hack and slash that feels like a union of Spartan: Total Warrior and Dark Souls with fun combat and itemisation that sees you wielding weapons with different playstyles, as Achilles in the Underworld after dying to Paris in the siege of Troy. A very interesting premise with a low budget presentation that is at times quite funny, for example when two characters clearly voiced by the same guy are doing slightly different voices and talking to eachother.The enemies in the game call you bastard all the time which is a little degrading but it is what it is. I would have personally used the ancient Greek word it comes from- nothus, which means the same thing. It just sounds a bit more Greeky than a bunch of people calling me bastard in Greek accents. A bit off putting.The combat really is fun. Achilles does a lot of moves iconic from the Brad Pitt performance in Troy, and there are plenty of different moves to try out with each weapon. I actually wish more ARPGs would do combat like this, where you feel like your character is actually fighting and doing combos, instead of just waiting for cooldowns to pop so you can flatten or explode everything on the screen instantly.That's why I compare it to Spartan Total Warrior more than I do other ARPGs like Titan Quest, although it feels a lot like that too at times.Thanks for reading my review you bastard

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This is just an initial impression. I will update this review as I get more time in and more updates are put up.So far the game is rather good and the gameplay seems satisfying.I was playing on the lower of the 2 difficulties available at the start.A few observations so far:1) Combat works well with a controller. Strong and normal attack. Block. Dodge. Run. But also abilities like a 'Spartan Kick' stereotype that pushes people over and a shield throw. All worked quite well.2) Leveling works with shrines you unlock. They allow you to upgrade skills & rest. A bit Dark Souls-like in that you collect life essence / souls to buy skills with.3) The skill tree seems varied and large. Special abilities, stat boosts etc. There seem to be several builds possible at first glance.4) After only an hour of play I can't judge the weapons yet but there is clearly a crafting system and you can find weapons in the levels and equip them.5) The story so far is nice. Troy, Age of Mytholoy, Titan Quest, Classical Greece slammed into the Troy era (so very Homer). The Gods are alive. There are supernatural beasts to fight but also bandits, hoplites etc.6) Levels so far look good. The game is beautiful. I like Achille's design and armor.7) I fought Hector and Paris so far. Judging by how these played out, the basis is there for some rewarding and more complex boss battles later on.Initial impression: Very promising. Hopefully they keep upgrading it. A very promising hack and slash / dark souls / loot & XP grinder game with an awesome theme.Update after some more playtime:1) Loving that they use a system of soul recovery but also have you collect soulshards you keep like in Dark Souls. Wouldn't mind a few more of these drop. Ensuring the pain of a loss of trying to push through is a bit lessened. Overall I like it.2) Good elements of Dark Souls but so far they thankfully don't overdo it either. It is after all partially an action hack and slash rpg with loot. So it looks for a nice blend of Dark Souls skill meets loot and level-up fun. 3) New boss fight I bumped into was challenging but far from impossible. Satisfying for averagely skilled players like me that struggle with hardcore Dark Souls but can appreciate an actual challenge.4) Unlocked some more weapons. I'm liking the selection so far. Love the Classical Greece inspired weaponry so far.5) There seems to be a decent variety of enemies from human to supernatural.Update: Got up to the part of the story released in Early Access.So far I like it a lot.Good combat, fun leveling.I'd love to see more visual/cosmetic variety. (unlockable in game!)And more fun sidequests.Main story is interesting. I get the impression the story will let you side with one of 2 Gods based on some choices you make. Not sure. But if you can go down 2 paths (or more) and thereby unlock other story content & weapons (ideal for replayability!) that's awesome!Update:Probably my final version of the review.Fully released. I gave the game another playthrough.Though not on a hard difficulty. I also did it in 2 or so sittings. So my memory of the early story part may be a little bit blurry. Still my criticism and praise won't be very influenced by it overall.The Story:The final story we got is both better and worse than the pre release version.I rather liked the teasing of picking Ares or Hades. The early interactions with Hades there etc.The story was massively changed (may always have been intended as such) and now focus on helping Hades stop Phobos.It works although i preferred a lot of the earlier story structure, the sequence of some plot events etc.Overall the storyline is satisfying though. With a fitting ending.A few criticisms though:- the flaws of Achilles though a crucial part of the plot are not that explored. HOWEVER I spared everyone. IF memory serves there was a bad ending teased that may dig a bit more into that.- It felt a bit rushed near the end. I feel the game could've used another map maybe fleshing out your 2 main support NPC's. And a map digging into Phobos's realm.Gameplay however is good.A bit of Titan Quest / Diablo, a bit 3rd Person Hack and Slash (traditional) and a little bit of Dark Souls mechanics. Play it at a lower difficulty and it plays more like a hack and slash looter and play it at a higher difficulty and it leans a bit more into the light Dark Souls mechanics. In short you can play it chill and you can play it a bit more stressfully.Upgrades and weapons are pretty varied with an interesting skill and build system with plenty of options.There is a decent amount of side activities and things to unlock.And a chill run will allow you to dive into New Game + at a higher difficulty, digging purely into the challenging combat while having unlocked a lot of the fun stuff.I Can definitely recommend this one.I wouldn't mind seeing them use this system for a Sparta themed action rpg in fantasy greece. Especially really early Classical Greece or Persian Wars era.Mixed in with a good dose of Greek and Persian myth.In any case as stated well worth picking up.If you're unsure wait for a small discount.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just OK for that small price. The idea of taking mechanics and a combat system like in Dark Souls only harms this game. I immediately turned off focusing on the target because it works terribly, it switches to the wrong enemy and constantly jumps.And in general, this seems like an unnecessary mechanic in the game. Because in this RPG genre, when you have a lot of enemies on the screen from all sides, the last thing you will do is focus on any specific enemy. This is the main problem with the combat system in this game. It was specifically made around focusing on one target, like in Dark Souls. Some of the hero's abilities are directed and without focusing on one target, you will simply use the ability past the target, even if the enemy is standing in front of you.But if you thought that for a normal game it’s enough to simply turn off focusing on one target and choose non directed abilities, you’re very mistaken.. Without focusing on the target, it is also very easy to miss with simple attacks, because the hero does not hit the nearest target, as in similar RPG games. The hero simply attacks ahead of himself. Therefore, you need to try hard to ensure that your hero is directly in front of the enemy at the moment of impact. I would say that the combat system is the biggest disappointment and biggest problem in this game. Just remove it from the game, make it like Diablo or Titan Quest and this game will shine with new colors and be 10 times better.Next, the looting and items systems. The game has a huge number of secondary items, such as bombs, traps, weapon oil, potions, and many other resources. And all this is useless. I beat the game using only healing potions, simply because everything else in the game has no value. And also because using all this is completely inconvenient, since it is again implemented like in Dark Souls, with crossbar buttons which you don't have time to use in the action battle and, again, you need to focus the target first.  Also, switching a huge number of these items causes difficulties, because only 4 items can be placed on the panel. They can only be changed through the inventory. It would be good to display the second panel by holding the button, but for some reason there is no such feature in the game.There is no value in different weapons either. During the entire game I changed weapons 2-3 times and it was just for fun. I essentially beat the game with the same weapons, without even really upgrading them. Played on medium difficulty. Many identical points of interest on the map - basements, chests, improved chests with search for keys. This gets boring by the middle of the game and you simply ignore them, not only because of the same type, but also because of the lack of value in these activities. There are also Metroidvania elements here; you cannot open some of the chests without receiving an ability that is given later during the story. I had no desire to go back and open it.  There is little variety of enemies in the game and they are often repetitive, especially in the second half of the story. I guess this can hardly be called a problem, given the overall length of the game and the small size of the world. The developers tried to make a good game, but for some reason they decided to build it around the mechanics of hyped souls-like games, which negatively affected the final result and only made the game worse. In general, I would rather rate it between good and bad, but considering the price of the game, the fact that I am a fan of ancient Greece and a more or less good story, I am more inclined to give a positive rating.

For a game like this, you need to have stability. The game is broken and buggy in so many different ways. Fighting enemies I was facing lag spikes and framerate drops in every single battle. And for a dark souls game that's pretty much always resulting in death. I personally give it a thumbs down right now because of how buggy and broken the game is. But you also gotta remember the good things.It looks good. It sounds good. It's very much like a dark souls game so if thats your thing then you'll really enjoy it. And for how much quality is here and the amount of time it'd take to complete it, the pricetag of 20 dollars is super reasonable.But it has almost no replayability, it's an unknown investment, and it's filled with bugs and glitches that ruin the fun.So is it worth it right now? No.Will it be worth it in the future? Possibly. So if that's good enough for you then make your decision but I'd HIGHLY RECOMMEND waiting until it gets ironed out. _childDocuments_.review: About 4 hours so far and will be stacking more.Fun and solid arpg. Not the most amazing game ever, but there's enough to make you work for it. You learn early on that dodging and blocking (or, just dodging) is mandatory. Doesn't matter your upgrades, there's always something(s) stronger than you. Upgrades require multiple mats you get by killing and destroying, but the upgrades aren't your primary solution to survival, they feel like a pat on the back with a "yay you."There's some jank with default settings. Change the settings, appearance barely changes, jank goes away, game plays fine. Most problems have simple solutions. Should you have to do that? No, but you do anyway, so... y'know... shut up?This game drew me in because of the theme. The take and story on it is well done, good voice acting, the questing/missions are singular and manually switched, there's enough to keep you engaged, and you're probably dead after a couple hours. Could just be me, I'm not used to playing an arpg with a controller, so every time I get the hang of it, I don't.Ultimately, there's a lot it does well, less it doesn't, but all-in-all, I think this is a good game that's worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isand I highly recommend it for everybody, especially for those who own Steam Deck!The game is strongest where it should be - in the interlocking mechanics that make it hard to tear yourself away 🔥 an example of such a gameplay loop? You have a task to complete, so you follow the marker. When you reach it, you decide to go a bit further to reach the checkpoint. Upon reaching the checkpoint, you decide to explore the nearby basement. There, you find a weapon that you want to try out, so you continue on, past the checkpoint. There, you level up and realize there's a side quest nearby, so you go for it. After completing the quest, you're close to another checkpoint, and why not unlock it? Especially since you feel your character growing stronger and sense their power. Words might not capture it fully, but the gameplay is incredibly immersive 😀Other strong points?-full voice acting-pleasant music and sounds-diverse landscapes and locations-the atmosphere of mythological Greece permeates from all sidesWhat could be better? Playing Achilles: Legends Untold is an exceptional fun & adventure, but the potential for a sequel to elevate the experience even further is undeniable. The game is great, but individual elements could be deeper. The graphics are OK, but no one will be picking up their jaws from the floor. The progression system is OK, but more skills and the ability to diversify builds would be welcome. The weapons are OK, but no one would mind more equipment and its features. Quests are OK, but it would be nice to have choices as well. Don't get me wrong - none of this hinders the game because it plays great. It's just that with a bigger budget, more time for production, and lessons learned from the first part, the creators would likely make a global hit. Achilles: Legends Untold is practically made for it. The game runs ultra-smoothly, both in terms of FPS and due to the fact that transitions between locations take a maximum of a second. Well-distributed checkpoints allow for both long and short gameplay sessions - but it's more likely to be a long one because the game is as captivating as a swamp! All buttons are perfectly mapped, and one doesn't have to ponder over the controls. Just fantastic!My recommendationSee you in ancient Greece!

_childDocuments_.review: Considering the game just started being in early access, it's quite good, has a lot of potential. At this point I'd rate it 6/10.Strongest aspect is the fighting. A proper planning and positioning is needed when getting into a fight - can't rush it, as it's easy to be overwhelmed by enemies. So far I found that it's possible to wield 2-handed sword, spear & shield, sword/axe & shield, dual swords/axes - all of those combinations provide different fighting styles and combos, so quite reasonable variety. AI could be improved, as enemies tend to act in a weird way, but it's not too bad.Voice acting for Hades is really good. Creates a proper, haunting atmosphere. However, voice acting for Achilles is really bad, both in terms of writing and acting, which is a major flaw. Hopefully, this will be improved.Story and writing are nothing special, I don't feel engaged by it, doesn't seem interesting. This goes for overall story and dialogues between characters.Another strong aspect is how responsive the devs are on Discord. It is a small team, but they are passionate about the project and are engaging with the community in a natural and genuine way.Bugs I encountered:- significant stuttering at times, and during some cut-scene alike events FPS can drop drastically (often)- enemies tend to get stuck in the ground (rare)- enemies are ignoring me (rare)- minor graphical glitchesTo sum up - if you don't mind few bugs here and there, and won't play it for the story or dialogues, there already are few good hours of fun in this game. Worth giving it a shot, but don't expect too much at this stage.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you to the developers Dark Point Games and publisher Galakus/DPG for providing a fun action game to fight, fight and fight again.My Steam Rating : Mostly Positive I am a huge fan of Greek mythology so for myself, Achilles Legends Untold(A:LU) checks enough boxes as a fun, action adventure game with a good original story. However It’s got some major flaws that holds the game back from being an easy recommendation.  It is very difficult to discuss the story of Achilles Legend Untold without spoilers so all I will discuss is the start. The story begins at the battle of Troy where Achilles is confronted and shot by Paris as it is written in the classic Iliad. However, In this story Achilles does not die but awakens on the cobblestones of Greece where he is greeted by a priest. The priest explains it has been 10 yrs since the war and Greece has fallen into dark times under the rule of Agamemnon. As you progress in the game more stories will come open that will lead you to more of an understanding of why you were spared death. I think the writers did a good job of this new path for Achilles and I like the narrative conclusion. However, the absence of a bio page of the places and major characters within the game could have helped tie that narrative together better.   The story is fully voice acted and covers 16 main missions, 14 side quests across a pretty large variety of beautiful maps which include Greece and its surrounding districts. The maps also include dungeons, cellars and challenge portals and the game ran flawlessly at 3440x1440(100fps). There are multiple difficulty choices but your first play through on any difficulty for veterans of the genre will have no problem as the game is pretty easy. I completed 100% of my first play through(Challenge) around 30 hrs at level 99 killing everything in my path and died just a few times. The game does have a new game + which adds some challenging game modifiers but I still felt it was only slightly more difficult. Also on difficulty I want to say this is where the challenge could have been addressed better. First , you start the game where you can already carry the max amount of health vials(8). The small vials also are equal to the large ones which when consumed will fill your health bar to 100%. Endurance and magic are also non issues at the start as both bars are large enough to never be any sort of problem.    The game play is a mix in between an isometric and third person action game that bills itself with Souls-like combat. It is primarily a melee fighting game so you have light/heavy attacks with a dodge roll and side step and do a leap attack. You also have bombs, landmines and darts along with the ability to equip 3 special magic abilities where you can throw your shield, have an AoE attack, light your weapon on fire as examples. While I get the reason to use the “souls-like” term If you have played any games in the genre or any action rogue likes the combat is pretty standard.   Along the journey you will be also collecting lots and lots of items, whether it is dropped from enemies, collected from chests, completing tasks or you rolling/breaking the thousands of barrels and vases across the land. Weapons are pretty standard with axes, spears, swords and you can go with a shield, dual wield, or two handed. All weapons include their own animations, unique stats, rarity and possibility of having effects of poison, fire, curses, bleed and light attached. You will also come across recipes for crafting but loot is so abundant, there was never a need. The only need for this was to make sure you had flasks, money and the pieces needed to upgrade your gear. As an RPG killing enemies and completing quests earn experience where you will then add pts into a constellation skill tree and while it looks nice they could have just kept it more basic. The skill tree is broken into the heroes 6 attributes (strength/health/precision/Wrath/Endurance/luck) but to earn a single point you have to spend 3 pts. You can unlock a few additional combat skills like parry and passives such as drinking potions faster, throw your shield faster or gather more xp from defeated enemies.  I was impressed with the numerous enemies in the game which included skeletons, plants, cyclops, animals, and soldiers to name a few who will use poison, fire, bleed and curses that can harm your character. The last area of the game really is the best and is by far the most challenging as you can get overwhelmed as mobs are much closer together and gives you that feel of an ARPG but if you have been doing everything, it will still not be much of a fight. Lastly, the boss fights are not up to what is expected. There is a nice variety but all of them were underwhelming and thru 2 full play throughs I maybe died once.  Achilles:Legends Untold is 100% complete, runs and looks great and most importantly is still a fun adventure game. While Its ambition and vision to be a big ARPG are clear it is unable to reach those goals with mainly its lack of balance across the entire game board. Still, if you are looking for an adventure set in Greece with spartans, Gods and some mythological creatures i think you will still have fun despite those issues. PositivesFun action game, 100% completeRan flawless(3440x1440) looks beautiful The last area is what the entire game should have been Original Achilles storyImpressive animations all special attacks and different weaponsSurprising amount of enemy typesPerfect length of game playSolid achievement listNew Game + with modifiersNegativesDifficulty balance- too easyBoss fightsInability to add/change gems in weapons/ shields Lots of inventory for no reasonSkill treeVoice acting is hit or missMusic is quiet

_childDocuments_.review: Achilles: Legends Untold ventures into the realm of Greek mythology with a Soulslike-inspired gameplay approach, offering players a chance to test their mettle against the trials and tribulations faced by the legendary hero himself. As an enthusiast of challenging gameplay mechanics akin to the Souls series, I was drawn to the promise of a mythic adventure steeped in the traditions of ancient Greece.The game's Soulslike elements are immediately apparent, with punishing combat encounters and a steep difficulty curve that demands precision and strategy from players. Every step forward feels earned, as players must carefully time their attacks, parries, and dodges to overcome formidable foes inspired by the mythic creatures of Greek legend.What sets Achilles: Legends Untold apart is its unique interpretation of Greek mythology within the Soulslike framework. From encounters with fearsome monsters like the Minotaur and the Chimera to battles against legendary heroes like Hector, Agamemnon or Menelaus, every confrontation feels epic in scale and significance, immersing players in a world where the line between myth and reality blurs.The game's environments further enhance the Soulslike experience, with labyrinthine dungeons, treacherous landscapes, and hidden secrets waiting to be discovered by intrepid adventurers. Exploration is rewarded with valuable loot and lore, encouraging players to venture off the beaten path and uncover the mysteries that lie hidden beneath the surface.While Achilles: Legends Untold may not reinvent the wheel when it comes to Soulslike gameplay, it successfully captures the essence of the genre and infuses it with the timeless allure of Greek mythology. Fans of challenging action RPGs will find much to love here, as they embark on a mythic journey filled with danger, discovery, and epic battles worthy of the heroes of old. So sharpen your sword, steel your resolve, and prepare to face the trials of Achilles: Legends Untold in this unforgettable adventure through the annals of Greek mythology.

_childDocuments_.review: Indie developer Dark Point Games' project Achilles: Legends Untold has been in Early Access since May 2022, and has since undergone some major content updates and revisions before its official 1.0 release this month. Achilles: Legends Untold is best described as a deft mix of ARPG dungeon crawling and Soulslike-style boss fights. The legendary hero Achilles was proclaimed the greatest of all Greeks, so if we extend that analogy would Achilles: Legends Untold be the best game of all games? This action-RPG has a lot to offer despite its Achilles' shortcomings.With Achilles: Legends Untold, you have a surprisingly effective combination of dungeon crawling gameplay and Soulslike-like mechanics. The game in much better shape than it was in its Early Access, but it still suffers from some core gameplay mechanics problems. With so many full-priced AAA titles that I now regret spending time on, Achilles: Legends Untold is a refreshing wave that the gaming scene needed, for just a fraction of the price; €23 and with 30 percent off during its launch week, it gets even cheaper. Hack-and-slash fans tired of Diablo IV for a while will certainly enjoy their time in ancient Greek mythology.NL-talige review:

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I played 20 minutes. But that was enough for me. Animations are kinda lame, heard the same phrase from enemies 8 times in the first 10 minutes. First boss was easy, figured it was just a means of learning how it works. Which is pretty straight forward, light attack or heavy attack. You can throw in a dodge or block to mix it up a bit (but not as much as you would see from any other souls-like I've played.)  Then came the final boss of tutorial. Far more difficult but only because of his ridiculous life bar and he caught me off guard with his first big fire move. After that I realized, Block all arrows with shield, close in, kick him over, light attacks were much more effective than heavy. then repeat. 5-10 minutes of a very straight forward, repetitive and boring fight later. I killed him.Then like most souls games, I wasn't "supposed" to beat him. But instead of something to tie in the gap, it just acts like I lost to him with a little dialog about how I was weak and he was strong and I wake up asking how I lived. (because I didn't die?)That's when I stopped. Movement, combat, animations, hub, and the map felt cheap and lack luster. Not to mention I was concerned after hearing the dialog/voice acting and seeing the animations in the very opening scene. This seems to have really worked for a lot of other people, and I probably just didn't get far enough to understand. But personally I will go back to No Rest For The Wicked and keep my $20 from this.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice in the way that it feels like the old school Titan Quest. You can probably finish this in 10-15 hours depending on the difficulty +  weapon you've equipped. There is a "souls-like" element but it is more forgiving than it looks, and the dodge has probably guaranteed 99% success rate in avoiding all sorts of damage. Whilst I am a sucker for skill trees and diversifying the character build, it felt somewhat grindy towards the later stages, and was slightly let down that the skills were more or less the same in that you enhance strength/ health bar/ stamina bar and a maybe few special moves. I was looking for something that could encourage me to build a certain way e.g. specialize in the spear etc. At the end I only stuck with 1 or 2 types of weapon which felt were the strongest to play, and disregarded other weapon sets entirely.Other areas for improvement:- Voice Acting: Hit or miss and could use some polishing. Sometimes I paid more attention to the delivery and tone rather than the story being told- Side quests: Sadly there were only very few side quests- Characters: Probably only 4 main characters , but there's very little attachment to anyone hereAll-in-all a fun game with some rough edge, but definitely has potential for a stronger sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: 2 hours in on this game and it gives me the same feeling the original Torchlight did... and I mean that in the way that Torchlight, compared to Diablo 2 and 3, was the more enjoyable, streamlined, and innovative-in-small-ways experience.It is immediately satisfying to play, and the kind of game you can easily lose track of time on because you figure you'll squeeze in one more quest step... go explore that extra bit of the map. I personally am playing this on a Steam Deck, and it feels really good in that format. Not perfect mind you... the movement, combat, etc. have their quirks, but they are minor and if you are not a total thumb'tard, you should be able adapt well enough to the system. It is not a twitch sensitive game, nor is it excruciatingly slow and timing-restrictive like Dark Souls (and the many uninspired clones out there).Achilles is more like Warhammer Chaosbane than it is Titan Quest or Diablo 3. And unlike Diablo 3 or 4, what you pay for is what you get = THE GAME. No battle passes, no hidden pay2win gear masquerading as "cosmetics." No multi-class systems that fool you into thinking replaying the game with a different class will really be all that much different (that is a Blizzard-always-online-era reference... no fake FOMO gimmick mechanics here).The process of the quests and exploring also integrates your learning of combat techniques and the skill tree, etc. as you play... organically... the way it should be. No forced tutorial trying to justify overly complicated systems and sub-sub-skill trees or overly involved crafting/upgrading/potion brewing/etc.. You can jump right in and it is obvious how to do things when they become accessible. You will find yourself, for example, immediately equipping a 2 handed weapon once you find one just to see how it feels, and you will pick up very quickly if it is a weapon you will care to keep using, or not. You won't do it based on any stupid stat analysis or RNG, but rather if you feel genuinely comfortable with the timing of your attacks and how it affects your movement (including the variants on your sprint attacks, which are very different from sword + shield, dual wield, or 2 handed).If you know your ancient history and mythology, in depth, Achilles leans heavily on the Hollywood representation of the "legend" version of events. Do not expect historical/mythical accuracy, there are also liberties taken (with the obvious inclusion of other Greek myth staples that don't quite align with when/where/who was in The Illiad). It is fun, but the dialogue at times is also very skippable, as are some of the characterisations for those of us that are overly educated on the topic. Not quite cringe worthy, but it does have an action hero flavour to it sometimes.Cut scenes are unremarkable basic illustrations with narration/dialogue... definitely not bad, but not high production value or dynamic. They don't quite live up to the in-game vibe... again, easily skipped.Combat animations are also very Hollywood. There are some very obvious Frank Miller 300 moves (most notably the Sparta kick and the leaping sword+shield attack). Again, not historically accurate, but these animations look like they have some real force behind them when they make contact. This is animation done "right" and adds to the feeling that you are connected to the simple isometric hacking & slashing that is happening on screen.Higher difficulty gameplay is, like most of these types of games, a simple bullet sponge scenario. This, unlike many other genres, appears to be within reasonable constraints from what you would expect from a decent RPG souls-like whatevers on "hardest."The gimmick of a custom group AI system.... it generally appears to work and be a real thing. Don't get your hopes up thinking the enemies are genuinely "smart', but they do vary their behaviour when in numbers that you can tell it isn't just a handful of lazy pre-scripts like you get in most games these days. This includes some of the more frustrating aspects of combat where a boss, for example, will properly evade some of your moves in similar ways that you happen to be doing to evade their attacks.The environment is pretty enough, with the world design atmospherics feeling very polished and "complete." It is as pretty as it needs to be. Art style is largely ancient "Greek," with minor fantasy embellishments... but not quite proper Mycenaean or Trojan. The feel of the game world is better for those liberties. And to be clear, the game's visuals "feel" a lot better when you are actually playing it than what it looks like in the trailer.Some games you just know that there will be replay value within the first 20-60 minutes. This is one of those games, as far as I am concerned. 2 hours in and I had to stop because I had real world obligations to tend to, not because I was getting bored.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Good graphics. Generic but good looking artstyle that fits the game. Some areas are very beautiful.- Interesting level design in certain locations.- God of War chest opening system is cute but a little annoying- Your attacks feel heavy and will ragdoll the enemies. I wish  more games have this. Mowing down lots of enemies when you have a weapon with a lot of damage feels very satisfying, until you get interrupted or knocked down.The bad- Music is nonexistent. The voice acting is terrible, sound is ok. Story and characters are awful.- Slow and very punishing combat. They tried to make a "souls like" but ultimately failed.- Stamina reliant combat is poorly implemented. Most attacks require to much stamina and the dodge move requires even more. 2 handed weapons require more stamina to wield and are slower to attack which makes them bad. Their damage is slightly higher but the resulting DPS is a lot lower, because you are slower and more open to interruptions. Dual wielding is also pretty bad. After you chain a few attacks your character will jump in the air to execute a very slow finisher attack. During this very slow animation you can be damaged, interrupted or knocked back. Additionally you need to upgrade both weapons.- Upgrading is very expensive- Interrupts and Knockdowns are a massive issue. The combat is aimed at fighting a few enemies at a time, however the player is consistently swarmed with enemies that will start interrupting and knocking him down. Attacks that are interrupted will consume stamina so you end up receiving a lot of damage + you are out of stamina and now you need to dodge out which requires more stamina. A lot of enemies will open with a knockdown attack and they will run at you until they execute it. You might dodge the first and the second knockdown  but there is more running at you. Prepare to fall. There is no stat or system in the game that allows you to resist knockdowns. - Items are extremely basic with very little affixes. There is pretty much no item game. Most loot is garbage.- Parrying is useless, shield  skills are useless-  Most skills are a useless or underwhelming at best with 2 exceptions.  The best skill in the game (a massive AOE leap slam) is hidden behind a decision to spare one of the game main bosses. Most players will miss this skill.   - The whole system with kill / spare a boss to receive a skill is very poorly thought out and it does not reveal what kind of skill you will get. - Curse is an extremely punishing debuff that not only makes your attacks slower but also your stamina regen a lot slower. Did i forget that it limits your max HP also. - Aiming attacks and skills in the game is very finicky. The game is made for a controller and it shows in a very bad way. - The passive skill tree is extremely underwhelming, and the player is showered with skill points that end up being used mosly on generic stats. Overall I cannot recommend the game. If you decide to get it make sure its on a deep sale  and you really really love playing ARPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with the most notable feature this game presents; it's a solemn ARPG in which you can pet cats. I almost gave the game a negative review for the fact that there is no achievement accompanying the said!Anyway, let's continue to other, lesser aspects.This title became one of the best surprises of this year for me. Despite the fact that the main view seems closer to Diablo-like rather than to, say, GoW or Darksiders, it's a *true* ARPG. Meaning: properly facing the enemy, positioning, timed attacks, minding the HP, dodging, blocking, etc., play the main factor here rather than the honed-dmg-mash-button playstyle. On top of that, normal hits do a small amount of slow'n'stagger. That means the player *feels* the hits connecting. Such a simple, working feature that many ARPG developers forget to implement.The combat feels raw in the best of ways. Uncomplicated, yet, at the same time, thoughtful about every well-known ARPG aspect. In particular, there are dodges, rolls (yes, there are both!), directional blocks, ranged attacks, shield throws(!), skills to gain and attributes to improve, AoEs, DoTs, two-weapon fighting, usually only heavy attacks do something to opponents who shield themselves, etc. On top of that, every kind of attack, roll, block, dodge, parry, usually has a specific follow-up combo.I enjoyed the combat very much, and I had only one slight, which some of the other players already pointed out too. There is one combat move—sprint + simple attack combo—that is insanely strong and very easy to master. Talking about either spears, or two-handed swords. Most enemies usually have no defense against it, thus it's super-easy to cheese most fights like that. You have to actively remind yourself not to give in, and try to implement other tactics. Otherwise, it could render your game somewhat boring pretty soon. Suffice to say, the developer is already aware of this, they said they will address the issue.Apart from combat, there are some light adventuring elements such as simple puzzles or riddles to solve , a bit of exploring in the way of going around some house despite not seeing an obvious path, and there, a little treasure awaits. Here and there, you get treated to small interjections such as cut-scenes or climbing, destroying barricades, a special way to reveal invisible enemies that kept destroying you before, and then some. You can expect some basic crafting; ointments, damage buffs, weapon upgrades, potions, and alike.The atmosphere is really great, and the same goes for music and sounds. They really capture the appropriate feel of the iron age, plus some magic and myths coming to life, obviously. There's one exception in this category though—the voice overs. They are not good, they are magnificent! The Greek accent, the not-overdone acting, every character talking in their own manner! Kudos to that, especially for a small studio.I won't go into detail about the questing and the main line. They didn't seem to distinguish themselves in any way but being on spot with the 'historically mythical' neccessities. However, with the gist of the game lying elsewhere, I don't think we need to care much about this part.I encountered no bugs in 10 hours of gameplay save one whimsical occasion. The subtitles' actors got mixed for several lines and instead of Lysander the Hunter woeing his deceased daughter, we had Achilles doing that and Lysander telling him words of condolence and how he lost the whole unit once. The actual timing of the bug in the whole conversation came out as notably funny.Last but not least, the loading times are nothing short of non-existent. A nice finishing touch indeed!Man, I almost cry tears of joy having encountered this refreshing piece of gaming development after bearing with many nowadays troubled, complacently compromising titles. I almost sense the faint mirage of Orpheus on the horizon, reaching for his lute and delicately smiling upon my heroic endeavors in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The videos and images looked cool, started the game, started to feel the B rated indieness of the game, then the game took me by surprise and absolutely won me over. The exploration is awesome, a lot of games tend to not reward you for exploring all of it's hidey-holes or for taking the alternate paths. _childDocuments_.review: This was a fun time, as mowing down legions of mercenaries and Greek monsters with a gigantic sword should be. Which is good because those action RPG elements are what sustain you throughout its (MERCIFULLY REASONABLE) 24+ hour campaign. The developer’s focus on hack’n’slash gameplay means its story feels as shallow as a kitty pool, however, some thin motivation laid down to keep you playing from one area to the next. But to an action fan like me, that’s just par for the course – so long as the monster mowing feels sweet (and it does), that’s all I need.	Achilles rarely gets in its own way – it wants you to have as much fun as you can by experimenting with its varied weapon classes, each featuring their own unique power moves. From tornado-ing your way with a giant sword through a crowd of soldiers squatting by a campfire, to akimboing blades against a cyclops’ legs before pile driving them into a ground with a seismic fury (the blades, not his legs…), it’s all designed to put a smile on your face.	The only major hurtles to maintaining that smile were the enemies. Specifically, how the field could sometimes be overcrowded by their presence. In certain scenarios, like the Void Arenas or the port in the last third of the game, the only way to win would be to cheese the fight with the same move (run and hit button combo, you’re my only friend). Which feels incredibly cheap, but to try anything else would be to wind up in an equally cheap knockdown-and-poison gang jump! Ugh, those void fights were frustrating...	Also, the enemies manning the port must’ve been eating their spinach because they’re… powerful! To the point where all the leveling you did beforehand feels wasted, as if you’re starting over again. Thankfully, this is short lived because leveling comes fast and cheap in this game, as if every piece of scrub brush in post-apocalyptic Greece were hiding a skill point, but that port never ceases to be a nuisance entirely.        My time with Achilles: Legends Untold was spread across my PC and Steam Deck, where it played exemplary on both platforms, if not as great to look at on the SDeck with FSR turned on. Go ahead and give it a try if you’re looking for an action game that’ll test your reflexes, just don’t be too upset when it starts testing your patience, as well. You’ve been warned!

_childDocuments_.review: So after the release of update 0.3.0 there are changes i liked and still some things that i think need to be improved and reworked.So,the things i liked are:1. The addition of new enemies.2. The new moveset with spears where Achilles uses more thrusting moves as spears are actually used in combat and not slashing with them like with a sword.3. The graphics and performance improvements.4. I feel like Achilles' attacks especially the heavy attacks seem faster than before.5. The expanded enemy attack types.Now,the things i think should be improved in future.1. For some reason after you kill an enemy with any type of running attack the game doesn't automatically lock to the next enemy so you should lock again manually.2. Even after i fully maxed the Endurance stat a dodge roll uses 1/3 of the full stamina bar which i think is too much in a fight with multiple opponents and ruins the flow of combat.3. The timing and recovery time for the timed block skill.After you perform it Achilles remains vulnerable to enemy combos for too long unable to move or block and against multiple enemies results in being combo'd to death.Also i don't like that the window to perform the timed block is too large so you can do it even if you hold block before the enemy attack has even started and as i said sometimes you don't want to use it against multiple enemies.4. Weapon stats i think need some improvement.What i mean is that a common weapon fully upgraded deals almost the same or even more damage than a mythic weapon but is a lot cheaper with less rare materials needed to upgrade with the mythic usually only having some skills like applying conditions like bleed etc. that don't deal that much extra damage anyway.5. The negative conditions on our hero last for too long like for example if you don't have any antidote you have to spend like 4-5 health potions to survive the poison run its course.Also some enemies like spiders apply poison too fast even if you block them so you rely on dodges which spend a lot of stamina so a fight against 3 spiders is not a fun time for me,mostly trying to recover some stamina for a single strike before i have to dodge again.Makes these kinds of fights too long and not fun.6. Also i noticed that the second strike of a light combo with the sword called Blade of Madness often passes through skeletons without dealing any damage.7. I was also wondering why when i block a normal attack from a fodder enemy i still receive a bit of dmg even though my shield has 100% physical dmg reduction.Unless even the basic enemies deal additional dark or divine dmg which would be weird meaning every NPC in this game has a magical weapon.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost fun. Held back by many little mechanical issues dying by a thousand cuts both literally (player) and metaphorically (the game). In its current state, I'd only touch it on a deep sale AND if you're itching for that Greeky/Romany vibe.This game makes me angry because it's so close to being good. The animations, level design, voice acting, cliche cheesy awesome one-liners with mythological doodads up the hoohaw. It's all great, except the glue that holds the game together, the mechanics. And it's not one big thing but many little things that add up to the unpleasant experience.Targeting does not work intuitively. From playing with a controller's perspective, there is no 'soft lock' that most of these type of games have where the closer enemy is 'sticky targeted' but a push on the right stick to force a direction. Instead it hard locks onto an enemy and you have to right stick flick until it hopefully targets the right enemy (which it doesn't most the time). Archer being a pain in the distance? Fight targeting and get shot to death because there's hitstun on every hit, with no invlun frames on hitstun or attacking animations and no animation canceling on attacks, AND these horse sons attack in rapid succession in GROUPS. But wait, there's more! Some attacks also knock back. Welcome to being chain stunned knocked into a corner. Is it over yet? NO! The enemies home in on you and if your character's legs tap even a pixel of the enemy, your attack doesn't go through, and you can't dodge because they're 'inside' your space. No dodge, no block, no attack. Just die or hope they stop attacking/ramming you long enough for you to wiggle loose from the pixel of immobility. At times the game would eat your input because there's a lack of animation canceling and at others (when you get knocked down mid animation) it might queue up an input on stand up. So you want to dodge but it doesn't let you because you're attacking, get knocked down, then it decides hey, you wanted to dodge so how about now? Right into another knockdown. Son of a Horse.Ultrawide monitor people, this game does not have proper scaling. That is to say even the puzzles (the hit 3 targets to open a chest thing) were not made for UW so some of the targets you need to hit are offscreen. And controller people? The aiming for these puzzle is butts. A lot of these targets are also in spots where you need to throw an object, which means if you're primarily using a two-hander like me, you have to switch weapons to a shield or have an ability you get later. In order to complete some of these for that sweet sweet loot on UW AND using a controller primarily, I had to lower the resolution to boxy mc box ratios, switch weapons to have a shield for the shield throw, and point my frickin mouse at the target to hit it, then switch back.This is the death by a thousand cuts part. All of these things on its own wouldn't be too bad but together it just makes playing through the game tedious.There's not only bad in here, as mentioned, everything else runs damn smooth and is fun in general. The load times are near instant, wacking a dude so hard their body flies up into the screen evokes Titan Quest vibes. Being constantly called a horse son of a beach is hilariously endearing. The plot is the right kind of 'oh no, it's *describes a popular mythological creature* I've never seen anything like it' kind of nonsense that I can get behind. Dr. Achilles is here to fix all the problems by grunting one-liners at things and hitting it really hard and I love it. But the meat and potatoes that make up my cheesy meal on wheels flatten those tires and makes it really hard to drive the narrative forward with such a bumpy ride. (I do not regret writing that)So, quite sadly this one is probably a skip for most people, there's too much wrong with it at the moment of writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to get a copy of this after checking it out at a friends house and i must say game is alot of fun Great graphics,control(full controller support),story isnt to bad(Its EA this can be improved upon for full release)even the skills tree is well done......voice acting isnt bad either If you love isometric arpgs i highly recommend supporting these devs and grabin a copy u wont be disappointed and with each update game will just get better and better....---Game win 7 x 64 support---Know little tip for those with windows 7 game wont start due to being set to dx12 api in UE4 engine its running on so easy fix...alot of time using a startup command line argument wont work either so i have a sure fire fix and this fix can be used on any UE4 based game that is win 10 or 11 only....start game up itl not wnat to saying blah blah blah about running game without dx12 argument command simply after that go to game directory in steam and locate the config folder which is located here--- SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Achilles Legends Untold\Achilles\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditorKnow after getting into config folder find the Engine config open it up using c++ note pad and add this line after the last config section for [WindowsApplication.Accessibility]make sure there is space between the sections and add this entire line[/script/windowstargetplatform.windowstargetsettings]DefaultGraphicsRHI=DefaultGraphicsRHI_DX11Save config..set to read only  by right clicking on config and going to properties(doing this ensures engine doesnt over write it again)Game will know start everytime using dx11 api and will run flawlessly on win 7 x 64Im a UE4 dev myself know alot of config tricks that can be done to any UE4 engine based game

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate to give negative review on a smaller developers game, but this game needs a lot of work. It's like no one bothered to QA any part of this game as you encounter issue after issue from the beginning (where it's not quite so bad) through the end.Some of the issues I experienced are:* Massive frame spikes at regular intervals. Some area's aren't too bad, and it was never enough to cause any issues.* Certain actions like healing and the shield throw don't reliably activate, requiring you to press the mapped button more than once. Fortunately, this doesn't cause issues like in Souls games where you'll take a couple chugs of Estus when you didn't want to.* Achilles commentary will sometimes remain on the screen for an entire area. This mostly happened in the final area of the game.* It's not open world and there only a dozen or so side quests which is kind of a mercy because it's incredibly repetitive.* You get crystals where the item descriptions imply they allow you to upgrade a weapon with their element but there's no option to do so when visiting the smith.* Enemies all have roughly the same attack pattern. It was incredibly easy, even on the 2nd hardest difficulty. On the bright side, people who like Diablo will probably enjoy it because most of the game can be played by spamming attacks, minding the character's stamina and skill cool downs.* Using a two-handed weapon eliminates the ability to parry (not all that useful) as well as the shield throw. There's no way to map another skill to accommodate for losing the shield throw which is one of most useful abilities in the game.* The manual aiming for the shield throw is super buggy.* The shield throw doesn't always work – later skills allow it to hit enemies when returning to the player, but sometimes it will circumvent a whole mob of enemies and do nothing.* The menu is painfully slow to navigate, getting to your skills is weird, and restoratives are way down in your item list which is a pain when using a controller as there's way to speed up the process.* There are many times your strikes simply won't connect. Fortunately, this goes both ways.* The dialog is bad and voice acting doesn't help. I understand this is a Polish studio but every few sentences in English are awkward.Finally, the game isn't awful. It's just incredibly half-baked at the moment, worse than some of the more recent early access games I've played.For anyone looking for a similar experience in a well polished game, I highly recommend Sands of Aura.

_childDocuments_.review: Good Not GreatThere is a core great game in there somewhere. What starts strong yet finishes flat.Performance:Achilles performed really smooth on my rig. I didn't have a crash to desktop at all in the 30+ hours I played.There were a few textures pop ins and load stuttering as I entered a new area but nothing that was distracting.COMBAT:Combat is interesting but mostly a frustrating mix of isometric ARPGs and soulslike features.The game description teased an enemy force that would work together against you. But what I experienced isthe enemy really only had a few special coordinated moves such as surrounding and leaping into the air from a shielded enemy to slam attack you. That was cool. Mostly, they just simply bum rush your pinning you and thus stunlocking you into oblivion. I am not convinced the stamina drain was truly needed here and the enemy certainly did have it. They could attack damn near endless combos in the upper difficulties.The hitboxes felt....odd. Sometimes Achilles would be spot on in soft targeting and other times he seems to forget where the enemy is and attacks in a rando direction. There were frequent instances where the attacks simply passed through the enemy. Enemy recovery is darn near instant when imbalanced from a parry or block.By the end of the game, I simply was ready to finish it after that. There were also times where Achilles just stopped attacking and just stood there allowing a free hit from the enemy. There is input queuing which got frustrating by the end as there were times where Achilles would stop, I would attempt to dodge, he would do nothing so I attack and then suddenly he would lurch back dodging and then attack. -_-Weapons are...basically five weapons: Shield, Spear, Sword, Great Sword and Axe. I found the spear to be the best for my playthrough as it has the best reach but felt a little...slow on the attack.SKILL TREE:A cool yet strange mix. It is a set of constellations that concentrate on a particular stat (such as vitality). There the skills that Achilles can perform but mostly just stats. Weapons and shields will tell you what they scale on but it is hard to tell just how much that scaling is.The skill dots can take up to 3 points to completely fill. The game does NOT tell you this. There were a couple of instances where I thought the game bugged and did not fill in a point but it was there just not lit up. The "star" lights up with at least two in it. It would have be nicer to have the stats be a single point and the skills be the triumvirates that increase the efficiency and potency of said skill. Also, missed opportunity to have a passive skill that leeches a small amount of stamina (like energy and life leech skills do).STORY:Story is original yet feels unfinished. Like there are elements left out for unknown reasons. Pretty typical revenge fair and stop an "unknown" evil. The voice is laughably cringey but I can't fault them for that. Small dev studios just don't have the capital for AAA talent.ENEMY VARIETY:Enemy variety is not bad. There are some of the cool monsters from Greek Mythology but A LOT are left out. I would have loved to see satyrs, centaurs, cyclopes, hydras. etc.DIFFICULTY:I managed pretty well with the game even on "Challenge" difficulty. I blasted my way through endgame without breaking much sweat here. XP is exactly the same regardless of difficulty or NG+. It would have been nice to see that be adjusted to be based on difficulty or NG+ level.Overall, I enjoyed it but it begin to loose that luster by the end of the game and I was just ready to beat it and move on. Co-Op is non existent except for "challenge" rings. It was marketed that it had co-op not just battle arenas for co-op. That was majorly disappointing. Also, if you go about trying to get the collectable achievements, do in that current playthrough; they DO NOT CARRY OVER. Score: 3.5/5

_childDocuments_.review: I was unable to get satisfactory performance out of this game on two different machines. One was the ROG Ally, a handheld PC, so kind of understandable, but the other was a desktop with an RTX3090. The framerate was fine, but I had a ridiculous amount of loading related stuttering on both machines. Every time I entered a new area,  I would be overwhelmed with constant stutters and pauses, making combat very difficult. Once an area was explored the stuttering would mostly stop, but the first time through would always be a problem. Both machines have SSDs and the game itself would load in the snap of a finger, so not sure why this was a problem, but I've heard the engine this game was built with is notorious for doing this. Despite the technical issues I was still interested enough in the game to want to continue, so I ended up double dipping on the PS5 version, which ran flawlessly. I completed the game there and did most of the side content, and overall my impression still falls within "do not recommend" territory. There are some interesting ideas here, but there are too many shortcomings and issues to work past in my opinion. These were the worst offenders:1. I experienced constant dropped inputs in combat. There were so many times I would run full tilt towards the enemy and hit the attack button, only for Achilles to stop dead in his tracks right in front of an angry mob, as if he wanted to give them a little kiss instead. This would also happen when attempting to use potions or abilities. I died a few times due to these glitches, but mostly it was just a constant annoyance.2. The voice acting is really bizarre in this game. Achilles and a few other characters are fine, but most of the enemies and minor npcs sound like the same person with their voice run through a modulator. In the case of the enemies it is very distracting and noticeable, as you will hear the same lines repeated constantly with the voice pitch adjusted up or down. It honestly would have been less distracting if the human enemies just didn't talk at all. 3. The weapons in this game are extremely unbalanced. The moment you find a two handed sword in this game, it is very hard to go back to one handed or spears. The running light attack for two handed weapons swings in a wide arc, comes out fast, and hits twice. There is no other basic attack in the game that even comes close to its effectiveness. This is compounded by the fact that you are almost always facing large groups, whereas one handed weapons and spears feel optimized for dueling one enemy at a time. Also, for a game that has three distinct weapon types and play-styles, why can't I equip multiple loadouts? I used two handers most of the game, but it was always annoying to have to stop and equip a sword and shield so I could complete one of the rune chest puzzles. It seems like a really obvious improvement to just give the player two loadouts you could switch between with a button press.4. Too many annoying enemy types that aren't fun to fight. Wolves and lions fall under this a bit, as they both constantly knock you down and force you to chase them with their superior mobility, but I'm mostly referring to the horrendous plant enemies that litter the second map. These enemies don't move and have a single easy to dodge attack, but they are absolutely everywhere and often blend right into the map. They're uninteresting to fight and way too prevalent in certain areas of the game. They mostly seem to exist to confuse your automatic lock-on, as there were many times Achilles would suddenly turn his back to the giant monster right in front of him so he could focus on one of these plants somewhere off screen. Those were the biggest headaches, but overall this game just suffers from not committing fully to being either a souls-like or a diablo style action rpg. The human enemies have well designed behaviors and are interesting to engage with, but the game throws so many of them at you at the same time you are pretty much forced to mindlessly mow them down with the two-handed sword. Either drop the enemy density and severely nerf the two handed sword, or lean into the mindless mashing by giving one handed weapons and spears larger attack ranges so they're more viable against mobs. If the technical issues were resolved and the balance adjusted somewhat this would probably be a recommend, but as is I can't really give it a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Latest updates to game make it a whole new experience, really fleshed out the potential I spoke about in my original review which follows:Game is in Early Access so I won't vote it down. It has a LOT of potential.  I'd like to get into the cons first.Issues:Glitchy.  First 5 minutes I ran into a total game crash.  Not sure what I did, I was in the menu. Not very well optimized yet.  Lots of big FPS drops, not very consistent. Control scheme is terrible.  Just poorly thought out and designed.  Honestly kind of a head scratcher it is so bad. It tries to use a Souls like approach but fails completely.  First R1 and R2(trigger) are your light and heavy attacks respectively.  That is fine. I would prefer custom mapping to X and Y personally for this style of game. But the real problem begins with how the other actions are mapped.  L2(trigger) is just a modifier you hold in order to activate actions with R1 and R2 that you dont get till later.  L1 is your block, but ALSO a modifier for actions on A and Y (really?) of all buttons...Otherwise Y has no mapping at all...  B button is a little side step dodge move, double tap for a roll or hold for running...awkward...It should only be for the roll move.  Dodge/dash should be L1. Hold for running, or click Lstick for run.  L2 should be block (plus attack modifiers while blocking). Blocking with the right timing should result in a parry. (maybe it does, I am just saying). X is some other special ability I have not unlocked yet. Feels bad and confusing. Rstick click locks on, which is good, and flicking the stick switches targets. That is all fine.  There is no jump action (unless a special skill I have not seen yet), but its not really missed much.  The D-pad is for item useage.  Instead of left and right cycling through your consumables, you can only have 4 and each direction uses one.  I think allowing more than 4, and having the down be activate, left and right cycles, and up can be reserved for maybe swapping weapon sets or something, would be better. There seems to be no camera adjustment. Not a big deal.  Main complaint so far is the glitches and the poor controller mapping system.  Game currently seems over priced by about 50%, but if it gets polished up well and the action scheme gets improved, it would probably be a decent investment at current price.  If this is basically how the game is going to be, then no.  Good things:Graphics are great and not too taxing.  I have a 2060 running on a PCIe 2.0 bus, and it runs pretty well on max settings most of the time, at 1080p resolution. Some FPS drops here and there like I said. Art style is on point. General attacks feel pretty good, timings feel reasonable and fair.  Animations are excellent. I have not dived into the skills and equips yet, but they are there and they seem nicely designed to enhance play styles and with plenty of play style customization.  Enemies leave item drops. I always like that. Total impression so far:Game looks like a AAA title but just does not play like one quite yet. Ton of potential though. Although the controller scheme is a huge drag and disincentives me to play, I am going to persist for a while in order to explore more of the skills and equips and such to see what is happening there.  I will probably update this review. Edit: Control issue is much improved.  However, the dash roll move is problematic. Tapping B twice makes It studder between animations, it looks and feels bad. I would just make hitting B while prone, be a typical back step dash, and a roll when ever the stick is pushed in a direction, and holding R1 for shield should turn it into a shield bash forward dash. Maybe a strafe dash while R3 is locked on, double tap for roll then (but fix the animation). The little dash move is unnecessary, just a roll evade would be fine. I also really do not like feeling like I want to start over because when I die during the beginning area, the whole area changes and I start somewhere else. The difficulty spike between regular enemies and mini-bosses is kind of ridiculous and all of a sudden I have this terrible controller latency that gets me killed... I was not done exploring.  Makes me want to quit. Warning to the devs, if the game comes out of EA in this state, I will down vote it.

_childDocuments_.review: Achilles: Legends Untold:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ After falling at the battle of Troy, Achilles found himself in Tartarus. Once a fearful fighter, he is now imprisoned in the underworld. To his surprise, the king of the underworld, Hades, throws him a lifeline and offers to send him back to the land of the living if he does him a few favours, such as finding or killing someone for him or bringing back artifacts. This is no time to waste, and Hades is not the patient type of god. Here is Achilles: Legends Untold.Achilles: Legends Untold is an isometric action/adventure souls-like game developed and self-published by Dark Point Games on the 13th of May 2022 on the Steam platform as an Early Access.After experiencing his death at Troy, which is an excellent tutorial, the first Hades request is to find his nephew Hephaestus and bring him back to his forge. Achilles will be able to upgrade his weapons and armours, but first you need to find him and his hammer.  The game is set up with quests which you can find in the character menu under the chapter tab. Each quest will have several objectives to complete, and they must be completed in order. There are several quests in this Early Access version that I have nearly finished. Each area Achilles visits is beautifully done, from the scenery to the enemies you encounter. In addition, each area has several shrines where you can stop and rest and also upgrade your skills, which are sensationally presented as a constellation. To do so, you will need souls you gather by killing enemies or by finding souls in the loot bags scattered around each level. Some enemies might drop items such as health or energy potions, to mention a couple, as there are stacks of them. Some chests usually have special items, including weapons and amours, so make sure to look thoroughly at all locations. As you progress through the game, you can also use the shrines to teleport Achilles through the locations you have already visited. There is constant fighting in this game, and you will encounter various enemies. So far, I have fought against griffiths, giant scorpions, lions, wolfs, cyclops and skeletons, as well as archers and soldiers with melee weapons. The combat mechanism works well, and I really enjoy the items and weapons interface; it reminds me of Diablo. So far, so good. As you would expect, there are issues with early access games, and I know they will be fixed. However, some of the problems I experienced were minor. Things like enemies running at you erratically without fighting or getting stuck. The latest one is part of a quest to gather an armour for Hephaestus but I have no idea where the last part is. I am going through all the locations and trying to use Hades’ vision, which allows Achilles to find objects in the surroundings that are not visible unless you use it. Now I am stuck! They might need to introduce a map, which they don’t have at the moment. Yes, you can use a key or a button on your gamepad, and it will let you know where to go, but in my case, I don’t know where to go. So a map with some reference points would be helpful.The graphics are good, and I enjoy the story so far. There are plenty of items and weapons to find, and the gameplay is solid. I strongly recommend playing the game with a gamepad, but it is also fine with the mouse and keyboard. In terms of saving, the game will autosave each time you visit a shrine, and  Steam cloud is also available.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics+	Well-presented upgrades and easy to use for both skills and weapons+	Various enemies, including mythical ones+	Stacks of loot per level+	Good combat systemNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Several minor issues-	No map, which I think is needed-	No achievements or trading cards yet.Despite having minor issues, Achilles: Legends Untold is solid with a good combat system and interface. If you enjoy Hack and Slash games, it’s worth a try.7/10  Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Achilles is a low-budget souls-like presented from a top-down perspective with some superficial RPG mechanics thrown in. It doesn't provide the level of depth I've come to expect from either genre, but by embracing its simplicity, I enjoyed my time with it. I played on the hardest difficulty and found the combat pretty satisfying. The first few hours were definitely the hardest, but after you gain access to skills and upgrades, the difficulty becomes trivial. There are, however, some very challenging "co-op challenges" found outside the main game with some additional unlocks for those interested. Exploration was largely straightforward, with most side areas providing a minor reward, or bonus skill points for defeating a boss or activating an altar. The skill tree, though, seems completely unfinished. Most constellations completely lack any skills other than stat boosts, leading to some fairly boring progression. Some achievements are buggy, so I had to use SAM to unlock them. The dialogue is paced so dreadfully slow that I can't find it in me to care. Every character speaks like they're in a middle school Shakespeare production, wasting 30 seconds of my time to say a single sentence. I wouldn't recommend Achilles unless you have an affinity for its setting. Fighting some iconic monsters and following the heroes journey was fun, but the gameplay did very little to keep it engaging.
