_childDocuments_.review: Hack and slash games are ultimately defined by their combat systems. Sometimes, other factors play a role, but if the combat isn't up to par, the game isn't memorable and doesn't make a lasting impression. Unfortunately, this is memorable for all the wrong reasons. The combat is so insanely boring from start to finish, with virtually no depth and only a handful of abilities at your disposal, this becomes a painful slog to the finish line after just a few hours. Very little enemy variety. Very little weapon variety. The voice acting was genuinely embarrassing, especially for the Smith and the Oracle. The story couldn't be more generic. The quests are unimaginative. The soundtrack is forgettable.I struggled through the game twice to complete the achievements and can't think of a single positive.

In regards to the actual story you are thrown into is very basic, but the fact that it takes place in a strange dimension, somewhere between life & death, ruled by intriguing, mythological monsters and devious men, while giving the main character just enough emotional motivation (& by proxy, you the player) to make following through till the end a worthwhile endeavor...I think it's worth mentioning that the skill tree(s) basically consists of very few paths that actually lead to in-game *new* mechanics (i.e. a charged heavy attack or a shield boomerang) with the rest being literally just minimal gains to your basic stats.  I really wish that each & every skill tree branch would have at least one new skill to augment your fighting prowess (which may be on the way from the looks of the upcoming patches later this year, if not already a new skill or two since my last gaming session--we are talking about several months since i've last played)PS *Attention all Legion Go users*  This game runs smooth as butter with minimal effort getting the settings lined up 👍

_childDocuments_.review: MASSIVE Thanks to the developers for making such an awesome game.- Fun game for the OG and Newer gamer- Story game lovers- I played Adventure mode: Difficulty was mildly challenging (difficulty can be set 2x higher and there is an easier mode called story mode)- Boss fights were easy/interesting and straight forward for the adventure mode- Beautiful Map: Explore without getting lost OR drifting off into the abyss- Nice controls (Slow start but you get used to it fast)- Moderately Interesting story but game-play and tasks balanced it out- Beautiful graphics- Nice upgrades that actually worked and in most cases very useful- Skill tree was OK and massive but it didn't break the gameOverall, this game is worth the money.If you are an exploring type of gamer that enjoys sword fighting, completing tasks and item collecting on a mildly big confined map. Then it is a definite add to your library.When you start, the game might seem boring. But it transforms.After it transforms, the map might seem intimidating. _childDocuments_.review: Would definitely recommend Achilles Legends Untold, under 1 proviso, that being - You own a Gamepad and wish to play the game on a Gamepad.   I began playing on M+K and found the game though playable, quite clunky with some actions just not working as they should or difficult to pull off with key presses, such as Roll instead of run. Also having to use Keys for your movement constantly combined with the mouse for attacks and tagging enemies meant having to hit other keys for potions or throwing items meant sacrificing either movement or attack.  Once a gamepad is used the game becomes much more enjoyable. Set in Ancient Greece ( kind of ) it's an ARPG where they've tried to make Boss fights more engaging and tactical and for the most part they have pulled this off really well. Add into this regular combat where enemies can be equiped with different weapons requiring variation in tactics to be more efficient. From the start of your quest you are lost in both a familiar and unfamiliar land. As you fight your way through your quest opens up with discoveries and people you meet, along with you strengths and equipment.  One major issue I struggled with at first other than trying to play M+K was, you can get mobbed or placed into an area where you can receive quite a lot of damage along with situations where the character you are locked on is passed by another unlocked character or another approaches you from behind, yet Achilles remains Locked on the original target. Getting stuck like this can result in being sent back to the nearest Shrine ( The Game has a Dark Souls alike system where you are teleported back to the last Shrine ( A-La Bonfire ) and also implement the recollect dropped Exp Points, though the game itself isn't as punishing or frustrating as a Soulslike by a long shot.  Getting back to the Target Lock/Select when using a Gamepad a Right Click on the Stick locks and Flicking the same Stick Up or Down alters quickly who you are Tagging, this ability transforms combat.  Yes, you can still get yourself in a bad spot and surrounded thus taking damage, BUT this is generally down to bad positioning and play.       So, yes can defo recommend especially if you like the Greek / Trojan War Setting / World. The Achillies Character Model is very much identical to Brad Pitts Achilles, Armourwise.  There's a decent selection of weapons all fitting with the setting / period i.e Sword, Spear, Axe, Double Handed Sword along with Shields, Throwing Knifes and Bombs. It doesn't get silly with the weapons coming after every encounter, and where you are constantly looking at what you've got and trying to decipher if it's better or worse. The twist of it being an ARPG but with that closer in view and more meaningful combat really works well for this game.          So far the Story has held my interest, though you could play the game purely for the joy of slicing through the Undead Jason and the Argonauts Style or recreating scenes from Troy with the Hero Boss Duels.Well worth a look and Play through.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Greek who grew up playing Age of Mythology and DIablo, this game was right on my radar. Having only played a few hours of it i have to say it's pretty good so far. The combat, although simple and awkward at first is pretty easy to get into and have fun with and i like how the map is structured with linear paths for you to take without getting too confusing. You can always tell where you are and you can use shrines to teleport around. Enemy AI is aggressive enough and i bet it can get pretty challening if you up the difficulty past normal. I've only used my controller so far and the controls were pretty decent and responsive enough so i can't really say something about how it feels with a mouse + keyboard. As far as graphics go, of course i wasn't expecting anything fancy given the fact this is an indie game but i have to say, i'm a bit disappointed with how it looks overall. Might be a problem with Unreal Engine itself or something like that but the game looks low res even at the highest resolutions which is weird, altought the artstyle and the environment look good. Of course you can expect things like mediocre voice acting, generic story and minimal to no cutscenes from a game like this but overall, for it's price i'd say it's well worth giving this one a try especially if you like that ancient greek vibe which isn't really common in gaming nowdays.

_childDocuments_.review: I have visited every shrine, ruin, and cellar, opened every runic chest, finished the story, explored every part of the map and I have to say; the experience was fantastic! Every location is beautiful, detailed and mesmerizing, you just want to look at the view for some time. The story was superb. It captivates some aspects of an ancient mythos, gets inspired by events and births a new tale that lacks neither action nor adventure.Combat is rewarding, challenging in some instances and your character has a great arsenal of weapons. My only complaint is the enemy locking system. Sometimes, the locking system constitutes an enemy itself, rarely being unresponsive, locked at a distant target or an of screen target. Also, it seems that it wasn’t designed with the “fighting multiple enemies at the time” in mind. Thus, it needs some work.Other than that, I totally recommend the game, it was a great experience that worths the full sale price!

_childDocuments_.review: So even though I gave it a thumbs down it has potential and it's definitely worth a play.The game overall is OK at best. And here are my issues with the game.1) The targeting system and slow pace combat makes the game feel cluckly. I get they were going with more of a dark souls combat compared to a diablo like game but in an isometric ARPG these system don't work that well especially the targeting system. Stun locks are fine but for how much you get animation locked in combat and EVERY attack stuns you it doesn't feel good at all. Blocking also feels kinda useless in this game considering when fighting groups of mobs they stun you even if you parry one the other 2 will hit and stun you anyway so dodging is best and for bosses most of their attacks are unblockable so you might as well just dodge around them too.2) The "skill tree" is sad to say the least. I think they could have done ALOT more with it especially since combat as it is now feels clunky. 3) Boss fights are fun in this game and I think they nailed it but groups of trash mobs feels harder than the boss fights and I'm pretty sure it should be the other way around? Again this circles back to my last 2 points and I believe can be fixed.Overall I'm enjoying this game for the price I paid for it and overall can't wait to see what else comes out of this...hopefully?

_childDocuments_.review: I put the thumbs up as i played the early access, liked it and decided to do a whole playthrough with version 1.0While i like the visuals, combat and the simple upgrade system, after a few hours playing i felt a bit bored as the game becomes repetitive and the encounters are always kind of the same. And the further you go the more the game uses some cheap difficulty mechanics like throwing a ton of enemies at you at once (even during the last boss fights, too bad)On the other hand the game can be fairly easy when there's not 15 enemies attacking at once, I only died a couple of times (3 or 4 i think) when i got surrounded. Otherwise i beat every single boss, including the last one on my first attempt. _childDocuments_.review: I liked the premise, setting and the combat of this game. After finishing it, I am torn between thumps up or down, but in the end its still a rather fun action game despite its many flaws.- It has some of the familiar Souls mechanics like Bonfires in the form of Shrines of Hades that reset all enemies when you rest, and a form of Blood Stains that drop your experience when you die that you can recover, though every skillpoint you earn from level up is not lost on death, and level up is so frequent that this is not really a factor to consider much which is a shame.- I would strongly recommend playing on Hero difficulty, which is "hard mode" in this game, which feels abit closer to what a Souls game would be at least in the early game, given all the same mechanics this game uses and styled itself as having Soulslike combat. And look, I wouldnt consider myself a particularily good player, that being said, the game gets way too easy even on Hero difficulty. The early game was fun and challenging but around mid-game you feel very overpowered and everything dies in just a few hits, you can facetank enemy red attacks which barely make a dent, and I forgot to use the smithy to upgrade my equipment and still this was the case, not sure what happened here with the balance and player progression. At least some of the later bosses were better designed, still I didnt die once during bossfights which is surprising for a game with souls-like combat.I was disappointed to see the challenge drop off so much as it felt like yet another powerfantasy game. At least the optional rifts offered abit more of a challenge during mid-game. I would've enjoyed it alot more if it pushed me to engage with its systems more (like upgrading my equipment because things would get challenging otherwise), because there is a decent foundation here. Im not suggesting they should remove the normal/easy mode for those that enjoy that experience, but rather fix up the Hero mode's progression curve and make it so that players feel incentivized to engage with upgrade system and learn enemy and boss mechanics and so on.- The target lock system is really bad when fighting groups of enemies. Sometimes when trying to switch with the right stick it switches to the wrong target and sometimes nothing happens at all.- Skeleton pack surprise ambushes are awesome! Those killed me the most times, because I wasnt careful to look and just ran into them. I see people online complaining about them stunlocking you to death so the devs might nerf them, but I enjoyed having to use my brain and be abit careful. Also its my own fault and not the game being "unfair" in this regard.-Fury meter is a nonfactor (basically mana in this game). Went through the almost the whole game without ever using the Fury potion. Very early on you gain access to a skill that gives fury regain on every attack from just a few skillpoints, so never having to consider the use of fury removed a layer of depth from the game. Only on some bossfights did I use the potion.-The story is abit bland. I was expecting something different based on the premise, like the old God of War 2005 style story, and not running some errands for a blacksmith. The late game gets abit more interesting. Last world map area was really nice, definitely the best made area, open and with lots of treasures and stuff to find, the aesthetics was great.- Some text during dialogues dont match what the person is saying.- Another negative for me is the voice acting, primarily the protagonist voice just sounds so off.- I also got stuck on terrain a few times and once I had to use "Return to last shrine visited" to get unstuck. *Edit *Just noticed the "Unstuck" option exists in the menu, which is nice.- Then there is the usual Unreal Engine 4 stuff, like stuttering and performance hiccups despite using high-end GPU that is only around 60% load. Hopefully they will continue to release patches to optimize the game. (While UE4 games are never perfect, they vary alot from game to game based on optimization done by devs).As I said, still a decent game for its price with some fun, albeit easy, combat.Umm, so yeah thats all I can think of right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Achilles: Legends Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a surprisingly fun little hack and slash. The weakest point is honestly probably where it's using Soulslike mechanics, but even those aren't too bad. It sort of feels like a blend of Titan Quest, God of War (the old kind, not the moviegame) and Diablo in a good way. Combat is punchy with a good amount of blood, relatively fluid and responsive. Could use a little more gore though, and this feels like a game that could really use some sort of "execution" mechanic, even if it's just a random animation that plays on the last enemy in a group or something. Hit feedback could use a little more work too; this is where the Souls mechanics negatively impact things I think, because while basic enemies feel great, the heavier ones basically don't react to blows (at least from one handers) and will hyperarmor through your attacks, leading to a lot of hit trades that you come out worse for.  There's also very little indication you as the player are getting hit, especially in a crowded fight, leading to moments of "oh crap, half my health is gone and I'm poisoned somehow." Enemies sometimes pile on a bit too aggressively as well, and I've noticed some of them continually spam unblockable red attacks which can break up the rhythm of the fight a little too much if you're a parry/block player.While the unseen world mechanic is cool, I feel like it should be one or the other, as it's easy to get ganked by wolves while you're fighting a bigger enemy or vice versa. That or maybe just nerf their damage a bit or something to show you're not fully in their "world" at the moment.The slower leveling doesn't bother me as long as there's no cap and we can grind as much as we like. I get what the devs were going for; it's basically a Souls-like stat leveling one at a time plus perk points for skills mixed in. Not super exciting, but serviceable. I'd like to see more passives mixed in to break up the parts that are purely sequential stat boosts though.Gear and loot feel pretty good, even early in I like having a lot of different choices of elemental types. I wish armor was in pieces rather than a single suit though. I haven't found more armor yet, but it looks like more like you just swap outfits rather than actually select individual pieces. Hopefully there are a lot of armors to make up for that.Graphically the game is acceptable; it can look a little dated but I actually kind of like the "older" look of it as someone that still plays a lot of Titan Quest and older games. I haven't run into any bugs or glitches so far either, which is a plus. Level design seems good so far as well, could use some more loopbacks since there's a lot of "just keep going until this level branch dead ends" but again that might be something that opens up more later.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Early Access, but already a very good game. If you like Titan Quest and always wished a more active combat system with melee weapons: here's your game! There is also the option of throwing your shield for a ranged attack.I am just missing an option to throw a spear and hope something like that will be added to the game later! Would be especially interesting since it's actual fighting technique for ancient times to first throw a spear and follow with your melee weapon. I definitely prefer that also in effectiveness than just throwing a magic shield, losing your only protection (even if you get it back easily) ;-)Conclusion: I already hope that, like in TQ, many more DLCs will follow, extending the current ancient world!

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe this game only has that many reviews. Dark Point Games is a developer (and publisher) that clearly is here to make a statement, this game lacks of very little, though beware, it is not for the faint of heart.It is best described as a fusion between Titan Quest and Dark Souls. Uh?!? You read me right. The view is isometric, à la Titan Quest, there's loot, not as complex as in an ARPG, but enough to expend your gameplay in a way that best suits your preferences and the mechanics are very much like a Souls-type game. I never thought this could work so well in isometric but this title is proving it certainly can. The environments are vibrant, well distinguished, you have mini-dungeons as you'd expect in games such as Diablo, enemies should not be approached all in the same fashion and certain combinations of enemies will give you a harder time, but with patience, timing and strategy, everything can be overcome. However, death is very much part of the experience, again, like other titles of it's genre.Right from the beginning, the game does a great job pulling you into it's story. While it is nothing you wouldn't have seen before, the narrative is well delivered and at good pace. Dark Point Games did pull the stops to not let the plot feel like an half-ass'ed effort, for a game where one could be forgiven to have done so, however they carefully crafted the storytelling. The sound design is very clever, you feel the environment you find yourself in. SFX are as immersive, as they helpful, guiding you through assaults, assisting your timings, etc. Best played with a headset by the way. Quite frankly, I sound biased but really, this game exceeded my expectations and already it had caught my attention a while back. And last but not least, this game is so reasonable in it's asking price. It really is dirt cheap for the quality it offers and the quality of gameplay, the variety in skills, weapons, build, etc.The one part that I can't comment on unfortunately is the Co-op but from having loaded a game, it would seem that they are unique layouts meant to be played with someone, however you can still carry over your progress to your main game, that is the impression it gave me.And so, this would be my one disappointment, which is a bit obnoxious as I haven't played the part, but nothing leads me to believe the main campaign can be experienced as a multiplayer game but it'd be SOOOO COOL. Imagine playing any Souls with a friend, how would you approach certain bosses, how would you deal with encounters, how differently would you both build your characters to make the most out of your playthrough?I hope the developers consider making the campaign fully playable in co-op, especially as this game is very difficult, though that's not a negative for me, quite the opposite in fact.Don't sleep on this title, give it the 2 hours and refund if you think it's not for you but honestly, it's much more than I expected it to be. And last but not least, I will address the length of some of the reviews I've read, apparently, the developer is working on adding more, YAY! However, I couldn't stress this enough, this game is undoubtly a "quality over quantity" kind of thing, let that sink in.Brava, Dark Point Games, brava.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: great idea, decent game, quite a bit of jank.Changing the idea of hack'n'slash from mindlessly slaughtering millions of monsters to carefully planning every approach works really well in this genre. It has a lot of Dark Souls elements: stamina system and relatively low health, souls we gather from enemies or bottles that are used to upgrade our character, shrines in which we rest or respawn after death, and enemies that respawn if we do. And it fits really well. Graphics are good, for a genre, and we have dynamic camera that can both give us great shots of ongoing battle and sometimes be a bit of a nuisance. Music is decent. Writing and voice-acting is nothing special, personally i find it pretty low on the list in those games anyway. And I do like the game set in greek mythos.Now, as it is still in early access it definitely has some problems. Some will require just minor tweaks, other might be problematic.One thing that was bothering me is the lack of map. While the game takes many inspirations from the DS series, in DS we could freely look around, to not get lost or notice places we want to explore. Achilles doesn't have that. In this way it's more like metroidvania games, like Hollow Knight for example. And without any kind of map (even simple, static, without showing where our character currently is) it's easy to get lost or just miss some things.The other thing was aiming with mouse. For some reason the character aims at a different angle, than it's supposed to, while it should look at the pointer. With fast attacks it isn't very bothersome, but for heavy attacks and shield blocks it's a nightmare.And sometimes there are frame drops for no apparent reason, which in this type of game is quite an issue.Minor issues I've found so far: - during the first boss fight on the bridge, boss spawned underneath it. Could do anything, had to teleport out and try again (which was successful then) - sometimes the sound of unsheathing weapons still plays even though the enemies are dead - big scorpions walking sound is waaay too loud - not exactly a bug, but menu managing for every single bottle of souls is a bit annoying - in some places text doesn't match the voice, and is displayed in weird paceDespite those issues, the game was fun so far, there is a lot of potential in this, and after some fixes it will be definitely worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is Dark souls with Titan quest. I must say its addicting and it really gets hard at times. When you learn the movement its really smooth and you can fight 7-8 enemies at the same time. This game is in early access so there are quite a few bugs and you can get stuck at places but just exit the game and log in again and you are back to normal. I hope they add more to the questline in the game , it has a lot of potential. It took me 11 hours to reach the last quest playing solo so far but it says its not available so I think its only the beginning. The world is huge to run around and you have a feeling of open world when the different parts connect.There is smithing and materials and interesting skills so you can occupy yourself for some more time if you want and not do the quests, i just played the story back to back.I really enjoyed this though and looking forward to moreEdit: I just read its only the first chapter in early access of five in the full product so thats really awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: Achilles: Legends Untold is an isometric action RPG game, greatly inspired by the souls-like genre and old-school hack&slash games. The players will venture through many unwelcoming locations, battling legendary creatures and trying to piece up the story of the world. The game is a bit lighter on the "souls" side, as the studio wanted to create an easy-to-learn but hard to master experience. Because of that, Achilles: Legends Untold may be enjoyed by the souls veterans and new players alike. And if help is needed, just summon your friends to play together in jolly cooperation, and explore various dungeons together.

name: Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes
detailed_description: Return to the battlegrounds of Bersia in Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes, the sequel to the Xbox cult hit Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders, updated into HD for modern PCs. Command new units across seven new campaigns, each featuring a new playable character. Medieval mayhem returns! Orcs and ogres, vampires, and knights - command them all in this epic conflict of steel and strategy! Enhanced for modern PCs: - Game controllers support (a gamepad is recommended for optimal experience) plus an all-new mouse & keyboard mode. - Revisit classic battlefields in widescreen HD (including ultrawide support). - Rock on and ride out, accompanied by a high-powered metal soundtrack. Bigger, badder, better than ever: - A massive new game in the Kingdom Under Fire saga. - Seven new playable characters, each with their own story-driven campaign. - Lead from the front as a half-vampire count, an ogre warlord, or graceful dark elf. - Command new forces, including powerful elemental creatures. - Call in airstrikes and artillery and watch the battlefield burn. - Conquer fifty complex new missions, plus an endless range of random battles. Become a master of war and wield the battlefield as a weapon. - Defend the high ground and ride down into your opponent’s ranks. - Lay traps and ambushes in forests, or smoke your foes out with fire arrows. - Call in air units to pummel foes with cannon fire or their own plummeting hulls. - Pay heed to the elements. Wind and rain can change the course of a battle. - Cast powerful magic and call on artillery. Scatter your troops to avoid reprisal. Master seven new heroes, both light and dark: - Lead the charge as spectacularly powerful new characters. - Lash your enemies as a half-vampire, or crush them as a massive ogre. - Crush your foes with powerful new combos - Build your army with monstrous new troops and powerful support units - Assign allied commanders to your forces, each with their own abilities & magic - Lead, fight, hunt. Master the tactical map and remember: One hero can only go so far. Reforge your soldiers in the fires of war: - Explore the continent across two different eras of the explorable campaign map. - Build your perfect army. Lead regiments of humans, elves, orcs, and more. - Loot, level, and grow powerful. Evolve your troops into new forms and master their skills. - Re-write the rules of battle with powerful combat magic, supportive and destructive. - Command the elements with Fire Wraiths, Ice Maidens, Thunder Rhinos, and Earth Golems. The battlefield calls to you once more, commander. Your troops stand ready.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Save your money and frustration, find a way to play the Xbox version.I don't write Steam reviews, but something is wrong with this port. I bought this in a bundle with Crusaders, which was fine, but this game has so many strange problems that ruin the game. I had to write something to warn people.The pathfinding is the worst. You can try your hardest to get units to just go straight up, but instead they will take a hard right, run in a few circles, go up left, then die because they were getting slaughtered by archers the whole time. This goes for retreating from battles too. Your units will not go in the direction you're telling them to escape and seem to just pick at random where they'll go. You will not see this in the Xbox original.Archers also don't behave as they should. Normally archers when told to attack will attempt to back off and continue to shoot at enemy units as they close in. That just doesn't seem to happen in this port. It's actually kind of useful since the enemies have more archers than you and they will just stand there and let you attack them instead of trying to run and shoot. Sometimes they run, but it's still not the expected behavior from the Xbox version.Damage is just off, units will die way faster than they do in the Xbox version. I felt like Ellen's first mission was a bit harder, but I figured I was just not used to the differences between Crusaders and this, but no. Booting up the Xbox version you'll notice that troops inside of units die way faster, they seem to get damaged faster as well, and it's not the passive damage mechanic that everyone in the Steam community is talking about. Your bar will go from red to empty in an instant unlike the original Xbox version.There's also minor audio and visual glitches, like the mini-map not being properly transparent in the fog of war zones. The dark elf death sound is just off, it sounds like it's cutting out a half a second into the sound then repeating itself. In menus or the map screen the annoying PC control pop-up keeps showing up and making a noise every time it does. Even if you turn the visual pop-up off the noise persists with an annoying clunk every second or so while you're trying to listen to the dialogue. There's gotta be more, but I just can't think of them.I beat Ellen's campaign and stopped part way through Walter's. On the mission where you're supposed to escort Leinhart. The pathfinder just ♥♥♥♥ it's pants so hard I had to restart the mission multiple times and take like an hour of time to beat a simple mission. That's when I got the Xbox version to confirm to myself that it wasn't this bad. Turns out I was right. I'm playing through the Xbox version now and haven't seen any of these problems. This is just a butchered port. Do not buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the KUF games on the original xbox, you will love this. Because for all intents and purposes, it's pretty much the same game. While the store page calls this an HD version, this pretty much only applies to resolution and even then just barely. Hell, even fonts and UI elements have had absolutely nothing done to them for this release, and look grainy and muddy as all hell. There are absolutely no graphics options or enhancements whatsoever, the draw distance is just as low as it was on the original xbox (covered by the classical ever present thicc sandstorm / fog / snowstorm), the framerate is limited to 30fps, you get the idea. And to top it off, although they mention they have implemented a keyboard mode for this re release, it's keyboard controls are about on par with dark souls in terms of being absolutely so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrendous and unintuitive that you may as well not bother with keyboard and mouse. Its the classical stereotypical asian-dev PC port where you kind of wonder why the hell the devs even bothered, given the improved experience you get of this port is marginal at best compared to emulating the original xbox game. Keys are rebindable, but the game was built from the ground up with a controller in mindNow you may be wondering why after that amount of scorching i would still recommend this game, and it's because if you have a controller (i wouldn't know, i dont have one for my PC), the game is truly amazing and there is nothing quite like it before or after it's original release. One thing that i really have to give the game credit for is it's implementation of multiple campaign , each with it's own viewpoint, playstyle and story and timing in the overall story for each game. While each campaign is relatively short (probably 8 hours in crusaders) if you rush it, you will want play each one because if you don't, you won't see the overarching story to it's end. And for Crusaders there's 4 campaigns. For Heroes there's 7 if i recall correctly.

_childDocuments_.review: KUF: Heroes is a semi-RTS mixed with some hack n slash based in a dark fantasy world. It consists of 7 campaigns, each taking place around the events of the previous game (Crusaders), so I recommend playing that first if you haven't to get a better grip on each campaign's story.Presentation - Not too shabby, especially when there are hundreds of troops on the map at once. Models are nice, with a large variety of human, dark elf and orc troops. You can see some of units raise their weapons when approaching an enemy troop. The maps and environments themselves are... decent; sometimes a map would literally just be a flat desert, though you'll mostly be focusing on fighting anyway.Music - A metallic treat for the ears. IMO much better than Crusader's soundtrack since I happily gave myself a migraine from all the head-banging.Gameplay - Very solid and feels great to play on the PC using a controller (a huge plus since it'd crash a lot on the original XBOX). Again, highly suggest playing Crusaders first because Heroes lacks a real proper tutorial, so the learning curve is a tad steep. You engage in skirmishes in a board and control a hero troop, plus any additional troops you wish to bring along. The troops you control are groups of units instead of single units (think of Total War). You control your troops in a semi-RTS mode and go into a Dynasty Warriors-esque style mode when your hero troop is in battle with another troop, and your other troops always stay in RTS mode. The campaigns consist of two factions: humans and the dark legion (dark elves and orcs). Both factions have different unit jobs such as infantry, archers, giant eagles and giant scorpions. Each job has strengths and weaknesses you need to learn in order to crush your enemies (and not get crushed yourself). After each battle you can level up your hero and troops, buy gear and hire mercenaries for more troops.Story - Not too bad. Each campaign takes place before and/or during the events of Crusaders and serves to fill in some holes and enrich the story. Voice acting is shaky aside from Morene and Rupert, but personally I find the cheesy quality to be enjoyable. Overall, a great and fun mix of RTS and hack n slash. I give it 8 dark elf butts out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! This is what you are missing if you like other RTS games like starcraft, warcraft, total war; more of a third person look at commanding multiple troops in a chaotic style battle!I would like to say with all due respect, to ignore the reviews saying this game was never meant for a keyboard. I have played other RTS games on console (starcraft 64, war hammer xbox360, ogrebattle) and can confidently say they would all be better utilised on the pc. If your take is the controller than by all means, play to your desire.In any battle the first thing I do is press space. The map mode is your ultimate tool for movement, controller or keyboard. I do not suggest moving your troops in the third person mode ever. You will be confused and lose track of where your troops should be, as well your rider units will be best utilised when on a multiple rout. with that said, im not gonna tell anyone how to win their war, but I use my riders alot. If you use riders too, then the SHIFT key will be your best friend. I keep the natural WASD and right hand on mouse for the whole battle. I only find myself in My heroes combat mode maybe 15% of the whole skirmish. Your gonna want your heals consistent, your riders riding, and your support supporting. It's chaotic because its meant to be, if you find yourself overwhelmed, it's because you're supposed to. Position is everything, thats why your map mode with the space bar is so important. keep your archers behind, your infantry infront, and your riders ultimately controlling the skirmish, by being everywhere. Have fun and die well!

_childDocuments_.review: Best thing about this game is the replay value. After winning the game with a main character you get to start over with the Army you built. This ensures you continue to play, you army gets stronger, but the game is still a fair challenge. That said, you want to unlock all the main characters so you get the maximum amount of maps to replay on and build up your army. It's fun trying different strategies and using different specific squads to win a map. Ultimately, the "best" army consists of using the long haired vampire guy with the huge sword as your main unit. Ensure you have two wizards with different magic. I usually have Earth and Lighting, but Fire is always a safe bet. The support troops I will have one Cavalry squad. This ensures you rake in the SP and you can truly decimate enemies once you build them up with the right gear. Additional support consists of two squads of Cavalry archers. They aren't as good as the regular archers at first, but speed is very important in this game so just build them up. The games graphics are definitely dated, but the game play is so fun it likely won't bother you.

The most important part is they added Walter who is the center piece or reason behind all the mess that happens in KUF:TC Okay, maybe a little biased but the fact that you can keep playing a commander after being done with the campaign just for the funs and that you can reuse ALL the XP of a troop to accommodate them as you want make this gameplay VERY flexible. _childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Under Fire is one of my favorite series of all time. A great mix of RTS and hack and slash where you can slaughter orcs, dark elves, humans, etc. with badass characters but also command cavalry, archers, mortars, eagles, wyverns, swamp mammoths to have a great mix of action but also having to use your brain. The game has some jank for sure being an older game but it tells a great multi-character story and is very replayable!EDIT: One small tip for this port: for whatever reason the ports for both Kingdom Under Fire games messed up the pathing for your units a bit more than the original Xbox games did. It certainly had some jank, but not as bad as in the ports. The best way to re-correct when the pathing gets bad is to lower the distance of your movements considerably almost as if you are working to turn them first and then when the unit is finally facing the right direction go forward a little bit a few times and then you should be all set for long distance movements again.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend if you like hack n slash, and RTS! Heck, just try it out if you never played a game like this!This game is the only game I ever wanted to see on Steam so bad. I remember when I first got on Steam I would try to look up this title to see if it was ported over yet. I did this on and off for awhile and gave up on it. At least I still had the games on the classic Xbox. I fan-girled so hard when I saw Crusaders finally on here and that would mean this expansion would be next in a matter of time.My life is complete now I have Heroes on here. Thank you to the developers for this!I haven't put enough time on this port yet, but I sank so many hours into this game on the Classic Xbox to be able to confidently say, Highly Recommend. *Review is subject to change*I'll start with the Cons;-It is a Classic Xbox game. This game came out 2004 so the graphics are dated for those that care, but this port does a great job enhancing the graphics.-It is brand new on Steam and there will more than likely be bugs, I remember coming across some bugs in the Xbox version.-Custom Games is like a skirmish mode that needs more content added to it. It isn't as awesome as the campaign. (Add the ability to play the game's awesome soundtrack during skirmish).-Character gets reset every time you play a round in Custom Games (But you get your XP back so you just have to reallocate the points to troops again, which is annoying, I am sure there will be a fix).-If you aren't patient at times, and think strategically, there are some big difficulty spikes in some campaigns, but just because the first mission may be brutal doesn't mean the rest of the campaign for that character is brutal, etc. (I'm looking at you Urukabaar, his first level was brutal. The rest of his campaign wasn't as bad though, but still a challenge).Pros-Awesome game play with the mixture of RTS and Hack n Slash with troop and equipment upgrades and all that.-Fan of Crusaders? More levels and more to the story.-Heroes has way more replay value since you have Custom Games to play on, and can replay the campaign missions once you beat that character.-Beat all the missions? You can play each mission with any character.-An awesome heavy metal original soundtrack. You may think it doesn't belong in some fantasy medieval game, but trust me, it fits so well, and it'll make you want to charge headfirst into battle!-Being on the PC now, it obviously has updated graphics and a better framerate.Now a note to the developers,Please allow mods so the smart people can mod the game. Mods in this game would increase the longevity of it and make it have an infinite amount of replay value! I want to see what kind of content the community can make!And last but not least, since we got the two best games in the series, you might as well bring War of Heroes and Circle of Doom on here so us KuF fans can have the entire collection in our digital library! And also release the soundtrack for this game like you did with Crusaders please!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game that made my childhood.I always wanted to fight in the middle of a great war, inspired by the scenes made famous by the Lord of the Rings trilogy.  If you have a love for strategy, armies of swords, and an album of metal rock to accompany you into every heated battle, this game is for you.Some may compare it to Dynasty Warriors and I say that similarities only go up to the genre of hack-and-slash.  Unlike Dynasty Warriors which involves an overpowered singular hero (the player) mowing down an entire army of cannon fodder soldiers, Kingdom Under Fire places great emphasis on the player's ability to not only control their hero, but the squads of units that follow them.  Soldiers are not cannon fodder - losing them and upgrading them can mean life and death in a battle.  If not careful, players can fall prey from simply charging into the fray without considering the layout of the incoming enemy force.  Cavalry is ideal for charging down foot soldiers, but die in seconds when inpaled by enemy spearmen.  Archers must be positioned to avoid melee and so that their arrow don't get hindered by trees.  Believing that your hero can alone take on the entire world is hubris here.  Strategy and game awareness go hand in hand here.  Simple soldiers can do damage to you, underlining the notion that you are more of a leader than an overpowered hero with ridiculous amounts of mana.  You are closer to Aragon leading an army of men rather than Lu Bu simply mashing the attack button to effortlessly make the world bend to your will.When it comes to story, Kingdom under Fire follows the tales of 7 individuals, each with their own role in the war raging across their continent.  Fans of the previous game (Kingdom Under Fire: Crusaders) will recognize many of the faces they walk next to here.  Newcomers don't have to play the previous game to get the full experience of Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes, while doing so gives you greater insight on the story.  Each character boasts a unique backstory, an individual set of moves and playstyles, and a faction from the religious Ecclesia to the vampire-ruled Vellond.  The world is at war, you play characters from different sides which give more perspective to the war in its entirety, and finishing each hero's campaign unlocks a form of New Game Plus.  Story stages throughout the map are unlocked, allowing the player to replay these levels with the heroes they've completed with.  If you love crafting your ideal army, making them stronger with better upgrades and skills and unleashing them in a map of battles you once conquered, all the more reason to complete all seven.For all those who have a knack for hack-and-slash strategy that is different from turn-based gameplay and Dynasty Warrior overpoweredness, I strongly suggest giving this game a whirl.  Enter a world of men, elves, dark elves, dwarves, orcs, and vampires who all fight for supremacy over the land.  Fight across snowy mountains, scorching deserts, and wide empty plains where the environment can be used for or against you.  Command a colorful cast of heroes whose stories you'll wield against a colossal tide of intrigue and impossible battles.  In a kingdom under fire, men go into war.  Heroes lead the way.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Crusaders is so much better than this game. Just play that. There's nothing of value here.Main issues are the game becomes repetitive much faster than Crusaders, because to get through all the campaigns you'll have to keep starting and restarting, and every campaign ends in like 3 hours, each, (If you're wondering about my play time, I just left the game on) so you never adapt or switch up classes or feel attached to your army through a long hard campaign like you do in Crusaders. Also all the stories (So far) are ether genuinely awful, boring or just fine because they limited themselves to being a prequel (Mostly). Every addition to this game has a draw back:There's now a skirmish mode! - you have to set up both players armies for a specific general, and the game does not save them if you turn the game off.There's new units! - 4 elemental monsters that can be picked by both factions (So there goes the asymmetry), that are so expensive to level up, die so fast when you use them and are so hyperspecific at what they are good at, that you ARE NOT using them, ever.There's skirmish maps in the campaign to grind - Did people want this? You couldn't grind at all in Crusaders because it was 4 well designed linear campaigns. It used an entire campaign to tutorial you how to beat the hard campaigns. (Even if you're scared of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up your build, just have a general on a longbow unit that can cast heal). Plus the skirmish maps themselves are just large, flat, empty maps with enemy units scattered around with their AI turned off... and they're in everyone's campaign.Speaking of which! Let's just rank the campaigns, so if you're determined to not get Crusaders instead for some reason, you'll at least know what to expect (No spoilers):1. Walter's - Amazing opening level that has you genocide a village screaming for you to stop, as you then hunt down the fleeing refugees (Someone mod this level into Kendal's campaign! as a reveal mid campaign). It is horrifying and well executed... rest of campaign's alright. This is 1 out of the 2 campaigns actually taking place during Crusades, so you know exactly what happens because Kendal's campaign in Crusaders is about hunting down Walter. So the impact's kinda lost, and they reuses an important cutscene that is meaningless to this game because what happens only effect the characters in Crusaders... 8/102. Ellen's - It's fine. It's the tutorial campaign. It at least attempts to have interesting gimmicks in its levels, gives some character to Ellen before she joins Gerald in Crusades, actually has a cinematic cutscene at the end. It was a good first impression 6/103. Cirith's - This was stupid. I haven't finished it (Burnt out from the game), but from what I have it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid! The main conflict is with your superior officer sabotaging your side of the war, while trying to get you killed. Interesting on paper, horribly executed. You're companions consist of a poet who uses paragraphs to wax poetic about how hot you are, and some gremlin girl who only cares about shiny things. They also turned Cirith from this carefree cynic, in Crusaders, into the most turns to camera "Can you believe this?" kinda character. It's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid! 3/104/5/6. Leinhart's / Morene's / Urukubarr's - I never played them and probably never will. I am interested in how Urukubarr's is the hardest campaign, but playing that requires me to play Morene's... which requires me to finish Cirith's... eeeeeeeeeeeehhh....7. Rupert's - I know I said no spoilers, but... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Who asked themselves, while playing Gerald's campaign, how Rupert got the alliance between the Dwarves and Elves, while you were defending the keep? was it the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that asked for the skirmish maps!? You know EXACTLY what's going to happen plot wise, so they tried to focus on the character of Rupert. Turning a meathead with a heart of gold, volunteering on a suicide mission to escort emissaries to forge an alliance to save his comrades, into Partick Star from Spongebob. He spend the entire campaign forgetting what he's doing, has zero urgency, constantly getting lost, crying about how stupid and useless he feels, and repeatedly getting drunk off of dwarven ale (Because it was mentioned off hand in ONE LINE he said during Crusaders, to humble the people congratulating him for saving their lives). I ♥♥♥♥ you not, the emissary who's your companion, leaves the party to forge the alliance without you. But you save his life at one point so he tell Rupert "No, see, you were useful all along. I guess we both have our strengths and weaknesses. Ha ha ha!". This is the most "derivative filler" campaign out of all of them and one of the worst pieces of content I have ever had to endure. I deleted this game initially because of this awful campaign.Like, Crusaders has problems, but they are not this bad. This feels like corporate meddling, and considering in Crusaders they censored the word "Pope" last minute, I wouldn't be surprised.

_childDocuments_.review: Played these as a kid on xbox and beat them..Start with female knight campaign. It teaches you the game and has super fun levels early on and is the most forgiving. The game has a few bugs that may discourage people from really giving it a shot, but if you work through them, the game is such an amazing experience. Controller is probably the best way to play it, but I am using mouse and keyboard now since im not on xbox anymore. It works fine. Game really takes some patience. You cant just hop in and start slaying, you need to take a good 10mins and learn all the controls. Im only 4hrs in, and it all feels natural at this point. So you can and will adapt to mouse and keyboard. Learning and adapting to the controls is the hardest part, but takes the least amount of time.The game allows you to customize your soldiers, characters, officers and more with different stats abilities, roles, skill trees etc. It has a medium difficulty that eventually ramps up to quite a hard game..and I love that...Call it the dark souls of large scale hack and slash/rts combat. This is a Niche game, but for those that enjoy this stuff, i cant believe how well its held up from 2005. The scale is still very large, the game play still very fun. You wont steam roll this game in a few hours like a call of duty campaign, expect it to be long, trial and error combat on missions and clock in at over 100hrs before you see it all. The hack and slash part is basic like dynasty warriors, except all the AI are actually moving around and fighting each other at a quick pace so it feels more dynamic. The Rts part isnt anything overwhelming either, yet some how it remains challenging and in depth enough to be very entertaining. Each campaign has an actual story with voice acting, and theres a lot of it. Bugs...this thing was not remastered very well aside from the graphics. It has small annoyances for instance, when you go to save your game, you have the game tell you all 50 save slots are corrupted and have to delete one and then save your game. F10 is the start button and menu button yet on most PCs f10 does something else so you have to juggle it some. You use alt to look around but it also freezes/pauses the game when you let go of it after looking around, and a few other things that can be annoying. Youll have to keybind some stuff to your mouse to work around some kinks. If the game wasnt so long and so good, I would tell ya not to bother with it, but it really is worth putting in the time to get it smoothed out and then play.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with an interesting world. The interaction between a real-time strategy and Dynasty Warriors-esque combat was an cool idea for the time although the more you play of this game, the more you'll realise how much better it could've, and should've been done.The game will take it relatively easy on you up until you get halfway through Ellen's storyline (who's storyline basically acts as the tutorial and warm-up to the mechanics of the game.) After that though, you BETTER know the in's-and-out's for optimising your troops and your characters or you'll quickly find this game to be a nightmare to trudge through. There's no New Game+ either so unfortunately if you intend to try and explore the game after finishing the story, ya gotta do it from square one again.The soundtrack is absolutely awesome. It's metal and chaotic and it complements the craziness of the large-scale warfare of this game perfectly.The voice-acting is kind of a mixed bag. There are a lot of big names like Robin Atkin Downes in there and there's also a lot of unheard-of voice-actors who are giving it their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ A-game on some of the minor characters and if that ain't admirable work, I dunno what is.It's worth mentioning, this game originally came out for Xbox Original and PS2 and was only just recently ported to PC this year so as you can imagine, it's kinda buggy. A.I. is often dumb as bricks, sometimes your character will dance around doing what you want, etc. Thankfully the devs are actively patching this game the best they can, which is honestly more support than I was expecting. Any other dev team contracted with porting this game might've just shoved it out the door and forgot about it, just focusing on their payday. I mean, it's an old game from a bygone era that even back then not a lot of people likely heard of, who's gonna care if it's buggy, right? Well thankfully that isn't the case, the devs seem to actually care about this game and it certainly shows.

_childDocuments_.review: The beginning of the end for the KuF series.Many people are claiming that Heroes and The Crusaders have survived the test of time and look beautiful in 2020. I can tell you that if you try to determine what's going on in the battlefield without using your mini-map 80% of your strategic gameplay time, you won't be able to even tell what is going on 30 meters past you because of the dumb vision fog that's intended to have the original Xbox have the game run on at least 30 fps. You must squint real hard to try and see the outline of a swamp mammoth on the middle of the map.  You literally can't see anything but shadows. They supposedly remastered and improved the graphics, but I've yet to see any difference between the original and this port.Also, this port is one of the worst you will ever have the disgrace of touching, this being the main reason why I make this review. This should be enough info to steer you away, however if you'd like to hear why I hate this game so much, then read on.I do not trust myself to give you an unbiased opinion on TC, but I can for Heroes. Here's my quick story explaining why:I never touched Heroes back when it was on Xbox. I only ever knew The Crusaders existed, and for my 10 y/o self, that game was more than enough to have hundreds upon hundreds of hours invested into it. When I learned Heroes was a thing was because a friend lent me Circle of Doom which was, in turn, their first game into the KuF series and I decided to Google the series. He didn't like TC, I didn't like CoD, none of us knew Heroes was a thing.Years later, I found a Heroes original copy on a BlockBuster at less than $3 bucks. It was used. I tried to play it on my X360 only to find out The Crusaders was backwards compatible, but Heroes wasn't. I still have it on a shelf, massively disappointed with Bluebox, Microsoft and Phantagram for that fiasco.2 weeks ago, I saw this released on Steam. I was beyond ecstatic, so I bought it on release. After finishing The Crusaders completely, I went immediately to boot this up. From the moment the main menu theme started playing, I knew something was wrong. It wasn't even similar to TC. I brushed it off as nostalgia bias, so I played a custom game. Accidentally chose Morene. She sounds like a teenager now, instead of a cold-hearted vampiress. I ignored it, so I went to boot up my first campaign as Ellen. 5 minutes in, I almost Alt+F4. The voice-acting is terrible and the OST is straight out of place for a game like this. I was amazed at how they went from good-great voice-acting in TC to literal anime English-dub quality in Heroes.I'm 2 missions in on Ellen's campaign now and I can't continue. It's legit torture. I had to watch gameplay videos at this point. Here's a breakdown of all the things that completely ruin this game:- The English voice-acting was done by a band of teenagers who tried really, really hard to sound like grown adults.- The music was composed by a starved high-school band and a rejected composer who were paid with 5 loafs of bread and were ordered to try and do their best. They couldn't decide on whether they wanted to make it orchestral or heavy metal, so they made it both.- Ellen's campaign and Ellen both as a playable Hero and as a character. She might be the weakest, edgiest, most pathetic trash can in this game. She takes years just to kill a single orc that's 2 levels above her troop.- The writing was very likely made by a fan who was tasked with making interesting backstories for the secondary characters in TC and ended up creating a fandom that includes all of their favorite anime clichés and excellent choices in dialogue, like saying "Uh", "Ah", "Agh" and the rest of their favorite interjections ad nauseum. They also changed the personalities of many characters just so they would fit in their fandom.- ^ They were also in charge of the translation for the subtitles for Heroes and The Crusaders. They weren't that great in that regard.- Actually, most of the new heroes suck. They are largely useless on the battlefield and are boring to play.- The camera is awful. If you have it high to see your surroundings, you get a isometric view of your character and can't see what's in front of you nor what you're hitting. If you lower it, your character blocks half your screen and you can only see the current enemies that you're hitting. How they managed to break something that worked in it's predecessor is beyond me.- I wanted to try out multiplayer because it was apparently the best feature in the game. It's been removed. Both from TC and Heroes. No one knows if it's ever going to be implemented.- Game is capped at 30 fps because the engine would otherwise break.- The developer for both ports has stated multiple times on the forums that they were not given enough time to implement many features from the original games. Therefore, they were cut from the PC port entirely. If you see the state of the game, this comes as no surprise. Example: The mini-games that unlocked after you beat Regnier and Kendal campaigns respectively in The Crusaders are gone.10/Rupert's manlet voice in Heroes. I want to cry.

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes is the standalone expansion pack that adds 7 more campaigns to Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders that take place before, during and after the base game filling in the plot holes with even more heavy metal Medieval High Fantasy violence that we know and love. Ellen of Ecclesia's story explains how she joined Hironeiden and Gerald's unit, Rupert of Hironeiden's story explains how he formed an alliance with the Dwarves & Elves for the much needed reinforcements, Walter of Ecclesia's story talks about his visions leading to the war, how the Ecclesians got into trouble with leadership as well as internal conflict leading to their late assistance of their allies then their eventual end at Nowart starting the Age of Darkness event, Cirith of Vellond's story explains how after Lucretia's campaign she meets her sister to join her unit to retrieve the Ancient Heart from the Patriarch but they end up in life threatening mishaps, Leinhart of Vellond's story talks about how he annexed Hexter but was forced to deal with rebel Kaedes Dark Elves with his newfound allies before joining Regnir's unit in the end after losing his castle, Morene of Vellond's story talks about how she attempted to retrieve the Ancient Heart but failed leading to King Waldemar's compromise and who is leading Kaedes rebels revealed & Urukubarr of Hexter's story details about how he united the Ork tribes to become the strongest WAAGGHH! We don't just get new campaigns but we also get powerful new Elemental units for each element (Ice Maidens, Fire Wraiths, Earth Golems & Thunder Rhinos) and a reworked XP skill allotment system that you can reset an officer's unit XP to reuse it to switch to another unit path or use that experience on another unit although it also limits how you can skill up due to having a flat upgrade price rather then a per level basis at least you can respec whenever you want. We also get custom game mode with a great degree of customization to make fights the way you want with a good amount of maps to combat at like Total War except with Kingdom Under Fire RPG-RTS-Musou system to make fights as varied as possible from what skills to what unit type paths to what hero leads them in greater numbers. Sadly no multiplayer yet like the original Xbox version and ideally you still use an Xbox controller cause if you want challenge wait till you reach Urukubarr's campaign cause you'll need those quick reflexes there as the stories get progressively harder to test your strategic & tactical limits. A worthy expansion pack that's more of the same which is fine cause its a ton of brutal bloody fun with some new units and some changes here and there. If you love the base game like me and want more simply get this expansion pack you wont be disappointed! Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend playing this after you've played KUF Crusaders. If you like that game, you'll find lots more to like in this classic Xbox gem as well. One warning to those who haven't played this game before: In the two starter campaigns (Ellen is the obvious first one, Walter is also considered "easy"), there are missions that are MAJOR difficulty spikes. You'll probably know when you find them, Walter's comes very early in his campaign, Ellen's later, but they can be extremely frustrating. I'd recommend looking up strats online, because you don't want those 2 bad missions to put a halt on the otherwise excellent experience of this game. It's challenging, unique (both this and KUF Crusaders have a formula I've never seen replicated), and fun, and has excellent cult appeal with it's iffy voice acting and heavy-metal fantasy vibes. I'd even suggest skipping Walter (once you've played Ellen you can jump to a few others) so you don't get bogged down and miss out on the otherwise terrific experience of this game. One problem with the port though: pathing can get seriously fudged up. If you notice you unit struggling, give them short direct move commands rather than long and queued ones. Hasn't been game breaking in any instances, and honestly helped me cheese the gonzo hard Walter mission when the AI unit you have to protect got stuck running in circles for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: EDITED REVIEW: This is one of my childhood favourites and I couldn't wait to play it. I initially gave the game a thumbs down because the developers basically used players as their QA team. There were many errors at the launch of the port from not being able to actually get to the title screen to some pretty bad pathfinding issues. I said I'd change my review if they fixed them and they have - in quite a timely manner too.Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes is a good game, it's fun to play and mixes it up with lots of playable characters. I think the script was originally translated from Korean so it can be a bit janky in the English translation but the dialogue isn't the worst.The gameplay is where its at. You command your own group of troops as well as plan the strategy for all your units. It's great tactical gameplay that allows you to get involved with the action rather than just viewing it from a top-down perspective. It's a shame there aren't more games like this. It's a shame the developers took the franchise elsewhere with Circle of Doom (A hack and slash with no strategy) and Kingdom Under Fire 2 (An MMO with some limited strategy elements).

Heroes also allows you to replay missions once you beat a respective story so you can go and replay your favorite missions. The game does have some qustionable voice acting (which is the charming part imo) and some bugs but other than that it runs smoothly on pc at 1920x1080 resolution. I highly recommend you give this game a shot. If the game is not your style than at least give the soundtrack a listen on Kingdom Under Fire The Crusaders store page, great soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Under Fire: Heroes is an action strategy game where you can command hundreds of soldiers. You also have spells, golems, and catapults at your disposal as you play through more than 50 campaign missions. The experience and gold that you earn during each battle can be used to train and equip your troops. You can also challenge other gamers online.

name: Source of Madness
detailed_description: Source of Madness is a side-scrolling dark action roguelite set in the Loam Lands, a twisted Lovecraftian inspired world powered by procedural generation and AI machine learning. Take on the role of a new Acolyte as they embark on a nightmarish odyssey. Uncover the cosmic secrets of the Loam Lands and The Tower of Madness, the moon’s mysterious Citadel. The horrific monsters you face are never the same, concocted with procedural generation and animated using a neural network AI Explosive close-combat magic, labyrinthine environmental exploration, powerful loot management and a skill tree filled with abilities, classes, and spells Rendered in a beautiful AI assisted art style, the fascinating world of the Loam Lands reveals a deep arcane lore as players uncover its many secrets

_childDocuments_.review: Has art style and physics are very reminiscent of games like Hammerfight or Swapper. Definitely has that indie "jank" feel, many would consider charming. Just about everything is physics based, so cloaks are flowing all over the place, and it almost seems as if your torso is getting led by your lower body. Not necessarily a bad thing, but it might be for some people. Environments look nice, if a little bit too dark, and the monster design is more creative than the usual for Lovecraftian games. The 2d overlay onto a background does create some muddling issues however, as it can be challenging to understand exactly what you're looking at. That may be intentional, since it certainly would make sense when dealing with eldritch abominations, but often I just found myself unsure if I was looking at a corpse, an enemy, or part of the background. A slight outline to separate foreground from background, and maybe a bit of cleanup on the actual units themselves (to see appendages vs the core vs whatever, just see what's connected where) would go a long way toward improving the clarity of the game.I have noticed a few graphics bugs here and there. After resizing from 1440 fullscreen to 1080 windowed, text in the controls menu is cropped on either side. Going to the graphics menu again shows the full screen resolution, despite that clearly not being the case. Minor bugs that will likely be fixed early in the EA, but I would rather provide a thorough review I'm only a little bit into the game, but the story is fine. Nothing amazing, but not really problematic. Nice to deal with Yog-Sothoth, since he doesn't come into play too often, and the narration is well done. I was a little put off in the very beginning however, when you're first walking past a handful of survivors. All of them comment on how they are insane, and how it must suck to not be insane, but this just feels lazy to me. These cosmic horrors break minds, show them what they cannot comprehend. Having someone who's very psyche has been shattered walk over and say "boy golly I sure am insane" rubs me the wrong way. As overdone as it is, I'd much prefer to see some becoming cultists/prophets, rambling about what turns out to be a future miniboss, or crying absolute incoherencies, begging for salvation that they know cannot come.I brought up above that the physics had that jank indie feel to them, and that it was a matter of taste. The controls have that similar style, but there are a few points that are much more black and white.  You aim with your mouse, and can cast spells with left and right click. Despite aiming with the mouse, however, you cannot normally cast behind you. While sometimes I have been able to hold right and shoot to the left, propelling myself forward a little quicker (spells have knockback on you), I'll also be fighting an enemy, back up, and suddenly be shooting in the direction I'm moving instead of where my cursor is. UPDATE: I have learned that this is the result of releasing your spell button before the spell actually casts. The spell only targets the cursor when the button is being pressed. Otherwise, it just faces directly forward. I still haven't figured out how to control the item direction though.Holding a cast will use an "Ultimate", with a cost associated with it. This is fine, but I can't really tell what that cost means. In fact, using the ultimate will often require you to just be spam casting the primary ability for a while first, then suddenly it will charge and come out with the big hit, as if it were the final part of a combo. This is likely a result of my misunderstanding the spells, but the complete lack of any real tutorial beyond "hit left click to cast" indicates that this may be a recurring issue.As of writing this, I have just finished the first actual boss, . The big stand out problem is that this is another roguelike that has plenty of stats to juggle, but doesn't bother explaining any of them. Clarity is a MAJOR issue. I might pick up a ring that applies Chill to targets on crit. What does Chill do? No idea. I would find a helmet that gives "Affinity to Nature". I have no idea what that means. There is a poison debuff in the game, but outside of the green pools, good luck finding out what applied it. You have a tiny debuff icon on the bottom of your screen, but it seems to cycle through 6-7 times before it goes away, and mousing over it shows nothing. As stated above, I still have no idea how to determine when an ultimate will cast, or what those little pips mean. As far as I can tell, there's no real way to find out what something will do without buying it, and even then you're often left in the dark.Hopefully, this will all be fixed early on. It's pretty easy to do, just involving updating tooltips. A bit more concerning is the actual combat. Mostly, it involves finding the rings you want to use and holding both mouse buttons while pointing at the opponent while kiting away. At first, I thought that melee might be broken. Enemies don't do damage on collision, but instead projectiles and periodic "swipes" with a glowing appendage. Knowing this, it should be easy to just dodge when you see the swipe, right? Unfortunately, the vast majority of my damage taken is the result of the crazy physics catapulting an enemy onto me, and just getting stuck. The blink/dodge won't get you out of the mess, often doing nothing at all, and moving is futile. Unless something is done about this, I think most sessions are going to end in frustration.In addition to the bug fixes and clarity overhaul brought up above, improving enemy confrontations would be great. Enemies seem to be procedurally generated, but at the moment that just results in incoherent blobs rolling over to you. Sometimes they have "phases" that occur when their health drops to a certain point, losing a number of appendages before continuing their chase. Instead, encourage the player to slice through these tendrils and arms. As far as I can tell, this functionality currently isn't in game (although it's nearly impossible to actually target a body part given how floppy and erratic enemy movements are), but even if it is, it certainly isn't clear to the player. Double down on the "shambling horror" aesthetic A foreground character was a coffin with long spindly legs. I was actually pleasantly surprised seeing it slowly patrol the area, only to realize it wasn't anything I could interact with, and I haven't seen anything of the sort since. Throw giant spidery monsters at me with 7 joints per leg, jerkily approaching at quick speeds. Let the player slice through their legs, causing them to tumble down as they continue their approach. If the creatures are procedurally created as I believe, the devs clearly have a method of locomotion that is indeterminate of the creature's shapes. Hopefully this isn't just "apply a force vector in the direction of the player", because that would allow you to transition from "walking" to "crawling" or "rolling".  This game is absolutely rough around the edges, but it's also an enjoyable experience under that. I'll tentatively recommend it to anyone who's really into roguelikes, while the rest should probably wait until a polish pass goes through.: I just finished what's currently in the game, and balance needs a bit of work. The ACT 1 boss was absolutely 0 threat, but took 5-10 minutes to kill. If you're having any trouble, just run double blood rings and heal your way through the entire game. At the moment, I have no desire to go back and play some more, since there's not really too much to experiment with. Very few effects interact with one another, just boiling down to "do X% more damage on Y spells". Will see later.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovecraftian rogue like game where you play as a cultist fighting against the monsters of other old gods.Pros-* You can unlock a variety of mage classes, the first one very quickly.* The art in the game is really well done and unsettling. * The real star of the game is the physics. The randomly generated monsters, with ragdoll physics can be a lot of fun and hilarious. I've had mini-bosses fling themselves into the air with such force that they just never come back down. It's also a lot of fun to bounce across the screen, using the pushback from explosives and shotgun blasts for additional jumps, keeping out of reach as some poor abomination flails impotently in your general direction.* The variety of weapons and equipment seems pretty good. I wish I had more control of what I get. You don't really do "builds" thus far, you mostly just hope you can find a couple of good weapons. The monsters get higher level with each new zone, so you'll need to replace each weapon every few zones, and you really hope they you don't get stuck having the replace two good weapons with two less desirable ones, with better levels. But two weapons that you actually want is a lot of fun.Cons* The levels are procedurally generated, so you quickly just start seeing random clumps of level tossed together to be jumped past. Apart from looking for hidden doorways, you quickly give very little regard to the world itself, since you already know there is no deeper meaning, besides random geometry.* The monsters are procedurally generated, usually ending as some kind of tentacle monster with any number of random abilities and traits. Since healing is very limited, you generally stay far away from each one, since you don't know if it'll suddenly blast you with poison, or explode on death, or deal contact damage, or who knows what else. So you just see them as random lumps to be blasted apart and avoided. They typically arent that hard and most of the time I get hit is when they do something unpredictable, like fling themselves at you from off screen at 95 miles an hour. Again, since you know that are randomly generated, you don't see any meaning or artistic value in them.* Small community. It just isn't that big of game, fanbase wise, so there isn't a lot of information out there. No real tutorials, faqs, guides, or explanations of game mechanics.* The physics get wonky. You get a teleport/dash to help move and avoid enemies, except sometimes you'll get snagged on the enemy and get hit instead. So even rolling past enemies with well times dodges doesn't reliably work. If your going to get hit, you might as well as mash that blink ability, but it certainly isn't reliable like in other souls-like games.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into the game without knowing that it was made by AI, and to me, it was just a mediocre game. I feel like most of the positive reviews must be cutting it slack because of the AI stuff. It's cool that they were able to use ML to make this, I guess, but ultimately, that's just a gimmick. There's nothing here that's done better than what a human-made game can do. Actually, it's a lot worse than games that are fully made by humans.The enemies aren't fun to fight. The AI doesn't understand how to use the procedurally generated, misshapen bodies, so they stumble around and you can easily avoid them. They're extremely easy to cheese. And I'm not even sure how you're supposed to fight them in a non-cheesey way. The character models are so random and incomprehensible that you can't figure out what limb to dodge.The level layouts are confusing: Everything looks the same, the paths loop back around to where you already came from, and there's no way to view a map. So I got lost for 10 minutes at one point, trying to find a path I hadn't already taken. Not fun.A lot of the art frankly looks bad. There are lots of weird pixellations and artifacts. And the art doesn't have a cohesive feeling to it. It feels like an asset dump. You'll have some really cool assets sitting next to some garbage looking pixelated assets. The vibe is a jumbled mess.
