_childDocuments_.review: +I've never felt dread like this in a 2D game, you'll be surprised with disturbing things falling from the ceiling, crawling from the corners of the screen or trying to reach you from bellow.+creatures are randomly generated so it becomes unpredictable how a lot of enemies will move / attack, you gotta adapt to them on the fly.+gameplay and combat feels very unique for a 2D game, you play as a mage and you're fragile, so you gotta be careful with your approaches. expect situations where you'll need to cheese or kite enemies (which is fun in this game), but close combat is viable too if you upgrade and make good use of your dash skill, there are also some close combat spells at your disposal anyways.+THE HORROR, this game is full of grotesque things, screams, otherworldly atmosphere and a beautiful but haunting soundtrack.+good sense of progression for a roguelike (specially in early access), I did a few runs and each one of them gave me resources to unlock useful skills.+the game has a "floaty physics" feel to it. at first I thought this could be a problem, specially during combat but actually it feels very good and distinctive to play.+good spell diversity and builds to play around with.I don't know what else to say, performance is great too even with a lot of stuff going on at the screen. No negative aspects so far imo, if this is an early access title, I can't wait to see what the devs end up implementing in the future, maybe a different character or two aside from the spellcaster could add a lot to the longevity and diversity of gameplay, and even tho I really like the AI generated enemies (seriously, this feature is amazing and resonates greatly with Lovecraft themes), I think that a few standalone / non randomly generated enemies here and there wouldn't hurt, just to give some identity to some encounters, thinking about something like the Black Knights in Dark Souls for example. anyways I'm really glad to have contributed in a way or another for this EA, this is a great title already with a lot of potential too, cheers to the devs, fine work!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something special and I want to see it grow and succeed.A sanguine moon hangs low and from it spews forth unspeakable terrors. This is no mere accident, some entity has taken hold of the Towers of Madness and damned your world with this horrific tide. The peoples of the Land fled to the Tower of Knowledge for safety and the cult took them in, seeing opportunity to increase their numbers. You are one such individual, newly inducted into the cult and sent out into the world to combat the Moon-born monstrosities and seek access to the moon once again... You will die but the Cult continues to swell with recruits form the cowering masses and so there will always be another sent out.It's a Sidescrolling rogue-like where you'll venture through areas, fight monsters, acquire loot, and uncover secrets. When you die you'll gain a new character and be able to offer the blood of monsters slain to unlock permanent upgrades.The Combat is fun with you unleashing devastating magics that tear apart your foes. You and your enemies have physics based movement so there can be some clunkiness but it kind of works with the setting. A big thing I think should be included is having enemies be able to flip around and face you.The Movement is floaty but handles pretty well, The platforming hasn't been frustrating or confusing and there's so far no fall damage.The Art is amazing. The areas seem to be procedurally generated or atleast randomized and the creatures are AI generated, combining an variety of semi-recognizable parts into perfect lovecraftian monstrosities. The Tower of Knowledge is particularly eye-catching and is like some gothic cathedral warped through the 5th dimension.It's a very competent game that looks amazing and is doing something very unique. If you love Lovecraftian horror, like weird action rogue-likes, and/or want to see something strange and unique succeed then get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Source of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid roguelite! I really love the Lovecraftian elements and aesthetics, the game does an outstanding job capturing the creatures and the landscape that you would expect to find in a Lovecraft story. The enemies move in a way that's very hard to read, and sometimes it's hard to tell if they're dead, which given the fact that Lovecraft entities are usually said to be indescribable, or almost impossible for the human mind to comprehend, that fits really well and doesn't sacrifice gameplay. The movement is very floaty, and there's not a huge amount of precision which I think are both intention design choices, but I do think tightening the controls a bit wouldn't hurt. The other main thing bothering me is the UI. The design of the menus and your player inventory is a bit of an assault on the eyes, and it looks very cluttered. I get that it's supposed to look embossed and intricately detailed, but for the sake of user convenience, I'd like to see something a bit more simplistic, especially with the UI that's in the bottom left corner which shows your rings and spells, and other activatable. Most of the time I cannot tell just by looking at that UI what ring or accessory I have equipped. Needs to be less stylized, more clean and effective. All in all, very solid action platformer roguelite, lots of fun and the Lovecraftian elements are really exciting especially for me, because I read a ton of H.P. Lovecraft's works.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I find rather hard to judge, it's something like a bastard child of Noita and Barotrauma. I found that it really didn't play in the way that I was expecting at all. At the beginning I was expecting something a bit faster paced, but it's very much a slow burner, defensive play is the order of the day. I think that having a learning AI handle the AI routines was a stroke of genius, with a lack of pre-conceived notions as to how something should move, the enemies movements really do come across as otherworldly and alien. I do have a few minor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ such as the lack of a save, the slightly jank movement and the inability to quit out immediately after death. On the whole it has massive potential and I'm extremely impressed with what I see so far.

_childDocuments_.review: "Source of Madness" is a handheld (Nintendo Switch)/console game that's also been put on Steam as a bit of an afterthought, as it's very much designed for the handheld/console gaming audience.  It's yet another of literally thousands of 2D retro platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.  But somehow, this one is much worse.  See, the developers not only couldn't do any content design, and not only went to procgen to try fill in their skill/talent gap, but they also went to use GenAI.  That's right, this is in at least some small part: AI slop.  I see this kind of the thing as the tip of the iceberg as we look back on what Steam is today and think forward about the endless amounts of AI slop garbage that will soon flood the marketplace, giving genuine developers zero chance at getting any visibility for genuinely created work. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The game is comprised of somewhat mediocre hand drawn 2D illustrations instead of professional looking 3D game assets.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget to arrange someone who can create graphical assets properly, or lack of talent.  Regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is very low, beneath what PC gamers have come to expect in this era of cutting edge photorealistic 3D graphics.  At least it's not pixel "art", but if you're looking for contemporary, immersive visuals, this game is a fail.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.The game assets are fairly mediocre/low quality, in some places they appear mismatched... Ultimately the quality of these assets, and thus the overall visual quality is lower than average, and low quality always makes for a less than optimal gaming experience.  Remember, we're looking for the best of the best of 100,000+ games on Steam.The controls and game handling are notably very clunky and unsmooth here.  It's janky and unsatisfying to play... and any experienced gamer will tell you, the handling, responsiveness and general gameplay feel of the control scheme must be well polished for this kind of game to succeed.  Unfortunately, this is something the developer seems to have phoned in, with little to no apparent gameplay testing.  They dropped the ball on this one.The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?"Source of Madness" has the utterly unrealistic price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $15 asking price for this game could get you games like "Resident Evil Village", "Cuphead" or "Valheim".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.

_childDocuments_.review: After initially posting a negative review due to some very specific performance issues tied to my gpu (a gtx770), I've had a lot of back-and-forth with one of the developers, who has helped me try and troubleshoot. My issue isn't gone, but I've managed to alleviate the near-instant crashes to being once-in-a-while crashes, by lowering the graphics to their lowest possible setting and clearing the game's cache through Regedit.I've since been able to play the game more consistently again and progressed past the first boss.What I especially like about the game is the world, its bizarre monsters, and the abilities. I'm also quite a sucker for the ability to progressively unlock more abilities (though some aren't really worth the time-investment imo), and though I haven't gotten past the first boss due to the crashing issue, I imagine that more characters are unlockable down the road, which is definitely a draw for me as well.One thing that the game accels at quite well in its hub zone is the sense of scale. An npc makes the comment that it's easier to get lost in the tower of knowledge, and its quite true. The texture used in the world also has such an overwhelming amount of detail that you can't help but end up feeling like you're in world that's beyond what mortals can fully comprehend.Besides the performance, I only really have one major gripe about the game, and that's the enemy collision. Due to the randomness of the monsters, you'll sometimes encounter enemies that curl up and surround you, leading to a quick death, unless you're able to spam-teleport your way out of their collision box. Encounters like these don't really feel like they're fair, even in a world such as this eldritch madness, because your character simply isn't properly equipped to deal with being shoved into a corner by enemies so large that you cannot escape, even with three consecutive teleports. You also get dragged around a lot by their collision boxes, which can at times be quite frustrating.I have faith that the developers will continue to improve this game and add more cool additions over time, and I think that, if you like roguelite and eldritch horror / lovecraftian mythos, you'll enjoy this game a lot. I really enjoy the random elements of the game, as I've seen so many variations of the different stages that every run feels adequately different to keep me hooked. The only stage where this is kind of lacking though is the second stage.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a functional game and a solid foundation here, but much needs to be worked on before this is a quality product. Those who enjoy Lovecraftian media and games will find something to love, particularly if you enjoy rougelike and souls-like games.I think the most challenging part of a Lovecraft game is finding the tone. The intro set that tone very well and I am eager to engage with more of the story once its completed. That being said, much of the game is rough right now and needs time, feedback, and the creative process from these developers to make something incredible. _childDocuments_.review: well the atmosphere in this game is cool but other than that it is fairly generic. Essentially you're going to shoot magic missiles at enemies and jump around to dodge. That's it. The "diablo" like inventory is in reality just 2 different rings that give you 2 different attacks (=magic missiles) and that's it. The only other inventory item is a hood that gives like +30 to life/resistences then you have room for 5 charms that boost you passively or you can summon some totem to shoot more magic missiles. This type of gameplay could be in space and it would be the same. The other thing is that the enemies are randomly stitched together tentacle monsters. No, you're not going to see any vampires or werewolves or ghosts. Just lots and lots of tentacles that fling themselves towards you and they might swing at you or not, I dont even know it's so hard to tell what it's even doing. Sometimes it jumped straight past me off screen and I couldnt find the monster again. So yeah, no swords/skeletons here, no vampires, no ghosts, no rpg-like diablo story or anything like that. They even announced at the very first screen that all the textures are randomly generated by an AI and well.. that's exactly how it looks but I thought that they would at least have monsters and cool weapons but it's just not there. I'm not going to be too harsh on the item drop quality/rate, that's whatever. It is early access after all but the concept itself doesn't seem good. I will never enjoy a game that throws tentacles at you. It just isn't enough, I'm sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: Source of Madness is a game that’s lovely to look at if you’re a Lovecraft/cosmic horror buff, but its haunting world and wonderfully oppressive atmosphere are sadly accompanied by clumsy combat, lackluster enemies and a somewhat unsatisfying gameplay loop. There are moments of brilliance here and there, like when a tentacled abomination the size of a small building lets out of a bone-chilling scream as it descends upon your unsuspecting protagonist out of nowhere, and having to fight off hordes upon hordes of relentless flesh-beasts can get rather intense at times. But at the end of the day, despite Source of Madness’ small successes, I simply didn’t find it to be all that thrilling to play, nor did it inspire me to keep coming back for more after each run.For more honest indie game reviews, check out our Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: Story was cool! To bad game play sucked...I will admit I only played it on normal but man this game was easy. I ended up beating act 1 and act 2s boss with no deaths other than the restart of my toon for act 2. Act 3s boss DID kill me two times but once I changed my go to load out he died in just a minute or two once I warped in him and basted away. And I know I have a bunch of time played but that was me mostly leaving the game on when I would go to work.Monsters seemed to be more confused in how to play than I was. Other than bosses who would try and bullet hell nothing in here could last long if you got heavy hitting spells. But the WORST part of this game is just the lack of a game mechanic. True you CAN unlock new classes, unlock new rings with spells. But its just so lack luster. Nothing in this game you have not seen 100 times before in other games. I could have lived with the idea of maybe having all kinds of world spaces to go off and search for rare, hard to get classes of cultists, something to replay, forgotten or hidden knowledge so that my cult could make powerful new rings. OR lean in to the idea that we are in a cult and let me do mean, culty things to power up toon or get buffs... anything... But once you figure out what spells work and what you like you just roll with that till you beat the game. Maybe I missed something but I felt like we could have had a lot more.I want to like anything that has a lovecraft tag on it and this game HAD a story we dont see often from such games. I REALLY wanted to enjoy this but ... All I can do is hope they made some money and want to make a Source Of Madness 2 where they really put the effort in! I hope to see it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has so much potential to be really good : story seems interesting, the overall setting is really unsettling and good, the eldritch abomination vibe is there. But there are two major things blocking me from enjoying the experience for now : the design of the game (includes art and animations) and the crypticness of the gameplay. Don't get me wrong, the art could be interesting but it just feels like it's getting in the way of the gameplay. With these kind of graphics (sort of collages ?), your character just feels heavy and not precise in it's plateforming and shooting ability. Most of the time, you won't be able to understand what you're supposed to hit with big wobling monsters rolling at you. _childDocuments_.review: It has lots of issues directly related to many of the unique things it does, but I'll let those slide because they're interesting.Some actual problems:- Doesn't carry over progress from the demo.- The three floating balls of light and especially their trails look stupid.- It's too hard to tell what's foreground and what's background.- Has a popup on starting the game that tells you about early access...and the Ukraine. I find this proliferation of political statements in unrelated places rather annoying.- The cursor is easy to lose in the action.- In some areas you really wish you had a minimap.- The camera pan and zoom are fairly erratic and, IMO, the player should have some more control.- Taking damage is too hard to notice.- Since most regular attacks have short cooldowns and cost no resources, you get through most fights by kiting and holding down both attack buttons.- The gameplay isn't varied enough for how long the levels are.- Most attacks have a basic and an "ultimate" option, with the ultimate either requiring a charge-up or coming automatically as the Nth shot after having continuously fired off N-1 attacks. The ones with charge-up are fine, but the repetition ultimates have really poor usability.- Since most enemies are mindless masses of writhing tentacles that fling themselves in your general direction, firepower matters far more than versatility and you're usually best off taking two of the same attacks and two of the same special skill, so you can deal as much burst damage as possible without having to worry about disparate attack styles.- The optimal way to play is probably to very carefully kite via blood magic (spend HP to fire, but gain more HP if you hit), which takes forever. The optimal way to play being boring isn't overly good design. I might be wrong about this, depending on what's unlocked later in the game.- There's not much depth to in the metaprogression and the most interesting part, the classes, is locked behind getting far enough into the game.- The maps seem to be the same on each playthrough with some minor randomization, so a few runs in you might be a tad bored by seeing the same place over and over.Other than that, if nothing else it's at least very interesting to look at. But it's also a solid roguelite platformer. Nothing really revolutionary in terms of gameplay, but some technical novelty and curious art direction.

_childDocuments_.review: Revised review.The atmosphere of this game keeps me playing. It's a could be a great break game with excellent sounds and interesting fight mechanics. Possibly allowing items to be put in a chest when saved for future characters or even allowing people to load from the last save would help.The fight with the Shub (dark youngling) zooms out way too far, the character isn't visible when the left hand portal is being attacked. Having only the lower section of this monster visible or even limiting the view so only parts would add to the fight and appearance. There is also some issues with what is background, what is a platform and what is a solid piece. This really kicks in with some of the larger monsters where it is possible to be trapped in the crock of a limb. Possibly forcing the character to step to the closest animation might stop this. I'd suggest dropping the requirement to find the shrine and buy it with blood. I've seen two shrines so far. Rather than the rings adding a buy; +10 to a stat, or resistance or damage type might be useful in each of the trees. This would make some of the trees that I suspect aren't the best choices more useful if player need to unlock them for a stat bump. Effectively a level, without having a boring level number.

_childDocuments_.review: A 2D Lovecraftian roguelike where you - a little cultist wielding various families of magick - attempt to regain control of your group's access to arcane knowledge and control of otherwordly portals while fighting abominations of various shapes and forms.The game's combat is a purely magick-based, with melee, projectile, explosive, and AoE types being the main groups. These magicks are vaguely copypasted in terms of design, but with various speed, auxillary effects, stopping power and trajectories which synergize with their respective starting classes (two of which you obtain at the start; the rest are unlocked via exploration and boss battles). In total, there are 6 separate cultist classes to choose from. Additionally, combat is semi-physics based, with monsters reacting to your shots and flying around the room with each hit.On that note, the eldritch horrors from beyond the Aether and Void are entirely randomized each run: some have melee tentacles, some have tendrils and probosces which launch tornados and energy beams, and some hurt you on contact. Their horrible designs are satisfying to attack and take apart piece by piece for powerful combos. Cultists can be made stronger with incremental upgrades, as is the norm for these games.The game's art style is uniquely esoteric, taking on a love letter approach to the many cosmic horror anthologies of our time and the the past and mixing it into a multi-act adventure for horror enthusiasts. Coupled with AI-generated cutscenes depicting the alien landscape, minimalist story-telling, and the overall "janky" feeling of gameplay, this makes for a bizarre but satisfying experience. (Note: I use the term "janky" lovingly, as there is a certain...bizarreness to the control schemes that make it feel unique compared to other more polished titles. Think of how you feel playing games like Dead Rising, Resident Evil 4, Lost Planet 2, etc: they have a certain clunkiness that adds to the experience, not enough to make it feel like you're fighting the game itself, however there may be a bit of that in this game that may frustrate the average player, especially given the random nature of monsters and their subsequent physics).I will say, the game is a little light on content; I managed to beat it in 30 hours, and this did not include the time spent idling or exploring the Cultist's tower (which is largely empty save for some one-off NPC interactions and light narrative drops). I got this on sale so the price tag felt a little more justified; for $20, I would have expected a whole other act and more balancing. This game absolutely has huge potential for further content; boss rushes, more biomes, more encounters with Old Ones and their spawn, more classes and unlocks. Hell, even moddable items would greatly benefit this. I hope the devs continue to build up this game, as an avid horror consumer and writer, it was a treat to see a proper representation of the Unknowable and Occult for once.
_childDocuments_.name: Source of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this is the best direct adaptation of Lovecraftian elements to date.I remember a picture of frog continuously distorted by Google's dream generator AI. Someone remarked if 'that was what Lovecraft meant by beyond comprehension'. This was a good joke, all things considered. I'd estimate that this game's author saw it too and decided to base its design language on the same principle.The way procedurally/AI generated pictures look kinda insane is used to great effect in Source of Madness.The genuine feeling of being immersed in illogical Lovecraftian worlds is the strongest part of the overall experience.The roguelike mechanic with unlocking new dungeons and the current ones changing at random—or playing around with predetermined set pieces—reinforces the theme of insanity and horror. The enemies appear also AI generated, which adds to their uncanny valley-ish horror. Sometimes their design even doesn't make sense and they fail to be a menace. In an world alien to human mind, that kinda makes sense.There's a lot of great design choices later on, but I won't go into those to avoid spoilers.The leveling between runs depends on two resources, and so far seems nicely balanced. The first is received from all enemies, and generally improves skills, while the other one is only provided by bosses, and improves items in the game. (Roughly speaking)New classes are unlockable at given moments in your progress. I've seen two classes placed in optional areas next to the straight path from start to finish. So exploration can potentially have huge impact on the game.I'm not an experienced roguelike player, so my only issue with the game may come down to that fact. Progress is placed quite far away from the run's start. Maybe too far for my liking. So be prepared to replay bigger chunks of the game by the beginning—and put in some of that grind—to see progress later on.But that's not a huge issue, and I fully recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game for little while I can think I can outline what the average person may want to know:PROS:1. They clearly did their research, the game uses a lot of Lovecraft elements and does so well while respecting the source material to make a good game that really does a good job at showing the player the scale of comic horror.2. The small cutscenes that can be found scattered around the game also add greatly to the style and setting of the game. I do not know who did the art or work for the cutscenes but they did a wonderful job.3. The game is difficult, but true to any rougelike, you increase your odds each death you have through upgrades. If you played and enjoyed Dead Cells, this game will certainly scratch that itch for you.CONS: 1.Sometimes it is a bit difficult to tell exactly where you are or what you're looking at. In an artistic sense this makes sense for the comic horror theme the game goes for, but other times it can get you killed.2. In this game, sometimes you will break appendages off enemies and be pinned by them. After a short time the appendages no longer collide with the player but it takes far too long personally. This pinning can get you unfairly killed if you play certain cultist where dashing can be dangerous, such as the pyromancer.3. Some bosses are far easier than others, to unlock one of the cultist you have to fight a very powerful boss that, arguably, is on the same level of difficulty as the final boss. You fight this boss in Act 2 and not even at the end of Act 2 either. Meanwhile the unlock for the other cultist in Act 2 is very easy.All in all I recommend this game for those who like a challenge and are fans of the Lovecraft aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: Source of Madness is a great game if you love Lovecraftian themes and enjoy roguelite type of gameplay. As a Lovecraft game, it's a 10/10, though I'd say at the moment a 6 or 7/10 roguelite with a great core concept that could easily be built on to make it a 10 in future content patches.The environment and monster design lends itself perfectly to the themes of Lovecraft. The way the AI builds creatures and the way some of them move capture the idea of indescribable cosmic horrors perfectly. You can never quite understand what you're looking at as it lunges towards you with its limbs and tentacles flailing about as it moves. To some, this may be a turn off as they tend to just come across as blobs with various, unpredictable move sets. I felt it worked perfectly for the theme but others might find it uninteresting.Movement in the game is pretty solid. Jumping is a bit floaty but I don't think it would benefit from being any less so. Dashing is a main mechanic of the game, not just as damage avoidance but some classes utilize dash for special functions like dropping bombs or colliding into enemies for aoe damage, changing up play styles from run to run. I've had a lot of fun with the various dash mechanics.Builds and gear are pretty straight forward. Pretty similar to Diablo where they provide various stat bonuses to things like damage, crit chance, health, resistance, etc. Legendary gear provides a little more punch to builds with their extra bonuses they provide and allow a decent amount of interactions between effects but I think I'd like to see more interesting interactions in the future though. A lot of effects depend on crit hits, which is fine for the most part as the stat increases dps anyways, but I found myself focused on that stat more than others just to get the benefit of a lot of gear. There's still plenty of synergy opportunities though.  A masochistic self-burning build to double my arcane nuke projectiles while I repeatedly stabbed with an ice dagger to proc a heal was one of my favorites.All in all, I had tremendous fun with the game and look forward to its future.
_childDocuments_.name: Source of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic little game. This game puts procedurally generated content on a new level. Not only the maps are procedurally designed, but also the monsters. And what creations I have seen in the several runs that I finished each act several times! I can assure you, due to this feature, it really never gets boring doing another run, just to see what kind of enemies will expect you!Gameplay is generally fine, with several classes to choose from, several weapons that are all quite different and heavily affect your playstyle, with a good upgrade tree and additonal support items. Depending on class and weapons you choose, you can either play very agressively or also prefer a more cautious approach - everything is possible!The graphic design, sounds, controls are all spot on, I never had any issues with them. The game is quite difficult at the beginning, but when you begin to unlock certain upgrades like healing and more weapons, in the end it becomes quite easy once you have found your preferred playstyle. I had a lot of fun while playing it, I hope the devs release some DLC or NG+ so that I may return some day.

_childDocuments_.review: If the first Dark Souls and HP Lovecraft had a hate baby that morphed into schizophrenic fever dreams, this would be it. On the real though, it's truly a great game at it's current status. Yes, it's an early access, but you wouldn't know it unless you saw a disclaimer beforehand. I'm relatively new to this game, but I've sunk about 11hrs into in just a few days, which while being a father of a 2 year old, that ain't easy so what free time I have the game better be damn worth that time, I feel it's a stroke of brilliance to have the creatures and levels (outside of bosses) totally random for the most part. It makes restarts feel fresh without punishing the player. Death isn't a set back, it's almost like a reward in a weird way. _childDocuments_.review: An extremely visceral and satisfying rouge-like souls-esque platformer. Spells are satisfying, jumps are floaty but consistent, and the action is fast paced with daunting legitimately horrifying monsters.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hit or miss at times. It feels like this game still has a ways to go in terms of consistent gameplay. Yes, I know this is in development.Pros:-Setting, art style-spells are cool-story so far is interesting- beaten act one so farCons:-Fighting feels very inconsistent with spells that don't penetrate.I.e. using great fire ball which does 20 damage starting off takes far longer to kill an enemy at a distance than fire wave 2-4 damage or arcane wave. The reason this is happening is it seem the extra limbs on an enemy doesn't seem to count for hit box or damage sometimes, and often seem to be blocking for the core. This could be intentional, but I feel this drags fights on. The solution to this is to get close, however that bring in the next con.-Any type of close combat feels bad. Everything to strange attack boxes, to getting stuck on enemies for seemingly no reason, to some attacks doing a obscene amount of damage to the player. -Runs are very inconsistent. Yes, I know that this is a rouge-lite with a lot of Rng elements, but I feel as though there should be some guarantees. Example: in one run I got lucky and had 2 blood offering gateways, 2 mini boss fight gates, and 3-6 other events for items in the first area. The run following I had 2 event doors (yielded commons) and an uncommon from the stage mini boss, no money for the shop, died in the next area. Feels bad.I will have to let this game sit for a while before coming back to it. Runs also need a brb option, as I don't always have long intervals of time to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Had my eye on this game for a while, from when I was first introduced to it from Facebook from what I can only tell is the algorithm gaining info on me based on searches for "the occult + bathrobes + tentacles + why doesn't anyone who loves me stay".What lies here is a little gem that I'm sure is going to draw comparisons to Dead Cells, Death's Gambit, Blasphemous...etc etc. But it really does it's own thing with a sort of diablo-style loot system, rarity tiers, and physics-based monsters and magic, all with a pretty cool written A.I. code to generate random looking monsters with infinite limbs. The spells all have strengths and weaknesses, the classes so far have little boosts to certain types of magic but are by no means limited to a certain type, so if you find a ring that says "Fire bomb" and you've selected the nerd-ass earth wizard, you can still try and fit in and be metal by burning everything to the ground. Poser.The best thing about this dev team is how active they are, and how much they listen in their discord. Pretty cool, listen to every suggestion and very friendly community in there. Some suggested changes from people have already been implemented, and I don't mean from me personally - I'm a moron. But a moron with a great taste in tentacle games.The gameplay itself is very satisfying and weighty, and I defy you not to brick in your pants when you see the first giant ass miniboss that's randomly sneezed together with stingers, limbs, skulls, jaws and a disposition to try and dry hump your character into oblivion. It should be noted that I do have a medical condition that makes me compulsively brick in my pants, but I swear that time, that time was because of the game. Really.Lastly, for someone that revels in things Lovecraftian (grim dawn, sinking city, the movie Underwater with the twilight chick that's actually really good, women in general who deject me because of a draw to a deeper more sinister mythos, and not due to my own shortcomings as a human being) this really commits to that feel and I appreciate it.  If I could give this a rating out of 10, it would be 12, because I don't need to color inside your lines. I'm my own man.Oh, and it's really good.Also, shout out to the spooky soundtrack and ambience of the game in general. Really well done. Again, another brown-note trigger for me. Excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: A staggeringly beautiful title, Source of Madness caught my attention some time ago. Reminiscent of Dead Cells albeit through a Lovecraftian lens. Lovecraft-inspired games are, of course, ten-a-penny on Steam, at present this does seem a little light on lore to truly "own" that categorisation but the potential certainly exists. The focus on action may be off-putting to many Lovecraft fans as it stands in stark contrast to the protagonists in his depressive tales. Therefore it's important to note the qualifier - inspired, it does not intend to be a recreation of his work wholesale. Overall this is pretty solid, so far I'm happy with my investment, One thing to note, all keys are rebindable and a joypad is not required, I found the game to be perfectly enjoyable on KB/M. I've seen complaints regarding the jumping mechanics, I did not find this to be an issue personally. I'll will update my review when the game is developed further. NB The soundtrack is phenomenal.

_childDocuments_.review:
Source of Madness is a side-scrolling dark action roguelite set in the Loam Lands, a twisted Lovecraftian inspired world powered by procedural generation and AI machine learning.

Take on the role of a new Acolyte as they embark on a nightmarish odyssey. Uncover the cosmic secrets of the Loam Lands and The Tower of Madness, the moon's mysterious Citadel.

The horrific monsters you face are never the same, concocted with procedural generation and animated using a neural network AI

Explosive close-combat magic, labyrinthine environmental exploration, powerful loot management and a skill tree filled with abilities, classes, and spells

Rendered in a beautiful AI assisted art style, the fascinating world of the Loam Lands reveals a deep arcane lore as players uncover its many secrets

name: Destropolis
detailed_description: Destropolis is a top-down shooter game, inspired by such classic games like “Crimsonland”, “Alien Shooter” or “Nuclear Throne”. It takes place in a futuristic city, filled with red, cube-like enemies. Tear them to pieces with bullets, lasers and nuclear explosions. Play alone or with friends in a local co-op mode. Destroy as many enemies as you can before they overwhelm you. Features Fight an endless wave of enemies in a futuristic city. Totally destructible environment. Every object in the game, every enemy, every building, can be smashed into pieces. You can blow up buildings, you can use them as cover, you can dismantle enemies bit by bit. 6 different types of enemies. Cubes are numerous and dangerous up close. Obelisks shoot lasers at you. Bomb spheres explode on contact. Pyramids shoot at you from a distance with artillery rounds. Wrecking balls smash everything on their path. Big, hexagonal bosses wreak havoc with their massive machine guns. 15 different guns at your disposal. Shotguns, assault rifles and machine guns shoot bullets that shred your enemies to pieces. Missiles and nuclear launchers create balls of fire that effectively clear out battlefields. Lasers and gauss guns cut through the enemies like knives through butter. 12 power-ups and 40 skills that enhance your abilities. Place turrets, create force fields and detonate nuclear explosions. Increase your health, damage or movement speed. Confuse your enemies that they will shoot at each other. Play alone, or with your friends in up to 3 players co-op mode. Compete with other players from around the world on global leaderboards. Unique art style. Clean and minimalistic environment. Distinct and aggressively colored enemies. Beautiful explosions and lighting effects. Synth-wave music. Created by a popular artist - LukHash. A fusion of chiptune mastery mingled with synthwave cyberpunk and EDM elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Proof that a twin-stick shooter can be a work of art. Destropolis' minimalist art style is bolstered by intelligent gameplay with precision weapon and skill mechanics, and persistent level progression across play sessions.The aesthetics and gameplay are elevated by LukHash's beautiful synthwave soundtrack and the integration of tempo manipulation with Bullet Time works to create a beautiful example of digital love.-

_childDocuments_.review: A clean and simple twin-stick shooter. If you love those and really need a new one to scratch the itch go for it - it's just $5. But otherwise there are many better ones out there. There's no real progression or sense of purpose in here. It's just you and hordes of enemies, ruined buildings, and random pickups. By accumulating total score you unlock new weapons or ingame perks, sure, but most feel just the same as the other ones and there's no permanent upgrades of any sort. In that sense, it's not really a roguelite but just a good old arcade twin-stick.There's no real purpose in getting better or lasting longer though. The leaderboard is pointless, there are almost no ways to affect your score (one random 2x score pickup), no permanent progression, no stages, no enemy variety, nothing. Even achievements are only based on your score.
_childDocuments_.name: Destropolis

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a fun, stylish shmup, but I'm also frustrated with some of its design decisions.Like the best shmups, you have to manage a lot of things at the same time in order to be successful.Short term: Red shapes are all around in desperate need to be shot by you. They start off small, but as you progress they rise in size, hit points, and lethality. Destroying them earns you points and sometimes items. These items are either active-use guns or passive-use items.Guns have limited ammunition. Continuous fire overheats them. You can carry and switch between two at once.Passive-use items activate on contact, last a limited time, and enhance your own combat effectiveness in multiple ways, including speeding up your movement, nuking the immediate area, and doubling your weapon's rate of fire.Get hit and your shield will take damage. Don't take damage for a time and your shield will regenerate. Deplete your shield and subsequent hits will damage your health, which can only be restored by an item. There's also buildings strewn about the  metropolis that  get destroyed real good.Long term: The points you earn raise your level. Each level, you can select a buff. These buffs include effects like gaining more ammunition on weapon pickups, item effects lasting longer, and increasing the rate that certain items will appear. Combining these effects is key to surviving as the run goes on. However, the buffs available at each level-up is four or six, chosen at random.Some guns are better to use at different times during the run. Others I would be happy to never use again. Same for the passive-use items and buffs. You earn new guns, items, and buffs as your aggregate score (across all runs) rises, but you never gain the ability to turn any of them . So you like that Minigun and you wish you saw more of it? The most you can do is use the "Favorite Gun" buff to boost its likelihood of appearing by 50%. But you can't, for instance, take the Magnum  of the rotation so that all of the other guns show up more often. It's deeply frustrating to have an idea of what you want to do each run and be stymied by randomness where your abilities are concerned.Another shmup, Beat Hazard 2, allows you to select your loadout before you start a stage. You can arm your craft with four of several weapons. Ammo for them appears at random, but you'll never see ammo for guns you aren't armed with. I'd like to see something similar in place for Destropolis, but the way that the game works suggests that the developer wasn't interested in giving the player complete control over configuration. This "random, run-based" game design still hasn't run its course yet, so I guess I'll just have to look forward to a Destropolis 2.Or make my own game. Hmm...

_childDocuments_.review: Destropolis is a simplistic, flawed twin-stick shooter that mainly qualifies as an artsy amusement that doesn't suggest reason to recommend it aside from artsy amusement.  So, watch a video, think about how mildly cute it seems, then move on and forget it.You can move, shoot, and swap between your two weapons (obtained as random drops), which are limited both by "heat" (cools down while unused) and by ammo (not replenished, pick up another weapon for ammo).  Enemies drift slowly at you in ever-increasing numbers, and you chew them down until you are eventually overwhelmed.  Along the way you are constantly interrupted by the intrusive perk selection that happens on level-up, as the game covers the screen with a poorly designed selection interface where you can pick one of several uninteresting and poorly presented upgrades, and then drops you right back into action.  You also get various "powerups" which activate immediately on pickup, most of which are boring and some of which are even bad (eg, bullet time just slows down the whole game, so it is more of a tedious time waster than a boon).There are no scoring mechanics to add interest, and if leaderboards are of interest to you, be aware there are significant random factors to how quickly you can kill enemies and your points rewarded, and at least one perk that very directly (but still randomly) increases scoring.Destropolis combines artistic minimalism with treading water, and doesn't make for much of a twin-stick shooter experience.  The developer could have done a lot better with little effort if they cared, but they did not care and have said they did not care, and you can do better for your time or money than playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Destropolis is one of those rare finds, you start playing, thinking it will just be one of your run of the mill top-down shooters, and instead it is an awesome, nonstop punch in the face of awesomeness!The main idea of the game is simple, you control a blue diamond shape cube, that can also fire weapons, you are surrounded by a fully destructible environment, and wave after way of red cuboid enemies. And that is it.After reaching a score threshold, you pass the level, the game pauses and you can choose from upgrades, that may be an increase of your help, weapon cool down time, increase rate of drops and so on.As you play you can collect up to 15 different weapons designated in a blue light, you pick up by pressing A on the controller, you can hold 2 weapons at a time and switch between them.You will also be able to collect different power ups. From speed ups, to bullet time (which slows down time, giving you more time to think), to my favourite the NUKE! Which is exactly what you think it is. Airstrikes, Vortexes and so on.Eventually and perhaps inevitably, you will be overwhelmed, and you will die. But then you just restart, and off you go again.Played from an isometric/top-down view, with 6 main types of cube like enemies,"Obelisks shoot lasers at you. Bomb spheres explode on contact. Pyramids shoot at you from a distance with artillery rounds. Wrecking balls smash everything on their path. Big, hexagonal bosses wreak havoc with their massive machine guns."Although a minimalist type structure to the game, it gets hectic very very quick. Throw in some synth-wave music by LukHash, and you have a true diamond in the rough when it comes to top-down shooters.The GoodThe minimalist approach to the graphics, just works, and actually looks beautiful. Each time you play, you will be a bit better, and find yourself slowly climbing up the leader boards.The BadMaybe some different areas to play in would be a nice addition to the game.OverallDestropolis was supposed to be a quick throw away type game, one I would play for ten minutes, get bored and forget about, instead it has entered my psyche and I absolutely love it.A real surprise find, and one I really recommend.Awesome game I score a strong 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: How can something so simple, and so minimalist, be so damn fun? Well, that's exactly what you will find here. As a rougelike fan, I really enjoy this game very much. The gameplay is very smooth, the sound effects are great, the weapons and powerups are satisfying, and more. My only problem is that it takes forever to reach higher levels and unlock new weapons and skills, and there should be more cosmetic options and new arenas, maybe in the sequel. Overall, don't sleep on this and grab it as soon as you can, don't let the games simplicity fool you, this game is very fun and satisfying to play, one of the best roguelikes ever on steam and if you have it on a portable console, even better. Highly Recommended!

name: This Way Madness Lies
detailed_description: Let us begin our tale, in the quiet city of Verona, Italy. A town for lovers... and giant, mutant flower attacks. As the leader of the Stratford-Upon-Avon High Drama Society, Imogen is no ordinary girl! Sure, she goes to school every day and helps produce plays for the community, but beyond that, she's a magical girl! With her powers, she can teleport to alternate dimensions based on Shakespeare plays, fight back the forces of Nightmare, and still get back in time for dinner! Join Imogen, Paulina, Viola, Rosalind, Miranda, Beatrice, and Kate on an epic adventure throughout the Shakespearean metaverse in this comedy JRPG! • Unique, turn-based combat! • Hang out with your friends! • Put on plays! • Shakespearean dialogue too difficult to parse? No problem with our unique Ye Olde English to New English translator! 110% accurate! • Multi-character unite abilities! • Teaches you while you learn! • Get a pet! • Pacing that doesn't waste your time! • Fun for the whole family! We believe that world needs more bite-size turn-based JRPGs - short, self-contained games that you can enjoy over a weekend or a few play sessions when you want a change of pace from big epics. Something that's all killer, no filler. We estimate that a single playthrough of This Way Madness Lies will take around 5-10 hours, depending on difficulty & playstyle, and we hope that you will enjoy every minute!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun jaunt. A lot of good customization in your party and cast but not as expansive as you might want to really explore them. Graphics are a treat.Seasoned RPG fans looking for something lighter to chomp down on should take a look, but this feels like a great game for a young kid to try to play through.

_childDocuments_.review: If there's one thing I want to communicate here, it's that there is an excellent sense of pacing in the classic RPG gameplay-to-story ratio.  Generally, nothing ever drags or goes on for too long before you're onto the next thing.  The same approach informs their writing and approach to jokes - maybe not everything lands with you but that's fine, you won't have to dwell on it long.TWML is a fun game to play, the battle system is a clever refinement of Cosmic Star Heroine with an absolutely gorgeous visual style, the dungeons are straightforward without feeling like you're completely on rails, the enemies vanish when you kill them so you're not fighting endlessly tedious battles, it's well-designed.  I'd have preferred more control over my party construction more often, but I understand them's the breaks.  Not enough Paulina :(The story is a mixed bag with an exceedingly fun premise.  I won't recap what you can read in the game description.   The choice to make the sections in-between dungeons be visual novels is an idea, but honestly not my favorite thing.  I understand that it speeds up creation, since designing wholeass towns and areas and flags and shops and events takes up a lot of time and if it means we get more cute microRPGs instead of a more involved experience, it's a fair trade-off...but I'd also have liked the chance to do more roaming with the gang here.  I'd love to see TWML's cast return at some point, but it's enough to be left wanting more.  No point in reviewing something for what it's -not-And ultimately that's my point here.  The simple truth is, if you like RPGs, you should play TWML.  Not every story is an 80+ hour epic and it doesn't need to be.  I'd love to see more titles like this.  Short, punchy and fun.ALSO the music is fantastic.  Didn't mention that earlier, but it deserves an addendum.

This is a playful incarnation of a daily animated series with an episodic structure. Don't expect depth or massive interactivity. It has funny dialogues, fancy plots and heroines with bright char traits. The presentation is top notch, the art & music are so beautiful. Most of gameplay is the skills equip management (lol, if you like it). The dungeons are small, and the battles are quite intuitive and sometimes predictable. A small and relaxed adventure for a couple of evenings. Only for fans of the all above.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface this, I loved Zeboyd's earlier titles. Cthulhu Saves The World was great, and I enjoyed Breath of Death and the Rainslick games as well. But around that point onward I just feel like some of the spark's been lost. Cosmic Star Heroine lost me before I had finished half an hour. I love magical girls so I thought I'd give them another shot on this one, but I can't say it was worth it.Right off the bat, I wasn't a fan of the battle system. Zeboyd games feel like they're trying way too hard to make battle systems that are innovative rather than ones that are good. There's a whole elaborate system about skills that recharge and hyper mode timers that are different for each character and can completely change what your abilities do. But rather than letting me feel powerful for using the system to my advantage, it just left me feeling like I had to jump through hoops in order to get what other games would consider basic functionality.(As a side note - this game also follows that modern trend of refilling all your HP/skills/items after every fight. I hate this trend because it takes away a big part of what I enjoy about JRPGs, which is resource management. You don't have to ration out your MP dealing with smaller fights and save your big hitters for bosses, so every fight ends out playing very similar.)At least the game has an Easy mode so you can steamroll the fights if you're not interested. But from what I've seen I don't feel like the story would be worth the time. The pacing is absurdly fast, meaning none of the characters get a chance to develop beyond one-dimensional tropes. You've got the main character, the nice one, the sporty one, and so on. Events like 'oops we got pulled into an alternate dimension' happen and are discarded never to be mentioned again. Anything that isn't combat gets cut down to the bare minimum and it's jarring to follow.To make another comparison, I want to bring up Cthulhu Saves The World again. CSTW's cutscenes didn't have many moving parts for engine reasons, but to compensate it had comic book like cutins to show things happening. It was simple and barebones but it helped the plot come alive. TWML instead uses the gameplay sprites with zero animation, and panels that change ever so slightly each time you advance the dialogue box. It just makes the whole thing feel lifeless in comparison.But Fiona, I hear you say! The plot doesn't have to make sense! It's a comedy game, remember? It just has to be funny!Valid point, person that appears when I forget to take my meds. But this brings us to the biggest problem I have with TWML: A lot of it just plain isn't funny.They make a big deal of the 'Ye Olde English -> Modern' translator, but it's mostly used in a predictable and childish manner. A lot of it isn't even used on actual text from Shakespeare plays, but made-up 'Ye Olde' prose by the devs that then gets some agonisingly sarcastic translation. "Poison met with Antigonus and he fared worse for the meeting" becomes "Poison poisoned Antigonus", for example.The two original plays I got to see were similarly unfunny. A Comedy Of Errors gets boiled down to 'people get confused for other people' and then that joke gets turned into a nonsensical play about baseball (because there are errors in baseball, get it?) and an even more nonsensical play about computer programming.Zeboyd has always tried to do tongue-in-cheek meta humour, but in my opinion it worked better in the old games which were very obviously based on NES-era RPGs. You knew the formula, so the meta joke was pointing that out or subverting it. Here you have the protagonist talking to the player/Bardolator/Thespian for no reason whatsoever, and whenever it happens the whole scene screeches to a halt while you answer actual questions about Shakespeare plays.This isn't a game about JRPGs anymore. It's about Shakespeare and magical girls. Those two topics are rife with potential for meta humour. You could have multiple Shakespeares running around to reference the common theory that William Shakespeare was a penname used by multiple authors. You could point out that the drama club conveniently only has female members because a magical boy would mess with the formula. But instead we get only the most base level jokes about Shakespeare plays, and it feels like the devs don't respect the works they're supposedly inspired by.I've rambled long enough, but what I'm trying to say is that Zeboyd feels like they're not aware of what they're good at. They did really well in the self-referential JRPG element, but spreading beyond that they still try to rely on jokes that no longer apply. They put a lot of effort into a complex battle system, but that just makes it feel like a hassle rather than something fun. And the technology hasn't advanced at all since CSTW ten years ago - if anything the cutscenes feel like a big step backward.There IS the occasional joke that manages to land, but overall I can't recommend playing this. If Zeboyd wants their new games to hit the same spot CSTW did, I feel like they have to bring some new ideas to the table. In this world of endless isekai anime, making jokes about JRPG mechanics just doesn't cut it anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: I was ready to love this game. It felt like it was doing most of what Cosmic Star Heroine got right, but with a more appropriate sense of its own scale. It gave off echoes of being inspired by other games I liked a lot. I can't really explain why, but its sense of humor somehow managed to land with me in a way that Zeboyd's other games did not.Then the game threw Miranda at me. She was both insufferable as a character but also changed up the game mechanics in a way that just wasn't fun. But I figured that with the game's rotating cast, at least I'd only have to put up with her roughly half the time. Then the game forced her into the party for nearly every dungeon, right up to the point where you can freely swap your party members around. It feels petty to say that one character eroded all of the initial good will the game built up. And she probably wouldn't have, if I ever felt like I got a break from her. But by Chapter 7 or so, I was yelling at the screen to stop making me use Miranda. By the time I got the choice to not use her, the well was already so thoroughly poisoned and I was so fed up that I could no longer find that initial interest.
_childDocuments_.name: This Way Madness Lies

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is a mixed bag. The gameplay itself is good. If you liked the combat of Cthulhu Saves Christmas or Cosmic Star Heroine, then you'll like this game as well. It also still has a similar art style, which is pretty, and the same sort of enemies and descriptions that I enjoyed from their previous games. The story itself is serviceable, but you really go for this sort of game for the little themed areas throughout. The idea of mixing Shakespeare and magical girls is unique, and mixing Shakespeare plays with disasters is also fun. But, something feels amiss with this title compared to this studio's other games. It started to feel off with Cthulhu Saves Christmas, but in this one it feels even further away from what I enjoyed about their games. Its hard to describe, but you can feel it in the writing. I think that they're sort of stuck in the same sort of writing style as Cthulhu Saves the World and Breath of Death, but their heart is not in it. I'm not sure whether they feel obligated to keep doing this style of writing, if they were too strictly confined with the Shakespeare/magical girl theme, or if its a new writer who doesn't quite get what made the other games funny, but I don't think it would bode well for the next game if it follows suit. There's also the issue of having party members being forced into your party. The RPG elements to it encourages team synergy, but when your teammates can be forced to switch at any time, it ruins that synergy and makes you dislike the character you've been forced to use even more. Its even worse when you get into a surprise battle and in between you didn't equip any new abilities/powers to the characters. I also feel like because you start in media res, you don't really get much one on one time with the characters. You start out with so many characters, but other than the story cutscenes and out of battle dialogue (which doesn't change too much and you can't select one person to talk to), they don't get to shine. The only time you get one on one time is in the save menu cutscene. It would've been nice if like in Cthulhu Saves Christmas they had their own missions to help you and them level up or gain abilities, or if like the Cosmic Star Heroine they had their own little story and goals going on. Overall, I think that its a fun little game, but I would wait for it on sale perhaps and replay Cosmic Star Heroine or Cthulhu Saves the World instead.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10TWML is a short RPG focused on Shakespeare and magical girls. Sounds crazy? It is, while no knowledge of Shakespeare is required, you will probably get more of the game if you have experience with his work. 8/10Pretty solid overall, every now and then it became repetitive, however, considering how short the game is, you can’t complain. There are also some voiced tracks, those are amazing. 6.5/10Most of the points here are due to the transformation sequence. The game maps look nice, even though they are kind of generic, and the enemies are pretty much copy – pasted. 7.5/10The gameplay is really simple and streamlined. You fight, recover all your health after each fight, gain experience and earn traits and abilities. I liked how most abilities are one use only and then you need to recharge them. Same as hyper (being super magical) or a few other statuses. However, AOE attacks seemed really lackluster and there were a lot of terms and usefulness that you needed to really dig-in to understand its utility. 8/10Simple, direct, Shakespeare tales or worlds are in danger, and, as the drama society and magical girls, you are in charge of saving them. A few other things happen, but for me, the best part of the game is the dialogue. Not only is it super fun, I loved how you have ye olde English, and with a simple push of a button, you can also read the “modern” version of what it would mean.

_childDocuments_.review: I like most games from Zeboyd, but the lackluster feel I got from Cthulhu saves Christmas is even worse here.Most characters have super uninteresting abilities that are worthless in most standard combats. Which is the biggest beef I have with the game. The boss fights are OK and some even fun, but the basic combat which is, ofc, the overwhelmingly largest part of the game, is horrifyingly boring and bland with half the characters having 1 or max 2 abilities that actually deal damage and then you have to immediately refresh them because the majority of their abilities is just not doing anything to spend LESS time in combat. Combat feels like a boring chore that drags on and on and really feels more like a distraction from everything else.The game has literally ONE new mechanic, that being traits, a seperate ability screen which can be used to assign 3 abilities that increase stats and/or improve a characters ability when performing certain tasks (e.g. healing or dealing fire damage, etc.).All in all, I tried to get into the game twice and couldn't be bothered to play further than just a little bit after the 2nd Boss. There's quite literally nothing new with everything more lackluster than ever before. Sad to see that after CSH, it's been *really* going downhill. Cthulhu saves Christmas at least had fun interactions and the way you could use the town was special. Here you get a screen to talk to your squad. For what, you may ask? Nothing. Fluff text.Cthulhu saves the world had more interesting ways to develop your character than this. Uninteresting abilities, redundancy, and new traits just being flat stronger than older ones when it comes to stat boosting, really all add to the feeling that there is neither reward nor reason for not doing the obvious thing with your characters, and for what the game is at it's heart, a turn based combat RPG, it leaves a lot to be desired. Maybe it gets better later on, but me wasting 3 hours on this is me also not being interested in that possibility anymore. I'd rather replay any other game from Zeboyd. This really feels lackluster to point of heartlessness. Sure, dialogue and sprites look cool, but... how does that make up for a failed core gameplay loop? And oh boy... Maybe it's just not for me, but the audio of the characters is just straight up annoying for me. Sorry. I'd rather have wished for better core mechanics than audio design that makes me wish I could turn it off as an option.

_childDocuments_.review: This Way Madness Lies is a pretty neat, very underrated but short JRPG gem. The plot of the game is that you're a group of Magical Girls traveling from dimension to dimension to save every play of Shakespeare under attack by vicious nightmares. Yes. The plot is really silly, and the game is absolutely meant to be 100% humor. If you come in expecting a deep story, you won't find it, but a bunch of very good laughs instead.The gameplay itself is refined- there is no magic, instead every move is single use (unless stated otherwise). To recover them, you simply rest and defend for a turn. Items are unlimited use and you have combination attacks that slowly build power over time. Simple, right? Wrong.The combat system has a bunch of dozen variations on how well you can break (or try, the devs are really good about this on Hard, which is the difficulty I played) the game. This Way Madness Lies actually starts by showing you this- before you unlock party swap, you are given pre-set comps with their own strengths and weaknesses so you learn how good the characters are and how well they mesh with a specific comp. And some of these combinations are very silly- which the game then immediately nerfs in the next segment to teach you something else. It's really clever about it. Gameplay wise, the best character in the game is Imogen, which makes sense since she can never leave the party. She can play literally any role you want- and a lot of the characters have rather interesting builds, where you change their traits and can change their focus. The tradeoff for this can be stats, but focus is usually more important.The graphics are handmade sprites- and they are really well made, but outside of the main characters they don't really feel unique for some reason? Though I think the genericness-feel of them is part of the point of the enemies. Hm.The music is really well made. It's got a good quality beat to it that keeps you focused and reassured, but it's not nothing too standout that gets "best music of all time". Get the soundtrack, it sounds really nice to listen to separately.Overall, Zeboyd makes a really good game once again, which is a great timekiller. My playtime says 13 hours, but my save file is more like 8-9 hours (I tabbed out a lot). TL;DR Story 6/10 but funny, Gameplay 10/10, Graphics 8/10, Music 8.5/10buy this game
_childDocuments_.name: This Way Madness Lies

_childDocuments_.review: Long time Zeboyd Games fan here, just finished the game tonight!  If you enjoyed the combat style of Cosmic Star Heroine, This Way Madness Lies improves on the formula with special effects on each of your skills during hyper mode.  The combat feels great, and supports a lot of different party compositions.  I played on hard difficulty and had quite a few fights come really close!  It's a satisfying RPG.Each of the members of the Stratford-Upon-Avon High Drama Society are so unique and the dialogue conveys their personalities very well.  As with other Zeboyd games, the dialogue is lighthearted, not horny, and makes frequent tasteful jokes.  It's rare that you see comedy in games in today's age without the cringe factor, and This Way Madness Lies does just that.  Also, very important:  The magical girl transformation sequence happens every time the characters transform, as it should be!  They totally nail the magical girl style!Last but not least, the SOUNDTRACK.  Oh my god.  This soundtrack is OOOOBANG Certified.  Buckle up before starting the game, because the title screen track is an absolute banger.  This Way Madness Lies is filled with rockin' jams throughout, and more than a few times, I stopped what I was doing on stream just to listen to the music.  Joshua Queen's compositions for the game are just outstanding, and I sincerely hope for a vinyl release of the OST!This game absolutely rules, and was one of the most fun games I've ever streamed.  Enjoy!!
