_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't recall how I blundered upon Fashion Police Squad (its title a clever backronym for the game's own genre), but I was so baffled and intrigued by the concept that I felt compelled to pick it up.This was the correct decision.FPS is a zany (and very much tongue-in-cheek) homage to the camp world of haute couture and the unique feel of retro FPS games (which seem to be having something of a renaissance of late, for some reason?). It was a blast to play, even if some areas were very challenging (and not always for good reasons)--but that, too, falls squarely within the purview of retro FPS games, does it not?If you are expecting a finely-polished game with dazzlingly precise play and mechanics (such as, say, Ultrakill perhaps?), this game is not that--but fortunately for you, those games do exist. If you're willing to have a hilarious time catwalking through an FPS with quirk pouring out of its gills, however, FPS is probably an excellent option to play.As a final note on value (as that seems to be a key consideration on Steam), FPS's main campaign is fairly short, and would be shorter still if some of the areas hadn't seen me need to retry them more times than I care to admit (again, some for reasons of legitimate difficulty, while others, distinctly less so). There are side challenge one-off missions you can undertake, usually for more drip, but that isn't everyone's cup of tea. I completed the story and a couple of the side missions in under 7 hours, if that helps you calibrate.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who likes a great atmosphere, or a good FPS.   Not only is Fashion Police Squad a great unique entry in the FPS genre, it's one filled with character and heart. It's easy to look at the subject matter and the surface and see only a game that may be a gimmick of some sort, but that would be a big mistake. The action is great, using the gimmick of specific weaknesses to force you to focus on particular enemies, while you're dodging enemies left and right. I played on hard difficulty, and even as a veteran of the genre I got a good challenge here, dying a reasonable amount but not to the point of horrible frustration. This is all in the backdrop of clever jokes and a great atmosphere: the game does a fantastic job in setting the stage and you really appreciate the level of detail put into the parodies and references. It's a colorful game with a fantastic soundtrack and great sound design, and it's definitely a game that you'll want to put your full attention into.Really, a lot of my complaints are small: dealing with specific rooms with enemy design that feels a little too cramp, or needing a tweak or two here with the movement on the belt swinging. A bug or two that would cause me to reset a level's progress, but in the big picture, they don't add up to overshadow the game's great pace, design, and overall fun factor. Great for new or veterans players, it's definitely worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Duke Nukem style boomer shooter.  Rather than having ammo pickups, the enemies can only be defeated with certain guns, more of which unlock as you progress.  This keeps levels cleaner, allowing you to focus on the pixel artwork and play style rather than hoarding ammo for the super powerful weapons vs. using it.  The sprite work and pixel art are top notch, with a great nostalgic soundtrack.  The writing is funny, coupled with the many video game references and pop-culture spoofs make this a game worth playing.  The game is rather easy, even on the hardest difficulty, but that doesn't make it not-worth-playing.  People have definitely been sleeping on this game.  I am excited for FPS2.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I've played long enough to defeat two bosses and I can comfortably say that Fashion Police Squad (FPS, haha) is a magnificent game reminiscent of the shooters of the 90s. Where Quake and Doom gave us blood and violence, the Fashion Police Squad gives us comedy and the freshest fashions.The game sports a small but diverse group of enemies, each one sporting a different weakness for you to exploit with your arsenal (and subsequent alt fire modes). Movement is quick and responsive (Especially when swinging with the belt, maybe even a little too fast). Characters are fun and quirky with a silly story line to follow that's littered with Easter eggs. The game even sports side missions as challenges, although it should be noted the only challenge is to really just get to the end. (I haven't found a mission that challenges me to beat a time or something).The game also sports secrets hidden away in little nooks and crannies on the map. Looking through the collectibles in the menu, I can see several things grayed out. I imagine that there might be incentive to keep replaying after my first completion of the game but I'm gonna take my time getting there.Overall, I'd say if you're a fan of the 90s shooters and you like to laugh easy then Fashion Police Squad will be just the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll be the first to admit that I have an awful fashion sense. I can’t properly match colours and my style is basically using the same set of shirts over and over. But you know, I’ve never actually been able to CONFIRM that my fashion sense is awful… until I played Fashion Police Squad. Now, I can safely say I have evidence! Jokes aside, the concept of a shooter that has you helping people become more fashionable (according to societal standards anyway) fascinated me to the point I knew I had to give it a shot - and I’m really glad I did!—--Despite the joke in the first paragraph being sub-par at best, it is based on . Fashion Police Squad is an  that doesn’t take itself seriously (and is all the better for it). Words are replaced by their more fashionable counterparts (“Get your sass over here right away!”, S.W.A.G team outfit instead of S.W.A.T, etc), a gun called “2DYE-4 Elite”, a title card introducing new enemies and what fashion crime they’re committing (you can see the one for the Tourist in the steam store page pics - I can also safely say I unfortunately have committed some of those crimes myself and am currently deeply ashamed), and enemies even explode in a dance when beaten, forever thankful to you for saving them from their existence as a fashion criminal!Everything in this game revolves around fashion.  You might notice that so far, I haven’t really mentioned the story, but there’s a reason: for me, the story here serves as mostly a platform for this thematic and charm to build upon. While it’s serviceable, and , the themes are what stuck with me. And those manifest everywhere: the story, the writing, the gameplay… The game even has tons of gaming and pop culture references and parodies! This is why I mentioned that  The graphics, UI, everything is carefully crafted to convey the old school feeling, right down to the main character’s face looking left and right on the bottom of the screen, in a direct reference to DOOM. You can clearly see each enemy’s fashion crime reflected in their model, as well as their “fixed and fashionable” versions after you beat them. The soundtrack, while not very varied within each level, makes slapping (literally, thanks to a certain power up) some fashion sense into people an absolute blast.But I think when a lot of people try to get an old school shooter, the main thing they’re looking for is quality gameplay. Is the game just as good in this area? Well… not quite.  As you play through Fashion Police Squad, you unlock several weapons to aid you in your fight against unfashionable beings. As you play through the game, you also unlock several of said unfashionable beings. The thing is,  For example: the aforementioned tourist needs to be attacked with a gnome that removes his socks. Said gnome, however, deals 0 damage to a Dull Suit - the game’s first enemy type that rocks a gray suit and needs to be colorized.Effectively what this means is that, when you reach arenas, you’ll have quite a few different enemy types thrown against you, and most of your weapons (save for an end game exception) will only be effective against one or two and deal no damage to the other enemy types. This results in you having to constantly swap your arsenal around so that you can deal damage to whatever you’re facing - and if the wrong enemy type walks in front of your target, tough luck! Better reposition yourself or change weapons because that enemy will now block all damage from the weapon you were using. While this didn’t bother me much, it did become worse when combined with the level design. The thing is  One, for example, throws gas that lingers around an area. If you find that enemy in a corridor just around a corner, you might just end up having to back away and wait for the gas to clear before you can pop back around the corner and keep shooting. The gas also visually clutters the screen a bit. Now imagine yourself in a small arena full of different enemies, some of which gas part of the arena, set fire to another part, and you have to keep jumping around madly and swapping weapons while trying to avoid AOE zones… It seems fun, and it often is, but it can be very frustrating to deal with as you’re simply not left with much room to dodge or maneuver.Due to that, some rooms may feel harder than intended, but overall, playing on the second hardest difficulty, I didn’t have too much trouble - it was just challenging enough, even if some of the said challenge felt a bit frustrating because of what I mentioned above.  The most common are platforming sections that have you flying around using your belt (yep) from pole to pole and another weapon that allows you to artificially speed your character up temporarily. While I did have some problems jumping while under the effect of said weapon, in general, the platforming is pretty fun. There are also other ways the game shakes up the gameplay, but I’ll leave those as a surprise.In terms of glitches and the more technical side of things,  (or at least ran well at max settings on my system - rtx 2060, i7 8th gen, 16gb ram, nvme ssd), but I did run into a few issues. Most were pretty minor, such as doors being a bit tough to interact with if you’re right in front of them. The only more major issue I ran into was in a late game arena. In an arena, you get locked into a room with a bunch of enemies. However, on this specific occasion, I got locked OUTSIDE of said room. It was an issue because I needed to get through the room to progress, and couldn’t kill the enemies. I ended up using a late game AOE weapon to fashionize my enemies through the door, but I suspect restarting the level would also have worked (I’m lazy though and didn’t want to lose progress). All in all, I had a blast with Fashion Police Squad. I think anyone can agree that, even if the gameplay is not for them, this game is certainly not lacking in style! If what you read here seems interesting, I also have great news:  so there’s really no excuse to not check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like Fashion Police Squad. It's not a bad game by any means, but I don't think its really a game that really grabs you.I played the Demo earlier this year and I really enjoyed it. There weren't many huge changes I noticed, and you get the first 3 missions, which is pretty substantial. If you enjoy the Demo, you'll probably like the full version.I think there's a lot of good stuff in FPS, especially if you like the tongue-in-cheek campiness and sillyness. I wouldn't describe it as 'laugh out loud' funny, but it's a good lighthearted romp, and it's not super difficult either. There's a good weapon variety and they all have two different modes, and you have to use the right weapon on specific enemy types. Unfortunately, none of them feel particularly great to use, and I really don't get much of an emotional response from defeating enemies. It's not the lack of gore, but clearing even through groups of enemies isn't super satisfying. It's kind of hard to articulate unless you've played the game.The first two sets of levels send you through urban environments and they're pretty good. A good mix of long and short range combat, and wide open arenas for you to deal with groups of enemies. Unfortunately, the third chapter sends you into cramped subway tunnels, which is a real bummer unless you really like corner peaking enemies. The enemy variety is quite good, and you have to use the correct weapon to take them out. But, most of them are just medium ranged enemies that throw things at you, making them all blend together, even if you have to use different weapons on them.Fashion Police Squad doesn't exactly ignite much passion for fashion in me, which is a real shame. It's got a lot of style, good music and great tone that doesn't take itself very seriously. Unfortunately, as much as they add to the core combat loop, I think it just doesn't feel as satisfying as it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for April 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before May 7th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Finally, someone arrests people wearing Socks with Sandals. Fashion Police Squad looks like a Boomer Shooter, and it has a taste of that.  Players will end up fighting fashion crimes, whether it’s people who have been turned gray, wearing neon shirts, or ill-fitting suits.  Players will shoot them with a dye shotgun, a sewing machine gun, or sock gnomes.  It sounds insane but it’s actually quite funny with tons of great moments and it’s also well written.  I found myself laughing multiple times.At the same time, this is a humorous take on the shooter genre, but it does have some issues.  So far every enemy is only weak to a single weapon, so if you shoot someone wearing a bad suit with the dye shotgun, it does zero damage.    In addition, the difficulty here more comes from the number of enemies than specific enemies themselves, and I’m sure the absurdity of it will wear off eventually, definitely not yet, and probably will last the full first playthrough, but it feels more like a joke that’s great the first time, but you’ve heard it the second time.  Pick this up if you want a refreshing boomer shooter.  This is unique for what it is, and honestly, I feel compelled to play more of it just to see what else it’s going to do. _childDocuments_.review: Is this game stylish and unique? Yeah. It's pretty cool that way and I can tell that it's made as a labor of love. I like all the references being thrown around and the inventiveness to the the world and writing. The pixel art is also rather inspired with all sorts of little flourishes.But some gameplay in this game is janky. The platforming feels pretty good while it's just the belt grapple, but once you throw the DRIP water gun into it, yeah, I start to hate it as you lose traction and can't quite see where you're going as you aim the water at your feet and often have to cross large gaps with long run-ups while enemies chuck projectiles that can knock you out of your jump.The combat arenas also get very cluttered and visually messy. With enemies having immunity to everything but the right mode of the right weapon and spawning right on top of you most times, it can often feel annoying, particularly getting to later levels.I guess for those much more experienced with boomer shooters, this will be something with a refreshingly new palette with more of a puzzle aspect to enemy encounters, but as someone slightly more casual, honestly, I'm having a bit of trouble loving it. I find it hard to recommend in that way. For most people, I'd just watch someone play this. You can appreciate its good qualities at that distance without frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, how I wanted to enjoy this game.People loved to level the complaint that doom eternal "forces you to change weapons for enemies".I never agreed with that and found myself to get a long just fine with using whatever gun or tool felt good to use.In FPS every enemy is hard locked into only taking damage from whatever gun(s) the game wants you to use. And some of them just aren't fun.Late game has an enemy that requires you to throw 5-7 gnomes at them, wait for the gnomes to whittle down a bar of health/armor, then switch to the first rifle, use its alternate attack which is a sticky bomb, THEN hurry and attack the enemy with your rifle before the timer from the sticky bomb ends. ALL while dodging a huge mess of projectiles, aoes, and enemies bumping you on scooters and sometimes chaining you up.Not to mention the dubstep enemy which is a bulletsponge with an AOE that covers the entirety of the ground of whatever arena you're in. This enemy can only be damaged by ONE gun.Except for the rocket launcher which they give you at the end of the game almost, but then they also only dole out the ammo for it when they specifically want you to use it.If you end up buying this, don't be surprised if by level 7 or 8 out of 13, you're feeling "I'm just over this". Level design is barebones to nonexistent. The jokes are just cringy and NEVER. STOP.There's only 5 weapons. 1 is a throwable used for only 2 enemies and isn't fun to use. 1 is the rocket launcher which you don't get til the last few levels and barely get to use.Also the final boss is an absolute joke. It's not hard, not at all, but it's an absolute slog and just boring. The final boss took me about 10-15 minutes, and that's because I would have to wait for an npc to deliver me THREE ROCKETS AT A TIME. The three rockets would do about 15% of the boss' health, then I'd have to wait until the npc came back. Rinse. And. Repeat.If you played the demo last year during the steam fest, I'm not being hyperbolic when I say you've witnessed the best the game has to offer.There's sooooo many good boomer shooters available right now. Do not waste your time with this one. Do not let the immediate style fool you. Buy anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: An original revision of the now-ubiquitous boomer shooter formula. Fashion Police Squad builds on a sunny, blithe atmosphere with plenty of memes, jokes, and trendy fads thrown in, as opposed to the usual dark, horroresque setting of its peers.The gameplay is, perhaps, the best part of the game. Each weapon and tool at player's disposal can only hurt specific enemies, which are weak to it, arranging a complex rock-paper-scissors ruleset to follow. It takes some time to memorise and get used to the weapons and the enemies that they counter, which leaves you rifling through your weapon menu mid-fight, while at the same time dodging dozens of projectiles; because of this, it gets quite hard later on even on lower difficulties.Sadly, the game is incredibly short at 16 levels total, and can be beaten in just about 4 hours, and also feels a bit low on content overall.Otherwise, Fashion Police Squad is a fairly worthwhile experience.

Plenty of grade a cheese to go around in the setting, enemies, and dialogue. Fun stuff.Biggest complaint is some truly frustrating platforming sections in a first person shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Just adding a note after  finishing the game, my thoughts are largely the same, but I'll say that things do get even better as the game progresses, especially the music and levels, the final boss was really fun too, with its only fault being that his twist required a quick text tutorial halfway through.Only played a few missions so far but I decided to make a review after Mission 8's boss.It's a really fun shooter, the gameplay is genuinely great, there aren't a lot of guns but they all feel pretty unique and one even plays into movement in a fun way, movement feels really nice during fights and thanks to the design of areas and the enemies I'd say that moving around feels better than in games like BLOOD. Enemies are fun to fight and encounters are pretty well thought out when it comes to the mix of enemies you face at any given time.Now what made me really love the game, was its humour and presentation, and Mission 8's boss sealed the deal, the game is pretty absurd as far as setting, plot and humour goes, it's very unapologetic about the writing it has, it's a constant stream of references and absurdist humour that is rare for me to enjoy but that really worked for me here due to the way the game's presented, the  character sprites really sell all the enemies and their fashion crimes, the locations are varied and look lived in, the sound design's pretty good, the mob's dialogue is pretty funny and the music's pretty nice.The only real downsides so far were a couple of bugs that had no impact on gameplay, and using the belt to swing around the map can sometimes be annoying because of slight bumps completely ruining the swing. But overall, it's a pretty fun game, fairly unique too despite the saturation of the "boomer shooter" market.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying this game is fantastic!  Probably one of the most unique FPS games I've played in a long time as far as the theme goes.  Fashion Police Squad is a very vibrant game full of memes, funny villains, terrible puns and god tier style.  It controls well, and plays smooth and fast paced.  The enemies get progressively stronger throughout the game, and beware the Karen, she will be back, and in greater numbers.On a technical level the game overall runs great being a doom-esque clone style shooter, the characters are well animated in pixel style and the weapons feel good to use.  The only criticism I have is there's a bit of a rendering issue when travelling fast using the belt whip between buildings on the 2nd set of levels, though I was lucky enough to have the Dev visit my twitch stream who confirmed they are releasing patches for little bits like that so this will probably not be an issue now.Overall, this game is fast, fun, colourful and has a fantastic grasp of humour making it an absolute delight to play.  Add all that to a fantastic low price and you have an absolute gem.  Get it in your steam library now!

_childDocuments_.review: genuinely great time with some fun mechanics. It's worth the money, even if most of what I did enjoy was just the humor and overall sense that the developers had a good time making this. with that said, the game does have problems, mainly with the combat. It feels great initially, but as it expands and introduces mroe guns and enemies thinks start to become pretty grating from a nice little challenge to a bit of a slow drudge, until it finally ends up being sadly a slog to get through, especially the mission before the final boss when there are just so many enemies packed into an area that the only solution is your fake rocket launcher. Trying to outmaneuver enemies or just trying to be better at avoiding attacks just turns into deal with more enemies faster simply because it's an impossibility  to be able to avoid all of them. There was even a bug with the ||gimp suit enemies with whip chains|| where trying to use your grappling belt to swing around would force the nearest enemy of that type to teleport in front of the belt in the air cancelling it out. This sadly makes the game at it's best when you aren't actually in a traditional fashion fight and instead is worth it more for the boss fights, special level segments and the comedic writing. Platforming as well wasn't as well thought out as I'd hoped and instead was simple platform hops with a "run" introduced later and a grapple that acts more as a spacer for the platforms.Overall worth your time, lots of creative things to love about the game but not enough of that same thought put into polishing and refining their gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom but its running on LGBTQ+ engine. Since the last Steam Next Fest, i have played over 40 demos and this game outshined a lot of them. I have been excitedly waiting for the day it gets released and i'm really glad to say that it really delivered. Fashion Police Squad is a brilliant and fresh take on retro shooters. In it, instead of mindlessly killing people, you have weapons to fix peoples fashion crimes. Each gun has a different use case and because of that, the weapons don't feel stale to use. It has one of the best pixel arts i have ever seen in a game and the environments, characters compliment it beautifully. The story is not really memorable and some might find the writing cringy but i really think you will realize how much it suits the game itself. Though the game is mainly a shooter, it is also a really solid platformer. Each level ups the ante bit by bit and thanks to the creativeness and uniqueness of most mechanics, the game just keeps getting better.  I have almost nothing bad to say except i had some fps drops in my playthrough that didn't necessarily break my immersion.  The game is short but super sweet since it has no fillers. I'm really looking forward to other projects this team puts out. I think this game is well worth the price you pay.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the first six missions, it's safe to say this game is an absolute banger as Des would say!This game is full of great humour, but I like that it's not the only thing it has to offer. The gameplay is very snappy and smooth which makes busting fashion criminals extra satisfying. There are some really creative enemies here, and I especially like the bullet hell type of dodging mechanics that they have implemented on a first person shooter with great success.My biggest gripe with these kinds of games is usually the difficulty being too easy, but I feel like after playing on the second hardest difficulty the challenge feels just right. I'm not steamrolling through the levels too easily, but also not getting frustrated stuck in the same spot for an hour. I will definitely have a second playthrough after this one on the hardest difficulty though. I also like that there are a lot of design choices here done with speedrunners in mind!There are a couple things that I didn't like and some missed opportunities with the weapons and enemies here and there, but no major complaints so far. This game really performs above what I expected going into it.This game costs less than a pair of designer socks and has a lot more swag, so I would definitely recommend giving it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to like that one, but i wasn't convinced, despite some good, interesting ideas. First of all, there's the obvious: the unique setting, universe and concept of "fashionizing" enemies instead of killing them. Then there's the combat: you can't use any gun you want on any enemy, you gotta choose the right tool for the right foe. While it's a cool gimmick during the early fights, i don't think it holds up really well in the long run. Because the devs wanted you to play in an overly specific way, there's absolutely NO versatility in there.  For that reason, i don't think there's much replayability either, and there aren't much secrets to be found anyway.And i can see the Doom Eternal crowd come and bring the good old  back up... but i completed the campaign on the hardest difficulty so i think i actually could, in fact, get used tot he gameplay and master it.  Somehow, i think that the "very hard mode" is what ruined it for me. I can think of a dozens of situations when a lighter difficulty would have made things much more fun and less of a hassle. So if you end up getting it anyway, i advise you to stick to "hard" mode (or whatever its in-game name is). That could mean less bullet-sponges, and less annoyingly unfair encounters.Would that be enough to redeem the whole game? I'm genuinely not sure. Fashion Police Squad has some of the most obnoxious and pesky enemies i've ever encountered in a boomer shooter. That's probably done on purpose but it really got on my nerves, and you can't get rid of this. Same for the constant rhythm-breaking narration through dialogue pop-ups. Sometimes, the NPCs don't even have anything relevant to say, they just interrupt you to tell something like . Speaking of this, F.P.S. is barely enjoyable to roam. It holds your hand way too much through bland boring levels. I can think of a few surprisingly good platforming parts. Same for a few specific mini-games. 2 out of 3 bosses were also nice. Alas, even if it has its moments, FPS don't shine often enough to earn a positive review in my opinion. Aside from those few parts, the rest was often drudgery to me. My review may sound harsh to some but it's not exactly a bad shooter, you can give it a try if it's on sale or if you got it the monthly Humble Bundle. But otherwise? I wouldn't put it in the boomer shooter priority list.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those classic shooter games that nobody asked for, but needed to play!PROS: fun and imaginative twist on boomer shooter design; quirky and creative presentation; fast-paced; amazing selection of "weapons"; top tier humorCONS: some platforming was a pain in the assCONCLUSION: All in all, Fashion Police Squad is a fairly humorous parody of internet and video game culture, wrapped up in an entertaining boomer shooter package. It confidently showcases smart game design knowledge with its sharp controls and engaging gameplay. You’ll chuckle at its dialogue, be thrilled with its gameplay, and take glee in fixing fashion errors that may cause you genuinely to roll your eyes in real life. Who’d have thought making your enemies stylish could be so much fun?
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is what you would get if contestants of Ru Paul's Drag Race were tasked with creating a new Duke Nukem game and someone overachieved that assignment. The hilarity of the theme was expected, but I'm most pleasantly surprised by how good this strafefest feels to play. To top that off, everything is just juicy, impactful, and stylish on the audiovisual side. FPS (I see what you did there) manages to feel both retro and fresh, forcing the player to not just blast away but employ the full arsenal of fashion weaponry. While repetitive at times, the game flows nicely into the next humorous story point and presents you with new enemy types. Simply fresh & chic!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A very wacky and non-violent FPS with plenty of cloth-related puns to go around.The game had me chuckle quite a lot at some of the puns and jokes going around as well as keep me on my toes with just how intense the combat can get with the various badly dressed perps act as they're introduced along with new gameplay mechanics to spice things up.Highly recommend it if you're looking for something that's a lot more lighthearted and non-violent than what you usually see in FPS games.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fun concept, great style, but by the final 1/3 of the game, the enemy encounters become unbearable slogs. So much of the combat encounter design sets you up to take gobs of unavoidable damage, then "apologizes" afterwards with health drops to build you back up.Having to switch weapons to deal with different enemy types is a potentially interesting idea, but in practice, it literally ruins the game by the end. Being swarmed by different enemy types in a tiny space (like a rooftop) creates situations where you're simply trying to race against your unavoidable health drain.If there were better defensive options to help with crowd control while switching through the different weapons, then it might have worked. As it is, it doesn't.Play the demo, that's by far the best part of the game. If you're insistent on playing the full game, stick with a lower difficulty, even if you're usually an "Ultra Violence" FPS difficulty player.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a lot of fun, but can at times get brutally punishing with enemy combinations in the latter half of the game. At twenty bucks, this is a steal, and overall won me over with the game's sense of humor, charm, action, and really well-designed boss battles. Overall a winner, but I'd recommend playing on a lower difficulty at first to get the hang of the weapon juggling before pushing into something more punishing. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Oh the common thread that is people complaining about gameplay loops being too hard despite the arsenal you're presented with during the late game. It's Doom Eternal all over again, lol.Stop throwing away your rockets and take advantage of the fact that you can clear dozens of fashion crimes at once with them. Utilize that sweet whip to escape from the scooter bros constantly pummeling you. Know which weapon to switch to and which targets to prioritize, etc. Boomer shooter 101. Are we really still complaining about games being too hard? Come on...In short, get good.6.9 hours in and the story has been bested. Game was amazing and hit all the necessary spots. I'm looking forward to 100% completion of the game and thoroughly enjoyed how much effort was put into it. The demo had me worried the gameplay would fizzle quickly but it kept delivering and kept me wanting more. Although it ended too abruptly, I'm still looking forward to revisiting levels and secret/achievement hunting the levels all over again. Game absolutely shreds with style and class. Wonderful change of pace to the average boomer shooters that have been dropping.

_childDocuments_.review: + Good, over-the-top humor* Story with text-only dialogue- Too much mixed enemy variety with need for dedicated, necessary weaponry and skills (quickly became too much)Personally, I disliked the text-only dialogue, and the the variety and necessary weapon and skill management, remembering, and swapping quickly became cumbersome and annoying - and even more so after not playing for a while, you have to remember again or try and re-learn.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Initial premise and ideas are very clever and funny, the first few levels are very charming and fun but later on it isn't nearly as fun.But late to mid game it drags on way too much, and even all the charm in the world can't save it from being annoying.-Inconsistent platforming, especially with the whip, this gets super annoying later on-The guns are all fun when you get them but later on switching between 5 guns to find the one gun YOU NEED is so annoying and tedious-Later game spams so many enemies, especially really annoying ones, the Gimps who prevent you from using your whip with levels designed with it in mind and chainstun you-You get a really OP rocket later on but it kept clipping on geometry and wasnt very usefulThe demo when I played it was so much fun, the first few levels are but It's so boring and annoying later on and it saddens me because I love the premise, humour and characters. I think im on the final level, the boat and I just can't complete this, it's no fun at all.If any of this interests you try it for an hour or close to two and if you feel like it's not as fun or it's beginning to frustrate you dip out and refund it imo, or buy it on a big sale.

Check.* Damaged by the only weapon with limited ammo?  Check.* Drops for ammo are random?  Check.* Attacks are quick and difficult to avoid?  Check.* Health drops are also random?  Check.It's like they forgot they were trying to make a fun parody of boomer shooters and decided to punish anyone who stuck around to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: - The main game loop of having to switch weapons on the fly to accommodate to criminal's needs never got stale. I had a blast trying to parse out all the different enemies in an encounter and strategize my priorities and everything.- The movement in this game is really fun. The belt grappling hook is fun to use, and the water gun—despite taking some time to get used to—was really fluid to use.- This game is hilarious. Simple as that.- Encounters in this game felt like they were just the right difficulty. Sure, I died sometimes, but it was never enough to make me get frustrated . I played on the second hardest difficulty, for those curious.- Surprisingly, the over the top and almost amateur voice lines never got old. They really add a lot of character to the game and I don't think I'd quite enjoy it as much without them. There is an option to disable them if you get tired of them, though.- The small platforming sections in some levels are well designed and fun to go through.- The characters are all enjoyable; from the main characters to even the enemies.- Sock Gnomes feel almost shoe-horned in as a weapon. I never really enjoyed using them, aside from maybe throwing them at the music person to ruin their beat drop.- The Fab-Slap, as funny as it is, always feels like you get it in scripted places. It almost takes some of the magic out of it when you're suddenly faced with like 50 enemies but you just so happened to get 100% fab moments before.- Overall Rating: 8/10 (Great)

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like about Fashion Police Squad, but to me, there's equally as many things to dislike as well. I was going to go on a huge rant and list the extensive list of bad points about the game, but then I realized that I would also have to list the equally long list of good points about the game (to give a fair review), so I won't be doing that; it would take too much time in a written steam review.I'm still giving a cautious positive recommendation because the game clearly had a lot of effort put into it and it is polished. And also, the lead designer is clearly an OG who has played many of the different classics (even from different media), as evident in the many references imbued in its gameplay, writting, art and even sound and music. So you've gotta respect that repertoire and influences.Just be aware that this is not a traditional FPS (for better AND for worse), it is more of a "gimmick" humorous niche game where the core gameplay plays second fiddle to the main thematic and narrative, and to be honest those 2 elements got old rather quickly because when every little thing is a nod or reference or pun (no matter how clever or funny those are) it gets overwhelming. It is a unique experience for sure, but it rapidly overstays its welcome and those 5 hours to complete the game went on for longer than I had hoped. Get it on a deep sale and see it for yourself; by the 2 hour refund mark you'll have a decent idea of what the game is all about.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of like a family-friendly Doom Eternal, you'll find yourself having to use red guns on red baddies and blue guns on blue baddies time after time, especially in later areas where you're locked into arenas with waves of spawning enemies.I regret playing on Hard, it was fine for the earlier levels but around level 10 it became a considerable struggle to keep advancing. You have a fixed amount of health per area outside of pickups and there's no way to come back from low HP, like in Doom Eternal. You just have to not get hit. This wasn't helped by readability issues: guns and fire effects taking up a large amount of the screen often made it difficult to tell what I was shooting at which is a very critical element for the 'Simon Says' nature of this game.That all said I enjoyed my time with Fashion Police Squad. The protagonist, Des, is genuinely funny and likeable in a sort of dorky himbo kind of way, and it managed to be pretty consistently funny at times, even though some of the jokes were just terribly groan-worthy. Like a Power Glove joke in 2024? Come on. If you're like me and you play basically anything that looks like a boomer shooter, you'll get a few hours of enjoyment out of this, but its contemporaries like Forgive Me, Father, Dusk and Ultrakill do outshine it slightly.One final thing I wanted to touch on that isn't bad or good, it's just weird: 90% of this game you could give to a child to play, there's no blood and enemies aren't killed, and there's only a little risque humour... but then in the final few levels gimps and flashers turn up which was just weird to me? I'm not a prude or anything but it just confused me lol

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Video review: The genre, which many like to call "Boomer Shooter", has never been as vibrant as it is now. And vibrant is the watchword when playing Fashion Police Squad for the first time, which despite being an FPS doesn't have any gore elements, nor will the objective be to finish with the species that are on the other side of the barricade. A title that is full of references, not only to titles that made this genre so beloved, such as Duke Nuken, but also to films like The Wolf of Wall Street, or to Drag elements such as the highly acclaimed Death Drop, when the game is charging and even when pressing the special skill button and even the finger snaps from Nintendo Direct showcases. This was one of the cases that caught my attention on Twitter for its creative and colorful side in terms of presentation but also in terms of gameplay. It's noticeable that the Mopeful Games studio put a lot of time and attention into every detail during the adventure. While the story isn't the deepest, every line of text lets the characters' personalities shine through, and there's even drama to keep things spicy.The player will take on the role of Sergeant Des, a policeman dedicated to fighting the wave of fashion crimes that is ravaging the city. The streets are full of people who have various problems in terms of their clothing, which, yes, are present in our daily lives and which, among them, are multiplied by examples of tourists wearing sandals and white socks (please don't do this), clothes that are too tight, the Karens of this life, &c. After playing this game I will keep an eye out for these situations! Watch me!As I mentioned there are no moments of gore or any kind of violence. Well... there are times when it is possible for us to throw a good b*tch slap in the face of clothing aggressors, however, all weapons are somehow related to fashion and affect specific enemies. The 2-Dye-4 Elite gun is perfect for solving crimes of monotony of colors against the gray suits of businessmen who throw suitcases at us, but it is completely harmless against, for example, bigger cases and when I say bigger I mean in terms of stature, since there are lockers (gym bros) in suits that don't fit the shoulders in the best way. In this case, Tailormade will be called to the noise to mend the stitches of a once-giant suit. All weapons have a different but very intuitive flow from the first contact with them. It should be noted that the water weapon makes it possible to wet not only enemies but also the ground and thus make the character move faster. This is a viable option for traversing the map faster, but it also makes it easier to reach platforms further away.I found myself often looking for the right button to pull the right weapon to fight the fashion crime that was in front of me. Yes, because playing in Hard mode is not easy at all. I had to repeat several sections as they were filled with waves of enemies that seemed endless. At certain times there is a need to cross the level again in the opposite direction. Not being exactly the same thing, since the enemies presented in a second round may even be different from the previous case, but there was a need to do so to add some game time to a level that seemed to be small.When it comes to level design, the colorful maps, which get more interesting as the story progresses, invite your exploration and become even more interesting due to the amount of secrets hidden in each corner and that reward the player with a poster of the character dressed in very special ways. What about a He-Man or a Harry Potter in a fashion game?Whether you understand fashion, whether you're a fan of Pop Culture elements, or on the other hand you don't understand any of these subjects, Fashion Police Squad manages to grab the player for the fun of its easy-to-recommend gameplay and still delivers a few laughs in between.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lovely take on the classic Boomer Shooter in a very "Yass queen slay" kind of way. Had this came out back in the day of Doom's original inception, it may have been seen as the Weenie Hut Jr. of Doom games, but what you'll find in this game is a colorful world full of fashion, fighting, and fun. This genre is not typically a game I would play, and playing at Hard in an attempt to prove something to myself, I definitely found myself whelmed by everything coming at me. Regardless, I was having fun in the chaos of it all, correcting fashion crimes the entire way. The writing is witty, and more than worthy of an audible nose exhale of humor. _childDocuments_.review: I first saw this game back in 2020 and was really, really excited to play it. The devs were posting it on Reddit and I was so hooked by it. Now that it's been two years and I've finally had the chance to play it, I would say that it's worth picking up, but it's definitely got some problems I'm surprised made it in the final release.The good news is that it IS fun. There are lots of puns and references to catch. The art style is clean and readable all the time. The bosses are really creative and have several phases. They are definitely a standout to me. The guns and enemy variety is good too, for the game's length, and really show how committed this team was to this goofy concept. The only real downsides are minor, but they're easily remembered when it's a relatively short game that's largely banking on the idea of the game, not so much the mechanics themselves.I had some annoying visual bugs during a platforming section (whole sections of the map would flicker, or disappear completely), which was already a low point in the game to me because the platforming felt a little under cooked. I kept falling straight through the platforms I was supposed to be landing on. It restarts you back several platforms too (not the one you just jumped from, but like three or so platforms back) which is incredibly irritating and I can't imagine why it's like that. The platforming almost always requires you to spray the ground with water and use it as a boost which means if there are several platforms, you have to constantly stop and spray the ground. I get the idea and I think it can work for some locations, but nearly ALL the platforming does this and it just absolutely kills the pacing.You also have to swap weapons CONSTANTLY. This may bother some people.Some QOL features could be implemented. Like, how about letting me turn off all dialogue for levels I've already completed instead of making me rapid fire jam the E key. Let me turn off all tips. That kind of stuff.Some areas toward the end absolutely overwhelm you with how many enemies there are. I was really shocked at how aggressive and challenging some of these little moments were. And you may restart fairly far back, which can be a huge bummer. I guess it isn't too much of a complaint, but more of an observation. Because I fully expected the game to be a breeze from start to finish.Either way, yeah it's a fun game. I feel like you sort of know if you'd like this game or not just from the concept and a short video.

_childDocuments_.review: So to be perfectly honest I don't like picking a thumbs up or thumbs down for this one, but if I had to pick I guess I'd prefer to stay on the positive side. I've not finished this game as of writing, but I've played enough that I feel hard pressed to say my thoughts on it will change by experiencing *more* of it. Fashion Police Squad is charming, it's got a vibrantly self indulgent personallity and a sense of humor so *eh* it almost makes me chuckle. The game itself is fine in concept and it plays well enough to be... palletable... but that's about it.Everything in Fashion Police Squad is *almost* good. Weapons *almost* feel good, movement *almost* feels good,The visuals *almost* look good,The gameplay is *almost* fun. But the entire experience reeks of a lack of polish that it desperately needs. It's difficult to put into words but everything is just *slightly* off in a way that makes the entire experience difficult for me to enjoy. It gets an A for effort, and like... a C- bordering on a D for execution.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an underrated gem of a game. If you found this on your own, you struck gold. _childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique 'boomer shooters' I've played. The fashion puns and theme can be a bit over the top, but that's part of the charm. I found myself genuinely laughing at some of the bizarre enemies and situations. The soundtrack is sufficiently retro, and punctuates the fights well. The guns are all solid-feeling, the movement is surprisingly good, and the game can be beaten in easily 8-9 hours on the middle difficulty, and 100 percent completed in 10-11. _childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is filled to the brim with fashion, style, and creativity in almost every aspect of the game. This was a complete joy to play through. Some of my personal highlights are.Presentation has so much personality and charm. The world is well thought out when it comes to it's main idea revolting around fashion. Everyone's life is full of fashion choices and design. This is reflected on some details like the billboards advertising certain trends of meme, and clothing. Whole companies are designed around a certain martial and style, which is really nice. The enemies you fight in this game are based around super ugly fashion trends and bad choices. Like socks and sandals, dull business suits, weird things and such. You can even fight Karens that complain to you the entire time which is just wonderful :) The pixel art and world graphics blend in with each other really nice and even work together with one another to create great visuals. The music is also really high energy to suit the absurd nature of it all. Sound effects every time you deal with the un-fashionable and some of the weapons are so satisfying and rewarding to the ear.The boss fights in this game are super creative, have super fun  gimmick, and their design in terms of fashion really does a good job in what to expect of that said boss. For example you get to fight a loser discord moderator. Now take this and imagine some of the stereotypes that center around that, and chances are, you know what the boss fight will look like. Super awesome design.Now for some of the things I thought were pretty in the middle.Level design is a mixed bag. On one side, you get levels that greatly paced, visual variety and surprises. Alongside awesome set pieces that are creative and add on to the fashion world. But on the other side of the bag, you get the subway levels which are super tight, cramped, and a barrage of foes in a artificial way. These levels don't create a good game play loop at all. And or some are bland that they don't really add on to the world and absurd adventure. Also from time to time, there will be some platforming  sections sprinkled through out the adventure. I personally liked them because they created variety from the shooting action. However sometimes, it's really easy to overshoot you landing on small and narrow platforms. Something to just note on.The weapons you get through out the game are pretty normal, but with the fashion flare and absurdity that is super great. But you have to use certain weapons against certain foes in order to defeat them. You can't mix match the weapons you want to use. I personally feel this is a pretty artificial way to create combat variety. There could be other ways to better this such as gimmicky arena design, and or special hit boxes or elements of the world. They kinda do this with fire hydrants to make you're first weapon stronger for a small amount of ammo. They should be more of this rather then selective weapons for selective foes. The only thing thing that I don't like about the game is the way they handle special challenge levels. out of the three challenge levels, two of them are bland, boring gimmicks, short, and out of place with how it was put together.  However, the last challenge level is fantastic, thrilling, and well...challenging. I wish the other challenge levels took the same approach but add in new ideas and gimmicks in the mix. The last challenge level certainly have great foundations for future challenge levels with great ideas waiting to happen.Overall if you are looking for a family friendly shooter with plenty of fashion charm, awesome presentation, creative bosses,  good level design (most of the time), and fun ideas, this is certainly a game for you. If you look through the screenshots of the game and don't like the fashion tone of it, chances you won't like it, since the game entire identity centers around the latest fashion trends. But other then that, this is a super great and humorous time to be had. I would personally give this game a 8/ 10. It would be closer to a 7, rather then a 9. This game is short, but never over stays it's welcome. A stylish game for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr- recommended with caveats- the general premise for the game is great, but the execution in places leaves more to be desired, and at worst, is frustrating. while i will expand on the negatives below, i still generally enjoyed my time with the game and look forward to what comes next from this developer.** i do want to note that the devs are currently patching the game to address many of the things i complain about below. since i have 100%ed the game already, though, i am unlikely to revisit this game again any time soon to confirm which of my issues below have been addressed, especially since this is already a 'recommended' review **level design is unremarkable (with a few exceptions) and fairly sloppy. there are a few different locations, and they all make heavy use of modular assets. i want to clarify that i think there is no harm using prefabs/modular assets, especially as a smaller indie team with a limited budget, so long as things don't feel copy/pasted often. things did feel copy/pasted often though. a lot of this is noticeable because assets don't line up, there is z-fighting, you can see/fall into the void, or you see the unrendered insides of assets. i normally don't care much about these things, but it was so common i started to notice it more and more.difficulty balancing is all over the place. some levels and encounters are ridiculously easy, while others account for 90% of my deaths and required my to grind/save up for a super skill to get through. the main issue with difficulty was limiting player movement in tight spaces with a lot of enemies and/or enemies who have attacks that are near impossible to avoid in a small space (karen gas cloud, for instance). i think part of why enemy encounters in games like doom and quake work so well is down to the positioning and choice of which enemies to combine in an encounter. it doesn't feel like the same attention to detail was utilized in the majority of the encounters for fashion police squad.negatives aside, i really liked the premise of the game. it definitely fills a void in the "boomer shooter" "retro fps" market and gives visibility to characters and ideas mostly unexplored otherwise. the colors are bright, there is some charm to the story, and the character art in particular is well done. i appreciated some of the movement mechanics too (even if i found them a bit inconsistent) like the belt of justice for swinging and the wet'ones for increased ground movement speed. in summation, i think some of my late game frustrations have unfortunately colored what was, for the majority of the game, an enjoyable experience. recommended if you play every new retro-styled fps or you are looking for something a bit different and you have some patience.

_childDocuments_.review: Among the flood of titles in the current boomer-shooter renaissance, we have Fashion Police Squad. This yassified version of Doom sure has style in spades, but is almost completely devoid of substance.As Sergeant Des of the Fashion Police Squad, your task is to rid Trendopolis of heinous fashion crimes. To this end, you'll use a variety of weapons and gadgets, such as a color sprayer that can liven up even the dullest gray suit, a sewing machine gun to combat those baggy fits, sock gnomes that will devour offensive footwear, or a water gun that will cool off even Guy Fieri's signature fiery outfits.This setup serves as a solid basis for a retro shooter. As such, the "combat chess" mechanics are on full display here - after the tutorial, you'll regularly have to fight groups of enemies, dodging and weaving to avoid incoming damage while strategically deciding who to take out first.It's a shame, then, that this aspect of the game isn't all that well thought out. While the combat is pretty solid, with fluid movements and snappy controls, it lacks the creativity and problem-solving prevalent in actual retro shooters. Each enemy can only be defeated by one specific weapon, with later, more complex, enemies having two or more health bars, where each has to be whittled down separately.Also, there's no sense of experimentation and discovery where you find a new weapon and have to figure out how to use it effectively - each is just given to you at the exact moment you find a new enemy type.The game also features extended platforming segments, as a way to mix up the flow between fighting sequences. However, figuring out the timing can be pretty tricky, making these segments more frustrating than fun.The pixel graphics are simple but effective, with the appropriate amount of effort given to details to ensure environments don't feel dull. The cinematics are done in a comic book style, with character outfits and poses clearly inspired by Jojo's Bizarre Adventure (which, in turn, was inspired by fashion magazines of the time, so I guess we've come full circle). The music and sound design are serviceable for this type of game, but nothing to write home about.So I guess the final question is: what does this game actually want to be? The shooting and platforming are solid, but not great. The graphics and sound are serviceable, if unremarkable. There is barely a plot, with the script relying heavily on lame puns, outdated references, and clunky dialogue to get by. And finally, the vibe is a bit off - it feels like the creators have a genuine understanding of fashion and style, but the game has a watered-down satirical tone where you're not sure if they're being sarcastic or earnest.The way I see it, either go fully down the boomer-shooter route, where we don't care about the plot, but the shooting and platforming are polished to perfection, or pick a lane for the story (satirical or earnest) and focus on that, while leaving the mechanics solid, but not spectacular. The way it is, Fashion Police Squad is stuck dangling in the middle, like an ill-fitting suit no one wants to pick off the rack.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine. Mediocre and average, which isn't a bad thing, but it's also not a good thing. The humor is fun but not laugh at loud, the aesthetic of the graphics is great but for a game about fashion, the levels are incredibly bland. There are also very, very few guns and their only use is based on the type of fashion adjustment an enemy needs. It's a new little puzzle mechanic.You may still like the game. I'm definitely not slamming it or hating on it. I just found it dull, repetitive, and easy even on the hardest mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with Fashion Police Squad. Loved the FM Synth inspired soundtrack, the way it forces you to weave between weapons, the movement with the belt. My only criticisms I have is that the level design is a bit on the basic side, and that ammo management is non-existent for most of the arsenal. Other than that I had a great time, and I recommend it to all.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I really dig this project but a couple of aspects set it back. Distinguishing enemies in crowded areas is a big one. The one weapon per enemy combat is a tough cookie as it cuts versatility. Perhaps have the wrong weapons do less damage rather than none at all.? I'm not sure how to fix it, but those are the two that stick out. Will stay updated as game improves or stagnates. Rocknroll cheers
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the most unique shooters I've ever played.The game's main appeal obviously is its art style and humourous story, but on the hardest difficulty many encounters can be more challenging than its lightheartedness may suggest. Couple that with a great soundtrack and a more than fair price and you've got yourself an amazing game!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Every so often a game comes along in a genre that upsets the apple cart and does something truly new. In the shooter space, that is a little rarer than in others. Fashion Police Squad is one of those rarities.On the surface, it looks like your typical linear story blastathon. But dig a little deeper and you'll find one of the coolest single-player shooters of the year. It's got great level design, clever writing, and enough dad jokes to keep you laughing over the course of the game. The mechanics are a nice mixture of everything from Bulletstorm to Bionic Commando. Save for one or two frustrating horde moments, I rather enjoyed my time with this one. If you love the FPS genre and want something different than the old school 90s kill everything experience, or the contemporary army themes and battle royale games popular today, check it out. Everything about it feels new, and it makes what should seem like a one note sight gag work really well over the course of a substantial campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the main story for this today and thoroughly enjoyed it, start to finish.Great sense of humour that doesn't take itself too seriously, fun gameplay with combat and light platforming that I never got bored of, really REALLY great music, references and easter eggs throughout and a good variety of levels that didn't drag on too long.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game really surprised me. I genuinely didn't think a game could be this goofy and fun at the same time. The gameplay reminds me almost of classic Doom while having its own twists on it. The point of the graphics aren't supposed to be 'OMG THIS LOOKS SO GOOD', its supposed to look retro. As I said, they give off the classic Doom vibe.The story was great. There were moments when I genuinely did not expect some things to happen. The pseudo-final boss was also excellent, it had really great mechanics while also being easter-egg heavy and goofy. The soundtrack, while not notable, was still great. I honestly think people should check this game out, it is a hidden gem.

_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute delight and I cannot recommend it enough. Absolutely dripping with style and personality, that the small kinks here and there can honestly be pretty easily ignored.Coupled with the fact that the baseline idea of having to use different weapons depending on the enemies is so much fun, I cannot wait to go back through and 100% this game. My genuine only small complaint was that there was a slightly big difficulty spike towards the end of the game (mission 11), and bear in mind I was playing on the 2nd hardest difficulty.Overall though, this game is covered from head to toe in queer culture, camp, and sheer stupid fun that it had me laughing several times, just from how much genuine fun the game was and how it very clearly wasn't taking itself super seriously.Cannot recommend enough. You owe it to yourselves.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: The train levels and the boss that followed left me feeling mind-fabbed to the point of exhaustion. 10/10, would be whiplashed by meme fashion to the point of cerebral malfunction again.Edit: Having finished this game I can officially state it is a fabulous masterpiece with no flaws whatsoever. Negative reviews were filtered by the difficulty and refused to swallow their pride and switch to easy mode, or the game just wasn't their cup of tea, in which case - fair enough.Buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Slight recommendation. Main issue is the first person platforming. It's not very comfortable and slightly missing a jump is frustrating. The belt swinging mechanic is good but it's easy to make a mistake. Long jumps are another problem area where you'll probably miss a few. The platforming doesn't get any better by the end. I was annoyed with the game many times.Also, the game becomes challenging by adding more projectiles which would be fine but they stick you in these really tiny arenas with no where to go. So good luck dodging everything. This is less of a problem and the enemies are interesting since they all have a unique way to defeat them. But with switching weapons so much it can feel like you had no choice but fail.This isn't like other first person shooters and one one hand that's great because we need something different. On the other hand it sometimes feels like the developer didn't take any of the important lessons from them either. Still, it's has good shooting and the humor is pretty good. I didn't get tired of it but that's very subjective. There are a lot of memes so be warned of that.I liked it enough to finish it and it's an interesting short game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: "I fell into the flames... and bounced back!"I love the way this game does comedy; most comedy games I play typically do the "stand-up routine approach," where you listen to funny characters go on as you experience standard gameplay. In this game a lot of the big laughs come from the little things. Its hard to describe, but the game knows when NOT to be funny in some ways. The enemies you fight don't tell jokes, but they're intentionally cheesy and over-the-top in a way that makes me giggle.Gameplay wise, Doom Eternal is clearly the biggest influence. Here though, its ride or die. Every enemy has a very specific weakness. It really depends on what you're looking for in the gameplay. If you're into freeform player expression (finding a favorite weapon or an unconventional approach to a problem), you will be dissapointed. HOWEVER I personally enjoy a highly tailored encounter. Combat is less "which weapon do I use" and more "where do I go, and who do I take out first". By no means would I consider it mindless.Lastly I have to hand it to some of these bossfights. FPS games used to be infamous for godawful bossfights but more and more these days I've been seeing exceptions to that rule. These recent boomer shooters, with over-the-top movement, weapons, and enemies, certainly lend themselves better to fun, personality-fueled bossfights then the gloomy shooters of older decades.These DJ enemies tho.... I'm sure the pro players will tell me to get good at the game, but boy do I hate them. They're not even voice acted either so they were especially disappointing!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I truly enjoyed this retro styled first person shooter that has an emphasis on the comedy and having the right weapon to solve any fashion faux pas from a multitude of enemies. There are so many fashion puns and references/nods to other games to at least bring a smile with the cheeky writing and voice/sound design. Fashion Police Squad also introduces new mechanics throughout the game that does not overstay its welcome, from a turret section with drab suits on flying boards and long limousines to a fashion sniping session to correct guests' fashion disasters.There's a lot of secrets to find throughout the game to unlock, so it encourages some replay of the levels to find it all that will unlock more outfits and visual treats. That being said, the platforming is a hit or miss as it requires some finesse with a certain weapon in order to progress. Each level will progress in adding more enemies to an arena to encourage movement and prioritize your arsenal (the belt whip will get a lot of use to keep opponents at bay). There are challenge levels as well to test your mettle.In addition, the music is very catchy and fits the mood of the game very well. The audio is very top notch with some endearing low quality voice lines from some enemies to give them character. The announcer letting you know when you have stylized your enemies is also a cherry on top of this cake. Boss fights are very distinct and memorable too! This all comes to a head for the end of a level where you get to see all the defeated foes strutting their stuff on a walkway.Fashion Police Squad is not a long game, but it was a welcome addition to my library that leaves quite a fashionable impression, which has been missing from the retro first person shooter genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty unique concept for an FPS. Rather than killing people, you need to fix their awful fashion, for example, coloring in a grey suit or fixing someone awful hair-do. It was pretty fun for a few hours but honestly the weapon switch mechanic really annoyed me and I wasn't able to finish the game past level 9. I may come back to this game at a later point.I'd still recommend playing it, but just know that some of the later gunfights can be quite disorienting, when several enemy types are attacking you and you need to switch to the correct weapon type in order to even deal damage to them.Lastly, even though I find the concept unique, these type of games are ALWAYS better when there is some blood & gore and unfortunately, this game has none of it.Final rating: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favorite game of 2022. The game mechanics are a real breath of fresh air. Each enemy can only take damage from a specific weapon. Some enemies take two different weapons in a certain sequence to defeat them. The result is an exciting dance between weapon switching, choosing the right firing mode (each weapon has an alt fire) and targeting the right enemy at the right time. At times, the intensity can be Doom-esque. The game certainly is challenging if played at the right difficulty. Just when you feel like you've seen all that the game has to offer, a new mechanic, weapon, or enemy is presented that shakes everything up. Some sections had me seriously impressed with their uniqueness and creativity. It's evident that so much thought and care went into creating this title, nothing feels lazy or sloppily put together. Absolutely check this out, it runs great on Steam Deck as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very unique! It resembles a strange mix of Doom and Spiderman, and it works very well. The weapons are designed so that you'll need to use them all, adding to the experience even more. It's clear the developers were passionate about this game, and the story is hilarious and doesn't take itself too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of boomer shooters, big fan of movement shooters, not a big fan of movement shooter elements in a game that's built mostly as a boomer shooter. Everything about this game is fantastic. The art style is what immediately got me interested. Gameplay is fluid and fun, fun storyline, infinite pop culture references, etc. The ONLY thing I'm not super fond of is the movement shooter elements like sliding around with the bubble gun or swinging around with the belt, but only because this is a boomer shooter at heart. Boomer shooters are slippery, that's how they're supposed to feel, but these elements feel just a little TOO slippery when combined with other elements, which can make some sections of the game a little frustrating at times. It's definitely nothing game breaking, I would still highly recommend this game.You can really feel the love that the devs put in and if you've got $20 to burn, I'd recommend you pick this game up over that $35 wingstop order that you're having doordashed to your house rn you slob

The game is paced really well and constantly introduces new enemies and weapons right things are starting to become stale. The story was pretty enjoyable as well considering how ridiculous the concept is, but it does just about everything it can with the premise of fashion cops taking down criminals committing fashion crimes.
