_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Really original FPS. Clearly inspired by DOOM with tons of stuffs borrowed from the Super Nintendo era (most of the voice/effects could be taken from Street Fighter IV or Turtles In Time).  What makes this game so original, is that you're not fighting demons or monsters, but people with an awful taste in fashion (like people wearing socks with flippers, or Karens..). Only a Finnish studio could come with such a weird concept 😄The sense of humor is top tier. One particularity in the gameplay, is that ennemies are only vulnerable to one specific type of weapons or ammos. This is quite an interesting approach at first, though it get a little bit frustrating after the mid-half of the game, because you constantly have to switch between weapons. Despite this little annoyance, I absolutely recommend this game, especially if you are looking for an original 16 bits retro FPS that doesn't take itself seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend playing the demo, you'll have one hour full of laughs. After the demo the game just repeats its own formula.The humor is great, the gameplay is meh.It's quick paced first person shooter gameplay but it's all about picking the right weapon for the right enemy type all the time.The level design reuses the same assets in every area so every part of a level looks basically exactly alike and you would be lost all the time if it wasn't for a mission marker that you blindly follow non stop.The exploration could have been interesting but the secrets are way too easy to find and there is no real reward besides a picture to look at.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: By far, this is the wildest first-person shooter I've probably ever played. For how ridiculous it looks, though (and trust me, it really is), the way the narrative and theme of fashion is integrated into the game design is incredibly clever. Every weapon works in a plausible way to fight a plausible fashion crime and the general moment-to-moment gameplay is solid as a rock. Fellow gay DOOM fans, take notice.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad offers a refreshing twist on the classic "boomer shooter" genre, injecting it with a vibrant and quirky personality that sets it apart from its predecessors. As Sergeant Des from the Fashion Police Squad, players are tasked with eradicating fashion faux pas from the streets, wielding an arsenal of weapons to combat crimes like socks paired with sandals and uninspiring business suits. Here's my detailed take on this stylish adventure:Let's start with the gameplay, which is where Fashion Police Squad truly shines. Unlike traditional shooters, FPS introduces innovative mechanics that tie directly into the fashion theme. Each weapon is uniquely tailored to address different fashion crimes, keeping combat fresh and engaging throughout. However, I must admit that the chaotic combat sections towards the end of the game were a bit overwhelming. With a barrage of enemies and constant weapon switching, it sometimes felt like a fashion frenzy that left me scratching my head in disbelief.Moving on to the visuals, Fashion Police Squad delivers with crisp, colorful graphics that perfectly complement its vibrant setting. The attention to detail is commendable, with each character and environment exuding personality and charm. However, I would recommend turning off pixelated text, as it can be a bit challenging to read.In terms of audio, the game doesn't disappoint. The music sets the tone effectively, while occasional voice acting adds an extra layer of charm to the experience. Despite the lack of extensive voiceovers, the humor throughout the game is undeniable. Even as someone not particularly well-versed in fashion, I found myself chuckling at the witty dialogue and quirky scenarios.Now, let's talk about the final boss fight, which, while exhilarating, can also be a tad frustrating. Balancing the intense action with strategic gameplay proved to be a challenge, but ultimately added to the overall excitement of the showdown.Overall, Fashion Police Squad offers a fun and relatively short gaming experience, clocking in at around 5-6 hours. Its humor, innovative gameplay mechanics, and vibrant visuals make it a standout title in the genre. Despite some minor frustrations with combat intensity and readability issues, I thoroughly enjoyed my time patrolling the streets as a fashion-conscious sergeant.Rating: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and challenging! Well designed enemies and weapons to counter them. Some decent movement tech even though I wasn't always happy to do the platforming. The game kind of fell apart for me near the end as there finally became too many enemies and guns to say I was enjoying the mechanic of enemy weapon-type immunity. DOOM Eternal style enemy spawns also became really really tiresome by the time it was over. Really exhausting final few segments. Still, the gameplay is slick enough that it easily gets a recommend from me. I enjoyed the references and humor but it may not be for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A slightly shorter but incredibly fun, robust experience of a boomer shooter. Puzzle-based gunplay never gets old thanks to regularly introducing new spanners into the works, every boss fight was interesting (especially the second one - with all the different game styles, I had a dumb smile on my face the entire time), and I think it has to be said how welcoming a shooter is in this space that doesn't take itself ultra seriously and just has fun. This was a fun, light-hearted game in a sea of overly grim and crunchy contemporaries and it didn't outstay its welcome either. I think the only thing that I didn't like were the gimp enemies, who were more annoying than threatening and harmed the flow of combat (instead of rewarding rapid responses like a lot of the other enemies do), but besides that, a home run of a shooter and one I can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A fun doom clone that doesn't take itself seriously. Makes references to older games movies, and memes. Visuals are good, game play is nice until the end. Boss fights could be better as the last one felt more like a chore than anything exciting or challenging. When you kill the final boss you feel free than accomplishing something. At a certain point in the game, enemy spawns and types feel cheap and irritating. Also, some enemy types tend to glitch through walls during fights. But overall, it's a fun FPS game to play if you're wanting to take a break from anything competitive. Would recommend buying on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Got this from Humble and it was a good game but sometimes too challenging. I almoast gave it up because of the chaos which was caused by too many different kinds of enemies which need to be killed by different weapons and the unavoidable attacks all the time. My Fab gloves were waisted a lot of times until I figured out there is a problem with the keyboard layout and other keys are activate this special power by accident too.. not just the one you set.Usually about 24-30 hours game play is prefered for me to complete a game.. I made it in about 10 hours with this game but feel it was enough really.. It was really exciting at first how this game is doing FPS without killing enemies.. just making them fashioned. :D+2 for the style and atmosphere-1 for too many different kinds of enemies and some of them are really a pain to defeat..-1 for combat system feels too slow sometimes compared to the amount and speed of the enemies. Some weapons should do more damage.-1 for upgrade system, there is nothing like that.. only a few clothes can change on the game.. but nothing else..-1 After a while it becomes too hard because of the reasons mentioned above..-1 for FAB power bug, it toke a lot of time to fogure out why it is activating when I don't want it.. and didn't press the key..7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hell yeah.I'm going to say that at the time of writing this review this little gem has made my day.At the moment we are going through a interesting time for FPS games. On the one hand you have massive super black-hole budget games like COD and such kinda just spinning the wheel BUT on the other hand you have had loads of smaller games like this one that are just an absolute joy to play.This game takes itself zero percent seriously and embraces the silly ass plot and style of its theme. The game play is tight and enjoyable with only a few small critiques on some of the movement mechanics.This game does one thing absolutely perfect and that is that it is the PERFECT length, no time is spent kind of mulling over the same game play for any real length of time, the game right up till the end is bringing in new enemies and challenges and ends after an appropriately difficult boss fight that was also fun as heck.I think this game is fun and like a fun that you dont get so much of any more. like its just light hearted and easy. the jokes are everywhere including the music of the boss fight. play it and see what i mean.I'm sad that i don't have a quote to put at the end.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for the first two hours, I can safely say that this feels like a true love letter to retro gamers, fans of Doom/Duke Nukem and to people who loves puns. This game just oozes with style! And goofy jokes.Playing on the second hardest difficulty had me on the ropes before I started to grasp the different combinations you can pull off with the weapons. Some enemy types are frustrating, but the level design and different movement mechanics, like the pole swings or the fashion slap, give you just enough versatility to make split second choices that let you stay away from being worn out (aka dying). I'm not gonna let you in with all of the weapons I already unlocked, but Portal fans should love the water gun. *nudge nudge*I'm really looking forward to playing this more and trying to speedrun through some of these first levels.If you are looking for good vibes while playing a 90s styled FPS game with well written, modern humor and fun game play, this should definitely be in your radar!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard to like this game, it was just a few little things that ended up making this a frustrating instead of fun game.Pros- Great music/aesthetic- Unique weapons and ideas- Very interesting story had me chuckling a few timesCons- The average enemy damage is a bit too high, it became constant in the later missions that I had to absorb a number of hits because it takes a bit too long to dispatch the enemies- Weapons are a bit too one note, it's good to promote weapons having certain strengths but it gets tedious having to switch every 2 seconds because the 10 enemies on screen all need different weapons to cause damage- Platforming is often frustrating, not so much the whip grappling but the sections where you need to use the water gun it just isn't my idea of fun in an FPStl;dr A interesting but flawed FPS game, pick up on sale if any of the points sounded interesting to you otherwise I cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Decent "old school fps". I say in quotes because of two things which heavy deviate from old school fps. First is the lack of quick saves which for some reason a lot of newer old school fps do. But more importantly every weapon except one has infinite ammo which I really disliked. This is such a simplifikation.The main aspect of the game is that every enemy can only be damaged by one or two certain weapons, and stunned by certain others. It's an interesting idea and means the game has a unique selling point. But if you really think about it, this just limits the way you can play the game. (Btw. there are just 5-6 weapons in the game.)A very subjective point is the theme of the game which is all about fashion which is kinda cringe imho. Still the humor isn't bad here. The look is mostly pretty nice, the soundtrack is dope and the gunplay is mostly pretty decent if you can overlook the fact that the game really ristricts which weapon you are supposed to use against which enemy.The game also consists of surprinsingly quite a lot of platforming. Those mechanics are pretty decent.Lets talk about balancing. I played on the highest difficulty and let me tell you that the game isn't that hard most of the time but has some huge difficutly spikes, even unfair at times, especially the boss fights. (In fact I couldn't beat the final boss on the highest difficulty.) The lack of quicksaves and the fact that checkpoints are sometimes too rare can make this frustrating. On lower difficulties the game should be all right, I wouldn't recommend highest difficulty though.

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad makes me really, really wish there was more nuance to Steam's recommendation system. I played the demo a month or two back and liked it enough to buy the full game day 1. The first few levels dole out more of what I liked from that- fun, peppy music, a concept with heart and soul, bright and joyful visuals, and some fun takes on the classic FPS arsenal. Things start to go a little sour with the introduction of some later enemies leaving lingering damage effects that add visual clutter and slow down a game that feels like it should flow much faster. The latter in particular, introduced just as the levels switch from fairly open urban environments to tight corridors and often fought two, three, or four at a time alongside other enemies, lead to deaths that feel cheap and unearned. This brings me to another issue I'm having that wasn't immediately apparent from the demo. Most enemies can only be damaged by one or two weapons in your arsenal, forcing you to switch weapons frequently.  Giving every weapon unlimited ammo sidesteps the potential problem of a lack of ammo leaving you unable to damage certain enemies, but not every weapon feels impactful or satisfying to use- meaning that fighting certain enemy types (looking at you, Guy Fiery) feels like a chore. I'm about 40% of the way through the game at the time of writing, and having an increasingly rough time of it- I really want to love Fashion Police Squad, but I wish I had watched some more in-depth reviews before purchase. I hold out hope that some tweaks to enemies or weapons may improve the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "Beautiful Art, Innovative Premise, But Tedious Gameplay."Fashion Police Squad boasts a visually stunning art style that immediately draws players into its vibrant world. With a premise that promises innovation, it's hard not to be intrigued by the prospect of enforcing fashion laws amidst such captivating visuals. However, as engaging as the game's presentation may be, its gameplay mechanics leave much to be desired.The concept of dispatching enemies with specific weapons initially seems like a novel twist on traditional gameplay mechanics. Yet, in practice, it becomes a cumbersome and frustrating ordeal. Rather than embracing the fast-paced action one might expect, players find themselves bogged down in a repetitive cycle of trial and error.Each encounter feels like a chore as players scramble to locate the correct weapon for each foe, disrupting any sense of flow or immersion. What should be a seamless blend of strategy and action devolves into a tedious exercise in micromanagement. The beauty of Fashion Police Squad's artistry is sadly overshadowed by the clunkiness of its gameplay.Ultimately, the game's potential remains untapped, obscured by its own design flaws. While the foundation is undeniably strong, Fashion Police Squad falls short of delivering the captivating gameplay it promises, leaving players longing for a more streamlined and engaging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually disagree with many of the reviews saying this game "starts great and goes to ♥♥♥♥ in the end." The game is tedious and rigid 60 minutes in, at most. I would say the greatest strength of "boomer shooters", arena shooters, arcade shooters, what have you, is the expression they allow the players. This strength is found in many of the shooters I love, from Doom '93 to Ultrakill. Fashion Police Squad, however, removes all of this expression by reducing the game to a series of concurrent rock-paper-scissor matches. Each enemy is taken down with (usually) a single weapon or strategy. If you use the incorrect one, you are entirely ineffectual. This proves to be incredibly limiting and boring, as well as occasionally irritating when you want to take care of a high priority but can't get through the wall of enemies only affected by your flaccid melee. If the game drops off after the beginning, then seeing the end is not worth the effort.

_childDocuments_.review: A funny and clever take on the classic FPS genre. There is a lot of interesting ideas however it still needs some work, specifically when it comes to pacing and balancing encounters. The game will just lock you in a small space and spawn a dozen enemies at once, and unless you happen to have your ultimate charged then I hope you enjoy being attacked from all sides at once by enemies that each require specific weapons/tactics to beat. The worst of this was on the rooftops during the beach level, I died at least a half a dozen times during one encounter because there was literally no room to maneuver without either eating tons of damage and/or being knocked off and taking damage. It's just cheap and goes against how the base combat mechanics are setup. There are other issues as well but the claustrophobic enemy spams really soured the experience for me. Overall I'd still recommend it, though in its current state maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliantly dumb fun game. I am honestly surprised that the tacky fashion jokes did not get old; maybe they will for you, but they didn't for me.The shooting action, sadly, is the weakest part. Even with the incredible boss fights, the major issue lies with the enemy weakness system. Every enemy has weaknesses and immunities, with nothing in between. this means that every attack will either have no effect, or a regular effect. As a result, you'll be forced to constantly switch out weapons, and if you've ever played Borderlands 2 in higher difficulties, Fashion Police Squad does it worse.Exploration in this game is quite superb. Using the belt melee attack as a grappling hook was very enjoyable.This game's saving grace is the incredible boss fights. There are only 3, but all of them are amazing, and honestly the 2nd and 3rd were incredible fun that I highly enjoyed.All in all, you are getting what you paid for, a ton of dumb jokes with mixed gameplay and some really strong redeeming qualities.

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is NOT a generic 2.5D Doom-clone shooter. While on first glance it may appear so, it isn't that. It is heavily inspired by Doom Eternal, even upping it a notch. Gameplay while chill at first, quickly ramps up in difficulty forcing you to swap weapons to defeat different enemy varieties. It gets as sweaty as Doom Eternal, and that is a good thing. It has actually challenging platforming sections where you can swing by poles using a whip - Prince of Persia style. And yes, the platforming in this game is definitely a notch or two harder than Doom Eternal. But if you got through Mario, you shouldn't have troubles with this one. If you're thinking, "meh, another 2.5D shooter with a cartoony art style where you're not even killing enemies?", trust me - you'll get over that bit quickly enough, because the gameplay is very enjoyable. All in all, a solid shooter, that punches way above its weight, and is an under-appreciated gem. Has good replay value as well, and I see myself replaying the game again when I'm older. I was starting to get tired of 2.5D Doom clones that are aplenty these days, but this one plays very very different. You won't be disappointed with this game if you enjoyed Doom Eternal.

_childDocuments_.review: Just not good.Presentation wise it does a good job of looking the part, but when you derobe it all you find is a dusty copy of Doom Eternal and several crusty tissues in the pockets.One of the major issues with this game is that it ONLY wants a specific weapon to deal with specific enemies. In most cases it does this by making every other weapon completely ineffective, that's fun right? Swapping to a shotgun because an enemy literally requires it, and not because you tactically benefit from it overall. Simon says gunplay. Barf.Outside of the MAKE SURE YOU SHOOT THEM WITH THIS gameplay, maps are pretty linear and sometimes involve swinging over pits with your belt, but it's never more than point A to point B type stuff, enemies don't require you to swing around even when the opportunity arises because strafing will usually be enough.Secrets reward you with either armour or the same picture of the main character in a different outfit over and over...? Thanks..?Look, I don't know if a prerequisite to liking this game is wanting to ♥♥♥♥ the main character, but it sure as hell ain't making me want to look for secrets lmao.You get an ability to instakill enemies for about 20 secs every so often, but it's not very fun. You just click and he teleports and defeats them. That's the only other mechanic you have apart from shooting. Shooting enemies with the specific gun the game wants you to that is, did I mention that yet?Difficulty wise, what difficulty? Just bash it onto hardest and I promise if you're semi decent at FPS games you'll have absolutely no issues. Enemies don't hit hard and all your guns have unlimited ammo soooo...It's just so much style over substance. Quite a lot of freezing you in place mid level to read dialogue too, cos that's what everyone wants, to stop shooting and read jokes based off old memes and other unfunny ♥♥♥♥.It has a vision but needs less slack on the belt because it's trousers (pants for yanks) keep falling down, and it happens so often I've stopped laughing and started rolling my eyes instead. _childDocuments_.review: Got it from a humble pack.As far as the theme goes, it commits to the bit and hams it hard, and I think it does a good job even if I can't say I enjoyed it. The game certainly has style!It's not a bad shooter. It runs fine, the movement feels fine, the grappling hook is fun. If you're big on advanced movement tech: look elsewhere. The actual shooting part unfortunately feels like a chore.The enemy weakness gimmick is unique but not that interesting, since it takes all the decision making out of combat. No longer do you need to worry about conserving ammo, or what guns work best on what enemies, or even target priority since some weapons (looking at you, belt and sewing machine alt-fire) have cooldowns long enough to force you to target something else. The only real choice you have is to press your berserk button if it's real dire.But that's not even my real gripe. No, what kills me is that the secrets are pointless. You get.... character art of the player character in bad fashion. I get why, if weapons are strictly gated behind progression because they only work on certain enemies and you don't need ammo, the only thing you can put in them is healing. And the game doesn't need more healing. But it's still such a downer to know that looking for secrets is basically pointless! Admittedly I may be more secret-hunting oriented than your average boomer-shooter enjoyer, but still.This game didn't do it for me, but I would pick it if I needed a boomer shooter for a person who didn't really play videogames. It's straightforward, not that hard, the game tells you EXACTLY what you need to do, and the tone and style would probably help sell them on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure why this is rated "Very positive".For 20 bucks you basically get a roughly 2 to 3 hour "pseudo" boomer shooter. I've played for like 20 minutes, 2 missions, but I'm just, sadly, bored to death. The game has about 12 missions or so. Let's be generous and say each mission takes 15 to 20 minutes (it's more like 5 to 10 for the early ones), so this is how you end up with about 2 to 3 hours, maaaaaaaybe 4 if you're stretching it. That's already a very short time to money ratio. There aren't any other modes than the campaign. You may choose a higher difficulty, and it's nice they're all unlocked from the start, the question is just ... why?This is one of those games that isn't offensively bad, it's just... why would I ever spend 20 bucks on ... this? Something that is essentially a glorified student project. The art style is ultry generic Pixel Art (think old school Doom, more colourful, but with duller environments), the combat and traversal is uninspired and slow, there's not even a "run" button, and your guy is pretty slow by default. The weapons are your standard fare, but with a "twist", because they don't kill, you see? The shotgun shoots coloured pellets, the Tommy Gun basically does the same, a beam of light sucks the colour out of things, while a belt whips some fashion sense into people... There's more I'm told, but I have no real intention of finding out I'm afraid, because each weapon only ever works on one enemy it seems, which means constant switching for each and every one of them. The enemies themselves don't really present a danger either, and their portrayal is "mildly humorous" at best. There's dudes in grey suits, super energetic "bros" on city scooters, bigger dudes in loose fitting suits, baggy pants users, you get the drift. You'll likely encounter way more fashion sinners, but they're not really interesting in combat.In fact they seem to just be haphazardly thrown together with little thought for the various combat arenas, but such a combat arena should be carefully curated, so that enemies complement each other. But they don't. The suits guys throw suit cases, and due to the weird graphics style and projectile speeds and the fact you need to hit them up close means you get hit every once in a while, but the baggy pants guy just stands there as a sort of "don't come near me or I'll ... bubble you"... yeah. While the scooter dude is just zipping around the arena, occasionally crossing your path... yes, this is just the beginning of the game, but if you want to grab the attention of people who are not toddlers then you gotta do better, I'm afraid.That basically leaves the "story", which is equally as yawn inducing. Some conspiracy is afoot, of course, and your fashionable police squad has to get to the bottom of it, with the help of a mysterious figure in a trench coat. There's nothing of interest here, it's just a vehicle to get you from arena to arena, from mission to mission. You could just as well remove it entirely and the game wouldn't suffer for it much, especially since it keeps interrupting what little actual gameplay flow there is. Every time I was feeling like I could actually almost enjoy the game it stopped me dead in my tracks to give me more exposition and tutorials...And the soundtrack just mellowly plays along without pumping you up. I have no idea who this game was made for. It's not for the "modern" shooter audience, it's not for military shooter fans, it's not for "boomer shooter" fans, it's not for serious players, nor for those looking for levity, because ultimately nothing fits together. It won't appeal to "moms" and it's certainly not interesting to little kids, because they won't even get 10% of the references (meaning you gotta be older, like in your 30s/40s, to somewhat get the humour).All of this is to say that it's on its own not a terrible game, there's just no point in playing it, even for free, because there's a vast amount of infinitely better games out there. A very good comparison imho would be "Forgive me Father", which costs just as much, has more content, a more interesting art style, every level is very different, enemies are actually complementing each other and pose a serious threat, the music is great, the story even is more interesting, and the gameplay is pretty damn good. While that one's a horror themed game, it's got the same niche idea. So if you want to make a retro shooter about fashion ... that's surely possible, but take a look at FMF and copy that game if you must. And yes, I understand that both games came out almost at the same time, but still... one clearly had more interesting ideas and executed them better than the other, so the question remains why? Why is a game about fashion among the blandest in the genre? Wasted potential.Maybe a sequel could fix this. Longer, more varied and interesting missions, more interesting art style, better combat and arenas, more tailor-made weapons instead of the standard ones in every shooter, but they shoot coloured pellets instead of bullets, a more pumping soundtrack, story bits that don't interrupt gameplay and is actually funny and clever, instead of full of dull word plays. Funnily enough this game about non-violence is rated ages 16 up for "sexual innuendo". Can't make this ♥♥♥♥ up, probably because of the exhibitionists in the game?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid boomer shooter with a lot of style. Its aesthetic contributes a lot in keeping the game fresh and interesting throughout its playtime, but that's not all it has going for it. The mechanics are on par with other classic-style boomer shooters such as the original Doom or Duke Nukem 3D. There are many different types of enemies who can usually only be hurt by one weapon type, forcing the player to remain engaged in combat and making good use of each weapon. The difficulty starts to ramp up in later levels, which I'm sure tryhard boomer shooter enjoyers will appreciate. The only complaint I have is that health items can be a bit sparse, making some combat scenarios even more difficult, especially in the later parts of the game. Overall, though, this title is a lot of fun and worth playing if you're a fan of classic boomer shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Just about style people! It's about damn Technique!Fashion police squad may seems like another boomer shooter with a lot of pop culture references, but actually is one of the finest experiment of the FPS genre.Let me explain: the game take the basic notions of the FPS genre like weapons and enemies, then it reduces them at the most basic function. After all said and done, it ''rebuilds'' them in a way that is actually pretty unique and yet simple and familiar: to each enemy,  a weapon ( or two). Seems trivial, but instead of simply following the ''structure'' of the most FPS ( boomer shooter or more modern ones), this game takes the very idea that started the whole genre ( basically, the entirety of the thought process behind doom) and  starts from there. If you think about it, how many games do this? not just adding some novelty to an already seen combat system, but instead to build from scratches an ''idea'' of FPS gameplay? Maybe I read too much into it, but I swear this game is damn awesome ( and fashionable).Furthermore, Fashion police squad manages to insert something more ''modern'' like platforming, weakest part but still done in a very clever way ( and even with this gameplay mechanic, the devs. managed to create a completely new way to ''run'', or better yet slide, for an FPS ). Plus... It's non-violent: all you do is fixing clothes! Besides that, Story and Design are a blast and funny as hell ( and, again, rather unique having an FPS on the fashion world, and even having jokes about it without being offensive), while the soundtrack is fitting and pretty good ( Actually, I loved the bit theme, but I see how this is more of a personal taste).So, worth it? YES. without a doubt. This Boomer-shooter enter with full honours into the pantheon of the games considered pillars for the FPs genre and gaming in general, and also a masterpiece among its peer... title that this game ''wears like a glove'' ( YAS, manage to insert that joke).

_childDocuments_.review: Been excited to get my hands on this one. FPS seemed like a fun satyrical boomer shooter, and it did live up to those expectations. Howevr, by chapter eight I started to loose interest a bit.There are a couple different weapons you unlock throughoput the story, and each has their own secondary attack. This is what caused my enjoyment to wain as obviously only certain enemies can be hurt by certain weapons or attacks, and as you get deeper in you come across some that require one weapon to start doing damage, then the special attack of it or another in order to finish them off. I'm not talking the boss battles, I mean the standard horde enemies.Which leads to the other issue: Artificial difficulty inflation through large hordes and weapon management, sometimes in tight spaces that make dodging pretty difficult. I'm running this on medium to just enjoy the story. I planned to do my second run on insane (as I normally do), but much like Dread Templar it doesn't feel like I need skill or a good strategy to survive, but rather whether or not I'm worn out from the amount of bullet sponges coming my way come the next wave and care enough to move on. Much like the other title I mentioned, I'm struggling to do just that.On top of that FPS just tries to cram too much into the story. Sniper missions is one thing, but when you reach the android boss you have to pay attention which weapon or alt fire to use to wear him down long enough to enter cyberspace and do these mini combat games to advance to the next battle to knock off another chunk of health. In those mini-games you'll find nods to classic titles like some platforming akin to Mega Man 2 (even has similar sound effects). It's fun, but it just interrupts the flow of the main story.Thankfully that's about it with the gripes. Fashion Police Squad is a good game overall that just does too much to the point it starts to lose focus on what made it so much fun at the start in the first place on top of increasing the hordes that progressively eat more of your ammo with each passing chapter. If that's siomething you enjoy then FPS will more then likely kep your attention from start to finish. However if you want more than just a war of attrition each mission then you'll end up checking in about half way through like I did. I'm stuck in the middle with recomending this or not, and given I'm starting to forcing myself to finish process I have to lean towards it being a no.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fabulous Doom, I guess. Fashion Police Squad's more interesting aspect would be it's limited weapon types/alternate-fires and how each corresponds to a specific enemy type. You correct their fashion crime. A paint shotgun brightens outfits, a sewing machine gun tightens loose, ill-fitting ones, etc. The aesthetic is bright and vibrant, the tone and plot irreverent, really stands out compared to other boomer shooters in this regard.Where I find Fashion police Squad falls flat is its platforming, level design and enemy placement. You can use your melee attack, a belt, like a whip to swing across various pitfalls and a water gun on surfaces so you get as movement/traversal speed bonus, but the level design for these platforming sections starts to become more frequent, clunky and frustrating. Where Doom had monster closets that would open usually on armor or health pick-ups, Fashion Police Squad likes to spawn enemies out of thin air in its combat arenas. Less annoying at the start but by the tenth mission I was just sort of done.I don't even want to bother trying to face tank the rest of the campaign, there's literally so many other boomer shooters out I'd rather just play one I actually enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad (or FPS, nice!) is a breath of fresh air for the arguably over-bloated realm of old school, “boomer shooter” genre. A colourful, light-hearted twist to a game style that is almost exclusively filled with endless violence and gore that also adds its own novel twists to the combat. While the most hardcore purists may find it’s challenge a little lacking and its length rather short, Fashion Police Squad is undoubtedly one of the best titles for people who dislike FPS games to try and get into FPS games with.For even the most die hard fans of the old school FPS games it is hard to deny one fact: the genre is now becoming over-saturated. While in 2019 it was refreshing to see high quality games made like they were in the past finally come out after years of bland military shooters, by mid-to-late 2021 the concept of shooting hundreds of satanic aliens in some hyperviolent, sci-fi environment was worn well past its welcome. Even if you added something new to the gameplay it was still the same gore-soaked mass of 1994 to 1998 gameplay. To stand out now takes something special!Fashion Police Squad (FPS) bucks the trend mostly in terms of its aesthetics. Gone is the brutality and in its place comes a far more wholesome affair: You are a member of the Fashion Police and in this alternative world setting you go around solving crimes against fashion on the streets of Trendopolis. Rather than blow people away with lead, you use your dye-based shotgun (2DYE4) to colour bland, grey suits in, or you use the tailormade assault rife sewing machine to correct ill fitting suits, and so on. While it can be said that a change in settings does not affect the core gameplay underneath, this change in aesthetic and setting does at least make it stand out from a rather large crowd these days, which in most cases is enough for some. More so, it can be said that the more light-hearted take can be attractive to people who previously disliked the violence and gore of other FPS titles. The SNES-but-3D visuals can help this even further. If there is someone in your life who may like FPS games but are put off by the gruesome and gritty nature they have, show them Fashion Police Squad and you may have a convert!Aside from the look of the game, FPS does have a couple of quirks up its chique sleaves to make it stand out. The primary factor is how combat functions. As described above, weapons are… tailor made (I’m sorry) to fit their enemies. The 2DYE4 has both a primary and secondary fire mode, one spitting colour in a shotgun spread and the other as a lightning gun colour drain. Against the first enemies, dull suited men and over-saturated bros on scooters, each fire mode will only work on the appropriate enemy. Dull suits will not be affected by the secondary fire as they have no colour to drain, and the scooter bros are already too colourful, so the primary fire does nothing. As such Fashion Police Squad takes the “combat chess” of titles like Doom Eternal and enhances them to the point of exclusivity; it is not that some weapons are more effective than others, it is that you  use the correct weapons on enemies. This may sound inflexible, but the general combat is never too hectic that it becomes unmanageable. There are some slightly rough situations with a couple of enemies though. For example, there are socks & sandals wearing German tourists who do a hitscanning camera flash at you, blinding temporarily and doing damage, and the only way to combat them is a “sock gnome” that is thrown out like a grenade. On occasion these enemies are placed in high spots, meaning you must climb up to get them, all the while soaking up any damage that they pump out. Bar this though most enemies are fine to deal with and have the usual threat assessment other good quality FPS games have.Tying into the combat are the bosses. I’ll keep this short as there are very few in the game, but all of them are fun combat situations, demanding you change up how you fight them as the fight goes on. While bosses are usually a low point of these types of games, thankfully FPS here has some fantastic battles. So much so I’d argue the second boss fight is worth the price of admission alone!External to the combat the general movement and level design is fairly run of the mill. Levels are linear paths with occasional, optional secrets to find along the way. While it occasionally does branch out into alternating paths and there are “key hunts” so to speak of, it is very hard to get lost here. The only confusing moments are likely to occur with the occasional first-person platforming sections, swinging about from flagpoles and bouncing about on shop awnings, but even those moments are solvable with a little observation.So are there any major issues with FPS bar the above ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? There are a couple of oddly demanding moments on the hardware when I noted the game dropped below 45fps, but these were few and far between. Similarly, the options are not bad but a little limited in some areas. Max FoV being 100? FPS limits capping at 120 before unlimited? Hardly world ending stuff, but a little limited. Indeed, the worst element I can think of comes maybe in the game’s length with only 4 chapters clocking in at about 4 to 5 hours. The time you spend in game is absolutely wonderful, but I can’t help but want to play a chapter or so more! Irrespective, these are a couple of loose threads on an otherwise immaculately tailored product!So do I advise Fashion Police Squad? Without doubt! It may be a little short and lacking in the brutality (both in theme and gameplay) for the hardest of the hardcore FPS aficionados, but as a fun little jaunt? It is without doubt one of the most enjoyable little distractions I’ve played this year!

_childDocuments_.review: Are you stylish enough to fix those various criminals' outfit?That's the question Fashion Police Squad wants you to answer. And you will answer it in a very old-fashionned FPS way, in rather linear stages in quite beautiful pixel art. You will get several weapons along the way, with each enemy having to be defeated by a specific weapon: a gameplay mechanic I felt worked well during my playthrough as you don't have to juggle too much between your arsenal to get it right.The game overall is a really fun time, with a good soundtrack, funny dialogs (even if they tend to stop you dead in your tracks too many times) and a well balanced level-design. Even the platforming feels quite right, which is never easy to do in FPSs. And the main theme of the game, fashion, is quite cleverly used and I never thought I'd see a FPS based on this!The game is quite short and I would have enjoyed a little more diversified environments (as we spend most of our time inside the city) but I feel it is paced well and knows when to end in order not to drag for too long. I still need to find every secret now that I know the game a little better.In short: it is a good game for people who like old-school pixel art mid-90's FPS!Also, your character is FA-BU-LOUS!

_childDocuments_.review: FPS is quirky. Normally I consider quirky to be a bad thing because I associate that with "unfun jank that doesn't work". In this case, quirky is a good attribute. It plays like your average DOOM clone for the most part and there are a LOT of well-thought-out setpieces and levels (versus something like DUSK's later abysmally designed expansions).If you remember the South Park "metrosexual" episode, this game kind of captures that vibe. It's all about stopping bad fashion sense with fashion & textile inspired weaponry; all the drab fashion victims are put into nice duds by your firearms. It's another fps without death, which I think is nicely done and doesn't feel lame or forced.Don't be too disgusted if you hear stuff you'd consider meme slang, it's tongue-in-cheek for the most part. The story is actually pleasant vs a fps where the story gets in the way of mechanics and gameplay, and there's a lot of callbacks to older traditional arcade shooters.I personally think this is the only fps game to  get boss fights in a fps game to feel enjoyable and challenging for what they are. Rise of the Triad you just circlestrafed around, DUSK's final boss was kind of good, but all of the bosses in FPS felt really well planned.FPS is a really good experience; it captures that indie spark that wants to try something different without that smug "heh, we're doing something DIFFERENT" feeling you get from the dialog of other indie games/shooters. Maybe not exactly worth $20, but you could do way worse for the pricetag.The only sour spot is that one of the challenge levels sucks ass because the game is made with Unity and I have yet to play a fps made in Unity that doesn't have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ air movement vs a game made with Source or idtech. It also interferes with one of the more prevalent mechanics in the game but it's serviceable.

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a very silly game. Unfortunately it's not nearly as fun as it is silly. However, its also super charming, super cheap and still a very good time for about 75% of the experience. If you can jive with its more frustrating aspects, there's a lot of replay value. At minimum, comedy shooters are far and few between and filling that niche is worth something on its own.

_childDocuments_.review: God I hate this game. Literally only good things about it are the fundamental mechanics of certain weapon types only working on certain enemies, the artwork, the music, the grappling mechanics, basic level layout, basic enemy behavior and mechanics, endearing story with lots of good jokes, as well as maxing one of the three stats (crimes, swag, secrets) making that stat be forever counted as perfected for that level, meaning levels don't require you to get everything perfectly in one run for it to count as 100%-ing the level.Everything else is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ god awful.If you decide to get this game, try doing challenge 3 without falling down once, or play it so that every time you fall down you click respawn from checkpoint.Hint: inconsistent platform distances, close to pixel perfect margins of error, and super tiny platforms are used in this mission. On top of that, you also have jump not registering unless you've been on the ground for a short period of time (such that it feels incredibly inconsistent), inability to jump if you're moving down a slope, and inconsistent ground detection, i.e. you can move along the very edge on the side of a platform slightly below the top of the platform such that you can't jump because you technically haven't landed yet.The level designers decided for some ungodly reason to put crimes, and swag in secret locations that are separate from the "official" secret locations in several of the levels, leading to tons of frustrating "where's waldo" searching. This searching will sometimes end with you finding a way out of bounds due to the devs not thinking you could reach certain locations despite having environmental objects in the vicinity that you could use to parkour your way to the location. Of the two I found, one was after you exit the train at level 7, you can get onto the top of the train, and crawl under the ceiling pipes, and get out of bounds, or soft-lock yourself by jumping back into the train through a wall. The other being a roof-top in level 9 that you can reach via a very well timed rope swing inside the arena that you can instantly clear by simply shooting the barrels, as there's only 1 wave of enemies, and strangely 2 flag poles to rope swing off of. The final boss's last stage is literally just RNG, and the only viably consistent strat is to cheese the fight by camping behind the big gun whenever the boss attack isn't floor scissors. (the floor scissors can hit you behind the gun).Levels have literally 0 indication for how many enemies you've dealt with out of the total in a level before the level is over, same goes with swag. Secrets are the only thing that shows any "x out of y" metric, but only for a short time after you've found a secret, and only the first time a secret is found. This makes it so that you will most often find out after you've beaten a level, and while feeling pretty good about your scouring of the level, that you've missed either like 1 enemy or 1 item location.The weapons in this game also love to forcefully switch between one another at random, for literally no reason, usually at the worst possible moments, which adds on a lot of frustration. I have no clue why the weapons do this, I have literally no issue with weapons randomly changing in other boomer shooters like prodeus, or postal: brain damaged.There's also the issue of "restart level" and "restart from checkpoint" being right next to each other, and clicking on either performs the one clicked, without any "are you sure?" warning that could let you get away with misclicking in the heat of battle.Additionally, after beating all 100%-in all the levels, there's literally not any real reason to ever play the game again, due to it severely lacking replayability, unless you are in the speedrunning scene, or want to see how easy the game is when you have unlimited ammo and the game's version of a BFG Rocket launcher.I'm going to be real honest with you, this game is so frustrating to 100% that I sat and swore and vocally proclaimed how much I hate this game for basically my entire playthrough of this game. At several points did I have to look up a youtube video to find what the damn thing I missed in a level was, as I had beaten the level and missed it like 5 times over.Don't get me wrong, the game is FUN, albeit extremely rail-roady (e.g. the fab glove being more of a story thing than something you actually plan around), the mechanics are solid, certain enemies can be dealt with using multiple weapon types, and the enemies have their unique traits that make them stand out reasonably well. Still, this game is actual agony to 100% and I extremely do not recommend doing it, since as far as I can tell it doesn't let you unlock costumes and accessories earlier, meaning it's solely a "I love this game so much on my playthrough that I want to go and get all the stuff I've missed" thing than a "doing this gives me an advantage in the game for later levels" that I had the unfortune to think it was. Especially since defeating the final boss gives you a costume that grants you infinite ammo and access to all weapons, letting you be less story-bound for your loadout in the levels.Still, as someone that wants to be rewarded for completionism with something more tangible in the gameplay, rather than something novel like pinups in an extras menu, I can't recommend this game. It's too frustrating.P.S. Devs, one tip I can give you, is to switch the 2nd and 3rd costume in the unlock progression, as the 2nd costume is so much better than the 3rd one that there's currently never any point in using it. Same can also be said for the 3rd and 4th accessory.P.P.S. reason my playtime is 15 hours is because at one point I started playing during a "Conquest of Elysium" session while I waited for the half of the party I was in to have their turn in doing their separate thing that the party split up to do, so I ended up with the game in the background for several hours after it became my group's turn. The game is definitely shorter than 10 hours (on hardest difficulty with 100%-ing the game) if you don't die too often or miss certain hidden locations too much.P.P.P.S. There's hints of an analysis of the game's incredibly vapid, semi-utopian, semi-dystopian world, sporadically spread around in the game. Most notable is in Mission 9, where the MC talks about how he used to wear speedo's, wondered why they were illegal, and was shocked to hear that there were posters that said speedo's were considered a fashion crime, however the game never goes anywhere with this. Could be inklings of a seed for a sequel, but who knows. Anyways, I'd have recommended this game if in addition to the campaign, players could create their own missions with ability to create their own dialogue, etc. that could be accessed via the steam workshop or something, as that'd let you get a better look into how normal work is for the fashion police squad, rather than something as grand as what happens in the campaign.

With each second you'll feel lesser of a man while playing it.It's just a bunch of sarcastic images and tone thrown over a doom mod. Boring except for the belt platforming areas. Switching guns (clunky) when multiple different type of enemies makes this a twitch shooter, otherwise it's bland.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: What seemed at first to be a pretty uninspired Doom clone with a different skin actually has some pretty decent writing and unique gameplay. The gimmick in Fashion Police Squad is that fashion crimes are all unique and require a specific response. Gameplay-wise, this means that you need to use different weapons on each enemy type. The game keeps this pretty fun, although having to switch weapons all the time can be a bit tiring as well as a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: FPS is a great comedic take on the Doom-clone Boomer-shooter genre, with colorful visuals, bumping music, and a really amusing story. Instead of killing your enemies, you're just helping them get fashionable! The trick is that enemies only have one or two ways you can fight them, so you need to always have the right "gun" out to do the job. That can create some chaos as you run around dodging projectiles and frantically switching guns. I didn't find it overly difficult, but the last few chapters definitely up the challenge. The platforming is mostly fun though occasionally really annoying. If you like the old-school shooter genre with a fresh coat of fabulous paint, then this is absolutely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Amazing idea, great execution, smooth controls, no filler content.What an amazing twist on the fps genre! Smooth controls, diverse gameplay due to each enemy being damaged by certain weapons, well crafted levels, unique bosses and a lot of references! The only thing that felt a bit out of place where the challenge levels for the sole reason that there were only 3 of them. With that said I appreciate that the game doesn't have any filler content. Also, as someone that has played a fair amount of fps games but isn't cracked at them, the game is fairly challenging. I played most of them on hard (the second hardest difficulty) and I felt the need to change it to normal during the last 3-4 levels. The only part that felt kind of meh where the sniper parts that you see at the trailer, but they are few and short.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fabulous and Fresh! Fantastic, Polished Shooter!I would recommend this to any fans of the genre.This fun-filled experience is brimming with character.The story is pretty great, the levels stay entertaining and the shooting is class!Don't skip on this one; you'll end up blasting through it. (Collectibles are there for to extend play!)
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is goated, I highly recommend it.I think the platforming in this game is a bit weak and frustrating, especially in the later levels.I found the sniper mission to be pretty frustrating, even though I only failed once, my eyesight wasn't good enough to pick out the fashion crimes quickly, the hit registration was not great, and it was very overwhelming trying to cover all of the angles.My eyesight also struggled in some rooms with hordes of enemies where it was hard to tell who I had already beat and who I hadn't.This was made worse with the respawning waves, I had enemies spawn right on top of me and those did not feel fair to get hit by.However, despite all that, I feel like the game makes it up in spades with the boss fights. The bosses have a ton of character and were genuinely the best part of the game.I think the humor was definitely not for everyone, but it was clear the game wasn't taking itself seriously and it was fun to go along with it.I felt like the game had fewer missions than I expected, but the missions themselves had some good length to them.If this game gets a sequel or some dlc mission packs, I'll definitely come back to play those.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny, but it doesn't rest on its humor.  It's a puzzle to solve too.  Each enemy requires a different gun or tactic to beat, and when you're surrounded by multiple enemy types, it gets hectic trying to dodge them while beating the highest threat enemies, unless you've got that glove fully charged and can just zip around slapping some fashion sense into people!  Level design is good too.  It's not easy to find all the secrets cold turkey.  It would be nice though if the secrets actually added something to the gameplay, but they are just easter eggs.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad: where fashion faux pas are crimes, and my wardrobe finally got the justice it deserves! Armed with a belt of fabulousness and a relentless eye for style, I strutted through the game feeling like the lovechild of RuPaul and Sherlock Holmes. Tackling clashing colors and saggy pants? Child's play when you're serving LOOKS and bringing law and order to the runway. The levels are so fierce, even my pixels started to sashay. 10/10, would slap a bad outfit with a makeover again!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: While a little rough around the edges, I enjoyed Fashion Police Squad. Its got a fun sense of humor, the enemy and boss design gets you thinking in encounters and the OST is a bop. On the down side, the gun play felt a little stiff and the difficulty curve is weird to say the least. I began the game thinking it was way too easy, while some of encounters at the end are frustratingly hard for all the wrong reason. It is fairly short, my play through coming in around 6 hours, which is great in my book but some people might want something meatier. Overall, I'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a pretty good game. There are some...Unique design choices that weren't super well thought out in my opinion. The guns are pretty cool, though there isn't a ton of variety. 5 weapons in total, but one of them you get about 30 minutes before the end of the game, and it has limited ammo (unlike the other 4 in your arsenal). The soundtrack is alright. Nothing really to write home about, but it definitely has the sound design of game that was made in the early 90s. The idea of having certain guns only damage certain enemies is a cool but scuffed mechanic, in my opinion. It feels fresh at the beginning of the game, but after the novelty wears off, it very quickly starts to feel like each combat encounter is a chore. Enemy design was fairly varied, though some of them are just bad, in my opinion. There are some enemies that get introduced in the last third of the game that will basically always damage you because their AOEs are usually about the size of the arena you're in and you can't always get high enough off the ground to avoid the damage. The bosses were cool. There was only one, though, that did anything outside of what you already expected the game to and that boss was by far my favorite. The end boss left a lot to be desired and you were forced to take damage throughout almost the entire fight, which resulted in 2 resets for me, one by dying to the actual boss and the other by falling off the arena. If I were you, I'd pick it up on sale. It's not necessarily a bad game, but it's for a very specific group of people in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Unique fps based on doom with nice visuals and good movement/platforming.My main critique is the amount of different enemies and that there are only 1 or sometimes 2 methods of damaging each enemy. So you have to switch between weapons alot. And with crowds of different enemies body blocking each other in sometimes small spaces makes this more annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: The unique quirk of this game, matching your weapon with the enemy, works pretty well and the presentation of the game is delightful, at least if you like various clothing and tailoring puns. If you are a fan of boomer shooters, chances are you're going to like this game.Just maybe wait for this game to go on sale, if you are on a budget and aren't a big fan of searching for all the secrets and beating high scores, since the main campaign is quite short.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique little game made by only a handful of people. Fun, engaging, but ultimately falling short.Gameplay needs a lot of work, and there needs to be some major hitbox fixing. I have fallen out of the map many times, been hit behind a wall, been hit through something that was supposed to have a hitbox etc. And at the last moment, it had the most prolonged boss fight I have ever seen. It dragged for so long that I forgot what I was doing here at one point. I get that the devs wanted to make fun of a lot of genres and games by adding this much Easter eggs, but then the game kinda loses its identity by only copying the said tropes. It was fun the first few times, but seeing another one just 10-15min afterwards gets repetitive fast.Overall, not a bad game, but certainly needs a lot more polish and time in the oven if a sequel or similar is on the horizon. 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Another game that makes me wish I could give a thumbs sideways review. This is a strategy shooter, which is not my preferred genre, but the gameplay was still pretty fun at first. The majority of the game was fun, but in the later game the difficulty had a sudden spike, for me, at least. This difficulty... was not very fun. However, the story, enemies, dialogue, everything about the theme and setting for this game was really creative and it is clear that a lot of thought was put into it. Between this and the fact that most of the levels (1-9, mainly (out of 13)) are fun, it is great, but I can not ignore the somewhat frustrating late game, so I give it a 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fun short and sweet FPS that really commits to its style! Even though there are few different enemy types the combat is interesting since you have to switch weapon for different kind of enemy. In the end the game is quite similar and gets repetitive but since the game is so short it okay. There is quite a difficulty bump towards the end and even easy is a real challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is one of those cases where I would have liked that steam had a mixed review option.On one side it's a small, tight controlling game that looks good and doesn't take itself too serious. On the other hand, it has problems with its enemy roster and leveldesign to the point where some of the encounters become an absolute annoyance to play.For one, the leveldesign hangs upon reusage of assets. This in itself is not a problem but it sometimes creates a bit of confusion of where to go because the leveldesign in itself isn't unique enough to stand on its own in places. If your leveldesign needs a marker where to go, it probably needs a pointer how to be done itself. A few times I was exploring the level in different directions rather than to go to the objective, and it turned out I ended up going to where I needed to before I needed to be there. In one instance in Mission 5, this caused part of the level to be not loaded back in.The other part, some of the enemies have either really annoying pathfinding or really annoying mechanics. A good example of that is the DJ2Loud enemy where it's not exactly clear how to evade the huge aoe attack. Sure it's telegraphed but it can't really be avoided, especially if you have to fight other enemies alongside her.In places, this creates some incredibly bad arenas like mission 7 where you run into this really small bar and get ambushed by 2 Loose Suits, 3 Flamers, 1 Spewdos and some Dull Suits (I think), creating a cacophony of area effects that are hard to avoid by themselves, but because you also have to use certain weapons against certain enemies, this created a situation where damage was not only unavoidable, it lead to frustration. In some cases it also means that overlapping enemies cause unavoidable damage or create weird situations because you want one dangerous enemy out of the way but can't because a dull suit blocks all your shots in a tight hallway.The last thing I want to highlight is the bad use of ambush scenarios in this game. Because arenas are often fairly small, enemy reinforcements spawn right on top of you and in blind spots. This lead to more than one death because of course, they also start shooting instantly. Not only does it give the player no room to breathe, it also doesn't give a warning of where enemies will be respawning from, creating blind sides and cheap shots, leading to more frustration.Now this sounds really bad and in parts, it is, but I ultimately still had some fun with this game because progress was steady (I played on hard difficulty), the story silly and fun and the 2nd boss is one of the best in recent years. The final boss however could've been cut in half and nothing would have been lost.Because of this, I will still rate this game up.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Had a good time with FPS, my only 2 gripes with it are that I hoped it had a couple more levels and that the screen gets too cluttered for me in the later levels because enemies stay on screen after you defeat them in their new stylish selves.Having to use specific weapons for specific enemies can be frustrating when you are not used to it, but it is better than getting guns that get obsolete because stronger ones appear and there's only really 4 of them so it's not a big deal. Everything else is charming, fruity, punny, cool and just downright fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good retro shooter that's very meta. It plays with the tropes of the FPS genre (turret sections, sniper sections, wolfeinstein level, etc.). The rock/paper/scissors game-play is gimmicky, but not too bad either. The humour is okay (the game doesn't take itself too seriously) and the design of weapons and enemies is pretty cool. My only real complaint is the use of a checkpoint save system. Which sucks when you have to through a platforming section.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Uhh fun first few levels but the last few levels are absolute slog that ruins the fun I had with the game in the beginning. From a flasher type enemy that genuinely, is really annoying not due to difficulty but simple due to you having to shoot and wait shoot and this simple enemy will take you 10 seconds off game play of you just standing moving slightly and shooting OR their is an absurd amount of them there and you are simple just being abused to not difficulty but unsight readable gameplay and being overwhelmed by the absurd number of other types enemies on your screen that just constantly pour out extremely bright lights so you can't see anything. I genuinely wish I could give this a recommendation but I do struggle with this simple due to the fact that that the last few missions of the game ruin absolute charm, fun boomer-shooter type of gameplay, gorgeous artstyle and fun lil characters in it. _childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent game, gets a lot harder at the end due to the bosses overpowered attacks and the small space you have to avoid them, but not impossible, and kinda fun. Maybe a little pricey, wouldn't be worth anything more than it is due to the amount of missions and overall main level's fun playtime.
