_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Short "boomer shooter" with a fun twist in that you don't kill or hurt anyone, you just fix their fashion...with guns. Goofy dialogue and overall just silly tone, with a story that doesn't really start or lead anywhere. Had a good time with it, just long enough that it didn't overstay its welcome. Easy recommendation if the idea of it appeals to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I will give Fashion Police Squad a pass.The couple of hours at the start are great after that it becomes burdensome to continue mainly due to fact that a certain type of weapon is required to deal with specific enemies and enemies tend to pop up all around you. Turning Fashion Police Squad into a tiresome experience which is a bit disappointment because the opening hours were great to experience with its setup and flashy colors.But yea, Fashion Police turned into a bad Transformer movie near the end with a seemingly endless boss that shows up.I will give it a 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game so far. I especially like the look, the insanely groovy soundtrack and the interesting but simple gameplay, with the different weapons and enemies. It's fast, entertaining and fun.It's nice when games become more retro again, but with new ideas. Turn off your head, have fun, enjoy the soundtrack and chuckle at the dialogue. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a very interesting take on the boomer shooter genre. Aesthetically, its obviously very different from something like DOOM, but it still brings some fantastic gameplay and a banger soundtrack to the table. The most divisive part of the game is most likely its "Rock Paper Scissors" style enemy  and gun design. Each enemy type can only be damage by a specific weapon (or one of 2 weapons in a couple of cases).  This style of combat definitely takes some getting used to, but once I got into the swing of things, it was a pretty engaging gameplay loop, especially in the last few levels once all of the enemy types had been introduced and the game really started throwing its most sadistic enemy combinations at me.The early levels feel pretty basic, but the game really comes into its own part way through mission 6 (which is about half way through the campaign) when you unlock the fourth gun. The additional movement and resource management it adds to your kit really make this game's combat shine.For me, the low point of the design is the third weapon you unlock, the sock gnome. It manages to have extremely limited utility and feel really unsatisfying to use. Only 2 enemies in the game even take damage from the thing and the amount of delay between clicking and actually throwing one felt pretty awful. Not to mention the first enemy you meet that you need it for is easily my least favorite to deal with. It felt like a very underbaked part of the game that desperately needed more polishing.Normally for games like these I like to fill out the collectibles checklist to cap off my time with the game, and it does have some fun secret hunting, but its knee-capped by not tracking what collectibles you've found during a level, only letting you know how much you found out of a total at the end of a level. This turns 100%ing the game into a much bigger chore than it should be, and is why i'm probably not going to do that for this game.Additionally, there's a pretty major bug with remapping keybinds. While the game lets you add a new function to any key, it doesn't unbind the old function, making the entire rebinding menu mostly useless. This didn't affect me much as the default control scheme was fine for me, but this really hampers the game's accessibility, and judging from other reviews its a bug that's been in the game for a while with no fix from the devs, indicating a disapointing lack of technical support from them going forward. That said, it was the only major bug I ran into in my time with the game.The campaign was on the shorter side, lasting about 5-6 hours for me, but it was a great time that didn't overstay its welcome. Overall, if you're hungry for a boomer shooter with a unique look and some interesting takes on classic FPS design, i recommend checking this one out. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pretty fun game.  You play as a member of the Fashion Police and stop people committing fashion crimes with various fashion-themed weapons.  There are five primary weapons and two special weapons.  The gun you start out with is the only one that "reloads", but it doesn't really add to the game.  The rest of your weapons have infinite ammo.The story is pretty basic, but good.  There's some form or another of unfashionable conspiracy going on and your team gets to the bottom of it.  The various enemies are committing different fashion faux pas and you have to use the right tool to correct it.  Some of them can be resolved in more than one way.There are secrets and collectibles, none of which unlock anything except for maybe an achievement.  So, there's not much point in getting them unless you're a completionist.I don't know that there's any death in the game.  Enemies are just transformed into fashionable people and the main character gets "worn out" if his health depletes.  Oh yeah, mocktails are your health.  I love mocktails.  So, I thought that was cool.My favorite part of this game is its look, understandably.  The retro graphics and urban, fashionable settings are gorgeous.  Very few parts, if any, looked dull.In the end, this game is good fun and is intended to be silly.  If you like retro FPS games and have an eye for fashion and comedy, give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating and extremely entertaining first person shooter! The characters and story are charming, even and especially Des, the policeman you play as. More than that, the mechanics behind the gameplay are entirely unique, in a good way. Certain enemies can only be defeated with certain weapons, making the player think about who they're fighting and how they're doing that. Each weapon and enemy is introduced in a way that helps the player understand what's going on very quickly, and without excessive exposition.There's never going to be another game like this one, and I am *very* satisfied with it even after playing it to 100% completion!(On that note, I *love* that you get an outfit that makes the game a breeze AFTER the main story is complete. With that outfit, I was EASILY able to rush through the levels to scour them for secrets and collectibles.)
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Although Doom Eternal was a disappointment for me, this game was a good surprise and a replacement of choice in the same shoes.Fashion Police Squad is all about using the right weapon on the right enemies at the right moment. Some sort of strategic FPS where you need to think fast.I'd start off by saying the very idea of swaping firearms for fashion and sewing accessories is brilliant and very well thought through and implemented gameplay-wise. You don't "kill" people here, you shoot at them to save them from their own unfashionable misery, allowing them to redeem with style. That's an absurdly refreshing and memorable concept, yet efficient way to make an original doom mod.The pixelart is nicely done, cute and fun; the animations are cool and detailed; the soundtrack is great and catchy; the gameplay is punchy and dynamic. There is no fault in the making of this product.It also has humor and resorts to various pop and internet references if you open your ears and eyes.Finally, there is much flesh on the bone for achievement completists, thanks to collectibles and secrets to uncover.Replay value is garanteed if you want to speedrun the game too : each level is timed and there are features and tools to improve mobility.Still, I did have my gripes about the game. For example, just like Doom Eternal, I found the balance of battles uneven and unfair at times : the further you progress in the game, the more enemy kinds you discover. And they continuously add up until the late arenas get eventually too confusing and intricate. This makes the game tiresome, especially in small areas where you need to watch out 720° around you and constantly move to stay alive. Beyond being challenging, it becomes mostly dumb luck if you survive.All that to say the difficulty raise pretty early on in the game, so be warned.Like all FPS trying to implement platforming and jump puzzles, it is a little janky and offers quite some retries despite its effort to be accessible and straightforward.Finally I found it unexpectedly short. Maybe that's why the difficulty curve felt so steep.But all in all, I got to the end of it, had a nice time and I am fairly glad and satisfied with this purchase.I even think there is still much unexplored potential for a sequel, to go deeper into the concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the bold game design decisions but the gameplay has too much friction. Seeing multiple types of enemies in an encounter gives me proper anxiety. Some levels feel drawn out.Also I could notice the garbage collector. Feels bad man.The bosses were fun. The setting sells the game and makes up for everything I've mentioned above.I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a different take on old-school first-person shooters.I've completed the game on Windows (100%) and played a couple of stages on Linux Mint 21.3. (It runs well using proton experimental.)The story is simplistic. You have to solve a major fashion crime going on in the city as you play through 13 stages (which also include three boss battles). There is some voiceover in the introduction. The enemies also say some words here and there. Apart from that, all the dialogues are text-based. It doesn't take itself seriously. The interactions between NPCs are quite hilarious. There are many references to pop culture, memes, other games, etc., and the characters do not shy away from cracking non-sensical jokes.The visual design is like Duke Nukem 3D (pixelated). The enemies and most objects have 2D sprites. I liked some of the maps. The music and sound design are excellent.There are four difficulty settings: easy, normal, hard, and very hard.I initially played on hard difficulty (up to stage 9), then switched to lower difficulty.You will fix the clothing of fashion violators by shooting (as well as sucking) colors, threads, needles for stitching, etc. Very funny take.There are mainly four weapons. Some of them have alternate fires. These weapons have unlimited ammo.The rocket (the fifth weapon with limited ammo) is given quite late in the game. The belt acts as a melee weapon. It is also useful to traverse, like Spiderman. There are a variety of cool enemies you will encounter as you progress. Some of the enemies are taken from internet memes (LOL)! They should have scrapped the last three enemy types to keep a good balance in the gameplay. But never to be.My main gripe about the game is the gameplay itself. Each enemy must be dealt with a specific weapon or a combination of two weapons. It sounds good on paper, but execution is very poor, in my opinion. It started off pretty well. But around halfway through the game, the fun turned into frustration. There is so much enemy spam of all types at once in the later stages. So, continuously switching between weapons (with alternate fires) became infuriating. On top of that, enemies have high health and hit points. So, you will constantly look for health. The same goes for the boss fights. The last boss battle has so many phases (around 7-8). Totally sucked.The platforming is done by jumping and swinging. The player will not always grapple (instead, snap the belt.) and the jumps are inconsistent, too. So, be ready for some retries. The third challenge stage is completely platform-based. It is quite absurd and unnecessary.The campaign takes 6 to 8 hours (without going for optional achievements). It may take an extra few hours to get 100%. Better keep a guide open.Overall, it was less fun and more frustrating for me. I was eagerly waiting for the credits to roll.You may play this just for jokes and cool music.Purchase it at a heavy discount if you want to give it a shot.My verdict: 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting take on boomer shooters with theme that doesnt take itself seriously. The enemies have a lot of variety and you need to use different guns onn different enemies which is great and horrible. Some enemies I HATED. Like the photographer ... he doesnt have a projectile and does annoying instant damage which on the ahrdest difficulty matters. Also the fire guy? He has like 3 different attacks and spams them constantly even if he doesnt see you.The gameplay is quick and satisfying if you execute everything properly. There are also minigames to break up the gameplay so it never feels stale.This game is worth a try for those that like this genre or shooters overall. The price isnt too steep which also means that the game is short but in my opinion doesnt end too early.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Usually not a fan of boomer shooters and rarely write reviews, but man this game is so good! The humor is so spot on, I was surprised that it got me physically laughing out loud during every mission ... not just blowing its load at the start, but constantly making me laugh and warming my heart with the joy of what a game experience can actually bring. The subtle dad-fashion-jokes (which is an area I'd never would have thought would work so well for these kind of jokes) is just fantastic + always caught me off-guard in a good way. Just brilliant!In terms of graphics, its was so nice to stop and look around at all the amazing references & beauty, I constantly found myself stopping (even during high action areas) to smell the roses at every minor asset. Sure, there is a fair amount of reuse, but I actually found myself relieved to see them again cause it was so good the first time! Absolutely love love love this mix of 3D and pixel 2D art to form a world! So much fluidity + detail in all the 2D graphics, followed by a solid, clean 3D environment to stage it all.The sound is unreal! This is usually an area I find that deters me from a lot of games, but here its clean a hell! Great music! Amazing voice snippets from all characters! Never feels repetitive, even though you are Slayin' hundreds of these characters and a quip comes from every kill. I smiled often when I felt like I cleaned out a room efficiently, and having all the funny quips to confirm every kill, just made every experience amazing!I feel like the gameplay in terms of switching weapons per enemy type, suited my style of playing. A design like entering a room, blasting like crazy, feels mindless to me, so having to evaluate every situation I encountered with what weapons were needed really enhanced my satisfaction of clearing out every area. Also, the variety is really refreshing, and always kept me engaged (not just clear room, move to next, clear next etc.)! Its rare that I finish a game and want to restart right away and play it all again. Only downside was that there wasn't many side challenges (even though I know they are basic + reuse area/enemies but again, was happy seeing that stuff some more anyways). But planning on replaying whole story again, so guess its not the end of the world :) Overall, crazy good game! Wish I had played it sooner! 9.420/10, love seeing the amount of soul from the developer shown here. Can't wait to see what more they will have in store for the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty fun. Was it a masterpiece? Nah, but it's cute and stupid and kills a few hours. I can't say that I like the railroading of having to use specific weapons on specific enemies because it really pretty much controls how you approach any given encounter, but the (two) boss battles are pretty phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Masterfully done, easily the most compelling throwback FPS I've played since the DUSK/Ion Fury/Amid Evil trio. Great presentation, fun movement feel, surprisingly satisfying weapons that feel like they pack a punch, and a very fun campaign that knows how to keep things interesting. I'm loving everything about this so far and I will definitely be keeping an eye out for whatever Mopeful Games does next!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: It was better than i expected it to be, the different puns i really liked.The gunplay was decent and movement as well though way to few poles to swing from in some arenas.Had some lag though my pc is getting old so could be why (really need to update my i5 7500 cpu someday)If they make another i'll pick it up sooner (got this one from Choice monthly bundle, was probably the best one out of them that month)Though some arenas felt way to small for the amount of enemies combined with those that have pushback and you just get pinballed all over the place, saved my special (pretty much Berserker from Doom, invincibility and one shot for a limited duration) for those moments so didn't get too frustrating.Though i didn't like the paparazi (guys with cameras) flashing the screen white, would have liked an option to fade it to black instead as i'm sensitive to bright lights and those encounters hurt quite a bit and makes me nauseus so not very fun.But aside from that it's was a fun game and felt long enough for what it was, each level had it's gimmick or a new weapon so didn't get stale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: ✅Humor and memes on point✅Sheer creativity➖Platforming controls➖Rock/paper/scissors gun mechanics➖Annoying world map mission layoutGame World: In Fashion Police Squad (FPS), the game world consists of basic 3D maps that are similar to old school DOOM, with some advancement in traversal and verticality. There’s not a lot of detail to these levels, but they do often have secrets that require some thought and precision to get to. The levels are massively creative. There’s literally a DOOM level. Car chases, sniping, FPS seems to push the creativity bar up higher every other level or so. The enemies are also pretty hilarious and also provide unique gameplay mechanics while each being their own fashion faux pas. Narrative: The narrative is your fairly traditional copper vs bad guy trope, but with a heavy dash of FASHION. That’s right, you’re trying to stop an evil tailor who is bent on destroying fashion shows with oversized clothes, bad hair, and crocs. The humor is here as the game continues to showcase its creativity. Length: A fairly short game. There’s 13 missions and about 3 optional challenges. I finished it in about 5.5 hours. Controls: Controls like a typical first person shooter from the DOOM era, 1-5 are guns, space is jump, you have no sprint but instead a belt. I played the entire way through with a KBM and the only point of frustration was that the platforming was rough. Especially when you have to increase the speed using the soap gun. One of the challenges is nothing but a platforming speedrun.  Mechanics: The entirety of FPS is based on a rock-paper-scissors type gameplay. Meaning that you have 4 guns (5th doesn’t count, it's the DOOM’s BFG), and each gun correlates to a weakness for a specific type of enemy. You need to use the color shotgun on the black and white guys, the water gun on the flame guys, the pin shooter on the big suit guys, etc. I found this fun and humorous for about the first 7 or 8 missions. Towards the later half of the game things start changing - you have enemies that require multiple different guns, or dual functions of the same guns. And you end up with fights with tons of these different enemies. It's very common towards the end for literally every fight to require you to quickly rotate through all of your guns to make it through an encounter. Things definitely get rough. I applaud the creativity, but wish there was less of a focus on constant gun swapping. Difficulty: First half of the game was easy, I beat all the levels on hard. Toward the later half I was dying many times on normal. The game gets pretty hard at the end. Quality: 2D Pixelated, but very well done.UI: Okay. For actual gameplay, it's fine. I like how the graphics are easy enough to instantly tell the difference between enemies and which gun you should be using. The world map is a bit bad. When you get to the later missions, all the missions and challenges just appear on the map out of order. Could definitely be better done here. Performance: Flawless played it on my desktop PC at 90 FPS. i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSDSound Effects: Good, All guns have a satisfying sound, the enemies say hilarious things. No voice acting aside from enemy lines. Music: Forgettable. Aside from achievements and secrets, there is not much replayability here. Super fun game. Just when it starts to overstay its welcome, something new is introduced and/or the game gets crazy with an entirely new playable concept. Overall, despite the shortcomings, I enjoyed this enough to play through it and would definitely keep an eye out for a sequel or anything else by the devs. $20 might be a bit steep, but definitely get this on sale. _childDocuments_.review: Absurd and somewhat funny, with one of the most interesting FPS concepts ever. The guns generally sound and feel pretty good, but ... the gameplay itself is incredibly rigid, completely railroading you at every turn. It feels like a game jam concept given a light polish and released into the wild, but could do with a ton of extra work.  Every level is wandering forward through very linear paths (often just zigzagging through alleys or offices), occasionally finding an obvious secret because you could jump over a fence or open a vent and it wasn't headed towards your objective marker. Weapons get handed out as a need occurs, so you'll be using nothing but the color shotgun, then get a sewing machine gun the next level, and so on. Every enemy can only be hurt by a certain weapon (sometimes two) - grey suits need color shotgun, scooter bros need shotgun alt fire or, from level 6 on, water gun, vape guys need the belt, etc. And over the course of a level you can save up Swag to get a super slap that gives you 15 seconds to auto kill anything you point it at, so of course the end of every level has a small swarm that shows up. The game is nothing but seeing the enemies, flipping to specific weapons to shoot the one or two guys that are vulnerable, swapping to the next weapon. Nothing is actually a threat. The belt swinging is fun for a second but you can't use it outside of a few areas, so again, just rigid use cases. The game has some charm, but not a lot else. Luckily I got it out of a humble bundle so paid about 2 bucks for it. If you can spend 5 or 10, maybe worth it for a chuckle.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: It stands out of the massive retro shooter crowd by adopting a rather original formula where instead of killing enemies you target them with specific fashion tools. It sounds ludicrous and the idea is quite silly but then this fits just fine in this kind of genre that seldom takes itself seriously.However, Its originality also happens to be its weakest point at times as you can't just shoot your way through but it's a bit like a puzzle game and I didn't find it always super fun for that reason. There's only one weapon near the end which damages every opponent and ammos are quite limited.Anyhow, some of the bosses are memorable (the glitch in particular), it's quite various in style and music, the platforming is quite good (I found it slightly frustrating only one bit near the end) and it's generally quite fun. The length is just right at around 6 hours.Definitely something worth trying, also considering you can find this one for peanuts as it's been bundled recently.Only avoid if you play shooters just to aimless kill enemies because it's not that kind of FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game.Light-hearted boomer shooter with 2D sprites in 3d environment. What I really liked is the entire vibe of the game and the music. It has its own style. Music in general is fitting for a level. I especially liked the tune in 11th mission. But I guess it's not the game for everyone. Although I liked the approach of using different weapons for different enemies (it's not that one weapon is more effective for the given enemy type, you HAVE to use a specific weapon to take down an enemy) it can be tiresome for some people especially later on when all enemies are introduced, and you have to switch weapons a lot during encounters. There is a weapon wheel in the game, but at least I find it hard to use and mostly used the scroll or 1–5 keys. From the completionist perspective, the secrets are fair, you can easily find them if you are attentive enough and explore the levels. There are really hard achievements in the game, the hardest I think is the one with shooting down fashion disasters at the red carpet. You have to be flawless, and some identifying features of the people you have to shoot down are hard to find, especially when there is a crowd.Overall easy recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little modern take on a retro shooter with a neat gimmick of dressing up enemies instead of killing them. It's pretty good to kill an afternoon, but I'd wait for a sale. The writing's fun, gameplay's enjoyable, with the twist that different enemies can only be hurt by certain guns (though some will still stun for a moment). This usually works quite well to make encounters almost like a puzzle. However it does start to fall apart at the end, and it's not great when 6 hours is overstaying your welcome. Personally it starts to drag at the end when every room has exactly 5 waves of enemies. that's way too many waves to be respawning in each room. It's not so much the number of enemies, it's the fact that  they're not coming out of doorways or such. they're appearing in that room, often behind or IN you if it's your first time and you don't know where they're coming. only really an had an issue with stage 12 due to that (and part of stage 7 I think), but definitely worth mentioning.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice change from the monsrers and gore of the retro[-boomer]-shooters. Having to use a specific weapon for each enemy while swamped by different types is a good challenge.That said some of the enemy-weapon combos just make no sense, like tourists and gnomes. Some other enemies are wildcards so you have to wait, and take damage, before you can see what attack to use.Which brings you up to the mid-game boss. Level 8/13. Its just the same attack over and over until he converts into a random type, you attack his secondary health bar, and then you start all over again against full primary health... it goes on for so long there's even a mini-game thrown in the middle of it, which was a welcome break. Anyway, the fight got boring and repetitive very quick so that's where I put the game down.There's a fun spiderman-like traversal mechanic shoved into certain parts of the game, but falling from there resets you very fast to the last edge of solid ground you were on, so if you're still holing forward.. you just run right off the edge again, over and over.The story and writing is great, puntastic, but overall it is only a good game for about three hours, and kind of wasted opportunity.

The map world is a nice touch as well, and there's more content here than I thought there would be. This is a pleasant fun surprise!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy retro throwbacks quite a bit, and this seemed like something that could be a fun Doom-like for simple and satisfying fun. Unfortunately, the mechanics and presentation underwhelmed me and I found myself losing interest after dying many times on a particular battle.To Fashion Police Squad's credit, it does do some things well. The character portraits are amazing (I found the difficulty select screen to be particularly entertaining), the Banjo Kazooie-esque jibberish talk is fun, the music's decent, and the controls feel generally responsive. It's fun to explore levels and discover secrets (the fashion faux-pas posters are a nice touch).However, I found the way combat works got annoying after not too long. As you progress you unlock weapons and enemy types, as well as secondary weapon functions. Each enemy type can only be defeated with specific attacks, which on paper mean you have to strategize and approach combat with a plan to focus on specific enemies before others. In practice, though, it just always felt like I had the wrong weapon out for whatever enemy I encountered next, quick-swapping weapons often equipped me with another wrong weapon, I'd often get hit by enemies that has just spawned right next to me, and it often felt more clunky and frustrating than fun.What's more, the whole idea of fashion police helping people get stylish doesn't really match up with the game's aesthetic. The sprites look downright terrible, not because of the chunky pixel aesthetic (which I'm always a fan of), but because they're just poorly drawn and look like sketches from a pre-teen's doodle pad. They clash tremendously with the (again, excellent) character portraits. You also fight tons of identical-looking enemies (at least three types of which are just variations on "bad suit") in environments without a lot of variation so everything just ends up looking boring after a while.It's not an awful game, and perhaps people more comfortable with FPSs than I might find more to enjoy than I did, but this just didn't click for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun romp with a very over the top style with lots of jokes along the way. Do not try this expecting a top of the line throwback shooter however this game as a shooter has many flaws.My biggest issue is their over reliance on enemies that just have outright undodgeable attacks like the tourist and the DJ. Enemy projectiles also seem really inconsistent whether they hit you or not. The weapon roster is fun except for the gnomes and while it makes sense in the setting being locked to certain weapons if you want to deal with an enemy at all is pretty limiting. The power up mode of the 2dye4 is a cool idea but you don't see this mechanic on any other gun in the game and you rarely get to actually charge the gun more than once or twice per mission. The final boss feels like it still needs some polishing. for example how our partner calls out that they are dropping ammo and refreshments (health) but then only dropping ammo most of the time.Belt swinging is unreasonably fun with the only issue being that it feels like the range is too short. falling isn't overly punishing thankfully but it does ruin the flow of high speed platforming at times.All in all I enjoyed my time with the game because of the zany style and the humor but it was reaching the point where the idea was overstaying its welcome.Get it if you want a really unique old school inspired shooter with a zany story and style but do not get it if you want a brutal but fair high end throwback shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: You aren't necessarily getting a great fps but it's short, silly, and interesting. Campaign is ~4 hours long. Most games have a rock paper scissors foundation where one option is more effective due a specific circumstance. This game turns it to 11 and makes it so an enemy can only be damaged by either 1 or 2 fire modes out of the 5 weapons with 2 fire modes each plus a melee attack. Can't say I like it but it serves the purpose of the silliness of the game and it doesn't stay too long. The weapons don't feel significantly different from each other either because of this rock paper scissors method. You don't use the shotgun weapon because it's the best weapon for the circumstance, you use it because you have to. It doesn't matter if you're 5 feet away or 50 feet. They do have some interesting variety with the turret, sniping, and platforming sections though. There's some annoying bugs in the game. The first is you can't unbind Shift or Mouse 4 from melee attack, even if you do so in the options. The second was just a bug that occurred during the sniper section where the game would visually show me as having a specific type of bullet but be shooting another one until I switched off and back onto that bullet type.I think the best part of the game is when you realize that the end of level Parole Ball catwalk is an actual thing that occurs inside the game world.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: If there was an "average" or similar rating it would be perfect for Fashion Police Squad in my opinion. I'm now playing through many similar DOOM-esque shooters as I have particular craving towards them and I stumbled upon Fashon Police. Main problem is the gunplay. I feel like juggling 4-5 weapons at once vs different enemy types and also trying to stun them in the same time is just too much to do. I finished the entire game, it takes roughly 4h to finish, which for the price is rather... lacklustre. It's a doom-esque game that doesn't take itself too seriously, has pleasant, light tone but comes short in too many places or is straight up too annoying to recomment. That + the parkour fragments are just... They can honestly go to hell. If the gunplay was the worst thing about it(different enemies being able to be hurt by only particular weapon and such), the amount of parkour levels is close second with how tedious and inconsistant it is. The music is pretty good, I have to admit that, humour is pretty decent. But I can't reccomend it fully, or at all at this point as it's pretty much lukewarm for me. There's many, many other, better boomer-shooters out there, Postal: Brain Damaged, Dusk, Forgive me Father(which is now getting 2nd part), Blood West if you're feeling more of an RPG-take on things, WH40k Boltgun... I can go for longer, but it's pointless.TLDR: Fashonless Fashon Police. Game is short for the price, has weird mechanics that don't really go together that much, gunplay is wonky at best, parkour is meh. For the price you can get different(Maybe even 2 if you choose carefully) doom-esque shooters which are much more fun. I can't recomment, but also can't say no. It genuinely lack soul and game itself feels like lukewarm water when you drink it. It's not disgusting, but some pazzazz is missing.

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a very creative take on the fps genre! Rather then the typical killing of enemies in other fps games, you instead solve their fashion crimes with an assortment of weapons from the 2-DYE 4 to the W.A.Rdrobe Launcher. Each enemy type has their own way of being dealt with via what weapon that lines up with solving their fashion crime, this keeps the combat fresh and engaging as your always thing about what weapon you'll need to use next as your amidst a onslaught of enemies. It's got a decent story that has lots of puns and references to not only just fashion, but pop culture in general .Took me about just under 5 hours to finish on the You Reap What You Sow difficulty which makes it short but sweet, there is also plenty of incentive to go back through levels and find all the secrets within them.Overall worth a playthrough if your looking for a unique take on this genre!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more surprising Boomer Shooters of the past few years. It has enough winks at the audience when it comes to the FPS genre, even segments that are very much akin to legends of the genre, but it does everything with it's own style. I love the fact that every enemy type needs somewhat of a different strategy to take down, without it feeling too gimmicky. The graphics are very cool. It reminds me of those early 3D Arcade games for some reason. The soundtrack is very much like that era as well and sounds great. Also a shout out to the self aware humor, which goes a long way in enjoying this game.Another thing that makes Fahsion Police Squad is the variety it has. Just when you think you know what's coming, it throws out another curveball. I love it for that. Although the game is not very long, it is well worth getting it. If you're really picky on playtime vs what you pay, then just get it on sale. But if you're a fan of shooters, you NEED to play FPS. It's fabulous!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is quite possibly one of my favorite FPS games I've played. On the surface it seems like a silly boomer shooter type game, and at it's heart it technically does count as a boomer shooter. But like the fashionable aesthetics, this game has *pizaaz.* The weapons each serve a different purpose and therefore only work on certain enemies, but there's a ton of variety with the enemies so it never feels like it's tacky or hard to play around. On top of that, you have a bona fide grappling hook which makes the combat fluid and flashy. The weapons feel punchy and weighty so you really get that visceral  oomph that an fps game should have. The boss fights are also air tight with a ton of unique mechanics and they're genuinely pretty tough. On top of all of that though? The game is just happy. It's very tongue in cheek with memes and other references, but the idea of fixing people's fashion is silly and surprisingly satisfying. Iduno, its just nice to see people in their snazzy new outfits doing a lil dance. The game feels just so fun and joyful. The way the main character Des is just always so happy to see everybody, the aesthetics, the story in general, it's so damn unique for an fps game. I highly recommend it, and i give it a 9 on the arbitrary number score scale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic example of successfully going against conventional game design. Most well-made boomer shooters would try to have more variety with weapons and have the player decide what works best on what specific enemy. This one decided to have enemies who can only be damaged with specific weapons which sounds absolute ass on paper but manages to have it work with unique enemy designs and good enough movement.Also It's a fountain of memes if you like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: If you like playing boomer shooters and want something that's a little different than the norm, this game is perfect for you. Very funny and with a great soundtrack and gunplay, Fashion Police Squad is definitely a hidden gem within the boomer shooter sub-genre. However, sometimes the game can spike in difficulty without warning and the constant weapon switching in order to attack enemies can get very tedious. Fortunately, the game is only 13 missions long with 3 boss fights, so it doesn't overstay its welcome. 100% the game can be very obnoxious, especially when you have to replay missions two or three times just to get every piece of armor or kill every enemy in the level.Overall, I would recommend this game, but don't go into it thinking it's going to be some kind of masterpiece or change the genre for the better. Probably in the 7/10 range if a numerical rating is what you go off of when determining buying a game. Worth a play, not necessarily worth it to 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Wolfenstein, Doom, Duke Nukem, or any of the other classic boomer shooter, you will love this game. It feels good to move, shoot, and fashionize those in need. The classic art and level design are top notch. The setting of each level aren't too varied in the beginning, but get much better in the second half of the game. The soundtrack is also superb with plenty of tunes to jam out to.Also, Mission 8 is so hype. It's everything I've ever wanted.Would highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a boomer shooter with a really fun gimmick that never outstays its welcome. The style of the game is impeccable. The sprites look great, the sounds including quips from the various enemies are fun, and the soundtrack is an absolute banger. The concept itself is top tier. I love the idea of a shooter where you don't actually kill anyone, you're simply looking to fix their abysmal outfits. The game oozes enough charm to draw you in, but foremost it is a solid shooter so its not just style over substance. Pair all of that with an entertainingly silly plot and some actually incredible boss fights, and you have an doom-like that really stands out from the crowd.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Great style, great energy, great music. The main twist is that each of your  fabric-fixing armaments only work on specific  weirdos. Thankfully, you've got infinite ammo, so no need to worry about running dry when, say, paint is in high demand. Although, the emphasis on switching weapons does mean there's no tearing it up with just you and your shotgun.Given how dime-a-dozen boomer shooters can be nowadays, most of the Fashion Police Squad’s real identity comes from the fashionista flavoring that's so frivolously flung about. It's a bit overly ambitious at times, but the dialogue and theming are constantly charming. That said, the boomer shooter gameplay is still suitably face-paced and high-octane, but the game may have included too many cramped close-quarter encounters. The boss fights are also a real treat. They're the peak of the game's humor and action. Besides whenever dense clouds of enemies produce obnoxious voice lines together on repeat, I can't say there's much to complain about in Fashion Police Squad. It's worth a play if the genre and premise draw your attention enough to read Steam reviews about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10A simple and fun FPS game with a different take on fighting enemies.Fashion Police Squad is a game that doesn't try to reinvent the wheel and keeps it simple - there are enemies and you must shoot them to defeat them. The difference is more based on the game's theme, as instead of killing enemies, you're instead fixing their "fashion crimes" like clothes too drab or too bright, unfit suits, sandals with socks, etc. However, this also affects gameplay somewhat, as each enemy requires the right gun to be used in order to defeat them.There are 5 guns in total, in addition to a belt that is used as a whip both to stun enemies, break boxes and to move around when latching it onto certain objects. Enemies are pretty varied - not only in how they look and their weakness, but also in their attack patterns, and it never feels like you're fighting enemies that are just copies of other enemies. Level design is pretty well done for the most part and keeps encounters with enemies interesting, with only a few frustrating sections, and secrets to be found on each level.Bosses are also interesting, with different weaknesses and attack patterns, in addition to having multiple phases - the last one in special is a lengthy but fun battle (though with some frustration sections too).The story, as expected, is all based on said fashion crimes and someone being behind them, with the main character trying to unravel what's going on while fighting through fashion criminals and it's all meant to be funny - not everything sticks, but at least some of it does and helps in giving the game a charm of its own.All in all, it's an enjoyable and very well done game that looks great and plays great.The only downside I can think of is that it's not a very long game that also doesn't have a lot of replayability besides achievements, though I'm personally not sure if I'd even call it a downside, as I'd rather have a game that knowns when to end than one that is needlessly stretched with filler content.The game could also benefit with options to turn off dialogue and enemy introductions, at least after beating the game once - there is quite a bit of dialogue in each level which generally interrupts the game and, while the dialogue and some scenes can be skipped, it feels unnecessary to go through them all over again after having beaten the game once and it'd be good to have the option to play each level without anything interrupting the flow.Easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: An original DOOM-esque shooter, this is a game you can expect to run around and take down baddies with your arsenal of tailor-made fashion weapons. From a tie-dye shotgun, to sewing machine gun, to grenade-gnomes that like socks, and finally a water gun that doubles as a traversal tool. Art design is in a charming pixel style with enough detail to provide pretty colors and an overall look that is very enjoyable.Writing is campy but in a good way, fun and a good laugh if that's your humor. Since it's all about fashion all the characters are absolute fashionistas and divas but in the best ways.This game is also *filled* with internet references that are a joy to find.Only downside is that I did not see any controller support when I first played, but must admit I haven't tried again since so that may have changed.Overall if you're up for a game that can give you a challenge while not taking itself seriously, and you enjoyed the DOOM style gameplay, then go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Spot onto the vibes of its sources of inspiration.+++ Novel twist on FPS gameplay mechanics.+++ Impactful sound direction.--- Some poorly-thought, over-chaotic encounters.--- Limited replay value.8 hours of a playthrough will almost feel like just 4 hours chiefly due to how slick-smooth the experience can be.  It's a wonderful lens into a bygone era of classic gaming, not restomodded so much as redesigned with all of that history kept well in mind and plentifully referenced.  Very much addressed to the 90s crowd, but younger players will absolutely find a lot of fun too.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: THE CAMPERY! This game is so amazingly made!Pros:- The Camp humour is amazing- The gameplay is well done with so much attention to all the small details- The unique aspect of certain guns for certain characters is a nice twist on a classic game style that they did so wellCons:- Some aspects of the certain guns for certain enemies can be Emerson ruining.- The swing skills can be a lil off to use in practice- I wish the ability to save and chapter select would be available more frequently and earlier.It's a lovely game and I think it is not just present well but ads such a fresh take. I give it 5/5 Fashion fixes
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: The AGDQ run of this game was so incredible I knew I had to get a copy. It’s a solid and unique FPS, with lots of humour, fun mechanics and a ton of secrets to search for.The boss fights all have interesting, unique mechanics; individual enemies require different techniques to defeat them; and the levels each have different features so the game never feels like you are just crawling from one area to the next. Highly recommended.Also, if you’re interested in speedrunning, the speedrun of this game has a low skill-threshold for entry and runs last between 25-40 minutes depending on the category. The community is also very helpful and welcoming.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun and very stylish FPS. It's not very tough (which I usually prefer), but that fits this games chill & goofy style. It's got a good sense of humour too with some great characters. It was always entertaining going through the short cutscenes and dialogue in each level. It's a little too linear for me, but that's not something that makes me dislike it very much. The enemies have a lot of fun variety and really pushed me to learn how to keep on the move, use the belt frequently, and quickly swap weapons for what was needed. Some encounters were a little overwhelming and felt poorly balanced, but that's really just the odd encounter here and there. Plus you should have more than enough tools to deal with those encounters.Pick this one up! It's a  time!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid boomer shooter with a unique twist. Visuals are my cup of teas, the platforming sections were pretty fun, though there was times it felt a bit jank. The gunplay and combat loop is pretty satisfying and fun imo. This game also has some pretty damn good music as well that surprised me. Game is a bit short though for the price, so unless you're a boomer shooter person I'd say wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to write a more detailed review but it was a struggle for despite my opinions of the game. So quick review format it is.Pros:-Gunplay that revolves around fixing bad fashion choices which emphasises picking priority targets with the right weapon.-Good level design that never makes you feel lost.-While I have no fashion sense since I wear woolly jumpers whenever possible, this game was really really silly and stupid and I love it. The reveal of the main villain was one of the funniest scenes in the game.-The boss fights are amazing. It’s really hard for me to think an FPS boss is good since it’s usually just shoot at it til it dies, but the need for different guns help spice these encounters by a lot.-I enjoy most of the game diversions like the intermissions of the Swagman boss fight, the sniping section that requires you to look at your targets carefully, and the turret section.-Music is fun and upbeat and the locations look great. Also find the lyrics to the final boss track, their ridiculous and really fitting for the boss.Neutral:-While most fights aren’t a problem, there are a few that can be a pain due to a small area like the final fight before the boss or an unfair hazard like the subway battle with the electric tracks in the middle.-I think there could’ve been more enemies with two fashion crimes and the flashers could had a bit more to them like flame cloths.-Could have used more challenges instead of just three like one where you have to use the rocket launcher to hit five perfect targets or harder versions of the turret or snipping sections.-The Dye guns reload can be a bit annoying since it’s the only gun that has a reload at all.-I know it’s for story reasons but I don’t really like that the characters talk about how I need a key to get into the next area where other games just have the lock door and make you explore.Cons:-While I didn’t mind the water guns’ way of making you move faster and I actually enjoyed those sections for the Swagman fight and challenge 3, the belt being used to whip across poles is annoying to get right and will drain your health fast.-While the final boss is great, the phase where you have to do a skating mini game is hard to control, stressful and just plain bad. Final bosses are the worst place to have new mechanics that are completely different from the main game.-DJ-2-Loud isn’t as well tutorialised as the other enemies as she has a nasty attack that’s impossible to avoid, but doesn’t teach you how to deal with it.Score:9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Certainly the game of all time. I've tried a few boomer/arena shooters, but this is the first one I've ever beaten--and I'm glad it was! A great combination of solid gameplay that teaches you the importance of using different weapons, insanely funny dialogue that takes the piss out of both the Fashion and Gaming industries, and an overall presentation that's goofy yet charming and stylish. Absolutely recommend it.Yaaasssss(gags)(falls over)(pukes)(explodes)
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: In one sentence: "Lighthearted FPS themed around fashion- more old school in approach than other boomer shooters out right now."I think Fashion Police Squad is a good game to play. The team behind it (very small) made something fun and pretty original (can't say I've played a fashion shooter before, or any game about fashion). There is a lot of care to get things right, which sadly isn't all perfect, but as a whole this game was a clever, bite sized shooter for me. I beat the game in about 5 hours on the 2nd highest difficulty- I'm not the best at shooters so this was a good challenge level for me. I am also working on getting 100% achievements which should take me a little bit more time.I mentioned some things don't quite work. For one, the belt whip attack/grapple is a bit awkward. I got used to it but it really needs more clarity on when its ready to use on the next flagpole or what your momentum will be post launch.Enemies are only affected by certain weapons which didn't bother me at first but when I got into a combat arena filled with a bunch of enemies, needing to rapidly swap between weapons didn't feel as cohesive as I imagine it should be. You swap guns quite smoothly but its when firing that the pace stutters. Unlike doom its not like weapons are less effective-some guns do nothing to certain enemies which can really bring you out of the experience.I wouldn't say that ruins the game but it is the central issue in FPS. The game doesn't develop on its shooting beyond "certain guns for certain enemies", partially because its not super long. That's a good thing too, as just as the charm started to fade the game finishes up.Overall, FPS is worth a play if you like shooters and want to play something more humorous and easygoing. I don't know if I will ever have a reason to play this again ( no multiplayer btw) but I had fun and think FPS delivers on what it promises.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: While so far I am enjoying Fashion Police Squad I do find the levels pretty linear and the combat and enemy placement a little lacking not helped by me having to use the specific attacks or combos on certain the enemy (it does lead to some creative boss fights though). It probably doesn't help I just finished Cultic which was cheaper and generally more fun. Still I like Fashion Police, the characters are funny, the art style is pretty colorful, and the movement feels good, I especially like the belt swinging once I got the hang of itI guess I give this game a thumbs up because I'm having fun, but maybe look at Cultic first which also has a free demo.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most original shooters in years! You don't mow down hordes of enemies,you fix their fashion!  Only negative is the later levels throwing a ton of enemies at you in small arenas,which things a bit too hectic,given the rock-paper-scissors nature of the shooting. Otherwise a fantastic,and funny shooter that is well worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: this game made me more self conscious of the way i dress, and THAT scares me more than any doom game ever could :) the flow/controls of this retro fps are just perfect. it just feels so right. some parts are kind of tedious and checkpoints could be more (in places). overall very fun experience (8/10)
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: All style, no substance.The game has a lot of charm and starts off really good.  Unfortunately, the ugly side shows before too long.  The level design is not competent.  The game designers must have been really impressed with their jumping controls, as there are many parts of the game where long-jumping and whipping is necessary, and they really aren't as great as they think it is (especially the long jumping).  The game commits the unforgivable sin of spawning enemies right on top of you without warning.  I could forgive the above and recommend this game, but the final boss is really a dealbreaker.  This is probably the most incompetently designed final boss I have ever seen.  It makes me wonder if the person that designed this final challenge has ever actually played a video game before.  Ultimately, it is a funny game that starts off very strong, but runs out of ideas by the end. 2/5
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fun take on classic FPS games. A nice change of pace, you don't kill the enemies, but fix their style. Each enemy requires a different "weapon" to fix them, and some require switching between "weapons" on the fly. This gives the game a bit more of a challenge than the usual "grab the biggest weapon and blast away" mechanic of most FPS games. I alos really love the visuals of the game, and the fact it doesn't take itself too seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The visual style and humor border on campy sometimes but it hits really well in context and it's apparent that's what the developers were going for. The gameplay is fun and refreshing enough, with enough variation to not bore you. There's improvements that could be made on the platforming and some of the bosses in general, but it's a blast to play either way.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Short but endearing, Fashion Police Squad delighted me even back when I only had the demo to play. The game is a fun yet non-violent shooter that involves solving "fashion crimes" in different ways, even if some overlap. It also rewards keen eyes with secrets hidden in different levels, and completionists with star ratings for each level, harking back to old FPS games with crimes solved, items found, and secrets found. My only complaint (aside from the short length of the game) is that some of the deviations from the normal gameplay, like certain extended platforming sections and  can feel finnicky and unintentionally difficult, even on subsequent playthroughs. At its core, however, Fashion Police Squad takes its concept and sews it together into a fashionably solid game, something which I can certainly admire the effort behind.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Found this game via a Reddit post on the Gaming sub, and definitely recommend. Gameplay is a fun and fresh take on the 1st person shooter. It's never not amusing to turn your opponents fabulous. The variety of weapons and tactics means that each encounter can be tense and as you progress, the more varied the skillset you'll need to employ becomes. Very few downsides, but one is the jump mechanics can be a little frustrating at times since you sometimes need to land precise jumps to reach either hidden easter eggs or platforms. This just means that you need to be mindful of your health and swag when going through certain areas as you'll need a couple tries to make it through. I'm also not a big fan of the default hotkey for the belt, makes combat a little awkward at times when you need to quickly change to stun certain opponents. But I'm playing around with other combos that may work better for me so don't allot too much weight to this. Overall, nicely crafted game, entertaining story, well done devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an 11/10 in my book. The humour is great, and the action is fast paced and constantly throwing new challenges at you. As you learn the game and get better weapons, the enemies match your speed and style with new attacks of their own, and a bunch of humour to go with it. The game leaves you with a satisfying conclusion, and it never seems to miss. If anyone is on the fence about buying this, don't be. Just buy it. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! Fabulous art and sound design, challenging gameplay with lots of interesting weapon/enemy interactions. Near the end, a few more checkpoints during some difficulty spikes would have been nice, but the levels and bosses were fantastic! The movement physics were also VERY impressive for a 2.5D game! 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, done right.A "Throwback" FPS shooter with a unique mechanic that you need to match your weapons to the target and with certain things like special techniques and generally useful weapons that stun and handle CC even if you can only defeat enemies with specialized weapons or specialized combos. The game is also super wholesome, with no death and ever villain getting a redemption moment as you fix their issues resolved, even if the issues are often wearing baggy or too tight suits. It's around 8 hours long, but longer if you want to go back through to ace levels and get a better score, along with challenge levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet retro shooter. Solid game mechanics, has a satisfying damage system that requires you to switch weapons on the fly. Stays pretty PG up until the last enemy type, made me laugh so hard when they showed up. The game has tons of jokes and puns throughout. Only about a 3-4 hour romp through, most "retro shooters" are 2-5 hours long. Not a deal breaker just something to mention of since I see it in reviews a lot over the genre. 9/10, heavily recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic!The gameplay is very fun, with a bunch of clever weapons that feels pretty fabulous to use.The humor is on point, and the music is banging!Movement is fun to use, but can be a bit janky at times.anyhow I can't give this game a recommendation, because Gianni is in it and I can't actually kill him 1/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a game developed by Mopeful Games and published by No More RobotsThe game offers some amazing graphics and a beautiful aesthetic, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessFashion Police Squad overall, however, is a fun game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a really good action arena shooter to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is one of the most fun games I played in 2022!It is an excellent comedy shooter where both the comedy part and the shooter part is very well-made. I chuckled a lot seeing the goofy story and all the references, and the gameplay was solid enough to keep me interested until the end of the campaign. The enemy design and the shooting is also great: new enemies are introduced just at the right times, the boss battles are awesome and the shooting itself is so satisfying that many other FPSes could easily take note!One or two levels in the middle of the campaign contain too many tight corridors for me but luckily, the last third of the campaign does make up for this with great level design and overall great flow. And that is pretty much all the criticism I have! Otherwise, there is a good gameplay variety and while the campaign doesn't take too long to beat, those 5-6 hours are a lot of fun and dripping in style. (I mean, have you seen an end level stat screen with all your enemies dancing and showing off?)So don't miss out on this gem - Fashion Police Squad easily earns my wholehearted recommendation even at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Received as a bday gift. Fans of Doom, Quake, Chex Quest and similar titles will find a lot to like here. The theme was refreshing too - Trying to make the enemies stylish using specific weapons meant each encounter required a bit of thinking in addition to the usual hopping around madly avoiding enemy attacks. The game had a big ramp in difficulty around the 6th or 7th mission, so if you are worried it's too easy see how you feel after you reach that point. I didn't have any issue with the rope swinging but if you aren't a big fan of platforming you may get frustrated at certain segments. If the game looks interesting to you, I'd definitely say pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Great game full of character, constant new enemies, some of the funnest boss fights ive ever played, and excellent engaging shooter gameplay. the only gripe i have is the checkpoints are a little bit harsh; i'd be stuck in an area and get to the next area and if i died it'd send me back to before the area i was stuck in. Other than that this game is fun af and always fresh
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Great FPS. Fun and well done. The core idea is that you have to use the right weapon against the right enemy or else it won't work. And you can have a lot of different enemies at time.And even if it can looks like a "joke game" at first, it is not. It's silly and lighthearted, but it can be difficult at time and is clearly made by peoples who likes classic FPS. The bosses fight can even be quite tight at higher difficulty.So if you like classic FPS but want something lighthearted where you don't kill anyone and have a couple of chuckles, go for it. It's totally worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Hella fun FPS game oozing with style, i went in thinking it'd be fun, but it was way more than i expected, its a super tight shooter that is beyond satisfying to play, add in a fun little story, great art direction and a bangin' soundtrack, and you've got yourself one of the best FPS games i've played in a while, can't wait to see what the devs do next!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I've only had the one 3-hour session with it, but I am thoroughly enjoying this game! Between the silly atmosphere and the satisfying, if sometimes overwhelming, combat, this is a great game. I also feel particularly targeted by a lot of these easter eggs and references sprinkled in! Don't just gloss over this as "just another boomer shooter," or "just another brightly-colored indie game," this is worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game dude. This. Game.  As a boomer shooter, it's great, combat is more akin to a puzzle in my opinion, certain enemies need to taken out with certain weapons. Mechanically pretty interesting and doesn't interfere with the flow of combat like you might worry it would, least in my experience. But beyond that. This game, it's just ridiculous, just completely over the top ridiculous.  Not just the type of ridiculousness you'd expect from a game named Fashion Police Squad lemme tell ya, it goes above and beyond that level.  I don't want to get into specifics as that'd ruin half the joy of seeing what's in store for you. If you want a fun old school boomin' and shootin' experience this game is certainly a good one, but ya know how people say it's got bells and whistles? This game has a whole marching band dancing and making noise with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: My Indie Ramble video on the game: I give this game a thumbs up because while it wasn't really for me, I can see a lot of other people liking it. If Steam had a sideways thumb option, that's definitely what I would give it.This game is soaked in a colourful style that while absurd, will make you laugh. In a sea of good, but often dark and grimy shooters, this is a very welcome thing indeed. The graphics are obviously inspired by classic shooters, but occupy a space somewhere between those and newer games. It's a good look that can make fans of classic shooters happy, while not requiring younger players to appreciate nostalgia so much. You also have unique variants on most classic shooter weapons, all themed around the fashion you're trying to restore. You also don't kill anyone in this game, which is definitely refreshing and can make it good for kids to play.Unfortunately, none of this style makes for an interesting shooter. While the guns are cool, they almost all have unlimited ammo and most enemies can only be damaged by one gun, or sometimes two, though the second won't be nearly as effective. This adds a unique enemy management strategy as you try to thin out crowds by quickly switching between guns, but it also removes the creativity to approach battles in different ways and having to manage ammo as you do so, something common in most other shooters.The level design is also very simplistic and frankly, pretty boring. Everything in this game is just boxy arenas. You'll go into a box, fashionize a group of enemies, move onto the next box, which is often separated by a small platforming section, fashionize another group of enemies, and so on. Later levels mix things up a little bit, but most of these arenas are small enough that again, there's no opportunity to approach things with much variance beyond what the designers intended. Everything is super linear and an attempt to deviate much from the plan is just not supported by the design and mechanics.I finished the game after streaming it, before I made my video on it. If I hadn't been given a press code for it, I don't think I would have been happy paying full price for it. On sale, it can make for a fun few hours (or longer if you want to find all the secrets), but if you're a big shooter fan, you're spoiled for options right now. This one just feels like more style over substance to me. That said, I recommend it because while this isn't really my jam, I could totally see people (especially younger ones) getting into it and you can tell this was a game that has heart. I do hope it can get a sequel and that the developers can flesh out these shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun and unique! I have waited 3 years for it and definitely worth the wait! I will say, Karen is possibly the hardest enemy I've ever encountered in a game. Some pros, it's beautiful, it sounds great and the soundtrack is phenomenal. So many funny and cool inside jokes and irl references, it's hard not to crack a smile at every new corner you come around in town. Also, plenty of weapons and items that make the game more interesting!Cons, the difficulty, even on Easy can be brutal. I'm not the best and some times I'd find myself at my wits end with the lack of healing items on occasion as well as the massive influx of enemies. Despite this, it's still such a fun game it's hard not to press through and see the ending!Also, cool outfits and unlockables, the secrets are fun to find and you can tell a lot of love was put into this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Not killing enemies and instead leaning their weakness to "fix" them is a really cool idea (and rare to find!) that keeps you on your toes with the ever increasing difficulty of combined enemy types coming at you.Haven't finished the game yet, but halfway through it now and can already recommend this fun twist on 90's style FPS games.Also, "Hamazon" being advertised as a service to buy Ham just makes me laugh every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: The cleverly titled FPS, or Fashion Police Squad, is a delightful, colorful and FABULOUS game! Instead of ripping and tearing, you're defeating your enemies by solving their fashion crimes, transforming them from drab to fab! It's a creative concept that works really well, giving you great enemy variety, and each type of foe has certain weaknesses to different kinds of fashion based weaponry, from a SEWING MACHINE GUN to the dreaded Sock Gnomes. The levels where you'll be solving these fashion crimes are cozy beyond belief, filled with secret areas to find. The main problem is that there is some copy/paste level elements here and there, such as seeing the nearly same exact park twice in one level. But I love these levels so much, where they take you from city streets to a glorious cruise ship. Heck, you'll even find some truly fab GOLDEN toilets here and there... for no reason besides being funny. Even the bosses are so extra, especially the final boss, that I can't praise this game enough. FPS is an amazing homage to classic shooters of the past, and takes some inspiration from more recent games such as Doom Eternal, all wrapped in a non-violent and fashionable package!
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Boomer shooter with enough mechanics to be different from the others.The story's tons of fun, character design and enemy design really stands out and I really dig the concept of a fashion police patroling the streets.Despite only having 4 main weapons + melee + ultimate, the game manages to throw the same mechanics with different twists, which makes it refreshing every time.It also has swing mechanics, what else can you ask for?10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good. Swag-man boss fight is extremely funny. The Sniper section can go rot in hell, They are don't fit with the rest of the game in my opinion. If there was an alternative where i have to protect someone doing the snipping for me, or an option to just skip the segments, I would gladly take it. the game is still great even with the snipping section. 8/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Great light hearted retro FPS with unique rock-paper-scissors design. If you're a fan of combat-puzzle style FPS design like that from Doom Eternal, this provides a lighter version of that with great music and humor that ties it into a complete package. I highly recommend this to retro FPS fans looking for something fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: A fresh breath in the FPS genre! The game's title is a pun on the FPS acronym itself.. This gives you a clue of the intelligent humor that you will find in this game. From the very inventive weapons and enemies to the non stop action driven story. I was hooked to this game since I played the demo, and immediately bought it on release. There are many things to like in this game, and some minor irritating platforming to be done; but nothing game breaking. Highly recommended to all FPS fans.
