_childDocuments_.review: A unique take on the boomer shooter genre. Some enemy types can be annoying as they throw millions of projectiles, especially when in a group. Has some cool traversal mechanics and clearly inspired by the Doom Eternal "right tool for the job" mindset. Some of the most interesting bosses in a retro type game. Some levels can be too long and they throw too many enemies at you towards the end of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad little game. Short but for the most part pretty good, save for a few bugs and design choices. Style is great, the writing is great, the premise is extremely unique, and the music is top notch. My only gripe really is the combat and platforming being kinda ridiculous sometimes. The subway in particular tested my patience on platforming, and some of the arenas really don't work well with the combat. Speaking of combat, this isnt Fashionable Doom 2, its more like Doom eternal's combat with its emphasis on using whats best against an enemy. Fashion Police goes further by forcing you to use a particular weapon to even have an effect against an enemy. Most wont mind it, but i found it a chore to constantly swap weapons to even deal damage. I would have liked it if the weapons stunned or slowed, then using the right weapon to defeat them. Personal preference honestly, im not going to thumbs down a game because i had an issue where most won't.The last bit are the bosses. Not going to spoil them, but they are EXCEPTIONAL. I wasn't a massive fan of the general enemies, but the bosses are insanely top notch. I highly recommend playing the game just for the bosses. All in all, the game is probably the most unique game i've played in a long time. I look forward to a potential sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty great game. The writing, jokes and references are what really stand out to me and make this special. It oozes with love for games and it's history, and a combination between gaming and fashion was not something I expected.Another big highlight is the bosses, they're all really clever and have fun gimmicks. The subway boss in particular is fantastic.The gunplay and enemy variety is all pretty creative although the lack of more advanced movement options do make the last few levels feel a bit too hard, but hey some might be into it. My only negative is that the game is a bit too short. I beat it in 4 hours 20 minutes but I think the average is around 5 hours. I wish there were 5-6 more levels since when everything clicked at the last few levels it felt like it just ended. A DLC might help a lot with this. Anyway lovely little fun game and I seriously hope theres a sequel one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: before I say anything else, this game is fun, and I highly recommend it. in plenty of fps such as Doom or bio shock the game gives you a wide range of weapons to choose from, however eventually you find one weapon that you prefer more than the rest of them, and all the other weapons are left to gather dust or be used as a last resort. the central mechanic of this game being that (almost) every enemy requires a different weapon in order to defeat them means that you are constantly switching between weapons and it is a lot of fun. sure, the game isn't perfect, there plenty of things I could nit-pick about, such as how the Karen's are annoying to fight as the pepper spray cloud covers such a wide area and takes too long to disappear, but my only real complaint is that the game is a bit overpriced for 4 hours worth of content, but hey, if my only complaint about a game is that I want more of it, I'd say that's pretty good. :)serious though, I'd probably bump the prince down to 14.99 or add a additional 2 hours worth of content.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem that both stands apart from the recent wave of boomer shooters and understands what the best example of the genre all have in common. Like in Doom, Blood, or Dusk, enemy encounters in Fashion Police Squad feel like puzzles that test your understanding of enemy behaviours as well as your arsenal and surroundings rather than just testing your reflexes. What sets Fashion Police Squad apart is the genius conceit of making each enemy type vulnerable to just one or two specific weapons or tactics, which turns that age-old abstract puzzle into a literal puzzle. Another thing that makes Fashion Police Squad unique is that it's completely nonviolent and family-friendly despite being genuinely funny. Now don't get me wrong; as my above list of "best examples" from the genre should make clear, I have no problem with ultraviolence and crass humour being in my videogames. It's just that those traits are so common to the fps classics of the 90s that they've become the unquestioned default setting of the modern boomer shooter. Fashion Police Squad is ultimately brilliant because, while it absolutely nails what made the likes of Doom and Blood so strategic and fun, it's also something that I can share with my young niece without any reservations. Kid-friendly games that are a) genuinely fun, and b), more than just a skeevy microtransaction vector held together by a thin layer of gameplay, are sadly few and far between these days.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Very good old-school FPS with the nice "no kill" twist. The game keeps bringing new enemies and features until the end, and the difficulty keeps ramping up which culminates in a, albeit a bit long, pretty cool last boss. Each enemy types requires a specific weapon and method to kill which makes all weapons useful and varied. A few elements feels like experimentation that weren't taken all the way through (ultimate mode on the first weapon, the gnome isn't super interesting, the slap feels a bit underutilised).All in all, pretty good game that scratches that old-school itch while being original on a few aspects. Easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun, fast paced FPS, with a very creative premise. I am not an avid FPS player but this game was the exception for me, especially with the art and soundtrack. It feels short at times but the references and the humor keeps me into it, even if they are not particularly made for you to fall of your chair laughing. It is a great time, but some glitches appear here and there, such as inescapable places, such as the back of the speakers in the beach levels or some text not displaying correctly, such as a weird overlapping or, in my case, GALA being accompanied by weird symbols. _childDocuments_.review: This game is way more fun than it has any right to be.It's funny, colorful, there's no killing, but it has everything you'd expect in a Doom-like: it has platforming, shooting, weapons management, boss fights, parkour, secrets, collectibles, and challenges.PROS:+ colorful+ challenging+ great sense of humor+ doesn't indulge in cursing or violence+ pixel-y goodness (great art direction)+ understands shooter mechanics wellCONS:- the art style or humor won't be everyone's cup of tea- there's no kind of multiplayer, a wave mode or a gantlet challenge with coop would have been niceThere is mechanical depth to the game, but whether you'll like it or not you'll be able to tell right away in the first level. Try the demo, and don't be fooled by the visuals. It's not "gritty" like every shooter tries to be these days--but it still a wonderful game. The demo's free and there's no harm in trying it out! Who knows, you might love it!I seriously am waiting for Civvie11's review of the full game.UPDATE: During the autumn sale review process it won't let you pick the same game for graphics and soundtrack. I personally find the soundtrack and graphical style to be nomination worthy. However, I ultimately had to pick one. I think I prefer the soundtrack award over the graphics, but I find both to be  good and a good fit for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only made it to the 7th level as of now, but I can assure you that this game is worth your time. The music and overall style  that this game has is great, but one of my favorite things about this game is how the weapons work. In most FPS games I find myself sticking to the same one or two weapons for 80% of the whole game because there is no reason to use the others. (when there is a gun with the best damage why switch?) However the game forces you to constantly weapon swap due to each enemy having their own weaknesses. The only issue I had was any custom keybindings resetting after starting a level or dying, but as of today (8/16/22) they fixed that.I also really like that the elevator music was E1M1
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: For me this was the most anticipated game for 2022, it felt like it took an eternity for it to come out, but it was copletely worth the wait.Fashion police squad is essentially a throw back to fps games from the early to mid 90's, with lots of reference to old videogames (both fps and non fps) while also having lots of references to contemporary art and pop culture.The game is also unique in that it's a non violent fps, similar to classic fps games such as Chex Quest, while also further adding the mechanic that certain enemies are only vulnerable to certain types of weapons. Hence when you got a lot of different types of enemies in the same room this can make for some very interesting situations!The environments are also great, with a lot of great looking architecture. While also having some really fun game mechanics too.The only downside I felt the game had after I completed it, is that despite the fact that there are plenty of varieties of enemies, I didn't feel like having only 5 guns was enough variety when it comes to the type of weapons you have. They could have also considered adding more powerups, instead you only have the glove ability you unlock when you kill enough enemies and the ability to power up your 2dye4 by sucking colour from bright enemies/objects, both of which were already displayed in the demo.At first I also felt the game was kind of slow, but for those who just picked up the game and also feel that way they should not feel discouraged, because if they play a few more levels they will unlock weapons that allow them to travel faster, which you'll also need to be able to advance in numerous levels.But overall it was an excellent game, I would definitely highly recommend it! I just hope they will add more content, whether they just add it into the standard game, or give us DLC's with more levels, weapons, enemies,  bosses and as already mentioned, some more powerups.So go buy and play it, it's definitely something you need in your life! I knew I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: Fashion Police Squad is a great boomer shooter. The dialogue is cheeky and the nods to (then current) shooters from yesteryears are delightful.Movement and controls are smooth and there is enough challenge even on the second lowest difficulty. You'll get plenty gadgets to dish out fashionable justice. There's a good tempo to the combat and the enemies are fun to engage with. Also, the game is kid friendly. That's a plus in my books.I ran into some minor bugs while playing. Mainly Karens flying through the roof but that's really nothing new in 2022. Anyway, nothing too major and I'm sure those pesky little wrinkles will be ironed out. Pun intended.
_childDocuments_.name: Fashion Police Squad

_childDocuments_.review: I am about four levels in (through the beta) and I love this game. This is, without a doubt, the least violent first person shooter I have ever played. In no game that I can think of does you filling someone up with needles or blasting them in the face with a shotgun improve a person's quality of life significantly.Every bad guy requires you to use a different strategy to pacify them. Sometimes it requires the dye gun because the target's suit is dull and gray, sometimes it requires needles because their suit is too big. Sometimes you need to whip a guy with a belt because he can't pull his damn pants up. And at the end of every level, you are greeted with every enemy you defeated (bosses included) going down a runway and looking confident, fashionable and showing it off for the crowd. The game is a love letter to so many different things it's not even funny. To retro gaming, to fashion, to progressive values, to boomer shooters. There is so much charm in this game, it is difficult not to enjoy in some form.. or fashion.

name: Curved Space
detailed_description: Curved Space is an intense arcade-style twin-stick shooter that takes the classic formula and plunges it into the weirdest reaches of space. Battle cosmic space-invading spiders across curved landscapes where bullets hug the terrain while the horizon drops sharply out of sight. Inspired by arcade classics, players will have to hunt for weapon power-ups and upgrades while dodging enemy fire, blasting interdimensional bugs, and wrangling some enormous boss monsters. Simple to learn as you fight your way through the branching story-driven campaign, but tough to master as you chase the glory of the leaderboards. Old School Shmup Reimagined: Enjoy the high-energy action of traditional 2D shoot ‘em ups in a warped 3D space. Climb walls, flip over to the other side of your environment, and experience breathtaking vistas. Play Your Style & Top the Leaderboards: Experience your space pilot’s harrowing journey in Campaign, take on new challenges, test your skills, and chase your place on the leaderboards in Daily Runs, Arena, Survival and Endless game modes. Ride the Synthwave: Get in the zone with a high-energy synthwave soundtrack in partnership with FiXT Neon, featuring artists like Scandroid, 3Force, and Fury Weekend. Upgrade & Take Them Down: Collect a plethora of ability and weapon upgrades. Weapons are varied (from lasers to flamethrowers to weed wackers!) and equipped with their own overdrive states! Campaign: Take on the role of an energy harvester in the midst of a galactic spider invasion. Your choices will lead you to take on one of three potential versions of the game’s protagonist to fight back the invasion on asteroids, space stations, and other intergalactic stages. Each unique version takes the story in a different direction. Arena: Take on over 60 randomized challenges from the game’s campaign for a chance to get your name on the local leaderboard. Survival: Fight through waves of invaders with each wave presenting a new, more difficult challenge.   Endless: Tackle waves of randomized challenges from the campaign as well as additional objectives as you adapt to what the game decides to throw your way. Daily Run: You get one shot each day to complete this daily run and achieve the highest score possible. Failed to make the leaderboard today? There’s always a new challenge tomorrow.

short_description: Curved Space is an intense arcade-style twin-stick shooter that takes the classic formula and plunges it into the weirdest reaches of space. Battle cosmic space-invading spiders across curved landscapes where bullets hug the terrain while the horizon drops sharply out of sight.

_childDocuments_.review: What is this game about:In 3 words Curved Space is about Push Forward Combat. The same phrase used by ID software to explain the combat philosophy of Doom 2016 which results in frantic, nail biting, free flowing combat. It is not that Curved Space was designed to mimic Doom, however good design decisions and good combat often share characteristics in common.Yes the name and the gimmick behind Curved Space, make a big deal out of the technology that enables acrobatic maneuvering and shooting over curved surfaces. Yes the Campaign has multiple paths and expertly voiced dialogue. Yes the weapons are many and awesome and absurdly unique. Yes there is an energy lash that lets you siphon energy from your enemies and energy nodes alike. But that is just where the game starts, that is just how the game pulls you in and shows you its wares. The game really comes alive and starts to shine once you get past all of that and start to dig deeper into the nuanced combat system.Curved Surfaces translate to free flowing navigation and multiple avenues of scape and attack when you are in the thick of battle, multiple weapons translate to choosing your own gameplay style and just as many upgrades translate to, optimizing that play style for maximum efficacy. The lash and the dash however are what will keep you alive, they are the way you ram enemies for insta-kills and extra health refills, and absurd amounts of points on chained combos. Let me tell you: A billion points is possible in this game, perhaps even a trillion, but it will take every ounce of concentration and optimization on your part to claim that victory in the game's public scoreboards.Come play the game, learn the basic combat through the Campaign, hone your skills in the Arenas, and come prove what you are made of in Survival, Endless and Daily Modes. Perhaps one day you will be able to finish the Campaign in Nightmare with all of the modifiers that make the game even harder, including the 'No Continues" (Permadeath) option turned on!But don't think this is only for the ultra hardcore audience, there is a casual mode as well as 5 more levels of difficulty for everyone in between to have fun and leave their mark on the corresponding score board or to collect their platform's achievements. Pick up the game and go as deep as you'd like, you will have fun! I know I have for over 200 hours, and am just as excited as everyone else to keep playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Curved Space

_childDocuments_.review: 'Curved Space' is a cosmic top-down arcade shooter with twisted level design that allows you to loop around corners as you strategically defeat wave after wave of enemies. It’s a novel approach giving you 360 degrees of control over your spacecraft, similar, in some ways, to fellow shoot ‘em up, Super Stardust HD.  The graphics are not the most striking, or original, but 'Curved Space' in motion is a thing of beauty. And the gameplay is super satisfying. Typical shooter mechanics are in place – there’s plenty of diverse weapons, a speed boost and collectable upgrades. One really original feature is your ship’s lash move. You are able to fire out a sort of electric lasso that allows you connect enemies to one another – or tether them to harvest stations.  This is a game that will keep you occupied for some time. There’s a campaign mode featuring an interesting story, with branching pathways, daily challenges, high score challenges, and more. I particularly liked the opening of the campaign mode. Rather than being tacked on, the tutorial is embedded into the story and slowly introduces you to the game’s mechanics one by one. A typical level features several waves of mechanical enemies, each requiring different approaches. You may need to harvest spiders, or destroy a specific radiant variety, roaming the battlefield. The giant bug bosses require strategy, and full use of the twisted landscape to take down. 'Curved Space' is an addictive shooter that has enough features to make it stand out from the crowd.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Game Review of Curved Space:I purchased this game specifically for my D-BOX setup, which utilizes native D-BOX Coded Gaming. All I can say is that this is a very interesting title, especially with motion integration. Essentially, this game is an indie mashup of two popular twin-stick shooters: Geometry Wars and Super Stardust Ultra. You navigate your starship on a 3D polygon surface to eradicate space bugs using geometric shapes. In your quest to climb the ranks and complete the campaign, you're armed with various familiar weapons such as torpedoes, sniper shots, blasters, and other unique arsenals.I would recommend this game only if it's on sale for less than $5. It's a nice addition to your collection of shooters if you're looking for something to play for short bursts of 5-10 minutes of mindless fun.D-BOX Motion Review:As for the D-BOX motion platform's native coding, it is done extremely well. You can feel the spaceship float and swirl on the platform. As you move around, you sway left and right, up and down, and suddenly feel blasts from every corner as the enemies attack. When you pull the trigger on the controller, you can feel the pulse cannon or a charged blast ready to annihilate the space bugs.However, be prepared: if you play for more than 15 minutes, it might test your equilibrium and induce motion sickness. A few of my friends enjoyed it, but the novelty wore off after 5 minutes before they paused the game. As for myself, I could play for hours since I'm used to motion from sim racing and loved the experience. If you have a D-BOX platform, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Curved Space

_childDocuments_.review: Curved Space is an absolute gem that effortlessly combines the charm of Mario Galaxy with the adrenaline-pumping intensity of a bullet hell shooter. From the very start, I was captivated not only by the game's enthralling gameplay but also by the fantastic people behind it, the devs who poured their passion into creating this masterpiece.At first glance, the unique curved environment is striking, reminiscent of Mario Galaxy's innovative design. But don't be fooled by its friendly appearance; Curved Space rapidly escalates into a heart-pounding bullet hell experience. The waves of insect-like enemies swarm you, demanding quick reflexes and precision in every movement.I was pleasantly surprised by how Curved Space manages to suck you into its universe, keeping you engaged throughout. The relentless and hectic combat is a true test of skill, pushing players to their limits while providing an exhilarating and satisfying challenge. Each victory brings a sense of accomplishment that few games can replicate.What sets Curved Space apart is the intriguing storyline that ties each level together. It's more than just a barrage of enemies; it's a captivating journey through space, uncovering mysteries and exploring new dimensions. The attention to detail in crafting this narrative elevates the game to another level, making every level feel purposeful and interconnected.In conclusion, Curved Space is a thrilling and addictive galactic adventure. The combination of Mario Galaxy's whimsical charm and bullet hell's high-octane action is an absolute delight. The passion and dedication of the devs shine through, making it an experience that will undoubtedly stay with you long after the final boss is defeated. If you're a fan of intense arcade shooters and a gripping storyline, Curved Space is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Curved Space

_childDocuments_.review: This game is outstanding and really deserves more attention. Very nice visuals combined with satisfying twin stick controls make Curved Space a great package on the whole. While I tend to favor more traditional shoot em ups as opposed to twin stick games, I really find myself enjoying this title. The presentation really goes a long way to help elevate the gameplay. There is some harvesting mechanics which can bog things down a touch occasionally but I didn't find it to get in the way too bad in my time with the game.Definitely recommend checking this out, and if it is on sale then it is a no-brainer but I think it's worth full price either way.

Probably best with a controller but with a bit of tweaking I got it to where I was pretty comfortable on Keyboard & Mouse.I did get a little bit nauseous after playing for a little over an hour in a single session but I don't play a lot of games along these lines and I do have minor issues with motion sickness so probably not something most people will need to worry about.

_childDocuments_.name: Curved Space

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay is very much a standard twin-stick execution with fast and fluid combat as you navigate these crazy levels blasting away at enemies while moving around the winding curved surfaces, often with disorienting shifts in perspective as you climb walls or even flip the level upside down when you crawl to the other side.  New weapons, power-ups, and other collectibles are scattered about that will keep you competitive with the increasing ranks and power of new swarms and some huge boss battles.What really sets the game apart is the level design, not just the twisting architecture but the Tron-like ambience and futuristic design that incorporate a lot of flashy lighting and neon accents.  Weapon effects are awesome with fire and electricity and disintegrating creatures all over the place.  The way the levels move around a static camera view is really interesting and helps to limit motion sickness, but it’s still a possibility, especially when entire levels flip when you crawl off the edge.  The game is in constant motion as you are always avoiding batches of spiders and other insect-style creatures that come at you from all directions.  There is a rather steep progression of difficulty that kicks in after only a few levels and it never lets up.Full Review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool twin-stick shooter. Its standout feature is of course the traditional 2d twin-stick gameplay mapped to 3d surfaces. But there is a lot of depth here beyond that one hook.  There is a good selection of weapons that provide quite a lot of variety. Playing with the beam weapons as they wrap around the surfaces of the arenas is probably my favorite thing in the game. The lash mechanic is loads of fun as well.There are score-attack game modes, and a number of score based gameplay mechanics, but I've mostly ignored those and played the campaign. The amount of content in the campaign is impressive, and there are some nice twists that surprised me.I found the default camera to be too tight in and twitchy for my taste, but it's highly configurable.A minor complaint and word of warning: when you finish a campaign boss battle and choose an upgrade, the upgrade UI has an option to return to the main menu. Don't click it!  You have to continue playing and let the game exit the level.  Otherwise the game won't save your progress, and you'll need to replay the level. The game does warn you, but I found the whole thing unintuitive enough that I lost progress twice before I understood what was happening.There is so much cool stuff going on in this game. If you like twin-stick arena shooters, and particularly if you like the score-attack variety, then you need to check this out!
_childDocuments_.name: Curved Space

_childDocuments_.review: A super creative and fast paced game that'll keep you on your toes! You'll start off feeling like you can take on anything with your little blaster. However things change very fast and you end up adapting very quickly without even realizing it. You'll start off keeping your distance and trying to stay safe, but after a short while and after gaining some confidence, you'll be charging in trying to lash and dash in no time. Additionally, with the various amount of weapons and enemies you'll have a lot of fun experimenting with combinations while trying to survive.If you're looking for something fast paced with an absolutely bumping soundtrack, definitely give this a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Curved Space

_childDocuments_.review: Curved Space is an intense arcade-style twin-stick shooter that takes the classic formula and plunges it into the weirdest reaches of space. Battle cosmic space-invading spiders across curved landscapes where bullets hug the terrain while the horizon drops sharply out of sight.

name: Death Come True
detailed_description: Everything rides on your choices in this new wave interactive movie game. Experience a thrilling science fiction mystery in full-length live-action format—from genius creator of the Danganronpa series, Kazutaka Kodaka! Simple, intuitive controls mean playing Death Come True is as easy as watching a movie! The choices you make propel the story forward. Which ending awaits? Introduction You wake up in a hotel room, roused by the shrill ring of the bedside phone. You take the call. It's the hotel concierge. 'If you have any issues, please feel free to visit the front desk.' You have absolutely no idea how you ended up here. Disoriented, you try to take stock of your surroundings when you stumble across a woman, tied up and unconscious. Still reeling from the shock, you notice the story on the evening news: You. A wanted serial killer. Then comes a persistent knocking on the door... Cast Kanata Hongo as Makoto Karaki Chiaki Kuriyama as Akane Sachimura Win Morisaki as Nozomu Kuji Yuki Kaji as the Concierge Chihiro Yamamoto as Nene Kurushima Jiro Sato as Kenichi Mino Theme Song Inner Circle Kami-sama, I have noticed (Warner Music Japan) Death Medals Each gruesome death you experience comes with a reward in the form of 'Death Medals.' Acquiring these medals in turn unlocks bonus 'DeathTube' clips. Try and collect them all!

_childDocuments_.review: Death Come True, created by Kazutaka Kodaka, the famed scriptwriter of the renowned text adventure game Danganronpa, garnered significant attention from its initial announcement. However, the final product proved to be a major disappointment. It's not an overstatement to say that the game used Kodaka's reputation more as a marketing gimmick than a hallmark of quality. While Death Come True is not entirely without merit, its quality and gameplay experience certainly do not match its hype and price tag.The game's concept aimed to blend gaming with film, creating an accessible experience for non-gamers through live-action FMV performances. In terms of immersion and realism, the game does provide a decent experience. Its cinematography and atmosphere are passable, and the performance of Kanata Hongo, a well-known Japanese actor, makes the viewing experience smooth and enjoyable. With a simple interface and click-based interaction, complemented by surprisingly good music and sound effects, the game initially seems promising. Yet, as a story-driven game, Death Come True's script is utterly mediocre, fundamentally ruining the player's experience.The game features a stereotypical, retrospective Japanese TV series style narrative, the elements of the much-vaunted reasoning are superficial and impoverished. The plot direction and the core narrative trick are easily predictable for most players. The character and plot logic, although somewhat coherent in the end, are often forced and poorly motivated, with some completely nonsensical plot developments. The other actors' performances might seem passable from a film perspective, but the poor script renders them stiff. The collection of branching storylines in the game is uninteresting; aside from completing all collections, most players are unlikely to choose incorrectly. The additional content fails to expand on plot points that need explaining, leaving much of the story unclear. Unacceptably, the game doesn't allow saving progress and must be completed in one go. The design of only being able to select chapters after completing the game is utterly terrible, and the fast-forward and rewind functions only work in 10-second increments. The game has little to no gameplay elements, which is a relief given its short game flow, otherwise, it would be a torment for players.Viewed as a film, the latter half of the plot is somewhat interesting, making Death Come True passable. However, as a game, it is not the case. Overall, Death Come True feels like an overpriced, cobbled-together work, with a script that often exhibits mediocrity and shallowness, greatly detracting from the gaming experience. If you are drawn to this game by the fame of Ko Takahashi and Tsuyoshi Gang, you will likely be disappointed. Therefore, I recommend this game only to Japanese TV series enthusiasts, FMV game fans, and movie buffs. Also, be wary of spoilers. If the core trick of the game is revealed, it becomes an utterly worthless experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the same creator of Danganronpa, Death Come True is a marvelous FMV with a very interesting and genius gameplay. You play as a person who woke up in a hotel room with no memories of what brought him to this place. He'll meet people who'll tell him what is his identity, or what they thought he is.  I'm not going to give away much about the story because it'll be more fun for you to discover it yourself.It has multiple endings, and the most interesting part that if you die, the game will restart but the main character will still have a memory of whatever event happened and the people he met. This will give you a chance to take different choices and decisions. The main character did an amazing job, you could see the character development very well done, the rest of the characters are good. If you are an anime fan, you'll notice that those actors are very well known, for example, 'Yuki Kaji' is the voice actor of Eren Jaeger from Attack on Titan as well as many others. I enjoyed the music and visuals, the way to choose the actions and options is to rotate the camera to where you want the character to go, there will be a written option to choose but I liked the 360-degree view. Pros:+Great cast and good acting.+invistigation detective style.+Good soundtracks.+Death Medals collection 'You get a medal for each death'+Two endings (with multiple deaths). +You can pause, rewind, and skip scenes.+Steam achievements.Cons:-Quite short, I wish it was longer.I highly recommend this game to every FMV fan and to people who enjoy suspense and detective games. this FMV is a very well done one, I hope to see more of this genre from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: Suspenseful, mysterious, and thoroughly enjoyable.If you're looking for a lengthy story with hours of content, then this isn't for you. It's basically a glorified 'choose-your-own-adventure' movie with total playtime similar to one. However, the experience it does provide is incredibly cinematic, surprisingly emotional, and fully in-line with Spike Chunsoft/Kazutaka Kodaka games.I highly recommend this if you're even remotely interested in these types of stories/games.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get false expectations: it's a neat thriller movie from Kazutaka Kodaka with some extra content in a form of several bad ends and an alternative ending. Think of it as an "interactive movie" they were selling on DVDs back then.It'll take you 1,5-2 hours to watch it, and it's a good thing since it doesn't overstay its welcome. The infodump in the middle is a tad awkward and it's all quite schematic, but the general story is nice and even a bit touching near the end, the music from Masafumi Takada (The Silver Case, Killer7, Danganronpa) is superb, the visuals and shot composition are good. They also subbed additional videos unlocked by watching bad ends for this release.So if watching a neat movie from Kodaka interests you, then give it a shot. (the fangirl bad end is the best)(I wonder if Death Medals are a reference to LET IT DIE or just a coincidence)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure most people have heard about the Danganronpa series here and there if they didn't already play it themselves. This time, the writer of the series worked on a new project: Death Come True. That being said, I went through the first game of Danganronpa myself recently and as I sadly didn't enjoy it as much as I would have liked to, I decided to give the writer another try. That being said, let me tell you: Forget everything you know about the Danganronpa series because these games are nothing alike at all!Death Come True opens with a man waking up to a ringing phone. Evidently, he gets a message from the hotel concierge and finds himself in a hotel room. However, he cannot recollect any prior memories and is, therefore, quite confused. It doesn't help that there is an unconscious tied up woman lying in the bathtub of his room. Not knowing what's going on, the TV news suddenly reports that the serial killer Makoto Karaki is on the run and still wanted. Unexpectedly, his own face appears.First of all, Death Come True truly feels like watching a movie. There is even the option to pause the game and rewind back or forth in case the player missed something or is just not interested in experiencing the specific scene. I liked that new approach as it didn't exactly feel like playing a game but at the same time, I still could interact with the game and make a few decisions here and there. However, that means that the playing time of this game is fairly short and can be completed within two to three hours. Nonetheless, a short playing time doesn't make a bad game per se and I found myself getting surprised by the storyline.So, let's move on to the important part of the game: The plot. I booted the game up and before I knew it I already finished it. I honestly wished the story would have been longer, not because I feel like it's rushed or anything but because I enjoyed it so much. I feel like, whilst I already enjoyed Death Come True the way it is, it would benefit from a longer playing time for sure. You see, it's noticeable that the game focuses on its storyline a lot, but the background stories of the characters, unfortunately, fell short as a result.It takes a while to build up a proper narrative and Death Come True starts off very mysteriously. Neither the player nor Makoto have a clue what exactly is happening and I found myself constantly questioning whether he was the wanted serial killer. For all I know, he could just have a change of heart after losing his original personality. Anyway, I found the mysteries presented very well and was surprised at one or another reveal.That being said, there are sadly a few minor issues with the execution of the plot. As everything is confusing I didn't understand some happenings in the game as well. Plot holes are to be expected in a sci-fi story, however, it could have explained its story better for some events. Whilst I feel like I understood most of the happenings after completing the game, I am still unsatisfied and feel like not everything is revealed yet. Again, this could have resolved with more playing time, so the game can spend more time explaining the mysteries.I could easily sympathize with Makoto thanks to his amnesia. As he didn't have a clue what was going on either, I could imagine myself in his shoes. It felt like I was discovering the mysteries together with him which made me feel more attached to him, although I sometimes didn't want to believe that he is capable of killing anyone and I hoped it wasn't true. After all, it's hard to accept that someone who grew on you could harm others. That being said, I think Makoto is an excellent protagonist who noticeably grows during the short playing time as he slowly gets his memories back.I read a lot of complaints that two characters of the game only have a short appearance in the story and aren't important at all. Whilst I would agree on that part, I didn't see it as a negative point. True, they only had a minor role, but I still think the story benefits from them as the mysterious story without any crazy happenings wouldn't be the same. In short, it didn't bother me at all and if it didn't get pointed out I wouldn't even have thought about it.The thing I absolutely love is that each time a death scene is reached, and the player continues their journey, it feels like an actual feature. Sure, some dead ends are rather random and don't contribute to the plot, however, some of them are intended and belong to the main story. I appreciate it every time a game doesn't implement random bad ends that could easily be left out but there is a purpose behind them, although it might only be noticeable later on. I sometimes felt hopeless because no matter what I chose Makoto ended up dying, however, that aspect is intentionally implemented into the game.Sometimes I noticed is that when the characters are dying, it doesn't look realistic due to the complete lack of wounds and blood. It might be fortunate for those who are interested in this game but are sensitive to that kind of content, however, it looks like the actors are simply passing out instead of dying. I made the experience that Asia mediums are a little bit different in that regard, but it still disturbed my immersion.Sadly, choices don't have a huge impact on the main plot and the player doesn't form their own story. However, that issue was a minor one for me and I still managed to enjoy this game. When the player reaches a bad end, they can continue the game and will be brought back to the critical decision to go on with the story. As aforementioned, some deaths cannot be avoided, although the story changes after that. When multiple answers are possible and the player chooses the wrong one the game just forces them to go for another choice.In total, the player can reach two possible ends. I had the impression that neither of them are happy nor bad endings. That being said, when the player chooses one end, they have to replay the whole game once again to reach the other one. I didn't like that aspect as I didn't want to go through the same for a second time only to see a few minutes of the other end. Luckily, the events can be skipped when the player decides to go for the other end, however, even that was quite a hassle.There isn't a lot to say about the graphics other than that it looks exactly like a movie and has real actors implemented. The actors were doing a splendid job with the acting and felt real. Unfortunately, I occurred a problem at the beginning of the game: Screen tearing. While some scenes are intended to look funky, this was not one of the features and greatly disturbed my immersion as it managed to confuse me, making it hard for me to focus on the plot. The Japanese voice-acting, on the other hand, was pleasant to listen to as well.I truly enjoyed Death Come True. Sure, there are minor issues with the plot here and there, but overall, it was a great experience, although I wish it was longer. This is one of the cases where more playing time would definitely have benefited to the storyline. Nonetheless, the reveals managed to surprise me and I loved the theme: A movie where the player has to take initiative. Death Come True is entirely different than Danganronpa, which I am grateful for, and I enjoyed it for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have similar complains about Death Come True (as I will point out later) they seem to forget that this is a ~15 bucks experience. Given the price, there is absolutely nothing to complain about. I hope this was an attempt to "test the waters" and we can expect full price experiences like this in the future with many more options.As I said, all the negatives can be explained with the price point. You can't create a bigger, better story with more branching and options without also increasing the price (and production budget).I hope Kodaka will create a full price experience in the future with dozens of options and endings. This was a great first live action attempt and I can't wait for more.

_childDocuments_.review: A young guy wakes up in a hotel room, oblivious to his past, but watching as on TV he is presented as a ruthless serial killer wanted by the police. Quite an inspiring start for the new Japanese FMV thriller, promising the player a lot of secrets, the ability to directly participate in the events taking place, experience the traditional Japanese creativity in writing scripts, and a bunch of other pleasant things. Did they manage to fully implement it? I'm not entirely sure... First of all, it should be said that the complete passage of the game will take a maximum of 2 hours, or even less. This is not to say that this is a boring two hours, but it is still a rather short time for such a project. Here, of course, the argument comes into play that creating an interactive movie with real actors is a very expensive pleasure, and it is difficult to argue with such an argument, but here another factor comes into play, which is absolutely not something expensive, and it hurts the game where stronger than its short duration. And I'm talking here about interactivity.I am a very simple guy, I do not invent anything myself, but I look at the synopsis of the game in Steam, I see the inscription "A new wave interactive movie game", that is, the word "interactivity" is obviously laid in the foundation of the game, this is not just a movie that you looking comfortably in your chair. But player influence is almost completely absent here. There are no plot forks that can lead you along different paths. There is only one straight road leading to the only possible ending. If you accidentally make a choice that deviates from this route, then the maximum is an interesting and inventive scene of the death of the main character and rewinding to that moment of the initial choice. And the only final scene, which culminates in the famous Morpheus to Neo pill line offering just two endings, isn't particularly inspiring either. The most bitter thing here is that, as a movie, I really liked this work. The actors act out just amazing, even if there are flaws in the script, but they are quite tolerant, the director demonstrated a lot of really interesting things in terms of style. The action is well built, does not sag anywhere, and there is enough creativity in staging the scenes. The only question is where in the game my participation is needed, and whether it was necessary at all... Therefore, the impressions from the game are rather mixed, everything is too ambiguous

_childDocuments_.review: This game is impressive from a technical standpoint, but as a game or movie, it's bad.The game frames itself as a choose your own adventure but there are only two ways a choice can go. Either it's a critical choice where one route leads to death and the other doesn't, making it a non-choice. Or it's a it's a choice of flavor text, which makes it a non-choice. There are no branching pathsIt also doesn't feel like there's any weight to the final decision despite it being the only meaningful one, well the game looks cool it really just should've been a film

_childDocuments_.review: More Kodaka is always good! Death Come True is a game from the same creator of Danganronpa, Kazutaka Kodaka. His games tend to give you headaches as you try to find out what the hell is going on, and this one didn't fall behind on that.This time, in a interactive movie type of game, we've got that followed by great acting, simple mechanics and gorgeous video quality. You can jump the video, go back... it's pretty fun and easy to meddle with. This simplicity wa something I really liked, and I actually laughed a bit when the tutorial came up because it felt like something unnecessary. The comedy/goofy moments - although they weren't many - made me want to marry this game. The OST, of course, was absolutely suberb and I'm in love with the ending credits song (Masafumi Takada, you're a god).It was a really fun ride that made me want to cry in frustration as I tried to figure out what the hell was going on... But... And there's always a but, I must admit the length of the game disappointed me. I was able to get all the achievements/check every possible answer in under 3 hours. Since I'm used to 20-40 hours games from Kodaka, this came as a huge let down... but only because I love his stories so much. And I guess I didn't know exactly what to expect, so be warned of that: This is a short game.Now, regarding the story itself. Everything was great at first, and you have no idea what the heck is going on. But maybe because I'm so accostumed to Kodaka, I expected more plot twists, and couldn't believe when things actually ended. I was like "Did it really end? No, it must be a joke. There's more, right?!". Some small things seemed to be random, like characters that would only show if you made one determined choice and that would vanish for the game if you missed that only choice (shouldn't they show up all the time, mostly if they're on the trailer?). I set my expectations in a different direction, and ended up slightly disappointed because of that. Still, this is a great & surprising story. I wish it was longer, not just because I would like to see more, but because I think it would make it easier for me to really get to know the characters and feel for them/their story. I didn't shed a tear watching this, even though some parts were actually emotional - and I'm usually a cry-baby -, so the only reason I can think why it didn't happen was because I wasn't close enough to the characters to feel that much empathy for them. In conclusion, I think the game could have been better if it were longer and if some parts were more well-developed. I liked it, but it could've been better. Of course, since I'm a big fan of the Danganronpa franchise, it only makes sense that I would expect so much, and this is something that affects experience. For somebody who never played anything by Kodaka, I believe this is a really good introduction to how he portrays stories and how crazy/interesting they can be. I doubt anyone who really likes him would skip this game, also. And I really don't think they should. It was a good afternoon playing this, and I'm glad. It may not be as memorable as I thought it would, but it's still a good and solid game.TL;DR: Please give Tookyo Games money so we can get more stuff from them.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: Death Come True is a sci-fi, thriller FMV game, where you wake up in a hotel room with no memorise, with a woman in your bathtube and finding out you are a serial killer, which feels off for you, but also the place and people around is not really makes sense either.First which I need to address, is how the game looks, because there was lot of effort to make the game like this. It looks really good in my opinion, effects and CGI also well made. However, the menu looks simple, but so awesome in my opinion. I liked it!Second thing is the controls. You only need to use your mouse to play the game. Of course, if you want to fast forward, rewind or pause the scence, you need the keyboard for that, but pretty simple.Sound and music is also a bright part for the game. Music is mostly ambients, but it can get intense and thrilling too. I really liked it in general and also, characters are hearable and good. Need to know, the game main laungage is Japanese, and because of that the characters are talking in that language, but thankfully the subtitles are English and it's pretty understandable for me what is going on in the game. Good one!Gameplay and story is going to be mention here together, however I want to make this as non-spoilered, because what really surprised me and never saw in a game, at the beginning of the game, the protagoinst ask the player to not upload content about the game and don't spoiler the plot. It will sounds stupid for some, but I will respect this statement, but I try to give the best about the situation. The gameplay is kinda poor, because you can only interact, when you have to obviously, like in a FMV game and you mostly going to watch the movie in front of you. This is usual FMV trait, but here it feels more poor, because of lack of choices sometimes. Plus points, because of the behind the scences footages. Really fun stuffs.About the story, it's interesting and thrilling. Slowly knowing what is going on, finding the route to success is really feeling good. Finding about what is going on feels satisfying too and the ending of the story is also good, but really sad at the same time. It's an okay story in general and the twists are not really big to be honest. But there are problems, one of it is some of the characters, which either random or just weird to be there. One of the woman character were especially annoying for me to see, but thankfully it was just one scene. One more thing which bothered me, is that you can't really stop playing the game if you want to play it through... well actually you can, but you have to start over the game. It has it's reason and actually there is a way to pause it for later, but it's not explained at all and really weird in general. I can understand the reason why it's not explained, but just makes some annoying to find out, that I exited the game, because I wanted to play through later, but the game told me that I have to start over. Another thing is, I didn't got what I think I will playing. I thought this is going to be a who you trust with lot of characters and indeed a mystery, but you will find out, it's not like this and had a cheeps solution, This is one of the hardest game to review, if I want to honor the request of the game and not spoiler anything, but I want to be still honest with the game. Consider this product as a movie more like, and you will get an all right story with all right, not too deep characters and not too unexpected twists. I still have to give credit the unexpected type of endings tho. The game is poor in gameplay, however I still think if you want to see a visually all right "movie game", then it worth to shot. I can recommend the game in that insticts, but for 13.3€ is much, comparing to what you get, so get it cheeper. It's not a horrible game, but really not what I expected in general, but it was still okay.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's my high expectations, but I was totally deserted by this game. I'm not huge fan of Danganronpa, but I respect Kodaka as one of best authors of adventure visual novels and japanese style quests these days. With premise about dying again and again I was hoping this game would be his chance to jump into sphere of his sempai colleagues such as Uchikoshi and Nakazawa, whose adventure stories are not perfect, but very fun to read and include many scifi, pseudoscience and fantasy elements to make reader jump between routes or even multiple protagonists to solve most mysteries behind story.However, I was wrong.I liked concept behind this game. I enjoyed design of UI. Actors are not ideal, but still believable. Plot is clichéd, but still nice. I love choose-your-adventure style games. What's the problem then?Kodaka stated in interview - this game supposed to be like film, it lasts three or so hours, finish it in one seat. But you see, films these days are mostly blockbusters with action scenes, horrors with gore and thrillers/detective with suspence and mystery unsolved to end. I finished first run in nearly two hours and there were few action scenes, deaths were bloodless, horror was laughable (in bad sense), suspence was thrown out right after exposition in middle of story and only fun I was having is solving simple detective problem which was present as short quiz during climax. I felt like "film" was kinda boring at times and "game" was really lacking. I spent another hour to replay and get all deaths lost by me on first walkthrough, but it only made me realise how some scenes in game were reused or filmed in few hardly distinctive variations. Also, to make up content in game there are bonus videos and Jiro Sato really kills in it with his weird sense of humour, but that's not enough for making up quality of main attraction.I'm sure cost of this game is still fair, since it's FMV, but look, there are many free mystery driven visual novels, FMV games which cost nearly same, but have more content, and also Spike Chunsoft games, some of which, like Danganronpa, were works of Kodaka too, and they are more enjoyable and less costy for content and gameplay they have. Looking cool and having good intentions, by the end of day for me personally Death Come True looks like unsuccessful experiment made to fill gap between creation of Too Kyo Games and their long time ago announced games without stated dates of release. You can try this game and it's still kinda enjoyable, mostly if you new to games like this, but don't expect much from it like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing is it's Simplistic nature and presentation, no need to waste time doing the same things again and again to get all achievements etc without skipping, The skip option is available first time playing the game.The story is simple but presented in an interesting manner, there are two endings and on your first gameplay itself you can get 15 achievements, and the last one after getting the second ending which if player don't want to waste time just skip to the end or use chapter select option etc and watch it and get the achievement. _childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative reviews for this game seem to stem from a misunderstanding of what it is. So before buying think carefully about whether or not you would enjoy a: Short (~2-4 hour) FMV style game with a strong mystery theme and a handful of (not-especially divergent) choicesThe plot is really what you would be buying this for, this game has a particular story to tell which is interesting and fun to watch unfold. But the game only has few hours to tell its story so match your expectations of the number of divergent plot points accordingly. There is not much 'game' here so if that strikes you as a let-down then this is not the experience for you.  However, if you are looking for a quirky, fun 2~4 hour 'movie with choices' experience with lots of twists and turns to keep you interested then you could do far worse than this and I would recommend it if that sounds like something you'd enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good, although not great FMV game where you play as a young man who wakes up in a hotel room.  He has lost his memory and, as you progress through the game, you (and he) piece together what led to him being there.I will say little about the story, except that it's made more exciting than it otherwise would have been by the use of a time-loop system.  The sci-fi element and the mystery surrounding it is the best part of the game, since the other mystery that features, which I will not discuss, is a run-of-the-mill story.I generally like time-loop stories, and this one held my interest, not least because I had no idea where it was going for quite a while into the game.  The producers cleverly created red-herrings and surprises.It's right, in my opinion, that the developers kept this game short (at around two hours play) for what they had.  Even at that, some of the individual scenes are very dialogue-heavy.  And it slows down the pace of the story without adding anything interesting to compensate.  Some of the dialogue should have been trimmed and the game could have used more twists and turns.The best modern FMV games like Contradiction: Spot the Liar, The Shapeshifting Detective, Late Shift and I Saw Black Clouds either kept the dialogue short, or had much of the longer scenes with sinister (or otherwise interesting) characters, in order to maintain interest.  The producers of Death Come True should have taken note of that when making their game.Depending on the choices you make, you will see two characters who act strange or suspicious.  Sadly they don't feature in the story much.  I would have liked to have either seen these two more or had more such characters, just to add a few more surprises and interesting moments.While the acting is decent, the lead actor looks to me to be quite a few years too young for the role he is playing.The ending theme is awful, and is the sort of theme you often find at the end of modern horror or thriller films - totally out of place.Overall, Death Come True is a good, but flawed game.  It's not as good as the best ones but it is better than The Complex, At Dead of Night and Dark Nights With Poe and Munro.  Basically, if you like Late Shift or I Saw Black Clouds - games where your interactivity is limited to making choices to advance the story, then you will probably like this game too.  Oh, and if you like time-loop stories, then I wholeheartedly recommend the game.  Enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: Death Come True is a short yet fun FMV game. It's more of a thriller movie then a fully fleshed out game something like Immortality which I'm really eager to play. The gameplay itself is pretty straight-forward, you're presented with various option as the movie plays and each choices leads to different path or bad end. There's 2 major ending in the game and I can say it's fairly easy to get both of them. The game is a choose-your-own-adventure genre and It took me about 3 hours to finish the game fully including all achievements and the collectables videos. What I like about the games are it's cast, casting Kaji Yuki as the Navigator is definitely a great choice. The actors definitely did a great job portraying their roles and it works well with the game design.What I didn't like however is it's plot. I felt like it could've be more fleshed out and involved other characters instead of it's awkward plot dumping session we have in the middle of the game. It does make sense to a certain degree but it's just not for me. The short duration of the game aside, the asking price of the game is questionable at best. I don't think it's worth if you're getting it at full price. Overall I think this game is definitely a mixed bag for me, it has the potential on the story and it's FMV design which I enjoyed but it's let down by the overall duration of the game and it's price. I'll give this game . Definitely try it out if you like FMV games or mystery in general but only during discounts
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: Did the line "from genius creator of the Danganronpa series" also entice you to give this game a go expecting interesting story twists and a story that would keep you glued down for hours?I'm sorry to say that this sadly will not give you a Danganronpa experience. The story is very linear and you're basically just clicking through a very short story. After less than 3 hours I had found all secrets, unlocked all achievements, and the entertainment value was not THAT high. You may still enjoy it if you enjoy interactive movies but there are plenty others that I would recommend before this one; Erica & Late Shift to mention 2.You may still enjoy it, but it's nothing close to what I was expecting when Danganronpa was mentioned in the Blurb.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun experience, though one with very minimal interaction.  This is quite like the old FMV "interactive movies" of the 90s.  You're not really in control, you're just occasionally branching down a short - and usually deadly -"what if" before continuing the story.You're sadly not going to find a twisted web of twist upon twist upon twist like Danganronpa or Zero Escape fans might expect, but it's a pretty solid 2-3 hours of entertainment
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: A short "choose your own adventure" style game - well, more like a movie with a few branching paths. Still thoroughly entertaining and while it is not a deep mastermind adventure like Zero Escape or Danganronpa (which this game keeps getting compared to due to the composer being the same), mostly due to the limited amount of characters, it is definitely an entertaining 3-4 hours until you have seen everything. It has the perfect length and does not overstay its welcome.Huge bonus for the great soundtrack (again, expected from the composer) and the "Off Shot" and "Making Of" videos which show some glimpse into how movies like this get made; I always love watching these kinds of videos. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this mostly out of support for the creators. This game is not for people looking for an in-depth experience nor for those that want the same experience as the Zero Escape or Danganronpa series.Death Come True is essentially the next logical step for visual novels - that is to say, DCT is a movie with diverging choices. In a similar vein to Netflix's Bandersnatch, DCT will play footage automatically until certain points, where you can make a choice that affects the story.The story and choices that you make aren't the most in-depth nor are they the most compelling. I feel like if I weren't playing with someone else to bounce ideas off of, the game would get bland very fast. That said, I enjoyed the time we spent deliberating on the mysteries of DCT. I think the devs and writers took too many cues from modern moviemakers, as a lot of the heavy plot points are telegraphed so hard that it was difficult to not see the end result from a mile away.That said, I did enjoy the time I spent playing through DCT and for its price point, I don't think its much of a stretch to call it an interactive DVD movie. If that's appealing to you, or you just want to support Tookyo Games' newest title, pick this one up, possibly on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but I'd be lying if I said it didn't leave me disappointed. Death Come True comes to us from the developer of the Danganronpa series and is a FMV mystery title. As the story plays out, the game will occasionally prompt you to make a choice where you then witness the outcome of your decision; like a Choose Your Own Adventure novel. However, that's where my primary criticism of the game comes in. Despite the illusion of choice, DCT is actually very linear. Usually you are left with deciding between one of two paths, but making the "incorrect" decision often leads to a quick Game Over and the option to continue the game at the last branch in the story line, so you can make the other choice and advance. It doesn't always play out like this, but in the interest of avoiding spoilers, I'll ease up on getting more specific. Also, this game is a lot shorter than I was expecting. In 3.4 hours, I earned all the achievements and witnessed all the branching outcomes. Granted, there is a fast-forward option that I used to bypass scenes that had already played out in a previous playthrough, but I still wanted a little more meat on this bone. So, why do I recommend it? Because it's not a bad game. The story is interesting, albeit not as mind-blowing as I was hoping. Just know that you're getting a bite-sized, Black Mirror: Bandersnatch-esque experience and not much else. With experience in the Zero Escape and Danganronpa series' prior to playing this game, it's conceivable my expectations were too high. Nevertheless, I look forward to the seeing what Too Kyo Games comes up with next. But as it concerns DCT, I recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of the FMV genre and loved everything about this game.  Great story, high quality acting, and easy navigation system. Fun fact: The lead actress is a well known Japanese actress whose film credits include Kill Bill and Battle Royale (2000). The game is about the length of a movie and plays like a Chose Your Own Adventure Book which limits you to minimal options at critical decision points.  You can fast forward throughout the game and I was able to complete the story and experience all the alternative options (and secure all the achievements) in under 3 hours.  Having paid for some of the "cheaper" FMV games from Chinese developers, where the acting or navigation was sketchy at times, I don't mind paying more for a higher quality experience, so the length and cost of this games was not a deterrent for me.Highly recommend it.  Fan of FMV and of Japanese culture in general will greatly enjoy it.  I hope the developers make another game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short FMV interactive movie from director Kazutaka Kodaka, the creative mind behind Danganronpa. It's about as long as a movie (took me 2 hours to complete) and should be completed in one sitting for the best experience.I really loved the story. It starts out as a stuck-in-a-time-loop thriller and throws a lot of twists and curveballs throughout the whole experience. It always kept me guessing.Production values are really good for an FMV game. Acting performances are also above par for this genre. Good work.While "gameplay" is limited in a game like this, the interactivity that IS there adds a lot to the story. It would not work as well as a movie. That's what matters, the interactivity enhances the story.I'm already looking forward to what's next from Kazutaka Kodaka.
_childDocuments_.name: Death Come True

_childDocuments_.review: is a "choose your own adventure" styled FMV game. But honestly I'd describe it more like an interactive movie with a bit of player choice here and there. I think the appeal of purchasing this "game" is to experience Kazutaka Kodaka's writing through this mystery thriller. I think DCT was generally entertaining throughout with some emotional moments here and there. However it felt a bit weak compared to the Danganronpa games in terms of the overall narrative development.I think maybe due to the short run time it feels like the plot is a little undercooked and variousnarrative elements could have been explored a bit better and in more detail. However what is presented here is still a very fun ride with some suspenseful twists and the setting especially at the beginning is enthralling. The length to finish an entire run is about the same amount of time to watch a feature length film at about 2 hours.  - The acting performances, the entire cast did a good job in selling their respective roles and adding to the tension of the story. - The cinematography, whoever did the camera work did a good job capturing the scenes and helped add to the atmosphere of the game/movie. - Sound design, generally speaking I thought the SFX and BGM selection did a good job adding to the suspenseful nature of the film while also adding moments of silence when necessary. - The simple but stylish UI that didn't ruin the immersion of the "game". - The concept, I really like these sort of "butterfly effect"/"groundhog day" type premises. Also having the protagonist as an amnesiac works well here as you get to learn things alongside them as the stakes become more clearer. I'd say this was for the most part executed well in this "game". - The story, while not totally disappointing felt a bit weak/rushed towards the second half of the adventure. I'm not sure if it was due to time/budget constraints but that portion felt a bit underdeveloped compared to how strong the beginning felt. It's just odd that the pacing at the beginning felt strong in getting the viewer invested in the world/conflict only to be rushed in the second half to one of the possible endings. Also there's an info-dump in the second half of the adventure that's suppose to explain certain "sci-fi" elements that felt a bit lazy and off in it's placement within the story. This overall point is more so a mixed one rather than a straight up negative one.- Length, for an FMV "choose your own adventure" this was pretty short, I don't expect a game like this to go on for hours since at that point it would feel needlessly padded out or bloated at the expense of ruining the pacing, but it could have been a bit longer to address certain underdeveloped narrative bits. I.E. Character development, and pacing the ending better. *(As an aside I do not mind short length games, if the experience is tight with no fluff or bloat then that's great, at the same time if it feels like there are underdeveloped aspects or wasted potential I'd notice/mention that too. The overall quality of the experience matters a lot more to me than length)- Weak side characters, I can't say who falls under this category otherwise I'd spoil some things, but you'll know them when you see them. They're a bit disappointing in that they add little to the overarching narrative aside from some minor screen time appearances in some scenes.Overall I think this is worth experiencing if you like mystery thrillers, however I'd advise waiting on a discount to purchase this. While good, I think this could have been better if Kodaka would have spent a bit more time on the script and perhaps paced the ending a bit better since that portion felt rushed making either possible ending you come to a little underwhelming. I'm hoping that Kodaka tries something like this again, and the next attempt will be a more solid outing because this had so much potential since all the ingredients were there, but unfortunately fell a bit short on the execution. Regardless if you know what you're getting yourself into it's still worth the ride despite the flaws just probably not at full price.Side note: if you get all the "deaths" you can unlock extras like some behind the scenes footage shoots of certain scenes of the game and more of the news bits if you're interested in that content.

The death special effects were... not good, but in a hilarious way. Someone gets stabbed with a sword in the armpit. I liked it because I love morbid plots but I'm not a fan of jumpscares. _childDocuments_.review: I think in a perfect world, I would just judge this game on its own merits and recommend it as like "eh, it's fine", but that isn't the world we're living in. We're living in a world where this game is made by Too Kyo, and a lot of the people who would consider playing it are people like me who reflexively purchase anything and everything in the Spike Chunsoft/Too Kyo sphere. In that context, the game is lacking.It's a "Choose your Own Adventure", but there aren't really meaningful branching paths. It's more like "Pick not the right path, enjoy your immediate unique bad end". Because there's really only one linearly correct path, the whole story ends up not being super mysterious, at least not in a way where I had a lot of time to speculate about the mysteries before the game just straight up told me.Another thing I consider an issue is its length. I don't particularly have anything against short games, but a 2.5 hour FMV CYA is coming dangerously close to competing with just watching a movie unless there's something very gamified going on it. I would say this is not such a game.If you are like me, and you bought this game because of the developer and the other games flagship members of the studio have been involved, I don't recommend because you'll be disappointed. If you just want to play a FMV adventure game, I still don't really recommend but it's at least a thought.

_childDocuments_.review: This was... ok. The live action l think actually HURT the game. Especially given the story and world of the game (it'd be spoilers to say why l think that).It took me 1:50 to beat the game. There are two endings, l only got one, but l don't really care to get the other one because the game basically tells you "hey, this is what the ending A or B will be like, pick one". Around the 1:10 mark l had figured everything out and it was basically just me waiting for the characters to figure everything out.The live action made it so there were so few characters (because it's harder to work with actors than just animate 3D and get voice actors). This meant some characters would be underdeveloped. Like there was this really fun character (Nene) who was only there for like a couple minutes. This is much unlike in a game like Danganronpa, where someone can be an unimportant character, but they still get fun times with the personal time and speaking with them during the slow parts of the story. Something made impossible by the live action. Not to mention, when there's SO few characters, it's easier to figure out the mystery. There's really one three main characters of this game. _childDocuments_.review: Death Come True is an FMV adventure/mystery game written by the mind behind the Danganronpa series, Kazutaka Kodaka. The story revolves around a young man waking up with amnesia in a hotel room. Bizarre events are happening within the hotel, including debating with his own identity and purpose there, the protagonists goal is to try to discover the source of the weirdness by replaying events slightly differently each time.As an FMV, the scenes play out until certain choices are asked from the player. Some actions will lead to bad endings, others will progress the story. There are 2 branching main endings that are mutually exclusive, so the game must be replayed again to see the other. Luckily, once you've gone through it once you should know both how to quickly reach the end, as well as which choices to select to see more of the bad endings. There are no manual saves, but this is due to a design choice that makes sense once you reach the end, but skipping ahead during a scenario is very easy so this was not an issue in the end.Every bad ending awards an achievement, an in-game medal, and unlocks bonus clips of behind the scenes footage of the filming process. It's worth to go out and reach them all to earn those extra bonuses.The total length of the story is about 3 hours, including the seeking of all alternate endings. The bonus clips will boost to around 3.5 hours of total content to see. The performance and effects are very good in my opinion, the plot has some twists here and there, though the player can piece together the greater picture as more clues continue to present themselves. It was enjoyable for what it was, worth checking out in a single sitting.

_childDocuments_.review: While Death Come True is inoffensive, it doesn't offer a lot new either. IMO, FMV Games only have a couple ways to stick out due to their format, their interactivity and their story. Well, to start with interactivity, there is little user choice here. When the player does get to make a choice, it is usually a binary between "right answer" and "wrong answer", and wrong answer will zip you back to the decision making point so if you want to see everything you should probably pick the wrong option. Getting things right is basically just a question of "did you pay attention", rather than taking any kind of thought or trial and error, which makes it just keep flowing. There is something to be said about making it easy to continue, but it shouldn't come at the cost of feeling like player interaction doesn't matter. There is a reason the game opens up asking for people to not stream it or post a playthrough up front, it's to "prevent spoilers" because the game wouldn't lose anything if it was a movie. So how is the movie? It's fine. It doesn't do anything that blew my mind, but it's not terrible either. Coming from the creator of Danganronpa I expected more. It's not broken, it isn't terrible, it just isn't special either, so I'd find it hard to recommend. If someone wanted to check out FMV games I'd point them to Contradiction! or The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker before I'd point them to Death Come True.
