_childDocuments_.review: Do you like pokemon? This is better. And this comes from a kid that grew up with the pocket monsters. Story - fantastic!Gameplay - addictive.Writing - almost perfect.Music - although not my jazz, pretty darn good.Playtime - 20 hours would be enough to 100 percent it. Price? Worth it on full price or promotion, or anything. You will love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: In a genre dominated by a singular series of games, Cassette Beasts is a massive breath of fresh air. Every other monster taming game more or less plays the same; Electric type move hits a Water type Creature expect some massive damage by way of super effective moves, but whats interesting for Cassette Beasts is that same interaction also applies differing buffs or de-buffs depending on what hit. The game is full of surprising game-play twists that gives new life to (in my opinion is) a stale genre     Lets take a look at that prior interaction, lighting vs water, in Cassette Beasts conductive is applied meaning whenever a future lightning move hits anything on the battlefield a small portion of lightning damage is applied to the affected creature. There are plenty effects some are similar in effect like Fire vs Plant (this should be obvious). Want to lower defenses on that earth type, you should use a metal type move. Dose your opponent like to use plant type attacks? Try using a poison type monster to gain a damage up buff.     Lets do just one more, Fire vs Plastic, what buff or de-buff is caused? Trick question, this interaction is a transmutation, the plastic type is melted by the fire and becomes a poison type. Sadly there are only 4 such transmutation interactions but there is a typing centered around transmutation, glitter, anything hit by it will become glitter type and any glitter type hit by any move will become the same type as that move.     I've only talked about type interaction up till now but rest assured there are more twists in the battle system to talk about like Fusion, Trainer KO's, expanded status effects, Recording (Catching), Coatings, Walls, Bootlegs, Stickers, and a probably bit more on top of that.     Overall I find the game to be charming but its not without its faults, for as fun and entertaining the battle system is it wont help when it comes to the slog that is post game. Overall Its a fantastic game with at least a 30 hour main campaign/story and satisfying fights sprinkled throughout, just be wary of post-game.TLDR: Good game, good monster battles, slog postgame.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical at first that this was going to be a cheap knock-off of pokemon, but right from the start you realise that the two can barely be compared. The game has lots of interesting movement abilities that function like HMs in earlier pokemon games, but they interact with the physics based movement fluidly rather than having to interact with multiple menus to use them. The combat is very different to pokemon, and could potentially have the potential for far more depth (Although I don't have enough time in this to comment on that).Edit: I just finished the game and wanted to say that I loved every second of it. The difficulty scaling got a bit wacky in the last few hours where I ended up steamrolling basically everything I came across, but there were still a few battles that required proper planning to complete with the setup I had.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a retro-styled creature catching RPG with puzzle elements, plus musical references and puns everywhere, this is absolutely a game to grab!It's practically a hybrid of old-school zelda games (Link to the Past, the Oracle games, etc) with it's overworld mechanics, and something similar to pokemon, though maybe a bit more digimon thematically. The AP system and all the ways that elements can interact keeps things fresh and interesting. The creature designs are fantastic (not that I love every single one but there's something for everyone), the pacing and difficulty curve feel really good, the openness of it all is really nice and helps to give a sense of discovery. The story is also really engaging, and most of the characters have a lot of charm and are well written. Have only done one playthrough but there's so much more I know I can do, and I'm looking forward to discovering every little extra thing I can! Also hopeful for DLC or added features in the future. Not sure I can overstate what an emotional ride and overall blast this game is, might be game of the year for me even.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a pocket monster genre player,  in fact the last monster battler that I played was Pokemon Blue 20+ years ago. So I bought Cassette Beasts on a whim due to it's recent plaudits and regard, and having now finished it, I adore this game. Brilliant monster battling gameplay filled with tons of beast varieties and options to customize your beasts to fit your playstyle, a great storyline filled with endearing characters, a well-designed open world filled with secrets and emergent puzzles, and an incredible soundtrack. All of this crafted by just a small indie team, and sold at a reasonable price, it's great.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell this is a passion project. IMO, I do not see this as a Pokemon clone. This game has a LOT of uniqueness and brings itself to be a lone styled Creature Collector. Sure, it has a formula that already has existed in one way shape form or other... But at the end of  the day it's easy to love this game for what it is and not what you can compare it to.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: So, the monster-catching genre has been getting a lot of eyes on it lately. To throw my two cents in, Cassette Beasts is still at the top of the pile for me. The AP combat, sticker moving system, unique type chart, and universal XP gains make it the smoothest experience I've had in the genre. On top of that, the solid spritework, fantastic music, and memorable characters mean that I heartily recommend Cassette Beasts to anyone interested in broadening their monster-catching horizons.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Real fun monster collector RPG that while clearly emulating Pokemon in style feels more like Mega Ten mechanically in some ways. The game starts off rather slow in how your MC doesn't have great movement but once you get the ability from the fire bullet beast you start moving around at a good clip. The game is also pretty open too allowing you to battle gym leaders and boss monsters in almost any order you can choose around the world map. Most beasts seem pretty viable too and I had fun collecting most of them. Overall just had a great time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first Pokemon-like games out there that actually seems to get the reasons why Pokemon is good in the first place, and understands the failings of the series and tries to improve upon them.This is an extremely easy recommendation to make. Anyone who has any passing enjoyment of Pokemon should absolutely play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: "C'mon, hero, show me what you got!"game is very fun and has randomizer and permadeath mode built in, so you can milk it for a lot of content if you're a pokemon-esque channel on twitch/youtubestatus effects instead of damage variance for effective/ineffective moves is a very interesting choice, same with the humans having their own HP in battle alongside the monstersdifficulty scaling both in AI Intelligence and in enemy level is something a lot of games need these daysmusic absolutely SLAPS, as it should, even the more relaxed songs are beautiful (Most of the battle themes also have a variant with vocals, too)actually has a postgame, which is admittedly more of a slow burn than the game itselffusions are VERY cool, even if it's basically just kitbashing two different large monsters together I like seeing it happenOverall I give this game a yeah/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amaziiiing!! It's definitely a unique experience, but if I had to compare it to anything it's like if pokemon and persona had a really sweet indie love child with a huge heart. ;o; I got addicted to fusing my cassette dudes together and I ended up playing all night! All of the characters have been really relatable and charming so far (especially my artist buddy Felix!!!), and the map has been super fun to explore! _childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recomend this game, but there are just so many little amateurish mistakes in this game.- moves don't tell you if they can be equipped to a specific monster or not until you open the three sub menus to equip it.- game has box stacking to reach areas as a mechanic, but the boxes have weird physics and sometimes your character chucks them up on a cliff so you cant retrieve them- If you swap from a low health monster the game doesn't remember this and will spawn you in as that low health monster in the next fight.- No tool tips for abilities or status effects so you need the wiki open to know what things do if you don't remember from the first time you saw them.- Flee is easy to accidentally hit, with no confirmation pop up so you can often just flee from fights accidentally. Happens very often when your trying to capture a monster since the buttons are right next to each other. The one time you REALLY DO NOT WANT TO FLEE..It's death by a thousand paper cuts. None of these are game breaking on their own, but there are just so many of them that it slows the game down. I really hope they do a quality of life update so I can recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: All the positive I originally said about the game mechanics / art style etc. remains.  But I got sick of the wokeism  - There is a quest where your job is literally to beat up capitalists  (Somewhat on the nose isn't it?)- There is a whole quest line which has a religion-is-bad moral- There is a boss (named after a Latin Catholic phrase) fight whose narrative implies that religion makes people think about death too much.- The ArchVillian is an incarnation of King Arthur (amongst other conquers) called "Aleph"  One can't help but think of "Alpha and Omega" - a tile for Christ.  The "Deux Calibir" (read ahead, have not gotten to this boss fight) is one of the characters move.  The character also wears traditional British military clothing, a subtle jab at the British empire.  I also can't help but wonder if the triangular mirror head is meant to be a mocking of the "imago dei" concept. - The museum in the game celebrates the abolishment of the mayor position (a reference to abolishing the monarchy)- It encourages the Pronoun Protocol- The chief villains are called "Angels" I saw one review say that it is a very "British" game.   It's not.  It is a parable about how everything British/Western - religion, capitalism, the monarchy, our traditional legends - is bad.  It, behind its goofy pixel graphics, is a seething rejection of Britishness, and by extension, the Western world generally.For some, they will love this game for the exact reasons I stopped playing it.  But for me, I prefer my Pokemon w/o woke.  ==From my original review-Fun battle system, Great characters Great pixel art and an open world filled with puzzles.  Feels like a Pokemon-like but also feels very unique.  The presence of a teammate, the double health bar and the unique type v type effects give the game its own feel.  The Open World is really open you can get a bunch of quests very quickly and have freedom as to the order you do them in.  The Pixel art for the characters is really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Nowhere near done so I'll edit when finished, but this game goes so hard. It's been a really long time since I started a game and had severe brainrot compelling me to play more of it every day. Soundtrack is amazing, all of the monsters are fun and cool, the art-style is refreshing and pretty unique, battle system feels new and novel, and you get to beat up landlords. I bought it on a whim since I thought it had the coolest trailer I've ever seen (probably not exaggerating for me at least lol) and have been very happy so far :)Thoughts after finishing: still kinda recommendI feel like the game really lost steam near the end for me sadly. Every possible partner has their own questline which was cool, but they all share a general structure so it gets really repetitive and annoying trying to clear each archangel for their quests. The first time you fuse is a very cool story moment, but it happens again at the end of every partner quest. It's annoying how this goes into the lategame, and this means that you'll have to give up fusing for a long time if you want to try certain partners which kinda stinks since fusion is a bit of a central game mechanic after the tutorial.And while the battle system is a cool new thing, it really goes stale by the end. You can make some goofy "nuke everything immediately" builds to end fights immediately, but aside from that I feel like strategies don't change much between fights, and the mechanics of building energy makes things a bit slow if you're not cheesing. It's cool how easy it is to transfer moves between monsters, but also means they're fairly standardized so you're rarely unlocking moves that feel very special or even much like upgrades.Everything I praised earlier is still def true though, I especially love the battle artstyle. I'd just recommend focusing on the main quest if you play, so you'll still be having fun with the game by the time you finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Omg I love this game so much. You don’t expect there to be so much content in $20 but there is. Theres SO much. But never to where it’s exhausting, always “omg i can do this too??” The music is delicious, the characters are all delicious, the monsters are delicious. I really like how you can’t brute strength your way through, allowing for alot of choice and strat in your teams. If you like open world rpgs, get it. Turn based? Get it. _childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is a great game, and dare I say the best current Pokeclone available on Steam!The gameplay within the game is so addicting, and brought out the "5 more minutes" excuse I always used to give out when I were a child. The world is pretty big in reality, and you are free to explore as you please once you've done the tutorial. You will need new abilities to reach other areas, but rather than be giving in HMs like Pokemon, you have to catch a monster who holds the ability you need to unlock the ability for yourself.The battling is quite different to Pokemon, moves are given as stickers, you can peel off stickers and put them onto other tapes/ monsters and gives incredible versatility. The battles are usually 2v2, and you are stuck with having a partner 99% of the game.One big thing that swperates this game from Pokemon, is the fusion aspect. You can fuse any 2 monsters within the game to create a super strong monster who shares the moves of both monsters and combines their stats to become uber strong. Catching monsters is also different, you can't just throw a quick ball on turn 1 - one player will need to sacrifice a turn to put their headphones on and "record" the monster you want to catch, although this leaves the user recording open to being attacked by monsters, which not only will decrease the catch rate, you also run the risk of the character being made to pass put after too much damage.The final few things I'll touch on are the music, multiplayer, and monster design...The music is astounding. Joel Bayliss has smashed it out of the park with the beats created for this game. There's a couple tracks in particular that hit different but when you reach the first town and enter the first building... Jheeze.... just go YouTube Joel Bayliss - Wherever We Are. Incredible. I literally sat there for 10 minutes just listening.The monster design is probably the weakest part of the game for me, and this being a monster catcher game you'd think this should be a much bigger issue, but it isn't, the game drawer me in with so many other factors, this became a sub note - although it did result in me sticking to the same old monsters and not really trying to learn type effectiveness.Finally the multilayer, you can play locally on the same PC with 2 players, and you can also play online with upto 8 players I think. This hives you the whole game world to explore together and trade/ battle/ etc. I never really delved into this side of the game but it's there for those that want it.Highly recommended title, it sucked 30 hours out of me before I even thought about loading a different game up, and I will be for sure going back to sweep up the last 25 or so achievements I need!
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game! I've recommended this to several friends at this point. As someone who grew up with the Pokemon games, I can assure you that this isn't just a knock-off. It takes familiar elements of the genre and adds a fresh perspective. It has brought me back to playing Pokemon or Digimon games for the first time as a kid. I love the art, the music, and the story. The beasts themselves are delightful. I already want more!
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: I really respect the work of a small team, but the game has quite a few shortcomings that made it much less enjoyable than I had hoped for after all the very positive reviews. The combat is fun at first, but there are a lot of underwhelming abilities and some very, very tedious debuff stacking mechanics in the later fights that do not feel challenging or make the fight harder, just longer and very annoying and unfun without counters. Has some nice touches and ideas, but is way, way too repetitive and does not respect the player's time or nerves. Fast travel exists, but only to very specific locations (why the f*** not to campfires, it would make this feature 100 times better), so you backtrack and walk dozens of times through the same areas, again and again, without any incentive to do so. Monsters don't scale, so you don't even get noticable XP or materials you want - just more of tons of materials you allready have - so there is no gain form all your walking through areas you have walked through 50 times. I really wanted to like the game, the art style is nice, but all the menus, dialogues and combat interactions take too long for something you need to do thousands of times. I got more and more annoyed the farther I got through the game. This effect gets worse through all the environmental puzzles that make you comb through every inch of every map to find another stone to put on a switch to reveal a second switch that reveals a third switch that opens a door if you find another thing you finally need that has you backtracking to another area. As other reviews mentioned the extremely tedious grind to achieve any progress in the really late game, I just gave up after 15 hours of gameplay I only enjoyed half of the time.  TL;DR:I like the artstyle, the combat is better than Pokemon in some ways but in other areas it is quite annoying and the game needs a lot of QoL features, does not respect the players time and I hate the cumbersome progression through the areas.
_childDocuments_.name: Cassette Beasts

_childDocuments_.review: I am very surprised to find that the reviews of the game are overwhelmingly positive at the time I write the review, because I am a very generous reviewer when it comes to rating games and this is probably gonna be my first negative review of a game. I have a lot of respect for the general concept of the game, and as a result I decided to write this after I obtain full achievements. There are a lot of innovative ideas in the game in comparison to Pokemon. For example, the type system is very novel in addition to simple damage modifiers. There are also a lot of side characters that the developer definitely have put in a lot of effort into unlike the plain and boring NPC you will see in other games. However, there are just more cons than pros in my opinion. Let's begin with the mobility. I love the idea of higher and higher level of mobility as we progress through the game. However, it felt very glitchy when using some of the ability at specific time. For example, I was able to reach a platform in late game by literally riding a magnet that I'm standing on. Moreover, the combination of those abilities can be very problematic because it is unclear which ability is correct for certain puzzle after you have many choices and it could be very frustrating for players to attempt a parkour that is not intended. Another specific bad design I want to point out is that when you land from a certain height, you will be staggered for a short moment, which is extremely annoying after you obtain the ability to leap, as you would often land from heights since then. The game offers you incredible mobility post-game, which I appreciate, but this stagger has been one of my major sources of frustration. This leads to the problem of map design. In early game, we do not have a lot of options for navigation. As a result, we have to move very carefully because we risk redoing a whole puzzle if falling of a cliff and land on the ground. However, such terrains in late game becomes nothing but obstacle courses because none of them are meaningful anymore but to slow you down while you move around. How about fast travels? They are stations which puts you in the interior of the building. You often have to navigate to get out. Furthermore, the fast travels are not evenly distributed, which results in a corner of the map not accessible through fast travel. What's worse is the fact that many puzzles / map changes can happen after you interact with the environment, but it is never clear which one would be permanent; You would assume it's gonna depend on something like the color of the buttons, but it is not. I am also not a fan of the fact that every ranger captain is just in the wild lurking with other random encounters and NPCs. There are more, but no space for them. Well those are just the trivial part of the game after all, but how about the design of mobs and battles? I am also not quite a fan! There are very good designs such as dynamic scaling, replaceable move sets, exp for the whole teams, etc. However, one of the biggest problems I have is that the type system and many status are not well instructed! You will get like a tutorial comment when you first encounter some type advantages / special status, but you only get them once and YOU CAN'T CHECK WHAT THEY ARE IN BATTLE! When you see all the status on your character but hovers/clickings does nothing, you can only guess what they are if you didn't pay enough attention. The way how status stack is also my biggest complaint about the game. Having more stacks of certain status will not affect their effectiveness, but only extends the number of turns they last. This not only significantly reduces the depth of combat, but also becomes extremely extremely annoying when you do not have items/backup moves to counter. For example, there is a boss fight that will constantly put you into sleep along with other random negative effects. This is normally fine in pokemon-like games because usually rewarding status like sleeping or freezing will have a lot of limitations, such as casting timing, accuracy of landing, etc. However, in this game, you can easily stack up those status with no penalty over times/turns. This specific boss will act twice a turn and has three moves that could potentially make you sleep. Using items won't help you much as you could very likely get leeched / accuracy down at the same time, which you would miss your only opportunity to strike and put back to sleep. These types of combos do not feel tricky but rather stupid, and because of the type advantage system often times you could just get stuck in one of the unfortunate loop of disadvantages. This is not to mention such disadvantages are carried along even after you switch tapes. The story of the game, despite many good comments, failed to align with the overall gamethrough. Many content of the game only really happens post-game, and the way how the game handles it is by allowing you to get back to the point before completion of the game, which means you are basically, in the story of this game, pausing your entire goal and let everyone wait at the final step. Would have been so easy to make it so that the player can fulfill their goal and travel in and out post-game, but it was so lazily handled instead. I will not comment on the other part of the stories as everyone may feel differently.  The post-game experience is also extremely bad. One major problem is that this game does not support online-pvp at the time I write this, although it is likely something they could offer in the future. But then it's all about pve, which should have been challenges and collections. Unfortunately none of those are fun and rewarding enough. The hardest achievement is locked behind a quest board system introduced post-game, in which the excess progression is NOT CARRIED THROUGH from level to level. This means if you did a lot of collections / rogue fusions in early games, they are all wasted. That hardest achievements requires you to progress through many levels of the board, in which is roughly 200 fights that are dynamically scaled by default, along with consistent grind of quests. The quests are also grouped so that you cannot get new ones unless you complete the whole set, making it very inefficient if you ever stuck in any of those. The fight from those quests are not challenging at all, but annoying enough as it becomes a meaningless grind. There are also achievements for each type of bootlegs, which makes no sense to me. Furthermore, there's another achievement for collection not for catching all of the beasts, but TO LEVEL EACH FORM OF THEM TO MAX LEVEL, which basically eliminates team building in the entire playthrough and post-game grind, as you want to always have two strongest ones on top and carry four others that you want to level up to be efficient. The quests on the board is also simply boring. There were a few new ones introduced as you level up, which does not provide much challenge but rather just more annoying towards the end grind. As I said, the major factor in my opinion is that without pvp, there's not much point grinding for best monsters as none of the pve's are challenging enough for players to make an entire team, and having this many grind towards end game content is just absurd. I even doubt if the developers ever tried to play the game from scratch, or they are just piling up the end game contents as they develop the game, which makes them blind towards how bad the throughout experience would be. All and all, I really cannot recommend this game to anyone at this stage. New generations of pokemon have better systems, older ones are so classic. This game does not have anything that makes it stand out from any games in the same genre. Maybe the ideas are, as I walked in expecting those, but the execution in the end concludes to this negative review. It is almost a relief that I don't have to return to this game for a while, if not forever.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, first and foremost, a Pokemon-like that RESPECTS YOUR TIME.Want to try a different moveset? Freely swap moves around between any/all of your monsters. At any time. For free.Tired of hoofing it around? Fast-travel's enabled from the very start, go nuts.The combat is also interested in more strategic depth than just plain STAB and type weaknesses. Strong type attacks against weak types inflict nominal maluses on the weak type, and weak type attacks inflict nominal bonuses on the strong type. I say "nominal" because type shifting moves are incredibly common and used by just about everyone, so what appears to be a bonus inflicted on you NOW can rapidly turn into a malus if you're not paying attention!Also, the soundtrack SLAPS.And the writing is good as hell.And might also be linked to Lenna's Inception which is also fantastic in its own right??Basically buy this game, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good.I was hoping it would be true, and they did deliver. Cassette Beasts feels like an almost unintentional response to the modern outcry of what people find lacking about the Pokemon franchise. Almost every gripe I've seen is addressed minus the truly "why doesn't game freak just make an action RPG instead" type stuff that I don't think I've ever agreed with, but I also want to be clear the game has a ton of it's own identity and doesn't just owe everything about it to Pokemon in the same way other games like Temtem are insanely similar. Really, the only part kept 1-1 is the idea of type matchup and the stat distributions. Otherwise, the combat is almost wholly original.People have gone over it, but here's a list of the "issues" I think this game addresses with monster collection games:- The world design. No generation 7 or 8 hallways, nor the cute but lacking open world of 9. Cassette Beast's overworld is pretty engagingly designed, and while the rewards aren't always supremely satisfying there's still a ton of interesting puzzles, caves, and even story events scattered about the world that made exploration feel really worth it. The abilities for exploration also feel delightful in how much fun you can have experimenting with them, like the best metroidvanias.- The creature design. This is contentious, and I actually have 0 beef with modern Pokemon designs. My only real issue is that the sense of exploration in newer Pokemon sometimes feels shot by how much newer games can crutch on pre-existing designs, and while variants are fun, there's so often stuff you've seen before. Casette Beasts has no such things to fall back on, and honestly, the collection is great. I can't think of any designs I truly thought were weak, and a lot of them stand out as not just good but completely amazing. There's a kind of "abstract" nature to them that's awarded due to the fact they're not trying to necessarily be animals that I think helps them really stand out.- The difficulty. This does require player input, so it's obviously not flawless, but with the level scaling set to the highest setting of "Harder" pretty much every fight always managed to keep me on my toes if suffering from the issue that Pokemon started of significant fights just having less monsters to work with than you (The "Gym Leaders" all have 4 vs your 6 until postgame). Even still, they had strategies and the AI often times did put me into difficult positions with their effective setups.- The characters. This one is a mixed bag, but I think it's positive. A lot of people say it really has the depth and story Pokemon doesn't have, and I think I disagree with the idea this game is particularly deep. The best analog is something like Persona 4, where characters have real issues that are more interesting than "I am your friend and love battling with you" but they're not explored too heavily and a lot of the content and bosses that represent these issues are bulldozed over in a way that leaves 0 room to really feel impacted by what happened. I've heard people mention Kayleigh's quest as an example of how flat this stuff can feel, but the big one to me was how abruptly Viola's quest just resolves as soon as you clear the fastest dungeon known to man as her entire character arc takes place in a 30 second conversation. In the end, though, I did find a lot of charm in their designs and conversations that left a lot more of an impression than not just Pokemon, but also many of the other modern creature games like Temtem's Max.In the end, as silly as it is to say, I just kind of wish there was a tiny bit more. Not more creatures, mind you, but just I wish the plot could stretch it's legs a tiny bit more. Maybe this is the consequence of the open world design, but I think the short length of character quests combined with them being disassociated from the main plot just kind of left the game lacking the punch it wanted to have, and I didn't feel much at all after beating the final boss. Also, the music is good, but one or two more battle themes would have really been sick.Either way, I think I thoroughly enjoyed the 30 hour runtime it took me to beat the game, and the post-game content so far has been fine enough that I'm obligated to continue. Highly recommend for any Pokemon enjoyers.

_childDocuments_.review: "Because Who Needs Pokéballs When You’ve Got Mixtapes?"Cassette Beasts is the love letter to retro mixtapes you didn’t know you needed. Imagine this: you wash up on a strange island, and instead of normal survival instincts like "find food" or "don’t poke the glowing creature," your first thought is, "I’m gonna slap this thing on a cassette tape and see what happens." That’s the kind of game this is, and it’s glorious.Right off the bat, Cassette Beasts grabs your nostalgia by the collar and says, “Remember the ‘80s?!” The whole premise revolves around recording monsters onto cassette tapes—because apparently, in this world, digital downloads are for cowards. You’re not just catching beasts, you’re recording their essence onto a tape and then morphing into them to fight. Yeah, that’s right. You become the monsters. It’s like a karaoke party where everyone’s belting out their best Godzilla impressions, except instead of embarrassing your friends, you're saving the world from an invasion of quirky, hand-drawn creatures that look like they came straight from a Saturday morning cartoon.The creatures themselves are a mix of the bizarre, the adorable, and the “Who in the dev team decided this was a good idea?” You’ve got your usual cute suspects, but then you stumble across a walking, sentient trash bag, and suddenly, you’re having an existential crisis about what you’re really doing with your life. And don’t even get me started on the fusion system. Two monsters? Cool. Combine them into a brand-new abomination of nature? Even cooler. I made a plant-cow hybrid once, and I’m still not sure if it was beautiful or a crime against creation. Probably both.Combat feels like the lovechild of old-school turn-based RPGs and a DJ mashup contest. It’s all about synergy, and not just in the “let’s work together” sense. You’re literally mixing monsters like you’re at a remix festival, figuring out how to turn your gooey blob and electric squirrel into the ultimate EDM banger of battle strategies. Pro tip: turn everything into fire. Fire is good.And let’s talk about the music. Cassette Beasts is packed with catchy tunes that somehow manage to straddle the line between funky retro beats and songs you'd actually want to listen to on your commute. Each battle feels like you're fighting inside your favorite mixtape, with the soundtrack making sure you never forget that your cassette deck is your most powerful weapon. It's like living inside a neon-soaked record store, and honestly, who wouldn't want that?The island itself is the perfect kind of weird, filled with quirky NPCs who have zero concept of personal safety. “Hey, go record this terrifying monster for me because I can’t be bothered” is pretty much their catchphrase. You’ll meet an assortment of oddballs who seem way too relaxed about the fact that their world is full of monsters and mysterious happenings. They’ll send you off to battle without blinking, which makes you wonder: are they just really lazy or secretly immortal?Cassette Beasts takes the monster-catching formula we know and love, shakes it up with a boombox, and throws in a dash of chaos. It’s fun, weird, and packed with enough mixtape vibes to make you want to dig out your old Walkman. If you’ve ever wanted to fight monsters while grooving to a retro beat, and maybe turn into a sentient trash panda along the way, this is the game for you. So grab your headphones and your favorite tape—it’s time to save the world, one sick jam at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: Been wanting a poke-like clone game for a while now and randomly someone showed the 'preview trailer' for this game to me when it was still in development (2 years ago). As the massive Pokemon nerd i am i was very skeptical and almost wrote it off just by what the trailer showed.Now that i have played the game i am so glad i didn't write it off..Anyone who loves Pokemon OR TemTem (the grindier Clone of Pokemon)is going to love Cassette Beasts because it falls right in between at that sweet spot.It has a really nice blend of being a Pixel-Animated-RPG-Adventure-OpenWorld (Free roam) game with a turn based battle system (like Pokemon) but with a WAY bigger and customizable move set in comparison to Pkmn or TemTem.On top of that Cassette Beasts also has a mechanic called Fusion which basically executes what it means.To keep it short and without too many spoilers, this game has over 16.000 different fusion possibilities!!

_childDocuments_.review: Yep, she's a winner, folks. You know what this is: Pokemon, but with it's own spin. The framing device of the characters being trapped in another world is quite intriguing, especially since it's hinted that they come from more than just Earth. But the main draw is of course the creatures and their terrific designs. So much charm and polish is put into each one, and not only is there a huge number, but they go beyond absurdity with the Fusion mechanics. I think the display said there was 14,000 possible permutations(!!). Absolutely absurd, frankly, but it's amazing that they put in the work to create them all. Great gameplay, great sound, interesting story; what more is there to say? Absolutely pick this one up if you in any like Pokemon or turn-based RPGs! You're in for a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.  100% recommend it.  OST's great.  Monster designs are cool.  Characters and their motivations are good.  Story's entertaining.  Gameplay is fantastic-- There's so many little parts to the battle system, especially with the fact you can 'stack' stickers (Moves/abilities/etc) on monsters leading to crazy stuff like being able to sometimes end battles before you even have to make a choice.  Like Pokemon, there's rarer versions of the monsters that can spawn that are called 'Bootlegs.'  They can spawn as any type including a special type you cannot obtain in the wild otherwise and have better versions of the moves they can learn that have special secondary effects.  There's even an option to bump up or lower the AI's difficulty and level scaling.  There's very obviously a lot of love put into this game from the devs and they deserve for this to gain more traction with how much work was put into it.  My only complaint would be that we could use some small quality of life changes, such as being able to adjust which tapes you carry without having to go to a resting spot.

_childDocuments_.review: The best not-Pokemon "Pokemon Clone". I've played a lot of games inspired by Pokemon - TemTem, Coromon, Monster Sanctuary, you name it - and Casette Beasts blows them all out of the water. The two most common pitfalls for games like this are either that they're basically just Pokemon (in which case I'll go play a Pokemon game I like instead) or they introduce some original stuff but aren't engaging enough to keep me with them. Not so with Casette Beasts. It's not only got a lot of engaging overworld gameplay, but it's also got a fun and unique aesthetic, some fantastic monster designs, and really interesting and unique type matchup effects that go far beyond just doubling and halving damage and will entertain both intense strategists and casual players alike. The writing is pretty good too!My only advice is that if you're like me and you intend to stick with your starter for a while, look them up so you don't get stuck with one you don't like all that much, especially because it's gonna be a LONG time before you get the other one. I'm 7 hours in and coming to terms with the fact that I think I want to start over with the other starter. I'd also suggest you minimize what you look up online after that point - I've been having so much fun just grinding to turn my Beasts into their next form and discovering the weird and wonderful new monsters they turn into.10/10, and I'm a harsh grader.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the platonic ideal of what a Pokemon game should be. This game is really well put together, the battle mechanics are a breath of fresh air and there are so many silly gimmick builds you can go for. I love the accessibility and QOL features here, if you know what you're doing you can fly through this game. That's not even going into the lovely story, aesthetics, and MUSIC... the game is endearing, heartfelt, and is super replayable to boot, somehow, which you would think is odd for a game with a narrative like this but there's actually a lot of variance between playthroughs in ways you might not expect. This is a must-have if you're looking to scratch that creature collecting itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating after pushing through a bit more:I've mostly finished the game; however, I can't bring myself to grind through the notice board quests for the final last part of post-game content. All of my previous assessments stand with another added point that I did not find much enjoyment in:The notice board quests are simply too repetitive and grindy. Requiring 100 fusion material for level up post lv 3 means that the majority of the quests you get at that point are "hey go grind X monsters" MMO type quests. If it was 5 or 10 batches of these fetch quests, I might have put up with it, but 100 is simply too much.I really want to love this game: the music is so fantastic; the story and especially the final fusion trope ending is something I should like a lot (the conceptual monsters part too). And yet, the story just feels too sparse and too spread apart for me to truly engage with the characters and the world.Maybe the zelda-esque exploration aspect is enough for others to fill in the huge narrative spaces in between, but I suppose it's not for me then.---------------------------I think I've played long enough to see what the game excels at and where the game doesn't work for me.Here's why I would recommend this game for its strengths:(1) Quirky breezy and inclusive atmosphere(2) Encourages fun experimentation through the implementation of stickers and such(3) Great art design overall, especially the archangels(4) Fantastic exploration mechanics that progresses smoothly alongside your monster collection progress (Pokemon HM done right)This is the perfect monster collecting game for people who are attracted to its aesthetics. Pokemon for liberal art students would be how I would describe it.Here's why it doesn't work for me personally: I've realized that what I want out of a monster collecting game is perhaps the sense of companionship you get with your creatures. I find it difficult to establish that here when the sticker compatibility has a greater emphasis on creativity. Then again, these aren't monsters you are capturing, but vestiges you are recording. So perhaps I went in with the wrong impression. The plot also feel too scattered even compared to the pokemon mainline games for me to grow an attachment to the companions. They are quirky and fun banter camp dialogue generators and I like the writing for the characters. It's just a shame that it's so far and few in between.I also can't bring myself to get past the sticker management UI which makes the process too much of a headache for me (why does the sticker pages have multiple pages while being scrollable???? Did I miss a toggle option or something??? And while there are filter options which seem to be added according to player feedback, I find myself making far less use of it than its existence would imply)I don't think I can bring myself to enjoy and finish this game despite its unique artistic vision and good enough execution, but this is a genuinely good game that I know someone out there, the right person, would fall in love with it in an instant.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best monster collecting game I've ever played. The difficulty is just right, there's little to no grinding, the battles can be challenging at times (especially in the postgame), it's overall amazing in the gameplay department. The story is quite good, but the isekai setting may not be for everyone. The characters are well-written and have cool and interesting quests. If talking companions aren't your thing, you can always recruit the dog and use him. He's a good boy. You can romance the other companions, if you want, but it's totally optional and doesn't confer any gameplay benefits that I've seen. Don't know if you can romance multiple, that's not really my thing so I didn't try that, but I assume since you can choose your pronouns, you can be poly as well. Seriously, pick this game up, there's nothing else in the monster collecting genre on Steam that's quite as good. It's like the best parts of Pokemon and Persona fused (get it?) in the best way.Meredith best girl 10/10EDIT: You apparently can't be poly in vanilla! But there are some mods that let you be that are very popular and CB is one of those plug-and-play mod games, so you can fix this oversight with one mod that doesn't give you any gameplay bonuses whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifetime Pokemon fan, one of my favorite genres is the Monster Taming genre.This game is *not* a Pokemon clone. And does *not* disappoint. Cassette Beasts tries new things, and experiments with the Monster Taming genre. And it did really well in my opinion.The characters are lovely, the music is amazing (I personally adore vocals in Boss Music, it reminds me of the Persona series), and the Monster designs (subjective) were really awesome. And with the unique fusion mechanic, there are over 14,000 Combinations, making for really fun team building.The world was fun to explore, and the quests were fun to complete. And the battle system, was just OK in my opinion.I enjoy that they tried something new, but I personally didn't find learning how all the types interact - intuitive? This isn't a deal-breaker for me, but if the battle system is for you, I would look into it more before purchasing.I think with some quality of life improvements the battle system could be made better. There currently isn't any "Super Effective" or "Not Very Effective" esq flavor text when you use an advantageous move. So I found it rather difficult to know when I was using a move if it would be my best option at the time.On top of that as other reviewers have pointed out, currently when you switch companions, they take the Monster they were currently equipped with, with them. And you can't access it without swapping back to them, then accessing the storage, putting it away, then switching back, and then going back to the storage to retrieve it. This was rather inconvenient to deal with.These things alone aren't deal-breakers for me and I really enjoyed my time with the game. Generally I'm a Completionist, but I do find myself not wanting to finish the rematches with the Ranger Captain's you can access during the post game.I would love to see the developers continue to work on Cassette Beasts in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: To start, don't let my hours here fool you. I also own this game on switch (where I have a LOT more hours in the game... like many times the hours), and it is easily one of my favorite games from the last decade. I have always been a fan of pokemon games, and this brought me all the joy of a pokemon game, with a wonderful breath of fresh air. It took everything I love about pokemon, and improved on so much of it. So much so that I played it here for just under 8 hours and decided that I needed to be able to take this game places with me and purchased it for switch.First off, the story is really fun and well written. The characters are all interesting and would totally love to see more of them, and with that ending, it opens up a lot of potential even for future stuff (and if ever this game gets a sequel, I am buying that soon as I can. Heck, I am eagerly anticipating next weeks dlc release <3)The game play is familiar, but unique. I loved collecting all the creatures, and the fact that rather than literally capturing them, you yourself get to be the creature. It was like all the best things about pokemon and digimon had a baby that surpassed their franchises in ways that hopefully they will see and adapt from. From the exploration abilities, the fact that you don't need to grind to make a tape worth using, and the variety in attacks, I adored playing this game.The music is wonderful and I have spent a bit more than a reasonable amount of time just sitting in an area listening to the music playing. The energy of the cafe is so wonderfully chill, battle gets my blood pumping, all in all I wish there was more songs, but I enjoyed every song in the game.Now, to avoid exclusively gushing (though, seriously, it is gush worthy. I do not regret at all getting 2 copies.) I will get into the negatives too. There are a good few creatures, but I do wish there were more, especially ones that have really cute/pretty final forms. (Mardiusa and Misamodeus are probably my favorite designs among final forms). Not really a complaint, considering that wanting more of something in a game is usually a good sign. I have a similar issue with most aspects of the game. I want more music, I want more creatures, I want more story, I also want more character customization. I just want to keep enjoying this fun world.My only real complaint, and I am spoilering it because if you haven't finished the game you should not read this next part.  Despite this, I adore this game, and will for sure enjoy playing it for many many more hours to come.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR. After getting all the achievements, I can say it's a very fun monster taming game that brings it's own unique (and also quite complex at times) ideas to the table, though it's not worth going for 100%.Story:While there is a main story to follow that acts as a hook from the beginning of the game, this game actually splinters off into multiple stories that usually focus on one character. The strength of each story really relies on said character but luckily the main cast are enjoyable and fleshed out enough carry them. While not super deep, I for sure enjoyed their presence and I assume it's a just a matter of taste as to which ones resonate with you (with Felix being my absolute favourite). The monsters:The cast of creatures are extremely important in any monster taming game and this game delivers with 121 fun designs (not including bosses). They are packed with personality and I can see each of them having fans. In addition, both of the starting tapes are a great choice, simple at the start but help to really show off the uniqueness of this games remastering (evolution) system.This remastering mechanic is also fantastic as it can give you extra choice when evolving. You can either pick blind and have fun with your new team member or google it to see what your options are. Either way, more player choice in how a team ends up is always a good thing. It also means that even if players pick up the same monsters, their teams and strategies could end up completely different by the end of this game. The one drawback of this system is that some of these split lines have one far more cryptic one, meaning the likelihood of you finding them on your own is quite slim.I do however wish there were more of them. 121 seems like a reasonable number but a good chunk of them are split evo lines. The most blatant example of this being the cariviper line taking up 5 whole slots in the roster. Overworld gameplay:The overworld is a small yet open map that allows you to go anywhere you can reach. At first I absolutely hated exploring it as it felt like a slog. This was until I managed to gather power ups. Once you have all of them, running around the map is extremely fun but for those first crucial hours of the game it feels quite bad sadly. In terms of interesting locations, this game is almost nothing but. With how small the overall map is, there is almost no space for time filler, each section of the grid having at least one interesting thing to look at, find or explore.Battling:This games battle system will either be a blast or overly obtuse depending on how much you want to memorise. Instead of focusing on big numbers for it's type chart, certain types can dish out either positive or negative to what they are hitting. This makes for a farm more dynamic system about a mounting wall of effects, buffs and debuffs that you have to worry about rather than "me use strong move knock out opponent". While fun this system is also quite exploitable once you get comfortable with it. Many an archangel was taken down on my playthrough through a combination of leech, poison and burn. If this was a multiplayer focused game this could be a massive issue but since it's not it's just fun to see how much you can cheese challenges that you're facing.Stickers are the equivalent of moves and abilities in this game, each one can be added, peeled off or replaced with a compatible move. This gives the player a great amount of power to customise each of their team members, helping them to feel truly unique. They are also pretty easy to get your hands on so players are encouraged to play around.During each battle, you team up with a picked partner. Having fights be a 2 vs 2 (or maybe even more with swarms a summoning) allows for a great deal of strategy in regards to targeting and switching. It also gives more support oriented beasts a time to shine (seriously, despite having a zero ap attack as it's only attacking move blossomaw was one of the most reliable team members). You can also use the type chart to your advantage if you're prepared enough.AP is this games version of energy or mana or power points. This is an extremely balanced energy system that feels rewarding to engage with. Many other games would have it deplete and then force you to do nothing to gather it back whereas in this game you can almost always do something meaningful with the ap you have access to.Player base stats are also a fun addition, this can be tweaked to help boost traits that benefit your overall party or battle plan. During my playthrough I gathered a quite raged attack heavy squad. This would be a bad idea in other monster taming games but for this I was able to lean into this by investing my players current melee attack into ranged for an extra kick when attacking. Postgame:Unfortunately, once the main story is done, it feels like the game runs out of steam. There are extremely fun elements. I loved the  but every fin part is surrounded by a sea of grind. Want to bootleg hunt, 50 fused materiel per ritual candle. Want to continue the fun story lines, not until you've beaten another 4 rogue fusions. Prehaps shortening the postgame would have made it far more fun to go through but as it is, it and some of the achievements tied to it are not fun. Artstyle:I know gen 5 pokemon is very in chic right now so I imagine most people are absolutely gushing over this games 2d pixel sprites on simple 3d surroundings. I can't say I disagree with them, it works quite well. Where I think this game shines is how it clashes with it's bosses. The archangels all have a completely different artstyle that helps to make each of them feel unique and alien. Bootlegs:As a final addition (and as an avid shiny hunter in the pokemon games) I wanted to mention bootlegs. They're a 1/1000 chance of happening and they completely change the monsters type. This is such a fun addition to the formula that helps them feel unique for their regular counterparts. It also means you can hunt the same one multiple times and have completely different feeling monsters. You could probably do a run with only one type of monster if you were crazy enough. I addition, this is the only way you have access to a natural glitter type which is a fun addition that would have been to mechanically crazy to have as a normal type. If you did somehow read this far into the review and plan on getting into the game, if you find yourself with an astral traffikrab during your playthrough, consider yourself blessed.

_childDocuments_.review: When PalWorld came out, I heard people talking about other monster-collecting games and this game came up quite a bit. It happened to be on sale at the time, so I picked it up. It's a good time, overall: the elemental mechanics are generally satisfying to use (and eventually break across your knee), the music is decent (the combat tracks are a highlight, though admittedly I am a  for tracks that add vocals at times of hype), and the artwork is all really good. _childDocuments_.review: 8/10.  It's charming and has excellent presentation and style and it doesn't overstay its welcome.  After 24 hours of play, I completed the main story, and a decent bit of optional content.  The monster designs are A+ across the board, and the music is consistently good from start to finish.That said, the story definitely won't set the world on fire, and the battle system can be a little too easy to break apart, leaving the mid-late game encounters mostly trivial.  There are a lot of customization options, and the player can create some genuinely OP strategies but outside of a few post-game super bosses, the game doesn't really tailor its difficulty around the options the player has at their disposal.  By end game, I felt like I was mostly going through the motions, dominating basically every fight with the same strategies.  Still, I think this is the best indie monster collector RPG I've played.  Just don't go in expecting something mind blowing.  It's got great style and awesome music, but the story's just ok, and the gameplay is poorly balanced IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: This is... wow. To say this game is a breath of fresh air is an absolute UNDERSTATEMENT. I wanted to finish the main story before I reviewed this game, to give it a completely fair chance and let it speak for itself. (I actually ended up playing it twice before writing this review, sorry devs.)First off, let's get something out of the way. It feels like an insult to even bring up pokemon, as the games do not feel like a rip-off or anything close. This is a brand new take on the genre that I had given up on, prior. This game has already found a place in my heart. If you are thinking this is just a pokemon game, I urge you to give it a shot and see for yourself. The story drew me in. It's cute, fun and emotional at parts. All of the characters feel really 3D and had very fun dialogue with quest lines. Even some of the NPCs made me laugh with their limited dialogue! I love the game's sense of humor. All the partner characters were absolutely fantastic, I loved their designs and how much they added to the adventure. Their storylines ranged from hilarious to heartbreaking, and the optional romance was a nice touch. I won't say the story is a solid 10/10 or anything, but it was pleasant!The battle system is engaging and very fun. Experimenting with different sticker combinations and different monsters feels really fun and refreshing! Even silly joke builds were fun as heck. Lategame stuff can make you feel like a god if you set yourself up right, but at the same time there's very few ways to feel invincible. The type matchups having different interactions instead of a 2x and 0.5x damage modifier keeps you on your toes for every battle. Also there's difficulty sliders in the options menu, so if things are too easy or too hard, you can fix it! Postgame you can start games with modifiers, like nuzlockes and random types. The replayability is high!The monster designs are absolutely great. I was finding it hard to build a team because there were so many good options for monsters and builds. I love 90% of the designs easily, and all the others I still enjoy. 10/10 Traffikrab and Pombomb are best bois.The music. It's a crime not to mention the music. If you haven't already, go listen to the OST. It has a very The World Ends With You vibe to it, and it fits the game so well. I can't pick a favorite. The game might as well be $30 because you're going to buy the OST anyways. Joel Baylis absolutely NAILED it and Shelby Harvey did so well with the vocals.My conclusion? This game is made with pure love for the genre and it being only $20 feels like a crime. This is absolutely worth every cent. I highly highly recommend it, as it's already found a place in my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I was a big fan of Pokemon growing up, but as the series went on I became more and more disillusioned with it. Each creature has only one type, and all battles are double battles. Rather than supereffective and resisted moves, certain types inflict buffs or debuffs against other types. Two cassette beasts can also fuse into one to create a dual typed monster. The game is pretty open ended in terms of the world rather than linear, and the abilities you get to explore the world throughout the game, such as gliding, swimming, and running so fast you can break through stone, make exploration pretty enjoyable. It definitely feels different enough from Pokemon to not feel like a ripoff, but similar enough to Pokemon or other creature collectors to feel comfy for people who enjoy these types of games. _childDocuments_.review: Cassette Beasts is the newcomer in the recent slew of monster-taming games, a genre that has mostly been content to follow the ropes and tropes set by a particular market leader. But I’m happy to report Cassette Beasts carves a new path through subverting expectations and refining the genre in ways you might not even realise you want.Let’s start with the main event – the combat. Cassette Beasts’ combat is focused on ‘energy,’ a resource that needs strategic management and preservation. Every turn you’ll gain a fixed amount of energy and any decent move has an associated energy cost. Between those powerful attacks your turns will be spent playing defensive options or doing mild chip damage. It’s reminiscent of the sort of resource management you’d find in tabletop games and interesting tradeoffs naturally emerge, even in wild battles that would feel inconsequential in other RPGs.These interesting play mechanics are all enhanced by Cassette Beasts solely featuring Double Battles and dedicating a significant proportion of its moves to enhancing or protecting your team mate. The combat possibilities are dizzying and the best indicator of those possibilities is in Cassette Beast’s equivalent of ‘Gyms,’ which are not based on monster types but each instead showcases an entirely unique battle strategy. It’s great stuff.I also never stuck to a single strategy thanks to team experimentation being made trivial. Experience persists across all your monsters and attacks can be outright transferred between them (so long as the receiving monster’s movepool accepts it). Once any final evolution was reached I swapped them out, meaning I was able to progress both the bestiary and storyline without falling behind the level curve, creating a rewarding sense of progression.Said story is well-planned - a somewhat sombre reflection on nostalgic escapism and those themes will resonate with the target audience. The execution is serviceable, is filled with late 90's charm, and the boss battles along the way are a stylish highlight. However, I do think more sidekick-focused quests would have helped flesh out the characterisation, as the game lacks that immersive ‘ensemble goes questing’ feeling you might desire in your RPGs. I think some of that comes down to a lack of “quality time” you get to spend with the cast, so keep those expectations in check.On the topic of characters I’d say ‘creature designs’ are typically the weakest point of other monster-taming games, but Cassette Beasts bucks the trend by drawing from a range of inspirations while weaving a consistent design language throughout. The spectrum goes from ‘adorable’ to ‘edgelord’ while always maintaining a unique ‘Cassette Beast’ feel. Shoutouts to ‘Djinn Entonic’, ‘Brushroom’ and ‘Elfless’ (my beloved).My only major gripe here is navigating the overworld, there’s significant traversal stutter when moving at pace and the visuals are just about adequate (in comparison to the excellent monster sprites). It also takes a while to unlock your full navigation moveset and the interim does feel like something is ‘missing’ which makes for a bad first impression. Keep at it though, once you unlock the  everything will start to click.So, to summarise, Cassette Beasts may be the monster-taming newcomer but imo it’s the most interesting of the lot. Serious effort has gone into identifying and challenging genre staples and using them as opportunities to innovate. I’ve kept details about a lot of that polish vague because the best bit of Cassette Beasts is in the surprises and delights you’ll discover along the journey. To any fans of turn-based battles seeking interesting yet accessible gameplay then Cassette Beasts is the one to grab. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version: Cassette Beasts is a game that was clearly developed with both intention, intelligence, and heart. You are getting an insanely high value even if you buy at full price. This game is worth $60, let alone $20.Long Version:A creature collection game lives and dies on its designs. Cassette Beasts has no duds. Literally the only drawback in the design department is that un-remastered (un-evolved) Cassette Beasts have no unique advantage over fully realized ones, and so if you love a cute earlier stage of a particular monster, you may not have it for long unless you deliberately handicap yourself by accepting lower stats. **That said, I have nothing but praise for the artistic designs themselves.** The cultural references are deeper and more creative cuts than you will see in many, if not all competing games in the genre. Combat has no wasted mechanics. All gimmicks come from the unique builds that are possible themselves. The sticker mechanic (equivalent to both moves/attacks/spells and passive abilities) offers an amount of flexibility that maximizes creative potential for the player, while offering just enough scarcity to *inspire* creativity in the player. Moves that trigger automatically at the start of combat are a minority, but plentiful enough to allow more fast-paced builds if turn-based combat doesn't hold your attention. The writing is... good. Charming, realistic characters that nonetheless feel memorable and distinct from one another. The story is not the main draw of Cassette Beasts, but it does not hinder it in anyway. On top of that, it explains the world in a satisfying way that allows for immersion alongside more eccentric monsters. Sure, a playthrough may only take 5-10 hours, but the depth of strategy available and budding mod community will almost surely provide a near-endless amount of replayability.I will not deny that there are some small quality of life hiccups. Swapping out beasts could certainly be more streamlined for one. This is however, heavily outweighed by other features that were clearly designed by taking into account the history of game development as a discipline. Much of the games flows very naturally and allows the player to control the challenge and pace. Cassette Beasts captures almost all of the lovable aspects of its genre peers and predecessors. Where it deviates, it does so with intention and a desire to improve. It succeeds.

_childDocuments_.review: Unapologetically political, unabashedly queer, and unrepentantly girly. But not inappropriate. While it contains many mature themes (environmentalism, capitalism, identity, it's a pretty explicitly leftist game), and i's not subtle, it's not dirty or obscene unless you view all queerness as such.It's got a lot in common with Pokemon, even for a post-Pokemon Mons series. It plays a bit closer to a Final Fantasy or Persona 5 in combat, with platforming like a good Zelda game. Mon design does not care to hide the inspiration and direction they got from Pokemon and Digimon (and likely other Mons series like SMT). This is a clear passion project from those involved, who love video games and Mons series in general. I also appreciate that "girl" is the default gender in the same way "boy" is he default Pokemon gender. It's small but it shows the girl demographic was not an afterthought or in periphery.As a lifelong Pokemon fan, some of the biggest distinctions that I liked:- Each Mon has only a single type. Type is also a lot more dynamic than in Pokemon, with natural type interactions sometimes having status conditions (A Fire move will always burn a Plant type, causing damage over time and being super effective; an Air move will extinguish a Fire type, lowering their offensive stats and being super effective; Fire moves will melt Plastic types, giving them a Poison coating type change and dealing neutral damage)- Equivalent of "Shinies" are Bootlegs, which learn rarer moves. There are 14 bootlegs for each Mon (one per type, this does include their native type)- Branched remaster (evolution) paths. Pokemon has some but they're kind of the exception. There's a ton here, including each of he 2 Starters- Ability to full Dex complete with a single copy of a single game- Sticker system of moves is really cool and creative.Some issues: the platforming is so much harder on a keyboard than a controller. No fast ravel to campfires. Massive resource inequity (past the very early game you'll basically have more wood than you'll ever need, pulp is basically an infinite resource without much trying, and metal is worth life itself).

_childDocuments_.review: Man...should have listened to the reviews sooner. This game is phenomenal.I haven't finished it yet, but there is absolutely no way this will get anything other then a massive thumbs up.The game is better then any pokemon game, EVER, period. The combat system itself is simple, but by using all the customisation options you have at your disposal, this quickly turns into the most complex turned based I've seen. There are so many abilities, so many monster types, so many ways for the different elements to interact with each-other; it's just insane. Things like air putting out fire element, so lowering it's stats, or other elements turning things into glass and then you have abilities that shatter the glass killing the monster instantly, or spreading shards that hurt melee ones; or monster that are asleep having access to very powerful dream-walking spells, but they have 1% chance to hit, so you use a buff that gives them 100% for 1 turn etc etc. You could write essays on how many things can happen.The game is also chock-full of references and has some amazing names for all the monsters.Other then that the game over-world is a really cool, puzzle filled place. where you have to use abilities and a bit of brain power to traverse it and find treasures/quests.The story is also very interesting, if a bit of a slow burn.To top it all off, the music is just amazing and it gets EVEN better when you use your fuse move.Probably the only mediocre thing is the animations. There are ton of monsters, so each only has like one animation.Overall, it's one of the best games out there. A must buy at any price. Every time I find a gem like this, it makes me happy to see indie devs still pushing the limit of what games can become with little money, but a ton of soul.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wished that there was a monster-catching RPG with fusion mechanics, an open world, Breath of the Wild exploration, a 3D-pixel art style, an 80's aesthetic and soundtrack, boss fights that make you say "What the **** is that", and character stories that bounce and up and down from warmhearted to surprisingly dark?First of all, that's an incredibly specific thing to wish for, but Cassette Beasts deliverers it, with a great combat system to boot. I already mentioned you can fuse these monsters together. Those fusions, from my experience so far, ALL have a unique sprite for every combination. Even different stages of Remixed (evolved) monsters will create different variations when fused with the same monster. Also, soundtrack vocals kick in whenever you use fusion in combat, and I'm a huge sucker for adaptive music.These monsters have types, and those types have strengths and weaknesses, but they come in the form of a wide variety of unique interactions, not just "More damage, less damage".  Hitting a Fire-element monster with water extinguishes their flames, dropping their attack stats. Hitting them with a Plant attack burns the plants, creating a smoke screen that raises evasion. Hitting them with Poison fuels the fire, increasing their AP generation. The various elemental interactions in this game are honestly pretty awesome.Also, have you always despised in monster-catching games that your character roams around the wild, and never has to worry about being hurt themselves? If you around out of monsters, you just lose, right? WRONG. In Cassette Beasts, your own characters health bar is just as important as the monsters you use; You transform into them, after all! If one of your transformations runs out of HP during a round of combat, you'll revert to your human self for the rest of the round, and take the rest of the attacks directly. Run out of health yourself, and it doesn't matter if you still have more monsters in your party; it's off to the hospital for you. This also applies to human NPCs that you might fight against. It's pretty hilarious to end a battle early because you took their first monster and just pelted the poor person with meteors until they drop to the floor.Fun note: This game has co-op! Combat always takes place with you in control of 2 people, so co-op in that is pretty straightforward anyway: But for exploring? You can run around, sequence-breaking the world together as you traverse it's oddly-physics-based landscape with the help of being able to throw boxes and rocks down and up to each other on platforms that you almost definitely shouldn't have been able to reach! Half of my game-time at the time of this review was with a friend, and it was a blast. Still a blast playing it by myself! Just, you known, still awesome with a friend.
