_childDocuments_.review: Hello Neighbor 2 brings a new chapter to the series, and even though I didn't play the first game, I found myself quickly immersed in the world of Raven Brooks. The game introduces you to a mysterious town filled with secrets, and the storyline does a great job of pulling you in right from the start.Exploring the town is both fun and challenging. The puzzles are well-designed, offering a good balance between difficulty and enjoyment. Each character you encounter has a unique personality, and discovering their stories adds an interesting layer to the game. While there were a few bugs here and there, they didn't significantly detract from the overall experience.The game isn't without its flaws. There were occasional technical issues, such as crashes and freezes [Had 2 crashes over the whole course of the game, which I completed in 7h~]. Moreover, the price might seem too steep. >aiting for a sale could make it a more worthwhile purchase.In conclusion, Hello Neighbor 2 offers an engaging and enjoyable experience, especially for those who enjoy mystery and puzzle games. While there are some technical hiccups and the game could be longer, the immersive world and intriguing story make it worth playing. If you're a fan of the genre, it's definitely worth checking out, preferably when it's on sale.I did it on stream and the VODs are available there if you want to check it out ! (in french)

_childDocuments_.review: It's an amazing game that I can't come up with a single criticism of. Late contender for game of the year IMO. I love the bigger map and the fact you have more than one location to break into and explore (almost the entire town of Raven Brooks, actually). It feels like the devs have learnt from some of the puzzles in the first game being a bit hard to understand as it's relatively simple to figure out what you have to do here.Another thing I like is that there's more than one enemy this time. Instead of just Mr Petersen (the Neighbor himself). there's a policeman, Otto and more!The controls are great, as they were in the first game, but it feels like they've been polished. Any problems with the controls are simply skill issues. The art-style is amazing and is a huge part of the game's charm. The graphics are better than in the first game and you might need a good computer to be able to run the game at the highest settings.10/10, worth every penny. One of the best sequels I've ever played. Anyone who hates on this game is wrong, including that one YouTuber who called it a 'pathetic joke'.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME! Not only is it a disappointment, but I will show you reasons why not to support tinyBuild.Pros:Great music: Intense and almost better than the game lol.Great graphics: Much better than the first game.Great art style: Realistic, but cartoony. Characters are not scary at all though. Game can barely even be called horror.Cut scenes are cool and dramatic, but don’t reveal a ton about the lore, mostly stuff we know or could have guessed.Locations are unique and present dynamic themes. I enjoyed traversing through them. Some layouts were much superior than others. Though the puzzles are repetitive between each one.Cons:VERY SHORT: Can beat in 1-2 hours on a regular play-throughTerrible AI: You can walk away from them as they chase you and they cannot catch you, seriously. AI also switch between 2 tasks basically doing nothing all day. AI does not learn from the players and does the same stuff over and over, they don’t set up traps either. AI also gets stuck on stuff sometimes, depending on the AI it can happen a lot.No neural network: Yes, they lied, the devs told us weeks before release there would be one, but there is not. Game is not open world: It’s linear and set into chapters. Once you finish the game you can explore the open world, but it is small and there is basically nothing to do.Puzzles are easy and repetitive: Solutions are sometimes in the same room as the set up to the puzzles. EVERY LOCATION has basically the same tools and puzzles, it gets boring FAST.Tons of scrapped sandbox mechanics: You barely can do anything, basically just using a few tools and objects. Vaulting doesn’t work for all objects, the developer decide what you can vault on sometimes.Story is boring: The story is really basic, sometimes not even being logical. The ending is one of the WORST endings I have seen in a game. Short and underwhelming. Game leaves more questions than answers, do NOT buy for lore.School DLC is good, but puzzles are easy to cheat by vaulting (without clipping through anything). It’s basically the same length as FG.Library DLC has no ending… Read that again. Yes it is just simply unfinished. Woo hoo, $15 DLC on steam!Very bare bones game, you beat it, then that is it. It’s one of those games where watching someone play it is similar to actually experiencing it, since it isn’t that scary or hard.THE “SCAMS”:WAAYYYYYYY too overpriced, game is NOT worth the money!All throughout their marketing they promised us a neural network where the AI learns from the community to evolve, an primarily open world game, and an improved sandbox experience. Guess what? It was all lies! They lied about a lot of other stuff I will not include here.They say the game will get post launch updates, but how are we supposed to trust them? They have lied many times. They marketed this game as the FULL RELEASE. Only to give us an unfinished product. I didn’t pay $60 for unfinished DLCs and a short unfinished game.DAYS before release they changed the steam description to not say the AI learns from the players and that the game is open world.This is not the game I payed for, this is way too overpriced.Lead game designer went on sabbatical right before release, who does that???Their discord server is harsh and sometimes BANS members who suggest or complain about their game too much, it’s horrible. Someone got banned for suggesting a hard mode for some reason.It is sad to get hyped over a promising AI only for them to straight up lie. I am pretty sure they just straight up falsely marketed this game, feels like scamming to me.Checklist format:Audience: Casual gamerGraphics: BeautifulMusic: FantasticDifficulty: EasyBugs: A few bugsStory: BadGameplay: Fun (sometimes boring, depending on player)Game Length: Really short (1-2 hours)Price/Quality: Don't buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello neighbor 2 is a significant improvement from the first game.. that being said it is not hard to improve upon a poorly put together game designed exclusively by interns. What sucked the most in the first game is that to beat the game you had to do what felt like glitches to beat it. I am glad to report that this game is much smoother and plays better. Controls and visuals look well put together which surprised me massively. The core mechanics just work much smoother which is what the first game needed. The puzzles were well put together and actually made sense, as opposed to the first game where you had to stack boxes or spend a few hours watching tutorials. Unlike the first game, there is a realistic prospect for you to figure the puzzles out without cheating. My biggest gripe with the game is the weird AI that follows you around each building. I personally feel that the game could do without the AI as I don't think it adds anything. It simply just serves as a nuisance to piss off the player. Do away with the AI or download mods to remove them and the game is so much more playable. I recommend downloading mods to remove the AI otherwise you will just be getting caught every 2-3 seconds. Trying to look at something to figure it out? instantly caught, stand still for 0.5 seconds? Caught. Breathe facing left? Caught. Stealthing around is lame and needs to go. it's more of a hide and seek simulator which destroys the puzzle element of the game because you have to spend 2 hours running around a house to avoid the AI and 5 or 6 minutes solving puzzles. I simply cannot recommend this game unless you are willing to download mods. To advertise this game at anything more than $1.25 is a scam. Avoid until a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Neighbor 2 is a really good, really bad game. The Pros and Cons of Hello Neighbor 2:-The story is a lot more fleshed out than the original, making sense and introducing new characters. The Con to this however, is that the game is not finished and has quite a closed ending.-The design of it is so much more improved than the first game, there was obviously an over-haul on the textures and quality of this game. Although some items floating, and some NPC's freezing, does throw this beauty of a game off-guard quite a bit.-The puzzles, so long as you actually try and figure them out for yourself and don't just watch a guide, you cheeky git- you may actually find challenging and quite fun to solve. The only downside is that, the NPC's which are meant to BE the obstacle preventing you from solving puzzles easily, are quite stupid. If I were to make one major complaint about the game, it's the AI. In Advertisement it was stated the game would work on a neural network AI, whilst here; not only is that entirely ditched, but it feels like they didn't even bother making the AI actively adapt and learn to your way of playing the game, and one of the enemies may just freeze altogether when chasing you.The game, as of writing this is on sale; so it's definitely worth checking out, but don't think for a moment it's worth the asking price of $30.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly fun. I'm kind of 50/50 on recommending it though.So for the positives:- The convoluted and seemingly impossible-to-solve-on-your-own puzzles of the first game are gone. The puzzles here are much easier to figure out, more fun to do and generally take you less time. Only had one instance where I needed to reference a video to find a key.- MOST of the bugs from the first game have been taken care of here. Not all of them, but most of them.- Love the neighborhood setup with a variety of different interiors to explore and run around in. Definitely love the different NPC's that were added in. Character design is great, music is great, and everything for the most part is very nice to look at.The negatives:-Far too little content for the current price point. I beat the whole game in maybe 8 hours and that was with a lot of fooling around. Even after snagging this game when it was on sale, I still feel like I spent too much on it.-One of my favorite things about the first game were the variety of items you could pick up and use to interact with the world around you (ex: picking up trash cans and throwing them to break windows, boxes to reach higher places, etc.). There are far fewer options here for items you can pick up. It makes the puzzle solving a little more straight forward with the limited item selection, but ultimately feels like it limits your options in general.-This may be just me but Mr. Otto, the third NPC you encounter is just straight up annoying. His house is way too small, and he is EVERYWHERE. I got so frustrated with this part because it is hard to make any progress or figure out the solutions to any puzzles with him on your ass so frequently. Think he could have been thought out a little better. Especially considering the NPC after him is so much easier to evade.-The NPC's in general are still buggy at times. At first it didn't seem apparent enough to complain about but as I progressed I discovered more more bugs with them. It's not anything like the bugs of the first game, but still worth mentioning.Like the game, the puzzles are fun and in general I am a fan of the series, but all of the games feel unfinished in one way or another at the end of the day. If tinyBuild really spent more time on these games they could be really great instead of just being kind of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game religiously since it came out out on gamepass for xbox and FINALLY got it on pc when patch 9 came outI dream about it, even when i close my eyes i hear the noises of the game, the small creaking of the wood as the cop walks on the porch, i run behind myself and jump on the trampoline placed conveniently right by the roof of the house that is across the street from the blue house the cop, Keith, is guarding.I parkour my way over to the tree house, and it's inconvenient but just close enough that i can do a run and jump with enough momentum and correct timingInside the tree house is tons of toys the children used to play with, concept art of a robot plastered on the wall and said robot on a table not far away in bad shapewithout missing a beat as if i could see into the future i push the wall where the artwork hangs and grab the robots arm and place it onto the robot, i flip the arms quickly, i memorized the way i should arrange them from when i looked around and immediately the chest of the bot opens and reveals a hidden compartment, inside is the switch i needI turn around and slap it onto the board and flip it quickly, just as the train passes by and goes into the tunneli for some dumb reason sit there and watch as the train pushes the scissors out... I could just grab it with my hands but for some odd reason i feel compelled to sit and watch as the contraption some random kid or two came up with...i snap out of it grabbing the sissors just as it reaches the peak of the box and jump out of the hole where the ladder is placedI run down and towards the blue house, jumping over the police tape and towards the backdoorWith a crowbar in my hand, i run inside and break a board off the wall, a little orange haired dolly in blue lay flat, i pick it up and twist around to slam the doll on top of the doll house near the edge of the roofthen i run towards the hallway and to a suspicious painting on the wall, it has three panels on them, words pop into my head quickly "N.O.T"and like magic i slide the panels of the puzzle up and spell these confusing words "N.O.T"And the wall slides open, a hidden room, i continue on using the scissors i acquired earlier to clear the upstairs of police tape then run towards the room next to the stairsa safe lies on the table and on it, a 4 digit combination codeThe first thing that comes to mind is people i know... Oh!"1984!" I whisper to myself before sliding the digits upward and!*Click* with a whirl the door opens and reveals a key! I hear the cop grow antsy and i make a run for upstairs, I run fast skipping the first door and head towards the second, stopping only for a split second to crowbar open a crate and take a photo before heading inside.It a childs room full of even more toys then the other room!In the corner is a pillow with a patch in the center, there's a pressure plate near it, a bed with a race car attached to a handman roller coaster.For now i rip open the pillow with my scissors and take the other photoBut the noise i make alarms the cop and he is now running upstairs, but as long a i know his location i can explore the second room without much problemSo as he runs inside the room i'm already underneath the secret doorway hidden inside the cabinet of the vanity...And into the room of the door i had previously skipped!I climb the dresser and eradicate the first spider web of the day and snatch the weight, it's quite heavy too...i some how place it in my pocket and jump down, running into the second of the room to destroy more police tape and snatch the next part of some puzzle, this would be the third photo, but once again, the cop is close on my trailso i need to be quick, before going back through the hidden doorway i pull the lever of the bed and it slides away from the wall to the center of the room, how the cop isn't noticing this and instantly becoming aware of my presence is beyond me but i count my blessing and rush myself anyway, grabbing my crowbar and removing the planks that were hidden under the bed... I gasp as i hear the door open, I run underneath so fast but i'm sure he saw me slightly, it matters not, i know he's in that room so i run out to the childs room and place the heavy weight onto the pressure plate from before and a wardrobe opens up, revealing the next and final piece of the puzzle!i quickly grab it and on purpouse i step on the squeaky toys scattered upon the floor and hide once more...this should be enough to finish this puzzle once and for all!I place the photos into the frame that lays on the bookshelf and inside a box that appeared like books was a key!I wasn't tricked but i'm sure if i hadn't dreamt of this entire place a multitude of times i'd be confused...right, there was something next to the planks i had destroyed, a box?I checked again and sure enough, a box with a lever inside!I snatch it and run towards the door, i latched it onto the motherboard and flipped it...Once again, a sliding door... This place feels more like an amusement park then a house, and while i'm enjoying the ride, i'm still terrified...Oh crap the cop!He's approaching the door!I quickly cut the second cobwebs of today and grab a battery out of the weird machine and as the door opens i'm merely caught! I dodge the chasing cop and run under the hidden doorJust as i think i'm caught he... gives up and continues looking around...?confusing, i think to myself but... i shake my thoughts away and continue, grateful for the second chance, i vow not to be THAT risky again!I take the battery and shove it into the machine where the racecar was placed and it activates, a loud squeak plays and it rolls down under the bedI jump and fear the cop may have heard it, so i press the button wildly, hoping to bring the car back as fast as possiblebut it rides back up slowly so i just snatch the key and hide back into the hidden area again... THIS time... that's right! This is the final time i'll hide under here! I'll never have to mention this "hidden area" again!I pump my fist in the air as i hear the door open, signaling the cop's departure! I check real quick to be sure and sure enough, he's gone! I wide up the clock just in case and jump down the hole i previously freed upIt kinda hurts but i ignore the pain for the satisfaction of solving this houses mystery!!I'm getting excited as i use the 3 keys i gathered to remove some locks, freeing more space for other items, i run towards the hallway i had opened using that code "N.O.T"... What kind of code is that? Is that raven brooks for ton? What kind of password would that be too? whatever, not important! Focus Quentin!That's not my name tho...uhI grab the boy dolly out extra room and examine it as i run towards the houseNow that i'm looking closer at it, it kinda looks like the missing boy!Hey! the girl dolly looks like the missing girl too!I placed it on the house next to the girl and run back towards the stairs, that's when i notice the painting placed above one of the dressers was slightly bulging! That's it! It must be ANOTHER secret room!I climb the dresser and push it open, just as the cop comes downstairs, i hide inside quickly!He doesn't suspect a thing! Oh and there it is! The last dolly i need! It's a dolly of the owner of this house too, Theodore Masters Peterson... A missing man too, suspected to be the parents and the reason those two children went missing...I shake my head, i see the cop head back upstairs and waste no time running back to the kitchen to place him downThe dolly now in place at the other end of house causes a clicking sound and the edge where the girl dolly stands opensa compartment which hid the final key!I grab it and open the last lock, entering the basement! Finally!I grab the newspaper and read it... forget it! I throw the paper and grab the red key, leaving quickly!But then... a piece of paper smacks me in the fast and it says..Hepl me... :3

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Neighbor 2 builds on the stealth horror of its predecessor, placing you in a larger, more open world with new mysteries to uncover. The AI is smarter and more unpredictable, adapting to your every move as you investigate the eerie town of Raven Brooks. The game’s atmosphere is both creepy and engaging, with a distinctive art style that enhances the tension. However, it still struggles with clunky controls and occasionally frustrating puzzles. While it improves on the original, some players may find the experience uneven. Still, it’s a solid choice for those who enjoy a challenging, suspenseful adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play it, the more I love this game. The music, the liveliness of all the characters, the puzzles that are so easy that they make the game more fun because I know I'm getting better at it with muscle memory. My favourite thing to do is laugh at Mr. Otto after getting the shovel and memorizing the code for the safe. At first I thought the vaulting system and the controls were pretty bad, but they both turned out great! This game is surprisingly supportive on PS4, and I honestly think that the PS4 version is better! I have a few problems, though. The DLC's. I wouldn't dare to play them because I'd be there for hours, scratching my head. Even when I tried to play the B.T.S. DLC yesterday, it just crashed. I'm fine with it though. The main game has a lot to offer. Including glitches. These are one of those instances where glitches benefit the game. When climbing the ladder outside the bakery using patch 8 (I think) sometimes you'd just infinitely climb a nonexistent ladder. And the speedruns, OH! The SPEEDRUNS! The sub 2 minute speedrun by Ajz was one of the reasons I played the game. And all of these good things where the reasons why I bought the game, beat it once here and 2 times on PS4 edition, aswell as a platinum and all trophies on here.                                                Overall an incredible game which I would highly recommend!                                                                                                               P.S. It's my favourite HN Game!

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral button for reviews. It's got an equal amount of pros and cons. I really enjoyed the first hello neighbour. It was fun, strategic and the AI was much better. Now in this second instalment instead of just going against Mr Peterson you come across multiple different people. This is pretty cool as it allows you to explore different houses and each new "neighbour" has their own thing. Like one with shoot you and stun you stopping you from escaping. The only problem is that I don't find the AI to be as challenging as the previous game. I did not struggle much as all with this one and managed to pass each section pretty quickly. ( Quick update a new patch was added upgrading the AI slightly with a few cool updates like the AI being able to find you more easily)I just think that the story is just a bit short. At the end of game there is a message to keep an eye out for future updates so I am really hoping they do release some form of update expanding the story further. It just didn't feel as full as the first game. I did enjoy playing through it though. Solving the puzzles and stuff. I've seen a lot of people complain about the jankyness of the game but I think that's how it should be the first game was like that and it gives it that same feel. Would I recommend?Yeah totally if you enjoyed the first game. But I cannot justify paying £30 for it. It is shorter than the first game and costs more than it. I got it discounted. I am yet to buy the dlc definitely when it next goes on sale because I am not paying £25 for both.

_childDocuments_.review: Right now there is lots of mixed opinions on Hello neighbor 2, some love , some hate it. So I will try to be subjective. I personally really enjoyed this game. I would agree that the full version of Hello Neighbor 1 was pretty bad and while the ai is better than in the first game it still isn't perfect. There is an improvement in sound and visuals and the puzzles feel a lot more fair (besides a few ones that are very hard to figure out on your own). Since you can only pick up relevant items though, you won't end up with billions of items with no use. Also, the houses themselves are not too big nor too small and the multiple characters make it more refreshing than hello neighbor 1. I'm not sure if it's worth it's current price and I would suggest waiting for sales, but I defienetly had lots of fun. One last thing is that it ends with a cliffhanger, which can be both bad and good, depending on what comes afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: this review will only be about patch #3 for the main game.The new update for the game came out and I have LOVED it. I've enjoyed the scenery more because of the improved lighting. The little details that make the game feel more alive makes the game a better experience for me. Especially that you can now use the scroll wheel on the mouse now to switch objects, a pretty useful feature. Some parts of the puzzles have been updated to be made a bit more apparent to the player (such as the gray 80k weight in the Neighbor's bedroom). The new jumpscares make each character stand out more instead of just the same old jumpscare they all used before this patch. The addition of lore makes the game more interesting (the cassette tapes), sparking my interest in the lore. Also the mirror in the reporter station is actually a mirror now, awesome. I look forward to future updates for this game and the roadmap of it, as long as they restore the false promises that were made for this game. I will give the thumbs up for the patch, but I don't recommend playing the game YET. I recommend playing it when the game is actually complete.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to say it, but this game was just hot garbage.I've been a loyal fan to the Hello Neighbor series since the release of Alpha 2, and have loved the franchise ever since. However, as the lack of content died down, so did my hype. The lore felt messy and out of place, and I was unable to piece everything together, which just made the franchise confusing.Don't get me wrong, I was pretty hyped when hearing about the new AI the neighbor would have, alongside a neural network AI. Little did I know, the developers straight up LIED to our faces. What they have basically done with this game was release an unfinished build. I feels extremely shallow in terms of game play and puzzles. Not only was the game bad, but the developers have been trying to milk the franchise cow to death with books and spin-offs to try to keep the franchise relevant. Their attempts have all been pathetic, even resorting to practically begging Game Theorists to make another video on the topic just to stay alive.Overall, the game and the overall franchise is a mess that lost it's relevance.

_childDocuments_.review: Parkour feels clunky, I still have no idea on what basis you can climb something, since sometimes you don't reach a surface and magically climbs, on the other hand you may have half body over the surface you want to climb to but it does absolutely nothing and you fall down. AI to be honest only chases you on sight doesn't learn: it spots you, chases you, loses sight of you, goes to the spot where you were last seen, stays there for a few secs and if you are not spotted goes back to patrol. Doesn't for example take account of where you have been seen and patrol more often on that area or if you were caught on a locker search them actively ... or maybe for example the items that you scavenged trough the house instead of just bringing them to their original location for example place traps around I mean HN 1 on it's beginnings at least "learned" and "acted" in consequence to the players actions and that's what we look for not just a puzzle game with an AI patrolling, there are already games like that.. And the DLCs at least library one is disappointing, at least I've lost all my interest on the game. I feel it to be over priced for what it actually is, I may reconsider trying another DLC if I see those issues with the parkour solved later on but right now I proceed to uninstall the game yet again with utter disappointment

_childDocuments_.review: It seems like we're right back to where we started with HN2. I originally started with a negative review that went somewhat positive since I had faith in the game again after Patch 9, but it's been almost a year since a content update for this game and I'm kinda losing my patience. I've tried to put up with the wait considering I've developed a game or two so I know the hardships but the fact there's no real teasers and the team seems to only be focusing on the Animated Series is just...it's sad.The game is linear, no real chance to be creative with your puzzle solving (except for in the forest to a degree), little to no replayability when you solve the side quests, ai does the same few things over and over. I'm not asking for the neural network, I'm asking for an ai that actually feels human and learns.Do not buy full price until more content is added. If you REALLY want the game, get it on sale. Coming from someone who's play since HN1 Beta 3...this is really, really sad. Please tinybuild, focus on your game or show that you have been. I wish it was marked as Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe i am writing this but here we go. Hello Neighbor is one of my favorite games but ever since this released I was NOT happy. It took them 2 years past launch for it to be fixed and polished. The game itself has no neural networking for the AI's (which was literally promised and advertised) which is what the main attraction was. They had all these trailers showing a great and promising game. They promised us in devlogs and trailers that there would be fun quests to  do from wandering "friendly ai" as they call it. We got none of that. There were 2 promised places to explore. Guess what!? WE NEVER GOT THEM. They had this very fun looking game showcased. This version of the game is known as "alpha 2", as the community call it. The description of the game stated "a constantly learning AI that will be trained by players across the globe". It sounded so awesome. Only problem would be something like: -"What if the neighbor gets too good and makes the game unplayable!?"- Days before release the developers quickly changed the description to something along the lines of "AI that you need to be careful of", or something like that. They literally false advertised the whole game. Why the whole game you may ask? Remember that really cool map with promised quests and locations, and FUNCTIONING ai? THEY DELETED ALL OF IT. We ended up with a small map with locations you could expl- oh wait. Sorry! You have to do this than this to get access to this which lets you go here. Also there were like 4-5 locations instead of the promised 12. The DLC's are horrendous and terrible. They get small fixes that just break next patch. Not to mention that the deluxe edition is the price of a triple-a game. (The dlcs again, are crap and short with bad puzzles) The main game is 40 dollars. I think it should be 20 due to the 2 hour long story and nothing else to do. The game can be fun with these new patch notes and content but the guest was another promise. At launch we get a 2 second frame of him in the opening then he is never seen again. It wasn't until the latest patch note/content update where he had this (pretty good) area that had that hello guest feel. But it wasn't as good. They teased a lot of wip cutscenes that would show there gonna be a "part 2" that takes place after the terrible cliff hanger ending. It has been months since the latest patch and I honestly think the don't care anymore. All that they are focusing on are new unpolished games. And the strange HN tv show that is honestly just terrible and uncanon feeling. If you want the true Hello Neighbor feel, go play the first 2 alphas of the first game. (they are free. also im mean pre alpha and alpha 1, not alpha 2. Alpha 2 is alright i guess.)

_childDocuments_.review: this game isn't bad, but it's not great. I only found myself thoroughly enjoying or being genuinely scared by 2 of the houses. Some of the puzzles aren't explained well (if at all), so if you buy this, be prepared to sift through a walkthrough a few times. It's definitely overpriced (I feel like 30 dollars would've been more fair), and especially with how many times I had to look up a walkthrough, I can't say I recommend this game unless you really want to try it. This game has a VERY good artstyle, it's nothing too groundbreaking, but it takes what the original Hello Neighbor did, and removed all the missing textures, empty environments and over-stylized models and finds a very good middle ground between realistic and cartoony. The music is pretty good, and just walking around the town and climbing up houses provides a strange amount of tranquility I didn't expect from a indie horror game- especially not hello ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ neighbor. Don't buy this game if you want a *good* product, but do buy it if you're interested in the story or need to form an opinion for yourself (That's why I bought it, atleast.) Also I don't think I'm gonna buy the DLCs unless they go on sale because YEESH I am NOT paying THIRTY DOLLARS for like 2 extra houses when I have no way to know their quality outside of watching a playthrough and spoiling it. If it's intended for the full experience to be WITH the DLCs, 1, they should've been a part of the original game and 2, they should NOT be FIFTEEN DOLLARS EACH, WHAT THE HELL. That's more than HALF the game's price JUST for some extra stuff. I haven't even played them and I know it's not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure why not, I'll give a good review because I actually enjoyed myself while playing although it is a complete mess. Honestly I haven't been following the game and I thought it came out a couple months ago but that was actually just a beta. So I hate to say it but I actually liked it no matter how big of a critic I am with games that are marketed directly towards babies and youtubers to make crappy thumbnail clickbait with these characters, I still ended up enjoying it because besides it being short af (I have completed the game in its entirety by unlocking all achievements) I did like it. Will I buy the DLC's? no way, I am not wasting my money on expansions that basically have nothing to do with this game AND that I know they are way more broken then this mess. On the bad side I think that it gets boring at times when I am sitting in a closet and they just won't leave because of some sort of bug, I guess people are made at TinyBuild or whatever their name is because they broke promises on AI and a lot of other things to rush this game out and get money which is a very scummy thing to do (especially the DAY ONE DLC'S!!!!!) but with patch 2 out it seems to run better although I got the game once patch 2 came out. Also MORE GUEST!!! PLEASE HE SEEMED SO INTERESTING AND HE LOOKED SO COOL, WHY IS HE IN THE GAME FOR 2 SECONDS TOTAL!! Ok so the goods of this is most of the gameplay. When the puzzles aren't impossible to figure out without a youtube guide it is fun to figure out the clues and complete these puzzles and realize what you have to do next and I had a lot of fun with that unlike the first Hello Neighbor game where it was be impossibly precise or go home. Graphics are good which made me forget about it being some of the goofiest thing i've seen when it comes to "scary" since it isn't scary at all. I also admit that the ending is not too bad, I knew how it ended when going into this because I realized the game had been out for 3 WEEKS SURPRISINGLY! so I knew how it ended but was convinced to buy it because JT Music and The Living Tombstone's fan songs on them were great and after witnessing the ending fully instead of a brief summary I can say that TinyBuild is a company willing to milk Hello Neighbor til people stop buying their games (I am looking forward to the VR game they are making cuz that could have potential to scare me), but on the other hand it does have a nice touch to it knowing that the Neighbor is just emotionally damaged and (SPOILERS) the kid comes up and gives him a hug and helps him escape, I thought that was pretty well thought out with the idea of infinite DLC's to come out of it (Spoilers over). I'm done talking about it so if you want a game that is very stupidly kid friendly but still has that sense of fun to it then I think this would be a good choice, but go buy Security Breach instead, it's way better for the same price. Screw the price. Screw the company. But sure it's a good game. Final rating: 6.5/10

With the current state of the game, there is recent news of weekly content updates coming from the team, as they did not have enough time before release to bring old and fun mechanics from previous builds back into this game. It's a guided investigation compared to the original build where you'd use your resources against a smart AI. There have been signs of the AI improving, but it is still unknown if the neural network idea has been scrapped or not. The DLCs are short, buggy, not connected to the main game, and don't have a checkpoint system. Save $20 and buy your normal edition.Overall, if you somehow forget any hype leading up to this game, it's fun and has a good story. Maybe wait to see if the developers update the game and then make your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's my personal opinion, and possibly hot take on Hello Neighbor 2. As someone who was gifted the deluxe edition and got early access, I loved the game, I loved what they were going for. It was honestly far more fun than the first game, where instead of just Mr. Peterson's house, it was the whole town of Raven Brooks to explore. But it's a shame just how unpolished and broken the game is, especially the Back to School and Late Fees DLCs, (Late Fees has no ending), and it's sad to see The Guest be given the Vanny treatment, advertised as this next big villain, only to have little to no screen time. I was able to catch on roughly on the lore for this game, and I was blown away to find out exactly what dark secret the rest of the towns folk are hiding, and makes me want to know more. While most are dissatisfied with the cliffhanger, I don't have really an issue with it. I do know they plan to expand the game with more updates in the future, so I'm hoping this will allow them to also fix some of the most crucial of bugs and issues already in the game. While it wasn't the best game ever played, I still enjoyed it for what it was going for.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was good! It had significantly better gameplay than the original, but the story wasn't as compelling. In true Hello Neighbor fashion, the puzzles were incredibly complicated and very satisfying to figure out. The open world and art direction were also big improvements compared to the original. I also loved the soundtrack.The only area where I think this game lacks is in its plot. The original game was full of subtlety, and in the end it delivered a very compelling story about fear and trauma. This game goes for a simpler narrative. It's fine, but it doesn't have quite as much personal impact on me as the original.Overall, I recommend this. The gameplay was great and the story was decent.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Neighbor 2 is a stealth horror game where you’re being stalked by a mysterious creature as you try to track down Mr. Peterson (The Neighbor) who has disappeared after the events of the first game. Play against an advanced, self-learning AI that tracks and adapts to your every move. Raven Brooks is an ordinary suburb, yet oddly filled with too many ravens. Mysterious events are happening in the city, often resembling a Tim Burton-style nightmare. You play as a private investigator tracking down Mr. Peterson. You break into his abandoned house searching for clues, only to find a bizarre, bird-like looking creature inhabiting it. From there, you explore Raven Brooks in an open world, survival horror-style fashion while staying true to the roots of the original stealth horror theme.

name: GetsuFumaDen: Undying Moon
detailed_description: GetsuFumaDen: Undying Moon combines intense roguelike hack-and-slash action with a stunning dark fantasy world, brought to life through the stroke of traditional Japanese art. As the chosen leader and guardian of the land of the living, wield the otherworldy arsenal and powers of the Getsu clan as you overcome multiple 'Death' and descend deeper into the depths of Hell to eradicate the source of the cataclysm. Distinct Ukiyo-e Inspired Visuals Inspired by the Japanese ukiyo-e art style, the world of GetsuFumaDen is as beautiful as it is deadly. Vibrant, dynamic 2D animations bring the artistic world to life. Brutal, Larger than Life Boss Battles A reanimated demon lord, a colossal centipede, and a five-headed hydra are only some of the myriad massive and fearsome monsters and yokai standing in your way. Defend yourself against their relentless onslaught and emerge victorious to descend deeper into the depths of Hell. Dynamic, Weapon-Based Combat. Master the rythmn of intense sword fighting action: pacing and timings of movements are inspired by Japanese martial arts. Utilize the unique special moves of a wide range of weapon types including katanas, battle umbrellas and spears to outsmart your enemies. Authentic Roguelike Action While death is not the end, the world of Hell lives and breathes, presenting new map layouts and challenges to overcome with each attempt. Permanent upgrades, customizable weapons, and variable level progression provide new opportunities and challenges for every run. Immersive Weapon Enhancement System The crafting process gives you complete control over the ability to collect, enhance and unlock abilities of main and sub weapons. Unlock enhancements to your favorite weapons at each run, and get back in the action! Soul Devour Power-Up System Collect souls during each descent to power up in real time. Utilize the unique power-up system to dynamically and strategically select enhancements. The Digital Deluxe Edition includes the following bonus contents. ・Bonus game - 1987 FC version 'GetsuFumaDen': discover the original game with an added English Menu (in-game text in Japanese only), the original Japanese guidebook and Quick Save features ・Digital Artbook: browse through 29 pages packed with key art, stage art, character designs and lore from the original world of GetsuFumaDen ・Mini-OST: listen to 15 tracks from the game's stunning atmospheric soundtrack

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad rogue-lite overall,  as far as the combat goes I don't have any issues with it, but you might find the progression to be slower and less intuitive than similar games. The game is clearly 'inspired' by Dead Cells, and for the most part, it works exactly as you would expect. If you die you don't keep the resources, but there are several ways to mitigate it. You can use the portal after the boss to end the run, and that way you keep everything, or you can use a 'return' in the menu to keep a small percentage. It's not that the game works differently from other rogue-lites, I just had a hard time figuring out where everything was - once you complete at least one run it's not so frustrating. Even though the game is not unfair in my opinion, it takes a little practice to memorize all of the enemies because some of them are kinda cheap with the visuals, especially on stage 3 where the foreground obscures your vision, not to mention that you can get hit by projectiles through the walls. I would say on average the run takes about 50 to 60 minutes, but it could take a few hours of grinding to have a fair chance. After you beat the game once, you can replay it on the higher difficulty that changes some basic stats, in addition to unlocking new levels that you can select after the boss fights.The only big problem for me is just the lack of randomized events for the stages, there is almost nothing that would even qualify to be that. Normally in this genre, you will get some kind of events that would let you wager your resources to get some random item or a bonus, but here you get 2 stores that sell the same resources and weapons that you might find from enemies - so essentially it has no variety aside from just changing the layout and having those stage forks with the portals. The only real variety comes from the weapons that you find because they all have a different gimmick to them, in addition to rolling various status effects. Most of the weapons have a basic combo and a special skill like a parry, you will find that game is balanced around choosing between high DPS and stagger potential. Interestingly, you can even stun the bosses which is not the same animation that you get when you kill certain parts, it seems to have a separate stun system if you deal enough damage with a certain weapon.For me, the highlights of the experience were the boss fights, and not just because they looked cool, mechanically I like the way the character can interact with certain attacks. Another small compliment that I will give to the game is in regards to the mid-air gameplay, I think it's helpful that you can roll in the air which combines with the double jump, and you can spam attacks to slow your fall which is extremely useful. Not sure how I feel about the soundtrack overall, it's very traditional, but I really enjoyed the song on the snow level, and most of the boss fights had good music as well.(+)  -  I don't have any issues with the movement personally, you can double-jump and even roll in the air which makes the character very agile, in addition to spamming in mid-air to avoid attacks below. While the combat is not very complicated, the stagger system adds a nice touch to the experience, making you feel pretty badass when the giant boss falls to the ground. Most of the boss fights were very interesting and had some nuances to them. (+)  - for a rogue-lite it's not too short, and you can unlock additional levels with new boss fights for the next run. You can replay on a higher difficulty and unlock various weapons and upgrades. That said, it could really use some randomized events to make the stages more replayable. Many achivos too. (?)  - here is a problem, I want to give it a compliment for the aesthetic, but it's not very consistent. Boss fights look great, some levels look interesting, but not all of them were enjoyable (**** that sky level, vision-obscuring nonsense). I guess I'll just say that I was sold on the art style.(+)  - sadly it's not in English, but we'll take it anyway.  - I would like to see some random events on every stage that would allow you to wager some resource or weapon in a hope of getting another. It would also be nice to have some mutating upgrades like pick one of the 3 that are not weapon-related, something like triple jump or extra projectiles with every sub use, it's a rogue-lite, possibilities are endless. Hell, let the player fight the shopkeeper to avoid buying items, like a miniboss.  - I could nitpick the upgrades all day here, but I will focus on one suggestion. There is a gold store on stage 2 that a new player can't use because you can't collect 30K without a gold boost from the upgrade. Reduce it to 15.000 for that stage, but also reduce the number of resources in it from 10 to 5, that way a new player can use the store, and the old player can use the store on stage 4 anyway. I think the 10% death passive should be on by default, and that upgrade should start at 15% - it will smooth out the frustration for new players. - in general, this game has a bit of a problem with the visuals getting in a way, especially on stage 3 where one enemy also makes purple clouds. The air and water elementals always get me because they are really good at blending in, you probably don't need the clouds in the foreground. The projectile from the green bug also looks a bit like a green orb when it breaks. You can also make the projectiles from the witches more prominent when they fly through the walls. - this is just my opinion, but I think the main+ and subweapon+ are just not worth it in comparison to the health boost and extra potion, I tried using them many times, they are almost negligible unless you doing a speedrun or something. Maybe they could start higher and have sharp diminishing returns like the health. Hard to say where the sweet spot is, I think it could be safely boosted by 1/4 of what it is right now. - I would like a little sheet that shows what you kept after the run in case of 'return' or death passive. You could even do it for a portal even though it's 100%, for clarity. There should be a damage number under the weapon in the bot left, in case I have 2 weapons of the same type.Decent gameplay, but everything else feels a bit lacking as far as RNG goes. I think it's a game that will be more frustrating for the first 5 hours or so, but it gets more enjoyable once you know exactly what is going on. There are definitely much better rogue-lites out there that cost less, that said, with a little work, it could be okay. The replay value depends on how much you like unlocking generic stat upgrades. The boss fights were great though.

_childDocuments_.review: Excavated from the depths of the classics, this franchise once again gives us a great introduction to 'Getsu Fuuma Den'Looking at the original game from 1987, I would have had no idea then that what we get to see in 'GetsuFumaDen: Undying Moon' was the vision of the game's development team since 35 years ago!Despite a link in the story to the game's predecessor, we have to admit that there is an amazing evolving result that provides breathtaking gameplay experiences!You can watch gameplay from the original game from 1987 here: GetsuFumaDen: Undying Moon is interesting for several reasons, but first I would like to refer to the beautiful Ukiyo art of the Japanese underworld, a fascinating art style to observe that graces the sessions through, for example, animated backgrounds, as well as the rest of the environments.Although the gameplay can easily become fast paced, I also advise you to stop regularly to appreciate this visual part,but not only the graphic elements keep you glued to the screen, also the audio part.The soundtrack, which is available along with the 1987 classic when you buy the deluxe package, consists of 15 ear-hypnotic tracks that absolutely provide 'that' appropriate atmosphere.Watch my first gameplay here: In this roguelite you will die more often than you hope, there is no automatic or other smoother healing process but instead you have to make do with a limited supply of potions, but don't worry, after a few sessions you will already learn how to use these potions must ratify,there are also different weapons and weapon genres, from swords, spears, to even a combat-ready umbrella, each with their own improvements, you are never obliged to use the same weapons over and over, you will often get opportunities to switch weapons and such use the perfect weapon that suits you best.You will also be able to return to the beginning without dying so that you can store your goods, the advantage is that if you die later than you can start with good weapons or possibly extra potions, the disadvantage is that you I have to give up these items first and then start over in the world again, or whether the choice to return to the beginning is really that beneficial I have a little doubt about that.It's also possible to get items after you die through certain upgrades, but you don't get them that quickly either.The game also plays fantastic on the steam deck: You will have to defeat a number of bosses throughout Yomi's world, but the world is so much bigger than the routes you could take directly to the locations to reach these bosses,the best way to fight these bosses is to observe the attacks first and adjust your attacks accordingly, believe me, this will be necessary as it can take some time to get back to the point where you last died, so commit the fights with these bosses with patience.The game also has perfect support for ultra-wide resolutions, you can watch a gameplay at 3840*1080 _childDocuments_.review: When I heard konami was making a sequel to getsufumaden on the famicom I was in disbelieve. Konami? Making an actual game? A sequel to one of their most obscure games? And it looks great? So even tho I had no trust in konami at all I was intrigued enough to give them a chance and......it payed of! kinda... it's a really solid game at it's core and it is gorgeous. For a rogue-like I prefer a bit more crazieness than this has to offer more weird weapons and effect combos but it is okay as it is and hey theres obviously more to come.I feel it's slightly overpriced (but only in comparison to indie titles  that offer way  more) although not unreasonably so.What really makes this bad is that they decided to make this always online (without any multiplayer functionality) for no apparent reason other than drm. Gorgeous art style, exceptional enemy and world design, good soundtrack, competent gameplay - I think konami is on to something here it makes me dare to hope for the future of their beloved franchises. going early access was a good call. Just let me play the game without internet!UPDATE: So they jumped from 0.4 to 1.0 without really adding anything. In fact the core game clearly isn't finished and even if they release it later on for free thats not a state of completion I would call 1.0. You also still need internet to play. _childDocuments_.review: Refunded after hearing about the always-online requirement. I don't care what their excuse is. A singleplayer-only game shouldn't require a constant connection to some distant server for no apparent reason. Best part is, this is NOT mentioned on the game's Steam page. Due to my principles, I can't recommend this game in good conscience.Apart from the ridiculous always-online requirement, the game feels like a standard roguelite with floaty controls and dated graphics. It's mediocre, but it was fun from time to time. One of the things that stung was how you retain NONE of your resources until you start upgrading a passive that lets you do that. Instead of this, they could have just reduced the drop rate of everything (everything drops like candy) and let you keep everything. It's a bit of a waste of time. At least you can return mid-run when you reach certain places to keep everything, so it's not as bad as I made it sound.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game but for the love of god the progression system needs some serious revamping. The risk/reward really isn't worth continuing runs after the first few levels in the early game because you lose all your items if you die and every unlock takes way too many materials. Until you unlock the ability to carry over items after death (which in itself is two abilities that you need to get from a random drop) you're going to spend a lot of time repeating the first couple of levels over and over just to make any progress. Do I recommend this game? Sort of. People who are a fan of this genre of game I think will like it a lot. It's beautiful, the weapons are all unique, and each run can feel pretty different depending on your set up. For a casual player of this kind of game I absolutely wouldn't recommend it too. It's overly grindy even for a game that's all about grinding and when you finally do get to the point of completing runs it's pretty short. Here's hoping as the game goes on they overhaul progression and add more levels.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, you were impressed by how stylistic this game is, and that holds true! This game is absolutely beautiful to look at. Every single moment of this game is like looking at an art piece.Playing is a different story. You'll find quickly that there are very few ways to play that get you far. The easiest being to stick with normal swords that strike fast, have decent damage and range. Then, you poke enemies through floors until they die. The game becomes a lot of that as you get your sword really strong, rinse and repeat.The reason I bring this up is that the combat is the roughest part of this game and it's the main focal point as well. It's intentionally sluggish to create difficulty, which is fine. But it's so intentionally sluggish that you find there's not many diverse options for you that allow you to actually kill any enemies. Slow swinging strong weapons are so slow you have to cancel your attacks to dodge most of the time. Plus, swords work just fine. You can kill with like 2-3 hits with a sword before the enemy gets an attack out anyway.Progression is rough too. You are going to have to die quite a bit to then build up residual funds to stand a chance. That's not uncommon in games. But the clear jump between that feeling of "I need to die more" and "I'm prepared" is jarring. I think it'd be preferable to slowly feel like you're getting stronger.After you fully beat the game once, there really isn't much in terms of replayability unless you are a completionist. You can make weapons stronger, you can unlock some new ones, but not too much more than that.Overall I had fun with trying to learn the game but after 10 hours, I'm not dying at all to go back to it. I also would not recommend picking it up at full price. If this game is on sale for 50% off, watch a YouTube video of the combat and see if you like it
_childDocuments_.name: GetsuFumaDen: Undying Moon

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, Konami and the development team take a good amunt of risk with this game. A sequel to an old japanese only famicom game that few remember outside that country? Sounds like a mad move! But.. they indeed make a cool revival... but something must change to better fit with the original Getsu Fuma Den... or at least take a good aim at his target audience.I will explain what I mean...Getsu Fuma Den: Undying Moon is, basically, a side scroller platform action with A LOT of elements from rouge-like games (and i notice some Darks Souls vibe too... I HATE TO SAID IT, but I can't put aside my fear that this game would be another DS clone.. only 2D). The game itself is really fun to play, feel a little rigid for the platforming aspect but I know it can be fixed with patch and whatnot. The thing that I don't like, though, are said rouge-like elements. It make the game less enjoyable to me. Its should be more focus on arcade side scrolling like the original or at least make possible to come back to the Getsu Clan hideout more easly so you dont loose all your stuff when dieing... and in this game you die A LOT!Personally, I'm okey with the full vision Konami and the team at GuruGuru embrace for this game and make the experience both deep and fresh, but this direction is not for everyone and will confuse and discurage fan of the original for sure. So to me, the gameplay need a lot of feedback to better understand the target this game is aiming for.Thats it, thats all i have to sai about the gameplay (the major concern point for me). Let's talk about everything eals... ITS AWSOME!! Music, graphic, art style. Everything really shine and give the game a unique feel... it really seems like a moving painting! (at least for me). I'm digging the art style and it should never change with subsequent update. It's perfect! :DThe option said "voice" but in game, there are any... i guess because its early access so its kind of normal.I raccomand it? Why yes. I mean, if you like the genre than the game its really cool and you will have fun no doubt, but for me... I will wait until Early Access is over... hoping that my suggestion will reach the developers. For now, give this game (and Konami) some love, it deserved it.

_childDocuments_.review: They rushed to 1.0 after a relatively short early access phase. Very few things were added during the time and a lot of promises were broken. The gameplay loop is also just lacking overall: enemies are more annoying than challenging, the grind for meta-currency is insanely long and incentivizes farming the early zones without making real progress. To try to make progress quickly in runs, you're forced to upgrade only 1 weapon at a time and discourages experimentation. The second character they added feels too similar and doesn't add any replayability really. I felt like I got baited into the game with the amazing music, art and first boss showcase (the subsequent bosses are much more lackluster in comparison). Game is all style, no substance. Seems like they gave up when sales weren't high enough during early access so they just released something mediocre.

_childDocuments_.review: I prefer the combat of this game to Dead Cells. One of my problems with Dead Cells is how quick the game is. I like the slower pace that GetsuFuma has with less enemies but slightly longer fights. There are also a lot of interesting mechanics taken from games like the soul series, specifically bloodborne visceral attacks. All enemies have a break point where when you break them, you can do a Slay Attack (visceral attack from bloodborne). Unfortunately, the combat and the visuals/art of the game are the only good things about it. EDIT: I am updating my review. As of 28 hours total in the game, I have all blueprints unlocked for weapons, sub-weapons, and talents. I also completed the game on the hardest difficulty. I have to still give the game a negative review. If steam allowed neutral reviews I would give this a neutral instead. Here is an updated list of problems and an explanation of new problems or problems that have been fixed/were an oversight by me. Thanks to steam review word limitations, I am unable to list pros, but if you're interested in what I liked about the game, feel free to comment in my review and I can provide a list. I will not be updating this review anymore until more significant changes are done or until the game is released.Another thing to note, the developers have addressed some issues that many players were having on updates. Potions are now received always from lore-texts (one per-stage), Hitboxes on demon enemies are adjusted, and the visual effects from blood are reduced to make it easier to see the playable character. This was done 5 days (May 18th, patch on May 21st) after the games release. This is promising to see active changes so quickly.Cons:These are my main problems with the game. I'm writing this review because I took a look at the GetsuFuma roadmap, and the next big update is releasing a new playable character. I feel the developers need to focus on the core systems they have in place of the game before delving on optional things like "more playable characters". There is a good game here, but unfortunately it's missing the mark on a lot of things. To put it to perspective, Dead Cells was released in early access at $17 and even at that point in time, the game had more polish on weapon variety, NPCs, and progression. I'm still interested in the game and what Konami has to bring to the table here. The game looks amazing, and I think the bosses are very well done on their difficulty, visual representation, and elements in the fight. I'll be keeping my eye on updates and would love to someday change this negative review into a positive one.

_childDocuments_.review: presents an ambitious attempt to revive a classic game, but it falls short in several key aspects. While it boasts stunning visuals and a captivating art style that pays homage to its predecessor, the game struggles to maintain the same level of excitement and engagement throughout.One of the major drawbacks is the lack of responsiveness in controls. Certain actions and movements can feel clunky or unresponsive, resulting in frustrating moments during combat or platforming sections. This detracts from the overall fluidity and enjoyment of the gameplay.Furthermore, despite the beautiful aesthetics, the game suffers from limited variety. The levels, enemies, and items can feel repetitive after multiple playthroughs, diminishing the sense of excitement and exploration. The sparse narrative also fails to create a compelling story to drive the player's motivation, leaving a void in terms of emotional investment.The other issue is the same graphics, because when the animations of the enemies are mixed up, it's hard to know what's going on. And this can become the road to the starting location.While Getsufumaden: Undying Moon attempted to incorporate roguelite elements with procedural generation, the execution falls somewhat flat. The replay value starts to wane after a few playthroughs, as the procedural generation fails to provide sufficient variety and freshness to keep players engaged in the long run.In the end, I leave a positive review, because the game is able to give many tens of hours of good mood, with a challenge and a test of your skill. P. S. If you want to unlock Kunoichi, you must defeat her between mission 2 or 3 by playing on Commoner or higher.

_childDocuments_.review: What a niche game. It hits such a sweet spot for me! Dead Cells is one of my favorite games of all time. I have 80+ hours into it on Switch, and repurchased it for Steam Deck. I’m also an huge Ukiyo-e (Japanese woodblock artwork) enthusiast. So when I saw GetsuFumaDen, I felt like someone must have created this game just for me. :) However, I was concerned about the tepid reviews. I’m so glad I gave it a shot. The look of the game is absolutely stunning, if you’re even the slightest bit into Ukiyo-e. The gameplay is reminiscent of Dead Cells, so if you like that and want more, GetsuFumaDen is a worthy take on the genre. While combat may not be quite as smooth (just a hair less responsive, maybe?), I can easily overlook this, given the unique mechanics and what appears to be a deep network of synergies. (I’m only an hour and a half in, and admittedly don’t understand all of the mechanics quite yet, though that speaks to some complexity, which excites me. That said, my only critique so far is that the game could perhaps do a better job of explaining things. Despite tutorial pages that do pop-up, it’s maybe a tad confusing all at once. Though, there are some decent guides on Reddit.) The combat and exploration is quite satisfying though, and feels well-polished. The lore is a lot of fun to peruse as you collect it within the Hall of Treasures. I’m incredibly impressed with GetsuFumaDen, as someone who came into it with unreasonably high expectations. The quality of the art direction—rooted in Japanese mythology—is really the highlight for me, and the Dead Cells style gameplay is well-executed. Side notes: I’m playing on Steam Deck and it’s almost flawless. I’ve had a couple of momentary screen-freezes, however I’m playing on the highest quality graphics settings. Also, I saw a lot of people saying that the game doesn’t boot up due to some glitch with accepting the Terms of Service. This wasn’t a problem for me. The Terms took a little while to load in (I ultimately hit a white screen after a minute or so?), but I simply backed out of that screen, was then given the option to accept the terms, and proceeded into the game without any issue.

_childDocuments_.review: OG Getsu is a great game, never thought we'd get a sequel let alone one THIS good. Pulls off the addictive "roguevania" style perfectly, has beautiful graphics and fantastic audio. Plenty of weapons to play around with, tons of depth with choosing what to grab on each run. Difficulty is great, rewarding both enemy/boss memorization and upgrading. Only minor complaint is upgrading items takes ages but the newest update seems to have fixed that.Enjoyed the original Getsu? Get this. Enjoy Rogelites? Get this. Enjoy Metroidvanias? Get this. Enjoy great games? GET. THIS.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't know how to start with this review. I go through my backlog to finally play what I have there, start a random game and get absolutely stunned by the presentation, go through the artbook and marvel at what's there... just to have my initial impressions shattered after playing for a few hours and cursing Konami louder than I have ever done in my life for what they have done to what could have possibly been one of the best rogue-lites of recent years.Before I begin, I have to mention that GetsuFumaDen: Undying Moon is a single player rogue-lite game, but still requires an internet connection in order to run. Please be mindful of this before purchasing the game.If there's one thing that the game does extremely well and puts it in front of everyone to see, it's the visual style. In a time when nearly anyone who makes a rogue-lite goes for common pixel art designs or normal 3D models, the madmen at GuruGuru took the capabilities of Unreal Engine 4 and created a 3D game with an incredible art direction. The developers have nailed the artstyle for GetsuFumaDen's revival, making the whole game look like an old Japanese painting that has come to life, with all of the enemy designs and depictions being directly based on them. One look into the game's artbook reveals how much care was put into designing the visual aesthetics of this game and I honestly cannot praise the devs enough in this regard.But unfortunately, I cannot say the exact same thing about the music. While the music tracks are done really well, some of them make you think maybe there wasn't any clear direction as to what should be done with them. Sometimes you hear traditional-inspired music, sometimes you just hear glorified ambience, sometimes you hear the composer going wild with electric guitars, and sometimes you hear abominable mixes of multiple genres. For example, the first boss' theme (Unfettered Chaos) goes too hard for a first boss, and the rival boss fight (Onwards! GetsuFuma) has this jarring transition from traditional to dubstep, then retro and then going back. And this lack of consistency feels jarring.I'm gonna say it: This game needed more time in the oven. It has everything it needs to be a great rogue-lite, but needed more development time to iron them out.If I wanted to explain the gameplay of Undying Moon in brief, I would say it's basically Dead Cells mixed with a little bit of Dark Souls. If you have played Dead Cells before, you already know the basics of Undying Moon's gameplay. The only difference is that Undying Moon asks you to engage with enemies in a safe manner by observing their attacks, baiting them and punishing accordingly instead of being fast and efficient. It also gives you bonuses that increase your damage output upon doing certain actions like clashing attacks with the enemy or surprising them to encourage this playstyle. This should already be a recipe for greatness, but the game fumbles this potential because of its gameplay loop.The game works like this: You go through a level and upon getting to the end of it, you are teleported to the boss arena. If you manage to kill the boss, you will be given the choice of going back to the main hub (Getsu Estate) or continuing to the next level. If you go back, you will keep all of the resources you have collected. But if you choose to continue and die before killing the next boss, you will lose everything; unless you have unlocked some skills beforehand that let you keep a percentage of the resources after death.This can make the game absolutely repetitive to go through, because the numerous resources you need for upgrades drop randomly, and their amounts are extremely low in early levels. The grind is absolutely real in this game and if you never find out how to get past the first two bosses, you will be stuck in this repetitive loop of beating first level, beating first boss, going back to the estate and repeating everything from the beginning. And even if you look past the repetitive gameplay loop and try to power through, there's not much in the game. Aside from one unlockable character, there's nothing else to find and whole game consists of you doing everything over and over again, with nothing to break the flow or add some actual value to your incomplete runs.And there are a bunch more issues that can suck the fun out of the game and make it appear very dull. These include additional levels being locked behind random key drops, frequent leaps of faith in some of the levels and the camera system being unable to show if you land safely or not, level layouts becoming repetitive after the first two hours, enemies being placed in locations where it's incredibly hard to fight them, or some enemies detecting you from far offscreen and attacking you through the environment. Even the unlockable character which could have added some variety to the gameplay ends up being lackluster as each character in the game has a separate skill tree, further increasing the need to grind.Whatever I mentioned so far are all issues that could have been ironed out with a little bit of dev time and feedback. Because it is apparent that the devs clearly had passion while developing this game and couldn't possibly have done this on purpose. So why no such thing has happened?You know what's worse than the game's potential not being realized? A publisher that kills the game prematurely. There were a lot of stuff planned for the game. The devs could have improved the game significantly and made a rogue-lite classic. But unfortunately, the publisher of this game was Konami.Two additional playable characters, a whole bunch of enemies, multiple bosses, a number of weapons and a few maps are already in the game in an incomplete state. The devs even had a roadmap to add these stuff properly. But what happened? Version 1.0's release was rushed and all of future updates were cancelled, resulting in a game that was panned by the critics for feeling incomplete. And since Konami has already done a Limited Run Games release, this means the game is considered finished by them.So, to sum everything up, Konami digs up a Japan-exclusive franchise that was dormant for 35 years, allows a developer to create a new game in the said franchise and release it in early access to fine-tune it over time, the developer goes all-out in the visual presentation department and creates an incredible looking game with vast gameplay potential, Konami does ♥♥♥♥-all when it comes to marketing the game and makes a shocked Pikachu face when it doesn't sell like hot cakes, and then the development process is finished pre-emptively because the game is not a financial success. Literally everyone who has played this game knows that it has immense amounts of potential. You have a game that has an incredible, and dare I say one of a kind visual presentation, and THIS is how you treat it? You have the perfect ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ recipe to make "Dead Cells but in Japan" and you do THIS to it? Only an utterly incompetent company such as Konami can do that. Great job guys. Keep on screwing up. Go make Metal Gear Survive 2: Electric Boogaloo while you're at it.Another victim of Konami's utter incompetence. It is visually stunning, looking like a Japanese painting that has come alive, but the rest of it clearly feels unfinished, unpolished and rushed.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly visually stimulating game with wonderful character design and excellent style that really comes together for a presumably lower budget game. Being based on an obscure but excellent game that deserves more love is a bit of a boon, too.However, the gameplay is completely half-baked. So many things in the game are highly inconsistent and it takes away from what is almost a fairly tight, decent run-based experience. The progression is incredibly poor, mostly giving you number increases to make it a little easier next time with very, very little variance in runs outside of choosing a different level path.Could potentially be fixed with some tweaks and patches to make the game's behavior feel more consistent and to make progression more rewarding, but in its current state at time of writing, I really can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: So, my first thought about this game was: "Hold up, Konami's making games again?!"Second thought was: "....and it's a niche title and NOT a more recognised name."Third thought was: ".... and sh!t, it's quite good! Even for early access! You guys OK down there at Konami HQ? Just that you're acting like...... well NOT Konami."  all seriousness though, taking the rogue-like approach to a metroidvania title is an interesting spin, and fundamentally, it works well. Gameplay leans heavily towards being more tactical and methodical than it does being stylish and fast. And since you have limited ways of healing, you're forced to consider how best to dispatch your enemies while taking as few hits as possible. It's not quite dark souls, just enough to keep you thinking. The most 'style', goes into the visual direction of the game. They've gone all in on the shinto folklore theme. And with the cell shading, the game literally looks like a Yakuza tattoo come to life. And I think that's awesome!Considering this is still 'early' access, one should consider my critiques to be suggestions here.....It doesn't feel like there's much of a story going on here. A pit to hell has opened up, Fuma, or Renge has to go and seal it, and also Fuma's brother is missing. Since there's no spoken dialogue, characters have the same charisma as cardboard. This doesn't need to be the case: Hades has proven that you can have an engaging story with your roguelike. Give us a reason to care about these people. The difficulty spike is...... weird. Bosses are actually the easiest things to beat in the game. They telegraph their attacks hard, and it becomes embarrassingly easy to stomp them without taking hits. At least until you encounter the 5th boss. Then, you MIGHT win..... if all your gear is platinum rank 6 at a minimum, and even then you're not walking out of there with any healing scrolls. There's really no difference between Fuma and Renge. Fuma is slower, but has higher health. Renge is faster, but has less health. There might be a difference in attack power, but the moment your gear is silver or above at a certain rank, you're one shotting most enemies, so you won't even notice the difference. So you pick Renge, because if you're anything like me, you're a man of culture. While it's great that we have a wide choice of melee and ranged weapons, I would have preferred certain weapons to be exclusive to either Fuma or Renge, while perhaps having a few more techniques with said weapons. As it is now, they're just character skins. That being said, it's a very tidy package overall, with plenty of replayability, so it gets a recommendation.
