_childDocuments_.review: It feels stupid to be critical of an early access game but I would not buy this in its current state. All I would say it the bones are good and it has a ton of potential to be a great game but its just not even close to ready to play by a wide audience. Core systems don't work or are punishingly unrewarding. Keep it on your watchlist but buy it when it's in a better state.To clarify my statement about core systems not working or being punishing:Demonize- does not work on slow hitting weapons- they have a tutorial for you to demonize with a sword but it doesnt hit fast enough to actually demonize lol. Beyond that of the weapons that you can Demonize with, it gives VERY LITTLE benefit. Your sub weapons hit harder and you run faster. Theres no dmg reduction if you are hit, or 1 free hit, or special move, or really anything to make this WORTH chasing.Break/Slay- similar problem to demonize, even weapons with high break tend to kill everything too fast to break/slay(except bosses). This mechanic seems impossible to balance and personally needs a rework of some kind. Its not fun if you can break everything, its likewise not fun if you can break nothing. There should be more clear conditions to cause a break, Ideally that changes based on which weapon you're using.Parry - Katana lets you parry and counterattack! sadly, counterattack does similar to a regular hit in damage except you have to put yourself in harms way with small windows to use it. Its a wasted mechanic, make counterattack guarantee a break or do triple the dmg. getting hit is WAY too punishing for this to be worthwhile.Flash - similar problem with parry, timing window for it is tiny and you should almost always just be dodging(attacking during an enemies attack stuns them and gives you a crit, but again - getting hit is WAY too punishing for this to be worthwhile)Progression - in general, way too costly for tiny upgrades that are also boring. basically everything is flat or % dmg increases, or worse yet, % dmg increases only on certain swings of your weapon.  Crafting a new weapon takes a STUPID amount of currency, and there is no way to target farm if you want to stick to a certain weapon type. Upgrading permanent stats/skills for your character seem relatively in line but everything costing the same is kinda a joke. 5,000 gold per run is equivalent in cost to +1 potion? are ya kidding?IDK, whatever, its early access. If you've got money burning a hole in your pocket do whatever you want. It will probably be a good game upon full release. It's not good at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm generally not a fan of roguelike games (dead cells, hades, etc) but this game won me over. It took a while for me to understand the games mechanics, but once I understood what this game was trying to do I fell in love. The game has decent variety in terms of its levels and their aesthetics. During one level you are barred from the exit until you complete a specific task which was really cool. The weapons are all interesting to play around with, but I find myself returning back to the katana because of its counter ability which kind of sucks considering this game has like 6 weapon classes or something. The enemies are pretty cool as well, but I wish the level design forced you to interface with them in different ways more often. There was only one level where I could make use of the arc offered by bombs to eradicate enemies that were tucked away on the other side of walls. Usually, you are just engaging with them in a straight line which can get boring if you are just mashing the regular attack button.Bosses are decent in that they have enough variety in their moves and patterns. On the normal difficulty they haven't posed much of a challenge. I haven't beaten the game yet, so hopefully they get even crazier. Overall, it's fun to play, but I wish the game forced you into unique encounters using level assets and enemy groupings more often. It's definitely a game I keep coming back to for "one more run." Nice / 10

_childDocuments_.review: Like Returnal but with saves mid-run.Like a lot of people my only previous contact with this series was Castlevania: HD, but stumbling across this game I was still curious enough to give it a go. And it's actually pretty good. It runs well and not had any technical issues with it. Controls are pretty sharp and responsive. The visuals are great, drawing inspiration from Japanese art. My only real complaint on that front is the effects are a bit out of control, as soon as you hit something it's utterly obscured in cloud of blood and rainbow explosions making it very hard to read attacks.The gameplay is a the now familiar rogue like of random equipment drops as you explore levels each ending with a boss. Difficulty is a bit uneven, some bosses once you learn attacks they are all easily avoidable, others dodging attacks is really fussy. Some of the hits landing seem pretty sketchy, hopefully that'll be ironed out. The systems aren't really well explained and a bit obscure.Overall risk/reward balance is a bit wonky, and there are a lot of systems and mechanics which are pretty counter intuitive and not really explained. But really I'm nitpicking, the basic loop of go out do some levels, kill some bosses, get some upgrades, do some more is fun. There's a lot of room for early access to improve but it's a functional and enjoyable game.So while it may be hard to believe Konami really did just release an actual game, and it's pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: The extent of my Getsu Fuma experience was the DLC in Harmony of Despair and I loved playing as him then but living in the states I wasn't privy to the original release back in the day. So when I saw this announcement I was pretty stoked, coupled with my love for the Roguelike/Metroidvania genres. I haven't finished the game yet so take some of the cons with a grain. Pros:-Lots of versatility and variety between the main/sub weapon types.-Multiple status ailments adding significant depth to the gameplay. -The original Famicom game comes with. -A living, breathing woodblock print art style in the game that looks absolutely exquisite.-Autonomous soul-leveling system adding even more depth and replay value.-Skill trees exclusive to each weapon tailored to different playstyles.-Fantastic soundtrack with amazing variety from atmospheric kabuki-inspired tracks to intense power metal renditions of the original OST.Cons:-Concept of reincarnation after death to begin new runs feels contrived-Characters in the game seem lifeless-Too much filler in the cutscenes for a game's crux being repetition.Overall, I highly recommend this one!

_childDocuments_.review: At first I didn't know what to make of this game.  It's not like the original game which was more like Zelda II: the adventure of Link, but this game is different being that the levels are more randomly generated and you're looking for the boss's lair to get to the next level.  It's fun, but I'd recommend putting more of your points into the ordinary katana since that is guaranteed, and all of the other weapons you will just randomly come across.Also while it is nice that this game includes the original Getsu Fuma Den game from the Famicom, I kinda don't recommend the original Getsu Fuma Den game on Steam.  The problem is the game is still in Japanese regardless of the English option, and while it is nice that the game does not really require you knowing a lot of Japanese, I'd still prefer to play the game in English and there's already fan translated roms out there.  So just play the fan translated GFD rom instead

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this game for over 40 hours and I think this game has a lot of potential. It has stunning graphs, great music and a fairly good gameplay mechanics. Ever since the update was released, several things improved such as the pace of the game and the grinding system. However, there are still a coupe of things that need to be improved in order to make this game even better.1. Before the update, it was way difficult to make any progress since you died a lot and you lost everything you collected because the materials and resources needed were pretty high. I decided to start and new game and I consider that I had made a great deal of progress in 10 hours of gameplay ever since the update was released. However,  I consider that the materials and resources needed to upgrade your weapons and stats are still pretty high and sometimes you need to clear the four stages (before you reach the final stage) over and over again to make any significant progress which makes the experience somehow tedious.2. I understand the differences among the weapons are the stats. However, it would be nice if each weapon had a unique skill. Some games allow you to introduce an input and the weapon does a different animation. I think it would be nice if the devs do so, because the combat mechanics would be more interesting and you would have a lot of options from which you can choose from.3. For some reason, it has been more difficult to unlock skills because the drop rate is lower with the new update. Same goes for the Glaciar key, which I haven't been able to find ever since the update was released. 4. The addition of the new character is awesome. However, it would be nice if she had other type of animations from the main character and I wish she could share the same skills and weapons with the main character.5. It would be nice if the devs could add secret areas in the stages.All in all, this game has a lot of potential. I'm sure there are many other things that I haven't been able to identify, but in my perspective, these are the key issues the game must focus on in order to improve the gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: GetsuFumaDen: Undying Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Can confirm that it runs just fine on a potato.Also, bring back more games like this, Konami! Getting the original game, artbook, and soundtrack is a pretty sweet deal.Some notes after playing a few hours:As others have mentioned, the grinding needs a much better payoff. It truly is an IMMENSE amount of grinding for very little benefit. The weapons are poorly balanced as well. Unless you get lucky and pick something extra powerful up, there's no need to discard your katana -- at least in the beginning. Some people have complained that the controls are subpar to Dead Cells, but I disagree 100%. Both games have excellent controls, but GetsuFumaDen requires you to be a bit more decisive with your attacks, as once you commit to something it's usually not possible to use animation cancelling to avoid a mistake. I also think the spastic nature of Dead Cells would look really out of place with the artwork here.I'm not very good at this game, so I can't really comment on the later stages yet :|

_childDocuments_.review: I might be jumping the gun here, but wow, I just want to say that I'm happy that this game even happened, and for it to be actually good is another joy entirely. To think Konami would A) Make a sequel to GetsuFumaDen, and B) release it in the west is very unlike them. It seems like the team behind this doesn't have much of an online presence, which had me worried, but if this is what's they're pushing out, I think we're in good hands. I also think the Early Access approach was smart, and if done right will build a good connection with the community, which is also unheard of from Konami lol. Here's to hoping this game turns out to be something special, it'd be really nice to play a Konami game and not have to remember the good ol' days.

detailed_description: Aerial_Knight's Never Yield on Discord About the Game STORY Take the role of Wally. A mysterious character that has recovered what was taken from him. Hopefully, you're fast enough to outrun your enemies. Expose the truth and try to uncover the mystery of what happened to them. With an average runtime of an action movie (about an hour and a half on Normal), a first run of this action-packed adventure can be enjoyed in an afternoon. Afterwards you can improve your score. GAMEPLAY Aerial_Knight's Never Yield is a 3D side-scroller that plays much like a classic endless runner. The game has an interesting story that keeps players always in motion. Run, Jump, Slide or 'Dash' for acrobatic variants leading to dope combinations and avoid the challenges that await. Aerial_Knight's Never Yield is being built for players who love to speedrun games while being an experience that casual players will enjoy as well. SOUNDTRACK This Soundtrack for Aerial_Knight's Never Yield is being done by 'Danime-Sama' A Detroit artist with vocals from artists from all over the world. NOTE FROM THE DEV This project began as just a passion project I started on my own to create something familiar but new for this generation of gamers while highlighting aspects of a culture that is often overlooked. I really hope you enjoy the game once its released and follow my journey to create new and interesting games - Aerial_Knight

_childDocuments_.review: Look, the game is... If you really think you want to try it, go ahead and buy it for $12. I beat the entire game plus bonuses on the hardest difficulty in 1.4 hours, so there's time to refund if you don't like it. The director of the game clearly had a vision going into this, and you can see it shine through in some levels, but overall the game just feels vaguely unprofessional. There are so many things that you can nitpick during a playthrough that it feels like the game was made, checked for bugs, then shipped once all were gone. No polishing here, no making it seem more fair. Maybe I'm just biased because I played the game in the only difficulty that doesn't have automatic slowdown for every obstacle. In that case, if the game was designed to be played that way, then it's belittling. Every single jump is slowed for you, so you have a full three seconds of moving through honey until you have to press one button. Ok then, maybe the reason it's so easy is because it wants you to focus on the story. Nope, the story is trash. Can be summed up as "guy runs away from people while carrying satchel" you never really get a motive or anything. The flips and stuff you do are kinda cool, but how cool can a game make you feel when there are a total of four buttons to push? I don't really know what the devs were going fo here, and I'm even more confused if they achieved it.

_childDocuments_.review: is a short runner obstacle course game with set levels and a vague story told through small animated cut scenes without words. As runner games tend to be, this game is mostly in the side-scrolling nature from left to right, with a few exceptions. Combined with flashy cyberpunk style artwork/theme along with a nice soundtrack, this game is rather fun and memorable overall.The overall game is split into 13 levels, with 3 available difficulty modes. After running through the prologue that introduces to you the control scheme, played out in Easy mode, you can adjust the difficulty to your liking. The easier mode significantly slows down time before each obstacle and gives you warnings ahead of time, whereas the normal mode gives you a mild slowing, and the more difficult setting completely removes time-slowing and adds additional obstacles.Each level is set up to be progressively challenging, and there are no randomization as far as I can tell, having played a few levels multiple times on different difficulties. After a while, the levels go kind of crazy, starting with one where you are running from the bottom of the screen upwards instead of from left to right. Sporadically in the final few levels, you also also at random switching sides and instead going right to left.The controls are easy to understand, you either have WASD on the keyboard, or you can use the controller. Up lets you jump into the air, Down gives you a ducking slide, whereas Left triggers a mid-height jump that also can be destructive to windows, and Right results in a sprint, letting you go through some closed doors. There's not much to the controls, but no matter the orientation of the screen, those buttons stay the same.The individual levels are not very long, and there are checkpoints at various places throughout the levels, so even if the game is difficult, it is something you can improve your skills with playing more and getting used to the game. The entire game took me about 1.5 hours to complete on the easiest difficulty, and at moderate difficulty, it took me another 20 minutes to run through the final and most difficult level.Sometimes it can be difficult to see the obstacles, but after playing for a while, you begin to see the color on the screen that's coming at you instead of the actual obstacle. This makes it a lot more intuitive and reaction based. Otherwise, some objects in the foreground/background look blended and difficult to see what is truly the obstacle in question. Each obstacle you have to act on is brightly lit at the colors and color-coordinated as well as to which button you should press.After completing any part of the game, all of the previous levels become available to replay with your difficulty of choice. This gives the player a lot more flexibility in terms of deciding whether to replay specific levels.One thing I have to point out is that I really appreciate the more forgiving hitboxes and i-frames just when you think you missed a jump, but the game decides that it's okay to not penalize you with yet another death. After all, those come frequently enough anyway. Fortunately there's a single-button press continue that resumes from the previous checkpoint after you die, so it's very simple to just keep going.You will progressively unlock some different style outfits as you play. These are cosmetic skins and nothing else. After getting through the game once and some more levels more than once, I managed to unlock all but 2 of the outfits. I do not know what it takes to unlock those.Here's my very first foray into the game, so be prepared for lots of mistakes I may have been able to avoid after playing for an hour or so.Keyboard or controller, just directional controls for the individual respective actions associated with each.I really enjoy the flare of the colors and the visuals, the cyberpunk style is cool too.The music/OST is rather nice, the sound effects seem to be a lot of explosions and not a lot of other stuff.People who enjoy runners will probably have a great time, but the difficult options make it more accessible to casual players, up until the screen starts going in funky directions, and it becomes a mental/visual strain that's not always pleasant. The directional switching is really terrible in terms of the mental stress caused by interpretation of the directional flow on-screen versus what you might think you need to press to get the action you want.It's not too expensive, but at $11.99 US as a base price, it might be a bit too high. Because the game is rather short, after all. But the game is pretty fun, though I am perhaps biased due to my personal attraction to runner-style games. If it's too pricey for you, getting it on a sale would certainly be an option.1. No leaderboards for a time-attack arcade-style runner game, which is a shame.2. No infinite mode for people who may want to keep going in an infinity runner style. This would require going off the preset levels and using a system to randomly generate the next sets of obstacles. I am not sure how feasible this is, but could add to the draw of the game. This should just be an separate option aside from running the campaign.3. (fixed)4. Some visual settings to turning down some of that flare might be nice for some people who do not want too much flashiness on-screen.5. It would be great to give a single option toggle to reverse the left-right button presses after directional changes, or turning everything 90 degrees in that level when you are running upwards. In terms of mental strain this would have made it a lot easier for me. Being optional is nice. I connect this to the feel of playing brawler/fighting game where all of the directional controls automatically change depending on which side of the screen you are facing. is a runner-style obstacle-avoiding game in preset levels and can be rather fun for the right player. Definitely worth checking out if you are a fan of runner-style games.Score: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: One of those pleasant indie surprises you get totally out of the blue. It seems the developer has a background story with the game and its inception so I'm glad it was able to materialize into a release. At first I thought it was like the Jet Set Radio series but, nope, it's a music-driven runner game wearing a neon/retrofuturistic aesthetic up its sleeve. Employing a soundtrack that utilizes rap overtones, big band, jazz, vocals and other more atypical elements through the 13 levels you go through.Your goal? Keep on runnin' and lower that timer. You can unlock a few outfits and harder difficulty settings. In fact, I recommend if possible that you start straight on hard because Normal mode has an extreme slowdown that is meant to help dodge things much easily but, ironically, makes things harder and sluggish. Of course, the first time it's a very welcomed tool to avoid getting run over by the difficulty and reflexes needed to do the inputs. And that Bonus Level... Well, good luck there and you better account for input lag or the delay between moves or you're toast.Performance wise the game isn't too demanding, the menu design is sleek and stylish and it supports multiple language. A controller is also very recommended. With the price being right, having a great OST, offering the right amount of challenge and not demanding you so many hours, it's hard not to recommend it if you want a quick dose of a runner that will not destroy your mind or ask you inhuman feats.Definitely looking forward to a sequel or a game in a similar style/aesthetics.

_childDocuments_.review: Never Yield is a 2.5D auto runner, mainly gameplay involves avoiding obstacles by pressing one of 3 directions that match the type of obstacle in your way.The game's visuals are nice and simple, and it has a really nice and catchy soundtrack.The game has 3 difficulty levels that unlock by the 2nd stage or so, with the hardest removing slowdown before an obstacle, which can offer a challenge for those interested. Stages can be replayed in order to clear them as fast as possible without any mistakes offering some replayability.I really enjoyed this game and recommend it to anyone who is looking for a light gaming experience and/or have a game on the side to cool off from bigger games.

_childDocuments_.review: Aerial_Knight's Never Yield~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Aerial is a brand-new 3D auto-runner, indie-platformer that features a colorful world in a sci-fi setting. Here you get to take on the role of the silent protagonist Wally, who is running as fast as possible to outrun those who are trying to catch up with him.During the game, you will get to experience a stylish none-combative platformer that goes through very linear gameplay with the character having quite a few awesome semi-pro parkour tricks up his sleeve. Although Aerial doesn’t bring anything out of the box to the Runner genre, it does bring in a sense of charm and style with its overall visuals and outlook.The game would’ve been totally out-of-the-box, badass insane with a few tweaks, in my opinion; first of all, ditching the linear gameplay with something more challenging, then improving the basic parkour system with something more advanced that gives the players more non-linear options, as well as some much-needed gameplay parameter changes. Aerial is already hosting a fantastic game with fun gameplay and catchy visuals (which am in love with), but I do feel the need for certain improvements and challenges. Gameplay: After a brief unexplained intro, you are thrown right into the streets of Detroit, trying to outrun people who look like they’re in security uniforms but are definitely acting kinda sus. Wally, the protagonist, is running for his life. Right from the get-go, you will be hit in the face with certain features that are freaky playing against such fun gameplay. As you face your first set of obstacles, you will notice a clear WASD graphic in the top left corner that introduces you to the gameplay and ways to overcome the obstacles.   Each time you get near the top left corner, the graphic kicks in and shows you how to get over that particular obstacle, with an unnecessary amount of bullet time, holding the intense moment hostage and ruining the challenge presented by the obstacle. Which would be okay if it lasted for a certain tutorial period, but it goes for a long while and kicks in every now and then. There’s a limited set of things that can be done while escaping and overcoming each obstacle. Each obstacle is color-coded to match a functioning key assigned to overcome it, which is totally fine by me, but it would’ve been great to see some more unique tricks that I could pull off while running. Four main key functions play an important role throughout the game:  W for high jumps, S for sliding, A For a running flip jump, and D for dash. And as mentioned earlier each are color-coded to W Red, S Purple, A Yellow, and D blue respectively.Obstacles: Although the game does feature quite a few unique and fun hurdles for the players to overcome, there’s honestly nothing that really challenges me (and this is coming from me, who doesn’t really like hard challenges and difficulty). But the obstacles are really fun and immersive, until….. The recurring issues keep coming up, such as the bullet time; I get the necessity of such a feature, but when it keeps popping up and breaking the fast-paced immersion, it’s really upsetting. Also the ridiculous hit registry system; I don’t really get it, I have seemingly crashed into obstacles multiple times throughout my playthrough and just because I’ve played the correct key for that obstacle, I passed it without getting killed!!! Why? I crashed! How does the thing work when I have clearly gone under the bus! How am I alive after going under it! World design: The game features a pretty decent stylish urban world design that fits the theme of the gameplay just fine. While running, the game looks fantastic and cyberpunkish, but as soon as you slow down, prepare to be disappointed. I would recommend that you keep speeding.Music: The game features a fun hip tune to fit nicely with the intensity. The same goes for the jazzy unique tune that keeps playing in the background. Aerial has a solid and fun gameplay at its disposal, but it’s not quite there yet due to some obvious mismanagements and decisions. I am quite hopeful that with a few tweaks, this can turn out to be an insanely fun 3D Runner. Positives: + Fun gameplay+ Basic parkour + Interesting obstacles + Fantastic world design + Fast-paced + Addictive background music + Smooth performance Negatives: - Lost plot - Linear gameplay - Needs to change some perameters- Needs more advanced parkour and obstacles- Bullet time needs to be killed- Pressing the right button just before the crash doesn’t kill Wally A stylish new 3D runner with a ton of potential and bloody addictive music. 6/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Aerial_Knight, the solo developer, has created an engaging cinematic runner that thanks to anticipatory colour-coding of attacks and an excellent jazz-infused soundtrack by Danime-sama makes for a fun, breezy rhythm game. The difficulty is balanced and I would recommend bumping it up to Hard or Extreme as the slow-mo is quite generous, but there was one visually confusing boss battle with a musician blasting attacks with their guitar from the back of a truck, and because of the overwhelming visual assault of colours, it's hard to distinguish the attacks from the rest of the environment which led to way more deaths than any other encounter in the game. While there is some repetition in the levels and elements (probably due to budget and resources), the spectacle of escaping from murdering police, drone killbots, mines, cars, and of course helicopters makes for a short and sweet romp in a dystopic world with appealing cyberpunk aesthetics. The film feature-length pace is so fast that I got confused by the story and I wish there were more cutscenes to explain the events although it does end in an exciting and topsy-turvy final level. It did scratch my itch of a cinematic runner since . There was a definite lack of sound effects and the transition animations can look a bit wonky, but the aesthetics and soundtrack elevate the entire affair. It's refreshing to have a black protagonist in the runner and rhythm genre that's often lacking in representation, and there are several unlockable outfits with cultural designs. Post-game content like twists to the level could increase replayability but I had an enjoyable time throughout the running time and hope for more good things from the developer!

_childDocuments_.review: An autorunner with a decent amount of effort put into it, but it has some weird design flaws around the edges that make it complicated to outright recommend. _childDocuments_.review: This simple-to-learn runner provides a healthy balance of fun and challenge. The bebop soundtrack is an excellent fit with the art style and gameplay. Enough to keep me engaged and always saying "just one more mission." I had some small performance hiccups in the later levels on a Steam Deck OLED, so there might be some performance tuning required. The game has a mechanic where time slows down as you near an obstacle, requiring a certain button press. Some of the obstacles took me a while to figure out what the correct timing was and some were way off of the slow down timer. I will definitely be picking up and playing this runner again when I travel or find myself with a small amount of downtime. This game will have a permanent place on my Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty cool runner that has some dope visual design and slick environmental storytelling. The developer obviously has a passion for games and I hope to see more from them in the future. I really hope that whoever made this makes another title that's bigger and badder than this one.The only negative I can think of is It feels a bit like a itch.io title at times in terms of polish but the creative vision is there. Lots of little nods to anime, cartoons, and comics throughout. Developer seems to be plugged into the culture in a good way. Soundtrack is a major selling point, it's great music and fits the game very well. Overall it reminds me of a jazzy version of the indie runner Canabalt.Update 2/24/2022 - "Da Upate" has lot of neat add-ons and bonuses that polish the game up. More music too.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly stylized and extremely simple "Arial_Knight's Never Yield" is an interesting game that I appreciated. I especially enjoyed the music.Never Yield is a runner but not an endless runner. It's pretty simplistic but the obstacles come at you quickly. On lower difficulties, the game gives you some slow down which makes hitting the correct button very easy. You still need to hit at the right time and there's a lot of time between when the slow down starts to when you need to hit the button. On every difficultly setting the game has generous checkpoints but the timer doesn't stop if you die. The timer is your score for the level, the lower the better.I like the way the difficulty settings work but easy is indeed a little too easy for me. I jumped straight to the most extreme difficulty! As you might expect it is more challenging! There are more obstacles, no slow motion, and it doesn't give you a color hint before the obstacles arrive. I had to restart in some places but it is manageable.The best part of "Arial_Knight's Never Yield" is the artwork and music. It's the reason you would choose to play. I would say it blends a comic book style with the real world. I want to make the point that the game chooses art over gameplay a few times by changing the perspective. For example, the camera will shift behind the runner instead of the side view that's used for most of the game. I like it but it definitely makes it to keep track of everything.Overall, Aerial_Knight's Never Yield is an interesting art and music piece with some running. I enjoyed it but it's not the most polished game or the longest one. Still, it's worth checking out if you love runners.Wonderful video review,

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr- complete the first level, then back out to the main menu so that you can continue on Medium difficulty. Unfortunately, the default’s overly generous bullet-time hinders the pacing of the game.Playerunknown’s Never Yield is a runner game comprised of 13 levels and four kinds of obstacles that correspond with a face button. It’s a relatively simple “dodge the hazards” joint, sending the player character hurtling through action movie setpieces (jump over the boxes, slide under the car!), and I often found myself in a complete flow state reacting perfectly to everything it threw at me.The presentation is king here. Great, passionately comprised soundtrack, combining influences of 90’s trip-hop, turntablism and whatever the ♥♥♥♥ Jet Set Radio is doing. Solid cel-shaded art style adorning urban environments that are bustling with details. Levels are bookended by clunky cutscenes that are hard not to love.Undoubtedly an impressive technical and sensory achievement from solo developer “Aerial_Knights”, but the game doesn’t quite come together in a satisfying enough way for me to enjoy it much beyond its surface.It doesn’t take long before I realised that I was merely responding to the ~colour~ of the upcoming obstacle’s telegraph, as the game instead strictly demands certain buttons be pressed for specific hazards. Many of my deaths were ones where the game demanded a slide from me, where the jump would very easily have cleared it as well. This essentially just turns the game more into Simon Says than a bombastic parkour setpiecefest. One such button corresponds to a “sprint” move, allowing you to crash through certain obstacles and increase your movement speed to push for a faster clear time. Sadly, this move breaks the game more often than not, messing with the flow of obstacles, confusing the bullet-time slowdown, and sending you to an untelegraphed death; come the final levels, I grew too scared to use it, the checkpoints grew fewer and further between.Honestly not a bad way to kill an hour lol. I enjoyed the game when it let me enter the zone, even if it had shortcomings that dragged me out of the experience every so often. Would be more fun if it allowed the player to respond to hazards in a more freeform way, very much belies the whole point of parkour, but ah well.

The gameplay itself while basic I think works for what it is trying for, however several levels are either extremely short or feel like a previous level (4, 9, and 10) without a lot of remixing. This game however, I would highly recommend just for two levels in particular being 6 and 13, which are honestly some of the most unique levels and exciting levels I've seen from games in a long time. However, I wish the game took more risks outside of those two levels and two more less exciting, but still fun a lot of the levels reuse the same basic elements and I wish they either had new elements in them or reused old elements in new ways. Another thing  I think the game missed on was the story scenes, I have no idea what it is trying to convey to me and I can't tell if this game wants to have a deep story or just be a simple story, however this is the kind of game where story doesn't really mater so I was okay with it being weaker. _childDocuments_.review: ‘Never Yield’ is an on rails runner, similar in many ways to the Bit. Trip Runner series. It’s been created by a solo developer and is a visual and aural delight. You play as a man on the run, why, or from who, is not clear. The game feature 13 chapters and has been designed to be completed in a couple of sittings. The creator, Neil Jones, wanted to make a game that could be played out like an interactive short story, or an action movie. And that is what we have here. Gameplay is super smooth, and character animations look wonderful as you acrobatically avoid obstacles in your path. The interesting perspective switches from 2D to 3D, along with frequent cutscenes, make the game feel cinematic and the funky jazz / hip-hop soundtrack perfectly suits the action. Controls are simple. You use fours keys, or directions of the d-pad on a controller, to slide, high jump, flip, or speed up. Each move is represented by a colour, and hazards in your way are illuminated by one of these colours, indicating which button to press. It all plays out a lot like many quick time event (QTE) games. I can see the game working perfectly on mobile devices in the future.  The game features three difficulty settings, available after completing the prologue; Normal, Hard and Insane. The Normal mode is highly accessible, with slow motion effects added just before obstacles to give you time to hit the right button. For Insane, the ‘slow-mo’ is removed and more dangers added. For experienced players of the genre, I’d suggest switching straight to this mode.  Some may find the game’s short length a put off, levels are quite similar and your move-set doesn’t change. Yet, the sublime graphics, high octane gameplay and overall high level of polish, make ‘Never Yield’ definitely worth checking out. _childDocuments_.review: Check out my video review for Aerial_Knight's Never Yield here: Aerial_Knight’s Never Yield started off as a passion project by the developer who also goes by the name Aerial Knight. The aim of the game was to create something that appeals to a new generation of gamers while highlighting sometimes overlooked aspects of culture.The game doesn’t really do a good job at telling a story, in fact it seems like the only way to get any backstory of why you’re constantly running away from danger is to read the description on the Steam page. So here we go:"Take the role of Wally. A mysterious character that has recovered what was taken from him. Hopefully, you're fast enough to outrun your enemies. Expose the truth and try to uncover the mystery of what happened to them." And yea, that’s pretty much all we get. There are some hints sprinkled throughout the stages but don’t expect any deep narrative plot here. The star of the game and main reason you’d want to play this is the music, stylish graphics, and gameplay.Let’s go over the gameplay, this plays like an endless runner. The total runtime of the game isn’t that long. I was told it’s about the average length of a movie so around 2-3 hours.The goal of each level is to reach the end, all while dying as less as possible and getting there as fast as possible. There’s no randomness in stage and enemy patterns so you can practice away to get high scores.You can play the game completely with one hand. There are four buttons, left to do a medium jump, up for a high jump, down for a slide, and right to sprint. Though you’re always running, sprinting is used to get through stages faster and avoid certain enemies.Stages last around a couple of minutes a piece and you unlock new outfits upon completion. These are just cosmetic and don’t have an impact on gameplay from what I’ve seen.There are three difficulties, Normal, Hardmode, and Insane. Before you approach an obstacle time slows down giving you a chance to read the situation and act accordingly. Each enemy and obstacle also give off a color signifying which action to use. For example red is for high jumps and purple for sliding.I initially played on normal but found that all of the slow down kinda through off the overall vibe and pacing of the game. If you want a challenge, are familiar with runners, and have good reactions I’d recommend playing Insane mode. The difficulty name might sound crazy but all it does is take away the slow motion, gives you less warning time, and increases the amount of obstacles in your way. If anything, because the game is pretty short, beat it on normal then move right on to insane. In my opinion it’s the most satisfying way to play. There are checkpoints all over the level and it’s very fast to quick start if you mess up.The graphics are pretty bland, with most of the settings and assets being used over and over again constantly. There are some stand out moments, especially during boss fights, however where the camera changes angles and attacks come from unexpected directions. The music is great though, it was composed by “Danime-Sama" A Detroit artist with vocals from artists from all over the world. It’s very chill and really sets the tone. This music and the urban parkour environment really compliment each other.Overall, this game is not bad for what it set out to accomplish. It’s not going to win any awards and will probably be played in one session by most people. For $12.99, it’s really up to you whether or not you’d want to pick this up. It’s very short and the gameplay is pretty limited by the genre. It’s going to be a very 50/50 recommendation from me. And that’s only if you’re REALLY into arcade runner games.Disclaimer: I received this game for free. I was not paid to promote or write a review. All thoughts are solely my own. Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: Sums it up. Snappy controls, 4 button interface ( you can use a controller and D-Pad and/or face buttons | Kb WASD + arrow keys ) Simple enough, you automatically jog - you can press right ( or right face button ) to run. The other commands are for dodging obstacles I would've liked to have the outline obstacles be changeable to match my controller's face buttons ( yellow would be UP, red would be MIDDLE ( left ) and bottom would be GREEN ( a button on an xbox ) this way I would be able to parse the info a bit easier, since I know the controller mappings sub-consciously. You go through a ( very ) long stage, and are faced off with a " boss " of sorts after you complete a few.  Couldn't tell ya. The cutscenes are snazzy, and well produced - but I have literally no clue what's going on - other than this man is  Absolutely, and given that it's a passion project by a small team ( very ), you should consider supporting them if this looks to suit your fancy.Fast paced ( or not, it's up to you ) speedrunning routes are unlocked by always holding dash ( which will change obstacles.. but not their colors. ) For instance, a car flipping at you requires you to slide under it ( blue normally ), but if you were dashing before hand, a slide will kill you. So you need to use a RED command to leap over the car instead. I dig this approach, and they don't really show you the colors changing- you gotta figure the hidden commands on your own.  One thing IDIDN'T like, was the musician in a van - and the attacks for it were nearly indecipherable, I had to go by memory alone. felt like the turbo tunnel in battletoads. Where as all other levels clearly show you the obstacle, and outline ahead of time - this particular segment only shows you a small colored dust particle effect on the screen milliseconds before you need to react, and it's really not enough time to react - even if you aren't dashing.  If the game could add accessibility options ( such as the aforementioned outlined obstacles, and changing their color - or even disabling them for masochists ) and a slightly easier tell to the musician segment - and you got yourself an extremely solid game. It's solid as-is, but I feel those two points are worth keeping in mind ( if you play on keyboard, you can eliminiate the neeed to change outline colors entirely, so this is mainly a controller thing. ) I highly recommend this, it's fun - challenging, and offers a few difficulty settings to ease you into the harder ones. easy and normal add small time-slowing before each obstacle, hardcore removes it. I prefer to remove it - which certainly made the musician in a van segment harder. so that's that. go grab it, it's mega cheap .( Gameplay of Stage 5 )

_childDocuments_.review: 3h+ (mostly depending on how good you'll do in Endless mode) 4/10 1 I wrote an achievement guide,  No No Not sure.. for me, the endless mode felt like grinding No No No No Yes, most of the game you can play on easy but the bonus level and endless mode can't be played in this mode NoThis is a runner with an amazing art style and nice music. You have to react to upcoming objectives with 1 of 4 button presses. A nice thing is that you have a lot of variety in which buttons to use. For example, I played this with a controller and there I could use the D-pad or the ABXY buttons (I believe even the left thumbstick worked but that sounds like a bad idea in this game). When you failed to react with the right button or not within the time limit you would reset to the last checkpoint in the main game, or in the endless mode, you will restart from the beginning. The obstacles will have a color code to know which button to press and the tutorial does a good job explaining this. There are 3 difficulty options.. on the easiest difficulty the time will slow down when you get close to an obstacle so you have time to recognize there is one and which button to press. And the higher difficulties have less slowdown time or not at all. Most of the achievements you'll unlock while playing the story. For some, you might have to watch a cutscene that you can easily miss if you're like me and automatically press a button to try and skip the game logo. That logo will pop up a lot, but pressing a button doesn't speed it up but already works in the background on what is loading. So you might have already passed the main menu at the start of the game if you pressed a button when seeing the game logo, or for this achievement, you might have skipped a cutscene while not knowing. Gladly you can replay levels so none of the achievements are missable, but I wish that button presses wouldn't work on content loading in the background that you can't see. Most of the achievements are very easy, the hardest ones are to complete a bonus level for the last outfit and for playing 30 minutes endless mode to hear all the soundtracks. For the bonus level, you can repeat it by going back to the menu and going to level selection, and restarting it through there. I hope that the developer will change this and make the "not yield" option work so that it would restart the level, as this level can be really challenging and after failing have to go back into the main menu for like 20 seconds to restart makes it annoying. The other hard achievement for playing 30 minutes in endless mode is the hardest because you can\t make any mistake for those 30 minutes or otherwise you have to start all over... This reminded me of an achievement in a Guitar Hero/Band Hero game where you had to play the whole set without pausing.. this was a lot shorter but here no mistake was allowed and in that mode, you can make a few mistakes. Both took me the same amount of time since I don't have steel nerves... every time I passed the 25 minutes in this endless run I got nervous and made stupid mistakes. If you have better control over your nerves, this achievement isn't too bad and you will be able to complete the game in under 3h. I did enjoy this game but it can use a little bit more polish. Like not progressing the game in the background when the game shows the game logo when the player pushed buttons to try and speed up the game, and being able to easily restart a bonus level without going through the game menu. If you enjoy runners and are up for an endless run of 30 minutes without mistake, you should give Aerial Knights a try!

_childDocuments_.review: A 4-button runner oozing great style and soundNever Yield is a beautiful game. First and Foremost, the art-style is awesome, with it's popping colors and effects.  The Many alternate outfits you can put on the lead look great; the environments are very lush. I wish there was a easy description for the style, somewhere between Graffiti, Street fashion, and retro games. With a little action-anime in there too.The game play is a simple, yet exciting affair. Four buttons control a dude who won't stop running: Slide, jump, dash, and vault through thirteen 5-8 minute levels. Every obstacle that approaches is marked with colors that correspond to the button you've gotta push. On easy mode, there is an automatic slow-down right before you get hit. I died a few times, but the game is very accommodating and gets you right back into it; plus the load times are short. Every level is a quick breeze marked with really impressive music. Hip Hop beats with a few vocals and some orchestral sounding stuff near the end. It contributes a lot to how fun this game is. For it's base price, what you see is what you get. I definitely recommend this to the type of gamer who likes short breezy action, and can't commit to extended play-times. Many levels have a golden coin to grab that lets you take on a bonus level, adding replayability, but I wish you didn't have to go back in that level for the coin if you die in the bonus stage. Also the game has no way of keeping track of what levels have coins to collect or bonuses to win.Between each level are visually appealing cutscenes that seem to tell of the character's escape from some kind of Sci-fi authority, but the story is kind of hard to follow. No dialogue, but also no facial expression or human characters besides the lead. Maybe there's room for some text to tell the story that the player could unlock? I want more of this world! Besides the story kinda lacking and the issue with the bonus levels, the regular levels themselves could use some more diverse use of challenging the player. It stays fun, but the last few levels use the same assests mulitple times. There's only one boss fight here, maybe expand on that aspect?Besides some chill criticism, this game is a real fun time. I'm very glad I came across it online and bought it. The team should be proud!TLDR: Awesome graphics, Great music, and fun gameplay. The levels could use more obstacles to throw at the player and test how you react. Not much goin' on storywise, and the bonus levels are questionable. A great time tho; I think it's worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: A visual feast with a narrative told purely through animation with a great soundtrack. Seriously the shader work in this game is great evoking a similar look to Into the Spiderverse. The gameplay is standard runner fair, but allowing players to sprint at any time gives players familiar with say the Bit Trip Runner series the ability to control when we want things to get more punishing (you can also just select Insane difficulty right away like I did).I appreciated the variety in the obstacles you encounter but ultimately how you deal with them never really changes. I'm disappointed that for the most part the game remained a side scroller throughout. The parts where the camera shifts to an alternative angle was done well enough that it wasn't disorienting (and in the ending in particular was integrated very well into the narrative).The last bits are mostly nitpicks. It was an odd choice to me that the music in the pre level cutscenes didn't smoothly transition into the level music. Other than that, I don't really have anything negative to say about the game. It can be completed it around 2 hours which for some people might be a turn off. But for me, the gameplay was fun, the soundtrack is a bop, and it was a stylized graphics feast throughout.Edit: Nevermind about the controller not working in the wardrobe, the controller cursor starts on the back button lol
_childDocuments_.name: Aerial_Knight's Never Yield

_childDocuments_.review: Sub-par runner with solid style and amazing music. I love how much effort went into the artistic aspects of the game but between some of the terrible hitboxes, obstacles being hidden behind foreground elements or blending into the background not to mention that hitboxes shift in weird ways when you dash, the game is frustrating to play through. I highly recommend the soundtrack but if that isn't your cup of tea stay far far away
_childDocuments_.name: Aerial_Knight's Never Yield

_childDocuments_.review: A tremendously well made runner with an incredible art style that compliments the gameplay and tone exceptionally well. Gameplay wise the simple controls are very fluid and responsive. The timing for jumping over obstacles is also very generous which is a big plus for me. My only issue was the constant slow down on the normal difficulty but this goes away entirely during the hard and insane modes. I feel as if hard and insane are the best ways to experience Never Yield.And lastly, this game has one of the best soundtracks I've ever heard and was the first time I've purchased a game soundtrack to just listen to on my own time. Easily one of my favorite games I've played all year
_childDocuments_.name: Aerial_Knight's Never Yield

_childDocuments_.review: So I just beat the game and the whole time I felt like I was playing a Jet Set Radio Future spin off. Which is a good thing for someone like me since that Sega classic is a top three favorite of mine. The stylistic cel-shaded aesthetic and the rhythmic jazzy hip-hop musicality feed into the rebellious atmosphere of the game and the protagonist perfectly. Especially as they attempt to escape from the clutches of a shady organization that attempts to capture or destroy them for reasons the game hopes you artistically interpret. In name, in story, and in game-play it tells the player to Never Yield to the powers that be and the obstacles that stand in your way as you dip, dive, duck, and dodge your way to freedom. The danger that hopes to halt your progress corresponds to a color tone that you then react and respond to accordingly. And to make things even more accessible the base difficulty mode briefly slows down time at varying intervals so you can better acclimate to each stages demands. If you end up scoffing at what's thrown at you there just bump that baby up for something a little more intense then what is given. Simple!This game is obviously not a big budget title but it is very charming and has a lot of heart to it. The dramatic changes and shifts in game-play on different stages were a clever and innovative treat but the final level remains so memorable to me for how significant musical and mechanical adjustment can convey tone. I do hope to see a sequel where a change in character "perspective" involves more remixes to expand upon intent. That would be very solid!Overall I believe it is worth a buy for the artistry, the ambience, and the affordability alone. It is by no means a big commitment of your time and I do not believe you have much to lose if the trailers enticed you to begin with. If you liked what you saw then what you saw is what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Aerial_Knight's Never Yield

_childDocuments_.review: Survive A futuristic Tokyo style Detroit in this 3D runner that tells the story of Wally who has uncovered the evidence that can change his city forever. Explore a game world with a dope-tastic soundtrack featuring the authentic sounds of Detroit Artist.

name: Stranded: Alien Dawn
detailed_description: Brave a new world in Stranded: Alien Dawn, a planet survival sim placing the fate of a small marooned group in your hands. Forge your story through compelling and immersive strategic gameplay as you make vital decisions to protect your survivors from starvation, disease, extreme weather and more. From basic camps to fortified bases, create a stronghold to defend the survivors from attacks by alien creatures that roam an expansive and deadly alien world. Experience an epic and unpredictable journey. Discover an expansive, living 3D world with remarkable flora and fauna Manage your survivors’ needs, health and happiness Construct and evolve your own unique base, and devise cunning defences to protect it and survivors from being attacked Plant, grow, harvest and hunt down food. Stockpile useful resources and salvage material from fallen space debris Research technologies to expand your horizons. Provide heat, light, devices for relaxation and more to keep survivors on top of their game, ready to face the next challenge. React to fluctuating weather and environmental events AN UNFORGIVING WORLD Stranded: Alien Dawn pushes you and your survivors to the brink. Limited resources, unpredictable weather, illness and hostile alien creatures make it hard to establish a foothold on an unforgiving world. The next challenge is never far away, requiring construction of an increasingly robust base using advanced resources and improved defences. STRANDED SURVIVORS Ensure your group’s physical and mental wellbeing by providing weapons, medicine, and much-needed entertainment. Every survivor has a unique backstory, varying levels of ability in key skills, and both positive and negative traits. Only by improving their skills and maximising their potential will you survive. AN UNPREDICTABLE JOURNEY In Stranded: Alien Dawn, every playthrough is unique. Experience a journey driven by random story events, alien wildlife threats and adverse weather. There will be setbacks; devise your own innovative solutions to problems and manage multiple crises at the same time. However, actions have consequences and as you strive to plan ahead, you must make difficult choices to shape the story of your survivors, balancing short and long-term outcomes with risk and reward. MODULAR BASE-BUILDING Design and build your base on an alien world and transform it from simple shelter to high-tech outpost. Protect it with perimeter defences, decorate it with furnishings, introduce automated devices such as defensive turrets, and discover new technology to create your own functioning space pad.

_childDocuments_.review: Yea, the foundation is very similar to Rimworld, but of course I'm not saying this as a bad thing. If they will keep adding more content this game really may become a very solid basebuilding sim. For now there is enough content to keep you hooked for at least 2/3 playthroughs, but as they will add more zones and modifiers and with that researches and items, this will be really nice replayability. What worries me the most right now is limited set of starting characters. It's not bad, but it can't beat random or created characters, this aspect may need some more love in future updates. Beside that, I like the researches so far, nothing very special, but if they will expand it it may become interesting. Building segment is very solid and I can't wait to see how it evolves... also, it feels weirdly satisfying to build in this game, which is very big plus. Character interactions are nice and overall default AI is good as for early access. I hope, that the Devs will keep up the good work and there won't be any 'other' issues with the development, as this might be really nice title as it gets more stuff.I'd say that nowadays Rimworld is 8/10 and Stranded: Alien Dawn is something like 6/10 but keep in mind, that it's first day review for an EA game, this might get much better (or worse:p) very soon
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded: Alien Dawn is like the space time lovechild of The Sims & any worthy survival game. The ingenious balancing act which the game masters hereby achieved is remarkably efficient, satisfying and deeply motivating! The same sense of achievement you received by evolving the quality of any simulated avatar being is reproduced with a complex series of alien environmental checks & balances. As your lucky survivors stand the relentless test of time, you shepherd a chaotic good gang of barbaric cave people out of the stone age, through the medieval wood / iron age and into the contemporary / space age of civilized awesomeness! When you finally lead long enough to see former troublemakers rise from their stupidity and make you proud time and again, they eventually even fall in love with their epic counterparts, fulfilling the promise of truly intelligent life. An evolved VR version with vastly more realistic combat would make for a legendary sequel! Highly recommended! :-D
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This EA game is already very wel playable.. lots of things to do in the many ways that a good survival game is having. Gathering, creating all kinds of stuff, certainly after you have done some research... many possibility's are already there for playing a lot of hours & enjoy it all. You can choose your 4 peoples team to start with, each with there own skills that will help u out. You can find them out many different woman & men that can make a difference.Maybe one good advice : Play the TUTORIAL it will give you the needed info to bring it out alife when you strugle the sometimes hard nature & animal attacks once they find your camp... Also good replayability, because every time you will land in another part of the map, with a new team of your own choise.. very wel done ! HAVE FUN !!!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: After like 40 hours of playtime the game starts crashing constantly... no options changed.The most I can play without crashing is 2-3 hours but mostly it crashes 10-20 minutes now.And the devs shouldn't dare say something like update your drivers and bla bla bla.I did EVERYTHING! And many many people have this problem!Unless the devs change their priority from trying to cashgrab with a "DLC" to fixing the foundation of their game NO ONE should buy this!A few things I noticed in my 60 hours of playtime:- no quicksave- constant crashes- idiotic behavior of survivors (tasks and order of them, pathfinding, etc;  example: a survivor is salvaging miles from base and when he is finished but his hunger is under a  specific treshold he won't transport the thing he salvaged. He is just running to get food. Why?  Just take the stuff with you...- you need to babysit the survivors (see example)- way more things like the exampleIt's just a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I love Rimworld and I do not mind clones/improvements on that system. This game is very well made and I really enjoy it thus far. Things I'd like to see improved:/being capable of riding them around for various increases. (One is faster, one is more of a pack mule, etc)-A vehicle. They are capable of crafting great things including laser rifles. Making a simple combustion engine for a moped or atv should be no brainer.-Humanoid aliens, space pirates, some kind of NPC enemy to capture and recruit. -More. Game is really good, but is early access so I look forward to more.Adding Mod Tools is a game changer. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely brilliant! As a developer I can see how much went into it. Its challenging, but the reward you feel when you figure out how to get things done in a better and more efficient way in the game is superbly addictive! I installed the game round 9 pm and only realized by 7 am the next morning how time flew by playing it. The last time I enjoyed a game this much was back with starcraft and warcraft! This game accomplished the shortfall of most new RTS games and I enjoyed it more than Banished, Farthest Frontier and a few other ones.  10 out of 10! The intricacies of this game, nuances of character traits and a few other factors make it playable over and over. It's so many classic and new mechanisms all mixed into one with it all balancing surprisingly well. When you start figuring out how to set priorities in the optimum way you can minimize the micro tasking if you like. Brilliant! Hats off to the devs! Wish I could meet the devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun city builder/RTS.  They did a nice job with the balancing of the game.  Early game is a bit slow, but once your past it, it moves a faster.  The technology tree is fun.  I also like the different scenarios to change up the game play a bit for more replay-ability.  If you like games like Rimworld or Surviving the Aftermath you will probability like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Only a yes because of early access, but it feels really early. Balance is a huge problem. I think the idea of the game and mechanics are solid and it will be a fun game if they see it through. I have seen a lot of these games get about half done and come out of early access to make a buck and you never hear from them again. We will see.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game despite having a few anomalies relating to AI and Game behaviour is a great game with excellent potential for improvements and new ways of playing. The premise is great the options are good and modders are already expanding how to play the options. One guy has come up with the idea of combining both a military and trade outpost together although it lacks functionality in some areas it shows the ongoing potential of this game.The idea of combining Sims conversations and behaviours is the icing on the cake although I have already taking the producers to task over the bad flooring making the place loo like a cave and then docking happiness points as lore unfriendly as people in a survival situation would not be concerned whether there was carpet on the floor. This game is the only game I have encountered in years that has been able to move me off Fallout 4 and play it instead. Both have modding capacity to make the game more to your liking or enjoyable however the difference however with the object orientated Lua scripting even I can alter some mods easily to make my version of someones mod do something different. Much easier to use then F4's editor and is built into the game's Menu interface making it very easy to view and edit mods as a start to creating your own.All in all I would give this game a 8/10 which is very good for my rating system as it puts it on par with the same rating I would give Fallout 4
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The worst thing about this game is that an early access survey pops up in game every twenty odd minutes.That being said, I really enjoy Stranded Alien Dawn.  It's your basic colony/town sim with a few novel twists.  Citizens are pregenerated rather than being RNG citizens.  The research/resource discovery progression system allows you to develop without being totally overwhelmed at first.I do wish there was an option to turn of the "wave" attacks that occur periodically.  And I wish there was an easier way to deal with colonist clothing.  That being said would definitely purchase this game again.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended for fans of survival and base building games looking for something fun and polished but that may not have some of the depth/replayability of some of the genre giants. However, there is enough content to be more than worth the full asking price and well worth it on sale. Personally I enjoyed it more than RimWorld, even though there is no contest in RimWorld's greater depth.+Visuals+UI+Options, customization, mods+Variety of game modes and goals+Wide range of research+Variety of clothing/weapons/armor/tools+Variety of crops+Intuitive building and infrastructure+Variety of buildings+Animal taming+Exploration, scavenging, observation+Choices for some events/adventures+Overall balance, ability to respond/overcome obstacles-Far too few creature types-Very slow pacing-Resource gathering for buildings can be slow/grindy-Progression of recruiting survivors can be slow/uneven-Very slow research-Survivor interactions limited/uninteresting-Lacking story, character development-Custom characters only through mods, cumbersome-Heat and clothing management can be awkward
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: this is great so far. they need to address the mass attacks in late game, improve how defenses work - like more than wooden walls, mote than 1 in a tower, turrets on towers etcthere's a lot to be done - but I can see this turning into what I always wanted Rimworld to be - only much much better visually.love the game - get on board!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It is smooth and runs fine. It is simple to use and manage the people. I really like how when building a house you can change the material instead of having to destroy and rebuild it. I think it could use some quality of life changes for some mechanics like changing clothes automatically to fit the weather, but you could also just click on a characters inventory and it brings out options to change into. It would be cool to edit character names too, and maybe a further zoom camera and mini-map would help. I Built near the edge of the map because I didn't realize that is where I started. The game looks good and lets you see past your area so I was confused as to which area was playable or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended, it still needs work with balance and bugs but that's to be expected from a early access title.Game includes base building. Electricity, wind generator, solar panels, generators, sensors, heaters, lights, turrets etc. Plant a variety of crops, farming is not as in depth as farthest frontier. There are also raids from creatures and events.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I had held off on buying this game at first because I usually wait for games being on sale for less than 10€ - or max. 20€ when I really want them. With this, I finally didn't want to wait any longer and what can I say, it's totally worth it.I haven't played many other games that have a similar structure and playstyle, but I really like managing this small group of survivors, discovering and researching your surroundings and all the alien species, and the variety this game already offers (currently 3 different missions with I don't know how many different characters to choose from, 3 different planets to land on and of course difficulty levels and special rules that you can adjust for each playthrough).I would love it if they keep new content coming, because I could see how it still becomes repetitive after a while. Still, I keep coming back :)
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game crashes so much, it's absolutely annoying.It's a fun game, I'm trying to enjoy it, and mostly am. But the constant crashing is so frustrating. I cannot recommend it because of the poor stability. In the beginning, on a new game, it runs great, totally stable. But over time, stability goes out the window and it crashes about every hour or less. Performance stays solid, no frame dips or anything, it's amazingly well optimized in that regard, it's just stability that doesn't seem to exist. I've already done the setting reflections to low. I actually just set them to off, and that helped a ton, but it's an improvement and not a fix.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible game.  DO NOT BUY.   You are put into no-win situations over and over and over again. Have a doctor? Doesn't matter, they can't heal their injured teammates because you weren't given medication or bandages and even though you researched it, you cannot MAKE them because your map doesn't have the plants necessary to craft them.  Bugs invading?  Tough, your one and only person with a weapon just killed himself by overeating and the rest refuse to be drafted because they have no weapons.  No weapons you say?  Oh you may have researched basic weapons, but you can't craft any of them at the table because you don't have the materials on your map to even craft a lowly smegging SPEAR.  So all of your people die on day 10 because bugs come and mow you down.What is the point of making a game and releasing it if  you have very critical key pieces of the game not implemented yet, and you CAN NOT play the game without said missing features.   You CAN NOT survive past day 10 as a result of this.   I know as I have tried 5 times in a row.  Always die on day 10 because the maps do not include crucial items you need to be able to survive and build. This is essentially a rip from Rimworld, but with different graphics and adjusted inventory items.   I have a ton of hours in Rimworld and at no point did I ever encounter a point in gameplay where I had ZERO chance to win because the game had missing elements in it that prevented me from surviving.   This game needed at LEAST another year in development before being released as pre-alpha or whatever they are selling this as here in late Nov-22.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I have 180 hrs on the "crash landing" scenario and I have yet to encounter any form of bug or unpleasantness from the game. Everything feels extremely polished and enjoyable. I recommend this game to anyone, a huge shout-out to the devs for their time and effort as it is greatly appreciated. I found my moving buddy :)

_childDocuments_.review: Really do love this game. There are a few things that irritate with the waves of attacks and animals breaking random fences but on the whole it is really worth it. _childDocuments_.review: Alien Dawn has much to recommend it: a wonderfully presented world, engaging tech progression, and a wide diversity of different resources to manage. They've made good use of the 3D perspective allowing for multi-floor buildings of whatever shape the player chooses. I didn't experience any bugs, except when it came to demolishing multi-level structures.Unfortunately, Alien Dawn is also in many ways an imperfect imitation of Rimworld, right on down to the key bindings in some cases. Storage is a mess with few options and a lot of fussing and fidgeting. The ticket system for production made its way over from Rimworld, but they botched automatic priorities and the game will forget manual priorities the moment the player switches them off.Build options are sparse, suggesting to me an aspiration for Workshop creators to pick up the slack. The social system between colonists can be safely ignored and its obscure enough to be simply irrelevant. Combat is a bland retake of that found in Rimworld with challenge so mild as to make me wonder why it's in the game.I think less reliance on Rimworld as an inspiration would have benefited Alien Dawn, but ultimately this game is defined by features which feel started, but not finished; good ideas wedged into the limitations of another game's concepts. I had to check twice that I wasn't reviewing an Early Access game. Maybe this beer needed more time in the barrel.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

I would give it a soso review if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game! It's been a long time ago that trying a new game gets me so hooked so quickly!For me the balance of managing everything (building, researching, planning, defending attacks etc.) is very good. I don't get bored and I don't feel like it's not doable. Also the visuals are great.Many people compare it to Rimworld. _childDocuments_.review: THE BEST SURVIVAL GAME EVER....I don't die every ten minutes, there's loads to do, enemies get harder as time progresses but you also get to increase defences at the same rate so it gets exciting but not too hard. Trading, fighting, building, electrical supplies and inventions to play with. Totally brilliant, well done.
