_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the worst task scheduling I've ever seen in a game. You give the order to mine some stones or ore somewhere. One of your guys will walk there, which takes him a thrdr of a day to get there, then mine ONE rock and then walk that huge distance back to base to - and I kid you not - refill some wall torch. And do you know what makes this even better? He doesn't even carry the stone he just mined back to base. You have 5 furnaces right next to each other to produce bricks for a house that you're building. All 5 furnaces are done burning a load of bricks and need to be emptied. One of your guys goes to a furnace picks up ONE load of bricks out of that furnace and carries it to the construction site. Let me get this straight: They can carry 20 times that amount of bricks. If he would go to the storage and pick up bricks there, he could pick up 20 times the amount he's carrying from that one furnace. Why doesn't he pick up the bricks from the other furnaces RIGHT beside him? Why doesn't he refill and start them before carrying the bricks off?The NPCs are so SUPER frustratingly bad programmed it will make you pull your hair out. They have absolutely no ability to plan ahead, e.g. "Will I be hungry when I arrive at the location where I have to work so that I will immediately turn around when I get there to go back to base and eat something? Should I maybe eat something now?". They are in complete ignorance of their surroundings when working on a task, e.g. the example above with emptying just one furnace although several others are next to it that could be emptied too.The option to give direct orders to one of your NPCs doesn't help much either. From what I have observed, after doing a couple or even just a single task of the things that you've given a direct order about (e.g. pick berries of 10 bushes), the NPC has a chance to just ignore your order and keep on doing what he wants to. To use the example of the 10 berry bushes, an NPC may pick the berries off of 3 bushes or so and then leave. Bizzarly that "check to see if the NPC wants to do something else" only happens after finishing a progress bar, but not while that NPC is working on a progress bar. So an NPC that has simply chosen on own to research a certain project, which takes a long time to finish the progress bar, may stay at the research table until he's "ravenously hungry" or sleepy to the point of almost fainting, which can easily be 12 ingame hours, but when you give him a direct order to, let's say build that last 10 walls of your vitally important defensive structure, he may just wander off (literally to take a walk or play an instrument for recreation), after finishing 3 walls in maybe 20 ingame minutes. THE DESIRE TO PLAY THE DIDGERIDOO IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE EXCUSE TO DISOBEY ORDERS!This game is SO super grindy, but not because you have to do a lot of action A to be able to afford object B, but because there's just SO MUCH useless overhead due to the sheer incompetence of your NPCs task scheduling.  Other things that are badly implemented are the moral system and the research tree. The issue of the research tree is pretty simple: You'll be done with all research after about 1/4 of the time you need for a playthrough. Very rarely you'll stumble on a special research project when doing exploration, but that is really rare. In 18 hours of playtime that happened 3 times to me and it took about 15 minutes in total to research these new research projects. The moral system is another thing that looks good on paper but is badly implemented. In short: Your people will sometimes just lose it and have a mental breakdown during which they are uncontrolable no matter what you do. Your NPCs can have a nice bed in an air conditioned room, they can have a variety of tasty food, several opportunities (and items) to have leisure time (dart games, music instruments, sports equipment)...but then you read something like "Had a an argument with Nancy" in the details of their moral status page which impacts their moral by a value of -18 (on a scale of 0 to 100). Several of such trivialities can add up and when it pushes their moral score to a value below 20, they have a breakdown. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TRACY, JUST BECAUSE NANCY WAS MEAN TO YOU AND THE FACT THAT YOU HAD SOUP FOR DINNER INSTEAD OF RATATOUILLE DOESN'T GIVE YOU THE RIGHT TO GO BERSERK AND SMASH OUR ONLY DIESEL GENERATOR!To summarize my review: This game isn't hard, it's just frustrating. The sheer incompetence of your NPC in executing their tasks produces so much overhead that the game progresses painfully slow. It's not relaxing either because every few minutes you'll be attacked by animals that just spawn at certain times and you'll have to manually order your NPC to go to combat stations. If one of your NPCs should happen to be at the place where those attacking animals spawn, well, tough luck, time to reload an autosave.Nice concept, good intentions, but everything is ruined by the bad implementation.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a classic survival game that is original in its genre for a variety of reasons: first, because of the strong characterization of the characters, which involves a good level of micromanagement with the goal of meeting the various needs of our crew. Second, because there are not many survival games where you have to manage a colony starting from scratch, on a generally hostile planet. The scenario, therefore, is quite good.However, there are some aspects that could be improved, of course. First of all, this game suffers from the same flaw aswell as many other survival games: at the beginning the difficulty curve is very steep, where resources are low, it is extremely laborious to procure them, and the available technologies are few. As the game progresses, as we discover new technologies, as our crew gets a few survivors, things get easier. The increased agressiveness of the local fauna is not enough to get us in trouble if we develop the right technologies (such as combat mechs).Maybe  a little more variety in approaching the endgame would be nice, perhaps introducing hostile human NPC opponents, introducing new natural disasters, in short creating new challenges when our colony is well structured and stable.In addition, more locations (planets) to colonize, perhaps introducing environments with unbreathable air that force the crew to wear, outdoors, suits and respirators, would introduce further variety, as well as more opportunity to explore the planet with small teams.Overall, however, an excellent, enjoyable game that perhaps in its current state suffers from poor replayability when all the environments have been explored.

_childDocuments_.review: I have nearly 100 hours on this game, so I can say fully with confidence: This game rocks. First off, shout out to the devs, who had been making impactful updates ones a month for 6 months straight. We got a new planet, new scenarios, new characters and abilities - and now that it's out of Early Access, it really has a ton to provide.I really value the replayability of this game. Though I fully understand the mechanics and functions of the game, each new seed offers a different layout and its own challenges therein, before even having to change the difficulty level. I love that you can randomize characters for an even bigger challenge (or advantage!), and I've pretty much started a new game with every update during early access and now just to see the full effects of it all. The visuals and design are so much fun and for the most part the survivors are smart enough to get tasks done on their own. The hierarchy system for activities is fantastic, and especially for the scenarios with larger numbers of survivors, being able to designate certain types of tasks for them makes everything really efficient. Having the survivors want to have celebrations, music nights, etc. is really nice, and I wish it happened even more than it already does. It's fun that they can also fall in love and get married - there's nothing like romance when stranded on an alien planet! The game is not without its flaws, but I would say that only rarely did any of these things annoy me enough to really be a bother. Nit-picks would be as follows:- When butchering animals with meat and hides, the survivors always take the hides back to the camp first, and not the meat, which goes bad a lot quicker/birds will eat at. It should probably be the other way around.- Speaking of, the hauling system I would say could be smarter. Expanding the hauling area when a survivor is going to pick something up would mean they have less trips to make. They can usually handle the quantity of items that are around, but they'll only go for items within a small range of their original haul unless you direct them further.- The randomized aspects can be too much sometimes: I spent nearly a year scavenging and salvaging on one map before I got any electronics, which meant I couldn't get electric items nearly as quickly. Yes, I could take a balloon, but even just a few of all the electronics bits should exist in the spawns nearish to the starting point. - More music. The one track is nice, but having some variations of it would even make a better impact. - Prioritizing activities: right now, when you prioritize multiple activities for survivors, they do them left to right, and you can't switch the order (which is frustrating). I wish there was a way to prioritize the items/actions on the map (i.e. constructing something, tailoring something, salvaging, etc.) so that survivors who have it marked as a priority will just get it done first, and then default to their hierarchy. Overall, a fantastic game you can play over and over again, and knowing even more updates are coming, one that will always have something new and exciting for you to explore and experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The similarities to Rimworld are fairly obvious, but I think the game managed to miss the points of Rimworld that make it great.In stranded dawn, you are in control of a handful of not randomized survivors, that dont really have any real personality besides being fussy eaters, and constantly choosing to wear summer clothes when its cold outside. Them breaking down has little to no impact on the game, and is largely forgettable. They will also occasionally catch an illness, that will also lead to nothing dramatic. Nothing seems to be an urgent matter at all in the game, so much so that Im not sure its possible to lose.This is what they did wrong when making a 3D Analog of Rimworld, Rimworld gets all its flavor from its pawns. Randomized, often snapping for insane reasons, having personality, getting addicted to drugs, being filled with bloodlust to where when they snap they will kill their fellow pawns. They will have conversations about things in game and have differences leading to potentially violent escalations. They can catch a cold and have a real risk of dying from that cold, even after spending the whole time in a hospital bed. In battle they can savagely beat the limbs off another character in hand to hand combat in a trance state. All Flavor adders that Stranded: Alien Dawn lacks.It really feels more like a more simple resource management and colony simulator style game, no real risk, pretty relaxing, with fairly trivial waves of bugs to fight and uninspiring building mechanics filled with limitations.Its still a game I enjoy playing and probably will still play in the future considering Mods could probably greatly enhance the title, but its a far stretch from the amount of detail, suspense, and joy Rimworld has.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential but is ruined by mind-boggling terrible decisions. The way the power/tech and clothing/temp systems are handled are great and interesting. But it doesn't matter because the beginning of the game (or at least the survival scenario, the one every game of this genre focuses on) is so horribly balanced that it becomes seriously unfun. The primary issues are the way things are paced, the terrible AI, and the uneven balance between you and enemy NPCs.The biggest issue is how slow you move. So many items, buildings, etc require a ton of resources and upwards of 6 to 18 hours to build. That's fine... except it takes that much in additional time just to walk. It should not take 1 or more hours to travel small distances. A small settlement of 30 tiles should not take 2 hours to walk from edge to edge. This becomes further compounded with the atrocious AI which will be working on one thing but not continue doing the same thing right next to them but instead walk across the entire camp to work on another (similar) thing.. before walking back. There's no internal logic of priority or time with the AI. And if you slow yourself down by minimizing spread of planning, like structures, you waste tons of game-time that could have been spent more productively.The AI is so terrible, you can select a SINGLE animal to hunt, the NPC will go attack it.. get attacked by.. get a literal papercut ("superficial bite"), and try to run to a bed to rest... while the NPC is still alive and attacking. On the other hand,  your base can be under attacked and a non-drafted (not directly controlled) npc will randomly decide to fight the BIG insects.. bare-handed. Without being attacked, while behind walls. Any form of healing is more baffling because the game will try to heal non-life threatening people while someone with their guts spilling out is told "good luck". Which, going back to the horrible walking speed of the game, a bleedout time of 5 hours is a death sentence.Fighting enemies is so terribly uneven it's just unfun. You can build walls and towers, but people on towers can't shoot at 90% of the enemies at the wall because they "can't see" them. Sometimes random plants will block YOUR LoS of enemies but THEY can see/attack you just fine. There is no stunning or instant-killing of enemies, you have to deal 100% of HP to kill them. But they CAN stun/knock-out you or INSTANT KILL you by pure random rolls. Hey, that'd be a cool feature.. if the game was centered around a PRESET roster of characters. Which means there's a very limited amount of people you can recruit, let alone actually find and get into your camp. And losing 1 person out of 6 or 7 people by literal random chance is absurd and effectively ends the game. Especially when finding new people is a random chance that isn't even uncommon, it's straight rare. There's one setting that ups the chance to get your first 2 additional people and that feels like a necessity with how absurdly low the chance is. This is even worse because the "armor" barely offers any protection despite the length of time it takes to make any of it, enemies usually attack at night (lol good luck ever hitting them before you unlock high tech light sources), but THEY have insane armor that makes non-guns practically useless... especially when bows and crossbows have insanely low range that the ranged enemies outrange. Because of course.TBH 7 people in your base is already pushing it. Because, again, the walk speed is so damn low that building shelters/houses for more than that would make your town/base unfeasibly large time-wise. Which only lightly touches upon how long it takes to build structures (very, very long).I'm sure the game becomes painfully easy when you can access the high-tech stuff like a base of automated turrets and mechs. But GETTING there is unfun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does a lot of things well, but I'd like to share my favorite.As a fan of the genre, this game communicates survivor priorities and workflow very well.If you want something done, you have a clear idea of what your survivor is currently doing to make it happen. _childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: What if you combined The Sims with a survival game in an alien setting? You get this, basically.The thing I always disliked about survival games is that they're massive time sinks/wasters, because YOU have to do everything yourself. Here, you only do the planning, and other people do the job for you, which is great, if they actually do what you want them to do, which is where the Sims aspect comes into play.These people are morons, absolute, and utter morons. They'd rather starve to death than actually eat an emergency ration or fix themselves a quick meal if they think that ANYTHING you've told them to do is higher on the agenda, like smelting metal or sewing shirts. No, you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, you don't need to work until you die, and just because I told you NOT to eat the emergency rations, when there's plenty of food available, in an EMERGENCY you can, of course, eat them!What I'm saying is: the game can be intensely micro-management-heavy. I had 6 survivers by the end, and everything was working, but I still needed to micro-manage quite a few tasks, like ... closing and opening a window, you know, things you'd think somewhat intelligent beings would do "on the fly". The whole window situation is crap anyway. These people can eventually research a nano printer ... and make windows out of carbon, instead of putting some damn glass in their windows, so they can have a look outside and feel happy WITHOUT freezing to death. (The nano printer is encased by glass, by the way).But in all honest, the game is good fun for at least 10 to 20 hours. My only problem is that I do not feel the desire to continue now. I've researched everything, I have a giant battle mech that can single-handedly deal with any threats, I'm more than self-sufficient, the only real danger now is stupidity and age, since apparently the only thing left to do is wait for a space ship to rescue me. So far I had one come by that offered to take ONE of my guys away, which I naturally declined, because if one leaves, everything will go to ♥♥♥♥, and I don't want to end up with less and less survivors. It's all or nothing!The other 2 available scenarios have you construct a trade hub or a military outpost, but apart from a few scenario-specific things, there's not much different from the survivor scenario. At least, not at first glance, so nah ... there's also another DLC scenario, but the reviews are mixed, and it's quite expensive!So, my suggestion is to just take it all in in 1 game, then let the game rest for a while, and if you feel like it, you can return to it later, test out a different scenario, other survivors, other maps and challenges, higher difficulty, etc.

The game is good despite (initial) minor bugs and LACK OF SECOND FLOORS. The Mechs are a cool addition, the scenarios do give it some replay-ability, but I didn't like the population cap and fixed characters. It does leave an open door for modders, but it doesn't seem to have caught too much attention within that community (based on the few mods I've tried). I think the developers did a great job, it's just not the kind of game I'll put 1000+ hours into. I'll not dissuade anyone from buying though.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: For the price, the game is very fun and seems like the type of thing one can pick up and put down over time. If you like Rimworld base game, you'll probably like this game for at least long enough to play through the various scenarios. That's worth $35 imo. Modding might stretch that further, although the game  came out so it's hard to predict what the modding scene will look like. With that said, there are some  concerns:The game is almost a direct copy of Rimworld but with prettier 3D graphics, down to the social mechanics, work priority assignment screen, mental breaks, color of building schematics, etc. It would not be unfair to say they plagiarized Rimworld, an indie game made and maintained by a single person!The two  that I can think of are the implementation of automation in the base game and that light/darkness affects ranged weapon accuracy. The automation system is awesome, but it does leave  to be desired because there are only 9 automation "channels," making it difficult to set up independent automated systems with similar purposes. For example, there are motion detectors that one can use to turn on auto-turrets and floodlights near gates/checkpoints. Well, if you only have one spare automation channel to use and your motion sensors are turning on all your turrets anyway, then it's not really saving you any electricity! It's still very good for things like turning on generators to keep your batteries charged when your wind and solar generators aren't enough or running a day/night cycle for your electric lights though. The decision to use Denuvo by the devs is also very unfortunate. Anti-cheat software in a single-player game? I fully understand that piracy is a concern for game studios, but Denuvo functions exactly like malware: running in the background without your explicit consent, hogging RAM, causing bloat in the game itself, and excessive wear and tear on your SSD. If it walks like a duck and quacks like a duck... If just one dedicated hacker manages to still crack the game, then there's no point to having it and whatever fees Denuvo charged will be wasted anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly recommend this game.If you are like me a person that is used to survival city builder (Banished, Planetbase) and someone that appreciate interaction between its characters (This war of mine) you should play this game. I'll tell some points that marked me, you'll choose if they are relevant to you or not1) Base buildingIn this game, you need to craft your base, litteraly. Its not "i build a kitchen" and all the module are inside, no. You have to take into account the size of the kitchen, the technology used inside (warmed with wood? Electricity?) the localization of the kitchen, because the warmth it produce will be useful to other room... Or a pain to other room. And of course you need to store the food you produce, in a cool place, but also a place that isnt too far away so your character dont waste too much ferry timeTo be improved : As on any production device, its too complicated for me to know what will the kitchen produce, there is something like 20 meals (i love it!) with 20 recipe (i love it!!) but you have to make a list of priority of the things to produce, and something need ingredients that needs themselves to be crafted... And your character wont do this crafting so kinda all of advanced meal will be often undoable2) Characters buildingSome are interested in some domain and will increase their skill very fast, it is simple but efficient and allow you a bit of RP. Plus, if they do the stuff they like (lets say combat) they get a positive modifier (+18), if they do this a lot, they get the state "euphoria" that make them even more efficient. To be improved : I would add more negative and positive trait (yet manageable) to force the player to think the best way to have the most efficient crew. Today you can quasi ignore the things your characters like3) DisastersThats the bad point to me. Not that the disasters arent a good idea but you have no visibility on the time they'll last (which isnt illogical in beginning of game, but less after a few years) and there is no good command toggle, like on planetbase, to tell your characters to go out of the base or in (for example). During "toxic ashes" your character will suffocate if they go outside, but their chores are outside, so you need to manually gather them and force them in your house. During exceptionnal heatwave, if you are a moron like me and have no air conditionner, you want them to spend time outside (it would be interesting to be able to have a modifier for places in the shadow outside)4)  Characters interactionLets not lie; its a work in progressFor now your character like or dislike each other, but i dont really feel any differences in their treatment of othersTo be improved : Give more tastes to human relation. GRRMartin said "the only think writing about is worth is the human feeling". That would make the difference between a good and a extra good game to me5) Tech treeAs often, the tech tree is too fast (you can basically have carbon laser sniper in two years, starting from scrap) but its not really a problem to me, it might be to hardcore fans. Maybe it would be interesting as in XCOM or Ark to add more "tiers" in technologies (Craftman (wood => stone)weapon) / advanced craft  (iron => steel) weapon and tools  and so on. This way youd progress all the time but wouldnt go from zero to big laser warrior hero in a pair of year6) ObservationThe big deception, i think you should be able for the animals as for the plant to know what they produce, and how to exploit them (yes im capitalist)..To be improved :  Domestication of animals and breeding is a must go6) My opinion as for nowThe game is expensive, absolutely unfinished. There is not a lot of bugs. And as you can see my opinion is very positive, why?Because the roots of the game are very good, the ideas behind it too. The team is active and we already had an update (a new map). I think the best idea would be to wait 3/4 months and see if other update have be done, that would maybe make my comment wrong.TL: DR, go and buy it !
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Very addictive.  The introduction of character personalities and growing skill sets into a sim is well done and entertaining.  Looking forward to more worlds to play on, more depth/expansion in exploration missions, ability to tailor game parameters (# of chars, growth rate of angry insects, etc).   Lots of fun now + tremendous long-term potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The clone of Rim World comments were correct.   I liked some things and didn't like others.  The waves of bad guys come pretty often, you can't do a lot of reconfiguration before the next wave.  People walk around so slow that it seems like you can't do much in one day.  Crops are so easy that you just plant and forget, but sadly it takes all day to harvest a few things.   I may come try it again sometime soon, but overall it's a so-so game for me.  I'll give it a thumbs up for effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not bad overall a good start for the developers of this game.  There are some issues that definitely need to be fixed.  I mean I can see some of the stuff that you can and do start off with are there, there are others that are not, not sure why though.  I mean you can start out with different materials to build from yet there is very little stone.  I mean you have to get that later not sure why i think that would be easier to get then wood in a few area especially with the nests.  The only down fall that this game needs is a priority function on what to build what to get and what to look for.  Oh yeah another blow that I have trouble with and not sure why but the AI that runs your peeps need a definite improvement.  I have so far lost people to the thing that should not happen "Starvation", this is where the priorities need fixing.  I have one dedicated cook with another right behind them and they do cook and there is food for them but the damn AI works them to friggin death, I mean come on have them at least have the priority to friggin eat.  I can see no food or none cooked but jesus christ fully loaded and they friggin ignore it to go cut some damn grass WTF.  To me that is the only major issues besides the usual issues.  I would still reccommened but not right away awfully expensive for where it is for now, wait till a few months down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access. Polished in terms of graphics and some content. Some balance and Quality of LIfe issues which the devs already aware about. I think this will be a great survival/management/strategy game. 90 sunk in. FInally got a "good colony" that I've been able to sustain and experience some of the mid game content. Figured out who to get people to strengthen relationships, Build the wedding arch. Craft in winter and immediately plant in spring. Devs aware crafting needs to be faster or degradation of gear and building items needs to be slower. Also travel to and from further resources needs some work.Give it a try. It has a really good feel to it and pretty good graphics, no major slowdowns some lag when attacked by 40+ irritated animals. Still have no idea how to build a 2 story building maybe there's a How To vid somewhere out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Think of it as a much simplified rimworld. In fact, they unabashedly steal ideas and names from Rimworld. This will be good for some people as Rimworld has a steep learning curve and this game is much more user friendly. With that in mind, Rimworld has been out muuuuuch longer and has a ton more content. This is Frontier we're talking tho, so expect no less than 20 paid DLCs in the future just to get to the point of a full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good start. Some significant work needed on the priority and mood system to be viable for long-term gameplay right now.Edit after about 100 hours.It's a decent game but I think it suffers from mid-game fatigue. Once you research most of the pre-carbon technologies (maybe a few in-game days), there isn't much need to continue with your game. It's more exciting to restart and try to do the run better. There is a limit to the fauna and hostile fauna where it becomes a repetitive wave grind. For a long time (2500+ hour Rimworld player), the end-game and replay-ability just isn't there.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game maybe copies a bit too much of Rimworld and feels like a mini version of it in the end.Its nice and tight however, more of a bespoke experience instead of Rim's sandbox style. It does mean that there is so much less here. If you like Rimworld you might not get much out of this , but if you know someone for who the look or density of Rim's experience is too much this would be a great alternative.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's rimworlds prettier looking twin, that's also less refined and slightly stupid in some areas. Rimworld has been brewing for many years tho so it's not really fair to bash on things that can be added in time. If you like rimworld and/or basebuilding I'm sure you will get some hours out of it. If nothing else definately watch for a sale. One thing not mentioned often enough: There's a VERY userfriendly mod-editor built in that makes it a cakewalk to make QoL changes, make it easier/harder, or make your own characters! Huge plus for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth both your time and your money IMO.I find it has excellent graphics, for a game in this genre. It's good survival, base-building, gameplay with an intutive user interface and a cool SiFi theme.Many have compared this to Rimworld, but to be honest it's not as evolved or complicated as RW yet. However, what's in the game right now, is working almost perfectly and I don't really feel like anything is "amiss".There's room for improvement however, and I hope in the future they'll add more stuff, and that they'll also keep being inspired by the good stuff RW already has, since they've been very good at taking it and making it their own.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda like Rimworld, but 3D and simplified.The only thing that is a slight annoyance is that the AI of the characters is pretty awful to work with, they leave jobs on 99% while they work over the scheduled hours of work. They don't collect the dropped items all at the same time, they do it bit by bit even though they haven't reached carry capacity and so on.Beyond the slight annoyances, great game, recommend playing if you enjoy survival defensive games with building and upgrading.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I've got to give this a negative review just to balance out how positive it's over all rating is. It's not bad but it's not particularly good either.First off it is not even close to Rimworld in any aspect, so if that is a drawing point to you then look somewhere else.Positives.Nice enough lookingBuilding mechanics are decent, you can create some cool basesWorkshop has some decent contentNo bugs other than the ones you have to killConsNo terrain management (roads/paths) making a base fit for OCD is nigh on impossible The observe feature quickly plays itself out of existence Manually doing everything is tedious (expeditions are over so quickly and for so little gain that it quickly becomes a chore)Decent sized map but settlers will struggle to cover long distances without passing out so a lot of wasted space New settlers constantly arrive whether you want them to or not and rejecting them gives you a -10 happiness penalty to everyone.It's an ok game but the longer you play it the more frustrating things you notice and the less enjoyment you get. It needs some quality of life improvements at the very least.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not as expected. I was expecting a city-builder type thing, instead the game plays more like the "sims"; micro-management of tasks and managing personally traitsThere are different scenarios, but they are all pretty similar. The basic scenario is... 1/ Crash land on planet with 4 survivors then, build/research your way off. Sounds okay, but it becomes a chore micro-managing  tasks and each new game is pretty much the same.A lot of effort has gone into the visuals, and they are pretty good. The HUD is intuitive and controls easy. The concept is good but there are (fixable) issues with the game-play. For example, you can set general task priorities for each of the characters (nice) but you can't actually control what they do next - I was left wondering for an hour why no-one was supplying my furnace with sticks and no obvious way to remedy (It would be good if the next 20 or so tasks could be shown in a single list and tasks could be added)I am going to continue giving this a go - i've not given up yet---part 2150 hours later... i guess i'm gonna have to change my vote to a thumbs-upThe different planets must be tackled differently, as the resources are different. So this is not as formulaic as I first imagined. The characters do behave differently also, so it matters who the survivors are.There is scope for lots and lots of mods, but there seem to be few published.The UI has it's weakness such as;There is no "map" (could be something that could be earnt)When clicking on a character from a remote resource the UI navigates unexpectedly to the character and its hard to work out where the resource was relative to the character
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I've been loving this game since I bought it. I recommend it, but, Frontier, for the love of all things good, I have to be able to take the dogs, too. I can't just leave them. They've fought and bled beside my people. They're part of the family. FAIR WARNING, DOG LOVERS. DON'T NAME THE DOGS YOU TAME AFTER YOUR BELOVED FAMILY PETS. YOU CANNOT TAKE THEM WITH YOU. PLEASE LEARN FROM MY MISTAKES.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: OK.....that was the most ......annoying last hour of a game I have EVERY played.The AI is absolutely TERRIBLE.  The characters don't follow their schedule or prioritization rules.Power fluctuates strangely and its not obvious why you need so many power stations for a bunch of lights and a handful of work stations.  Maybe someone should go look into what these solar panels and wind generator power in real life.  Cuz yours severely suck.You get to a point in the game where it drags with nothing to do but wait for research to finish.  It gets really boring...and time consuming.   Every time I wanted a 'new survivor' to extend my base you'd make me find a charred body at a wreckage. Then suddenly the whole unit breaks over and over and over....requiring one person whose AI doesn't work to salvage everything trying to keep it alive.  Like 1-2 hours I'm sitting here going "Are you KIDDING ME?" BUT you never get there.  Like FIVE radio signals and they won't send the last rescue pod.  Its like the developer forces you to watch your last survivor die.  Because he's just a sadist.  And nobody thought to save the dog at all?  We're just going to leave it behind? _childDocuments_.review: great game so far, have really enjoyed it. wish it was easier to find more survivors, at a faster rate. you end up losing 1 or 2, but very lucky if you find 1 at all. would be nice if every 1/2 hour a survivor finds your base and wants to join. love the game, would love to see more tech tree branches in the game.update:  have been playing for a couple of days now, the biggest problem that i'm running into is that there is just way to much tasking for 6 people. yes 1 found 2 while exploring.  i find myself waiting for simple tasks and waiting way to long for things to get crafted.  i think you need to find more survivors at a faster rate. every time u open a task it says waiting for survivor, there simply isn't enough survivors to get all the tasks completed. and u had a huge complex going.Bottom line need more survivors or you cannot max out on a base.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Quite captivating, but nonetheless annoying and has a lot of room for improvement in term of optimization.  This is not like Banished where you can just set-it-and-forget-it.  The characters require constant micromanagement because the AI seems extremely inept at order of operations or self-preservation.  For examples:1. There is a salvage site faraway.  A character assigned to that salvage site attempts to leave camp and head to the site when they are at 50% hunger (or rest, or relaxation), so they spend half a day to walk there, then when they get there, they immediately turn around and run back to camp to eat (or rest, or relax).  AI should be optimized to know that, the character should fill up on those bars BEFORE heading out if those bars are low.2. There was a battle to wipe out a bug nest, and there are lots of carcasses laying about.  A character assigned to butcher and harvest the meat, would only butcher, but once they're done, they don't pick up any of the meat and just heads back to camp while leaving it all on the ground.  AI should be optimized to know that, if the character is going back to camp, they should simply gather all the nearby loot while they're at it.3. A character can only carry 1 type of item at a time, so if there are lots of types of items, each a very small amount, then the number of trips the character needs to take to gather all of the loot, becomes astronomically large.  Surely it cannot be that hard to code it, so that the character's Physical stat determines how much "weight" they can carry regardless of type of item.4. The in-game text is full of "engrish" and grammatical errors.  The tutorial is excellent, but flavor text in other places could use some proof-reading...5. Player-controllable units cannot shoot through ceilings and walls, as expected.  So why then is it that Hostile ranged units (Shriekers, Hummingflies) can shoot through ceilings and walls?  Something is grossly wrong with the coding here.  6. Characters with dietary restrictions, should not just starve themselves to death if their choice of food is not available given the circumstances. The vegetarians, for example, should simply suffer a Happiness penalty or something if forced to consume meat when plant food sources are scarce.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRIf its your first survival-sim game I would recommend this heavily starting out since other games expand upon the mechanics greatly however, offer very little hand holding compared to Stranded: Alien Dawn. If you're looking for a different or unique take on the genre you might want to find something else or play Stranded: Alien Dawn i with mods.Stranded: Alien Dawn is undeniably a visually pleasing game. The alien landscapes are brimming with vibrant colors and intriguing details, drawing players into this uncharted world. While the soundscape successfully conveys the alien atmosphere, the survivors' repetitive vocalizations became a little grating over time.Unfortunately, getting used to the controls/mechanics can be a minor hurdle in the early hours. Actions often felt less precise than I'd hoped for. Stranded: Alien Dawn takes clear inspiration from genre heavyweights like Rimworld, but initially, some core systems like combat and medicine felt a bit too simplistic.The early game may feel a bit tame for seasoned survival sim fans, but the challenges ramp up as you explore and draw more attention from the alien wildlife. Be prepared to make some tough choices to keep your colony alive.Stranded: Alien Dawn boasts a captivating setting and the potential for engaging survival gameplay, but it initially feels oversimplified, and clunky controls take some getting used to. It has a burgeoning modding community, offering potential ways to customize the experience. If you're intrigued by the idea of a space survival adventure and are willing to invest time to unlock its strategic depth, Stranded: Alien Dawn may still be a worthwhile journey. However, those looking for an immediately complex and polished experience might want to wait and see how the game develops with updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good (but not great) game. The positive aspects are the crafting (very well balanced), the music, and the interfaces. I like that there are a lot of mods in the steam workshop to tweak the game.What I'm disappointed with is that the resource management aspect is quite easy, especially once you get through the early stages of a mission. Most things are quite plentiful and easy to grow yourself once you have observed them.The main difficulty modifiers seem to be the weather (makes it a little tougher, but pretty easily managed) and the frequency and intensity of attacks from the local wildlife. For me, the battling the animals is by far the most boring and repetitive part of this game. I wished they had focused less on the combat stuff and more on making it a challenge to find and produce the items you need to survive, particularly in the trade scenario. It feels like they went all in on the combat aspects and added the other stuff for a bit of variety but not really to challenge players in any significant way.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: 3D Rimworld... So much potential here. If the developers and the modders (mod are what MAKE Rimworld imho) come through in this game, it could truly be amazing. I've been playing non-stop for a couple days, but I know I'm about to hit the content limit. Please developers - give this game more love, it's so close to being great.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended but with caveats.The early to mid game is great, making something out of nothing and getting your settlement going is enormous fun, however the later into the game you get the less interesting it becomes and the more the design issues start to show.I've enjoyed my 35 hours with it but can't see me playing it much more without some changes.* Most of the map is impractical to use as you can't get your characters to move past jogging speed.  Needs some kind of transport.* Flagged areas have been created to try and help with the first point but it just means you have to split everyone up it doesn't really help and maintaining satellite bases is just a pain.* You spend far too much time late game micromanaging silly decisions that the survivors make, such as walking a long distance to kill/chop/farm something only to have them turn around to go to bed and not even take it with them.  Again I think the flag system is supposed to help with this but it doesn't.* I have 2 survivors with ranching set to priority 1 and STILL i have to keep reminding them to feed the livestock.There is a reviewer on here who's spent 500 hours replaying the early-mid game until they get it perfect.  I think they've got the right idea.  Ultimately the idea is to get them rescued which in practise just means losing characters same as if they had just died so it's not really an incentive to keep going.I will probably keep at it see if i can get any of them rescued and then park it for a couple of years and see if it's improved.Great game don't get me wrong, but it needs some more work.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent base builder - really enjoying the early access. Pretty bug free (apart from the monsters :P). Will probably not play again until a few updates have been made (if planned). Like:Base constructionPlant research/discovery --> crop mechanic Rimworld like people mechanics and traits. Dont like:Monster attacks - would like to be able to turn it off. Its clunky and not super fun. keeping me from playing more tbh.Crafting is very slow. Clothing upkeep / weather setup is a bit like being a fussy mother.  Pulse rifle crop destruction (lesson learnt). No water system - which seems oddly lacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Difficult to understand, and lots of stuff makes no sense.  There is over 3000 food and 24 cooked items, yet people are starving, and eating raw items?????, 3 Dogs die because the keep feeding the dogs hay and vegetables???????? Why??  There is 7 wind turbines and 4 solar panels, with 3 batteries, yet devices have no power????  The concept and most play is good, but the stuff listed above makes the game super not FUN and makes no sense???  Food is rotting and people and animal starve?????
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of my favourite games, and here's why:-Scenarios each with their own focus (survival, production to trade, fighting, and research)-Base Building with lots of options-Meaningful fleshed out characters-Good variety during game set up which can change things up-Intuitive controls and menus-Farming-Research-Production LineAnd best of all ...... DOGS. Always tame the dogs.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Not just 'Rimworld but 3d' but far more basic in features and stiff in how scenarios play out as well. Huge, gorgeous maps but you'll never even visit more than 15% of one due to slow movement speed and no vehicles. Lots of research and cool features, but a static RNG will lock you out of a good number of them. Static colonists with backstories, but they don't interact with each other in meaningful ways. A tiny variety of weapons and armor, structures are boring as well. There's some interesting alien species, but enemies are just waves of mostly earth bugs-but-bigger. Maybe there will be more updates later, but as far as Rimworld clones go this one is thoroughly disappointing for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: A really good isometric Survival/colony management game. Instead of playing just one survivor, you are in charge of a group of 4 (more can be added later) spacefarers that crashland on an alien planet. At the start you scavenge for food, but a few hours in you are able to build lasers and turrets. The Alien swarms coming at your base steadily increase in difficulty, so you need to constantly improve your base if you want to survive. The map is Seed generated, so every game will be a little different. You have an impressive amount of survivors to build your starting team from, and each one has a speciality and a flaw that makes the teambuilding an exciting excercise as well. The game is in early access, but there is already so much to like here. This one gets two thumbs up from me. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I have found my new favourite game to play!  Even in EA, S:AD offers solid gameplay and just enough RNG to keep you on your toes.  The characters offers a good amount of diverse options to make you have to think carefully about who you start your colony with and I really enjoy that your colonists know close to nothing about the strange planet they crash into.  The crafting progression is practical and progression steady enough to keep me interested.  I absolutely recommend hauling out your credit card for this one!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: During gameplay there occurs a few points of frustrating situations. Such as survivors prioritizing long distance scavenging over crafting when being severely cold or after wildlife started attacking. Forcing you to draft. Demands micromanagement every second in Winter season even 'only' on hard mode. Quite frustrating when you look away for 5 sec. Also, flying mobs occur so sudden without warning. Would be nice with an initiating attack.  Otherwise a lovely game and I would recommend any day. Great job. 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Character AI can be frustrating at times.  They can be starving or complaining about the food, yet there are resources nearby and a stove to cook on.  Similarly with tailoring clothes,  "Awaiting resources" when they are nearby and people are freezing to death.  Unless you unassign every other type of work to force them into that activity, they would rather starve and die of hypothermia.Having said that, the game does excel in other areas and I think overall it's worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a perfect copy of Sapiens but in a sci-fi enviroment and better graphics, with some Rimworld mechanics.It's a game that requires a long term approaching and your base needs to be well planned in advance, to avoid bottlenecks in future.At current state i can define the game as "interesting" (as Sapiens is) and can be a great game if developed more: with little effort the developers could expand craftable items and add some more mechanics. The technological tree could be expanded too, to add more flavour.Some stuff that requires a fix ASAP:-once you create crops you will spend a considerable amount of time repelling wild beasts, trying to eat your food. Building a fence just adds more wasted time, since the fence needs to be repaired very often. Wild lfe searching for crops should be intended as a random event imho.-your survivors will be haunted by every sort of sickness of the body and mind. Basically at least one of your survivors will be ALWAYS sick in a way or another, in a sort of rotation of pain and desperation. Recreation utilities don't seem to help that much (they don't even work at all imho...). Rimworld has a similar mechanic too, but remedies are more effective and frequency is more balanced.-strange to say but this is the first time in a game like this that crops give an enormous amount of yeld, which basically requires a LOT of space to be stored and before refrigeration basically you loose 90% of your yeld before winter comes... Some more balancing in yeld amount and time to spoil could be took in consideration.-Not sure but i think it's not possible to level the terrain. Can't say if this is on purpose.Anyway, as a early access the game is good, i consider the money well spent. Had no crashes or performance issues. If the developers continue to improve the game the result could be VERY interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good, The UI is a bit stiff even after setting up the options. I am sure that will be taken care of before game launch. _childDocuments_.review: A game I really want to love, but just don't.It's beautiful, it has great mechanics (for the most part), the controls are pretty good (that there's no way to turn off edge scrolling is my biggest complaint!) The core of a solid and highly polished game appears to be here......but it's just... boring.There's a deep research tree, but progressing through it manages to feel both trivial and a chore at the same time, and unlocking stuff never feels like a reward, because it just means "more stuff to do" when you're already constrained by how much stuff you can actually get done with your characters.This ends up being a running theme: every bit of new gameplay you unlock ends up being a "so what?" because you're already capped on how much stuff you can fit into the schedule, and the new things are largely just the same things as the basics, so what's the point? You've already got that covered. You don't ever feel that you're progressing.Then you get escalating alien attacks that appear to have little to do with your progress and exist "just because". I've encountered no themic explanation of why a bunch of random critters spawn outside my base and attack me every 15 minutes. It just feels super gamey and immersion breaking, and rather than building tension it's just an annoyance, one you either deal with easily or utterly wrecks you.There doesn't seem to be any actual gameplay mechanism to ride this difficulty curve without tech rushing combat stuff and doing nothing else, and hoping RNG doesn't slap you with a bunch of permanent negative modifiers on your colonists that will degrade your save for the rest of eternity.None of this feels like a challenge, it just feels arbitrary and leads you to hoping you notice your already-slow colonist has randomly been slapped with a -10% speed modifier for the rest of the game before you progress too much further so that you can save-scum to just avoid having even more fun sapped out of the tedium.Oh right, tedium. Game is hella tedious. Even on max speed, everything takes FOREEEEEVER to do. Not helped by the fact that colonists will take so much time walking even the length of your base to chop a single tree of wood before immediately turning around to go get a meal, then walk back, chop another tree, then walk back again to play darts, then walk back to chop a tree, then get tired. I get it, building an efficient base is a thing, but colonists move so slowly that you need to build a full set of entertainment buildings and food stores and everything every 20 squares to stop this, and I'm already bored just writing that, let alone hating the idea of idiotic base designs to deal with gameified mechanics.And ultimately, what's the point? The game never feels like it has a point. It doesn't feel like you're telling a story like Rimworld or other self-directed experiences, nothing that interesting ever happens. I've sunk thousands of hours into games like Dwarf Fortress, Rimworld, Banished, and Factorio, and every single new save I created in those felt like it had a story, even the ones I set out with no theme or idea behind. I remember those experiences even years later.This game, I load my save from yesterday and I'm like "so, what was I doing? I dunno and I don't really care", at no point have I felt like I have even a self-imposed objective I'm working towards. Nothing at all ever feels like progress or a success. It just feels like a grind to nowhere, and then the game will tell me I've won. Or that I've died.Either outcome fills me with the same indifference.

_childDocuments_.review: The opinion that this game is Rimworld3D isn't quite wrong.  It COULD BECOME Rimworld3D, with time,attention and dedication of the dev team. It is said it crashes.  I have yet to experience a crash.  (I7, GTX1660Ti, 16 GB RAM)  This is a good foundation for a 3D game in the Dwarf Fortress -> Rimworld family tree.  But this one also takes inspiration from Space Haven, which is particularly noticeable in the menu system.  I like seeing reuseable ideas.  They do it in Metroidvanias; you pick one up randomly and you know virtually all the controls going in.  Likewise this, if you know Rimworld (I have 3600+ hrs).There are balance issues of course, and an awful lot of things that need to be done before this can be considered Rimworld3D.  But the foundation is here.  I'm in early in hopes it will help the game grow.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this title. It's very rare that I request a refund for a game on Steam, but in this case I did.First and foremost, the game has no soul. There is no immersion whatsoever; the art and music and everything are just kind of... blah. It lacks any kind of style or character.The 'choose from these pre-built characters' aspect is a huge mistake/weakness. As others have stated, most of the characters are terrible, so it's really more like 'choose from these ~6 or so characters that are not so horribly unbalanced as to be unplayable.'The game is very very simplified and dumbed down compared to say RimWorld, DF, Songs of Syx, etc... it's a lot of prebuilts and templates. The combat is a joke, it's just swarms of alien insects occasionally attacking you, which you attempt to corral into a path where you have built some turrets to deal with them - kind of lame tower defense style. There don't seem to be intelligent races or other settlements opposing you.For bonus points, the devs have already raised a lot of red flags... If you read closely in the EA text, they say that EA will last at least 6 months." HUGE red flag - EA generally goes on for a couple of years at minimum. Then in the discussion forums when players asked about a roadmap, the devs cryptically responded that "we don't have a roadmap to share at the moment, but we can say that there will be updates coming to the game in the future." Uhhhhh yeah obviously. Holy crap do they not understand what EA is all about? Seems like they don't. If you are expecting a lot of additional content, I wouldn't hold you breath - nor do I get the impression that updates are a priority to the devs. It strongly feels like they think they basically have a complete game here, and they are just using EA to beta test for a few months and then will call it a day. (Maybe their plan is to then roll out a bunch of DLC with stuff that really should have been included in the base game?) The laissez faire attitude toward updates is especially concerning when one looks at the forums and sees the steadily increasing number of bugs and issues being reported - no way to remove spoiled food, insulation issues with doors and doorways, and issues with placing structures and objects on structures, to name a few.Oh and they are shutting down and deleting comments in the forums when they don't like what players have to say. So again I say... maybe they don't really understand what EA is all about.

_childDocuments_.review: I´m really sorry but at this moment I cannot in good conscience recommend this game. Here is why: While the overall design looks beautiful and allows an in-dept management of the various aspects of a survivor camp, herein lies the massive problem this game has - micromanagement. The camp and character management of Stranded: Alien Dawn is ridiculously complex to the point that the game is unplayable. You cannot just order your characters to do anything directly. You mark what is to do, which leads to a storage shelf marked to be emptied and deconstructed to keep standing where it stand for days (literally!), resulting in the stuff in the shelf being exposed to the elements and rot away. You enter orders to make new clothes and nothing happens for days. It says "waiting for resources", but nobody picks up the resources and makes the bloody clothes. So, somewhere in the complex chain of getting stuff from the storage, bringing it to the tailoring table and making some clothes is something missing. The problem here is that you have no idea where to start looking, which is - how do I say this nicely - ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ frustrating. The game needs a major overhaul of character behaviour and mechanics (oh yes, they behave like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ morons - run out in the cold for no apparent reason and then complain about hypothermia) as well as complete redo of tasking and commands. Also an overhaul of psychology/happiness aspect is urgently needed. For space travellers they not only ♥♥♥♥♥ about everything, but also don´t do anything about it, no matter how many toys and distractions you build for them. Happiness goes down fast and is sometimes just impossible to restore - or it stays low, leading to one temper tantrum after the next, which is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying and frustrating. Until this is done, I cannot recommend this game and give it a 4/10 - do not buy. Sadly, given the layout, look and feel, possebilities etc. I would have given this game an 8/10, but character behaviour, controls, happiness etc. are so bad and frustrating that I have to take off 4 points. Edit: I managed to make the moron survivors to somewhat do what they were supposed to do by clearing the schedule and leaving the activity in place they are supposed to do - but that didn´t really work as they do everything else before what they are supposed to - unless you stop any and all production lines too. However, that leads to other things not being done etc. So no, no actual improvement here but a kind of workaround that comes kinda close to a solution. Again, it cannot be that making a couple of shirts takes all summer.Too bad close enough only counts at throwing horseshoes, handgrenades or thermo-nuclear weapons. 4/10 it is.Edit 2023: Since the game left early access, I though I had another go at it. Sadly they didn´t solve any of the problems I mentioned. They smoothed a bit around the edges, added some features, but the problems I mentioned remain. Well, so does my verdict - 4 out of 10, do not buy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderfully immersive gaming experience that scratches my fantasy base-building itch. Like many others, I'd liken the character-control to Rimworld and the base building to Dawn of Man, yet, the graphics and art style brings this science-fiction based alien theme to brilliantly rendered life with a good serving of The Sims realism in there too. PROS:1) Seamless and stable game play...if there are any bugs, I've not encountered any during 124 hours of exploration so far. 2) Breathtaking landscape graphics, and truly beautiful alien animal/insect designs and skins. I enjoyed the 'Observation' tasks to discover and correlate all the species in the current game world. I also love that every biome type will have a couple of different types of fauna and flora, as well as altered recipes to keep things more mixed as you play through Sobrius (Temperate Meadow), Desertum (Hot Dry Desert) and Saltu (Humid Jungle).3) Micro-management heaven: put item counts on or off and designate what can be stored on a shelf or in a stockpile, and what should not. Have fun building your base its own large storage warehouse because you'll need plenty of space to keep the vast amount of items and ingredients you will encounter.4) Research, Build & Craft everything you're going to need to first survive, and then, to thrive. There is always plenty to do here, sometimes, more than you can handle with too few colonists.5) Identify fauna and flora, then farm, cook and produce saleable products in order to conduct trade with passing spaceships, and also, to buy in anything you desperately need with the currency of Galacticoins.   6) Take care of your survivors, pets and animals with God-Like control: you can draft and move all your characters, and give them orders according to what you want them to do immediately, later or when they find the time for it in a task queue system.  7) A WINNER for me: You can turn off the attack threats as you make the choices for your initial game set-up, and play either the chilled out or fighting-tooth-and-nail-for-everything type of game that you most enjoy.   CONS:1) Character pathing is sometimes needlessly indirect, but it's not the greatest frustration if you just leave them to get on by themselves. They eventually get to where they are going, even if its not via the most direct route.2) Some of the micro-management needs a little tweaking, for eg. the animal feeding troughs. If you feed a carnivore, expect that your entire stock of 300 dried meat will end up in the trough because you can't designate half your stock to colonist consumption, and the other half to farm animal consumption. But again, only a minor frustration and there are ways to work around that. 3) The Electrical Grids and accompanying producers/users system of 'control switches' is quite complicated, and requires a vast amount of resources to build once you get to the point of trying to establish radio communication with the inter-planetary world, and beyond. Perhaps I just don't understand how to get it to cross-function or I'm doing something wrong, but it never works out correctly for me. I just bypass the automation mishugas and simply make my colonists switch stuff on and off as I need it. It's not brilliant, but it works.I confidently recommend this game to fans of base-building, micro-management, and jeopardy/combat in colonising fantasy-realism worlds. You're going to enjoy unpacking just about every aspect of this one. The developers have put a lot of love into it and it shows. It is well-worth its current asking price so I am pleased to support the on-going development of this richly created game by taking it on as one I will be buying more expansions for, as and when they are released. I'm looking forward to the onward journey.   You've done a magnificent job so far, Haemimont Games.  Regards, GQ

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. I'd say it's a simpler Rimworld in alot of ways. It hits a lot of those Rimworld checkboxes. Rather than pointing out the laundry list of what I love about the game, I'll just say there is a LOT.Some of things I didn't like were: 1. Zoning. In Rimworld you could Zone areas so animals or people wouldn't leave certain areas. For example: if there is a cold snap, I could confine them to being indoors and they would still do work in the base and stay warm. 2. Inventory Managment was pretty lacking. Rimworld does it right with stockpile priority, durability and quality threshholds. 3. A trashing mechanic where you can choose to trash items from stockpiles and storage. 4. The ability to drop items you craft on the ground and keep crafting so other workers could haul them. 5. Clothing priority and eating Priority (Rimworld had outfits for the seasons etc)Maybe this will come with updates or mods and aren't really game breaking. Just some things I ran into that left me wanting to go play Rimworld so I could control the things I wanted to lol. You have a smaller group in the game compared to Rimworld, so efficiency is key. It would be nice to create 1 square zones with higher priority than your main inventory storage so that workers would bring items to the 1 sqaure zone located next to a crafting table. This would reduce walk times for your workers and they could keep working at the crafting station.

_childDocuments_.review: Same Genre as Rimworld, it borrows heavy influence from the UI. I think it is done well and hope it becomes more robust over time with new labors for the characters. I really enjoy the 3D it makes the characters really resonate with me and I find myself playing more role play than just efficient like I usually do with these games.I think the characters are a huge strength and I hope to see all kinds of cool creative ones added. Its fun to choose a character to build around fill spots with their family and then throw in a wild card character with no family members to round out the squad.I think it is a fair price with hopes of a good long time of support from the devs. The game works which is always a good sign for a day one early access title. I think if it goes on sale for >25$ it is a no brainer must buy for anyone who likes this genre. Otherwise buy it if you like the genre and can afford full price, you might really enjoy yourself.The biggest weakness for me is the music though. It sounds like rimworld at home which isn't good for a few reasons. This game feels more scifi than scifi western like vanilla rimworld is. So the twangy guitar doesn't fit. And there is one song with a loud boom over and over that just has got to go.

Double shot is amazing especially defending base and hunting meat.- RAW INSECT MEAT are abundant since most monsters that you will fight are insects. So take advantage of farming CHITINS to produce meats, fats, oils even fuel.- Concrete Tower can protect you from flying monsters. Add Machine Gun Turrets for damage.- OBSERVE PLANTS! Took me a year to figure out how to get things like Tea, cloths and others.- Get someone at least level 3 Farming skill. So youll be able to plant veggies, grains and cloths.- (Interested) on Skill are much better than innate skill. _childDocuments_.review: CAVEAT -They created DLC but the game is hollow in vanilla?This is very much like Rimworld, with some unique features. It looks pretty good graphically. HOWEVER, there is a lot missing, some soul and some content, the pathing is not great, the queuing tasks is very limited it seems, significantly less depth to using resources, the mobs seem to exponentially grow EACH attack (tell me if I can do something to stop that?), it feels like its missing a lot of content if I am comparing it to vanilla RImworld. IF I am not comparing it. Its a pretty good game that needs some work. I dont regret buying it. If they add more content for free and flesh this out more, it will be a powerful alternative and leave a mark like rimworld. If not I wish them the best, and will play it until it loses its glimmer because right now it doesn't have that replay value I feel when playing Rimworld. Update about 35 hours in reporting issues:Cant release wild or tame animals from trap, I have to kill them or wait till they die.Cant queue walking path beyond twoNot getting anything but food from most mobs, lack of contentGame spawns giant mobs of bugs inside my camp walls and sometimes outside, they just magically appear with no rhyme or reason, no coming from off map.Auto lead after train sometimes seems to happen but usually it doesn't. Changing tasks or drafting someone just drop item, no option to put in inventory while drafted often leaving items long distances from base and having to make two trips. Pawns don't look for closest item, instead they will go all the way to storage despite the needed item next to them. Nice to have option to leave housing door open. Will walk far to get med kit then walk far back near were order was to heal self regardless of distance,. Does salvaging improve physical?Cant can complete marriage task unless the object is very close to middle of start position.Allow assign cabinet for certain people El cooking stove wont mirror basic crafting list. If in tachyon source and looking at survivors stats the +1 bonus will not show up until you close and reopenCant lead while in draft modeMy pawns will never complete marriage despite how close they are. It says they didn't make very shortly after the time it starts. The attacking A.I. seems to have odd paths sometimes allowing me to cheese kill. There doesn't seem to be much in the way of influencing increased relations between colonists. There is no cover implementation that I have noticed. The lack of other groups of people isn't terrible, but just fighting hoards of bugs that randomly spawn in increasingly large numbers breaks immersion and feels like there is no source from which they came, just a rhythmic timer that the DM of this RPG decides magically appear next to your base or in it. I have 7 survivors and have explored about 20 hours away. Not having electricity has made defending challenging at 200ish mobs.

_childDocuments_.review: To summarize what this game is: it's basically Rimworld 3D. Everything in the game is more or less shamelessly stolen from Rimworld. I mean almost literally everything. To the point where I suspect that a lawsuit from Rimworld would have a pretty good chance of winning in court. Now, if there ever was a game you'd want to make a 3D version of, then Rimworld would be a pretty dang good choice and so this is a pretty dang good game. And Rimworld stole a lot from Dwarf Fortress in turn, so anyway...Standed: Alien Dawn is not quite as complex as Rimworld though. Those who might find Rimworld a bit too intimidatingly complex might like this one better - it is very similar but without the extreme micromanagement possibilities of Rimworld. Unlike Rimworld you cannot (as of yet anyway) create your own custom characters. Instead you have to pick from a pool of pre-generated but well-made ones. You'll ideally want at least one NPC who can fight, one who can build, one who can farm etc from start, or you might find yourself overwhelmed by aliens or starving to death. You start with 4 but can find up to 8 in total (or 10 with a recently added option). Each of course with their own skills and quirks, all got some strength/weaknesses. Like for example one guy is a real killing machine in combat, but others find him intimidating and he knows he is dying (and will eventually do so after a few in-game years). One girl is a  research genius but real clumsy with most practical matters and doesn't help out that much initially save for coming up with new inventions. One guy is a great jack of all trades but got a real bad mood and easily gets depressed. And so on. Characters can train most skills though if you let them grind enough, so this is mostly a matter for early on in the game. They also seem to be more or less compatible with other characters. Some are family. Like in Rimworld, they build up positive/negative relations with other characters. Romance is supposedly possible, though so far I've yet to see it myself.The game is nicely bug-free for an early access game. The devs should be given credit for being focused and making sure everything is running smoothly before coming up with new features. Far too many games suffer from "new creative features are fun to make, while bugs are unfun to track down and hard to fix". This game could easily have a tonne of graphics glitches for example, but there's just a few very minor ones.Graphics aren't really top priority for this genre of base building survival game, but the graphics are very nice by genre standards and I was able to crank them up quite a bit while still running smoothly on a pretty old gamer PC. There are a few minor glitches but nothing major, overall it looks real pretty, with day/night cycle, weather and season changes making the map change its look quite a bit over time.I particularly like the visual item storage system. Every single thing you farm and stockpile can be placed in piles and shelves that literally grow by one item at a time - stuff isn't just tossed in piles with numbers or some container with an inventory window. So you can literally see how much food you've stockpiled for the winter or when it is dwindling (yes there are numbers too of course). Building materials and the like is best stored outdoors underneath a roof in a shed, while more precious items like crafting ingredients and medicine is best to store on shelves inside the building.Like Rimworld, food eventually grows stale unless refridgerated or frozen. Early on you can store food in cold rooms and similar to make it last longer, before you invent electricity and fridges.You can research picking and similar preservation technologies which are handy early on.And like Rimworld, you pretty much need one of your characters to be a 'kitchen slave', cooking all day long. Well, you don't -have- to - many forms of food can be eaten raw without health consequences, but you really want the mood bonuses from food as the most efficient way by far to keep morale up. The better the cook, the fancier the food you can unlock and the better the mood bonuses.I think some of the crafting and cooking timers are a bit unbalanced. Like, a crafter could spend all day making simple smoke pipes out of dried tobacco and then the whole gang smoke that up in 5 minutes in the evening... not time well spent. For complex things like making firearms and electronics, the craft timers are better balanced.The combat system is quite crude and there's not many options. Basically rifle > pistols > bows > melee. Supposedly you should build your own automated defenses and mainly rely on those when a hostile creature attack wave spawns. But once you got your hands on a couple of sniper rifles, you can have a few of your characters solo the whole attacking horde. Initially these don't attack instantly but stands around waiting for a while before doing so (like in Rimworld...). While they do that you can have your snipers pick of a few, pull a smaller band of creatures away from the horde, kill 'em off and then repeat. This feels a bit poorly balanced and the hostile AI is dumb as can be. Well they are mindless zerg:ish aliens I guess, but still. But on the other hand you might not have the luxuary of having several combat-oriented characters and then automated defenses is the way to go.Healing skill doesn't play as big a role as it could. Unless you get completely mauled and nearly whiped out in an attack, characters can quite easily heal themselves even with poor skill. Characters with trained healing only get to shine when someone is really close to death, which doesn't happen often at all once you got the hang of defenses.Also the very detailed wound/body part system of Rimworld/Dwarf Fortress wasn't used, for better and worse. No craftable cybernetics or organ transplantations as of yet, though it smells as if this is something planned for the future.One of the very few original features of this game (as in not also present in Rimworld) is that you initially don't know anything about the alien plants and creatures. Someone with high research skill has to study them first. Is this edible, is this dangerous, what can we do with this etc. And once a plant is studied, you can grow it using farming instead of chasing it down in the wild. This is a nice system but the lack of RNG is a huge missed opportunity. Imagine if some plants had random characteristics every playthrough. Imagine if some plants were very similar and if you didn't study them you risked picking a poisonous one instead of the real. Imagine if there was a herbalist skill so that if you send Connor the mercenary sniper to gather herbs instead of Laara born a farmer, you'll end up with poison ivy for dinner. That would have added another dimension to the game but alas procedural generation of this wasn't implemented.Overall, a very good base builder/survival game. Nice new content is getting added, previously a whole new desert biome was released, as well as a taming/pet system.
