_childDocuments_.review: A decent competitor to Rimworld. Good as it is now, but man if this thing had gotten more content this could have been an easy recommendation over Rimworld. As it stands, I think most people will agree Rimworld is the better game, but I can't imagine many fans of Rimworld wouldn't also like this game.Basically this is a colony sim that took inspiration from Rimworld and in many ways tried to improve or at least change the formula. There are no randomly generated survivors, instead all of them are unique characters with their own traits who when they die, die for good. This actually allows for some interesting situations such as trying to play around a character who refuses to do certain tasks, or having a limited amount of time to finish the game before a character's terminal health condition kills them. Each character also has a unique character model with every item of clothing. Compared to Rimworld, this makes it so each character has more actual "character", but it also means there can only be a limited amount of characters in the game. Every character will always be a known quantity rather than the randomness of Rimworld.In terms of general gameplay, this game has one serious advantage over Rimworld, and that's the introduction of a Z layer due to it being 3d. Height matters for construction and for shooting. Combined with the freedom you have in room construction, you can create very elaborate bases, with platforms for elevated turrets and areas where the walls will block ranged enemies from shooting in. Even the tutorial actually does a good job of showing how this can drastically impact optimal base defense strategies. Speaking of, the tutorial is overall pretty good, which is unusual for this genre of game.Other than that, there's typical colony builder gameplay mixed in with some unique mechanics. You farm crops, tame and hunt animals, build structures, do research, craft gear, cook food, and treat wounds. Where things get a little interesting is in requiring "observation" of local flora and fauna before you can figure out what to do with most of it. It's an alien world with things none of the survivors have seen (and dogs for some reason), so they have to spend some time learning about it in order to figure out uses for plants, or how to tame animals. There's also an expedition mechanic where you send survivors on hot air balloon trips to look for resources or check out sites off map, occasionally resulting in you obtaining various unique rewards such as other survivors or gear you can't craft yet.The main issue holding me back from recommending this over Rimworld to most people is simply the low amount of content. There's plenty there, but not plenty compared to Rimworld, which is still clearly being worked on. It's not clear if this game will ever get another update, but it really does not need much more in order to really stand out as a top tier colony sim. The main issue right now is the low enemy variety. There's multiple scenarios, but outside of the DLC one, each one just has you fighting a few varieties of bugs, which eventually makes having automated turrets and mechsuits feel like a bit overkill. The DLC scenario adds robots to replace the bugs, but again, it's still not a lot of variety.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this is Rimworld with pretty graphics, and not nearly as much polish.More in depth, however, this game isn't bad, it just needs more time in the oven.  There's a very solid foundation of a game in there, and I like the "exploration" aspect much better than what Rimworld uses to serve a similar aspect of gameplay.The graphics are good all around: characters look great, equipment changes their appearance appropriately, there's a good amount of native flora and fauna, though it requires some suspension of disbelief that they just so happen to fit into what humans need to create a functioning "society".  I think it would have been more interesting to see more things like the plant that you harvest to create low-tier armor, though its name escapes me at the time of writing.  I would have found the game much more enjoyable AND immersive if we had found ways to use native materials to fill similar roles to materials we're used to for our modern society, but that may be a personal taste issue.  The music is also a positive, it sets the appropriate moods, but it's not a soundtrack you'd likely want to listen to on its own.  And as I said, there's a solid gameplay concept at its base, and while I like the ways it departs from similar games, nothing it does really sets it apart from the rest of the crowd.Now for the negatives, and while they aren't numerous, they're honestly really damning. My biggest complaint is the lack of optimization around character schedules.  Other reviews mention similar problems, and while I thought that could be to those players not fully understanding mechanics or how to schedule properly, I'm sad to say those are accurate criticisms and the optimization is SO poor that it actually hurts the game massively.  Especially considering games like Rimworld have things that can make your colonists crazy fast (either at their jobs or at moving), which this game does not.  Which leads into the second major negative: task efficiency.  Another complaint I saw that I considered stemmed from a lack of understanding how the systems worked, turned out to be accurate as well.  It simply takes too long to perform most of the vital tasks that each colonist is assigned to do, primarily cooking and crafting.  Weapons, or at least the ones I managed to try and make, were acceptable, and in some cases I'd say even too short, but clothing and armor, which are much more vital and deteriorate much more quickly, take significantly longer.  So much so, that even a maxed our crafter couldn't keep up with his OWN needs for clothing and armor (and that was even with someone making the materials so that all he did was craft the clothing/armor, eat and sleep).The positive takeaway is that both these major issues that make the game basically not worth playing (or at least for me) is that they can be addressed, though maybe not easily.  The scheduling issue is, imo, really about the slow movement.  I think if colonists moved between 75% and 100% faster, this would alleviate that problem.  The length of time it takes to perform most of the tasks isn't really too bad (with the exceptions of cooking and crafting clothing/armor), so just adjusting the travel speed of characters would make a huge difference.  And the crafting times just need to be reduced, and while armor should just be a little faster, the essential pieces of clothing (the "left side" of the character equipment) should have a much MUCH shorter completion time.  The realism aspect makes sense in that regard, but by that metric, the deterioration of equipment is way too insanely high.  They could make gear last longer to solve this problem, too, but they'd have to at LEAST quadruple the length of time they last, if not more.

Everything(specifically crafting; I can understand research taking long) takes too long in comparison to how fast the various troubles come up.I have mixed feeling towards this game. The experience is similar to Oxygen Not Included where you have to micromanage your survivors but you don't get to micromanage them enough. For example, I forgot to turn on a turret before a seige, so I "un-drafted" a survivor and turned off all of his activities except Handling, but instead of turn the turret on, he just idled. I survived a year in the game and I had to spend all of that time just trying to survive without getting to go on the attack against the nests. _childDocuments_.review: tl;wr: Stranded: Alien Dawn (S:AD) shows a lot of promise, but it's not quite there yet.Everyone compares it to Rimworld, and I'll do the same.Superficially, Rimworld works because the mechanics are deep, it exposes them all to you, the graphics are easy to grasp, and there's always something interesting going on. It also wholeheartedly embraced mods, and has gone to big lengths to make modding easy, including tutorials on how to decompile the game.S:AD left me wondering about the mechanics, and while the graphics are gorgeous, the characters routinely fall into the uncanny valley, and uses Denuvo DRM to prevent decompiling, which also gets mentioned a lot in the EULA. So while bugs in Rimworld would get fixed quickly by the community, S:AD will be more limited in what's possible. Which is a shame, because it could be *so good*.The biggest disappointment is the writing. I can't express how much it feels like someone copied and pasted from ChatGPT. Let's look at the example of 'Hydroponics Racks':What the heck? A hydroponics rack using soil instead of water is called a 'planter box', or a 'greenhouse', or an 'indoor farm'. The game doesn't have aeration, pH, or pesticide mechanics. By the stage you've researched these you've been growing things outdoors for quite a while. The whole thing is just bad writing that doesn't actually tell you *why* you'd want this.Unfortunately, this is the level of writing throughout all the game. It routinely breaks immersion, and I still don't know why a number of structures and technologies exist.Where Rimworld exposes lots of information (and has mods that expose more), S:AD makes it hard just to get basic things that should be obvious. Case in point being farming. There are different soil types, and some plants grow better in some types than others. But how can you tell the difference? As far as I know, the *only* way is to try and build a farm, and carefully see what is reported when you mouse over a patch of soil. There's no fertility overlay. One crop depletes the soil it's grown in, but doesn't give any details on how quickly, and I have no idea what happens if it's put in a 'hydroponics farm', or if I can even do that.So what does the game do well? Well, the graphics and building are good, although there's a learning curve to using them. The discovery mechanics are very good; you can't plant a plant or really know much about an animal or thing until you've spent some time observing it. The animal animations are , everyone loves to play with the big cow-thing I tamed and it's clearly into it. The game has some basic automation baked-in; you can have devices switch on/off based upon movement, temperature, time, and battery levels. You can have workbenches and furnaces mirror each other, which makes a lot of crafting management easier. You can do multi-level constructions, there's some solid tower-defence mechanics. You can 'craft until X' to make sure meals and clothes are automatically stocked up, but you can't 'craft with excess' to automate some of the bumper crops you'll be harvesting.With better writing, more quality-of-life (eg: fertility overlay, temperature overlay, being able to pin resources, etc), removal of Denuvo, and some more furniture options, and some balancing, S:AD has the potential to be a really great game. The game is still getting lots of updates, and I recommend it because it has so much promise, but right now it's just a 'good' game that's very pretty.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played many management genres, but this one is the best imo.  To me this is what makes it the best:- The Devs nailed what so many have failed to do when it comes to buildings and being able to see inside and design the inside.  Putting a roof on does not block everything unless you zoom in 10x to take the roof away.  Same thing with the walls.  It will show the walls but as you move closer they remove to have great vision.  It just flows and you aren’t playing with the camera angle to see what you want to see.  This should be the standard. - Love the similarities to Rimworld, but how different they are too.  Graphics are gorgeous.  Love having to observe something new to know what it does.  - I like having the ability to plant crops without getting the seeds elsewhere after IDing the vegetation.  Taking out the micromanagement, but still allowing the perfect amount of micro management is my favorite part of this game.  - storage is so simplistic. Awesome work devs on making it where things can stack and not have to take up half a map of storage on the ground because only 1 item fits in a slot.  The Devs very clearly took all the games like this, did their homework on what could be improved, removed the tiny annoyance things and this is the end result.   Awesome job putting in that time to really understand that small nuisances makes a big impact on play. Game is just fun, smooth, beautiful, allows you to be creative and destroy what you have and start over anywhere on the map without feeling exhausted. Glad I bought it, especially on sale.  Only change I would have is the ability to make the meals into emergency rations right away instead of make the food then pack them.  I didn’t see anyway to change that and by the time I made 20 meals to make into the emergency they had spoiled so it was a lot of back and forth micro in that one small area.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely polished for Early Access. This game borrows a lot from various other games, to the point that if you play a decent amount of colony sims you will actually pick this up very quickly as the systems will be familiar. That said, I don't really have a problem with that because they clearly knew what they were doing and picked and chose great elements. As an example, this uses a Rimworld-esque "Job Priority" system. No need to reinvent the wheel, that's a great system that doesn't need fixing. What I would like to see more is a bit more "character." At this point the mechanics are great, everything runs well, there is a good level of challenge (things that I feel like some other derivative Colony Sims get completely wrong), but there's nothing that really stands out to me that is particularly unique or compelling. But I think they could get there. There are hints and some trails that they could go down that could make this very intriguing. For example, they might lean into the pre-built characters as opposed to other colony sims with randomized character gen, and make this more of a handcrafted narrative as opposed to a "Story Generator" type Colony Sim. They could expand on the (currently somewhat barebones) expedition system to develop compelling storylines and player decisions. Just a couple thoughts. TLDR Great mechanics, borrows a lot from other colony sims but generally good things and implemented well, could use some more distiniguishing characteristics to come into its own and feel less derivative.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's like "The Sims" but stranded on an Alien planet. Actually, it's way better than just that. Pros:1. Excellent core gameplay loop2. The extra game modes are fun!3. The tech progression is satisfying.4. Graphics are good!5. Building and management systems are solid and should be somewhat familiar to Surviving Mars fans.Cons:1. Character AI needs a bit of work. While the task priority system does fix some headaches, you'll eventually need to manually manage things to repair in time for the next wave.2. Enemy AI needs work as well. Right now there's a clear meta-game of "Create an opening in your wall that leads to a series of traps" that tends to work okay. I'd like to see the AI get a bit more clever, like splitting into groups and attacking different sides and other more novel tactics. The enemy ai also will even fall asleep instead of attack. 3. Desert maps lack a variety of Flora/Fauna compared to the temperate ones. This may be by design, but ultimately doesn't really ring true to me (I'm in the Sonoran desert IRL - it's way more diverse of an ecosystem).I really hope they add:1. Water management - it would be great to be able to water crops in the desert and get a bonus. Also I want the realism of managing water intake and storage for my survivors.2. Sewage management - Even if I just need to have an outhouse - I think this would also provide an interesting mechanic and twist to the game. 3. Waste management - What happens to all the bones and other "unusable" materials? I propose a burn-pit mechanic of sorts, maybe have the electric version be an incinerator.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very challenging, an a lot of fun. You have a very good list of survivors to choose from, or allow the game to pick at random for you, and a beautifully rendered world with lots to explore and build. The crew "research" different tech to unlock it, though it takes a short enough time that I suspect this represents more the crew studying materials and files from their ship than actual time to develop new technology from scratch, and I really like that idea as it is more believable anyway. There are two things I think I might suggest the developers consider for future ideas (assuming that they aren't already there and I haven't gotten there yet): Animal Husbandry of some of the local fauna, and vehicles - in this case meaning Travois, Hand Carts, and eventually electric or gas powered Rovers - making resource gathering at longer distance more feasible. A rover might also carry multiple crew members, and perhaps allow some to fire weapons from on board. There are threats in the game that this would be a useful technique for. In any case, a ton of fun. To the developers - keep up the great work!

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on my wishlist for quite some time and finally decided to buy it. After completing the tutorial and spending some time in-game, it becomes glaringly obvious that the trailers and screenshots don't represent the gameplay and feel of the game. For a simulation game it doesn't feel like one at all. It feels very barebones and soulless when it comes to seeing your survivors. A lot of the interactions between survivors, the animations, the sound effects and general ambient sounds are very lacking and it's disappointing they put out a DLC instead of giving more love to the base game in general. At the start of the game one of your survivors can cry out due to the panic of just crashing and your other survivors can 'support' them. What that entails is standing around the panicked survivor, doing or saying nothing. When scavenging the ship you crashed in, the game shows you a survivor banging on the ship in the exact same place over and over again with a hammer. When putting food in a freezer, it shows the survivors clipping through the freezer instead of opening it. The game is filled to the brim with things like this and for a simulation game put out by a developer with a decade of experience with simulation games, it's not that fun to play and not great to look at either. I very much wanted to like this game but it's nothing at all of what I expected it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: As I'm writing this after 110 hours of beautiful graphics (that's the only remarkable point of this game, the very nice eye candy), I have the last survivor to embark, with a large carbon-walled base. _childDocuments_.review: As others have commented, it's essentially a really pretty version of Rimworld, but with a really well thought-out interface. Most impressive to me is that you can box-select an area, the game will list everything in it, and clicking on each item will display context-sensitive command possibilities for each item. Building is well done, and I appreciate the option to build a "room" that has a floor, walls, and a roof without necessarily needing to select each one individually (although that's an option). I'm generally not a big early-access guy but this is already hands-down worth the money, and I'll be supporting any DLC in the future without a doubt. I look forward to seeing continued modes, map-types, and challenges in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: My first impressions of the game, my criticisms,+ The artificial intelligence of the characters and the logic of queuing things are very weak.+ Characters don't even do the simplest defense when they get a direct attack. You have to draft it.+ Bug attacks are constant and pointless. It's pretty boring.+ The frequency of breakdown of the machines is very high and this creates serious costs.+ It is very difficult to increase the number of survivors in the game. This is a little discouraging.+ I have not seen the characters acquire new personality traits. The skill points they receive contribute little to their production.+ Processed food production takes a very long time and requires one person to devote to this work. The yield is relatively weak.+ The frequency of characters getting meltdown is too much, which gets boring after a while.+ The flying butterflies are really overpowered.+ It is difficult to understand why insects really attack us. It has no logic. They just attack.+ The relationship between the characters is weak. There is no such thing as emotional intimacy or friendship.+ After a while, it turns to repeating the same things pointlessly.+ Fuel is quite difficult to find in the early game, which hinders expeditions.+ Leadership, politics, decision making, similar things are not in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game!Love the mix of survival game with RPG elements (gaining skills based on usage) with an isometric view and developing 'party'.Bugs (literal bugs, not software issues) can be an annoyance -- there are definitely right and wrong ways to deal with them (engaging in melee is the wrong way -  fenced enclosure with large corridor leading with traps and turrets and/flamers is the right way).Getting the hang of prioritizing the task bar for each survivor is highly recommended!  Task are done in numerical priority, and in L to R priority - so if two tasks are  prioritized at 1, the one of the L of the row will be done first.  Once that is done, you just need to watch, monitor, make manual corrections in exceptional circumstances or as new survivors join your crew.Love the SEED mechanics for setting up your planet, even though it isn't understood very well.  Easy to find SEED banks if you want to tailor some aspects of the game, like resources, location, or amount of survivor walk-ins, etc.  ANd those will only grow more over time as people add SEEDs to it.  I've probably started a hundred games with different SEEDS just to check out the start and what research options come up.Haven't played since the mod support became official, but love the move by Haemimont to do so - wish every game developed felt the same way and thought about modding right from a games' inception.All-in-all a nice game to while away the hours.Looking forward to more development, like the animal taming.  Allows for an alternate way to craft some necessary resources or components, like manure to fuel, or Haemimont's own mod to grow meat plants.  This can get around some resource bottlenecks that can make games stall - I had a game where despite salvages and dismantling every ship part nearby, I still had not found fuel and had no way to make it by year four and I gave up that game in frustration despite what I thought was a good start initially with two walk-in survivors showing up within the first 10 days.Maybe we will an expansion or patch dedicated to making the stay on the planet more permanent, rather than the goal of everyone leaving it behind?

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of survival games, I was thrilled to dive into "Stranded: Alien Dawn," and I must say, it has exceeded my expectations. The game offers a unique blend of survival mechanics, base-building, and sci-fi elements that keep you engaged for hours on end. The game strikes a perfect balance between resource management, research progression, and the constant threat of alien wildlife and environmental hazards.If I summarize everything in bullet points I would do it like this:- Unique Sci-Fi Setting: Love how it plunges you into different alien worlds with exotic flora, fauna, and atmospheric conditions.- Dynamic Weather System: The game features a complex weather system that directly impacts your survival strategy.- Character-Driven Narrative: Each survivor has their own backstory, skills, and personality quirks, making colony management more personal and engaging than in many other survival games.- Tech Progression: The research tree is extensive and satisfying and evolves whenever you find x item to unlock it.- Alien Fauna Interaction: Instead of just avoiding or hunting wildlife, you can research and potentially domesticate some alien creatures, adding a unique twist to resource management, LOVE IT.- Modular Base Building: The base construction system is intuitive yet deep, allowing for creative designs.- Scenario Variety: Multiple scenarios with different objectives and starting conditions provide diverse challenges and storytelling opportunities.In conclusion, it is a must-play for fans of the survival genre looking for a fresh experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Novel mix and overall promising. Check back in a year, maybe it will get better, skip for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying the game so far. It feels very polished and I love the graphics. It does feel a lot like 3D Rimworld and that's great because I love Rimworld too. There have been some challenges - getting through the first winter, clothing falling apart before you can replace them, losing a survivor - but there have been some highlights as well - getting everyone and everything inside a house in time for winter, getting electricity, going on the first expedition, a wedding between survivors, and the annual memorial service for the survivor who died. Lots of room for QOL improvements and I look forward to seeing what new content they add. I've seen the complaints about the DRM, but it hasn't impacted the game as far as I can tell, and the game also runs well in Proton (my gaming computer runs on Linux Mint). Overall, I definitely recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hour two "This game is buggy as hell, why do my people keep puking? I am so done" Hour 22 "Why aren't Ken and Vivian getting along?"Hour 32 "oh hell is that....daylight outside? OH CRAP I gotta get to work!"Game is definitely addictive already, however there are a few balancing issues that still need to be worked out. The presence of the much hated, and CPU challenging, Denuvo means people cannot even mod some of the more annoying things out. Frankly the biggest issue is the crafting time. At about mid game you will find your seemingly maximum 6 people have no time in their day to do any side tasks to "double up" on anything. Specifically the slow as mud crafting. The likelihood that you are going to get a full set of winter wear before winter hits is 100% dependent on taking a specific character named vivian. You will still not be able to get a full set so you need to have a heated building before the first winter. This causes a forced chain of required steps that will severely limit replay-ability . Eventually you will research everything their is and this will free up one character to do "busy work" tasks and help with the crafting. Sadly the characters are designed in such a way that the likelihood you will have the perfect 6 to manage all maintenance and say....build a half dozen CPU's a week is slim. The expedition function need to be more rewarding as well. It is only really valuable very early game, and by the time you can craft fuel for it to be repeatable it becomes redundant and fairly useless. Scrap iron and meals 80% of the time. It is very much like Rimworld with modern graphics. However....would you play Rimworld without Mods? I know I would not.

_childDocuments_.review: Good management type game over all for early access.Some things that would make this an A+:- Music is pretty repetitive. I've turned it way down and just listen to podcasts or other ambient music in the background. I think a space themed procedural soundtrack would really help here, or simply fading the music out when it's looped too many times in a session.- Ambient sounds are also repetitive and sometimes annoying. I've heard the same insect sound at least 1000 times now. A much longer intermittent delay with a maximum times per hour played would help make the ambient noises a little more unique and special.- I would expect space faring workers to be a bit smarter with their task planning. If there is a resource queued for harvest a long way from the camp, I would expect the worker to wait until sunrise to go after it. As it is, I have to manually un-queue the task otherwise the worker will walk all the way there an hour before bedtime and turn right back around.- A "show me this item" option in the UI would be really helpful. I have many stockpiles and sometimes I loose track of crafting ingredients. I know I have 100 skinbark available, but I don't know which stockpile they are in, leading me to waste time hunting through all my stockpiles.- Priority management for stockpiles would be really nice to have. I try to organize smaller stockpiles closer to the crafting stations, to maximize production time and minimize walking time. This is difficult to do at the moment, because all stockpiles that allow an item are treated as equals. If this were easier, I could dedicate one worker to just manage stockpiles, which would make production times a little smoother.- Food forecasting is difficult! How many items are my people eating every day? Will I have enough for winter?- I'd love to see more future tech implemented. Diesel generators and batteries means tractors, powered carts, vehicles, etc. Vacuum sealers would be a great option for food preservation. Handcarts for larger resource gathering. Drones for planting or pest control. Hot air balloon upgrades to electric airplane to speed up expeditions. - With vehicles a local expedition could be a fun system; pick a few workers, a vehicle (tractor or powered-handcart), some basic supplies and order them to travel overland to a further out resource node. As it is, I won't send them to harvest resources more than a few screens away from the base.- Animal domestication is a must. I want to capture some yaks!- Happiness management is tough because the highest rewards are high quality food and drinks, which share the same base ingredients. Implementing more "relaxation" options with different inputs would be nice. Star-gazing, painting, or even work related happiness (some people love their jobs!).Overall good base for expanding ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, but in my honest opinion, it's a bit overrated. If you compare it to Rimworld, this one is barely as good as vanilla Rimworld (no DLC or mods).The good part is that it has a built-in Mod Editor. The bad part? Nobody's using it, and the mod community is dead. It seems like there hasn’t been any development since April 2024, as if the developer has already abandoned this game.The default key for panning/tilting the camera is the middle wheel click or the ALT key, but you can’t rebind it to other mouse clicks (including side mouse buttons). When this issue was brought up in the discussion forum, developers responded with comments like, "Don't you guys have a left hand?"Every survivor in the game has a unique name, skills, and traits. There’s no randomness, and it’s far from balanced. You can’t easily edit anything even with the built-in Mod Editor or by editing Lua. Soon enough, you’ll find yourself picking the same few characters as starters over and over again because the good ones are too good and the bad ones are just bad. You can find guides like "Best Starting Survivors in Stranded," but I don’t want that stuff in this kind of game.The developers aren’t listening to feedback or the community, and now it feels like the game is practically abandoned. Maybe it had some hype at first, but the reputation and reviews don’t match the current state of the game. I can hardly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded: Alien Dawn is a fun game to play. While it may have some quirks or AI inefficiencies overall it nails the general concept of Survival Games.Things I like:- I enjoy the characters and their quirks.- Building is straight forward and easy to understand- Graphics are beautiful- Random world seeds to keep things fresh- Love that birds come to peck on carcasses - The general concept of the game and it's potentialThings I Wish:- I wish we could save more survivors then 8 this really limits the colony vibe of the game (Ideally I would love to save them all)- I would like to see more tech options and that they are more meaningful. ie stone age ---> modern You can pretty much be done in two years if you are careful. I would also like the tech stages to be more meaningful ie laser pistol vs bow... lets just say bring a bow to a laser pistol fight! Just shoot and kite forever plus it's way cheaper and not so far off the damage mark.- I would like to see an upgrade option for existing building or objects should an upgrade be made available.- I would like flood lights to light more then a standard bulb would... I mean realistically they should light a massive area.. even in game I would expect 2-3x more then what they do.- I Would like to be able to customize my own survivor quirks and everything.- More flora and fauna exploring is too short lived- More social stuff and group activities to help make up for the fact everyone seems to always hate everyone else but one person.- Vehicles or some kind of transportation option. From hauling vehicles to scout vehicles. Ever wanted to move your base but didn't want to spend 15 yrs to move a 2 yr base?- Taming/Ranching- Not to be rescued one at a time.... I kind of feel it might make sense for the first one, but after that it would be hey my friends are alive go send a ship to get them! If not that hey random space ship we get you are full please send a rescue request thanks!- Back packs or inventory for travelling characters to store rations med kits etc... nothing like a 4 hour walk to a site okay time to walk back....- Crap ton more research options and ways to improve stats like intelligence ... say chess make friends while learning something and having fun.- More advance medical equipment to treat permanent conditions or severe injuries (late/end game)- More weapons... love the idea of the pulse rifle's  stun it's great.... now if we had an attack rifle too... or heavy weapons or just more in general!- Special skill unlocks with aptitude... combat 2 attack faster combat 4 attacks more accurate and so on.- faster ways to craft at late/end game, crafting starts to feel tedious by this point. Want to explore or hunt nests more.- Survivors have kids with greater needs early on to expand on the whole colony vibe- Wider variety of major events.... I mean how many solar flares can happen in 4 years? (Think i had one a year at the least)- More power options and power re balance- Set up a quarry or mine for rocks/ore/oil late game.... see massive rocks everywhere yet cant get stone...- Set building priorities not just build order in terms of placed.- Fishing and other uses for water- Use rotten food for fertilizer and improve farming soil quality.Things I do not like:- Even though having a gate open is supposed to attract the critters they often just decide to go through walls... Tutorial you lied to me!- Enemies should not spawn within your walls... maybe need a zone of control or something.- AI will do weird things atm. Lets make all these walls but one then run a mile away and make those 5 then come back and get that one.- I don't like that it is a rinse an repeat style of game play vs a more drawn out style that is a colony game.- You grind your butt off to electronics to only spend every waking moment maintaining them and hating them for breaking down twice a day.- Power consumption is way to high on defences... I get a laser would need high power, but then I would expect the damage to warrant the consumption. I think my pc uses more power then 5 automated machine turrets though so I can't understand that cost....All in all I do really enjoy the game so far and hope it develops and adds content for many years to come. It could be a great game if they keep adding to it consistently. For early access it is tons of fun, but not really intended for sustained play. I have only had one play-through so far and pretty much beat everything in 3 game years and have spent the next 3 waiting for rescue ships... ( to break 3 yrs of game play to real time I'd say around 6-8 hrs). I am totally hopeful that this game will continue to evolve and develop and hope that modders show interest in it! (please remove population cap I gotta save em all! Rescuemon!)

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this a week ago and came back to it the Monday of thanksgiving week and could not wait until autumn sales to buy it. I don't regret paying full price for this, though on sale the premium edition is about the same price as the base game; so that would have been nice. Game does not disappoint however, I've put in a decent amount of time over the past two games. I will say that it is pretty graphically intensive: playing it on a laptop with an i9 and a 3050ti I get around 50-60 fps on medium preset. On high preset 30fps was fine and playable though I do prefer the higher fps and didn't notice too much of a graphical difference between the two. Coming from Rimworld I can say the experience is pretty different aside from it being 3D. I do miss having the occasional tribal or pirate raid on rimworld as right now I'm playing on the Jason moon and medium difficulty so maybe this game doesn't have raids like rimworld or they're experienced later/on higher difficulty. So far I've had 3 insect attacks two of them being the same kind of insect. Though keep in mind I've only put less than 10 hours into this and don't know for sure if there are other kinds of attacks. Overall highly recommend and see a high degree of replay-ability similar to rimworld.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally play these types of games but I've found this enjoyable. It's in early access so I expect many things to change/improve as it progresses but it's actually a fully playable game as it is. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who plays this genre of video games. A few things I'd like to see improved on is:1. ability to save presets for characters. I generally have team builds that I make so it would be nice to be able to build teams and save them so you could use them faster. This would include keeping their schedule and priorities set. I ended up saving a screenshot of their activities after getting all the numbered priorities the way I want them and setting them up for every run is mildly annoying.2. It would be nice if we could simplify some of the tasks. For example, if I want wood it would be nice if I could say go cut some trees and not need to go specifically select a bunch and try to figure out whats closest. The same would ideally go for plants for observation/harvest. This might ruin some of the challenge of the game but it feels a bit unnecessary to me at times.3. Not sure if possible, but it would be cool if the survivors could reprioritize a bit when short on supplies. I generally keep mine/scavenge/cut all at the same priority, but if I have an alert saying I'm short on rocks, I don't see why they would keep farming trees. This is easily self managed by pausing and telling them to constantly go do rocks instead, or you could go change the priorities frequently.4. This may already exist and I just don't know it but it would be hide to hide like trees and such when fighting. Early game trying to take on 20 insects in the forest, kiting and seeing where the bugs are under the forest has been a challenge. Once you got a base built then it's not as big of a deal cause then you can wait for them to come to you.5. I think a bit more information displayed when crafting would be useful. For example when I'm making food and setting the "until" values I don't know at the time how much base materials I have or how many I can make before I run out of materials. I usually cancel out and go look at the materials and then go back into the crafting screen, so it's only a minor inconvenience. Maybe more alerts when you are missing resources for a craft as well.Again, overall great game and I look forward to the new patches/content. I'm still playing default settings and made it through one winter so far. I have a bad habit of constantly restarting to see if I can improve over previous starts.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is mostly good, I didn't want to put the tumb down only because I had the feeling that the devs tried to do the things right.It has a nice graphic, many little things are well detailed (like the hot air going out from the AC), has a lot of things to do and has workshop which will make the game great one day (thanks to all modders in the world). On the downside, many things are scripted (like the horde attack after a character is saved) so its easy to predict what will happen. AI is very stupid, so stupid that you will need to micro manage everything in the mid-end game. Eg: if you have one character doing stuff from the opposite side of the map (after half a day of walking), like salvaging a space ship junk), it will stop doing so just because one plant suddenly become in need to receive a bit of fertilizer, so it will neither finish the task and start the loooong journey back home. Characters interaction is bad, almost useless. Many things are almost useless or incomplete or bad balanced, like exploration, insects hive (they give soooo much carbon...), robots and mechs (one mech kills easy two hundred of insects). Last but not least, terrain can't be flattened, is very annoing and after 8 year I had half of the map full of holes.This game can be great, right now is a "meh", I hope the devs will balance and improve the game in future

_childDocuments_.review: It is hard to recommend this over Rimworld.The graphics are meh, the ai pretty weak, managing happiness is no where near as good. There is no real benefit to skills aside from not failing and a finishing a bit faster. Is it a bad game at the moment? No. But it is not as good or even on the same level as the game it is emulating. Some interesting things it does. Massive maps. Being an alien planet it makes you research the flora and fauna which is very cool. The research is interesting and it does storage way better than other games of the same style. Game speed is slow even at the top speed. There is no quality system. Finding some of the plants or ore is very difficult. Combat is pretty weak. The pathing and hauling AI is pretty meh. Characters move pretty slow. Lightning strikes colonists too often. In my play through only one person ever got hit but they got hit like 6 times.It is interesting and I hope modding can fix it up a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is still not recommended due to the major bugs and Denuvo! Citizens sometimes won't bring food to injured even though there is plenty of food... "No food available" in red is what I got. Citizens fail to accomplish tasks, even though they are right next to the task. Citizens won't use the resources they are right next to... chopping down trees when there is an abundance of wood on the ground next to the tree they are cutting down!!! Choosing less important chores instead of the urgently needed chores... fix punching pole instead of repairing the electricity outage, go plant more seeds that are not needed instead of chopping badly needed sticks for the empty cooking fire/stove... meanwhile your citizens are starving! Citizens go hunt for badly needed meat but after killing the prey, they walk off back to base instead of butchering the kill and taking it back to base! Real hunters butchers the kill or take it with them... not leave it there on the ground then go back to base to eat, sleep, play darts, etc. The citizens are stupid, they don't use any tactics or strategy when facing the enemy, they will just rush in and get killed, you have to micro manage them too much to the point that it's a real grind. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty cool. I like the fact that every time you restart you crash in different places. (Keep that in mind when starting, some places are less desirable than others.) You have to learn to cater to the survivors needs they are all different from foods to activities. You have the management tools to set up their schedules and tasks to perform actions to minimize micro managing. Do they wander off and do other things? of course but that's most likely because you left a large block in the management section that pretty much lets them do what they want. Its a pretty unforgiving game coming into it without knowing anything, you really have to think strategy pretty quick. Or perish pretty quick. For an early access there is a ton of stuff. I have restarted about 4 times and have loved every minute of it. But it is a micro management game so keep that in mind. Putting vents in the wall of your building to let heat out in the summer and close them to keep heat in the winter is just one of many things that I find pretty neat. Its all about the details. You cant just produce one kind of food and hope for the best. some are vegans some wont hold weapons etc. You cant forget to produce clothing and weapons. the list goes on. The fact you can pause the game if things go south could make the difference between life or death, its gives you some time to plan a strategy for when the bugs come. Or pray lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid foundation for a modern base builder/management/survival game.  I really enjoy the setting and the world.  Its dynamic enough to make it interesting as a background setting to a management game.  The characters seam believable and their interactions are interesting.  I hope the models get fleshed out a bit more and have less of a generic look to them and match the avatars a bit more, but that's a little observation.  I also hope the DEVS bring in an away mission to the game dynamic where we could have randomly generated events pop up to actually go to even if its a closed of map , and explore.  Would give the game a much longer lifespan, and possible expansions with mission themes.  Also any more random crew interactions even if superficial would add to the immersion of the game, more character based interactions and animations to make the settlers really fit into the well designed emotion/relationship system.  Am only on my first play through so these are my initial impressions with about 1 in game year cycle completed.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth full price, not even close. Buy it on a steeply discounted sale.In many ways, this game is a copy of Rimworld (which is fine), but with a number of interesting changes. Things like "shelves can hold more than one thing" which, imo, is great. I'm not a huge fan of Rimworld, so this is a welcome improvement. I like how the game looks, it does environments very well, and your survivors all display the gear you have put on them. This is great.Where things fall off a cliff: the time it takes to make things, and the number of things produced, is just ridiculous. Food items will take 1-2 hours to cook (not including fetching the ingredients), and will produce 2 items per cycle (compared to 4 in Rimworld). With even just 5 survivors (eactin 2 meals each, per day), this makes it extremely difficult to build up a backlog of cooked meals. While one can argue that scarcity is part of the difficulty, for manufactured items this is a bad argument.It's one thing for raw materials to be scarce (which is what is normally referred to when speaking of 'scarcity'), but the issue with these production bottlenecks is not one of scarcity, but of having to tie up 2-3 survivors cooking all day, every day, when the colony only has fewer than 6 people. While yes, this makes the game "more difficult", it's on par with making a shooter "more difficult" by giving the enemies more hitpoints: it's boring, unimaginative, and it doesn't require creative thinking to solve. You just... make more people cook. This is bad game design.Similarly, the rate at which electronic devices break down (solar panels, batteries, freezers, etc) is ludicrously high. Moreover, when they break down they *always* require rare components to repair (electronics) if rare components went into their manufacture. Apparently merely soldering a connection is impossible, the entire PCB needs replacing every. single. time. Given how long it takes to manufacture these items yourself, this is (again) a very uncreative way to suck the time of your survivors away.Enemy attacks are part and parcel of many colony survival games. In Rimworld/Dwarf Fortress, they appear at the far edge of your map. In other games, they have a visible spawn location (which sometimes you can take out the spawn location, otherwise you can build your defences in response to it). In Stranded? They just pop into existence beside your base. Just... 100+ insects... *pop*. No-one saw them coming, no-one raised a warning, they're just beside your base.In one of my maps, I had enclosed 3 sides of my base, and created a choke point on the other, and the insects/angry animals sometimes just... spawned inside the choke point.Meanwhile, there are Insect Nests all over the map, with new ones spawning periodically. Which are completely disconnected from enemies spawning to attack your base. The one has nothing, at all, to do with the other. A thoughtful game designer might have set the nests to spawn new insects every few days, and once a critical mass is reached, they start moving on your base, but the game designers involved in Stranded do not appear to be thoughful.This game design is neither interesting nor, frankly, competent.While the DLC brings with it some interesting improvements (ie delivery/battle drones, service/harvesting bots), and I hope that other creators take note, it's just a parsley garnish on a ♥♥♥♥ sandwich.

I'm horrible at it, yet I can sit down and spend HOURS getting my camp together, only to lose control of everything and be overrun by critters (does it seem like once you start to get a little headway, they just come almost non-stop?) - Really fun, and I see lots of possibility here!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded: Alien Dawn introduction starts you out with a cool spaceship crash to begin your adventure. This is a survival / crafting / combat challenge to test your ability to get a rescue ship to your base. You'll have a lot to deal with priorities, qualifications, construction, combat, and weather situations. Game saves are critical just in case you have a major decision planned. New recruits are available but crew size is limited to six. The crew all have attitudes, traits, and skills to deal with & understand.I couldn't enjoy the game until I traded all my refund time for tutorial hours. Learning the game is deep so don't get stressed burning thru your refund window. The game was purchased with the robot dlc on sale but I'm not ready for that right now since I have so many other map and seed selections available.I have not escaped the planet... after all this time I have not come up with success. I had the orbital transmit radio but couldn't find or craft the rest of the pieces to make it functional... so back to the drawing board.Update 12/21/2023  Well folks I did it! The last survivor departed my outstanding base in the rescue pod and I took Annabelle my Level 9 K-9 with me. If you discover my base enjoy yourself and please mow the lawn.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing, and with workshop support it will hopefully increase in amazement.I don't often write unofficial reviews, as I don't like bias perspectives, but as someone who play rimworld, going medieval, oxygen not included, prison architect, medieval life and a few other similars. This one is climbing the list.I am guessing it highly inspired by starship, because THIS is what I wanted the starship game to be! Horde of hundreds of insects slowly coming towards my walls. I wish they climbed them instead of trying to break them, but I am guessing that would make it too similar.In any case, graphics is great, better than the other games I have on my list, and I never expected a 3D game to run so smoothly, yet over here I am fighting against around 2000 insects and still running smoothly (Except when I blast them with a barrage of missiles and having their corpses go flying)And I love the UII wish there was more weapons, like modern, as there is only medieval ones and high tech ones, but with the workshop, I know there will be mods out there, or I can just create my own.I recommend this game fully.-Cheers
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: When I sit down to play this game, hours fly by! In comparison to a game like Rimworld, this game has fewer systems and less random events, but the tech progression is good, and I enjoyed the 3 scenarios in the base game.It can be challenging working with your survivors, especially those who are harder to keep happy, but once you can button down the scheduling and task management, it becomes easier. But don't get complacent because things can get out of hand quickly if you are not paying attention!I did wait for a sale to pick this up (20% off I believe), but not because I didn't think the game was worth it, but because I have tried other survival colony games (Rimworld being one) that I just couldn't get into. Now that I have played it, I think the asking price is reasonable.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Great Potential but not really there yet. Rimworld with awesome graphics. You can see they REALLY took care of the graphical side of things. Small animations when they do certain tasks.. i love it. The Endgame is a slog though and everything happens REALLY slowly (i m looking at you advanced crafting) to mask the rather barebones stuff you can do. You mostly just wait around for tasks to be completed and they take FOREVER.  Partly because of poor AI prioritization, partly intentional. This game really needs a task priority setting. It s a "meh" for now.  Still enjoyable for a day or two. Really looking forward to what the game will become.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of fun i'm having playing this game is crazy. Its both fun and frustrating when things doesn't go the way you planned, which is the whole purpose of the game and making sure they all would survive this harsh planet and environment. Now I've been playing other strategy survival/rts games like these in the past and i must say this game has a quite interesting game mechanics that i've never seen in other game before which makes this game more interesting and addicting to play. It's overall a never ending fun and i encourage to devs to make more game like this in the future and perhaps make more dlc for this game. Truly a fun and addicting survival building game with unique simple mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended in its current state for people looking for colony sim or Rimworld fans.This game seems to be a very limited set of bits and pieces from Rimworld, packaged into pretty graphics. I've played Rimworld a lot, possibly that's biasing my review here, but while playing Stranded: AD I constantly felt a mixture of "how are the developers getting away with literally copying that stuff from Rimworld" and "there is so little depth to happenings, they should have learned more from Rimworld". I came for a colony sim, and as such found the game falling short.Seeing that it's in early access, I hope there will be more interesting things to come, and hopefully not all of them will be copy/paste from Rimworld.

_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game, and it's opening hours are fantastic, however once you move into "phase 2" or the establishment of the camp and the expansion of resources, things get way too grindy and monotonous. The economy of the game is set entirely too steep. Take a battery for instance. They are necessary for everything in the middle to late game. However, if you are unlucky enough to have to actually build them, it takes days of in game time to construct one circuit board, and the battery requires five of them... We could move on to auto turret which require CPU cores, which require circuit boards, and of course require massive amounts of power as well... I get the escelation of economy, that is present in all colony / civ builders, but this one takes a crazy sharp turn up. It would also be much better to be able to set up some kind of survivor beacon. Going to get them with a razor slim chance of finding someone alive is super not fun..Anyway, the game is in early release and it shows a lot of promise, but as it stands now, I am not sure that I can recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Good:- Interesting concept of futuristic base building survival game- Characters that you can choose to play is well though of, some is somewhat related to one another, have their own story , traits and personality and pretty balanced. _childDocuments_.review: If you're here like me, looking for a great storytelling game, this is not it.If you like Rimworld, stay with Rimworld.This is not a bad game though, can't give thumbs down.It's also not worth 35 bucks. What really bothers me: If you decide to make a 3D game in the spirit of Rimworld, why is everything looking exactly like Rimworld? Structures, roads, erverything: rectangular. 90° angles everywhere. Look at how beautiful Manor Lords is! I want this game game to look like that. The Rimworld-engine is limited in floor levels and thus multi-story buildings or underground mining (all the mods failed) are not possible. This engine could easily do it, but they decided not to. One floor level, no underground. At least you have ground elevation, but that also brings other unwanted effects.And then there's so much that is max. 5% of Vanilla Rimworld:- There is no overworld. Imagine Rimworld on one tile with no world to explore.- There are no factions / other people. You have 4 starter colonists and can have a few more through "quests".- The quests are (boring) text adventures. Because there is only one tile, you know. And no other people. You lift off in a baloon and 2 in-game hours later you click through 3 pages of texts with option like "1. danger! return!" or "2. search for signs of life". If it had just a bit of FTL charme...- Battle: Since there are no other humans / factions to fight, it's literally horde mode with bugs. The bugs are totally uninteresting and get bigger over time. I play on normal, no challenge at all because salvaging old spaceship parts gives you laser weapons from the start. meh.- Stats: All things have hitpoints, that's about it. No wild statistics and useful info. - Art desgin: This is Nova Scotia. Nothing here is alien.- Music: 0% and a Youtube window (Recommendations: Factorio, Rimworld, FTL Multiverse, KKND2 ...)Also do not expect anything like ideologies, genes, children, a comprehensive overarching story, feeling of loneliness in a vast universe / planet ...Some good things:- Research is fine, nothing groundbraking- Construction / storage is okay, some QoL is 1998 though ...Conclusion:If you like Rimworld, stay with Rimworld. It has about 95% more to offer than "Something: Alien Something". If you must have 3D and / or Rimword is "too much" for you: This may be it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:Alright, 1.0 is out and I gave it another go. I tried fresh characters, a harder moon, and a different win condition. I'm still not convinced that I shouldn't just be playing RimWorld instead. Not enough new and unique mechanics are present in Stranded: Alien Dawn to make it worth it in my opinion.Original review:As of right now, it's just a little too similar to RimWorld. A lot of the mechanics are not just similar, but feels as if have been directly lifted with only a graphical improvement. Combat, crafting, construction, researching, labor management--even falling spaceship chunks! None of the important parts of the game feel unique enough to feel worthwhile quite yet.HOWEVER! I really do enjoy the process of discovering and learning about the alien flora and fauna. The shame is that part of the game does not last very long. You'll be sending your survivors out to all the weird veggies and bug-cows in the vicinity in the first week of the game, then there'll be pretty much nothing left to discover.As it stands I can't recommend this game over something like RimWorld. But I can definitely see some great potential and will be amending my review as Stranded: Alien Dawn moves through Early Access.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: There's potential but it needs more. I enjoyed my time with it, but to be honest, I feel like I've seen all the game has to offer. RIP to that one guy. Perhaps he should have gone around. I'll keep an eye out for new mods and updates to see if there's anything that can spice it up. For now, 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded: Alien DawnIt's 3D RimworldIf you've played Rimworld, you've basically already played this game. Yes, there's a handful of small, new mechanics; the most notable of which being the requirement that you have to Observe each piece of alien flora and fauna before you know what it is and what it does. That being said; it's... Only done one time per item, so once you've observed one Small Broadleaf Tree, you don't ever have to do it again.I can't say I 'liked' the game. It certainly wasn't bad, but it wasn't particularly new or exciting, either? Yes, I can build multi-story buildings, but all that really means is I'll maybe build a 2 or 3-story building every once and a while, but that's kind of it.The game sees your crew of survivors crash-landing down on an unknown alien world with the goal of escaping. You'll have to build up a base and prepare defensive measures against the hostile alien life, alongside surviving the harsh climate of such a locale.That's- kind of it. If you've played any colony sim before; you know how this works. Assign tasks, have your colonists do those tasks to obtain what it is you need; repeat ad-infinitum while researching new things to set up tasks for, and eventually you'll reach the end-game all while occasionally having to defend your base from hostiles, before you presumably figure out your means of 'escaping the planet'.Nothing in this game is exceptionally 'new' or 'fresh', but it's also not bad? It's very passably good, and it appears to have about 850 workshop items (Though given this is a 3D game, I'm not sure how many of those mods add brand new things or are just slight tweaks/recolorations of existing models).Eh.Not bad, not great. Just, good, but there's certainly better out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of 'autonomous' games, games where you create living beings and then watch as they do what they want to do (with a little guidance from you).  Been a fan of those ever since the Majesty series a million years ago.  Probably Rimworld has come the closest to fully scratching that itch, but I've never been a fan of pixel graphics.  I'm an old fart, so I grew UP with pixel graphics, and was thrilled as we made each advancement forward in the graphics/FX departments.  I guess I'm one of the few who doesn't really enjoy going backward.  Some people say "graphics aren't important, gameplay is important" - and I agree - to a point.  There's no reason not to have both.  A game like FTL is amazing, pixel graphics or not.  But I always dreamed of that game in fully-rendered 3D glory.  Alas, I guess I will have to continue waiting.  The same holds true for Rimworld.  I thought "If only this game looked as good as it plays!"  And voila - now we have Stranded: Alien Dawn!  I LOVE it.  It's still in Early Access as I write this, and only incorporates about 1/3 of everything a game like Rimworld has achieved in its longer life + DLCs, but it is absolutely ON ITS WAY!  Gameplay is as compelling, thanks mostly to fully fleshed-out characters with specific strengths and weaknesses - a gorgeous planet with a fair amount of flora and fauna to discover and explore, and even occasional 'events' in the forms of monster attacks and exploratory excursions.  There's tons of resources and a pretty good spread of recipes for crafting, building and menu items.  And once the game double or triples all these things, including (and especially) special events - I think Stranded could easily overtake Rimworld as my favorite 'autonomous' game of all time.  My hat is already off to the Devs, who have done a fantastic job so far, and have created a truly engaging early-access game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very initial review of Stranded: Alien Dawn as I have not put a full hour in of play time, much less dove in very far enough to get a real feel.  I will come back later after a few hours and try to update with a better idea of what my experience has been.I have seen many people state that Stranded: Alien Dawn is almost like a 3D version of Rimworld.   I can certainly see that from the time I have spent playing the game so far.  As far as the graphics are concerned, the game is nice to look at, and I don't have any think to complain about so far.  I had no lagging or tearing, and while I didn't run a FPS tool, I felt that I was getting at least a solid 40+ the whole time I did play.  This is on  an aging i5-7400 @3Ghz run 16GB Ram, 1060GTX and Samsung SSD.  So I am sure a newer machine would handle it even better.   I haven't tried it on the Steam Deck, though it looks like the major issue is text size and until I get a better feel for the game I rather hold off guessing on what text prompts might be.There are a few places that you do have a bit more control over your pawns than in Rimworld, but this mostly pertains to combat.   Characters do argue and such with each other, just like Rimworld, so there is that.  From my understanding however you are stuck with the lot you are given so you will not have any babies running around.  Some of the menus and UI features are a bit clunky and nested deeper than I would like, but not so bad that it makes the game not fun to play.  I am sure that these will get changed as the game progresses through EA.    My biggest concern with any game of this type is that the developers have a clear path and not give up progress and leave us hanging.   I have no reason to think they will but I just like to put that out there as someone that has been burnt a lot by similar lofty games.The game has a great premise, has a great feel and has a ready audience with Rimworld players as long as they keep up the good work and don't go off on a tangent. I look forward to playing the game more, and wish the devs the best of luck in turning their dreams into reality as I think this could be a big hit if they handle it right.

_childDocuments_.review: I came to this game by coincidence while looking through the Steam store. I bought it and have played it for two weeks now. My impression and review up to this point is very positive. There are a few scenarios for learning where the basic elements of the game are told and can be practiced. From my perspective they are good, but already have some experience in games about survival etc. I someone is completely new to this kind of game the might be not detailled enough.The game itself starts in its current stage with very little options for the crash site and surroundings. Basically you can define the games difficulty. Then you have to choose four characters from a pool of appr. 20 characters to start with. During the game there is the chance that more survivors join the team. This has proven to be very helpful to me.The first things to do during the game are to get resources like food, material for building (wood, stone etc.) and to develop the skills of your survivors while they are working. Also you have to research new technologies and craft tools as well as basic materials you need. You also can explore unkown areas with a hot air balloon as soon you develop yourself to this point.The whole game with working, crafting, researching, building and exploring takes some time to figure out the best way between large scale buildings, crop fields and defense systems on one side and energy production, crafting spare parts (to repair all electric and electronic devices), clothes (all clothes need to be replaced at some point) as well as available space within the storage facilities on the other side. To gain a perfect match not to run low on needed materials and still having time to explore and develop is far from easy. I now play my third round and I do get the balance better and better.For me this game is already quite well delevoped but of course some bug fixing and balancing can be done. I am very much looking forward to the next steps the game will take.

_childDocuments_.review: *Review Qualifier* I have played A LOT but I haven't reached "end game" yet because I have too much fun starting over to try new strategies for bases and survivor groups. I'm probably not even close. I hear we're supposed to try and escape the planet, but I keep playing it like a colonizer or survivor that might end up liking it enough to abandon society and start over. I'm not even sure what end game is supposed to be but maybe I don't want to define it yet myself or leave for that matter! :)  Ecosystem - Alien creatures are a feature here. It has cool varieties and cool interactions with predators and prey that you can take advantage of (e.g. running bug swarms that attack your base into predator groups). Some predators are deadly to other animals but not your survivors and you can harvest meat and hides (for periods of time) without having to do any hunting based off of looking for those interactions. You compete with alien scavenging birds to harvest carcasses if they sit out in the wild too long (such an awesome little realistic touch). Room for more cool improvements but great already! A+Environments/Graphics - You're playing in randomly generated earth looking environments with alien elements sprinkled on top. Sometimes this works ok (even great) aesthetically, other times it feels a bit like assets were bought and plugged into the game. It'd be cool to have a fully alien looking world added to the planet types in the future. This goes the same for base building and tech. You're a space faring survivor (which presumably means you're from an advanced human society) but most of what you build aesthetically feels very "old world" in design, even in terms of base building as you tech back up in progression... and then advanced weaponry scavenged from spaceship hull chunks are thrown in on top of it. I've not unlocked everything so I don't know if that might change a bit more at some point. It's a weird blend that at once feels natural for spaceship crash survivor progression mechanics and a bit off at the same time. So it's a bit of a mish mash but not so jarring that it detracts overall. The graphics overall are very nice and border on realism in may ways which makes it feel like you are playing an advanced version of rim world even though it's not fleshed out quite as much, mechanically speaking, (yet) but has a unique vibe of its own going. And despite the mish mash, it still looks good with alien fauna and certain flora being highlights. B+Gameplay - Is this a rim world knock off? Yes and no. In both cases that is a positive thing in my opinion. It certainly didn't feel like a cheap rip off especially as I kept playing and enjoying it more and more. It features a lot of derivative rim world mechanics and elements but that isn't a bad thing or done in a bad way here. There is a fun little touch where, after observing/researching alien flora and fauna, your survivor plugs in funny naming conventions based around its closest earth like counter part. So this game also has it's own cool vibe going in this area as well. It also has a lot of room to grow and expand in it's own different way on this front. Which is very exciting based on the updates we've had since early access release. The UI is clean and easy to use. Solid AReplay Value/Randomness - One of my favorite aspects of the game and a very important one not to over look. All your game set up options, that I see, can be set to random. Each play through and difficulty is unique not only based on those settings and randomly generated environments but also based on the random nature of the items you scavenge from crashed spaceship hulls scattered around. This can only get better as new world and biome types, environment features, and events are added to the game. Currently, for myself, I can use all the settings and randomization options to hit a great sweet spot with challenge vs fun vs randomized novelty and replay value. Limited in some ways due to early access starting point but A+ Summary - I love this one. I personally enjoy it over rim world for its much more realistic aesthetic and 3D environment. It's not as feature rich or balanced, being in early access, but still really solid in content and playtime for where its at currently. The only rim world thing I've really noticeably missed thus far is tunneling and bases built into hills/mountains. Despite that, it has become my favorite "comfort game", which means I can totally chill with it but also stay hooked in the challenges of keeping my survivors alive and developing my base(s) of operation. I hope it continues to be for a long time to come as they update and improve it. _childDocuments_.review: The game is very addictive as a team based survival base game.    I been playing over 200+ hours on hard difficulty and its hard.   A stronger bug wave comes every 5 days, and Year 2 (48th days) would ramp up the bug attack with aerial acid bug or King Scrpio that shoot long distance acid.The new patch make it even more difficult, as it was easy to deal with single type of bug with different defence formation, aerial bug need tight group, while melee bug need U shape cross fire, and range bug need to take cover behind auto-turret or form single line defence.     The new patch make it that auto turrets is probably the best way to research if want any chance of survival.CON: However, there is one major big game problem (design bug) that need to be fix.   Solar Flare disable auto turrets so the game end basically by default when Solar Flare occurs during bug attack. It is not possible for survivors holding little guns to fight off hundreds of bug, especially aerial bugs (in the hundreds) that ignore any base defence and attack the survivors directly.   (I think during the solar flare, the game needs to be like 10x energy consumption instead 100% disable auto turrets.  Otherwise even with all survivors holding rail guns 2.0 and one of best base designs, the campaign just ended with all dead.   I was like WTF and rage quit).CON: another game problem (design bug) is attack bug spawn point sometime is too close to the base.    Sometime bug spawn right by my base and start attacking after "magically appeared".   This is not very fun and unrealistic.  I think it can be fix easily by spawn bug wave at least 200 squares away from survivors or campfire or cook stove at the center of base.CON: survivors queue still need to be improved.   The construction queue & bug butchering queue is just horrible.  Survivors would ignore the closest work and runs 100 square away to do a fence wall section and run 100 square back to do another fence wall door.   Also butchering is like harvest 1 bug meat run back to base and come back to do another bug for 1 meat etc.   I can over-ride the survivors queue with manual control, but it is just so annoying.PRO: The game is actually amazingly stable for early access.  Its run smoothly with all camera zoom angles.   No degradation of memory even after hours of play.  The survivors can be polished up a bit more with more type of clothing.  The end game need to be have more SIM4 style items that will pro-long the fun factors after have extra resources to do luxury items like freezer, AC and room decor.I definitely recommend this game.   Only play hard difficulty if really want challenge.  otherwise medium difficulty is more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I do like city building survival, and survival games in general.And for a "Early Access" game I was very impressed.I have played this for a week straight near 100 hrs so far, so I can offer a very  accurate review  of this game.I really can tell a great deal of effort has been made to make this game have plenty of depth, and  a broad scope to survival and crafting elements of which the devs did a GREAT job on. I was very happy to see it has what real community builder ,survival fans are looking for. the UI= Very good and intuitivethe Pathing! = better than most I have seen, and except for a few minor glitches does work pretty well. still needs balancing... in some instances...The  AI= also better than most I have seen. very difficult to achieve I know, but hats off to the devs here!It is Amazing the amount of updates and additional content that has been added in a short time ! well done,  a labor of Love to be sure by the Dev Team  "Thank You for caring about the consumers of your work"! NOTE!_ some of the following may have been fixed by this edit!Now the negative that are few BTW...1-The crew eat waaay too often not reality...2-Takes way too long to craft clothing! 3-The Food can Spoil in a perfectly good Freezer,- needs fixing4- the Automated Turrets  (when not being attacked) most often wont activate when animals come near or in range even right in front of turret.? this could be intentional ?  as the player will have to hold the hands of turret control unless an attack to fences or players happens, but fields will get destroyed by wildlife, if you dont! OVERALL!, its a Good  start to what I believe will be a legendary game in this genre IF, the devs continue to add to the game features and content and fix the minor bugs.I really enjoyed playing and getting the recipes for character control priorities, job assignments, and crafting orders just right just right to survive the seasons.
