_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, pretty good in fact but not great. That being said its "Early Access" so expectations still exist.For starters the game is as others are saying, its a Rimworld type functioning game with a different look and feel.Cons It's the look and feel that both brings it up and brings it down. Being more immersed visually creates the feeling to have a mental and emotional need, this doesn't give that (yet). There is no real story or end game goal and by that I mean the experience is at the moment very short lived, what you get 1 hour into it is what you get the rest of the game so far (speaking of the gameplay itself here). That would be the main con in my opinion but again EA so its to be expected at the moment.Combat is an area the Devs can really put more work in on future updates as it is well to be frank pretty bad. The Draft system as it is "should" be a secondary system for the active combat. To make effective use of turrets you pretty much have to create an uncomfortably large power grid that clutters the space making TD the secondary combat system atm. The taming is indeed involved in the combat however its pretty unreliable simply being an accessory to the draft system. Resource and space "balancing" are also currently more of a chore than a fun part at the moment (specifically when trying to be organized and optimized), this due to terrain constraints such as empty craters from debris sites that remain once the debris is cleared, which some Terra forming functions being implemented would greatly help while staying (realistic).ProsThe modding support, there is a lot to get comfortable with and can just as easily make the experience better as you can break the experience however, it provides a lot of capabilities. Everything that is currently in the game feels and looks unique and drives the exploratory nature as you play.The variety in resources, and equipment are amazing, in fact having this variety is currently what drives most of the  current replay ability as each map seed creates a different look and feel with scarce open plains to densely resource filled maps. with different resources available on each seed.The Seasonal effects and time spent within each greatly help the current depth of the game and what it can be.ConclusionIf you like games like Rimworld, you will like this game and will probably spend countless hours on it even in its current state. Devs are active and consistently working on the game so there is more to look forward to with an already good game. Just understand the game is EA its lacking in areas but excelling in others.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing new to see here - and when you throw in DeCrash-O software; its not worth it.When I wishlisted the game there was no mention of DeBug-O being a requirement, I bought it off of the wishlist direct and didn't see it, I only found out it was there when I tabbed out to the new screen and opened discord and it thought there was tampering and crashed.  The hundreds of people in the forums complaining the game won't load, or crashes - same thing - its this "software."Back to the game itself (at this early release stage) - there is nothing new about the game at all.  New labels but not new content over other games of this nature / type.  All of these forms of games require balance and choke-points.  In this game the choke point is labor as you are stuck with a very limited labor pool.  Resources are plentiful, but there is no way to prioritize them.  You can micro-manage (which I hate) and just say "MINE" without any other tasks, then change tasks, but that is tedium ad infinitum el puko!   You can "Draft" the labor pool, but that only works to attack things - you can't direct them to mine, chop, butcher, etc.   As the routine tasks grow, tending the still, barrels, smelter, etc.  they start dropping other tasks to tend 'those' and things just don't get done.  This is where direct control is needed and it is not there.Music - well, at least they didn't waste a lot of time there (maybe that means they will work on some game issues first).  The image of Burt Reynolds paddling down a river fill my mind after listening to that for a while.Load Times / lockups / frame loss - is all there from DeCrash-O.  If you open your task list and watch it load down your system you will see why.  Most DeCrash-O games are cracked on the first day of release,  the rest are cracked within that week, added to the fact that there is no multi-player side to this game just makes "that software" push this game to the negative side.Given all of this, I wouldn't pay anything for the game with DeCrash-O on it; without it I would pay $9.99 in its current state.   I'll amend this review as the game progresses, IF, there is anything to amend.  I've found that too many developers go into the "Our Vision" defense mode of late - which spells the final doom for the game, as those developers miss the "game" part of their work.

_childDocuments_.review: A shameless Rimworld rip-off with less to do, smaller research / tech trees, and none of the weird humour or wacky charm.To be fair, the visuals are very nice (though not without bugs) but, without the depth of the original, it ends up feeling tedious. Very futuristic and sci-fi.  Needs to do away with the backstories and instead have a random skill (and name) generator to create a unique pool of survivors for each playthrough.  Nobody cares if Bob was a farmhand who enjoyed sunsets and ice cream:  the story begins when they crawl from the wreckage...It's ok, but if you can deal with its odd-ball visual style, just play Rimworld.Edit:  After 82 hours, and finishing the game, my opinion remains unchanged.5 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool game. I have 6000+ hours in Factorio, Space Engineers, Surviving Mars, Kenshi, etc. This game is the "modern" version of Kenshi, that is a current GUI, graphics, and resultant polish. Just like Kenshi you take your small squad of characters and survive in an alien wilderness. Crafting, combat (at least against dangerous animals), base building, mining, research, it's all there.So far no bugs or crashes but I am playing unmodded in this my first play through. I usually play with a ton of mods, but so far in Stranded I haven't needed/wanted any, as yet. The game handles weather, i.e. seasonal differences between winter and summer exceptionally well. Kenshi does not have that. You better have good boots and a warm coat if your base is in the mountains because winter is going to get cold, and your characters don't like it.The game has a lot of nice touches, such as when you build an enclosed structure and then heat it with a fireplace the room takes a while, just like real life, to go from 0 degrees to 13 (centigrade). So, so far, in this first play through, I'd rate it a 4.5 out of 5. My only nit is I can't explicitly make my characters run, unlike in Kenshi you can set the speed at which they will move. In Stranded the characters WILL run, but only at their discretion.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is deceivingly fun for a good amount of time. It seems to have some pretty good bones, until you get far enough to realize that the advancement in the game suddenly hits a dead end.Then you notice how wonky, basic, and downright terrible the building is. Trying to build a second floor is a nightmare. Want a staircase inside your base to the second floor? Well, too bad; you can't build a roof over it, even though it's a 1st floor staircase and you're trying to put on a 2nd floor roof.The amount of gear in the game is just way too basic. It feels like a alpha version of a game as far as gear goes for your survivors. Then there is the way the game eventually forces you out. Enemy waves don't cap. They just keep getting bigger and stronger. You're forced to either die or leave the planet. Players want to play their own way. Let them.Then you get the minor grievances like how the Gujo bird goes extinct in the first year as they attack things tougher than themselves and don't respawn. Getting poultry can be a serious pain. Crafting times for simple things like a single piece of electronics is ABSURDLY long. It takes way entirely too long for your people to work at their work stations. When you get an electric smelter you can only put 10 iron scrap into the thing at a time. It spends more time waiting for someone to transfer to and from it than it spends actually smelting because the inventory space on it is so low.The game is fun, but once you get to a point you'll suddenly feel like it's a half-finished product.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Rimworld; this is not as in-depth as that game on a number of levels. However, it's excellent at what it does which is bringing the scope down; giving a 3D paint job; and centralizing the game to your primary settlement. Go through the MOD list though; there are some great ones that add a little more to the mix such as elimination of endgame reqs, adding androids etc. My first 13 hour game ended as such:Researched; production up to a mid sized settlement with 13 survivors.Fending off multiple attacks over time but ultimately taken down by a  group of 43 of those spike throwing aliens. (Definite Starship Troopers vibe)The only survivor was my first military/soldier focused settler. But his wounds were too grave and he couldn't self heal so he was steadily bleeding out. Also under his health tab was -10 happiness for each of the 12 other settlers who died; my man was PTSD depressed. So what did he do? After the battle he went to the Leisure room I made, played darts as he was bleeding out, worked out on the bench as he was bleeding out. After which when he was done with his work out he just stood up and died. I'm fairly certain if I had bothered to build the items I needed to make Alcohol he would have had a beer first. I've played for 13 hours total and will stop for awhile with BG3 release tomorrow. However I fully intend on giving it another go down the road after that cinematic ending on my first run. Give it a try if you liked Rimworld; I'm excited with the potential this game has either through further Developer content or the modding community.

_childDocuments_.review: I bounced off Rimworld despite loving the concept, and found this an easier gateway into the colony-sim-with-random-attacks genre. Stranded is more intuitive to play, has a better UI and tutorials, and you start out  more basic - building scrap metal shelters and a campfire while you gather the resources and research in order to start constructing a base.Liked: Choosing from a pool of designed characters, each with their own traits, likes and skills. The ability to add modifiers like a larger team size or increased walking speed without it affecting most achievements. The look of the game. Sending people on expeditions in hot air balloons. Finding new survivors. How happy my survivors were to get carpets and musical instruments and tea and cake. Didn't love: The waiting around. Once you set your team's priorities, they quite happily get on with life and there's not much for you to do until animals attack or you have to answer the radio. Nights are particularly slow - this game really needs a faster max speed. It was disappointing that interactions between survivors were so shallow and they mainly seemed to dislike each other. The animal attacks also felt tacked on and boring (playing on normal difficulty). The game just... doesn't quite have challenge in the right places. I mean, tea and cake and carpets just a week after crash landing...I had a fun, if sometimes idle, 30 hours with it, and will probably have a go on harder difficulties to see how much that changes things. It gave me the courage to go try Rimworld again, feeling more prepared for it, and ironically bounce off just as hard as I did the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This one is hard to recommend, although I want to.  It's clearly a copy of Rimworld, but only a narrow amount of the basic aspects of Rimworld are implemented so just by that fact it's disappointing right out of the gate.  If someones going to copy a game they should at least be adding to it.CONSCompared to Rimworld it's got such a limited number of things to build and therefore a limited technology tree, it's probably 20% of what Rimworld is, and really doesn't have anything that Rimworld DOESN'T have except nice graphics.  The nice graphics apparently comes at a cost though because you can only have 10 settlers maximum, and even at 10 with a decent PC I can notice performance dropping.   Also there's no real good reason to keep playing when you've exhausted all the things you can build (which is very limited) because your colony can't grow because you can't have any more settlers.    Also I have a ton of crashes, usually revolving around if I'm task-switching.  The autosave is thankfully aggressive and when the population limit is reached there's no reason to build anything more and therefore no work lost really when it inevitably crashes, so I haven't been too inconvenienced. Also it's unclear how some things work, like what the difference between a fridge and a freezer is other than in a fridge food will still decompose.  But logically in the real world some foods shouldn't be put in a freezer, especially when it's fresh cooked (like a stew) yet apparently it's fine to put in a freezer.  Anyway a lot of little things like this are unexplained or fiddly.  Toggling things is a UI nightmare.  For example you can click on an animal's corpse and then toggle it on/off for a colonist to butcher.  But it's not clear of the state of the toggle, it's just got a green checkmark or a red X...so when it's a green check does that mean when I click it that means colonists will be able to butcher the animal or does it mean they can butcher the animal as it is?  A tooltip saying "Right now colonists can butcher the animal, click to prevent animals from butchering this animal" is all it would take to clarify things, but it shows that the devs are not really thinking about the user experience because there are lots of little things like this in the game as of writing.There is no underground mining which is a disappointment.  "Mining" in this game is restricted to rock picking.  No underground bunkers for YOU.PROSThe graphics are great and having a 3d version of Rimworld is fantastic in principle.  If they add in more reasons to build things, for example building stuff for people's bedrooms to make them happier, this would be a really great game.  It's a decent game but should be early access still until there's more added.SUMMARYRight now if you already have Rimworld there's no reason to buy this game since this is a watered down version of Rimworld just with nice graphics.  Keep checking to see what the devs do, if they continue to add things then I'd eventually recommend this game for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is trying to be a 3D Rimworld, but forgets all the details that makes Rimworld so legendary.  However, it adds some elements that Rimworld lacks.+You can build a cool base with a huge house with many floors and actually shoot enemies from the top. I had a fun time building my mega house with solar panels and turrets on the roof-Combat is not fun. It all comes down to funneling enemies to a single entrance. And enemies are dumb, they will just go to the only entrance you leave open. There are no breachers or drop pods. There are flying enemies tho, but they are easy to deal with. There is a pulse rifle that stuns in AOE. 3 guys with these rifles can kill everything at the entrance to your base.-Only a few enemy types. Wildlife is not rich enough. Few weapons, armors.I recommend this game because of cool base building mechanics, but, as of now, I feel like it needs a lot of love until it becomes replayable and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Ajánlom mindenkinek, aki szereti ezt a stílust, de...A játékban rengeteg apró hiba, "csukás" van még, amire lelkileg fel kell készülni.- A karakterek hajlamosak abszolút módon figyelmen kívül hagyni a napi beosztást, és addig dolgozni, amíg vagy össze nem esnek a fáradtságtól, vagy idegösszeomlást kapnak a stressztől.- A feladatok automatikus elvégzési sorrendje abszolút logikán túli. Lényegében az elvégzendő feladatok keletkezési sorrendjét követi akkor is, ha az azt jelenti, hogy 3-szor szeli át a teljes térképet oda-vissza a karakter/robot/szállító drón.- Az építkezés, épületek felépítési működése (statika, hozzáférhetőség, terhelhetőség) abszolút kretén módon áll össze. Egyáltalán semmi köze sincs a valósághoz, illetve a praktikumhoz. Példa: Egy asztal fal mellé lerakható, viszont ha ezen falrész ablakot is "tartalmaz", akkor már ez nem kivitelezhető.- Ha átépíteni/modernizálni szeretnél egy épületrészt/elemet, hát borzasztó nagy türelem és aprólékosság kell hozzá, mert az átépíteni kívánt rész kijelölésére nincs egyszerű "egy adott típusú elemet kijelölök" mód.Még messze nem volt módom minden aspektusát a játéknak kipróbálni. De nagyon kellemes és szórakoztató számomra. A grafika jó, a zene élvezhető, s bár egy idő után monotonná válik a játékmenet, de remélem a jövőbeli fejlesztésekkel ezt orvosolják majd a készítők.I recommend it to anyone who likes this style, but...There are still a lot of small errors and "loopholes" in the game, for which you have to be mentally prepared.- Characters tend to completely ignore the daily schedule and work until they either collapse from exhaustion or have a nervous breakdown from stress.- The automatic execution order of the tasks is beyond absolute logic. Essentially, it follows the order of creation of the tasks to be completed, even if it means going back and forth across the entire map 3 times on the character/robot/transport drone.- Construction, the construction of buildings (statics, accessibility, load capacity) is put together in an absolutely cretinous way. It has absolutely nothing to do with reality or practicality. Example: A table can be placed next to a wall, but if this part of the wall also "contains" a window, then this is no longer feasible.- If you want to rebuild/modernize a part of a building/element, you need an awful lot of patience and meticulousness, because there is no simple "I select a specific type of element" way to select the part you want to rebuild.I haven't had a chance to try every aspect of the game yet. But it's very pleasant and fun for me. The graphics are good, the music is enjoyable, and although the gameplay becomes monotonous after a while, I hope the creators will fix this with future developments.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the haters who claim  is Rimworld and then hate on it for all the reasons it is not Rimworld -- after playing eleven hours.  RW is a fine game, but if the haters try to go back and play RW, they will wish it was more like SAD.  Part of the genius of  lies in the struggle to get your survivors off the planet one-by-one.  Attacks from local megafauna increase in intensity and frequency, so you find yourself always calculating how quickly you can evacuate, who should go first – and who should be the last person standing to hold off the worst attacks.	  This game mechanic creates a real sense of urgency and tension as each survivor bids adieu.  It’s nothing you cannot handle, as the game supplies you with a variety of automated turrets, traps, fortifications and weapons. 	  Ideally, you reach a point where your defenses do all the heavy lifting.  It can be great fun to watch as your flamethrowers and traps dispatch several hundred bugs without you so much as lifting a finger.	  But to get to that point, you have to collect resources, build up a food supply, establish a power supply, work your way through a research tree – all the things you associate with a first-class survival simulation game.  If you have dabbled in the genre before, you will find much familiar in SAD, but the beauty of the game is in its accessibility.	  Even if you have never played a survival sim, you can have great fun learning the ropes at the easier difficulties as you ponder tackling Insane/Chaos mode.	  The downsides include skill degradation, which the game never warns you about.  If you have a survivor who specializes in, say, research, but you give them tasks on occasion to help build up a secondary skill in crafting, e.g., you can come back just a few days later to learn that they have lost all those crafting points and more, because they are not constantly using the skill.  You never lose a skill level once you attain it, but any progress toward the next level can vaporize.	  Steam discussion threads are full of folks who complain about travel times to distant places.  The most obvious response is that it is not an exploration game.  After you crash land, click and drag across wide swaths of the map and all the resources in the highlighted area will be revealed.  If essential resources are not relatively handy, pick a new seed.  There are ways around any shortage, but especially if you are just beginning, you might want to minimize the challenges.	  And then there is the micro-managing.  If you set up the Activities schedule and the Priorities menu reasonably well, and you are playing on easier difficulties, everything will get done eventually.  I would suggest that this is actually the most fun way to play the game.  But let’s just agree that efficiency is not your survivors’ strong suit.	  When one of your survivors almost, but not quite finishes scavenging a wrecked spaceship, and instead of completing the task decides to meander back to camp to eat a fruitcake, the temptation is to jump in and direct the survivor back to the wreckage.  Odds are some other survivor is already heading out to finish the job.  But you have to be a certain kind of person, that I am not, to just let things unfold, however inefficiently.	  Finally, allow me to praise the online community, which is extraordinarily helpful and generous with its time and wisdom.  Flin Fredstone, Bjorn, tommy_b_schmidt and many others are the unsung heroes of this game.  The devs are a pretty constant presence on the forums as well, which is always a good sign.	  I have replayed the game numerous times without a single glitch and every playthrough has been different and uniquely challenging.  There are many different seeds, different teams that you can choose, different biomes, and two additional scenarios (Military Outpost and Sow and Sell), not to mention an active modding community, that make the game almost endlessly replayable (although if there are glitches, mods are almost always to blame).  I appreciated that the achievements could be obtained, more or less, just by playing the game.  Beware, though, that a Perfect Game with all achievements can become imperfect when they add content and new achievements, even after the full release -- and after you have moved on to some other game.	  This is one of those rare games that appeals to casual gamers, but as well to those who prefer a game into which they can invest many hours.  There is always one more thing to research, one more fortification to build, one more preparation for winter.  So feel free to blame me when you look at the clock and are surprised to see it is two or three in the morning.  Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: The AI of the survivors and their task scheduling could use some improvement. It can be frustrating to have to redo their schedule every time I need them to repeat a certain task. It would be helpful if there was an option to order survivors to craft a certain amount of items until they return to their regular schedule. This would be an easy improvement to implement.The electronics in the game break too quickly, which can be a limiting factor for players who enjoy building megabases. While I understand that this is supposed to add a challenge to the game, it would be nice to have the option to slow down the rate of decay.Manual farming for a game set in the future feels a bit outdated. It would be great if there were options for automated farming devices as a late-game option. This would add another layer of complexity to the game and make it more enjoyable for players who have progressed further.The game could also benefit from more advanced automation options such as the addition of NOT and OR gates, as the current automation items are fairly simplistic.Overall, the quality of life in the game could be improved as in  current state its 1/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally like survival based strategy games but I am really enjoying this.I like relaxed games that I can play at my own pace with little  real challenge.  I did put the settings on easy but the menu suggests that only affects starting resources. I could be wrong.I like the degree of randomness to each game.  This early access version doesnt feature seeded worlds just one very large world and you are randomly placed within it.  U then get to choose where to place ur base but my second game seemed to be in a very different area to the first.  Breakthrough technologies, creatures and resources are random.  Having said that there are plenty of each of them.  The graphics arent amazing but are very good for this kind of game, I recently played Manor Lords which looks very impressive.  Quite happy with how the game world looks.The mechanics of the game are pretty much what you would expect.  Scavenge resources in the early game then start mass producing them for processing into better resources to produce better technologies.  There is a great deal of freedom and creativity to how you create your base.  There are lots and lots of technologies to research.  After playing for 12 hours I had only got about a quarter of the way through the tech tree.The only real threats I have experienced are two different types of bugs that, if left unchecked, will eventually attack your base and colonists.  But you get a notification that they have spawned on the map.  Then you just need to squad up your two baddest asses and go bug hunting.  It was quite low stress and easy to manage.  I am sure the full game will have more challenge if thats your thing but the point Im making is that if you want a chilled game this fits the slot nicely.Things I dont like:You only get four crew members, that you get to select from a large selection of pre-built crew.  Initially this is fine, but once you get your base up and running you will find yourself struggling to balance all of the maintenance and production needs of your base.  There is an explorer mechanic that throws random missions at you that can reward you with new colonists and resources, but this is random and it takes (at least for me on  my two play throughs) too long to get to this point.  You will be frantically juggling your work priorities and micromanaging to a ridiculous extent cos 4 people alone arent enough way too soon.I have played survival builders before but usually, not always,  you will have a large population so if you lose one or two cos you messed up then its no biggie.  I lost one of my 4 colonists on my first play through.  This made the difficult task of managing an expanding base virtually impossible.  Shortly after a second one died and, at this point, I had no idea if or how i would replace them.  So 12 hours of gameplay down the drain when I pulled the plug.  This was my first play and probably largely down to my ignorance and error but pretty annoying when you realise you just wasted 12 hours, kinda...As its early access I am sure that the developers will change and add many things between now and release but the game is worth the entry fee as is, IMO.   Thats not to say I dont look forward to future developments and improvements but if your on the fence and you like this kind of management/builder type of game you will probably enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access game, its ok. Visually its very good, its like getting rimworld but with a good graphic engine and 3D camera.For what ive tested so far the game is not super hard, except for the energy management that is a real nightmare. I have 25 wind generators and 18 solar panels for 5 colonists and im constantly having shortages. I have 2 freezers, 2 fridges, 1 electric furnace, the advanced research table and 2 automatic turrets, i dont think i need a nuclear reactor for that, but it seems so. Must be like in Tropico, where you need 20 nuclear plants to provide power to an island with 2000 people. Another problem is the extremely short durability of any item you make, you need new clothes and weapons every few months, and thats alsot not very realistic, and annoying.The random animal attacks can also be annoying and ive suffered 4 in a row, with like 10 seconds interval between one and the next, and this is also not ok since you take ages to recover from any injury. The tutorial teaches you fences are useful to funnel enemies, but they arent, mad animals will constantly destroy the fences, even metal ones. The randomness is a little annoying and i would like to rely on how many animals i see in the map instead of having random spawns of 10-12 mobs every few minutes combined with local animals getting mad and attacking too.The time the colonist spend working seems super short, they usually leave tasks about to finish for stupid crap like taking a walk, when they can just finish it in seconds, but no, i better stop, take a walk and then i finish this critical stuff i have to build for survival tomorrow better when im more relaxed. Some resources are for some reason absent in some maps, like not having a single cloth plant in miles around the base and having to resource only to making bark leather.The tailor must be broken because making clothing takes like weeks for 1 garment alone. Equipping the whole colony while making one jacket takes like 4 days, not ok. They really need to speed up tailoring A LOT, and i mean like 3x or faster than current speed. Its not ok to build a wall in 5 seconds and take 10 real time minutes to build 1 garment when you need a full gear every season with the stupidly fast durability decay.Another little fail: When you manage to get the radio and build everything related like the antennas, the animals get angry, but if you turn off the radio antennas and the radio table the animals keep attacking as if they were active. I would like the animals to stop being angry if i turn them off.The random chance to get a new survivor landing near and auto joining is super low, ive only got it in two games and one was like 2 days after beginning and the other game she joined after like 2 years. The only other survivor i got was from a balloon mission. Hard to increase population.Needs lots of balancing in the durability and speed of some tasks, but its a promising product. EDIT: seems they fixed the tailoring speed, i tried it and its still too slow, i think they sped it up by 10-20% but needs double speed or more, not a slight increase.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is the colony sim I have been looking for, for sooooo long. I have a thousand hours on Planetbase, Factorio and Frostpunk, but I have 100% completed them and all challenges. There is nothing left to do. I have tried other games in search, currently addicted to Sons of the forest which is a phenomenal game I might add. However I need something with more over sight. THIS GAME, is the perfect colony sim. It has all the best parts of all three of those games. Personal and base management oversight, skill building, researching, tower defense against hostiles, scavenging, seasonal challenges, exploration and more. I am 7 hours in, and I am straight hooked. This is a game I will play for years and years by itself, and in between games when I need to zone out and refresh. Two thumbs up for gameplay, graphics and play style. If you are a simulation fan this is the game for you. Like all good sim games, scavenge fast and build a defense around your base as soon as possible because you will get attacked relentlessly and repeatedly. My other advice is to get some heavy clothing ready in the fall, stock up food/ration packs, winter will hurt.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: After 20 hours i feel totally bored. The game pace is extremely slow, yet there is nothing to really play it for. Very barebone game. In Rimworld i have over 1000 hours and there is still things to do. In this game, after first in game year, there is no reason to play further. Sterilised Rimworld. Very sterilised.The movement speed of the game characters is incredibly slow, even at top game speed. And i played a lot of game with slow pace, but not intentionally made by making chars move as slowest as possible to prolong the game, which has near nothing to offer.BIG NO. This is not a game, it is a screensaver.EDIT: Gave it a second chance. After next 40 hours, I can't change my mind. this game is just artifically extremely slow. It's like playing city builder like Banished or Ostriv with just 4-6 people whole time. The characters move speed does not suit to game with just 4-6 guys, could manage tenths of them with this speed. Extremely boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Game works fine until year 3 or so. Your people will start having constant mental breakdowns even with all rec structures available, or they'll be drunken bafoons who die to the attack waves that come every 3 days at a maximum. Or you won't have gotten that far and you'll die because your doctors will just refuse to heal someone, despite you manually telling them to multiple times, because they'd rather put on a new pair of shoes than heal your soldier that is now bleeding to death protecting said doctor. Game is a waste of money atm.IF they can fix the pawns simply refusing to do as commanded, and IF they decide allow you to actually do literally anything at all after year 3 or so (I cant even go on expeditions or I wipe at this point), and IF they decide to allow you to build multi-story buildings instead of just multi-tiered buildings, the game might eventually be worth looking into. But I'd wait at least a year before attempting this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ again. I've never actually wanted to kill my own pawns in a survival game before, and I've played RimWorld for a few hundred hours, and that's ignoring the problem of having attacks so often all your pawns can do is fight, recover, and fight again.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Rimworld style games, but want more updated graphics, this game is definitely worth a try. The developers have been very active and providing not only new content, but game improvements that make the game even more fun to play. In the first iterations of the game, you couldn't build multi-level, but after a lot of requests and working on the game, they implemented that and it was a huge game-changer.Some critiques I would give are related to things like the size of maps being SO BIG that you really can't traverse them in realistic times without something like a bike or hovercraft or even riding an animal. While they have added robots and drones to help with some of this, it still would be nice to see vehicle building to maybe get to those really far-away wreck pieces and whatnot. It would also be good to see more variety in the way of characters that aren't mod-specific, and people getting a prompt as to something like a %chance to find a new crew member during an expedition. Great game overall and one I've enjoyed most of the 300+ hours I've had so far at review time.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game Rimworld? No.  I would say it has its similarities but if I wanted to play Rimworld I would go play Rimworld. So far the game has been very fun and enjoyable, some things can be annoying like not being able to assign crafting bench priorities and assign character to certain benches.-The Ai does have some intelligence like know when to put warm clothes on or replace gear.- The happiness meter makes no sense. I could have someone with 200 positive mood influence points and 9 negative mood and yet they are really unhappy.- using a crossbow against a monster snaking you in the face while you have a spear in your inventory doesn’t make sense. Sometimes they will swap to a spear and sometime they won’t. I think it depends on the monsters hit box.Overall I’m having a great time with the game, I wish it didn’t have denuvo because I’d imagine the performance would be a lot better.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded is a good game, and with a few tweaks it could have been a great one, even with it's flaws I thoroughly enjoyed it.  I played once through the primary story mode, (Stranded), on Hard difficulty.  Without giving anyway any spoilers, I'll just say that the ending can wind up being fairly anti-climactic for how much build up you do to escape the planet.  A bit more tight scripting on the 'escape' portion of the game could have elevated this to absolute greatness.  My understanding is that some of the other scenarios have mechanics in them that scratch this itch.Recommended for fans of colony builders and sim games.  I have yet to play Rimworld, but my best guess is that it's a much smaller scoped version of that, with much better combat and graphics.  There's also quite a few mods available to improve QOL issues.  Solid game, I hope they do a sequel with a bigger budget!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: You've crash landed on an alien planet... lets explore ... asymmetric pedantry!What do I mean? Well you can micro manage your survivors; you can tell them not to eat raw meat, duh!. you can tell them how to prioritise farming, scavenging, crafting and other tasks so that they act (fairly) autonomously. You can even tell them not to eat any other survivors favourite foods! (I'm guessing that by default they're fairly self obsessed and don't give a hoot about anyone else, go team!).But Ken, my favourite psychopathic team member (he likes observing death , +6 happiness, that's not worrying is it?) can't seem to go to the shelves and choose a thermal jacket (crafted days earlier by Vivian) when the weather starts to turn - or can anyone else for that matter.Ken is unhappy (-6 happiness because he's cold), this is more than counterbalanced by the fact that he has nice 4x5 tile bedroom (+18 happiness). Kens got his priorities right!No he hasn't, Ken died 10 days later from hypothermia because I had the game on fast forward, desperate to believe that he could dress himself appropriately from the choice of over 25 different items of clothing without me telling him to do so.Why Ken, why? If you can prioritise your daily tasks and eat when you're hungry - why can't you dress yourself when you're cold?I would like to think he died happy - because I told everyone else not to eat his favourite meat stew, but now it's going bad because Ken isn't around to eat it anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game!  I have replayed over and over again and while the basics are the same on any map, the wide range of characters and near limitless map generation make every game a unique experience.  Creating my own characters through mod manager was the icing on the cake.This game is seriously deep and is a perfect blend of so many types of games.  It's like Sims, but with strategy, resource management, base building and a large tech tree.  Unlike anything else I've played.  Can't recommend this enough!The only complaint I have is how much of a time warp I get into while playing.  I can't believe how many hours I've played this over the last few weeks.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a "meh" category.It's not bad, but it's far from great.  It's  current Rimworld.  It's closer to Rimworld during the early alpha days (I backed Rimworld on Kickstarter).  It has an end-game.  You can win it.  But . . ..The "colonist" AI actively fights you when you try to fight.  It loves to spam massive hordes of enemies to zerg-rush your base.  And your non-drafted colonists will actively "go for a leisurely walk" right through the horde.At least, unlike AColony, I didn't die within one second of starting a map.  But, being able to successfully win a game (evacuating a total of 6 survivors) on my second game . . ..And let's talk about those survivors.  Sure, they have pretty art for each one, but, they're all pre-made characters with pre-made baggage.  And those are the only survivors you'll get to see.  You can't make your own.  And with the Denuvo Malware, you won't be adding your own, anytime soon.This game  Rimworld.  It wants to be, but it isn't.  It's not a bad game.  It's pretty, but coupled with Denuvo, I'd say go play Rimworld and avoid this until they remove the bloatware  it goes on sale.  It still needs an epic amount of work to approach Rimworld.  It's not a $35USD game.  It's a $20USD game.  With Denuvo, it's a $5USD game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is to Rimworld what many might claim Rimworld is to Dwarf Fortress. Better graphics, but severely parred down. There is nothing in this game you couldn't find a more in-depth experience doing in Rimworld instead. Add to the fact you can only have 8 total survivors and things like a basic inventory system for survivors to carry meds/food/bandages and it sort of seems like this could should've stayed in Early Access with the promise to continue expanding on the foundation it's built here.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Updating my review for post early access launch.Stranded: Alien Dawn is a colony survival builder game not unlike Rimworld.  It has 3 game modes that all center around building a base strong enough to survive wave after wave of giant insect swarms:Crash landing:  You crash land on a planet have to flag down passing ships and escape one survivor at a time over the course of a few months.  (So you have to build a base that can basically defend itself.)Military Outpost:  You have to build and defend a relay.Trading Outpost:  My favorite game mode.  You start with up to 3 survivors and a dream: Buy the planet.  Any members past your initial set must be hired, and they will leave if you fail to pay their wages.  You get credits by trading with passing ships, with each transaction costing you 50 fuel to send the trading pod up.I do recommend it, but the game is lacking features that other colony survival games have.  For instance, although it is a 3D game, this game does not let you build multi-story buildings unlike "Going Medieval".  As far as Rimworld features go, it's missing the ability to auto deconstruct old/damaged clothing/weapons, the ability to teach dogs how to haul, basically any relationship features save for marriage, a more fleshed out priority system that lets you prioritize workbenches and probably a few more that aren't coming to mind at the moment.  That said, I played through every game mode and enjoyed it.  Plus the game does have mod support.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: A spiritual successor to Banished that improves on it in several ways.  It benefits from shrinking the scope to a small group rather than a village, while increasing the depth of the crafting system tremendously. Be as primitive or advanced as you'd like, but achieving a balanced sustainable home base is satisfying and worth the effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: So I have put about 150 hours into this game since it released onto early access.  For an early access game I found it surprisingly well fleshed out.  It is early access and I look forward to seeing where this goes. Currently you kind of get the same old grind of things after a bit. Not Much Story even among the character interactions which is an area I hope that they develop.  I Do think that this is intended in order to create a lot more interesting goings about and add some variety to it on playthrough. It has a lot of potential and is enjoyable in its current state. The Things I did find after 150 hours is that this game for me gets a bit too repetitive and it is my sincere hope that the developers finished product will have extensive modding support and more depth to its characters and social interactions among a few other things. If the mission is to survive I did not find this much of a challenge and would like to see a bit more attention paid to the logistics of managing the survivors.  I Spent the majority of the game on the highest fast forward setting and easily overcame the few pickles i found myself in managing my survivors.  Its worth buying and supporting the devs and i sincerely hope they put up a roadmap.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Denuvo and their weird choices on the EULA aside... This is one of those "I wish there were a neutral button" reviews. This game was REALLY fun initially and I am hesitant to post a negative review after only paying $30 for 30 hours of entertainment but I probably won't play this game again after getting to a point where the micromanagement of ridiculous tasks started impacting my ability to enjoy the rest of the game. This was sad because I really was having a good time to this point.The main source of my frustration is from the wear and tear mechanic, or more specifically how to avoid that mechanic. You'll find yourself manually un-equipping and reequipping items constantly in this game for various reasons since there's no interface which allows you to automate this that I'm aware of. Your futuristic weapons have no option for repair or recharge and for some absurd reason even if never fired while equipped will break within a few years. The same goes for your synthetic high tech armor, and presumably just about anything else you can wear in the game. So, you're left with a decision to either remove them manually after combat (season or weather change etc) or watch them wither away. I can understand a straw hat made from hay lasting a year but a pistol or a set of synthetic armor being destroyed after 3 years is pretty silly.This mechanic would not be a huge deal at all if switching gear was easy, reliable, or if there was a way to automate it but as it stands it takes way too much time to do this and it snaps me right out of any immersion I had going on at that moment. I realize they have to create scarcity but this is just not a well thought out way to do it in my opinion and a very simple solution would be to decrease the decay on items which make sense. There is really no danger from the combat (for the most part) in the normal difficulty mode so I'm assuming this is their way of balancing it a bit once you start getting better items but it just makes for a frustrating experience.The rest of the game is a solid 8/10 so if you don't mind micromanagement on that scale you'll probably like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun. Save often (But there are only about 10 save slots so you'll have to reuse them which is my only complaint) and try different seeds and characters. Each changes the game enough to keep you interested. Enemy attacks scale based on multiple stats (some you can control some you can't) and difficulty Lvls seem to lend themselves to balanced play for different player skills. I also recommend Project X Repaired Mod once you get the hang of vanilla Stranded. Watch Tacticat on YouTube to see how to play this Mod. This Mod allows many more settlers and changes the goal to settling instead of escaping from planet.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Base Building, Community Management, Resource Management, Social Management, A little bit of everything in this game. It even has a fighting mechanic. You vs an untamed planet filled with hostile and docile alien creatures. How long will you survive? Will you lose your favorite character to disease? Starvation? The elements? Who knows! Best get the game and find out for yourselves!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I've played this for a few hours now.  So you pick 4 premade characters and all you pretty much do is try to juggle their affinities so they don't go mental.  The core of the game is not to gather resources or fight the elements and the local fauna, no, the core of the game is to manage a bunch of mentally ill people so they actually do their job instead of burning down stocks or furniture.This is all you go, make sure everyone does what they like once in a while so they don't have a mental breakdown.  You have to do this in between growing giant beetle invasions.That's all there is to this game.  You manage a bunch of morons so they don't off themselves.  This feels like Shutter Island...It's fun for a while but it gets old really quick and eventually, nothing gets done because everyone's on zanax...Oh and one of my guys tells me "I have a brain parasite, so I am going to inject myself with a poison but there's a chance that I become mentally retarded"...  Mentally retarded!!!  And of course, he did...FFS...

_childDocuments_.review: A promising 3D Rimworld-like. For an early access there is already a nice amount of content, despite the fact that we can expect a lot more from it. Hopefuly the devs can be inspired by Going Medieval and reach the immense potential this game has. It could very well be a gem in the long term.Overall, a pretty game, playable already and with a lot of potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Got this at 35% off, and it still wasn't worth the price. Could have been a thumbs down, but there's nothing egregious about it.It's an ok little game. More sane and playable than Rimworld, but limited in scope and appeal. Controller support is a huge plus, and I was able to play this from a couch start to finish (thanks for that devs).  I guess you could replay this over and over, but I feel no urge to what so ever. It well done, reasonably stable (got one freeze deconstructing a complex building) and polished enough.  It's not AAA at all, but still gives you a decent experience although a fairly blend and generic one. The characters are uni-dimensional, no voice, no real story, nothing memorable. This made me appreciate Riftbreaker, which left a stronger impression in the same style, even though it was a small game too. It's a competent product, but overpriced for what it is imo (although I do not doubt how much effort went into making it).  Sort of a take-it-or-leave it kind deal.  I don't regret my time with it, but it was once and done for me (which is fine, except for the price tag).
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Good game for EA. Lots of good mechanics in here, good graphics, and the unique traits of characters are good. I really, really look forward to the full release.That said, there are weaknesses. The AI and tasks need significant work. When you hunt or butcher an animal, the task excludes the hides. The butchering character won't go back and transport them. You have to either manually designate it or hope whatever character you have on delivery duty gets to it before it rots.The characters also forget tasks, or interrupt themselves. It's frustrating to have someone doing a task, hit an anything or relaxing hour, drop the item, do whatever else, and then start a new task instead of continuing what they were doing, because if you weren't paying attention you'd never know that now there's some resource sitting around rotting.Research breakthrough being tied to Seeds instead of randomized is a weird choice, as well. Effectively, it encourages making a Seed list (I think there a few that are starting), list all the starting area resources, all the breakthroughs, and then people just picking the "best" start for the gameplay they want. To me, randomized would be much better.Resource uses aren't really balanced either, which I can sort of understand, but you wind up with the mushrooms being a holy grail resource since it's food, healing, and with just being under a roof it lasts forever. Find a seed that gives you hay cloth and with two crops you have food, clothing, and healing covered, which is a huge chunk of the resources you need covered. A bit of balance here is needed. Maybe giving the mushrooms a shelf life and some sort of drying research to extend that, like with pickling.Fruit bushes are another bumper crop, but goes bad with no way to preserve it besides freezing. Maybe some sort of preservatives research, with the action of making preserves be an active task (like crafting a weapon or clothes)?Overall, a good start to a game that gives me good hope, but balancing and AI improvements will make or break it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: They make the game look so fun in the trailer. The issues with the game start to show when you see the menial AI attacks that hit your base every so often, this can be tweaked sure, but no amount of tweaking frequency in attacks changed the fact that the AI itself sucks donkey shlong. The game play loop ends up becoming the usual, "farm and get ready for winter," with these attacks that really break pace in the game. This creates a system that is frankly kind of lack luster and doesn't know what it wants. The game introduces expeditions for your survivors, giving little text based decisions that might result in resources or another survivor. The game caps out at 8/8 survivors, show me another base building management game that is that ass. You could honestly play something like this on game cube or something with its sort of bland game loop. The only thing going for it are its graphics, which already leave a lot to be desired if it is to be considered its redeeming factor. I haven't even gotten into the DLC policy which shows exactly how the company sees you, a money bag. To top this all off, there are whispers a second one is coming out already. skip this one.-mak

_childDocuments_.review: Survival, Base Building, Simulation, 3 of my favourite things in a game.I've played similar games that dump a couple of randos together and it's all about them and their petty issues with each other. This one doesn't totally focus only on that which is good.I love The Sims (except #4) and it has that feel but they are smarter and not as quirky. I don't have to turn off their free will, lol, and micro manage them.  It's fun but tedious with more than 1 person.The base building isn't too bad. 12 hours in and I'm still using the shelters but put together to make lots of rooms.One day I'll build houses for them, but maybe next game as I'm trying out each biome and seeing which settings I like the most.Having a lot fun with it all so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded is a solid offering at it's price point. I'd give this game a 3.75 out of 5, and it could easily pick up some ground with some small tweaks. Lots of base building, resource management, a little combat, and the RNG keeps you guessing on some variables. Worth the pickup to relax while between other games if you need a change of pace, or just want to veg out in your chair for an hour before it's time to crash. The good:Randomly generated maps, resources, events, and even any potential new characters that you pick up after your start? Nice touch. I dig the farming system. There is a little variance in terms of what you may or may not find on some maps, but for the most part it gives you a lot of what you need - while putting strain on the amount of time you have to complete tasks. The more you invest in your farming, the less you can craft or build things. Nice balance with this. The random groups of monsters that attack your little camp is a fun way to force you into action - and avoid this from basically being sim city - from time to time. Anything from little inserts to a giant mantis type creature. Kill em, and harvest those bodies for food or other resources! I like it. I enjoy the research aspect as well. There are a handful of random projects that will vary from game to game that gives you a nice boost, and can change how you have to play. Exploration gives a nice twist to getting additional resources, characters, or exploring some of the unknown on the planet. Middle ground:The OST is so-so. Could have been better, but it's not a train wreck either. Equipment feels like the standard offering, so I can't knock it, but the recent addition of mechs so far feels pretty OP. I haven't played on the highest difficulty or with hardcore modifiers, so maybe they are intended to be more for the harder game modes, but wow they mow down anything in site. Jury is out for now. The bad:The AI/pathing drives me bonkers half the time. While the system to prioritize/schedule things is a great concept, I find the computer taking longer routes to get to locations it needs to go. There are times when one of your characters will pick up only 50%-75% of the resources around it and head toward the storage location - while they could have still picked up a bit more that they walk right past! I will also watch at times the character that I dedicate to farming switch back and forth between harvesting and planting the same field - or sometimes multiple fields! The pathing is getting marginally better, but it still needs work. I will watch characters bounce back and forth from stack to stack as if it's considering the location of that stack from the distance it is from the starting point, instead of the current location. Over the course of farming a plot of land, harvesting that plot, or having someone run over to pick up food that was just harvested, it makes the total distance traveled a LOT longer, meaning more time invested in the activity. These type of issue forces you to manually manage individual tasks when you shouldn't have to.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I'm obsessed. It plays similar to the Sims except you manage survivors on an alien plant battling the elements and alien life. The world reminds me of the one on the show Scavenger's Reign. This is one of the top 5 games I've ever played.Around year 6 in the game, I encountered repeated crashes each day at 10am despite which save I reverted to. I was able to resolve it by sequentially deleting the latest save file until one worked that got past 10am. It was important to delete the latest save files and not just load the next one for some reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable experience but missing late game polish.The Good: -Starting out is very enjoyable, love the early game base building and learning about the world around you through the observe mechanic.  - Having different survivors with unique talents and personalities is great for fresh experiences. - Lots of ways to keep your survivors happy and healthy (or not) from clothing, food, recreation, enviroment, etc. Even something as simple as sleeping next to someone or in your own room can change how they feel. -Power grid is intuitive and not overly complicated while still allowing lots of customization. -Natural Disasters pose interesting and sometimes legitimately scary challenges. -Leading an army of bugs into your gauntlet of tower defense turrets is pretty satisfying. -Scheduling and task priority mechancis do a good job of helping you organize yours survivorsThe Not as Good: -Once you need to try to expand further than your immediate area its becomes a chore. The game spawns this whole big beautiful map but realistically you will never visit 90% of it. Getting your survivors to travel the map is time consuming and makes them so unhappy they tend to have a meltdown after maybe a day or so of game-time travel. Being able to research some sort of transportation like animal wagons or even gas vehicles in the later stages would really open up the map for more gameplay.  -The enemy variety feels not great. All the ground based mobs feel mostly the same even the ranged ones. They all funnel in in the same way and don't really change the dynamic of how you would build your base. Every attack is basically the same unless some of the flying ones are mixed in. Some unique tactics for different mobs would be interesting maybe some can (dig/climb/jump).  -The cost and creation of the later game building materials like concrete and carbon is so time consuming that i spent almost the entire playthrough with a wood and stone base.  -For the survival game mode you have to evacuate your survivors one at a time. I like the idea but in practice all it means is that you have artificially added 4-5 hours to your victory time. If you have built the base correctly then all there is for you to do is just stare at the orbital radio waiting for the next pod. Your part in the game is essentially over except for clicking 1 button every 20 minutes.Final Thoughts:I enjoy the game and think that it has a very solid foundation to build on. Some additions through later updates to open up map exploration and spice up the late game from becoming stale/repetitive and this could be a homerun.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun game I've played this year.  There is so much replayability with the different game scenarios, characters, difficulty setting, moon setting, advanced game rules, procedurally generated worlds and achievements that every new game is very different.  You can micro-manage your characters every move by queuing their tasks manually or you can let the activity menu handle tasks for you (I find a combination the most fun).  I can't wait to see what the devs come up with next.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic survival builder.  Looking forward to other scenarios and additional features.Some things I would change.The pace is pretty good,  though because 100% attention inst given to the game all the time, it would be nice if the combat system allowed for some automatic responses outside of fleeing away from your camp.Exploration. _childDocuments_.review: Really fun game with well designed mechanics.  They haven't done the best job at dialing in the difficulty curve (save early and often, sometimes the game will just demolish you out of the blue), but that can be forgiven.  I expect to keep playing this for years to come and the price is extremely fair given all that it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: i'm so addicted! I love that characters have their own personalities and skills. It keeps things interesting when trying to keep everyone alive. I also like that they allow you to speed up the game (I use it mostly at night when the survivors are sleeping) and that we get to tame animals (I LOVE THE ANIMALS). Graphics are decent too and the game gives you just enough time between attacks at the early parts of the game to recuperate and advance. I'm still pretty early in the game, I have not found many other survivors but so far it is still manageable and fun. I play to relax from real life and playing at medium difficulty is perfect for that. In addition, this is a single player game, non-MMORPG, which is exactly what I look for in games. I just want to play, relax, and NOT have to interact with other people online (I get too much human interaction IRL as it is). _childDocuments_.review: This game is as close to a hybrid as you get. Part Sims, Part Rogue-like (tactical engagements), part Tower defense, part RTS, part resource management, Part base-builder. It hits just the right places for people who want something to do while watching tv, vs the sped up mode when they actively want to engage and build with resources on hand. The time management, the bits of depth (such as the requirement for survivors to retrieve materials from nodes similar to classic RTS's make it's time management engaging and frustrating in all the right places. Pros:* Engaging in the ways mentioned above* Something to do as a second time spender while playing other games on say, a console, or otherwise like watching a TV show.* Difficulty is tuned about right in most of the right places. (Weapons feel good, Timing of waves seems okay. Learning curve is fine, and the game is easy to pick up and play) * For an early access game, and a 30 dollar price point, it's worth the value. More updates, maps, and such will enhance what it gives filling the game out more. Looking forward to new worlds and seeing what's going to be made available.* The interface, base building and other wise is easy to manage, but hard to master as you juggle what resources feel critical based on what's available.* Mechanics are common and well done to keep it engaging.Cons: (Note, part of this is feedback for the devs)* 1 world at launch (tomorrow there will be 2). I'd like to see a total of 4-6 biomes ideally for this set up* The wave / difficulty tuning push you towards common & specific research things immediately, preventing an initial building phase from being transitional to making certain research mandatory at certain stages.* The Seeding system does not fully, dynamically create maps. It in some instances seems only to alter the starting point of a map. I have had 1 map repeat it feels like 3 times where it was nearly Identical if not identical 3 times. (I have some 10, though not fully successful campaigns)* Crafting is Incredibly punishing timewise unfortunately, as having 2-4 people out of Gathering, salvaging, mining or tree chopping building or forced to craft electronics endgame short of a specific research upgrade make said research upgrade break the game by terms of difficulty & Utility.*Cannot build tiered bases; the fact that you can't build a second floor out of top teir materials Like Brick, stone may be because vertical isn't fully implemented from a building side, but it feels like a small if not critical oversight.* Unable to easily replace and upgrade the built base. (If I want to swap a wooden wall or stick wall (God, why build using sticks?!?) with a concrete or Brick wall, then I need to deconstruct and construct that wall as the improved one. Rather than having the simple method like the gate does with fences, you have to manually do this) *Waves can develop towards ridiculous numbers which cause the game to become CPU bound performance wise (I had a 10 year campaign, where I was getting waves of 400 + mobs. This is a bit out of control. Quality over quantity would be better in most of these instances, if not boss monsters)* Lack of variety regarding monsters/waves. It's always a swarm, not 1 big dude and a few little ones.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot going for it but it is still early access for a reason.  Vital things are extremely difficult to obtain/craft such as clothing and electronic parts.  Even after getting the appropriate resources and having maxed out settlers producing these items it can take several days to complete.  This is pretty bad considering it can take a few days to each items to break so by the time a settler creates their first pants, everyone is already walking around in their underwear.The interaction between settlers are also lacking.  They can fall in love but that's about it.  No friendships/rivalry/etc.  There is a wedding arc but they can't use it at the moment since it is buggy.  Lovers also do not have a way of sleeping with each other which is odd since they get a daily penalty for not sleeping with each other.  I figured they would just remove it for now until they add that possibility.This game is a better copy of Rimworld in terms of graphics but it fails to compare to it in terms of content.  Once you get to the end game content, it's a grind to get anything done.  Oddly enough, it gets harder to survive the more advanced your group gets. After more content becomes available and things get finely tuned, this game is going to be amazing.  I will happily support this through EA and hope they don't take that support for granted.

I think I finished my first map in about 30 hours completing everything, but there's definitely some replay-ability with the various characters, difficulty settings and different maps/biomes)Has Denuvo, but I don't experience any weird performance issues or problems relating to it. _childDocuments_.review: The game, as it stands, could be likened to a basic version of 3D Rimworld, yet it lacks the same level of charm and variety, featuring only a single type of enemy. The available DLC adds some unusual features, but these don't quite elevate the game's overall appeal.Its mechanics are reminiscent of tower defense but are hampered by an underdeveloped technology tree. The game also seems to struggle with realistic portrayals of electricity, physics, and technological progression. For instance, players transition from using primitive bows to constructing AI-controlled machine gun turrets from mere scraps, which feels disjointed.There is potential for improvement in future updates, ideally focusing on enriching the game without relying on frequent, revenue-driven DLC releases. It may be more prudent to consider purchasing this game during a significant sale, or to wait until it undergoes further refinement and thoughtful development.

_childDocuments_.review: As another user has pointed out, they have a very crappy End User Licensing Agreement. They really can do whatever they want and they even outline rare circumstances where they reserve the right to do so, this sounds reasonable in theory but in practice the developers are always holding your copy of the game hostage in a manner of speaking. Anyway since I am stuck with the game now I will have to get my moneys worth out of it. Are you ready to hear my thoughts developers? I hate that I cannot rebind the alt key to my side mouse buttons, for anybody with a gaming mouse like me your thumb is probably resting on those side keys while playing.. games like Dyson Sphere Program allow me to rebind it and IT'S NOT AS IF THERE IS A CONFLICT, THIS BUTTON IS NOT IN USE IN GAME AT ALL AS IT IS.Also the time options should be on Q and E respectively, why on earth is the default controls set to the - and + keys? I wouldn't even care if you just copied Oxygen Not Included and its approach by having the TAB key use fast forward, pressing repeatedly brings it back to the previous options.Now let me say what I am honestly thinking here. In the tutorial you get to observe a mushroom and simultaneously set a craft on the work station. WHY ON EARTH DID IT TAKE LONGER FOR THE GUY TO OBSERVE THE MUSHROOM THAN THE DUDE WHO HAD TO GO CRAFTING? I'm not mad here, don't mistake my caps for that or hostility/negativity.. it's just baffling that in a pre-defined circumstances such as tutorials that this can happen, it could even give off the impression that if general observation is this slow the game is going to be a real slog all the way.There's also a light flickering through the trees that really, really breaks immersion and I toggled some settings off but it didn't change it. I will again investigate it later but I'm not holding my breath I can turn it off. This review is IMO rather fair unlike the EULA. Big fat not recommended, even topping my disdain for Rain World because that was actually a very good game despite the complaints I had with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly by-the-numbers survival-management game with actual full controller support and great base mechanics, hindered by non-sensical updates and even more non-sensical DRM. And no, it's not an online game, it has DRM for no reason at all.If you're the kind to play long hours and mouse + keyboard become a pain, you probably love the "Full Controller Support" tag, and know the tale of seeing it and going "hmmmmmmmmm". Well, it's not Tropico levels of controls streamlining and ease-to-use, but it's great.Aside from that, the good twist that some games of this genre only started doing now, Stranded AD already does, which is the character selection. Instead of the "randomly generated peeps with numbers that either make-or-break-the-game or make-no-difference-because-we-don't-want-to-kick-the-player-in-the-nuts", you choose between different pre-made surviors (or leave it to fate), and it's then a matter of covering your needs. When they like a task, they get happy doing it, and sometimes just can't do it. It's a great start.Different than most of the genre, it also focus not on continued survival, but you do have an end goal (different on each scenario). Good amount of difficulty options to tailor how things will go until then, and survivor combinations and how to approach things will help keep the replayability high.Development went really well out of Early Access, with set goals and roadmaps. New game modes got added, mod support got implemented, and more importantly, several quality of life features got introduced that reduced micromanagement. It's still a personal pet peeve of mine that doing micro to battle is LEAGUES beyond not doing it, and this wasn't nowhere touched so far, so this might be a heavy turn off for those who prefer the management side more than the battle (but there is a "pacifist monsters" option).New DLC dropped, and I was anxious to try it and give a bit more of support for a game that is on the cheap side for the amount of content, but the update came with changes that did nothing but create more busy work while making no sense at all, creating artificial difficulty for the sake of it. Given that, and the fact that the developers have not even bothered addressing keeping a DRM on a single player game that is doing nothing but being a pain on players with poor internet connection, I'll just change this from positive to negative to steer away anyone hoping that things would have changed for better after launch.

_childDocuments_.review: Five hours in and I'm having mixed feelings.  To be sure, the game isn't bad, but there are some issues.  It really does remind me of when RimWorld launched, which is appropriate since so much of the gameplay seems directly influenced by that game.  Also, very similar to RimWorld, modders have stepped in to shore up, modify, or add completely new components to the game - allowing people to really customize their experience - if not for this, I'm not sure how I'd feel about the game overall.As I haven't progressed that far into the game, or the tech tree, based on the gameplay videos, this won't be a comprehensive review or a final judgement on the game.The game has a lot of good points, but most of those are based on the similarities to RimWorld.  I don't think I need to elaborate on that too much.The things I feel that need a bit of work are the pacing, speed control, and setup options when starting a new game.  The pacing feels a bit slow overall and even when changing the game speed, the highest speed feels slow.  My survivors go to bed and it still takes awhile for night to pass - it isn't like we're talking minutes, but compared to RimWorld it just seems slow and considering how progression overall seems slow, it makes the entire game seem to drag.  Then there are limited options when creating a new game.You can enable or disable raids, but you can't actually change the frequency.  Because of this, the raids appear to follow a set pattern, which just makes it seem like the insects have a calendar that they follow for attacking - "Uh oh boys, we've got a raid on the calendar for tomorrow - let's go kill some humans!"  I'd like options for changing the frequency of everything from storms, raids, weather events, etc.  From 0 to however many days (to set the random frequency), but raids must be y days (again, 0 to whatever) apart at least.Anyway, if you like RimWorld, there is a good chance you'll like this.  It isn't a one-for-one copy, but if you've played RimWorld you will immediately recognize a lot of its influence.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Haven't bumped into any bugs, but the AI could be improved upon. It's annoying to watch the survivors go back and forth instead of going in a straight line. I think the game is adequately challenging on the harder levels, but is mind numbingly slow on easy mode and since the attacks are rare you have a hard time getting resources from the critters since they are sparsely populated on the map.I would like the ability to prioritize the activities and crafting tables so I can control what all my survivors are focused on.

_childDocuments_.review: Its ok, I just expected more. It gets really slow at a certain point where you kinda have to build Mechs in order to scout out the map... exterminate bug colonies, rinse repeat. Then researching that technology gets a little bit dull and I cant imagine that it gets any more challenging from a survival standpoint other than the fact that the game just evolves in to a tower defense as you progress. I've put a lot of hours in to Rimworld, and I think the reason there is because there are so many permutations and weird stories that come up in that game - thats what keeps me coming back to it. In Stranded : Alien Dawn, that is not the case though. You don't really get the suspense of different interactions and strange permutations of neighboring tribes... endless moments where random people could join or leave. S:AD has a very static approach to forming your caravan and embarking on your journey. Its less chaotic, sure but its definitely a bit more boring to play this way. In S:AD you will only ever encounter the static characters that you can choose your initial group formation. The interactions those characters have is not all that interesting, and accessing the log of what conversations happened, what their preferences are or what makes up their personality is a little cumbersome and not as rewarding by comparison to something like Rimworld.But if you're the type of player who has never experienced a Survival Sim Base Builder, this could be a good entry in to your series. If you're veteraned up from your experience in Rimworld, you'll probably find this game to be a bit more like the "diet coke/walmart" version... If you are a hardcore Rimworld enthusiast and play with various mods, creating religions, experiencing all that RW has to offer - you'll find this game super boring.Like I said, its ok though. The graphics are pretty fair for a 3D adaptation. I'm 20 hours in and I feel like I've experienced all this game has to offer, make of that what you will.
