_childDocuments_.review: Another survival game, that has breathtakingly annoying rot cycles asynchronous to useless growing cycles, based on seasons that only serve the threat of winter. Another survival game with uselessly exaggerated damage by use. Another survival game, in which whatever attacks has x-ray vision and therefore spends more time doing random buildiong damage than hunting targets in the open. Another survival game, in which its protagonists whine, that their Chardonnays doesn't have the universally accepted serving temperature - 20 days after crashing into an alien world. Reason enough for yet another meltdown. Hoo-ray!Stranded Alien Dawn looks interesting and could be fun. It isn't. It is just another game, which tries so very hard to be Rimworld, but instead of a presenting a nifty, fresh idea or three to lift it above the classic template, it does nothing more than falling short in direct comparison. There is not enough novelty in this game to make it interesting, even if and when its wonky base game loop is fixed.A tip to the developers?Survival games should be 4X - explore, expand, exploit, and exterminate. SAD, like so many others of its kind, is merely 5R - rot, repair, replace, riot - and ultimately repress.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Initial review: ~8 hours. Edited review: ~14 hours and completion of Crash Landing scenario on Medium.I can definitely understand why some people have given this game negative reviews. It is a very, very slow-burn of a game. In the first few hours, at least on the scenario I played, although I was enjoying it, I just didn't feel as though I was really progressing much, mostly because there's a ton of setup. With only 4 survivors to start out, there is a lot of micro-managing that needs to be done, between observing crops and animals to see if you can grow/tame them, keeping food stocked up, gathering resources, taking care of aggressive mobs, researching tech and then building up your base. I also noticed, again in this specific scenario, that getting extra survivors is incredibly rare. In my ~14 hours I managed to trigger 1 special event that got me a 5th survivor, which was definitely helpful and sped-up progression. Now, I do have to mirror some of the negative feedback here. Tweaking the "assignment panel" and setting priorities based on what my survivors are best at, still led to certain things not getting done and a lot of manual "go here, do that". It seems like the game only wants each survivor to do 1 or 2 specific tasks and stick to them, but it's simply not possible when you've only got 4 guys and a ton of different tasks (some of which probably shouldn't be considered tasks) to do. It also feels like certain tasks within a specific task-type have higher priority (which you cannot see or change) than others.Also, because of how tasks are categorised and divided up, in some scenarios, 3 survivors will all be doing parts of 1 thing. For example, you'd think cutting a crop, replanting it and then taking the produce to storage would be 1 complete task within "Farming", but it isn't, it's actually 3 different tasks (Cutting, Farming, Delivering), which all have their own priorities (and therefore survivors set). Meanwhile, crafting items and cooking are done on a "what's first in the list" priority system, so you'll constantly need to tweak what you actually want your survivors making. Also, when I say "craft until 3" and those get crafted, why doesn't it get removed from the queue instead of staying there with "limit reached" on it? Small thing, but can make the menus cluttered. Once you progress through the research and start getting into electricity, you might think a lot of these tedious tasks would end up no longer being an issue and therefore streamlining gameplay. Yes and no. For example, the drones (a much later research) do improve gameplay, as they will handle delivery of resources to/from storage (only the delivery), however your actual electrical grid can be very fiddly to set up. Although at the start, it can be as simple as slapping down some wind turbines and solar panels and then linking everything up with power-poles, some tedium creeps back in when you want to start setting up and automating things, especially base defenses, as they can be a massive power-drain. Changing circuits on any electrical equipment is a task that a survivor has to complete and turning a switch on/off is also a task that a survivor has to complete. Therefore, constructing a bunch of turrets, linking them up to a switch and having everything set to specific circuits can still be a lot of manual "go here, do that" for a survivor. It's even worse when the switch is off (so the turrets are too), then you get a raid on your base and need to select a survivor to manually go and turn the switch's state over to activate the turrets. You can only get true automation when you've further researched the various sensors and have then spent the time linking everything up to their respective circuits and such. You then think you can relax and let your survivors get on with tasks that matter, like feeding themselves and researching/crafting stuff, but what then happens is that electrical equipment constantly breaks down and needs repairs - and I do mean constantly. By the time I was finishing up the scenario, I had about 20 carbon wind turbines and I am not joking when I say that every ~30 seconds, one of them was "malfunctioning". For some of the tech, this can be a major hassle, as you'll need 1 of your survivors permanently stuck to the soldering bench making CPUs or some-such to keep up with the repair demand. That is unless you get lucky and keep getting them from passing ships (when you've got the orbital radio set up), or from expeditions.As for the combat stuff, I'm on the fence. It felt a little tacked-on to pad-out play time. From what I can tell, the amount of enemies that will raid your base depends on your stockpiled resources and researched tech. It starts out with a couple of raiders, then ramps up to 10s of them and then 10s of multiple different variants. When you've only got 1-2 survivors kitted out and any good with combat (and no turrets yet), it can get hairy pretty fast. In my playthrough, I had a raid of like 80 enemies and had 3 of my 4 survivors bleeding out and fainted, while my commando was on an expedition; Needless to say I wasn't prepared to lose 6 hours of progress and my entire base, so resorted to some "sneaky" methods to stop that from happening.In regards to the whole "managing morale" mechanic, it's going to depend on your selection of survivors. In the entire ~14 hours I played, I only had 1 meltdown happen and it was my crafter/carpenter who was constantly moody because of... well, I don't really know why. He was fed, warm, clothed, had his own house with bed and fireplace, was constantly getting happiness from the leisure items... but nope. After his meltdown though, he gained a ton of happiness through his supposed self-enlightenment and then was never moody after that. It basically became a pointless mechanic about 4 hours in honestly. Don't overwork, sleep-deprive or starve your survivors, slap down some leisure items and give them a warm bed and you're set. A note should be made here that the selection of survivors is not balanced. I get that these are meant to be "real people" and therefore all have different skills and tolerances, but the fact is that there's a handful that make a scenario a walk in the park, while the rest of them are pretty terrible. Setting difficulty to easy but picking terrible survivors will make a scenario harder than if you played on hard-mode, but with the "OP" survivors - it's just a bit silly. I picked Greyson, Nova, Melody and Laara (Paulette joined later) and outside of the previously mentioned poorly-timed raid, I didn't have any issues. Lastly, the "end game". The end game of the scenario I played through was essentially sitting around and waiting for the next spaceship to come through on the orbital radio. The game does slow to a crawl at this point, as the more survivors you have leave, the less stuff you can get done in a given day. The best practice is to make sure you have stockpiles of everything (especially food) and have done all the research, so then it's not a big issue if someone suddenly gets rescued. For me, Nova popped up on screen telling me to leave her till last, possibly due to the fact that she had every skill at max level, thanks to an expedition she went on, or possibly due to her innate ability to completely avoid meltdowns. It is definitely best to leave the most resilient person till last, as others can become lonely and experience meltdowns because of that. Overall, despite the visible flaws, I am still enjoying my time with this game thus-far and I am glad I got it from Humble after eyeing it up for quite some time. It's definitely a case of needing to enjoy this genre and slow-burn type of game though.

_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, i've just finished the game! My last guy left the planet during an attack that he would probably not have survived ! Very addictive and not so easy. Really loved it. A few, small bugs (only a few days after the release of the early access !) but nothing serious and a very rich game. In a word (or little more) you select 4 survivors (out of 20 I think). They escape from a crash and will have to survive on an alien planet with only their bare hands. So choose wisely ! They don't have to same abilities. They'll have to cook, make their own clothes to survive fierce winters, houses, fields etc. You may even marry two of them which would increase significantly their mood (and you'll see that it is VERY important!). The second part of the game is the toughest from my point of view : you'll be able to contact vessels that will be able to rescue your survivors, one by one, diminishing slowly but surely your already small team. And to my point of view this is the most difficult part of the game (especially when there's only one left).This game is amazing and will put you through the most opposite emotions in a very short period of time. You're totally free to build everywhere you want the rooms and buildings in the shape you want (no second floor to buildings though but that's not a problem). So think well : not to lose time, no to disregard the well being of your team (temperature, distractions, dry and clean clothes, good and diversified meals, a nice living space), and you'll have to organize weapons to take care automatically of unfriendly visitors (bc even when there's one or two left, you'll have hords of enemies running to your precious devices).  Then yes, I do recommend this game 100% !
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  If you want a chill, no-challenge little game where you set people to do stuff and then basically walk away, or if you *really* can't stand the Rimworld graphics and don't mind playing a much more simple version of that game, then this may fit what you're looking for.I'm not totally sure how to rate this, but I've enjoyed my two playthroughs a bit, and it's only $30, so I think it deserves a thumbs up.The problem with the game is that it's really easy/simple, and it's really a one-time play type of game.  There really just isn't that much to do.  I won the first time I played (easily), and played through a second time when they added animal taming, but that really didn't add much to the game unfortunately.Basically, if Dwarf Fortress is college, and Rimworld is high school, this game would be early elementary school (but with okay graphics).  If you have never played any games like Rimworld, then I assume Stranded: Alien Dawn will provide some challenge and a lot of fun.  If you've ever played Rimworld, then this game will be a complete breeze and just a relaxing, semi-boring little builder game with some farming and crafting, and some attacks by animals that you will dominate.Also, I highly recommend NOT playing with the random survivors option turned on.  To me, random survivors seems like it should be the base way to play the game (A spaceship crashed, but in this game you get to pick all of your survivors?  That should be an option in my opinion, and if you choose your own survivors you shouldn't be able to get achievements or something).  If you go with random survivors like I did on my first playthrough, you start with each of the survivors having a railgun sniper rifle which is the best weapon in the game (there are only like 5 weapons, although you can research "advanced" railgun sniper rifles... *snore*).  With 4 railgun snipers, you basically don't need to build defenses until the 2nd or 3rd year, if even then.Anyway, the game was fun to play through, and the second time was okay I guess, but I don't know if I'll ever play it again unless there are a lot of major updates that make it more interesting.  I had been looking forward to this one for a while, so it's a bit disappointing that it's so simple and easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan f this game. It really is just a re-imagining of RimWorld. It feels a little less fleshed out but it has big enough skill trees and enough scenarios to keep you busy. If you've not gotten Rimworld full edition yet on sale, get that. If you have and you're looking for a prettier adventure this fits that niche nicely. I've had great fun with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: There is most definitely a good game in here screaming to be let out but i dont believe it will ever be realised (thats why after my first review [left below] I kept trying to find it).Rather than focusing on big updates the devs clearly need to focus on getting the basics right. Pathing is still a joke.two examples Hunt far away killing multiple animals the survivors still wont collect all of the items (of the same type) meaning multiple inefficient back and forth.Planting a perfect square/rectangle field where the fertility is the same through out does not result in clearly efficient planting of straight lines but zig-zagging random patterns that make no sense what so ever.And again as mentioned before attacks seem completely out of kilter with your ability. Again i love a challenge but sending scorpions on day 30 when all i have is a pistol and bows and arrows makes no sense.The only reasonable explanation is the devs expect you to behave in a certain way any any variance means failure which makes for a disappointing experience.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Original review (left after the first patch):Attacks are Totally Unbalanced after the last patch.While i love a challenge the new attacks are totally over powered. I always felt that at 1 every 5-7 days was a bit much but now they are totally overpowered (Hell i have one save with three major attacks in a week and one set of hungry visitors - you cant recover with that frequency). While the fix addressed some of the issues vomit, craft time, too frequent malfunctioning and added a bit of variety to the attacks over all its done more damage than good. The most frustrating part is while a fair few early access games tweak the balance with regular patches over the first week or two it was three weeks before the first patch that has wrecked the game and days later still no word of anything to resolve the screw up.There is a fair amount of potential in this game but being so slow to address the issues gives me little hope it will live up to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable game - I cant believe this is only just released in early access, it's miles better than other more established games in this genre.  A well thought out research tree and loads of content already!  I love the turret defences, they feel powerful and work well with sensors.  The game even has an ending to work towards at your own speed.  Great visuals and atmosphere, cant wait to see the finished article.. Worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate its an early access game - Bad Storage Management, Lack of prioritisation, Missing a lot of simple content which could make it better - Not to mention the amount of bugs encountered (no pun intended) - Its promising game but unfortunately they need to fix a hell of a lot things before I would come back to this.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: One of my biggest issues with this game is the fact that AI/pathing, often you will find your characters standing around not knowing what to do when they are already assigned for certain task, it seems it takes them a little bit to calculate and realise what they should be doing leading me to manually assing them to their tasks which is rather annoying as this happens really often. _childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game on the basis that it is Early Access. The other complaints listed here are valid, this game has a lot of room to grow, and I am hoping that it lives up to its potential. It can be very frustrating as there is a rather steep learning curve. I have gotten my group to 4 years and its more tedious and frustrating than anything at this point. The game definitely needs more ability to directly give orders as I spend most of my time trying to manipulate AI priority so they do what I need them to do instead of just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around. Overall, good game - definitely solid for early access.I hope it keeps up.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Paid $50 AUD. Played for 6 hours. Still wanting to play, so I guess it's good? It's easy to pick up. I think the draw to it is the taming animals options. It can get very hard during Winter.I do think there is room to improve though. I think paying $25-$30 would be more appropriate. I would like to see some kind of PVP option.I would LOVE to have more A.I given to the animals. It's pretty good though! Just enhance the grazing, hunting, sleeping. Give them all a little life. Maybe even show them getting playful. Currently good though. You see them hunt/graize and sleep. I found it hard to set priority tasks. Could be me. But that could be done easier. You can prioritise in sub catergories, like what clothes you're making before other clothes. But if you have to click the arrow over and over until it's at it's position and each time you click the arrow it moves up the position so you have to move your mouse too. It would be better if you could click and drag the order instead. Also, you can't move storage shelves once they have items in them. It should be like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: To start out, I don't review games that often. This is basically a 3D version of Rimworld which I absolutely enjoy. I have hundreds of hours on Rimworld. This game right now as it is, is pretty good but It could be a lot better though. My first thoughts on improvement would be little Hauler/Transporter robots, if we can research and build Giant battle mechs, then I don't feel like a little Roomba type Hauler droid would be that far fetched. Possibly even trained animals being to be que'd for pickup/transport. 2nd idea is that something for transportation to move around the map faster and to be able to carry more things, Perhaps a little go cart or even a wagon attached to a tamed animal, Hell i'd even settle for the mech being able to carry stuff...  My people have to traverse for like 20 to 30 seconds or maybe like 1 to 3 hours in game just to go pick up 100 pieces of whatever. They soooo much rest and food and energy for something that could be simplified. Hell even rollerskates or something to quicken movement would be great. Maybe Jetpacks???3rd though is being able to repair clothing, Unless you happen to get carbon armor breakthrough or are able to get a ton of synthetic thread for armor, this stuff breaks down soooo fast. While we're on the subject of clothing make it an option for them to change by themselves unless ordered not to! Their adults have a wardrobe and let them make heating/cooling decisions(unless ordered not to).4th thing, Need more power generating options, if you don't get lucky with the Graphene Breakthrough or the Carbon wind tunnels then you're out of luck. A regular solar panel is only +20 the Graphene is +60! You'd have to have a whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ solar farm plus they only work during the day. so hopefully you got those batteries set up well enough. 5th thing, more options with animals. If I have a tamed vicious animal, allow me to attach it to a hunter that will follow them around and attack with them. 6th thing, add fishing! there's always these little ponds around or next to the giant ocean, there's already alien life everywhere, why is there no sea life?! Should be easy enough to be able to configure that out. 7th thing, easier allowance to building on water. If I want to build an ocean bungalow or a resort then let me. Granted if would cost a lot of resources then so be it. That's all that comes to mind right now that would massively improve gameplay, in my opinion.I'll end with saying the game is still very fun, I hope that he gets more love and attention. Could easily be the next Rimworld if they keep working on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Even in the early access stage, the game is very playable and as a survival/base builder game I find it excels in both those areas. I enjoy this game and know that further updates will only increase the time I send in it and I already have over 230+ hours since October 12th as it is, highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very similar to Rimworld in almost every way minus the Rimworld DLC. If you are looking for a prettier and more ambitious version of Rimworld, I highly suggest trying this out. There is plenty to do and lots of interesting mechanics. I am happy to support this game. I know they are using Denuvo, but it is not noticeable to me and is a very minor con. Support this game is you enjoy colony sims, you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, a 3D rimworld yes, but hey I'm happy with it, but:It's 3D, why can't we build upstairs? Why can't we build turrets on some sort of wall structure. At least let us put a floor on top of another floor to gain a bit of height.That all said it's early access, I'm sure these points will get sorted.Was it worth the ~£20 I paid yes and if you bought and liked Rimworld a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: this is a fun game its almost identical to rimworld without alot of features of rimworld. that being said the 3d environment is much more appealing to look at. i will continue to play this and hope that the devs add things such as "room restrictions" to keep avatars locked to certain locations of the builds. animal husbandry would also be a great feature.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access obviously, but I've been having a lot of fun so far. The job priority system needs a little fine-tuning, time certain things take to do definitely could use a re-work, but overall it comfortably lets me mostly focus on macro-management.Combat is... Fine? Nothing remarkable but nothing terrible. If weapons need to degrade while carried I'd love there to be a weapon cabinet or something that survivors can use to hold their weapon loadout without them degrading, unless given a command to retrieve them or a job that requires them (like hunting, or even observing/salvaging). This would let you choose to risk them being unarmed if you forget to tell them to rearm before a swarm of angry bugs arrived, without turning into fiddly management to let them do combat-oriented duties.Base building is simple, solid and easy to work with. Will be exciting to see new additions to what's already available!As with any early access game, best to wait for the full release, but looking super promising!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to Going Medieval except sci-fi based. Anyone who plays Rimworld or Going Medieval will get this. Definitely some mechanic improvements over GM and RW. However, it lacks content. 9 hours casual play and I have maxed out the research tree. Resources (ore/scrap) has become very scarce when at this tech level that is your primary resource you need, which makes for tedious play. That being said, it's early access and has a lot of room to grow. There is also modding support in workshop and already several mods made. I see a lot of potential in the future. Devs seem to be committed to improving the game. I recommend purchasing however, don't expect a finished product atm
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I am very pleasantly surprised by this purchase.This is practically Rimworld in 3D, but frankly already much better by my taste.In fact this is the only early access game I played, which does NOT feel completely unfinished. Sure, story line or character building is lacking, but the entire base building and research aspect work pretty well.There is a lot of room for improvement and fleshing out the game, but If the devs continue on this path, the game should turn out a big success.I bought the game and played nearly 20 hours - no crashes or issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It looks and plays like Rimworld, and I have played Rimworld over 700 hrs but this game still brings me new excitement.Z axis is awesome. It's an interesting view that you see survivors rain bullets to bug tide on the roof! Yet the system is not solid or deep enough (organ replacement, prosthetic, human enemy, prisoner system...) I wish to see it grow gradually. Great job, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, don't get me wrong, but it has too many unrealistic concepts, such as humans melting down because they're a little tired (not exhausted, just not fully rested, and well-fed), as well as taking hours to traverse short distances adds to the unrealistic feel of it.   I can buy into the 48 day year given it's a moon, but the concepts of physics and chemistry are obviously alien to the engine developers. No understanding of material.  Elements don't decay, for example (although they may oxidize). It's just designed to make you spin endlessly in circles.They added a rule to allow for faster movement, however the standard engine hasn't been updated with the correct values. I'm sure there's a player base out there for it, just not any that are familiar enough with physics to care/notice the difference. Water is not a concept here, but rather a given, so if that aspect of survival is part of what you were looking for (I was), then keep looking.It's good for obsessive builders, if you can tolerate the rate of breakdowns (the false economy concept is baked in as far as that goes - nothing lasts longer than a couple of years).
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: A new take for a single player survival game that is refreshing.I'm really looking forward to further development and additions to the game.Still on my first go and used default difficulty but if there was a setting to make some of it random I chose those.  And overall it is still a bit to easy.  Random survivors having rail guns is likely why.  I think it would have been way more difficult without them and I'll try a new game later.Graphics is good enough.  Sound is ok but with a minor cooking bug where the mixing of ingredients doesn't stop unless you scroll away from camp then go back.  I'll have to judge difficulty later as I think the random survivors having railguns to start is likely why it is to easy.  I thought random survivors was going to be a big challenge addition, but the railguns likely make up for it way to much.Overall the game is somewhat well balanced overall though.  After 31 hours I still have a bit to try before starting a new game though.  Also I hope when it is finished that there is a lot more to keep me interested for at least 10 times what it has taken me to do so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: For a game about a small group surviving on a strange new world, this game is suprisingly cozy. Most of the time, i am just sitting there, chilling, helping my colonists survive and thrive while vibing to the really good soundtrack. The combat isn't boring, it just comes too infrequently to be a real threat (though you can certainly turn that up, i am playing on Medium difficulty with the Jason moon (whatever that means)). Its weird how relaxing this game actually is. But i like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game, just don't expect it to be too similar to Rimworld or Dwarf Fortress. Same genre, but plays differently in some major ways. This amounts to it being more "on rails" over all, but that ends up working pretty well.Also it seems you can't build multi-story buildings, which seems very counter intuitive for a game with this 3d art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: OUT-%$%@ing-STANDING game.  Seriously amazing.I bought this game in early April 2024, my initial reaction was "Oh no, God please no, it's one of these mobile games where you build a town and wait for energy, and they're going to try to micro-transaction me, etc.." and I couldn't have been more wrong.  I did the tutorials (which, during the first one is where I had that thought), and then jumped right into the gameplay after about 15-20 minutes.  This game gives you all of the elements!!  It has exploration, city building (well, base building), combat, and people management like The Sims, except there's not a bunch of LGBTQAAIP+-=1234 nonsense thrust into, and it's actually GOOD.  I'm in the basic crash landing mode or whatever still, I haven't even touched the other modes, and I already feel like I got my money's worth out of this game.  I've played for 38 hours, and I'm fairly certain I paid less than $38 for this game, at WORST that's $1 an hour, and I'm just scratching the surface of this game.  EXCELLENT, EXCELLENT game.  Some suggestions:- Make the amount of stuff that the settlers can do in a day "more" relative to the length of the day, or add automation to more tasks.  By the time I get my base to the point where I should be able to branch out and do some other things, my settlers are all completely engulfed in "handling" tasks, and can't actually get anything else done.  OR perhaps make a droid that can perform handling tasks, much like the drone that does transport.  That was a genius addition to the game, more like it would be welcome. - Make mech cores craftable, even if they're ridiculously expensive.  I want to build a mech and I'm near end-game, and I still have zero mech cores.  I have 2 settles always scavenging and going on expeditions and can't get the RNG to give me one.  Please remove the RNGness of mechs in survival mode (or whatever the base game mode is called).  Once again I LOVE the game, awesome job, just some suggestions that would greatly improve it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Do you want a game that forces you to make tough but fun decisions, right through to the late game? Do you want funny interactions between your survivors, challenging disasters and a massive variety of challenging raids? THEN GO PLAY RIMWORLD! Like Going Medieval and Stardeus, this game takes the basic RimWorld concept but doesn't really expand on it in any meaningful way, resulting in boring mid to late game play. You'll have more resources that you know what to do with, and you'll be so powerful that raids become trivial and, very quickly, boring. Yes it's got some pretty graphics but this is simply RimWorld on Very Easy Mode. I recommend skipping this and going back to RimWorld.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: If you came thinking this is rimworld with graphics - better skip this game.Let's forget about rimworld. Still this is buggy, repeatable, low content game, which I tried almost a year ago thinking "It will age well", but it haven't.New DLC is ♥♥♥♥. Crashes and freezes, which partially was fixed by community advice(reflection settings to low) and wasn't fixed at all by devs. Game still crashes sometimes, once in a few hours.New drone techs are bugged, defense drone doesn't protect your base, but it goes on hunting, lol, etc etc etc.Became bored of this game after ~8 hours yesterday, and was fighting crashes ~3 hrs few days ago.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far.  The graphics and nice, no lag on my system, and I can see potential for lots of updates to make things even better.I would like to see some form of transport building ability like Mechs or Local creature pulled carts, wagons, carriages.  I did mod this game for things like locking doors, better sacks, Activity planner by tasks (craft, farm, research, etc.), Faster clothing builds (1/2 a year for a pair of shoes, I mean really), Sleep/Eat/Relax priorities, & a big freezer.  It would be nice if they could build towards departure/rescue taking parts from all the junk falling from space... like an end goal - escape! _childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I love the open world concept where you can control individual people trying to survive on an untamed world.  There is a lot of customization when constructing a base of operations and this game has SO MUCH room to expand.  Would love to multi story buildings and underground bunkers built into this.  This formula would be absolutely amazing in a modern post-apocalyptic setting.  Can you imagine fortifying a fast food restaurant and scavenging resources from other buildings?  This game is amazing and I hope the developers keep this formula going when they decide to branch out.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions are very positive. The tutorials and included hints/tips where uncommonly good compared to what I see in most games I normally play. But that said there is a learning curve, especially as to what is the best way to spend the early days. Importantly you start with only 4 persons and there is an obvious limit to their ability to do all the tasks you would like them to. Do not bite off more than you can chew.I belive that some gamers will  complain about stupid AI, hopeless pathing, to much or to little micromanagment, «sims functionality» building options and so on. A loud minority will probably shout for different survivor camps and much more focus on combat and warfare. The latter should be ignored, there are tons of combat/war-games and it is a bad idea to destroy a very good survival game by trying to include mechanics that most likely will not work anyway. My advise to devs is to keep the balance more or less as it is in the game today. It is my impression that the devs intend to have a solid survival game then develop multiple scenarios. That is probably a good idea.So far I have not seen any serious bugs, but that may be because I have focused on  finding the best strategy for the initial phase. The only really annoying thing so far is the repeted request for feedback in the form of handing out stars to different aspects of the game. Do not get me wrong, feedback is important but to be useful it should probably be a bit more text based. Just to rank with stars seem to be quite  pointless – i.e what would 4 stars  indicate, compared to what?If you like challenging survival games that includes base building, short and long term strategy/planning and much more do give Alien dawn a try.  The only serious risk is that you will get to little sleep to be useful at work in the real world :)
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible, and will probably remain one of my favorites for a long time. I'm finishing up my first playthrough and am already looking forward to several more, trying the different scenarios and upping the difficulty to see if I can manage it.I'm finishing the survival scenario now, and have really been enjoying the fantastic graphics and animation. You really feel like these are real people you are caring for. My base is a mess, but that is because these survivors have never had to build a base to survive for years in (neither have I, but it is very easy to role-play the survivors a bit). As I near the end it is very satisfying to see how it evolved from a fire pit and a scrap shelter next to the crashed ship, to a fortified, comfortable base stocked full of food and building supplies, with robot helpers and a small army of robot soldiers to help defend it, along with the turrets.I want to mention the graphics again - everything looks great, with day/night and seasonal cycles. The survivors, objects and wildlife all are well-designed and animate nicely. I love watching the base at dawn as the advanced solar panels all move to start tracking the sun. There are lots of little things like that which make it seem like a real place, with real people you are trying to keep alive. Definitely my game of the year, and almost certainly a favorite for years to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty version of Rimworld. Aside from the graphics, it is, in almost all ways, less interesting and more poorly put together than Rimworld.It's not terrible. It's just not that good.There are a few systems that are a bit nicer. I like Stranded's power pole system for electricity distribution more than painstakingly laying power conduit everywhere like Rimworld.And the fact that it doesn't randomly generate people and instead has a specific roster of people with specific backstories is interesting, and I kind of like it, though I don't think it's better or worse than random generation, just different. It does fit well with having good graphics because you can have an artist create all of your characters.And no, it doesn't have multi-story buildings either.And I find looking for things on the map, or know where things are in relation to each other to be frustrating. It needs an overhead 'schematic' map of an entire region rather than just zooming out to some level and letting you wander all over the place (and get lost).But mostly, it's just simpler, duller, and cruder. Except the graphics. They're a lot better.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: a good game if played on PC, but unfortunately unplayable on steam deck because the game freezes and restarts steam deck every game-play in about 5 too 10 mins. Even with all settings on the lowest possible and reflections turned off. tried every tip on internet possible and also all compatibility modes.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Keep doing what you're doing guys and/or gals. This is a great game. Would love the ability to build bridges to connect buildings over a highly successful kill path that I simply refuse to change :) Poor Jack was the hero in my last play-through. He saved everybody and the final stand "twist" at the end made it a brand new game all over again. I love it. Was a little sad that they didn't get any fan-fair or final achievement for having survived (especially Jack) the last man standing who barely made it off the planet with his life. But I know it's still WIP - this is great!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Its a decent game that falls short of good. If you have played Dwarf Fortress or Rimworld this is similar. Overall its fine, but there are certain problems in the design and game balance. For example happiness, a survivor wakes up after a full rest, eats a meal, relaxes a bit, heads off to work in a great mood. At the end of the day though they are approaching a mental breakdown. The morning buffs have worn off, and they have grown a bit hungry, tired, and now its dark out.As you progress it feels like you should be able to accomplish more with less direct work, but with a few exceptions it just gets worse. Electric power should make things better but at the rate things break down it just means more time repairing and more time making the parts for repairs.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little ambivalent about the game. I really like the graphic presentation and realistic look of the worlds and people. The user interface is clean and easily understood. I like that there's an effort made to create a pool of characters who are individuals with unique traits, which really adds color to the game-play. But there are some aspects of the game that need work, and I don't think the "Tame and Train" game mechanics impact this at all: Once you understand the game mechanics (build a shelter, research and plant crops, defend your base, research a bit of the tech tree, explore and find a radio, talk to passing ships, get your people rescued one-by-one) nothing really changes, which limits the replayability. Changing locations and crew members in different games gives only minor variations, but your strategy to get your people rescued doesn't change from game to game. The challenges are essentially linear and consistent each time.I like the game, but I feel like I've already seen everything it has to show me.  Some ideas that might change things up:- More in-depth character interaction/conversations that affect relationships (characters can elect to leave your base and go it alone if you anger them sufficiently). Right now you have no control over character relationships--you're just a spectator.- Multiple methods of rescue (sometimes you can get your people out all at once, or in groups of more than 1).- Provide a "No Rescue" option where you have to create a self-sustaining colony (right now essential resources are finite and wouldn't support this mode). This would provide more value from the tech tree research; about half of it right now is unnecessary to get rescued.- Other camps of survivors, providing conflicts over resources and supplies.There are other things, too, but right now the basic strategy is too consistent.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review mostly for Rimworld players. Stranded has a similar play style, but it's not nearly has complex. If you're a veteran rimworlder than you'll be a bit disappointed ( i was ). I find myself wanting to play Rimworld more than this, Rimworld just does it better. The only improvement Stranded brings is it is 3d. I was always annoyed that Rimwrold wouldn't allow multi story buildings, and would have assumed Stranded would allow it, but it doesn't. If the details and micromanagement of Rimworld annoy you then Stranded might be a good fit. 13 hours into Stranded and it just really made me want to play Rimworld. Overall, good game. It's fun, but lacking compared to RW.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. You crash on a alien planet with a small team and have to survive. You can eventually acquire other survivors all with their own skill sets. You can build skills with all of your survivors by researching, hunting, farming, crafting, mining, etc. You can build awesome weapons to help you defend your base and gardens etc. This game is a lot of fun. Id recommend it to everyone that likes survival, exploration, crafting, researching type of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's Going Medieval with more "realistic graphics" and a lack of tera forming mechanics. I think the game desperately needs it. Also, I think the game would be funner if the drafting combat switched to a top down shorter control scheme. Suggest to the devs, maybe implement a hot key comb to switch to top down shooter mode while a survivor is drafted. Also, I feel the exploration needs to have some type of fog of war. It would make the game more challenging. Maybe add some thirst mechanics well. I never understood that in survival games. Like why do some games make you only manage one or two things for survival? Realistic you need to manage food, thirst, shelter, and hostile enemies. The game need more survival mechanics and a sense of "oh crap I'm gonna die!" I like the game because it's relaxing but the game is being sold as a survival settlement management game. Where's the survival mechanics? Good game though. The graphics are great. Gameplay is solid. Music is repetitive. So far I give it an 8+ out of 10. I'm sure it will get better
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: The most underrated game there is. If only developers would continue working on it but nothing suggests they do. Why this game isn't a big hit is beyond my understanding. It's the only game for which I completed all achievements and after almost 500 hours I still crave for more content. Please make another DLC. (I've finished all scenarios only on "insane chaos" including single survivor challenge, and once on very hard just to get achievement "Roll with the punches".) Loved the game and it's definitely my most favourite of all times.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's just RimWorld without anything that makes RimWorld special. It may have a few gimmicks that RimWorld doesn't, but its not enough to justify gameplay this similar. And it crashes all the time.And the devs are audacious enough to charge the same price as RimWorld, ask for nomination for most innovative gameplay, and call a plant smokeleaf (What RimWorld calls weed if you haven't played it).
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game because it is a building survival game.  The challenges are good.  Though the manufacturing speeds are slower than they should be with the day clock speed, even with higher levels in that area.  Making a pair of pants, primitive as they are, should not take all day with higher levels.  Also, a more logical path should be followed when picking up items for transport, as I watched someone bob back and forth from one end to another instead of picking all the items up in one area at a time.  Another item to note is that these people seem to be hardy as they were traveling in space and you have to be fit, both mentally and physically.  Having any kind of meltdown should be few and far between.  In the tips that show up when someone is having a meltdown, it says that giving a direct order can break the meltdown, but everything is grayed out or red and marked with having a meltdown, so no attempt even works.  The infestation of aggressive animals are too many and ramp up too quick and they show up out of nowhere as the migrating animals have a more native path to attacking your walls, though they do just spawn randomly.  These animals should spawn more naturally and roam and find your settlement versus just popping up at random intervals and they really should not ramp up with each attack.  Another things is explorations.  These messages keep popping up, but a balloon is required to go.  If a balloon is required, then the messages should not pop up until you can build one.  Please fix these little issues.  Otherwise this is a great game and I will continue to play to see the improvements and enjoy watching the survivors and what they do.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Very Good game, interesting and challenging, Quite a wide variety of Characters (20+), interesting environments and alien creatures. Very close to how I would imagine how it would be if stranded on an alien planet. Choose your character's carefully as it makes a difference to your experience. Would like to be able to create my own character, maybe that would be considered in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great game and I am hooked.  As many others have commented it is like a 3D version of Rimworld (which I really like). In some respects the character AI is far better. For example your resource gatherers will skin/chop/farm/mine stuff and then take it straight back to the base/storage (unlike Rim).  There is base layout and tower defence planning required along with people management (you have to keep them satisfied otherwise they throw a tantrum and do own thing for a little while until they calm down).I like the fact that the research tree can be slightly different in each playthrough although that can make it harder for some scenarios (the fuel and power breakthroughs are key).  There is a Scrabble-bag of characters of which you can choose 4 to start off with all with different traits (some negative) and you may be joined randomly by others during the game.  It's early access and does have some minor issues particularly storage and I have had 1 game crash during 60 hours of play. Overall it is very polished and has a lot of content and depth.  I cannot wait to see what the developers will add in the future.  Definitely worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Do not recommend.Played about 13 hours with no issues. New update drops, game won't run. Tried uninstalling/reinstalling, no luck. It appears to be something related to Denuvo - I had no issues with it previously, but of course there's no way to roll back to a previous working version.This is what happens when you prioritize releasing an unnecessary DLC over maintaining a stable base game.Sadly it's too late for me to refund. Learn from my mistakes, just pirate this instead. The concept is fine: Rimworld Lite with a lot of the depth stripped out, but in 3D.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded: Alien Dawn is like Rimworld with great looking 3D graphics. It has a tighter scope of survival where you are stranded on a bug infested planet and will be under attack by larger and larger swarms of insects as the game progresses. The aim at the time I played was to get all your colonists out before you get overrun by the insects. The game has some variety to the insects but it would be great to see more insects along with more options to kill/defend against them.The game is a great mix of colony sim and base defence making it a must buy if you are into any of these genres. The devs are great and we have seen many bug fixes and free additional content so far. The devs are now working on a paid DLC which should add more to this already wonderful game. An overall great experience and a recommended buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: At this point, it's fun, if a little heavy on the micromanagement. For example, you have to manually set different containers to store which stuff, the 'default' is store everything, so the nice outdoor stockpile that's appropriate for things like bricks, concrete and the like will also get fresh food slapped in it, so it can uselessly rot away. Foods that are fully shelf stable, as long as it has a roof over it, will take up space in fridge and freezer, again pointlessly. Workers will often harvest a food, and then just leave it laying in the field to rot away, instead of picking up the thing THEY JUST HARVESTED, and putting it into storage. That sort of stuff. Little QoL issues.But yes, it's fun and with all the options available, you can make it as easy or as difficult as you desire.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of potential for a great game here, but it will not stop harassing you. Every couple of days, without fail, there is another wave of the same few groups of aliens, constantly draining your resources and stopping you from probing and poking the rest of the game. Seriously, just back off a little bit. Leave the player alone every now and then to explore! But no, didn't spend a bunch of time min-maxing resource management after the last wave of stupid amounts of enemies to get everyone heals, get everything repairs and pull in some additional resources? Well guess what, you're going to have to slog through.This is not a fulfilling or interesting game-play loop. Its grind. And its not why I play videogames.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Great little survival base builder game, you have to set the priorities right or your survivors ... well, won't. I've played through a good few times and enjoyed them all. Hopefully by the time it's a full release it'll have more scenarios and some sort of meta progression / "story line" to tie them all together, that would give it a lot more replay value. I definitely got my moneys worth though!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, I was looking for a game like this for a long time and I couldn't find it.I just find the order of priorities a little confusing, I recommended this function just by clicking on the construction and clicking "Priority" and it became a priority there, as well as in agriculture, clicking to be a priority, because the current function of priorities often the dolls do not comply correctly.Otherwise, PERFECT!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best games I've played in a long time.  Take SIMS and add actual survival, instead of just "going to work".  Watch as your characters harvest materials, build out multiple bases, survive the elements & monsters, then party naked 'till they puke all night from your own home-made ale. The best part of the game is the randomness: Swarms of bugs eat your crops and any teammates that are unprepared, severe thunder damages your buildings, extreme cold grinds everything to a halt... death is always nearby.  Use the Steam Workshop and get your favourite mods... they are amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really get why this is so highly rated or popular... It's an OK game, it's really quite shallow, lacking depth and complexity, it's where Rimworld was when it was still at the very start of it's Beta phase. The only thing it has going for it over Rimworld, is being 3D and considering the huge gulf of features between this and just Rimworlds base game, It's really not worth getting just for the fact it's "3D".It really needs Character customisation, some basic UI elements, like being able to see more of the map when zoomed out or a minimap type feature/world map button, notications for when characters get long term illnesses, I've recently had 2 characters in 2 different games have major long term health issues that I don't know how they developed or when It started, plus no way to fix it. More options to recruit people, playing for over 2 years with just 4 characters is so slow to get things done it just becomes boring.Really should have been left in EA for another 6-12 months to flesh out but I feel like the dev's needed the cash to either continue developing the game or to start a new project, either way it's not a great way to release a game or treat your playerbase.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Causal version of Rimworld.prosThere are a few exploratory events where you could find resourcesgood tech treeRandom creature attacks pick up throughout the gameconsIt would be nice to have more 'survivor' interactions to grow your camp, trade, or in conflictThe default mode appears to be 'aspire to leave the planet', other game modes including settling would be fun
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I love Rimworld and seeing that someone attempt a 3D version of it made me all the more excited to try it out. This game, as it is in early access, is really well polished. While it clearly has some ways to go to reach the amount of content as Rimworld, with steady progress and continuous support by the dev, I believe Stranded: Alien Dawn will shape out to be a good one. There are rooms for improvements to be sure. The most glaring for me would be the combat which is a little lackluster but I think they'll improve as time goes by. Overall, enjoyable and I'm looking forward for more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: pretty fantastic!!! Scenery is awesome, gameplay is decent a little on the cumbersome side. individual clicks or giant selection box for deleting structures is almost to much, research time, trying to get across the map to find some food or seeds people faint from exhaustion, (sit down and take a break). Hopefully more is released with wider research options or unlockables, rescue is choppy (just 1 at a time). All in all absolutely wonderful this will get a lot of hours of game play from me as it sits just to see how each play through can be different.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Now this game is a blast i do love the building aspect and tech research. I love the attacking aliens here and there. the different difficulties. now the issue i do have with the game-cons: Lack of people to choose from or get         : Lack of objectives to do.         : Lack of dangers. Its always aliens or weather event         : Lack of customization for colonist.Now i know this is a EA game and they are working hard on it! So please give it a chance. I was hoping to terraform more or build into a mountain. I found this game from a artical that stated it was the new rimworld. I was hoping to make bases where ever i wished. maybe they will make it happen maybe they wont. but where is the win condition? Rimworld has that option.  I hope this helps new players give it a go. they are working hard on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Realy good Start!!! If you are a fan of rimworld, then it is quite possible that this game is made just for you!  At the moment, the game has a very small number of items, buildings, research.  But this is early access and the game has huge potential!!!!!!!  I do not regret a single € that I paid for the purchase.  If in the future the game will have as many features as in the "other" game, then I and many other players will spend a lot of time in it.  Difficulty setting: hard.  From the first minutes of the game, you are immersed in the atmosphere of survival and the struggle for the right to call yourself an inhabitant of this planet.  Choosing the right starting characters will increase your chances many times over.... The interface worked very well, except for some small things that I'm sure will be improved in the future.  The food system, for me personally, is one of the best of all games.  You don't have to use 250 pumpkins to cook one meal, as seen in some other games.  Personally, I lack data on the calorie content of a particular food and data on the needs of residents.  As for the battles, I can't say anything bad here either, but a weapon like a sniper rifle should shoot at least 2 times further.  Buildings are erected without any difficulties.  The availability of resources is at a high level (maybe it is worth reducing the number of shipwrecks???) the mood of the characters: everything is simple, hover over and get information about the reason for the bad mood.  But it's not very clear to me why the characters start to hate each other, there is not enough description of the reason .... I would like to be able to choose the size of the map, or at least have a choice among 20-30 maps that would be 2 times larger than those that we have now.  I would like more variety of biomes, flora and fauna on one map.  As well as the possibility of moving to another map maybe?  The developers have a very good example (another game) of what needs to be done in this game, and what needs to be improved.  And it will be a masterpiece.  The game has many aspects that you can talk about and write about for a very long time.  I wrote about what I really noticed and what I missed in 5 hours of playing.  But I will continue to play for another 5.10.. 20 hours and more :)Buy it, play it!For early acces its 7+/10!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded: Alien Dawn is a enjoyable colony management experience because of all the elements that need to be managed to be successful. As a player you have to dance around keeping each colonist needs met. Be it Rest, hunger, happiness, and relaxation all while dealing with seasons, disasters, illnesses, social traits and attacks.Through all of this stuff you need to explore the local area and expand your camp while doing research to accomplish your goals. But you also need to skill up your survivors so they can do more complex tasks like build more advanced things and go on expeditions. I found all of this to make an enjoyable gaming experience.The game has an odd performance problem that does not seem to have anything to do with how big you build a colony. The game just has some unexplainable performance drops that seem Inexplicable. it seems like the day / night cycle has a problem during the winter season. During the night time it's too bright and in the morning their is an abrupt drop in light.Colonist interactions with each other are more often negative causing a problematic happiness drops.Negative happiness events stack but positive ones do not stack.Some colonist traits are unnecessarily annoying. More specifically rest recharges at half the speed for one colonist. While another is constantly vomiting because of an implant.Overall I like the game and the issues are not enough to get in the way of having fun with this one. Thumbs up for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: non verbal; controls very cumbersome, overly complex, and often characters are unresponsive to direction and orders ; feels like decades old engine;  tutorial sucked up 1 hour  rather than having narration explain things in 10 minutes;  just not what expected.  A shame really could have been great game.  Very disappointing. Clock for time played not synced with  Steam, asking for refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the price. Without mods it has the depth of a puddle. It feels like its so damn close to being something good and worthy of rivaling Rimworld or other great colony sims but falls flat with half-assed systems like NPC interactions or there seems to be no decor for your rooms to boost productivity or mood, just a cluster of things missing. Such a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: **Great Game – A Perfect Mix of RimWorld and The Sims***Stranded: Alien Dawn* is a fantastic blend of colony management, survival, and storytelling. It takes the best elements from *RimWorld*—the deep colony management, resource gathering, and research tree—and adds a touch of *The Sims* with its character interactions and personal needs. Managing your colony is rewarding, with plenty of side quests and a detailed research system that keeps you engaged. Balancing survival with the personalities of your colonists makes for a dynamic and immersive experience. My only wish is for more DLCs or additional content. The core game is strong, but I’d love even more scenarios, biomes, and challenges to dive into. Highly recommend for fans of colony management games!
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: I've played off and on since launch. Coming back to it reminded me why I like this game. The simplicity of starting a new game, and the draw of so many possibilities. I can't wait to see what the devs come up with next for content, but the core gameplay is great. if you like survival management games, then this is a must-have IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, with a lot of promise as it gets further built out. Some have called it a 3-D Rimworld, but having never played Rimworld, I can't speak to that. I would call it a combination of Sims and Banished/Dawn of Man, but the survival and combat are more sophisticated than the latter (and, obviously, set on an alien world in the future). Despite being early access, there is a lot here already and I had loads of fun playing it to the end-- nothing felt unfinished, though there's currently only one alien world, so replayability is somewhat limited. I hope in the future they build out the structures/furnishings some more, especially the fortifications-- it would be nice to have some electrified fences and/or something stronger than just wooden walls, especially when you have carbon nanotube structures-- and add the ability to manipulate terrain. It was annoying not being able to extend my building the way I wanted because the land next to it was ever so slightly higher and not on the same level. Being able to raise/lower terrain would also add a very cool element to base defense because line-of-sight is key, though you can partly address this by building elevated floors.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! Haven't encountered any issues across my first play through at all. Content is strong and there are lots of opportunities to create your own scenarios, so the replayability is massive. The different survivors all have their own story and their own skills and weaknesses, so the number of combinations you can have, with different end goals and game rules makes this game an absolute bargain for the price. Easy recommend and will be playing this a lot more.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically a stripped down, 3D RimWorld with some additions and some substractions.If you liked RimWorld, and you like colony sims in general, you will have a few hours of fun in this game.There are some balace issues, there is some things missing, and I believe there is not much hope for getting things better, the updates are sparse if any at all. The research "tree" is much more sparse than RimWorld, too.The developers have made some shortcuts and basically let you farm for most of the resources, except metal, which is acquired by salvaging and smelting, going on expeditions. There is no mine par se (maybe in different modes I haven't tried yet), so there is no real stabilisation when it comes to this specific resource, everything else is basically infinite, but limited by time taken to grow things).The general playthrough is rather enjoyable, not to slow, not to fast. You don't have to abuse the active pause to keep up, the combat is rather simplistic, but RimWorld-like too (drafting, shooting, damage etc.).Basically, if you don't mind playing a ripoff of RimWorld, with a slight twist, you will enjoy it. Is it worth the price? Not really, I got it really cheap on a sale, so it didn't hurt that much, but for the normal price look into other games of the genre, they are much more inventive and will draw you in for a longer time (Farthest Friontier etc.).
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoiler Alert in the last sentence*I love playing this game. When I'm not playing an action game and need to unwind, I go to this game. There is some strategy in which team you choose. You will have to micro-manage depending on which scenario you play. Most are fun and easy. The "Guardian" scenario requires you micro-manage Hope. The combat is a little on the easy side. The strategy is basic. Just chose from the research tree and move along. Each various upgrade requires research which can last from 3 hours to 5 days (In game time). I this point I have most of the achievements. I have to go back and do the military scenario again. It was one of my early tries. DO NOT pick Conner for this scenario. He dies within 3 years of a brain tumor.
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded: Alien Dawn

_childDocuments_.review: AI complains about starving but refuses to prioritize tasks that would remedy the situation. Quite literally able to pull themselves up with their own bootstraps, but choose not to.Tried to refund, but played too much, which is wild because I haven't even progressed far into the save.Edit: Forgot to mention that the AI also sleeps through being attacked and fellow survivors would rather  heal the sleeper than attack the aggressor.Edit edit: Like that's cool make your game difficult to succeed, but when the 'survivors' are so dumb they breakdown because of lack of necessities wouldn't it be common sense to have them ignore tasks that don't further their own needs? If Jim-Bob is naked because of a lack of clothing and there's tasks in the tailoring bench why do I need to FORCE them to do this task? Like bro just make the item and equip it, don't complain about it, breakdown and make the player direct them to make the equipment. Which gets even more sad when they make the shirt, put it in storage and then cry about how naked and afraid they are (again). My guy YOU are the problem.I'm not here to wipe the survivor's rectum, I'm here to direct them as to what would be most beneficial next in the medium to long term, except in the case of emergencies. It's just tedious and possibly lazy game design.Quite literally...if (naked() or missing clothing()):{    make_clothing();    equip_clothing();}instead it iswhile(naked() or missing clothing()):{    do_anything_but_make_clothing();    store_clothing_found();    cry();}I'm no longer wondering why they crashed, the captain probably went to the washroom and came back to a self destruct sequence hitting zero.Edit edit edit: Why does the game continually reduce speed upon a survivor attacking an aggressor? Like I know that it's happening I drafted all of them and ordered the attack. It would be better if the game paused upon their arrival and didn't reduce speed every time I they engage a hostile. I end up having to hold '+' until it finishes.Edit edit edit edit: 'Survivors' path themselves through dangerous areas. Drafting them only makes them change task, and I can't force them to do the task through drafting. This only reinforces my opinion that the AI is dumb af.. SOMEHOW every ship I contact only has a single escape pod and they're ALL only fit for one. Okay first off, why? No seriously why?

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts as described as a survival game.  Micromanage virtually all decisions early game but quickly devolves into a tower defense game.  For some reason the devs do not want you to get to the end game with anything but defeat.  In theory, the end game is to get all survivors off the planet.  In reality, it's to get some off the planet and the rest left to die.  What this game does wrong is that it scales each attack wave up regardless if you have less survivors or even destroy all insect nests.  One person theorized (but may have been trolling) that if you don't scale up defense, the wave difficulty won't scale up.  That is tested and false.So if you like survival games and tower defense games but also don't care that you can't win, this is the game for you.  You can save some survivors and you can keep up your defenses with the scaling of waves but inevitably, the game ends when your last survivor dies.

It's similar to other survival sims, but maintains its own unique style and it does it well. Sadly, it sometimes feels bland. The progressing and research tree, while slow at times, feel nice and have some variety, based off of your crew.In my opinion, I recommend it, but its currently not worth $35 due to how much you really get out of it.I would say to buy it when it drops to around $20 to $25

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good idea but fails to ultimately deliver.  If the game drops to around $15 its worth a purchase.  If you're looking for a base building game managing survivors, this isn't it, its a "get off the planet as soon as possible" type game and that could be okay but the longer you play the more likely the game mechanics will eventually overwhelm you and you will fail.  Its a good idea but the game has too many quality of life issues and the team is not interested in addressing most of those problems.  There are tons of issues with the AI and efficiency that have been present for over a year with no real attempts to fix it.  Like really dumb things like exhausting themselves by taking on tasks they can never complete (too far from base etc) and not sleeping or doing jobs in a way where they will walk across a field to pick something up instead of the pile right next to them, and many other frustrating issues.  Things break too quickly, can't repair, your characters wont equip the right items for replacement, you will micromanage your people where you shouldn't to make up for the poor AI programming, bug waves and aggressiveness are proportional to your base size, upgrades are a distraction that will consume the most precious resource in game (time management).  Variety is lacking.  Read the discussion boards and you'll see many of the same types of posts complaining about the same things without it being addressed or fixed.For $35 there's plenty of other great base building games I would buy before this one that don't have these challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: People have expressed that it's unfinished or frustrating or buggy or has some issues. I disagree to an extent. I love the game so far and I'm very glad I supported it this early.That said, it's early access. It's got development and growth that need to happen, but I've had an absolute blast so far in my 27 hours. I can see opportunities that could easily be improved, like interface or shortcut keys getting refined, etc.I get some mild vibes of Factorio and Frostpunk, and can see how people relate it to Rimworld, but I never played that. It doesn't have factories of Factorio, but it does have turret defense and challenging waves of enemies to tackle. It's not as hard as Frostpunk, but I feel the pressure of making sure I have enough to survive the seasons, a similar pressure I've experienced in Don't Starve or Timerborn. In all, I like that Stranded has a mesh of and/or draws mild inspiration from aspects of other games.I struggled at first with some resources until I realized I should just send my farmer to plant a ton of X plant somewhere further away to grow faster rather than rely on a tiny farm inside my defenses.I'd also really like to see a good Wiki built by the community of players, soooooo hint hint let's hope someone does that. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: First impression after a few hours of play - it's (obviously) like Rimworld, only not as good in almost every aspect.Pros- It's a simplified and less difficult take on the DF/Rimworld genre. That will appeal to people.- Variety in the fauna and flora, and I like how they need to be observed before you can discern their full usagesNeutral- Graphics are okCons  - Ugly UI- Repetitive gameplay loop- Few emergent stories- Survivors lack personality in comparison to other games - Rubbish sound effects- nonsensical (gamey) technology barriers - why would you crash land on an alien planet yet forget how to construct buildings? - Far too derivative of other games in the genre. Struggle to see why you'd play this over Rimworld As for an overall verdict, it's closer than the above lists would suggest. Had I played less than two hours I probably would have refunded. However, I don't feel the same level of regret as I have done with other games with a similar number of cons. Despite its many issues, I have found myself wanting to play S:AD again. Perhaps, with more time, it will grow on me. So it's a no for now but it may change in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: "Stranded: Alien Dawn" offers a diverse gaming experience with its wide range of biomes, scenarios, and resource-rich, randomly generated maps. It supports a variety of play styles, from a peaceful, meditative experience to challenging tactical tower defense gameplay. The AI minimizes the need for micromanagement, and the beautiful graphics paired with stable performance enhance the overall experience. Continuous development post-release and a vibrant modding community add further depth to the game.However, it falls short in certain areas. Some gameplay mechanics feel overpowered, diminishing the challenge once your base is established. It lacks complexity in social interactions, trading, and health systems compared to similar games. Pathfinding issues, a cumbersome construction process, and imbalanced task completion times detract from the enjoyment. While visually appealing and offering hours of gameplay, it doesn't quite measure up to its competitors in terms of depth and refinement. Recommended for fans of the genre, but be aware of its limitations and ongoing development.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but unlike most survival sim games it becomes less fun and a lot more of a chore over time as you progress down the tech tree.In short, your colonists become less and less efficient over time (as well as more demanding in their needs/rest time). So each day you get less done as they waste more time, but the items you need to craft require greater volumes and variety of components, so you have more resources to discover/gather/farm/refine and less work hours to do it.For me, the gameplay loop became unenjoyable and increasingly frustrating; fighting the games inefficient and overly complex systems to do basic things.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fantastically fun game (10/10), like a higher-res Rimworld but with fewer people to manage. The game isn't stingy with the amount of resources that you get per trip (e.g., chopping trees, mining rocks, etc.). Lots to do in a game but probably the best part is the construction. Lots of freedom in building houses or warehouses or combinations. The only thing I would like to see in this game is a bit more customization with the starting game and end game goals. I'd really like to have the option of playing after the end game goal has been reached. It'd be great to be able to play the crash landing scenario but have the option to do galactic trading. The modding community thankfully has that sort of thing covered. But what I'd really like to see is something like establishing other outposts on the same planet where you could transfer resources between outposts. So once you have one area functioning really well, you can recruit another team to establish a new base and set up a trade route between them.Really, a fun game well worth it. I really look forward to seeing how this game will develop in the future.
