_childDocuments_.review: An Open letter to Spike Chunsoft.*Ahem* Dear Spike Chunsoft, As you are well aware, this game is seen as "Mixed" by a number of the community. However, I believe that this game is more than that, and is truly worth the time, if you wish to give it. The attention to detail in relation to the source material, it's all there. Personally, if horrible things weren't happening to orphans, it just wouldn't be MiA. However, while the game is good in its own right, I do have some complaints...Okay just one complaint.The game is fantastic, the Abyss draws you in and keeps you coming back (if you've the stomach for it of course.) so much so that I, someone who barely plays modern day games, kept coming back, and aside from the story mode, I have every achievement as of this review. The music go harder than it should in some places, and the atmosphere hit that sweet spot of being just daunting enough to make you want to turn back and take a break, while being tantalizing enough to keep pushing forward for that sweet SWEET Dopamine. However, we must address the elephant in the room, or rather, the twelve and a half foot flying rat on layer three.THAT'S RIGHT, The Madokajack, I'm talking about the Madokajack. Seriously, Satan's birds must be stopped. This is a plea of war against the wall watching sky dwellers. I BEG of you, please PLEASE patch their hitboxes in the future so we don't get knocked down while HALFWAY IN A CAVE. Seriously, I'm trying to climb inside the safe zone and suddenly a KC-135 Stratotanker sized monstrosity hits me with little warning besides the ominous music.As such, I beg the devs to please take another look at the rats and perhaps reduce their size ever so slightly, beyond that game's a solid 8/10. It has some slow moments, and random bandit attacks are kind annoying, but if you like pain, you'll love this game. Bought it twice so I could get the collector's edition on PS4.Update: I now have all the Cheevos.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Made In Abyss, you will most likely enjoy this game. To preface this review, I downloaded mods that disabled the infinite spawning mechanic and replaced the soundtrack with the anime soundtrack, so I won't mention them as negatives since they can be fixed. Overall, I recommend this game with a few caveats.Pros:- Exploration and survival elements are solid. There's nothing quite like traversing and conquering Lovecraft's Brutal Hellhole of Loli Abuse and cooking up a storm as you run out of stamina on a cliff and turn into a blood stain on the floor, just like Ozen said!- The Deep in Abyss mode is a good idea for a Made in Abyss game like this. Instead of rehashing the main story poorly (I'm looking at you, Hello Abyss), you get a simple and believable story about joining the Orth orphanage and taking various jobs and requests while fulfilling your own goal of becoming a White Whistle and making connections with fellow cave raiders and returning characters.- The graphics are commonly referred to with scorn, but I like the janky PS2 graphics. Makes me feel young again.- The difficulty can sometimes be unforgiving. When you travel down the Abyss, you'll eventually find you made an expedition unprepared and you'll have to start it all over again. This can easily mean wiping a good 30 minutes of playtime, but I enjoy this aspect because its as punishing as the Abyss is always made out to be and it makes the preparation phase of the game impactful and thoughtful.- The progression system is fine, you upgrade your whistle rank and get more abilities when you do. Nothing too in-depth, but it works and opens up for more options and areas within the Abyss as you climb the ranks.- It's Made in Abyss. Seriously, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MADE IN ABYSS game. C'mon.Cons:- The partner system is extremely buggy and aggravating to the ears. They constantly repeat lines and cause noises to glitch out when they get stuck on a slightly elevated piece of dirt. Very annoying and takes you out of the experience when you have to take someone along with you.- The main story (Hello Abyss) where you play as Riko and Reg, while not necessarily untrue to the source material or poorly written, is a slog to go through since all of the cutscenes are boring to watch and the best aspects of the game are not present in this mode at all. Worst of all, you're forced to play through it to get to the real game. This essentially makes it a 3 hour long tutorial, and a poor one at that.- The enemies are generally slow and dumb, making most of them a nuisance at best. Its rare for an enemy to actually scare you or challenge you after the first time you encounter them and learn their moveset. Some are a complete joke, like the Inbyos.- $60. Enough said. This should REALLY be a $40 game at best. But if you love Made in Abyss, then money is no object.TL;DR Too expensive and rough around the edges, but Made in Abyss fans who have been waiting for a game where you can traverse the Abyss and abuse your loli will be satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so bad. I was living in the very definition of a cope since I spent the same amount of money to buy a girlfriend and take her out to dinner at a nice restaurant. I have been a very big fan of Made in Abyss for a good while and was very much looking forward to getting a new perspective on the universe and hoping to learn about certain artifacts or aspects that were less touched on in the manga/anime. There are a LOT of issues with this game but there are some things that I enjoy and want to speak on those first.The nostalgia aspect is very nice. I know people clowned on the graphics but that's actually one of my favorite things about the game. It had a very nice PS2 feel and it actually brought me back to playing games in my room all night long. The colors were nice and just very warm and nostalgic for me. I know many people would disagree with that statement but personally it was something I really enjoyed and am glad they leaned into it as much as they did.Another thing that I really enjoyed was the fact that it ran very smoothly. My computer is good but nothing special and I was streaming with consistent 240 fps, no frame drops, cuts, skips, anything. This is a small thing but it's something great about the game that needs to be recognized. I'm trying so hard to give this game as much credit as I can...One of my biggest problems is that there is nothing new to experience, but instead just the first 16 chapters retold in a visual novel-like manner. This is one of many nitpicks I have but I'm especially disappointed that the team did not even finish off at the end of chapter 16, which is (in my opinion) one of the best scenes in the entire show/manga since it not only gives much needed support to Ozen's actions, but also beautifully shows the very important connection between Lyza and herself, strengthening the connection to Riko. I assume this was done to save money from having to rig Lyza's model and get the spoken lines in. Understandable, but leaving off right before a very cathartic conclusion of an arc just strikes me the wrong way. Another thing I’d like to point out is the actual world in the abyss. When you think of the abyss, you imagine a vast, beautiful biome of incredible creatures, beautiful flora, and amazing views. Instead, what you get is a few bland creatures with simple attack patterns and seem to be placed haphazardly using a dartboard. The creatures don't roam or explore their own environment, they stick to their box and attack the player if too close. Instead of being able to walk through the amazing city of Orth, seeing the houses for their glory, you’re stuck in specific rooms that you essentially fast travel to. It really is unfortunate to see such potential of a great steampunk cityscape get underutilized in this game.This segues into another gripe I have with this game. The fact is it's way too linear for it to even remotely feel like the abyss. An important sliver of the horror in the series is the vastness of the landscape. Something touched upon in the 5th layer especially. In the game, it feels like you’re on a set path where you can't get lost in. At least personally speaking, the idea of getting lost in the abyss and trying to find my way out sounds so intriguing since you get to put yourself in the eyes of Riko and Reg, though this is just a personal preference. I do, however, stand by the fact that the linear aspect removes a large chunk of mystery and horror from the abyss.I really hoped that I’d see models of the artifacts and whistles in greater detail. I was quite upset when I found out that the physical objects were reduced to jpegs on the screen. I really think it took away all the power that these insanely important items hold. Having Habo come up to me, giving me Lyza’s whistle, would have made much more of an impact than being transported to a VN style cutscene with a white whistle jpeg.There are a lot of smaller things that don't really fit in a whole category alone but are still important things to mention. These things include: Poor combat system, recycled lines from the anime, terrible controls, boring fetch-quests, story ending too soon, and the cooking system feeling way too underutilized.I do want to note that this is just the Hello Abyss mode, but being forced to play this before you start another mode that’s advertised is such a hassle. I also did not want to continue further because I knew I wanted to refund the game and get my $60 USD back in my account. If a game like this is going to use the anime story so poorly and as a tutorial type section, it at least should be interesting and even a little challenging.Needless to say, I am extremely disappointed with this game and I seriously hope the dev team makes real improvements to this game because it’s a great concept and could be such an incredible horror/exploration game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not enjoyable. For starters I was excited for this game before launch as a fan of the anime so when I saw the $80 price tag I assumed the game would be extremely well polished with interesting mechanics and story. What I found was exactly the opposite.For starters, playing on a PC was a nightmare. The controls where badly managed. For example, I have a mouse with the usual left and right mouse buttons but also two buttons on the side. The only button I was able to use in gameplay was the left mouse button. The other buttons wouldn't bind to other actions in the keybind settings. moving on to the mechanics. there is nothing complex or interesting about them. the mechanics are straight out of your average rpg or adventure game. there's nothing particularly bad about the mechanics, but they seem out dated since you could probably find an adventure game from the mid 2000s with similar mechanics. Since the mechanics don't try anything new or ground breaking it makes the game feel stale. Moving on to the story, the tutorial which doesn't tell you its a tutorial, follows the story of Riko and Reg from the manga and anime. Its basically a shot for shot and line for line remake of the anime but in a game format?? which handles the story much worse. despite this, I was actually enjoying reliving the anime in a game format. I was so excited to get to the deeper layers to get to the more interesting story lines like Nanachi and Bondrewd. And wouldn't ya know it, the tutorial stops right before you enter the third layer which was very disheartening.Moving on to things I enjoyed about the game, the soundtrack was very good. It reminds you of Kevin Penkin's score from the anime but yet the songs aren't just copies of said sound track. In other words, they did something original while still paying homage to the source content which I think the game could have used a lot more of. additionally, despite some low polygon walls and cliffs, the scenery and creature design is beautiful. the art style and its relation to the game once again reminded me of the anime. In the anime, the cute, cartoony art style fools you into thinking the show is for kids. thus when the gore hits it subverts your expectations. I experienced a similar phenomenon in the game. Once again the art style draws you in as cute and cuddly, but the game isn't afraid to show some horrific death scenes. I also appreciated how they didn't stick strictly to what was shown in the anime but also added some new items like a hunting bow and pistol. Also, part way through the tutorial there was an anime opening style credits sequence that was really hype.Overall, there is something in this game all though it is buried deep below layers and layers of issues. If you haven't checked out the anime or the manga don't even consider buying this game. You wont understand anything so go read/watch the series then come back. If you do decide to come back be prepared for an unpolished mess of a game that OCCASIONALLY has some high points.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to give the most real review I can for this.Overall:The game is not bad. I would give it a flat 6.5/10The developers did try, but a good portion of the game falls short.The Good Parts and Effort:- The cutscenes are great. The cutscenes actually follow the story down to a T. With a few exception but most are minor.- The Side story for your custom character is actually decent. I found myself more interested in it than the canon storyline.-Canon storyline is pretty decent. Mostly regarding the storyline.The Bad Parts and Improvement Areas:-Combat is very basic. Just one attack kills most stuff or does nothing at all.-Stealth is next to useless in most early areas. It does work but when it does work, it works TOO well.- Some storyline areas are a bit odd. Ozen's library is WAY too small for what the anime potrays. If the idea was to make it seem claustrophobic, good job, but it makes the atmosphere terrible. -Riko's storyline is OP. In other words, Riko is given so many materials + Reg, that it makes the custom character mode seem odd. If they didn't force you to play Riko's first, this point could be removed, but playing it first gives you the wrong idea for the game. One final addition so it doesn't have to be another point, Reg is  OP. Not as an ally, but as free rope when traversing the abyss. When playing custom character, rope is paramount and often needs to be built up over multiple runs.- AI Can be avoided easily at all costs. This point is slightly moot when doing the custom character route.Keeping is short Overall:Game is not bad for a first entry to the franchise but a bit disappointing for such a great show.Worth $60?Hell no.Get it on sale.If you are desperate, go for it but don't expect anything life changing.Is it worth a try? Perhaps. I would say its a bit like a easy mode animal crossing. If thats your thing. Dive in.Enjoy ^^P.S. _childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying this game only costed me 20 dollars, so my opinion is based around that pricing.Well it's what you'd expect from an anime game, down to the cringe indulcing name, but still on the upper end of anime games.Editing to add: The game displays Keyboard inputs when using a controller, but that can be CHANGED with a setting in the Options menu. It is NOT a bug, just a really odd design choice.• GRAPHICS: The graphics are fine, they look certainly better than the PS5/Switch, but the lower areas are just hastily modelled. They're very lazy and empty compared to the areas of the 1st layer. The same can be said about enemy models. Some look really interesting while others look like low poly junk.Cutscenes are fine I guess, I skipped most of them because I just recently rewatched Made in Abyss.• GAMEPLAY: It's the best part of the game. The game is basically a bunch of interconnected dungeon maps, similar to old Monster Hunter. There's two modes; Hello Abyss and Deep In Abyss.-Hello Abyss- Nothing short of a glorified tutorial, where you play as Riko while Reg walks around behind you one shotting everything within a 30 mile radius of you. It's thankfully very short as the mode itself is extremely garbage but it's something you can easily get through in an hour. Hello Abyss ends right after Seeker Camp.-Deep In Abyss- This is where the meat of the game is at. You MUST complete the Hello Abyss gamemode first to unlock it. You play as a CaC who slowly progress their way through the Whistles rank by doing repetitive fetch quests in the Abyss itself. It may sound boring at first, but the gameplay loop of it coupled with the dangers of the Abyss itself makes it for a very entertaining time. It is a bit clunky but it does help feeling like you're a child in an otherwise very hostile environment. Some areas are really annoying when it comes to the amount of enemies and how unavoidable they are, while others are more chill and relaxing. Enemy AI is also very basic, so don't expect them to be anything more than farmable hazards.Deep In Abyss ends at the 5th layer, so if you were expecting to transform into a Hollow or a Narehate, you'll have to wait for the sequel, Made in Abyss: Trio Of Solitude And The Stray Soul, or whatever other cringe name they decide to come up for it.It also has an endless spawner after 7 or so minutes which seriously harms an otherwise relaxing experience.If you were expecting some sort of survival mechanic, DO NOT BUY the game. All the survival meters you see on the screenshots were REMOVED. There's NO SURVIVAL MECHANIC, the screenshots are outdated from an alpha dev build or whatever and I have no idea why they're still on the store page. The only thing you have is a food meter that you need to keep full since traveling from one map to another costs you food and health.• Audio: It's decent, but the voice acting is abysmal and the creators either ripped the acting from the anime itself, since I remember everything they said from the sub, or somehow managed to have the most phoned in performances ever.Riko is the only character that portrays any sort of emotion, everyone else feels like they're reading off from a book while being very bored. On the bright side, I found it quite amusing when I fell off a cliff as Riko, only for Reg to let out a mildly disappointed "Damn it."There's also the huge annoyance of lines being overly repeated. Your character will grunt the exact same way everytime you do a specific action, and all the gameplay lines from the Hello Abyss mode are ripped straight out of the cutscenes, and OH MY GOD do they repeat. You will hear Reg saying "Are you ready?" and Riko replying "Of course I'm ready!" OVER AND OVER. Same thing with every other line they speak while playing.Overall, it's a decent experience. I enjoy the first season of Made In Abyss a lot and I've enjoyed the game so far. I personally wouldn't pay 60 dollars for it, but at the price I got it for I can't really complain. Steam really needs a neutral option when it comes to reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game despite some issues that come down to a lack of polish.Pros: - Original story different from the anime/manga, but follows the universe faithfully- Looks beautiful despite the limited graphics (you can tell it was build for Switch then ported to higher-end platforms)- Tons of content, will keep you busy for 30+ hours easily- It is a hard game, so people who want challenge will be served, and mods exist to make things easier for those who prefer an easier approach (it will still be hard though)Cons:- If you want the anime/manga story, you will be disapointed, as that part is only a very short tutorial- A gamepad controller is required, mouse&keyboard is rough- No odd-resolution support like 21:9 (you will get black bars on the sides), again, built for the switch first- Game balance is rough in some aspects, an infamous "respawn timer" causes ennemies to spawn at your feet non-stop after a while, making the game almost unplayable in early levels, but thankfully there are mods on PC that can fix that.- Lack of polish in general. On top of the clearly rushed balance mentionned above (early on it is hardcore, then a single skill can completely change the way you play the game and obtain resources), other issues that are not game breaking can be annoying like the very limited amount of sound effects for human characters, or the inaccurate combat mechanism, or some animation glitches that take you out of the immersion. Mods can fix some balance issues, but not the core gameplay.In my opinion, worth the price despite the flaws if you are a fan of the series, especially on PC as the community is hard at work with mods both for QoL improvements / bug fixing and add-ons. If you go into this game blind though, you may notice the flaws more than the amazing universe it's based on.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: They patched it so you can skip the "Hello Abyss" prologue. I recommend skipping it if you already watched/read Made in Abyss.The reason why people hate it at first is because the prologue is essentially a 3+ hour long tutorial that is missing the several key RPG mechanics that the OC mode has. The game actually starts for real after you beat the Riko/Reg prologue (when you reach the end of the second layer, no you don't need to play all the way down to the fifth layer). On top of the lack of RPG mechanics making the game feel stale and linear, the Riko/Reg prologue story is of course also very monotonous if you've already read the manga/watched the anime.Once you beat the prologue, you actually unlock the fun RPG mechanics, and exploring and combat feels much more exciting and fulfilling. You're incentivized to explore and find relics to gain EXP, which you don't need to do at all when you're playing the Riko/Reg prologue. You have a catalogue for all the relics, monsters and characters in the world, showcasing Tsukushi's expansive world building. You have to genuinely think about how to get around and explore since you have limited resources. Reg's cable arms are OP on purpose, and the introduction of weapon durability makes you think about avoiding needless fights, especially considering you don't gain EXP from combat, but instead gain it from quests and relics (aka, exploration). I've only done the first layer on the OC character playthrough but it's 10 times more fun than the prologue. Rush through the prologue, and give the OC mode a shot. You'll be surprised.>>> EDIT (after beating the game):Pretty good, yet very disappointing in some areas.The World+ Good adaptation of the Abyss.+ It's great experiencing what it's like to be a Delver who actually has to regularly climb up from the Abyss (and not have Reg). It is rewarding to actually come back from a hard and long trip.+ 1st and 3rd layers are full of verticality, detail, and have intricately connected paths. Definitely the best areas in the game.- 3rd layer is a tad bit TOO difficult. There is no smart way to deal with the flying monsters. You cant bait them using squirrel meat, as depicted in the anime. They are also not affected by paralysis or electricity effects. Ascending requires you to know how to stay out of their aggro range with horizontal distancing, and vertically dodging them once you're forced to get close.- 2nd layer, especially the Inverted Forest, is an incredibly linear, uninteresting slog. Also filled with lots of potential soft-lock scenarios due to how it's set up with the main story (unexpected forced combat scenarios in a game with limited resources)- 4th layer is very disappointing. 4th layer's Goblet of Giants is somehow linear and very short, despite being such a key location in the series. It should have been the area with the the second steepest verticality. - To double down on the 4th layer, the Eternal Fortunes Garden was nothing like how it was depicted in the manga/anime. Too small and too dark.- 5th layer feels empty, not just in environment, but also because majority of the enemies are docile. The only difficulty is ensuring you have enough salt to cook since the food/HP requirements from travelling are (rightfully) very costly in this zone. Also the floating water bastions above Ido Front are not supposed to be purple energy blobs, devs.Gameplay+ Difficult and very punishing.+ Exploration requires planning with supplies and travel routes.- There are soft locks (and even hard locks if you manage your saves badly) depending on how poorly you prepare.+ The limitations on fast travel based on your Whistle are great, and make sense thematically. + Combat is serviceable (aside from melee combos not damaging some enemies since they receive i-frames during some stagger animations).+ Durability and repair system creates an intricate resource-allocation game between your weapons and food. - AI is non-existent. Boss battles are all a joke, especially ones that rely on movement.- To double down on the AI as a seperate point, Bondrewd's boss battle is the most disappointing thing in the game."- Infinitely spawning Mobs could have been handled better. Sometimes it comes in clutch if you need food though.+ Relics provide a great gameplay loop to level and make money in the 1st and 2nd layers, and give an incentive to explore.- The Relic gameplay loop is less enticing in the 3rd and 4th layers before you are able to fast travel, since it's incredibly difficult to ascend and the rewards are not worth the effort.- Relics are essentially just generic high-tier materials used solely for crafting generic high-tier weapons with better stats, they do not have unique gameplay purposes like you would expect from the lore. Even if they were given subtle stat-increases similar to Ozen's Wedge, that would have been great. Relics are definitely the biggest let-down in this game. Everyone I knew were looking forward to seeing what unique special-grade, 1st-grade, and 2nd-grade relics we could use.Curse of the Abyss+ The symptoms from the Curse of the Abyss are very well balanced and is thematically accurate. It even has its duration scaled based on your Whistle, which is a cool way to simulate the Delver's tolerance to its symptoms based on experience. - However, the Curse system isn't entirely accurate to the source material. You accumulate the Curse whenever you increase your elevation by any amount in the game (even if it's small, consecutive bumps in the terrain which move you up-and-down just by a few inches). In the manga it's more of a hard threshold once you reach a certain distance (~5 to 10 or so meters). - In game the intended strategy is to wait for the Curse to alleviate before pressing on, which could be interpreted as bearing with the nauseating symptoms, but doesn't make as much sense for the 3rd, 4th and 5th layers where there should be unavoidable consequences. It's clear it's for the intended gameplay design and would have been too punishing, but I would have welcomed a change that forced you to push through with the Curse symptoms when ascending, instead of outright avoiding it.StoryDecent. If you know anything about the series, you already know how it's going to end. The original main villain was meh, but his boss battle was actually the only decently designed fight in the game. I was also hoping that the story would have been completely separate from Riko and Reg's adventure, and at the very least were slightly linked indirectly. Once your character starts interacting with Reg and Riko, you stop believing that your character could exist in the world. The game quickly starts feeling like your generic self-insert fan service anime adaptation.The post-Reg ruined state of Ido Front doesn't make sense, especially considering you meet with Prushka in this game, and Nanachi and Mitty are still chilling in their hideout.Speaking of Nanachi, the secret way to meet her took me for surprise. I wish there were more secrets like this in the game.OVERALLCool game. I'm a huge Made in Abyss fan so it was worth the time. I'd say any Made in Abyss fan should try this. It's not polished enough to be full-price though, I'd wait for a sale. You will definitely get your hours worth though.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no way i can compile on a short review how much this game is broken or is not properly done: bad economy system, dull souls-like fight mechanics that feel extremely simple, tremendous item and mechanic restraints everywhere, some of which could be easily fixable... and many, many more, all of this that leave a trully frustrating game. Very little of the game is properly constructed and is clearly half done (the last level is clearly unfinished, it looks like a testing developing area). The game really feels as if it had been developed under extreme time constraints, low budget, unexperienced game developers or any of these combined. It was also most likely not tested at all since so many problems are evident in both existence and solution but still remain on the game. The soundtrack is all over the place, it's composed of short tracks which don't really fit the environment and since they quickly loop they become annoying. As for the story: First of all I'm a huge fan of Made in Abyss, if you have never seen it and wish to experience it, I'd strongly recommend to go watch the source material, dont take it from here for the first time. In this game, Story is composed of two different campaigns, one follows part of the descent to the abyss of the two main characters, the other one is the story of a new character (you) that gets in the abyss recently. To put is shortly, the main campaing is the tutorial with no new events compared to the source material and the secondary campaing should be considered the main game. The overall theme of the second campaing is basically a non-cannon fanfiction that drastically changes the events of the original source. On this regard, there are good stories, bad stories, and then there is whatever Made in abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness is... like the rest of the game the story is half done and i swear to god at some point I sarted wondering if time travel was involved in the later stages. Even if you can step over all these game limitations and commit to go througt the game, progress on it comes at the cost of spending A LOT of time on it aswell, but every now and then the game feels slightly satisfying to play. I must add, i am actually on a second playthorught and i have started enjoying this game for what it is, it's a 5/10 at best, but it really feels that if this game had had 2 aditional years  of development and tested it adequately, it would have been an astonishingly good game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Made In Abyss fan this game filled the desire for more content from this series. But even for a fan I can only recommend getting this when it's on sale like I did. The game has a lot of fun simplicity like exploring, discovering, combat, meeting characters from the series, going through a new story by the author himself, and more.----------The game is not as difficult as most reviews like to let on. I beat it without any mods and had very little issues with the spawning enemies. But, you will find yourself inevitably having to restart levels whether it's because of being under prepared or running out of items mid level. Main issue I had is I don't know why all the cool cosmetics, skills, whistles, and weapon (the blaze reap) are after the main game when there is really nothing left to do. It really makes me wish for a ng+ or some type of dlc where you go to the 6th layer just so you can get to use them more. There are def a lot more game play issues that can be discussed but I'm too lazy to list them. ----------Overall I enjoyed the 61 hours i put into this game and getting all the achievement's. I would have liked more from a MIA game but this will have to do for now.3/5

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I like the concept, but no.The control scheme is atrocious, especially in menus. Stuff like 'ESC to confirm, SPC to cancel', or having a mouse that does actually nothing except having LMB mapped to confirm (aka, if you click on something, it instead confirms whatever was previous selected with WSAD). That's exceptionally crappy levels of console port, right there.And, of course, absolutely no key rebinding options.Ingame controls aren't much better, combined with a weirdly stiff animation and movement system (i.e. characters halting and pausing half a second before doing a 20cm hop). Combat seems a bit weird, too, but I haven't played long enough to see whether there's more to it that would be considered redeemable (given other reviews, I wouldn't count on it though).It also took me less than 2 minutes of actual gameplay to run into the first bug (glitched out dead mob that kept attacking me after dieing), so that's promising.I won't necessarily diss the game for it's graphics or dialogue quality, because the animation is in the end meant to imitate an anime, and the dialogue is run of the mill visual novel stuff (with decent voice acting, to be fair). But it definitely won't win any prizes.So, as much as I liked the setting and the anime itself, the game just seems like a horribly messy console port cash grab on first glance. And with Steam Refund policy being what it is, a first glance is all you get before I got to make my choice.

_childDocuments_.review: If you do like the series in general , i'd recommend you not to try it despite liking it . The world setting is based on the source material which is what really interests me the most to play this game . Despite that , i'd say if you're here with no prior knowledge to the series whatsoever then i don't recommend you to try it , There's a lot of issues with this game that is clearly not polished even at final release :-The combat feels sluggish as your animation lag is so bad that you barely can dodge attacks from the monsters . I have experience in monster hunter and despite that it's still pretty tight to even dodge attacks as monsters dont leave too much opening . Speaking off there's a bit of a cheese in the game where you just hit the monster once repeatedly to keep them stunlocked . Now comes the second problem .-Weapon durability is very bad design wise . I understand its a resource management game but with that limited durability you are forced to just not fight at all and run from monsters which somewhat kills the fun in the challenge . The worse thing is that small enemies have infinite spawnrate whenever you're like climbing or running around and will attack you . -Remember that cheese from earlier? The cheese is actually very limited to how much stamina you have so its not like a forever stunlock kind of thing its limited to your weapon durability + stamina . But im not complaining about stamina for the cheese but mainly for climbing (I'm talking about you 3rd layer). The stamina has basically gatekept me from ascending in this game for like hours and hours and its annoying every time you try to climb and you almost barely reach the top but ran out of stamina and fell down . At one point , i had to grind food just to be able to climb back up and boy that wasnt fun .While adding to that if you are trying to ascend which 60% of the game if you hit halfway through the game you are going to ascend a lot , makes climbing even more stressful especially in the 3rd layer where there's just a big wall sticking out with one shotting monster that will try to attack you as you climb and then if you climb up you'll get hit by the curse or die getting one shot . This by far is the worst part of the game for me . -Coming from a guy who played monster hunter a lot , i find it very disappointing that when you kill big monsters (like the splitjaw from the anime in the 1st layer if you remember that big snake thing) , they actually don't drop special materials . It'd have been cool to see armors based on the monsters which would've added more depth into the armors in the game or even weapons . I distinctively remember that in the manga there was like a description for one of the birds called Hammerbeak , it says that the head has a part that supposively works like a flint. Would've been cool if that was a thing in the game but nope . They only drop either bird meat or egg which i find disappointing too as they just remove some of the cool aspects of the original material . All and all , i don't recommend this game .

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the manga, so I thought I would enjoy the game. I absolutely love this game. It's a lot of fun and there's a lot to do and explore! I would, however, recommend buying it on sale; it is NOT worth the full price as it still plays like a buggy beta build.Pros:Going through different layers, beautiful level and monster designs, exciting gameplay. A lot of the mechanics do follow the game. I know that the curse of the abyss is a pain for a lot of people, and it's definitely inconvenient, but I love that it was included because it fits the universe. You get to see a lot of main characters, and go on quests with them!Cons: This game's mechanics are NOT well done, and the game is so hella glitchy it isn't even funny. There are instant kill enemies who WILL kill you even if they don't touch you. The jumping mechanics work about 75% of the time. The PC controls SUCK; this was developed for the Switch, so if you have joycons it's a way better experience. The AI is probably the most broken aspect of the game; they're pretty useless and get stuck CONSTANTLY. They also have extremely repetitive voice lines that basically play back to back to back. There are also REALLY annoying useless moths and bugs that infinitely spawn to make your life harder and use up your weapons, but there are mods to remove them. Interesting: This game is not forgiving and will punish you for bad choices or improper preparation. This can make it a pain in the butt, but it's also very in line with the real story. If you take on the wrong enemy, you'll die. If you aren't prepared for a delve, you can get soft-locked and unable to get back to the surface. You have to approach this game with a trial and error mindset. I've found this game about as unforgiving as Dark Souls. I like the difficulty because it suits the universe, but I did get stuck in certain areas with massive learning curves for hours or days. It was really rewarding when I finally surfaced.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly ignore anyone who only played Hello Abyss mode as it is just a retelling of early parts of the anime and is INCREDIBLY limited (you can only go to areas the game lets you and alot of the mechanics aren't available) it functions as a very basic tutorial, with it missing many things (including weapon durability which I will get to later) and a taste of the original story.tl.dr. Absolutely worth it (at half price) if you love Made in Abyss but you'll probably want to give up at the 2nd layer in the Deep in Abyss mode unless you're a masochist (it goes to the 5th layer). There are some mods to fix a few things (without necessarily making it easier) but I can't exactly recommend a game that needs to be fixed by the players.This game is only for people who really love Made in Abyss and even then I'd only recommend if it's 50% off or more (~$40AU or less) so while I personally have played the game for 48hrs, (I installed the mods I mentioned after exploring, but not completing, a majority of the 2nd layer as it simply wasn't very fun trekking all the way up to the first layer with barely anything done) in the 2nd layer in Deep in abyss mode it goes downhill as far as enjoyment factor and good game design, the creatures are a non issue (which is very disappointing as the hostility of the abyss just isn't there) you can walk (literally walk no running or dodging needed) past them unless you need a resource from them and then they are, for the most part, very easy to kill.The difficulty at this point comes from your entire hunger bar emptying in a couple minutes (2nd layer dives take over 10 minutes) and weapons having ridiculously low durability (5-10 hits depending on the weapon, it takes 1-2 hits for a small creature and like 5 for midsize one, you'll need multiple weapons for some of the larger creatures) plus an incredibly small inventory limit compared to the resources needed to complete a raid, which on their own wouldn't be the worst (it should be a punishing place).It's completely fine on the 1st layer as you can get away with carrying 5 of a weapon and just replace them as they break because it's easy to get resources to do so and a particular creature is constantly dropping food and weapon resources. ( one of the mods I installed replaced the weakest weapon, a hatchet, with an even weaker, essentially unlimited durability hatchet which allowed me to go down longer and made it so I didn't require 6 or so weapons just to get the food I needed to survive) It's when you get to the 2nd layer that things go bad you can no longer just kill enemies for food 90% of food drops need salt so make sure you have plenty of that and getting back up from the low 2nd layer to the 1st layer requires more than a full hunger bar as it is consumed to move between areas as well as the constant drain (just going to the 2nd layer costs 20%).With incredibly weak weapons the fact that creatures tend to drop either practically useless food as it doesn't restore enough to travel between some areas and you lose half of what it gives getting more food from one of the easyish enemies to farm for food, the other one that seemed somewhat worth farming dropped bone FAR more often than meat which you can use to make more weapons, assuming you're carrying enough stone, but you don't get enough to keep up with the rate you'll break them or if you do you'll run out of food/hunger which instantly empties your energy meaning you can't swing your weapons anymore (you can use ranged weapons without stamina but they break in ~5 shots and are far more difficult to craft) this can make getting back VERY RNG dependant, it's not only a massive jump in difficult from mostly mindless exploration on the 1st layer to planning things out far more carefully and having to contend with the RNG on the 2nd layer this makes a very poorly designed game.After the 2nd layer is the worst of all 5, the 3rd layer is a massive hole with some tunnels in the sides of it, you'll spend most of your time climbing here so make sure you have some stamina resupplying food to get back to the top when you want to return to town, this wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for the flying creature that lives on this layer that is very difficult to avoid and, at this point, near impossible to kill and very much not worth killing yet, so make sure to have a save close to any climbs needed to make it back up, they aren't generally a problem on the way down (though they can occasionally get you, it's rare) it's trying to go back up that really sucks.Completing this layer without mods would be awful, as the food and weapons to resupply the food you'd need to return to town would prevent you from achieving much, unless you want to bank on finding an abandoned bag that gives you weapons and/or food.After the 3rd layer, particularly since you can fast travel past completed layers once you get the associated whistle, the game is pretty fun again, the 4th layer is probably the best,  it's scenery is personally the most enjoyable and exploring felt fun, though it does introduce the worst enemy (this one is the only one that cannot simply be walked past but you can generally sneak past without much difficulty)The 5th layer has fairly boring scenery but it does give a bit of a harsh feel so it doesn't detract from the experience, the only thing I found worth doing on this layer is the story, but the story was kind of interesting so it's atleast worth finishing from this point and shouldn't take too long once you've hit the 5th layer.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet of this review: If you're a fan of Made in the Abyss world/lore and this game is on sale for 50% off or more I'd recommend getting it!This game has two different game modes: one mode follows the season 1 anime and is considered a tutorial since it's quite short. The second mode allows you to create your own character and delve down to the 5th layer, starting out as a red whistle and progressing all the way to white whistle. You spend time in "town" and then go back out to the abyss to collect relics and try to descend deeper. If you're familiar with the anime then the dangers of the Abyss shouldn't surprise you; you might be admiring the view of a flower-covered hill until a Corpse-weeper swoops down, bashes your head in and carries you off to it's nest to devour you. I honestly have really enjoyed slowly exploring the world, and you do need to take it slow as the game implements weight limits, requires you to climb back the way you came to return (depending on your whistle rank), and the curse of ascension. I would recommend that you download the mod for this game to eliminate infinite enemy spawn timer, as I find it extremely annoying, but your mileage may vary. I would love for this game to be more easily modifiable (like be on the steam workshop) because there's so many features that were cut that would be wonderful to have (weather, camping, character statuses, etc), but honestly I still really enjoy the game. The Bad: I'm not sure if it's due to my computer but in some maps I'll have an instance where my FPS drops to 1 and I need to wait about 10 seconds for the game to resume. The enemy AI isn't very good, and the infinite spawn timer is annoying AF. Combat is a little clunky, but that also may be because my combat skills are low.

_childDocuments_.review: if you can get it for ~$10, go for it. otherwise dont bother.  the actual game is only about 4 hours long, painfully stretched out by making you go through each floor 1-5 times before you can progress to the next one, and giving you almost no inventory space/equipment durability to force you to go back and forth over and over. fast travel mechanics dont unlock until they arent of any real value. the first half of the game is a poorly made rehash of the first season of the anime, except almost every "cutscene" takes place in visual novel style, with 1 or more character models just standing there staring at your screen, delivering lines in the most lackluster "i dont want to be here" manner. its also completely effortless, and not any fun whatsoever unless you simp REALLY hard for the anime, and somehow dont mind this terrible version of it.  the 2nd half of the game is the actual game, but its designed more around disrespecting the player and wasting your time, then allowing progression. it was very clearly NOT tested to any degree, as certain areas of the game are borderline impossible to get through without cheating, following a video guide, or already knowing the single possible path to take to progress. 2nd half has an enemy that will poison you, and said poison will never stop until youre dead, UNLESS you first found the secret cutscene to find nanachi AND finished her long, 15 step fetch quest. otherwise, youre screwed, and will soon be dead.  combat is trash. you have just a single basic attack, and after leveling up a skill tree you get access to a basic 2-3 hit combo and/or charge attacks. either way though, you just spam the 1 attack you have from the 1 weapon thats worth having. theres no sense of wonder or exporation, and dispite what some of the other reviews say here, the areas are absolutely nothing special looking. on average youre looking at early PS3 graphics, and early ps1 gameplay.  worst of all, the entire game is a bug filled mess and very clearly had NO QA testing done. every single map has dozens of spots where you can be walking along and...BAM! stuck in an infinite falling cycle because of poor geometry. the bug enemies have a strange quirk to their model, where if you touch them they are treated like a bicycle ramp, and youre sent launched into the air and to the side. and said bugs are EXCLUSIVELY placed in spots where touching them flings you off a cliff to your death. the entirety of layer 3, like literally every single inch of that map was very clearly not tested at all.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played.Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness does not try to win you over. It doesn't try to be convincing by existing as a game a casual player would be comfortable in. This is a game that aims to be a specific way, and it accomplished that excellently. Games are about the gameplay, not the graphics. And I tell you, the gameplay is high tier.At any moment of the game, you risk dying. It is tense. Without preparing enough, you'll be stranded and lose lots of progress. Frustrating for sure, but that's why it's amazing. You're efforts are rewarded because they matter. Harsh consequences for mistakes. This game forces players to slow down and pay attention to how they play and what they are doing.A tip when looking at other reviews, there's two types of negative reviews: 1, They simply do not like the game and point at what makes it good as a negative. 2, legitimate complaints, as there are issues with the game. It is our choice to deal with the jank to enjoy this gem of a game.  Not worth 60$, at all. Buy on sale.

I would say skip. You can go in blind, but the game will probably be rather mediocre for you, and there are better options for the money out there. For the series hardcore fans it's worth it on sale....You have to have some endurance for this type of game tho, as some of the "difficulty balancing mechanics" can be a little... offensive, like the tendency for the game to spam annoying critters any time you start climbing a rope or wall. There are mods to solve this, but imho it makes the game "too easy" because other than making you fall to your death the game doesn't really have any proper way to kill you since the combat is completely lackluster and exploitable in your favour once you know the enemy you're facing.

_childDocuments_.review: While watching the anime, I was always thinking that MiA had everything for a good videogame; the core concept of cave raiding, the strain of ascension, the whistle tier system, the flora and fauna of this world and most importantly the Abyss itself  seemed just perfect for a game. I wanted to explore this world for myself so badly, to climb the ranks of cave raiders and to create my own adventures. And then they actually made it possible!Coming from a developer who, best to my knowledge, never really made games like this (Chime Corporation) and the publisher Spike Chunsoft (whom I love, but again, not for this kind of games) I was a bit skeptical. I was afraid this game would turn out to be some low quality spin-off akin to a flash game.Fortunately, I was wrong. This game was made with love and I'm certain the developers wanted to give us the experience we were dreaming of while watching the anime / reading the manga. The story is even supervised by the creator of the manga, Akihito Tsukushi himself!The game has two modes: "Hello Abyss", a sort of tutorial / warm-up mode and "Deep in Abyss".The former focuses on Riko and Reg's story (~3-4 hours) until they reach the Seeker camp in the 2nd layer. A lot of people complain about this because they wanted to continue the story of the anime.I personally don't understand the frustration. We've already seen it and the game wouldn't be able to reproduce the same awesomeness of the story. When I said that "I" wanted to experience the Abyss, I didn't mean through Riko, and I think most people understand me here. She is her own character and her story is already written, let us have our own.Also, towards the end of Hello Abyss I even started to dislike it. Following their story meant linear progression, no exploring, little crafting, no leveling but it ended just at the right time. They taught us enough to begin our own journey.Deep in Abyss starts with your customizable character becoming a red whistle and going on their first dive. The game quickly introduces the main cast and a little handholding later you're free to progress and explore at your own pace, which is the beauty of this game. The new story itself isn't anything mindblowing, especially if you watched Dawn of the Deep Soul things become pretty apparent pretty early on, but it's still good and fits in the world well. It's a decent story but the game's main appeal is the cave raiding, as it should be.It's surprisingly good honestly. I was expecting way worse from this studio but I'm pleasantly disappointed. That said, it still has problems, just minor ones. Gathering resources is quick and easy, you'll never need to go out of your way for some plants.Excavating rocks may yield you common, well, rocks, or relics. Mining will be your primary source of relics which you can sell for xp + money, or craft armors and weapons with them later on (which I highly recommend).Fishing is really good in this game, but still fishing. You see a fish in the pond, throw your bait close to it, it bites. Quick and easy. That said, unless it's required for an armor set or quest, you really shouldn't spend much time fishing.Hunting primeval creatures for food is relatively easy (just bring salt, for the love of god BRING ENOUGH SALT). Side quests that require hunting have the well known curse of getting too tedious too fast. I'm talking about "kill "x amount" of "y creature"". Yeah, they are there but a lot of them are not even worth it for the XP. You can get enough XP from other sources, so don't feel obligated to complete them all, there's no achievement for it.The controls could be better. I used a gamepad for my playthrough (I used mouse occasionally for ranged weapons) and remapped nearly every button. Maybe because I have other preferences from other games but I just couldn't get used to it, but since you can freely remap them it's fine I guess.You dash holding down a button. Dodge is the same button. "Kinda like Dark Souls, eh? Cool!" THINK AGAIN! You need to DOUBLE PRESS the button to roll. This may be my single biggest complain with the game. Some enemies require quick reaction time and double pressing takes a lot of it.Also when an enemy dies you were locked on to, it would be nice if the game automatically targeted the next one that's close to you. Otherwise, the combat is decent.The cave raiding itself is quite enjoyable and the level design is perfect in my opinion. I was afraid it would suck but they actually nailed it. The verticality is good. The thematic resemblence but uniqueness of individual areas inside layers is just awesome. The loot placement, enemy spawns and everything else, I didn't find a single problem. I was so afraid in Layer 1 that they made this amazing map for they first part of the game to reel you in and then you'll only get generic levels after that, but they kept it up till the end.You'll be climbing walls a lot but for me it was fun after figuring out the exploits.There are not many gimmicks, and virtually no puzzles. It's a wild environment, not a pharao's tomb.The leveling system is okay I guess, and the whistle tier progression is satisfying as with every new whistle you can unlock more skill for either combat, crafting or cave raiding. I love that skill tree, it's very well done.I heard there were more survival mechanics, kinda wish they weren't cut. You only have to worry about hunger and status effects really (including broken arms / legs but easily managable). This reminds me, there were critics who said this game was too hard, and there were some who said it was too easy. Fans of the original works know the Abyss is unforgiving. I personally enjoyed the challanges and never really felt like I was too comfortable either. It kinda works like this: first time you explore an area, you don't really know where you are going and try everything. This puts you in much more danger than later on when you're running through the same area you are already familiar with and I guess thats all right.The strain of ascension is very well implemented.This game is very easy on your pc. I have a midspec machine and it ran this game 60fps on epic quality the whole time. Honestly it feels like this game came out in the PS3 era. That said, the textures are not at all ugly, they create the perfect cartoon world for this game. The characters are rather simplistic as well but you'll get used to them. The 2D art for the items and creatures / plants are very nice though. I'm not usually critical of graphics so can't say much more.All in all, It satisfied my yearning for adventure in the Made in Abyss world. I would recommend this to anyone who loves the franchise and wants to experience the thrill of cave raiding, and for survival game enhusiasts who want a fun time. Waiting for a discount is always recommended.Small addendum:I forgot to say this but if you're like me and cringe at every word english dubbers say in anime (no offense to them, I just can't stand it) fear not, this game has japanese dub you can turn on in the options menu. It also makes companions more tolerable as they talk a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definitely rough around the edges, a more mid-budget game, but I really enjoyed my time with it. I would say that enjoying Made in Abyss does help, and especially if you always wanted to explore the Abyss.The game is a difficult RPG / Survival game, kind of. You have to manage stamina, hunger and health, and explore the Abyss from the first to fifth layer. The Abyss is truly unforgiving and hostile, but also beautiful. You have to climb a lot and navigation is a constant puzzle. Climbing up hits you with the curse - but it mostly is boring as you just "wait" for it to disappear. Not sure if it could be done better as a game mechanic though.There are 2 modes, the "Hello Abyss" is really just a tutorial though and follows the manga/anime story only until the third layer. In "Deep Abyss" mode you make your own character and truly play the game and explore at your own. There is an original story to follow, which is nothing great honestly, but good enough. There are cameos and lots of side quests, also none of which are stand-out. Some side-quests also are super grindy, requiring hundreds of creature kills - you don't have to do them though.The progression and eventual mastery is really fun. You keep improving as you rank up and get better equipment, and it is fun to look back how difficult the first layer was in the beginning when you now explore the fifth layer.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky but lovable. It seems that most of the negative reviews are from people who didn't even bother giving the game a chance. This game is clearly made with love despite the few hiccups, and the developers understood what makes the abyss so enchanting.I had a rocky start and some frustrations along the way, but the more I played this game, the more I started getting attached to it, and at this point I adore it. I've played it for 57 hours so far (and I believe I might be nearing the end), so to me, the game is worth it, provided you play it with the spawn rate fix mod.Let's start with the basics: Don't expect a AAA game nor an engaging combat system, and play this if you're already a fan of the series, because the story might be difficult to understand with no prior knowledge of the world. The game has 2 modes: "Hello Abyss" and "Deep in Abyss". The first one acts as a 3-hour "tutorial" and retells part of Riko's journey (but ultimately I found it quite boring). The 2nd one is where the real game takes place, so you can skip or speedrun "Hello Abyss".While this game is clunky in terms of controls (you can remap them though) and may contain a few broken features (which can usually be fixed with mods), it is excellent in exploration, the main gameplay loop is fun, the characters are lovable, the music is really nice, and you can learn many interesting things about the world. Even some side quests feel meaningful because they allow you to spend time with your favorite characters.Overall, a solid 9/10 if played with the mod I mentioned. The negative reviews feel misleading and harsh, because my experience was better than I expected. If they ever make a DLC or a game that covers the remaining layers of the abyss, I would definitely buy it!I'm off to go say hi to Bondrewd, thanks for reading!(PS: You don't know true peace and cozyness until you've found Nanachi's Hideout)

_childDocuments_.review: Short version - Imperfect-but-soulful, if you're a fan, pick it up (when it's on sale).'Binary Star' is not without its share of bugs, flaws, and weaknesses: The tutorial (Hello Abyss), in particular, feels hastily thrown together and I recommend skipping it unless you want the achievement, and the main game could have benefited from fleshing out the combat, skill-tree, and adding in a few more survival mechanics, but overall it's such an endearing, comfortable, and soulful game that it's easy to overlook its shortcomings. The fundamental gameplay loop of delving, exploring, treasure hunting, and trying to survive the ascent to cash in your haul and upgrade your gear for the next sortie is incredibly satisfying, especially when your well-laid plans inevitably go awry on the way up and you're forced to think on the feet. The plot is mostly window dressing for the setting and the gameplay mechanics, but the new characters are nice enough, and the story does work in a few good moments, and works in a lot of dialogue and details from the series along with some fun cameos from familiar characters. If the game is even remotely on your radar it's probably because you're a fan of the series and you're looking for an excuse to spend some more time in that universe, and at that, the game excels. While it's not worth paying full price, if it's on sale for $20-30 dollars you'll absolutely get your money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: If I didn't know better I'd think there was an early access label on the game. The second part/game is really corny but fun for the first two layers, but then the story kind of drops off and the game just slams what is possibly the hardest part of the entire game in your face in the form of the third layer. After that it's just several floors of grinding though. There's almost no story outside a few tidbits on the fourth layer. The game just sort of expects you to want to get to the end without really giving you any driving factors to keep going. Sure there's sidequests, but after a while sidequests just start feeling like unnecessary chores to extend your playtime (kind of like fishing for better armor), and you realize you're already capable enough to just keep advancing to the next stage using the profits from quests you completed accidentally and relics you bring back between dives to fund further trips (I realized this shortly before getting my black whistle). At that point Bonedaddy's quest just feels like a punch in the 'nads, you know?It's a fun game. I would only buy it on-sale since it feels half-finished, but it's worth playing.EDIT: Oh right, and make sure to use Japanese voices.

_childDocuments_.review: To start I would preface this review by saying that in my personal experience I think Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness is a good game that is very enjoyable. I feel that the overly negative reviews focus too much on the few negative points that the game does possess, and completely disregards the many positive aspects of the game. The game I think is a solid 7.5/10...maybe an 8/10 if I am feeling generous.To begin, there are two modes. Hello Abyss and Deep Abyss. Hello Abyss is meant to be a tutorial, and is completely optional. It is simply a faithful adaptation to the anime up to the end of layer 2. You play as Riko, and you have your travelling companion Reg to help you with fights and act as a never-ending rope. It's a good way to acclimate the player to the general mechanics of navigation, resource management, preparedness, etc. You don't get to keep any of your progress when Hello Abyss ends, so many people just end up skipping this part. If you are confident you don't need a tutorial, and don't feel you need to see the first few episodes of season 1 in a video game adaptation. Hello Abyss is an easy skip. I should mention here that Reg does get stuck a lot in Layer 2, AI pathing is awkward at best. Plus there is a lot of repeating dialogue that happens every few seconds. It gets really annoying, and I think this is another good reason to just skip the tutorial.Onto the meat of the game, Deep Abyss. This is where you get to control your own character, and go on your own adventures into the abyss. This is clearly the best part of the game and is the main mode you will be playing. There are tons of quests to do, both main quests and side quests. There are skill trees, an abundance of items to collect, multiple zones in each layer to explore, wide variety of enemies and side characters, recipes for food items, clothes, weapons, etc. There is a lot of content here that you will find, and the gameplay loop is both entertaining and engaging. Much of that comes from the exploration of the abyss itself. There is so much to discover and see in each layer. A variety of pathways you can choose, new and interesting enemies, plenty of things to collect and loot, areas to discover, and other things. Indeed just exploring new areas is extremely fun and rewarding. As you complete the main quests and layers you will get promoted to higher ranking whistles. With these you can fast travel to previous layers you have completed, depending on your progress in the main story and what whistle you have. This is a great time saver as you won't have to start at layer 1 and go all the way down to a deeper layer.  There is a lot to talk about, but it would involve going into spoiler territory.In any case, there are some negative points to talk about as well. Combat and odd development choices to name the biggest two. Combat is very simplistic, and outside of just whacking enemies with your weapon. You have a dodge, that must first be unlocked. Nothing really special here to talk about. Hit and run mechanics are useful. You have ranged weapons too, but otherwise combat doesn't vary a whole lot. Sometimes dodging doesn't work when it is supposed to, and the hitboxes of some enemies are bigger than the enemies themselves. Sometimes there are "lingering hitboxes" from attacks that visually should not be there. There are some features in the game that could have been explained better. For instance, you can make climbing easier once you unlock the lunge ability. Game doesn't really tell you that. Yes it's in the skill tree, but you won't know how useful it is until you unlock it and try it for yourself. There are shortcuts in certain areas that you will begin to see in layer 3. You have to do something to unlock them, usually pushing a rock. But unlike the ropes you have used before. These shortcuts will reset once you leave the area. Not the layer, or the abyss itself. When you leave that specific area, things will return to normal. For no logical reason. This can strand you in bad a way, but there is always a way out if you look for it, and find it. I suppose an argument can be made that parts of the abyss are canonically ever changing, but there are some shortcuts that not even this is a good explanation for. I will also talk about enemies spawning behind your back after you have been in an area for an extended period of time. These will be flying enemies that will harass you constantly when climbing or just running around. Most of the time you can crouch to make them disappear, but you can't do this while climbing. You either have to beat them up as you climb upwards and your durability on weapons will suffer plus drain your energy, or let them wail on you as you sit waiting for the curse effects to disappear. I can understand why they are there. The developer wanted to keep tension high, and force the players to make difficult decisions. Though I feel a better way could be found.In addition, small gripe on my end, but there isn't a way to customize the clothing appearance of your character. For example, one of the skills you can spend skill points on is increased backpack space. Which you will obviously want as how much you can carry will always be a constant concern. This has a secondary effect of changing the appearance of your backpack, neat. But at some point it make your backpack's visual appearance huge, like visually massive. It covers 3/4 of your character from the back view. It literally looks like your character has become a backpack with legs. It's actually ridiculous to look at. I looked for a way to change my backpack appearance to something less goofy, but the option is not there. For the rest of my adventure I felt like I was "Backpacky The Explorer". Odd development choice if you ask me. I also liked the look of some gear sets, but they had worse stats. There is no way to equip one set of armor, but have the appearance of another. Fine I suppose, but at least let me change the appearance of my backpack.I think this is where I will end my review. There is much I could say about it, but this is the basics I feel that will help other people make a more informed purchasing decision. For what it's worth, I think the game is good. Get it on sale for sure! I want to see more from this series, and this is a good...start. Definitely needs improvement, but I am looking forward to the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all sorts of jank, but behind all of the glitches and questionable game design is a generally addictive and unique game.It's a difficult game, and it's more than happy to throw you into inescapable scenarios if you didn't think to prepare yourself properly. Half the time the difficulty is challenging but fair, and during those times it's a lot of fun. Unfortunately though the other half is filled with artificial difficulty, the biggest issue being aggressive enemy spawning in many locations. This would be fine in any other kind of Dungeon Crawling game, however this game actively encourages you to scan the environment and take your time - this is a lot harder when enemies are spawning a couple metres away every few seconds if you dare move the camera slightly. This might sound like a trivial issue, but when you're in the mid-to-late stages of the game trying to fight a difficult boss, smaller enemies will  spawn just out of sight. They'll make you flinch, then it's game over.However if you have a calm temperament and don't mind losing progress due to some unfair circumstances, you get a unique innovative game. The locations are beautiful and varied whilst the soundtrack gives off an ethereal vibe - The Abyss has the perfect combo of awe and horror. The gameplay loop of exploring further and further into The Abyss collecting relics to sell back at the surface is addicting, and each time you descend you take on more risks until you inevitably bite off more than you can chew.Honestly I think this is a great game, just don’t expect it to be a polished experience. Also if you're a fan of the manga/anime, you'll appreciate the extra lore.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the negative reviews deceive you. Most of them were written during a time where the game forced you to play its inferior "Hello Abyss" Gamemode.With that being said, the game features 2 Gamemodes. The aforementioned "Hello Abyss" is meant as a "Tutorial" in which you play as Riko and Reg on their way down the Abyss. Nothing you do in this gamemode carries over to the "Main" gamemode "Deep in Abyss". Do I still recommend playing Hello Abyss? Yes. But don't waste your time collecting stuff (especially Relics, they're useless in this mode). use it to get accustomed to the gameplay. The game will get tougher from here on out.Let's talk about the main gamemode now, "Deep in Abyss" has you create your own cave-raider who enlistens into the Belchero Orphanage to eventually become a White Wistle. This gamemode is where the game truly shines. The Abyss is unforgiving and even the first layer can prove deadly if you're ill-prepared. Collection and crafting equipment is fun and the skill system which is tied to your whistle rank, forces you to delve deeper and deeper to unlock more content. Many of the characters, monsters and areas from the Anime are in the game as well. I was surprised when I found the spot where Riko initially found Reg during the first episode, and standing in front of the deep chasm of the third layer gives a feeling of dread.Who is this game for?The gameplay loop kind of reminds me of Monster-Hunter a bit, with the exception that it's not (always) about hunting large monsters. You use the City Orth to equip and buy goods (Weapons, Clothes, Food, etc.) to prepare for a dive, accept quests from the Guild and other NPC's and then dive down, carefully planning to be able to make your way back.. if you can't make it back to the city from down below, you'll lose it, so plan in advance.The game has a tiny but very friendly and dedicated modding community that's hard at work fixing smaller issues.There's Mods disabling the countdown enemy spawners, replacing the ingame OST with the official Anime OST, reducing weight of items and increasing durability, allowing for more character creation options and much more.I just recently got this game on a 50% discount and I don't regret my purchase at all. It plays well on the Steam Deck and on my PC and it has me hooked.

And the time it takes for the layer movement effects having to stop less than every minute if I'm climbing up a tall wall. Again, overall I enjoy it quite a bit. Graphics, voices (except for reg...hes very puppet-like and emotionless in here for some reason knowing these are the original voice actors), designs and originality of the art and music and atmosphere it gives off like in the anime. If I were to rate it, I'd give it a 6.5/10 for the lack better acting and not really any facial changes in certain lines and scenes of any of the characters, the length it takes to level up past a red whistle not letting you increase your backpack space which makes it difficult to craft and carry several things causing you to run out of something when you really need it and the amount of time wasted sitting in one spot waiting for the layer curse to dissipate. But overall I love the game and have been playing it almost every day/ :)

_childDocuments_.review: When I first watched Made in Abyss, my biggest thoughts about the show was that this franchise would make the best freaking game ever. The world is amazing and beautiful, and the story is captivating, but definitely room for more exploring and world building. The characters are pretty memorable and awesome too!Onto this game. This game was not what I expected at all. When I thought of a Made in Abyss game, my mind immediately went to a Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild style open world exploration game where you would have to venture into the abyss and follow the main storyline as Riko and Reg until the end of season 1 or when they got to the entrance of the 6th layer after the 3rd movie. (However, now that we have season 2, integrating some of that would be pretty cool as well.)This game is NOT that at all. It's semi-open world where there's not that much to explore and you're always having to travel between areas through hubs rather than it being completely open. The saving system is both a blessing and a curse (no pun intended) where I either forget to save, override my old save or some other mishap (It's a skill issue, I know). The crafting is a pain because I don't know where to find some of the resources needed and the game doesn't tell you anything, I always need rope (always have rope), navigating a new area when you can't fast travel yet is the biggest pain and if you're ill-prepared for a adventure into the abyss good luck getting back. I wish the combat was a lot more snappy and not so slow, especially for the bosses and mini-bosses where I want to move around and spam my attack button. Don't even get me started with the keybinds for M&K. I would personally use controller, but you can't navigate the menu's properly (unless they fixed that). I mostly bought this game because it was a Made in Abyss game which is something that I had always wanted. I kept playing because it is fun even if it is annoying sometimes, especially if you like the franchise and that is why I am recommending this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not recommended to people who are unfamiliar with Made in Abyss and looking for an entry point to the series, or fans who want a game comparable to the anime in terms of quality.  It is only worthwhile to play if you are deeply in love with Made in Abyss’ world, lore, and characters that you want to see more of them after you watched the 1st season anime.A few glaring issues are gatekeeping.  First is the $60 price suggests this game to be something it isn’t; my advice is to wait for a sale.  Second is the ridiculously overtuned infinite enemy spawning that is a deal breaker for many players, myself included.  The solution is to download the mod that removes the infinite spawning, while the overall difficulty of the game remains unchanged.  Lastly, don’t expect a stellar original story from this game… The plot certainly has the series’ signature cruelty, but its narrative is way too incohesive to enjoy.What this game does well is to present a gameplay loop that is faithful to the original source.  The process of the main character going into the Abyss, obtaining relics, and coming back to the surface alive is the main loop of this game.  Resource management is the key to any successful expedition, and the player is rewarded by carefully planning ahead, dealing with the enemies and terrain accordingly, and finally bringing back as much relic as possible for money and exp.Another notable mention is despite the game’s PS3-ish graphics, each map and area has an overabundance of the mysterious, alluring, and dangerous atmosphere as is mentioned in the anime and manga.  With the exception of Layer 3’s maps being a massive pita, every other map is a good tourist trap and should be explored fully.TL;DR: Buy this game when on sale if you love the Made in Abyss series enough to overlook the various faults it has and enjoy the aspects it does well. Also use the mod to disable infinite spawns so this game is actually playable.
