_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Buy if you like Made in Abyss and want to experience the Abyss in some way, pass if you don't.I was on the fence whether or not to buy this game, and after reading the top review, I had decided not to. A few weeks later though, I heard a few good things and thought "Why the heck not?"I'll preface this review in that if you're not a fan of Made in Abyss, this game probably is best passed. It's nothing special if you're not interested in the story, and it's not going to make you interested in the story by itself.If you're a fan, I feel the game does a good job in representing what the abyss in Made in Abyss is supposed to represent. It's dangerous if you're not careful, it's tedious, and can be repetitive. That's likely what a cave raider in the MiA universe experiences. Going down and up the same paths in the abyss to find the ideal path, trying a different path and realizing you might not have the supplies to return, picking up a relic only to find you have to throw something out to bring it back.The downsides:* The price of the game is AAA for something that's not AAA polished.* Graphics aren't the best; there are areas where tiling is obvious, or the texture chosen doesn't quite fit. It's an anime game, so the graphics aren't going to be realistic, but they leave something to be desired. * Enemies spawn off camera depending on how long you're in an area. It can get quite irritating, but there is an item that keeps them away.* Relic "nodes" are almost too obvious, the locations don't change, and the variety of relics is limited.* Quests boil down to either kill quests, fetch quests, or craft quests.The positives:* Inventory management is essential, as is proper planning prior to and during a delve.* The areas have some variety to them, and are interesting to explore.* The music is rather catchy* Enemies can be extremely deadly if you're not careful* Fast travel is limited based on progress in the game. I recommend against using it for immersion purposes.Overall, I enjoyed the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The ugly news first: animations and landscape models are very mid. Anyone that has played the game will tell you the Inbyo boss fight is embarrassingly bad, and this is true. Boss battles also feel a bit clunky and not dynamic because of the status animations and movements. I also had no idea how to proceed in the 3rd layer at some point, but the game assumed I would have unlocked a stamina upgrade by then, which made me able to climb a certain wall and proceed. This oversight took me a while to figure out.The bad: You  N E E D a spawnrate fix mod. I've poured almost 30 hours into this game and didn't need the mod for the first 10. But some creatures can respawn WITHIN 2 FEET OF YOU and will hit you to push you off the wall you're climbing or bridge you're crossing. This infinity nearby enemy spawn is useful to avoid any softlock you might get yourself into and helps you farm materials faster, but it can be a real nuisance. Use the mod to fix it and turn the mod off when you feel like you need enemies to spawn faster.Another bad is some mini-bosses also feeling clunky. However this is not a huge issue, since ONLY the early game mini-bosses feel like that, and in the early game you should avoid these guys like the plague, and by the time you can deal with them the clumsiness isn't an issue anymore.The good:Many reviews get this wrong. THE MAIN GAME LOOP AND HELLO IN ABYSS ARE GOOD if you ask me. Hello in abyss is a 3-4 hour long tutorial where you play as riko and reg. People were very happy hello in abyss could be skipped with the new update, but you will be completely and utterly lost in the first layer of the abyss if you skip it. The main game loop for the first 30 hours in the game is somewhat like this:>Complete main story quests in the lowest layer you have access to.>Gather relics and turn them in to improve your gear.>level up, unlock the next layer and repeat.Something else that's really important that reviews don't mention: The sound design.The sound effects are satisfying, the music does not get stale after hearing it for hours while exploring, and even 30 hours into the game I keep discovering new music tracks during new types of combat and in new areas. Every BGM is fitting for the area you are in, and doesn't get repetitive as quick as most BGMs do.Another thing that a lot of reviews don't mention is RELIC SYNTHESIS!! You can make INSANELY strong weapons using relics, but crafting these is a skill tree unlock late into the game. However, at this point you still have 8+ quests to gather a certain amount of materials and research in the first and second layer. I had abandoned those quests assuming they were boring filler content, but you need some first layer relics to create your first relic weapons.You might get where I'm going with this.If you end up playing the game and progress, you will VERY likely start fast traveling to skip traversing the first layer on the way down. This is where those "filler" quests come in, the game cleverly has some half-completed quests waiting for you in the first later, along with relics and certain items you need to craft weapons which only appear in the first layer. I've not yet finished the game but I'm assuming when I unlock higher level crafting recipes, I'll start needing to use 2nd and 3rd layer relics and so on.I already poured many hours into the game, I've seen what made people think its bad, but I've been having a blast. Unlocking a new layer to discorver, holding 8 different maps next to each other to plan out a route, taking that route, making sure you dont starve, making sure you dont get hit by the curse of the abyss, fighting off pests and creatures, all while you're killing some rodents to make food to keep yourself alive. This part of the game gets very immersive and despite not having good graphics or animations, it is really fun in my opinion.VERDICT:If you love the made in abyss franchise or don't really care about graphics then yes this game is for you! If you're not so much into exploration in games and want a challenge you should definitely wait for a sale. As you can tell even most negative reviews have at least 20 hours into this game. Even though some parts don't look good or are visibly rushed, the game is **BIG**. Despite the content not being worth the triple A price the AMOUNT of content definitely is.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, This review is meant to help new interested people to answer the question "is this game worth $60?" and a simple tutorial of basic functions, I will give my opinion and a simple no-spoiler review, let's get started.		Hello Abyss: this is a basic introduction save that goes through the general story of the show, it is very short and introduces the main functions of the game. This part is not as strong as the main gameplay and has no effect or continued story (aka you can't level up as Riko and you don't get to explore or do much besides basic functions). All in all, it has its hard moments but is a really good tutorial for people. Personally, I recommend speeding through this part and getting to the main game (unless you want to learn the story, which is amazing and you should go watch the show if you like this part). Again this will only affect that specific game mode nothing in the rest of the game is affected.	Deep In Abyss: alright so this is the main game of well the game, you can pretty much go anywhere at the very start (after the required story mission). The story in this one is actually really good with new characters and lots of gameplay, This part of the game is where you can level up your character with quests and collecting relics to turn in. Now onto the actual gameplay and game aspects! Deep in Abyss gameplay: Collectables: in the game, there are 2 pick-up items (different kinds of material that all look different but are functionally the same). 	Plants: along the ground, there are many different plants that you can pick up, with different uses in crafting and quests. 	Rocks: on the walls, there are two kinds of rock that do different things, Blue sparkles: if a rock is sparkling blue it will give either a crafting material for weapons or a normal relic, Red sparkles: if a rock is sparkling red it will always give a relic with a chance to give a high-grade relic. On every level, these rocks will take on a different look but give the same type of loot (if you look into it you can find a thing called rock standing too). Enemies: This is pretty simple, there are a few kinds of enemies that give different things, but they all generally give the same loot depending on the area, Again this is spoiler-free so I won't tell you the enemies, but I will give advice on that there are small weak enemies, and large big enemies (and subsidies that are more medium). The small enemies mostly give meat and nothing else, but the bigger ones give more materials. Unfortunately, you don't get multiple drops, if you kill something you get a chance to get something out of the pool of their drops.Equipment: simple, you get a helmet slot, body slot, leg slot, glove slot, shoe slot, and backpack slot (keep in mind the backpack slot cannot be changed or removed throughout the game only upgraded through skills). some pieces of clothing can have a ruin equipped onto them that gives you a substat that will help with specific damage or statuses. next weapons, bow, gun (yes there is a gun), pickaxe, and machete, these are all simple and can be crafted, the higher whistle level you are the higher one you can buy/craft (if you unlock the weapon crafting skill required). there are different ammo types too but that's not important, weapons have durability and can break, but will be replenished IF you can make it back to the surface before they break. Skills: you have multiple different skills you can progress into, most high skills are locked and will unlock when you get a higher level whistle. You have Battle, Cave raiding, and Crafting, pretty self-explanatory.Quests: you get main quests that appear in the quest section, and side quests to complete that you get from the city after unlocking a layer/going to a new layer.	Food: what do you want from me? you eat it and depending on what you make it gives back health and hunger, you can craft or buy it. but a little hint you didn't hear from me FOOD IS LEGIT THE MOST IMPORTANT THING TO HAVE... so let's get into why	movement: you can jump, climb, sprint, attack, collect, and climb ropes, if you don't have hunger up even a little, you have no stamina, if you have no stamina, you start moving extremely slowly and can ONLY jump. Food goes down fast. way too fast, so always have food on you. Layers: so far there are only 5 layers, no spoilers though so you'll have to figure it out by getting there, (Big warning for level 3 though, just be prepared)Characters: No spoilers... duh! but I wanted to say that the characters are well voice-acted, true to the original story, and very fun to interact with. One thing you will find very early on is that anytime you pick something up they will say something generic which was annoying at first but really funny the more I played (but that might have just been because I was happy to finally do something other than suffer) Difficulty: Alright so right off the bat you will already know from other reviews this game is MEAN, if you die you will be sent back to your last auto-save (it saves every time you enter a new area, aka. gold rings) and you will lose everything you collected in that level. Fighting some enemies can be fun and quick, but some are impossible to fight whether you can touch them or not. the enemies WILL spawn infinitely in certain spots, which can get extremely annoying, but if you go into an area without much food, DO NOT mod this out of the game (this is my pure opinion, I could handle the worse parts of it which I get into soon), in curtain places if there was no infinite spawning I would have lost hours of gameplay because animals are a food source, and no food = no stamina = no climbing = absolutely f**ked. climbing can be brutal and some small enemies will spawn and body block you off your climbing killing you instantly, some can fly and instant kill you, and others can knock you off the side without giving any benefit of food. Do not be ashamed to turn it off it can get really really annoying. A problem I had was controls, throughout the game I did not use the lock-on feature once for a fight, why? because the game wouldn't let me equip it in a more convenient spot. changing controls is fine but major controls like left click or right click, it would not let me change, and I had to put major keys like q and e on attack and pick up (again no re-binding of left click for me so I couldn't change it to attack) running out of food with no hope of animals nearby is a game over, so I suggest keeping a save file near the beginning of the layer so you don't lose everything.Conclusion: Alright so we have talked about most of the functions and gameplay, now then, the true question... in my opinion "is this game worth $60?" A triple-A price indeed, So my verdict? no, I don't think this game should be sold at $60, BUT I absolutely love this game, as hard as it can be it is fun gathering, the skill system is perfect, leveling up is fun, and getting a new whistle and new main quests are fun, and the difficulty in my opinion :does not need to be changed at all: Why? it stays true to the show, the abyss is a literal hell hole that will kill you in the blink of an eye and it does, a lot. It is very infuriating at many times, but I learned and grew and so did my character showing just like in the show, how whistles grow and get better at exploring, and the game captures this absolutely perfectly, amazing game system, amazing gathering system, great fighting mechanics, and if you're familiar with the show there are so many new experiences and moments that just shinned through the pain. I personally have fallen in love with this game, it's a lot of fun learning, it's a lot of fun collecting, and the pain of failing only felt SO MUCH BETTER when you finally figured out how to survive and get back. The ending was good, and it was fun all around, But! back to my answer... Why did I say no, if I love this game so much? well... (continued in comments)

_childDocuments_.review: Well having played this game for 47 hours and getting all achievements I have some thoughts. The game is good (if you like the show/manga) and is worth playing just to experience certain things in a slightly more hands on way. However you must play through a neutered version of the first half of the season of the anime which lasts 3-5 hours before getting into the good stuff. Afterword you get to customize your torture orphan and start your bloody descent. There are many neat concepts and fun creatures to fight, although enemies constantly spawning just off screen can get tiresome. For an example you can make relic gear similar to that of white whistles, and there are even full on boss-fights with very nice rewards. However there are some major downs, the game is nicely stylized to be similar to the anime and manga but otherwise has looping textures and some wall textures are passable at best, combat is fairly simple even with max level combat skills and most enemies can just be stun locked by basic attacks. I would say in spite of this that some of the late game areas are very good looking for the graphical style, and the boss fights while cumbersome are fun and not stun lockable making you have to actually try. Over all I suppose I would give the game a high 6 or a low 7 if you like the show/manga and probably a 4.5 if you have no interest in the world or characters. (I hope as the story progresses the game will get more content also)

_childDocuments_.review: The best way i can review this game in a way that captures its charm is through a story. I'll try to sum it up in a TL;DR at the bottom in case you may find this long winded.I can see why reception on this game is mixed. It's incredibly unfortunate the first three hours is a poor tutorial that doesn't really give you a proper idea of what the meat of the game is. After clearing the forced story mode with Riko, That restricts your ability to truly adventure, which is supposed to be the main appeal of the game. You can finally start your adventure into the Abyss with your own character and experience an original story. Just like the anime, Don't let the look of this game deceive you. This is very gameplay over graphics. The gameplay is, much like the abyss itself, Unforgiving. Without including any spoilers, I went on a dive and made multiple mistakes along the way without thinking anything of it. I threw out salt to make room for more treasure, Didn't manage my food correctly, and had dived too far deep into the abyss, running out of food and resources (because i threw away my salt, i couldn't properly produce more edible food) to actually be able to make it back to the surface. I had lost 1.5 to 2 hours of progress roughly after taking another 30 minutes to realize that there was no way for me to make it back to the surface.In this moment, in any other game, i probably would have dropped the game. Yet, Despite my bitterness, each of my long term mistakes started to click in my head as i realized everything was my own fault, and such mistakes are what a careless cave raider would actually make if they became too complacent or overconfident. For some reason, this felt acceptable and kind of genius. I didn't know my character was for all intents and purposes dead until it was way too late. In this instance, the abyss had claimed another Cave Raider, and i had no one to blame but my own hubris. Now I have to start this whole dive over, but now i'll be better prepared.TL;DRThis game is not for everyone and suffers from a bad first 3 hours that misleads you on what the game is actually about. This game past those 3 hours is incredibly unforgiving, but thats how it should be if the devs TRULY wanted to capture the dangers of the abyss and how being prepared is the defining edge between failure and survival in the Abyss. You can lose large chunks of progress if you are under prepared, and this game will not hold your hand. I give this game a 9/10, but if you just read the TL;DR this game probably isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a ton of fun with this game. After the Reg and Riko tutorial mode, the real game is a fun, pretty standard, RPG-style game where you level up your character and go on deeper and deeper cave dives as you do. It's been a blast to play through the different layers I've seen in the show, interact with the characters, and get that satisfactory feeling of progression whenever I complete a long and dangerous cave dive deeper than I've ever gone before.The controls are a little clunky but after rebinding some keys/buttons they're not hard getting used to. The graphics aren't impressive but they're enough to make the world look very pretty and true to the anime - think Breath of the Wild, not impressive but they do a lot with what they have.Some minor bugs here and there, but nothing game-breaking.I've seen complaints about the gameplay but I disagree. The punishing aspects of the game are there for a reason. The curse of the abyss is a huge part of Made in Abyss and can't be removed, the durability and respawn systems are there to encourage you to complete your objectives in a timely fashion. The abyss is dangerous and it's a bad idea to stay in one zone and think you can just kill everything. And when you overcome these challenges and get back to town with a bag full of valuables to progress your character, it feels great.Overall, I recommend for anyone who's a fan of the show and doesn't think the gameplay mechanics talked about would prevent them from enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a diehard fan of the series, and just love the world of Made in Abyss in general, you'll be wonderfully charmed by this game. That being said, it's as tough as a soulslike and frustrating a lot of times. Super immersive for the world, but not really good for casual fans of the series. I don't know if it's really worth $60, but I've already got 29 hours in it upon writing this review, so maybe?
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: As many have pointed out, the first mode "Hello Abyss" is rather dull and off-putting. As a fan of the source material, I really dislike how the story was butchered. Don't really need to talk about the graphics much; everyone agrees they suck. The reason I would recommend this game is for the second part, "Deep in Abyss." Its an original story by the author of the manga, and the game really opens up to allow tons of exploration and customization. Mind you, you will probably have to remap the controls to your liking, cause the default pc controls really aren't well planned out. Well, that, or get a controller.With all this being said, though I am having fun, and would recommend this game to anyone who is willing trudge through the first part, I can't excuse this price. I recommend to wait for some sort of discount. Only reason I got it at $60 was cause I wanted to support the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: Rough around the edges with many things feeling unfinished, but has a lot of good content and is very fun once you get into it.If you are a Made in Abyss fan, definitely try it out if you can spare the cost or it goes on saleOver 95% of the game occurs in the Deep in Abyss mode after the 5-6 hour Hello Abyss mode. It becomes a very different game after that with skill trees, quests, additional weapon types, clothing, relics, levelling and more. It took me 5 hours to clear Hello Abyss, and 60 hours to clear Deep in Abyss excluding most of the side quests.It was really fun to see familiar characters interacting with each other and doing quests for them. I loved to see new areas of the Abyss and learn about the creatures within, filling a bestiary with information on everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of awful in many ways, but I'm still having fun playing it.My biggest issue is how the curse doesn't really seem to matter that much, and you just avoid it pretty much entirely just by pausing every few seconds when ascending--I'd love to see a mod that tried to change that, but it might be challenge to do without redesigning a lot of the game...
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty jank and not worth full price unless you're a big fan of the IP.That said, once you get through the pretty awful and barebones tutorial mode 'Hello Abyss' (I just ran through the last quarter or so to get it over with, you don't need to gather/craft anything not required by the main quest) and reach the second mode, 'Deep In Abyss', it becomes far more fleshed out. It's clear that this mode is where 90% of dev consideration went.In this mode, the game gets a lot more open ended exploration wise, and the real game loop actually begins (explore, look for relics, craft/manage resources, track a path back to Orth, sell/appraise relics and level up, improve gear and repeat but getting a little deeper each run). The difficulty ramps up, and there is also a new story written by Tsukushi for this mode that is surprisingly compelling with several easter eggs and character interactions for the fans. There are still issues with this part of the game as mentioned in other reviews, like the spawn rate of trash mobs and the weight restriction, but these can and have been modded. Looking at the patch notes for Chime's other game on here I'm not holding my breath for an official fix.Overall I would say give this a chance on sale if you have a tolerance for jank, are an MiA superfan, or both, as there is a genuinely fun game here with some interesting mechanics I haven't seen anywhere else, that decently evokes the feeling of the anime. Piss meter restoration mod when?
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am really enjoying it. It does have a really slow start and long tutorial.. and there are definitely some QoL things I would change. I would definitely also change the spawn rates for enemies and how close they spawn to you. That is honestly probably the most annoying thing in the game. Other than that I would say this is mainly an exploration survival game, and its actually pretty hard once you get to Deep in Abyss mode. Lets of prep work to do before each dive into the abyss, because you really can easily become soft locked down there and have to start completely over if you stay down there too long and are not prepped to be down there that long. Once you get to layer 3 you really start feeling how open and big the game is. Slow start, and some weird design choices, dated but still surprisingly pretty graphics at some times. Over all its way better than I expected it to be. Lots of reviews judging it far too early. Also if you don't like games with a lot of gathering, crafting, and survival elements, you probably will not like this game. If you like the show then you know the Abyss is brutal, and they didn't change that here.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: It's really an excellent game. Makes you as if you're in Abyss. It's not an easy game and you may game over for multiple times, but it's really what'd happen in Abyss. I also like the story very much. Still in Tier 2, but looking forward to meeting to Riko later.  Another thing I enjoy is the detailed description of the ecology (and different items) in Abyss - it completes the anime and manga. People complain about how annoying part of the game is, but I'd say that's just small problems and the point is to enjoy the world of Abyss.
_childDocuments_.name: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness

_childDocuments_.review: I had bought this game day one and had done quite a bit in the couple of hours. The tutorial is around 3 hours long and that does end up putting people off but once that is done you get into the real meat of the game. It is amazing how it pulls you in and invokes you on exploring the abyss as we have always wanted from those who have watched the Anime. It does require some polish though and the AI is very aggressive but you can turn that into an advantage easily. I do recommend a sale but for someone like me who wanted to jump right in there. I can recommend this game!

The game isn't for everyone and I would recommend for a average person to get it on a discount but for a fan of the series it can be a treat.

This game is, in its current state, not worth $60. I will not be asking for a refund, as there is still more for me to do in the game; but if you are looking to buy this, wait for it to go on sale.Next, the """Tutorial,""" Hello Abyss. To me, I don't really see it necessary to go through the Anime's story. I'm not exactly against it in theory, but the way it was executed here is just... not the best. _childDocuments_.review: Lots of bugs and bad design choices can make this game incredibly frustrating. However. The sense of satisfaction from accomplishing a goal is very strong in this game.  Little touches, like the save function being an in-universe item (that doesn't function if you don't have a clear view of the sky) add to immersion.  The early sections of the Abyss with poor lighting and boring platform-hopping give way to some rewarding scenery as you get deeper.  The community for this game is one of the better ones I have ever seen, and the games first mod fixes the problems with endless spawning mooks.A lot of people have complained about how easy it is to get softlocked.  They are right, it is really easy to find yourself trapped with no choice but to give up and lose hours of progress.  Once you realize that is reality and start meticulously planning every piece of equipment you take on your dives, the game completely changes.  I genuinely have fun laying out all the salt, light hatchets, torches, and mountains of boiled eggs.  Setting a weight goal of my pack depending on where I am headed and what I plan to accomplish is completely engrossing.  Even with careful preparation, it is still entirely possible to get stuck so you never really relax.  As you get stronger whistles, you become able to fast travel out of earlier layers and that sense of danger is lessened.  I still kinda miss the terror of climbing out of layer 3 once the last of the salt is gone, hoping I have enough supplies to make it back and cringing as I discarded hard-earned relics to make a little more room in the pack.I don't know if this is what Tsukushi was thinking when he imagined the Abyss, but it sure does feel like I am lost in Uncle Lovecraft's Funtime Murder Hole.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Made in Abyss, its my all time favourite manga and anime. While this game is well made in some aspects like music and atmosphere. the game itself is not worth the triple A price. The graphics are mediocre at best and the recurring audio cues and voice lines from any partners you have (Reg, Nat etc) trigger every time you scavenge an animal or a plant which does get annoying. The game also does not help you much, I had to go into the control settings to figure out I had a headlamp to use. Please wait for this game to go on sale or have a reduced price if you really want to play it, it is not worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness is a great game that suffers from some very questionable design decisions and brutal difficulty – the „I want to waste your time” kind of difficulty, which will put off a lot of people. If you are not into that, you most probably won’t enjoy it. It’s not buggy nor glitchy, but it’s very unforgiving and may be downright unplayable without at least minor modding.The first big problem is the game mode selection, which sounds good at first because it makes it seem as if there is more content in the game. The reality is that the original story-based game mode is really a form of a tutorial for the main mode of the game. All shops, crafting and leveling are very limited, which you are not told. The real game gets unlocked after beating this 3-5 hour „intro” based on the original story. This also makes it seem as though the game is very short. The length of the main story is already listed as 4 hours on some websites, which is false, as this is not the real game mode but just a sneak peek into what’s to come.Once you get to the „Deep Abyss” mode, which is the actual true gameplay of Made in Abyss: Binary Star Falling into Darkness, is when things get real. The difficulty ramps up in a crazy way. Hp, food, stamina meters, bag capacity, limited fast travel, curse of abyss and worst of all: Infinite enemy spawning behind your back after 5 minutes of exploring will all be things that will accompany throughout the journey. Thankfully, there is a community made mod that removes the Infinite enemy spawning, which for me personally, was what made the game playable. If you’re planning to get the game please get it for your own mental health. The devs have posted that they are looking into bugs and game balance so maybe this gets fixed in the future by them, but we will have to wait and see.The gameplay loop itself can be fairly enjoyable. You set out to explore the abyss, each layer divided into multiple areas. You harvest supplies, kill enemies, navigate cliffs and so on. The game follows a main story quest and also offers a lot of side quests, both randomly appearing as well as available in the guild location in the city. Once you set aside the game’s issues it will be a great experience for any anime/manga fan for sure. In the game you can explore up to and including the 5th layer and meet many of the characters from the original story on your journey. Beating the whole game took me about 40 hours. Then there’s also a good couple hours of ‘endgame’ content, you can keep leveling, getting gear upgrades, and there are actual optional side quest lines including characters from the original story.All in all if you can get over the punishing difficulty there’s a lot of fun to be had here, especially for enjoyers of the original material. The general reception wasn’t that great so you can probably expect discounts soon. Get it then, if you’re on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: Very tentative recommend. I was going to recommend against this, but, I instead opted for a "yes". I have only gotten as far as beating the retelling of the anime, and I looked at it and said "is this it? this is meant to show off what the rest of the game is like?"After I beat it, I immediately jumped to the other mode to see. It has much more available...which I've yet to get to, and may change this review later but. The game clearly has much more available I've yet to try, and the tutorial (the OG anime story) made the worst of potential impressions for the rest of the available content.Otherwise, it's a fun game with a bit of repetition. I was able to go almost 5 hours through it nonstop.  I did experience a semi-soft lock toward the end where I didn't have any salt to make food with, and because travelling between two zones costs food...well, yeah. I'd run out of food, not be able to craft more, and be locked. So I had to go into Cheat Engine and edit my food value to 100. This was partially my own fault, 'cause I'd craft a lot of food and just keep eating it for fun (I was joking with friends while looking at the eating animation), and ate way more than I should've. Still, should've been opportunities later on to craft more food that wasn't egg and bug recipes (if RNG favored me)

_childDocuments_.review: You're initially made to play as Riko and set out to do bits and pieces of her 'story' if you could call it that. It's basically just an hour or so long tutorial without an actual tutorial.The actual 'game' starts after you finish that tutorial which so far? It's a bit of a mess, the curse system becomes a major pest  instead of a major mechanic of the game. Even traveling up small inclines would have your threshold fill up, or simply jumping in place like a gremlin which was funny at first.Just writing this down for friends and such. It has potential, but nothing a patch will fix at all. Probably would have been great if it was just all Riko and Reg with QTE's like Asura's Wrath at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Came back to change my review like I promised. The graphics are so bad I can't believe I don't get motion sickness from this. (From someone who puke after 30 minutes on minecraft.) The keyboard bindings are horrible, you can't change it to bind with mouse. I've had my left pinky on the ctrl for the entire time running. Z for targeting is basically useless to me, as you won't have a finger to press X for attacks while running on WASD and Ctrl. I've seen people mentioning the enemy spawn rates, sometimes they're helpful, but with the fast travel doesn't worth the two cents it implements. You can only fast travel to the start of each layer after you obtain a higher rank than your current depth, which doesn't make sense because you'll be doing tons of exploring in the new area and not the repetitive quests. It's not about making the game easy. Traveling back up to a certain location doesn't sound that illogical to implement. Imagine coming up and having to go down again to a point in-between, who does that?Games at this price should at least have 30hrs of play time full of content. The game makes up for this by its horrible amount of gathering quests to prolong the time you have to spend on this game. I don't even see an open world game this bad. The hello abyss mode was horribly executed, such that they only explain the tutorial to you in the second mode after you trial and error yourself what skills Riko already possessed. It's blatant. After you spend your three hours replaying a bad version of the anime getting amazed all your imagination in 3d only to find it stops at layer 3 you can't refund the game. Had I been able to see all their horrible quest system had to offer I would've stopped playing 30 minutes in.I'll add more but this doesn't worth 60 bucks. I've seen people say 30; I'd say 25 at most.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've gotten a chance to play the deep abyss mode my opinion has changed a lot from my first impressions on day 1. The hello abyss mode (story mode) really didn't put the games best foot forward and left me very disappointed. If there is a hack or something in the future that let's new players skip it I would recommend doing so and go right to the main game (deep abyss mode). I can't say much about the quality of the game mechanics and gameplay because I dont play rpgs and have never played a game like this before but I can say that I have been having fun with it so far. I know people have been upset with the graphics but I knew this game was coming out on switch so I didn't have high expectations in that department. When comparing the graphics to a switch game like pokemon legends arceus I think it holds up suitably. My advice for new players is to not play this game unless you have seen at least the first season of the anime. Even though the game trys to explain to you the story in hello abyss mode it does a horrible job and will spoil the beginning of what is an amazing show.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll leave this review short and sweet. This game is severely misunderstood. Frankly if you haven't made it past the admittedly obnoxious tutorial, you shouldn't be allowed to review.Here are my criticisms:Characters look fantastic*Some* locations look great.*Some* locations look like ass, aka they are out of a wii game.Tutorial is nonoptional and is around 2-3 hours, which is why this game got a surge of bad reviews on its release. Keybindings for controller on PC are strange, but you adapt. Curse mechanic is there which I understand is the series's staple, but I think it'll frustrate people new to MiA.After the tutorial the game is much more enjoyable with lots of creatures to see, characters to meet, and relics to find. I saw someone complained the character creator is limited but I thought it was okay. Its about the same as Animal Crossings. While the abyss may not be pure open world Skyrim experience you are looking for, it offers a sort of rogue-like Metroidvania experience that I personally find satisfying. You might find a special grotto, a rare relic/creature, etc!Overall, I think this is best for Made in Abyss fans. If you like the anime and can get past the tutorial, you will probably like this. Seeing the characters and creatures come to life is really cool, and exploring the abyss at your own pace is fun! Whether you decide to pay full price for it is up to you, but I think it's worth playing whether you decide to wait for a sale or not. Ps, The company that made this game said they won't be releasing DLC, I figured that's worth mentioning. I wouldn't be surprised if a mod or too comes out for the game though.

_childDocuments_.review: Take the Dive of Your Life! Made in Abyss, the breathtaking manga and anime series by Akihito Tsukushi, is getting its first ever video game adaptation! Experience the Anime's Story - The story begins with Riko and Reg's meeting in the first episode of season one. This marks the start of their great adventure, and together they travel to Seeker Camp in the second layer of the Abyss. Experience the awesome power of the Curse of the Abyss, as well as the astonishing, legendary entities known as primeval creatures. Prepare to glimpse the world of Riko and her friends. Experience a Brand-New Story - Another story takes place many days after Riko and Reg depart for the Abyss. The world’s sole remaining, unconquered chasm, the Abyss, is the stage where many adventures are born...and disappear. Those who appear in these stories are mesmerized by the power of the Abyss and aim for the bottom of the netherworld. The story about to be told is of the adventures of a nameless Cave Raider in the Abyss.

name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef
detailed_description: Join the Discord! About the Game Prepare to charge Luteus Prime For many centuries, the planet of Luteus Alpha has been producing much needed materiel for the wars raging on in the Armageddon sector. Many are drawn to the planet, and so is the great Warboss Ogruk Gutrekka. Upon arriving on the planet, Gutrekka took your most precious hair squig. Filled with vengeance you’ve sworn to do anything it takes to return your hair squig, and prove who is the strongest! And so your adventure on Luteus Prime begins. Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef is a hand-drawn 2D action adventure taking you on a wild ride of dakka, gore and explosions! Krump your way through the hive city of Luteus Prime; battle Humans, Orks and Genestealer cultists; and ultimately retrieve your luscious hair squig from the hands of the Warboss Gutrekka! Who’s ready for Waaagh!? Game Features: Classic 2D side-scrolling goodness, filled with intense action, funny one-liners, screaming deaths and comical dialogues! Choose your class, picking between four distinct characters, each with their own unique toolkit true to the Warhammer 40,000 lore. Inflict chaos with an arsenal of weapons at your fingertips. Expand your armory with up to twenty different weapons. There’s no such thing as having too much dakka! Unleash your Waaagh! at the right time! Wreak carnage and rain destruction on those puny ‘umies. Challenge the mightiest empire in the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Become victorious, bring the planet to its knees and lead your very own Waaagh! Earn hats by destroying compelling bosses, completing milestones or exchanging Teef at the Mekboy shop. Teef are collected by tearing through the story. Beautiful hand-drawn scenery gives an incredible sense of depth to a side-on world. Break up the action, and immerse yourselves in engaging cinematics. Set foot on Luteus Prime in single-player mode, or get a party together of up to four Ork Boyz and have some fun together! Multiplayer is available both online and in local co-op. Brawl it out against your rivals in an all-out epic battle to decide who is the baddest Ork in the warband! Up to four boyz can scrap it out in the arena, both online and in local PvP. Get your socks rocked off with an amazing heavy metal soundtrack, composed by Deon van Heerden. Yes, there will be explosions. Like, a lot of them!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very short for its price, and while it can be described as a 'good' time rather than a long time, it is still very overpriced. Even farming kills in multiplayer for the last achievement only took me about five hours; the campaign was 2.5 hours on the hardest mode. I think for the price, it should have more content. That being said, it is very true to the lore in the 40k universe and one of the few games that accurately portrays 'Orkiness'. The soundtrack is one of the best I have ever heard in a 40k game, so that is well done too. There are still crashes; in my five hours, the game got locked twice, and it quit with an error in multiplayer once. This game still needs more patches. I hope the devs fix it soon.Overall, good to pick up to kill a few hours minus the bugs for a rip-roaring good time. But it ends too quickly. Pick it up on sale if you want it, not for full price. I give it a 7 out of 10 until the bugs are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: I'z reallly torn on dis. On da one 'and I'z zoggin grate dat wez gots a proppa game, da humor iz grate, da muzac is great and iz fun. On da uva da classes lack diversity with the storm boy and beast snagga being the two most different with the storm boy having a jetpack that can light enemies on fire and lets you evade over a longer distance while the beast snagga has a throwable explosive melee and an attack squig bomb. The Weirdboy and Flashgit don't really have anything going for them. Some of the guns are fun, the laser shotgun especially since it can fill up the entire screen with lasers, the flamer feels nice, but over all most of the guns lack punch and feel like someone tried too hard to balance them so they end up kinda weak. I feel like this game could benefit greatly from a level up system and adding more variety to the classes. The game is fairly short, which isn't bad since it's a fun little story, but I also crashed multiple times during it. I guess I'll recommend it since it would probably be a lot more fun with friends and because I feel like it's so close to being a fantastic game like castle crashers but its just missing something.Now I'm just going to kinda list some ideas I had playing that I feel might help.As I said before some sort of level up system so that as we progress we can feel ourselves getting more powerful and rather than just picking up boxes of teeth having enemies drop them.What I would really love to see is mixing up the ults so that the classes feel more unique, like having the weirdboy do some psychic nonsense, the beast snagga goes berserk increasing melee damage and attack speed, the storm boy jets around and the flashgit can keep the unlimited ammo. Just some ideas

_childDocuments_.review: I love Warhammer 40k and fantasy and I love how fun this game can be; however, a game that is only 3-4 hours long (story) with frequent bugs and crashes along with a multiplayer that is even buggier with more crashes is simply not worth $20. _childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to recommend this, it's just not worth it at the moment. I beat the story mode on normal in 2.5 hours,  which isn't worth the $20 price tag imo. I hope they keep working on this, it's just a slice away from greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: People who view any game purely in a dollars to hours ratio are dooming themselves to picking up dinosaur ♥♥♥♥♥ forever.  Me, for the price of purchase, I got an absolutely brilliant soundtrack. That soundtrack also came with a fun game, by coincidence, and that game came with a hit of nostalgia for Flash and the old websites that hosted Flash games.  RIP in peace, Flash.But this is a game site.  So let me tell you about it.  You want an executive summary?  Platforming combat.  Really combat, with a side order of some platforms, but there's no tricky jumps to make.  You're an Ork. You don't do jumping puzzles.  You shoot things.  Dakka is the solution to every problem.I say it's like Flash because every character has this chunky kind of animation that looks like several discrete pieces are rotated, but nothing is ever really deformed.  Flash did a lot of that.  Here's an arm piece, there's a head, maybe two torso pieces, and you rotate them around to make it look animated.  And, usually, the animations are really overdone.  This is no exception.  It's the flashiest flash animation since a site that sounded like "congregate" but with a K.In the Warhammer 40k universe, well, most everything is dour.  Really, every last faction except the death-killer "undead" robots... and the orks.  The orks are ramshackle, live only for fighting, and they'll fight each other if there's nobody else to fight.  Nothing else enters into the equation. And then they talk in goofy but gruff cockney-esque voices and... honestly, I could go on, but it's enough to say they're an entertaining faction, a rare bright light in a world full of soggy concrete hallways and for-the-emperors, and I had my fill of that a long time ago.Is this a short game?  By the time I wrote the review, I'd completed it.  I enjoyed it, I grinned like an idiot at a few of the cutscenes, I shot a lot of boyz, beakies and other assorted oomies, plus a couple spiky boys and extra-armed oomies.  I'm quite satisfied.  I could do the PvP mode but likely never will, and the odds of me replaying this in coop are vanishingly small.And I don't mind one bit.  Like I said, the purchase price was the soundtrack.  The game, for me, was the extra.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game from a really good creator. If you've played Guns, Gore and Cannoli you just need to know this game is that same dose of goodness except in 40k flavor.For those of you who haven't known fun yet i can describe the game as thus;you're an ork thats obvious, the gameplay is pretty straightforward which is good because as an ork you are pretty damn stupid.There are several weapon categories to choose from and you can carry 1 of each type furthermore you can choose between 4 versions of each said weapon each one with different effects, some minor some major.You also get some bare bones class options as you can play as 1 of several types of character.These different characters only get a few minor differences between each other. Namely grenade type and melee weapon, despite how different the skin of each class might make you look its sad that you only get these minor changes between them.Now while your ork is great and all and has his own fun personality you get to ride along with its the enemies that really steal the show with their variety and designs. If you're a fan of 40k you'll be able to easily recognize not only each faction but each unit type even, the fact that i can pick out each type of proper unit  easily is testament to how good the art design for this game was, there was some real love put in here.Sound track is nothing but constant bangers with fantastic heavy metal tracks pushing you through each combat, one might wonder what kind of music plays during down time but thats irrelevant as downtime is NOT orky and therefore not worth even considering.The cutscenes (which are unfortunately pre rendered) are really fun and well animated. This team has come a long way from the GG&C's stiff newgrounds tier animations. The entire adventure feels like a fever dream told to you by a drunk ork in some dive bar. Its constantly over the top but not in a way that ever yanks you out of the game.I've had some crashing issues with the game but hopefully these will be addressed soon.I had lots of fun, its worth getting for the simple asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're in need of not just a game to play with friends but an actually good one too, look no further than:WGGHH!!!!While some might complain it's short, just like I tell my girlfriend, it's not the size that matters, it's how much fun 1-4 people can have with it that matters. A huge benefit of the size of this game is the fact that you get to try out new weapons against fellow orcs, chad space marines, and mechs at a fast rate before you can get bored. That’s when the final boss shows up and feels lackluster compared to earlier ones, a classic example of bigger doesn't always mean better, I'm talking about boss size here. Speaking of killing, you can friendly fire, which is a way for a co-op game to be in the upper echelon of amazing co-op games, so I would highly recommend it if you have these things called human friends. There's even a combo for co-op play: where one shocks and stuns with an AOE lightning gun, and the other chainsaws freely without risk of dying unless they are immune to stun, which I “never” experienced. Unlike lazy games, here modifying your weapon changes how it functions, not small percentages. Your shotgun can be turned into basically a flamethrower, a laser scattershot bouncing off walls thing, or a beefy big quad shotgun that takes forever to reload. Each variant of pistol, rifle, or rocket has a use case, so try them all out. My personal favorite weapon is called a “deathbeam”. Apparently, the game and its bosses are lore accurate or so I'm told by my Warhammer friend that gifted me this game trying to convince me Warhammer is amazing. I'm not sold yet, but this game is on the right track and is easily approachable to anyone not aware of the universe. It's more humorous than other ones I've played and the story is simple. The orc boss steals your cool hairpiece, you need to retrieve it. If you’re not convinced this short cheap game is worth getting, there is that short highlight video posted above that also showcases how metal the soundtrack gets at times. Also, there are specials from classes you choose at the start of each level and the one I picked happened to be more deadly against us than our enemies, so I don’t want to talk about it, I’m not mad, just embarrassed.

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence on whether to give this a thumbs up or down, but will ultimately give it a thumbs up for just the sheer love and passion these devs have given to the orks. If you are a ork fan, this is a must buy. If you are a warhammer fan, this is on the upper scale for warhammer games and has some great fan service you'll likely enjoy. If you are just a regular gamer looking for a fun "castle crashers but with guns" type coop experience, then you'll probably like this game too as the gameplay is really fun, boss fights are intense, and the music is top tier. However, I have some warnings. First, the game can be pretty buggy (especially for coop). Between playing this with both my friends, we had disconnections,dying as we killed the boss caused the game crash, people failing to spawn, and one instance where a leman russ boss disappeared half way through it's boss fight. It's not down right enough to kill me loving the game, but it is common enough to be annoying. Second warning I gotta give is this game is SHORT. You probably can finish it within 2-4 hours, and while you can find teef to buy new weapons and hats, you'll probably get most of what you want in your first playthrough. I admittably haven't tried the verse mode yet so that might add some more value, but I still debate if this would be worth $20 (though these days video game skins are worth $20 so I guess there are still worst ways to waste $20). My recommendation would be wait for a sale and see if any friends would like to play it with you. Then you can do a single and coop playthrough. Despite it's issues, this game was a nice short, but really fun and funny experience. It's just got too much charm and WAAAAGH for me to hate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong this game is amazing! Satisfying gameplay, excellent voice acting, a simple story to follow, and amazing soundtracks (Same guy who also composes Broforce apparently). This is entirely perfect for an Ork game. That being said however I wouldn't recommend this game for the reason that it's just too short.You can beat the game's story in just about 2-3 hours, even on the highest difficulty. After that, there's not much you can do other than multiplayer. Sure you can go and find all the secrets in the game, unlock every cosmetic or achievement, or play on a higher difficulty......Which is essentially playing the game's story again. Overall, Gameplay, voice acting, levels, and soundtracks are great! But content-wise, It's too short of an experience to justify its price. I would recommend this game however if this were to receive some more content or DLC (I doubt that would happen anytime soon.) or if you find this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop is basically running around shootin' or krumpin' things with yer mates, and pretty much flying though the who's who of the 40k universe. The action is exceptionally smooth, and the gunplay is lots of fun. Often times you find yourself beaming a big ole smile (like your Ork) as you mow down wave after wave of enemy.The weapon choices are exciting, each costing a fair investment of teef, and dramatically changing how you approach encounters. I enjoyed trying different weapons, seeing what worked and just generally switching between them to be the most annoying ork possible. Not sure which was my fac , but it kept the loop engaging, and made it fun to stay at it, even for a couple of hours at one sitting.The game's pacing is fairly fast, and while it never gets truly adrenaline-pumping, it's engaging and there's always a squig to find, humie to krump or shootin' to be done. On to the negatives (boy, there are more of these than I'd realized)- - I realize this game has just released, but I've had persistent issues with restarting from checkpoints whenever the entire team goes down. The loading screen does show up, but the bar tends to get stuck at about 70%.- There are also times when moving pieces of the level (trains, conveyor belts etc) are in different places for different players. This makes it difficult to keep your dakka in one place, and in tougher sections could even get you kilt.- The classes fail to distinguish themselves throughout the entire length of my game with my friends. There were certain sections where we even tried to deliberately play into the roles to get that synergy out of them , but it was almost always better to just improve movement and learn boss patterns.- The objectives at certain parts are poorly signposted, we often spent a few moments at the ends of each level wondering what to do, only to realize that the entire party needed to go to the far right, or needed to group up in a chamber or on a lift.- One slightly more thorny issue is that imo the campaign mode doesn't fit the price tag (and I blame GW's licensing cut). There's maybe 3 hours of good waagh to be had, and without any further fun game modes or story to play through, the player experience just ends right there.- Finally, there was an odd bug we had with one of the players on our team (who picked Evil Sunz) who just straight was invisible to us for most of the playthrough. It was incredibly hard keeping track of where he was, and without discord to help, we'd have spent hours trying to group up in the right places to progress the level.Overall, I'd give it about 7/10, fun, cute, and a great introduction to 40k through the eyes of the best faction (fight me), but ultimately lacking the oomph to follow through.

_childDocuments_.review: "Shootas, Blood & Teef" is the beautiful lovechild of "Doom (2016)" and "Scribblenauts" with a deep affection for "Warhammer 40,000's" rambunctious, heavy-metal enthusiast Orks, and it's fantastic. The art style is adorable, the gameplay is fast-paced and engaging, and it has a simplistic fun factor to it that really makes it shine.  I would highly recommend "Shootas, Blood & Teef" to anyone with a place in their heart for goofy, fun loving Orks and classic two-dimensional "Run and Gun" shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef is an enjoyable and entertaining game, especially due to the delightful Ork humor that permeates the experience. The gameplay itself is decent. However, the game does fall a bit short in terms of length. After my first playthrough, I completed it in about 3-4 hours. Extending the gameplay by an additional 2-4 hours would have made for a more fulfilling experience.One notable issue is the game's tendency to crash, particularly during boss fights. Given the game's relatively short length and the fact that it is 2D, these crashes become more frustrating. Despite this, most of the boss fights are well-designed and some are exceptionally amusing. Unfortunately, the final boss does not live up to expectations, proving to be extremely easy and somewhat anticlimactic.

_childDocuments_.review: After Guns, Gore & Cannoli 2, I was looking forward to this game more than almost any AAA title in recent memory.However... Everything is worse, and I mean everything.Movement: You don't move as fluidly in this game, the double jump is lower, and the dash doesn't seem to have any real benefit while in a combat arena aside from getting away from groups of enemies, whereas in GGC2 it was integral to reach different platforms.Weapons: You hold 1 pistol, 1 machinegun, 1 shotgun, 1 rocket/grenade launcher, and presumably another couple of types. While it seems like you would want to be switching depending on the situation, it's more likely you'll find a variant you prefer for handling the stages, and then switch to an appropriate one when coming across the boss challenges. They all have infinite ammo, which seems fun until you see what effect that has on choice and game balance; gone are the decisions you'd make between squeezing the last few rounds out of your favorite weapon or holding onto the ammo for a tougher encounter.Art direction: Everything is shades of brown, grey, black, and yellow. The lack of detail in anything, including character models, but especially the foreground, makes moving through the world incredibly boring. You'll see the same graffiti a half dozen times in the first hour of playing the game on the same surfaces and wonder what the artists spent their time on.Sound: The MC doesn't say much, and what he does say is repeated far too many times to be interesting to hear. Vinny from GGC was a stereotype done right, with interesting and funny things to say which don't boil down to only being angry and saying waagh. Also the sound effects for guns and things getting hit are soft, no impact. And the music is barely there, a droning bass that doesn't really go anywhere. Where is the rock? The drums? The metal?Story: Orks are dumb and the story is silly, which is 100% totally fine. What isn't fine is how redundant the events are. An ok intro to the story leads to a lot of WAAAGH and nothing else, and you'd expect something else, anything else.Enemies: They still run at you, and the still shoot at you, and they still die and lose heads and explode, but for some reason it's not as satisfying. Also, their bullets travel extremely fast, too fast for your eyes to sometimes tell in between the zoomed-in action and samey backgrounds.Level design: GGC2 had so much detail and inspiration in the levels and their design in concert with the weapons and enemy placement that Shootas just can't reach. Compare the first levels of both games back to back; one filled with verticality, introduction to your main abilities, and weapons, and see for yourself just how much was lost here. I don't understand how you could go from a city with awnings, which let you enter a building from multiple floors, and snipers to some boxes with a single snipers above some "spawnboxes" of enemies and not tell you are doing something wrong. In fact in the first level there are engines dangling above enemies, but you cannot shoot them down; there doesn't appear to be any stage interaction aside from exploding barrels and ripping a dozen-shot heavy gun from its mount.After Guns, Gore, & Cannoli 2, I expected better, but what I got was much, much worse.If you loved GGC2, do yourself a favor and pass on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Shootas, Blood, & Teef is a nice short game where you play as the only race that's having fun in this universe the orks. The story is simple, you want your wig back from the guy who shoved you out of a plane, along the way you'll kill the imperial guard, gene stealer cultist/tyranids, the baby crocodile you flushed when you were 6, space marines, and orks who look at you funny.The gameplay is 2d platform shooter, and your given the 20 guns to do it and 4 dinstinct...ish(I'll talk about them soon.) classes to kill anything to get your wig back and be da boss. The game can be beaten in about 4-5 hours (3 i your just stupid good), but it's got some fun replay value if you wanna kill an afternoon. While this game can be played with friends it isn't required to have a fun time.Now some flaws with the game, other than it's short run time, but (I want more) isn't really a flaw. I just lied to you, 20 dollas is a lot for 4-5 hours if you don't feel like replaying it. The classes are also a mixed bag. The, Flash Git, Storm Boy, Weird Boy, and Beast Snagga all use the same guns with grenades and melee being different. Now those grenades can make the difference since the weird boy's can stun, and melee isn't really encourage except for the beast snagga because it isn't a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ melee it's a spear that explodes you throw(and it's good). The flash git also sometimes doesn't use ammo when he shoots and uses molotovs. You will notice a difference when you play a campaign with one and switch9I beat the game with flash git and wondered why it felt i reloded more as a beast snagga before i realized), but they still feel a little samey since they all use the same guns.Said guns can sound a little weak other than the shotgun, but they get the job done and the music should be blaring loud enough you won't mind hearing it more than your guns. The only real downside is the short time and class semi-diversty in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: A short, fun action filled run n' gun that can be appreaciated by fans and outsiders of the Warhammer community.My review to Shootas, Blood & Teef after 60 hours of playtime: Story: It's obvious that the story is more of an afterthought than the focus, but it works lorewise, because player with no knowledge of the 40k universe find themself in Teefgrabba who cares only about fighting and his mcguf... aem I mean hairsquigg and 40k nutters can enjoy all the easter eggs and inside jokes. Powerscaling is completly off though. Yes, in a book some Orks and a buggy killed a Titan, but they didn't just shoot it until it dies, meanwhile a single Ork in this games mows down Tanks, Knights and White Scars like nothing. I feel like we give it a pass just because it's "whacky Ork game" which brings me  to Asthetics: The cartoony artstyle can be called...controversial when the first trailers dropped. But from Hammer and Bolter to the 40k mobile games I'd say it's not the worst. It definitly helps that we play as the comic relief faction that allows a lighter style in the grimdark of the far future to work. I personally call it the "pyrovision" effect, where a brutal and violent world is shown cute and funny through the eyes an inhuman character. But outside of 40k compatibility it's a solid and strong art direction. Especially the Knight, good work converting this overdetailed monstrosity while still being able to see it as such. It's going to age like fine whine the coming years and will keep its character. I only have a few nitpicks with scaling, f.ex. how big a regular guardsmen is compared to Teefgrabba. Now finally to what we came for: Gameplay: Not many have played Roguesides other games, but I did so let me tell the following: This game feels like Guns, Gore & Cannoli 3. A lot of enemies, obstacles and set pieces have been slightly altered and been used from Guns, Gore & Cannoli 2 and implemented, which isn't inherently bad. They fixed a lot of issues I had with this game, f.ex. the lack of weapon feedback and the sheer amount of superfluous weapons ,like 4 automatic weapons that all feel the same and just overcomplicate the weapon wheel.The weapons in Blood & Teef feel amazing. The sound, the kickback, the enemies reaction, way better than the Cannoli 2 roster who all felt like the tanks of Wii play. The change to from 10+ weapons to 5 weapon slots with 4 options each was a great change to make the combat flow more smoothly.

_childDocuments_.review: This is almost a good game. The animations are basically Flash from the early 2000's, but whoever set that up really enjoyed making the cartoony look. The music's annoying Metal more often than not, and I turned it off.The problem, as with so many games like this, is all the little stuff.1. Control loop feels mushy and unresponsive. It's like the controls are polled only once every quarter-second or something. It's hard to do a double-jump sometimes, and as that's integral to gameplay, well.2. Gunplay isn't very good. The problem here is that I think they balanced the weapons for multiplayer, which does not work out for singleplayer, at all. There are weapons that just feel useless, like the saw- its damage output and hitbox are both tiny and wrong. There are weapons that feel like they were nerfed into oblivion because they worked too well in four-player free-for-all, like the Zzap Cannon- it's useless for SP. There are weapons where I'm really not sure why they were allowed to suck, like the Deth Beam and the Squig Launcher, the Sticky Rokits, the Quad Shotgun, etc. These all feel like things where nobody tested the feel in single-player properly before release. Very few of the weapons you buy feel like genuine upgrades, other than the totally-broken Guided Missile that allows you to clear whole sections by shooting off-screen. It's like, in a game that's basically supposed to be silly good fun, the developers just kind of forgot that balance in a SP title isn't really all that important, beyond making the player feel challenged. There were spots that weren't terrible, in terms of boss fights and arena challenges, but if the weapons had had more crazy, punch and silly side effects, this could've been so much more than it was. The AI's pretty bad, but it's largely OK, because there are plenty of enemies to kill. The game relies on numbers and bullet sponge enemies for the most part, and they gradually get harder and harder, while also showing up in huge numbers. The final boss fight is kind of a joke, but it's fine, at that point I just wanted to be done.3. Level design, visually, is OK. I'd say that enemies blend into the world a bit too well for this style of game, but overall, it's fine. The art's great in places, copy-pasta in others. Some of the areas feel really well-designed, but quite a few feel like somebody was rushing to meet deadlines.4. The sound design, with the music off, is barely passable.5. There's a Dash that's 99% useless. I don't know why it's even in the game design.6. The boss designs range from meh to excellent. However, they tend to have too many fights where you grind a shield or spend the whole time jumping and dodging while your guided missiles sloooooowly kill the enemy. Other than the final fight, there aren't clever weak-spot mechanics or other things that keep something like this entertaining.7. There are a few really interesting enemy mechanics, like an Ogryn with a shield, that never get used again. 8. The game's terribly prone to crashing at the oddest times. I'm pretty sure it's a memory leak or malloc, because it often happened during boss fights, cutscenes or when switching levels. However, the developers didn't leave any crash-reporting in the build, so it's a silent crash-to-desktop with zero explanation.9. I haven't played it multiplayer, and honestly, after seeing the weapons mix, have no desire to. It's not tight enough, and the controls would be a serious problem, even if the weapon balance is right. My theory remains that they made the classic mistake of balancing it for MP, and that's why SP feels so bad... when practically everybody who buys this will play it SP. Ah well.Overall? This could have been better than "ok, I guess". For the asking price, it's not, even though I got it on sale. Dear developers, instead of quietly abandoning this to go work on something else, come back, do a polish pass on the balance and feel of SP so that Easy is punchy, responsive, fast-paced and fun, Normal is a bit tricky and Hard is moderately brutal in places. As things stand, I had zero desire to play this on Hard or play it past seeing the end, because I'm guessing that enemies get 200% base health and do twice as much damage, which will make all the weapons that already felt weak and boring feel even worse. Since there isn't a level editor and there's no way to mod it, it's a dead-end title for me.This is a game that could've been fixed up mainly with tuning- everything from how quickly the control state polls to how the weapons feel. There were so many things that felt like wasted opportunities, like the Squig Mines that felt powerful-ish, but were so awkward to use that they needed to be much better to feel right.At any rate, this isn't the worst thing I've ever played. It's just so much more meh than it deserved to be, and it was entirely fixable. Disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing pretty regular crashes on Linux under Proton, just like the native Windows users. Besides that, the gunplay just doesn't have the impact to match the otherwise gorgeous art. Both the player character and enemies are pretty spongy and there's no real sense that anyone's scored a hit. Even the rocket launcher is disappointing. See Streets of Rogue, Nuclear Throne, or Enter the Gungeon for how to make a rocket launcher feel powerful in 2D. For a game that focuses on shooting, having anemic shooting is a pretty serious flaw.Besides this, there are some frustrating bits of bad design: often in a level I have to hold a button or key to activate something. This takes me out of the shooter trance just like the timing-based platforming sections in 2D Sonic games take me out of the speed trance those games are known for.This is so disappointing because I desperately want to love this game. The aesthetic is absolutely on point, and I found myself chuckling pretty regularly while playing. The background art, the incidental voice barks, all of it really sells the Warhammer feel. It's a shame that everything else feels, well, like I'm playing with some cheap, hollow plastic figures and environments. If this game was a series of action figures, I'd be quite upset to receive them as a Christmas present.

_childDocuments_.review: Shootas, Blood and Teef came out of nowhere as a game. Me and my friend were amazed with how charming and fun the game was. It had a surprising variety of weapons in it and an ASTONISHING amount of enemy variety, like: Guardsmen, Commanders, Commissars, Scions, Ogryn, Grots, Orks, Nobs, Killacans, Sewer monsters, cultists, genestealers, space marines and more! There's a lot of cool references in the game that are a delight to see.The story is pretty simple and short, but it was still good fun. Took about 2 hours to beat with a friend.In terms of difficulty, it's not that hard. Has some moments that might be tense, but it should be manageable.Had some crashes, but they weren't too problematic on my end.For achievement hunters: very easy completion. There are some are some really useful guides in the community tab if you need help with it. Took about 7 hours to 100%.8/10, would love to see more like this in the future!

The reason the trailers jump around so much is to hide how poorly this plays minute to minute.  This feels like a fan enjoyed sketching cartoon orcs, and was shown that you can use a stock game engine to rig them and get them to move.  Avoid it, even in a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives: Great soundtrack that keeps you going during action scenes and when it tones down during inaction it keeps you on edge. _childDocuments_.review: As a long time 40k fan I can say that the story of this game is exactly what I wanted from an Ork-based shooter. Your boss stole your hair, so you gotta murder everything until you get it back.The gameplay though is atrocious. Firstly having more dakka is not enough, you have to manage constantly switching weapons to deal with specific enemies (which is inherently anti-ork). You'll want to ensure you've practised quick switching from explosive, to projectile, to energy weapons as you'll need to do it a lot.Secondly the platforming is extremely slow. You're not incentivised to move quickly and rip and tear like you would expect, instead you have to advance, wait for set pieces, hunt for teef (which is infuriating as it's the only way to get unlocks because apparently killing a baneblade isn't valuable somehow), and then slowly but surely move through a level. This is made so much worse by the multiplayer input lag. You're expected to react to timing windows which are always out of sync if you're not the host.Thirdly there's no real melee options. We're Orks! All the artwork in the game shows choppas, but your piddly little melee weapons barely tickle enemies. Where's the melee classes?! If they come later in the game I'll be disappointed as they should be in from the get go given by default most Orks use their sluggas to get close enough to krump.Lastly the class and clan system is pointless. The variety between each class is so minimal as to not really be relevant to the average gamer, and selecting a clan offers no real bonus other than looking different which is incredibly disappointing.As a final note: the best way I can describe this game is that it feels like a generic, poorly-designed, lacklustre shooter platformer that was bought out and had 40k material taped onto it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I had fun with the campaign mode, and loved the Ork flavour of this title, the campaign's length (beat in about 3 hours of casually playing) and gripes with controls make me not recommend this game at its current price (10% off). The movement isn't great, guns feel weak after the opening minutes of the game, you can't hold down the firing key and keep shooting after reloading, the burna weapon tree doesn't inform you about their overheat mechanic, and the enemy types aren't that varied. Some later combinations of heavy enemies are harder than boss battles to deal with. Default controller bindings are rather odd as well (namely jump being LT on XBox controller).Despite all that, it's still a fun time, but not for full price.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 Preheat the oven:Place rack in the middle and preheat the oven to 400°F.2 Assemble the pie filling:In a large bowl, gently combine the rhubarb and the strawberries with the sugar, tapioca, salt, and orange zest. Let sit for 10 minutes.3 Roll out the bottom crust and fill the pie:Roll out one disc of pastry dough and line the bottom of a pie dish with it. Trim to 1/2 inch from the edge. Transfer the filling into the crust and spread out evenly.4 Roll out the second disc of pastry dough and place over the pie. Trim the edges to an inch from the edge of the pie dish. Tuck the top crust edges over the bottom crust edges and use your fingers or a fork to crimp the top and bottom edges together. Cut slits in the top for the steam to escape.(If you want, for a nice glaze on your pie, use a pastry brush to brush a thin layer of egg white or cream over the top of the pie.)5 Bake the pie:Place pie on the middle rack of the 400°F oven with a baking sheet on a lower rack to catch any juices that might spill over.Bake for 20 minutes at 400°F, then reduce heat to 350°F and bake an additional 40-50 minutes longer (50 to 60 minutes longer if doing a 10-inch pie). The pie is done when the crust is nicely browned and the filling (that you can see through the venting holes) thick and bubbly.6 Cool and serve:Remove from oven and let cool on a rack.Serve warm or cold. If you do cool to room temperature, the juices will have more time to thicken. Pie can also be covered and stored at room temperature for up to 2 days or refrigerated for 5 days.
