_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game ever since I first heard of it. Playing a WH40k game starring as one of the not so usual Orks seemed real fun to me and the Demo showed, that they encapsulated the Ork-Feeling quite well. Now that the game is released, it feels a little unfinished to me and so I am disappointed. Of course, you can not demand an overwhelming amount of game time and deepness of a 2D-side-scrolling shooter, but completing the campaign in 3 hours total game time is a little too less for the price.On top of that, there are still several annoying bugs in the game, ranging from regular crashing the game, to checkpoints not correctly saving your progress and enemies that behave wired and are thus easy to fight. This seems to be the case in some levels more than others, leading to the final boss beeing waaaaay to easy to beat, even on the hardest difficulty, especially compared to other bosses in the game.Overall it is a good, but still unfinished product that I'd not recommend getting into at the moment, until they did fix some of these issues or the price has been lowered.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very ok.  The biggest disappointment for me is the lack of upgrades or progression. This is simply a linear game with not much to do after you beat it. I've unlocked all the weapons and tried them out and there is only one that I will use. Most of the others either pale in comparison to the one, or they are just unusable because of the spread (or lack of range). Literally one gun that was "good". Everything else to unlock is just cosmetic, IE, hats. Just not enough, and the hats do no boosts, or anything. The gameplay is fun for the most part. I found the bosses irritating because it is just a pattern over and over again and they have too much health. Very bullet spongy.  In between that was fun.  The game allows you to carry 5 different weapons, but switching to them on the fly isn't really an option. You are forced to use a weapon wheel or click the appropriate button but I haven't played enough to even know which weapon type is in which key slot.  The game doesn't freeze when you use the weapon wheel (tab, and it opens if you just click it once, it isn't a hold situation) so it doesn't really allow you to switch to an appropriate weapon based on the enemy. It crashed once for me, and booted me out of another game (both offline). Was surprised that there wasn't more to the game, but I should know better being that it is warhammer.  Glad I got it over half off.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game through on normal. I waited until it was discounted during the skulls event, I'm glad I did so. The game play lacks, no weapon upgrades, no continuous game play, and no one is on the multiplayer servers anymore. If this game was 2-5 dollars or if they added more content maybe I'd re visit this review. I would like to try the multiplayer, but it's impossible to do so without friends playing. I wanted to recommend this to a friend so we could play, but I'm not. There's not enough re-play content to ask someone to spend money on it. On a good note, I feel like there is a lot of potential for this game, and hopefully the developers go through and tune it up a bit. I do love the animation and the overall feel to it, the sound track is amazing, and I feel like it does capture the Orks very well.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give a decent Warhammer game a negative review seeing as there's a metric TON of trash ones, but sadly this game just isn't for me.I'll leave this disclaimer: If all you're looking for is a game where you can roleplay an Ork dakka-ing humans mindlessly all day, this is the game for you and you'll love it. For me though, and in 2022 the era of progression gaming, I need more. I want to customize my Warboss's mech suit. I want to choose the territory I go into, with pros/cons and rewards/negatives for each territory I invade. I want to customize my guns and unlock new parts for them. I want to customize my ammo. Hell, I want to customize my ork!There *is* a VERY limited progression system in this game. In the time I played (50 minutes) I had unlocked the ***entire*** progression system. Woo. So after this all I had to look forward to was grinding humies into paste endlessly over and over. For some, that will be enough. For others that want progression, customization etc it will not be enough. I am of the latter category.All this being said, I wish there was a "neutral" option instead of yes/no on Steam. The game itself plays flawlessly and it's actually a decent Warhammer game. But the lack of strong progression kills it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like it should be loads of fun, but its not! The style design and animation are great. the voices are amusing and the music is good.having been a 40k ork player for decades I love the look of the game and i really want to like it.......but the gameplay is rubbish! its extremely annoying, and there is NO satisfaction from playing it. you play it for a bit and just end up irritated.The controls are really awkward. its a keyboard controlled platform game....that uses the mouse for facing and aiming.  You battle through difficult sections to get to flashing loot boxes... that you cannot collect. if there was no reward it wouldn't be as bad, but there's a reward sitting right in front of you and you are actively denied access to it! the platformer game type is annoying enough, but this constant loot taunting makes you hate it. You get dropped into boss and minboss rooms, with nowhere to go, so they just straight up kill you.The weapons look cool, but are rubbish and the upgrades make them worse or completely useless. There is no explanation of how the weapons work but it seems like most enemies are immune to at least one of the guns, at random, there is no indication which and its awkward to switch between them. so its just a case of "this gun doesn't seem to work because I'm dead." and, as if that wasn't bad enough, you can kill yourself by firing your own guns at the enemy!!its just rubbish, don't waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great short game.You can really tell a lot of nerdy love and care went into these designs of the characters and backgrounds, going so far as to directly reference the actual sets that you can buy with all the weapons, characters, enemies, its a very nice touch. Shame that the Mek workshop, although accessible throughout the game at every checkpoint, shows up once? I guess we just carry that thing on our back the whole time.The game play is good, and its fantastic that it has the option for four-player local co-op. Although I played it alone, I imagine it would be way more frantic with more people. But I have a real bone to pick with the designer of the achievements, for gods sake (although I guess Gork/Mork's sake would be more fitting) stop adding "challenges" that are just kill x enemy 1000 times! Nobody enjoys that! And designers please stop adding sewer levels into your game, nobody cares if it's thematic, just skip it and get to the cool set piece we know your teasing already, fans know whats coming (as you're not too subtle with your symbolism) and others are just bored trudging through killing just straight up rats. Padding is padding and this would be a much better overall experience without it.The weapon selection is fine if exactly what you expect, although a certain weapon trivialises most boss encounters it's cool and dangerous to use so i'll give it a pass, it is great that there is no out of place rpg mechanics strapped in, and you're as powerful when you start as when you end, just with more weapon selection. Trying the weapons out is a fun experience.Overall, I'm pretty sure that even if I wasn't nerding out over all the references it is a silly good time through and through. I would recommend, 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright.The game crashed on me one time on my playthrough, and it takes a while to load at the start, but other than that it runs well... just don't expect it to run in ancient laptop though, the game is a heck of a lot more demanding than it looks.As for the story? You play as an orc that gets bullied by another orc, he even rips your hair at the beginning, and that jumpstarts the whole quest of getting your hair back. Then nothing much happens, you fight a number of warhammer factions along the way, but all of it feels fairly incidental? Is good, because the characterization of the orcs is really well made, and the dialogs are really funny; but the overarching plot is not really anything to write home about, it's just an excuse to play around as an orc and hear that same orc taunting "humies" and wanting to smash things and the like.The gameplay is also fairly mindless, but fun; it has three difficulty settings and they're properly balanced -hard is hard, easy is easy-, so on and so forth. As you progress through the game, you get teeth (or "teef") that you can use to get upgrades and hats, as you play through the levels you get checkpoints where you can buy these things, or alternatively change your equipment; strangely though, you cannot change your hats here, only your weapons, if you want to change your hats you need to back in and out of the main menu. Which is a bit of a hassle, but whatever, is fine...I think the real problem is that, unlike previous titles from this developer (Guns, Gore Cannolli 1 & 2) the game doesn't really evolve that much when it comes to its levels or its set pieces. For the most part you'll go through the same looking stages, killing a number of random enemies that more or less behave the same way. It's fun, but it's nothing that really feels meaningful or impactful in any way, it's simply okay for what it is.A problem that I did have with the weapons, is the fact that the guns have some fairly abstract images to refer to their stats, as well as some minor descriptions here and there... the issue is that even if you are to follow these images for what they -might- appear to be; a lot of the times the weapons don't seem to have accurate descriptions, nor correct stats. Like they give you a rocket launcher that's supposed to have a really good fire rate, and you buy it, only to then use it and realize it has the worse fire rate of the three available in the game... It's just stuff like that, that makes the game a tad bit annoying.The game does have some cool bosses, all based on emblematic characters from the Warhammer universe, so stuff like that is really nice.Like many have said, the game is short -about 4 to 6 hours depending on how much you explore and your difficulty of choice-, but I think for what it is, they game is fine. I already think games are too long anyways; like I've mentioned, I think the game not really evolving much and just kinda reiterating on the same concepts is kind of what prevents it from being more than a decently fun time. I really like the orcs, and the combat is fun, but there isn't that much to it other than that.It's fine, get it on a sale if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: FINAL VERDICTIf you love the Warhammer universe, orcs and stupid twin-stick shoot-'em-ups, this game is for you!OVERALL 9/10Stupid twin-stick shoot-'em-up fun! Worth a replay and it has fun 4-player multiplayer (real-time Worms)!GRAPHICS 9/10Simplified, cardboard cutout-style art reflects Warhammer orcs' simplistic mindsets. Some excellent set pieces such as the imperial knight (giant robot knight) and the temple of the gene stealer cult. Even though the environment was a war-torn wasteland there was enough visual variety to keep the visuals interesting.SOUND/MUSIC 10/10Powerful on-point sound effects and the soundtrack bring the action to visceral, pulse pounding life! It took me until the ending cinematic to figure out that the music the orc band was playing was the theme song of the game ("SHOOTAS, BLOOD AND TEEF!"). They should have put it in the trailer.CONTROLS 8/10Using a controller I had some issues with aiming the snazzgun (it kept drifting up and down) and since there were so many important commands I had to map dash to a button instead of a trigger so I had to keep letting go of the trigger buttons to dodge (dash). You also walk and jump forward very slowly. Other than that very easy to control.PLOT N/AShoot-'em-up so not much of a plot to speak of; the warboss steals your topknot and you have to fight your way through swarms of guardsmen, tyranids, orcs and space marines to get it back.GAMEPLAY 9/10Fast paced stupid twin-stick shoot-'em-up fun!That being said, I would have preferred more weapons and for them to be slightly powered up (eg. the burnastikk should have more rounds, perhaps 6).I also would have preferred the weapons to do more damage or for enemies to have less health. Large battles turn into a bit of a grind with even minor enemies soaking up damage as you dodge back and forth for what feels like forever. I would have preferred more enemies with less health that dropped like flies to really emphasise the Warhammer aspect of the game. Boss battles with little enemies running around were somewhat annoying as you had to spend quite a bit of time being distracted by the small fry.MOST OF ALL I WOULD HAVE ENJOYED HAVING A SQUAD OF AI BUDDIES (BOTS)! IT WOULD REALLY BRING THE SINGLE-PLAYER CAMPAIGN TO LIFE.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't tell if I enjoy this game because it is a 40k game, or if I like it on its own merits.  I suppose it's more that it is a 40k game where the player gets to play as an ork.  Plus, I like retro video games, and the 2D run 'n gun is one of my favorites.The first thing that struck me with this game is the long load times.  While I don't have a powerhouse PC, I wasn't expecting the game to take a few seconds to boot up or load stages.  The filled me with a little concern.  And that concern was warranted, as the game is a little buggy, and I have already had it crash on me once.  With several times it threatening to.  The game play itself is 2D side scrolling twin stick run 'n gunning.  It's certainly not the best I've ever played, but it's far from the worst.  My biggest grip would be that even with the strongest guns, even the weak enemies take multiple hits.  Which further slows and already relaxed pace run 'n gun.  My next issue is the weapon wheel is a little clunky to use.  So I just cycle through the weapons instead.  Which is also frustrating as if I had the option to not take certain weapons, pistols being one of them, I wouldn't.  Just to make cycling through easier.  Speaking of weapons, Shootas, Blood & Teef have a bunch to pick from, but I found myself only using like three.  And of those three, I use one weapon 3/4 or more of the time.  It's too much of a pain to cycle through what the character carries and the carried weapons are by category leaving most of the load out at the save points.  To be sure, there weapons that work way better versus some enemies, scorcha vs. rats for example, but whats in hand and melee are work well enough to not want to bother.The game offers a fair amount of movement options from double jump to dash.  I try to include the dash in my play, but much of the time jumping and moving seems to be enough or better to avoid enemies and/or their attacks.  Perhaps mastery of this is more suited to the higher difficulty settings.  I probably won't ever know.Do I find the game fun?  I certainly did when I played the demo and the first portion of it.  The game isn't becoming more fun the further it goes on for me, but I also don't think the fun factor is dropping off a cliff either.  I think the more I play it, the more it goes from a fun game to a pretty fun or okay game.  And I can't separate how much of that is the 40k IP carrying it for me. As I am a 40k fan, and the story is entertainingly funny to me.So, I don't know quite if I recommend it or not.  I'm glad I added it to my library warts and all.  However, reading over my review it doesn't sound like I cared for it much.  So I'll recommend it if you like 40k and retro game genres like run 'n guns.  But caution anyone that isn't much of a fan of either.  Hopefully, the game's technical side gets tightened up in the future as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Its not a bad game but too short for the money. The game story is solid, and it really doesn't call for much more. Each weapon set has one or two decent guns but there is always one that's not worth it, you only get it because you have the money for it, and why not?I really enjoyed the lighthearted take on War hammer 40k which matched the tone perfectly. Unfortunately that wore away quickly. The game suffers from glitches, poor hit detection at times and just a general feeling of jank. What is the point of the melee? Also why can you hit your Ally with it? I understand explosions but the melee? Really? I wish it had more levels, as there are too few for the price. I wish I could have done more with my teeth other than just buy new weapons that failed to impress or new hats I can't change into during the game. (Why?)All in all the game is not worth the price. Its not a bad game but it feels like it could have been more. Maybe spend teeth to improve guns, maybe hats provide different bonuses. For that matter why not have the hats hidden on the levels, since the hats are a major part of the story. Regardless buy it on sale if you want to experience some old school side scrolling shooting, but don't get you hopes up for much more beyond that.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and really fun sidescrolling shooter.   Playing this actually reminds me of my childhood days playing browser games.  I played a lot of stuff like this, but made with with flash animation and a budget of a ham sandwich.   But I think that those cheap old games worked the same way this one does.   The levels are short, sweet 5 or 10 minute affairs.  Pretty much every level you'll have enough drops to unlock a new weapon.  Just simple challenges, fun guns, no long grind, no microtransactions.  Just pure, innocent game design.   It's actually shocking how refreshing that feels.  The story setup is great, you're on a quest to take down your old warboss who betrayed because you have a shiny fing on your head and he's da BOSS!  So takes it right off your head and pushes you out of your craft.   And rather than dying tragically like some lame hero of the imperium, or succumbing to corruption like a thrall of chaos, you simply shake off the landing, pick up your gun and start krumping your way back to the git.   I couldn't write a more orky story if I tried.   This game is great.   Buy it, sale or full price, it's firmly worth the money.  I'm confident that if you've liked games that are similar before, or this game is catching your eye, you're about to have a fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game with a good soundtrack (even though it can seem like the same song is playing over and over). The humor, voice acting and art style are all great. Despite these, the game was still enjoyable and kept me coming back. It's short, but I got this game as well as a lot of other warhammer games from getting a single issue of White Dwarf. _childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game? Yes, but with a few asterisks attached.Shootas, Blood & Teef is a 2D platformer/shooter where you play as an ork who was wronged by his warboss and now you want revenge. You fight your way through an imperial hive world's battlefield full of imperial guardsmen, orks, gretchen, and even some interesting factions you won't see coming. You fight some bosses along the way, and eventually you get your revenge... but it happens way too fast!You can see my playtime in this review. It's about 3 hours long, and not much more than that, unless you want to go achievement hunting. So I wouldn't say the game is worth it at retail price (19,99€ at the time of writing).There's also the case of the humor. This is a 40k that does NOT take itself at all seriously, but on the other hand, it's a game about orks, it probably  take itself seriously, considering what the orks are like. If you like your 40k games gritty and dark, this game isn't going to give you that, but if you like the zany kind of humor that the orks can provide, there's lots of laughs to be had in this game. If you can find the game at a discount, 30% or more, I'd say it's worth it, but not at retail price.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40k: Shootas, Blood & Teef is a nice sidescroling game, where you are an orc, hellbent on revenge on your Waaghboss, who stole your head-squig-thingie. You fight a lot of humies, other orcs and bosses - who are kinda unfair at points - like that imperial commissar in is overpowered Baneblade. Damn coward - but what to expect from puny humies. Overall it makes fun - though it kinda is difficult. So why the negative review? It constantly begins to crash and there is no support for this game. Others have the same problem. And 13 € for a faulty product? Warp no! Maybe I'll reconsider it at a 75%-sale for like 4 - 5 €. Until then this Waagh will be delayed.

_childDocuments_.review: Shootas Blood and Teef is a very fun game. The guns and combat feel very nice with an excellent Warhammer-Orky feel. _childDocuments_.review: I think Warhammer has a game in just about every genre these days. Lol. Actually, I don't think there is a match-3 Warhammer puzzle game yet, so somebody needs to develop one!                                                          Ok, I digress.  Shootas, Blood, & Teef is a multiplayer (it has local co-op) run and gun where you play as one of four classes of orcs attempting to take a gasoline plant from humans. Each class has a couple of minor differences (such as what their grenades do, what melee weapon they have, etc). The variations are subtle but noticeable.  Along the way the you collect "teef" (or teeth: orc currency) which allow you to purchase a handful of new weapons at every check point and the main menu (divided into types: pistols, shotguns, rifles, explosives, and another kind that unlocks later after picking up a flame thrower). You can also buy hats which are purely cosmetic.                                                                                                                                     *The game's graphics, while simple, are good and fit the game's humorous tone.                                                                    *I would say that the music is symphonic metal. While it is subjective, I like the energetic sound track and       feel it fits the game well. Weapons and explosions sound appropiately boomy and voices are sprinkled       throughout.                                                                                                                                                                  * The controls are tight for the most part; however, sometimes my brother, nephew, and I had trouble        quick swapping weapons.  We had to push the button a couple of times.                                                    * The game is a little short, but there are three difficulty levels and you can select stages individually to        collect any "teef" missed (it shows you the total "teef" of each level and how many have been acquired        on the level select screen).                                                                                                                                                          I purchased this game on sale, but honestly, I would have been happy with it even if I paid full price.  Also, it does work on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Review: TL;DRShootas Blood & Teef is a straightforward, 2D platform shooter that manages to be a fun, funny, brief experience. It’s very short, but it’s also so simple that it doesn’t overstay its welcome or get too boring as a result. It could have done more to be more complex and it has its issues with bugs, especially in online co-op environments. But it also achieves what it sets out to do just fine. It has some funny writing and countless references to the Warhammer 40,000 universe that most fans will be able to recognize and enjoy. If it’s cheap and you’re looking for a short and sweet shooter, you could do far worse.

_childDocuments_.review: A very well executed, if brief retro-style sidescrolling shoot 'em up Pros:- The setting, visuals and atmosphere have been recreated with the utmost care and love. It's clear the developers understand and care for the world- Very simple, but very functional gameplay: there are no upgrades, no stats, no puzzles or even platforming challenges, it's nothing but non-stop action from start to finish- Very tightly designed: you have basic movement controls, a melee attack, a grenade, 5 different weapons and 4 different character classes to choose from. Each function is designed with a specific purpose, allowing for slightly different gameplay styles. There's zero fat.- A wonderfully colourful, expressive artstyle that's just the right amount of goofy, and the visuals are always extremely clear and easy to read.- There are tons of easter eggs and funny background details for fans of the setting to find. Be on the lookout for motivational posters, they're very funny- Relentlessly fast pacing, there's never a dull moment- A kick-ass soundtrack that fits the game perfectly- 4-player co-op is available, but I finished this game solo so I can't comment on its quality muchCons: - Very short. I cleared the main campaign in less than 4 hours on normal difficulty- Very linear. This game would really benefit from some exploration elements. Though with how tightly the game is designed, I can't really say what you'd put behind that exploration- There are no transitions between levels, and very few cutscenes to establish context. When you defeat a boss for example, the game cuts immediately to a loading screen and drops you into the next level within seconds, giving no time to adjust to what just happened. Many times I was confused if I was even at a new level, or just continuing the previous one. Given how short the game is this isn't a huge deal, but it's jarring nonetheless- There's basically zero exposition or explanation of anything. Things like what a Waaagh is, what the Imperium is, why there are aliens in the sewers, what the white armored big guys are are just things you're expected to know- The pricepoint. $20 is simply too much for this game, no matter how tight the experience. If the game were half that, I'd recommend it without reservation. As it stands now, you're best off waiting for a sale.Despite its (literal) shortcomings, this game makes up for quantity with quality. It's clearly a labor of love and passion.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely satisfying {if short) arcadey game with a quirky art style that seems to actually reflect well how the orks view the world of 40k. If you wanted grimdark 40k to be less grimdark This game fits it well.There's fantastic attention to little details (mushroom calanders? lol), the storyline is suitably orky (and crazy), and the various bosses you fight have some of the most hillarious intros I'd not seen since borderlands series. Guns are suitably fun to fire and all the unlocked guns are typically sidegrades of each other so you don't have to unlock everything to finish the game. Co-op play is fantastic as well. The ragdoll physics are hillarious. My main issue with the game is that it crashes very often (at time of writing this), in my playthrough I counted it crashing about 4-5 times. And while the game is fun, The solo/co-op is rather short. Would be nice to have some extra content post-campaign as well such as a co-op horde mode or challenge/ leader board modes (e.g. an arcade mode with scoring similar to Gears of war)Also there's friendly fire with the melee attacks, beast snagga spears and explosions. Your melee attacks do feel rather weedy and lacking impact (even when you're swinging a tankhamma as a stormboy it can take a few hits to kill most mobs!) which is quite un-orky. Despite all this, overall I'd still recommend this shooter if you just like a bout of mindless mayhem and watching things run about in flames.... now time to go paint a mushroom tattoo on one of my ork minis....

_childDocuments_.review: After game was announced on "Warhammer Skulls 2022" I was really excited to play it especially after what I saw in "Guns, Gore & Cannoli" and "Guns, Gore & Cannoli 2" from same creator [Rogueside if You missed this part my dear reader]. Some information were shared with players, a part of soundtrack (which is really, really good to be honest!) was presented and game finally arrived.And I cannot say that this game is "especially bad" or "superb." because it is somewhere in the middle. What You going to feel from the beginning is the fact that this is, as previously mentioned "Guns, Gore & Cannoli",  an indie game that tries to be AAA title on license and fails because of it. What need to be mentioned is fact that it has less to offer than "Guns, Gore & Cannoli" and "Guns, Gore & Cannoli 2" and at the same time more to offer. Yes - this is a paradox that is hard to easily explain without playing the game.What You need to know is that, that game shows exactly how Orkz from Warhammer 40k Universe "thinks" and "works" and how they "see the world around them". If You expected "serious game" because "" then prepare Yourself to look at very nice and humoristic look into that grim universe. You'll be surprised how well it suits this universe.And one more thing - don't buy this game at full price, show some respect to Your own wallet and buy it when price goes down or when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Art, sound and especially voice acting is great but the gameplay is very mediocre and the game itself is super short.Gameplay - Very basic and doesnt require any thought, you run through the levels too fast to even notice and there are very abrupt stops and starts, youre fighting a boss and the split second its dead you get a loading screen and then you spawn in another level.Graphics - I like the cartoony artstyle and the animations are good, especially mechs and such "shake" in a very styalized way which fits the game. Screenshake is way too strong but can thankfully be turned off.The screen is cluttered with visual "noise" and its really hard to tell whats going on, differentiating between your teammates attacks, your own attacks and the enemies attacks is basically impossible. When we played we died very often without understanding what killed us, sometimes rockets/bullets/lasers fly straight through you because theyre friendly sometimes you die because theyre not.In general its hard to tell whats going on.Sound - Voice acting is really good and I was surprised by the music, theres one rock track with vocals which is really good but weapon sounds are very meh, no punchiness in explosions or dakkas.Cinematics - Theyre humorous and well animated but the video files are compressed beyond whats reasonable and there are a lot of artefacting and pixelation.

_childDocuments_.review: Shootas Blood and Teef is a simple game, and it's meant to be. It's a classic 2d sidescrolling shooter like Contra or Metal Slug, but painted with the 40k brush. And what impressed me most was just how much this game gives as far as detail.To go without spoilers, your enemies will range far beyond the standard affair of orks and guard and Space Marines. As a tabletop player, I found myself shouting out in surprise whenever a new enemy showed its face, many which have either rarely or even never had a video game representation before. Seeing these often overlooked factions and species was extremely refreshing.Of course, the gameplay itself is great. It's fast and simple, with tons of options for weapon loadouts and, not to mention, classes. You can choose from Stormboyz, Beast Snaggas, Flash Gitz, Weirdboyz, all of which have unique actions and looks to them, different melee attacks, different grenades, and overall feels. Combine this with a total of five weapon slots each with four weapon options, the game has a ton of replayability.I will say that the game is on the shorter side, but with its arcade-y nature, it is very easy to pick up and just run through a level or two with an entirely new loadout. Half the fun is going back and trying a level with a new class and new loadout, and seeing how it performs.Overall, this game is simple fun, a very fitting soundtrack, and probably my most enjoyed 40k game so far. Of course, that might be the ork in me being biased. Either way, I absolutely must give this game an obligatory-

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I've played it exclusively on Deck. It's everything I ever wanted from the basic premise. Shoot 'em up and with Orks. An orky perspective on things without being annoyingly grating. Fun background details are included like what the posters say, the shrines to Old Bale Eye / Yarrick, and the hand drawn elements are charming. The music punches above its weight and feels appropriately epic in high intensity.  I'm usually one to just play a campaign on easy and finish, but I've already started replaying.  The only downside in gameplay is that some minibosses feel harder than the main bosses, and you tend to explode more barrels than intended. The playable classes feel mixed. The Weirdboy seems the obvious worst of the four as its main effects can be replaced by the Shokk pistol, the Stormboy's hammer is a little clunky to use but makes up for it with his dash attacks, the Flash Git is the general best for the small chance of not using ammunition, but the Beast Snagga is my favorite because using his explosive spear is so satisfying as it rewards good placement and can help pierce shields and take down large beasts.  The variety of enemies feel healthy and never tiring. I wish they could've kept every enemy they had considered in development, like the Big Mek instead of choosing the Killa Kan, but that's just life in videogames. The weapons are generally fine. It capitalizes on what I considered a missed opportunity for the tabletop and put the Boomstikk on Infantry. The self damage weapons feel a bit hard to use in practice. Game never crashed for me.  The multiplayer seems a bit bare due to a bit of a lack of a playerbase but I hope that starts getting better, or I just start exploring LFG threads.  Maybe the game is too "indie" for the price for some but for me it was an instant purchase with no regrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Cutscenes and voiceacting are great,the story fitted well.Nice concept overall,The enemy varietie was fine and the portrayal of the 40k universe is cartoonish yet faithful.BUT The gameplay is repetitive,you have not enough guns and varieties,cant upgrade ork or nades,despite having too much money to shell out!Autoaim on controller makes it stupidly easy,but the ai  has it as well so i had the feeling you could not dodge all attaks,which is not intended anyway.Most parts are too easy,but the game is not deep or fun enough to bother changing the difficulty to hard.You could just run past most enemies,but that would make it really boring.I quit at the stompa fight(i think its the last one) because the autoaim kept correcting my aim which made me not hit the weakpoints( blieve it or not!) so the fight took forever and i quit and deinstalled after my second try.Felt like a waste of time in the end ,so dont waste yours ! O yeah and it crashed 5 times in almost 3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Was expecting to play this longer than 2 hours n a Castle Crashers vibe to wait out for Darktide. The alternatives for each weapon aren’t all great, same for the classes. Have to leave the game to change your class, same for your hats you buy. Joining multiplayer matches doesn’t give ya an option of you want to go as, just your last used from what you last played in the story or vs. Story is funny but with how much it is n how short it is, I could only recommend it when it goes on sale for five bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a step down from this developers previous games in the shoot-em up genre. The art style, while I guess fitting for the theme, is unappealing to the eyes and the weapons dont have the same impact i'd expect coming from said previous games. I couldn't really play it for more than an hour and that sucks, I really wanted to enjoy it but you cant win em all I suppose. If you enjoy it all the more to ya, I just cant.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: A Fun Co-op Shooter with some flaws.Good: Fast Paced, hectic, explosive action on par with MagickaMultiple legitimately laugh out loud moments for a 4th edition 40k grognardDifferent classes make different weapons more or less viableBright, colourful, low complexity, simple funArt style is great for the content and play styleBad:Contrast is lacking in some places so that with all the movement, it can be difficult to tell what the player character is compared to, e.g. co-player, enemy, scenerySound design lets the game down; gun sounds, explosions etc are all underwhelmingBoss difficulty is all over the placeFun, but you can get everything the game has to offer in 4 hours and quite likely never think about it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet little 2D indie platformer that lets you play as the silliest 40k race. It's filled with the hilarious ork humor that (I think) was first invented in the Dawn of war series. The game also has 4 player co-op (that can get pretty crazy) and tons of crazy ork themed weapons for you to mess around with. It's great and I do recommend it, just be aware you won't a crazy amount of content for the price. But once it goes down a bit, it will be Worth every WAAAAAHHGH in your wallet.Would love to see more ork themed 40K games!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a BLAST - WAAAAGH!It is highly addictive albeit being disappointingly short - but with great replayability value if you find some friends to play with. Online lobbies are still rather empty, but since the game is rather recent and fresh while it is certainly a niche game, this is not very surprising. Sound is great (although still buggy). The music is a BLAST (WAAAAAAGH!), sounds are convincingly accurate and fun to listen to, while the voice-overs hit the spot. The mechanics are easy to learn and not that hard to master, but coop-wise it is rather limited for its' short story, that entangles you nonetheless. If you're into WH40K, you might enjoy this for its' humourous approach and accurateness of lore, while still being an orky game. Guns and skills suit most play styles, and while class differences (there are four) are subtle, you're invited to play around with them, especially with friends or co-players. Other than that, the game has an active discord server. It's been active since the demo release 8 months prior to the release of the original game (I myself joined rather late), but the devs are listening there as well. It still has some flaws and bugs though, since progress is stored per machine and not per account, so some unlockables are unavailable if the game is played over various computers. To summarize, the game is well worth the money and is a great game to play, especially in local coop. Get krumpin'! WAAAAGH!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: I played and beat this game in singleplayer. It's relatively short but enjoyable. I'm sure it's a lot more fun in multiplayer, maybe even on a higher difficulty. I did have severe crashing issues whenever left the game paused for too long and one crash during a cutscene, but I am sure these will be fixed if they aren't already. Overall, it's a goofy but fun 40k ork game.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Beat it in three hours on the dot. Laughed for two and a half of it.Game is short, to the point, and really fun. The Middle drags on a bit, but on the whole really fun. Probably even better coop. Has some decent replayability since it has different classes you can play as, each with a different ability and custom cutscenes. Glad I bought it, though my skin has turned green, my canines elongated, and I feel a strange need to krump everyone I see.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: The campaign can be difficult at moments on first moments by the looks of it with bosses but with all the different weapons you can unlock it can be a fun breeze. The AI is certainly not perfect but it is certainly fun. The variation in enemys makes it really interesting. I would love a longer campaign but I did enjoy certainly what is already there a great deal. 9/10 Will certainly try to play this with friends when I can.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Have just finished the main story, so, I suppose, I can say sa couple things about that beautiful gamePros:– The story is truely orkish and pretty funny– Tons of references to WH40K stories and they are actually good– The soundtrack is AMAZING. Definetly worth adding to anyone's playlist– It's really not too long. Don't get me wrong, sometimes a short story can be a problem, but in that particular case the length is just perfect to enjoy the game, but not to get tired if you want to cover the whole story in one evening– You can try different ways to play it. 4 classes, 20 guns. You can always find your style– You can take your friends and play together– I haven't expirienced any bugs yetCons:– If you know nothing about WH40K orks the story might seem a bit wierdConclusions:I definetly recommend the game to anyone. Funny, pretty, full of jokes and it can be run without bying a new graphics card. If you want to have some good time and rest after work/classes, you like guitars and Warhammer 40000,  it'll be difficult to find anything better
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty decent, the music itself is a 10/10. There are things that need to be improved. The game play is simple and fun but I felt like it was too easy at some points. The Boss battles are really lame, they need to be reworked cause they either have few attacks or there just big targets. And for a game that has blood in the title there really isn't any blood, I thought it would be more gory. These a simple things that can be ironed out in updates. Its great we have a warhammer game that doesn't take itself to seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: +Playing as an Orc in WH40K universe+Cool music+Lots of Dakka+More Dakka-All four classes play the same-Most weapons won't be used (Flamethrower and Plasma is all you need for 95% of the game)-Enemies are dumb-Single player is only about 3 hoursGood or bad?Well, I'm biased because it's Orcs in WH40K and that's why I give it a thumbs up but if you don't know who are the Evil Sunz or the Goffs, you probably shouldn't by this game or at least wait for a big discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: The campaign is short but has a lot of replay value with the achievements and different classes to choose from. If there is DLC that comes out for this through another campaign, added classes and clans, or just more hats and weapons then I'd easily buy it. Haven't played the online yet but it has a lot of potential as like a screw around game if you have friends to play this with. Highly recommend to anybody that loves orks and the silliness they bring to 40k.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Some people will have gripes about the price and campaign/story length (from reading the forums), but that's all down to individual personal perspective and disposable income levels, that a side. I really enjoyed the game, I've completed the campaign once on normal, as the Flashgit, and now re-doing a harder difficulty as one of the other (4 total)classes. Waaaaghhh!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Get ya shoota's boyz! We'z got Krumpin to do!This is such a great game! Loved every moment of the story mode. The humor was spot on, the attention to lore and detail was great, and I loved seeing all the little easter eggs hidden around. I would recommend this game to anyone who likes Warhammer 40k, Metal slug like games, or just like Da Orks, cause green is best. I have only TWO complaints about the game:1. Stability: So, many, CRASHES. However, with the check points scattered around gnerously this wasn't TOO much of an issue, still this really needs to be addressed. 2. The story mode was short! I beat the game in just under five hours taking my time. I loved it and I wanted more! I really hope there is a expansion or dlc to come out for this because I'll be getting it. For now I'll go achievement hunting and go for hard mode. (Extra hard mode might be fun too...)Though I do have a question for the Devs...Any chance of fightin' the only humie Orks respect? Commissar Yarrick? DAT would be a good fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy Metal Ork side scrolla. The art was great and I spent a lot of time just admiring the backgrounds. Every locker, poster and piece of trash was lovingly drawn and very entertaining.  The game was super short but there was a fair amount of mayhem and unit types encounteredAs far as weapons go they could use a little more balance. Its feels like the Bolta is hands down the best gun for krumpin. Nothing else even comes close. The enemy behavior got a little wonky sometimes too with bosses not engaging, units getting stuck in loops because they cant reach you, or simply not activating because you weren't close enough to their spawn during a "Kill em all" eventOverall. pretty damned fun
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy side scrolling shooters and/or enjoy warhammer Ork-style shenanigans then you probably have a blast with this game.It is a light challenge and a bit shorter than I would have liked, but the levels are beautiful, the art is great, and the story is pretty funny.All in all, the game is a great casual 3-4 hour arcade experience with a fun assortment of weapons and hats to unlock for your character.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: This game "gets" the orks in 40k and the sense of humour you need to have with these characters. The metal slug style game play is a fun change of pace from most 40k shooter games, the control set up can be tricky to keep a handle on during the more frantic firefights but you can adjust your play style to control the enemies better and you can re-map controls to help yourself.The enemy AI can get a bit confused trying to find the best path to you, especially when jumping up levels or dropping down to get you. Some parts of levels that you can walk on are obscured by other layers of artwork, but it doesn't affect game play too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: A enjoyable game. Soundtrack is awesome and the humour is great and in true Guns, gore and cannoli spirit. It's a great game to play with your  friends and it's easy to learn. There are some moments where it can get really crazy on the screen and even moments where the game can get a abit difficult. A Guns, gore and cannoli game set in the warhammer universe.As of right now doing this review me and my friend who played stumbled upon a game breaking glitch that was fixed the next day. My game crashed a few times but other than that game worked as intended.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: ORKS ORKS ORKS! well i have to say i love this game, lets just get that out of the way. this game is for the Ork boyz, for those of us who never seem to av 'nough DAKKA! its a simple side scrolling shooter but that doesn't detract from the 'mount av fun oi've bin avin WAAAGHing my way across the face of Lootius. I would suggest this game to everyone, (deep knowledge of 40k isn't required at all!) its a fun, humorous good time.p.s.WAAAAAAAAGGGGGHHH!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: played the beta, played the full, and ive even played other games from the devs, all i can say is that its a good game, hard to find ppl online, and the story is short for 20$, but honestly this may be the best w40k orks game that exists, if they add more stuff to make online more lasting the game would be a definite 10/10, but the lack of replay-ability makes the game lack luster at times.im still leaving a positive because the game-play is awesome, and i have hopes for the future of the game, but be aware of the problems the game seems to have before you buy it, because 20$ is a lot for a 3-4 hour game...still with all that id say its a good game overall, twice so when compared to half the piss that is other warhammer games, its not perfect and has a lot of room to improve, but its not the worse game ive ever played, its even enjoyable, i did have fun playing this game! witch i cant say the same about 90% of games from warhammer. lastly when compared to GGC and GGC2 there's a lot of things learned, i love the UI changes from GCC, miner things like how your ammo and health is over your head rather then on the corner of your screen, whale GGC2 had your health the ammo was still difficult to keep track off, not that that really matters, sense ammo in infinite in SBT, witch i dislike because it makes it easy to just spam the better weapons for the entirety of the game, along with this, i have noticed a visual decline from GGC2 and SBT, with the art of GGC2 being HD and having an almost 2.5D look to it by using art techniques, this is absent, and i understand that SBT is meant to be cartoony but so is GGC2...overall, when compared to there old titles they have improved mechanical elements like UI and some game-play bits, but the art has seemingly suffered abit in return...with all this i would give the game a 6.9-10, should you buy it? yes, but i would wait and keep an eye on how this game evolves if it will, and understand that if your only in it for the story your only gonna have like 3-4 hours of game-play...and that's on the hardest setting....
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little game, but quite a few bugs. Crashes seem to be frequent on boss loading, and progress/weapons seems to be saved locally rather than cloud based. I played for a while on my switch while my son used my PC, when I came to play on my PC and he on his, I had all of his weapons and he had none since he hadn't played on his PC at all. The elevators are pretty horrendous in multiplayer too, very glitchy.Worth the price tag for the comedy value with friends, if you don't see the value in that then don't buy it expecting a long and involved game, because it isn't one. A decent amount of effort went into the art, voice acting and references, which I enjoyed. Very true to 40k and Orky as hell.The good weapons become obvious quite quick, swapping between all 4 is simple and intuitive and the special ability keeps you ripping through. I do think the Flash Git is my personal favourite for the neverendig bullet spray.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: exactly what it looks like ork madness with dakka a good 5 hours gameplay only 2 things i can complain about is friendly fire isnt nice on this kinda game and could use some upgrade tree for extra damage ect for repeatability as once uv unlocked all the guns there isnt much to aim for just replaying to shoot stuff which isnt really bad just would be nice to have a little moreand the screen shakes like crazy so if ur epileptic of any short avoid at all costs an option to turn it off would be great

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts out fun and hands you new weapons at a fast pace.  Then....it doesn't any more, the enemies get spongier and spongier, you get no real ways to deal with them...Most of the weapon options are pretty rubbish, there are points where you need to switch weapon loadouts but can't, weird level transitions, just all manner of hair pulling annoyances piled up on each other.Plus points, it is a rare humorous take on the 40k universe and its humor stays amusing throughout, with loads of references sprinkled through the levels.If they could have kept the frenetic starting pace going this would be a definite recommend but unfortunately it ends up as a slog.  Only really recommended for very hardcore 40k afficionados.TLDR No Bloodaxes dont buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: I mean...c'mon...you get to play an irreverent big muscled Ork, what's not to like?  :DLots of good one liners, good action, good paced fights...love it...and it has a good range of bad guys to shoot at too. _childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming and fun. Though not terribly long, the amount this game gives you for its price is very reasonable and fair. There's a lot of weapons, four different classes, and a lot of hats. It never felt like the fighting got old, nor did it ever feel unfair or unfun.There are, however, some random crashes occasionally, but the game gives you checkpoints liberally enough that you don't have to start from too far where you crashed.Really good game. If you like funny orks and fast paced shooting, then get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: It's a delightfully silly take on the only faction in 40k that is having a good time. The weapon selection is acceptable for a game at this price, and the length is short, but at the same time the soundtrack is spectacularly orky in a way that makes you really enjoy the time you do have playing through the game.All in all, I give this game 7 teef out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun gameplay (solo), with orky dialogue thats on point.Control wise, boss mechanics, etc. nothing revolutionary but engaging. Might be fun co-op but levels are pretty small, so not sure about that.Soundtrack is pretty damn great.Have not tried the PvP but im pretty sure its not gonna be for me.The thing that brings me to sort of not recommend it (since steam is lacking a mid score i will give it a thumbs up tho) is a lack of randomised mode (like randomised levels, that you can just run through for loot). After campaign is done, you are done, and from everything i have read its about 3 hours long and thats not a whole lot for the money.Limited weaponry options are also a slight bummer (no upgrades?), this is because most weapons feel like they dont bring anything to the table and or are just bad/feel bad.All in all, for the little i played a fun romp, but pretty expensive for what it is (and i hope it gets more content, game modes mostly).
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game although it was short. I was able to complete the game in about 3 hours. I do wish there was more replayability to the game, currently the only type of progressions is 'buy all the guns' which can be done on a single play through. Great soundtrack. The game can be played online/local with other people, more people, more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: First Impressions: Fun movement and Weapons, but the enemies are a little buggy. For example the Genestealer boss was attacking me like normal and I threw my Squig Bombs which it started attacking instead. Once the Squigs blew up though the Genestealer just stayed in the middle of the arena not doing anything. Overall I would recommend trying the game out, but know it just came out and you may encounter some glitches.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it simple, I would say this game is a *SOLID B*. A fun and short game.I was getting alot of enjoyment out of playing this game. Most of the bosses were fun, the shooting felt good, and the humor was on point. Worth playing if you love the Orks, Warhammer, or games like Metal Slug or Alien Hominid. Getting into it, there's some issue I have with it, having played the game single player. 1) The auto-aim for controller is on by default. You can turn it off but it seems to turn back on when you go to main menu.2) The game has crashed 4 times for me. Shocking for a game with little requirements to run.3) You can't increase or decrease controller stick sensitivity like you can with the mouse (at least from what I could find).4) You can remap the controls to your liking. The issue being that the weapon wheel and next weapon function cannot be tied to the same button/key, even though by default they are the same button (Y/Triangle). Same with the interact function or etc.5) Maybe a little too pricey for how short it is. 6) At times it felt like the regular enemies were harder and tankier than the bosses. I found myself yelling "JUST DIE ALREADY!" alot. 7) *SPOILERS* ---> There were 3 moments that I thought were frustrating or unfair. The 1st being the elevator in the Imperium. The 2nd being the 2 Killakans. The 3rd being the final boss. Each of these moments felt like taking damage was unavoidable. I hope these issues are addressed by the devs in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enough game but nothing mind blowing Great music, great art direction, tons of great nods to the 40k franchiseGameplay can be a tad frustrating even on medium and the guns left me wanting but I think it's a fun enough way to kill 2-3This wasn't game breaking but I think it's funny: My play through ended with the credits crashing
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: I personally love the orks from 40k and seeing as this is purely the game made for ork lovers. Premise is simple, gameplay is smooth. Guns for everybody and every situation, and even small rpg elements to each class and what each ork can do. I love everything about this game and I simply want more orkz.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Shootas, Blood & Teef

_childDocuments_.review: Just a good game with solid gameplay, nice variety and good game design. Every enemy type (so far) has been visually distinct which lets you target appropriately. There's a surprising amount of weapon variety (5 weapon categories, and 4 types of each category).  There are also 4 classes to play as, each with a unique melee weapon and grenade type. The story is sufficiently orky and mildly silly (a nice change of pace for 40k games) but still feels appropriate. I have 3 complaints and they're all pretty minor. I would like an even harder difficulty than hard. I got used to the game within a handful of levels and more or less stopped dying unless I was doing something really orky. Levels can be surprisingly short. It's always a bit disappointing when I feel like I've not been in one very long and it's suddenly over. But on the other side of that coin, loading times are *quite* fast.I would  like actual numerical details about the weapons and classes. Honestly not a huge issue, but just something I'd like to see personally.

name: SILT
detailed_description: More Great Fireshine Games About the Game SILT is a surreal underwater puzzle-adventure game. Alone in an underwater abyss, you are a diver searching the deep to uncover long-forgotten mysteries. Possess the creatures around you to solve puzzles and travel further into the darkness… Nature has evolved into bizarre forms. Discover strange organisms, unexplored ruins and ancient machinery hidden beneath the water’s surface. Survive encounters with giant deep-sea goliaths. Harness their power to awaken a long-dormant force at the centre of the abyss. Experience art brought to life. SILT’s unsettling, monochrome world is constructed from the sketches and dark imagination of artist Mr Mead. A harrowing journey awaits you… EPILEPSY WARNING Please read before playing this game or allowing your children to play it: Some people are susceptible to epileptic seizures or loss of consciousness when exposed to certain flashing lights and moving patterns in everyday life. Such people may have a seizure while watching television images or playing certain video games. This may happen even if the person has no medical history of epilepsy or has never had any epileptic seizures. If you or anyone in your family has ever had symptoms related to epilepsy (seizures or loss of consciousness) when exposed to flashing lights or moving patterns, consult your doctor prior to playing this game. If you or your family experience any symptoms of seizure while playing this game, such as dizziness, nausea, or loss of consciousness, stop playing immediately and seek medical attention.

_childDocuments_.review: I will open by saying Silt is a fascinating game with incredible atmosphere, beautiful art, and concepts that immediately grab your curiosity. However, it ultimately fails to deliver. I beat it in under 3 hours, and that was taking my time and taking in the scenery. Puzzles felt arbitrary, and I often felt like I was not actually utilizing any problem solving. Just using whatever fish was next to me at the time until I got progress. Game difficulty spikes from a slow and casual experience to requiring precise timing and finger dexterity, with almost no build up to that point. Sort of a thrown from the deep end vibe. The boss fights feel unsatisfying - aside from the chapter 3 boss that was the only time the game sparked an emotional response from me aside from 'thats pretty!' or 'thats creepy.'The story of the game is nonexistent, and I honestly felt like I was baited with one. I'm no stranger to open ended and interpretative stories, however this felt like it was simply throwing fascinating imagery and hints of a story at me just to entice me, constantly prompting new questions with implications of abilities, locations, and the statues that all point in the direction of a fascinating world. However. Contrary to what the steam store synopsis says, there are no mysteries that are unraveled. The game ends abruptly. Giving you only questions, and never an answer. While its a brilliant art piece, its appeal is superficial. The game has little substance.As an addendum, Other players reported many bugs. Personally, the only bug I encountered was an inability to claim collectibles. I will replay after there has been a patch, to see if perhaps getting collectibles is paramount to enjoyment, but as is, I am underwhelmed.

_childDocuments_.review: All style no substance.Positives   - Looks good sounds good.Negatives   - Lack of anything, the puzzles are not really puzzles.    - Cheap deaths that will send you back to the start of the level. In Limbo you started not far away from the place you died, In SILT you have to do the whole level over again and that is frustrating as hell.    - The patterns go like this. Swim very slowly and watch a cut scene, solve some very basic puzzles that you know the solution of but fail because of the poor mechanics, swim through a section without doing anything just to reach a loading screen, fight a boss and another cut scene again of course.   - You play as a diver and you will often swim in an unnatural position for 10 to 20 seconds before turning back in a natural position. I often didn't have a feeling I was under water really, the 2 things that reminded me that I was under water were my diving suit and some fish. So in my opinion poor atmosphere overall.   - I even managed to soft lock myself :)Conclusion :If I wanted to see something that looks and sounds good I can always watch 2001: A Space Odyssey, this is a video game...well at least I think it is because the whole thing is badly done. Boring, frustrating...I could add more negatives but I think that is enough. Do not buy this, it is not worth your time or money.

_childDocuments_.review: SILT is a surreal and atmospheric adventure-exploration-puzzle game.I think for most people, the two main potential downsides to this game are that the puzzles are generally quite simple and it's slow-paced. I personally don't necessarily consider these elements to be bad, so they didn't detract from the experience for me. Additionally, the exploration, atmosphere, and surrealist elements of the game more than made up for them. Basically, I think if you buy this game for the art, adventure, and atmosphere, you're likely to enjoy it; if you are buying it because it's listed as a puzzle game, I think you might find it middling at best. I found the game length (~3-4 hours for a playthrough) to be appropriate; the game didn't feel too short or like it was overstaying its welcome. I generally recommend this game provided you aren't looking for a primarily puzzle-driven game and can appreciate an open-ended (and slightly weird) narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Dive into this underwater nightmare as you encounter terrifying sea monsters and use your ability to possess sea critters to solve puzzles.  is a fascinating game with incredible atmosphere and beautiful art direction. Even though it is a brilliant art piece, it fails to deliver a solid game due to its puzzle simplicity, clunky controls, nonexistent story, and short playtime (can be completed within 2-3 hours). Only would recommend to buy this title with a steep discount. [7/10]

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game. I was so excited for it when it finally released, but after giving it a run, there are just a couple of things that are wrong that end up making me dislike this beautiful piece of a game.Firstly, the art style is wonderful. It looks like Limbo, with that dark, grim atmosphere. However, it isn't as smooth of an experience. I feel like Slit falls off the hardest with its lack luster puzzles. The solution is simply whatever fish is floating about. Take control of said fish, solve the puzzle, then head over to the next zone. Rinse and repeat until you beat the game. All of the puzzles just feels hollow with no real eureka moments.On top of all that, sprinkle in a couple of immersion-breaking bugs and you end up with Slit, a beautiful game that could of been so great, but falls just short. I'd recommend the gamer whenever the game is on sale and they have fixed the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible graphics and intriguing story, and I wanted to like it, but the controls are too floaty and wonky for the speed of the puzzles it wants you to do. It's unnecessarily difficult and it restarts you really far back when you die in some areas, so it just became a hopeless slog to the finish until I eventually gave up right before the last boss. Puzzles don't feel rewarding, it just feels relieving to finally be done with them. Just watch someone else play it, it isn't any fun on your own.

_childDocuments_.review: I have one good thing and several not good things to say about this game.The good part is the artwork. Beautiful visuals, wonderful backgrounds, kind of Samurai Jack - vibes.Other than that, the game is a waste of time. Fans of LIMBO, INSIDE, Black the Fall, Little Nightmares etc. will find this game a poor excuse for the titles listed above:The puzzles are simplistic at best,The progression is not always clear,Bosses are unsatisfying,Too many loading screens.Overall it is a nonsensical game. Obviously most people enjoyed it but I wouldn't put it up there with the other titles. I was very excited about it; alas it was a waste of time. Even DARQ was a better game.At least the hearts of the creators were in the right place, or at least adjacent to the right place. _childDocuments_.review: I love the idea of this game, but the execution leaves a lot on the table. For one, and most importantly, the puzzles here are not good. Puzzles are hard to make, and it takes a while to plan them out in way where they are fun to perform and come with 'eureka' moments. As far as I've gotten, they've all been relatively obvious solutions but actually doing what is required to solve the puzzles feels repetitive and frustrating. Some of this has to do with the core gameplay tenets feeling kind of tired and slow, but unfortunately these aren't really "fixable" or "patchable" problems due to the design of the puzzles. You'd really have to take a sledgehammer to this thing and break it to rework it. Which sucks, by the way, because visually I think this is a pretty cool little game. It's clear they worked hard on the visual presentation (though, they couldn't escape some of the iffy animations that come with procedural texture warps). Silt has a world that, like its primary inspirations Limbo and Shadow of the Colossus, really does speak to me. I want to know more about it, and even though real answers probably aren't up for grabs the curiosity still lingers. I'll no doubt finish the game, but it's a shame when finishing something like this feels like work instead fun. Now the bugs: unfortunately, this thing came too early. It clearly needed another few months to iron out the obvious issues and presentation mistakes. Fortunately, these elements can be fixed, and I think with a few patches and maybe a sale, this could turn into a conditional recommendation. For now, I'd have to say, give heavy consideration on whether or not you want to get this right now. It is not in the same quality tier as its spiritual predecessors.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but I do feel partially mislead by the demo. I liked the demo of this game as it was a creepy underwater adventure with terrifying sea monsters, and that expectation is what drove me to purchase the full game. Suffice to say that for me the rest of the game did not live up to expectations. While creepy, the environments and storytelling made me feel like the game was trying too hard, while both the gameplay and atmosphere provided by the sound design and music were lacking. The gameplay eventually became repetitive in a way, and there was no urgency or sense of danger in most of the sections (aside from when you just die instantly from trying the wrong thing or a surprise attack from a new enemy). TL:DR, Overall if you wanted an underwater horror that actually uses the underwater theme to its fullest, then the game only gets worse after the first level (from the demo), which was somewhat disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the atmosphere and the creepy environments! Best played on a big screen with lights down and a good audio setup to appreciate all the visual detail and underwater sound design.The possession mechanic is innovative and versatile and I enjoyed the ways the game found to make use of it. A short and well crafted indie experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played LIMBO and INSIDE, then you might be interested in SILT, though I can't really recommend it because it doesn't measure up to those games.  All three games tell their story visually and there is no dialogue, but unlike LIMBO and INSIDE, I couldn't figure out the story in SILT.  You play this diver who can possess other creatures and corpses, but I never knew why.  You swim through this underwater ruin filled with statues of furries, but I never figured out why my character was there to begin with.  I suppose I should play the game a second time to pay closer attention to the story, but the puzzles aren't all that thrilling or difficult so I don't have the motivation to do so.  I will say that the artwork is beautiful, but I also thought that about Scorn which is another game that looks great but has uninteresting gameplay.  If you're really, really hankering for another game like INSIDE or LIMBO, then you might want to check this one out since it isn't terrible, but it's not going to blow you away.

_childDocuments_.review: this one is a bit of a mixed bag. _childDocuments_.review: What initially enticed me was the interesting visual style and darkly enticing aesthetic. Sadly, those are not enough to redeem the game itself, which offers little more than a couple of hour's worth of content. The puzzle are not complex enough to be satisfying, there's no semblance of plot, and ironically given you're a diver little depth. All these are made worse by infuriating controls. Strangely, I had no issues in the first two chapters, but the possession mechanic started to break down for me from the third, randomnly stuttering or failing to activate for extended periods. The worst, however, was attempting the control the stingray, which would frequently fail to use its power, sadly resulting in many failed attempts at level clearance for no reason beyond a bug. It could have been a cool game, but it hasn't been developed enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is a 2D, atmospheric horror game that takes place deep underwater on an alien world filled with danger and mystery. You play as a nameless diver who has the ability to possess nearby creatures and use their unique abilities to interact with the environment.The first thing you'll notice when looking at Silt is its fantastically stunning art direction. The environments are heavily inspired by the designs of Mr Mead, and what you're given is a plethora of outstanding set pieces that immediately draw you into the world. It's easily my favourite aspect of the game and it's what kept me hooked.Past the visuals though, the story is one that's open to interpretation. You're given a text blurb at the beginning which gives you an idea of your objective, but that's it. No dialogue, no narrator, no notes; nothing. Despite that, it's difficult to get lost since the levels are linear; it's just a case of swimming in the right direction and moving your way past puzzles.The gameplay loop thrives through the character's ability to possess other creatures. You'll encounter numerous challenges that'll require you to think outside of the box, using each creature's unique ability strategically. Some of these puzzles are relatively simple, but there are more complex ones as well.The only major problem I had with Silt was that parts of it were too vague for my tastes. This is directed more to smaller parts of the levels, as there were times where I had to die repeatedly in order to figure something out. Regardless of that, I highly recommend Silt. It's short, but incredibly well-made. If you wish to see a more detailed review, check out my video review for the game here:

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere is great and it's a short and overall enjoyable game but with notable flaws. Unlike Limbo or Inside which seem the most comparable this is significantly easier and feels like there's less there to experience. Puzzles are usually nothing more than finding the right critter to possess to open the way, with occasionally needing a few different critters per screen as you advance. It's mostly in the fourth and final area that it tries to add more danger by needing to move at specific times or open a way and quickly move. Even then it won't take long to figure out what to do.It does look really nice and I like the aesthetic, I just feel more could have been done with the deep sea theme and terrifying monsters to threaten you.Play time is probably 1-2 hours for a first play.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: To be honest the idea of this game looked promising, it reminded me of Inside and Little Nightmares and was hoping to get same gameplay and vibe as those games, but unfortunately it wasn't able to deliver.The world and visuals look unique, you wake up underwater chained and have an ability to posses some fish which each one has unique ability and you can use them to solve puzzles in game. The puzzles are not that hard and with couple of tries you can figure them out. There are some boss fights, although there isn't really a fight you just need to find a way to use those fish abilities to kill them. My main issue with this game was control, I played with M/KB and in some areas had really hard time navigating and solving puzzles, I don't know why developers didn't utilize the mouse control in this game but it was really missing, in some cases you needed to be very precise and controlling your character's movement was really clunky which caused me to die a lot in some areas. The puzzles were not really hard it was just the way that I wanted to control my character and failed to do with M/KB. Maybe people who used game-pad didn't have this issue but this was really annoying to me and I just gave up.I didn't encounter any bugs like some users mentioned, the game ran smoothly. The other thing that I noticed was lots of loadings, every time you went from one area to another there was a loading, it wasn't a big deal and I am sure developers had some reasons to do this.Gameplay is around 2-3 hours depending on how many time you die which to me seems pretty short.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been this hyped for a game release for a long time, and Silt is just what I hoped it would be: dark, mysterious, unnerving but beautiful.You can see how much work was put into the hand drawn paintings. Every level looks different and wants to tell you something about the strange underwater world. And just when you relax to enjoy the little fishies doing their thing, an unnameable horror comes around the corner.Awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric, charming, and full of discovery, Silt is a wonder to look at and a joy to play. If Mario Odyssey and Limbo had a child that could breathe underwater it would be this game. It's easy enough that your emo little cousin can play, but the mysterious story and eerie hand crafted creatures will surely have experienced gamers entranced. Excited to see what Spiral Circus does next!

_childDocuments_.review: It's hauntingly beautiful.
