_childDocuments_.review: Astounding visuals, very reminiscent of Limbo and Inside but with its own tone.A short game (1,5-3h depending of how clumsy you are) with a cool mysterious background but with a not so well balanced puzzles, as most of them are really easy (this is not a problem) but a couple of them managed to get me killed more than the rest combined, and with the savepoints being improvable, it can become annoying.Nonetheless a nice game for its price or discounted if you are in doubt, looking forward to know about this studio's next project.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is an amazing game.Many people, including myself, were attracted to Silt because of the amazing art style and aesthetic and of course it does not disappoint in those areas. However, the game play is indeed really fun. The puzzles are changeling without being too difficult and come in all sorts of flavors and diverse mechanics. Without spoiling anything, players that enjoy boss fights will be particularly fond of this game.The only downside is the game is pretty short and lacks repeatability, granted these are qualities indie puzzle games are not generally known for. I finished my play through in about three hours, which is not a lot of time for a $15 title but atleast I enjoyed most of it. Playing it again is difficult, whilst there are some collectibles to chase, doing the game over simpily presents the same puzzles you've already figured out, as is the case with many puzzle adventure games.Overall 8/10- Amazing Aesthetic- Fun & Challenging Gameplay- A little short for the price

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is an ambiance puzzle-driven game that I stumbled upon randomly. I am more than halfway through the game if I'm not mistaken. I'm pleasantly surprised by the ambiance that is quite reminiscent of games like Limbo or Inside that is perfected by the beautiful visuals and landscapes. I've been really liking the core mechanic of the game which is to "possess" objects and creatures to use their special abilities. Although some parts might be confusing, I felt that all the puzzles could be resolved logically rather than randomly as many others suggest. That being said, I am a big fan of this type of puzzle-driven games and I am acquainted with the conventions of such genre. The game is slow-paced and I appreciated the more contemplative sections where the character is wandering around huge landscapes although some might find them boring. You should not go into this game thinking you will be challenged with hectic gameplay, it's a game that likes to take its time.For a first game, Spiral Circus has nailed at creating an impressive ambiance and a compelling world, although it remains quite mysterious (maybe too mysterious, I would enjoy more narrative clues to understand what is going on, I might be missing some since I've clearly haven't unlocked every achievement nor have I finished the game). If you liked Little Nightmares, Limbo, Inside, or ambiance/puzzle games with a pinch of horror, I believe this game is for you. The price is more than reasonable for the quality and the effort put into creating the game and you will have a good time playing it. I'm quite interested in seeing what the studio will put out next !

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game. The art style is incredible - that alone was worth the price of admission for me. The game mechanics - swimming, possessing animals - are unique. A surreal, Lovecraftian story is told without any words.There were points where I was a bit confused, and these might be design issues that need ironing out (but on the other hand you could argue figuring stuff out is part of this kind of game).Takes a few hours to complete (which is fine with me, less is more sometimes). I'd say it's worth getting on sale if you want to try something a bit different.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool art style and atmospheric experience, but I can only recommend it if you spot it on a sale.It's a pretty short, about 3 hours, and the overall feeling is positive. It didn't drag itself out. The gameplay, however, is really rather lacking. Navigation is sluggish and the puzzles are somewhere between boring and frustrating. A lot of them are just trial and error until you learn enough to complete them. Never so complicated you really struggle for too long, but also never quite satisfactory enough to actually enjoy. You're just happy you get to swim to the next area and see what's there.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is an absolutely beautiful and mysterious game. Perfect for a quiet evening where you can take your time exploring the magical deep sea world.The architecture, the weird creatures and the atmosphere create a surreal game world but all the little artistic details and the naturally behaving animals make it feel real. It's this wonderful juxtaposition that makes Silt such a unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving it a positive review because I think the art style and atmosphere deserves it, but overall I would say this is a fairly unremarkable game with a weak gameplay loop. The best way I can put it is that this is basically underwater Limbo with much weaker puzzles, level design and storytelling. Overall I'd give the visuals a 9/10 but the gameplay 5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Good atmospherics, but clunky controls I am a very inexperienced gamer, so take my review with a grain of salt.PROS: What the game does really well is building the eerie atmosphere. The background art is beautifully drawn and the creature designs were very creative. The sound design does a great job of setting the scene, often with no music and only minimal atmospheric noises. Despite the spooky atmosphere, I’d say it isn’t really a horror game. An enemy may sometimes get you by surprise, but it is never a jump scare, and once you know they’re there you can clearly see them. There are no loud booms or blood pressure-increasing music. Enemies’ attacks are clearly telegraphed. CONS: This is NOT an epilepsy-friendly game. The diver’s lamp flickers sometimes. Multiple extended parts of the game involve flickering lights and crackling electricity in dark environments. There are two parts where the entire screen flashes light and dark. If you are photosensitive, you should avoid this game entirely.  If you are terrified of the deep ocean, being underwater, or carnivorous sea creatures, this is also not the game for you. Animals are eaten by other animals or carnivorous plants frequently. There are brief sections with disgusting squelching sounds.The worst part of this game are the controls. I was using keyboard to play. It was very difficult to position myself correctly or change direction, which was detrimental to the few parts of the game that required speed. I would also get stuck on corners. This was particularly annoying when I was trying to possess animals, and I would often end up spinning in circles trying to get a good angle. I haven’t tried playing it with any other controls.The puzzles became tedious in some places, just using the same mechanics over and over until the enemy died. I consulted walkthroughs to solve several of the puzzles, but I’d chalk that up to my laziness rather than any fault of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: A decent into the unknown in this underwater LimboRating 7/10Purchased Cost: Free is a sub-aquatic dreamlike adventure that draws inspiration from many sources. From games such as , the art of John Kenn Mortensen and Edward Gorey to the unsettling otherness of David Lynch. It's a unique experience as you explore this underwater world with a story only hinted at and hidden from view. This strange world is filled with ancient ruins, odd machinery and terrifying creatures from the depths. Although  is no horror there is an underlying dread which is communicated via the atmospheric music and haunting visuals.As you explore the game begins to present puzzles that you have to solve in order to progress. The game does a good job at presenting simple mechanisms that you will then use to solve the next puzzle. These puzzles are often solved by possessing other underwater creatures and using their unique special ability. This can be anything from electric eels powering up ancient machines to a Manta Ray creature that can teleport through walls.While these puzzles are perhaps overly simplistic and linear they do offer some ingenious methods to solve them. When you arrive at a new puzzle location the game presents a new creature for you to posses which you then use to solve the puzzle. As well as the puzzles there are a few chase sequences which rely on some quick thinking and trial and error although the game is very forgiving.  is far more interested in exploration and atmosphere than action.It is also a short game, it's quite possible to complete it within two hours although for most players who take their time and want to complete all of the achievements more likely five to six hours. However short isn't always a bad thing and the game offers enough of an experience to make it worth playing. is a game with a unique and interesting theme that forces the players to fill in the gaps of the story, to ask their own questions and come up with their own answers. A game filled with beautiful black-and-white art design and a strange brooding atmosphere. It may not be a game that you will replay but it will be a game  you will remember.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the whole campaign on Steam Deck™ and despite the unknown compatibility status, it ran without any issues. _childDocuments_.review: This game could have been much more,lots of potentials in this game. for me its like 7.8/10they definitely can improve to game play like increase difficulty in boss fights and puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: I played this game on release and found it as an really good horror puzzle game. The 2D view of this game makes it really good, because it has an unique art style that, I had never seen in any horror game before. The story of this game is full of mistery,  with an open ending which is very fitting. The sound is very immersive and is appropriat to the invironment. The monsters in the deep of the sea and also the other objects to interact with are realistic and have a good style. The enemys are quite varied which is very good. So now some downsides of this game are that bosses you find are scary and wierd but also lame at the same time because the dont react quickly and dont have many attacks but only a puzzle to kill them (which is good but there could be more). I found the levels were too easy or at least for (me) and also not enough. There also could be even more things that you could do with the divers abilitie or maybe some more FISH to controll. So to the story again, I have not really and idea what it is but im thinking that this is about a trapped divers soul in a body trying to free other divers souls, also that you need to harvest the souls from monsters in the abyss of the ocean to insert them into a creepy looking machine, which gave me a bit of goosebumps. I was a bit confused how to get to different sides from the machine but I figured it out pretty fast, you just need to swimm in the direction on which side you have to enter. All in all I love it but there could be more, also worth the money
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, Silt was awesome, very nice artstyle, gothic looking with a fantastical flair, similar to sunless sea in that respect. I enjoyed it and figured out the achievements I missed in my first run through, and I will probably try to get them for a quick second run, now that I know what to do, I do feel like there could have been a bit more actual story told to us, rather than just leaving it fully open to interpretation, but it can be fun now and then to purely speculate on what is, was, might have been, and what could be. I look forward to the next project from Spiral Circus, and I hope they do something just as, if not more, wild than this first ride

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a pleasure to play.  It's beautiful, the sound design is very atmospheric and it's manged to hit  a very nice balance of being both deeply relaxing but with waves of tension that come at well plotted times to keep you engaged.I see a few other reviews remaking on bugginess and occasional soft locks...but I think the heart of the game rises far and above that as a criticism at the moment.  No doubt a patch will sort these things out...and in a world where Bethesda gets semi celebrated for it's quirky bugginess on a triple A release...I think an indy game from a tiny team on their debut release gets a pass for teething issues in the first few weeks.So far it's a delight...looking forward to getting deeper in if I can resist the urge to keep making my diver do somersaults and barrel rolls.Oh and it's formatted for ultrawidescreen...that's a big plus to us nerds out there who bought silly screens that want more tentacle than is healthy to look at.Now where did I put my Lovecraft books...getting a strange urge to pick them up...

_childDocuments_.review: I first opened this game on my Switch upon its release, but only just recently have I picked it up here to complete it. Likening SILT to LIMBO because of its art style or INSIDE because of its visual storytelling is a stretch. There is no “story” to SILT. It offers delicious art and ominous worldbuilding that amounts to nothing, as the ending answers no questions for the gamer. This, of course, will be important to you only if, like me, you’re a gamer who values the narrative in your experience. It’s disappointing to feel left hanging in that regard, but it’s something I could deal with and alone wouldn’t deter me from recommending SILT to others, as it is truly lovely to immerse in. It’s the wonky controls and haphazard glitches that have soiled an otherwise gorgeous experience, as the puzzles require precision to complete and survive—especially if you aim to grab all the achievements. Unique, but I’d say to grab it on sale when you catch one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a mysterious and creepy vibe, the music supports that same feel. Many screens/levels/boards you just pass through with no problem to solve. It's mystery wore off for me after a few hours and the actual game-play was very boring to me. I really wish people who developed games did some actual research on what makes playing games fun and worked their artistic ideas around that model. Or maybe they do but this game just wasn't for me?
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is a truly stunning game, with dark visuals that draw you in and impressive sound design that underpins a murky and sinister world. The simple puzzle solving acts more as a conduit for the artistic vision than to offer a legitimate challenge, but the experience is undoubtedly enjoyable despite the gameplay offering little in the way of difficulty. The story is a little vague and open to interpretation, but artistic-types will find it genuinely intriguing – the only real downside is that you’ll certainly be left wanting more, with the story reaching a haunting crescendo just when it feels like it could open the door to so much more. I would play another game set in the universe of Silt in a heartbeat.Full review:

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely short but enjoyable surreal horror puzzle game featuring underwater monsters and a story told entirely through visuals, similar to Hyper Light Drifter. A fun quick playthrough, but I'd wait until it's on sale or available freely, as it only has about an hour and a half to two hours of content.

_childDocuments_.review: A very pretty and mystifying experience. The art style, scares, and puzzles are all wonderfully made. The 3D model of the diver in certain lighting was jarring compared to the flat environment but not a huge deal. The story is incredibly cryptic. Even after completion of the game I have little idea of what was going on. Perhaps this is an issue of media comprehension but it is a shame that a casual play through stays so mysterious. Ultimately there is one thing I really want and that is more! More puzzles, more creatures, and more of the world to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an easy recommendation for fans of other similar indie games such as Limibo or Inside. Silt has some unique cool concepts which sets it apart from those similar games though. This is first and foremost a puzzle game with a neat art style. and a rather short one at that.  But it is a memorable diversion worth grabbing on a Steam sale. I did have a little trouble with one of the controls bugging out with one of the creatures (the stingray) that you control in several of the puzzles. Other than that the game was technically solid for me.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: The game time is about 3 hours in length. I took my time playing it and was comfortably under that time. The game really isn't worth getting unless it's on discount and you really just want to do anything to keep your thoughts busy for a while.For a horror game, it's not scary, at all. It's design is a good kind of creepy but it's just a visual choice. For a 'horror' game, there is shockingly nothing that will give you even the lightest of shivers or gasps. The puzzles are easy. The only challenge to the puzzles is an unethical practice of making the tools of a puzzle hidden to make it seem like the puzzle itself is difficult. An example is giving someone a lock to solve while tossing the lockpick they require out of their sight without indicating a lockpick may even be used. That's not a puzzle.What's good about the game is the visuals and audio. Both are good with the visuals being especially pleasing at times. The audio is good but not outstanding. What ultimately drops this game into the bad category is the story and gameplay. There is no story but it drops tons of visuals of animal statues and interesting building designs to make you think there is some sort of narrative but there isn't. Nothing is deeper than surface level, which is ironic for a game based deep under water. The gameplay is by far the worst offender, however. It's easy to have your game get stuck and have to be closed off and restarted. There are times when events that are meant to be triggered, don't trigger. Some of the bosses are beat with puzzles, as intended, but one of the bosses in particular is simply 'beat into submission'. That's not really a puzzling task. Overall, it's not terrible but it's below average and not something worth purchasing unless you're really scraping the bottom of the barrel of okay Steam Games.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is a decent game, but it does get a bit annoying in its later sections. Luckily, it's not long, so it doesn't hurt the game too much. I loved the artstyle though, and I'd say that's the main reason why it's worth playing. Looked wonderful on an OLED. It just feels like some of the later parts could've used more playtesting, but if you can look past that, not bad. I'd say get it during a sale.Edit: Another thing, loading happens way too often. You move a little bit, then it's a new area to load, move a little bit, new loading screen. It loads fast, but it's the interruption in gameplay that's annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little game. It's relatively short at 3.5 hours from start to finish, but it's SO Beautiful. And there is a background lore that is never fully explained... which I like. It contains an air of mystery which kept me intrigued. Aesthetically great, SFX & Music were fantastic, it was chill and yet puzzling and there wasn't a single point where I was bored or disengaged.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: SILT is an eerie underwater puzzle adventure akin to Inside, Limbo and Little Nightmares. It has great artwork, usage of black, shades of grey and yellowish white from the light sources set an interesting mood. I cannot stress how much I enjoyed the visuals.The puzzles aren't demanding most of the time. I had to look up one, the rest I could figure out by myself. If you don't expect to encounter the most challenging riddles ever you're fine. Similar to games like Inside and GRIS, SILT exclusively does environmental story telling. If the non-verbal exploration of mysterious worlds isn't for you, you might want to skip that one, if you enjoyed the comparisons mentioned above, treat yourself to this short underwater adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Great 2.5D puzzle game with a beautiful thalassophobic atmosphere. That said, it works perfectly with what it's got.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphic style and sound design that create a unique atmosphere. The puzzles are pretty simple though, which for me fits the game. _childDocuments_.review: Overall I recommend this game. Its short, interesting and very atmospheric. While it is shorter and less in depth than some similar games out there, I still highly recommend giving it a shot.Positives:- Has a similar aesthetic to Limbo and pulls it off quite well.- Interesting storytelling although there is little to go on.- Game play is fun and relatively satisfying.- Sound design is inoffensive and compliments the game.- Dev's agreed to put the game in the jingle jam over Christmas where profits all went to charity. This is how I obtained the game.Neutral:- Its short. The average player will probably complete this in 2-3 hours. I'm placing this in neutral as I believe a short game that doesn't require a massive time investment is appealing to a lot of people with busy lives.- The mechanics and game play would get old if the game was longer, however, since its short I didn't really have time to get bored of it.Bad:- Difficulty. The game in my opinion was a little to easy and the puzzles and "boss fights" were often trivial. I actually found the bosses towards the beginning of the game harder than the later ones. Although that's likely because I was still learning the mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Art style is incredibly well done, reminds me a lot of Swallow the Sea & even Limbo with the black & white colouring.But the part with the giant angler fish, I cannot get past without having to look through a walkthrough.Overall, it is good, but in that section, there's no indication or hint of where you're supposed to go or what you're supposed to do.But still a good art style, which is why I'm recommending this.

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is a very short and atmospheric game that has a very straight forward style. The puzzles gradually increase in difficulty, but never expand the mechanics too fast, nor too little. The game is not hard and the positives stem mostly from the visuals and atmosphere while the gameplay is quite slow with some up beats.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend SILT for its wonderful art and animations, for a very smooth experience and capturing the feeling of moving underwater perfectly with adequate controls. But it didn't get me emotionally and it also didn't start me thinking. While I don't need a game to spell it out or tell a coherent story, I didn't feel a connection, I never knew why I / my character was doing something other than that it was required by the game to continue. And because the different areas of the game were so disconnected - even random - I didn't feel any kind of achievement by the ending or its imagery.It's also a very easy and short game (3.5h for me) which isn't necessarily a bad thing. But I guess I'd have been happier with a "pure" underwater game with cool creatures, a sense of adventure and discovery and more varied, fleshed out use of the possession mechanics - and less metaphysical allusions to Egypt gods (Erich von Däniken’s “theories” come to mind) and your character as a savior figure. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great first game for an indie studio!The artistic style is the gem in this games crown. I personally loved the luminescent coral reef.At the same time the game is quite short. I've finished it in one and a half evenings. The puzzles don't break the flow of the game. They are not too difficult to make you stuck and not too simple to regard is a s a filler.I personally didn't get the plot of a game, some of the parts seemed "rushed", but they nonetheless kept a good pace.They nailed a mini ecosystem in some parts of a game, especially leeches and glow fish.The "windy" atmosphere in the overall underwater environment was bizarre, it made no sense. But hey, this world has masked-human-birds in an underwater tree!Now try to get a sense from that mess of a review, but I recommend that game Try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been craving something that will fill me with the same dread and wild curiosity as LIMBO and INSIDE. SILT goes above and beyond. It's incredible, a very nicely contained horror game with the ability to possess other creatures to awaken the machine. Play this game, it was an absolutely fantastic time.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! With a tense atmosphere, it holds the player from beginning to end. Minimalist aesthetics and sound effects recreate the feeling of solitude at the bottom of the ocean. My only criticisms refer to the campaign time (around 4h), the lack of more abyssal creatures and a little more explanation of the story, but these details do not compromise the experience. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is one of those short sidescroller puzzle games in the vein of limbo, inside, gris or white shadows. It deserves a mention alongside those great titles because it understands what these type of games need to be good & memorable, which is atmosphere. The gorgeous visuals combined with the downright perfect sound design (play with a headset!) make the whole experience incredibly immersive & moody. The game pulls you in and does not let go, not because of it's gameplay but because of the feeling it gives off. A strange sensation that is irresistably fascinating. Even though by the end nothing made sense i still felt engrossed in the 2,5 hour experience. Gameplay is fine and gets mixed up often enough to keep it from becoming monotenous. There's not much replayability though as the main joy comes from discovery so keep that in mind as you judge wether or not the game is worth it for you. I found the base price a bit steep for the lenght but the experience is so good that i'd recommend it to anyone, especially on a sale. The game is well made with steady framerates and no bugs so there's no reason to not give it a try if you like the aforementioned games. (Also don't be a douche and refund if you beat it in less than 2, indie devs deserve our support!)
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Silt and it feels like a bit of a hidden gem.It's a horror game in an unsettling way with a creepy atmosphere and more than a little Lovecraftian influence, though like the game it has the most obvious comparisons too, Limbo (a black & white puzzle game where you learn-by-dying), there were a few things that made me jump.It's not a long game, which I actually appreciated (puzzle games can sometimes out-stay their welcome for me) but if that's a concern for you then it's around 2-4 hours.  Also the puzzles aren't hugely challenging to figure out and sometimes rely more on timing and perfect execution, which can be a little frustrating, but checkpoints are, on the hole, appropriate.My only criticism was the very end.  I guess this is spoilery, but not being specific: it didn't quite land for me, as I was expecting it to conclude with a shocking / horrifying revelation but instead nothing really happened.  I guess because it doesn't really give a definitive answer as to what's going on it does leave the door open for a sequel, which would be welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Very detailed and good looking game-Good ominous atmosphere -Interesting gameplay mechanics that make up for some interesting puzzlesCons:-Quite short considering the amount you pay for it, other games of the same genre tend to offer a bit more in game length for the same price-The final chapter is really frustrating and annoying compared to the rest of it, and the mechanics feel quite janky and bad whenever you face such a spike in difficulty.-Story is almost non-existent, and what you get lacks any correlation and significance.Overall it's a fine game that I feel tried a lot to fit in with games of the same genre like Limbo and Inside, where it in some places succeed and other places fall behind. It tries leaving you with a story up for interpretation like Inside does for example, but the difference is that Inside gives you a lot to work with that you can puzzle together, while Silt just kinda throws a lot of stuff at you, with 0 indication that anything could fit together. Nevertheless though it's still a fine experience and I'd recommend getting it on sale if you want something you can beat in an afternoon. Just know that compared to other games in the same genre, it doesn't quite keep up with the ones at the top, but does a solid job trying to give you a unique experience, and being independent enough to where it has it's own twists on concepts
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt rides pretty heavily on atmosphere and artwork. The only narrative you're given is that you got to kill four giant monsters, of which only one of them could really be considered a boss fight Puzzles are pretty easy, and a lot of the time you can use fish to scout areas ahead safely, making Silt even easier. Finished in 3 hours of leisurely promenading through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing in terms of its atmosphere and artstyle. Visually it's an amazing, memorable experience that stands out among other Limbo-esque games.However, I did specify that it's an amazing experience *visually*, as the core gaming experience is less pleasant. To begin with, controlling your diver is clunky. That is not really a problem in most cases, but when precision is required, like in chapter 3 crab puzzle or in chapter 4 left tentacle puzzle, it really shines. Speaking of puzzles, my next issue is with puzzles. If you have not understood how chapter 2 leech puzzle was supposed to be solved and brute forced it or struggled with the awful crab controls in chapter 3 — I'm with you. Finally, I have to mention bugs. My custom controls reset every time I quit out of the game. The crabs kept getting stuck under production lines. I did not get the Machinist achievement despite it physically not being possible, as it is granted for solving one of the puzzles in chapter 3, and I have beat the game.I still would recommend this game, as it is purposefully slow, and I'm not a fan of being slowed down, so I feel as though I am not the target audience for this game. I still really enjoyed the visuals, I just hope that the developers actually work on the bugs. The game was great, just not entirely for my tastes.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles aren't particularly complex but they don't tend to be in this rough genre of games and are satisfying enough to complete, though I do offer a spoiler free caution of looking closely at things before you go forward. Game looks pretty much as good as it does in the preview images and of course you can tell how long it took me to beat it from this review. Story is pretty damn ambiguous but is that par for course.  Overall I did find it fun and short.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game - beautiful art and scene design, every frame of this game is an epic wallpaper in of itself.If you love puzzle games this is absolutely a great way to spend an evening or two - all of them are incredibly satisfying with loads of new mechanics as the game progresses. (They also have a great difficulty curve on them which makes you feel great when you solve later ones).If you're a fan of Inside or Limbo, this is absolutely the game for you. This game balances between deeply relaxing and terrifying at the same time (which is very impressive).
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: The beautiful artwork and haunting atmosphere fail to make up for the irritating, impenetrable gameplay elements, which feel more like an interruption of the player's sightseeing than anything. Just let us swim around looking at the spooky stuff!I'm loathe to review negatively honestly, this is so close to something mesmerizing and potentially memorable, but it just falls short. I really hope we can get something a bit more polished from this studio in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt was an interesting game to play:Pro's - Visually stunning. Just looking at the trailers and screenshots you can tell the art style is rich in detail and setting the atmospheresound design was also great and really kept me immersed especially when I was all by myself and all I could hear was the breathingCon's - The gameplay was lacking slightly. Not a bad, but, I had originally thought it was a adventure game which leaned towards horror. I found out that the main element of the game was actually puzzles. I'm not sure if I've just played too many puzzle games but didn't find them particularly difficult and the try and try again element of the puzzles made me lose my fear of dying and fear in general in the game. I think if they'd committed further towards the horror and adventure element as well as developed the possession ability further it would feel less gimicky and become a far more amazing game. That being said it was still good just saw a path for it to be even better
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to leave a bad review for this game, especially since it's clear a lot of work went into it. However its just not fun. The art is amazing and creates a stylish and unique atmosphere, but the game play is an absolute trudge to get through. Everything happens very slowly, swimming from one side the screen to the other feels like an eternity. When you die which will happen more than a few times, you will have to restart the area and swim VERY slowly to your objectives again. It's often unclear what the objective of a particular scene is, and the solution doesn't always make sense. I had to look up how to beat one boss and the answer left me a little confused. There are a number of non-puzzle areas that also have no direction of where to go.The puzzles themselves aren't rewarding, but feel more like an annoying obstacle.There is no story. The game is VERY short, like 1 - 3 hoursI would recommend checking this out if its on sale for closer to $5.99, but $14.99 is just way too much.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: This game has such a beautiful style that I could not get enough of it! I can't understand annoying complaining that this game is short. If you played through this game you looked at all the hand drawn practically everything! So I don't know why you think the insane amount of time it must have taken to do what this game has was not good enough. Also the price alone is well worth the clear effort put in if not just for the "experience" When I drop this kind of money on a game especially one like this I know what I am getting myself into. I would rather play 100 games like this then pay the same price or way more to get less time of entertainment from a movie. Pros1. The incredible hand drawn art style (I have become obsessed with this artist now)2. Immersive sounds and music3. Creature designs that will leave you feeling in awe to uncomfortable4. The whole areas you see and visit are just amazing to exploreCons.1. Personal opinion of course but you are going to get a cryptic story. I would at least have liked to have someone what of an idea what was happening. But this doesn't take away form the game in the slightest!2. Very few "puzzles" felt annoying (spent some longer time then I would have liked but can honestly blame myself for that
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Abzu meets LimboSilt is a dark puzzle solving game with no real story to speak of other than a few lines at the game's inception.That being said it attempts a form of environmental story telling though it doesn't weave a cohesive story that can be followed, such as Journey, this vagueness can be improved upon.Gameplay requires you move, faster or slower, switch on your flashlight and most importantly possess other creatures.The mechanic is well executed though the number of possessable creatures is fairly limited with some creatures being more or less endemic to their regions. That being said they all provide a unique function which is good game design.Enemies are defeated or avoided using possession puzzle-solving, this is done well, though tolerances in some areas such as the worm tunnels are very tight and could be frustrating to some.Playtime is short but I do not see this as a negative, this is a game for the ambience, not the playtime. You will notice and stay for the atmosphere. Replayability is fairly limited with missing an achievement or going for a no death run being the drawing factors.The greatest asset of this game is without doubt the art direction, monochrome, but painstakingly detailed through most of the game with an eerie beauty that draws your attention, the occasional low music tones add to this ambience. There are a few areas that are not to par with others but overall it is amazing.Was it worth what I paid, in my opinion yes, the work done in this game deserves it, but mileage may vary by how deeply you value the overall vs the rough edges in gameplay.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is a beautiful experience. From an artistic standpoint, it is simply GORGEOUS to look at. The atmosphere they created was brilliant, a little creepy but also mysterious. It really draws you in. I enjoyed playing through the whole game and the subtle story and unique experience was very fun. I enjoyed the puzzles too, it was challenging but not too difficult. I do wish the game was a bit longer. Once I finished, I was sad it was over, and given the price tag, I do think it could've been longer. I did also struggle with the controls being all on the left side, I recommend changing the default keys you play with. Still, the experience was worth it, in my opinion. I think the art and the stunning visuals make up for the shortness of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game. The puzzle difficulty stays pretty constant, that difficulty being kinda easy. Visually very good, some of the puzzles are pretty satisfying but the "boss" fights are extremely easy and disappointing, aside from the first one. While a lot of the non boss puzzles have a decent depth in their complexity, the last 3 bosses are ridiculously simple, essentially "do this mechanic we used in complex puzzles, but do it in the most basic way a bunch of times with maybe one obstacle." Story is alright, hard to make sense of, however, I think it is an interesting one that I would enjoy looking into more. Maybe not worth the price though, especially for the length of the game
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a very pretty greyscale art, each area looks beautiful but it clashes in some places with the underwater thematic,For example, the third area is like sunken industrial factory and there's no real explanation of why. There's also an "intermission" area which is temple-like but the statues' art clashes heavily with the rest of the game.As for the music, it fits the underwater atmosphere but it's not memorable.This game doesn't really have a proper story (or if it has, it eluded me), only a concept of surreal ocean that is so random at times that you won't know what to make out of it. so if you're not into very abstract artsy games, you might end up feeling like you got nothing from it other than just an art showcase.The gameplay is  basically: While the fish gimmick it's interesting at first, unfortunately, it gets old very fast due to the fact that each fish's skill isn't versatile (Fish A is always used to cut ropes, fish B will always be just there to break a wall). This means mechanic wise, it becomes repetitive and even taking the novelty away from new areas as you see obstacles or fishes you've seen before and connect the dots to predict the puzzle in its totality.As for controls, I played this in a keyboard and it felt good (doesn't use the mouse). The gameplay itself is on the slow side so I didn't need to plug my controller.I wouldn't recommend it to anyone that gives priority to gameplay or needs clear story to enjoy the ride. If you want to buy it, it will depend on how much value you want to give to visuals because that's what's carrying this game the most.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun game. Some might compare it to Limbo, and while not wrong aesthetically, the game mechanics are very different. I finished the game in one setting, about 3 hours. The puzzles weren't terribly hard, but grew increasingly more difficult over time. I would say this is a good intro into puzzle games for people who may not have a lot of experience in these types. The sound and ambiance were great. The controls took a bit of gettting used to because it's both WASD and Arrrows (no mouse) but once you get the hang of it, it works just fine. I had been waiting for this game for some time, and I was pleased with how the developer put it all together. 10/10 worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Going to start by saying the art and atmosphere is amazing in this. Love the ambience and the OST.That being said, there is *literally* no story here. You wake up with the ability to possess other creatures and have to fight giant boss monsters to take their souls and "awaken the great machine". No explanation of why, who we are, nothing. If this game was longer or the puzzles more varied than I would recommend, but otherwise there's really nothing here.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond the stunning visuals and exploration of creepy deep seascapes, I also really enjoyed the unexpectedly soothing ambience created by the hypnotic sound design, dark colour palette, and gently drifting player movement.The puzzles were a nice addition and contrary to some other reviewers I found that they progressed in complexity at a good rate to a level that was challenging but not excessively difficult - I just regret that there weren't a few more of the satisfyingly tricky puzzles thrown in.A short and sweet indie gem crafted with plenty of attention to detail.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: When I picked up Silt I was looking to recapture the enjoyment of games like Limbo and Inside, and it didn't disappoint on that score.  It isn't as creepy or tension riven as those titles, but has a strong sense of mystery, strange and unsettling hand drawn backdrops, and a brilliant set of deep sea sound effects.The puzzles are not too demanding but there's a real sense of achievement when you pick them apart, especially as there is no "hand-holding".  Here is your ability and that of the other creatures, go play with them and see what you can and cannot do with them.I would have liked it to be a longer game, but that is only a minor ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and it was well worth it for the money.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a fairly creepy and beautiful (in some unsettling sense) short puzzle game with not too much to otherwise offer. It is about 3 hours long. It provided basically no story and left me confused and disappointed with the ending. Puzzles are unique and interesting but pretty easily and sometimes frustrating/repetitive. CDN$ 17.49 is too much for a game of this length and lack of intriguing narrative. If you are willing to pay ~5$/hr for an interesting but vague, easy, and short puzzle game go for it. I'd recommend you look up gameplay for it first and keep by comments in mind :)
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Length <1hr 40minSilt is a 2D game in which the player will be swimming in the deep ocean surrounded by a variety of fish. Each fish the player is capable of taking control of and using their power to progress. The deep ocean is filled with dangers and the player is right there on the food chain.Silt feels similar to Limbo, where you need to learn the hazards of the level in order to progress while also having puzzles to complete. While the game has a lot more planning as the player needs to work out what fish they need to utilise in order to progress further. This is seen at its strongest in the boss battles, none are long but each require a unique use of the fishes to deal with themWhile the game does need a lot of planning on how to progress through rooms the main challenge of the game I found was timing. You will need to escape from fish and avoid others as you go through the tight caverns. At times this was difficult and annoying, the player does not usually die, it’s the fish you control and the player can quickly grab another.The game looks amazing, the bosses really stand out and look otherworldly, especially the later ones that become more mechanical in design. While the background of the otherworldly kingdom is really mysterious, the cathedral-like eternal structure which is used to hold the souls of the giant creatures is amazing.While playing I have only seen one bug, though I did also manage to softlock the game once. Generally the bug was a fish literally attacking me through walls, not sure how this happened but it did happen multiple times, the giant worm things that chase you can kill you through walls. While I got softlocked when having to use light to move through barriers, I got trapped inside with no way of escape but resetting the game.Overall Silt has been a really fun game with some great puzzles that really make you think how to use the characters. Although the game has left me malding multiple times with constant deaths and finding it hard to progress, the problems were not impossible, it was only a challenge I had to overcome. Visually there are a lot of great scenes and the giant bosses look amazing and diverse, really worth the play although the game is not long.If you wish to see some of the gameplay below is my playthrough:Looking for horror games worth playing check out my expanding Curator page for everything that I have played and reviewed, 100+ and counting:
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun and creepy but not creepy enough. I felt that it ended very quickly as well. It's a nice little game and it took me 4 hours to complete. I was hoping after the final act that there would be something else, maybe two-four more acts to complete the "what the heck is going on" kind of question I had. I didn't feel that I really understood why or what was going on when it was over. The puzzles are pretty simple but also fun. For the price I would recommend it if you like Limbo and Inside but just know it's a small game.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting game! It has a very good artstyle that I have never seen in any game before, and I think the game is worth playing simply because of that. The sound design sets the mood well, the story is quite interesting and I was very curious to see what was going to happen next when I played the game. The game is pretty short and the gameplay hasn't got much to offer though, and mostly consits of swimming and taking control over strange underwater creatures, but those are pretty much my only complaints. To conclude, this is definetily a game worth checking out if you have some time and money to spend! I'll give it a 7,2/10
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: A short game (completed in 4 hours), but some excellent graphics and sound make for an immersive game.A puzzle game with some nice twists. Some tough areas that rely on good timing (and some luck). Some helpful hints along the early stages, but the rest you have to work out yourself (not too.... difficult).Artwork is great and the ambient sounds really fit in well.Some nice (tricky) Steam achievements if you want to complete the gameIf using keyboard, be careful about hitting the possess key too quickly instead of holding it (in some areas).
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: A very high quality, although short game from a studio of 2 guys. Definitely worth your buck if you like high quality indie games in general, and gloomy underwater diving. The game is full of tense abyssal atmosphere. Takes your mind completely into it's world, making you feel like you're actually swimming among all the inhabitants of the deep, that live in this branch, plant and cavern filled wasteland.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! The atmosphere was haunting and beautiful and the graphics were gorgeous. The ability to possess different creatures was a really fun game mechanic and worked incredibly well with the dark, deep sea tones of the game. It was short and sweet and I highly recommend, especially to fans of Limbo and other similar games.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game which has a great dark atmosphere. It manly consist of light puzzling. You need to think what to do next, but nothing had me stomped for more than a minute or two. I would say it is even too simple and it sometimes requires you to basically repeat doing the same thing twice or thrice, which felt boring. However, the game as a whole don't overstay its welcome, so it is not that big of a deal. PC controls surely could be improved, they feel quite clunky. When I switched to pad it immediately felt better.So, gameplay wise it was average, but original art and atmosphere were enough to keep me engaged.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt has a wonderfully beautiful environment and atmosphere. It's an awe-inspiring puzzle platformer where you'll see something very weird and either run away from it or figure out how to use it to your advantage. I can't stress enough how beautiful all of the scenery and creatures are and to me the atmosphere is unlike anything I've seen before in any media.The gameplay itself is challenging enough to keep me engaged and interested in exploring this strange environment. There's been a few puzzles that make me feel quite clever when I solve them. I haven't beat the game yet but would imagine I'm getting close to the end and I'm very much looking forward to it.I'd highly recommend to anyone who looks at the art style and wants to see more of it! The exploration alone is well worth the cost of admission :)
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, though I would have preferred if they leaned more heavily into the deep sea abyss setting. Its awfully bright for the bottom of the ocean, and there's tons of more interesting creatures in our own ocean they could have pulled from. (That "gulper eel" was not a gulper eel at all! The real thing is way scarier looking!)Its also fairly buggy. I got softlocked a couple times, but luckily it autosaves at the beginning of every room, so you can just quit or die and try again.
_childDocuments_.name: SILT

_childDocuments_.review: Silt is a puzzle-adventure set deep within a harrowing ocean abyss, where you play as a lone diver searching the deep and exploring dangerous waters to uncover long-forgotten mysteries. But the diver has a secret. Harnessing an unusual power, you’ll be able to possess sea creatures that roam the ocean void, discovering new creatures and using their unique abilities to solve puzzles, traverse the environment, and make your way deeper into the darkness.

name: Sons Of The Forest
detailed_description: An entirely new experience from the makers of the ‘The Forest’ Sent to find a missing billionaire on a remote island, you find yourself in a cannibal-infested hellscape. Craft, build, and struggle to survive, alone or with friends, in this terrifying new open-world survival horror simulator. A Survival Horror Simulator Experience complete freedom to tackle the world how you want. You decide what you do, where to go and how best to survive. There are no NPC's barking orders at you or giving you missions you don't want to do. You give the orders, you choose what happens next. Fight Demons Enter a world where nowhere is safe and fight against a range of mutated creatures, some who are almost human like, and others who are like nothing you have ever seen before. Armed with pistols, axes, stun batons and more, protect yourself and those you care for. Build and Craft Feel every interaction; Break sticks to make fires. Use an axe to cut out windows and floors. Build a small cabin, or a sea-side compound, the choice is yours. Changing Seasons Pluck fresh salmon directly from streams in spring and summer. Collect and store meat for the cold winter months. You're not alone on this island, so as winter rolls in and food and resources become scarce you won't be the only one looking for a meal. Co-op Gameplay Survive alone, or with friends. Share items and work together to build defenses. Bring back-up to explore above and below ground.

_childDocuments_.review: A game where you must survive cannibals... How ironic when you turn around, proceed to bash their skull in then become the cannibal yourself. The only game where it's okay to kill humans and eat them, 100/10 highly recommend.Jokes aside this game takes the survival / horror experience to another level, the insane building mechanics combined with the jaw dropping environments from the terrifying caves to the lush and dense forests. It all comes together to make a survival experience unlike other games can do. This game is also better with friends! Keep in mind this game is early access (as of this review) I have personally experienced some bugs, EX: Not being able to place down stick pathsEX: Not being able to interactEX: Arms glitched when drinking and opening inventory These are pretty harmless and fix when restarting the game but still pretty annoying, as a fan of the series I can ignore these very little issues and I am sure they will get fixed in the future.If your looking for a fun survival / horror game this is your game to get!

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is an excellent survival horror game that will keep you on the edge of your seat with excitement and fear. Developed by Endnight Games, this sequel to The Forest takes players on a thrilling adventure in a vast, open world filled with danger and mystery.What sets Sons of the Forest apart from other survival horror games is its multiplayer gameplay. Playing with friends makes the game even more enjoyable and hilarious as you work together to survive against all odds. The game's mechanics and graphics are top-notch, providing a truly immersive experience that is sure to keep you entertained for hours.Exploring the game's environment is one of the most enjoyable aspects of Sons of the Forest. As you gather resources and craft items, you'll discover new areas and secrets that will keep you coming back for more. The game's storyline is also captivating, keeping you engaged as you unravel the mysteries of the forest and its inhabitants.Overall, Sons of the Forest is an exceptional game that is well worth playing. Whether you're a fan of survival horror or just looking for a fun game to play with friends, Sons of the Forest has something for everyone. So grab some friends and dive into the world of Sons of the Forest for an unforgettable gaming experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that the new building system is amazing; placing each log by hand really made it feel like you were building a base by hand. The enemies are just as scary and fun to fight, if not better than the previous forest title. I gave this a negative review because of the sheer size and emptiness of the map and the lack of content found in caves throughout; many caves had fun dungeon-crawling adventures with rewarding loot at the end. Many others were just one room with a few boxes of average loot, which was very disappointing, especially after walking for what felt like five to ten minutes through an almost empty forest. Overall it's not a bad experience but the oversized map and lack of full caves made it a bit frustrating and boring at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the forest might be a little janky, but it has it's own charm and will immerse you in a way you didn't think was possible. There are some gauges to watch for (healt, stamina), but no x-ray vision, no healt bar on top of ennemies, none of that rpg thing.Enemies LOOK like they take damage, and hitting them FEELS satisfying. The gameplay is nice, but not on like mw2 level where you go fast as an f1 car with a 50pounds sniper rifle. At first, the game might be unforgiving. However, you will learn your way trought it and it has a pretty nice skill celing. Sure, it's not pvp (for now, unless you get into games that do I guess), but the cannibals will give you quite a challenge. I think that what was lacking in the first game was some company, and they fixed that on part with the ai helper (kelvin) and miss mysterious (virginia), who'll slaughter your enemies when you just want to build your little shack peacefully. It is totally worth full price, even on early access, just for the sheer amount of things to try (gameplay wise) and sandbox possibilities. Sure, it's not the best building mecanics, game runs a little rich on graphics (but looks dam good), but in any case:This is a game you want in your steam library, because you'll get back to it every so often (in my opinion).- No lootboxes.- No DLC.- An indie dev that seems to care about the community and feedback.- Pure game dev passion.Seriously, this one is a gem. _childDocuments_.review: I've found this game to be a great survival experience. I love the attention to detail throughout, the way crafting handles is, the weather system and it's interaction with the world. (Previously thought I'd be safe on the island in the lake... Then the lake froze over come winter.) Sure there's a few bugs, but it's early access and the next planned update hasn't even dropped yet. My only gripe with the game itself is the story. Or sort of lack of one? You explore and find notes and hints at a greater threat and the longer you're on the island the more prominent the threat becomes which could almost be seen as a descent into your own madness. There's little explanation for why or how things are and it's left up to your interpretation. And the ending? Completely out in left field and left me questioning 'thats it? That doesn't explain anything' and for whatever reason you can choose to stay or you can choose to leave. Why stay? You don't have much of a story reason to stay.All in all, the gameplay itself is enjoyable for me. The game runs really well for me, even when playing with up to 7 players being hosted and me streaming the game through discord with no dedicated streaming rig. The story left me wondering if they just threw it on there last minute. I never played the first forest though, so perhaps that could be it? I don't know.

_childDocuments_.review: The thing about intrusive thoughts is, that you shouldn't act on them.However.... I have been able to do things "accidentally."  I feel like I have committed atrocities that would make a majority of people question my character.  The older I get, I feel like certain freedoms are stripped, not only physical freedoms, but mental as well.  I was able to peruse these wares in real time.  I started with the best intentions, and soon realized that the leash was off.  After I ate my first man flesh(accidentally), I realized I regained my will to pursue different avenues of this wondrous entitlement.I feel like I have been dug out of the cemented earth.  Unearthed, unscathed, I arose anew into the arms of the sun.  I no longer feared the tribals that littered the land.  I was an animal myself.  I realized that life was filled to the brim of possibilities.  I started slow, almost cautious.  It's as if my parents were silently looking over my shoulder, but alas, I had not a care in the world.It comes in waves.  The hunger, not just for sustenance, but for trying new obstacles.  Armed with my newfound hope for the future, I built wondrous things.  With my comrades, my family, I built ungodly things.  I enhanced the human experience.  Every spear thrust, every lively spark of my stun rod, further drove me into madness.  A madness I embraced.Building only filled a small void, although creative, was enjoyable.  I yearned for what is best in life.It wasn't the open steppe, or a fleet horse, or the wind in my hair.It was.... Crush your enemies. See them driven before you. Hear the lamentations of their women.And to think..... I only invested $30.  What a time to be alive.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to... well "the Island", another location in The Forest franchise that, well, for <insert reason> is cannibal-infested and mutant-ridden as well!After a helicopter accident, you are left stranded in this "paradise". This time you aren't alone though: Kelvin, one of your crew members, survived with some serious brain damage. He will follow simple commands an help you building/maintaining a base. I absolutely loved The Forest, but Sons of the Forest blows it out of the water. The building system was MAJORLY improved, graphics are in another level. Mutants and caves are WAY CREEPIER. The sounds, ambience, lightining were all improved and crawling a cave for the first time gave me chills the whole time. And Kelvin's brain damage... bots are usually dumb, but Kelvin is  That was pure genius. The behaviour of the Cannibals is awesome too: they can be intimidated, scared, might run away, or plead for mercy. There is a tribe system, they even mourn or avenge dead friends. The story telling style from the first game was kept, but there are some cutscenes (loved the last one). Expect more characters though! Small spoiler:  As a downside, some of the building resources are underutilized. The game gets easy rather quickly, there is no scarcity of anything and you don't *-need-* to build a base (though... why wouldn't you?!?!). Performance-wise it is lacking some optimization (lots of stuttering on my Laptop RTX 4070). The game is constantly being patched and improved though.Worked on Linux via Proton with the aforementioned stuttering. Achievements were all great and fun except for "I Like Blisters". WTF was that?SotF is a rich game, full of new ideas, interesting AI behaviour, beautiful scenery, great horror, good story, fun building... Endnight Games, please, feel kissed by this bearded nerd. Keep doing this, we need more game devs like you guys!

_childDocuments_.review: Really had a lot of fun with this game. If you're looking for more The Forest, this game does the trick. It is a must to play with 3 or more friends and just wander the woods. This game really is the fun of being lost in the woods, but with the added bonus of there being something to find or do out there. Exploring the island never stops being a joy, and the game itself is beautiful. The monsters are also ghastly and unique, and the comedic elements of the game are very enjoyably implemented.I have some gripes. The story does not cohere, certainly not in a satisfying way, so you're left with a sense of "huh, that's odd". The central antagonist of the game, for example, is not really introduced or explained outside of some reading material you may or may not find. There are also a number of things you can do, build, use, or interact with, that I had no clue were in the game until I had finished it and read posts from the community. These kinds of things should be able to be discovered in-game in a reasonable way. The challenge is also very light, and could've really gone for stronger or more numerous enemies - something to use the weapons and tools we've crafted. The idea of upgrading anything, for example, seemed laughable due to how overpowered we already were.So, I hope they address some of these in the next game, but I also am very much looking forward to the next game. This is such a fun multiplayer series.

_childDocuments_.review: feels like a DLC to the original game, failing to take cues in the years of evolution in the survival genre boom propagated by Endnight’s own original game  There is new mutants, firearms, a vast, lusciously beautiful but unnecessarily big and empty map, seasons and weather system, a redesigned, better custom building system, NPCs to make you company, and sadly, the same almost ten year old survival system from the original The Forest. I suggest you buy this only if you’re after the absolute most similar The Forest experience. If you’re after a spiritual successor, that builds upon what the original game laid out and makes something even greater, fun and impressive, I suggest the similarly priced The game inherits almost everything the original game had: hunger, thirst and energy stats define your character’s available stamina, wild berries, mushrooms and animals can all be used to recover hunger & health, and be a source of crafting recipes such as beneficial herb mixes and pelts for crafting armor. The inventory bag is now bigger than ever, allowing that satisfaction of decking out your inventory even more enjoyable, also it has RGB gamer lights for those dark times ;).Speaking of which, the cannibals are now split into two, there’s the normal tribesman-like cannibals that were featured in the first game, and there’s a new, creepier, faceless nude cave dwellers similar to Sandie’s clients in Edgar Wright’s ‘Last Night in Soho’, which are also the mutant enemies this time around, that are even more weird than the first ones seen in the original game, and the cannibals seem to have a strife with their countrymen, since they can be seen on the overworld tied up to a post on the cannibal camps scattered throughout the island.Combat is essentially the same as the first game with a few additions, a new stun baton, a pistol, shotgun, taser, tall stronger enemies, and real-time dismemberment.If you’re a hoarder and the new expanded bag is not enough to store all your guns, limbs, bombs and axes, you’ll need to build a base, and to help you with that we now have NPCs! Crash landed with you, Kelvin is a fellow agent who suffered a concussion and blown eardrums, leaving him with a catatonic stare at the horizon but functional enough for you to give him orders, such as follow you, stay, clear an area and grab resources for you, like sticks, logs, rocks and berries, allowing you to build a base in single player faster than in the original game, keep in mind that Kelvin is also available in multiplayer as well. There is also a shy, curious, mutant woman that you start to see after one or two days in the island, that can be interacted with after some time and is able to use firearms to help you defend your base.When it comes to base building, the custom building aspect of the first game has been expanded, instead of deploying blueprints of walls and fences out of a book, you now physically place the logs on the ground, stack them on top of each other if building a wall is your intent, and then cut them horizontally or vertically with your axe to form a window or a door respectively, the same principle applies to fences with sticks or bones. This not only expands what you can do with the custom buildings but also increases the player immersion. The pre-made blueprints for shelters, log cabins and treehouses are all still available, so it’s great for everyone, be it for those who just want a quick shelter, those who want to have a unique manor or someone in between.I am happy to say that, despite being in early access, I had a pretty stable single-player experience, with just one game breaking bug that got me killed.With that said, I have other issues with the game that prevents me from recommending it if you’re after a new and improved The Forest game, the most significant one being the map size and lack of reliable transportation. The map is big and beautiful, but mostly empty, you can find caves and points of interest using your new GPS and use the beaten paths to reach them, and in the process find some cannibal settlements and past human encampment, but that’s it. As I read by other fellow players, it feels like the map is twice as big, but have the same amount of POIs in the first game, which, combined with the lack of transportation, feels utterly pointless to have a map this big. Of course you have a zipline gun, and printable sled (which some players thought it was a log sled, but in reality it’s a human sled that you can use to slide down rivers and hills just like a tortoise shell in the original game) , but these are methods of travel that only works if you’re going downhill, and most of the time you need to go up the island mountains. My optimistic thinking is that they will justify the map size by adding more settlements, POIs and a faster, reliable method of transportation like a small helicopter, seen in games like ‘Far Cry 4’ and ‘Stranded Deep’, since driving through thick forests with a golf cart doesn’t seem that much more efficient.I also talked about how great the new building aspects of the game are, but in reality there is no need to build a base, just like in The Forest you can crash land in the island, immediately eat and drink what you have and be off to a nearby cave getting all the items you need to beat the game, building a base offers no rewards other than something to brag about. I would think this would be remediated by an also expanded survival system, which would force you to rest occasionally, but since eating is still as simple as hunting food, killing it and then cooking, bases are pointless. If you take Green Hell for example, which I believe took inspiration in The Forest, has the hunger divided into fats, proteins and carbohydrates, which need to be sourced separately, instead of a one stop solution found in both The Forest games. Also in Green Hell, the player needs to manage other affliction from insects and infections you get from living in a forest, of course the island fauna and flora isn’t like Green Hell’s Amazon forest, but it still IS a forest.The expanded bag is great, but the static camera has now been replaced with a slow moving and potentially nausea inducing camera that follows your mouse, which I got used to but dislike it wholeheartedly. I’m a pretty fast The Forest player and having to wait for my camera to move around as I click for the items to combine is frustrating, it’s even worse when I am searching for a new item that I don’t know where it sits on the inventory yet. The only reason I can see this being implemented is that the inventory bag in now bigger, meaning the static camera would need to be positioned farther out or use a higher FOV, which would make some of the items small and difficult to click. I don’t think the moving camera is a great solution, but since it’s already implemented, I would suggest to give the players options to toggle between a moving and a static camera, and increase the size of some items in the static camera if needed.The new quick access bag is great for finding multiple items without fully opening the inventory, but it doesn’t mean it justifies getting rid of hotkeys, especially in combat situations. This is without a doubt a top priority for version 1.0 of the game.Overall Sons of the Forest as it currently stands is dangerously similar to the original game, it introduced some new toys for players to have fun, a bigger, beautiful yet empty map, a new story to uncover, a better and immersive building system, NPC’s to help the player, but failed to evolve the core element of the game, which is survival. I would think Endnight would take the years of evolution of the survival genre since the inception of The Forest and work it’s way into their new game, but it’s not the case here. It feels like a DLC for the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: the good: my previous review mentioned the game being un-optimized, it is optimized now so i'd like to shift my review to the actual content of the game.  Let me start off by saying it is a great game and definitely a great successor to 'the forest' a game i have over 800+ hours in.  This a perfect blend of survival craft/combat and horror.  Just surviving in this world,m finding new enemies, new things to craft and new locations/caves is entertaining enough, especially because the world is beautiful and the traps are super satisfying to play around with.  However, the fun doesn't stop there because there is also an (admittedly bare bones) non-linear story line that is picked up on by finding notes, newspaper clippings, locations, and even camcorder videos.  They do a really good job of making the island feel alive with all sorts of animals and cannibal mobs.things I would change: I personally think the motivation of the story of 'the forest', the game before this one, was much stronger than this one.  I legit wanted to get through the story to save my son.  In this one, you're just a private security company hired to find some rich dude ... not as good of a motivating factor off the rip imo.  Additionally, the forest' received updates and spent a longer time in early access and it feels like there were more crafting options, getting different biomes and animals was way more important and impactful in the first as well, now you only get meat from most and can only skin deer and moose (super lame and makes crafting less exploration based).  no more carefully aiming your spear to get those rabbit pelts (one of the most challenging and one of my favorite parts of the game)Summation: this is a fantastic horror survival craft blended with fun combat and a bare bones story.  While it is generally a good successor of 'the forest' I will say that it does not feel like as much of a passion project as the first.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't recommend this game just yet. My playtime says 19 hours but I'm pretty bad about leaving a game on the home screen and doing other things so I probably have about 15 hours of actual playtime. Game could have been beaten in a few hours.I loved the first game and when I found out this was getting released soon, I was very excited but after playing and beating the story I'm disappointed. For a game that has been being worked on for years I was surprised at the content they decided not to release. I completely understand Early Access and I play many of them but this isn't the problem. The devs have left out key things that the first game had and I don't understand why. Hot keys and log sleds were two things I missed the most. I don't understand how things from the first game don't get automatically added into the new game. And for people to say "it's early access! It'll be added!" is a cop out in my opinion. There's no reason we should be missing key elements from the first game.The story is terrible. At the end I was confused at what was going on and who was who. The story needs to be reworked. Unless you read what others are saying you have no idea what's happening. Honestly I couldn't have cared less about the story if I tried and that's disappointing because I was invested in the first story. I just feel like this game dropped the ball. Base building is absolutely pointless so it's no wonder they didn't add half the stuff from the first game. My boyfriend and I spent time building a base (this took a couple hours so there's some of that 15 hour play time) and make shelves for storage, only to never have to come back to the base because there's so much loot EVERYWHERE. There's really no reason to ration it either plus even watching a streamer play on HARD mode they had just as much loot as we did and we played on normal. I wish there was a reason to build a base but there's not. It's not like in 7 Days to Die where you have a hoard you HAVE to defend from every 7 days. Cannibals can walk into your base, through the door, have a seat, eat your food, sleep in your bed and you can't stop them (besides killing them of course). Also you can't give Kelvin a gun or a weapon of any sort. Honestly he was more trouble than he was worth. Most of the time he just collected items or stayed at the camp because he was a liability. Virginia at least could help you defend if you were out and about (if she was even near you with a lot of the time she isn't). Could have used her in the bunkers!Idk. I just can't recommend this game right now. Not for $30. Get it for $20 and have a good couple hours of real game play but most of it is spent running around a very empty world and finding the shovel so you can literally unlock everything.Give it another 6 months or a year and hopefully it'll be ready to play. Until then, just avoid it.
