_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS A SHOCKING WASTE OF TIMEthe forest 2 is an absolute mess of half arsed, poorly executed "realism" based gameplay mechanics that make no sense, dont work, and serve as an antithesis to the actual gameplay - let me explain the forest creates its entire identity around realism, buildings are made from singular segments of felled trees, beds and furnature fashioned from sticks, powerful firearms with attachments, and hard to come by ammo. clothes for different elements, seasons, large caves to explore, etc.now let me explain why none of this worksstarting with the firearms - jesus christ what a mess, guns have attachments yes, but also not really. you can get a flash light silencer and a laser, to put on the pistol, and the shotgun. both require a rail before you can use them, the flashlight mounts on the bottom of the pistol, and does almost nothing in the way of light, this is because the devs didnt want it to need batteries, so they had to nerf how much light it gives making it useless, then in what to me seems like the most insane and outlandish MESS ive ever seen in an FPS, the laser is mounted ON THE TOP RAIL OF ALL THE FIREARMS making it impossible to see during ADS, when you crouch the location of your ads moves SIGNIFICANTLY making it very difficult to even know where your bullets are going, further more both the 9mm pistol and the revolver use 9mm ammo, and do vastly different damage, so much for that realism. the silencer removes almost all sound from your gun, making it feel like a bb gun. the building - not much better here, im guessing the philosophy of this game is take what kinda worked in the first game and then dial up the tedium as high as possible, they removed the log sled so you have to truck these puppies by hand, i guess they removed the log sled for the sake of realism, dragging half a dozen logs on the ground isnt very realistic, but neither is hoisting 2 on your shoulder, and then throwing them into a large pile, that you then progressively biff further towards your base, thats NOT realistic, its just brain numbingly boring. this might not be so bad if there where ANY other building materials other than sticks, log cabins are made of EXCLUSIVELY logs, and approx 100 of them, and thats a small cabin too, the roofs could have atleast been made of leaves or something but not, full ass logs. speaking of leaves they have NO USE i finished the game with like 600 in my inventory. this gets even worse when you looks at a camp fire, dear jesus the game makes you manually break sticks in half, and then light them on fire, very realistic right? nope. its 4 sticks, the fire is made from 4 sticks, and if often burns down to 2 sticks, resulting in the most LAST GEN camp fire ive ever seen. this game is FILLED with problems like this, game mechanics obviously done in the name of realism, but then delivered in ways that arent realistic, remember that cool stick bed i mentioned earlier? yeah its about 3 feet long, only suitable for curling up in the fetal position when you cant face manually trucking anymore logs. the map - 4x bigger, 10x emptierthe caves - less interesting, less complex, less of them in general, my friends and i had so much fun arguing about where the heck we were in the last game in a cave, in this one all caves are simply forward, and back. you cant get lost. season - theyre cool but totally pointless, my friends and i spent all autumn "prepping" for expected food shortages during winter, there was none. nothing changed except the lakes froze making it hard to find water, as this game has NO WAY TO STORE OR COLLECT WATER FROM RAIN.HUGE letdown, this game is a waste of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: most underwhelming game of all time.  >take over 4 years to develop what you can barely call a demo atm>postpone multiple times>claim its complete and needs polishing >2 weeks before release label it as EA to save face>game is a complete shell of the first oneMany features are missing, content that was in the first game is non-existent. The map is huge with no reason to explore it, as all the items/important caves are in the starting areas, and there's just a few items you need to actually complete the game. 70% of the map is just fluff, most caves are just one room with some basic loot you can get anywhere. Restarting the game still respawns items, the survival aspect has been dumbed down, you can eat raw meat and drink stale water from ponds with no ability to craft water collectors anymore. Building is confusing and barebones, although it's just "okay" once you figure it out. The beam/support system is frustrating and building ceilings is dreadful. You literally duplicate logs by building basic furniture.  AI is nowhere near as good as they hyped it up to be, they're the same boring cannibals that sometimes do an action that makes you go "huh, cool, I guess" for the first time, but for the most part they're just an annoyance that mess with you while you're busy building. You can't even attempt to be friendly with them because even if you choose to leave them be, they'll attack you out of nowhere and drain your health.Virginia and Kelvin don't do a whole lot, Kelvin can be a decent helper when he's not bugging out which is rare.  The seasons are buggy and don't sync well between players, you'll just end up waking up to snow after summer which adds nothing to gameplay. The ponds freeze, but you can just drink from streams. Animals are abundant regardless of season.Story is the most godawful thing I've ever witnessed, the ending is so random I feel like it was a fever dream. There's only one voice line in the entire game and it was clearly made for the trailer where they showed it off. Entire animation sequences feel like they were made in source filmmaker by someone who just started out, awkward and janky with no explanation to what's going on. The Forest itself was clunky and not that great, but it was fun. This game had nowhere to go but up, and impressively they managed to make it worse. People are defending it because they called it Early Access at the last second, but I don't see it getting much better, at least story-wise. "Stop complaining and be happy with what you have" is the worst type of fanboyism I've seen. Don't defend mediocrity, they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ you over too.But hey, enjoy your hundreds of millions from this one, devs :-)

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest struggles a lot with a design choice Endnight Games seems extremely reluctant to let go off, that they are terrified of making the player do anything.Most of the gameplay elements suffers from this design choice as you have no need to engage with any of the games systems. Survival is a joke; the map is cluttered with so many processed food and drink items that you will never need to worry about creating your own food source. Environmental factors like cold and being wet is a simple hit to your stamina bar. You can sleep in the dead middle of winter with a tent made from a stick and a tarp. There is no need to build your own weapons, armor and invest effort into fighting enemies because the game gives you so many new toys to play with that combat at all stages is trivial. Base building doesn’t work due to your inventory being the size of a small truck therefore not needing to do any sort of resource management, you gain nothing in turns of survival benefits and lastly the map being approximately 4 times the size of the first game. Someone didn’t learn from the mistakes of Todd Howard, the absolutely colossal size of the map is an enormous detriment to this game. So much so that they had to add these comically out of place transportation options. Get ready to jump on your very own one wheeled hoverboard and blaze through the forest at mach 1 speeds or better yet get behind the wheel of Chariot 1, (a golf cart) indestructible and instantly kills anything you ram into. There are other options like a glider and ziplines make a return now with the ability to go up the lines as well, but once again it clashes with the map size. Building infrastructure to make use of these ziplines is a massive undertaking. The devs have placed so little faith in the game that they’ve built that they would rather make playing it optional then potentially making people upset that they must engage in a system that isn’t perfect. It. Is. Boring.The Story and narrative are up next and while I won’t talk to much about it as not to spoil but it is essentially the same formula as the first game; being told through environmental storytelling and notes scattered at key story locations. Endnight still nails this part but for the sequel they’ve decided to experiment with cutscenes and voiced characters. These cutscenes appear out of nowhere same with characters. You cant interact with them, they arrive say a few lines and then round the corner and disappear. Never in all my years of playing games have I seen something so jarring, these moments are the opposite of seamless. So, are there any parts of this game I did enjoy? Yes, building while pointless it’s actually a lot of fun due to you are now being able cut up logs and shape a structure to your liking. Que up “House Building Theme” from Red Dead 2 and have a good time, its surprisingly satisfying. So in my opinion the original “The Forest” is still the superior game. The Sequel fails to deliver any meaningful change to the formula. Endnight might have gotten caught up in the “More is better” sentiment bit I think they lacked any real direction with this game.Edit: Spelling/Grammar

HE sucks at cutting down tree tho, so when you want to gather logs you want to cut down tree and leave the pickup for him. Just don't forget you are limited by 50 logs pieces of any kind on the ground on the whole map, outside of stored logs.However having a few more option could looks cool, like small stone wall and the like. Right now you build with logs and that's it.Trap are costly unless you keep reloading your save (that respawn the very little amount of material you can find), but you can freeform build spikes by placing a stick on the ground and sharpen it. And it's super cheap & deadly.Sadly, caves aren't as interesting as in The Forest from what I can see. Unlike the previous game you aren't often going in at one entrance and going out somewhere else confused. Probably because of the sizeof the map. And I miss the more confusing inside layout.And we still can't see anything insides caves when you play solo. Most weapon require two hands so it's total pitch dark (100%full dark) in a lot area where you need to fight back mutants that run/jump around all the time super fast. Your only option right now is building line of campfires as you explore the cave and fall back to them as soon as you aggro something. And don't bother with flares, they are only good to throw down in some further area to see how many of them are waiting for you - they don't stay long and barely light their surrounding, with a flickering red light that reflect around.And honestly I really don't see the appeal in this, it's not scary or fun. Building tons of campfire isn't interesting and doesn't feel "right", and staring at a black screen doesn't feel "right" either.However some part of the caves have some small lamp laying around, sometime it's enough.While it sound quite negative I still have some fun playing. If the game was more costly I might have not recommend the game tho. Some more polishing might help a lot but thing like the cave will probably never change.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game. Story and cut scene animations are a bit clunky but with the engine i suppose its acceptable. gameplay itself is great, the graphics are stellar, the survival aspect is amazing. The caves are scary, the enemies are dark and the mutants are terrifying. This is the original forest but 10x better. Free build dramatically increased the creativity and individuality. The addition of companions not only made the experience less lonely, but made it better. With Kelvin being a helpful builder and Virginia being a loyal defender the world feels so much less empty. Highly recommend this game. Its a fantastic solo experience and even better with a friend or group.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is a great game there is no doubt about that, and if you feel like you want to play the game then by all means go ahead, I did and I enjoyed it, but if ever there was a time to wait for a game to come out of Early Access it would be now. As someone who enjoyed The Forest far more than I could have expected I had very high expectation for Sons of the Forest, but sadly I think SOTF is just not there yet, and here’s why…1 – The IslandFrom what I’ve been able to gather is seems that the general consensus is that SOTF’s map is roughly 5 times bigger than that of The Forest, but bigger isn’t always better. I don’t recall a single time in The Forest when I felt like I was losing out on anything because I had to travel across the map. Though the map was much smaller, it was balanced for the amount of content the game offered and nothing was ever really “too far” away. At this point in time there just isn’t enough content in SOTF to justify such a large map. Surprisingly there are about half as many caves as there were in The Forest, at least for the time being, of course they’ve added bunkers but even then we only get a handful. Don’t get me wrong, the game looks AMAZING, but when everything is so far away that it takes you half an hour to run across the map it will eventually start to wear on you.2 – The CavesOne of the most iconic aspects of The Forest was its intricate intertwining cave system that could be easily accessed from almost any part of the map thanks to its many cave entrances. You could venture into the darkness and emerge almost anywhere on the map depending on how far you went, this made everything feel connected and really helped tie the islands overworld together with its cave system. Not only that but finding certain equipment could help you dive even further into the depths of darkness which in turn upped the danger levels as you delved further and further… well, this is gone now. In SOTF each cave is its own standalone cave, many times with the exit being only a few meters away from its entrance. Not only that but most of the times the caves don’t really pose any type of threat, either they’re completely empty and you can just run through them, or they’re filled to the brim with mutants and you can still just run right through them because there’s nothing limiting your progress through the caves. Worst of all is that most of the caves in SOTF just aren’t memorable, I feel the reason for this is mostly because after looting a cave there’s really no reason to come back, you get the main loot from the cave and that’s it, that cave is done and you never have to visit it again which sucks.3 – The SurvivalWhile this might be a bug and unintentional, as the game stands now it allows you to re-loot absolutely everything in the game, suitcases included, making it so you never have to worry about running out of supplies. Now I know that this was also a thing in The Forest, but it only applied to items in caves and some very basic overworld items (yet another reason you don’t need to return to the caves). That and the many duplication glitches that currently plague the game make it so you never really have to worry about survival. Wanna build a house? You can build a mansion by just chopping down one tree and using a stick. Ran out of ammo/grenades/crafting materials? Just save and reload next to a camp as many times as you need till you top off everything. Also, did I mention that the end-game armor is infinite? That’s right, you will never run out of armor, and even the best armor can be fully crafted early to mid-game after restarting a few times in the correct bunker. Not to mention that our friend Kelvin offers a never-ending supply of fish so you’ll never go hungry again. Basically, you never have to worry about surviving in this game, hell you don’t even need a base, everything you need will fit in your backpack, and even if you do go hungry or get thirsty you don’t really get punished for doing so.4 – The StoryThis is probably what hurt the most for me, while The Forest didn’t have much of a story per se, once you reached the end you got enough of an explanation for everything to make sense. In SOTF however, the ending is so bizarre and non-sensical that it just leaves you confused as to who everyone is and where they came from. It wasn’t until I went onto Youtube and found someone who put in the time to do the detective work and piece everything together that I was finally able to understand a bit, and even then, it was just an interpretation of the events that happened, you really have to stretch your imagination for everything to make sense.Now don’t get me wrong, in spite of all of these issues I’m fully aware that the game is in early access and thus not complete, and while I did enjoy the experience during my first playthrough I can’t help but think of all the possibilities of how much more the game can improve during this early access phase and how I could have had a much more enjoyable experience in a complete game, because you only get one chance at a first playthrough. Sons of the Forest has all the potential to surpass The Forest, but as the game stands it just isn’t there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game that I have actually bothered to write a review for because of how disappointing it was.the game has very little content, finished it in under 12 hours. _childDocuments_.review: At the time of release I would not recommend this game.Gameplay - lacks key mechanics compared to original.There are game play elements which are still missing such as an enormous amount of crafting recipes for tools, diseases, building, resource gathering, and traps which were already fully fleshed out in the original. I expected the addition of and expansion on these mechanics at the very least. Caving - entirely subpar compared to the original - severely lacking in content.I enjoyed caving in the first game immensely and expected this element to be expanded greatly in the sequel. However, in its current state, the game lacks as robust of a cave system as the original. Graphics/map - Improved versus original, but not with 16x the detail.The graphics are improved across the board and the map is quite large. However, the map is also quite empty, but no more than the original.You could enjoy the game on release but it is surely incomplete as of the writing of this review. It seems like 60-70% of the content is complete. For an early release game these days, that is par for the course.

_childDocuments_.review: For being early access, you can't judge this game too harshly. But damn, it's not as good as some people are saying it is. The concept is there, it's just right now it's not great. The story is idek, confusing as hell. The ending was just absurd (again didn't understand it). There are a lot of bugs in this game that people don't really talk about it. The gameplay at first is actually pretty fun. However, the more you keep on playing it, it just gets way too repetitive and annoying. Same thing with the mechanics. It's cool at first, but later on I just don't want to see the same damn animation over and over again (For example, making a tent). Also, the map is so huge which means lots of stuff right? Nope, it's a huge map with a whole lot of nothing in between key points of the map. The game is basically a walking simulator just to get from one cave to the next. Also, building a base is the most useless thing ever if you're playing to beat the game. Building a base just wastes time, and you're never gonna use it again. Caves are super boring in this game. They're ridiculously linear, usually with one way in and one way out. The Cannibals are honestly pretty boring. In fact, they become more annoying than scary/worrying. I really feel like they didn't know what enemies to put in caves because there are so many babies. Like actually, a ridiculous amount of babies. The guns are cool, but they just honestly make the game way way way tooo easy to deal with enemies. Especially since you can basically have infinite ammo with the whole 1.loot ammo 2. save 3. exit 4. join back  5. loot. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Very impressed so far.Played a bit of solo, was good, decided to join a random server, got lucky and was much better.The building feature is one of the best I've seen in a while, its intuitive but limited to just logs right now, I hope they add different material types, like stone.The AI is interesting, and seems to be progressive with different types of cannibals visiting you, some harmless, others not so much.Some nice little features are starting to pop up, throwing logs off a cliff into a log storage pile automatically stacks them into it for example. logs will float down stream too, its these little things that make this game better.I haven't personally had any performance issues with an RTX 2060S, i7 10700KF, 16GB ram and SSD, infact it runs really well for me.Looking forward to what gets added next.

_childDocuments_.review: (EA, first week version)Very well executed atmospheric open-world, FPS survival with a compelling campaign (although very placeholder story at this point).                                                                                                                                                                            Many key elements that a game like this needs to be doing right, this game is doing right. If you need a break from frenetic shooters, this game is a great antithesis, forefronting survival and exploration.(++) Scenery(++) Immersive inventory solution(+) Project priorities very well sorted(+) First-person animations (with nice details like one-handed variants in case you're holding something else in the other)(+) Story focused (although the story is really bad)(+) Many great mechanics(+) Almost no serious bugs (if any)(-) The maps is huge but rather empty. Needs more interactive POIs, 'attractions'.(-) Needs assignable quickslots (as in, the backpack quickslots should represent a bindable key)(-) Combat is a bit unpolished and wonky(-) Environmental story-telling should be improved as well as the lore-logic where certain items are and why they're there(--) AI is bad (although Kelvin is so dumb, at a certain point it becomes a part of his charm)(-) Respawning of items is ok but needs to be done more elegantly (worst example: that dude with a geotag that respawns every time I load)(-) The geotags are unnecessary clumsy, let the player put any waypoint they want into the sat-nav (additionally, the green dots are a nuisance; at least, they should change color when the location was searched)(-) The "survival" book (for building and crafting) is awkward to understand and use

_childDocuments_.review: Falls short in the "survival area." But the game is ace, beautiful graphics if they do cause FPS drops often (High settings and i'll drop to 20 or below randomly.) Story is cool, confusing but mysterious, leaving me going "that was cool, but wtf I still got questions" Also F you shark for being the only horror factor in this game for me...But here's some feedback for the devs and anyone reading:You can drink from any source of water, other than cave water and the ocean. - I'd rather need to take extra steps to clean/purify it, or suffer a penalty. Why? Cause you've no idea if it's actually safe to drink, it might be clear water but it can still hold bacteria/particles and whatever else. Starving, being dehydrated isn't a big issue as is in game, but I've not really suffered much from it since there's enough food to find like MREs etc, to keep you going and often water sources as mentioned can all be drank from, it's mostly going into caves and the like that's where you'll need to actually manage it. Doing extra here could make players actually pay attention manage their supplies and so on.I'm not 100% on the stealth in this game, you're technically wearing camo by default but it doesn't actually hide you that well unless you're directly in the centre of a bush, and you need "Leaf Armour" to make stealth a viable options. But it requires a rare resource to craft so it's makes me debate whether it's worthwhile crafting it early on. Often I leave Leaf Armour till i have other armour to swap it out for, I'd rather run away/past cannibals early game than stealth. The Seasons added, doesn't really do much from what I see. Spring, summer and Autumn don't do anything. With Spring and summer seeming to be the exact same, with Autumn offering orange leaves and the like. Winter has a Coldness mechanic that's rather basic. Just need to find "warm" clothing or carry a source of fire (Torch or campfire) and ta'da, not cold.Feels more like Spring should encourage animal spawns and plants (Trees) grow faster. Summer should affect your thirst and provide less water. Autumn should just have more varied weather but pretty much do little to the player's health and stats. Winter could be reworked so there's very little animals and water (that's already the case I believe) but being cold zaps your stamina, and health as well.Other Changes:I think some of the weapons could do with a cross-hair or their iron sights fixing. Both bow's I struggle to work out when I first use them, I can't figure out where I'm aiming until the first shot is fired and often if that shot is short it can mean being detected. The Crossbow I have no idea what my sights are, so aim for body shots with that. other weapons are clear, UNTIL you crouch and the weapons become harder to aim accurately. So a HUD mini cross-hair or something could be helpful (allow us to toggle it on/off too) It also makes stealth harder; because I can't aim very well whilst crouching, I can't headshot easily, so often the arrow/bolt/bullet hits or just misses and stealth is pointless now.More reasons to build a base? - I don't really base build, it's mostly to give Kelvin a log cabin, and a wall around it to keep him safe. Beyond that I don't really stay in one spot, I'll just build a Hunter's Shelter and keep on the move. If I do base build it often attracts a fair number of cannibals which can get annoying, more so cleaning up the bodies. I Feel like it needs a deterrent or something? Like, having structures that reduce the chances of cannibals coming to attack? A structure to purify water would encourage me building a base, part of me wants fast travel since travelling get boring when the camps are hidden and you don't know where they are.(ignoring the GPS locations btw) I'd rather fast travel between bases, than walk/run from one side to another.More Lore! I don't understand a number of things; like I don't understand who the woman in white is who knocks us out, and who is supporting her because I'm sure she has army guys with her. Similarly, there's little on Virginia on how she ended up that way, by still "sane". Finally there's emails talking about "things" but we can't seem to find them or anything. In addition to some environmental story telling, because whilst there's some, its not enough to make me see or formulate the dots of what happened there or on this island without reading emails that I can find. UI changes, can we have tips on what the Custom difficulty changes do? - Like I don't know how long a "Realistic Day" or "Season" actually is...  This could also compliment telling us what the different seasons do. And having the Season on the GPS would help because I can't gauge how long a season is, seeing what season I'm in could also help. (Beyond seeing snow and orange leaves ofc...)Similarly:  can the text on the GPS be made clearer? I struggle to read the clock sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2022 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories..

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much promise. The gameplay is fun, the building is clean, the idea of AI companions is neat and the enemies are interesting. The story is just as mysterious as the first game, which leads to a lot of intrigue.Spoilers ahead for those who haven't beaten the game.Now that I've finished the game and am looking back, it is such an incoherent mess. It was so promising, with fun gameplay and mechanics, but the story is just so incomprehensible and poorly written it completely ruined the experience for me. The first game is, I believe, one of the best survival games ever created with an interesting story that can be pieced together by the average player. I shouldn't have to immediately go to the internet to figure out what the hell happened.Overall, 5/10. Good gameplay, mechanics, exploration. Horrible story, even worse ending, and they used AI generated art.

_childDocuments_.review: It is the Forest, but with a more natural looking landscape/forest and interesting mechanic changes.You have a follower who helps gather, but I find him most useful to point out enemies I can't see through the foliage. Instead of placing a campfire 'ghost' and adding the materials, you place sticks (from your hand) and then light them. Your lighter now emits a purple light and you can 3D print items, so a future twist? I love camping, and the world feels like the Pacific northwest. If I can make a canoe later on... Runs 50-60 fps @ 1080 on a 9600k/1660ti/16GB system at high draw distance (a must) and a mix of high/med settings with motion blur (ugh) off and vsync on. Some pathfinding issues, and other EA quirks, but playable and I'll be playing more tomorrow.

But then again, immersive log cabin building and three armed lady with shotgun.

_childDocuments_.review: *Early Access Review (in case I decide this update needs revision)Wow, this sure is early ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ access.The season mechanic is rapid and provides nothing fruitful to the game experience other than being just another annoyance to add to the list. NPC logic for (best boy) Kelvin needs a lot of work, because he chops down your tree house. Nothing says fun like waking up to dying because there's literally nothing stopping any NPC from walking through fences, walls and doors. The game looks great, but ONLY runs smoothly at medium settings at 60fps max. Audio cues are misplaced and often not the distance or angles they're intended to be. For a bonus mini-game, take a shot every time it sounds like a stone, fish or tree fell into the river nearby but there was literally nothing there. Take a shot if you have a cannibal screaming to its tribe about spotting you as if it's using your ear to audition for Dead by Daylight. You'll be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, or wish your ears got clapped like Kelvin's, within ten minutes.You have a limitation of 16 meat available for consumption SERVER-WIDE at a time, meaning at a full server of 8 people you constantly are wondering where the ♥♥♥♥ your meat disappeared to whenever an NPC hasn't decided to eat it on you. Cannibals cannot be harvested, either, probably for that reason. This is hilarious because you can store an entire Walmart in your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ backpack like Dora the Explorer-- complete with over 10 candy bars, at least a six-pack of energy drinks, and enough sticks, stones, leaves, flowers, bones, skulls, weapons and tools to start an underground civilization of dwarf hippies that became necromancers. _childDocuments_.review: This game is in early access and I made the mistake of buying it.I don't understand why the reviews are so positives honestly. Maybe it will get good, but right now I'm not pleased.I guess people love to pay 40$ to endlessly run on a storyless empty island killing cannibals and weird stuff because it reminds them of a good old game they used to play.Problems I see for now (and solutions):1. GPS... You can litteraly go straight to the objectives looking at the ground all the time and it will work. The signals appearing on your GPS  should only appear when you get very close to a point of interest.2. Survival... Another game where the survival components are just here to down your stamina. In the actual state, the game consists of running from a point to another on your GPS so yes it is annoying if you don't have stamina. There should be something more incapacitating. Maybe there is, but guess what? In 9 hours I've never had any problems from the surviving conditions except a stamina drop and I've ran accross the island without eating or sleeping.3. Play time and replayability... Took my friends 7-8 hours to complete and we took time to build stuff. I missed 1 play session with them and surprisedly they completed the game. There's no point of replaying for them since nothing is randomized. Everyone ran to the signals on the GPS and the only challenge was sometimes there is a certain order to respect because you need an item first. Well, we now know the order, so why replay it? You need to implement some sort of randomization or something.4. Building... I love building in games. Put 300+ hours in Icarus, 400+ in Valheim, etc. There is some really nice stuff in the building system of SOTF, but sadly it is overall very annoying and useless to build stuff. You can get away with only the basic build just to save your game and sleep and it will give you nothing more if you build a gigantic mansion with furniture. Building in this game will only waste your time because the goal is only to run to GPS signals as fast as possible. The game needs to make building essential to survival which is not the case right now.Lot of work left to make this a good game. Coop is nice and stable, almost no loading and game runs very clean for me. The island is beautiful and I like the interactions with the tribes. Crafting is nice when you understand how it works (some stuff could be more intuitive/automated but overall very nice).I suggest working on randomization for the objectives asap, because soon there will be no active players left to give you feedback. Same for the GPS, completely change the concept or make it more harder to see objectives from a distance.Hope feedbacks will help to improve the game in the coming months!

_childDocuments_.review: So let me get right into this and start of saying that this is very fun and a lot more polished than I initially expected from Endnight saying this was going to be early access. Myself, my brother, and lots of our friends have already been kicking it into high gear with finding items and trying to get through the game.Below is more or less a bullet list of things I find awesome about SoTF.- The quality of life improvements: Base building is so much more fun and immersive now.- Sharing items: In both multiplayer and singleplayer you can share items with Virginia and with Kelvin, but in multiplayer I believe this function really shines in contrast to The Forest. It is a lot easier and more streamlined than having to pull out a tray and put an item on for each item you want to share.- Gameplay: Overall, a big improvement from The Forest- Environment: I think that they did a lot on making the world look a lot nicer and more in-depth than the previous game. That being said, one of the things that still wows me is walking through snow leaving trails that stay there for awhile, as well as the dynamic seasons and weather.Those are some of the more positive points I have for SoTF. However, that being said, I still do have a lot of things I hope that the devs take into consideration (considering they opened this for Early Access for people to provide critique on their works)While I do enjoy the game, there quite a few issues that I think the devs really need to address, many of these we have noticed and while we find funny and ludicrous, definitely have to be fixed as time goes on.1. Guns & Ammo: Guns are definitely by no means a bad addition to SoTF, but I got SoTF to have a realistic and hardcore survival horror game not to be the Doom Slayer with a 12 Gauge Shotgun. I think the damage is up to par with what i'd expect from a shotgun or 9mm pistol, but I think that the issue isn't the damage as much as it is the fact of ammunition being so plentiful that ammunition for guns is easier to find ammunition for a bow or crossbow. This is an obvious issue regarding balancing and I think as much as it is fun right now, it can lead to a slower level of replayability for the game as time goes on. Guns should be a reward for a lot of hardship and survival, but still something you need to use sparingly.2. Audio: Alright so this is something I am sure they will fix in the next update, but I am going to include this here anyways. The audio can be really neat, but really bad and broken at times, this is especially noticeable with the wind in which it will become choppy and robotic at times and also incredibly loud even with AudioFX turned way down. Again I am sure this is something they plan on fixing next update, but I am including this one anyways.3. Stability and Performance: I do not know if its just my system or if it is a common issue (though based on the response from friends and my brother it seems to be an issue across the board), but I get severe frame loss that does not relent. It is pretty odd that a game that would appear to be less taxing than a game like star citizen, I get less frames in than the latter.I have a lot more I could include, but I think these cover the biggest issues I am having with SoTF. Again, I am well aware that this game is in early access and there will be problems. But to the inevitable commentators who will mention I am judging the game too harshly since it released early, I have this to say to you: Early access is designed for criticism and critique of the game, that is why devs even bother to do early access. So if you are going to waste your time commenting to me that this is "early access so it is going to have problems" then just don't.I still recommend people to get this game, but just know it does have problems and factor that in before you buy it. I believe that Endnight will 100% turn this into one of the greatest games of 2023 right alongside Hogwarts Legacy.

_childDocuments_.review: As a player of the first game the sons of the forest was unfortunately nothing compared to the first game. a half baked experience all in all with poor performance, building was worse, crafting was worse, story was painfully short and pretty boring other than the final cut scene, i counted 2 cut scenes total after entering the island, the story in general was uninformative other than a couple hints on some papers you can find. The island was bland and exploring was very boring with limited places of interest. The only way to find anything interesting is to use the map phone but these places of interest mainly progress the already short story, which by the way the user interface with the book and phone is absurdly annoying to use and default mapped keys are very badly organized. left and right click is used for almost everything in the game for some reason, there are no quick slots in game allowing for easy inventory item swapping instead they implemented a quick-grab out of backpack feature that is barely any faster than pulling out your ground matt and constantly replaces items you placed inside. The addition of the sleep mechanic seemed tacked on and useless, I saw no improvements in the intelligence of AI and their animations seemed wonky, janky, and worse than before. The sound quality of the game is great but there are some interesting choices made, for example windy weather is excruciatingly loud blowing out my eardrums in my headset compared to the rest of the sounds in game. Items can phase into walls and the ground causing them to be lost forever by walking over or around them, even enemies can make items disappear from the face of the earth if they happen to step on an item and fling it into a black hole which is very annoying. I'm not sure if the first game had dedicated server's as its been a while since i booted that one up but this time around for sure if the host of your game is not online you wont be playing your save. I can say however that the graphics of the game are very beautiful but the experience is heavily hindered on the poor optimization of the game in my opinion, cutting trees down is still as satisfying as it was before of course but not as fun when the things you can build either don't exist from the first game anymore, and or are bland and boring. I would not recommend buying at this current state unless on a sale of 5$ or less, maybe in a couple years of development the game will be a lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give it a mixed review if I could. Exploring is fun, the crafting system is expansive, and the combat is serviceable. Overall a solid open world survival game with well-functioning online co-op.The primary thing I don't like is....what am I supposed to be doing? Like why am I here? What should I be doing? What is the end-goal? Feel like I'm just wandering around aimlessly and mostly finding copy/paste camps. Occasionally there is a cave with something more interesting. Is that the objective? to explore all caves and get their unique loot? Why is all the interesting loot only in caves? Aren't there other geological structures that they could have done anything with???The other thing that bothers me is that the crafting system has zero tutorialization and doesn't follow a standard template. You just have to mess around to figure out how things work. Every item - try left clicking and right clicking, and holding click, and using it against various structures or the ground. A simple log can be used dozens of ways depending on where you are standing in relation to the log, what you have equipped, what you are looking at while holding the log. I wouldn't mind if I was holding the cooking pot and it just told me straight up - left click to drink, right click to dump, E to place on campfire to cook, E to fill at water source. But no, you just have to figure it out. And some actions are somewhat counter intuitive against the actions of another item. Like some melee weapons can right click to block, others can't. Electrical items, like stun baton, how do they recharge? Not with your solar panels. Well they just expend consumable batteries automatically and don't ever tell you they are using batteries. Why is everything so confusing?

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I've played for over 300 hours and I still want to like this game...but I can't. And I was a big fan of The Forest and I love builder survival games, in general. My favorite aspect of the game is the building and I've spent most of my time doing that. But it's super buggy, wildly inconsistent, and way too convoluted for what should be simple concepts. When something as simple as building a staircase with walls requires you to 'place a piece, remove a piece, place a piece, trick it, remove a piece,' there's something fundamentally wrong with the mechanics. And you can only learn that through a google search because the game sure doesn't tell you how to work that out. Sometimes you go to place a piece and nothing gets placed but you still expend the material. Sometimes you place something, then go for an adventure or supply run, come back and pieces are missing...yes, even with structural damage turned off.The story is very interesting, but short in comparison. The graphics and audio are beautiful but I get the sense that the dev team cared more about making it look pretty than working and playing well. I would rather them sacrifice graphics for quality mechanics and a building system that doesn't randomly break for no reason, making hours of work feel wasted and being a real design killer. It's a really sloppy system for how good it looks and it's a shame.My real distrust of this game started shortly after buying it. Keep in mind, I had been eagerly anticipating this game and had been hearing that the game would be a "completely fleshed out game" at release. When it dropped, I was not aware that, a week before release, Endnight changed their tune and said they were bumping it down to EA (likely due to mismanaged funds, greedy fingers, and an unrealistic deadline). So, I start playing it thinking it's a complete game only to be sharply let down. To top it off, it wasn't even close to a complete game at that time. Since then, Endnight has added quite a bit of stuff to the game (some of it kinda cool but honestly unnecessary) while seemingly ignoring all the major mechanical issues that more than a fair amount of people complained about. To my dismay, many of those issues persist today in the "Full release" of the game.The AI for Kelvin and Virginia are sometimes helpful, but mostly they just get in the way or they eventually geek out and start doing really dumb behaviors, like walking into a wall for 40 min because the AI can't comprehend that stepping 2 feet to their left will solve their pathing issue. Kelvin...ugh...It's almost better if you just let him become a cannibal chew toy. It's better than sending him to go gather logs and then he proceeds to walk 3 miles away to cuts trees when there's fairly dense forest just outside the base. At that point it's faster to just ignore him and do it yourself. Once you get the zipline gun, Kelvin pretty much becomes obsolete.  And the AI's affinity for getting into places that they can't get out of is...impressive! I can't even begin to explain how Kelvin manages to turn every door he walks through into some kind of weird out-of-phase ghost that gets lodged into the wall.All I'm saying is, for a "complete game" it feels like it's still in EA. I'm super disappointed in Endnight for playing dirty marketing tricks with much less than truthful advertising and then passing off this, Still unfinished, game as a full release. For the amount of time they put into making this game, it should, at very least, be mostly consistent mechanically. I don't see it reaching that milestone any time soon, if at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, Sons of The Forest is one of those games that I want to like, and in theory, I should. A co-op survival horror game where you’re in a monster / cannibal infested forest? Conceptually, it’s great but felt rather lackluster in execution.The game introduced new mechanics, building options, and crafting choices from the previous title yet somehow fails to feel unique enough to be considered a full sequel. Somehow, it feels like it is a big update or DLC and lacks substance to be a successor. On that note, after exploring the story and unlocking all the collectibles, tools, and weapons– there really isn’t much to do in this game. You can continue to build and make a wonderful fortress and gather resources but your surroundings (of course, the monsters) don’t progress alongside you. Eventually, there is no real sense of threat as this game doesn’t necessarily have a scaling system for the threat. You just continue to build a sanctuary, have an arsenal of weaponry and armour whilst they continue to exist.In short, I’m sure as time progresses, there will be new content introduced and this kind of game will appeal to a certain audience. However, in my eyes, it just isn’t worth the full price tag and in the state it is now. 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: "Sons of the Forest" isn't just a game; it's a masterpiece that transcends the boundaries of typical gaming experiences. From its breathtaking visuals to its immersive gameplay mechanics, every aspect of this title is meticulously crafted to deliver an unforgettable journey into the heart of darkness.One of the most striking features of "Sons of the Forest" is its stunning graphics. The game's lush environments are rendered with such detail and realism that you'll often find yourself pausing just to take in the beauty of your surroundings. Whether you're exploring dense forests, eerie caves, or abandoned structures, every inch of the game world feels alive and teeming with atmosphere.But "Sons of the Forest" isn't just about looks; it's also about gameplay that keeps you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. The survival mechanics are deep and challenging, requiring you to scavenge for resources, build shelter, and fend off the horrors that lurk in the shadows. Every decision you make feels meaningful, whether it's choosing how to approach a dangerous encounter or deciding which upgrades to prioritize for your character.Speaking of encounters, the enemies you'll face in "Sons of the Forest" are some of the most terrifying creatures ever seen in a video game. From grotesque mutants to sinister cultists, each foe is uniquely horrifying and poses a constant threat to your survival. But despite the danger, there's a sense of exhilaration that comes from facing these challenges head-on, knowing that every victory is hard-earned and well-deserved.Of course, no review of "Sons of the Forest" would be complete without mentioning its captivating story. As you unravel the mysteries of the island and uncover its dark secrets, you'll be drawn into a narrative that's equal parts haunting and thought-provoking. Every twist and turn keeps you guessing, and the emotional depth of the characters ensures that you'll be invested in their fates until the very end.In conclusion, "Sons of the Forest" isn't just a game; it's an experience that will stay with you long after you've put down the controller. With its stunning visuals, immersive gameplay, and gripping story, it sets a new standard for what gaming can achieve. Whether you're a fan of survival horror or simply appreciate a well-crafted adventure, this is one title that shouldn't be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand this an early access title but at it's current state I have to leave this review as NOT recommended overall.Performance issues aside, the game is very fun with friends. Being able to grab a GPS and roam around this larger new map was admittedly alot of fun! It's just a shame that after a few hours you start to notice the same enemy variety over and over as well as when exploring the land it's just a lot of running without actually seeing or finding anything from 20+ min at a time. I haven't tried it on SOLO but I can imagine it being much more difficult and horrifying. The game starts you off with an NPC who helps gather supplies for you and is a nice addition to the gameplay and gives you a nice companion if you are running this SOLO (especially for beginners to the series). However, there were many times when he would either get stuck on a  structure I had built or he would seemingly go out of his way to dismantle any of my previous houses to get materials for my newest build (which is insanely annoying). It got to the point where I had to put him down in order to keep a house standing longer than 1 day. And sadly once he's dead, that's it. As for the rest of the gameplay, I feel the inventory system, building mechanics and combat have been improved from the first in many ways. The inventory is now much cleaner and faster to sort through and use. Gun play still feels janky, but any form of melee feels fun and hits feel weighty. My only issue is the fact you get a GPS with infinite battery and it literally shows where you need to go in order to find clues to finish the story and/or find new weapons/key items to progress. I felt this took away alot of the mystery and exploring that was present in the first game (and also added ALOT more play time to anyone's first playthrough).My only real complaint with these new additions is the crafting mechanics. I was saddened that with this new build mechanic they did ended up removing A TON of blueprints from the original game to sort of force the player to use this new custom building mode (which I am not a fan of personally). It's a bit confusing to get the hang of and it takes alot of trial and error before you truly get the hang of it. I just prefer the simple "plot a blueprint down here and go get the materials needed" type of building and it is nice they brought some of that back, I just wish there was more.When it comes to the story? I haven't 100% gotten to the ending yet in my playthrough, but I have had a few friends already complete it within 8 hours of gameplay....which is INSANE to me compared to the first game which I felt took more around 15 to 20 hours to complete the story on a first run through. From what I can say without spoilers is that the story feels rushed and un-finished in many aspects. I truly hope the devs implement more creatures to find, more cave systems, and maybe more weapons to liven up the combat before it's full release. For my final thoughts I would say that my overall feeling towards Sons of the Forest is disappointment. I have been following the developer updates for this sequel for years and every new peace of info we got made me incredibly excited for its release. However, seeing that it was another early access title immediately made my blood boil. Thank god this isn't a full-priced game at the moment, but it's sad they didn't just wait to release this as a finished game this time around since they had all the player data they could ever need from the first game's 4+ years of early access. This entire experience just feels half-baked and rushed out the door. I do truly hope that Endnight Games can make a comeback and fix all the issues I stated above before the final release because if not...I will have to keep my rating of "not recommended" which I really don't want to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Vintage chocolate chip cookiesIngredients150g salted butter, softened80g light brown muscovado sugar80g granulated sugar2 tsp vanilla extract1 large egg225g plain flour½ tsp bicarbonate of soda¼ tsp salt200g plain chocolate chips or chunksMethodSTEP 1Heat the oven to 190C/fan170C/gas 5 and line two baking sheets with non-stick baking paper.STEP 2Put 150g softened salted butter, 80g light brown muscovado sugar and 80g granulated sugar into a bowl and beat until creamy.STEP 3Beat in 2 tsp vanilla extract and 1 large egg.STEP 4Sift 225g plain flour, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ¼ tsp salt into the bowl and mix it in with a wooden spoon.STEP 5Add 200g plain chocolate chips or chunks and stir well.STEP 6Use a teaspoon to make small scoops of the mixture, spacing them well apart on the baking trays. This mixture should make about 30 cookies.STEP 7Bake for 8–10 mins until they are light brown on the edges and still slightly soft in the centre if you press them.STEP 8Leave on the tray for a couple of mins to set and then lift onto a cooling rack.RECIPE TIPSFREEZING THE BISCUITSIf you’ve frozen the biscuits, take them out and arrange them on a lined baking sheet. Once defrosted, pop them in a medium oven 190C/170 fan/gas mark 5 and heat for 2-3 mins to crisp up. Don’t leave them too long or they’ll dry out.STORING DOUGHYou can keep the uncooked dough in a sealed container in the fridge for up to two weeks. Simply take some out, dollop on a lined baking tray and allow to come up to room temperature for 5 mins before bakingThe game is really good to I just figured i'd give you my cookie recipe first so you could have some great cookies to enjoy with this great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you are a fan of The Forest, I'd stay away from this one for the time being. Many, many bugs, some of them quite substantial, and the game as a whole feels quite unfinished. Of course it is in Early Access at present and this might change pending future updates, but there are a number of problems that I feel are truly central to the game which likely won't be going away.First and foremost among those is the short length of the game, which can be completed in just a few hours if you're only focused on doing the caves and necessary POIs, and there really isn't any need or particular reason to engage in the (admittedly fun) base building. Provided you are just moving from cave to cave, you're not going to need to have a base at all: there are places to save in the caves/bunkers and you can always just put down a simple tarp with a stick to save or sleep if you can't find a world save point. This seems bizarre for a game that so heavily features the base building and raids from cannibal and mutant AI, given that that aspect of the game has nothing at all to do with progression in the 'story'. The story of this game is told almost entirely through notes, to the extent there is a story being told at all. This is similar to The Forest, but I think if you cut the walking times out, the content here comes up much shorter than the original. Basically you go into a cave or a bunker and you get the items inside, until you get all the items needed to open The Final Bunker. Hints of what is really going on imply the game should feature some (many) set pieces it currently lacks, and there are some truly bizarre non-sequitur moments that surely aren't meant to be taken as something the player can possibly understand. Maybe these will be addressed in future updates..? For the time being I can only speak to what is present, and what is present is mostly a jumbled, incoherent mess.While the new building construction mechanics are enjoyable to mess with, the lack of structures that were in the first game, especially critical ones like the rain collector and log sled, severely limit what you can do with the base at present. Moreover, as mentioned, there just isn't anything you need from a base, it generally attracts more hostile attention than it protects against, and you're better off just running from fights you don't need to take anyway. About the bugs, I strongly recommend against saving using the tarp in multiplayer, as it may not actually save for you. It seems to be safe to save using the beds and tents already in the map, but otherwise you are rolling the dice on whether or not your character's item progression gets deleted. You'll frequently encounter a bug where you cannot interact with any objects in the game world, or where you're otherwise stuck in some animation and unable to attack or open your inventory. There are a couple of ways to fix this but the only one guaranteed to work is a full restart of the server - something made more annoying and time consuming when you can't reliably save using the player-made beds.There are a number of things to like about this game but at the time being I do not recommend it for purchase.UPDATE 3/12/2023There's been some patches and an update to the game since I initially reviewed it, and I believe the specific stabiltiy issues I cited here in MP were fixed (though I haven't read the patchnotes, it just worked the last time I palyed in MP). They did add content to the game and listen to the community feedback, so it is definitely trending in the right direction. However, I think the developers misled people with the marketing and some of the cavalier statements that they made about the game (such as a claim that it just needed "polish"), and until it's in a more complete state I still say it's not worth buying at this time. Perhaps they will develop it to be as splendid as the first Forest game, but only time can tell.

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting for what seemed like an eternity, my prayers have been answered. Yes, this may be missing features and functionalities from the first game, but the quality in my opinion is still pretty good. For most of you that played The Forest, this will be a similar experience with more visual flare than it's predecessor! Since The Forest came into early access in 2014, it evolved with its community for 4 years before its full release into the world! The game was very bare-bones when it first jumped into early access, with barely any features. Sons of the Forest however, released into early access with most features the first was missing in its infancy! This game does building in an interesting way. It lets you build free-form structures (although it's kinda buggy). With enough work you can make a beautiful structure in no time!There is plenty of weapons ranging from guns to axes and other melee weapons.The gameplay feels pretty good, it is pretty buggy at times though. Food Water and Sleep controlling the stamina bar as well as the new strength mechanic add a new twist to the survival aspects of the game. In this game, chopping trees, fighting cannibals/mutants, and spelunking into caves/exploring labs and scientific complexes, discovering the lore and backstory of the island and its inhabitants is your goal! The game can be completed in as little as 10 hours, but lets be honest, who rushes the story in this kind of game! Its meant to be explored and enjoyed! As early access progresses, we have the chance to help shape the future of this game. We most likely will see features returning from the first game, but keep in mind that directly porting these features could prove to break the game more than it already is!Optimization is a quite spotty and can vary greatly depending on in game weather which is especially true in the winter season.Graphically, anything above the low preset looks pretty good as long as the textures are at full resolution.The landscape can be breathtaking depending on where you're looking from, an example being at the plateau on top of the mountain near the can opener! The view is astonishing up there! The lighting is pretty and the atmosphere in the underground complexes/labs/caves can be quite unsettling at times. There are plenty of enemies to discover and fight in all of these caves and complexes!Will update review as i rack up more hours!

_childDocuments_.review: Waited 3 years for a fully developed game that ended up getting delayed 3 times before getting released as early access, many bugs, and I mean A LOT of bugs. From falling through the map into the void to sliding down a mountain while going through your inventory, the game feels like a mess. Sure, it's "Early Access" but they really only released it in this state to save face from having to delay it a 4th time. Seasons changing is literally boiled down to waking up from sleeping and the entire area around you is suddenly snowy, then sleeping again and it being gone the next morning. The story is supposed to be finished but feels too dry and rushed, making little sense. It's too easy and straightforward to progress through the game, even on the hardest difficulty, having all the caves be small and almost identical to each other. The Forest was really fun and had a great immersive atmosphere, and this release felt like a big disappointment. It's still really fun with friends, so wait until a sale if you want to play with your friends. Hopefully they can make up for it in the next 6-8 months for their "full release", but without a roadmap I'm really skeptical for what they're going to do.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel there isn't a right way to review this games as it is in early access, however for a game that has been in development for years, I feel like some things are missed, but the graphics are pretty good and the overall game play is new compared to the forest, but I feel it is lacking in story, the ending to me felt dull, lacking story to it, however maybe they will add more to it as it is early access but I am not sure they will. _childDocuments_.review: Been playing for 11.5 hours on normal mode (technically custom mode to turn on hunger and thirst damage) so far with some friends. Made it to day 10 in the game so far. Wanted to leave an honest review of what I think so far (I'm aware it's early access). Overall I would recommend the game, but caution against having high expectations for this early access version.It started out very fun getting to experience exploring the very large map with friends and fight enemies together and I was very excited about the base building aspect. Easily explored caves and bunkers together and it was fun. However, the longer you play the less there is to be excited about. By default normal mode, hunger and thirst damage is turned off which doesn't make sense for a survival game's default gameplay mode. The caves were way too simple and not a challenge at all to explore. Enemies should really scale more with more players. With just three of us, the enemies are a joke and easily handled with lowest tier gear. Aside from the spear and bow, you don't get to craft many weapons or tools and have to find specific items to progress the story which is fine and a good way to progress in some ways. It became clear very early on that there is no real incentive or need to set up a base camp or build more than half the structures in the guide book. As long as you have tarp and sticks, both of which are very easy to overflow on, you can sleep through the night and save your game. Even if you don't have one of the resources, you could easily avoid night in a cave or bunker(there's actually a bunker at the beginning that has a bed you can sleep and save in). The only storage options available outside of your backpack are for storing resources you could need a lot of, such as sticks, bones, large rocks and logs. However most of those resources are extremely abundant any way and can be easily gathered when you need them. There are also way too many resources in the map compared to the uses for those resources, such as meds, canned food, rope, cloth, etc. (We found so much rope in camps it's ridiculous). Kelvin is a bit OP when it comes to fishing because we will overflow you on fish in a matter of minutes. Another major QoL issue is the inventory access. There are no hotkeys for items to use, you would have to hold the inventory button which pulls up your backpack UI and you have to click an item slotted there which can be finicky at best. However there are not enough slots for weapons and opening the UI stops your character which makes it bad to use in battle when you would want to switch between bow or spear or something else and you just take damage while standing still. We've also encountered many bugs which is expected in an early access game, but some were game breaking. If you get killed by a shark it can prevent respawn, animals run through rocks and other terrain. Small animals can easily run through rivers while it slows the player, proximity sound really needs work because screaming enemies sound like they're all around you and directly in your ear regardless of how far away they are or what direction, climbing the mountain is easy even though it's a nearly 90 degree ascent. The freezing aspect in the mountains is also pointless. all it does is limit your stamina to a half bar, no damage or danger.All in all, I think this game has the potential to be very fun, however, a lot of things need to be added and changed to make it a more balanced and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo mother, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single mom to my son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2022 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So I decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and started playing but I was stuck on what you were supposed to do. I asked my son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my son since my husband had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: 2.5/5We waited for this game and bought it immediately upon release. Well, it was amazing and interesting at first but when you get to finish the game, it won't satisfy you that much. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first run through of this game. As it is in EA my comments are meant only as feedback and not complaints.Graphics are great, snow is brilliant leaving footprints etc weather changing all brilliant.Kelvin is very entertaining and a great help especially when building just beware when you ask him to collect logs he may cut down the tree holding your tree house lol. Virginia is great at helping protect your base after she is tamed so to speak. Love the new building mechanics you can be way more creative with your base. There aren't alot of blueprints and the book/manual itself is nowhere near as in depth as it was in the forest but hopefully that's something they will be working on improving. I really like the rope gun it's a way better way to make the zip lines. I love the new backpack visually looks so much better and the lights are a great touch. One big problem I had was the fact you couldn't keybind your weapons like in the first game I suffered quite a few deaths due to not being able to change weapons quick enough that's something I really hope they change as the way it is currently is far too slow. Crafting is much the same as the first game but was really hoping they would have a quick craft option for when you need to make something during a fight etc.  Loved the 3d printing can't wait to see if there will be more added to what you can make it was a great addition to the game. The ingame menu and options seemed alot more in depth in the first game I would think that is something that will be added to in time hopefully giving more options to change elements of the game without starting a new save and option for changing the light in caves/bunkers.The map I found to be much like the forest minus the giant hole (which I actually missed lol) although ALOT more sparse. It didn't feel like there was alot to interact with and you start to feel like your just wandering around doing nothing. I hope there are more camps added and more variation of camps as they all looked the same, would be great to find more information on the enemies and what their weaknesses are in the notes that you find, clues in skin pouches leading to things like treasure of some sort or points of interest, more interactive victim sites ticking off the victims you find like in the first game would have felt better like what you were doing had more of a purpose and making you feel more involved in the story.Getting into that the story felt weird, I didn't really feel like I did in the first game I felt sort of detached from the story and the characters and alot of the time it didn't feel clear what my aim was or what I was supposed to be doing most of the time but maybe that was just my experience. I really hope that as this game is in early access there is alot more to come as I really loved and enjoyed playing the forest and was really looking forward to this game coming out so I'm holding out faith that this game will just get better and better as time goes on and more updates are released ☺️

_childDocuments_.review: Way to Early for early access, at the current state it's more like a hiking simulator, with good building mechanics.Things that should be added to have a enjoyable game:· More monster/enemy verity· Actual things to find like caves that aren't on your GPS (There are hundreds of waterfalls in this game, and not a single one had a secret behind it.) how is that even possible?· Things to do other then the main story, like side quest or events.· Actual bosses in caves.I played through the entire story in approximately ~12 hours in Co-Op and would NOT recommend getting this game in it current state. and the ending is straight up underwhelming.The absolutely worst thing is, there are game breaking bugs like, if you walk out of the second to last story bunker without a specific item, you are locked out of progressing, because there's a event that closes the door behind you the when you enter, witch you can't pass when you return via the main entrance.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've played this game for about 12 hours and I seriously can only recommend this game to other The Forest players or players that haven't played the first game. It's a massive visual and gameplay improvement from the first game. For example the animation when crafting and building is Insane. Even the Graphics of the environment is a huge upgrade from the first game. The AI controlling the Cannibals are so smooth and Interesting to observe after playing the first game, since the Cannibals now "make plans", climb trees, jump on rocks and watch you from affar before attacking. So far I've mainly played Co-op with Friends but playing Single player is just as fun, the story and Missions are self explaining so if you are looking for a survival Horror game this is definitly a good pick!The only glitches and bugs i've experiences so far are the following: - A Log duplication glitch when a joined co-op player tries placing a log in a invalid location- when building the shelf you don't spend the wood you are holding so you can make as many shelves as you want- when I died while taking medication (while in my inventory) I was stuck with no health, really dark vision and I couldn't respawn so I had to restart- Kelvin being stuck in a lake cause he can't swimAlso some minor changes that I hope are coming soon are:- Lockable doors to keep cannibals out of your house- When hitting the Ice on frozen lakes it still makes the water splash noises and spears/arrows etc fall through it- maybe a raft or some type of boat - some markers like the coloured flags/houses of the first the forest gamebut all in all its a mindblowing game! cant wait for future updates!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not good. The map is 4x the size of the original but that isn't a good thing when 90% of the map is nothingness. Traversal is also awful, the vehicles get caught on the geometry constantly and walking is far less annoying. The design of the caves look cool but most are just confusing labyrinths with an item at the end.The game play is no different than the original other than the addition of guns. The guns aren't good and the view models are absolutely atrocious. The iron sights are so far away from the camera and are held from the bottom half of the screen which just makes aiming challenging not to mention looking ugly. There's also the modern axe weapon which clips through the GPS when you block which is just immersion breaking and obviously blocks what you need to see, probably isn't the only weapon that does this either. The original game is far better in my opinion and this game is a huge let down. The first game has a way better map that isn't congested with hundreds of thousands of trees and you could get across it in 10 minutes. This game tries to give you a wide range of weapons but most of them aren't good. It tries to "improve" building but now it takes hours upon hours to make a basic structure. The new enemies are cool but I don't think I'll complete this game anytime soon. This game isn't engaging and I often feel bored 90% of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the first one. This one is a little too easy. Part of the first installments enjoyment as a survivor/horror game was the difficulty in finding the cave locations by just wandering. This game had a GPS with locations to explore on the map which led us to finish the game very quickly that the story felt just unfinished. Building shelters was actually used in the first game because you needed a place to come back to after wandering in an area and a location to store food an items but this game just spoon fed you food items. You never even have to hunt.  We never even built a base because we could just run from location to location because it was on the map. Stamina and tiredness felt like it really didn't affect you at all and it shouldn't even be an icon or stat to track. Just pop a energy drink you have and find a ton. Would rather they fed us materials to upgrade weapons or have to build certain items like the canteen and force us to spend time hunting just to go on an expedition to try and find these caves. The survivor aspect of the game feels as if it was stripped compared to the first. The game is still early access so these issues can be addressed and more story or events added.
