_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Do NOT buy this game yet if you are expecting plenty of content or substance. When I saw they decided to go with an Early Access release at the last minute rather than the full release 1.0 release that they were about to drop,  I was under the impression of  "oh the game must just have some bugs and minor things to change/polish up" and boy was I wrong. 80% of the caves are literally just one small area with some mediocre loot that you probably can't even carry more of anyways. The story ends horribly and overall makes no sense in the way its presented. The pacing of progressing through that "story" is just abysmal. It took us maybe 10 hours to get to the point we had the shovel and keycard and then about 3 hours at most to beat the game from there because you just suddenly start getting everything you need to complete the game in rapid succession. Other smaller issues I have:    -Building a base feels kind of redundant, they should definitely look to Valheim for inspiration on how to make building a base both feel rewarding and necessary for progression since they put so much time into a nice new building system    -Why do all the items still respawn upon loading the save? There should definitely be an option to turn this off or at the very least they should be on some sort of respawn timer of 5-10 days or so.    -The "survival" aspect is far too easy even on Hard. This is partially tied into the items respawning I just mentioned above but also just the fact that food items are too abundant in general. It may not seem like it on your first day but I promise after a couple in-game days you will have a full inventory of food that will be constantly topped up along your way and you'll be wondering why there's even the ability to hunt animals.     -Guns are maybe a little bit op but I think its mostly due to the amount of ammo you can amass pretty quickly, they are fun to use but it's certainly a lot less threatening/intense when a large group of cannibals ambushes me if I can just pull my shotgun out and blow every one of them across the damn river and not even use half my ammo supply.     -Combat in general is a bit underwhelming. The mutants don't feel nearly as threatening as in the first game (especially with introduction of guns) but even fighting a few regular cannibals at a time the optimal tactic just boils down to running away a tiny bit, stop, whoever is chasing you will also stop for a moment before attacking, you pull out one of the 5 ranged weapons you can carry on you at all times and shoot them in the head while they stand there, they die, repeat for remaining cannibals.I really do think they've got a great base to work with here and the new graphics and animations look great. If they just flesh out the caves more and pace the overall progression better while hopefully fixing the story up a bit and making some changes to difficulty balancing and combat, this game will be amazing. As of now though I realllyyy wish I wasn't under the impression that the game was pretty much finished content-wise before playing this because now it just left me with a bad taste and ruined my expectations of the game. I hope to play it in "6-8 months" when it's supposed to be out of Early Access and get the experience I was initially hoping for.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally do not leave reviews on games, but this game has compelled me to do so. What a complete circus show. _childDocuments_.review: Playing this game was quite possibly the most painful experience of my life. I have never cared to write a review, but at this point im going to bill the developers for therapy. The story is abysmal and makes no sense. There is no sense of direction or game progression. and you learn lore through printed out emails in caves. The inventory system is a map and finding anything is a challenge, not to mention having to sit through every animation for each crafted or used item. I couldn't find where they hid the arrows until i was almost done with the game. Speaking of maps, the game world is way to large and empty. Outside of maybe 3 caves, every "cave" or location of interest in the game is a tiny room with practically nothing inside. I would be shocked if anybody has ever managed to finish this game without looking up a guide. It is that convoluted and confusing. I see why Sons of the Forest 2 is considered a psychological horror.... I truly hope nobody ever plays this game. I would not wish this on my worst enemy. Somebody could burn my house down, kick my dog, and shoot me in the leg and i would forgive them before i would put them through the absolute suffering that is playing this game. It is that bad. The fact the reviews are not horrible make me think they are faking reviews. The way i see it, either the developers hate their players and people who were a fan of the first game, or they were contracted by the cia to develop new torture techniques for guantanamo bay. I'd rather be waterboarded than play this.

_childDocuments_.review: having finished the game once, i can say so far I've gotten a pretty good impression from the game. This game is a massive improvement over the first one visually, mechanically, and from an immersive perspective. and while it's still in early access and I am anticipating the devs will add a heap of new stuff between now and it's finish.I thought the new building was pretty fun and also seamless. It was a nice transition to go from all the blueprint based builds from the last game to a more customizable feature, though the building does take a lot longer in my opinion over the first game and having kelvin collect stick and logs for me does help a lot.I think a couple things that should be added is maybe a faster way to travel. getting around the island that is 4-5 times bigger than the first game is always a long, long, trek. And having something like a utility cart like the broken down ones you can find all over would be a pleasant option. though I am grateful you start the game with a full gps map with points of interest to check out, the game would be very frustrating without that.I also was a little disappointed to see that you can still quit out and rejoin the game to respawn loot crates like you could in the first game, and get infinite amount of any item that has a chance to spawn in a crate within minutes. It was curious to be able to drink pond and river water without getting sick and I wonder if that will be permanent or not. the cannibals were a lot more human like in this game, with more enemy variety than the last game. The caves were better designed too. I liked the addition of more underground facilities, which felt more ominous and suspenseful than the caves to me.Overall very solid start. I would recommend to those keen on survival horror or if you liked the first game, though do not expect a fully complete game, as it's still in early access. And although the game already has a good amount of content to explore, the story felt very incomplete and left so many questions at the end which is to be expected from early access but I'm very excited to play through the game again in future years  when more is added.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, this game impresses, and it continues to captivate even after 30+ hours of play. In its genre, it stands out as possibly the best, thanks to its engaging building system and dynamic enemy raids.However, it does have its drawbacks. The storyline lacks excitement and feels too brief. Figuring out how to conclude the game can also be challenging (for me xD). Additionally, despite the vastness of the game world, it begins to feel somewhat empty after 100 hours of exploration.Furthermore, certain elements in the game are puzzling in their purpose. For instance, the recipes involving turtle eggs are lackluster—not only are the eggs uninteresting to obtain, but the resultant soup offers little utility in gameplay and can be readily substituted. The architectural limitations are also perplexing; for example, building diamond-shaped structures should be feasible without resorting to exploits. I believe there's significant room for expanding the construction features in the game. Enhancing these elements could not only enrich the gameplay experience but potentially triple the amount of time players like myself would spend engaged with the game.Developers, there is an issue that needs addressing regarding the environmental interactions—specifically, the dynamics of fire and snow. It's unclear why fire does not affect snow on frozen lakes. Enhancements in these areas could significantly improve the realism and enjoyment of the game.Despite these issues, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game and consider it well spent.

I cought my self many times just mindlesly following the gps to the nex entrance or point of interest and not even looking around me to admire the nice surroundings. I think that making the map smaller but having the player really exploring the island without this unnecesery help would result in a much more engaging experience. Not to say that the story as of now is basicaly completly missing in this game. The end cutscene could have been fully omitted because you have no way of knowing why these things are happening anyways.looking forward to playing the full release non the less, but i really hope that some serious changes are on the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished... only a few caves are actually done, most are just a single room with a few crates. The AI is no threat at all, mutants can easily be avoided by just running past them and go down with a few hits of a good weapon, these weapons are far too easy to find and make fighting far too easy. The building system has some great ideas, but after your house is done there's just nothing more to build, and since resources are everywhere there's no need for storage at all. Eating raw fish is basically the same as eating cooked fish and has no negative drawbacks. The 3d printer has no use after the first visit, except for crafting a few arrows, which you can craft anyway, since a single bird drops 4 feathers. Most points of interest are identical and offer the same resources. Just like the first game it's gonna be a while until this game has actual content to offer, but paying 30 bucks for a game, which we finished in a single day just doesn't make sense. And I'm not talking about finishing just the main story, we "explored" every cave, point of interest, built a rather large base, collected most items and saw every type of enemy.

Probably the most frustrating part of it is that base building feels pointless - it's really not needed for survival. You can quickly pitch a tent anywhere to sleep through the night and enemies rarely feel like a threat. Loot is so plentiful (and respawns regularly) and so you have all the food, drink and tools you'll need just by revisiting points of interest.I'm sure there will be more to do in 2 years time when they finish the game, but my interest in it is already spent.This game is largely propped up by fanboy reviews. _childDocuments_.review: It's impressive that they have a great idea for a game yet screw it up YET again. It is fun to make a small house/base and fight off cannibals/monsters but the game feels so clunky. Everything is a chore in this game and takes too much effort which saps the fun out of it. Trying to complete the game felt like Walking Simulator, not a survival game. And to top it off, the story is completely god awful. We get zero context apart from emails and drawings which were made by a toddler. The ending is also terrible and makes no sense. Maybe if we were told who certain characters were and the meaning behind building/artifacts we could understand what was going on the game but nope! Let's make everything ambiguous because the people who made this game are either incompetent or don't care at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game in it's current state. The first few hours you're in the honeymoon phase, but that quickly wears off.The actual forest is beautiful; the graphics leaves nothing to be desired. The sound gives the world great ambiance. The seasons and weather give the world a nice flair. It's all beautiful.There's just no content to be had. You can build a base and defend it from the same 5 enemy types. You can wander back and forth across an empty island,  stumbling across a small camp of 3-4 enemies on your 15 minute walk.  I have a storage shed built filled with 16 shelves of supplies, but I have nothing to use it all on. There is no  the survival. Once you get one certain key item, you can finish the last bit of content within an hour or two (most of that spent walking through a quiet forest.)The survival aspect of the game is as simple as 1.) drink from any stream (of which there are many,) smack a squirrel and eat it (or eat people consequence free,) and sit/sleep/slam energy drinks occasionally.  If you want an aesthetic walking simulator, where 5 dudes occasionally show up to try and bust your base, this is for you. Hopefully the developers add a little more story content and a fleshed out sense of progress.You can tell a lot of effort went in to the design. Is it worth it? Does it make you feel like you spent $30 on an  game? Yes. Is that worth it?  I don't know anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent almost 30 hours in this game playing coop and solo for about the same amount of time. At the current state of the game i cannot recommend it for the price it is being sold, since i feel like i paid to play-test this piece of work.  It’ll be a pretty long one and may be rather chaotic because I have a lot of thoughts that I’d like to share.-Starting with the map – it’s huge and it is not a good thing. It doesn’t utilize the given space properly and so traversing the island feels like a long tourist hike with some mad people trying to jump you from time to time. We have probably spent more time running from one location to another, than actually exploring something. And since most of the caves are just dead-ends with minor supplies that may not even find place in your bag, it can be really frustrating by the end of the trip to realize you just spent about ten minutes for nothing. Why even add those small caves? The goods? Yeah, I’m very happy to find some more rope and cat food that I can’t even feet in my bag, since this stuff is all around the island in large quantities. -Mountain in the center of the island just sucks. It’s big, it’s empty, it’s annoying but it is fun sled down, if don’t get stuck on some tiny bump that is. At least we felt like herd of mountain goats climbing steep those slopes. -The NPC’s are rather underwhelming. It’s a nice change of pace to have an AI companion while playing alone but you probably won’t use Kelvin much, unless you want to settle somewhere. In that case he can provide you with sticks and rocks while you focus on some major tasks, did save me some time so he is not entirely useless. Didn’t utilize Virginia much, gave her a handgun once and haven’t seen here since-Who thought it was a good idea to place gun attachments right on top? How the hell am I supposed to aim down sights if I can’t see ♥♥♥♥.-Variety of ammunition for a bow and a shotty is pleasing. Not that big of a deal, but why would a revolver use 9mm ammo, wouldn’t it be like 357 or something like that, considering that it looks kinda like Mateba Autorevolver.-Crafting. It’s a little lacking for me. There are no pouches and bags to be crafted from deer skin but you can carry more stuff by default.  Sparing you the time to craft the items that enlarge you inventory but at the same time there is no feeling of progression whatsoever. And why can’t I attach a flashlight to the bow? Shooting bow requires both hands, as it should, and so I can’t use it in the cave, because I have to hold a lighter or a flashlight. “Just through a flare” one could say but the flare doesn’t give a lot of light and you have to KNOW there is something to shoot at, therefore you throw a flare in advance, preparing the stage for the upcoming fight. If you are caught with your pants down, better stick to melee of firearms. -Building. It’s animated real pretty from my point of view. But it’s pretty for the first 10 times, then it just gets annoying, because if want to build yourself a nice big NASA-like headquarters and your alone… lets just say it will take longer than half-life of uranium 235. I’ve spent half a night to build half of my base and the spiked fence made of logs took the most. Maybe I am an idiot and there is a way to place a schematic of a wanted fence and then just add logs but I have not found it. SO, two logs at a time, I’ve been running back and forward to just abandon this idea in the end, leaving half of my chosen territory open. I guess, don’t try to do everything you want at once, juggle exploration with building, at least try.-Story. At this point it shouldn’t have been added at all. We were left with the feeling of utter disappointment at the end of the “campaign”. I know it’s not finished, but then why put it in the game? Who the hell wants just some half-assed snippets of the plot with not even a boss-fight in the end. The ending sequence is just a long-run in the lava cave with a ton of one and the same enemy type… just why… who would think of that as entertaining…-Enemies. I just hope they add more varieties of the mutants later, because four for that matter is a rather pathetic number.-Combat. They added a parry option. You can’t upgrade your melee weapons like it was in the first game, where you used teeth and feathers to increase a specific stat. No sticky bombs and no head bomb, that’s a shame.-The major issue I have with the game is bugs. To be fair, they are mostly present in coop for some reason. There ain’t that much bugs but they occur too often and they break the game entirely. You play in constant fear of something breaking for one of your comrades to the point they are unable to continue and god forbid it’s the host, cause all of you will be forced to reconnect. The inventory key just inbound once for one of my friends and we couldn’t process what’s wrong for some time. You can power drill through the floor through intense spinning thus falling under the map. If you play with your friends they might push you through the ground while you goof around in your inventory.  You can walk underwater. Your camera may bug out preventing you from doing anything.  Sometimes you items lock on your hand so you can’t chose anything else. Sometimes enemy hitboxes don’t work properly but fairly it is quite rare.   I’ll be surprised if anyone reads this long-ass essay up to this point.  Overall, coop experience has been rather buggy, which killed a lot of fun for us. Playing the game solo afterwards has proven to be a lot more stable in terms of bugs and glitches, they still occur from time to time. Enormous map is still a problem, since it destroys the value of having a home or fortress because the distance you have to overcome is too great to build a home and make scavenge runs. I really hope this game gets better with updates, since I liked The Forest a lot back in the day. Definitely looking forward to this game becoming an amazing survival experience. I might have forgotten some details but I believe I stated every other major (for me personally) aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: 25/02/2023 For an early access title with a very small team, this is great, although its very basic in its current state. Building needs a whole lot of work and more options to custom build, I much preferred the building mechanics in the first game. The ending was very lack also, End-night need to add in end-game boss fight to make it exciting and improve how they tell the story throughout the game and add more to the game-play, The end section is just a copy-paste of one enemy type 20 times over then a cut-scene. Overall I'm enjoying the game just wanting more. the updates need to be massive or this game will be a great disappointment for me, as I've been waiting for it for around 5 years. 09/03/2023 Patch 1 has released! Endnight have added massive tweaks to the AI, new buildings and prefabs, the hand glider, binoculars & the first boss fight of the game, although the boss fight was quite underwhelming it's a step in the right direction. Nerfs to the shotgun and pistol feel needed and I find myself getting used to the bow more now and it seems to have improved aim. Fi-Z & MRE Packs have been halved as well, a much needed change! Overall a really good patch for the first couple weeks of release! Looking forward to plenty more. 23/03/2023 Patch 2 is Out! New Boss Fight, New Cave, Dead Cultists, WATER COLLECTOR HELL YEAH!, Loads of bug fixes and changes, keeping the game fresh. Keep it up EndNight!

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 a good few tips for any noobs. Eat freshly severed limbs in front of the dying original owner to assert dominance over the cannibals and make them fear you more.there is a completely free pistol in the orange lifeboat with no risks thanks to the cannibals not knowing how to swim.opening every boarded cave entrance early on increases loot quality around the world.killing cannibal children and mothers causes the population to decline and them to not attack you out of fear. the moment you spawn in, any cannibal you see, you kill on sight to prevent them from warning the others thus leaving you with a greater period of total peace.destroying cannibal camps further reduces the cannibal spawns making the area much more peaceful.when starting out any cannibal group you see acting weary and not immediately attacking can be pacified via acting aggressive and killing their members thus making them fear and not attack you for the length of the game.red mushrooms both damage you and provide a 5% movement speed bonusif you jump off a cliff and hold control you dont take any fall damage no matter the height

_childDocuments_.review: Very very disappointing!  I was a huge fan of The Forest since its release in 2014 and was very much looking forward to this release.  Sadly despite having a solid base "The Forest" of which to improve on and generate new content, somehow the Developer destroyed almost every aspect of the game.  The bugs are completely overwhelming and make the game unplayable.  To the point where it is virtually impossible to even build a defensive wall.  The Survival guide for example instructs you how to put a gate in a defensive wall.  So spend an hour trying to figure out why it won't work just to google it and find out its not implemented in the game yet.  And if you have a one foot sudden drop in the terrain forget about ever building that wall.  But even more sad is that even with your broken incomplete 20 foot long wall (That needed to be 50 feet) the AI is so broken that they jump right over your spiked wall and take no damage instead of just running around it.  This is only one example of the broken elements of the game.  In all aspects the game is plagued with bugs and virtually unplayable.  I have never seen such an unpolished game even as an Alpha.  Save your money for a few years... this one is gonna take more time to fix than the original I am sad to say.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, if you are not done with the game, and dont want to be spoiled, dont read the following review.---------------This game is super unfinished, in all ways. The game is super unoptimized, laggy and just annoying to play at times, sometimes me and my friends would lag through the map, and not being able to die or reset, lose all our progress due to not saving beforehand. The npcs were pretty unfinished, as Kelvin would chop down our treehouse, and Virginia just didnt shoot the enemies with the gun that we gave her. I found the game very uninteractive as for example, Virginia didnt need anything to trust us, she just did all of a sudden, we didnt even have to find her, but she just came to us randomely when we were building our base. The ending variations were super wierd as all of us seemed to have different endings, i saw Kelvin, my second friend saw virgina, and my third friend didnt see any of them. There were atleast 160 gaps in the story which left us all unsatisfied. There were 4 cutscenes in the entire game, and none of them except the ending and starting one felt impactful. The sled sucked, and wasnt really used for anything, except jumping down mountains not taking any fall damage, and either way there is an exploit while clicking B for the building book, used to not take any fall damage and glide 10x more effectively than the sled. But without a doubt, the worst part of the entire game was the unpolished story. There was no explanation as to how the Puffton family was relevant to the story. No explanation for the Sahara and Puffton bidding war. No explanation for why they warshipped the cube. No explanation as to why and what we wanted to go inside the cube for, except a wierd society that was just futuristic and didnt offer anything to us except a cool view ig? The story also contradicts the story of The forest 1, since they have completely different ways of describing why and how mutants come to be. The Forest 1 was just better in every single way. They made the game seem religious and scientific and the same time which just confuses the ♥♥♥♥ out of you. The story just didnt make any sense. Why were there demons, the demons are not related to the mutants, since the mutants dont burn by the cross. And no boss fights? Like come on, atleast ONE boss fight, after two years of delays. We didnt even get to end our playthrough because the game did not specify that if we pick our backpack in the ending, we are not allowed to escape with the helicopter. And since when you die, to get ur gear back, you have to pick ur backpack, we obviously thought that we somehow had lost our gear, and therefore needed to pick it up again, and then escape. But no, the game just ended and Edward Puffton just flew away, without us even getting to do anything about it. And who was the guy with the silver clothes that kept following us, and how was he relevant to the story?Idk i just think the game was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ confusing, laggy and just unfinished in every regard. If you are going to delay the release date for two years, make ur fans super excited and then release a ♥♥♥♥ game, for 30€, why not just delay it again and fix everything so the game actually is satisfying and fun. If the gameplay is going to be this laggy, and unoptimized, why not just focus on making a good story and ending for the players to engage in? Imo almost none of this game was worthy of the hype that has brewed up over these years that we have spent waiting for the game, and i could mention atleast 500 things more that annoyed about the experience, but i dont want my review to be longer than the essays that i write in school.The only good thing about this game is that the bugs are so damn stupid, that me and my friends had a good laugh at times because of it. The survival aspect was fine aswell ig. Please just fix the game with the following updates and we might give it another go in 2025, expecting that it will take atleast another 2 years for them to fix everything that makes this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: This game improves on everything the old one did. With an amazing storyline, beautiful graphics, and new features like the inventory, zipline, weapon variety, and tougher monsters, it captures what players loved about the original while adding more. The game feels like a true survival experience, even with its weird creatures, and the market needed something like this.After playing for weeks, my friends and I can't get enough of the surprises. Exploring caves often leads to finding new  mutants, badass weapons, or storyline pieces, keeping the game exciting. We’re nearly 100% complete without even trying because exploring is so much fun.Although the building system could use some work, which I hope will be improved in future updates, this game is a must-buy and you won’t regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most visually appealing games I have ever played. It also happens to be a great survival game with interesting and well thought out crafting/building mechanics, absolutely horrifying enemies, and an underlying narrative tying it all together layered with mystery and intrigue.But perhaps the best thing was that during a 4 hour session with 3 people, no one had a single stutter. Its without a doubt the most stable multiplayer experience I've had personally.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Almost everything is improved from the first game and its alot of fun.Positives:- Animations are way better- Moving around feels better- Controls are better- Graphics are improved- Audio is a good start- Gameplay is good fun- AI are creepy as hell- Base Building and crafting are great- Good atmosphere- There is actually alot of depth to this game under neither the top layer, tons of caves, lots of exploring, building tree fort bases, getting a 3d printer and so much moreNegatives:- Performance needs work- A few bugsOverall its go its issues with bugs and what not, but for day 1 early access release its in pretty good shape. Performance needs work, but other than that and the bugs I am loving everything else about this game. I am excited to jump in for some more and explore some more! It is early on but its a good start.This game has some of the best basebuilding around to, I would put it just behind Valheim and Enshrouded's basebuilding, as the 3rd best in the Survival genre.**Coming back for 1.0 today and its in better shape no doubt, performance is better, can use golf carts now, bigger map,etc.. lots of new stuff since I last played in Early Access. Its in pretty good shape now. Probably my 3rd favorite Survival game after Enshrouded and Valheim**
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: I had some reservations about purchasing Sons of the Forest due to my lack of enthusiasm for the first game, which wasn't necessarily bad, just somewhat tedious. Additionally, I had to play it alone since none of my friends owned a PC or The Forest. Although it was still enjoyable, the world seemed desolate and silent. Nevertheless, Sons of the Forest presents a world that feels inhabited even when I play alone, thanks to the presence of Virginia and Kelvin, who give me greater liberty to explore and combat the cannibals. Furthermore, the game's graphics are stunning, surpassing my expectations.If you're in search of a survival game, I highly recommend this one. However, be cautious, as the game's sounds may cause jump scares.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: The game is too linear. It doesn't feel like a survival game but more like a co-op story game. I don't know how to explain it but it just does not have nearly the same replay value as a lot of other games in this genre. The shelter building part of the game being pre-constructed things that you just place ruins it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Nowhere near what The Forest was. Sure the map looks good and is bigger, but that is IT. Caves are terribly planned out. There ARE no scary or threatening creeps, there are only a bunch of humanoid mostly bipedal thingies. Nothing to hunt but deer and moose as far as leather gathering is concerned, and both of those give the same type of leather. The story is so half-assed that I would call it quarter-assed if that was a thing. Some of these shortcomings are merely unjustifiable because all they had to do was to copy paste a few things from the previous game in order to at least give a satisfactory product for those who play the early access version. I am utterly regretful for buying this game. Dont buy it. Wait for them to 'finish' it, and only then give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: To give a genuine review after basically beating the game. (Possible spoilers)The first five minutes of the game brings back nostalgia. It is very similar to The Forest. The map is honestly way, way to big. There may be quite a lot to explore but out of the 10 hours I have played at LEAST half of it has just been walking. Which is insane, being teased with broken down golf carts and not being able to drive any of them? On such a huge map? I wish they would add forms of transportation, ziplines... sure. You would have to set them up, and they definitely would not be of huge use across the entire map.There are plenty of weapons, a pistol, revolver, shotgun, compound bow, crossbow, katana, machete, and more. The combat mechanics are basically the same as The Forest. I have no issues with them really, except the irons sights (for me) were shaking too much... and the attachments were put on in place of the iron sights? (Unless you can change it).It is somewhat confusing and honestly not worth the amount of time it takes to walk everywhere. I hope they improve on it, obviously it is early access.My biggest issue and I will say it again, was that it was a walking simulator. Exploring the same types of caves and basically seeing the same camps over and over again. I really do not want to crap on the game, and I really did enjoy playing it. But after 10 hours it just gets boring. Game has SO MUCH POTENTIAL! And clearly it is early access. But wait to spend the $30.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Has a lot of jank to look past and a lot of features that are missing from the first game but overall can still be fun with friends. The price tag is steep for early access, however you can rest easy knowing the devs will most likely deliver on making this a great game; as they delivered with their first game and polished it from the fun mess it was in 2014 to an amazing game over the next 6 or so years.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Few times am i as excited about a game like Sons of the forest. it builds upon the AI system of the first to add tribes and leaders to cannibals. More enemy types than ever before but the minecraft style building and survival aspects of this game make it the real deal.it should be a smash hit. And if you are looking for a co op game what are you waiting for? Me and my girl live off this game
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: After reading the negative reviews I really thought it wouldn't apply to me, I really like the first one and wanted more Forest.  I guess I got it - it's more of the Forest, but not in a good way.  Everything feels like it's been multiplied to take longer or be more difficult: the map is bigger, there are more items to find, more stuff to build, more enemies to fight.  My only side note is if this sounds good to you, this is exactly what it is.  The original Forest was a really tight game, that felt like the perfect length.After a while I just ran out of steam.  The story doesn't feel like its going anywhere.  The new characters don't really do anything - you can give them tasks or weapons but there's little interaction beyond that.  There's more enemy types but many are just annoying spear/arrow/bullet sponges that return again and again and again.  It's The Forest with Quantity, but sadly just doesn't feel like Quality.  It might be good for multiplayer, I played both of these solo.

It is now patch 2 and they improved the story, added a new boss, etc etc. I think the end result of sons of forest is going to be a really good complete game and the future seems bright. If you want the full experience I would wait untill it near full release so you don't have to wait but the game as it is now is good.

_childDocuments_.review: SOTF looks gorgeous, feels great and has a lot of people excited considering the first game was amazing.This game feels empty. Kilometres of Forest, and no activities to fill it apart from a handful of empty caves that get your hopes up, and some pointless graves you can dig up for the same loot you can find in the barren caves and underground bunkers with next to no danger.But you can build cool tree bases!Unlike the first game, finding documents and pages don't give any feel or importance to the story. In the first game, if you found a document, there would be music to signify the importance, and it would get everyone excited because it genuinely meant a lot and left you to piece together the puzzle.In SOTF, if you find a brochure or document, it genuinely doesn't feel like anything. There is no feeling of building up to a grand story climax. We spent 2 hours last night exploring in hopes to get somewhere, where we explored 2 locations and we walked for 90% of it. The underground systems we explored were underwhelming, lacking any significance apart from the endgame door we randomly found, which again had no lead up to it. Caves are bland and are just dumped full of the same loot over and over again. after a couple of hours of playing, you literally have everything you need to finish the game resource wise.I haven't played a game in a while where dying has no consequence. If you're exploring and happen to die, you just respawn back at a cannibal camp where you literally pick up your backpack with your items and walk straight out. NO consequence. This game is so underwhelming and unfinished. I hope to come back when the devs finish it.

_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so, this hurts to write. I love survival games, I love the Forest, and I love Kelvin, but this game falls short on so many levels. It's buggy to a fault, so buggy that when playing in a multiplayer game, half of our group glitched out and did not get to complete the story. The progression in the game made little sense at most times, oftentimes we would not have a need for the majority of items we found, relying on the same few that we did already have until the end game, and then only having those for a short period of time. Exploration felt like a drag, there was very little purpose in doing it at all besides to get the few items that are integral to the story, and even then they are barely integral. Along with that, the story itself was lackluster at best and bad at worst, there was seemingly zero reason for anything to happen, and random cutscenes and events would play out with some boring and honestly disappointing outcomes.The ending was bland, uninspired, and frankly just bad, meaning everything that you progressed for felt wasted. I cannot help but feel like this is a massive departure and downgrade from the Forest, and that's horribly disappointing. I hope that in time, this game will be fully released, but as of now, I could not recommend to anyone wanting a time as enjoyable as the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: To build a basic tent is 1 stick stuck in the ground and a tarp you throw over it. It looks as dumb and impractical as it would in real life. This is just one of the many examples of how the game threw out the heart it had in the original "FOREST". I came in thinking it was just going to be a sequel to Timmy's story,  It seemed he was still turning into a mutant at the end of the first one, so i thought him and his father would return to the island for that reason. Or maybe they found out there is a "sister" island, doing the same thing but still ongoing and at a greater rate, and they might have the cure to being a mutant or find others like Timmy so he won't feel isolated/different.  Instead i got the military goes to save rich people, because they are missing and they are rich.So not only did the fun survival element against cannibals turned out to be a let down, the story did too. And it really doesn't make sense why they would go for this angle because, assuming if everyone has played the first game, you already know the island is filled with cannibals and the secret behind that. So there is no mystery element this time which means you'd have to rely on the investment you had with the already established characters (Timmy and Father) and how the game operated already.Speaking of the cannibals, i liked the old design better because they looked like feral people, now they look like  they could be in Fallout. Not to mention there are way less variants than the original. Now the island itself... it feels so empty, its too large, there isn't enough landmarks to recognize where you are. So it creates the feeling that no matter where you go, you're in the same spot. The Ai helper is a bit of a weird addition, and sort of destroys the feeling of being stranded on a island alone (or with friends) and although its nice to have a constant stream of sticks flooding into the base, it just feels like it takes away the challenge of having to survive in the wilderness, but you can kill the Ai which is nice. One more thing i will mention, the game is less... "iconic". In the first game you had the opening title song which i thought was suppose to be a way to give the game an identity, like have it as its "theme song", and now that's just gone, and replaced with generic action music. The little gags like how the voice acting was a bit silly, is also gone, instead it just seems like it takes itself too seriously. The "Son's of the Forest" just reminds me more of "Green Hell" than "THE FOREST".All in all, i just thought i was going to get the "FOREST" with more blueprints a new story that relates to the first game, maybe have that one part of the island where its all covered in snow now available, and then just have the weather system included, and more unique cannibals to kill.(Yes i know this game is in Early access but more times than not, the early access game resembles the final product but with all the bugs and glitches fixed.)

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game, and I'm loving this one even more. I am officially addicted.Post full release review:If you loved the first game, you will love this one even more. They took all of the great things from the first game and built upon it to create a truly immersive, addicting experience. I can't recommend this game enough. Although you do not have to play the first game to enjoy this one, I still recommend playing the first game. There are lots of little details hidden through out the map that reference the first game. The content that you get for the price is remarkable, and it really puts a lot of these triple A games/companies to shame. Grab some friends and enjoy exploring and surviving this terrifying, beautiful and mysterious island! You won'r regret it... or maybe you will when you go to sleep at night... way past your bedtime... with dishes in the sink and laundry piled up... because you haven't done anything else with your time... attempting to go to sleep because you have work in the morning, but you're dreaming of dark, dripping caves... just buy the damn game and play it lol

_childDocuments_.review: Expected something more, even in terms of a late 'early access' change. I'm of the opinion that early access was the way to go from the beginning for it and that it was slightly like upsetting for them to change it last minute. I'm leaving a not recommended review only because I think too many people are blindly giving it a good one. Perhaps I'm an outlier but while I did enjoy the first game, I didn't put more than fifty hours into it and I absolutely love survival games. Why? Because the world is empty, the systems are empty, and the only saving grace was cave exploration and enemies.Perhaps I didn't get there yet but I really wanted some larger cannibal settlements, like where you could actually see this 'amazing AI' living their lives and return to. Instead they all seem to be in small camps. I wanted hostile bears and wolves at the very minimum... and I'm not even sure if the boars from the first game exist or not? Imagine hostile bears and wolves that fight the cannibals too, or perhaps some tribes even have wolves working with them? Why do the enemy types solely have to be cannibals? Well, it's because animal AI just sucks. Other people complain about it so I'm not going to get into it, but animals are just dumb, they clip through rocks, deers run underwater as if there's no water there.Cannibals still can't swim, why? Who knows. I come out of the water in a cave to find several of them and probably would have lost the fight if they didn't all chase me into the water and drown in literally two seconds. The world is bigger than the first game but it just amounts to more time playing running simulator as there's really nothing interesting that warrants running that far. Seasons change... very weirdly? You wake up tired? There's no log sled? Seriously how is there no log sled? Oh right, we have Kelvin so that means no more log sled? If only Kelvin's AI wasn't so jank. Seriously the lack of a log sled is incredibly upsetting. In multiplayer with up to 8 players, there is only one Kelvin, and yes you can send logs back to points on ropes or use water but water is really jank, logs glitch and bounce up at times weirdly it's all really jarring. This game is not finished. The cave system is linear and spelled out to you, seriously every spot is marked on the map there doesn't seem to be anything really hidden. I explored in caves in all these little secret spots expecting to find some hidden loot even if it was a few duct tape, nope, they kept everything super linear.Honestly this game adds almost nothing cool and just removes so much of The Forest's items. Very weird. Squirrels also run straight through rocks and trees, even cannibals do too sometimes. The AI talked so highly in the vidyas really didn't amount to much either, basic improvements to the first game's AI. (Yes I'm sure there's technically a lot more done to them but it doesn't really feel like it.)I will say though... the best thing about the game is that Virginia's white t-shirt in the rain becomes see through. Amazing innovation.I'm not sure why we had to keep the same system of applying armor to get like 1/9 bars of armor or however many it is. I would have much rather have had outfits you wear for each piece like chest, legs, head, etc, and perhaps they had durability. I get that they're trying to do their own thing but other survival games just feel better, and we have tech armor but ultimately nothing's that cool because if you do get a full set of some sort of armor it just breaks super fast like an extra health bar and then you gotta make more. I want to see my survivor decked out in some wolf headress and actually roughing it.This feels like a game, much like the first game, where it's just short of greatness but ultimately bland and not replayable enough unless you like building a base/defenses/traps but that's the limit of what you can do and I'm not even sure if you can get the horde mode item to bring a bunch of them to you, or even a lot of the items for base building from the first.Oh lordy I didn't even mention the 'hotkey system' no longer can you hit 1-4 to pull out selected items. You have to be at a complete standstill, take out your backpack, and select something from it. It takes forever and in combat it is super frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty fun but very short lived for $30. Played multiplayer and we had nearly no problem running through all the caves in the game. I had several bugs where I would pull out my backpack and the game would then replayed the sound effect every 0.1 seconds and then it would drop frames until it was just frozen in the matter of 2 seconds. Had to quit and close game completely to fix as just leaving and rejoining my friend didn't fix it. Also had another bug where after encountering a cut scene the game wouldn't let me pick anything up or open my backpack and to get back to the location I would have to travel a large distance again and I was just not in the mood for running simulator.Section TLDR: Game breaking bugs found in Multiplayer that require full game restarts not just disconnect and reconnect to fix.So besides bugs we also have caves marked on the map but not all of them are caves to explore. Several are just resource caves that have a few wooden boxes in their one room. Super annoying when you hit the point where you already are max on every piece of equipment. You can get guns and attachments like flashlight and laser sight but be warned they suck. They cover the iron sight so you can no longer aim down sight and for the crossbow you're guy doesn't aim it straight ahead he has it pointed down to the left so the laser just doesn't work on it since you have to aim down the sight of the gun to get the laser pointed in the right direction but by doing so your entire view is blocked by crossbow and the laser sight device placed on the iron sight.Section TLDR: Caves are either explore-able caves or resource rooms and Gun attachments block iron sights and just suck in general.Guide book also sucks. The first game's building was by using a book and flipping through different tabs and having several options on each tab. It was quick to flip through. This one gives you a book where you have to switch which hand is holding it to change what you want to build and its a press and hold to switch hands. Then to flip through the book you get tabs that aren't really labeled well for what they are and you get two images of things you can build before clicking to go to the next page so you have to spend more time flipping through pages looking for what you want, not to mention possibly having to switch which hand the book is in as the piece you are trying to build may be in the other section. Also some recipes you need the item in your hand instead of in the book. Campfires need sticks in your hands to craft instead of in the crafting book like everything else is in it.Section TLDR: Crafting is split up with no hint as to what you need in your hands to craft and takes a long time to find the one thing you are trying to craft.NO ACTUAL STORY. Game had this random guy in green jacket just show up and no explanation of who he is.Full TLDR: Game is just not in a good spot. Bugs that are game breaking, features that weren't thought out for ease of use or simple functionality, and cave systems that were enjoyable experiences are now a coin flip if they are an actual cave or just a pointless resource room.

_childDocuments_.review: And by this I mean, that it is a decent game and it has a lot of the elements what made The Forest so great, but somehow it falls short what it was aiming to deliver in the first place. And this is especially true for the story.In the first game (The Forest) everything is a mystery right until the very end when you discover the labs, within the artifacts and what they do and suddenly all pieces fall in to place and make sense. The crash landing, your son being taken, how the mutants came to be... (except the cannibals, those are never addressed). Of course what the artifacts are, where they come from, etc... are still unknown, but you have the sense of accomplishment in the end. You feel like that part of the story is irrelevant in the conclusion.Here the game tries to focus more on the artifacts and the mystery around them, but things are detached, vague and meaningless at best. You piece some parts of the story together about the Pufftons and the guy who smacked you in the face in the beginning. (Don't know why he just didn't killed you by the way...). But all these tiny nuggets of lore are meaningless. Too small and too vague to make sense.The funny thing is, that on the Island you visit places with information source galore. Books, laptops, papers, etc... but the few little things you can actually pick up are just some pieces of paper of an email printout with 1-2 sentence saying absolutely nothing.It feels like the game tries to be mysterious whilst you are constantly denied access to sources of information along the way.The hows and whys are detached as well. On one hand you know how the mutants came to be on the Island, but then you ask the question why are there unmutated cannibals? What is the relationship between these mutants and the ones from the Forest?Nothing gets answered.And the ultimate culmination of the story. Absolute garbage, uninteresting, unresolved mess, with meaningless cut-scenes.Another disheartening experience in terms of the story events are that the triggers happening over and over again. Like when you get near a military camp where a chopper takes off when you get close. Now that animation happens every time. It just doesn't make any sense and completely breaks the immersion.One of them is useful for maintaining base gathering stuff.The other is dumb, can't shoot proper and you cannot tell her anything to do.Anyone else you encounter means absolutely nothing.The guy in the beginning (the main villain so to speak)? You see him 1-2 times, but no interaction, no meaning, no cut-scenes where he tells  you some info. Just an empty shell that has absolutely no context.Timmy? The same. Appears out of nowhere, does absolutely nothing, tells you nothing and overall a useless character in the plot. Him being there does nothing to the plot.Crafting is the same concept as in the first game, but besides giving you more resources and such, you can't really make more things. For example you can't make rope, whilst that is an essential for bone armor, so you scour the points of interest for respawned resources.Or sticks... You can't go and chop up a log to make sticks? Or that there are items you can have hundreds of it, like the cloth piece, but you can only have 6 rope or so?I am pretty sure 500 pieces of cloth is going to take up more space then 5 rope.And then there are the things you can't even throw away, like animal heads you picked up, or the human arms, legs and head you picked up. You can only throw the human parts away, when they have become rotten, but animal heads don't rot?It's insane how certain things just don't make any sense whatsoever in the menu system.So this whole situation makes the gameplay kind of awkward. The story revolves around an event that happens at a given point in time. A point which can be as far as you want it to be, because there is no countdown, no sense of urgency, nothing. This makes the story and the survival and building aspect of the game mutually exclusive and one has to suffer and give way to the other. In this case it's the story.You could spend years on the island not even lifting a finger for the sake of story progression, which just doesn't make any sense whatsoever.Bumping in to Timmy at a big door, trying to open it, then going away to for X  (where X >= 1 day) amount of time and he is still there doing the same thing, just standing and contemplating about what the key to the door is. Or perhaps meditating about his poor life choices.So from a story standpoint a simple explore, uncover and solve kind of game type would've been certainly a better choice. The old Farcry game comes to mind. Punch it with a time limit and you have something great. Sure it's not replay friendly, but this isn't either.From a survival aspect, it has a lot of boxes ticked, except for a few, which sound silly. Like the rope thing. Not being able to craft such a necessary item just makes the game dumb by cheesing the respawning of resources.It was fun playing with a friend, but ultimately a letdown compared to the first one. I am a big story guy and if the story sucks, or the delivery of it sucks, I just cannot give it a thumbs up.And this story, or at least how it was told sucked big time. It completely made me lose interest in whatever comes next. I like some mystery, but when you go through a game and you just don't know what the hell happened in it and you come away from it more dumb... Then it's a bad game.It's just a rushed, hot mess. Or at least it feels like that.

(If this dev makes it there) Spoilers ahead:- The voice acting is some of the worst Iv ever heard.- You will never be allowed to have enough ammo and all these modern guns are dwarfed in power by The Forests Flintlock Pistol which is a complete joke. - The rifle is LITERALLY weaker than the crossbow and doesn't have any attachments.-The alt ending to get the artifact makes no sense for having both a worse version of an artifact than the previous game and its a laughably terrible ending only beaten out by an even worse version of the main ending from where it was in Early Access.- Being as aware as possible as to what the entire story of Sons of The Forest is in its entirety, the story makes no sense at all. Why did this random doctor at the end know about Timmy's affliction or the ores existence and therefore purpose? Understanding it all, its not hard to see that the entire existence of Sons etc. is to just be a buffer story setting up for game #3 in the laziest way. - Getting through the double door wearing the charged alien armor, apparently Timmy is using gods personal sidearm because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does he just do the entire run through himself leaving the players in the dust to kill nothing at all until an obligatory boss fight 30 seconds before the main obligatory boss fight who dies with like 4 explosives.Worse than original in most ways with very few improvements which mostly stem from the graphics. _childDocuments_.review: A mix of the classic horror movie "the Descent" and what it would be like to crash landed on a hostile cannibal island. Once they respect you, you can generally find your way unimpeded. The cannibal AI is a lot of fun to mingle with. Trying to stay neutral with them for as long as possible at first was interesting but sooner or later things will get ugly. A fantastic title solo but I imagine playing this with buddies would be an absolute blast. Melee combat feels really good and the dismemberment is a nice touch. If you enjoy Subnautica but wouldn't mind more horror, combat, and defence elements this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a good game once released, but for now I would not recommend it.  This is based only on the Early Access version 33592 (March 2023).   The current game progression is gatewayed behind time wasting destinations at all ends of the island.   Which beacon signal do you go to first?   The game doesn't tell you.   So you may well spend 30 minutes of your real time traveling to a beacon on the GPS only to find out you need a certain key card to enter the bunker/cave.  So that's 1 hour of real player time wasted because now you have to walk the 30 minutes back to camp.  To make things worse, all the key card readers are exactly the same (Blue) and you have no idea which card you need.Walk to a beacon the other side of the entire island and you can enter a cave only to discover you need both a Zipline gun and an under water breather to progress. Again, I think the game will be great, but only once they address all the walking and walking and walking and walking required.

It's more in depth, a bit more realistic, and just as scary. For being in early access (in my experience) it runs pretty damn good. I have nothing bad really to say about this yet.

_childDocuments_.review: It has carried over the best parts of "The Forest," and improved upon the bad parts. It is graphically stunning, the map is bigger and the A.I. is now more complex. However, I will admit that a ton of work needs to be done. First of all, I have come across a ton of bugs: automatic walking in the survival guide menu, cursor stuck on the screen when exiting out of the survival guide, needing to go in and out of the menu to drink water from streams, A.I. characters walking through walls (there's more but they're the major ones.) Also, while Kelvin was a nice idea, he doesn't always function the way you'd want him to. Sometimes, when asking him to gather logs, he will start taking the logs already on the floor around you and give them back to you which renders him useless. He also, occasionally,  gets in the way when you're trying to build which makes him a bit of a nuisance too. I do believe that if Endnight put in the work, they could actually make him useful, but at the moment I can't say he is.I find the building system to be interesting and it is certainly unique, but is also unnecessarily difficult and counter intuitive. It also can be a pain sometimes. For an example, it is nearly impossible to place vertical beams against horizontal beams because of the snapping feature. I also don't understand how you are even able to make a base that is defensive, baring in mind that they haven't re-implemented the lockable gates they had in TF (Please add them back in Endnight.) Apart from those major complaints, I am enjoying the exploration and immersion Sons Of The Forest offers and I do understand that this game will see a lot of changes in the future as it is in Early Access but it feels far from being a finished game at this stage. I'm excited to see how this game comes together though. Edit: Defensive wall gates have now been added.

_childDocuments_.review: It is basically The Forest with prettier visuals, a bigger map, two NPCs that can help you (or stand in your way, asking to be accidentally murdered by you while chopping trees) and a mediocre story.If you haven't played The Forest: buy The Forest instead.If you liked The Forest and want more of exactly the same and don't care about a worse story: buy it on sale.If you liked The Forest and expect a vast improvement or overhaul or a better story: don't buy it.It promised to be revolutionary with its creative building system and building animations, but it disappoints with sometimes frustrating mechanics that won't always allow you to do what you are trying to do. Even after the 1.0 release, the game still suffers from day one bugs like disappearing food, water splashing sounds when throwing logs on to solid ground etc. The map is huge and is good at one thing: wasting your time traversing around cliffs and mountains because everything of worth is scattered. You may use vehicles, but their controls are abysmal - running is usually faster. There are some nice new traps or objects, but most of the blueprints are copies or variations of the ones from The Forest.I wish I could give this a neutral rating since we had some fun in CoOp. Still, it pales in comparison to its predecessor (with the exception of its better graphics).

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded on an island teeming with cannibalistic creatures, players are thrust into a world where survival hangs by a thread. As they venture deeper and deeper into the abyss, they are swallowed by the very darkness they once feared. Day by day, they started to descend into the depths of moral ambiguity and ethical uncertainty.What was once a struggle for survival evolves to a twisted game of dominance as the players mercilessly prey upon the natives of the land descending further into madness, feasting their flesh, burning the remaining parts as they gather the bones to craft their very own armor. The fear of the cannibal became a distant memory as they ravel their newfound weapons, building effigies adorned with the body parts of their fallen foes — a twisted monument of their wickedness.The villainy of the players didn't end there. As they face more powerful foes such as the mutants  they show no mercy as they ruthlessly skin them as they fall helplessly into the ground, gruesomely wearing their skin to enhance their armor in their pursuit of dominance all over the land. Yet, in the amidst of chaos, Virginia, a mutant herself, defies the expectations.  Her actions force us to question who the real monsters are.Though the sight of the cannibals consuming their fallen comrades or taking unattended supplies was a chilling reminder of the harsh realities of their world. Occasionally, they can be observed worshiping and hitting one another.Little did the players know, these cannibals are not mindless and heartless beings. They know how to scout, taunt, ask for help, and even assist when their ally falls down. They beg for mercy, retreat, retaliate, and avenge their fallen comrades. They mourn and become angry when their companions die.Despite their savagery, a curious sight emerges: within their camps, captured mutants are left unharmed unless released by the player. Similarly, even players, instead of being killed outright, are captured and left unharmed until they attempt to escape - a very strange relationship between the island's inhabitants.The game is a chilling reminder of the depths to which humanity can sink in when faced with the ultimate test of survival. Will you embrace the darkness, or will you rise above it and reclaim your humanity?

_childDocuments_.review: (I feel like this game will be worth the 16€ it was on sale so I'm recommending it despite the issues I list here.)We wanted the balanced/true experience much like in the first game, so we naturally picked normal difficulty, being the next step up from "peaceful".So far base building has proven itself to be absolutely useless. With Kelvin the resource grind is much more tolerable than in the first game, but in the original we still managed to build a bigger house faster despite having to fetch all the materials ourselves. Additionally, all your stats are blinking red and you're getting the fourth instant spawn swarm that's coming over to one shot you and break your stairs and a wall.Overall swarms kind of lose meaning when you semi-permanently have three crawly guys stalking you from the bushes and harassing Kelvin, plus a swarm whenever you find a minor new location.This is very much more "Forest", while it improves on a handful of aspects it does not on many others. _childDocuments_.review: I just played through it in co-op. I really enjoyed playing the first Forest part. Accordingly, I expected a lot from the second part.The first few hours were really good and exciting. The typical forest feeling.But then things quickly went downhill: You realize that the large open world is completely pointless because there is almost nothing interesting to discover. And if you happen to find something by chance, it's what feels like the hundredth generic cannibal camp. The building mechanics work well and do what they're supposed to do. If you want to build a base, it works really well. But that's not really necessary, as you could just rush from cave to cave (we didn't do that). And anyway, you can find so much food that you hardly ever have to hunt or grow plants and stuff like that. It's a real shame, because in the first Forest it felt much more convincing when you had to rely on these survival mechanics. Anyway, I found it very strange that you can find so many of all the items and that the inventory is very quickly full of all sorts of stuff. Not exactly a convincing survival mood in which a shortage of resources should happen (at least at the beginning).The whole atmosphere and feeling feels off: I didn't feel the dense mood from the first part again. Often it didn't feel like survival either.Some items you find don't feel like they fit into the setting. Golf carts and unicycles, for example - even if they were fun to ride at least at the beginning - do not contribute to a convincing immersion. Even though you need the vehicles to traverse the empty and uneventful world, it doesn't change the fact that something like that doesn't fit into the feeling of Forest for me. The whole game feels like a bad and inspired copy of the first part. The caves, which were intense and dangerous in the first part, are also (sometimes) dangerous in the second part, but somehow offer little excitement. And it feels like the caves are much less branched and oppressive than in the first part, which doesn't add to the immersion.The finale of the game is absolutely disappointing and doesn't offer a good, final boss fight or anything that stays in the memory. The bad ending made me feel ripped off. Unfortunately, the finale is the worst part of the game.I'm sure I could think of other points that I didn't like, but I said enough.At most a 4/10. Before the final it was still a 5/10. But the finale leaves you completely speechless, it's that bad. There were some moments and phases in which I had fun, but the bottom line is that unfortunately the negative outweighs the positive.If there is a third part, I hope it will be more like the first. Perhaps the second part was an attempt to make Forest accessible to an even larger audience. In my opinion, this is not the right direction (purely in terms of gameplay). If you have never played a forest before, you should definitely prefer the first part.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this while it released in Early Access and part of me wishes I would have waited for a more complete release. Despite the island feeling mostly complete, there are major balancing and mechanical issues present as of today. Several mechanics in this game seem down right unnecessary. For instance, there's this fleshed out, expansive building system that has been re-worked, improved and expanded upon. Building now provides the player freedoms that simply weren't present in The Forest. The only issue is, there's absolutely no need to build any structure beyond a cheap two-second tent which costs nothing more than a stick and a tarp. Then you can disassemble it when you're done to get your parts back. The world provides you with more food, water and items than you'll ever require. Your inventory is basically 20 times the size of what's actually necessary for the difficulty of this release. I went the entire game without ever touching the majority of the items or weapons I was offered. I don't believe my health ever dropped below half and that was only during an AFK moment. There's no exaggeration in claiming that you could easily beat this title with nothing more than your starting tactical axe and a few food items. Even thirst can be satiated at almost any water source you'll run across. Focusing on the story brings up other concerns. I don't want to spoil what's been written but completing the game in its entirety with the "good" ending might leave you scratching your head. Hopefully, this will be revised or improved in some way prior to a full release. I'm going to give this game a positive rating because what's here is still fun to play, especially in co-op. Brokenness aside, I still believe anyone who enjoyed The Forest will find pleasure here but you may want to hold off until it's no longer in Early Access.Edit: Came back to play this entirely from beginning to end once again with a buddy here in 2024 now that the game has been officially released. Most of what I previously mentioned still stands, although they did add some additional locations, mechanics and story beats. Overall, a fun adventure and world to explore with friends. You still won't have any necessity to build anything more than the most basic of shelters nor will you use 90% of what you collect and pack into the most insanely stocked backpack I've ever seen. I'd still recommend the experience to others.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most disappointing, overrated game I have ever played. I am extremely doubtful that 6-8 months of early access will fix a game that was last delayed for "polish" and has fundamental gameplay problems. The game is a shallow, boring, sluggish, trek through an obnoxiously vague and incomplete story and ultimately takes a giant step back from the first game overall. The enemy AI is unbelievably over-hyped by the developers and community. If there are any intricate or complex systems beneath the hood of the AI, they certainly do not present themselves to the player whatsoever. At best, they have a small handful of visually striking but quickly repetitive animation states that unfortunately just loop back into "attack the player" or "run away and attack later" every single time. There is no depth to the player's relationship with the AI at all, and they do not actually do anything intelligent. All this talk about factions, religions, individual feelings, competing for resources, leadership, etc is nowhere to actually be found despite a few surface level visual instances that make the AI seem more interesting than they really are.  There is no reason to not just run past everything or kill everything you see in your path because you will always just get attacked no matter what. There is no tug of war between peace and violence with the AI. There's no trading, recruiting, alliances, morality, decisions, dialogue, borders, friendships, romance, etc that we see in other games. There is nothing to them besides attacking you very often. The base building is shallow and pointless. The only reason you would build a base is to scratch a creative itch. There is no gameplay incentive to build a base. It does nothing for you, and nothing requires a base. If you do decide to build a base, enjoy a tiny sample of building options that is somehow missing multiple things from the first game. Have fun building your variation of an empty log cabin and attempt to fortify your walls guarding a few pieces of drying meat you really don't need. All you are doing by building a base is prolonging your progression through this horrible game. There is less to craft than the first game. There is an overabundance of everything and most of it is completely unnecessary. You can totally get through this game with just your starter axe and a couple "key" items.  The survival elements - hunger, thirst, and sleep - feel more like an annoying inconvenience than something that actually matters. There really isn't much of a penalty felt for being low in these stats besides taking a hit to your stamina, which only sucks because you know you have 50 more miles to run to the next boring part of the map. How they work between each other and in conjunction with the "strength" stat is not explained by the game either. I didn't really understand the "strength" stat the entire game, and it didn't matter. There are no player stats, perks, upgrades, skills, or anything else to work towards for your character besides adding more useless junk to your inventory.  Almost nothing in your inventory can be upgraded either.Combat is janky and bare bones. Every single enemy in the game is melee focused. They all blend in with each other. You can approach every enemy the same way. The guns feel ok and powerful. Almost everything else is a variation of the same function. Some are very overpowered. But it also doesn't matter, because you can also just run past everything if you want to, even in the late game. There's no arenas, no boss fights, no enemy traps or surprises, or anything remotely memorable about combat. Caves are horrible, linear hallways with a rocky texture that lead you to some other item you most likely don't need. They are far worse than the first game. There's no network, branching paths, boss fights, nothing. Literally just sprint in a straight line through each cave and you are good to go. Some "caves" are one-room environments that offer just a couple resources you are probably full on. I don't know if these are simply unfinished, or intended to be this way. Hunting is bland and boring. Animal life just randomly paths around. They are just there. There is also fresh water just about everywhere. The story is once again communicated through picking up mysterious pieces of paper, books, pamphlets, etc in no particular order that I guess you are supposed to look at in your inventory and then try your best to come up with something cohesive yourself. There is one line of dialogue. Characters appear out of nowhere with no context. The ending is atrocious. I have no idea what happened. I don't even know who some characters were. Story is virtually nonexistent. This time around, you have a GPS that somehow doesn't have a compass. This GPS is marked with points of interest you are supposed to visit as the player. There is very little to be discovered organically this time around. Caves are marked on your GPS. Story progression areas are marked on your GPS. All of these are overly dependent on one particular item as well. The whole game, you are just bouncing from ping to ping on your GPS in search of this item, just to backtrack to everywhere you've already been but couldn't do anything at because you didn't have this one item. These areas are almost copy and paste in their assets and ideas as well. There's no clever puzzles, problems, to solve, difficult decisions to make, or anything that requires you to actually use your brain. The game is just wandering around this huge map with nothing in it praying you find the one or two items you need to push through a garbage story not knowing or caring why you're doing anything you're doing. The graphics are ok. The weather effects are decent, although the different seasons simply load in right before your eyes. There is no smooth transition between them. They are on a schedule and just happen. They don't do anything that I could tell to impact gameplay either. World is empty. Cannibal camps might as well be copy and paste prefabs sprinkled around the map. That's about it. There's seriously nothing else to see.Audio is horribly mixed and buggy. Some weather effects are abhorrently loud. Sometimes you'll hear random water splashes beneath the surface of the grass. The most annoying one is when you swear you hear a cannibal scream right next to you, only for you to turn around and see nothing there. Overall there is just nothing interesting here aside from a few enemy animations that wear thin after the first couple times you see them. This is particularly disappointing following all the hype, delays, and the developers' ambition to deliver "the next step in survival games." I feel like every other survival game I have played has done it better than this. Again, I do not think I am being too harsh as the initial release date was May 2022, and its last delay was for "polish," in the developers' own words before this sudden "early access" announcement a mere few weeks before a supposed 1.0 release. Disappointed is an understatement.
