_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's been obsessed with the first game I've gotta say that this one is almost a disappointment. I've been anticipating this game for a long long while (as far back as 2019 when it was announced) and I was obviously mindful of the fact that endnight are a small development studio, but I feel like this is not good enough. Don't get me wrong the game has some amazing features and upgrades compared to the original such as:- better visuals- cooler weapons- very interesting building mechanics- Kelvin and Virginia- bigger map- better AI- really cool inventory and craftingHowever, despite all of that it feels like they haven't fully fleshed it out (or at least the core functions of it). I am obviously aware that the game is in early access and I am more than confident that it will be a much better product to purchase a couple of months down the line (or an year), but they had more than enough time in my opinion. As for some of the negatives:- map is wayyyy too big (nothing to do and hard to travel through)- caves are either stupidly hard or stupidly easy- story in unfinished- many assets are reused- building (albeit interesting) is expensive and heavily limited- HORRIBLE optimisation (rtx2060, 16GB RAM, ryzen 5 3600 and I get 45-60 fps on the lowest possible setting)Genuinely I thing that those things are easily fixable and within a couple of months they will be done, however, what I really think the developers should focus on is the cost and flexibility of building and the optimisation. I wouldn't mind playing on the lowest graphics, but for the love of god can I get 60-70fps consistently. I realise that I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for what seems to be small stuff, but "The Forest" is also badly optimised.In conclusion, get this game now if you are on the dickriding wave (like myself) and you will have a fun time trying to figure out how things work-out. If you are a more casual fan of these games then I'd recommend you wait until the end of the year when the game will be in a bit more stable and playable state as right now you will get bored of it and feel like you wasted your money.(sorry if I was waffling a lot or was being unclear, this is my first ever review)

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: This is an early access game. Don't buy it if you expect a full release. You'll definitely run into some optimisation issues and things like that. So keep that in mind before you hit the "Buy" button.This game is absolutely great. The graphic looks amazing, the AI is fantastic and the gameplay is a lot of fun. If you'd played The Forest, you'll feel home again - even with all those changes you'll figure out while playing. The map is really big, the forest is amazing and sometimes I am completely stunned watching nature doing it work.The enemys are harder now as in the first game in my opinion. Even in "Normal" difficulty, it's a challenge. You're not Rambo... a group of mutants can beat your a*s down quickly. This time you have to think a lot more than running around beating all the people on this island.The game has it issues yet. Especially the FPS drops sometimes can be annoying, even if you're using top hardware right now. But this is what I've expected and I am sure the developers will fix it later on.Conclusion: If you like survival and/or loved the first game, it's a "No Brainer" and absolutely worth a buy. Would definitely buy it again for this price.(And sorry for my english, it's not my native language)

_childDocuments_.review: for the love of god you absolutely HAVE to make the combat feel better in this.I've played thousands of hours in games known for having unforgiving and punishing combat (Souls etc.) and have no problem with them at all, but the balance in this is totally absurd. I've also played games (like Pathologic 2) where the combat is intentionally unbalanced to make each encounter feel extra intense and meaningful, and to dissuade you from fighting everything you see. But the encounters are just constant in this and usually very very dull.Maybe I spent too much time building at the start when it was just the very easy enemies around (I've heard there's some kind of levelling system), but the amount of damage even basic enemies output is so dumb. Given the barrier of entry to armour crafting (ie needing the ingredients, and the time it takes to craft and equip each piece) it's laughable how useless it actually is.I mostly got this game for base building, so I appreciate I could play with enemies turned off, but I don't want to do that, I just want to actually enjoy my encounters with them. I played The Forest and while I'd never say the combat was hugely enjoyable, it felt balanced and reasonable. Even if you put this on 'peaceful' you're constantly being hounded by cannibals at your base to the point you can barely get anything done. This is made so much worse by the fact you have to go somewhere to manually save constantly. When the punishment for dying a couple times in a few days is potentially losing half an hour of building / gathering work the combat just needs more fluidity. Something as simple as a dodge button (with i-frames, ideally) would make it instantly better. This is EVEN MORE crucial because the map is pretty big and mostly filled with identical forest that contains next to nothing beyond enemy encounters. I really, really want to love this game. There are some cool building mechanics and having Kelvin around to help you gather stuff (assuming he doesn't get stuck somewhere in your base for a few hours) is a great mechanic to make solo play feel better. I encountered a sort of mini-boss the other day at the end of a bunker and just ran past, because doing anything else was way too risky. If I can lose half an hour of trudging through a bunker and picking up items because I dare to try and do the fight it just starts to feel miserable. And yeah, I know I can throw down a tarp and a stick and save, but constantly feeling like you have to do it because even very basic enemies can kill you in a couple of hits while combat feels this clunky isn't a fun or rewarding experience.Beyond that, not having the options to alter the difficulty (the 'custom' sliders specifically) mid-game strikes me as a little silly. I ended up altering json files to turn my save to peaceful mode, because I obviously don't want to throw away the 10 hours I've spent so far gathering food and building a base. Maybe if I started again and did a bunch of combat at the start (which is, I presume, how you level 'strength') I'd feel differently. But as it stands the combat is just so miserable I feel deeply uninspired to do so. Maybe if I played with a friend (as I did for a chunk of my 'The Forest' playtime (most of which was on PS4, not on here) the balance would feel more reasonable. But given the meagre amount of health gained from eating cooked / dried food, the relative scarcity of meds and the stupid damage numbers the enemies do I'm still not convinced that would be the case.I'll give it another shot at some point, start on custom mode with the enemy damage set to low, and make sure to do more combat early on instead of focusing too much on base building, but even if that helps, there should probably be some more advice given early on about levelling strength if it's THIS crucial for the game to feel sensible, and damage set to low should probably be the default. I'm not saying a total overhaul is necessary here, just for an attempt to be made to make combat more fun and engaging. I don't want to always stand at a distance and throw spears or fire arrows all the time, I want to have scraps with cannibals and enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty much the best a survival game can get. The game drops you onto a cannibal and mutant infested island and gives you the complete freedom to do whatever you'd like. It can be pretty tough at times, but you are able to customize your difficulty in whatever way makes it a more enjoyable experience for you. You can change enemy health, how much damage, indestructible structures, and tons more.The graphics are beautiful, and the attention to detail is top tier. The seasons change. Summer is bright, green and lush until you get to slowly see the leaves change color, Certain crops stop growing and eventually snow begins to fall. You leave a path in the snow where you walk. Freshwater lakes freeze. The amount of small, more obscure realistic physics I noticed while playing was amazing. It really feels like the devs thought of even the tiny things that don't matter much but increase the immersion a ton.The story is optional. If you just wanna survive on the island forever, build a massive base, you can do that. However, I found uncovering all the clues and the mystery extremely exciting and interesting, especially after playing the original The Forest.If I had to make one complaint, although a very minor one - it would be that certain, small areas of the map feel a bit empty. But this is contrasted by the amount of things to do, and other portions of the map that are very well done and fleshed-out. So trust me, do not let this deter you from playing the game as this is simply me just nitpicking.There are very few survival games who knock it out of the park the way Endnight Games does. I have a lot of trust in them, and am really hoping for a 3rd installment of this series. This has easily become my favorite survival game, and easily in my top 10 games of all time. It's just a must-have experience for gamers. Very much worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played nearly 30 hours within the first few days of release, I think my main issues were early game. The progression is a little unclear and once the map has been explored for a while I would say it is almost necessary to use a guide to find one specific item, unless you very luckily come across the cave(s) you need early on. There is also a huge lack of gameplay hints which I think is meant to add to the realism, but my main issue is quality of life ones not being included, e.g. how to zoom in on the GPS. It would be best to add hints that pop up on screen when you first use something that just let you know the basics of how to use whatever it is. These are honestly my main two complaints about the game and they could easily cause someone to stop playing, which I nearly did do several times with frustration in the first few hours, but I am extremely glad that I continued now. I do have other complaints but they are less significant and I think some things are unfair to say due to it being early access and having only just released. An example is that the AI companions (especially Virginia) have quite a few issues, but by the time the game is fully released I imagine they will be completely fixed. There is still a long way to go in my opinion before a full release, but there is plenty of content available through the exploration, base building, few caves and some other things available for the time being and I think a price tag of around £25 is a good price too. Overall, this is an very good game like the prequel and has so much potential to become better, so I hope they take their time with quality updates rather than rushing out a full release.

You swing weapons like you're wading through treacle, guns pack no punch and do little damage, archery is awful so good luck hitting anything further than 5 meters away. Nothing about it feels satisfying. Skunks piss in your face every 5 minutes, serving to annoy you for no reason. _childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the first game, I was really excited to play sons of the forest, I believe I got it as soon as it came out and it was really buggy and seemed unfinished, wich I didn't mind at the moment, but coming back to it a year later it still is incredibly unpolished in many ways. The graphics are pretty good, but that's the only thing this game has going for it. The AI is very erratic and buggy, the gameplay is quite frustrating as you aren't told how anything works at all (wich I understand, since its a survival game) but a few tips on how stuff works binding wise and general advice would go a long way. The building feels bad, you are given the pieces to construct what you want, but it's extremely annoying to try to build something that is custom, and having to open the inventory and whip out the guide every time is very annoying.Overall, I think this game could definitely be good, like its first part was. But what I feel at the moment is that this was just a cash grab trying to capitalize from the fans of the first game, so please prove me wrong, devs.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I ran out of space but there is so much more to talk about AHHHHHHAlright here it is an honest to god review. Ignore all other reviews as this one is the only one that actually matters. Unless you dont want spoilers. For those looking for the short of it. Go play the forest. This game is not ready. All this is at the moment is a better looking forest with less stuff in it. In fact its not even a survival game at this point. Now onto the essay portion of this review. Complete with incomplete sentences and grammatical errors.The Map: The island you find yourself on is definitely bigger then the previous game. You'll spend a whole in game day crossing about half of it. However with that said bigger doesn't necessarily mean better. The world as it stands feels very empty. I stumbled onto several points of interest. Some interesting. Some just generic campsite #15 with some loot. There are no real large cannibal camps. Just small encampments with like 3 tents and about 5 or so cannibals roaming around. The map ends up feeling rather empty as a result. Cannibals and Creepies: The cannibals have both been improved and neutered. Improved in the sense that the ai has slightly more personality to them. Nothing incredible but they might cry over a fallen friend or attempt to steal from you. They dodge alot more now and at least in large numbers (which doesn't happen) can be a threat. Ive noticed that they appear to have buffed their damage as they do hit harder when you dont have any armor (we will get to that). There appears to be alot more cannibals in this game. With skinny cannibals everywhere. They dont appear in large numbers but rather more frequently. I encounter numerous groups while traveling the map. Far more than in the original forest. However when it comes to them coming to your base it feels alot less like a group is coming to scout you out or a camp sent a raiding party and much more like the game just spawned a group near you. The variants are interesting. But ultimately are just stronger variants of regular cannibals with nothing much to differentiate them. Something I did like alot is that as your conflict with them increases they will start to wear armor. Was very cool seeing cannibals roll into my camp with creepy armor on.As for the creepies they are alright. They are strong and make for interesting fights. However I dont think they really stand up to the previous titles mutants. The only one that really is good in my mind is the twins. The fat slug creature is just insulting considering it isnt an actual mutant and is literally just a set piece the devs tossed in. The biggest problem here is the pale mutants. Treating them like regular mutants and letting you get creepy armor from them trivializes the whole game due to how armor works. Kill 2. Harvest their flesh. And bang you can now tank any and all damage from the mutants and will absolutely kill the mutants in any cave room before they can even damage you. Snowballing until you have full creepy armor and a full inventory of it as well.Building: The building is an incredibly bare bones simple system masquerading as something complex. Im honestly insulted at the state of it. You cant fill triangle gaps. You cant do anything besides 90 degree angles. Your building in squares and thats it. You have literally no other choice. Your base will be a square with a peaked or flat roof and that's that. It leaves no real room for true creativity. Some features are simply missing. Such as a gate for the defensive wall. Leaving building one ultimately pointless. On top of this there is very little reason to build a base in the current release version of the game. As simply building the emergency tent thing is good enough for the entirety of the game.Other then base building there is not much reason to build anything. The stick fences are ridiculously garbage and break if you so much as look at them the wrong way. Firewood is pointless to cut as it never actually burns out in the firepit. Every storage besides stick storage is useless as it can barely hold anything and has no large variants. Mannequins cant hold armor. There are no water collectors (More on that later). The entire system just feels like something is missing.Companions:  Kelvin and Virginia are the only two companions in the game right now as far as im aware. Not sure if they are planning to add more or not. Lets start with Kelvin. Kelvin doesnt require any maintenance. Never cleans the blood out of his ears and is mainly useless. When his AI works its ok. He slowly does any task and can certainly help sometimes. However, from my experience he rarely works properly. Often getting into a "taking a break" loop. And sitting around doing nothing. As for viginia she is the same as kelvin but you cant order her around. You have to befriend her which amounts to you standing there staring at her while she dances (idk who but im sure that says something about someones interactions with women). She will eventually give you some gifts of food or aloe. Shes pretty useless and is almost certainly some devs horny devianart page fever dream. You can however give her guns. She has infinite ammo somehow and will kill everything in site. That is if she decides to stay at camp. So often she decides to just run off somewhere and you will have to track her down because she will not come back. Ive found that once you find wherever she went she will show you a point of interest and then come back to camp. This wouldnt really be a problem if there was a way to order her like kelvin. The devs describe her "like a cat" well she needs to be more "like a dog". ALSO I WOULD LOVE TO KNOW WHICH HORNY DEV ENSURED THAT WHEN IT RAINS HER DEFAULT OUTFIT BECOMES SEE THROUGH. THEN HAD THE NERVE TO CALL THE DEFAULT OUTFIT A "SWIMSUIT".Game Balance: Now lets talk about guns. Guns trivialize the experience. Dont get me wrong the gunplay is horrible. It feels bad to aim. It feels bad shoot. However, the shotgun murders literally everything in the game. Realistic? yes. conducive to a horror survival game? no. This problem could be fixed by one simple fix though. STOP LOOT RESPAWNING ON RELOAD. It was a terrible problem in the original forest. It is a terrible problem in this one. You end up with more shotgun and pistol ammo then you could possibly need. Removing any and all difficulty of the game. Another problem is armor. Armor needs to be % damage reduction not completely negating damage. Like I said earlier after one or two caves you are basically unkillable. The only things that should give creepy armor should be the actual mutants. Not the tall pale cannibal reskins.There needs to be some sort of way to see your stats and the stats of your companions. What does the strength stat do? Does it make you stronger? does it give you more stamina? who knows? Is kelvin broken again or is he just tired? who is to say.The 3D printer is kinda dumb ngl. Printing a flask is dumb. The mask doesnt do anything. Tech armor is useless because of the other armor types. The only useful thing is the printed arrows. Survival: Well this isnt a survival game. Hunger, thirst, sleep all only matter to your stamina bar. You cant starve, dehydrate, or freeze to death. You dont take any damage after not eating for 10 days. You dont pass out after staying up for 3 days. There is literally no point beyond keeping your stamina bar topped up.Missing features: there are too many missing features from the original game. No log sleds. no large storages. No gates for walls. No water collectors. The list goes on and on. However, most insulting of all, there are no boats.Remember this may be EA but up until a month ago it was a full release. This isnt a little indie studio in their moms basement with a $100 loan. This is a multimillion dollar company with years of experience. They deserve just as much scrutiny as AAA companies. End of essay.Feel free to comment

_childDocuments_.review: wish I could give this game a "sideways thumb". The Good:The crafting/inventory/UI system is very unique and visually pleasing. I haven't seen or used anything like it before, so kudos for a fun new systemThe game is beautiful. The game's horror atmosphere is dissonant placed against the backdrop of a beautiful boreal forest. Its a creative juxtapositionFinding snippets of lore is incredibly satisfying, as is trying to piece together the story by speculation, changing a little with each little email, sketch or item found in the worldThe Bad:That same unique UI system gets tedious over time. Its much easier to press tab and click on a recipe or item you need.There really is little need/use for the entire survival/crafting/base building aspect of the game. It's enjoyable and you can spend your days fighting off cannibals if you want, but it does nothing to progress the game. There are ample places with relatively quick respawn rates to find all the supplies you need. My friends and I used our base to sleep about 3 times and lived just fine on tarp shelters, energy bars and energy drinks, which were not in short supply. Our time building a base felt like a massive time sink that amounted to nothing.All those snippets and speculation are basically for naught. The game doesn't have much of a story to piece together. Its just a giant pile of lore. There is no character development, dialogue (aside from a couple lines during cutscenes) or story arc. The motives of the characters and the factions remained mostly a mystery (looking at you JIANYU), even after the game was completed. The ending was hot dog water. It was trying to evoke emotion where there was none, because again, there was no character arcs, no emotional attachments, nothing. The story was half baked, with some random flavors thrown in and no real resolution (See the TV series Lost for comparison). Cool lore, no story.

_childDocuments_.review: As hard as it is to write this I feel I have to counter some of the overly positive reviews of Sons of the Forest.As big fans of the original we were excited to get our hands on sons but this is sorely lacking in many of the great aspects of The Forest. There are less building options, no clear direction for the story, too many supplies that litter the map and the difficulty is non-existent. You can literally sprint past any of the islands inhabitants, there are shotgun shells right from the start of the game so by the time you find the shotgun its open season.There are some nice touches, the forest looks incredible and is packed with hidden areas to explore. The cave systems are diverse and suitably scary and the island is huge. Sadly there is no reason to create a base despite the new base building mechanic. There is no storage option, no real reason to have a base at all in fact and you might as well just wonder the island saving and sleeping at any of the numerous campsites dotted across the map.Yes this is early access and this review is for the game in it's current state, it just isn't there... yet.Still looking forward to see what comes from further dev time but it needs more content and a lot of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: The same game as The Forest, but even more walking with only 3 caves being decent, the rest are just crates filled with cloth and canned food (all of the ones in the snow biome). Less content than the original game, and all the blueprints are copy-pasted from the first game.Don't even need to build a shelter, it's just a waste of time because there is no survival aspect as mobs only actually spawn on like day 15, you'd complete the game by then.Heavily underwhelming combat, exactly the same from the first game. The new mobs contribute absolutely nothing as they all have boring attacks but look different. The core game is the same, similar 'find items in caves' as the first one. If you've played the original, don't buy this, if you've never played The Forest, then yeah it's not bad.90% of all sounds are used from the previous game, which doesn't seem like a big deal, but when you actually play it, it's highly irritating and also the mobs have no footsteps and so you don't hear them coming until they've actually hit you.All it is, is the original 'The Forest' but with improved graphics and less content. The appealing 'seasonal' cycle in the game isn't dynamic, when you sleep on day 10, you wake up and it's suddenly winter for 5 days, which isn't even difficult because there's about 100 cans of cat food and 100 MREs which respawn in the numerous boring caves and camps that exist in the game.The inventory system added really cool lights! This is to hide the fact that it's actually worse to use as you have to rotate your camera to find the item you want and if you have too many items then it just reduces your FPS dramatically. The inventory system is WORSE, but they did improve the crafting animations when making or combining items.When you've finally got the sled to enjoy some mountain sledging, it's actually comical because you're going faster than the speed of sound so you actually have no clue about what's going on until you've hit a tree.I can't emphasise enough that the appealing '4x map size' makes the game worse, it's 4x the size with 4x less content, so you're walking through the forest with absolutely nothing there, the only part which is populated is the first quarter island you spawn at, the rest is just emptiness.Also Unity in 2023? Come on now, you're taking the mick, it's terribly unoptimised and the general gameplay is just poor.Unsure how it's got 'very positive' reviews, when it's literally the same as the first game, but worse.Edit: Finished the game, the story is comically bad, don't waste your time.People are also complaining how I didn't mention the 'improvements', the crafting animations, the core building mechanics is more more intuitive (but once again, base raiding happens pretty much late game when you've got everything and the ONLY resource is logs). Kelvin is cool, but is so buggy he almost becomes useless, the amount of times I've told him to go and collect sticks to then walk straight into a cannibal like a buffoon or runs off into the sunset collecting that one stick he found 200 metres away. Honestly there's literally to no improvement from the first game and is in most aspects a step back, mainly because it's copy-paste with some more eye candy fauna/flora.kind regards,trot888

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pulse-pounding survival horror game by Endnight Games, building on the success of its predecessor, The Forest. Stranded in a remote wilderness after a helicopter crash, players must scavenge for resources, build shelters, and fend off terrifying creatures.The game's dynamic environment, ranging from dense forests to eerie abandoned structures, keeps players on edge with its day-night cycle and weather system. Combat is visceral, requiring players to use weapons and traps to survive encounters with mutants and other threats.What sets Sons of the Forest apart is its weird but gripping narrative and more action-oriented elements.With stunning visuals and immersive sound design, "Sons of the Forest" delivers an unforgettable adventure into darkness, perfect for fans of intense survival horror experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game should be easy to learn and difficult to master. Sons is unfortunately the opposite--difficult to learn but very easy to master. It's insanely difficult and confusing to get your bearings, but once you do the game is brain dead easy, at least on normal.Why didn't I play on hard? Because I restarted like 4 times; the beginning is so difficult to get past and the game does such a terrible job explaining how to play that it seemed like the rare game where "normal" is reasonably difficult. But that wasn't the case. After I got set up I never needed to use a single health item for the entire last 3/4 of the game except for fighting one of the two last bosses. Based on how easy normal was, I imagine hard isn't sufficiently difficult either. It's also generally not a game that respects your time.Did I play all of it? Yes, but it was mostly going on momentum for the second half.Think of Sons as like one of those interesting 6 or 7 out of 10 games. It's got some interesting ideas and bright spots but it never comes together to make for a cohesive game. Not worth buying at full price at all.

_childDocuments_.review: "Sons of the Forest" is the highly anticipated sequel to the cult hit "The Forest." Developed by Endnight Games, this survival horror game takes players to a remote, forested island in search of a missing billionaire. The game masterfully combines elements of survival, crafting, exploration, and horror, creating an immersive and terrifying experience.Graphics and Sound:The graphics in "Sons of the Forest" are stunning, with the lush, dense forest environment rendered in exquisite detail. The day-night cycle and dynamic weather system add a layer of realism that enhances the immersion. The character models, especially the grotesque mutants and cannibals, are disturbingly well-designed.Sound design is another standout aspect. The ambient noises of the forest, the distant cries of mutants, and the eerie silence of night create a tense atmosphere. The soundtrack, though minimal, effectively ramps up the tension during key moments.Gameplay:"Sons of the Forest" builds upon the core mechanics of its predecessor, refining and expanding them in meaningful ways. The survival mechanics are deep and engaging. Players must manage hunger, thirst, and health while crafting tools, weapons, and shelter from the resources they gather. The crafting system is intuitive yet complex, offering a wide range of possibilities for creative solutions to survival challenges.Exploration is rewarding but fraught with danger. The island is vast and filled with secrets, from abandoned campsites to dark, underground caves. These areas often contain valuable resources and story clues but are usually guarded by terrifying enemies.Combat is brutal and visceral. The AI of the mutants and cannibals is impressively advanced, making them unpredictable and challenging opponents. Players must strategically decide when to fight and when to flee, adding a layer of strategy to encounters.Story:The narrative in "Sons of the Forest" is engaging, delivered through environmental storytelling and cryptic clues scattered throughout the island. The mystery of the missing billionaire and the island's dark secrets unfold gradually, keeping players hooked. The game effectively balances storytelling with open-world exploration, allowing players to uncover the story at their own pace.Multiplayer:The cooperative multiplayer mode is a highlight, allowing players to team up with friends to survive the island's horrors together. Cooperation is key, as players can share resources, build shelters faster, and fend off attacks more effectively. Multiplayer adds a new dimension to the game, enhancing replayability.Conclusion:"Sons of the Forest" is a remarkable achievement in the survival horror genre. It successfully builds on the strengths of "The Forest," offering an experience that is both terrifying and captivating. The stunning graphics, immersive sound design, deep gameplay mechanics, and intriguing story make it a must-play for fans of survival horror. Despite minor bugs and occasional performance issues, "Sons of the Forest" stands out as one of the best survival games of recent years.Pros:Stunning graphics and immersive sound designDeep and engaging survival mechanicsIntriguing and gradually unfolding storyCooperative multiplayer modeTerrifying and challenging enemiesCons:Minor bugs and performance issuesSome may find the difficulty curve steepOverall, "Sons of the Forest" is a gripping and haunting journey into the unknown, providing hours of tension-filled gameplay. Whether you're a veteran of "The Forest" or new to the series, this game is sure to keep you on the edge of your seat.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually, a big step up from The Forest, but gameplay wise it feels like a step back. Most of the above-ground encounters I've had are non-hostile or at least very avoidable, turning the entire above ground part of the map into a walking simulator. I trudged through the snowy mountains with zero preparation and wasn't punished for walking in normal clothing through the snow for a whole day, nor for simply camping under a stick and a piece of foil.Basically, it's a survival game where survival is a given. That mostly leaves exploration to find caves to go underground, slowly progress the story, and fight the more aggressive enemies down there. Frankly, it just isn't enough.That said, this is in Early Access, and there's a lot of promise here. I wouldn't be surprised if 6-12 months from now I delete this review.

_childDocuments_.review: I have put 157 hours into the game at the time of writing this review, and at the current moment I can't really recommend it.Here's why.The game has no fundamentally changed in any meaningful way since Early Access. When I first played the game a couple years ago, it was a relatively novel survival experience, and I could explain most of the incredibly rough edges with "it's Early Access, they'll fix it". Instead, we have had around a year since of monthly updates that all added novel new things that didn't really warrant logging in; they did make balance changes and adjustments, but there are still very glaring core issues remaining.For reference, I play on normal difficulty for a good balance in combat and building.- Building still feels really bad most of the time. Stone and wood don't mesh well together, and the building pretends it's deeper than it is.- Cannibals are way more aggressive straight from the onset. They're also not any smarter, and in many ways, feel dumber. You don't get much time to set anything up until you need to worry about 3-4 6+ raids per day.- Mutants and Demons now attack your camp early game (????)- Companion AI generally isn't great- The engine sucks. Like, really bad. I have a good PC and can't hit consistent 60fps on 1080 to save my life.- Gunplay feels awful and arrow flight paths range from "good luck" to "never-ending". I'm not complaining about the last one necessarily, but the difference is jarring.- The story, world and by extension Lore, has not been fleshed out in any meaningful way since. You could play this as minecraft and simply never know there's a story.- If you DO play the story, it's "Point A to Point B" with very little in between.Like it's cool we got helicopters checking on us and half-dead soldiers with flares, but that doesn't make up for the fact the core experience feels paper-thin on a good day and "make your own fun" at the worst times. I originally kept the game thinking "ah well, it'll probably get updated into a full experience. That isn't really the case, and the devs are already teasing a third game. If I had known what 1.0 would be when I first bought this, I would have refunded it.

_childDocuments_.review: • The game looks gorgeous, even on low graphics settings. • There are some features that I have been dying to see in the original game, including a GPS and larger inventory space. • There's even a higher concentration of enemies compared to the original game. • The map is amazing, and it is seemingly much larger than the original. • Firstly, inventory management and crafting are wildly different from the base game. You no longer can switch between items using the number keys, instead, you have to open up a smaller inventory and select what tool/item you want to equip. • Crafting structures such as tents, walls, and fireplaces is no longer as intuitive, and I found myself struggling to try to build a tent for a few minutes because I couldn't figure out how to add a stick to it. • Interacting with some structures is still a bit clunky, and you have to finesse it a bit in order to save/sleep. • While crafting walls is easier, you can no longer plan out custom structures, you have to almost build them to see what they will look like. However, they did add a deconstruction key bind, so I guess that helps. • NPC AI is rough around the edges. • Performance is lackluster but it's an early-access game, so I will go easy on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy mother of goosebumps, let me tell you about Sons of the Forest—a game that made me soil my undies with fright, while simultaneously snorting with laughter. This game is like that one weird friend who cracks inappropriate jokes at a funeral. It's a wild rollercoaster ride that combines terrifying moments with ridiculous antics and will have you questioning both your sanity and your bladder control.Let's start with the scares. Sons of the Forest doesn't just dip its toes into the horror genre; it belly flops right into the murky depths of fear. From the moment you step foot on that haunted island, you'll be tormented by grotesque creatures that could give Freddy Krueger nightmares. Every creak, every shadow, and every flickering light will send shivers down your spine, and if you're anything like me, you'll find yourself screaming like a banshee and using your controller as a makeshift weapon.But here's the twist: amidst the bone-chilling terror, Sons of the Forest is a master of comedy. It's like a demonic stand-up comedian with a penchant for ♥♥♥♥ jokes. The absurdity of the situations you find yourself in is both hilarious and slightly disturbing. Picture this: you're being chased by a mutant creature with teeth the size of your head, and instead of running away, you trip on a rock and end up flailing around like a drunken flamingo. It's comedy gold, my friend, even if it leaves you wondering what kind of sick mind comes up with this stuff.Now, let's talk about the difficulty. Sons of the Forest is the equivalent of playing Dark Souls while balancing on a unicycle and drinking tequila shots. It will push you to the brink of madness, testing your reflexes, your problem-solving skills, and your ability to withstand countless deaths with a smile on your face. You'll be torn between wanting to hurl your controller out the window and begging for more punishment like a masochistic puppy.And just when you think you've mastered the game's challenges, it throws you a curveball that hits you right in the... well, let's just say it's a metaphorical punch to the groin. But hey, there's a strange sense of satisfaction in overcoming the game's twisted trials. It's like conquering Everest while wearing a banana suit—it may be absurd, but damn, it feels good.In summary, Sons of the Forest is a rollercoaster ride through a haunted carnival. It will scare the bejesus out of you, make you laugh like a hyena, and leave you both frustrated and oddly fulfilled. If you're a fan of horror, raunchy humor, and torturous challenges, this game is your ticket to an unforgettable experience. Just make sure to keep an extra pair of undies handy—you'll thank me later.Rating: ★★★★☆

_childDocuments_.review: I know the game is still early access so take this with a pinch of saltpros -cool ai -i like that mutants and cannibals fight eachother (and they capture mutants that you can free to cause chaos in their camps)-new enemies look cool, the fingers are creepy af + general cannibal design is great-can build wherever you want (new building system is way better than tf1)-stick spikes are great-some nice new ranged weapons-melee weapons feel weighty and like they hit hard (especially late game)-different seasons look great and are a great addition-game looks beautiful and runs super smooth-virginia is a beast and can take a dozen cannibals solo-that boi kelvin can build-'find the missing x' is a interesting plot for whatever reason, and the alien ♥♥♥♥ is always cool toocons-inventory takes too long to open sometimes and can click the wrong thing in the heat of the moment-hiking 10miles to every new location gets boring fast, its slow as ♥♥♥♥ too-for some reason some of the OG traps weren't included in this game (i loved deadfall in the last game) traps feel a bit underwhelming because there's only really two for cannibals-enemies are repetitive and samey, they're not currently hard at all and i thought there would be more unique enemies, it was mainly just the common cannibals and two others who weren't even a threat tbh-story right now feels very weak but i do like that its left open to interpretation in some instances (ending)-some of the cutscene sequences look goofy and don't make sense (that corridor scene where you seemingly die only to wake up in the same spot with everyone gone) but i'm sure they'll make it look better-minus the odd cannibal camp here and there, the world feels pretty bland. _childDocuments_.review: While the game is for the most part visually stunning, and there are quite a variation of monsters, it feels to me like most of the budget went to this and I sadly feel like they don't seem to have had any writers involved in putting together the story.To keep it spoiler free, there are elements spread out through the game but in the end it mostly amounts to nothing. There's no questions answered, if anything it just gives you more questions and not in a sort of "wait for the next game" way either. It's more like unhinged events chained together and none of them were instructed that a story is meant to be told.The main reason I give this a minus tho, even if I overall enjoyed the gameplay, is the complete lack of tutorial and downgraded build system from the first game and then ultimately leading to a story that could've been more fleshed out it just feels like if they put a little bit more time into actually making a tutorial at all (explain controls or how to approach the build menu) as well as an improved build book (search function would be nice) then the game deserves a thumbs up for how fun it is to build and explore. Right now tho, too many will sadly just not have the patience and understanding to figure out the building and just have to resort to exploration and miss out on a great part of the game.Oh, and a difficulty mode that doesn't escalate the enemy threat except for "key parts of story progression" would be great for LOTS of gamers that don't want to have to pick between Peaceful and unbalanced Normal.

The story didn't really make sense and I ended up googling what the hell we witnessed and even with that, it's all still theory because the story line doesn't make sense. I wish gaming studios would stop putting games out in EA when they know it's nowhere near completion. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know if this game is good. SOTF looks better than The Forest, and has better enemy variety. But the world is much larger and doesn't really add much for it. Enemy swarms are much more aggressive, but looting decent weapons is much more difficult given the expansion of the map. A couple of creepy mutants will exhaust your weapon stash very quickly. And sleeping at night is a nightmare - you can clear an entire wave and not see any cannibals from one horizon to the other, only to be ambushed mid-sleep by half a dozen more mutants. Even when I bug-out halfway across the map into a hidden corner, the mutants still found me after dark. Nightime ambushes are infuriating, seemingly impossible to avoid, and tedious. Kevin is a big improvement on grind but the building system is oppressively obscure at first. Go play the Forest instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The indie jank of the original Forest game was accepted as charming because Endnight Games was a newcomer to a well-established survival horror genre, but I find myself unwilling to be as forgiving with the second installment given that the original has practically become a cult classic and has paid out in dividends. Endnight has released an unfinished and unimpressive demo of a game whose core features - which were at least functional in the original game - are incongruent non-factors at best and completely dysfunctional at worst. Though this game  in early access and should not necessarily be condemned so soon, they did at least feel that their product was finished enough to release it in some form after numerous delays, and I think it's fair to judge what has been put before us. Perhaps they'll pull this one out of the hat, but I worry that few will be willing to come back around to find out.It is fun with friends, though.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is gorgeous: graphics, building and combat mechanics, interacting with enemies and realistic friendly fire are a treat. It's an enjoyable game if you're into exploring for days, building a base, getting spooked in caves and finding out there's always an enemy spookier than the first one you've met. But after playing The Forest (1) and looking forward to getting another forest game, the story was really disappointing. I've spent days playing, exploring, reading notes and fighting all enemies throughout the forest and across the island and never had any clue about any storyline or whatsoever. Suddenly, I came to the point of the story ending, without knowing what it actually was about.It just doesn't add up to each other, from golfballs to cubes. I get the whole fresh storyline and different take on the game, but I wasn't invested in the story as I was when playing The Forest. Clues don't add up and just add more confusing information, which adds up to more confusing information. TLDR: Sweet game for fun foresting/exploring/hunting nights with the homies, not so great storyline. Would still recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Heartbreaking Letdown  As an avid fan of survival games, I was beyond excited for the release of Sons of the Forest. Unfortunately, this game is nothing short of a disaster. The positives are the graphics and the new weapons they have added but this does not fix the lack of story and absolutely an atrocious ending. The gameplay is tedious, and the storyline is so poorly developed that it feels like an afterthought.  The AI is laughable, with enemy behavior making no logical sense. Crafting and building systems are convoluted, and the user interface is a nightmare to navigate. This game feels like an unfinished product, riddled with bugs and crashes. _childDocuments_.review: The game's beautiful, but the story (among other things) definitely leaves something to be desired.The game is absolutely beautiful. Definitely one of the best looking games I've seen in a while. You can pick a nice, scenic place to build a house and just stare at it; it's amazing. This game has an atmosphere like no other. The cave atmosphere, the nature atmosphere, it's stunning.The building is very robust. You can build just about anything, and it's so much more gratifying than the original game because  placing each and every log on that house. Plenty of options, and you could easily make this game a sandbox.Kelvin is useful. Set up a log holder and tell him to go get logs and fill it; he will, albeit slowly. He's still better than nothing though, will take out some of the tedious work of the game.You get a second chance when you die. From what I've seen, the first death in a day will lead to you being sent to some sort of capture point, whether it be in a cave bubble or strung up at a tribal camp, it's not over when you die. However, when you die the second time in a day, you will be forced to load a save or restart.The inventory system, crafting animations, and weapons are far better than the original game. There's animations for drinking, eating, crafting, reloading, shooting, all of that. Adds another level of immersion to the game, for sure. The backpack-holding-up-thing that replaced the keybinds system is better too, in my opinion.The caves aren't as rich as the first game. They're extremely atmospheric, which is awesome, but they have next to no depth. No ropes or anything like that. They're also not interconnected, to my knowledge at least, like the first game's caves. The enemies are also quite annoying, which I suppose could be intentional, The AI isn't all it's touted to be. It's definitely interesting; the cannibals won't attack you immediately and will instead watch you and observe you, and they will also mourn fallen comrades sometimes; that's all I've seen though. Kelvin, while useful, can become a liability. He often doesn't follow you and will lag behind you, and you'll have to wait for him (you can leave him too, but then you miss out on what he's actually useful for). He cannot defend himself either, so do not expect him to help you out in firefights.The whole tribe system is quite underwhelming. Yeah, they're there. Yeah, there's 7 foot tall dudes that want to beat your head in. More was expected, though. The game is fairly straightforward, and the story isn't deep. The performance isn't great. It's a pretty game with tons of foliage, and that takes a toll. But the optimization leaves something to be desired too. 32GB of ram and a 3070 OC only getting me 70fps on high WITH dlss? Come on.Currently, The cons outweigh the pros. This means i'll give the game a negative review. If anything changes or I feel I should add anything, I'll upgrade this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is the 'early access' release of the sequel to the much lauded Endnight debut, The Forest (2018) and is a complete sideways improvement. Nearly everything that The Forest does, 2023's Sons of the Forest improves upon in almost every field. Animation quality and variety are both numerous and exquisitely visualised if somewhat superfluous, the graphics and environmental production tower over anything in The Forest and the audio work is first rate with a killer soundtrack and ambient sound design that brings the rainforest to life. The excellent and satisfying melee combat of the original makes a return.Where The Forest explored themes of isolation, body horror and fear (with a sprinkling of b-movie mystic shlock) 'Sons' relegates these horror themes to the back seat, with the emphasis being on shooting guns and big budget set pieces. Both films are loving pastiches of the genre pieces they take their inspiration from. The workmanlike and DIY production and direction of the original Forest has been replaced by a slicker, glossier production that wants you tobe some badass action movie star. However, the pace of the game is ironically quicker in the first game due to the smaller size and tighter plot of the original than it is in this more or less straightforward survival game.However, as technically brilliant and graphically superior as Sons is, it is where we make the comparisons to the gameplay of the The Forest that we can see the glaring deficiencies in actual game experience and content. The Forest had an organic sense of progression in terms of plot, exploration and reward, whereas Sons leads the player to the new locales in a much more linear fashion with progression being rewarded with ammunition and animations. The original had a forest that was deep in spite of its small size, extensively detailed with each part of the world map given its own character and environmental design, whereas Sons feels like a map that is admittedly more convincing as a real world location but suffers from its own size. There are simply too few points of interest for a map this size and the locations that do exist are barely worth exploring. The Forest had caves that each felt different and each had a character to them, places that really needed to be scouted, prepared for and deliberately explored, not just a place to go to because we needed a key item, or that there wasnt much else to do but go and actually explore them. The Forest felt alive with malice - Endnight paying homage to the largely Italian-made cannibal exploitation films of the late seventies (Cannibal Holocaust, Cannibal Ferox, et al), yet Sons really just leans into how realistic the forest is as its main feature. There a few grisly props lying about, but there are no eviscerated japanese businessmen or plane crash survivors strung up, just a few faceless mooks impaled upon sticks here and there, which in itself does not lend itself to much emotional connection to the game and oh boy, we will get to that....Instead of placing you in the shoes of plane crash survivor Eric LeBlanc, protagonist of The Forest, tasked with finding his abducted son Timmy, Sons establishes that you are a member of a PMC group, an operative sent with a mission to go and discover or recover the family of billionaire capitalist Edward Puffton. Without going into too much detail, there is a definite tonal shift in both approach and presentation of the main plot. In the Forest, Timmy is your emotional connection to the world, the driving force behind the plot and the general atmosphere of the game is one of horror and fear. Sons of the Forest had you down as Action Man, you shoot guns, have things with 'tactical' in their name and you have a straightforward mission. There was a plane crash subplot in The Forest which tasks you with tracking down exactly what happened to the survivors, some of whom surviving one catastrophe to be rewarded with an even more unfortunate end. Now in Sons of the Forest there are a few corpses strewn about the place, faceless operators we couldnt give a toss about. There are no cues or environmental story telling as to how they met their end or who was behind this. Just some impaled tacticool guys. And that is our emotional payoff on discovery of what happened to our mercenary comrades.Now, Sons approaches its emotional commitments differently. The Forest has you exploring the game trying to rescue your child and escape the island, there is an established connection between a likeable player character and his mission. He at least has a name, a noble goal and is armed only with his expertise in fieldcraft and an emergency exit axe. Sons however allows to develop your emotional connection in a more organic fashion by ones relation with the only other survivor of the heli crash, Kelvin. It also introduces us to Virginia, who almost becomes something as a surrogate for the Timmy emotional connection by way of character interaction. This is a departure, but a welcome and sophisticated piece of game design. But the sophistication is only skin deep, Kelvin carries logs, Ginnie shoots things. So if youre not into building, Kelvin doesnt factor into the game (I tell him to hide at the heli crash to be shot of him) and if youre more interested in discovering the true depth of the AI NPCs by playing in a non hostile, observational style, Ginnie will make sure the full range of AI behaviour becomes locked to hostility by shooting up the place. One of the standout features of the original was the apparent depth of player interaction with the NPCs who populated the peninsular, be that in either non violent or hostile interactions and this has been improved upon by Sons of the Forest, but nothing that is present here was not present in The Forest. Only the sophistication of its presentation. As a side note, Endnight has introduced two new player companions and a deeper AI system, but couldnt implement an insanity system that would create interesting gameplay scenarios? For all the imagination that Endnight have put into both games, surely there must an idea unscooped from a brain cell somewhere in the office.The reason the emotional connection is important is because people remember and empathise the triumph of Eric LeBlanc in The Forest. We will probably remember seeing the twinkle of life in Kelvins eyes as we resuscitate him or the first time we watch a impromptu ballet recital from Virginia but in the end, do we really like or care about our own player character? Will we remember our nameless hero's escape from Site 2? After all, we are simply a guy with a gun who needed to shoot progressively bigger monsters as the game goes on.Although it may seem as though the negatives are the only thing being explored in this review, that is only because these are the only deficiencies in my eyes, and once solved, this is would be not just an outstanding game, but an outstanding sequel. Right now it is definitely the former, but arguably not the latter. This game disappoints and exceeds expectation in equal measure.It has a beginning, middle and an end, with a solid if limited building system that fans of building games will enjoy to keep those inclined that way playing for a few hours more. But if the world of the Forest captivated you because of its outstanding story telling and environment design, this world may feel a bit cold and underwhelming.Six months on from its initial early access release, £25 buys you a fleshed out world with a strong enough story, deep enough gameplay and a badass shotgun*. With future updates and considerable content added since release, this is a game worth playing and keeping an eye on.*unless you are using slugs. It feels like a giant pea shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: *****Should be as spoiler free, I will try not to list any specific info (what items, what points of interest etc)******I ADORED The Forest, like it basically it ruined every other game for me. It was a Indie that felt like a full production AAA game. It had interesting mechanics, both gameplay  and building mechanics. It always kept you on your toes.Sons of the Forest, though still fun and at times terrifying falls very short from not only a complete game but way short of the first forest.I don't want to hear, small team, early access blah blah blah, it doesn't matter. I paid a full 45$ for the product, it was delayed twice. I played EA because I assumed that they were pretty much done but maybe missing certain minor events or even some voice acting. It was missing ALOT, many mechanics found in the first game and even was a buggy mess. I'll list out some of the missing mechanics now or toned down mechanics:- Sanity (You would go crazy slowly, you were discouraged from using skin armour only if you absolutely needed to...its just gone)- Body State (in the previous one, bad food yielded bad energy, it doesn't feel like that it has any impact no obesity etc)- Certain Food mechanics that were nice in the previous (Turtle shells for water, etc). Just felt better and less overpowered (here food spawns back, and is everywhere, I mean everywhere.) - Base building is a waste of time, it doesn't actually progress the story or help you survive. (though the base building feels and looks is better than Forest 1)So really, I had high high hopes for this, waited a crazy amount of time for it. I will say I regret playing the EA because I don't see myself going back to play it again. Maybe to do waves of base building but then its just like any other generic survival game.=======PROS========- GAMEPLAY- I'll probably list this in both pro and con, but the game play still feels fun, its fun with friends and over all still has that nostalgic forest feel that I liked.- SETTING - the setting  was great, the island looks amazing and is immersive. The addition the of seasons was a delightful surprise. Good suspense here and there and it just felt creepy a lot.- AI - the AI is top notch, though it has its faults, its by far one of the more immersive AI I've ever seen. This is an actual upgrade from The Forest.- ITEMS- It feels good to see new items, and even guns which was heavily missing component of the first one. The diversity was good, and finding the items was rewarding.- GRAPHICS - This was definitely a notch above, beating out even AAA games in this field. Nothing really bad to say about the art direction and attention to detail (though it does need a beefy system:))- SCALE - The scale of the game is much grander than the first, so it has to be said. The Snow sections that were once empty dead places, are ready to be explored.- CAVES and POINTS OF INTEREST - It has diverse sections, and feels eerie to explore them. I was looking forward to the caves/poi more than anything else while playing- BUILDING MECHANICS - Top of it's field, nothing more to say. Its a pleasure to build stuff. - PACING - This is another that will be in the CON section as well but pacing was perfect at times. See cons for other.======= CONS ========- STORY - None, really none, No Voice Actors, just hints. It was a huge disappointment. NONE! Meaningless objectives a lot of times.- GAMEPLAY - It's in my opinion a step down from the first, the survival mechanics of the first were just better. It made you go out of your way to survive while this one you can brute force through and eventually still be ok. I never felt threatened or in danger (very rarely). Inventory is bad, it was bad in the first but had way less items, so here you need to use the quick inventory to make it much better. A of of repeating corridors, which can pass in a cave system but is more evident in other sections (will leave this spoiler free). The game is it's own enemy as well, telling you where to go from place to place. So you could straight shoot through.- CONSUMABLES - Consumable items are everywhere, it makes hunting or any type of survival just pointless, and since everything respawns you have nothing to worry about. Water is readily available as well which is a step down from the first.- SCALE - Though the scale is impressive, there's a lot of dead zones. Just zones that either had loot not worth the trip or just empty and confusing (like entering somewhere and thinking...this can't be it)- BUILDING - Beautiful, but pointless. It has no impact on you, it doesn't give you any advantages other than immersion. If anything it was holding us back because it's just a burden. You can just build a quick save/sleep spot anywhere with almost no stress or items.- SURVIVAL - What survival? Food is everywhere, water is too. Cooking just leaves you exposed and just doesn't benefit you since you can find food everywhere. The survival aspects are optional in a horror survival game.- HORROR - Missing, it doesn't have the same impact as the first one (this might not be a fair comment, since the first one we weren't so sure what is happening or the scale of the events), but I just never felt the tension, it was missing the monsters scale of the first (sizes, etc) is absent.- ENEMIES - Though enemies had more variety than the first one, there was a serious lack of Monster variety and was just simply missing some of the cool and shock factors of the first one.- KELVIN - Don't, just don't. He is a cool idea that was executed poorly. He is buggy, and usually ignored. Though absolutely jokes and funny to be around, we did admittedly laugh and enjoyed his antics. - PLAGUES WITH BUGS/GLITCHES - This section can be the size of the review itself, but my god it was plagued with problems. From building glitches, to spawning glitches to item glitches, to combat glitches, to attachment glitches, duplication glitches and even game breaking glitches. At one point I lost an item, it just left my inventory and never came back. Sometimes you can't complete actions (even saving) which makes you restart and hope you didn't save too far behind. Crashes, though not quite as frequent (COD crashed more haha), lag spikes/stutters galore. Menu overlapping, sometimes you try to building something and your character just pauses either for a while or never unpauses. The list can keep going, but I'll try to keep it as short as possible, just know others experienced worse than us and others less than us.ConclusionSo in the end I'd say this is a competent game, and although this will sound like I'm contradicting myself, it is an overall more complete/step up from The Forest. It's what I expected of The Forest back 5 years ago (full) and what 10 years ago total to be.That being said it was a let down especially with the delays and the announcement that it was going EA. It should have been delayed again.WAIT FOR THE FULL RELEASE. I paid a fraction of the cost with The Forest and it felt more wroth it. Its just not ready, the Story is just no where to be seen. If you haven't play the first Forest game, not only cheaper but it's a complete story and will get you started (Frankly even if this was a better game I'd say to play the first).If I think of anything else to say good or bad, I still think this game should have been delayed and we should have swallowed the sadness.SCORE: 5/10. _childDocuments_.review: In the current state of development, I can't recommend the game. It's fun, it's very playable, and it's beautiful. My biggest, and perhaps only real complaint is that there are no dedicated/standalone server options. The first iteration had a very buggy dedicated server that only ran on Windows, but at least it was an option.If you play with friends, your current option is to select one member of your group to host the multiplayer session. From that day forward, that person needs to be available and willing to play Sons of the Forest in order for everyone else to join the multiplayer game. If any of your group have schedule changes, there's no options for them to join. It's for this reason alone I can't recommend the game in its current state of development. It's meant to be a social game, but has very limited group options. My regular group lost interest fairly quickly due to fluctuating schedules and having to replay every cave multiple times to keep everyone's progress sync'ed. It might as well be a single-player game.

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this game to anyone who highly favours the building aspect of survival games, I also really enjoy the combat and the overall presence of the AI, End night has truly stepped it up from the previous game, each cannibal tribe will act different to the last you will mostly notice this difference in aggression levels but it also comes down to smaller things such as mannerisms, certain tribes prefer to annoy you more than others and some tribes will just mind their own business if you don't bother them. Currently the story is a work in progress and the play through of it isn't anything special, although the actual plot is quite interesting which you can learn more about in game if you choose to.This game is amazing and truly immersive, regular updates so you wont be in lack of content to explore buy it now to support the devs and also they may end up rising the price once the game is complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of the Forest is an exciting and immersive game that is sure to provide hours of fun and entertainment, especially when played with friends. The game's multiplayer mode is a joy to experience, as it allows players to work together to explore the mysterious forest and survive its dangers.One of the standout features of Sons of the Forest is its intricate and well-designed hunting system. While some people may find it a bit repetitive or lacking in variety, the system is nevertheless engaging and requires skill and strategy to master. Players must carefully track their prey, set traps, and use a variety of weapons and tools to take down their targets, making each hunt a unique and rewarding experience.While the game's graphics and overall design are impressive, I have noted that some of the idle animations are a bit lacking in detail. However, this minor flaw does not detract from the overall quality and enjoyment of the game.Overall, Sons of the Forest is a fantastic game that is sure to appeal to both casual and hardcore gamers alike. Its multiplayer mode is especially enjoyable, and its hunting system is both challenging and engaging. While there are some minor issues with certain animations, the game's overall quality and entertainment value make it a must-play for any fan of survival games.

_childDocuments_.review: I, like most fans of The Forest, counted the days before its early access release. I absolutely couldn't wait. This game was my #1 wish listed game a year ago. I think this has proven both very positive and very negative for myself as well as many others. The game is beautiful. Fantastic visuals, weather, scenery, etc.. Once again Endnight has redesigned the building system just like the original game. possibly a slight tedious, but customization is through the roof. I want a game that i get engrossed with, that i can loose hours and possible days with. The original Forest gave me that. There was something about that game that grabbed my attention. I remember when I downloaded the final release and was finally able to use the key card at the underground bunker. Seeing that red hallway was such a complete 180 from being in the woods for days that it was amazing to experience. The story was something I could relate to. You felt connected to LeBlanc and to experience the moment he found Timmy and tried desperately to revive him was definitely a heartfelt moment. I font feel anything like that in this game. Its more cold in a sense. Like so many people have said, theirs something missing in SotF. Sure it has great visuals, its a decent survival game, the building mechanics are great, but something inst there. Sure, many people don't care about story elements, they just want survival or combat and this game has that. But for me, theirs just something off. Maybe my anticipation about the game being something amazing ruined it when I played the game. It was actually hard when it was first released. People complained the enemies, especially the muddies, were too difficult. This has since been nerfed. Enemies are easier and that cautious,calculated play style I loved so much is gone now. This game can be so much more. I want this game to be its absolute best. The devs can do a ton to make it interesting. They have before. Its a small team, but they can be creative. They've already proved that. I really hope the full release is worth it. I want a jaw dropping experience just like the first game. Come on Endnight!

_childDocuments_.review: After 2 years of delays. this game is unfortunately terrible. I loved the original game. The atmosphere was absolutely unlike any other game and exploring the massive CONNECTED cave system was thrilling and terrifying. The enemies weren't very diverse, but that didn't matter. All the claims this game made at improving upon the original fell short beyond marginally better graphics, a dynamic building system, and a (unnecessarily) larger map.The graphics are there for the most part (I don't really care about them but some do) aside from the rock textures. The moon was pretty and the trees and foliage looked nice, but nothing that is better than any recent releases going for that style. But the sound quality... is just unbearable. Enemies sound like a whining rodent that sometimes grunts. They don't react appropriately to getting brutally assaulted. THE WIND SOUND. jesus christ the wind is so loud. At 30% sfx volume my ears were raped anytime a breeze blew by. Every sound scales very poorly if at all with your distance. It is impossible to ascertain how far a cannibal or flowing water is based of the sound, as every audio bit just gets slammed right in your ear like its inside your ear canal.  I could maybe excuse the glaring sound design issues if the exploration or story was compelling. They are not. The open world might be 4 times the original map but its 10 times as empty. 60% of me beating the game (no guides) with my friends is just running across empty forests scattered with copy paste villages every 15 minutes. The caves are just linear in and out systems, some just being a hole with loot (JUST ROPE SO MUCH ROPE) and no enemies or anything of interest despite the mark on your map. Their are 4 mutants that you will likely encounter, and not once are you ever forced to kill one. The story is actually laughably bad. Two cut scenes with almost no buildup or context and some printed emails, most not of any relevance. if you were considering this game for a compelling story turn right around. It is a complete joke, after the final cut scene we just laughed asking ourselves "is that actually the ending for a game we'd been waiting for for 3 years?" The cut scene itself is just funny, at the end of the game the conclusion feels like watching spongebob on 10 benadryls.The greatest (not that great!) strength of the game is not the combat, it is the peaceful survival. No fast swap option makes engaging cannibals a nuisance. The shotgun is hilariously broken, one shotting everything and making them rag-doll. I love the inventory space, its a nice expansion of the original,. The building feels like legos and kelvin is a helpful guy. Anytime we started having fun something would remind us of just how early access this game was. They should've just delayed it again, the state it is in now is embarrassing and disappointing from such a respected development team.3/10

_childDocuments_.review: I love the new graphics, game play, cannibals and mutants in the game.  The build mechanic is taking some getting used to, but I love the improvements over the original.  The changing seasons is a great touch, sound and visual effects are great, and the fact it is a much bigger world are all welcome changes.  It is still early days, but I am hoping the story line is easier to follow and is more logical than the original.  The new weapons are also great and a welcome addition.Things that could be improved is the need for hotkeys for combat, like the 1-4 hotkeys in the original or a scroll wheel option.  Having to hold Q to change items is too cumbersome and slow.  The wind and river noises are waaaay too LOUD!  Please lower these significantly or allow us to have an option to adjust it.  And please bring back raft building.  It was one of the best features in the original game and it makes logical sense that if you can build elaborate buildings and furniture, surely you could build a simple raft.  It makes exploring better too.  I would also love to see islands brought back into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So for anyone that hasn't fully explored the island, just know that about 3/4 of it isn't filled in at the moment and there are a ton of blank spots with cannibals running around, but some areas don't even have camps / other locations. It feels very empty in portions and its extremely noticeable. I beat this with a buddy in 24 hours. We built multiple bases, collected damn near everything in the game, and beat it. Again, no spoilers, but be aware that you need to put in some serious exploration to find certain locations as they're stretched far and wide. A good portion of items have multiple locations you can get them from, but a lot only have a single location. This means you could go all the way to the end of the damn game and never find one. This happened to us with one important item in particular and it made us pretty salty.The Good: Fantastic graphics and runs like butter. The cannibals all act appropriately and can be a moderate challenge until you get the hang of things. Building feels well polished, items feel great to use (for the most part, there is one exception my buddy and I noticed) and exploration of caves / areas feels pretty good on interiors, even if there are some copy/paste locations in the game. Its a wide world that ranges to drastic amounts and I'm sure after they fill in some gaps here and there, it'll be a great game that'll give a substantial amount of time worthy of fully investigating each part of the world.The Bad: First and foremost, Kelvin is absolutely awful to babysit (character you start the game with). I found myself hating the character because of him constantly getting beat and the forced interaction to keep getting him up and it seemed to be a running theme throughout our gameplay that we were more annoyed by his existence than aided.To anyone looking into buying the game at the moment or just starting, be aware that there are cut scenes. None of them will make sense to you unless you fully explore the lore of the game. Hell, even the last cut scene is confusing as hell at the end. They clearly still have more to add to the game before its coherent at all.Lastly, the bugs that pissed us off beyond belief. Randomly getting knocked down and losing all your armor by trees, even though they CLEARLY don't hit you. We also encountered a glitch where weapon attachments just vanished. Infuriating considering how difficult they were to find. The only way to get them back was to log off and go all the way back to the original location to find them again. This happened no less than 4 times during our playthrough. Absolute pain in the ass.Tricks we discovered:1: If you and another player (only tested with two, but I'm sure this works with multiple players) are trying to skin something, if you do it at the same time, you'll both receive the skin. However, if you do it by yourself, the other person won't be able to skin it. Super useful for multiplayer.2: Placing logs on a steep slope vertically (it has to be VERY steep) will glitch the log and create an additional log for free. You can make an infinite number of logs doing this.3: Tree bases can have items built in them. If you're playing multiplayer, you can just throw logs up to your companions and they can build at the top of the tree. Super effective when you're just beginning.Overall, even with the complaints that I'm sure will see fixes in the future, great game. 8-9 out of 10 for sure.
