_childDocuments_.review: Congrats to Endnight. This is a beautiful game. I like hanging out in my base a night with a campfire. And during the day, I sometimes just like to admire the trees, lakes, waterfalls and creatures.I don't play this game for the story line.  I like to build bases and ziplines all over the map. It is a creative outlet that is so much fun. Compared with the Forest, some of the tedium is removed with Kelvin. He is useful, especially with the new "maintain base" command. I have a large base (just sayin')  that is surrounded by a stone wall. Parts of the stone wall is also surrounded (nearly) by an electric fence. Its so much fun toying with enemies at the fenceline. Its very satisfying seeing them fry.After nearly 400 hours, I'm maybe 1/2 way through the story line. This is the weakest part of the game. It is not really that interesting to me and you only do it to get better weapons. However, I get by with stone arrows and the shotgun if I'm gang attacked. You don't have to go far in the story to get the shotgun. (I thought it would be good to get the crossbow, but meh.) For my play style I like the game mostly as is. But I think there could be improvements. I think it would be better if some of the items were necessary for progress, e.g. some enemies can only be killed easily by fire, spears or the crossbow because of armour. Or, if you needed to learn a skill such as rope bridge building to cross a path to a critical item or place. I think you should have to earn a lot of the weapons by finding blueprints or the weapon its self. Too many are just given to you. And, it would be more challenging if the enemies learned how to make better armour through the game and therefore became harder to kill. Essentially, the easier levels should get a bit harder as you go along. Perhaps hard should remain the same. TIPS. There are two ways to create a safety zone. 1. Build stone walls or log spike walls (two layers of logs thick). The enemies can't bust through these as a general rule (you may get a freak event where several attack a wall and bust through but its the exception). Adding electric fences makes for additional fun. You can watch enemies die and then go collect stuff. Deer run into them and die. Add traps in your base for fun, but they are also not necessary.2. Enemies drown. build a base or platform over deep lake water but just the right distance from the shore. When attacked, retreat to the platform. Enemies will try to follow you and will drown. You can have a lot of fun with this.  Most enemies cannot jump electric fences. To keep everything out you just build extra height to the fence (above the electrified bottom rungs). To get out of the base you need to build a zip-line to get over your perimeter fence. Virginia and Kelvin find their way across electric fences, taking some damage but not dying.The swat traps are great for taking out babies. Fun to watch. You can eat food raw and you are fine. Put it on a drying rack if you want it to keep longer.Use hotkeys for all your main weapons and healing/energy mixes. ***To enjoy the game, you need to teach yourself how to build with logs***. For building, read the survival guide carefully. It shows you a lot in pictures. Teach yourself to build flat platforms on uneven ground. Start at the lower ground and build toward higher ground. This is easier. Put in a pillar, then add a log at 45 degrees sloping down. This only works if it slopes down to higher ground or the same level. Use the game feature of placing a log under the end of the sloped down log. The game will cut the new upright log to size.  When working from high to low ground it's trickier. You need to place a pillar log on the high ground then use two logs on the lower ground. After placing a pillar on high ground, place one pillar on the lower ground at a suitable distance from the uphill pillar. Then, use your eye to cut it to the same height as the base of the uphill pillar. Then you add another log on top of the cut pillar, and place a cross-beam that will be level.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: This game just feels like a re-skin of the original. Some aspects of the game feel a lot better than the original, such as the building system and the graphics. The enemies, caves, and the story were all better in the first game. This game feels incomplete. The ending was extremely disappointing. There was this huge build up with a cut-scene and then the game was just over. I wish there was more effort put into the story. I was so hyped for the release of this game and extremely disappointed with much of it. I really hope that the final product is better than what has been released. I would like to recommend this game, but I don't feel it is complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, it's a really great successor to The Forest. Playing Sons of the Forest felt like you were really playing The Forest 2.0. It retains the essence and feel of its predecessor, but brings a lot of new things to the table. I think the new building system in particular is outstanding. Considering that the game is only in Early Access, you can already do a lot and it is already very mature, even if here and there is still minimal potential for improvement. For example, minor graphics bugs or Kelvin's pathfinding, which sometimes takes a while until it understands where to go when you for example place new walls. (Its really bad).... All in all, however, a very good successor to The Forest and I'm really excited and look forward to seeing what will become of Sons of the Forest in the future. All in all a raiting of: 7.5/10 with good potential for a 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Really liking the game so far. Minimal bugs that I've come by so far which is a good sign this early in EA, nothing game breaking. For me my issues lie in the new building and the AI teammate getting stuck on structures and confused. He is a nice addition for those who play solo and want some help building or collecting resources. Annoyingly the AI teammate is the biggest chicken sh#$ in the world and will watch you get murdered and wont pick you up. If he isn't ever going to pick up a downed teammate, give us the option in the menu to remove him all together as he is just an annoyance at that point. Some of the new building I just don't understand why you would change it from The Forest and leave others. Fences are a royal pain in the azz to make now. Doors don't seem to have locks on them anymore so those are kind of pointless as the cannibals can just let themselves right in through my gates. Makes no sense to keep somethings the same and change others as it seems the ones you changed were the easy to make things and now they are a pain to make. That aside, runs pretty well for me, not quite as well as the forest did when it came out in EA but this game is a big visual improvement over the original so that is to be expected. Overall I'm rather pleased how this has started, and can't wait to see it all get ironed out, but for the love of #$%@ just put the building system back the way it was for everything.Looking forward to seeing what silly achievements I can get like "Worlds Worst Father" from the forest.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually such garbage and straight up a money grab. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good experience,  Graphics are great, got to appreciate the effort they've put into the image quality alone. The companions are an interesting concept aswell, fits in well especially for those of us that are not running a 4 men or more server.  A true survival with a touch of story to uncover, ( hopefully they're gonna develop on that more in the future) top building mechanics and a big map to explore. _childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest survival games ever made and with the most original building systems I have ever seen. I really enjoy the crafting system and how the inventory is organized. It's great that I can store items if I have too many of them. The sleep, hunger, thirst, and fatigue systems are essential to a survival game.  Also appreciate the inclusion of seasons, particularly the snowy winter season which I found to be really immersive. The wetness and coldness are interesting features.Fun fact: The fire lights up more when there is high wind, what a cool detail
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: This Game, for the first few hours i have played it, is what i can call early access amazing!The map is bigger than the first, but i did not expect it to be so intricate and beautiful, The paths and streams make such a beautiful landscapes, (and even though my graphics settings were turned down to avoid a PC funeral) the view from the mountain was amazing. The cannibals are still menaces, with their annoying screams and body paint (I love this game), The new NPC Kelvin (Although i think he needs a doctor) is a great help, And the woman is a lovley addition. I have not got to far into the story, but in my opinion the bugs make it better (We found a log duplication glitch on the first day)! I got many good laughs out of it and many more to come!I can not wait to see what the finished game looks like! 100/100 Recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: After following The Forest from early access, I was keen to get started on Sons of The Forest. Being an EA game, I expected a fair amount of bugs and issues, much like the launch of The Forest.I know this wont reflect what others might have experienced, but so far, apart from a few annoying bugs, such as gates not working, the game is extremely well polished.The enemies are clearly harder, as well as smarter and the companion system is incredible. In fact, I hope to see other games use similar mechanics.The new building system is so much better, giving you much more freedom (When Kelvin isn't destroying what you've built then gormlessly giving you a thumbs up)Visually the game is stunning too. However, I appreciate that it's early access, yet, while the map is much bigger, to some degree it also feels more void of reasons to explore it. There are several caves that are either not finished yet, or simply extremely small.Either way, Sons of The Forest is an incredible game, that is only going to get better. If you're a fan of the first game, give it a go. If you want a more complete experience, perhaps wait for a few updates or release.

_childDocuments_.review: People are complaining that the sounds in in Sons of the Forest are subpar and worse than The Forest. I'd like to say that I recognized a vast amount of sounds specifically FROM THE FOREST in SONS OF THE FOREST. I personally like the current sounds as they as nostalgic from the first game, it gives a sense of familiarity. People are also saying that the cannibals are harder to kill. I concur to a certain extent that they hit harder than necessary but still they're savages in the woods eating god knows what and have been living there for god knows how long. These are not that bad of things to consider when reviewing a game like this and I hate that people are solely nitpicking these tiny details when:1. The game is early access just like the 1st one. 2. Building is slower than the first BUT it's WAY more realistic and hands on which is personally more appealing.3. The map is understandably a a bit too big, but that adds MORE scare factor as to finding where you are and where you need to go running into unexpected trouble or loot. 4. Food is harder to get because it's more REALISTIC NOW. Deer are FAST and so are rabbits. (Who would have thought)5. The crafting system is different than the 1st game. I don't know why people are upset about that.6. YOU HAVE KELVIN STOP COMPLAINING.7. I can't name all the other things people complain about this game because it's tiring and confusing and I'm just gonna end my little list there.Enjoy it for yourself. Find value in the things you do in the game and enjoy them for yourself. Don't rely on the opinions of others.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the original The Forest for a bunch of hours, I was eager to jump in and have a great time here.  Man, if disappointment was cake I'd have one hell of a cake.I'm sure by the time the game reaches the full release I'll improve on some of the bare-bones feeling of the game, and hopefully improve it all around.  Until then, I'm going to have to step away and play something else.So why'd I stop so soon?AI is miserably awful.  Kelvin might as well be a little mini base destroyer.  At first it sounds awesome to have him assist you in building your base.  Who wouldn't want some assistance in gathering trees or other items?  Well, no idea on how the AI decides what trees to chop down - but nothing beats watching them turn their axe on your almost built log cabin instead of the tree next to it.  Nothing quite so exciting as having your almost built house be felled in a swoop by Kelvin.  Or is it Klevin?  I don't remember, because to me he was the base destroyer.  What else did he do?  Set things on fire.  If I wanted to cook, he wanted to be in the fire.  It was so bad I tried to have him follow me across the island so I could leave him there.  No dice, he got lost about halfway and somehow ended back at my base.Crafting somehow feels like it's taken a step back from the original, making it more cumbersome and annoying to deal with.  The new map, using GPS, is awful and the map making markers(at least early on) requiring the GPS trackers to set up is terrible due to the short number of them found.  Maybe there are more, maybe not. I don't know.Swimming will often leave you wondering why you can't get out of the water, or wondering if you've forgotten how to swim upwards.  Despite your best attempts you just won't do it.Combat is about the same as the original.  The environment is beautiful, and I look forward to eventually coming back to it.. But man, first impression is a solid dose of disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: I looove this game.It's super fun to play with friends! I wish we could build more modern things that you can find the yachts and bunkers. It would be cool to be able to add bunk beds, sinks, showers, toilets, other things. It would be cool to have some cozy and cute options since we can only build pretty primitive things right now. I wish you could store things on the tables besides the radio. I just love the aspect of fighting creepy enemies and having a cute, cozy home to come too afterwards. Overall I love this game it's a 10/109

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT - After finishing the so called "story" i do not  recommend this game, AT ALL. Trash trash. 🟩 Pros	- A vast, detailed sequel following the standard set from The Forest 1. This game is absolutely beautiful. Definitely one of the best looking games I've seen in a while on max settings, although you better have a high specced PC to see all that glory . You can pick a nice, scenic place to build a house and just stare at it; it's amazing. The detail with the wind, the rain, the foot prints left behind whilst you walk, i give credit to those involved in creating these details.- The building is a nice upgrade from the first game.🟥 Cons- The caves are boring. Aside from a select few, most of the caves end up hitting a dead end within 20 metres of walking. Unlike the original, there's no wall pick axe jumping, no ropes or things to interconnect the caves to new areas. Its rather, disappointing. - Bugs, glitches, bugs, FPS drops, bugs? I've run into a few bugs with teleportation glitches, sounds bugs when dying, AI just not responding or doing dumb things. - The inventory layout is horrendous. I hate it, you have to move your mouse cursor quite around and at times its finicky and not intuitive.- Enemy camps feel not as "scary" or as polished as the previous title. --- Whilst in Alpha, it still needs work, overall if you are a Forest 1 Fan i would recommend, if you are new to the series possibly hold off until things are sorted. ---

_childDocuments_.review: [Original review posted on 2nd March, edited on 23rd June]In the 3 months since I posted the review, almost every single aspect of my feedback and suggestions have been implemented into the game. The game isn't perfect and there's still a lot more content that needs to be added, but the silver lining here is that it is quite obvious that the devs read and care about the player's feedback and are constantly updating the game.In my previous review, I recommended the game but I tried to highlight the many flaws and lack of content that the game had. But after seeing the massive progress that has been made in just a few months, I am excited to see what more the devs can bring to the table. The new features, locations, bug fixes, etc. are all great, but personally, I am now waiting for more full fledged story content to be added. Once the devs implement the full story and game is finally out of early access, I think that is when I will sit down and spend some more time in the game. Can't wait to see what's next!

Also one of my friends disconnected because of his Internet and when he came back it seems he lost progress and lost one of the most crucial tools in the game which he had already picked up before.Save your money and give it a year to see how it shapes up because so far this is a disappointing alpha at most.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a  big fan of "the forest" since day one. That said, "sons of the forest" is a worst "the forest" with a better graphic. The trailer of the game is misleanding, You expect advanced enemy interaction and reaction, but you'll finish just killing everyone at sight. The developers, like for "the forest", have still no clue on how to carry on a game, and they once again rely on player's community ideas to make a mediocre game a good one, it worked once, let's make it works twice... and I have no problem with that, but that's what it's all about. Some gameplay dynamics are still disconnected, like You are playing two different game in one: the building system is totally useless, as for "the forest", and You can just go around making no structure and survive anyway. Completing the story is one game, building a base another one. A game like "Green Hell" did a much better job forcing You to survive thanks to building system in order to progress . "Sons of the forest" map is four time the map of "the forest", and as well four time empty. You'll end up running for hours with nothing to do, just to find the few area of interest. There's no real danger and no real punishment, You will just respawn. No scary situation and much much less charisma than "the forest". As already said, that game confirms what I always thought of "the forest": developers were a really mediocre team with an interesting concept that players made great: let's wait till the community make this game great too. And don't get me wrong, having developer that listen 100% to community nowadays, is a blessing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is solid. If you're on the fence about purchasing it, just get it. Honestly, for an early access game it feels pretty complete. I've seen non-early access games from big name studios have way more bugs at launch. I don't think I've seen any game-breaking bugs at all come to think of it. The only gripes I have are some creative differences with processes in game. For example, getting the shovel is a bit of a pain and it's absolutely required to get any decent weapons. The building mechanics are also a bit different than the first game. Neither of these are game-breaking issues. I would just make the shovel a bit easier to get and maybe make defensive wall building mechanic like the first game. I like seeing an outline of my wall before I start, personally.Again, those are super nit-picky gripes and my personal preference. Overall it's a solid game for being early access. I would absolutely buy this again. The addition of Kelvin and Virginia are great and add so much more to this game. It's a step in the right direction for a sequel.

This does not feel like a survival game anymore, but more like an run and gun FPS game.I had to hunt nothing, or get angry that I lost my spear while trying to get food and starved because of that.I had to build no base (like before), nor cook (like before), nor scanvange(like before), nor explore(like before).This hurt me as much as Resindent Evil 1 going to Resident Evil 3. Its not the same game  anymore, even if it is.Game still will be fun and thumbs down is to harsh, a medium level thumb by me!!!Sadly its not the same hard survival experience as before. Even if the Inventory system etc, is nicely progressive and something not seen before in that way.   Well done!!! You just lost your way that made this game stand out before. _childDocuments_.review: I've played around 15 hours, and all i can say from SOTF it's great. Most of these hours are based on working on my base. Building compared to the precuel it's 10/10. You can shape wood the way you need and make interesting houses, or if you prefer, like the prequel, making a prebuilded house is not a bad idea.Combat is greatly improved: Looking down and top off without intending on the prequel always bothered me. Now, if you want to do that, just hold left mouse button. So that helps for making a normal cut with an axe, for example.Inventory:  I think it is very well organised, with everything in its place, so, a big improvement. Also  I like the rgb leds :)Fight with cannibals:  Now some enemies are trying to make some stealth to us, around grass, or behind some trees, with I find a really good implementation. Also some cannibals (not mutants) cannot be flinch, so be careful with hitting them and blocking your attacksKelvin: Some bugs with him like hitting a wall, but nothing that can be fix it. I consider Kelvin "in my case" 20 times better than Ashley from RE4Graphics. Just amazing. When you start playing, the atmosphere quickly gets you.Performance: With a i9 9900k, RTX 2080 super, 16GB RAM it runs all in ultra settings and DLSS balanced around 70-80 FPS.Bugs:  Keep in mind that this game is not fully completed (Early access). Some bugs are very present in this game. Try searching on youtube or game's comunity to be aware of.Difficulty has has gone up considerably even on normal. If you want to play great survival game, and play with friends (which I don't have) this is your game. I cannot recommend you more to use Kelvin as a slave :DPD: Sorry for my bad English, I'm trying to improve it :)

_childDocuments_.review: Early access is not an excuse for this mess. I have played this game's predecessor in early access and it was nowhere near as bad as this. The issues with Sons of the Forest glaring and numerous:- The world is completely empty; the map has swollen many times over in size compared to The Forest, yet it has far fewer landmarks. The map consists of last swathes of nothingness occasionally interspersed with cookie-cutter cannibal bases. This makes travel boring at best and annoying most of the time.- The game is tragically badly optimised; I have played the game on GeForce RTX 3070Ti and hardly ever got over 40 FPS on the lowest setting. Quite regularly, I have encountered locations where the FPS dropped below 25. For comparison, I hardly ever get lower than 70 FPS on medium to high settings in other games of comparable visual quality. A friend of mine with whom I have passed the game suffered through it with only about 5-10 FPS fewer than me at any given time, despite having a significantly older setup (GeForce RTX 1070).- The game is too easy; I have finished the game on the hardest difficulty, yet there was little challenge to be found past the first days. The Forest managed preserve the tension much longer and made managing of one's base a necessity. I distinctly remember a horde of mutants charging at my base and smashing it into pieces roughly two-thirds into the game. Here, once you manage to build a base, you need not ever worry about it. It is there to stay for ever, no matter how incompetent a defender you may be.- The story is a joke; I profess no admiration for the story of The Forest, but here the developers have not even tried. I doubt anybody at the Endnight Games' studio had ever taken a pen to paper with serious intent.- The ending is anticlimactic and my hope is that it is a placeholder for something else to be rolled out at a later stage in the development.The game's strongest point is construction, which has been notably improved; it, nevertheless, hardly compensates for the drop in quality in almost every other aspect. At present, I cannot recommend purchasing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics, cannibal interactions, new weapons, the 3d printer, and the general beauty of the landscape and caves are all wonderful. The changing of seasons, the sun rays glimmering through the trees, the ocean foam cascading down the sand, the eeriness of the caves and sounds coming from the walls are all so captivating compared to The Forest. The building it also WAY more customizable than The Forest. Ok… now…Being a HUGE fan of The Forest I am really missing hunting animals for their hide and having a main objective in the game which was to save Timmy. It was so amazing and fulfilling at the end when I beat it for the first time. An absolutely crazy ending, and the anticipation for the new game was substantial. I am finding this game to be quite boring. I really hope the game devs add a different objective other than… finding the billionaire and seeing the emails between him and his team randomly. I want more excitement in the story line since I’m not huge into building. I tried building a base with my friend and the cannibals got through the defensive wall every time. I could improve on my building but I felt The Forest was so much more user friendly. Also in The Forest the cannibals had very specific paths and you could build in certain places to avoid them. Here they seem to be running around everywhere with no real path.The map is super empty as well. It’s like 3x bigger than the old map with virtually nothing in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons Of The Forest

_childDocuments_.review: Game is incomplete.  Physics are totally broken, you can walk in a straight line up a vertical incline to the top of the highest mountain on the map right when you spawn if you'd like, with no trouble at all.  Also, try chucking a log in to the water and watch it launch 50 feet up into the air over and over again fro 20 minutes straight.They also removed rafts and boat building from the game which is a huge detraction from what we had available in the first installment.  This both removes the potential to have a base on the water, and the potential to load a raft with logs and construct and island or stilted base over water unless you do something really roundabout and dumb like launch giant logs across the water with the current physics interactions.Map doesn't seem well thought out, half the caves I explored during my first day were merely resource pockets with some light decoration, and were not part of any continuous cave system.Will update review, but for now this is a totally incomplete game.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's my early access review... I will avoid spoilers such as story elements, bosses etc. Please also keep in mind I play in multiplayer so some experiences could be very different in single player.Pros:-Kelvin is great at filling holders and bringing resources... plus he's a goof you gotta love him-Building system is unique and immersive-The map is gorgeous... if you've ever been in a Northern forest you'll be a happy camper-Virginia is great with a gun-There are a few options for travel around the map... all of which are fun-The traps are brilliant and hilarious-The new mutants are unique and have incredible designs-The sound design is amazing as long as you aren't near a waterfall (waterfall sounds seem to bug out a lot)-Many, many unique cannibals, some with very specialised combat skills-The weapon upgrade system is amazing and unique-The music is amazing and sometimes reveals hints about the story-The ending is intense and exciting-The comedy that's in the game is great-Guns are great but melee combat is still relevant-Caves/bunkers look gorgeous and are mostly well designed-The visual storytelling is brilliant-Points of interest are worthwhile and rewards for exploring are adequate-The cooking system is great-Big head modeNeutral: -Virginia wanders and only visits from time to time... she's more likely to visit if there's a waterfall near base-The cannibals are very human, takes away from the horror a bit but also adds a bit of psychological horror in my opinion-The new mutants aren't gargantuan in size... takes away from the horror element a little bit but in my opinion they are still scary-There's no real incentive to build a large base other than for storage and the fun of building-Certain enemies only spawn after endgame-The hang glider is kind of useless since it's almost impossible to carry up to high vantage points after being used... hoping it gets replaced with a paraglider that can be found and stored in the inventory-Cave D is still a bit of a maze even after it's re-design-Armour is weaker than it was in the forest but is mostly easy to replenishCons:-Kelvin is a bit buggy if working on something for too long-Kelvin and Virginia tend to get in the way-Kelvin and Virginia tend to get stuck really easily-The map is huge and has a large mountain in the middle that is hard to travel over... hoping that endnight adds paths or  zipline system that is part of the map to get up the mountain. Even perhaps a ski resort with a gondola the player can power-In winter gifts from Virginia tend to fall through the mapOverall I love this game, upon full release it may become my favourite game of all time. Despite how Kelvin and Virginia have some bugs and the AI pathing can get annoying, I love both of them and still find both to be useful. The story in early access is fascinating and it will be expanded upon full release.

_childDocuments_.review: As an alpha test - 8/10As a £25 game - 4/10- Visuals 8/10 - It`s a game with great visuals. Although, in the first session, the game was running 15 frames on recommended hardware. It got better after closing the game and restarting the PC. Other visual bugs were experienced - random lighting, seeing through stone walls etc. - Sound 4/10 - Odd volume levels not really tied to the player's distance from the mobs. Sometimes gets very distorted and sounds like the game is about to crash, just to get back to normal as long as you leave certain areas. - Performance 6/10 - it does appear that different people have different experiences but, all the people in the party experienced freezes and frame drops at times. Needs further optimising. - Assets 4/10 - logs/plants that float in the air, roll on the ground to unknown destinations, mountains that you can pass through, items falling through the map etc., cannibals that cannot be interacted with- Building mechanics 4/10 - highly expected but less diverse than the ones found in The Forest, with certain dropped Items (e.g. Turtle Shells) having no use. Restrictive custom base building mechanics (I do miss the building mechanics in The Forest), but I hope these will be changed and/or improved. No boat houses, no rafts.- A.I. 2/10 - Sons of the Forest gives us a follower, which is not very useful besides asking him to carry resources. Kelvin (or as I like to call him, Kenny) can be downed and revived forever, likes to carry rocks and logs, especially those that you already carried yourself to the base. He can`t speak or hear and loves to crouch down and cower whenever he hears explosions or fighting (although he is supposed to be deaf). On the other hand, cannibals, spawning out of thin air next to your base, like to climb through windows that wouldn`t fit a toddler and hit like they are armed with laser swords. Don`t think doors will stop them as doors cannot be locked (yet) and even if they could, they are easily destroyed. They know where you are and our unfinished log cabin was under constant assault from waves of 6-8 mutants wearing bone and creepy armour during day 10. - Food and drink survival mechanics 5/10 - No debuff for turning into a cannibal yourself. Enjoy tasty leg steak and arms galore (if they don`t fall through the map the second you cut them off). Drinking is really clunky when trying to find a spot in the water. No way to collect rainwater. No explanation of what the status icon means, or a stats page. - Feels awfully empty - took almost 3 in-game days (at the long setting) to cover all the beaches of the map (which is huge), only to find around 6-7 spots where you could loot anything: an area with 3 derelict buildings with very poor loot, a tent area, a dock, and the rest were just abandoned boats. The forest itself is full ... of trees and a couple of caves and rarely any options for looting other than the OP mutant villages. The game feels shallow and pales in comparison with The Forest. I know it`s an Early Access game, but taking into account the time it took to develop, the release delays it was subjected to and the price tag of a AAA game, it`s not worth a buy and it feels like the game is treating us exactly like this cannibal:As one of my friends said: We`ll play it next year when it gets good! Hopefully it does!

_childDocuments_.review: Potentially fantastic game ruined.  Insane mutant cannibal attacks which destroy the game. Base building is dire. You need a safe base to defend yourselves but you are constantly attacked whilst building it. If you manage to fend off these constant attacks why do you need a base anyway? You can put down stakes which do help but these are knocked down and you are replacing them often. It takes ages to build even a very small hut. Supposed to be open world survival but you will not last a day without the plethora of equipment  left lying around. You can get tooled up but your supplies wont last once you get deep into the forest. Game looks fantastic and runs perfectly well but it has an "empty" feel to it sometimes. I have stopped playing this now,shame...

_childDocuments_.review: An entirely new experience from the makers of the 'The Forest'. Sent to find a missing billionaire on a remote island, you find yourself in a cannibal-infested hellscape. Craft, build, and struggle to survive, alone or with friends, in this terrifying new open-world survival horror simulator. Experience complete freedom to tackle the world how you want. You decide what you do, where to go and how best to survive. There are no NPC's barking orders at you or giving you missions you don't want to do. You give the orders, you choose what happens next. Enter a world where nowhere is safe and fight against a range of mutated creatures, some who are almost human like, and others who are like nothing you have ever seen before. Armed with pistols, axes, stun batons and more, protect yourself and those you care for. Feel every interaction; Break sticks to make fires. Use an axe to cut out windows and floors. Build a small cabin, or a sea-side compound, the choice is yours. Pluck fresh salmon directly from streams in spring and summer. Collect and store meat for the cold winter months. You're not alone on this island, so as winter rolls in and food and resources become scarce you won't be the only one looking for a meal. Co-op Gameplay - Survive alone, or with friends. Share items and work together to build defenses. Bring back-up to explore above and below ground.

name: Turbo Overkill
detailed_description: ' Turbo Overkill is the best Tony Hawk game in years.' - Fanbyte 'If Sam Raimi's Evil Dead movie made the Chainsaw Arm an iconic piece of weaponry, wait till you see the leg chainsaw.' - Sportskeeda 'Turbo Overkill isn't just one of the best boomer shooters on the market right now - this is one of the best games on the market, full stop.' - Superjumpmagazine Half-metal, half-human, all murder machine Heavily inspired by some of the all-time greats like Id's Doom & Quake , and Apogee's Duke Nukem 3D , with stunning cyberpunk visuals, Turbo Overkill is the most savage FPS ever released by Apogee. You play as Johnny Turbo, augmented with hidden arm rockets and a chainsaw that extends from your lower leg allowing you to slide-slice enemies wide open. In this Blade Runner -meets- DOOM hellscape, Johnny returns to his hometown of Paradise and finds its entire population possessed by Syn, a rogue AI, and its army of augmented minions. Desperate for enough money to outrun his past mistakes, Johnny takes on the impossible job of destroying the greatest AI ever created. Rival bounty hunters want to claim the prize first. Nothing is easy in paradise. Turbo Time, wall-running, dashing and grappling hooks, oh my Turbo Overkill takes over-the-top to never-before-reached heights. Activate Turbo Time(™), a new form of slow motion with a twist. Build incredible speed by wall-running and dashing. Slide on your chainsaw leg, eviscerating foes and opening up bosses for critical damage, and go car-surfing on the hoods of flying cars. Blast away with the Twin Magnums, which lock-on and instagib several foes, the Boomer Shotgun and its attached grenade launcher, or the Telefragger sniper rifle, which teleports Johnny inside an enemy before they explode from within. Race through two dozen stages packed with secrets, bonus arena stages, and white-knuckle combat puzzles. Find game-changing collectibles to unlock punishing modifiers like triple-monster-speed and insta-kill. Combine all of Johnny’s weapons and powers to outsmart, outgun and outrun the corrupted legions. TL;DR: o Kill a boss, get its augment (special power) o Play Spider-Man with your grappling hook o One-up Duke Nukem with your chainsaw slide-slice kick o Kills = cash. Use cash to install augments, upgrade your weapons, and add new abilities in your talent tree o Be a ghost runner while wall running o Attack from above riding the hood of your flying car like a kung-furious badass o Mini-rockets built into your robotic arm? ✔ o This. List. Will. Grow. Wishlist the game to see it happen Don't quote us on nuthin' “ Turbo Overkill is fast, frenetic and ferocious—excess personified,” said Sam Prebble, one half of Trigger Happy Interactive. “This is the game we’ve always wanted to play; making it is a dream project. Relentless enemies, extremely deadly and fun weapons, speed and precision above all else—if you love Quake III Arena , modern and classic DOOM , or Apogee’s legendary first-person shooters, you’ll feel right at home in Paradise.” “As the guy who helped launch the shooter genre with Wolfenstein 3D , Rise of the Triad, Duke Nukem 3D, Max Payne , and Prey , I haven’t been this excited about an FPS since the golden era of Apogee/3D Realms,” wrote Scott Miller, founder. “ Turbo Overkill is a sandbox of fun and original gameplay ideas that come together like a night of melty hot pizza and your favorite cold, frothy brew. Playing this game made me a Turbo Lover all over again.”

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is already spectacular and blows away some finished retro shooters this early in early access (only Episode 1 is out as of writing - 7/16/2022). My full meandering review follows:The closest thing to this is definitely Doom Eternal, down to the double-jumping and boost-dashing, though it does not have the health/armor/ammo loop. Overall, it's very fast-paced and more vertical than actual 90s shooters - but as of writing you  use the console to lower the game speed if desired (code is "slomo 1.0" where "1.0" is default 100% gamespeed. I set mine to 85% most of the time). (and "story")Think Painkiller or Serious Sam rather than Quake or older Doom games; rarely does Turbo Overkill have enemies waiting and muttering in small rooms before you enter them. Instead, rooms where you fight are usually enormous and arena-like, with enemies warping in either all at once or in waves as you kill them. Levels are usually very big, taking me on average just over an hour to complete, but if I wasn't obsessively looking for secrets in all of them - another super important feature of 90s shooters - they'd probably take a third of that or less. The levels are just super-cool. Most of them are outdoors, in an exaggerated cyberpunk megatropolis, down to the pink and blue neon everywhere and absolutely constant (acid?) rain. One level has several rooms that appear to be outdoors, until stray bullets hit the screens that make up every wall and you can see the skybox is just a facade for hollow metal infrastructure, which you can get behind for tactical and equipment-finding purposes. Another is set on a hovering train moving through robotically-fast flying car traffic, and at certain points you're forced to ditch the train to jump from car to car. My favorite level is literally the entire Peach Trees apartment mega-block from the movie Dredd, down to the squished remains of the hobo caught in the threshold of the main blast door. Generally the levels will let you backtrack as much as you want, with only a few exceptions where there are points of no return near the end. I wish these points were a little more clearly-defined, but it didn't generally stop me from finding every levels' six collectibles (three each used to unlock one mutator mode and challenge level). Also, the levels don't do a whole lot to restrict you from speedrunning them, in terms of invisible walls or intangible ledges to keep you from climbing. It means you can easily skip rooms or go out-of-bounds to places that you're not supposed to see if you try, but I much prefer it to the alternative.Also, I was surprised to hear some dialog throughout the game, which currently consists of the player character's flying car AI, the megacorp exec who hired your character, and the main villain, the rampant AI named SYN. It's not frequent (which is better than , ), but the voice acting is the same quality you'd expect from any high-budget game.The guns each have two firing modes; some use right-click to quickly transform the gun from one mode to another, but most use right click to fire a different projectile that takes a long time to recharge, temporarily locking both modes of the gun off, though you can switch weapons to keep shooting during this. Most guns feel distinct and useful, though I never felt that the shotguns were quite right in terms of their balance of damage/firerate/penetration/spread. Not that they're bad, but they're just kind of weird. The biggest case of redundancy, I think, is the smgs' and minigun's primary fire modes, but for space reasons I won't go into detail here.Melee is restricted to sliding into enemies which automatically uses the chainsaw-leg, which does more damage the faster you are moving prior to activation and slows you down slightly with every enemy killed. Much as its hyped up, I didn't really care for it. Thankfully it's never necessary to use.Turbo-Overkill uses a system somewhat similar to Bioshock for upgrading your character - you collect money as coins called Zhen that explode out of random fallen enemies (often unreachably dropping into bottomless pits), and can spend this on augments to your bionics or unlocking your guns' secondary fire modes, both at vending machines spread around each level. A third vending machine allows you to equip up to two augments into each one of your limbs; augments say which limb can receive them. At the time of writing, only the legs and left arm are used, where your right leg (the chainsaw) mostly receives melee bonuses (with one exception) like heal-on-chainsaw-kill or chainsaw-slide-faster, your left leg gets things related to non-offensive movement (faster-dash-recharge, wall-jumping) and your left arm mostly gets augments to your lock-on rockets superweapon.However, some of the augments are just too important for me to ever consider replacing. Faster-dash-recharge is the best augment, hands-down, for combat or just getting around levels to explore. Wall-jumping might have some combat utility, but its main feature is allowing you to jump two more times than normal (provided any vertical surface), which is indispensable for exploration. For whatever reason, your rocket-arm gets "Zhen magnet," which makes coins just go straight to your account rather than needing to be gathered (or lost in a bottomless pit), which is basically a must-have that locks off a rocket upgrade until you buy everything else you want. Also, since I didn't like the chainsaw-leg much, once I got "Steady Footing," the only non-offense augment for the right leg which makes your normally-slippery-feeling movement perfectly stable, I didn't look back.The graphics are a lot like another amazing retro-shooter, Prodeus - low-res textures and low-poly models, but with modern lighting, reflections, and other effects. They're lovely. Plus, this game has (skippable, if needed) cutscenes that actually look phenomenal given the simplicity of the models.Speaking of Prodeus, Turbo Overkill's enemies are much better in terms of visual design than Prodeus's current offering of "vague orange gremlin" and "vague blue gremlin". They tend to go down in hordes, but they all look quite distinct and also just pretty awesome as far as bionic body-horror. Sort of like more lively and cyberpunky Quake II Strogg; though less grim, asymmetrical, and industrial. Not better or worse.The soundtrack is phenomenal. At first I thought it was another Andrew Hulshult score - which would not be an insult by any means; he just seems to do the music for  retro shooter - but it's a lot more "electro" and varied than Hulshult's sort of industrial-electronic-metal stuff. From what I can find, it's all done by "Gribblesnap," one of the game's devs (though I'm not exactly sure how many people are on the dev team). As you move throughout the levels, the bgm subtly alters to keep things fresh, and basically any time I was taking a second to think about how to get to a potential secret, I'd catch myself thinking how damn good the music was.I can't say I really "noticed" the game's sound effects much, which could ironically be due to the volume of the music - though I left the sound settings at default.There are a few places where I can tell it's not totally polished - mostly just being able to get (stuck in) places you weren't meant to, and some things related to the vehicle segment - but it's not Skyrim-buggy or anything. It doesn't crash, and the game autosaves frequently enough that I never lost more than a minute or so of progress. No big deal.Again, this is (very) early access, and everything is already well within the margin of error for "finished" AAA titles these days.it's good. it's a good game. get it. yes.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best singer-player FPS I've ever played. Better than Titanfall 2, Doom Eternal, or any other great in the genre.I'll admit the story is flimsy but it's really only there to set up some increased platforming & action setpices. The gunplay is absolutely perfect and it's arsenal is as inventive as it is functional. I'm going to gush about this game a lot but first some critiques.This is a classic boomer shooter, so if you're not down for running at 100mph & never reloading, this may be too much for you. In fact, it was almost too much for me and I love these kinds of games. I had to tone down the difficulty from normal to the easiest level twice because I felt I just died too quickly to react. Some enemies, especially near the end when they appear in groups, can wipe away your entire health bar in one hit. You get a dodge, a grappling hook (that can set enemies on fire), a double jump with additional modifiers, and sometimes environmental movement enhancers like jump pads, so it's usually easy to dodge tougher enemies. But when the game purposely locks you in tiny rooms, it can be rough. And that is especially true in the final level when time limits are introduced.The upgrade systems here are satisfying, though simple. Killing certain random enemies will make them drop money which is used to by modifications for your limbs & head or weapon upgrades. It may seem like it'll take a while to unlock them all, but you'll have all of them early into the final (3rd) episode. This means that for roughly the final 25% of the game leaves you with nothing to spend your money. This is fine because it feels like you've finally reached your final form at that point, but I wish I didn't have a functionality pointless number continuing to go up in the final levels.There's controller support, and I played the entire game on Steam Deck. It was nearly flawless, but it takes some tweaking to get everything mapped in a way that feels comfortable. In particular, it was hard finding a place to map all of your special powers (slow motion, micro missiles, grappling hook) as at least 2 of them are abilities that you'll need to aim while using. These abilities make sense for the shoulder buttons, but you also have alt-fires & weapon swapping up there usually, so you may have to get creative (thank God for the weapon wheel).And finally, I understand this is an indie game so I don't want to go too hard on this point, but I've gotten hard stuck twice due to checkpoint-related glitches. Luckily all I needed to do was restart the level, but considering these both happened in the final levels, I had to replay sections that I barely completed in the first place. Plus, because the game is so hard, I find myself trying to outsmart the game and trying to access health & ammo that should have been locked behind previous doors, which is the very reason one of my glitches happened. When the game can be this difficult, it encourages cheesing, so maybe a tweaked difficulty could change that. Hell, it really is only a few specific fights that were rough, so maybe just check those encounters. Also, this game could use some kind of more prominent "danger zone" warning state similar to Doom Eternal. In that game you rarely died in one hit, if at all, in normal. You'd at least get knocked into a fragile state & had a split second to recover. You almost never get that split second in Turbo Overkill, and perhaps if I had ot I never would have been frustrated in certain moments.But the rest of this game ♥♥♥♥♥ SO HARD.You get every gun under the sun it feels like. A sniper, 2 different shotguns, SMGs, an LMG/flamethrower, a plasma rifle, rocket launcher, and orbital Lazer, & chainsaw arms (which are charged by killing enemies with your chainsaw leg). Every weapon feeling great to use (especially if you turn on hit markers) and with a moderate exception to the plasma rifle, every weapon has heavy utility. And despite how frustrating they were initially, the timed fights forced me to find the most effective weapon for each enemy. I couldn't just pick a weapon and stick with it, I had to react to every specific encounter.I mentioned weapon upgrades and body augmentations earlier and I gotta say they're mostly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible. Body mods can do simple things like give more mod slots, extend slow-mo times, or give health or armor when killing with your chainsaw leg. Or they can give you crazy useful perks like igniting enemies with your grappling hook, adding a second chainsaw leg, or giving yourself the ability to wall jump once before touching the ground. In some cases, weapon mods just fix an initial flaw with a weapon, like eliminating the chain gun's windup. But sometimes the entire use case of a weapon is changed. For example, x the starting pistols can be upgraded to (after landing enough shots consecutively) transform into a magnum that does more damage than any other gun in the game. And it stays that way until you finally miss a shot. The variety of these upgrades is insane and takes the power fantasy of the gameplay up to 11.I mention that there's a story, but it's nothing special. It's very campy in an 80s way, and tonally it's humor is very Duke Nukem (but with none of the meanness of Forever). It makes for fun cutscenes at least, and many of them show off the impressive level & character design.Oh yeah, I forgot that this game is BEAUTIFUL. It has a PS1 look to it, but so many detailed enemies get jammed into such massive & detailed arenas that it's hard not to be impressed with the game in context of modern releases. It might be working with half the polygons when it comes to texture, but they lean on vibrant colors, insane boss design, and varied level design to stick out.There's even more I could talk about, like how great the platforming sections are and how they feel like if Titanfall 2 & Doom Eternal had a baby, or how satisfying it is to rain fire from above thanks to the forgiving floatiness of its jumps, or how satisfyingly hidden the collectibles are, or how brilliantly the scale & stakes of the game escalate throughout, or how there's apparently community maps to play now that I'm done, or how the audio logs gives some surprisingly tender back story. But, I gotta go to bed I've been up for nearly 24 hours.So I'll just say that if you've ever enjoyed a Boomer Shooter (any game like Dusk, Doom Eternal, Ultrakill, etc.) then this is a must-play. I'll be surprised if this isn't on my top 10 of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥... Its like I died and woke up in 1996 and graphics are better.  Do you like old school shooters?  Do you like fast movement and frantic combat?  Do you like gibs?Apogee is back and better than ever and they arent a name like 3D Realms.  The original founder of Apogee is back in charge.  This game is an unforgiving hectic monstrosity.  This game is like sticking your head under Niagra Falls.  This game is like slapping a Pit Bull in the face and smiling.  This game is like ordering a pizza and when the delivery man shows up, you strafe to the left and shoot your money at his fore head and he falls as you slide in and grab the pizza and slide in the door before he even hits the ground. Its the natural progression before money took over video games.If you like Duke Nukem, Rise of the Traid, Doom, Blood, etc etc... all the good games.... you will be right at home here. Theres absolutely nothing like this on the market right now and all I got to say is....APOGEE IS BACK!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: The best Bang for your Buck Boomer Shooter Ever. An amazing cinematic campaign with 25 replayable good size levels to 100% with 2 types of collectables that unlock new cool secret levels and cheats. Arcade mode turns the story levels into a classic mode, limited lives, sKillshot point based speedrun for leaderboard ranking. Endless mode which is an arena switching survival mode that now has co-op and custom user made levels that hopefully get co-op support in the future making it truly "Endless". And finally the Godly Level Editor worth a full price buy alone.Can't forgot the amazing photo mode with great extra setting and toggable poses worthy of a Johnny Turbo action figure.Almost 200 hours in and I've only played 1/3 of all the content because I've been obsessed with the level editor since day one, already putting out 2 great levels out so far, and with the level editor being in the early stages it's already one of the best and its still improving. We still get updates, fixes and even a new dev made map recently for Endless Co-op so I can't wait to see the game and community grows to its peak for more endless co-op and improved custom levels. Seriously one of the best of it's kind and easy to use and run on the Steam Deck. This game is already a 10/10 for the price but if we get endless co-op for custom levels and possible campaign then this game would have everything I'd want out of it. Absolute must have, even has a demo which is what sold me outside of seeing the level editor.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about halfway through but at this rate this game is just utterly spectacular. It's not only one of it not THE best boomer shooters I've ever played (overtaking the throne held by Dusk), it's full stop one of the best shooters in general I've ever played. I'm in complete awe that a game of this quality and length was made by what I assume is a pretty small indie team. The game makes it SO easy for you to jump in and start enjoying it, there are no barriers here. Mechanically it's practically perfect. I haven't played a game in a while that puts me in a flow state quite as well as this one does and I attribute that to how smooth everything feels. The movement is fast and very easy to control and understand, and the weapons are varied, interesting, and overall awesome. The level design is as good as it gets in this genre with plenty of opportunity for exploration and well designed shootouts. The visuals, sound design, and soundtrack are all varied and fit the game's theme so well. So far if there's one single minor critique I can find it would be the sound design for some weapons (more specifically shotguns) and how they sound pretty underpowered. I got used to it pretty quickly and it's extremely minor overall. So far at the halfway point (and at this rate) TO is an EASY 10/10 and in my opinion one of the top 5 best games of the year. I seriously can't wait to see what this dev does next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute master piece, I remember buying back when it was in EA, and i played it a bit and I thought "meh", dont really know what all the fuss is about, I then played it again after full release and man was I in for a ride.Everything around this game is really well done, the enemies, the weapons, the pacing on the upgrades, the maps, everything. I even enjoyed getting all the achievements (i have 1 left ). There were LOTS to get and I loved the craziness of the requirements for some of them. The Tech chips that you can activate that does not disable Achievements was a really nice touch as i wouldn't have been able to get some of these without those. _childDocuments_.review: It is quite hard to put into words how good I think this thing is, but if you'll allow me a few, I want to add some context to maybe help make a point: In all honesty, at the moment I've become a bit fatigued with all the "Boomer Shooters", that's not to say i don't enjoy them or anything, but we have been fed well over the last few years and I think I'm pretty full, so yesterday with the release of 1.0 of this game I decided to boot it up as I bought it in early access initially and enjoyed it but didn't think too much of it at the time, I remembered it as a cool shooter with fast movement and a funny chainsaw-leg gimmick that still kinda blended a bit into everything else but I figured now that it was out I'd give it another go....I binged this thing over the last day because I couldn't get enough of it; it was fun and fast but what started getting to me was the sense of scale and ambition, an early level had me going through a tribute/parody of the Megacity "Peachtrees" from the Dredd movie, I thought that was kind of fun and novel until I looked down about 20 minutes in and realised how many floors of this building I'd fought through... this level wasn't using the aesthetics of the megacity as a fun reference, it was using it to create an immense sense of a journey because I didn't fight through a bit of a megacity, I fought through all of it, floor after floor going up and up, sometimes outside and looping around to higher floors, hitting the roof and still going...The scale of it was overwhelming and yet the game made it feel effortless, the frame-rate stayed high, the level's pacing felt well tuned, and the combat and platforming all flowed into each other with variety and great pacing and I was just floored by it...And then the game refused to stop being constantly interesting and ambitious and fun; the sights and sounds were varied with little vehicle segments that didn't feel just gimmicky but actually felt like they gave certain levels their own individual sense of pace and flow. I don't want to spoil it but some of the levels just feel like such an adventure and yet beyond that the combat remained fantastic to match; this is a game that up at no point did I find any gun redundant, even the starting pistol became a gun that I was using consistently in the last levels of the game; every gun has its moments to shine and yet it was never in a way that I felt arbitrarily forced to need to use a certain gun, I used every gun because every gun was useful right up to the end. Beyond that though is just the absolute speed you can get up to in this. A lot of air control, chainsaw legs, double jumps, and boosts can all be chained together for absolutely insane jumps and platforming that the game does expect you to do and yet it's never overwhelming; it's always smooth and responsive and I never lacked confidence in making some of the absolutely absurd jumps the game demanded. Obviously different people have different tolerances for first person platforming but for me I adored it and never had any frustrations with it.Look I can go on all day, the game ran really well for me, the game looked great, sounded great, the soundtrack was varied and fun and there were some absolutely phenomenal tracks, especially in the last episode, Add to that the fact that custom levels are a thing and then I look at the price of this game and honestly....I think that's a steal, i would easily recommend this at twice its asking price, I genuinely would.I really do think this was something special and my only worry in saying that is that I'm overselling it, I don't want to ruin your experience in doing so but at the same time I want to be honest about my experience, and it was a phenomenal one.If you find yourself enjoying this even half as much as I ended up doing, then you will have had a really good time :)

_childDocuments_.review: For a quick review this game is great. It is like Quake 1 on steroids with a 80's vibe and some more story and cutscenes. It progressively gets better and better as you play the game too. Highly recommended to buy. I will continue to see what these devs make next like is upcoming Total Chaos game.For a longer review, this is probably the best boomer shooter I have ever played. The creative talent knew what they were doing.There are negatives, certainly not game breaking listed below,The collectibles need to be taken out the game. It goes against everything this game represents which is fast and furious gameplay. If you want to provide unlockables make it to where it compliments the gameplay like killing enemies or finishing levels within time limits. I am surprised the creative talent made the collectibles to where it will slow you down searching for them. This was a mistake. If you want us to explore the world you created, viewing the already well designed levels is the prize, not some artificial collectible. I will not scour the levels or will I look up YouTube clips to figure out where they are. I will not go back and play the game again in different ways because of not having the collectibles that I missed the first time I played it. At the very least just give us the collectibles after beating the game.Other smaller issues include,-I would like the option to move the weapons more to the side of the screen to not obstruct my fov,double-barrelled shotgun shooting too slowly,-levels can be a bit lengthy,-the fog, and the onscreen effects while having 30-second power-ups need better perfecting, hard to see what was on screen, I wanted to play with the fog on but it made the game hard to see.-Too much explosions while shooting enemies blocks my vision of seeing the enemies being hit with my bullets, this takes away some satisfaction from hitting my enemies. Make the effects shoot to the sides or something else so I can see the damage I am doing-I would like pvp multiplayer at leastEverything else is great though such as,+I constantly used all the weapons provided with the exception to the double shotgun cuz of its slower shooting capacity,+the game quickly gets better and better as you play+graphics and sound top-notch,+plenty of weapons and enemies,+the vehicular shooing sections did not overstay its welcome,+pretty lengthy game for being a boomer shooter, 15-20 hour game,buy the game, i'm looking forward to seeing what else the developer is making...would be great to see some sort of old school zombie survival horror game by these guys.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest of the retro boomer shooter craze. It combines fast, responsive controls with genuinely amusing humor, satisfying weapons, great music and a surprisingly substantial campaign. The only real criticisms I can think of are, 1. on the default difficulty setting, you can become so OP with the right upgrades that the game becomes trivial in the last third. & 2. the later stages reuse a major boss enemy a few times too many. _childDocuments_.review: I had very high expectations for  as I've seen it appear on many "Best of 2023"-lists. And while it starts off very strong, taking a page out of the new wave of Boomer Shooters reminiscent of DOOM 2016/Eternal, it does unfortunately fumble the ball and severely outstays its welcome.Episode three just becomes a constant slog of the same encounters spammed over and over again complete with a boss rush sequence at the end as well. By the time I was done, clocking in fifteen(!?) hours on the highest difficulty, I was completely drained. After the credits rolled and seeing the other modes offered in the main menu I just couldn't fathom why anyone would want to bother with the Endless or Arcade options. It's far from  mind you and does plenty of good such as the frenetic combat itself, the epic synth-wave soundtrack or being able to upgrade Johnny Turbo's abilities to your own liking and playstyle. Sadly though the positives are buried beneath far too much fat that  needed trimming. And while I understand its odd to complain about there being 'too much content' I feel like a snappy retro FPS like this could've been much more enjoyable at half its length. I would even go so far as to say it would  its replayability if it was shorter. However even some of the levels themselves just drag on and on and I shudder the thought of having to go through all of it again just to uncover the remaining collectibles. Its core mechanics are certainly fine and when you're chainsaw sliding into multiple enemies right into a jump pad and unleashing an auto-missile barrage at the height of your jump in slow motion, seeing enemies below explode in a mess of gibs and health drops before grapple-hooking into another foe on the periphery of your vision it definitely hits that endorphin rush. That said when all the chaos unfolds even the visuals themselves can become an assault on the eyes what with the exaggerated cyberpunk aesthetic and areas where the colourspace devolves into a saturated fluorescent mess. It all adds to the feeling of exhaustion which makes this game difficult to recommend. Ultimately  is a prime example of "too much of a good thing" and dilutes its own experience by artificially padding its length. So get it cheap, play the first episode and then decide if you want to stick with it. According to the achievement completion rate many of its most vocal fans certainly haven't...

_childDocuments_.review: The pace of the combat in this one is absolutely off the rails. It feels like every mechanic straight-up breaks the game, and once you find your rhythm, it is incredibly addictive. After 11 hours it still feels like i haven't even scratched the surface of whats possible when it comes to play-styles and level routing.8/10Here's where the disclaimer comes in. The physics are not for everyone. Even some that liked DOOM 2016/Eternal might find them difficult to get a handle on. The sheer speed you have right from the beginning can be overwhelming.  I could see people not making it through the first 5 hours due to the difficulty the speed alone creates. The last disclaimer is more of a nit pick, but every level seems to last too long (except the first couple). If they were 2/3 the length that would be perfect for me.Over all its a great game if you are itching for a new fast-paced shooter, but be prepared to acclimate to the speed and play-styles you'll need to get good.Just a side not, i wasn't sure if I would get used to this style of retro graphics, but they grew on me pretty quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: It honestly pains me to review this as early as I am but seeing how the game's core combat is going I don't imagine adding a couple of new weapons and some gimmick missions are gonna do anything to save this.For the record the game isn't too hard or anything, I actually found it quite easy even on the second-to-hardest difficulty, which is what I usually start with on these games. That being said, after playing the game for about 40 minutes, I already feel like I've experienced half of all the game has to offer me.At its best, Turbo Overkill is a game that can be best described as the lovechild of old DOOM & Ultrakill; extremely fast gameplay where your character feels like he's perpetually moving at Mach 10 with some additional movement gimmicks that are fun to play with at times, but aside from that this game has a lot of things missing out on it that I can't say I truly enjoy.None of the enemies are memorable. Enemies generally blend in with the environment and are extremely small and hard to notice, making it usually very annoying to shoot them with more accurate weapons, despite how generous the game can be with those at times. Regardless, the impact of shooting and killing enemies just.. isn't there. There's no satisfaction beyond the ridiculous aspect of what you're actually doing; i.e., moving at inhuman speeds with a chainsaw for a leg dual wielding uzis and a sawed-off SSG wannabe. Enemies usually blow up in very well made gore and viscera but the gore itself is so tame and just blends in with the rest of the environment, not to mention the sound design for most of the weapons feels weak as hell and makes some guns just outright not fun to shoot.Turbo Overkill is an objectively fun game at its core, but it's missing a lot of extremely important keys that I think just hold it from being as good as DOOM Eternal and Ultrakill were, even though both games have their fair share of issues as well.Why am I still recommending it?Like I said, it's a fun game at its core and if that's all you care about then by all means buy it, it's very amusing for the first few minutes and if you care for the story and deeper mechanics I'd recommend you check out the rest. However, to me personally, this game is limited behind a couple of technical issues that are mostly personal and I'd understand if not everybody had aligned thoughts; the game is far from perfect, but it is worth what it's worth. Try it out on sale if you want, full price is ok too.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a very special game, and I highly recommend it. I give it a 10/10, I would give it a 9/10 for no co-op campaign, but I respect it too much to lower it's score. The music is an incredible 10/10, and the SFX is 9/10 because it's just barely not chunky enough for me. The graphics are cohesive, and the gameplay is immaculate. Story is quite fitting, no notes. Rating up here because I can't expect anyone to read what I've gushed below lol.I've been playing shooters a long time, and I was very good at them, I hesitate to say I could have gone pro but when your scores are comparable to people who cheat, you tend to wonder. Anyways, I love hyper mobility shooters. They're not as common as they used to be, and the big names, like destiny 2, come with their own problems.So for the last 10 years or so, I've not really been touching the genre. Everything felt the same, as imo, most FPS combat has been largely stagnant. It feels as if most lead designers seem to think that merely adding newer, zanier guns is the equivalent of adding new mechanics. Sure, guide-able bullets is rad with snipers, dashing is a nice addition, and combat slides are fun, but at the end of the day, none of this is a great departure. In the FPS genre, there are three extremely common types; cover, looter, or one of the boomer shooter revival games. They make up about 75% of shooters and if you've played one of a type, you've basically played all of that type. Not to throw shade at each, but at this point it's rare you find anything with a  twist on gameplay. Just varying levels of execution.Turbo Overkill is different. It gives you a chainsaw leg that can be used in tandem with all movement tech. You can chainsaw slide jump/dash/circle strafe. All weapons have different firing modes making each gun effectively 2 guns, each alt fire being just as effective as the primary, albeit for different situations. Augmentations for your character exist as well, which make additional changes to movement tech. You can basically tool Johnny to be good at whatever you like best, and for me, that's the chainsaw. Unless I am playing endless mode, I often forget I have guns because the movement tech is so strong. Use that as you will.There is a lot I am not covering, but I'll put it this way; no weapon is a dud, no mechanic is just a gimmick, and sewing it all together while you play basically turns you into a chainsaw tornado that ♥♥♥♥♥ out bullets, fire, missiles, and the blood of your enemies.But to close off this meandering review, I will conclude with a story. I played through episodes 1 and 99% of 2 on the 3rd hardest difficulty. Having not really played FPSs much over the last 10 years, I had become pretty rusty. I was still better than most but just that, firmly above average. I had a pretty easy time for most of the game, just chainsawing through everything for regen, then brute forcing anything that I couldn't just instantly decapitate with a chainsaw dive. Pretty much only died when I did stupid ♥♥♥♥ like chainsawing into explosives.Then... something strange happened.I hit the boss for the end of Episode 2 and I was just getting annihilated. I was timing my dodges, trying to strafe as well as I could, but it was an uphill slog during the first 2 or 3 phases of the fight. I was being forced to "get gud". The more I started to weave the movement techs together; the double jump, chainsaw slide, dash, and grapple hook. The more I started to succeed. But on the 4th phases I just hit the wall. Up to that point, I was timing things, as you would for a boss fight. I was doing what the last 10 years of shooters had trained me to do, and I was losing.Then I had an epiphany: why am I timing things? How fast can I actually move?Everything changed. I started weaving grapples onto the boss for speed and ending with the saw to carry the momentum, only ending the slide to merely change direction, boosting my speed back up with the dash. If you're running during combat you're playing the game wrong =p. It felt like I changed from a dude with a chainsaw leg to a chainsaw leg with a dude passenger. If you don't feel like a racecar with chainsaw wheels, you're doing something wrong. I became ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ untouchable. The tables completely flipped, and I trounced the boss no problem, like they were an ant to my chainsaw'd shoe. Continuing through the game I realized I was playing significantly better, not just movement tech but everything in general. It was like I'd Ascended.That bossfight forced me to understand the mechanics, gave me a challenge I actually wanted to overcome, and in return, my rust is gone. For the first time in years I was thrilled to play an FPS. I love it, I feel revitalized. I feel a sense of joy in the genre that I've not felt in a decade. Actually new mechanics. Actually new game tech. Not just new executions of old features, actually NEW THINGS. There will be more than the current 3 episodes, and I for one cannot wait for more. As a single player experience, this game stands tall above it's contemporaries. Well worth your money, sale or not. A truly refreshing experience I won't forget, and will continue to play for years to come.
