_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely underrated, great game. I went in expecting just another average boomer shooter but it really develops past expectations as the game progresses in pretty much every element.Starting off with the most core mechanic of boomer shooters: the shooting. It stays true to the tried and true method of no aiming down sites, no reloads, satisfying gibbing animations, and extremely fast weapon swapping. The arsenal in this game starts off basic (pistol, shotgun, assault rifle) and then evolves to include incredibly novel weapons (orbital laser, a rifle that telefrags enemies) that standout even in a genre saturated with great gun ideas. Additionally, upgrades are well thought out and all the aforementioned basic weapon archetypes become something WAY more. They never become stale to use. Secondly, movement in this game is very fluid and familiar. Accelerate or stop on a dime as you skate past enemies delivering your preferred brand of death. It doesn't try to reinvent the wheel in movement tech but I much prefer it that way. Sliding, dashing, double jump are industry standards and it does a good job of adding a gimmick to also make them lethal. Then we have story. Most stories are pretty minimalistic or basic in this category. But while basic, T.O.'s story is so over the top that it stands above most others. The cutscenes were way more enjoyable than they had any right or need to be, and the characters actually intriguing with a personality that places them beyond being just another voice or target.Coupled with a great story, we have incredible, lengthy level designs. There are some absolutely gorgeous sets that hit the requisite cyberpunk theme, but also some truly awesome set designs. One in particular for me was fighting in flowing traffic on top of flying vehicles backlit by the glow of a neon city, and then boarding a moving train to fight on, in and under it, to finally disembarking and continuing at a station.  Lastly we have the gimmicks. It's not enough for games nowadays to just have guns and sprawling levels. T.O. decided to take the route of making movement in this game deadly and at higher levels, a necessary weapon. But it only adds to the fluidity of the game if properly used. There are also numerous body upgrades you can swap out that, while not drastically changing your playstyle, will add to it in satisfying and noticeable ways. The final important gimmick to mention is a favorite of mine: bullet time. I'll just add that I'm happy they included it so you can see your destruction in glorious slow-mo while also providing a brief respite amidst combat chaos.As a final note, I have to say that the demo truly does not do this game justice. I tried the demo and was on the fence of purchasing this until it went on sale as it felt like another average boomer shooter. The demo only superficially demonstrates the core game mechanics loop and fails to elaborate on all the wondrous points above since it's a demo. If you're looking for a game that's not so supremely complex like Ultrakill but hits that quake-like / doom feel of fluid combat, this won't disappoint. Hope this game somehow hits it big and the devs add more onto it, but right now it seems very underrated as a sleeper hit.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 game.  It's extremely fast paced, lots of guns, lots of ammo, lots of interesting enemies (which is a massive point in and of itself), and fun maps.There's a dodge, a fast paced slide, a grapple, a double jump, some wall slides, teleports, options for wall grabs, the list goes on.  The combat is fast paced, guns have alternate fires, and I found myself using almost every gun in most situations.  The enemy designs are all well done and it's nice to see some really new kinds of enemies that aren't just the stock standard.  Story is fine, too.  Music is phenomenal and map design is fantastic.I played on No Pain No Gain.I think there's only three points I'd dock it for:1. There's just too much money.  I'd bought every upgrade and gun type way before the end of the game.2. There's too much ammo.  I was frequently maxed out on just about everything.3. The difficulty for the first 2/3 of the game is very easy.  Like, way too easy.  Then it ramps up really fast and gets really hard.  The final stretch of the game was super hard in places (in generally a good way!).  I just wish the whole game had been more difficult.  Not sure I'm a fan of the final two bosses either as I was mostly just getting killed from one-shots.I still whole heavily recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Old school FPS in a cyberpunk world. Wall running, jump pad, car shooting, chainsaw slides... Great game!Turbo Overkill set a high standard retro FPS should be. If you are familiar with classic 90s FPS you won't find this game a stranger. Game offers regular firearms from pistol to dual machine gun to rocket launcher, and part of the player character's body for melee weapons, a chainsaw on the biotic leg is extremely convenient, slide to use it and the faster you run the more damage it does. In each level there are vendor machines for ammo and upgrades, similar to Cyberpunk 2077 you can insert chips to each limb for boosts. My favorite is to gain 6HP for every enemy you kill by the chainsaw, this quickly turned the game into a racing game. There are more chip options like extra wall jump, higher damage, but when I finish the game I do not find chips for head and left arm, maybe more for future development. Like the Doom games, hidden collectables (tapes and chips) scatter everywhere, well hidden and fun to find. It is said to find all to unlock secret levels, I haven't done that yet but would love to in the 2nd run. Colored keys for colored doors, but with no map  offered and no way point occasionally I lost my way, a way point is given only when you are on the right path sometimes. Each level contains a relatively big map with many floors, players will revisit places so it can be confusing. I only assume enter a place with prawn enemies is the right way.Level design is great. Map is complicated and allows the player to explore almost everywhere. It is nice, I feel like I'm off the map some time but eventually know it is supposed to be this way, players are given more freedom to move around in combat.5 difficulties and I choose the 3rd - Hard mode. I play FPS often and know what to expect, I read it gives enemies x1.3 speed and x1.5 damage output, after beating the game this is exactly the challenge I want and not too overwhelming. A bit hard at the beginning but once you know the game it is fun - keep moving and dodge bullets, control your position in the air!Another thing worth mentioning is the action part. Double jump + up to 2 wall jumps +dash + ladder grabbing turns this FPS into a challenging ACT game. I LOVE games to test my controls of jumps and landing, this game is so right for me. In two maps I do long and precise jumps (one in the chamber with chainsaws and the other one on top of cars next to a moving train) so challenging I thought I was on the wrong path. So rewarding just to beat the level.I finished in 7 hours, I cannot wait for future levels, card drop and achievements. 10/10 recommend at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best new releases I have played in quite a while. Highly recommended for fans of games like the recent Doom games and other boomer shooters. The presentation is impeccable with cohesive art direction and level design, a thumpin EDM soundtrack, a huge variety of satisfying weapons, and a simple yet surprisingly fleshed-out narrative. It starts out a little slow at first, but this was the right choice as the drip feed of new mechanics and abilities stays intriguing throughout the runtime of the game. Some of the weapons/abilities seem totally unique to this game, which really helps to make it stand out and feel fresh. Also, the game runs like a dream. I've experienced zero bugs, minimal frame drops, and there's plenty of settings to tweak to your liking. Really happy that Apogee published this, a worthy addition to their line up of classic FPS games. Please buy this! It's a bargain even at full price, and I hope that the success of this single-player feature-rich experience goes on to influence Apogee's future projects as well other studios to make more incredible "AA" type games.

_childDocuments_.review: Heartily recommend this one. I didn't feel so at the beginning, it starts off pretty slow in a generic cyberpunk theme that I didn't really care too much for. It did have memorable levels and the gameplay was alright enough to keep going. However Episode 2 is where the game really comes together, the difference with the previous episode is like night and day. By this point the gameplay starts to be quite similar to nu-Doom (think lots of fast-paced fights in arenas with tons of movement options and plenty of verticality). Might not be for everyone but I loved it. Some amazing songs in the soundtrack start to pop up as well. I did see high praises for its pacing, I don't know if I really see it that way as it is *mostly* arena fights for the remainder of the game, with the occasional (well done!) vehicle section. But I can't complain.I think towards the middle of Episode 3 the game starts to run out of steam a little bit. It does manage to have bombastic set pieces in this episode but the gameplay loop itself stops throwing new elements in the mix by this point. It is compensated by a terrific penultimate level priming you for the final battles to come.FPS fans and certainly those who liked Doom 2016 or Eternal will not be disappointed.

Collectibles are rewarding to explore for and are generally easy to find. Huge replay-ability, one unlockable secret level per story level, co-op, wave survival game modes, and custom community maps through the workshop. Cannot recommend enough.Oh and Johnny Turbo? Yeah, that guy ♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a masterclass in design. I bought it when it had just came out and already thought that the first epsiode was insanely good for what I paid for it. Once I finished it I stopped playing since the endless mode wasn't yet implemented and re-running the same levels over and over is just not my cup of tea. Once I came back to the game when episode two released, I was mesmerized by it's sheer size and amaount of content that it has within. The recent release of the first part of episode three just goeas to add to the experience.The levels are decently sized (at least for me) taking on average around 27 minutes to beat. There's a lot of them and it really feels like every level adds something new, be it a new weapon, new enemy or a vehicle you have to use.The weapons are great, they all look increduble, the sound design is punchy and crisp and they feel like true powerhouses. No weapon gets outclassed by any other, you will be using your first weapon at the biginning of the game just as you will at the end of it, no weapon is useless. But if that was all, they wouldn't be as insane as they are, since all weapons have upgrades you can buy for them, turning them from really good to incredibly good.The enemies are all pretty challenging and fun to fight against. There's a wide variety of sizes, attacks and health pools. Some can be destroyed very quickly if you have the correct weapon on hand, but the chainsaw leg is always useful on all of them.All in all, this is a definite buy. I think that the lads at Trigger Happy Interactive outdid them selves with this game, and truly created something truly worthy of my hard-earned cash.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - I feel this game is overall, objectively, better than Doom Eternal with some caveats, those being music and graphics for obvious reasons. I think this game deserves to stand proud just behind the three greats boomer shooters that started this whole revival of Dusk, Amid Evil and Ion Fury.This is a modern game in a retro inspired shell. It owns it and while using modern graphical techniques, the retro-tag lets it focus on gameplay and level design instead of spending loads of money for them textures. Story is one of the reasons I compare it to Doom Eternal, with the difference that unlike Eternal, the story and characters are campy and cheesy from the beginning in a Duke Nuke'm 3D kind of way without murdering the main characters origin like Eternal did with the 'Doomguy' after the great 2016 reboot.Levels are great, fun to navigate and jump around and break. Movement only helps, it is incredibly smooth and fast paced. You start with two dashes and a double jump, and it only gets better. Each level has secret secrets, less secret secrets for plot and world building, and some collectables for side grades. I'm bad at finding them so I guess I can only say they were hidden pretty well.The OST is great, starts cyberpunky and keeps the pace throughout the game. Can't say much than that really. It's not Andrew Hulshult like we're used to from almost every single other boomer shooter out there, but it does the job well and fits the game very much.The way the Acts change the scope and type of story the game shows and tells is also great (though I do wish the second and third act would go into a bit of a horror theme for story reasons)Guns I felt were a bit of a mixed bag for me. They all felt good bar the missile launcher (it needs a big boom oomph sound when rockets explode I think) but didn't feel like one is much better than the other, with some actually feeling weaker, like the double barrel, with its incredibly long reload time and weaker enemies taking more than 1 shot to kill. Alt-fire and weapon upgrades on the other hand was satisfactory, and even allowed me to fight the final boss with the starting pistols for efficiency, actually!That said, augments are neat though I don't think there's enough of them to actually let you pick anything but the most obvious ones (healing, jumping, damage). In short I think they do not change up the gameplay enough.The biggest negative for me was the silent protagonist (Jon St. John is great, but I felt he was underused for only voicing the AI companion because it was only scriptet) and you do need one-liners for this type of game. Other thing were enemies - they were alright in design and such but barely made a sound, I had the game sound cranked at 10 for all of the options, and I barely heard a grunt or a moan from them, felt a bit dissatisfying in fact.The last thing I found was the difficulty  playing on hard for the first try - I found the game to be very hard, with dying only once or twice to the final boss due to not paying attention after my reflexes went to bed. Slide is incredibly powerful, and with the healing augment I never really needed to look for slightly hidden armor or health pickups at all. Just slide into the conveniently placed onehit trash mobs. Can't say it isn't satisfying though.All in all, this is a great game worth its price and time to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally do reviews, but Turbo Overkill has been on my radar for a while, so I'm happy to give a short review after 90 minutes of play (so far, anyway, I expect to get plenty of replay value).So, Turbo Overkill. You can pretty much gather the visual style from the trailer, and the gameplay - a retro inspired completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mental shooter. If you liked the Doom games (either the early versions, or the 2016 Doom/Ethernal new versions, you'll love this. Quake? Ditto. Unreal Tournament? Also ditto (although there's no multiplayer). Combat is fast, furious, and filled with gibs.It does remind me of Strafe, another similar shooter that came out a few years back. And I will heartily reccomend both.My only (teeny tiny) criticism is that it would be nice to be able to view the settings and options before being kicked into the game. The music, the visuals, it's obvious a ton of effort has been put into this. You'll see snippets of inspiration from other games, plenty of collectables, plenty of replay value and lots of secrets to discover. And hey, there's a Demo, which you don't see often these days. Give it a shot, what have you got to lose?
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: While Turbo Overkill has retro-inspired aesthetics, I'd compare it most directly to Doom Eternal in terms of gameplay. The ballet of both combat and movement abilities, switching between different weapons, using melee takedowns to recover health, armor, and ammo, and using environmental interactivity to get around the combat arenas works beautifully. Unlike Doom Eternal, fights aren't as prescriptive and there's plenty of room to approach them in your own way. The graphics are beautiful and sound design and music are top notch, the game runs well and I encountered very few bugs and glitches in my platythrough.If there's one criticism I would have it's that like it's id inspiration, some levels overstay their welcome a bit. Overall though, this is a strong recommendation and top contender for my game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an action packed adrenaline rush. I've been following it since it's early days and the way this game has evolved has blown me away. The amount of variety the combat provides via weapons, utilities, and environment makes every encounter heartpounding. Combine that with the aggressive synth soundtrack and you've got a bombastic experience. The story is largely just a framework to hang the amazing set pieces and colourful enemy designs at you, but this isn't the type of game where you focus on the story or characters much (although you and your AI have some nice moments even if you're a silent protag).I would say my biggest criticism is the rooftop vehicle levels. While I applaud experimentation and even enjoy the other vehicle level on the cycle, the rooftops felt a bit slow disjointed and is probably the only time I really got lost in the game for an extended period. I don't like offering criticism without suggestions, but I'm not too sure what to say. I love exploration but this section didn't really feel like it rewarded it. I'd say maybe make that section on rails (have the AI drive the car while you shoot) or put some notable stuff around the map for straying off path. Granted I may have missed what might have already been there which if so that's on me. But if you love FPS and intense action you must give this one a chance, the first two acts are incredible and I eagerly await the remaining epsiodes!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like (2016) Doom and Doom Eternal, you will love this game. Combat has that same feel of managing your weapons (ammo and which is most suitable for a target) and managing your risk with distance. Distance management comes in two parts like Doom, the first being that some weapons are better at close-range while others are longer-range. The second part is replacing Doom's glory-kill system with a chainsaw leg which allows you to slide through enemies to deal damage.Upgrades are pretty good for weapons and you as you can feel the difference as your body has limited slots for personal mods, making your choices have an impact. The level designs are also very clear and each episode is unique. My only real disappointment would have to be that by the time I reached halfway through the last episode (Episode 3) I had run out of things to buy with all my money. This is a bit of my own fault as I used a mod to collect all money when they drop and another to make things cheaper as soon as I could. I believe the upgrades and mods would likely have been paced adequately otherwise. Great pacing and doesn't take itself too seriously while still having a solid identity and themes. Very nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Great shooter with super smooth movement and tight controls, has some similarities with Doom Eternal which is a  compliment. Weapon variety is also excellent although I did settle on a few that I used the most by the end. Ran very well most of the time.Couple of drawbacks were the occasional navigation issues which required a video to find the next area as there's no marker and the path was very well hidden which was annoying. Additionally, on the last level a couple of times I came across a progression bug where after killing all the enemies in a room the next event did not trigger. The level had to be re-started only for it to happen again at a different section. It eventually worked by not dying on the last level as it seems to happen on a reload.Overall a great fun shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: if you're looking for a good boomer shooter this is it. turbo overkill is a ridiculously unhinged blood-and-guts romp that keeps you playing. it’s not perfect by any stretch of the word, but it shines where it counts and at least seems aware of its flaws to some extent. absolutely pick it up if you’re interested at all.with that being said, i have opinions about this game.i think my biggest gripe with this game by far is its balancing. you're given ten whole-ass weapons (on top of your chainsaw leg), each with their own alt-fires and upgrades and techs. this, on the surface, sounds dope as ♥♥♥♥; you're never strapped for options in any fight and you get a wide variety of tools at your disposal. the problem with this is that of the ten the game gave me, i only really used three.the chainsaw leg is too good. it's a no-cooldown, momentum-building behemoth of a weapon that just melts crowds of squishies. this is exacerbated by the upgrade system, which allows you to double its damage as well as gain health + armor for each kill you get with it. this, in effect, almost completely invalidates half of the weapons in the game. assuming your double damage leg isn't enough to take on stronger enemies on its own, the sawed-off shotgun cleans them up instantly. you're able to become this disgusting vampiric semitruck that just bulldozes through levels, and it doesn't take long for you to reach this point. that's not even counting the late-game chainsaw arms, which (while fulfilling my chainsaw man power fantasy), only further reward this playstyle, giving you another semitruck option fuelled by... kills with the chainsaw leg.on the one hand, this is cool. it feels awesome tearing through clouds of enemies, the chainsaw leg making that satisfying "bzzzzt" sound every time. on the other hand, though, this rends the game a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cakewalk, and so many awesome weapons are just completely invalidated by this strategy. the telefragger is a sniper rifle which, when charged, teleports you to your enemy and telefrags them. that's . however, excluding some options where the map design forces you to use it, i never got much use out of it. it's got an enormous windup, you have to stay still to charge it, and it only kills one enemy. i could get the same result by just grappling to the enemy and pressing ctrl. there are tons of guns that fall into this trap: plasma cannons that allow you to catch mid-air projectiles, flamethrower chainguns, . all overshadowed by a shotgun and a leg.the pistols are a really pleasant exception to this, because they actually scale later on in the game. you get a powerup in the second act which reworks them entirely: should you hit ten or so consecutive shots in a row, your pistols become supercharged and deal thousands of damage per shot, the effect only wearing off once you miss or switch weapons. this, coupled with the bullet time upgrade you get later on, is actually comparable to shotgun-chainsawing, and encourages you to switch up your strategy. it was a new and exciting way to play, instead massively rewarding consecutive single-shot accuracy as opposed to raw speed and manoeuvrability.i wish the other weapons had reworks like this. unique mechanics that gave you huge rewards for switching up your playstyle, encouraging you to switch weapons even if you're not out of shotgun ammo. as it stands, however, i have yet to find a practical application of the plasma cannon. i think this game would really benefit from a style meter. you don't have to go full ULTRAKILL, but an incentive to switch weapons/playstyles beyond a self-imposed handicap would be nice.and before you tell me to just play on murder machine, i did! this game's approach to difficulty, however, doesn't change my criticisms one bit. i found myself still being rewarded for chainsaw-shotgunning, the only difference being i would occasionally get one-shot by one specific type of enemy (who would have one-shotted me regardless). if anything, higher difficulties actually reward this playstyle more; you need to move more quickly, preserve health and armor and deal with squishies before they deal massive damage. the telefragger doesn't exactly sound like a useful weapon there.it's really good and you should get it, but damn i hope there's a balance patch at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a cyberpunk/fantasy first-person shooter game that takes place in a world inspired by classic cyberpunk novels and movies, as well as fantasy classics. Turbo Overkill makes other FPS games look like a joke.The game starts out easy enough as you learn to navigate the world and gun down basic enemies. But Turbo Overkill is not for casual players. Even on the easiest difficulty, it will make you cry for your mommy. Once the game gets going, you’ll be up against multiple enemies at once, sometimes with rockets or lasers. And to make matters worse, there are often even more enemies off-screen firing at you.It’s impossible to fight this kind of onslaught with a regular gun, so you have to get creative in order to survive. Luckily, Turbo Overkill has some seriously cool special weapons that help turn the tide of battle.Among new Indie FPS releases, Turbo Overkill is a welcome blast from the past. Though it may not reinvent the genre, it has enough elements that make it fun and worthwhile. Do you want to ask your grandma what the name “Apogee” means? Then Turbo Overkill might be for you!Overall Rating - 8/10FULL GAMEPLAY WALKTHROUGH PART 1 -

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best "modern retro" FPS games I've played so far. The game is not holding back and gives you all the tools to go completely berserk. Movement is extremely fast and smooth, you're jumping, dashing and zooming through the level, if not slashing through lines of enemies with your chainsaw leg.Levels are nice and varied, ranging from tight corridors to open futuristic cityscapes. Enemies are not that much of a challenge on their own, although there are some tankier ones. It's the arena style battles that can get pretty challenging, where hordes of enemies come at you in different formations.The guns are nice although the double barreled shotgun feels a bit useless compared to the other guns and the rocket launcher is pretty clunky. It generally does not really matter which gun you use, which means you can take every fight the way you want. A little more game design could have been put into that, as in the new Doom games. It's still a lot of fun to wreak havoc with this arsenal.It's clear the developers don't take the game too seriously and want to deliver the most wacky, fun experience they can. I think they succeeded at that.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, after 4 hours, I think I have to throw in the towel on this mostly excellent boomer shooter. It was a good ride.The good:The guns.That brutal slidekick mechanic.The cyberpunk vibe.The dark synth soundtrack.Smooth performance. Will likely run on a potato.Difficulty levels.The meh:The upgrades. A bit stingy, to be honest. It's depressing seeing so many vending machines that allow you to affix upgrades, while getting so few upgrades to actually affix.The precision platforming.  I got stuck bouncing over and over again trying to get to this ledge and then finally I somehow made it! - but then didn't know where to go, made a wrong jump and then couldn't make it again.  After 15 some minutes, of bouncing like an idiot on a launchpad in a section that really shouldn't be that punishing, I called it quits.Also, the levels can be quite large and can sometimes be confusing.The verdict: It's a great homage to shooters of old. But if you don't like very challenging platforming sections, be warned. Even on the easiest difficulty, you'll have to deal with them.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is an absolute masterpiece of a game! From the moment I fired it up, I was greeted with jaw-dropping visuals that pushed the boundaries of what I thought was possible in gaming. The neon-soaked cyberpunk world is a sight to behold, and every corner is filled with intricate details that make it feel alive and vibrant.But it's not just about the visuals; Turbo Overkill delivers on gameplay in spades. The fast-paced, adrenaline-pumping action is a rollercoaster ride of fun. The controls are buttery smooth, allowing for precise movement and jaw-dropping acrobatics as you mow down hordes of enemies with an impressive arsenal of weapons.The level design is top-notch, offering a perfect balance of exploration and intense combat encounters. Each level feels unique and presents new challenges, keeping you on your toes and eager to see what's next. And speaking of challenges, the game's difficulty curve is just right – tough enough to keep you engaged but never frustrating.The character development and story are surprisingly engaging for an action-packed game like this. Turbo Overkill weaves a compelling narrative that adds depth to the world and keeps you invested in the protagonist's journey.The soundtrack is an absolute banger, with a pulse-pounding electronic score that perfectly complements the game's fast-paced action. It's the kind of music that will have you tapping your foot and feeling like a cybernetic killing machine.In summary, Turbo Overkill is a tour de force in the world of gaming. It's a visual spectacle, a gameplay delight, and a must-play for any fan of the cyberpunk genre or action games in general. This game sets a new standard for what we can expect from indie developers, and I can't wait to see what they come up with next. Bravo!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I played, not only of this year, but ever. If you're into Cyberpunk, you love nostalgia and a great shooter, then this is the game for you, period. The story is simple yet fun and engaging enough to make you care about it's world and characters, and the perfect setting for some over-the-top mayhem. It's basically Doom Eternal with a Duke Nukem texture on top, but sum of its parts is so much greater. The combination of old pixelated graphics with modern lighting effect works perfectly. _childDocuments_.review: Even in early access, its one of the better shooters I've played in the last few years. Feels like the perfect blend of boomer shooter and modern, taking from games like Doom Eternal with fast and fluid movement and ultrakill with its pixelated aesthetic. Sick music carries you through all the ultra violence as well, dynamically changing from a more subdued sound during exploration to the heavy beats during combat. Its also hard, even on the normal 'regular joe' difficulty, but not unfairly so. It simply demands that you learn its mechanics and use them to your advantage. 8 base levels make up the chapter currently available, with two more chapters on the way. However, there are secret levels to be unlocked based on the collectibles (tapes) found in each level, for those of you out there who like such things. Other collectibles (chips) unlock modifiers which can be enabled on all other levels, such as one which adds a big head mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo. Chainsaw. Leg.Turbo Overkill is an excellent modern first person shooter. A member of the twitchy shooter club, it is a fast paced game that encourages constant movement and weapon switching, while providing excellent environments where to do so, with an outstanding weapon rooster, and good enemy design (with some caveats here and there).The music is overall excellent! The composition and progression throughout the game is just great, perfectly in tune with the game themes, and pumps you up just right. The music sounds production (that is, the mixing and post production) is also outstanding, making the whole thing very cohesive. The same goes for the sound design; weapons sound are very nicely done, and so are the enemy, environmental, and voices for the most part. I will note that there is some recurring "sound stacking" bugs with coins and some specific sounds (remember BUILD Engine sound stacking bugs? Exactly like that) that do need to be addressed, because they can occasionally hurt :(.The game graphics are also beautiful; the levels themselves are colourful and very detailed, and the backdrops, set pieces and in game cinematics also show a great level of care into making sure that everything is detailed and pretty, but still allowing the player to (mostly) understand what to do and where to go at all times. Fittingly, the level design is amazingly well done; they are giant environments, and even with the usual trope of keys and backtracking, still make for immersive set pieces that flow really well. Your movement options are very versatile and overall quick; sliding (with a side of chainsaw), dashing, multiple jumping, and grapple hook, all of which encourage constant and rapid movement, both of which are 100% required to survive basically all the time. Everything you could want out of a modern FPS is there, and done very well (except for the starting delay of the grapple hook which I just hate ¬¬). It reminded me of ULTRAKILL at some points, but here, the flying around shooting things and looking awesome is done both out of necessity, and just pleasure :P.The weapon rooster is just great; every single type of weapon that was ever done in an FPS is included in it (except for a BFG I guess). You get 10 slots overall, plus extra modes for each which almost gets you 20, and despite the quantity, all are implement solidly. Mostly every type of play is accommodated within it, and while enemies have "weaknesses" that encourage using specific weapons, you can still do your own thing if you want. On that note, the implant upgrade system is nice; it allows to bolster specific skills and movement options, but with limited slots, forcing you to choose specific ones depending on what you favour the most. The enemy design is pretty nice too; graphic wise, all look amazing, and fit a function within battles and overall in the game. Johnny is very much a glass cannon; the game makes it clear that movement is required at all times, but it will occasionally thread over the line of cheapness, rather than challenge, and this is probably my main and only complaint about the game: The cheap instakills. A single enemy can just wreck you with some of their attacks, and the game will repeatedly throw hand fulls of them at you at some points, along with buckets of common enemies. On Streetcleaner difficulty, I counted 3XX damage from a SINGLE attack that left me alive with 4 health from full health and armor (and some seem to do even more than that!), and even lower enemies can just take 1XX health/armor in a single swipe. In all cases, there seems to be some "random" variation of damage; after some out of nowhere deaths that pissed me off, I stopped to probe damage from single enemies, and found that sometimes they would do 20 damage, and sometimes 150, with no clear indication of why. The solution was basically to get good and not get hit at all, but as noted, it felt pretty cheap at some points. I do not want to think how bad this would be on the higher difficulties :(.That said, I do not think this overshadows all the good things the game is and does at all; Turbo Overkill is an outstanding example of a modern day FPS that implements basically everything we have learned about these kinds of games throughout the years, and does so well.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been an avid fan of FPS games ever since we got our first family computer in 1995. Between then and now I've played damn near every shooter worth playing. _childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a well-crafted old-school FPS game with ridiculously complex mechanics that are easy to learn but hard to master. The gameplay mechanics include double-jumping, air-dashing, wall-running, grappling hooks, and of course, the iconic chainsaw slide, whereby you slide across the floor while shredding anyone in your path with the chainsaw built into your prosthetic cyborg leg. And the weapons bring their own unique mechanics too! For example, there's a sniper rifle that kills its target by teleporting you to their exact location, thereby "tele-fragging" them, i.e. blowing them to pieces as you take their place. There are also heat-seeking missiles, a flamethrower, plasma rifle, double-barrelled shotgun, and more, with alternative fire modes too.All of these mechanics would be pointless if you could easily beat the game just by running and gunning. But even the second-hardest difficulty is brutal compared to the average FPS, so the game really forces you to get good, which I appreciated.Overall, I highly recommend this game to fans of "boomer shooters" and fast-paced FPS games with a high difficulty ceiling.

_childDocuments_.review: Wtf is this production value ? I was thought it will be your regular indie boomer shooter, but just wtf.The gameplay is out there with Doom eternal and Ultrakill, a really solid roster of weapon with quickswitching and a lot of movement options (dash, double jump, shotgun jump, rocket jump, wall ride, telefrag, grappling hook...), and the chainsaw slide is really cool and well integrated.The pacing is perfect, new weapons, new mechanics almost every levels, vehicule sections and some very good platforming ??!The set pieces are insane especialy in the final episode.The bosses are fun and varied wich is rare for a FPS.The story is badass and epic and there is some really cool cinematics (like a lot, but short, like in doom eternal) and the voice acting is nice and funny.TLDR, this game really feel like an AAA game (the only give away is the  modernised retro art style wich i dig), this is surely one of the best FPS of all time. _childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Part boom shoot, part character action FPS, this is the cream of the crop of the retro shooter genre. The gang's all here: incidental combat, lock-in arena fights, exquisite level design, an appropriate(ly cheesy) OST, and a story line that gradually matures past the usual drivel over the length of the campaign. You don't  get a super shotgun, you get a super shotgun with a grenade launcher. You don't  get a railgun, you get a railgun that can telefrag people on command. And most importantly you don't  get a chainsaw, you get a chainsaw for each limb. Turbo Overkill lives up to its name for better and worse. It's balls to the wall action from start to finish, but the finish line is about an hour or two past where it needs to be. Even so, it is well worth your time and money. You'd be doing a disservice to yourself as an FPS fan if you don't play this.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat of this game hits the heights of DOOM Eternal at times, trying to refill ammo/armor through different attacks is especially fun with the chainsaw leg. There are some bugs however, enemies can hit you through certain walls, and certain floor effects (poison, fire, etc.) seem to hit you even if you're a short distance above the ground. Either way it's an easy recommendation from me.

THEY HAVE ME PILOTING A MECH IN CHAPTER THREE THIS GAME IS SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ COOL ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!!!The spectacle completely changed by the end of it, and I went from fighting mega corporations to fighting gods, and THAT is a spectacle worth paying for!!! _childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, after two previous reviews that were "I want to recommend, but can't yet", I'm happy to say I can finally give Turbo Overkill a big fat . The chainsaw leg works the way it should again. Problems with checkpointing seem to be fixed. Navigating the levels isn't a pain anymore. And fights are properly fun again instead of just a grind.The gunplay is great, the music is fantastic (special mention to Sunset Synthetica which somehow mixes Djent, Electronica, and  of all things) and the story is the good kind of wallpaper that simply gives you motivation to flying-chainsaw-kick cybermonsters in the face. Levels have a lot of cool gameplay setpieces and interesting visuals. Augments let you lean into gameplay styles, and of course I mostly went with chainsaw buffs. Many points in the game also go extremely hard into bodyhorror and existential/cosmic horror, which I'm a fan of and here it's done pretty well, I'd say even better than INCISION did.My only negatives are personal taste:Gianni Matragrano is now on the same tier as Steve Blum or Tara Strong where I'm tired of him being in  lately, and without spoiling, you will hear him talk A LOT in the second half of Turbo Overkill.Also, the audio logs don't really contribute much to the story. I don't even know who some of the characters are because they never appear in the gameplay or cutscenes, and I know at least one non-character is just some youtuber I've never heard of. That being said, you  just skip them.Those two very subjective complaints aside, I'm glad to consider Turbo Overkill to now be one of those "must buy" boomer shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me in so many ways. A genuinely good, high paced retro shooter with great weapon feedback, great retro visuals and some dizzying level design. _childDocuments_.review: As of right now unfortunately i cannot recommend this game. World is really beautiful, killing enemies and overall gameplay feels satisfying but there are 2 glaring issues that made the game a pain to go through. First and the most important one is the game has no invincibility frames when you get hit. This wouldn't have been a major problem if there wasn't this many projectiles at all times coming at you. You can literally be at full hp and in just a blink of an eye, you are dead. Worst thing about it is, most of the time you can't tell that you are getting hit until its too late. I got annoyed by this a lot especially because i chose the average difficulty. The game isn't hard to be honest, it is just unfair. Second issue is, you will get lost quite a lot. There are mostly no indicators pointing where you should go. Again this wouldn't be a problem if the maps weren't quite big and confusing. I have spent a quarter of my time playing this game searching where to go.There are also some minor issues such as some bugs, some weapons and upgrades being useless or too gimmicky.The game is still in early access which means that the issues i have stated can be fixed/improved. I will keep an eye on Turbo Overkill and play the upcoming updates and see what comes out of it. I really want it to turn out good because underneath the issues, it has a massive potential to be a great game. Sadly at the time of my review, it's not worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal done right masquerading as a boomer-shooter.Fast paced combat, fun and coherent implementation of pretty much every major shooter mechanic out there (grappling hook, double jump, alternative fire modes that are more effective against certain types of enemies, secrets etc.), stunning visuals and awesome soundtrack. Surprisingly engaging but not overbearing story line.Most notably, it manages to walk the fine line between a mindless W+LMB and an overly restrictive weapon specialization.A must buy.

_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended because the game is still in early access. It's fun for the first 5 levels but if this was a full 1.0 release it wouldn't be worth it.I recommend it for the gore blasting fast paced action. 1980's cyberpunk Doom, this game is a load of fun. It doesn't BS you with fancy plot, just get right to the killing. Levels start out simple but increase in complexity pretty fast. Customization isn't much but it's there and each weapon is pretty fun.Biggest downside that annoys me is broken level design and lack of a waypoint system on the later levels. I was exploring every nook and cranny of a level to figure out where I needed to go next, and some areas that you can walk on just suddenly kill you because you are not supposed to be there.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Very mediocre so far.I understand there may be bias due to me being a massive fan of Ultrakill and also enjoying DOOM Eternal quite a bit, or maybe even I set my expectations to high and the disappointment only exacerbated my already negative feelings, but my god is this game boring.This game feels like it should have been perfect for me because it's a culmination of a bunch of ♥♥♥♥ I love, some of which it even delivers; the music and overall aesthetic/world design is amazing. It just feels so bad to play. To clarify, it's not really even that difficult (I play on second hardest diff), but the game doesn't require any creative thinking and there's so little cool/satisfying ♥♥♥♥ to pull off, which is only worsened by how boring the enemies are. No cool interactions or anything, they don't at all compliment each other or the player, it's just "hold m1/ctrl over enemy/group of fodder till they die" and dodge a couple projectiles here and there. None of the guns feel particularly nice to use, audio design is meh, enemy designs are cool ig but nothing striking, couldn't give two ♥♥♥♥♥ about any of the characters or story (not that any of that is super important for me in games like these), movement is cool aside from the pathetic jump, but yeah none of it works for me. This wouldn't be fixed by upping the damage to 7X the regular and getting one shot by everything. It's a fundamental issue with the design of the game.Edit: After finishing the game, my general criticisms remain, especially the issue of the difficulty being between "you won't ever die" and "you will be randomly one-shot from a particle of dust", but the gameplay does get way more dynamic and fun, still not to the standard I'd like but it is undeniably a good time. Other than that all my praises only have rung more and more true; the environments and music is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible, just wish I could give a single ♥♥♥♥ about any of the characters, and that the game didn't take so long to engage me. 7/10.

Decent story (others may care about that more, but for me, I focus on the gameplay, but what I've seen so far has been nice), and secrets that'll make you rummage through each area til you know it like the back of your hand. Stop reading this and play it already! EVEN JUST THE DEMO! JUST GET ON IT!!!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best shooters of 2023, in a year already filled with amazing games.An over-the-top comic-book-like gorefest made by FPS-fans for FPS-fangs.Pros:+ Extremely fast-paced combat in the vein of DOOM 2016+ Very fluid and fun movement mechanics+ Awesome cyberpunk visual style+ Good variety in gameplay with some vehicle sections+ Head-banging soundtrack+ Great over-the-top voice-acting with voice-actors like Jon St. John (Duke Nukem), Gianni Matagranno (Gabriel from Ultrakill), Tay Zonday (Chocolate Rain) and Patricia Summersett (Zelda from Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom).+ A lot of bonus levels and features+ You get to kill Gianni Matragrano multiple times while he trashtalks youCons:- The small flying bug-robots are annoying- The final levels are close to dragging, but fortunately end just before they become too long

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun boomer shooter. If you like Doom Eternal its totally up your alley. Homework borrowed heavily, but if you are going to borrow it, do it right - which Turbo Overkill definitely does.Love the unfiltered textures with modern lighting and depth of field. Has a nice visual sauce to it. Weapons all feel great to use though I was flush with ammo for my favorites so I never really used some of them after a while.The narrative is exactly what you expect, light and unobtrusive but not thought provoking. The setting is varied enough but like many of its peers it leans into the 'hellish monsters of flesh' vibe.My only critique is that at a 13 hour playthrough, I felt it could be a little shorter. Some of the last chapter just went on longer than I'd have liked, particularly in the very last section. But all in I really enjoyed it. It was a fast paced action packed romp that let me turn my brain off and mow through waves of bad guys - which sometimes is all you want!

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe later game gets better, but:The only thing i think about when playing this game is why other games are cool, but this one isn't.Enemies feel like gray blobs, none of them are memorable, and none of them have weaknesses or a special way to deal with them(except drones, but i don't feel like they belong to this game considering that you can't kill them relying only on your movement), all you do is just dodge random projectiles and shoot them with whatever you have ammo for, or just ignore them. After playing Quake, Half-life, Doom 93 and most importantly Ultrakill, this is just not itI have only 6 out of 15 weapons at this point, but even now i don't understand why you need 2 shotguns and 2 full auto guns(smg and lmg) if they're not that much different. _childDocuments_.review: This fast paced FPS with a cyberpunk setting and a unique chainsaw leg slide mechanic piqued my interest immediately but honestly I didn't expect it to be this good.Unlike some games stuck in the Early Access limbo, Trigger Happy seem to be adhering to their very realistic roadmap and their game is shaping up to have a triumphant 1.0 launch. They also deserve praise for being so responsive to feedback. Some people aren't happy with the checkpoint system? Quicksave option in one of the next updates. Some can't spot certain enemies because of the color scheme/artstyle? Enjoy your enemy highlighting option in the accessibility settings. You've conquered the Murder Machine difficulty and your itchy hands need extra challenge? Custom map support and an endless mode with a ton of customization. Go crazy.Can't go wrong with Turbo Overkill if you're a fan of the genre. There's something for every FPS player here from pathological git guds to "every game needs an easy mode" journos and of course everyone in between.

_childDocuments_.review: My first time doing a proper review of a game that I liked a lot... Maybe another boomer shooter for many people, but this is THE boomer shooter, badass character, badass weapons and a freaky chainsaw leg. The gameplay is pretty damn smooth and intuitive, the story is okay nothing crazy. While writing this review I finished the main campaign in the hard difficulty, but I'm going to probably try to beat it in the harderst one with all the unlockables and stuff like that. _childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: There is something really special about this game, the quality and attention to details/weapons/animations/level design/gameplay and music is something I haven't seen since the original Perfect Dark came out, well that's what my initial thoughts were.Runs on the Unity engine, and while the developers have managed to get the best from a difficult engine than most there are some fps issues on the level infestation, it might just be limited to my setup or this level but then MSI AfterBurner showed no bottlenecks, with only 4 cores really doing most of the work below 50% and the others around 20%, GPU 59% usage, maybe it's a thread optimization issue.But I have to mention some downsides of the game, it is hugely dragged out at the end (unfortunately they didn't know when to stop), add to that the difficultly ramps right up despite changing the it's level, also they take away the quick save system leaving you to repeat sections over and over till you want to pull your hair out, they do add it back later for a bit but then you are on a timer to kill waves of enemies (they also take the quick save away again) while trying to navigate which way to go, the end boss fight feels like it never ends along with what comes after it.Anyhow at the start  when it's doing things good it's Just that magical (also earlier levels are shorter which is good, they feel better than the massive longer ones) feeling you get from very few games, but with endless bugs after release and the way they chose to do the last two awful tedious levels/boss fights really is sour to the point I got to the last terminal and just gave up (as If the MAW battles weren't enough) after what seemed like endless retries of trying to do it on time and falling with the grapple hook or missing with the sniper shots while the timer runs out, then having to do it all over again, this is not fun and IMO not what fun gaming is about but more about frustrating the player to the point of hating/forgetting what was good about the game to begin with.Despite the bugs I recommend the first two episodes as there is still some fun to be had but I do not recommend episode 3, as a full game I do not recommend so maybe get in a sale and skip the last episode to save yourself endless frustration and annoyance.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Fast paced shooter with arsenal of a bunch of modern mechanics: slowtime, hook, dashes, many weapons with alternative firemodes, passive augments and of course sliding with chainsaw! Pretty long campaign, nice music, extremly good movement, decent amount of bosses, all weapons usefull. As a minus, I will note the excessively high damage to the player of some opponents on higher difficulties. Its like u fully hp plus armor and then boom and u with ~ 20 hp left.100% recomendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: An insanely well-done boomer/movement shooter. You can tell that a lot of passion went into this game. From the self-aware humor to the over-the-top crazy weapons and mechanics, this is a game that absolutely maximizes fun. Just when you think this game can't get any crazier, it does, and beautifully so. I enjoyed every second of the campaign, and the endless mode and arcade mode add a ton of replay value. Plus, cherry on top, there's a co-op mode. This game is literally everything I could ask for.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Play as Johnny Turbo and saw, grind, blast your enemies to hell as you battle the evil AI bent on dominating this cyberpunk dystopia. Turbo Overkill has creative level design, creative gunplay, and creative visuals that all mesh together to make a great game. You have CHAINSAWS on your LEGS!The level design is awesome, the game keeps introducing new features, combinations, or layouts to keep things fresh. On some levels you get level-unique vehicles such as hover cars or motorbikes. The boss fights are great, they are engaging but never unfair. I love the use of leitmotif in the game. The music is great, fits the theme and augments the brutal gameplay.The progression is also great, with new weapons and tools being introduced to you throughout the game, as well as upgrades for existing weapons. The weapons are creative too, your starting pistols lock on to and splatter groups of enemies, your first shotgun can launch an electric stun blast, a gun can call in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ orbital strike laser, and you get a sniper rifle that telefrags enemies.There is a plethora of creative upgrades that you can customise to fit your playstyle. Some can even change your playstyle alltogether. I was very happy late in the game when I got an upgrade that allowed near-instant weapon quickswapping for some nasty combos (however it may be a liiiiittle overpowered in that it allowed me to ♥♥♥♥ out rockets at a faster rate than a chaingun, but who cares it's a blast)The story is pretty simple. I didn't expect to like it, but I actually enjoyed it quite a lot. Each level starts with a cutscene that characterises the crazy badass that is Johnny Turbo. _childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill hits three demographics really damn hard: Quake III fans, 80s action film buffs and cyberpunk fiends. It’s a fast, explosive, loud first person shooter that doesn’t pull any punches and showcases the best retro shooters have to offer while adding a healthy layer of modern game design elements.As Johnny Turbo, you will be wallrunning, double jumping, dashing, gunning, swapping weapons to deal with some ridiculously long recover animations and skating on your chainsaw legs through an ocean of lamp-headed zombies (weirdest sentence you’ve read today, I bet) on your way to defeat your traditional Big Bad of cyberpunk: a rogue A.I. named Syn.Nothing particularly complicated about the overarching narrative: a cyborg kills both street and corporate scum while going after crapshoot toaster in a hi-tech/low people sprawl. The structure of every level is in itself an homage to the Doom structure we all know and love: most levels, you have to collect two different color keys and progress to the next unopened door while occasionally dealing with gauntlets of enemies. The color palette is vivid and neon-drenched, a cold, artificial maze to serve as a backdrop for the rain of gore that fills up the screen during most encounters.Even the overarching structure follows the 90s shareware-type formula: 8-mission episodes that get increasingly more difficult and really test your grasp on the movement and shooting fundamentals you’re gradually introduced to as you gain more tools and power-ups. You can spend the cash you collect from your fallen enemies at talking vending machines (à la Bioshock) and then augment yourself with different modules. You’ll also come across upgrade chests that you have to find the key for. On top of that, every level has three tech chips and cassettes you can collect, the former unlocking gameplay mods you can activate, to varying degrees of utility (and some punishing effects).The guns you find are also more or less what you’d expect from a classic shooter — nine firearms, each with their own special alternate attack. Knowing what to use against which enemy will be critical to surviving the more difficult levels in the second and third episode, where tight-spaced gauntlet events don’t give you a lot of room for error — one-punch enemies destroyed me more than i’d like to admit towards the end of the game’s second act. Still, the controls are so responsive, the gameplay so fluid that I can’t in good conscience blame the game for my own shortcomings - rather, I felt rewarded once I finally figured out how to overcome every fight. Classic arena concepts like map control — knowing where to get armor, health, temporary buffs and ammo especially during the third episode when things can get hairy in a split second will make the difference between progress or a loading screen. Jump pads, suspended platforms and the need to always be in motion to avoid death make for a really intense, engaging gameplay experience that really evokes that classic feeling of getting your blood pumping. The mechanic you will probably use to kill most enemies won’t be tied to any firearms, however. Johnny Turbo’s ability to skate on his chainsaw leg can be further enhanced with cybernetic augmentations and has the considerable advantage of instagibbing most basic enemies without expending any ammo. It is useful both for escaping impending death as well as dashing through enemies, and with the right build it can be a reliable source of health and armor (there are multiple Collector-type chips that reward you with a bit of health and armor every time you kill someone while skating into them).It cannot be overstated how eclectic Turbo Overkill’s sources of inspiration are, a philosophy that oozes into the level design itself. The radio chatter references classic lines from Aliens, there’s a clear similarity to Judge Dredd’s “Peach Trees” sector in the “Appletree” section, most of the achievements are named after one-liners, tropes and classic action film titles. There are easter eggs galore, little gems that reward those who are exploration-inclined with nuggets of memberberries. Going through the game and getting all these hyperlinks to other works really enhanced my experience and made the whole thing feel like an homage to what kids today would probably call “boomer media”, but really enables the narrative to take a lot of detours through atypical levels and over-the-top, explosive changes of scenery.You’ll drive a flying car that looks straight out of Blade Runner as you traverse immense gaps between skyscrapers and escape Syn’s Laser Beam Eye on a motorcycle that reminded me of Akira. At one point, you’ll even pilot a mech, and none of these sections feel shoehorned in: there’s always a degree of integration that ties the experience together really well. Killing mercenary bosses gradually unlocks a few really useful upgrades: micro-missiles you can send at multiple targets, an 8 to 12 second bullet time and a grappling hook.Platforming sections, though not many, are pretty fun as they will have you using all of your navigational boosters: you can double jump, double dash, hook onto things, wallrun (a Titanfall 2 flashback ensues) and telefrag enemies with your sniper rifle. Put all of these things together and I anticipate a really fun time for speedrunners and explorers.Special mention to the sound design and especially soundtrack: the track selection is on point, really knows how to create tension and imbue your mass murder ballet with a sense of rhythm. It becomes orchestral during boss fights, swivels into trance during traversal sections and cyberpunk-themed fights, takes industrial undertones when you’re navigating the rust-dominated sewers and frankly is just stellar all around. Once you’re done with the campaign, you can take a shot at the game’s Endless Mode (a survival arena that changes layout every few levels and has a separate upgrade/arsenal progression tree from the main story). I guess if you’re looking for a downside, you have to remember that Turbo Overkill is an indie game and the graphics aren’t exactly current-gen in terms of lighting, model poly count or effects. But the design works so well I frankly didn’t care - there are more creative ideas and decisions in this game than in the vast majority of AAA titles for about half the price. You can tell that Turbo Overkill is the result of labor done with love, the kind of shine that can’t be bought with piles of money and focus group checklists.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun and polished for a fast paced shooter.On the technical side, the game ran well and I encountered very few bugs: in a few cases I got stuck in the level geometry, but then a failsafe teleported me back to a safe spot after a few seconds, and in another case I got softlocked by a broken level trigger but reloading the last checkpoint fixed it.All the weapons are fairly useful and interesting, and they can be combined in creative ways instead of the extremely boring "use A on B" seen in Doom Eternal.Enemy variety is pretty good, even the lowest tiers are different enough to require a bit of attention.The levels also aren't bad, but you have so much mobility that it's easy to sequence break by accident and in some cases skip past large chunks of them.Secrets aren't terrible, no wall humping required in this game, but given the sheer size of most levels they can be pretty tedious to find even when no attempt is made to hide them: in some cases, the opposite is true and you'll just walk into a "secret" by looking to your side as you follow the intended path.Difficulty is odd: I was playing on Street Cleaner (the middle of the 5 difficulty levels), and around the halfway point the game went from "very easy" to "very hard", with plenty of attacks dealing 300+ damage when the most you can stack is 200 health and 200 armor.At least, the augments you collect in-game and the mutators you unlock by finding secrets offer plenty of ways to fine-tune the difficulty level: for example, you can enable infinite ammo and instagib to breeze through even the hardest difficulty, or disable all weapons but your chainsaw leg and triple enemy spawns to turn even the easiest difficulty into a bit of a challenge.Finally, there's a level editor and that's always nice.Worth playing, even at full price.

For that type of gameplay, the game excels and you are able to effectively survive as long as you are taking advantage of what you have. The game is a bit longer than it maybe needed to be as it does get repetitive in parts, with no new challenges being introduced to help keep it interesting, but I can't fault it too much for giving more of a good thing. _childDocuments_.review: I have slowly played this game over the last few months, playing a few levels then taking a break just to keep it fresh. I was enjoying it a lot until Chapter 3. The gameplay itself is wonderful, good movement, forgiving platforming and solid shooting. Your compatrion S.A.M.M. is solid, and the ultimate evil is decent. The reason why this isn't a positive review is simply off of the ending of the game. The last 2 levels are simply just a test of how long you can hold down your finger on a trigger and avoid damage. You have to kill the second to the last boss in 3 separate rooms, the first two times you have to drain his health bar 5 separate times, followed by a tank version at the end with a massive health bar. While just shooting a boss and dodging bullets would be a fair fight, you end up having wave, after wave of enemies to deal with before you can deal more damage to the boss. The final boss is worse, there is no health bar, you are perpetually swarmed by enemies, and this is after you have had a 4 timed arenas that are incredibly obnoxious and laid out poorly. I attempted the final boss many times before I gave up after the transformation. This game had so much potential, and turned into simply a button mashing bullet hell, almost as if the devs ran out of solid ideas to finish the game. I doubt I will go back and try and finish the final boss again, it was annoying and frustrating just to get there, and to continue to reset at the beginning of the fight, after the previous boss would allow you to reset whenever he lost a health bar is brutal. Sometimes, you can finish a shooting game without it being abusive to the player with how much they have to do to simply finish it. What is the point of selecting difficulty levels when the end of the game is just a slog to kill everyone and spend an eternity fighting bosses without health bars?

_childDocuments_.review: The gist: One hell of a wild ride, but not without some problems.The pros:-The presentation is one of the best I've seen in a shooter. Bright, popping colors, an absolutely killer soundtrack, and some breathtaking setpieces and cutscenes make it a treat to watch.-The game loves to one-up itself again and again with the upgrades. Your killsat gun turns into a nuke. Your shotgun turns into a long-range sniper rifle. You go from one chainsaw leg, to having every single limb be chainsaws. Even your pistols turn into damage-dealing monsters that work great with the bullet time powerup.-The vehicles (for the handful of segments they're used) feel genuinely powerful rather than a forced gimping, usually with powerful machineguns, regenerating health, and a very strong secondary weapon on a rather short cooldown.-Most boomshoots have one or two secret levels for every batch of levels. Turbo Overkill has a secret level for EVERY level, giving you a lot to do even without specific completion points.-The voice work is stellar, barring maybe the Teratek Executive getting rather grating.-Johnny is already a highly mobile character at the start, with a fast running speed, dashes, a fast slide-kick, and double jumps. But by the end game, you'll have more movement options than you know what to do with.-The skill ceiling for how the weapons and movement pair together is absolutely insane.-E2M8.The cons:-The weapon balance gets kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the endgame. The chainsaw gets so powerful you're gimping yourself by actually shooting anything less than a Leaper, and the single assault rifle is insanely powerful for how plain it is - accurate at longer ranges, lots of damage per shot, and a ton of ammo basically makes the plasma gun obsolete. (It doesn't help that I couldn't seem to figure out how to get the projectile catcher to work - skill issue on my part?)-Levels are long, especially if you're going for completion. For most of the game it's negligible thanks to the wonderful set design and movement, but episode 3's levels in particular can be real slugfests with waves upon waves of spongy enemies; and the later levels have enemy counts that push towards 1,000. It feels less like a test of skill and mastery, and more a test of endurance.-E3M7.The overall package is wonderful enough for me to recommend it, and I consider it an S-tier boomshoot up there with the likes of Dusk for its energy, presentation, and its total embrace of over-the-top carnage that a game called "Turbo Overkill" ought to deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the core design, Turbo Overkill is one of the greatest FPS ever made. It's design, weapon roster, movement, world ; it's all so immensely fantastic and creative and well made. Aside from the Uzi after it's level 3 upgrade  (seriously, I preferred it at level 2. WTF) and the entirety of the plasma gun, I used every single weapon frequently depending on the situation. The upgrades push weapons in and out of viability too in cool ways ; upgrading the shotguns was such a fun moment, pushing them from very underwhelming to extremely fun and powerful.   Unfortunately, and it pains me to say this, a lot of small blemishes knock the game down from new genre titan, to just a very good fps. The game lagged very inconsistently ; in some areas I was on max graphics without a hiccup, and in others the game chugged at minimum graphics. I also got stuck in geometry more than a few times, and tutorial popups and the recharge notification for the chainsaw arms would often just... not happen.Money is very oddly balanced. I played on the middle difficulty, Street Cleaner, which turns off buying ammo and health in shops. So I just consistently had WAY more money than I could possibly use. I bought almost every upgrade as soon as it became available with money leftover. Even cutting zen gain to 2/3 would make the process of saving up for upgrades way more fun. The damage attacks do feels very lopsided. At max health and armour, I could take dozens of bullets, or two enemy rockets. Frequently against big enemies my health would jump from full to near dead in a single hit, and the game's feedback on these attacks wasn't strong enough for me to generally figure out what I could've done differently. The Sloths, Technopedes, Rammers and Teddies were some of the worst offenders. And there were a lot of small things where I just went "HUH?" Like how single armour fragments don't charge you above 100 armour, but single health point vials do ; and how easily I voided out when looking for collectables or hit an invisible wall in the car stages. The game is lacking polish in a lot of small ways. Despite all that, I still wholeheartedly recommend TO. The movement and guns are joyous, and the story was a blast to see. I hope trigger happy games consider patching some of the game's issues, so I can update this review to read "Chegg. Charms. Chenis. Game of the year"

Syn, is eventually planning to corrupt all that's left of the earth. It's the ordinary "save the world" kinda deal but it's presented in an interesting way and doesn't get in your face most of the time.While on the topic of story, may I add, the voice acting is actually AAA quality, I was surprised by it.On the gameplay side, yeah, it's pretty much all you could ask for. Fast movement, fast weapon switching, all that goodness. Let's address the elephant in the room first though.The CHAINSAW LEG. If the concept of that alone doesn't get you sold on the game, then don't worry, this ISN'T even the best part.You can use your slide to shred through enemies as a melee move, which gives you an enourmous boost in speed, and the faster you go, the more damage you deal. This move ALONE is SO. MUCH. FUN. You essentially gain an extra dash while in air, allowing you to DROPKICK the enemies with it. I REPEAT, YOU CAN DROPKICK PEOPLE WITH A CHAINSAW LEG.On the other side, we have the actual weapons.You start off with the dual wielding magnums, which while yes, they're a pretty much an FPS standard, they have an alt fire lock-on mode that is devestating towards most small opponents, sometimes even wiping out a whole room. The alt fire does have a cooldown, and here is when the weapon switching comes in. To surpass the cooldown, instead of being a sitting duck, you can switch to another weapon and fire that instead. And an exploit comes to mind "Can I switch back and forth to fire the magnums' alternate firing mode wiping out everything?"No, you can't. You can use the normal firing mode, but not the alt one. This, is INCREDIBLY smart. It encourages weapon combos really well, and not only encourages you to play stylishly, it's FUN to play stylishly.The shotgun is just that, a shotgun. It has an alt firing mode where you can charge up an electric grenade of sorts that deals a lot of damage, killing small enemies, or stuns the bigger ones, making them take double damage. It can also be used for vertical movement,  since if you fire it under yourself while midair, you will be propelled into the air higher than normally, granting you an extra jump. Same with the super shotgun (or rather in this game, a literally SAWED OFF shotgun), it just deals more damage while consuming more ammo. The alt firing mode launches a sticky grenade that can easily disintegrate large clusters of enemies, sorta like the normal shotgun's alt firing mode, but weaker, although the sticky grenades are way cheaper, making you think if you should use one or the other.You can also swap between the SG and SSG to deal massive amount of damage, but this requires pretty good hand coordination and aim.There is the dual wielding machine guns as well, that are incredibly powerful if it lands in the proper hands.It's a DPS MACHINE, and melts anything in it's way (Just like another weapon we'll be talking about later), while being innacurate. If you're not a fan of the extreme innacuracy of it, you can get the alt firing mode, which combines both of them into one, heavy damage dealing, accurate machine gun, and while it's way slower, it's way more versatile.Onto the minigun. It's pretty much another flavor of the machine guns, but it's way less accurate, and fires like a gazillion bullets per nanosecond. It also deals more damage per bullet, which makes me call it the Incinerator™.On the topic of that, it's alt firing mode, is a literal FLAMETHROWER, which is a very close range but insane dps dealing weapon (They made the flamethrower good, forbidden!). I like to pair it with the slide to basically disintegrate opponents in tight spaces/hallways.The rocket launcher. It's pretty fun to rocket jump with it though, and it does have a very satisfying sound effect when you hit the enemy with your lethal shot. Also can be paired with the shotgun and sawed off shotgun swapping. The alt fire is you holding up 4 rockets to release them all at once. It's pretty damn devastating, and when paired with [REDACTED] it's an instant kill.You also have a missile launcher arm, and it's just the magnum alt firing mode on steroids, pretty much a nuke get out of jail free card weapon.There is some other weapons I won't mention because of spoiler reasons for episode 2 and 3.Pairing all these weapons together creates a great balance of stylishly comboing weapons together to create the perfect F U C K I N G MURDER MACHINE.The soundtrack is one of the best fps OST's I've listened to in a while, aside from maybe ULTRAKILL, and you should give it a shot. It won't dissapoint you, and I think it's really underrapreciated.This is my shooter of the year.Anyways, so, since I don't know what to do with this review anymore, Imma just debunk a couple stupid points brought up by the community (WIP)"Movement is too fast, I can't get used to it"Okay, if you're coming from a military shooter, I understand what you mean, but in about 30 minutes of gameplay you're already used to it with how much control the game gives you. I often see people complaining about falling off bridges because they were "too fast". It's really not, it gives you just enough vertical and horizontal movement that, even if you fall off (which really isn't an issue when you actually PLAY the game for more than 5 seconds) you're gonna be able to get back on with your double jump, 2 DASHES, midair slide, and probably even more I didn't mention.MANDATORY POST EARLY ACCESS EDIT: This game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece. Get it right now.
