_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game I'm convinced that Sam Prebble is one of the most astute, discerning FPS designers ever. As a voracious consumer of FPSes, I've played most shooters since the year 2000. Even my favorite games have objective mechanical drawbacks, but I think this game has the least in my experience. All mechanical aspects are fine-tuned to perfection. TLDR; Buy the game if you like fast-paced shooters. If you're invested in the state of FPSes and care about where they are going, buy this at full price! The quality and quantity of content you get for this price is unthinkable. Now let me attempt to provide some long objective analysis/evidence to back my statements above.MovementFast-paced shooters that follow the doom/doom eternal design philosophy (movement shooters?) are enjoyable due to fluid movement first and shooting second. The movement in Turbo Overkill is fluid, intuitive and very forgiving. The level design also never gets in the way. You'll rarely get stuck on anything or miss a jump. Some reviewer on youtube put it best; The game "operates at the speed of thought". The controls are so smooth, that if you think of something, it will seem like it happens automatically. Seriously, the quality of the movement mechanics and control in this game cannot be overstated. The design philosophy of this game is to the liberate the player by giving them all the tools they might want and more. You have a double dash, double jump, doom 2016/eternal style full directional control in the air, "chainsaw leg slide". You can double dash and then do the slide to cover more distance. The jump, dash, slide all cover a generous distance so you can zip across an arena quite easily. You can add an augment to the jump to reset your double jump when you hit a wall so you can essentially get 4 jumps if you want. If that isn't enough you also get a grappling hook in episode 2. Everything else is given to you in episode1 IIRC.You can also selectively wall run during certain fights. The wall run and ladder climbing in this game have zero jank and zero fighting with the controls. Sadly, I can't remember any other game executing these basic things this perfectly. Using the chainsaw slide gives you health/armor back. You can insta-kill fodder enemies with the slide so you can quickly get health/armor back and focus on the tougher enemies. This brings us to combatGunplay/Combat loopAgain, the philosophy here is to give you a large number of tools (probably more than your need) and let you loose in the combat arena to approach combat the way you want.I view player freedom as an equally valid choice as compared to the more restrictive, but also fun, doom eternal approach. Turbo Overkill seems to be inspired by Doom 2016 in some ways here. You get a varied arsenal of course. An alternate fire mode on all weapons. For example, the double barrelled shotgun launches grenades. The plasma gun secondary has a microwave beam and a mode that "catches" projectiles so you can throw them back at enemies!  You even have a gears of war style hammer of dawn weapon! In episode 2, you have a sniper rifle that teleports you to the enemy if you charge it up! This game borrows the best tools from every shooter you can think of and integrates them in a well thought out, intuitive way into your toolset. Since the player has so many tools at their disposal, the game has to be balanced such that the enemies are large in number and hit hard. I did become over-reliant on a few guns due to all the chaos (for me it was the chaingun and rocket launcher). However, the number of enemies that spawn in will deplete your ammo fast enough to cause you to switch your weapons reasonably often (yes fast weapon switching and animation cancelling is possible but not required!). The enemy types are quite diverse and pose different types of threats. The enemies' movement and attack patterns plus the level layout makes it fun to discover a valid set of tools for the job at hand while you're flying around the level. Like for example is the level big and easily traversable such that I feel confident enough to dodge projectiles so I can charge up some rockets and then unload on the heavier enemies? Are there obstructions in the way so that I can use the plasma microwave beam and quickly dash behind around a wall while taking out a chunk of a heavy enemy's health? One thing I found interesting is that you can kinda take a quick breather mid-combat and control a small space around you for a moment (YMMV). This gives you a second to strategize movement and weapon selection unlike Doom Eternal where I felt like the noose tightens when you pause even for a second. Maybe I'm just not good at Doom Eternal but I mostly ended up using the guns the game pushed me to use rather than really strategize (no knock on Doom Eternal, I loved that game). Level Design/ProgressionThe levels are designed to loop in on themselves and are largely big and open. Generally you won't feel claustrophobic or feel like you're getting stuck on objects. There are exceptions to this, but I found those exceptions tolerable due to the fluid movement. The number of secrets in each map are always the same and they are fun to find. Enemy types and weapons are trickled out to you slowly over the game so that you can get familiar with each of them before you fight them in tandem with other enemies. There is some buildcrafting with augments that you can add to the protagonist. But you can equip a ton of augments at once and some are clearly more impactful than others so most people will end up with similar builds. This is good IMO because it gets you back to the action quickly rather than keeping you crippled by indecision in front of an upgrade kiosk. Not much else to be said. It works well. Can't think of any big drawbacks here. MusicSubjective. I would buy this OST. I'm not into this type of music (death metal is more my jam), but this music fit so well, kept me entertained and mildly moving my head throughout all the levels. I occassionally listen to the soundtrack while doing other things as well. Not much game music makes it into my daily playlists. Visual Aesthetics/Art DesignGenerally each section of the level is unique and structure differently enough so that you don't feel like it's all a bunch of similar looking spaces separated by corridors.  The levels are fleshed out in terms of background art, especially the paradise city locations. There are some memorable locations that will stay in your memory. At the same time, there are some levels that felt a bit samey either compared to other levels or sections within the levels themselves. The art style of the levels was cool. The enemies were ugly and I didn't like how they looked. I'm not good at analyzing this aspect plus much of it seems subjective so I'll keep it brief. I don't like pixellation in 3D. I prefer colorful 2D sprites like in Duke Nukem rather than the brown and gray 3D models in Quake. Turbo Overkill was like a blend of the two art styles to me.I loved the cohesive art style of Doom 2016 and I wish someone makes a game like this in that style!Summarily, I would say the aesthetics were functional in the sense that they communicated a sense of place. They didn't bore me, they didn't wow me. No complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled. This is called a boomer shooter or a retro shooter, but it's closer to Doom Eternal than anything else. Doom Eternal meets Blade Runner. Minus Doom Eternal's ammo management and the weapon-to-enemy pairing. Instead, this game is a greatest hits of all the best FPS mechanics. Dash, double jump, wall run, grapple hook, ground pound, slide, slowmo, weapon upgrade, body augmentations, jump pads, it's all here and it all feels useful and worth engaging with.The combat arenas just keep coming. They are always good, always getting crazier. By the third episode, I wasn't sure how the game could get more intense and frantic, but it does. You know those games that allow you to enter a kind of flow state? Turbo Overkill does that. Turn the FOV way up, turn the volume way up, and let the subconscious parts of your mind take over. Every night this week I've felt like I was in a trance.What are AAA devs even doing? Seriously, who else is out here providing FPS campaigns this good? Id? Anyone else? The retro shooter scene can no longer be considered a gimmick, it's no longer just a fun little romp in the nostalgic hay. It can no longer be ignored or downplayed: this is where the real talent is currently located.On top of excellent combat arenas, solid guns, smart upgrades, and incredible music, it also offers a pretty neat story. It's not exactly Baldur's Gate, but it's also not as simple as something like Duke Nukem 3D...even though Jon St. John is in it.No gun reloading, no puzzles, no annoying recourse management, no downtime, no data entries to read, no cover system, no stamina system, no useless weapons. It's the perfect pepperoni pizza of a game that hits the spot in a way few games can. If you're a fan of fast paced FPS titles, then this is an must play. Oh, and it never does that thing where you arbitrarily lose all your weapons and have to get them back. The game ought to be nominated for an award just for that decision alone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Cyberpunk First Person Shooter where you can chainsaw slide through hordes of enemies, shoot rockets and grapple on them, Telefrag into enemies to taverse the map, become Chainsaw Man and and throw enemy (and your own) prjectiles back at them. I could leave it at that and would just recommend you either buying the game or checking out the Demo! But I won't, cause there is so much more to love about this game.First off,  24 Levels (AND THE SAME AMOUNT OF SECRET LEVELS), each of them visually diverse in different environments. It's all Cyberpunk Themed, you travel through severs, over rooftop, a toxic wasteland, through a powerplant and later on even in space.The levels are overall really well paced, you got mostly swift and fast combat encounters, some bigger and longer arenas that are broken up with some platforming section which never last too long.The combat is really tight. You got over 9 weapons, each of them with purpose, there is nothign that doesn't feel useles, except maybe the Minigun at times, but even that one has a super good Alternate Firemode. Most enemies are running around shooting at you and while their behaviour doesn't overall change, the variety comes from the projectiles they throw at you. Some projectiles are threatening for different reasons, which is somethign you gonna particularily feel on Murder Machine, the highest difficulty where you end up dead in less than 2 seconds for some enemies. I spent most of the time playing on Murder MAchien Difficulty with Triple Enemies just for the fun of it. That Soundtrack is also top notch, though it really start bopping starting from Episode 2. Anything else? Oh yeah, there is also and Endless Mode, which is great fun and a Level Editor! This game is through and through a full experience, and one of the most fun shooters around.My personal GOTY in a year where ACVI comes out and actually has to match this.

_childDocuments_.review: First the major negative for me, character writing is pretty cringe. A little too much "badass-humor" and tropey cliches for me. And the main antagonist AI is basically a much weaker written Shodan.Thankfully this is a movement shooter so the writing isn't the important part, the movement and shooting is. The game passes these categories with flying colors.For movement options, you've got double jumping, dashing, grapple hand, wall-running, and the crown jewel; chainsaw slide. The slide easily being the biggest innovation despite how simple the idea of a damaging slide attack is. But if you spec your traits around it, it becomes both one of the strongest weapons in your arsenal and an ammo replenishing/healing maneuver.For shooting, the entire arsenal of weapons is both satisfying to use and comes with a series of upgrades. From my own personal play experience, I found myself cycling through each of the weapons throughout the entire duration of the game. Many are given specific advantages over some enemies, a great design choice for making everything feel like it has a use. And even though weapons are paired up and share ammo types, I still found the balance between using them both well thought out too.The story, while I have my gripes with the dialogue, still leads the player into some great set pieces and successfully amps up the scale with each episode.Overall, game proved to be an enjoyable movement shooter, and an impressive feat for such a small development team.

_childDocuments_.review: Fast, Fluid, and Fun! Turbo Overkill is the ADHD of video games, and gives you the movement tech and weapons to gun down hundreds of enemies like they were all chaff. All jokes aside, Turbo Overkill is an incredibly fun game with a visually appealing art style that is only enhanced by its visceral combat. Combat is all about movement, positioning, and chaining together different weapon attacks to maximize your destructive potential.If you're a fan of the above then you'll LOVE this game.The level design is amazing as you'll be running and gunning through halls and open arenas while wall running hundreds of feet above potential deadly falls. There is destructibility in the environment, but it isn't  a massively relevant feature in the game. Another fun note is that, like most retro shooters, there are a variety of collectibles/secrets to be found. As someone who loves searching every nook and cranny of a level this is always a net positive; some of them REALLY stumped me at points.The story is passable, and doesn't seem like the major focus on the game, but I will say it's interesting enough and not tact on like some games tend to do.If I were to give Turbo Overkill a rating between 1- 10 then it would be an easy 8.5.The only things that really dragged down the game for me were that some levels don't really "loop" around so if you're missing a collectible then you're ♥♥♥♥ outta luck; gotta run through the mission again! I also encountered a couple of bugs where I'd get stuck or where I'd just fall through the geometry and die.

_childDocuments_.review: The short'n'sweet intro goes something like this: it establishes who you are (a cyber-badass), what you're here to do ( purge), then you dropkick your chainsaw leg into some cyberdude's face and off you go into neon-soaked rain. You see, not only do you move across arenas quickly, you also turn a whole mob of trash into red chunks (as well as the customary pickups) while you're at it. ... and it still gets better with the weapons roster which is Syn-damned fun to use. _childDocuments_.review: Best boomer shooter in recent years. And behind this one I would put Postal Brain Damaged and Prodeus.Its not because it recreates memories very well, rather opposite - because of indie nature it experiments with mechanics. For me this is mechanically better version of Doom Eternal.Its quite unique because of movement, mostly because of chainsaw leg mechanics which can be combined with double jump + dash + grappling hook. You can stay midair most of the time, providing very unique flow to the game. Other game advantages - great enemy variety, cyberpunk environment.However my major problem is that creator was chasing same thing as Doom Eternal so game is bloated with abilities. Therefore close to the end of the game engagements are too chaotic. Therefore you feel 2 things : 1 - you realize that some abilities you dont utilize, 2 - you spam same abilities all the time. Just for reference here is list of major abilities:- double/triple jump- regular dash- chainsaw slide- missile launcher- grappling hook- chainsaw arms- turbo time- weapon swap- weapon alternate modsReducing number of abilities by 50% and adding depth to them would benefit gameplay greatly IMO. Great game does not need overcomplex rules to become popular or to have lots of room for skill development. For example chess - there are 6 types of pieces and 8x8 board. Very unlikely that if these numbers were doubled this game could become what it is. Need to mention that while i believe that gameplay wise this game is more fun than Doom Eternal, production quality is no match for AAA title like Doom. So it would not be fair to say its overall better game than Doom.Wishing dev all the best and hoping for polished sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game. The first 2 episodes are very strong. finding new weapons and mods is exciting and learned the ins-and-outs of each mod and weapon mode feels very rewarding. Movement is fluid, fast, and just feels good. There's a nice variety of enemies and it does help to pay attention and prioritize which enemies will give you the most trouble. The vehicle sections are not horrible and help change up the pace, giving the player a break from the relentless assault on Syn. The 3rd episode is sadly the weakest in the game. Its just a grind. Every time the player fights Maw its dragged out and gets stale fast, but Ep3 Maw is simply a bore to fight and by the end I was just glad it was over, only to get quickly tossed into the Syn fight which is also a long, drawn out, and annoying fight. Its not the difficulty of the fight, I beat it first try. Its how the game doesn't really tell you what to do, how many phases there are, and unlike the other bosses there is no health bar so the player doesn't know if what they are doing is working. All in all if it wasn't for the 3rd Ep this game would be among my favorite FPSs but with how truly tedious the ending portion on the game is I don't really feel like playing it again. With the great art, awesome moment, and super satisfying gun play, I am sure I'll pick it up again eventually - just not right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a retro First Person Shooter similar to Dusk or Amid Evil, where player character Johnny Turbo must fight through hordes of Human and Cyborg enemies to stop a rogue AI from taking over the world.•	Movement speed is very fast.•	Good weapon variety including magnum, assault rifle, shotgun, double barrel shotgun, minigun, rocket launcher, plasma rifle, sniper rifle and ion cannon. Most weapons have a secondary fire mode.•	Your leg has a chainsaw attached, which lets you slide through groups of enemies, instantly killing weaker enemies. This can be upgraded to restore your health and armour with each kill.•	You’ll also gain a slow motion ability which is very useful for dealing with more dangerous enemies. Killing enemies during slow mo will make them drop ammo pickups.•	Customise your playing style by equipping upgrades such as increased maximum health, triple jump, and nearby ammo/health pickups being magnetised towards you.•	Level design can be annoying at times. This is one of those games that has lots of small platforms where you’ll need to jump, double jump, air dash, double air dash, wall run and grapple hook over bottomless pits. Thankfully the airborne gymnastics is fairly lenient (there were times where I felt like I missed a jump but the game decided it was close enough). But sometimes the level layouts are confusing and I’d spend a few minutes trying to figure out where I’m supposed to go next. And I lost count of the number of times I accidentally fell off a small platform while trying to shoot enemies.•	Hard difficulty is nicely balanced for an experienced FPS player during episodes 1 and 2 (each episode contains several levels), but episode 3 at times felt a bit too much. I got through it, but it was less fun. Most encounters involve being trapped in a small room with not much space to dodge and even less cover, while having to defeat multiple large waves of enemies. Eventually one of the rocket launcher wielding enemies would spawn right next to me and kill me before I had chance to react, sending me back to the start of the first wave. Probably more enjoyable on normal difficulty.•	I also want to give a special mention to the final level, which has several encounters where you have to defeat multiple waves of enemies within a strict time limit, or you’ll die instantly.•	Boss fights are mostly just bigger waves of the same enemies you’ve spent the whole game killing, while occasionally shooting the boss between waves.•	Story is nonsense. There’s not much of an intro to explain things and there are several occasions where NPCs refer to past events that I’m not familiar with, which made me wonder if this is actually a sequel to a game I never played. (I don’t think it is).•	Voice acting is fine.•	I finished the game in just under 17 hours.•	Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.•	I didn’t have any problems with bugs, crashes or framerate.•	Default field of view is too high. I don’t think I’ve ever changed my FOV in any game before, but everything looked really weird while I played through the first level. After consulting the forum and changing FOV from 90 to 74, everything looks normal.Turbo Overkill is a good game that fans of retro FPSes should mostly enjoy, if you’re in the mood to just turn off your brain and shoot things. Worth buying on a small sale.

Weapons/Augmentations: Hypnotically enjoyableSoundtrack/Voice Acting: 10/10Community Content: HAS A BUILT IN LEVEL DESIGNER!!Overall rating: 9/10 (only -1 point because sometimes levels can feel like a maze, but then I feel dumb once I finally figure it out and it turned out to be simple. _childDocuments_.review: This *has* to be the most adrenaline-fuelled, manic, massively over-the-top thrill ride you can play today.   Whatever mechanic you like in your FPSes, Turbo Overkill's got it but polished to absolute perfection.The wonderful thing about T.O. is that if you can dynamically adjust the difficulty by pre-selecting the difficulty level and then adjusting it with tech chip mods. For example, I played at "standard" (aka Street Sweeper), and it was a nice challenge for a Doom/Quake/Duke veteran, with lots of high-speed combat in tight hallways and huge spaces, but I was picking up hidden "tech chips" along the way.  Collecting all 3 on a level gives you a game-altering tweak that can help or hinder.  If you fancy seeing what it's like playing as a porcelain teapot, sure, there's a mod that makes you die on the first hit.  But, if you've already done a level and want to replay it to get an achievement or missed secret, or you're finding a level too hard, there are mods that can make you pretty much invincible.  There's one that lets you play in slow motion all the time. There's another that gives infinite ammo, and one that makes all enemies insta-gib.   Even the most uncoordinated granny who's never seen a mouse before would be like death itself with those three tech chips.After I got about halfway through the game, I got a little fed up with hunting for ammo, so I turned on "infinite ammo".  By the end of the game I found my reflexes slightly too slow for the last few levels, so I turned on "infinite Turbo Time", which made those levels passable.But, be warned:  This game is friggen un-put-downable.   The levels are one long hyper-intense smash-fest at warp speed set up to give you maximum changes to rock like a god.   Anyone who played doom and tried the -turbo 250  command-line switch will know what I'm talking about.  The game just feels like it's running at a million miles an hour... But, like in Max Payne, as soon as you kick in Turbo Time (bullet time), everything slows down to a wonderful anime-like action sequence.  You can take your time lining up shots. You can speed over chasms and drop a few grenades down, or pop a couple of rockets into the mouth of a big beastie, and then land safely on the other side before spinning around and nailing a headshot at the sniper on the ledge above you...The really big warning is... if you play it long enough, when you go into the outside world, everything feels like it's in slow motion. I found myself driving almost too fast and needed to force myself to slow down.    This game is so FAST, and just so INTENSE, it makes your brain run at 250% doing jumps, leaps, shots, rebounds, dodges. It all feels so natural as well. The controls are beautifully set that you find yourself executing a ballet of perfect death, a whirlwind of chainsaws and miniguns, leaving just a fine red mist behind you.  So, when you turn off the PC, step out into that big blue outdoors, and you're "just" walking along, it's like in futurama when Fry drinks a hundred cups of coffee and he can see the flapping of a hummingbird's wings.   There's even a loading screen hint that says "If you want to know what Turbo Time is, drink 100 cups of coffee".. It's *EXACTLY* like that.   The weapons are AWESOME.   there's no "BFG" so to speak, but the Ion cannon comes pretty close, making the full standard set of FPS weps from Melee to OP exotic complete.  The sniper rifle that lets you telefrag enemies has so many brilliant uses,  it's an interesting twist on a mechanic I've never seen before.  The grappling hook can be used to wonderful effect at dodging and leaping, just like it did in Quake 2 Capture The Flag...Simply put, the devs have sat down and written a list of all the epic things they loved from Duke, Doom, Quake, Quake 2, Halo, Doom (2016), and a myriad other games and said "What if we put just the best stuff in, and leave out the filler".The music is absolutely gorgeous.  Some of the levels have their own themes, and the game itself has a theme that ripples through the pieces.   Taking on an army of mutants in Turbo Time while a thumping techno track blasts from the speakers... Listening to the bullets whizz by my ear in Surround Sound, listening to the distant explosions of monsters that just caught my rocket volley to the face...  It's all so wonderful.  There are also challenges and arenas you can test out your skills on.   Some of them are immense fun.I can't recommend this highly enough, but there IS a lot of bad language.  a profanity filter would be appreciated with possible alternate dialogue for anyone who doesn't appreciate the F-bomb being dropped all the time (not the wrist-cannon mod).  I often had to pause the game when my kids were anywhere about, lest they hear someone's dropping S- and F-bombs like confetti.I'm a completionist, so I've hunted all over for the tech chips and cassettes, hence the 60 hours playtime. I reckon a speedrun would be about 10 hours, with a solid playthrough  being about 30.

_childDocuments_.review: Fast paced non-stop action. If Ultrakill and Doom: Eternal were your cup of tea, this is an easy sell. I played on the 2nd highest difficulty and had a pretty comfortable time. 3 hours to complete the first episode. Love the biopunk aesthetic.Now since I'm a critical person I'm going to do what I do best: ♥♥♥♥♥. The checkpoint system is awful. I'm guessing it's based on crossing a line on the map. However, the game has you running around like a maniac so chances are you're going to cross one mid combat multiple times during a playthrough, so you respawn in the middle of a previous fight. There was also a situation I ran into during a platforming section where a switch opened a shortcut in case I fell. The check point however, flagged before I hit the switch the first time. So I respawned, fell and found out the switch hadn't been hit.The weapon balance is a little off. The Chainsaw Leg and the F-U Rocket are too strong for things that doesn't cost anything to use. With the augment upgrades the slide turns the melee enemies into health and armor refills, any encounter with them left me with over 100 health and armor. The Rocket with the damage upgrade can gib what's supposed to be the episode's big bad enemy, and it can target multiple other enemies along side it. The harder encounters ended up being situations with a lot of smaller enemies I didn't want to use the rocket on. The game's abundance of bright lights can be an issue as well. Enemies with bright lights on them don't really stand out in the environment that is mostly bright lights. I didn't even know where my crosshairs were most of the time, I just went with the wall of bullets approach. The stores feel superfluous. On higher difficulties especially you can't buy a whole lot. The weapon stores were for a 1 time weapon upgrade, and the general store sold augments that you then took to the near by splicer vender to install. The weapon upgrades could just be included, they're available at the first store after you get the gun anyway. The general store and splicer vender could be combined, so you buy them and install them at the same place. You would also get to see the nifty video demonstrations were you buy the augment.

_childDocuments_.review: The first few hours had me on the fence, but then I started having a lot of fun afterall.  There was something graphics-related that looked a bit scratchy or off to me.  I lack the technical knowledge to specify what it is exactly, but there's no issues with motion blur or anything like that.  The game has many 'arena shooter' parts which is not my favoured style for FPS.  On top of that, the movement is very fast with a bit of parkour and it is just a very untypical FPS experience.  The game reminds me of Doom Eternal quite a bit actually.Turbo Overkill is one of the most impressive FPS's, especially given the size of the dev team.The game mixes in more features from other FPS's than you would normally get.  From wall jumping, grappling, vehicles, bullet time, sliding, and more.  Most of these features are implemented well.  One thing however, after getting the grapple, you get an additional crosshair on enemies that you can grapple, and I found that this made it more difficult to spot my actual shooting crosshair.  There is a lot of power fantasy to the experience, your guns feel OP, but at the same time, enemies are very threatening and the game is no walk in the park.While its not a personal favourite, I really enjoyed Turbo Overkill in the end. _childDocuments_.review: This game is everything I wanted from a movement shooter, it's got tons of weapons, weapon combos, enemy variety and most important of all... MOVEMENT, there is a LOT of movement in this game, no other game I've played has such movement, you have a grappling hook (mid-game) that allows you to grapple on enemies and certain spots in the map.Not only that, the game also allows you to dash, chainsaw slide + dash (Yes, you have a chainsaw on your leg that allows you to tear enemies while sliding and that is also interesting) and gives you an arsenal of devastating weapons, no weapon is useless in this game, they all allow you to frag a lot of enemies at once.Dare I say that this game is the best movement singleplayer shooter I've played, yes, Ultrakill is good and it's also awesome but Turbo Overkill is just way more frenetic and the weapons are more devastating and simpler to use, it's all just mindless killing combined with hyper aggressive movement and air control and that is exactly what I want, it's really relaxing in it's own way.

(coming back to this after chapter 2 has been released. There are at least 3 areas in the new chapter which ive had to have multiple sittings to complete...)Art design is great.Presentation = Very goodPolish = not great - okImo requires an endless mode like the cybergrind in ultrakill

_childDocuments_.review: The game in its current state is ok, but I can't recommend it as it is now. It starts off strong with good mechanics, great level design, and has a wonderful aesthetic. These things are what originally drew me to the game, but now having played a fair amount of it.... The game just doesn't maintain the same quality from start to finish. Enemies from the start already suffered from blending in with their environment, but this becomes far more of an issue as the game goes on. It doesn't help that the game has many of it's later fights in super large arenas with break neck action. Another issue is the enemies themselves. Far too many bullet sponges. This is a very serious issue that makes fights feel like a slog to run through. This also creates an issue for ammo. I need to dump hundreds of rounds into enemies at times only to realize the game is barely giving me enough ammo for the next enemy encounter filled with sponges. It forces you to play less aggressive and choose your battles (which is not the intended idea behind the game). When your action shooter is encouraging me to avoid enemies, you've made a poor choice in design. This isn't a bad game, but games like Ultrakill are already doing what this game is trying to do and better. Buy that instead

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine, unfortunately not amazing.It does feel like style-over-substance, and it's noticable how there is a big coverage by Retro-FPS community in reviews, but almost 0 activity afterward, like in guides, let's plays and the like.I do, however, want to congratulate the small dev team for delivering a finished and good game to the finish lineI'll be honest, it took me quite a few attempts to "get" the game. I did find the game boring, frustrating, or tedious at first, even thought to leave a negative review.But then I decided to just get through to the end, and in the end, it clicked.I could not shake of the feeling of kitchen-sink design, that it's unbalanced and doesn't fit together well.I learned to stop caring and just go "chegg goes brrrr" and found the experience quite enjoyable.If you come expecting the tight and smart design of Ultrakill, lower expectations. Don't feel weird if you forget that you have certain guns/abilities/upgrades and use the same 2-3 guns on anything that your Chegg (titular chainsaw leg) does not outright instagib.Weapons do feel really kitchen-sinky, like anything goes, doesn't matter if it fits really.Like after 50h I still don't really know what's the tactical difference between two Uzis and Twincendiary Machinegun. And the flamethrower mod of above-mentioned gun? Game doesn't really give you great feedback on how much damage fire does, it sometimes obstructs what you are trying to burn, and also has confusing death animations, where grunts stay upright burning, and it's not clear who's dead, who's burning, and who managed to escape the flame.And same-ish problems occur all around your arsenal, they aren't designed to interact with each other really, there are only few clear interactions with questionable utility, like grabbing your rockets with plasma rifle. Oh yeah btw, how does Plasma rifle really fit in? Why, again, would I use it above my 2 machineguns, and it also has this meme-beam, at least it's not as bad as in Doom Eternal, maybe it's projectile grab is somewhat useful.Arsenal feels like it tries to copy Doom Eternal, but shares it's pitfalls.I only found useful altfire of Magnums, altfire of Waster shotgun, Boomer shotgun and Uzis, ah also maybe Rocket LauncherSee how I mentioned altfires? Because the primary fires feel like trying to kill an ant colony by shooting individual ants with a slingshot.I just overused the OP chainsaw leg and didn't feel good about it, as if I was playing wrongEnemy design is also at times questionable. For me it felt that either I would mainly receive inconsequential chip damage, HP rarely being lower than 80, but then I would catch some stupid and unfair attack that would 1-hit-kill me outright, with almost full HP/armor(main offenders being Sloth's rockets and armored flamethrower dudes).Higher difficulty settings only make this problem more noticable, and in general feel untested, unbalanced and lazy(yeah, hehe, x6.66 damage received, funny number, ah also way faster projectile speed, have fun catching instakill rockets with your head, no hp/armor pickups BTW)In order for me to start enjoying the game, again, i really had to start ignoring these issues, turn the brain off, and just enjoy blasting whatever

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot begin to describe just how much this game does correctly. there is not a single weapon, enemy, plot point, boss fight, level or piece of dialogue that feels redundant or wasted. every upgrade has a purpose, every weapon is a beast capable of downing gods and every story act is an escalation worthy of the name overkill. the only thing limiting you in this game is your own skill and your own imagination. if you have any interest whatsoever in arena-fight to arena-fight design similar to nu-doom or painkiller? I am of the personal belief that this game is nearly perfect, and with some polish and a bigger budget it would have even outshone doom eternal. if anyone ever manages to top this, they may well have to create a perfect game out of necessity. where can you go up from here but to heaven itself?

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a must-play for first-person shooter fans. With a cybernetically-enhanced protagonist, intense action, and excellent weapon mechanics, this game delivers non-stop excitement. The levels are well-designed with plenty of hidden areas to discover. The soundtrack is also excellent. If you want a game that will get your heart racing, Turbo Overkill is the one for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a wickedly fun Retro FPS that oozes charisma! I don't remember the last time I had so much fun playing a shooter! I don't have a lot of time to play games on the regular these days, so it's nice to have something I can jump into and play in short, fast paced sessions. For full disclosure, though, I do know the main developer on this game personally (he's almost a one man show, believe it or not!), and have worked with him in the past, so there's probably a bit of bias, I admit. We were never afraid to tell each other when we thought each other's work was crap, though, and I think most people would agree (especially based on reviews!), that he's made something special! Bravo, Sam!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is pretty much everything you can want from a boomer shooter. -Fast movement speed, with a chainsaw slide, double jump, wallrunning, and dashes-A wide variety of guns with that feel good to shoot on top of having alt-fire modes for extra usability -A decent array of enemies, that require different methods of defeating-Good music that gets you are heart racing-Vehicle set-pieces that are an unexpected and enjoyable surprise-And satisfying boss fightsOnly real complaints are the "redness" in of some levels in Episode 2 and 3. It just made it hard to see what I was shooting at times. Some battle arenas near the end where more annoying the challenging to fight in. Humor could also be hit or miss at times, but not enough to hamper on the experience.In short: You should buy this game and OVERkill every last enemy you see.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, I will recommend this game as it is a well made boomer shooter but I do have my gripes about it.Level design is a hit or miss for me. I can't pinpoint it but they don't feel good. It maybe because there's too much backtracking in the game where you're taken to a door and you need to do X things on different corners of the map so you could open the door. It feels lazy. The best way I can describe it is it is Hallways made to be traversed like a big open map. Arena and Encounter design is also a hit or miss. There's a lot of Area Denial enemies in the game, and there's a little too much "cramped" arenas. And I usually find the enemies a little too tanky for my taste.Enemy Design is somewhat subpar IMO. Subpar because there's a lot of enemies that are unfun to fight. Particularly the enemies that leave behind a damage puddle, they're also usually put in tight areas accompanied by enemies that fires rockets that deal AoE damage.A lot of the "difficult" encounters just felt tedious. May it be too little cover with enemies that fire lasers and homing projectiles, or too little room with enemies that deal a lot of AoE damage. I felt like the arenas were specifically made to be completely against the player. I get that kind of design but it's a bit too much here. Arenas should be a neat balance between being good for the player and enemy but here, the case is almost always enemy-favored.After all those negatives, why do I still recommend it? Because despite all of those, it is still a genuinely well-made game that would benefit greatly in polishing its level and encounter design. Johny Turbo feels good to play, the weapons are decent and each fulfills their own niche, and there are some great set pieces at later levels. The Splice upgrade system is very well designed with upgrades that are genuinely good, the weapon design and their upgrades are very well designed.In summary, I think this game was a result of fully refining the player character and making artwork of the setting and aesthetics of the levels but kind of fell apart when designing enemies and level layouts.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best Boom Shoots I've played in the last decade. If you're a veteran of the genre or looking to get into it, I cannot recommend this game hard enough.The entire weapon arsenal is a joy to use - nothing gets put into the 'worthless' box for a majority of the game. There are times where a weapon may be tucked away or neglected for a bit, but it will always have a use at some point. Barring a couple enemy types, the game has no "this weapon counters this enemy" - allowing you to play the game however you wish.The OST is an absolute banger, the second to last boss has the best tracks in the game. They do reuse assets in their level design, but its used/reused so incredibly well that unless you're really looking hard for it you may not even notice. I didn't notice myself until it was pointed out to me!Overall, amazing. 11/10. Play Turbo Overkill!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. Fun movement, unique weapons and enemies with certain weaknesses to exploit. Level design is stellar as well. The story is serviceable for this type of game, although sometimes it pushes it too much when it really isn't anything to write home about. Last level and boss fight is ass though, they really didn't need to make it so tedious. There's also one enemy that has an OP missile attack that kills you very quickly which becomes annoying quick due to how much it's spammed throughout the game.Overall entertaining game that you can devote 10+ hours to. There's some pretty badass ♥♥♥♥ in there too. Also watch the credits 'till the very end, trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta be the negative Nancy here. Mainly because the highest difficulty "Murder Machine" is so ridiculously unfair, it's crazy:No quicksaving, even though the game has quick saves otherwise, no health or armor pick ups except from some enemy drops (Like WTF), most enemies (even the weakest ones) can one-shot kill you, or at least take away most of your health in a blink of an eye, enemy projectiles are either hit scan or so incredibly fast and numerous that it's either impossible to dodge them or completly luck based.Because of the no health or armor pick ups basically your only way to get back health and armor is by having certain implants and then doing chainsaw kills. This is fine when you have low tier enemies to kill but not when there are only high tier enemies left.I played a lot of old school fps and I usually play my first run on the highest difficulty and sure it was hard at times, but never as hard and unfair than in this game.What pisses me even more off, is that this game has an achievement for beating the game on the highest difficulty (Unlike for example Doom (2016) and Doom Eternal or Doom 1 and 2 in Doom 3 BFG Edition which all have ridiculously hard highest difficulty but thank god no achievement for beating it). And despite all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I managed to beat most of the game on it, even though a lot of the fights took me like 50-100 tries, maybe even more. Yeah, was very "fun"But then you get to the boss fights which are even worse. And for some reason the devs thought it was a good idea to include 3 bosses just in Episode 2. Episode 1 had 1 boss fight which is more than enough. I managed to beat the first boss in Episode 2 but the other 2 are so extremly unfair I couldn't beat them. Honestly they would be doable if they would at least include check points after every boss phase, but that would be too fair I guess...So, what did I do: Well, during the game you collect tech chips in secret areas. And each of them varies the game which you can activate through the main menu. Some of them make the game even harder but some are basically cheats, like insta gib (which for some reason works on some bosses but not all), infinite ammo (which isn't even needed as the game gives you way too much ammo) or infinite turbo time. Thank god those cheats do not void the achievements, so after having tried those bosses way too often, I decided to use them at those points.I "love" it when a game is that hard you basically have to use cheats to beat it...Yeah I get it what some of you might say: just lower the difficulty. Yeah, fair point but in my opinion a game on a highest difficulty should still always be fair and doable if you properly learn the game (which I did).But what about the rest of the game:Well, honestly the rest of the game is mostly fine but still far from perfect:-some of the weapons are so weak, like the super shotgun (which is a crime in itself), the chaingun or the plasma gun, basically after some upgrades you just need a few weapons to effectively kill enemies, namely the regular shotgun (only for alt fire), the assault rifle, the rocket launcher and sometimes the sniper.-soundtracks: some of them are really good, others some annoying techno bs-the devs tried to include a story but that was so boring and generic, they might have just cut it entirely, same with the characters, all but Sam were super annoying, sometimes dialogues are even pretty cringeSo is it all bad? No, of course not. At least the non-boss fights are mostly quite fun if you ignore the underpowered weapons. If you don't care for achievements or beating a game on it's highest difficulty, this is a decent old school fps, otherwise it's just pain and because of all the pain this game gave me, I have to rate it negative. Cry about it.Honestly the best way of playing the game is to play your first run on the second highest difficutly unlock all upgrades and collect all tech chips. Then if you care for the highest difficulty achievement, just use the cheats to beat it.

_childDocuments_.review: I demoed This at PAX West 2021 and I loved it. Bought it day one of early release and loved it more! They kept all of the core mechanics from the demo and expanded more upon it. This game is fast paced, a bit gory, and hard (on the higher difficulties). Gun-play is fantastic and effectively quick-switching to melt heavies feels great. The graphics are fantastically stylized and the game is just funny. Comical cut-scenes and flipping the bird at many opportunities is just great. This game does have a story to it but it is like most other games in this genre, that being it is totally optional to listen to and you just gotta shoot the pretty colors. My mains gripes are:-Reloading a level or quitting the game and pressing continue will put you on the lowest difficulty possible with no apparent way to change it back. Meaning you must do all your game-play in one sitting and start new missions from the chapter selection menu after closing it. I did beat the game on Bring Me Pain (after a few resets due to mentioned issue)-The shops seem to be sorta whatever, not all to needed to have added in the game but they exist to fulfill their purpose, possibly turn down the volume of the noises it makes as it can be annoying.-To many augments and not enough ways to use them. In the first "chapter" you can get tons of body augments that change how you do certain things, you rapidly get to many and have no use for most of them.-Last level has an odd intended path, first it seems that you jump on the floating cars and fight enemies, but then you cant go any further and the jump pad shoots you up to the ceiling to instantly die and jumping to the train from here sticks you in an infinite death-loop. I then found out that you have to scale the train top to go to the next arena. -A lack of apparent ammo at the final boss? You have 2 pairs of guns that share shotgun ammo for one pair or heavy bullets for the other, which limits your ammo pool to realistically 3 different weapons. The ammo you are given didn't seem to cut it for the boss which led to me to get creative with my chainsaw slides to take it out. May just be me being bad.All of these are fairly minor in the scheme of things and can be either disregarded or not encountered. Part of it is just feedback for the devs, bugs or not. Overall I'd recommend this game if you want a blast of big guns, stylish kills, fast mobility, and a helluva time! It is well worth the purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is rad.Featuring a diverse selection of monstrosities eager to tear you apart and an equally diverse range of weaponry to put them down with Turbo Overkill is not only a great arena shooter, it's one of the best games in it's category.Every level throws in something new, whether it's a fresh face to blast apart, a new toy to assist with the blasting, some new traversal puzzle, the occasional vehicle level to keep the ante as high as it'll go capping each section off with a climactic boss battle that will put your skills to the test.Three episodes split up into a myriad of levels from water logged docks and winding canyons of scrap metal to the insides of a super sized flesh beast and the besieged capital ship of a mercenary outfit.No good cyberpunk dystopia would be complete without cybernetic augmentations and Turbo Overkill has a plethora of options, most augment your abilities; reduced cool-downs, extra damage and tweaks to the functionality of related abilities, all customisable to your preference.If you're into movement shooters, arena shooters, boomer shooters or any variation on that style of game, heck even if you're just getting into first person shooters in general I can't recommend Turbo Overkill enough.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: ok... let's run down the check list:Thrilling ✅Cyberpunk ✅Solid but still innovative gameplay✅Dystopian ✅Full of secrets✅MASSIVE✅'Neon' Design ✅Apocalyptical ✅Synth-Soundtracks full of kicks and that makes the game recognizable✅ 90's badass-ery✅A Cheesy-but-with-great-moments-that-will-keep-you-playing-story✅......Yup. I really don't need to say anything else. Go play it.....C'mon.....OK! Fine! But I won't say that much: Turbo-Overkill truly rocks, and it rocks so much that enters with its own right in the pantheon of the modern boomer-shooter. I got the copy in EA and unlike most, Trigger Happy Interactive did deliver not only a well rounded experience... but one that has a fre****g Identity. Not only style, but an Identity of its own (in a genre that, although full of truly fun games, some of them lack a... personality... Turbo surely doesn't).I mean the game is a cohesive experience: weapons, movements, power up, enemies and all the rest are perfectly thought to be together and not just mix-mashed like 'Hey, this is cool, just throw in it. Doesn't matter if it doesn't work that well.And that, dear friends, means an astonishing gameplay which separates the games from the rest of its peers: multiple secrets that actually have a purpose (they unlock new and new LEVELS!), and not just to be a collect-athon (which is not bad, but for me are a time waster and nothing else), more than 20 hour of gameplay (now almost a rarity for modern FPS) in single player mode with all the levels being FUN, parkour that doesn't break (mostly) the game but actually is required in order to survive higher difficulties, and a f***ton more. (It even manages to deliver a good story, with some great voice acting).Now, it does have some downside: sometimes the checkpoint system can mess up your game and some levels being too... long (which is weird, usually is the contrary), and the main character doesn't utter a word (even when damaged).But again, nothing of the technical problems can even touch this masterpiece of game! Really recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: doom-style levels of corridors and rooms full of enemies for you to slaughter and key/secret-hunt through, and ultrakill-style movement emphasizing slides, dashes, and being lightning-fast. that being said it is unique, with its own combat styles and movement with emphasis on upgrades and augments, though the claim to fame for this game is of course the chainsaw leg, which on top of just sounding kickass in general means your sliding does some major damagethe story is fun and serves to funnel you through the various levels with some sense of purpose, thought it's secondary to the gameplay of course. the characters you interact with are charming and funny and i enjoy them a lot. visually the game is great, with a strong aesthetic in the absurd neons of a retrowave cyberpunk future- though it also features some varying aesthetics from map to map, from calming and cute to industrial and disgusting. there are bloodier games out there but this game's unique technogore is still very satisfying to turn enemies into, so thats also a plus. game has a sense of humor about it too which is obvious from the get gooverall fun game and i would absolutely recommend for some colorful, fast-paced action. its not a masterpiece but what is?  its a damn good game which is all it needs to be

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a fun game made by an amateur developer, and it shows.The game itself is fun, with understandable mechanics and fun enemies. if you like other movement shooters such as ultrakill or doom you will like this. just buy it its worth it. but here are some cons that ive found.Difficulty settingsthe difficulty settings in this game rely on the same awful method of every other game in the genre of making you a glass cannon. its very obvious they didnt test the different difficulties, because on the higher difficulties the game becomes impossible without cheesing the game. higher difficulties increase enemy dmage output, projectile speed, and walk speed. later difficulties prevents you from buying ammo (not a big deal), and prevents health packs from spawning outside of killing enemies. the final difficulty level, murder machine, is something i can oly describe as ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. 6x damage, 2x projectile speed, increased enemy run speed, and no health packs outside of enemies. they did not test this difficulty level, while playing on thsi difficulty it is simply luck whether you survive or not, and its impossible without using two specific augments. it is very common to enter a boss with no hp, and be unable to beat it because you cant heal, forcing you to restart.speaking about the bosses, they suck. theyre just boring, simple, and one dimensional. revolving around a specific gimmick that youve seen a in every game known to man, or just being boring. it doesnt help that the cutscene plays everytime you start again. because they didnt think putting a checkpoint after the cutscene was a good idea.oh yeah, the checkpoints, they suck. checkpoints happen before big fights (not after so if you die after a big fight you just spent an hour on you gotta do it again), when you interact with a shop, or when you pick up a collectable. there is a non zero chance of soft locking yourself by interacting with a shop just as your about to die. the reason its this way is because the game is designed around quicksaving for some reason, which you cant do on the later difficulty levels.overall the game is fine, dont play it on the final difficulty level and you should be fine. its a good game made an amateur developer, and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: Holt cow, this game is on the podium 100%. I was skeptical at first, I've never liked any games like this. and I still don't. but this is the one outlier. For a game so satisfying and smooth, it also is pretty funny. everything feels balanced, and if it's too hard for you, there are different difficulties. Also, I was expecting 6 hours of gameplay, but no this is 20-24 hours. and every second is just as good as the last. there is ONE thing I don't like: a single enemy on the second hardest difficulty can one-shot you if you have 200 health and 200 armor. you'd think "Oh well, that makes sense, it's the second hardest difficulty, and it's probably an advanced enemy." you'd be right. I'd completely agree, but the only problem is there is no sound cue, and it's a fast-ranged attack. that pissed me off for like 10 minutes but that's it.  everything else is so perfect and satisfying. And as far as I know, there aren't really any ways to cheese anything. you can play any way you want, i loved this one gun, and it brought me through most of the game, but then my friend hated that gun and did a different gun I hated that brought him mostly through the game. and if you don't like guns at all, you can get a powerful as heck chainsaw leg, that destroys everything. It fits whatever playstyle. Also, voice acting is great. play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Took a while to get going, but it was worth it. During Episode 1, the gameplay is nothing special. When Episode 2 rolls around and you've unlocked most of the weapons/mechanics and the levels occasionally force you to fight in arenas, that's where the game picks up. That's when it starts to feel like Doom Eternal gameplay. Otherwise, it's too easy to just kite/funnel enemies and kill them without much difficulty.I will say that the Chainsaw dash is also a little OP, especially when you've unlocked the perks to get armor and health per kill. With no real limit/cooldown to using the Chainsaw dash, it was a little too easy to fly around the map killing dozens of trash mobs and getting health and armor. In many cases, it was more beneficial than using my weapons. I feel it should be another tool in the arsenal, but not a primary means of offense.The music also became noise after a while. It's always going at max intensity even when there's no action going on. Eventually I had to mute it and play my own music. What did me in was a bug I encountered in the final series of boss fights where the Cyber Maw boss stopped spawning after reloading a checkpoint -resulting in a progress blocker. I didn't care enough to restart the whole level to fight the previous bosses again just to get my progress back, felt like I saw enough of the game at that point. I might replay the game down the line when the game has less bugs.Despite my complaints, there is a lot of fun to be had here. When the game is at its highs, its insanely addicting. It is clear the amount of effort that was put into making the game fun. The game also has a lot of charm, humor, and homages to 80s/90s content.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is one of the most fun games I have played in recent times. _childDocuments_.review: Played the demo a while back and although graphics in the 90s looked good in the 90s, not sure people realise they don’t look so hot now. Anyway, the demo was reasonable fun so something to consider if it became cheap. Which it did, not from a Steam sale but a key reseller where I picked it up for just over £3. What the demo didn’t show me was that there would be parts where jumping became key to progress and that there would be a grappling hook introduced. Utter nonsense and ruined the game for me, several points I was close to giving up – spending almost an hour trying to get out of an area because the grappling was so difficult for me. I watched videos and people were moving around like Tarzan, but most of the time I could not grapple onto the 2nd point. So was I terrible at it, it is supposed to be difficult or something else? On the very last level there is a part where you need to grapple up a column and I had basically decided to give up on the game as it was proving impossible.Then I had a thought, this is a PC only game and I’m playing with a controller. Could it be that the game works better with mouse and keyboard and although a controller “works”, could it maybe not be ideal? This proved to be the case – it wasn’t easy with mouse and keyboard because I’m a controller person, but this made the difference between me giving up and completing the game – I used mouse and keyboard for the last bit of grappling and then returned to the controller.The game also suffers from not clearly showing you where to go, the jumping and grappling bits compound this problem as you don’t know where to go and it results in falling to your death with the fun of doing it all again. Not. This resulted in me checking videos on YouTube to see where I was supposed to be going. Do people find it fun dying over and over to work out what you should be doing? Certainly not my idea of fun.On the last chapter the developers really out did themselves. What could be more fun than increasingly difficult combat and poor jumping and grappling? Adding a time limit! What fun! Not only could you die because of the combat, find it extremely difficult to do the crappy jumping and grappling, but then also die if you do not complete it all within a set time. I mean, who wouldn’t enjoy DOING EXACTLY THE SAME THING OVER AND OVER AGAIN.One final slap in the face for me, I was playing this on easy and it was still damn difficult (unfortunately difficulty level had no impact on the jumping and grappling).Relieved to see the back of this. Deleting a game never felt so good!

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus Christ this is some impressive stuff. In its best moments it can give Doom Eternal a run for its money,The combat loop is excellent, you fly through the arenas at breakneck speed and use your whole arsenal all the time. None of the weapons and powers ever feel redundant and unnecessary, the balancing act is *chief's kiss* The pacing and set pieces are *almost* always top-notch too: there is something sick and distinctive in every single level. Even the vehicle sections are totally amazing, the bike and the mech ones especially.And it looks and sounds absolutely gorgeous, and it's mostly one guy project, are you kidding me?9/10===============================I hated the last two levels tho. They are the definition of an overkill (*ba dum tss*).The penultimate boss arena just drags on and on and on and on, way past the point of not caring. 12 stages. 12 gоddamn stages. With annoying platforming in between and Nihilanth-style teleportation to the separate arenas mid-fight. And *now* you decided to start punishing players for jumping-into-the-abyss, in the penultimate level, seriously?And there is the final level, when the game out of nowhere presents the most annoying gimmick in the entire thing - time trial fights. I was screaming at the screen at that point. And there is the sensory overload endless final boss after that. Your cute companion S.A.M even complains about it in game. Guys, if you felt the need to lampshade it - maybe just tone it down a little bit, huh? All of it left me exhausted in the end, and not the good kind of exhausted. And that a shame, the game this excellent deserved better send off than "thank god I'm done with it".

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: computer crashing issue has been fixed, my highest recommendation i could give on this game.original review:this game is genuinely amazing but equipping certain chainsaw augments straight up shuts my computer down. i'm only not recommending the game that causes such a massive issue like this but i know they will fix it. this is just a warning to new players that this could happen, and will instantly recommend after its fixed.TLDR: games a wonderful 9/10, but this game loves its most miserable unfun thing, maw.                                             !!!potential spoilers ahead!!!Review: you know that meme of a drawn horse being perfect all the way to the end being a child drawing? thats this game full stop.I think this game is genuinely amazing. super fluid, i feel in control of almost all my abilities, and that bike combat is so smooth, i haven't played a game with a better hoverbike since like perfect dark. the music matches the tempo of gameplay, most the weapons i used almost throughout the entire game, and also the pistol stays relevant for once in a shooter!there is genuinely so many small things i love in this, between small upgrades to your character making you feel more powerful all the way to the very end, unique designs, weapon utility, and enemy pool. i love most the arenas, this game never ever lets up, unless it needs to. at the beginning i was struggling, but by the end i was doing so good that almost nothing way that much of a challenge (dont worry though, if you stop moving they will absolutely kill you, its still very challenging).the hoverbike level by far had to be one of my favorite missions,  its just near perfect in everyway.its graphically beautiful, while keeping the aesthetic of what an old quake shooter wanted to look like, almost like how n64 renders were what Nintendo wanted you to imagine the blocky characters to look like on the system. and the music is a straight banger, i've listened to the so much out of the game, like i did with dooms music. the color pallet stays consistent, only the ladders are hard to find sometimes though. here are some things i'm iffy on, that doesn't really ruin anything but still takes me out abit. the car, its nice, but its kinda clunky, i kinda wish it had just a little bit more polish on the maps its in. cutscenes also feel way too floaty, and kinda weird (i know its a really small team making this and these don't effect the gameplay but i still wanted to mention it). some weapons don't really flow too well, like the ssg, i just feel it doesn't really warrant it in here, that being said i did use it alot, comboing the ssg+sg+ssg+rockets, but on its own just kinda felt weak.  the sniper while really cool just never really worked well outside jut hip firing (ill get back to that) its still a wonderful weapon, but the crosshair is kinda bad for sniping in this game being so small. the assault rifle upgrade though? overpowered. literally best weapon, dealing so much more than anything else, the only gun that can make noticeable chunks on boss health bars(ill get back to that as well) it just became my most used gun, with using the others for rotation clearings. the venders, you cant mute their voices and it was irritating hearing them after awhile lol. also i'm not sure if there's any sort of map, but i couldn't find it, and some places could really use something like one. turbo time also while nice i used once and then forgot it ever existed. just abit too many things in this game, but you know? there may be someone who loved that mechanic more than  the grapple, or other things. so while it didn't get used by me i could still beast the game with never using it.Now here's the teetering thing that effected me the most. MAW, his boss fights are bad and tedious, and not really in a challenging way. if there were no checkpoints in them id actually have to not recommend.  he eats so much ammo and has so many phases, with barely anything to replenish lost items. hes absolutely brutal if you try anything EXCEPT serious same back strafing away from him hipfiring the sniper. it mulches him, and not even the charged up shots, just the regular. it went from a genuinely brutal fight, to a braindead S+D+LMB simulator. beating the game, i have to say MAWs final boss level is garbage, awful looking character design, and miserable wannabe doom marauder. pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ garbage. its so bad that the last few levels with him he spawns in, in almost every combat encounter. hes not hard, hes boring and PADDING. his final fight sucks so badly. i genuinely hate that level with a passion just cause it literally goes on forever. you can only make an unintelligent knockoff of the marauder interesting for so long. and my god there being like what 10 phases to his uninteresting bossfight? its mind numbing. the only thing that dents him at all is that unbalanced assault rifle,. and i beg either balance the rest of the guns, or heavily reduce his health bar, cause its B O R I N G. i feel so bad bashing this lovely game so much here, but this game bashes me so badly in its last act.that was a chunk of things i wasn't fond of, but they are such a small chunk of the game(except maw)  and literally everything else has been p e r f e c t. i genuinely have high praise for the devs here. i cant stress enough how much fun i have had playing this. i plan on playing through again and again. _childDocuments_.review: It's impossible nowadays to play a arena boomer shooter and not compare to Doom Eternal or Ultrakill.I finished the game on the second to last difficulty, so my review is based on that.Turbo Overkill is super fun. You have more weapons than you can count, with many variations.They twist your gameplay all the time. New power ups, mods, vehicles, abilities, transversal moves. You can customize your experience like in Ghostrunner.Also, many movement options. Double jump, slide, wall run, grapple, rocket launch. You can grapple your rocket? Also there's a telefrag sniper? This feels like Quake on crack with ADHD, just go nuts.Game progression is good and will not make you feel overwhelm. Everything is gradually introduced to you.Story is good and the voicelines are funny. There's also many references and homages to other games and pop culture.The arenas are fun and well balanced, but the map design sometimes make you feel lost like a metroidvania game.There could be more interaction between your weapons and the enemies. Some enemies are just bullet sponges and could be more fight while in air. Also I hated every single homing missile enemies. Anything that explodes deals too much damage and sometimes you don't even know why you died.Game runs well on my PC. Loved the retro-cyberpunk-synth/vaporwave style.8/10 waiting for Turbo Overkill 2.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Turbo Overkill is a fantastic love letter to the retro FPS genre, the story is oddly charming with likable characters despite largely being an excuse for 'go here and shoot anything that moves', the soundtrack has no right that good, and most importantly it's just good old fun.However there are some flaws I had with my hours with Turbo Overkill. Some enemy types can feel quite bullet sponge-y, some levels can drag on for a bit more than they should, some checkpoints can be wildly inconsistent with the amount of enemies you're expected to fight through again, and some of the boss fights go overboard with the amount of phases they have.Overall it's a good time. _childDocuments_.review: For 2023, if CRPGs have Baldur's Gate 3 and action-adventure games have Tears of the Kingdom, first person shooters have Turbo Overkill. It's such a fantastic game for like 95% of its run time. Movement feels great and you're provided with a ton of options to spice things up like a grappling hook, two different dashes, wall hopping, and wall sliding. The level design is great, with some more linear levels and others that feel far more open. While you start off with only a measly single chainsaw leg, by the end of the game, all of your limbs are chainsaws; this is the closest thing to a Chainsaw Man game that we're gonna get for a very long time, if forever. Plus the neon dripping cyberpunk and 1980s synthwave aesthetic is excellent. The setting wears its inspirations on its sleeve, ranging from Blade Runner and Terminator to the pink and purple palm trees often found in vaporwave album covers. Also that soundtrack though, I keep going back to All Aboard the Pain Train and Sunset Synthetica because they're so catchy.I do have some complaints, despite this being one of the best games I've played in 2023. While Turbo Overkill has 22 levels that range from good to amazing, the last two levels feel very weak, partially due to the final two bosses. One has three exhausting phases and really should have been the final boss. The final level is just kind of mid until you get to the true final boss, which was shockingly weak for this game. One section of that boss is highly reminiscent of the Bed of Chaos's final section from the original Dark Souls, and that's not a good thing to be compared. There were also some glitches, including one door that wouldn't unlock at the end of a level (thankfully easily fixed with noclipping) and some of the collectibles in the last two levels not spawning for some reason (even more reason not to like those two levels). There's also some unlockable bonus levels too if you want to mess around some more, but I didn't like them as much as the main game.But that doesn't mean that the other 22 levels aren't great and worth experiencing for anyone who enjoys boomer shooters. This is easily one of my favorite shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill puts you in the cybernetic shoes of the titular Johnny Turbo, your not-so-everyday space merc that gets tangled into a struggle for controlling a powerful AI called SYN. Things do get out of hand really fast, and Johnny, willing or otherwise, will have to save the planet (and perhaps the galaxy as a whole) to ensure his own survival.It’s a story centered around the topics of greed, lust for power and all the other wonderful traits oh-so-common in us fellow humans. It’s not deep, nor complex, but it’s alright considering the genre at hand - if anything there’s an amount of lore and info superior to what could be expected from an old-school shooter to begin with. The quality of it is more than passable, with some highlights descending (ascending?) into the macabre and bizarre, of course peppered with coarse speech befitting lowlives, mercs and other scum inhabiting the neon-lit dystopia of Paradise.Tremendous care was put in building levels, not only on a functional design standpoint, but visually, too. The retro aesthetics, featuring purposefully washed-out palettes and low-res models, blend superbly with all the modern tech goodies as real-time lighting, physics and advanced effects. More than a few times, stages will have dynamic, evolving backgrounds where battles play out, destruction happens, and mayhem usually ensues. Despite its fast pacing, Turbo overkill lets its art direction be appreciated and enhanced in smart ways.In general, levels have a linear but wide structure that develops throughout multiple height levels (exceptions apply), and can even become quite complex. Most environments feel spacious enough to take full advantage of the diverse mobility options at Johnny’s disposal - options you will have to use, if you want to get all the various secrets and Easter eggs scattered in the most unthinkable recesses of this crumbling colony. Other than achievements for the serial pain seekers, secrets unlock interesting gameplay modifiers and secret levels for each chapter, so they’re definitely worth your time. For the rest, levels play out in the classic old–school fashion, which features color-coded keys, switches and at times objectives to clear, arenas to conquer before being able to proceed. The crown jewel of TO, combat is extremely fast paced, high-stakes and surprisingly deep. Only a few hits from stronger enemies will be enough to demolish you on the higher difficulties, but there are ways to counter that: a fluid, intuitive movement system comprised of sliding, dashing and jumping allows you to combine these features into acrobatic evasion, often granting you temporary i-frames that negate damage - even more so with specific upgrades. Your arsenal features weapons with multiple fire modes, each suited to specific situations and moddable with upgrades which alter, even significantly, their functioning. The bread-and-butter of combat is, however, Johnny’s signature chainsaw leg, a lethal slide-based melee weapon that will be critical to staying alive, as it’s one of the few ways to generate healing / armor from foes with the right upgrades - and since on higher difficulties medkits are only dropped from kills, you’ll need that a whole lot. A selection of gadgets, both offensive and defensive, will also be unlocked, like the micro-missile implant raining destruction on your foes, or the Turbo Time, slowing everything (including you) down and dropping extra goodies from each kill. Temporary upgrades boosting damage or even granting invincibility can be sparingly found in the more difficult arenas and sometimes bosses; you should save them for when crap really hits the fan. The arenas are challenging but fair, and feature multiple waves of enemies as customary. The checkpoint system is fair and respects your time while not being excessively forgiving: it strikes a great balance, and there’s also manual saving, although not at the higher difficulties.Boss fights evolve as HP goes down, and usually feature additional mobs in-between phases (and sometimes alongside the boss itself) - normally, a boss fight relying on “adds spam” would be a sign of bad design - however, in this case, Turbo overkill uses such enemies to give you a chance for recuperating HP and Armor, so it’s actually something to look forward to. Killing enemies will always drop coins, in turn used to buy Augments for both your cybernetic body and weapons. You’ll be able to decide your own “build”, and assign the augments you prefer to focus on offense, defense, utility or a mix of all these combined, based on each augment’s passive trait. Some of them can’t be bought, but are instead found in TeraTek crates, opened only with a secret key well-hidden in each level. Weapons are instead upgraded in a “straight” manner, gaining new functions and always being better versions compared to the previous one. It’s a compelling system that makes it worth it to get 100% kills in all levels, as well as secret-hunting for keys or money stacks, because you’ll definitely need all the cash to buy augments as soon as possible, on higher difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: This is FPS perfection; one of the best shooting experiences I've had in a video game. The weapons arsenal is incredibly powerful and varied; the movement/mobility is insane; the soundtrack is good and fitting; the vehicle sections were handled perfectly; the level design and art look pretty good, despite being low poly; the game is fairly lengthy (close to 20 hours for me); the story was decent, and the dialogue was genuinely funny at times.This easily stands alongside other giants in the FPS genre of recent times, such as DOOM: Eternal and Dusk, and I can easily recommend it to any FPS fan... unless you're the kind of person who thinks Call of Duty is peak FPS... for whatever idiotic reason...My only complaint is the final fight against Syn. Not giving it a boss health bar, like all other bosses made it a bit confusing, as I thought I had to kill her infinitely spawning henchmen to proceed. Also, giving the boss insta-kill death lasers, in a fight where you're unable to quick save is generally ♥♥♥♥-ish. Thankfully, this doesn't take away from the rest of the game's enjoyment factor.Easy 10/10 from me. Go play this game. Now!
