_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag. At its best, it's probably the best modern boomer shooter I've played. But at other times, it feels really half-baked. The difficulty is absolutely all over the place in a way that doesn't feel deliberate. I think a little bit more polish and play-testing would have gone a very long way.All that being said, I'd still recommend this game because it absolutely nails the most important things: weapon design and enemy variety. The guns look cool and feel fun to use, and there's a ton of different enemy types with varied behaviours. I also enjoyed the frantic movement - it's not exactly what I was expecting but it's fun and it feels right at home with the over-the-top cyberpunk setting.Finally, I have to shout out the almost perfectly placed checkpoints. This is, I think, the only boomer shooter (old or new) I've played where I felt like I could actually rely on the checkpoint system to put me back at a reasonable, fair save point when I died. It makes the game feel like a genuine challenge rather than a test of my ability to resist the urge to save scum through difficult fights. The game still does have quicksaves, so that might sound like an insignificant thing, but it had a huge impact on my enjoyment of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I came, I saw, and I kept sawing – and to think I almost skipped Turbo Overkill, figuring it was just one of the dozens of retro shooters that seemingly get released every single month these days... It is not! Instead, , and it should get way more attention than it’s getting at the moment! If you give this game a chance, it will utterly steamroll you with its countless awesome gameplay ideas, intricately designed lengthy missions, beautiful set-pieces and even a proper story that ties everything together without detracting from the gameplay side of things. .Turbo Overkill follows the high-mobility shooter style you may know from games like  or, more recently, . In stark contrast to id Software’s most recent release, however, . No forcing the player to use insta-kill buttons because of a ridiculously limited ammo capacity, for example – Turbo Overkill gives you all the tools you need, and then some!In fact, I think that ‘excess’ is the defining term I have in mind every time I think about Turbo Overkill. And I mean ‘excess’ in the most positive way possible! From boomsticks to orbital lasers, from grappling hooks to micro-missiles and from slow-motion to double-chainsaw berserk mode, . It even throws some vehicle missions at you – and manages to make those feel awesome instead of limiting, to boot!Level design is another area of Turbo Overkill best described with the word ‘excess.’ Sure, 25 missions spread across 3 episodes may sound like a pretty standard number, but , making me feel like I played double that number – with not a single dull second to be found. And I’m saying that as someone who tends to get a little tired of non-stop action after a while. Turbo Overkill held my attention throughout by  over the course of its 25 missions. And while I felt that , the fact that I never ran into a wall of frustration or boredom speaks volumes, as far as I’m concerned. And on top of its campaign, the game also has secret challenge maps and a feature for downloading user-created maps. Once again: ‘excess’, but in the most positive way possible!Perhaps surprisingly, another thing that kept me fully engaged with Turbo Overkill throughout were its story and the deliberately garish ' meets ' setting. Sure, the main plot about stopping a megalomaniacal AI isn’t exactly Shakespeare, but  – a genre where many devs notoriously just handwave all of that away. Turbo Overkill manages to have its cake and eat it too, as .At the end of the day, I’d be seriously surprised if Turbo Overkill doesn’t become a true shooter classic in time. ! Perhaps, like me, you’ll end up falling in love with a game that you almost skipped because you took a look at it and thought “just another retro shooter, I guess...”

_childDocuments_.review: The game start off simple - short levels and basic weapons that you know from all other shooters. The only gimmick you have is the chainsaw leg which is very useful because you can replenish health and armor with it. Given all that you might think that this is just another retro FPS... But then it just start giving you more, and more, and more...Weapons have secondary modes which can be completely different from the main mode (electro-burst on shotgun, grenade launcher on sawed-off, flamethrower on minigun, gravity gun on plasma gun etc; reminds of Painkiller) or you can unlock upgrades that add something new to the gun.When you get used to the game's basics it opens up, starting with a flying car section. Levels become bigger but not a chore to traverse because you also become faster (as a player and as a character).And it doesn't stop there. E.g. you get to jump on speedy cars and trains, ride through the whole city on the bike with miniguns and chainsaws, jump around the space from one ship to another and then ride a robot.The level and arena design is great, looks like new Doom games. It's hard to get lost, the game always show you where to go without relying too much on objective markers.Visually it's gory techo-body-horror stuff. The graphics are pixelated but it's noticeable only in static. The music is also great and fitting, hard stuff during the fights and more ambient when you just run around.All in all, this is the best FPS of 2023.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Turbo Overkill I feel like a weightless worm shooting a plastic gun at a shapeless mass of pixels and neon lights. _childDocuments_.review: Ugh, I hate to give this a thumbs down but I just can't groove with this thing. I may return later but I can't even bring myself to finish the levels currently in the game. The world design and general feel of the game is great but there's also a lot of annoyances that crop up after playing for even just an hour. The world design was what originally drew me in. The sound design and animation work on the weapons is superb, and the skyboxes are really a sight to behold. Lots of great secondary fires too, really love the pistol lock-on. Also, the chainsaw leg is obviously a blast. One of the best melee weapons in any shooter ever. It's tons of fun in the right levels and feels great to rev it up at high speeds. Unfortunately, level design is confusing and not full of a lot of clear indicators on how to progress. I spent a lot of times in these levels trying to track my way around and without a map it's very easy to get lost. There are also a lot of levels that require you to move very carefully too lest you get instakilled. Which is obnoxious when one of your most useful tools is the chainsaw leg which uncontrollably rockets you forward at 900 miles an hour. To add to the annoyance; good luck identifying any silhouettes during combat with this many particles flying around. It's excessive and you need to sort through a lot of visual noise in order to find what you are actually looking for. I can't tell you how many times I got killed by something I just could not see through the gunfire and explosions.To add to this, weapon damage and enemy balance is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Everything either does too much or too little. The double barreled shotgun in this game is an insult to all double barrels but it's alt fire does a ridiculous amount of damage. The SMGs feel way too inaccurate and do too little damage to be viable in a room with more than 3 enemies. The pistols too, that primary fire is so situational that the pistol is just going to become your occasional room clearer with the secondary fire. Enemies attacks are so fast and do so much damage even on just the hard difficulty that you can't afford to waste a second not putting enemies down which just invalidates so much of the current arsenal. The rocket launcher is pretty much the only thing that feels right, although even that feels like it should have a minor damage buff. It's a good base, but so many of the design choices and current balance of weapons makes everything feel off. I'd love to see the full release of this game dial in the level design a bit more, trim off a lot of the fat (Like seriously they don't need to be 30 minutes long). I would love to see a complete re-balance of the weapons and a visual overhaul to make enemies and their attacks more visible. I love dark cyberpunk aesthetic as much as the next guy but this is also a super fast shooter that requires split second reactions. And for godsakes get rid of that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dated upgrade system.

_childDocuments_.review: From the creator of Total Chaos, a horror Doom mod that's become a modern classic, we get Turbo Overkill. But don't let the developers previous Doom fame let you to believe that this is a derivative doom clone, what we have here is something crafted with lot's of love and passion. Turbo Overkill's first episode is a very solid first introduction to the game and its world. The game wears its sci-fi and cyberpunk influences on it's sleeve and you'll find lots of references both in the levels and in the story to popular movies and games.The level design is all incredibly well crafted, and it throws in some variety in a few levels just when navigating the cyberpunk cityscape starts to become a bit repetitive. There's a lot of enemy variety in episode one although a few can become tedious to deal with later on. The game starts off as a fair challenge and can grow to become pretty difficult in the last 2-3 levels. There were one or two difficulty spikes that seemed to come out of nowhere but hopefully the dev's decide to balance to those out in the future. Overall what's here is great, Turbo Overkill doesn't feel like a halfhearted attempt to mimic the first person shooters of days past so much as put it's own spin on that tired formula. Give this game a spin it's absolutely worth your time and money.

The enemies are mostly good; most serve a purpose in constructing a fight and all are instantly recognisable. The only enemies I don't like are the flying sentient poop holes, they never actually harm me they just annoy me and the buff ass TV head guys, they are essentially the same is the skinny ♥♥♥♥♥ that run at you but bigger and goofier. The only times I got lost in a level were more related to my soft pressed in skull rather than the game so I guess the level design is good. The game is a little bit too long; it feels 2-3 hours longer than it really needs to be. The bosses are kinda mid unfortunately, they all feel either extremely easy (i.e syn and that artifact ♥♥♥♥) or feel mildly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (i.e Maw and Ripper (Ripper only because I had to use the sniper and Maw because phase 1-2 are hard then 3-4 are piss easy)). Core mechanics and features need to be cleaned up, bugs need fixing, and some missions reworked.The core foundation provides a lot of potential but everything else on top of it harms the game. Still early release, so things may change.6.5/10Gameplay : Core loop = good but game mechanics don't work well together or not thought out well enough.Graphics : GoodMusic :  GoodStory : Arena shooterBeat EP 1 on level 4 difficulty. Stylized, so don't expect the most realistic anything.B/c it leans heavily into the Neon cyberpunk style, don't be surprised when you start having difficultly seeing enemies. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished the campaign and overall this game is pretty solid. If you're a fan of the "boomer shooter" type of FPS like Dusk, Amid Evil, Ion Maiden, Prodeus, etc then this is a pretty solid bet. Guns feel nice to shoot, you move at lightning speed, music is serviceable. Story is cheesy as expected, I mean if you watch the trailer you basically get what this game is. The name is Turbo Overkill for god's sake. My only complaint is the levels get to be a bit long and the game kinda wears out its welcome by the end. I put 15 hours into this and pretty much ran through levels as fast as I could the entire time, and by the 10 hour mark I was pretty done. Feels a bit weird to complain about TOO MUCH content, but a game like this needs a bit better pacing. I'd give it an 8/10 overall. Worth a buy, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best shooters I've ever played. Obviously a lot of comparisons will be drawn to Doom and Ultrakill, but I think this game outshines them. It's not hard as all heck if you play on a reasonable difficulty, but the high difficulties are suitably punishing. Every gun has at least one alternate fire mode which I freaking love. Every single level tries to introduce something new, whether it's an enemy, gun, ability, etc. Graphical style isn't just a novelty, it really helps with environment design and the feel of the combat. Every head explosion and insta-gib is very punchy and crunchy and feels like there's impact to your shots.The story actually has me hooked. Very little is revealed about our protagonist, and he can't speak, but I need to see this story to it's conclusion as I feel the bad guys are owed some serious payback. Most importantly, the soundtrack is banging. Every stage has it's own theme, and there isn't a single bad one. Furthermore each stage has a 'Half-way' or 'Third-of-the-way' point where the music shifts to an alternate version of the same track, usually just after you've acquired a new way to spell "♥♥♥♥ you" in your enemy's blood all over every nearby surface, so it ramps up the feeling of increasing in power ten-fold.Some detractors do exist. The game has differing versions of 'kill-floors' some of which actually mean instant death and some mean you get teleported back up in real time. It varies by stage and area, and it's fair, but nonsensical. The hardest difficulty can sometimes be a case of 'stop moving for 1 second and you die' but I'm enjoying the hell out of it and the checkpoints are mostly decent. There's no way to track WHERE the last few enemies are on the map if you're aiming for 100%. Everyone spawns in with a loud noise and a flash of light and will attack you relentlessly, so they're easy to see, but every so often you'll miss one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the corner of a room he blends in to. So far though I think 100% enemy kills is just for bragging rights. Lastly, and sad to end on a downer, the chainsaw bike is not as fun as you might expect. It's a cool feature but feels like a rollercoaster with no safety brake, not a part of the game you can master like the regular combat, It's only made one appearance though, so not a major impact on the experience.*Edit: they changed it to a hoverbike. It now handles 10x better and the entire level was revamped around it. This developer really cares about making this the best experience for it's community.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game and must play for single-player FPS enjoyers.Clearly borrows many things from other shooters like DOOM Eternal, even down to replicas of certain level set pieces, but in most cases Turbo Overkill improves the borrowed designs and does them better (I'm glad Glory Kills were not copied). Calling this a retro or boomer shooter does not fully entail that this game actually has very modern and innovative things going on, in some parts maybe even the most modern.Thoroughly very well rounded and clearly well gameplay tested product, but there are always things that could be better. While soundtrack is superb, gun and combat sound design was the weakest point in my opinion. Combat and projectile visual clarity and seeing what actually hit you is other thing, and in combination with lacking precise combat sound design, these can make it seem slightly unfair at times, as this game can be "rippy" how quickly you can die.Even thought the game is about AI Syn, enemy AI is not particularly impressive or dynamic, but it's not the worst either. Gun and chainsaw balancing is often brought up, but I didn't think it was that big a problem. There are many great guns and gun combos available, and weak chainsaw would probably end up being more annoying than powerful one. Also I understand pace changing with vehicle segments, but I wasn't too fond of these when general movement is so good in this game, that I only wanted to leave the movement limiting vehicles behind. Replayed all levels in hardest difficulty and cleared leftover achievements. Game still held great on second playthrough, although I'm glad that I didn't do hardest difficulty on my first playthrough, as it would have definitely diminished my thoughts about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fairly fun and well made game at the start. I really enjoyed the pacing and the story-telling. However, after half-way point story completely derailed and branched out which was quite confusing and made me forget about the entire plot.Then a lot of one-off mechanics were added, like flying car, motorcycle and mecha sequences that serves pretty much no purpose other than "why not".But the worst offender was the quests becoming mindlessly repetitive. You can easily tell the developer looked for a way to prolong the lifetime of the game to increase play hours, which is understandable. However, the way to achieve this was simply gimmicky and diluted the whole experience. Simply put, one mission is divided into 5 different parts. So instead of "shoot corruption to clear the path", it becomes "shoot corruption in 5 different spots to clear the path". This essentially makes you do the exact same thing 5 timesThis method gets exponentially worse in further levels where each of those objectives get their own branch of several other objective. For example, you need to destroy a terminal in 5 different locations. However, when you get to the terminal, you need to "kill" each terminal 5 times before the mission is completed. So what could be one mission artificially becomes 25 different mission.Apart from that, boss fights also become repetitive, where one boss has 3 phases and each phase has 5 separate healthbars. So you have to kill the same boss 15 times. You get the idea.The game was cool at the start but it overstayed its welcome. The meaningful part of the game is basically half the length of the entire playtime. If not for that problem, it would be quite a pleasant experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk is an interesting and often misunderstood genre.What seems like a fascinatingly bright and colorful aesthetic at first glance is often underlined beautifully with social commentary and thought-provoking propositions both subtle and upfront. Beneath the superficial gloss of neon paint and shining lights, you will often find biting criticism of politics, corporations and capitalism. Dig a little deeper, and you will find yourself pondering more abstract quandaries; how much machine can you be, before you cease to be human? Does the thought experiment of Theseus' Ship apply to human? A well-written cyberpunk setting can leave those that engage with it thinking; about the self, about one's life, about where we're headed, where we came from, and about the nature of man itself. A masterpiece will have those that engage with it asking questions the game never directly proposes upfront. This game in particular poses one question about humanity, and so I  ask:Why on earth did it take us  long to name a man , strap a chainsaw to his leg and give him a crouch slide that turns people into red goo?The story premise is as simple as it could be; you're Johnny Turbo. Your left arm is robotic, your right leg is a chainsaw, and you get paid off to put a stop to the machinations of the AI Syn, whose major plan is to merge machines and man into one being. To this end, bio-cores have sprung up all over Paradise; a dystopian, neon-lit city of artificial pleasures galore, where flying cars zoom by at blistering speeds, where night-time is illuminated by billboards and bright signs, and where the horizon is a glowing mess of advertisement boards the height of skyscrapers. An already dystopian city, giving off a seedy vibe, and yet it pales in comparison to the future Syn has in mind for humanity. Throughout ruined buildings and along the brightly lit city streets, you'll encounter its increasingly nightmarish minions everywhere. These range from human thugs spliced with somewhat minor augmentations and brandishing conventional firearms or having their limbs replaced with limbs or guns directly all the way to more-  creations; barely humanoid mounds of flesh hopping on all fours and dispensing lethal amounts of electricity, augmented people ripped in half and still animated by the power suit strapped to their bodies and towering, worm-like technopedes armed with rockets and an ocular laser beam bolted onto a quadrupedal platform carrying its immense bulk around.Naturally, though, a game like this couldn't just let the enemies outdo a man like Johnny Turbo on the weaponry front, so you bring to bear your own little arsenal of augments and guns, the most basic of which are a pair of akimbo pistols with a homing secondary firing mode that, if charged for a sufficient amount of time, will vaporize lesser enemies in an instant. A lot of conventional weapons are present and accounted for even in Early Access; shotguns both pump action and sawn off, sub-machine guns, a minigun, a rocket launcher, and all come with an optional upgrade adding a secondary fire mode that you can spend your hard-earned money on. Could I interest you in an electric blast upgrade for your shotgun that stuns most enemies, leaving them vulnerable for easy dispatching? I don't have to, it's on the house, go ahead and give it a go.How about that twin minigun, bit too reasonable for your taste? How's about you pop off those barrels and use it as a flamethrower instead? With how close and personal the fighting tends to get, you'll appreciate having the option.Now, for the important bit; would you want to pay 2500 dollars for the ability to throw away one of your akimbo SMGs? ...Well, you should, because it comes with a lifetime supply of backup SMGs to pull back out in case you want to sacrifice accuracy and damage for spraying and praying again.And all of that isn't to speak of the upgrades for your cybernetic limbs that can further tailor your playstyle; do you want your chainsaw leg to be your main tool of engaging? Pop an augment in that increases the movement speed when sliding; damage is based on speed, so you're less likely to get stuck in hordes of enemies as you plow through, too, as a little benefit. Or you use it for sustain, and make it recover health and armor with each enemy killed? Perhaps you're not overly fond of the chainsaw leg in general; why not slap a mod in that makes you send out a shockwave after falling for a certain distance?There's plenty of options and they're all amazing. Combat simply feels good; the weapons are nice and meaty, movement feels great, enemies hit hard but always seem fair and manageable. Whether you blow someone apart with a sawn-off shotgun blast to the face or slice through a group of weaker enemies with a crouch slide like the Reaper through a field of wheat, feedback is nice and meaty. In short, despite only having one episode out so far, the game is already  promising; and not in that unfortunately common Early Access-way where it's an "everything is off but the idea of the game is nice so might as well give it a thumbs up I guess, hope it improves"-sorta deal, no. Things feel , they feel . You can tell a lot of care and effort went into making things feel good; it's a very inspired game, with a team that knew what they wanted to do, and by Jove, .It is  one of the best throwback shooters I have seen so far.Also it features a man called Johnny Turbo.Did I mention that? Because that's worth a recommendation alone.

_childDocuments_.review: READ THIS REVIEW IF YOU'RE CONSIDERING BUYING THIS GAME. (its so good.)-I got bored one day, so bored, that I decided to see if there was any action packed games on the Steam Store, turns out I had never played the beautifully crafted and intense game that IS Turbo Overkill. It's like if you took Doom Eternal and Far Cry: Blood Dragon and shook them up in an adrenaline junkie trademarked blender from a sketchy cross-fit store. ----PROS: * Doom Eternal Mechanics, Jump, Cut, Slide, Grapple, and KILL. * Fast Paced Action, AND I AM NOT OVER EXAGGERATING, ITS FAST ASF* Take control of Deadly Vehicles that you couldn't in Doom* Sickest and Coolest Motorcycle chase scene ever* The Villains are your classic Cyberpunk Comic Characters, and their designs are KILLER* Boss Battles that will either break you, or boost your confidence * Annoying Enemies that will make you want to go back and finish them off* CHAINSAW LEGS* Skill System and Weapon Upgrades that truly make you feel like a bad ass* Beautiful and Colorful Synthwave Environments * Story-line that mixes Movie References with Classic Futuristic Media * CHAINSAW HANDS* Robocop type Revenge Plot with a rage quit inducing boss battle (its still a lot of fun)* Everything else. This Game is and was Brilliant, and I bought it on a whim cause I was BORED. ----CONS:I don't see a Turbo Overkill 2 yet.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is another hyper-fast boomer shooter, which have been coming up a lot recently - Ultrakill, the new DOOM games, etc. So what makes this one different? Well, firstly, the style and story are actually fairly interesting. The grungy, cyberpunk aesthetic city is dirty and gritty, but also it's full of life and has a real feel to it. The environments all feel like true places.Additionally, the gimmicks that it comes up with are fantastic and unique. I use "gimmick" here positively - I don't want to ruin them here, but there are constant new ideas and ways the game interacts with you.And to top it all off, there's the traditional New Blood seal of quality - movement and gunplay feels amazing, everything looks great despite the low resolution, and the minute-to-minute gameplay is so much fun. The guns are fun to shoot, and the enemy encounters are built for the perfect challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥. Yes.Jazzed up Doom Eternal gameplay in a cyberpunk future with beautiful neon pixel art.Could not tell you anything about the story, didn't pay attention. Seems deliberately over the top and cheesy. Gameplay is smooth, fast, vertical, and rewards skilled quickswapping. Staying airborne for huge portions of combat is possible and satisfying. The grapple leaves a little to be desired when compared to Doom's meathook.Occasionally forgot about some of my weapons and abilities but generally I used all of them. Loved augmentations and upgrade system.Wish the wallrunning was better incorporated into arenas but that's because I'm still waiting for Titanfall 3.There was a bizarre fog in a couple levels that I assume was a glitch but aside from that there were no technical issues on my 8 year old machine.There are a handful of level designs and combat encounters that took clear inspiration from Doom Eternal; this might be offensive if they were done poorly or if the game didn't stand on its own two chainsaws but it does so it feels more homage than theft.Any complaints are nitpicks. Delivered exactly what I expected and nearly everything I want from a movement shooter. Absolutely incredible.plz buy

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best retro shooters even though it's not retro, it's actually closer to DOOM Eternal.Combines a whacky premise with great gameplay mechanics, insane speed and hordes of enemies.Leveldesign is good but due to the insane speed of the game there are hardly any breathers. With a runtime of 12+ hours for a hyperfocused campaign means the game is exhausting after a while and one should take breaks while playing.Even though the leveldesign continously varies between full on assault, movement & jumping passages and even vehicle sections that are not annoying the game runs out of steam a bit in its final chapters and I was happy I had finished the campaign when I did. Maybe some radical mood shifts and tempo variation within its already lenghty maps would have helped that a bit.My main gripe with the game would be that the weapons themselves feel kinda weak. Not necessarily actually weak even though the Double Barrel and the Plasma kinda are before they get their upgrades, no, it's the design themselves. The weapons lack that meaty, punchy feel. The rocket launcher feels like I popped a water balloon in someone's face. Causing an explosion that gibs a half dozen thugs from a jump off a building shouldn't feel like I performed a long jump in a high school competition. Combat sometimes lacks a responsive "oomph".All in all, good game, 8.5/10PS: Rockets vs player imba
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute blast.  Everything you've ever looked for in a Boomer Shooter except this is way more than that.  For it's genre it has all of the usual: retro graphics, high octane fast and furious, tons of enemies, bloodbath, find the secrets, find the exit and so on.  What separates it is that it incorporates a lot of today's gaming but in a much more streamlined, simpler way consistent with the game.  The game takes place in a corrupt, Cyberpunk world and your job is to clean the bad element.  In addition you also have a score to settle.  It's a nod to Cyberpunk 2077 and Ghostrunner.  It contains RPG elements similar to it and it's complexity is relative to the game.  Weapons can be upgraded, your character has a skill tree you build up as you go along and there is a story to follow.  The weapons look great, they sound great, the overall game looks really good and it all just fits so well.  There are definitely some challenges in that the game is very vertical for lack of a better word.  Moving around involves a lot of ultra high jumps, running on walls, a lot skillful maneuvering.  This aspect I wasn't crazy about but all in all I am having a great time.  Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Remember when games used to be fun? This one does. At first I wasn't enamored because the enemies were a little mid, but it turns out they aren't supposed to be Halo elites- they're just fodder for your many, many toys. They just keep giving you cool explody toys and all the room in the world to play with them.Great map variety, and design. One problem I usually have with these retro shooters is that I'm often getting lost due to samey level textures and no map. Not here, the directions are always plain as day because either bright neon doors aren't open yet or enemies are spawning in X direction. This keeps the momentum going and dodges a common pitfall.Speaking of, the movement in this game is ridiculously cool. You have a chainsaw dash that is omnidirectional, plus two jumps and two dashes you can use in the air, plus other goodies I won't spoil. And the level design lets you use ALL of it. You are soaring through the air blowing up baddies and the devs don't care if you ever touch the ground again.Story is a fun backdrop for all the killing you're doing, but what they nailed is the constant escalation. You are always going to more and more ridiculous places and killing bigger and badder dudes. Vehicular sections are fun and don't overstay their welcome.The one issue I had is that some bosses are small and so fast that I have a hard time hitting them under normal conditions. Other than that it's an incredibly good time. Game just lets you have fun- a must-buy if you like retro shooters with an emphasis on mobility
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: One can compare this to many games (dusk, necromunda: hired gun, EYE divine cybermancy, doom eternal, ultrakill) but honestly it seems to beat out all the competition by incorporating their elements into a more cohesive and fine tuned experience than any of them. I think this might be the best first person shooter made in modern times be they retro inspired or not.Movement is fast, fluid and responsive and the speed is insane. The best thing about this is that the levels are clearly made with this mobility in mind being very large scale and accommodating to the mobility of the player. Often times you'll find yourself backtracking through levels finding other paths thanks to how non linear they are, running into newly spawned enemies guarding a door you previously weren't able to open.The way the game handles these enemy encounters is great too, rarely ever do you run into anything you could call a bullet sponge, instead most of the difficulty comes from evasion and quantity of enemies and it allows you to fully utilize the movement freedom you've been given, including a chainsaw-leg-slide boosted by rockets that can one-shot hordes of cannon-fodder. In-short this is a fast game about flow where a couple hits of enemy fire can mean the end in mere seconds. The weapons at your disposal are entertaining, each having an alternate firing mode to switch to that greatly alters the behavior of the gun. Some even feature three firing modes.The game also features an upgrade system that allows you to add behaviors and traits onto your body parts through cybernetic augmentation. These are meaningful and tangible effects that really influence how you play the game and change things up. An example is the ability to wall jump, another is adding extra chain explosives to the rockets from your rocket glove.Vehicle sections are placed evenly throughout the campaign and do a great job of breaking up the pacing by switching up the gameplay a bit, they're very entertaining.Graphically the game is serviceable, looking just about good enough for them to be able to carry the visuals through often solid and other times downright inspired art direction and the game runs very well.The story is simple and the tone is campy and over the top, being mostly there to set up the gameplay but it does escalate further and further as a relatively local conflict balloons into something much grander in scale.The music ranges from solid to great being made up of mostly synth/rock blends and during the final third of the game it incorporates orchestral elements that work surprisingly well and are somehow reminiscent of lotr and the matrix trilogy. Definitely get it, even not on sale, if you're at all a fan of fast paced shooter action you'll probably love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fast paced and fun, the world is colorful, and the game has a sense of humor that long time FPS players will definitely appreciate. Are the graphics up to 2023 AAA standards? No. Are they trying to be? Also no, and this isn't a game with a AAA price tag and then three different DLCs available within a month of launch. The value per dollar is excellent, and I hope more games adopt this model.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a Doom Love Letter but BETTER! The Game is silky smooth, the weapons is like an outstanding remix of the Doom Weapons, etc. This game is a MUST have! The story VERY well written and ties in perfectly to each level. Even the character and the game itself has the old school graphics mixed in with the modern graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I just directly started on the hardest difficulty, didn't even try the easier ones - so these comments are specifically about the hardest difficulty.You can die 0.2 seconds after making a minor mistake, but after your death, you pretty much always know what you did wrong. I practically always knew what I should change to avoid doing the same mistake on the next round. I like this.The checkpoints are common enough and respawning is fast enough, that sometimes getting through a fight can feel similar to Super Meat Boy - reset after reset, until you figure out a working route. It can arguably feel a bit frustrating and "trial & error" at times, but on each death I always feel like I learned something new about the particular fight.The amount of "trial & error" also goes down as you keep progressing through the game, as you become more familiar with the level design / enemy placement philosophy as a whole.---A comment about the weapon design: many weapons have primary fire which feels like the same machine gun with different bullets. All weapons have secondary fire modes, which are fun and quite unique - but I feel like the primary shots could've also been a bit more different from each other.Basically if I make an active choice to pick a certain weapon for the current fight, it's because I think their secondary mode fits well for the particular enemies - not because of the primary fire. I guess it's fine this way too.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Where more and more companies are content in not meeting expectations and charging out the butt for newer games (And don't forget the micro transactions), Turbo Overkill constantly ups the ante. Introducing new game play elements and inventive set pieces, and having a sizable amount of baddies to fight. Not to mention a lot of the setting and monster design is downright inspired. This is a game I would whole heartedly recommend to new and old gamers alike. For a while, my interests was waning on video games, but Turbo Overkill has renewed my love for games. Thank you Apogee.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill delivers an enjoyable retro 90s style gameplay experience set in a captivating dystopian cyberpunk world. While the graphics may appear basic by today's standards, the heavy useage of lightning effects and over-the-top violence and gore elevates the overall aesthetic to perfection. The soundtrack complements the action well, and the challenging difficulty keeps you engaged throughout the game.Overall, it's an exhilarating experience that truly embody the spirit of of the 90s fps genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turning my review from negative to positive, now that I figured out what was wrong with wall running (you have to hit the wall at a steep angle, wasn't a bug at all). Anyway, this is one of the best, most addictive, fast-paced, and awesome boomer shooters on the Steam store, so pick up a copy right away.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece, up there with the likes of Half Life, Doom 2 and Duke Nukem 3D. And I'm not even being hyperbolic. It genuinely is that good. It's a modern classic and I don't doubt people will be talking about this game for years to come.I could sit here and nitpick all day - the second act drags a little bit towards the end and for some reason the game froze for me after the end credits rolled - but these issues don't detract in any way from just how polished the game is. It's a masterclass in boomer/movement shooter action. The developers understood the assignment. They knew what the audience for this genre wanted and they delivered.Map design is unbelievably tight and well thought out. All the weapons are fun to use and remain relevant until the end of the game. Enemy design is fun and they compliment each other perfectly. Visuals are fantastic, music is S tier, voice acting is flawless from start to finish. I just can't fault any of it.Just when you think you've seen it all the game throws another pleasant surprise at you. It just doesn't seem to end.If you're into boomer/movement shooters you *have* to get this. This isn't game of the year, this is game of the decade.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game, this game might actually be my favorite shooter. It's so well rounded and the ideas are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. The way that the grappling hook is on a cool down separated from a gun makes the game feel so much more organic as well. The movement feels way too good in this game, it's like a crime. This game is definitely a must have and I would directly competes with Doom Eternal and Ultrakill for the best shooter I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: The movement here feels amazing.  Tons of mobility options to zoom around levels quickly, including the famous chainsaw leg slide.  The campaign is surprisingly long and it Just. Keeps. Escalating.  The writing is good enough for a laugh or two.There is some jank here, though.  I got stuck in a wall post chainsaw slide a couple of times during the campaign, but a quick reload at the last checkpoint was painless enough.  There are some vehicle sections and the polish on the vehicle controls just isn't up to the rest of the game.  The sound design could be improved to make the weapons sound more impactful.None of that makes me regret my money or time spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Fast as hell. Cool ass level design and cyberpunk graphics. Very polished EA game. It's an oxy moron I suppose, but I hope you get what I mean - I'm loving the "modern retro shooters" that we've gotten where they take that old school FPS and blend it with modern mechanics. Turbo Overkill nails this in my opinion and I highly recommend it.Also chainsaw leg. I mean, c'mon.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Major Pros:1. Nails the feeling of becoming more powerful over time better than most other games I've played, especially other boomer shooters. Actual RPGs need to take cues from this game on how to make the player start small and feel like a god by the end.2. Lots of freedom to define your playstyle since the game has strong customization that lets you favor specific parts of your kit and every weapon has some way to deal extreme damage.3. This game is a must-play simply to see just how over-the-top and insane the setpieces get. Turbo Overkill is the definition of a game that's as cool in reality as it is in your head.4. Most of all, it's just a super fun game to play. Clearing out varied enemy encounters in varied environments is simply some of the most fun I've ever had in a video game, and it would be enough to make me recommend the game even if it didn't have great aesthetic and storytelling qualities.Pros:1. Great music, visuals, weapons, voice acting2. Extending off that last bit, it's really cool to see great cutscenes in a game like this. They follow a similar formula to Doom 2016/Eternal and have a similar sort of appeal with giving the player's avatar a lot of personality without saying a word. The very definition of doing more with less.3. Turning the slide into a melee attack is very clever, I like it even though I kinda miss not having a regular melee weapon.Cons: 1. Enemy readability isn't great. You look at a mess of metal and body parts and need to figure out in half a second whether you're looking at an enemy you're supposed to close the distance on or stay away from. The biggest issue is that the pump shotgun's alt-fire is the strongest attack you have against half the enemies and is useless against the other half. Figuring out which is which in the heat of the moment can be hard and obnoxious.2. Especially near the end of the game, the levels take FOREVER. Like over 30 minutes per level. They could have easily been 15-20 with just a bit of fat-trimming. I'll admit that this makes the experience seem grandiose and epic with how much endurance each level requires, but it still can test your patience.3. Bosses are pretty lame. Not horribly lame, but not great either. Mainly it's just that there's not a ton of middle-ground between the bosses being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and way too easy. And no matter which one you're up against, they're going to be way too bullet-spongy.Major Cons:1. If retro shooters want to bring back having 10 weapons while also introducing a bunch of character abilities that need their own keys, they need to step up their game with making the controls accessible and sensible. Pressing 7 to switch to a weapon in the middle of a fight is ridiculous, and the player should not be responsible for finding a sensible bind for it. Combine this with the weapon wheel being weirdly laggy and delayed, taking like half a second to appear after you start holding Q, and the game's combat ends up a lot less accessible than it should be. In particular I have a bone to pick with binding micro-missiles, an ability you need to hold down to use, to Mouse3, a button that's very difficult to hold down.2. So if the controls are the biggest issue with the game, why don't I just rebind them? Well that brings us to the second biggest issue with the game: Spoilers in the menu. The primary appeal of Turbo Overkill is this unparalleled feeling of anticipating what insane things will happen next in the story and gameplay. This part of the experience would be massively damaged if you knew exactly which enemies and weapons would be around the next corner. Unfortunately, the resources the player has available spoil exactly that. Rebinding your weapon and ability keys in the menu requires you to tactically not look at most of the options unless you want to be spoiled on the insane superweapon you get in Act 3 while you're rebinding your micro-missiles halfway through Act 1. The worst by far is the beastiary. I hope you don't think to follow the tooltips telling you to learn more about the enemies in the beastiary, because for some reason they have all the enemies from Acts 2 and 3 while you're still in the middle of Act 1.

_childDocuments_.review: Go 500 mph and shred everything, or get shred, or explode, or fall off a cliff, or fly a flying car, or Level Up Your Eyes, or use a chaingun flamethrower, or telefrag people with your sniper rifle, or get annihilated by the highest difficulty, or get lost in the levels because they are full of secrets.But mostly go 500 mph.If you're scared of going fast, don't buy this. Or do it, and finally be free.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic shooter and an amazing modder success story. I've been following Sam's work for sometime now and seeing him graduate into the indie scene with this bombastic shooter is amazing. In early access this is already buying as it stands, nevermind that there's almost twice the initial level count in secret levels, many unlockable features that change play style considerably, and that this is one of the greatest of the new wave of retro shooters. Dripping in charm, oozing with violence and pulsating with style, this is an indie shooter you should buy not only to support the work of a hobbyist-turned-professional, but for yourself - because god forbid you never get the chance to experience Turbo Overkill first-hand.EDIT: Turbo Overkill is my game of the year. Easily.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't put my finger on it. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favourite genres, so I really wanted to like Turbo Overkill but I just couldn't get into it at all.Experience:I breezed through the first handful of levels in 30 minutes without any challenge from the enemies, the biggest obstacle being the environment which all blended together which killed the pace when back tracking was required.Core Mechanic:The sliding mechanic is a nice idea, but in my experience it was WAY too OP, and given your seemingly unlimited arsenal there just wasn't any friction; I was plowing through the enemies with no issue but also without much satisfaction.Aesthetics:I also bounced off the aesthetics which felt really unfocused to me; a cute robot on the walkie talkie, a military guy smoking a joint on the main page, the borderlands inspired vending machines and the enemy design all felt like they were pulled from different IPs in a way which, for me, didn't come into an interesting whole.imo new age movement shooters like Ultrakill, post void and Chop Goblins do this genre right; simpler and more focused. Turbo Overkill just didn't scratch that itch for me; simply ending up with a load of cool mechanics and ideas crushed together into one over produced and scatterbrain package.

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic game minus the fact i somehow played the entire game on "steam deck" graphics level quality, which made every level seem like i had cataracts and weapon feedback was terrible. i only figured that out and fixed it during the final level. thanks game.also, the language defaulted to russian, and i had quite a time trying to fix that.suffice to say, personally, not a good first impression. but, besides those two problems, it was pretty damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most fun first-person shooters out there and it is not even finished yet. It fully commits to its charming Cyberpunk aesthetics, and it is glorious to look at. Also, you have a chainsaw for a leg. Do not sleep on this one. It already has plenty content, and they will add one more chapter in 2023. I reckon it will be quite popular at release.

_childDocuments_.review: I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game, hands down has to be my favorite game right now. The guns are super great, the augments that you put on your character are really fun, the bit of driving you do in the game controls really well, the soundtrack is absolutely amazing and never gets repetitive, it's really challenging and really puts your skills to the test. I HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone that likes games like, Doom, Ultrakill and Dusk. This game is more then worth the price, And for there being only 2 chapters out so far, the game is still Incredibly long. If you like high speed, non stop, fps games then this is definitely for you. 12/10 will replay this over and over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a game that has weaponized movement as well as this game and it is absolutely phenomenal to play! Once all of the movement upgrades have been unlocked gravity is more of a suggestion as you weave around the map like an angry hornet bisecting enemies with your chainsaw leg. The weapon selection is great for an old school shooter, and there are some fun and unique options thrown in, like a telefragging sniper rifle or an orbital laser(that works everywhere). All of them served various niches and felt well designed and satisfying to use, although I'm not exaggerating when I say I killed at least 80% of enemies in the game(hardest difficulty) with the cheggs. Not only is sliding around cutting people in half a blast, but with the right upgrades it's not only viable, but one of the best weapons in the game! Also, you can grapple onto your own rockets!Level design was nicely done, and I appreciated all the platforming sections, it would've been a tragedy to have such beautiful movement mechanics and not get to flex them. Speaking of which I would 100% play a version of this that was just platforming too, love me some first person platforming! There were a good variety of areas and the developers did a good job of exploring some fun locations while still fitting the cyberpunk theme. The  freeway/train fight, fighting through a debris field in orbit trying to escape the planet, and Vector-4 where all some immediate standouts as far as cool locations go. Few games can make going this fast this fun! I would strongly recommend this one if you have a need for speed, or just want a quality retro shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Despite playing more Boomer shooters this year(2023) than I've played my whole life, I feel that none have really expanded upon the genre like Turbo Overkill. It really scratches the itch that DOOM Eternal's base game and TAG1 left. Side note I found this game from a facebook ad of all placesOne of my favorite games ever
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Every aspect of this game is really really good. If you like cyberpunk and over the top plot of some sci fi and action films and boomer shooters you will 100% gonna love this game however, I encourage you to follow patch notes before attemting or playing on higher difficulties sometimes developer's finger slips or something and currently in murder machine difficulty even the basic low tier enemies deal 5 times the damage of your entire healthbar. This kinda stuff might make you think this game is really bad but it really isn't it is just one man developer sometimes struggle with too much work he has to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimate crossover of Duck Nukem, DOOM, Blade Runner and Dredd. Love this. A nice blend of modern and retro FPS games. The demon was badass so I pretty much had to buy this. To the devs: Thank you for this fine piece of art. Loving the super shotgun with the infinite grenade launcher attachment. The best Cyberpunk game in so long. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know anything about this game going in besides "fps", so imagine my surprise when I found something so clearly in conversation with both modern Doom, original Doom, and the progression of first person shooters through the early-mid 2000's. This game wears its references on its sleeve and is all the better for it, delivering ultra-refined visceral flowstate arena combat - this is where it apes Eternal most directly; however, resource management's existance is not laborious or stressful in the slightest, but instead a gentle nudge towards variety, more firmly than 2016 but kinder than Eternal. Enemies do not require specific hard counter weapons allowing for more flexibility in approach, and changing your routine up rapidly feels optimal and flashy but not mandatory in the way it did in Eternal - where favoring one or 2 weapons basically didn't work.The movement here is similar to Eternal as well, and feels just great. The chainsaw legs are an excellent mechanic implimented well - aside from the damage component, you can shoot while sliding in arbitrary directions; the potential for interesting combinations of movement and abilities seems tremendous. I will say that the grappling hook is nowhere near the level of satisfying Id have achieved in Eternal though! Beyond the comparisons to modern Doom, the game's tendrils snake back through time drawing tropes and mechanics from the aforementioned influences and many more, as is apparent from the start through its presentation, to things life seamlessly integrated free-movement vehicle combat sections throwing me right back to Half-life 2 and its episodes.This is a game willing to pluck the best ideas from many moments through time and mush them into something greater than the sum of its parts, which is often the abstract ideal for boomer shooters but RARELY realized with such precision and intent, all while weaving in a lot of truly original and surprising mechanics, ideas and moments through the beefy campaign. To read the above and conclude this is a derivative game would be misguided - the developers have a deep and clear understanding of what makes an FPS fun, and have built on the shoulders of the best possible giants to their own ambitious goals. I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys fast shooters. The only ding I would really give would be occasional awkward dialogue and somewhat cluttered storytelling, but it really, really did not impact my enjoyment of this tremendously fun and inventive game.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent and very underrated boomer + story-shooter. Similar mechanics to Doom Eternal or Ultrakill with its unique art- and visual style set in a depressing Cyberpunk/Blade Runner world named Paradise. As a street cleaner, your job's cleaning the city of the so-called Syn virus. The story is good enough and becomes attractive over time. The game is divided into three chapters underlined with varied gameplay passages and levels. Clean movement and shooter mechanics with cleverly designed guns, all fitting for different situations, are building up to a solid gameplay foundation. Paired with a chainsaw leg, you will find yourself dominating a large horde of enemies while listening to the banging soundtrack surrounding it. Upgrades for components of your body can be bought and applied, along with purchasing a secondary gun mode for each one. Thanks to the well-thought-out level design, the game always feels fresh with new ideas, armory, and gameplay passages. Overall, it is a great game, with the only flaw being the music banging 24/7 instead of only in fights, making it feel more like background music. Give this game a go if you like other fast-paced shooters or shooters! Such a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: If I didn't get lost in FPS games easily, I'd rate this a 10/10.Unfortunately, unlike Doom (and other games in the Doom series), it lacks a map. I will easily get lost for a while in stages if I don't have a nudge to point me in the right direction. Eh. I've got issues and suck, but the game is very, very good. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all of the boomer shooters - this one stands head and shoulders above them all. A perfect fusion of old and new FPS design sensibilities makes for a game that is unbelievably  satisfying to play due to very strong balancing between your vast and ever expanding arsenal and the hordes enemies and their combat behaviours and encounter design. Every gun and fire mode has a place in the combat puzzle, as does every enemy in forcing your behaviours., much like doom eternal, but lacking the restrictiveness of that title.  Couple all these positives with razor sharp control, outstanding level design, rapid movement and utterly engaging shooting mechanics and you have FPS nirvana. Absolute must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: If Titanfall 2 and Doom Eternal had a baby, this would be that game. Combat is fast-paced, never overstays its welcome. Enemy variety is diverse, with boss fights being fun and well-spaced.Everything feels very punchy; pixellated gore and absurd visuals in low-res create a visual masterpiece that is just as big of blast to play as your micromissiles. The soundtrack is phenomenal, too; every level has at least a decent track, with some exceptional ones like Sunset Synthetica. Turbo Overkill is a 10-12 hour FPS experience; try it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal. This is the perfect combination between Doom Eternal and Ultrakill. If you enjoyed either of those games, or both of them, play this. The level design is amazing, the enemy density is perfect, and you feel like a god if you can master the movement. The game never stops throwing new mechanics and goodies at you to keep the gameplay loop feeling fresh and saturated. I cannot believe I found this game at a monitor display at PAX west. Amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is easily the best FPS game we've had since Doom Eternal, full stop. It almost doesn't feel like an indie game just because of how quality it is. It's movement is so smooth and so fun it puts most other movement shooters to shame. Tons of crazy weapons and enemies, and the chainsaw leg mechanic is really fun to mess around with. The campaign is about 11 hours which is super long for an indie FPS and the story/characters are pretty well done too. You can tell the guys making this just wanted to make something awesome and they succeeded in my books.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, feels like DOOM Eternal but much faster. It also have nice and surprising (in good way) level design. It has much of variety of weapons and tricks. Recommending it for everyone who likes fast shooters where u feel yourself like harbinger of death to everything. Thank you developers it's very good game, wish u all the best!
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is well deserving of its success, being a true bargain for the amount of content it provides.Paying homage to the sci-fi/cyberpunk genre with several on-the-nose references to films like Robocop and The Terminator, It does not shy away from its inspirations. Respectfully and masterfully, it delivers an experience that is a cut above the rest in a long list of retro style shooters sweeping the market.Yet despite all this, I must stress one important criticism I have, in that it suffers from a lack in moderation. The game runs a bit too long, culminating in a finale that left me exhausted when it was all over. I think after the 10 hour mark, my brain felt like it was just spinning a bare-tread tire in place in an attempt to cross the finish line.In summary, Turbo Overkill is a testament to what indie developers are capable of, but ultimately lets their passion for game design get a bit carried away. Still, I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Should you buy Turbo Overkill? 100% yes! It's easily one of the best FPS game of the past five years, especially if you love Doom Eternal or Ultrakill then it's a no brainer. But that doesn't mean it's flawless, actually, not only it's flawed to the bone, it's also a buggy mess. Plus, 19hrs into the game, my save files got corrupted and lost all my progress. Fortunately though Sam Prebble, the lead developer, was kind enough to sent me a save file on Murder Machine so I could continue my game without starting again.In my opinion the worst part of TO is the checkpoint system, on Murder Machine you can't save and load, so on numerous occasions the game spawned me surrounded by enemies and it goes without saying that on MM they kill you with one or two hits, so it's pretty annoying. I believe that the Ultra-Violence difficulty on Doom is more balanced than MM is here, it's not a matter of "git gud" the game is just "♥♥♥♥ you hard" and doesnt care. In general, balancing is a huge issue.Last, the final two missions (TeraTek Showdown + Final Purge) are the worst levels in the game. Repetitive and boring, letting the game end on a sour note. I'm sure that in time the devs are gonna patch most of the issues, but there's no patching for those two missions, they are just bad and waste of time. It seems they run out of ideas by the end.I don't want to sound negative towards the game, I love it, but since I played it on the highest difficulty I got some tough love for it. Turbo Overkill has excellent gameplay, fast gunplay and the best OST of the year!9/10 (maybe a ten if they patch the bugs and balance MM difficulty)
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews, but this game is too damn good and too damn underrated for me to not write one. Turbo Overkill is an absolutely phenomenal game, and while it does have its issues, they're very minor or hardly affect the main gameplay at all. The gameplay itself is amazing, and if you want a good ass movement shooter like ULTRAKILL, this game is amazing. To summarize everything, the gameplay is amazing, the story is good(albeit a bit flawed, I still enjoyed it nonetheless), the mechanics are amazing, the graphics are straight up beautiful, enemies are fun to fight, and there's endless content in here! Literally, there's an endless mode, but there's also a level editor, secret levels and "tech chips"(basically cheats that you can activate) that you can unlock in every level, an infodex, custom difficulty which just got added, achievements, and a great campaign that's a blast to play and replay through. As of writing this review, I've unlocked 100% of the achievements, and I've got to say, Turbo Overkill nails what makes a good FPS fun! Highly recommend this underrated GEM of a game! My only issues are that the level editor can be a bit jank at sometimes(e.g. not allowing me to use the "save and play" button properly to playtest or freezing on the loading screen when trying to leave) and that parts of the story are a little lacking, but I can't really think of anything else wrong with it! BUY THIS GAME
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: This game is insanely fun! Great fast-paced action mixed with a great art style and a unique take on weapon mods/attachments and skill upgrades definitely makes this one of my top boomer shooters of all time. _childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: I can wholly recommend this game to anyone who likes Doom or Ultrakill. Its incredibly fast paced and offers plenty of opportunities to go crazy with your weapons. It remains balanced throughout and the only time i found myself struggling was when i wasn't using my arsenal to its full capacity. There is a wide variety of enemies that all function differently, while never feeling like too much of a bullet sponge. I started off by playing the demo and i bought the full game almost immediately after finishing it. You get excellent air control and plenty of opportunities for dodging. Theres no unique gimmick or advanced tech that this game runs on, and mostly keeps things interesting through its fantastic set-pieces, super fun weapons and high-speed movement.The campaign is extremely long, providing me with roughly 20 hours of content (i was taking my sweet time experimenting, exploring and getting lost though, so expect something closer to 15 hours). The gameplay changes up frequently so i never felt like it was getting boring. Fair warning, the story takes some time to get started and only really speeds up around the halfway point. Despite this, the story was actually really fun to follow along with, the characters were interesting, and the cutscenes were funny. The ending scene has me hyped for a sequel. The visuals are fantastic and really bring that "boomer-shooter" vibe into the 2020s. The enemies, weapons and levels have great readability most of the time even if sometimes its a bit vague on where you need to go.One major help in improving my proficiency was discovering how much the game depends on the chainsaw-leg. You should be using this thing every 5 seconds with the armour and heal gene addons to keep your health up. My only minor criticism is that in terms of performance, Turbo Overkill is fill-rate limited. This wont be a problem for most as this game can easily run at 60fps 1080p with no issues even on mid-range or even low-end hardware. Considering it has a native TAA implementation, (and a very good one at that) it would be a massive help if there was some sort of upscaling tech, such as FSR 2.2 or FSR 3 to maintain high framerates at high resolutions. The game frequently dropped below my target 165fps at 1440p and i ended up having to cap it at 120fps. I know, these may be minor problems considering most people don't play like this, but the performance was similar to Doom Eternal at max settings, and i expected it to be much better considering the art style of the game.All in all, just buy the game, its some great fun. Good Hunting.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was awesome! If you like action FPS you owe it to yourself to get this. I could get into details on why its so great but I don't think I have to. _childDocuments_.review: is this game still in early access? because where are the sounds? whoever did the audio in this game did a really SH!T Job! guns sound like futuristic toys and not futuristic guns they all seem like they use the same audio file too! just with different tones the flamethrower attachment on the minigun doesn't even make a noise!? there's no character movement noises such as footsteps or running theres wall running audio yes! but even that audio file is really quite also all of the enemies sounds when they attack or shoot sound delayed and waaaay off! so with all that said is the game good and worth your pretty penny? yes! i think so because the story the gunplay and the gameplay is all there and done incredibly well it is a fun boomer shooter its fast paced bloody and set in a cyberpunk city with some of the best pixel art graphics youll ever see in video game to date i just wish the audio wasnt so SH!T in this game otherwise i would have rated it alot higher 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive, intuitive, fast-paced movement shooter done extremely well. Fun humor, knows exactly what it is doing. _childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: It is cool, looks nice, smooth, fitting music, feels like I die way easier sometimes than others, there is just very little originality. It is forever going to be compared to ULTRAKILL, DOOM, DUSK, GhostRunner, etc. Because that is exactly what this is. From the enemies, to the visuals, to the weapons and their abilities, it is just like ULTRAKILL and DOOM. and the name says it too, Overkill - ULTRAKILL, come on. I am only around an hour in, so maybe there is some originality coming. It looks nice, I can run it full settings on a 1060 3GB so thats impressive. There are quite a few bugs. Only way to start a new game is to load the game, hold Shift - N - S - F then exit. Very unbalanced on higher difficulty, it is following the early access release plan. "Release now, fix later" which is disappointing, but oh well. Overall it takes a lot of (a bit too much) "inspiration" from other games that came before it and have done very well. It is fairly priced, quite buggy, but there is fun to be had, I just get picky about originality.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Turbo Overkill is a very difficult game. It's very fast paced (which I love), Serious Sam like but set in a Blade Runner dystopia future. This atmosphere permeates the entire game's universe. Get ready to do a lot of dodging, strafing, chainsaw sliding, and constantly moving to the point of paranoia. Graphics are awesome and are well defined, with a tip of the hat to old school shooters with some pixelization happening here and there.Sound and music are fitting for the game Low key and appropriate. Nothing spectacular just adequate and sometimes great.I recommend the game although some of the platforming in the later levels are too demanding in my opinion and make you want to quit and stop trying. If you can stomach this weakness in the game then it is well worth the hectic and frantic play style which I find exhilarating..
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Started out pretty bad, weak weapons, unispired enemies, bad level design, weightless movement that's extremely fast - first few level i barely got through just not enjoying it, but by the end of the first episode it started getting a bit better, weapons got a few upgrades, leg started making more sense, level design got a bit better. And then the second episode started. Level design is significantly better, movement is utilized a lot more and a lot better, weapons got even more upgrades and new weapons are great, there's way more enemies and the way they are mixed is much better, everything really started clicking for me. And then the third episode started. Oh boy is it amazing. Everything got even better, music is way more interesting, visual design of levels is a lot more varied, cutscenes are very cool and that's on top of already one of the most dynamic, fast and just fun shooters out there. If turbo overkill 2 or dlc or whatever can pick up from there and continue on this trajectory it's going to end up a masterpiece. But third episode is already pretty close to that, only pulled down by a bit of a lack of variety in level objectives, and a bit of an overlap in weapon usage making some of them feel fairly useless.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly if the difficulty balancing wasn't so dang bad, this would be in my Top 5 FPS games of all time, but even still every other aspect of the game is so incredibly well honed that I can somewhat overlook it (definitely helps that there's a custom difficulty option now). There are some nitpicks I have still like not all enemies having unique sound effects for waking up etc., or how only a handful of augments are genuinely useful while the rest are gimmicky, but other than that the difficulty balancing is really the only thing I dislike about this game. I would hope that over time more adjustments are made to how damage is calculated, but regardless I definitely think this is a game every FPS fan should experience for themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best FPS games I've played. The dev deserves your moneydollars. I recommend playing on at least hard difficulty for a first playthrough. _childDocuments_.review: GAMEPLAY REVIEW:You have WAY WAY more and faster mobility options than in Doom Eternal(DE), (FFS, you get full air control, double jump, and double dash) right when you get started, but to compensate, in the hardest difficulty, most powerful attacks one shot you, or at least cripple you even at full stack. But, unlike all those noobs saying this game has random deaths, I assure you EVERY high-damage enemy/projectile is loudly/brightly communicated, you just gotta learn  what that the beep from a syntaur, the wooshing rockets from a sloth, and the mace notification from a ram, those massive bright blue slow projectiles from splits, the clinking grenades of a , etc all mean and how you ALWAYS could have done something differently 1 or 2 seconds ago to have saved yourself via foresight alone(no hindsight).As for weapons, there's not as much underdogging of weapons as in DE or D2016 (the starting pistols will be highest DPS weapon in the game, even more than the token based SATELLITE BEAM gun). AND each and every weapon is SO distinctively unique(the least of which is a machine gun that switches between brrrr and fshhhhh).Coming back to movement, most enemies don't lead your trajectory while firing projectiles, so you always gotta get creative with your movement if you don't want to go back to the LOS that has 5 fatal rockets coming at you and eat them all. I actually find this quite entertaining because yes, for one enemy, you can just run a circle around them and they can't do much against it since they don't lead their projectiles, but you put an arena full of enemies, all with different types speeds and methods of attack, and *chef's kiss*. Now THAT is a movement shooter, you gotta think fast, get creative, spam your cheggs and dashes(unlimited, and refresh on jump pads and grapples respectively) and most importantly, NEVER go back to the same angular LOS of an enemy sloth as 0.5-2 seconds ago.You're also welcome to pick not murder machine and just go to ham on every super, heavy, and trash mob you see with your cheggs. Or smash your buttons with no consideration of anything and go braindead on a second playthrough with my least favorite augment of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Serious Sam + Cool movement system. The core "chain saw leg" mechanic is fun to use, and you are constantly pitted against foes that challenge how you mix up between using your guns and your chainsaw leg. An absolute blast if you want some speed in your fps shooter.The guns also come in some cool varieties with thoughtful secondary modes.Having said that, I have not finished the game but feel like I have seen everything it has to offer me at this stage. _childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: We live in a time when small studios can make masterpieces using free game engines and when high-budget large studios just stagnating and make crappy copy-pasted games every year. Turbo overkill is great example of cool action game that shows that games must be about fun and gameplay, and graphics with other stuff are secondary. Turbo overkill just delivering to you a LOT of fun and gore action in low-poly, but, nevertheless, stylish graphics. Level design is good, platforming is breathtaking and sometimes a little annoying) This game gives you exactly the experience you are expecting. And difficulty settings are very ajustable. You can lower it through your run if you like to, but actually I like it playing on high difficulty. At the same time, the highest difficulty settings (last option), in my opinion, is for mazohists or tryhards only. So if you do not like to die and restart every 30 seconds - select something less challenging.UPD. Just finished the game. I can tell you that I literally hated some levels and wanted to change my review to negative very badly. When you think that they can not make your playthrough harder - you are wrong - they can. Sometimes it became just ridiculous. At the end I cached a game-breaking bug and have to restart level because of that (it broken the checkpoint so necessary event was not triggered). Final battle (I used only infinite ammo modifier and only at final levels) was so hard that I maybe restarted it 50+ times. I can not believe that I managed to beat the game at Serve Me Pain difficulty. After all, it is still very good game and it was worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing achievement for a small team.Follows in the footsteps of Doom Eternal more-so than the traditional boomer shooters that its aesthetic might suggest.Does an excellent job of gradually ramping up the intensity of the action as you grow in power and speed.There's an impressive amount of game here and the well designed vehicle sections provide welcome changes of pace.The mechanics, arsenal, enemy roster, level design , setting and soundtrack are all 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Turbo Overkill

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10Turbo Overkill didn't try to be a great independent game. It is a perfect game that is performs better than the standards in many areas and made it a game that can compare to AAA games. A fast boomer shooter that you must be fast and also dominate in shooting because enemies are very cruel and can kill you very fast. So, set your gear ready and enjoy this crazy fast shooting cyberpunk adventure.+:Fast-paced gameplay that requires concentration in shooting and dodgingGreat music that helps the rhythm of the gameEnvironmental diversity at each levelVery good level designVariety and good design of enemiesSurprisingly, admirable cutscenes-:Some levels are too long and so hard, especially in second and third act

_childDocuments_.review: The holy trinity of indie fps is now complete for me.Movement, gunplay, level design, all damn good.Hear me out, this game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, you know I played lot of fps but this right here can easily be in my top 10 best ever if they manage to keep that level of quality through all episodes, and it's just in early access.Already a must have, just need few balance tweaks, some qol updates, more levels and it will be perfect.Can't wait for more, keep up the awesome work !

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-For an indie game, it's quite the package for the price.
