_childDocuments_.review: Ah remember when you could just imagine a whole different world while playing with toys or when playing outside. Letting the time slip away as there was fun to be had. Lost in Play is about what you can guess based on the title: two siblings being lost in one of their play sessions.The game starts with a quick dream sequence, a look into the young girl’s dream which also gives us how whimsical the adventure will be, before it’s time to wake up for the day. She ends up waking up first, mainly due to the sun shining right in her face, and proceeds to wake up her brother (which is actually the first puzzle screen in the real world).These two siblings, while we don’t get their names in-game, are Toto and Gal. Today seems like it’ll be another boring day where they have nothing they really need to do. Toto is what you’d expect, a broody boy playing his video game and trying to not let his sister mess up his gaming streak. Well, after some puzzle solving to build a helmet to cosplay as a creature in one of their favorite comics, Gal gets her brother Toto to start playing with her outside. This turns into an adventure where innocently passing under a frog gate caused them to be transported to another world filled with weird, but familiar, creatures, magic, and goblins.Despite the game taking place in their imagination, making things more whimsical than they would normally be, the puzzles here are easy to figure out. They have a line of logic to it despite the imaginary and fantastical setting they take place in. And even though there is no dialogue, the characters will have a little speech bubble with a picture of the needed item. Each area will have a handful of puzzles for you to figure out, which completing one will help you progress in another puzzle in the area. As the game goes on, these areas do become slightly bigger, with more puzzles to do and slightly being trickier.There is a hint system in place so you can check if you’re a bit lost. While I didn’t have trouble most of the time, it does help if you just forgot where you needed to go with a certain item or the times where you are lost on what you have to do (which I only encountered twice).Honestly, the difficulty really comes with the minigames. There are two kinds: puzzle minigames and just traditional minigames. The puzzle minigames will give you the first two to get the hang of it before throwing you two hard levels to finish off on. These can be pretty tricky, sometimes the hint will help but sometimes not so much. Though it helps you can easily look them up if you’re just done with being stuck. With the regular minigames, the only difficult ones are where you go up against an AI. An early example is where you play a game with checkers, but you have to corner your opponent (and you can only go forwards with your pieces). These really straddle the line of being frustrating, with only one being not so bad. While you can pick up what the AI will do when faced with certain moves, it has enough of a random factor that can totally ruin your day.I did come to wish that there was an option to skip at least the minigames where you go against the AI if you’re stuck after a certain amount of tries. You have to hope that your moves and the AI’s will just click in place so you can finally continue.Though, I was disappointed at one sequence towards the end of the game. Right before you get to the frog gate, you get a cutscene that shows a handful of different scenes where the siblings are going through different areas. These looked like it would have been interesting to actually play, especially since one scene looked like it was a puzzle sequence, and it stinks that we couldn’t (whether it’s because they were originally planned to be levels but had to be cut out or there weren’t any ideas for them to be fleshed out and fun to play through).Aside from that, I loved the artwork here. It has a really nice and pleasing cartoon style and all the different areas are beautiful to look at. I did find the voices the characters had, so they’re just not moving their mouths without speaking anything, a tad annoying, but that was mainly when it was just the longer “talking” segments.Also, while this does have controller as a recommended way of playing, I do suggest mouse and keyboard instead. It might have just been me, but I had a good amount of moments in minigames where I clicked the button on the wrong direction, which ruined that try. Plus, I had a habit from other games where it will automatically use the item needed if you already have it in your pack and I always had to remind myself that I had to select the item while by the interact point (whereas with a mouse you just have to click and drag the item over, which felt more natural if that makes sense).Lost in Play made me so happy playing it. It really had me at the beginning with the brother being uninterested and broody, but I really loved how that they spent the whole day playing and imagining a whole world where they have to get back home. I especially love the credits where we get to see the real life counterparts of certain areas that seemed more out there. If you’re looking for a wholesome point and click adventure that takes place in two sibling’s imaginations where the majority of the puzzles are easy to figure out, Lost in Play won’t disappoint. Though, I do see a lot of people finding this game too short for the price (it was about 4-5 hours for me, and yes I used the hint system when I got stuck), and the minigames do lean towards being difficult (especially ones where you have an AI opponent).
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is a charming and feel-good Point and Click Puzzler that follows the adventures of a brother and sister as they find themselves in a dreamscape after entering it unknowingly when they were too engrossed during their playtime.Right from the bat, Lost in Play pulls you in with its high quality cartoon-ish artstyle and feel. The world in Lost in Play is so colourful and vibrant that it welcomes you in to meet and befriend all the magical creatures, be it whether they are friendly or not so friendly. The world and characters that you’ll see and meet are very well designed and unique. It truly resembles and reminds you of times when you’re lost in your imagination from days when you’re a kid.In terms or story, after getting carried away with playing, you’ll guide Toto and Gal (the Brother and sister) through their adventures to make their way back home before the “portal” they went through by accident closes before sun down. Fret not as along their journey they will meet and help magical creatures who will assist them one way or another. That’s not saying it’ll be a walk in the park for them as some creatures will be in their way as obstacles in their journey (except for the Big Cat, he’s just vibing at the “end”).Being a child-friendly game, Lost in Play exemplifies it well as being easy to understand regardless of what language you speak and such by doing away with any written text or spoken word throughout the game. This may seem tricky or risky but pays off by having a well thought out visual language and clues displayed that you’ll know what you have to do next or how to solve the puzzles.As a puzzle game, Lost in Play has a number of it and where its main strengths lay. Almost every puzzle you have to solve has a mini-game tied to it and every mini-game you’ll encounter is a fresh new one and not recycled. The sheer amount of work that goes into them should be praised as every mini-game brings in new ideas and lessons that after solving them, no matter how simple they may (which not all are simple) be, that after solving them you’ll feel a sense of accomplishment and never feel like it’s wasting your time. The mini-games also helps to keep things fresh and helps to break down the main puzzle in the area into enjoyable bite sizes.For the experience and joy Lost in Play gives the player, it is certainly a stand out for the Point & Click Puzzle game this year which has always been blessed. The quality, polish and heart that Happy Juice Games has embedded in Lost in Play should make them proud and for one should be applauded for establishing such standards and experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play does a lot of things right, but makes enough mistakes that I didn't finish it. It's a puzzle game based around two children who are (presumably) playing and imagining all the things in the game, rather than being whisked off to another dimension. This gives the game a lot freedom and variety in the set pieces and characters. The puzzles are generally fairly self contained, which is a breath of fresh air compared to some of the older ones where you carry objects around for hours. The art style and animations are beautiful, and the controls are great. Towards the end it starts to drop the ball as many of the puzzles I didn't think made any sense, even after looking up the answers.- The animations and art style are beautiful- Gameplay revolves around moving through self-contained puzzle areas that are usually 3-4 "rooms" each. All the items you need are used in those rooms, then lost when you move on - so there's no carrying something around for hours wondering what it's for- Wide variety of puzzles to solve- Nice sound effects- Really creative environments to explore- Puzzles are either too easy, or are very unclear in their goals. Usually the problem wasn't that I knew what to do but couldn't work out how - it was that I had no idea what I was supposed to do. On several puzzles, even with the hints giving you half the answer, I couldn't work out what the patterns were supposed to be- In the later part of the game, there's a lot of just walking back and forth between areas to take an item from one place to another- Several puzzles that take a long time to do have no skip option, and no hints- It's about 4-5 hours long, so don't buy it at full price

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is a truly enjoyable point and click adventure game.  It has great art, charming and whimsical narrative without text/dialogue, and logical puzzles.  It's about 4 hours to complete.Some minor issues:- The audio level got a lot louder about 20% into the game- The AI based 2 player mini-games were more frustrating than fun, and a large difficulty spike vs the relatively straightforward point and click puzzles- SPOILER!!! The ending feels incredibly rushed, You have all these great scenes, and then it's just this fast sequence of cutscenes and boom, we're home.  It's like there were another 5-10 scenes planned, but the team ran out of time/money to make them.  Maybe if the game sells well enough, they can get added?

_childDocuments_.review: Full Throttle, Grim Fandango, The Monkey Island series, Broken Sword and Day of the Tentacle. The 90's was such an amazing time for me as a gamer. All these adventure games that took your mind of school or whatever what was going on at home. They took you to a place full of wonder, full of amazing characters, puzzles and stories. Unfortunately the genre never got that popularity back and maybe a handful of games ever gave me that same feeling again.And here I was browsing Steam an coming across Lost in Play. With graphics that gave me that mid 90's feel and by the look of the trailer a true adventure type game. Point and click, but this time with some more puzzle heavy elements (which also is one of my favourite genres). Bought it, installed it and mannnn in a little over 5 hours you get such a gem of a game.Everything about this game is just perfect. The main characters (a brother and sister), the expressions, the people/creatures you meet along the way. How the first couple of puzzles requires logical thinking but the further you go there's some out of the box type puzzles as well. It manages to surprise, to spark that curiosity and wonder that's still somewhere in your adult brain, it gives you moments of laughter and feels profound all the way through.I can't recommend this game enough. Doesn't matter if it's not your 'type of game', get it, you won't regret it. It might be time to boot up all those old classics again after this. A-ma-zing game. Get it a whatever price, support the devs, they deserve every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lovely game I'm sure. It's clearly made with whimsy and has cute moments but it does not make for a fun point and click game. I watched someone play the first chapter and thought it looked like great fun - until I had to play it. Maybe I'm missing the run button or the skip button for the interaction animation I accidentally triggered for the third time but it feels like it's wasting my time.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is a point-and-click game, where you play as siblings Gal and Toto who created a surreal fantasy story while playing with each other. The game has no real language, everyone speaks gibberish, but speech bubbles showing what you should do appear. I particularly like the artstyle, it's cute and reminds me of cartoons from the 2010s. There's also a creative hint system that shows images that are clues on what we should do next in case you get stuck.Gameplay is mostly the same for its kind, finding and using items while interacting with characters. One unique thing is that there's lots of minigames, and quite varied, like how there's one where you piece events in a chronological order, reflect a beam of light, play checkers, etc. Most of them are quite easy, but some can be a bit too difficult for my liking. Still, it's pretty doable, and if you like cute point-and-click games, Lost in Play is worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely tale about 2 siblings lost in play trying to find their way back home.At first, I was a bit taken aback by the gibberish speech used by the different characters, but then I found it blended very well with the rest of the game as I got taken by the story and the puzzles.And the imagination put into the game design was so impressive! Each chapter just kept surprising me!I also wrongly expected this to be an easy game, but no. Some puzzles required some serious brainstorming and trial and error to reach a solution. I just love the feeling of achievement after succesfullly solving a difficult puzzle!I definitely recommend this game if you are looking to play a great puzzle adventure. And hopefully, we will see again the siblings lost in play 2?
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is a point-and-click adventure with great drawn visuals but where few things make sense and with restrictive controls and animations.+ Great drawn visuals+ Charming animations+ Great fantastical theme (excluding it not making much sense)* ~ 4 hour playthrough* Pseudo-language-voiced characters* No text dialogue, only animations and occasionally pictograms- Most things don't make sense; puzzles are non-obvious, intractability, controls, story, …- Character animations stretch their bodies- Slow animations- Repeated animation-lock-ins; made worse by actions not triggering as expected, and the need to manually select inventory items for interactions- No skipping of animationsIt started quite interesting, with an interesting, well-executed setting of kids playing with fantasy. But it quickly became irritating, and annoying, and lost all sense of direction, continuity, or making sense. All that was left felt like forced [animation] jokes where they do not make sense, confusion, and irritation.The fantastical world still had interesting aspects. Things that could be appreciated. The drawn world and characters. But it's an interactive game. And all interaction and progression felt irritating or annoying.Confusion: Some items worked as I expected them to, some worked where I did not expect them to, and some did not work where I expected them to. Characters stretch in animation. How far they can reach is entirely random between locations and interactions. The tip system is sometimes helpful, sometimes not. In one case I was able to skip a mini-game, in all others I checked, that was not an option. Most of what is based on physics makes no physical sense. The tip system was often not helpful.Irritation: Having to walk back and forth, slowly. Inconsistent interaction placement. Interactions leading to the character walking elsewhere then back to start the interaction. Animation lock-in even on repeated playback. Non-obvious intractability. Item and interaction combinations where they don't make sense. Everything confusing adds to the irritation.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is highly recommended for people looking for healthy entertainment or simply a nice time with a tale to appreciate. 100% suggest it for someone who has to have fun either alone or maybe even with family members. I can totally see even parents play this video game with their kids and both parties will enjoy it for sure.You will find the puzzles challenging. You need to chill, think and solve them in time. Sometimes with critical thinking. I personally don't suggest using the light bulb (hint) because it might spoil your game experience. The only disappointment I have for this game is lack of replayability for puzzles once you solve them unless you redo the whole episode. The devs should know some people might want to redo the puzzles only without going through the whole episode. Personally, I really liked the card game and I wish I could play it casually. I mean why not even multiplayer puzzles for the ones you complete?

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been thoroughly reviewed so my opinion isn't really needed, but I just feel compelled to say how good this game was. It's clear that everyone involved knows what they're doing. The art, the animation, the puzzle design, the game design, the sound design, the writing, everything is top notch. The comedy beats landed great in my opinion, the style managed to pull off childish whimsy in a way I actually found charming instead of rolling my eyes, the difficulty hit what I think was a sweet spot for what this game is going for (and has a hint system, though I can't review that, I didn't use it), and the whole thing is visually constructed at the level of a Cartoon Network animation (daytime not Adult Swim, this is a very wholesome game). If you're a fan of point-and-click games, or if you just appreciate animation as an art form and are willing to do some puzzles to experience it, this game is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel I need to point out some things that annoyed me but might not interest other people:1. The game's art seems rendered (and has some minor compression artifacting) instead of being vectored so it always looks lossy, especially when it's zoomed. In a game that places such an emphasis on it's art it's very noticeable. 2. The settings menu seems very lacking with settings only for resolution and a post processing toggle. Fortunately it has Music and SFX sliders in the audio section. (No idea why separate them when it's so bare-bones.) Also it has language select only at the starting menu with a large selection of languages except when using mouse the arrows don't work so you can't go back and have to cycle through them all just to find out the game virtually has no words in it except for the menus.3. Loading screens.4. Sometimes puzzle instructions would fail to load and bug out.5. driving puzzle.6. Movement controls and pathing are janky and don't feel good for lots of parts.* You can always pause regardless of what's happening even though the game is like one big cut scene, seems trivial but I've learned not to take this one for granted.Overall nice game despite the issues. Maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most endearing indie titles I've played in recent years. Perfect for a relaxing weekend when all you care about is getting a well-earned rest and keeping your brain active to an extent.Most of the puzzles require basic logic, while a few ramp up the challenge quite a bit. Also, I chuckled more than I would like to admit - even though Lost in Play will lead you to believe it was made primarily for kids, a lot of the jokes land well with adults, too. Last but not least, the language used in the game reminded me of the Simlish used in the Sims series, it's super cute!Man, as I'm wrapping up this review, I just cannot help but smile knowing I spent several super-fun hours with this game. I really couldn't ask for more!

_childDocuments_.review: This is just beautiful - a really lovely puzzle game. Good difficulty of puzzles for an adult (a few had me stumped for a few minutes, in a good way!), story and world engrossing and suitable for a kid. I played through with my 6 year old and we both agreed it's one of the best games we've played. Lots of fun! Took us about 6-7 hours, taking our time, no hints, but extremely fun and polished hours they were.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is a title I've had my eye on. Getting more into point-and-click titles, I found the art style charming. The characters looked to expressive. How the story just seemed like two kids getting lost with adventure. A tale of whimsy and imagination. And while that is there, this title sadly falls flat.The music I think it was quite nice, but the star of the show is the visuals. The two main characters are expressive and standout. You can immediately tell each of their personalities simply by looking at them. As you make your way further through the game, each area feels unique in it's own way. Why the visuals are such an important aspect to the title is because of one thing: imagination. You really feel like you're exploring with the two and apart of their 'world'. How it pulls you in and makes you forget that all of this is just the two just having fun together outside. The visuals really hold the experience.The story is not really anything to write home about, but that's okay. Two kids completely being taken in by their imaginative play and needing to get back home. It's short, sweet, and simple. And sometimes, that's okay as you explore the world being crafted.The gameplay is the thing which pulls the game down. It's a point-and-click, but I find myself wanting more charm from what those games can offer. What is here is nice, but the game makes me want more. The puzzles are rather simple and don't allow the player to really look at that they have. There is no examining the items you get for thoughts from the characters. You can talk with characters, but there is no dialogue. It's scripted, usually telling you what the character needs to move on.Lastly, there are 15 chapters, but it really makes the whole experience feel more shallow. The reason are the levels are all fairly small. Each section is made for simple puzzle solving. The visuals and whimsy beckon you to explore the world these kids are playing in. And yet the game doesn't want you to explore. The game puts you in small spaces where it's hard to get yourself stuck. The puzzles are simple and leave you wanting, even near the end of the game. Everything just feels more flat when the game invites you in for so much more.Lost in Play is not bad. I wouldn't recommend it for a starter point-and-click, but would say it would be good for someone who knows the genre and doesn't mind something light. But the price just doesn't justify it. For $20, it's a game that needs makes me yearn for something more. I wanted more interactions with items, or at least commentary to hear the main character's thoughts some more. Hear them talk about the world, talk to the characters. The game just leaves me wanting. If you are interested, I would say pick it up once it's on sale. However, there are other titles for the same price which don't leave me with the feeling of dissatisfaction. Not bad, but something that is close to being something special.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like this sort of game, this is the sort of game you'll like. The attention to animation detail is fantastic: it would have been sufficient for the chicken to throw the nail in the air and catch it in her mouth, but having the chicken throw the nail in the air, catch it in her mouth, glance at the nail-shaped deformity now in her throat, push the deformity down her gullet with her wing, and then belch? That's dedication to craft. Small touches like this are ubiquitous. The puzzles are thoughtful and fair and primarily require that you pay close attention to the environment. As you play through the game you'll progress through self-contained scenes and leave the previous scenes behind, which eliminates tedious backtracking, inventory bloat, fruitless 'inventory to object' experimentation, getting lost, and other not-fun aspects that often plague point-and-click adventures. There's no padding--the design is tight and purposeful.  In addition to puzzles, there are a few mini-games (no action/reflex games). None are optional and some might be surprisingly challenging but not frustratingly so (YMMV), and there are zero penalties for failure--just hit 'retry' and give it another go. Most took me several tries, but each is fun and quite winnable.The voice acting--despite the characters speaking gibberish--is magnificent and frequently hilarious. Lost at Play is a winner all around.

In fact, whoever programmed the AI for these mini games deserves an applause. I was told that this was by-design. So just be sure to help your kids pass the difficult parts... assuming you have what it takes to beat those nasty Orcs in cards!

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in  Play is simple yet fun. With just enough challenging puzzles to feel rewarding. The story is chock full of imagination and adventure. From the moment it started it immediately drew me into the world of the sibling's imagination. And even though we experience their real world journey only briefly I thought it was a great way to ground the story in reality, if just for a moment.The game's point and click mechanics aren't complex. With each chapter you're clearly presented with goals for progress, which is something I appreciated. Albeit, this game wasn't very long, and it didn't need to be. The worst thing a game can have is filler for the sake of filling time. And if you ever hit a roadblock there's a hint system in place that can help you out of the various situations you're in. I found the world's characters to be endearing. There weren't many but all the ones you met along the way, even if briefly added their own flair and personality that complemented the siblings' story well. I always appreciate a game that doesn't need words to clearly convey it's story. This is a fun game for all ages. It certainly wouldn't disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: In a word: delightful! This game had the perfect balance of old-school adventure game charm and slightly trickier logic puzzles, as well as a fun little story that tied it all together. With its Over the Garden Wall vibes (I see you, frogs and cone hats) and seamless gameplay, Lost in Play is definitely worth getting if you love solving your way out of tricky situations. While classic LucasArts games will always be a favorite of mine, I love how Lost in Play created a slightly less moon-logic heavy game than classic adventure games tend to be. In Lost in Play, there are many chapters, and each chapter of the story has its own goals, its own puzzles, and, most importantly, its own objects. You're not going to be carrying around a quarter or a screwdriver from scene 1 throughout the entire game, wondering when it's going to become useful. Instead, whatever you collect has relevance for that scene only, and objects that need to be combined automatically do so in your inventory--yet the inventory object puzzles still require a little thought! Nothing is so complicated that it's impossible; I didn't need in-game hints or walkthroughs, making this a very welcoming game for newcomers to the adventure game genre. Because you're working within a limited space, there are really only so many combinations to try before you have your Aha! moment.On that note, the design of the game eliminates annoying backtracking, which is fantastic. While sometimes the beauty of an adventure game is finally realizing the unique connection between one object from one side of the map and something all the way on the other side, you know what ISN'T beautiful? Walking back and forth between them. Walking to every location trying to figure out where to use that roll of tape. Trying to combine every object in your inventory until you figure out exactly how the hell the game wants you to use them (and sometimes trying twice, because it really seems like that gum and that piece of string should go together!). Lost in Play has NONE of those problems. It leapfrogs all those hassles by creating fairly contained environments; you won't be wandering back and forth for long before you know what to do.And then there's the puzzles--by which I mean, occasionally you'll need to play a minigame/do some kind of a logic puzzle to escape a monster, persuade a character to give you an object, etc. If anything, I'd say the minigames and puzzles are a few steps above the rest of the game in difficulty, making it just a LITTLE off-balance. I'd say that in the narrative and the exploration scenes would be very friendly to younger players, but some of the puzzles and games get quite a bit trickier! If kids are playing this, these might be a great place for an older sibling or a parent to help. The minigames and puzzles are extremely fun and satisfying to play, though--I'd play a whole game of just these puzzles.This game is definitely worth your time if you want a fairly easy, relaxing game with a sweet narrative that still requires some thought. It's just the right length, too--you can finish it in 1-2 sittings, so it doesn't overstay its welcome or get boring. It's also incredibly easy to get 100% achievements, which is deeply satisfying to me as someone who loves a checklist. Definitely give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: So...I really wanted to like this game.  I'm a point and click game creator, I love the genre, and as others have said, the visuals are stunning, the characters adorable, the whole setting and concept is charming.However - about 2/3 of it is just bad game design.About 1/3 of the puzzles were good, well signposted, not flat out easy but just enough of thinkers to feel satisfied when you solved them.  Classic point and click adventure stuff.Another 1/3 were moon logic puzzles, what I call "guess what the author was thinking" puzzles, based either on actions you'd have no logical reason to take, or game functions you'd have no reason to assume existed (go back to -50 on the time puzzle, pan sideways at the keypad/guard puzzle).  The creators clearly knew how to signpost, they just failed to do it at enough critical moments to be really frustrating.The final 1/3 were the constant, constant, unskippable mini-games.  I'll be honest that mini-games in a point and click are a pet peeve of mine - they're usually unnecessary padding, "stretch the game time to make it feel longer" filler material that has no bearing on the plot.  And the creators here stuffed their game full of things exactly like that.  I only saw an option to skip a couple of times, and believe me, I looked.  After that I was trapped into non-plot-related games I didn't want to play, using a hint feature that often barely helped, and constant searching online for walkthroughs.  I nearly quit for good during the card game, and at the frog-tile puzzle at what should've been the climax of the game.  These things aren't satisfying to win - it's a slog that leaves you feeling like "oh man, finally, that's over with".There were also several "unnecessary extra step" puzzles that creators can solve easily with simple variables - if you have the inventory item a NPC is looking for, don't make the player character shrug like they have no idea what the NPC is talking about (like at the void door/pitcher puzzle).  Trip a variable so the player produces it automatically when the NPC asks.  For experienced point and click players, it gets an eye roll and some unnecessary extra clicks to complete the puzzle.  For inexperienced players, it's a "wait, what?  Am I still missing something?  I better go wander around pointlessly pixel hunting."I think the whole thing is so frustrating because it clearly had the potential to be something amazing.  The creators have art, animation, sound, and some puzzle design on lock.  If they'd spent extra time planning and designing better, it could have been a masterpiece.

The game is kind of split up into several hubs/levels where within each hub there is lots of point and click inventory style puzzles with an overall goal, mostly its to find various items that will allow you to proceed to the next hub. There is also several small mini-game style puzzles thrown in as well as some interesting movement based puzzles. Nothing too difficult, game flows along nicely.- Nice music- Lots of humor.- Great performance, 120-fps through-out.Cons- While the game is mostly playable completely with just the mouse there were a few mini-games were keyboard was required. Its strange because the first mini game I came across you could actually click on the on-screen representation of WASD but in subsequent games this didn't work so its possibly a bug.- There is voice acting, I'm not sure if its a real language or just gibberish and while it is very charming and I suppose fits the theme very well I still would have appreciated English voice acting for more immersion.Overall highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: "Lost in Play" is a FREE mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as a paid product, as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.This mobile app is admittedly charmingly animated, but that's the only good thing about it.  Simple, dumbed down puzzles, a mediocre narrative (at least it has one, I suppose), some okay-ish cartoon artwork.  But the games themselves, this being basically a collection of minigames, are underwhelming and somewhat dumbed down.  The characters also talk in Simlish, the gibberish that EA uses on The Sims, so there's some hope these mobile devs will at least get sued for that.  Scamming PC gamers is probably something they'll get away with, consequence free. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just iPhone screen tapping stuff.  The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction.  You'll get none of that here.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this mobile app?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is $20 USD, on app stores, it's free. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a premium for a free mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.  If you really want to play this, grab your iPhone, it's free.  Don't pay for it here. Charging PC gamers TWENTY BUCKS FOR A FREE MOBILE APP is disgusting.  This is a scam.  Just who do they think we are?

_childDocuments_.review: CHILDHOOD WONDER   I am not really a fan of point and click games, I’ve got nothing specific to complain about the genre tho. For some reason, these games just don’t sync with me, Disco Elysium is a very good example: Good story, great gameplay, interesting protagonist as well as multiple dialog choices, and yet, it’s accumulating virtual dust in my Steam library. So that makes me wonder, why I’ve loved Lost in Play so much? What kept my smile throughout my entire playthrough? Spoiler alert: The answer is probably something cheesy like: “It reminded me of my childhood days.”  You play as siblings Toto and Gal, both embarking on an epic journey with lots of puzzles, visual spectacles and silly jokes. Throughout my short, but rich, 4 hour playthrough I've explored: a goblin camp, a haunted cave, a big desert, the open ocean and, of course, a living room. This game is the perfect example of quality over quantity, you will never get bored or feel like the game is not respecting your time.SIMPLE PLEASURES  The game is quite simple and it is filled with a variety of distinct puzzles for you to solve. Most of them require you to collect specific items based on the necessity at hand. But don’t assume that this is another one of those “Fetch” quests, the puzzle variety is quite extensive and there are a lot of mini games at play to keep you entertained. Every puzzle is unique in its own way and I was quite impressed by some of them. Luckily, the puzzles are not the only factor that will keep you entertained.  Certain games will never look outdated even after decades of its release. That’s the result of a good art direction, the visual presentation of a cartoon-style 2D game is timeless and won't go out of fashion in the years to come. And even if it did, I would still consider it a worthwhile experience.  Overall the game is quite polished and bug free, the performance is excellent and it works great on the Steam Deck, but there is definitely some space for improvement. The mouse and keyboard controls sometimes feel rather clunky and unresponsive, I highly recommend playing this game using a controller. Some specific puzzles are also frustratingly non intuitive, which made me lose a few minutes looking for something that was never intended to be found.VERDICT  I loved this game so much that I even got my wife to embark on this adventure with me. Its the perfect game to have a great time with your family and be reminded that even adults can get lost in play.Highly Recommended

Some of the puzzles/mini-games could be a bit too difficult for the younger players. A teenager should be fine though.The game may be short but it didn't feel like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Art direction? Adorable.Story? Simple yet whimsical - The world building is perfectly weird.Puzzles/Flow of the game? Simple without being too tricky (Admittedly, the answer for the final pattern finding one with the fish and the dragon head buttons was a tad obtuse - But forgivable), and plenty of fun little games that not only tickle the brain, but also could easily be played at home with friends/the kids.Also, it's very funny. The chicken, in particular, had me laugh out loud a few times and I am actually a bit annoyed that we only got to enjoy the chicken so late in the game.Did I only play it for 5 hours? Yes. But I was smiling and enjoying myself the entire time. Easily worth it, very very cute and fun, and I'll be passing the controller to my kids to watch them stumble through.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is an adventure game developed by Happy Juice Games and published by Joystick Ventures. It is a heartwarming and whimsical game about two siblings, Gal and Toto, who get lost in their own imagination.The game is played from a third-person perspective, and the player controls both Gal and Toto. The game's puzzles are mostly logic-based, and require the player to use objects and the environment in creative ways.Lost in Play features a variety of unique and memorable characters, including a talking fox, a giant robot, and a magical bird. The game's world is also beautifully designed and full of interesting details.Overall, Lost in Play is a charming and enjoyable point-and-click adventure game that is sure to please fans of the genre. It is a perfect game for players of all ages, and it is sure to put a smile on your face.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Great casual puzzle game with an amazing art style and some slight humor.This little puzzle game has quite some exciting puzzle challenges, dont expect a big or emotional story however, altough it is still very amusing.Gameplay isn't that much but the artstyle, the cutscenes and the overall vibe that goes with this story is well worth it.I really enjoyed it and it gave me the occasional laugh.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Simply adorable !The whole game feels like a proper kid's cartoon, the drawings are great and so is the musicGameplaywise, don't expect a grandiose Point and Click : these parts are veeeery easy for someone used to point and clicking. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored this game.It was incredibly fun and entertaining, with a good amount of puzzles (they're all different and unique) without being too hard. _childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Flawlessly polished and relentlessly charming, Lost in Play deserves your attention for its imaginative storytelling alone. There is immense satisfaction to be found in each of its point-and-click puzzles. Even when the game's dreamy logic leaves you scratching your head, there is a generous hint system that will never make you feel like you are taking a penalty if you decide to use it. Just push the button to dissolve your frustration and let the story carry you onward.Lost in Play is not a lengthy or replayable game, but it is more than worth the price if you grab it during a sale. It's one of the few cases where I don't mind bending my personal "$1 per hour" guideline.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: What this game lacks in playtime, it makes up for with stunning visual and sound design. You feel completely immersed within this incredible make-believe world and the puzzles are challenging and refreshing. The game has also been localized in a wide variety of languages. _childDocuments_.review: Fun and whimsical point-and-click adventure where two kids get lost in a fantasy world. The puzzles are, for the most part clever, but several annoying logic puzzles rear their ugly heads. Sliding tiles and other logic games will never be fun for me, they ruin the pacing, and there's even one "mini-game" that's all about betting limited resources that I completed by luck on the first try but still took a good 10 minutes for the animations to play out. If it sounds like I'm coming down on Lost in Play it's only because everything else is so pleasant.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing little puzzle/point & click adventure game. The animations are amazing, the characters are great, the story is really nice/cute, found it really funny at times and the music/sound is really great overall. Even the menu track is a bang.The only two things I didn't like that much was that it is too easy and too short, but I'll still recommend this game, it shows it was made with a lot of care and attention to detail.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is an adventure puzzle game where you play as a sister and her brother as their imagination soars. The game seamlessly transitions between the two in real life and their imagined world, in which a box with crayon drawings becomes a monster, a bicycle becomes a magical flying dragon, and video games become important puzzles that must be solved in order to defeat the big bad and rescue your friends.The game consists of progressing through chapters, where each chapter gives you access to a few screens, and you must utilize objects and NPCs in each screen to solve puzzles, win at mini-games, and ultimately complete a goal. In this way, Lost in Play is very much a point-and-click game, yet it is best played with a controller to walk around and interact with the world around you. I had a grin from ear to ear throughout playing this game. Every animation is adorable and relatable, every dialogue is cute and delightful, and every puzzle and mini-game is original and entertaining. The gameplay can certainly be considered quite slow, with many unskippable animations, which does hurt replayability, but I never once wanted to skip those animations on my first playthrough.Ultimately, given the short nature of Lost in Play and the limited replayability, I think the price is ever-so-slightly high and would recommend waiting on a sale, but would highly recommend this game nonetheless to anyone looking for some childlike fun in their life.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely one of the cutest games I've ever played! Very much enjoyed the story and the cartoony art style. I was a bit afraid the game might be too easy because of how it looks, but the puzzles are surprisingly clever. None of them were too difficult, but there were a couple I got a bit stuck on for a while. Can absolutely see myself replaying this at some point in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is one of those games where you just sit back and enjoy, the characters are unique, the adventure fun, the puzzles are decently challenging while still fun, the game was well paced and to finish it off the art style is very pleasing and fun to watch with a decent amount of play time, puzzles that will make you really think while not being too difficult and characters that actually seem like real people.Overall Lost in Play is a very fun and casual game to play that reminds me of my childhood and what it was like before having to go out into the real world, with its fun animation, unique and interesting characters and its plot which gives plenty to enjoy.[9/10] Would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Very Very good game. Short and Sweet. You're Looking at about 8 Hours or less actual play time. It's worth whatever they're asking for it or more. Beautiful graphics, fun and interesting puzzles, simple yet engaging story, easy controls, and actually funny through out. It's just a good time. This is not a "kids" game. I feel like only a teen 14 and up would enjoy this and be able to finish it one sitting, maybe 2 sessions at most. Music is great, wear headphones if possible! I played this on my laptop but now I wish I would've put this on the biggest screen in the house. Full screen, no HUD, Pixar quality visuals here. Don't think about it, if you can play this game; please treat yourself. 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Great point and click/logic puzzle game, feels like you're in an episode of Adventure Time - amazing animation and genuinely funny interactions throughout. Veers between super easy point n click gameplay and actually quite challenging (for me!) non-verbal reasoning puzzles which thankfully the droobus-spawn helped me with, having been tutored for various grammar school exams. 😁 Well recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem, a thrilling quest that deserves a solid +8yo rating. From start to finish, it captivates players with its remarkable features. It has everything - nice graphics, amazing soundtrack, characters, imagination and good sense of humour of the authors. Humour plays a significant role in this adventure, with the authors injecting clever and amusing moments throughout. It's delightful to encounter unexpected laughs that add an extra layer of enjoyment to the gameplay. This lightheartedness balances perfectly with the intriguing story, which keeps players engaged The story is interesting and fun. The quests, while not overly challenging, strike a satisfying balance between entertainment and brain-teasing. Most can be completed without too much difficulty, but there are a handful that present a delightful challenge, taking even the most experienced players around +5 minutes to crack. It's a testament to the game's design that it can engage both children and adults alike, allowing everyone to participate in the adventure.Speaking of children, this game stands as the pinnacle of quests created specifically for younger players. In fact, it's the finest kids' quest I've encountered in the last 10 years. This glowing review is not just the opinion of a single individual but the collective sentiment of four individuals who found immense joy in playing the game. With unanimous agreement, they awarded it a perfect 10/10, solidifying its status as an unforgettable experience. Kol ha-kavod! Waiting for Lost in Play 2)
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is an amazing game. I reminds me of the puzzle story games I grew up with. I was able to play this with the whole family and we had a blast. There were puzzles that the kids could figure out and some that needed a little parental help. I recommend this to anyone that has kids and is looking for a great family game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: The game is short, cute, and fun. Item gathering and application is very straightforward, and you never get lost not knowing what you are supposed to do. Puzzles vary a lot and while there were a few that weren't easy to solve, for most of them you don't really need to stop and think of a solution. You can just try different ways, retry, figure it out on the way, or just stumble upon a solution. Story-wise it feels like the game had much more potential, sort of like Gravity Falls, but has been cut short (especially the fast-forward part towards the end). It also reminds me of Tohu, same sort of cuteness and similar complexity level (but different kind of puzzles).
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with a 5 year old, and we both enjoyed it a lot. Great game to play with a kid, the puzzles difficulty is varied, some parts can be done by the kid, but some puzzles are quite hard. There's a hint system to reduce frustration with the latter. The game doesn't have any real text (or real language speech), so there's no language barrier for the kid either.Very nice and creative graphics. The "story" is weird and quite interesting. As for the puzzles, some of them are a bit random, but they are overall fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful little gem of a game. Taking place in the dreams of a brother and sister, Lost in Play takes you to very imaginative settings, none of which overstay their welcome. The animation and art are amazing, the puzzles are straightforward but perfectly entertaining with a little bit of challenge sprinkled in between and the story is very cute. Loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: The game's graphics are beautiful and whimsical, creating a vibrant and inviting world that draws players in. The puzzles, while not overly challenging, are fun to solve and keep players engaged throughout the game. While "Lost in Play" is relatively short, it packs a lot of heart and soul into its game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: What a super well done and charming puzzle game! I loved all the different ways that the puzzles were incorporated, they never felt repetitive or like they dragged on. Excellent character design, I loved the frog movement and the farting sheep especially. I honestly wish more games like this one existed so I could play them!
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzle game, this is a "point and click" game where you need to find and use items in the correct order to progress.  I find was best played with one or more people watching/helping out.  The main part of the game/adventure is requires just enough thought an planning to be easy but fun.  There are the occasional mini games though that can be a lot tougher- which I found helpful to have someone watching/helping.  My biggest gripe would be the discrepancy between the easy "main" part of the game and the sudden increased difficulty in the "mini-games".  The mini-games are not impossible, they are just much more challenging and requires a different puzzle-solving process to accomplish (with a bit of luck you may solve just by accident).The story is charming even though they seem to speak an imginary language. Also, I was a little surprised with  the length of the game, we completed in just a few hours (taking our time).
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in Play is one of those indie games that is so full with creativity and inovation (or at least something new that other games don't do), that you enjoy it so much.It's been a while since I played a game that made me feel so happy and challenged at the same time, haha.Everyone should give it a try, the game is not that complicated and even if you get stuck in one or two puzzles, the hints help you get through.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: Much like the title suggests, I was lost in my playthrough of this game. Time flew by. The artwork is really well done; probably one of the best I've seen in an Indie game. The puzzles weren't too difficult, allowing you to focus on the story rather than getting frustrated over what to do next. This game even had me laughing out loud sometimes. Overall it gave me childhood nostalgia of the games and imagination I had with my siblings growing up. My only negative review is that it felt too short; I needed more! Very well done and I would absolutely recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent point-and-click game, very well made.  (Graphics, subject matter and content all very strongly remind me of the "Gravity Falls" cartoon.)Good variety in puzzles and mini games, and the creators tackled the speech system very well: there is no written text or dialog trees, everything boils down to simple pictograms explaining the problem at hand with gibberish (?) vocals. Parts of the game are very abstract and dream like, and other parts are much more grounded... The puzzles are always fairly clear, and there is a built-in hint system to point you the right direction if you do get totally lost.Main character switches between multiple individuals throughout the game: sister, brother and even a chicken.It took me a little over 5 hours to finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I noticed a number of reviews that said they played this with their kids.....well I am fully grown, mature (perhaps) adult without kids who totally loved this game!I like to play for an hour or so after work to wind down and this game is perfect for this. _childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: In technical terms, this game is great. Graphics are great, the humorous bits are actually funny and the story is fun and imaginative.But all that is fluff for me and this game fails at the most basic and important level for a point and click adventure game - the puzzles are not interesting. They are mostly very easy, many are simply pattern matching. The few difficult ones suffer from "moon logic".I've been playing adventure games since the Apple II days. This game reminds me of the Sierra adventure game "classics". Even the arcade mini games that I disliked are present. I preferred LucasArts adventures, and this game is no LucasArts. I'll recommend the game because obviously lots of people like this style of game, and if you do, it is well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful, fun(ny) and original all-time great adventure. The cartoon graphics are timeless and beautiful, the made-up language used for voices is charming and together with the general lack of text makes the game also incredibly accessible to younger players. Most of the puzzles are simple (and yet: not dumb) and perfectly conveyed via the character's actions and icon bubbles. With about three hours the game is on the shorter side, but it also does not overstay its welcome. I felt I got my money's worth, as while the game is linear, it is so funny and charming that I can see myself replaying it in the future more than once, at least for the laughs.

_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 tbh I was expecting the game to take a dark turn like Little Miss Fortune and I was happily proven wrong.Some of the puzzles we're a bit annoying but the charm of the game even just the art style alone more than makes up for it.I love that the had the hints available, you don't ever see that in these types of games.Absolutely loved the ending.Over all great work, fun story, creative details, and it made me feel like I did when I was little and would get Lost in Play
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: When you open this game the first thing you will notice is that its soundtrack absolutely shlaps! The next thing you will notice is the gorgeous stylish cartoony visuals. Both of these stay constantly phenomenal from the start screen to the end credits! The art direction in the game is just so good! The gameplay is basic point and click fare with some surprisingly difficult puzzles sprinkled here and there. Maybe it is just me but despite the cartoony aesthetic these puzzles are not for kids, some real mind puzzlers here. The story follows a brother and a sister on an endearing journey across imaginative play world.  All the side characters are zany and fun. It really captures that Sunday morning cartoon adventure time type feel. This isn’t the best game I have ever played but it kept my attention for the 4 1/2 hours it took to complete. I would recommend to anyone who likes the aesthetic or fans of point and click adventures. Some people may find the short playtime a disappointment but it was just what I was looking for. Something to finish in two play sessions, enjoy, and move on.
_childDocuments_.name: Lost in Play

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game that will remind you of your childhood. The game follows two siblings, who play around the neighborhood. We experience the world as they see - trough the eyes of their imagination.The artwork is splendid, looks and is animated like a well made cartoon for children. The voice acting is done trough jiber-jabber, with animated chat bubbles that show you everything that needs to be shown. Outside of menus the game uses no words. Everything is communicated trough images and sound. The presentation is splendid trough the whole game, with no cut corners, and some surprising elements later on. As this is point and click game (that is perfectly playable on a controller) there are puzzles to be solved. One would think that with a game that looks so cute and childish all the puzzles would be no-brainers. But I actually found them all to be unique, interesting, and they usually require thinking to solve them. You might even get stuck on some. There's build-in hint system, but I've never used it. It's never really hard, but it respects your intelligence and perception just enough.The game is joy to play on a controller. The interface is quick to use and snappy. When you stand within the range of an item and choose something from the inventory it's used instantly, without additional confirmation, which works really well. Every action you do, including wrong ones, is animated. It's just gorgeous. There's also tons of minigames and riddles that take you to a separate screen, which also play very well.It takes about 4 hours to beat, which is just perfect for this kind of the game. It never gets to a point where you would get tired, and it will take you 2-3 evenings to beat. The game changes between both playable heroes, and they both get their time to shine. They are just siblings who play together, and it's warm and fuzzy.This is a game that took me back to the time I was 7 years old. Steam should have double thumbs up, even if it would be just for this game. Imagine it's what I gave this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Look at all the stuff we did not put in the game!This is going to be a very weird recommendation. It's a point & click adventure game, which is interlaced with puzzle minigames. I quite liked those, but many people would probably want to skip some of them. The Gravity Falls esthetic is pretty neat and though a tad easy, the game is very enjoyable.However... The story of the game is that two kids lose themselves in their play fantasy and need to find a way home. So, there is no real narrative to follow here, the various set pieces basically could have been done in any order and you're playing these mini-episodes. Now some of the journey home is done in montages... and that comes across at "look how much bigger the game could have been, if you'd just given us more money at kickstarter". With a pretty steep price and only about 4 hours of playtime it tastes like you just sucked on a greedy middle-finger.Yet, on what we got, we can't complain. So, it really comes down to how much money you want to pay. I would easily recommend it at 10€, but I payed double. Also don't trust trailers or screenshots on what seems playable. It feels like buying a pig pizza and after paying the delivery guy eats 3/4 of it, leaving you with a kid's size pizza. But at least it is delicious.

name: Override 2: Super Mech League
detailed_description: Override 2: Ultraman Deluxe Edition Override 2: Ultraman Deluxe Edition includes the main game, Ultraman Season Pass: Containing 4 super-charged Ultraman characters – Ultraman, Bemular, Dan Moroboshi, and Black King. About the Game The gigantic robot brawler is Mech-ing a super-charged comeback in Override 2: Super Mech League! Seven years after the Xenotypes that invaded Earth have been eradicated, the giant mechs that were once the planet’s defenders are now their entertainers in global mech battle leagues. As a new pilot of these repurposed weapons of war, climb the ranks and represent your Club with a tuned-up roster of returning and new mechs, each with their own unique abilities, moves, and super-charged attacks. Override 2: Super Mech League is playable both in single player and multiplayer campaigns for up to 4 players locally and online in stages set all over the world. Start as a new pilot and propel yourself through the ranks in a deep and robust Career Mode. Join Mech Leagues and earn reputation by competing in Arenas located across the globe. Duke it out with a tuned-up roster of returning robots and new mechs across various versus and co-op game modes of up to 4 players online and locally. Defeat your opponents using an arsenal of unique moves including super-charged ranged attacks, metal-busting combos, or an arena-shattering ultimate attack! Career Mode: Fight in Mech Leagues and soar to new heights, aiming to be the best mech pilot. Represent your Club and work together with its members to earn Influence and rewards! Ranked Rumbles: Two Mechs enter, one leaves. Battle through the competition and climb the ranks to become a legendary pilot. Mech Mania: 20 playable robots including brand-new mechs with unique abilities, skill sets, and Ultimate moves. Hazardous Arenas: Competitive fighting grounds that include dynamic elements such as geysers, lava pools, and platforms that encourage strategy and unexpected outcomes. Upgraded Game Modes: Pick your playstyle across match types including 1v1, 2v2, free-for-all and several games such as Xenoswarm, King of the Hill and more. Expansive Customizations: Unlock a slew of cosmetic items and attachments for your mech of choice in the Garage.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic Arena brawler that hits every itch I could want fighting as a giant robot.  However it is very apparent it will be falling short just as its predecessor did.Override 2 was my hope at finally getting a player base that Override never had, however it appears the same lack of marketing is taking place so the player base will be non existent within a week or 2 just as the first, but that isn't even the most upsetting part that I was let down by when trying to enjoy Override 2 with my friends.The game has the new league system which is great! However, they added in 2v2, and multi person battles to the leagues but don't allow you to actually play in those multi person games with friends.  You and a buddy wanna go fight 2 other people out there in the world? Sorry, you can't.  Override 2 only has 1 way to play with your friends, in a private match versus scenario.  You can't group up and play against other people in the world you can only play in your small circle.  You also can't even unlock any items when playing with your friends unlike the first, so no fun cosmetics or new mechs are being unlocked if you ever want to play with your friends.Override 2 gave me tons of hope and joy again, only to crash it all down realizing they learned nothing from their first mistake of a game, and even dug the whole deeper removing any way to play a "party" brawler as an actual party because you can't even queue any games with your friends.Final quick point - you can't change any controller bindings in the game only keyboard bindings (the game being a console port to pc) which is kind of a joke of a setting to be missing on release at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Put it short.Game looks great, sounds great, weapons are actually nice addition now.And thats all I got from this.The joy I had from playing the first game does not exist in this game.This game has been dumb down, at it shows. Seems more like a "Cash grab" over thought out development. Seeing how the previous game used several years while this took.. what... 1?Here are a list of all the wrongs I found in my short but quick decision of "Keep or Refund" playtime.- There are now only 4 attacks. All tied to the attack buttons. Previous game had 8. No more Charge, or having combos. Only "This button does THIS specific move, and this does that specific move".      Sure you can do combos, but... the combos are eh...- Maps are super small- No more overheating. So all the attacking can be spammed.- No more special bar. Only spam.- Ultimates are now not tied to the players health, and more on "who can stand in the special charge circle the longest", which would been better if the maps werent 3 feet bit and if it was removed for charging your ultimate instead of a "king of the hill" thing.- No more Party controlled mech. Which is what I wanted from the Pre-release version of the first game.- The amount of new mechs are so small, it could have been a DLC for the first game, and probably played better.- No more Hover, and no more sprint either.Overall. GG on not building upon what the first game had for it, but remove tons to make a cheap "console arena battle game".For its price, its nice, but compared to the first game, or even all the previews and demo videos of the first game, nah fam.Hard pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Override 2: Super Mech League

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna keep it simple: Pros: - Looks great and sounds great - League Mode is a nice addition - Mech variety is still wonderful - Ultraman (Even if it is Netflix Ultraman which is trash) - Throwing and the added air game - Ultraman Cons: - Loss of the original games controls (Or no option to choose between them) so now the game feels incredibly generic and not much like a mech game.- The grind to unlock mechs feels terrible and wasn't needed. - Loss of any sort of story mode (There was potential here for a story about the league and the people you meet in it, a new pilot, anything.) - AI clearly hasn't gotten any smarter. - Environmental destruction feels lesser since things just explode now instead of fall to pieces. - Maps are incredibly small and bland, they do shift and change at least in certain levels but it doesn't help the levels feel large. That would be better if the arenas weren't so small and cramped. - Always online. - Attacks feel so incredibly weak, ultimates especially just feel useless.- The heat system was a great way to prevent abuse, removing it outright not only makes things feel less mech but also opens things up to violent spamming. - Not much in the way of cosmetics. This game is disappointing in almost every single way compared to the first. It feels like something they should have tacked onto that than a proper sequel. I was looking forward to them building on the first game to make something truly amazing but that is clearly not what this is. I wanted to like it so much, and while there is fun to be had...just play the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Mech League (SML) takes the entire game in a new direction. For the uninitiated and return players, I will outline the differences from my experience. I would recommend both games, though SML provides more content and would be recommended first.It is important to note that the fundamentals of fighting have changed since OG Override. In both games, each arm/punch and leg/kick was individually assigned to the shoulder and trigger buttons. This was a distinguishing feature in playing like a lumbering mech.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't wait for this game to come out.  I loved the first one.  the previews looked great.  the game looked faster and way more slick.  but when I started playing I realized that they had taken all of the things that made the first game out.  the unique way you control your mech was replaced with a much less intuitive faster simpler brawler system.  you no longer feel like a huge mech just a generic brawler like every other brawler.  they gutted the games mechanics.  here is a few of the features the first game had this one doesn't.  Co op where each player controls a different part of the robot.  feinting. parrying. flying. charging hits.  mech pilots and characters. a compelling story.   this game is a hollow imitation of the first game with no understanding of its success or its failures.  we needed a better marketing campaign to bring in more players to help the matchmaking which is an issue in this game already.  we needed you to refine the mechanics you had already in the game not take them all out and reduce it to a button mashing simplicity.   much of the game is luck now no skill is needed.  additionally the stages are bland boring and infuriating.  the ground moves on almost every single level.  I've already had opponents get stuck in glitches because of moving parts.  a lot of time you are fighting the game rather than your  opponent.  you can't choose which modes you want to play as they are presented at random.  you have to unlock mechs and cosmetics slowly and in a trivial fashion.  There was so much potential for this sequel but its clear the developer doesn't know what they are doing or what audience they want to appeal to.  stuck in a limbo between casual brawler and fighting game.  its clear that modus is in desperate need of better leadership.
_childDocuments_.name: Override 2: Super Mech League

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly I cannot recommend this game.  Though it is technically a sound game (at least for me) it just lacks so much the original game had.  Story mode is gone, now replaced by league which is default PVP.  You can press a button to force AI to be your opponents instead but it's weird you have to do that every single match in league.  The option to set if you wanted to go online or not would have been nice.  The only real sense of progression is earning cash from performing tasks during battles and earning short term sponsors.  You then just the use money to unlock basic customisation of the 'mechs and that's it really.I can see it being more fun as a 4 player party game but even the cooperative 3 players controlling 1 'mech has been removed.  The maps seems very small compared to the original game and the combat feels more streamlined which sounds good initially but now you can't do things like charge your punches and kicks or do double punches for example.  Everything just feels like a compromise to add a few more 'mechs and some Ultraman crossover content.This could have been the next war of the monsters but it just doesn't reach that level of chaotic fun.  Hits feel very weak, being knocked into buildings doesn't have the spectacular impact you would expect and matches can be over so quick it kind of ruins the fun.  4 player brawls are just button mashing madness, the AI is wonky in these matches as well being either super quick to react and pummel you with rapid combo's you can't counter very easily or they are braying dullards, standing in a huddle waiting to be punched into oblivion.For the price it is clearly a budget title but I can think of better games with more going for them for the same price.  Maybe worth a sale and if you can get some friends to buy a copy each it could be good for the party atmosphere.  Otherwise it just isn't worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Override 2: Super Mech League is an extension of Override: Mech City Brawl.   For those who have not played Override: Mech City Brawl, Override is cross between Pacific Rim and Rock 'em Sock 'em Robots.  Override 2: Super Mech League is mainly about your Mech fighting other Mechs.  It's a fun game and I would advise everyone to but this game.  After you have purchased Override 2: Super Mech League, you can also buy the Ultraman DLC.  I have been a fan of Ultraman for years so I was looking forward to buying Override 2: Super Mech League along with the Ultraman DLC.  To be honest, I feel that Override 2: Super Mech League should have been made a DLC to Override: Mech City Brawl.  Making Override 2: Super Mech League a DLC as well as the Ultraman DLC would have allowed players from Override: Mech City Brawl to enjoy this experience.   Again, I would give this game 9 out of 10 stars!

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I get it. It's not the same as the original, but that's okay. The original was a fun, story-driven homage to Pacific Rim. It had wonderful characters and the slow, methodic slapping around of enemies was great! However, it clearly didn't sell well and as much as that really does sadden me (it's a lot of fun!!!) I can understand why: modern fighter fans don't want slow. Modern fighting games have to be lightning fast, otherwise the snobbier players will dismiss it. Instead, we need to look at the sequel for what it offers, not for what it 'should be.' It's fun, frantic, and fast while still carrying a sense of weight to it (though I admit I feel like there should more oomph to each hit. The visual feedback is kinda weak.) The storyline is pretty much a throwaway but who cares? It narrows its focus to try and become easier for people to jump into for a few couch multiplayer bouts. While the original's combat is awesome for a single-player "kick some kaiju ass!", it was just too much for people to take in for a quick brawl with a buddy. Overall, don't hold the sequel right up against its older brother and say "You're different. No sir, I don't like it." Instead, enjoy it for what it IS: a shallow but mindlessly fun WWE with mechs.

_childDocuments_.review: Completely different game from the first.the first game was like a test run not bad but needed more time to mature through the likes of a sequel and then we get override 2 a different game from the first in too many ways and just like the first it feels like it is a test run that needed more work before release both games are like tech demos... they are playable no bugs or glitches from what i can tell graphics are good (better in the first game) gameplay can be fun at times but mostly dull most fun is had with 2-4 player splitscreen especially because the game has no community but as long as you have friends/ family its a non issue however this game ditches the story mode that the first game had in place of a lazy league mode that tries to force online on you and since there is no community you wait for long periods of time for it to stop matchmaking (cant stop it unless you go offline on steam) to fight bots anyway. they also just straight took away customizations from the first game feeling like they are trying to add them later as paid dlc sleezy.... speaking of sleezy devs have a habit of releasing the game and dropping it after release they did it with the first and quickly did it with this one they are no where to be seen dont expect balance patches or qol gameplay changes to advance the game further.+++split screen up to 4players (wouldnt be worth buying otherwise)+big robos+graphics+decent sized roster some missing from the first game though+- different from the first cant say is any worse or better---missing a lot of customization from the first game--no story mode (was in the first game)-forced online for single player league content with no way to silence annoying manager-lazy bare bones gameplay mechanics with little thought put into it especially for a "sequel"-want currency? prepare to grind forever although not much to buy with it anyway unless you like hats-still no playable monsters until season pass completes you will get 1-combos are too simplistic, lockon is atrocious and jump button is more like a very short hop-stages are extremely small compared to the first game-dash button doesnt cover much distance and no run button means people are glued to your faceboth the first and this game could have been amazing or great but both ended up being mediocre at best.dont buy it at all especially without dev support but if you must buy get it on a deep sale 75% off.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how people tested this game and didn't find the issues I have in the first 10 minutes of play time. There is no way to play online with friends outside of private matchs. Why would this ever be a thing in a game that allows you to do 2v2 in the "Leagues" Mode. This game is supposed to be a party brawler but you can't play with a party unless you're fighting your friends. You get nothing in-game for fighting in a private match. No currency, no progression, no satisfaction. As much as I like Override as a whole, I can not and will not recommend people buy it when there is no cross-play at launch when the player base is already small, no party system to 2v2 with friends, and no incentive to play private matches when you get nothing for it.
