And no, you can't go through the menus to stick to the game mode you prefer. This is also an online-only game, meaning you can always come across someone who will completely wreck your day when you just wanna indulge in some power fantasy by spanking bots, like I usually do. I lost my voice screaming at the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.Oh yeah there's no charging attacks anymore, which I feel makes the gameplay overall less fun because it eventually boils down to mashing buttons. Especially with three or more players, which is already the majority of the gameplay modes.All the characters and pilots are gone too, instead your character is some nameless nobody who wants to be the best that no one ever was. Which is disappointing because that completely nullifies the best part of Override, the fact that each and every mech is full of such character and charm, you'd expect it to be full of loud stereotypes and stuff like that. _childDocuments_.review: Game seems really good, mechanics are expanded drastically from the main game (now having various aerial attacks etc)I feel the game might be a bit unbalanced for now, since lock on for projectiles seems to basically ignore jumping, making projectiles pretty hard to consistently dodge (especially day 1 when noone is super good at the game yet). This paired with the endlag on blocks seems to make zoners very strong. Right now I've been playing Atlas, who has some good movement tools but for bulkier characters this might prove even more of an issue.Only downside would be that I feel almost scammed by the lack of single-player content. The "leagues" aren't a "career mode" or "single-player mode". They're just online games though you can press Y to cancel them in order to fight a weak AI. I don't know if they have matchmaking based on player rank, but I hope not since you can way too easily raise this by just fighting AI and there doesn't seem to be a way to move downwards. Other than that there doesn't seem to be any sort of matchmaking.Overall a good fighter to play with friends across the world since this game has roll-back netcode, the 10% launch sale is a good time to get it since single-player is very shallow.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on release after enjoying the first one a fair amount. The mechanical changes were fine and felt like a way of giving each character a more unique fighting style, but they seemed to have leaned into the concept of this game being more online-focused than its predecessor. However, just like the first one, Override 2 never found a dedicated player base. My friend group tried to revisit this game in 2024 through any of the online multiplayer, but found that we couldn't connect to the game's servers. It's unlikely that the developers will revisit this game, so I think it's safe to assume this game is completely dead with a significant portion of its content unavailable to new players.

Kind of like Rock'm Sock'm Robots.I mentioned that this is not meant as a single player experience at the start. I said that because this was meant to be played against other players. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a good time. I played the first Override and had a blast. I haven't played Override 2 long, but I already love it. The game looks, sounds, and feels amazing to play. There's a variety of mechs and stages, the OST fits the setting and genre, and the controls and movements feel fluid and rewarding. After a long day I enjoy a good session of smashing buildings and beating on AI opponents. I don't typically enjoy playing fighting games against random human players, so having the options to play the Versus mode with/against friends/AIs or the League mode against AIs is great. My only gripe so far, and it's a minor one, is that I have to press F3 before every League match in order to play against AIs and not be matched against human players. I wish there was a setting or switch to enable/disable AI or human player matching while in League mode. Other than that personal preference, the game is solid fun. The "cos-mech-ics" for the mechs cover "cool" and "silly" options and are all able to be earned by playing the League mode. So far I haven't had any bugs, errors, frame drops, or other irregularities. In an era when many games are broken on launch it's refreshing to play a fun game that is built and polished well. I won't make any claims about netcode as I have yet to - and probably won't - use the matchmaking system.

name: Nexagon: Deathmatch
detailed_description: Fight battles in a televised tournament in a completely destructible environment where losing means death and winning means freedom. Recruit an unstoppable team of cracker-jack combatants with varying fighting skills and weapons and construct an impregnable fortress of defense, laden with deadly traps and devastating weaponry. Traverse an unforgiving arena collecting rewards and infiltrate the enemy’s stronghold with the intention of destroying it... Happening the years following the brutish skirmishes near the Orion Nebula, a strong feeling of general well being seemed to permeate even into the darkest corners of parliament, where a wild and daring decision concerning the treatment of prisoners was made; a chance for freedom that would supply the Galaxy with an extraordinary new form of entertainment ... THE PIT. Delivers the full package of character building, strategic resource management, and a never-before-seen depth of real-time tactics!! Story Since the late 25th century, Earth's population has skyrocketed, and the face of our blue planet has been transformed into a complex grid of concrete, polymers, and steel. Oxygen trickles into the atmosphere by virtue of precious biospheres that dot the skies in a suspended fragile mesh several miles above the surface. Humans toil and commute alongside the masses of alien races that have since inhabited Earth's centers. Together they have concocted the most voluble and copious of environments known to mankind since the Garden of Eden. At the turn of the fourth millennium, pessimistic speculation led philosophers to believe that Earth was bound for troubled times and that great suffering would engulf the helpless inhabitants. As usual, they were wrong. In fact, in the years following the brutish skirmishes near the Orion Nebula, a strong feeling of general well being seemed to permeate even into the darkest corners of parliament, where a wild and daring decision concerning the treatment of prisoners was made; a chance for freedom that would supply the Galaxy with an extraordinary new form of entertainment ... THE PIT. Features Nexagon is real-time 3D tactics with a refreshing twist on action/strategy gaming. Strike out into a completely destructible environment, where every structure, weapon, building or otherwise, can be entirely obliterated. Design and manage your own persistent, editable base of operations, build defensive structures, traps, weapons, and lavish gardens to please the crowd and protect your investment. Purchase units that gain experience and undergo physical changes over time, becoming more powerful from match to match. Battle your way through 3 separate divisions of enemy contenders, increasing your network value to one day compete in the ultimate fight for freedom … the Nexagon. Gain extra credit supporting your network sponsors through the use of billboards and control of advertising locations. Earn sufficient credit to buy some heavy hitters who will send smaller enemy units crashing into buildings or flying right out of The Pit entirely. Take control of stationary weapons and send mortar fire raining down upon your rivals.

name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch
detailed_description: Six years ago, the Machine Legion invaded and colonized the Torch City, which was originally inhabited by animals. Rayton, the former soldier in the resistance war, has been living in seclusion since then. After his friend is forcibly arrested, Rayton reclaims his mechanical fist and steps to his journey fighting back. And he never expects that he has been involved in a bigger scheme between the mafia, the rebellion, and the legion. Exploring the Metroidvania game world with a dozen of areas with distinguishing vision themes and level designs. Earning the rewards by conquering the challenges of combats, puzzles and platformers in countless chambers, tunnels and shortcuts. Interconnected and automatically loading game map makes the detailed Torch City more convincing and beautiful. Mastering the Fist, the Drill and the Whip, depending on the situation of the battlefield, switch your advantages between the long hits, the high damage and the wide range, taking every enemy standing in front of you down. Dozens of enemies wielding their unique weapons challenge you with exquisite cooperation tactics, and various bosses with totally different combat patterns provides you never repeated experience. The combining of the dieselpunk aesthetics and the oriental-style architecture constructs the core visual style of Torch City, exposing the world with the intense conflict between the furry animals and the mechanical army from their appearance to the nature. Powered by Unreal Engine 4 with physically based rendering and extremely detailed textures, presenting a gorgeous 3D visual performance and pushing the genre to a whole new level.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun, and very pretty looking Metroidvania. Definitely worth a playthrough if you like this genre. It took me about 37 hours to 100% it.Most of the game isn't terribly difficult, but a lot of environmental challenges are unforgiving. However, the master level martial arts challenge and final boss are extremely difficult and are, by far, the most challenging parts of the game - even on normal. The few critiques I have are:- You can't see what your moves are unless you're at a repair station.- Drinking carrot juice takes far too long and is extremely clunky, which is weird because the rocket item that uses the same mechanic is vastly more responsive.- There aren't enough fast travel location and there was no reason to have a subway system and a "teleporting" system, they should have stuck with just 1 of those, or given the subway more spots to travel to.- Putting the teleportation device to the main town inside Urso's attic(?) was an annoying choice. Especially when you couple that with the fact that once you leave Urso's attic to go to town you have to wait for the town door to open every single time you go to it from Urso's.- The combo system, while kinda fun and interesting, is sorta pointless since you can't use them on anything except low level normal enemies. More difficult enemies and bosses will just ignore your combos and special moves while hitting and interrupting you. Learning the master combo is completely pointless since you will never ever be able to use it outside of that challenge.- The Underwater portion needed more polish. The fact that you are forced to only use 1 fist type the entire time underwater seems like the mechanics weren't fully fleshed out. The underwater fighting isn't intuitive at all.- There are a lot of enemies that fight dirty or just take way too many hits to kill. The ninja frogs are a huge offender. They do look cool, but we never learn why there are a bunch of frog and wolf-like robots that are the enemies.- There are some mediocre treasure chests that take a ridiculously long time to get to. It feels like the secrets in this game could use a tune up. Sometimes you'll spend a ton of time navigating to a secret room only to find 20 coins in a chest.I would still recommend this to anyone who likes Metroidvanias because it is a good one, it just needs a little more polish.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on . I am about 2 hours in, and I am loving it.  OK, so I am 12 hours in and I did NOT expect like 30 to 40 % of this game to take place UNDERWATER...It is fun to use your drill to propel yourself around, but it gets old rather quickly, and there are plenty of underwater traversal and combat sequences, where your options are limited. I still have a very positive opinion of the game, but I think it could've cut down on this. I mean, it gives you so many great options for both combat and traversal, yet takes those options away for a large part of the game, which I think is frustrating. Other than that, the review stays as it was before.F.I.S.T. is a 2D Action Metroidvania, not unlike Guacamelee, with heavy emphasis on traversal and combat. The premise is very simple: you play as a bunny with a giant mechanical arm, and are trying to rescue your friend from an oppressive force.The arm is your main weapon and it allows you to perform all sorts of crazy wrestling moves. Combat is tight, responsive and the animations and audio-visual feedback are just insane. The second weapon I unlocked was a Drill, and that is even more over-the-top, as it allows you to perform tornadoes for huge AOE damage. There is also quite a nice amount of depth to be found, as you can switch freely between your weapons, to create stylish combos and toss enemies around, like in Devil May Cry (although the game does NOT have a style meter, that rewards you for switching up your tactics).Outside of that, the usual metroidvania stuff is there, exploration, opening up new areas, backtracking, finding secrets/upgrades etc, I am sure you know the drill. What I commend the game for, is that the upgrades that you unlock in order to open up previously inaccessible areas are actually woven into your general gameplay, rather than just being one-off keys. I found so many metroidvanias underwhelming, because you would unlock an ability/tool that can only be used to open a door, and that's it. But not in F.I.S.T., as here you will learn to do a Sucker Punch, that allows you to break-through doors, as well as send enemies flying. Some minor gripes include an over reliance on ranged enemies. Thankfully projectiles are generally slow, and you have enough movement tools to avoid damage, it's just a little repetitive to always have to prioritize the same enemies in every encounter. There was one boss which I also found to be a little frustrating, but I did manage to learn its patterns, and checkpoints tend to be generous enough (although I found no way to skip the intro cinematic to the boss, which became a little annoying on repeated attempts, even though it was less than 15 seconds long).Should I have a major shift in my opinion as I play through the game, I will be updating my review. But for now, this is a  for any action game fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed F.I.S.T. that much that I chose to 100% it.It's my favourite metroidvania that uses the combo-combat you find in fighting games.  Probably because I dislike those systems and F.I.S.T. allows you to get by without needing to really master much of it.  It's also arguably the nicest looking metroidvania to use a 'somewhat' realistic 2.5D artstyle (Grime and The Mobius Machine being some other examples).You end up with 3 different weapons that attack in UP/Down/Left/Right directions and have 3 buttons to attack (X, Y and B) that can be combined with different directions, though many attacks require you to train and unlock them.  You can pretty much get through most of the game spamming X and using the 'press and hold X' attack with your starting weapon, though you will fare better if you can throw in a bit more than that.F.I.S.T. is a high quality release that gets most of the basics of metroidvanias right while looking quite nice as well.  The map is for the most part what I want out of a metroidvania map.  Areas in different colours, anything I missed marked.  ..Except for the collectable Posters.  Fortunately the one I was missing I could look up online and locate it that way.  They are quite easy to walk past, plenty of other posters in the game are just background scenery which contributes to not always spotting them on your first pass.The fast travel points are a bit spaced out which I can imagine irritating some players, but I found it fine, but then I don't mind a bit of a hike.It rates as an A- for my personal enjoyment.  To get any higher than that it would've needed to:1.  Draw me into its world with great music like Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom or Astalon: Tears of the Earth.  The music in the game is perfectly fine, it's just less my style and kind of quiet in the background, perhaps I should've increased its volume.2.  Provide more non-linearity.  The game did have plenty of places to backtrack whenever I got a power, so I can't fault it too much, but I think everything had to occur in order (Of course, don't quote me future speedrunners!)and 3.  ..I suppose I never cared much about the bunny and his story.  It was perfectly serviceable as a plot and world, but it didn't capture my imagination all that much.Basically, F.I.S.T. does almost everything right for a metroidvania while at the same time just not appealing to some of my tastes to become an absolute favourite.===================== =====================  Aeterna Noctis |  Astalon: Tears of the Earth | Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom | Hollow Knight |   Blasphemous 2 | Cathedral |  Afterimage | The Last Faith |  Elderand | Ori and the Will of the Wisps | Doomblade^ |  Ender Lilies: Quietus of the Knights | Depths of Sanity | Environmental Station Alpha |  |  Blast Brigade | Haak | Biomorph | Turbo Kid |  Alwa’s Legacy | Steamworld Dig 2 | Islets | Blasphemous | After Death | Pronty^ | Mortal Manor* | Escape From Tethys | Outbuddies DX* | Monster Sanctuary | Elliot Quest | Rebel Transmute | Moonlight Pulse |  Haiku, the Robot | The Mobius Machine | Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown | Ultros |  Lone Fungus | Ghost Song | Death’s Gambit: Afterlife | Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night | Kunai | Kingdom Shell | Axiom Verge | Rabi-Ribi | TEVI | Treasure Adventure Game |  Flipwitch | Infernax | Plague of Yamorn* | Column on the Sea | Jrago* | MF-01 Aerostrike^ | Laika: Aged through Blood | Xanthiom Zero | Carrion^ | Chasm | Wuppo | The Mummy Demastered | Momodora 4 | Momodora 5 | Catmaze | Castle In The Clouds | Omega Strike | HunterX | HunterX: code name T | Aggelos | Midnight Castle Succubus | Sheepo |  Ato | EldritchVania | Cookie Cutter | Elephantasy | Rusted Moss^ | Grime | Moonscars | The Messenger | Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth | Iconoclasts | MindSeize | Ebenezer and the Invisible World | Luna’s Light* | Tales of Kenzera: Zau |  Castle In The Darkness | Alwa’s Awakening | Nitrojet* | RIN: The Last Child* | Pharaoh Rebirth | Yoku’s Island Express | Guacamelee! _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: I personally wouldn't recommend this to someone who wants a fulfilling metroidvania experience.I understand where all the praise for this game is coming from. It is gorgeous, and it really nails the dieselpunk aesthetic. From a visual standpoint, an overall experience, this game is a 10/10.Unfortunately, once you start paying attention to the gameplay, it becomes clear that there's a disconnect.  This game has everything a metroidvania should have, on paper at least. It's got the distinct areas, the unique movement mechanics, the unlockable abilities, the boss fights, the traversal puzzle rooms, the secrets and backtracking, etc. However, in practice, these elements don't really mesh together well.For one example: You get three very unique weapons by the end of the game, but their full use is locked behind memorizing combos. Most combos aren't even useful in most encounters, so you end up with this unfulfilled potential of weapons that you use to do the same attacks over and over. Another example is the boss fights. You can tell that someone(s) put a lot of work into the boss animations and movesets. However, they must not have worked very closely with the people working on the main character's movement abilities. The first 3 attempts at most bosses have you end up getting stunlocked to death just because you didn't anticipate one of three different juggling attacks that the bosses trap you in. A final example is the map layout. There are a lot of unique areas, but in most cases, you're only going to go through each once. The story will throw you into an area, you'll go through it in a relatively linear fashion, beating enemies and solving puzzles as you go, and then you'll leave 90 minutes later with a new ability and a couple of collectibles. And that's the last you'll see of the area. Even though the map is all connected, the access points between areas are almost useless. If the story doesn't throw you into a new loading zone, then the transporters around the map become more convenient to get to. You have to be very motivated by 100%ing the game to get you to backtrack through old areas. These are specific examples, but I don't think they are solely responsible for what's lacking in this game. I really think it's just the case of a new studio putting out their first game, and trying to figure out how to make things work. They've definitely gotten their art department locked in, but their game design team honestly just needs some more experience. I think this would have been a more enjoyable experience if they had narrowed the scope a little bit. I would have loved this as a 6-8 hour game. Once I got 10 hours in it started to drag.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to think that Chinese game studios only made gatcha games and rip-offs of better games made in other countries. Then I played FIST. What else can I say? It's a masterpiece among modern Metroidvanias, easily up there with the likes of Bloodstained, Guacamelee and Axiom Verge. The map is sprawling without being confusing, the combat system is in-depth while being easy to pick up, and the story is a compelling tale of corruption, betrayal and heroism in a dieselpunk world inspired by early 20th-century China. If you only play one Metroidvania this year - hell, if you only ever play one Chinese-made game in your entire LIFE - make it this one. You owe it to yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah it's a terrible name. I’ll never get over the PTSD I have now after seeing all the terrible google results for the word “FIST” from trying to find more info about the game. Should have called it Shadow Torch or something.Never saw a Rabbit this badass since cat six one. It's like a Metroidvania with Smash Bros/DMC Combat.It's ultra responsive, nicely weighted, impactful and just a lot of fun.The difficulty feels just right. Not brutal but not easy either. Decent amount of variety in the enemies and it's not afraid to put you in the thick of it.Story is fine while not amazing but it's enjoyable enough and doesn't really get in the way. Characters are likable and well acted for the most part.It has a few small niggly quality of life issues like not being able to skip certain cutscenes but they're pretty minor.It looks great overall and the music is great.Very little to complain about.Treat yourself to this game if you’re a fan of Hollow Knight, Ori, Guacamelee, Super Metroid etc. You won’t regret it.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to say that this isn't a bad game by any means. I think this game has a good foundation. But there are multiple problems with the game that lead me to say that I would want them to do something a bit better than this. Firstly, the story. It's rushed, all over the place, and lacking the character development to make you actually feel something about them. One minute, Rayton is being praised for his heroics, and the next, he's being bashed for being stoic and dense. Lady Q and Urso do not have enough time to be fleshed out as individual characters to have a meaningful impact on the story. The same with Cicero. This guy is seen, what, 4 times in the actual story!? 5 maybe? And out of all the characters, I probably was the most interested in his backstory, which we got basically NONE of. Without spoiling anything, I just feel like he was one of the most underdeveloped characters I've seen in a while. And honestly, the same could be said for the main character, Rayton. Like, he's a "rabbit hero," while having no flashbacks to his heroics. We're just told he's one, and given one scene that's supposed to prove it. We don't see enough interactions of him that aren't business. He's just bland. Boring. The ending is rushed and empty.In terms of gameplay, there are pros and cons. The combo system is actually pretty good, especially with the weapon-switching from Fist to Drill to Whip. The ground and aerial potential of combos is impressive. The problem? There are a lot of bosses in this game that either armor through your hits, or are unable to be launched into the air, making these "master combos" largely useless. The final boss is about 3x harder with the Fist and the Drill, mostly because of the parry that takes off 3 health bars from you, plus the fact that you can be parried MID-COMBO. The Whip makes the final boss a joke. Insane damage, hardly any combos. Fights where you can launch bosses and do combos are actually entertaining, but without that? Fights are just stale. Use the best weapon and do the same optimal combo that can't really be punished because of the whip's range. The Drill honestly becomes largely useless after the Whip is obtained.Collectibles are fine. No issues there. I did a Normal playthrough, but didn't 100% the game (only managed to 98% it), but did like the Plant Seeds, Posters and Data Disks. Platforming was also for the most part, pretty good, though there were times that were scuffed in the hovering sections. Not going to mention PC specific issues because by their own admission, they are still attempting to optimize it.All in all, I think this is an ok game with a subpar story and decent gameplay. Personally, though, I wouldn't recommend it. I just feel like after beating the game, I'm left unsatisfied. Hell, the ending is just like dumping a bucket of water on an already dying flame. It was a complete letdown. But hey, just my opinion here. Platforming: 8.5/10Story: 4/10Combat Gameplay: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Metroidvania 2D platformer with a steampunk theme. Plus there are fuzzy wittle animals! Pros- Interesting storyline- There are a variety of difficulty settings to suite your preference- The collective of maps is fairly large with plenty of opportunity to explore, numerous items to collect, and plenty of save points... plus there are a few "transports" to  quickly move between maps- "The fist" -and it's variations ;)- are pretty cool, each having several visually striking attack upgrades- The "execution" option to demise foes is pleasantly reminiscent of the MK series-Controller config makes sense and is adaptable - Devs borrowed a few SSB Melee/Brawl moves. I loved those games so I'm counting that as a plus. - You can move faster by dashing and it doesn't drain energyCons-Attacks are slow and easily interrupted by an enemy hit... if you don't upgrade/are slow to upgrade combos the fights will become very repetitive-Areas within maps look very similar making it easy to get lost or become reliant on your map tool for orientation- Much of the first part of the game requires travel by foot between maps, which can become tedious and "transports" aren't an option until you exit the 3rd map- I don't notice the music and in a Steampunk themed game, I think I shouldI definitely enjoy this game. Is it worth the money? I'm leaning towards yes, but the jury is still out. But it's available to demo so you can see for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I currently wouldn't recommend FIST, I think that will change if the developers can patch out a lot of the bugs and glitches.Several crashes, graphical glitches, entire areas turning into slideshows for 30 seconds at a time (settings didn't matter), and a really poorly thought out control system mar what is otherwise a pretty good time for the most part.The "training" section is a great advert for how poor the controls are when set against what they were attempting to achieve.  If you can't complete the "training" (for combos you literally will not ever, ever use no less), you cannot complete the game 100% as one of the missing shards is tied to completing the "training" challenges.  With a parry system so horrendously implemented as to be completely useless (you need to face toward an attacker, then push toward them at the right time on an analogue stick), you are going to get hit an awful lot in combat, and often stun locked.  It goes down with a special dash later, but it is still nowhere near fit for purpose especially when it really seems to be a core part of the combat.  There's no block either, with you having to attempt to parry attacks from both melee and from ranged attackers while you go.So I'm currently writing the review with the 2nd final boss fight still to do, and the "Master" level of the training challenges.  I don't think I'll be bothering with them to be honest, with the main reason being the convoluted control system.There is a really good fun time in here, it just needs some polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, tight controls but the issue on parry using stick is a deal breaker for me. I play on controller. After some testing, I found it registers flawlessly using the d-pad, but not on stick. It appears it is because of the "walk" animation due to the sensitivity function of stick (you cannot parry while walking). Unfortunately, I am not used to playing movement on d-pad anymore. There is no option to remap this to another button press.I enjoyed Sekiro very much, and loved mastering the parry timing so this is very important to me. Will become a positive and enthusiastic upvote from me once this issue is fixed.If you don't want to bother with parrying on stick (or use keyboard/d-pad for movement), go ahead and purchase this as you won't encounter issues.

_childDocuments_.review: FIST is a great game, but I'm hesitant to call it a good Metroidvania.Each area the game takes you through is fairly linear, and you'll only revisit them if you want to get collectibles or data disks (used to unlock some moves).  Otherwise you never need to return.  There's a few areas midway through the game you can 100% complete on your first pass.I find the combat system enjoyable, but I question some design decisions.  It's a gambit every time you go into to attack, because you don't know if you'll interrupt your opponents move or not.  Many attacks from enemies will just super armor their way through and hit you anyway.You start with a dash, but not really a dodge.  You can't dash through enemies until you get a VERY late game upgrade, which personally made combat flow much better not being body blocked by enemies.  You aren't given a block / parry ability until about halfway through either.  I've played games with a similar parry mechanic, so it wasn't too out of left field for me to figure out, but it does NOT like analog sticks.  I had to swap my movement to the D-Pad on my Logitech F310.  From there parrying was actually pretty easy.  But just like with enemies super armoring through attacks, sometimes parrying will stun the enemy completely, and other times it will just negate damage.  Early on you also get a charge up punch which is shown that it can be used as a counter move against a bosses rocket punch, but it's never utilized again after that.Storyline wise it's better than most Metroidvanias.  My only complaint is that if you press the confirm button too soon in a conversation where action is happening, then you'll go from talking to punching without seeing what triggered it in between.Eventually you get a hang of the combat and find what combos work well for you and steamroll most enemies.  Some of the bosses can be challenging, but not anything too rough.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Important:I played the game on SteamDeck. I had to reduce nearly all settings to "low". This way the combos were not lagging etc. but maybe this was also the cause for some strange effects.COMBATThe combat is pretty nice. It starts easy with same easy enemies and will get harder later in game. Also "old" locations will be upgraded with heavier units. The only thing I didn't like about the game were the enemies who can shoot. I am not sure if it was only coincidence, but it somehow always felt like the enemy is exactly knowing where you will land with your character and shoots at exactly this position.In some cases this is really painfull since you cannot even move. I had situations where I was hit by multiple enemies in different combos in a row and believe it or not: I could not even stand up and was killed. These moments made me nearly smash my controller.BOSSESThe bosses are a huge pain. If you get angry really fast due failures ... then avoid this game. Some of the bosses are such a pain, you will curse the developers and all gods you know. But in the end ... the solution is to memorize their patterns (for this you need many tries) and learn to dodge or counterattack. But using the SteamDeck it was sometimes only luck if the controls did what you told to do.And you also need to learn the combos. If you use them correctly, you sometimes can instant kill a boss. But in my case it was most time the same combo (a very basic one).GRAPHICSThe graphics are really nice. The atmosphere is pretty cool. I liked all the characters and all locations. Also the "minigames" and achievements are pretty well done. But on my SteamDeck I encountered some issues if you switch between some locations. The textures and objects were not loaded so you had blue background and colliders ... after running for a while the level was build correctly. But you could watch the renderer building everything ... it was that slow.STORYVery interesting. Also very well done because of the characters. I only miss the german audio. Would have preferred a full german language included.You can discover a lot of stuff in the game and you will get some weapons and utilities during the gameplay. I liked it very much. All in all, it was a nice adventure. But difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical when I first heard of this game, but being such a fan of the metroidvania genre I had to try it out. What got my attention from the get go is the art direction. This game looks fantastic! All of the modern graphical bells and whistles, packed into a side-scrolling platformer featuring anthropomorphic animals — what's not to love? The world looks and feels lived-in; a fictional China if the population were a bunch of furry animals, and with a surprisingly high level detail of from neon signage to in-game decals, it's the small things that deliver the love and dedication the developers had for this game. Not to mention how many different biomes it has (it has several), the world will keep you going back to reference the map more times than expected. The cast of character's designs are spot-on and memorable, voice acting and animation is well executed. Even the NPCs were given enough attention that they feel like they're part of a cast rather than just random placeholders in the map. F.I.S.T's gameplay however is its strongest suit. The action lends itself well to a controller and has enough weight that you feel Rayton's punches land. There's a certain satisfaction that you get if you manage to run a difficult combo and execute perfectly. I'm a sucker for that, that's for sure. There are a few instances when the moves didn't register as I wanted, but not too often that it broke the experience for me. The difficulty in the AI is good: not super punishing, but not push-over easy, and the variety of different enemies kept me wanting in anticipation for the next one. The tedium of grabbing all the collectibles was made lighter by the many varied enemy instances that it didn't come off as boring or taxing. But if its gameplay is the high point, the main story falls short and is something i'd consider pretty generic; typical hero narrative, with a supporting cast that don't really do much. As memorable as Ursus the bear is or Chuan the red panda, I wish they had more involvement in the narrative as I would have loved to see them in more scenes. That said, I wish they worked Lady Q's character more into the game. Despite that, I still felt the story to be compelling enough for a 20-hour playthrough. Lastly, the sound design in this game was amazing. The SFX they used for the attacks, enemy soundbites, ambient sfx of traffic and chatter were all top notch. The music perfectly complimented the action, and it almost took a life of its own with all the orchestration and jazz licks that you are able to sample as you play through the game. I thought that the voice acting (except for Rayton's stoic performance) was pretty good, and the cutscenes — particularly the fight choreography — are gorgeously made. Overall, I think this game is one of the better metroidvanias I've played in recent years. I'd for sure be on the look out for future DLCs or sequels, as I'm sure this wouldn't be the last to come out of the studio. A definite must-try for casual gamers, and a sure-buy for fans of the genre. An easy 8.5 out 10 carrots.

_childDocuments_.review: The China Hero Project is an interesting initiative, a few years ago Sony’s Playstation division decided to sponsor and help new promises from the chinese indie scene and quite a lot of projects appeared from that new initiative, the most recognizable were “Lost Soul Aside”, “ANNO: Mutationem” and “F.I.S.T. Forged in Shadow Torch” which is the one that I will be reviewing. I must confess at first I didn’t give it any attention, yeah, it looked very promising but it wasn’t in my radar, that was until game released and I started reading about it and damn, everything looked really good, so, after completing it at 95% (save, no achievements) and 18.5 hours of gameplay I think I can safely say that this is the surprise of the year for me.Is this game worth your time and money? Let’s find out.We play as Rayton who lives in Torch city, a place under the Iron Legion’s domain, an authoritarian regime. Rayton refuses to be part of the resistance as he lost a lot in the big war that took place prior to the regime but that changes when the Legion takes his friends as prisoners and he must rescue them. In the process they will meet Q, a mysterious feline warrior that tries to protect something that the Legion wants at all cost, the Spark, something ancient. The more we get involved in this, the more we will discover about the spark and the true intentions of those mechanical enemies.I’m going to be completely honest here, the story is flat, it’s a mere instrument to keep you busy going from one place to the other as most metroidvanias do, it is not a bad story at all, however, I don’t think it’s deep or interesting enough to highlight it because this game truly shines thanks to two main factors, level design and gameplay loop. Characters aren’t bad but once again, they are flat entities that at the end of the day won’t matter that much as everything is very straight forward, this doesn’t mean this is a bad thing, not at all, it works perfectly for what the game wants to accomplish and in this case the story is what it should be, the main line to follow from beginning to end.In the same way characters seemed to be built specifically for gameplay purposes. The cartographer, the seed boy, the vendors, Urso for paint upgrades, etc… At the end of the day all elements are part of a mechanical system that works perfectly to make this a very fun and engaging experience.While I said that story is not that interesting, I must say that visuals are over the top for a game like this. Is this level of detail necessary for the experience? Hell no but holy smokes, this game is truly beautiful.Torch city and nearby areas have a very distinctive visual style, it kind of reminds me of a mix between Hong-Kong streets in the 80’s combined with a dieselpunk style, a mix between classic real world style with a mechanic heart on it. The streets are fully detailed with 3D elements in the background to give you the sense of depth even though it plays like a 2D game, the main hub of operations, which is also a street but with interiors fully modeled, is STUNNING too as it’s the most visual intensive area, those background streets look phenomenal. In general I would say they nailed every inch of the map to create a cohesive and interesting world.Animations are something that sometimes are a bit weird, specially when characters are talking and in-game cinematics are running, but in general in-game animations are responsive and really well done. Visual effects like particles and dashes are also really well done, in general I would say this game has a really good visual level, way more impactful than it needs for the kind of game it is, however, this really helps us to get immersed into this world and this journey.I won’t comment on level design just yet as I think it makes more sense to talk about once we talk about the gameplay loop as it’s a very important element.What about sound? Well, music in general is really great, in fact once you explore each area at 100%, the cartographer will reward you with a music disc to listen to those tracks, each area has a different music track and I must say that they are really great. When it comes to voice acting, I played this game with english dub and the cast did a really good job, although there were a few lines in which I think two different members dubbed the same character for different lines? The one that I noticed the most was the cartographer when rewarding you, I don’t know why the line in which he shows his appreciation sounds like a different person, nothing bad just weird hehe.Anyway, let’s jump directly into the juicy stuff, gameplay loop and level design.Torch city is an interconnected labyrinth full of tunnels, hidden spots and alternative routes that you will be unlocking the more abilities you unlock. There’s a room there you can’t reach? Keep going and once you get a new ability try reaching it again, this is how it works with metroidvania games, backtracking is required in order to unlock all content and trust me, there’s a lot to unlock; Seeds, Data disks, posters that will unlock paint jobs, locked boxes that require special keys and mysterious shards that you will need to find. All those elements will be hidden but they will come in handy for upgrades and to unlock even more content. Don’t forget about HP, SP and side effect bar upgrades, they look like capsules and you will need 3 in order to get an upgrade, most are scattered around the map while others require special things (like buying them or getting them via activity completion) this will come in handy, trust me.Once you unlock all three tools from your mechanical fist, you will get access to a ton of movements which once unlocked will make the combat experience and the traversal something really great. Let’s start with traversal, once you unlock the three main movements that are needed to completely reach all places of the map things will get fun, why? Because movement becomes something dynamic and not only that, exploring the map is in general fun as it will make you move constantly, it’s not about straight lines but jumps, coordination and in general a fun route.When it comes to combat, things can get ugly for our enemies, at first our movement set is quite limited but it won’t take long until we start having upgrades that will make each combat something spectacular, a combination of movements and an upgraded SP/HP bars is something that by the end of the game you will truly appreciate as things will become dynamic and fun, you can also switch your weapon in the middle of a combat, however I don’t think I would recommend doing that, try to learn each tool by their own and master them. My favorite without any doubt is the drill, that tool is brutal as heck, and executions with it are amazing.As for the PC performance, I didn’t have any problem although I think it might be a bit demanding but can’t say I had a bad experience as my performance was perfect all time, no drops, no stuttering, in general a very smooth experience with everything at max.In conclusion, F.I.S.T. is a very solid and stunning metroidvania that might not be in your radar, but trust me, it is very worth your time even if you don’t want to complete it at 100% although I would say it won’t be a hard thing to do if you enjoy movement and traversal, in general I would say that, while it doesn’t really create anything new, it refines the metroidvania formula and does a very great job.I seriously hope you have an amazing experience with this game as I did, Rayton and Torch City need you.

_childDocuments_.review: To the people complaining there is no exit button; its in the game settings menu like so, so many other Chinese/Japanese games. Yeah I know its not how we do it in western games but its predictable.I have a short amount of playtime as of this first posting, but the TL:DR is, this is a combo-based fighter game in a metroidvania world wrapped in a anime-style story. Gameplay holds up and is challenging, if you expect to dead-cells your way through this, think again. Enemies will stop you in your tracks, you can't roll or dash through them (at least not yet, at my stage of the game) and so you *have* to learn which attacks clear which mobs best. And when you nail it, its awesome. When you don't, you will get clobbered.My only real gripes are, not being able to turn off motion blur completely, DLSS settings being vague, and.. the music is pretty good (especially the level-up skills menu lol) but.. the tracks are *so* short. They loop after a very, very short time and with an obvious fade-in. Given how long you might be in an area, or paused, I think the soundtrack should have room to breathe and set the tone but *the tracks are so damn short*. Why? Is it stock licensed music or did they just tell the composer to only write like 1-2 minute long loops (that don't even seamlessly loop, but probably could if they didn't have the fade-in every time). Just, an odd choice for a metroidvania which usually have elaborate area soundtracks.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this game really blew me away... i'm generally not that into steampunk and certainly not into antropomorphic animal characters but this game is just too good to miss out on! It exudes charm and attention to detail in every single area... Environments and characters feel lively and the backgrounds burst with personality thanks to everything that's going on such as people getting extorted by crime gangs, cars driving by, machinery buzzing and pipes leaking. The whole city feels alive and the whole experience is incredibly immersive because of it. I got sucked into this game for 3 days straight, doing pretty much everything the game had to offer bar a few things. I'd gladly count it among my favorite metroidvania's of all time along the likes or Ori, blasphemous and haiku the robot. It really is because of games such as these that MV's are my favorite genre, and i can't wait to revisit this one later down the line. If i haven't convinced you yet to pick it up i'll go ahead and discus each aspect in more detail but suffice to say that i really think this game is worth your time and money, even at full price! Now to get into the details;I say this for every metroidvania but level design is the most important aspect for a MV to get right. I'm glad to say that FIST is pretty much a ten out of ten in this department. Not only is the map absolutely ENORMOUS, it's also filled with secrets, collectables, side routes, shortcuts and all the other metroidvania goodness. I'm not gonna say i rushed this game but i went through it at a steady pace and it still took me 15 hours to fully explore all the areas. The mapping screen is super usefull and clear to help with backtracking, so navigating and 100%ing the map was an absolute joy as well as being worthwhile with usefull upgrades. The movement in this game (which is imo the second most important aspect for a MV) is also super fluid, so all the wall climbing, grappling and platforming around the map was super fun, even in combat.Combat itself is also masterfully done with a robust and indepth combo system that allows you to chain lock enemies once you've mastered it. I never played street fighter or smash games but this is how i imagine they feel like. The combo's are diverse with satisfying animations, particle and sound effects. Each one is also usefull so you're not just sticking with one but instead are actively encouraged to keep mixing it up. Enemy variety isn't that high but each one is a joy to fight, there's some especially nasty ones that can quickly take you out if you're not carefull. Enemies are also mixed and matched often to create a large variety of encounters, despite the small assortment. There's also a dozen or so bosses to really test your skill, most are doable but some took several tries without every feeling unfair. The final 3 bosses especially were super well crafted, and without giving away anything there's even an ori style escape to test your quick thinking and reflexes!If level design, movement and combat in a game are this good it's already a great experience so visuals are sort of like the cherry on top. Once again the game knocks it out of the park here with high quality models, textures and lighting in every nook and cranny. I'm normally not that big on 2.5D but this game looks absolutely gorgeous. Like i mentioned at the start it's also chockfull of little details that make the city feel alive and breathing. There's also a very large variety of environments, from flooded caverns, to power plants, abandoned miners, ancient temples and bustling streets. This game has it all. The music isn't that memorable but it felt like it fit with the whole tone and mood of the world very well. Sound effects are great, they really add punch to your attacks and the voice acting is superb. Sadly the english VA is missing for side dialogues but for all the main story related stuff it's there and it's very well done. Especially the main character rayton, who has this satisfying gravely voice.Speaking of Story this is one of the areas where the game doesn't stand out as much, it's decent and doesn't detract from the otherwise great game but it is relatively predicatable and not as interesting as it could've been. The writing is mostly pretty good, apart from one sorta cringey side character, but most of it is borderline cliche. Still this doesn't matter to me because the world itself does half the storytelling, and it does that extremely well. Lastly there's bugs and performance and while the game does have a little bug here and there, the quality and polish of it all is too high for those few bugs to hamper the experience. Performance is smooth once it gets going, but loading in a new area can cause a big framedrop (down to the 20's) for several seconds. However once that's loaded in the game stabilizes and the lag is gone, even when returning to areas once they've loaded in during your play session.i can hardly say anything negative about the game and the things i can say are understandable little flaws or nitpicks. I know this review is full of superlativs but that is for good reason. The game is all around extremely well made, and an easy recommendation to any fan of sidescroller, metroidvania's or steampunk. It's one of the best games i've played this year and has earned it's place among the favorite games in my library. I think scoring a game is a flawed concept but if i had to this would probably be somewhere between a 9-9,5/10. An easy recommendation even at full price, and a steal at a sale, don't miss out on this one folks!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally it is released on Steam after initially launching on PlayStation first! We had to wait a few weeks but boy was it worth it. This game just oozes quality! There are lots of moves and combos to unlock as you progress which keeps things fresh.From what I've seen so far, there are lots of secrets to uncover in the city metroidvania style, so this is going to keep you going quite a while especially if your going for all the achievements as well, as I will be. _childDocuments_.review: The new metroidvania about a rabbit with a huge mechanical fist that puffs out robotic invaders literally embodies the "hurricane gameplay" thesis, reducing the parry value to about zero. This is one of the few drawbacks of the game, but parrying here is the thing that you really do not want to use, moreover, this ability appears quite late and you no longer want to retrain. The game very skillfully forces you to be fast, mobile, constantly strike, get away from attacks with the help of dash, predict the moment of the attack, use special attacks in time, disrupting possible damage from the enemy, make long and most deadly combos. Parrying does not fit here at all, especially when it is performed in such a very peculiar way. Fighting enemies here is incredibly fun, you arrange crazy brawls on the screen, throwing enemies with your fist, pulling and pushing them with your drill, predatory whipping them with a whip, or even combining all three available styles. It's a real adrenaline rush, it's a decent challenge to player skill, it's fun.But no matter how fun it was to fight with ordinary enemies, the main thing in such games is the bosses. And they decently hit you in the back of the head. Almost each of them makes you experience a gamut of emotions from "It is impossible to kill him, I want to remove Steam" to "I figured out your secret, scoundrel, well, now you will get it in full, my fist rules here." Bosses are varied, fights with them are very entertaining, there are also hidden bosses that you may not even meet in the main plot. The main opponents here really feel like the main ones, the completion of some important segment of the path, and not just rotten blockheads to fill the time. The design of the levels is competent, I just did not like the levels with swimming at all, and the pace of movement is too slow in them. Yes, you will have to do some serious backtracking to find all the collectibles and improvements, but this is not particularly forced. The game is insanely pleasing with its visual picture, so juicy that you want to drink it like juice. The plot is sometimes too dramatic, but keeps itself within the framework of a completely competent story, in which everything must end well, which is a pleasure.The game has a lot to offer both the hardcore player and the amateur unfamiliar with the genre. She is fast, angry and cheerful, abundantly wetting the rusted gears of spinal reflexes with adrenaline. Unambiguous positive recommendation

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty ok! Has moments of genuine coolness mixed in with bits and bobs that could do with an improvement, and a couple small things that are very frustrating to boot.The story itself is ok. It's not going to win an award by any means but it'll take you on a simple enough journey.--Pros.The setting is truly wonderful. The 3D backdrops for this 2D side scroller are gorgeous to look at at times - and the way the lighting is utilised just makes for such immersive scenery. I hit a hanging light by accident and the thing threw itself around - lighting the character and the environment dynamically as it moved. There are enemies that use the 3D space nicely as well, so it's really cool.The character models and designs are memorable, unique and the main char Rayton is so damn fluffy.The premise and utility of the fist strapped to your back is really interesting and unique.The soundtrack by Caisheng Bo does the job well, with a couple of the songs truly slapping. (you'll know the ones)Once you unlock yourself a couple of abilities, navigating the world starts to genuinely become a fun experience.--Cons.Parrying never really felt reliable. Using the joystick you have to tap in the direction of the projectile or attack to parry, rather than just having a dedicated parry button a-la Sekiro. Hold that direction button for too long and you're no longer parrying. Just felt a bit clunky.There's very little diversity in foes. Expect 5 or 6 robotic mob types, and bosses who are regular enemies with a couple extra moves and a health bar. You'll fight the same baby blue bomb throwing tank at least 4 times in the story, and then you can expect most bosses to have a double boss or a mob rush encounter later into the game.Localisation. Expect a few incorrect words here and there. Some of the speech is hokey as hell, and when it's not stiff it's very basic. There's a lot of "saying the same thing but from multiple characters" repetition. Also some pretty strange turns of phrase. There's a bunny collecting seeds who will ask you "Did you find it? The seed in the glass?" Referring to "it" like it's a singular seed, when no, there are loads of them to find in the map.A few instances of odd 3rd person declarations, particularly from Urso. Sometimes they'll use other character's names as if they aren't in the room - despite talking to said character directly. A paraphrased example: "I should really take Rayton out some day" - Urso, talking directly to Rayton. Just weird and a bit unfortunate, but hey, it's fine. It took me out of taking the characters seriously a little bit, but it's not a deal breaker.Traversal. There aren't very many fast travel points. Expect a lot of map checking and back tracking.Plot Twists. They were not handled well. Saturday morning cartoon level "mwahaha"ing threw me thoroughly out of the experience.A major personal gripe that did bring nothing but annoyance was a dummy training set of challenges. Screw wasting time on that. I have better things to do than grapple with inconsistent controls and unforgiving time windows.All in all this is a game i want to like, and in some ways do. But not without a robotic fist sized dollop of "could be better." Still, for the first outing, this is a fine experience if you like metroidvanias, moreso you're furry trash like me. :3

_childDocuments_.review: It looks fantastic - especially the animal people, I'll give it that. But during my two hours I found the world uninteresting, and the combat was so awkward it drained all my will to continue.It feels like the enemy designer and the combo designer never talked to each other. Enemies are fast, have quick attacks, their projectiles are slow; it feels like combat perfectly suited for parry/dodge-heavy gameplay. But you can't really "dodge" (you can dash, but it's just a large, not very fast move), and parry - once you find it - costs points which also are used by the healing potion. On top of that, your movements are slow semi-combos that feel hard to execute. So you'd think you're a juggernaut, one/two-shotting bad guys, yeah? No - they all take far too many hits; you almost don't want to engage them.Then there's the issue of enemy variety. All enemies are robot troops, except there are also those annoying robo-frogs. Those are a total pain to fight due to, again, them being quick and agile while you're slow. They come in big and small varieties, but are essentially the same. The robot troops I saw three types of: sword, gun, and heavy axe. Sword and gun feel almost exactly the same, heavy axe are a little tougher and resistant to pushback, but otherwise also the same. I feel like a good metroidvania should have decent enemy variety, and perhaps there are more enemies later on, but I'll never know.Another thing that defines a metroidvania is "ability locked doors". The fun comes from figuring out which tool do you need to open this passage. Here, it's not only marked on the map, but also a popup shows up telling you exactly which ability you need to use to open this door, no matter if you have it or not. There's no way of turning those popups off. Taking away all my fun from experimentation is what it does. They appear more than once, even after you've learned that those doors can be opened with this ability, insulting your memory.The music in the first area is so repetitive, it almost drove me crazy. The (English) voice acting is alright. What's great is the clear attention to detail when it comes to backgrounds; a lot of work must've gone into that. The characters also look stellar in all their furry glory, retaining their animal characteristics while displaying human-like expressions. Excellent work. That said, the first thing you see in the game is a cutscene where a shapely catgirl runs away from some drones, while breasting boobily doing parkour. Lots of effort on display. Too much, perhaps; I'd rather have the game played well - I know of other places where I can look at catgirls breasting boobily.Don't get me wrong; there are far worse games out there. If you don't care about the metroidvania aspect and don't mind clunky combat, the worldbuilding seems somewhat interesting - during cutscenes at least. However, there are also far, far better experiences if you look for them. Hope that helped.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely my GOTY 2021. An excellently executed metroidvania beat em up with well designed areas, great feeling movement, super fun (and challenging) boss fights with gorgeous graphics to boot. The soundtrack is also quite nice, and I found it extremely fulfilling of my need for a fun fast paced metroidvania.The story is pretty simple, about a rabbit named Rayton who, when his big bear friend gets thrown in jail, decides it's time to fully un-regime his city from a bunch of robo-soldiers oppressing it and break his friend out of jail with a big mechanical fist that he wears like a backbling. You get some other weapons further into the game, each with their own movement ability that makes the platforming more interesting, with an excellent interlacing of both combat tools and movement tools at the same time. The depth of the combat in this game is quite high, with optional combo challenges that are even quite useful in learning creative ways to juggle between multiple weapons simultaneously, and with a boss rush unlockable post game and a massive myriad of collectables that are cleverly hidden throughout the map, 100%ing this game was a blast. For some reason i've read people thought there weren't reasons to revisit previous areas, but there are plenty of secrets and items that you can only get with later power ups, so I don't know what they were on about.My one criticism of this game personally is only a warning that the combat may be a tad difficult late game for people who aren't that good at beatem ups or combos (or parrying, woof some of those later bosses). If you worry about "getting juggled and having to use the same moves over and over (because you don't want to learn the combo system)", this game may be a tad tough for you. If you enjoy fighting games though, it might be more up your alley. Overall, this game is a 10/10 for me, a shocking sleeper hit that doesn't get talked about enoughI also found it quite funny that they introduce the cat woman like she's going to be some kind of relevant love interest but rayton visibly doesn't care because he'd rather fight an entire army for one of his male friends, lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrying a giant fist on your back as you go about slapping mechanical constructs sure sounds like a fun premise. So let's see if this little rabbit is hiding a butterfly underneath his paws, or is it perhaps something more fetid.Perhaps my IQ isn't high enough to fully comprehend the complexity of this cheesy and predictable story set in a dieselpunk furryverse, but I do know that the glowing thing everyone wants is orange. And what is orange? That's right - an orange...also carrots. Hence the hero bunny, Rayton, wants to find it, so the villain bunny, Cicero, doesn't. Conflict ensues, friend becomes foe, and only one will have the orange thingy.Orange aside, the furries are bland and forgettable. None has any depth to their motivations which ultimately makes them flat. Heck, the main baddie is on screen for 10 minutes and is severely underused, as is his connection to Rayton. It should have received more attention than a  Also, Rayton is a pretty forgettable protagonist. Ma man goes from "" to "" in two seconds. All it took was his friend getting thrown in prison. Cool. But what about all the people who lost their lives before that? Guess that just wasn't good enough of a motivation for our great hero.And even if the game is fully voiced and ripe with cutscenes, the writing made sure all of it went to waste. There was some cheesy dialogue, so that's nice. But I did love the performance of the English voice actor for Rayton. My man channelled his inner Christopher Daniel Barnes during impactful moments.Ah, childhood memories.As a Metroidvania, you know what to expect; Lots of backtracking, barred off areas inaccessible just yet and plenty of unique abilities and weapons for you to find and try out. But, a couple of crucial missteps drag the whole experience down.Since exploration is a crucial part of the experience, it had to be good.  It was fun to hop around Torch City thanks to the game's fluid animations and amazingly responsive controls. But, the world is utterly lifeless. I like the dieselpunk aesthetic, yet so much of the map is just useless empty space. I couldn't even be bothered to hunt for the many secrets, finishing at a measly 76% completion. They succeeded in conveying a sense of scale with the map design, but so much of it is empty that made exploring tedious. It's simply too big . And the area design didn't help either. While there are some standout areas, like the streets of Torch City under the jurisdiction of the Rat Gang, most of my time was spent traversing bland, ugly and empty pipes and caves with zero personality.Nevertheless, everybody is aware that exploration is not a core part of a Metroidvania and thus shouldn't be fun. If the combat is good, then there is still hope. And it is good. Indeed it is. I love the combo approach and had fun mixing weapons mid-combat to continue my slapping of the enemies iron cheeks. To help you do that, you have the  and . Each weapon does have its own unique set of moves and advantages over the others. The fun comes from switching them on the fly during combat, chaining together devastating combos. But, the  are not that useful for bosses or mini-bosses. So I stuck to ? And these special moves deal tremendous amounts of damage but need one bar of  to use. However, you needn't worry about not having enough of it; Besides some enemy drops that restore it, slapping enemies around with your light or heavy attacks recharges it. So get to slapping! And these special moves are obtained from the games pretty extensive skill tree. You'll need  alongside the game's currency to unlock skills. Sadly, there are no new moves in tier 3, as those picks just add more damage to these moves. But let's talk about my main issue with the combat - , you must first  to reach you, and just as it's about to boop that little bunny noes of yours, then you . This single design choice made me loathe combat with more than one single enemy. It just doesn't work when you are getting ganked. Also, the parry window is small, and there is no specific animation to let me know if I even attempted the parry. It'll either work or not. And that's how I'll know. Wonderful.And now we move to - . There are four unique pieces of equipment you'll utilize to rid Torch City of the Machine Legion - a  (yes, there is a second parry option for whatever reason) and . Now, these items should complement the combat. But not here. No. Instead, let's limit the player by having all of the equipment use the same . Why use the rocket shotgun or the exploding puppets and risk running out of health potions during a boss fight? This problem isn't as terrible during your clashes with the mobs because of a specific skill that regenerates one EP bar per execution. But yeah, during boss battles, using anything other than a health potion is not a sound financial investment.Yet, a few rays of sunshine still managed to slip through these cumulonimbus clouds.Platforming and puzzle-solving were quite enjoyable, even if they lacked variety or challenge. It was more like a fun distraction as I made my way towards another group of mobs in need of some good ol' fisting. Speaking of mobs, their variety, visually and gameplay-wise, is excellent. At first, it might seem like you'll fight the same two enemies, but as the story picks up pace, new enemies start showing up, all with unique movesets and skills. , making some sections quite challenging. The samurai gave me more trouble than I'd like to admit, mainly because of the god awful parry implementation I ranted about earlier. Besides smashing mobs with my giant fist, . They have a great variety of moves, and as the fight progresses, they become stronger and adopt new attacks, ramping up the challenge. But, I do have an issue -. Some show their point of impact and range, but some don't, leaving you to take it like a man first and ask questions later. And since the parry system is awful, I had to die just to see the full scope of the bosses arsenal. But, I still did enjoy fighting the bosses once I knew the whats and hows of their moves. And lastly, the game's soundtrack was surprisingly good, with certain boss tracks getting the juices flowing. I also loved the jazzy background tune as you stroll through the Rat Gang controlled streets of Torch City. I just have a soft spot for some good ol' jazz.So while my 15h adventure in Torch City wasn't a steaming pile of rabbit droppings, it also wasn't entirely enjoyable either. Too many poor design choices hold back what could have been a standout title of 2021 and a damn good Metroidvania as well.

_childDocuments_.review: F.I.S.T is an...interesting...metroidvania. I mean, I logged 20 hours into the game and I've almost 100%'d it, but I'm not sure if I'd be stoked to play it again.I really like some parts of the game! The art direction for the game is absolutely fantastic, does a good job at immersing you in that dieselpunk type setting for the most part, and has areas that, while they blend together a bit too much, are all nice to look at. The combat is..alright. I love the idea of more combo-centric mechanics, but it is admittedly frustrating to do them sometimes. It takes a LOT to stagger bosses in the earlier parts of the game, and you don't have the tools to efficiently evade their attacks yet so it can often feel frustrating to try and pull off a combo you think you can cancel out of in time, only for the boss to armor through the attack and pummel you into the ground. Not a lot of the bosses are terribly difficult, but some of them took me more than a few tries to beat.  I will say that I had a lot more fun with the bosses later in the game, as at that point you have several weapons to pick from and switch between on the fly for some cool chain attacks.Exploration is a bit lack-luster. There's only really 2 unique collectibles to the game, which are plant seeds and posters. The former works similarly to grubs from Hollow Knight, though the rewards are pretty much just money and Data Disks that you can use to learn new skills, and the latter is weapon skins. I personally don't really mind the lack of collectibles for FIST, as the game doesn't really place too much emphasis on it, but for the size of some of the areas in the game I was disappointed with how much of it was just kind of...empty space.The music is pretty good, I think they stick out just enough to not be too "ambient", and there are a couple that I'll probably listen to outside of playing the game. Now here's the biggest issue I've had with the game. The technical side of stuff. Take this with a grain of salt, as my computer is pretty good, but the graphics card is a bit outdated. I could run the game at 60 with graphics set to medium (they're set to that from the start), and ran into a lot of issues outside of framerate, mainly that textures would pop in a lot along with some lighting which was a little annoying but not experience-ruining, however there were several instances where I'd enter a room and it would just be...completely empty except for a gray background until the room fully loaded in a couple seconds later. For the most part, like I said, I like the game. I'd definitely recommend it on sale, but make sure you have a good computer as I feel like the recommendations for it are undershooting just a bit, but that's just my thoughts. Gorgeous art, good music, alright combat (a small thing I didn't note but the story is just kinda meh), and some technical issues, I'd say it's like a 6-6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this game so far, my favorite Metroidvania-style game since Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.The thing this title does very well that makes this sub-genre of 2D Platformer so appealing to me is giving players little glimpses of areas that you're unable to access until later in the game, when you've unlocked more of the games powers. That was something I loved about Castlevania: Symphony of the Night as a kid, and I also loved about Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night a few years ago. It sounds simple in theory, but it requires smart game design to achieve since you must construct the game in a way that allows you to backtrack while not feeling like you're actually backtracking. You do this by unlocking these Dark-Souls styled shortcuts that connect the world, and it's something this game did time and time again and I loved it.This game is also HUGE based on what I've experienced so far. The combat is solid and there are tons of skills to unlock. Combat was also refreshingly challenging at times in all the right ways. Story and graphics are great in my opinion, and the sound design is also notable, although I'm no expert in that arena. I was happy with the voice acting even though the main character Rayton, a rabbit/bunny with a giant robotic arm attached to his back, takes himself a bit too seriously (at least in the English voice acted version).My only real gripe with the game is there seems to be a screen tearing issue for me, even with V-Sync turned on. I looked for a solution online that recommended a couple ideas but so far, no luck.I hope more people become aware of this title so that maybe we can get a sequel someday. I recommend this title if you're into this style of game. I took a chance on it and was extremely happy I did.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game. If you love Metroidvanias you'll want to check this out at least once; it contains a very stylish world and your character has a lot of maneuverability that makes exploring fun and intuitive. The graphics are great, the English voice cast is excellent, and it has a simple but satisfying story.  My main criticism is that, in order to unlock the game's most powerful move (and get 100% completion), you have to do combo training. The combos can be VERY hard to pull off, especially for people with disabilities (getting the timing right, the lag between switching weapons, having to press multiple buttons in quick succession), and it's very unlikely that you'll actually use the combos when combating enemies. The actual combat can range from very satisfying to very frustrating (some enemies take too long to kill or deal too much damage; there is no way to block damage and you don't get the parry ability until later in the game). There should be an accessibility feature that makes combat and combos easier to pull off (activating slo-mo, simplifying combos, health bars for all enemies so you can tell how long it would take to beat them, etc.).As for technical issues, I did run into a few crashes, though thankfully I didn't lose any progress, and they didn't completely break the game. Keep in mind I have a more high-end PC so people with a lower grade computer might have more trouble. Overall, yes this game needs a little polish and better accessibility, but is still an ultimately enjoyable and worthwhile experience and I'm glad I checked it out. The devs definitely show promise and I'd like to see more games from them.

_childDocuments_.review: A quality metroidvania, but not without some noticeable blemishes.Pros:- vast, diverse and beautiful setting you can easily find yourself be immersed in- a more fighting-game, combo-oriented fighting style than in other metroidvanias I've played- the story is OK+ - I wish the setting was developed further however- an easy to use map that does its job properly (not a given in recent metroidvanias for whatever reason)- varied, fun bossfights (special shoutout to last three boss fights)- no bugs of any kind - the game runs smoothly and without any issues on my PC without any dips in framerate or whatever- perfect price for its content and length- no overused, somewhat outdated nowadays mechanics like dropping your coins on death or whateverCons:- the focus on comboing hits diminishes the moment you obtain the whip which more or less breaks the game and makes the game sans a few bossfights a breeze- underwater levels - I've seen other reviews complain about them as well and I think the general issue is the fact that your moveset is much more limited underwater, there aren't many enemies and the platforming with limited, sluggish movement can get pretty difficult at times. Once you die you respawn way back and have to begin again. The underwater levels are also very vast for some reason- Ancient Complex - kudos for trying out something else for this location but I haven't enjoyed it at allAll in all it's a solid metroidvania, whose staggering amount of content reminds me of another quality Chinese metroidvania, Afterimage. Perfect for its price, no need to wait for a sale in my opinion. Patiently waiting for a sequel

_childDocuments_.review: Another pleasant surprise from my adventures into genres and franchises I normally wouldn't play but decided to give a shot. Graphics and character models look great, little bit of ray tracing here and there really make the anthropomorphized animal world really pop and come to life with a nice variety of different environments, enemies and things to figure out. Enemies and bosses provide decent challenge, but button-mashers beware as combos and proper timing to dodge and land hits become crucial in the endgame and for bosses.Voice acting was actually mostly pretty good, which was surprising considering it's a foreign game. Localizing from another language can add obstacles and challenges that aren't always present when working with the native language and voice actors, but of course, the performance that seemed to lag the most was the main character unfortunately, while the other problems with voice acting seemed to be due to writing/translating.Despite some stutters here and there and a crash or 2, I enjoyed myself more than I thought I would and went after all achievements even after spending an hour and half on the final boss (felt like I was playing Sekiro again, though I admit I was just being sloppy and impatient trying to beat the game before midnight).

_childDocuments_.review: Hi Guys, I have to confess that I am disappointed in the game. The setting and graphics of the game are gorgeous and I really enjoyed the cutscenes.
