_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea why this game flew over my radar, but I am glad I dig it up from my dusty video game piles. FIST: Forged In Shadow Torch is a well-made metroidvania focusing on action. Combat feels tense, and the combo is really satisfying to pull off. The art style may not be my taste, but I cannot deny the effort the developers put in to make the level gorgeous to behold, especially the stylized china town that is Joffre Street. Even though the levels aren't inter-connected like the others in the same genre, the game still delivers the core features of a metroidvania. But most importantly, Being an action-oriented metroidvania, the game offers players a decent of tools to create their own combo. The main draws here are the three primary weapons players gain through progression: Fist is the big mechanical arm strapped on our protagonist's back. It is the default weapon and also the most versatile one out of the three. The move sets of Fist are great for both starting combo and bridging the other two weapons. You can easily knock down or launch enemies for more combo options. You can even throw weaker enemies to create some breathing room; Drill focuses more on linear damage. Its multi-hit nature can easily stun-lock enemies for quite a while but the move sets lock you in place. Therefore, it is best to use this weapon as combo finishers; last but not least, Whip is a pair of grappling hooks. While the normal attack cannot flinch enemies like the other two, the speed and range can easily make up the gap. Being a grappling hook also allows you to grapple toward your enemies, forcing the downed ones to stand up. What makes the combat the most interesting is that you can freely swap between the three weapons. Attacks are cancelable and they can seamlessly connect with each other. It is always satisfying to pull off the more complicated combo in combat. These power take time to gain, however.Dual-purposed abilities are my favorite in the recent metroidvania. I am glad FIST: Forged In Shadow Torch get this idea right. The three weapons are the best example: Fist can punch button on doors and break ceiling vents; Drill allows you to glide, moves faster underwater, and opens fan lock on doors; Whip lets you grapple on to drone to reach higher places and close electric fences. Even though most of other gating abilities in this game are common trope, it is more important to see how they interact with the levels. Platforming challenges in each area aim to help you familiarize the tools you just get, and these challenges are satisfying to complete. The developers certainly takes time and effort to refine the mobility players have. With a few abilities gained out of order, you can even sequence-break some secret areas without proper tools, which is something I always cherish about in metroidvania.→Story is quite decent.→Love how well the characters are animated.→Many hidden items in each area. →Weapon paints have a lot of nice reference and easter eggs.→Enemies variety are lacking.→I wish the levels are more inter-connected.→You can only throw enemies left and right. At the very least you could and should be able to throw mid-air enemies downward.→I hate that any interaction with NPCs always close the menu, forcing me to interact with them again.中文小簡評→遊戲體驗很棒的類銀河系惡魔城。→最重要的一點，不獸控制啦！→雖然這種類寫實畫風不對我胃口，但不得不說一些場景設計真的很好看。→戰鬥主打連擊，三把武器各有優缺點，能夠在連擊中自由切換，打出你心儀的Combo。→三把武器同時也是關鍵技能，能解鎖更多機關及完成特定跳台挑戰。→其他關鍵技能雖然了無新意，但最重要的還是製作團隊如何在關卡設計中反映玩家取得技能後的機動性，這點我覺得做的很棒。→故事還不錯。→關卡藏有許多隱藏區域及道具。→武器烤漆有一堆致敬彩蛋。→敵人種類重複性高。→各個關卡並沒有相互連接。→只能把敵人往左往右丟，無法上拋或下砸。→很討厭每次跟NPC講完話後互動選單會直接關掉。

_childDocuments_.review: This is an OK game but it suffers from the same issues as Ori in that there is very little reason to go back to each area with each of the unlocks other than to just collect things.  Sure those things can be useful but they are in no way hindering you from completing the game.  this is an incredibly linear experience considering its a metroidvania.  This is very much a game on rails with just collectables locked behind abilities.   The enemy diversity is non existent, theres about 6 different enemies which just have colour swatches changed, sometimes with an added hat to tell the player they are stronger.  This hat is only different per type of enemy.  The combat and movement mostly feel fluid, so long as you dont do any advanced combos (which is actually ok, because there is pretty much no standard enemy which can withstand a standard combo and mini / bosses dont flinch or ragdoll in the same way leaving advanced combos useless) until you go to do the combat challenges and you suddenly realise that the combat is actually very clunky.The story is ok, the cutscenes are fun.  the non-cinematic cutscenes are jarring to say the least.  the text appears at a different speed than it is spoken, and the characters movements are scripted to be timed with the conversations.   So if you skip any text box at all then characters can start teleporting from point to point as you have also skipped their movement animation without realising it.  Also the subtitles often start with the last line of audible dialogue.At no point in any game ever should there be a collectable in the literal room before the final boss which requires a turn in.  this means about 20 minutes of back tracking and then again to get this collectable, turn it in in the safe zone and then return to finish the game.  I don't know if you get returned to the safe zone after beating the boss as once the credits finished rolling the game crashed and I wasn't going to do it again just to check.  all in all i got 96% on first play through though I don't know if this includes the collectables i gathered but didn't turn in.  I certainly had no where else to go on the map and nothing more to collect, so I'm assuming it doesn't.  in which case, 100% collected and completed and 4% not turned in.  all in all, its a fun game.  it just has some things I don't enjoy and have found other metroidvania games to have done better.

_childDocuments_.review: Update/TLDR: So - after another extended underwater section (and the promise of many more!) and the terrible combat, I've had enough; This is not a good game.--- F.I.S.T is a very loose game adaptation of a 1978 movie [citation needed], but instead of Sly Stallone we get a fluffy bunny with a giant mechanical fist attached and an action hero movie rasp, and instead of a story about unions and the mob we get a bunch of generic dieselpunk fantasy twaddle. So yeah, not very faithful furry version of the story. It takes the form of a metroidvania game- I'd say this is an attempt to create as pure a metroidvania experience as possible. It's hard to explain, but with most games you get the feel that it's a game first, and then it fits into a genre; Here it feels like the reverse is true. This gels with my opinion that it's a pretty uninspired take: technically very competent, but in the end kind of soul-less. As a game, it's mostly fine - a 2d platformer with great technical presentation that quickly gets its hooks in with the typical genre exploration and ability progression. Combat is a low point, as the dodge move does not grant invincibility and does not go through enemies. Later on you get a parry move, but it's mapped to the same stick as movement so it's very fiddly (and to me, next to useless.) Exploration is OK. The areas are varied and have the requisite secrets and bits that you'll need to backtrack to later; The map tool is pretty good, marking down everything you run into with clear icons; The main problem is that a lot of screens feel empty, and while varied, they're mostly some variation of city street or military facility. The art style isn't very striking, but it does manage a few cool vistas - the 3d is very well made, and there are a lot of graphical bells and whistles (ray tracing and such.) Because the plot and the characters are pretty bland, and the game as a whole feels like a retread, it's the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the points of friction that stand out. Underwater levels or multi-stage boss battle difficulty spikes. The fact that you can't skip some cutscenes. Backtracking through a ton of empty screens to an unexplored room, only to find a handful of coins. The combat. It's not enough to offset the core draw of the genre, but... I don't know, even what's good in it feels very rote. Like a technical team flexing its muscles, an engineering exercise rather than an artistic one. I'm certain that's not true, and hope that the team proves me wrong with whatever they chose to do next. It's a generous game in content, with tons of things to do and places to go, and it's got a ridiculous amount of polish; it's just a shame it doesn't make more of an impact, and that the annoyances are so pronounced.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, one of the better Metroidvanias I’ve played.Pros:+ Combat is fun, with satisfying combos. I especially liked using the drill.+ Difficulty progression felt very steady throughout. Every time I felt like I was starting to master an enemy type, the game would introduce me to a new variant of that type, forcing me to adapt. The challenge was always solid but nothing ever felt too hard.*+ Gorgeous semi-realistic graphics & aesthetic.+ Furry characters.+ Main theme music is a banger.Cons:- Healing uses the same gauge as several other functions that could be useful in combat (namely ranged attacks, a parry ability, and a decoy dummy). Because you’ll probably want healing to be available as much as possible, those other functions will barely ever be used, if at all.- I occasionally encountered a glitch that caused some of the buttons on my controller to stop working temporarily.- Ending is a nothing-burger.(*Except the mechanical core boss. _childDocuments_.review: 5/10: The Good, The Bad, The UglyThe Good - Has nice graphics and environment. The backtracking is pretty decent and the platforming and puzzles are pretty good. The level diversity is pretty vast and the use of weapons as secondary equipment are pretty clever; like the drill turns into a helicopter and a propeller for underwater levels. The Bad - Most enemies are pretty easy until the bosses and then its die a couple times, learn their attack patterns and call it a day. That alone isn't such a bad combat system but the way the boss fights unfold sucks. There's never any reason to switch between weapons and pretty much all boss fights follow the same system... get 2-3 hits in, run, evade, repeat until fight is over. It becomes very systematic and tedious making most of them forgettable and boring.The Ugly - Combat just ends up feeling cheap. Often I'll start out attacking the boss and getting 1 hit in just to be turned around the other direction on the immediate following swing . You never have a chance to use your more powerful, unlocked chain attacks cuz the enemy will just hit you, so its more cheap hit and run tactics. And the worse... F*ing STUN LOCK. Prepare to be stun locked and incapacitated a lot. Game just turns you into a punching bag so often that it hardly feels fair or like your skill set means anything. Personally, the game just feels cheap and lazy after awhile. Any game that relies on Stun Lock to add to its difficulty is just more lazy bs from uncreative crap devs imo. Sucks. I really was looking forward to this game but its combat is just so stiff and mechanical that it lost all appeal & the fact that some enemy attacks are so fast paced and the input feels so unresponsive at times just ruins it.  If you're into Metroidvainia style games you'd probably enjoy this, but if you're a casual gamer I'd pick up a gamer that's higher on your "To Buy List"

_childDocuments_.review: Really great metroidvania game.2.5D: 2D gameplay on 3D engine. Two difficulty settings.Beautiful graphics and relaxing music, large locations that differ from each other, well crafted.Nice story where steampunk meets furry creatures and one tough brawling bunny, with voiced characters.Fighting is done very well, smooth and responsive, no issues, really nice finisher moves as well.Should take you around 13-16 hours, and it's not too difficult.The downsides:Master Wu training is the most difficult and frustrating part of the game. It's not required but most powerful skill in the game is gated behind it (and few achievements)Lots of travelling back and forth, especially when you get new powers. There is a fast travel system but it's not that easily accessible (ie. one per location) so you still spend some time getting to it.Had a blast with it (excluding Master Wu part)Definitely recommending.

_childDocuments_.review: Hidden gem, surprised this one didn't get more attention. Extremely enjoyable, snappy "Metroidvania" set in a creative, well-fleshed out world inhabited by interesting characters. I was consistently surprised by all of the little details that brought this world to life. Combat is good and responsive, choose between 3 different weapon types/styles that can be insta-swapped to make your own combos. Lots of secrets to hunt down and skills to unlock. The only downside I encountered was the rather abrupt, "Okay, but what happened after?" ending, no real New Game + to speak of (if you want to unlock further secrets and such it must be done by loading your last save before the final boss) and some janky custscene animation that often would not sync with dialogue. Aside from those minor downsides a real quality title, must-play for fans of the genre, would buy any sequels.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best metroidvania to release in 2021. FIST doesnt do anything groundbreaking but it does almost everything right in regards to the genre. If youre looking to scratch that itch you cant go wrong here. It has great combat, nice graphics, some solid platforming and the game paces really well. One thing I didnt like was some of the secrets you find is just extra coins, imo they should have gotten rid of shadowboxes and replace them just to make those secrets more rewarding. You can really style on enemies in regards to combat but some just dont have enough health to go crazy on and some bosses wont allow you to go off so you just need to stick to a high dps bnb instead of trying to juggle. If you like fighting games you might enjoy this system, combos arent too hard,you dnt need to master them and the training mode trials gives you some good ideas, my biggest issue was getting confused with the weapon switching since you cant really map anything besides your movement or attack. There also a decent difficulty spike for the last 3 bosses outta nowhere. Just parry stay patient and use a high dps bnb I just tried to do any combo that ended in the down special with the fist. I didnt really care for the story but its passable, dnt really play this genre for that but I'll give them the nod, I didnt really care for the zootopia type animals but it makes for a really nice setting that feels alive with some history. Theres full english voice acting in this game which is impressive since this was made by chinese developers, they even sync the lips and it sounds good. The only reason why this game didnt get as much praised as it deserves was probably because its chinese. This might be the best recent metroidvania I've played since blasphemous and bloodstained. I personally would rate those games higher but this doesnt lag far behind. Definitely deserves more love and will go down as a solid staple of the genre. You cant go wrong here.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that honestly should be worth triple A levels of price. They are a little cheap on save points and teleport room, but whenever you pick up an item/collectibles it will act as an anchor save so you never lose too much progress on death.All in all, it's a fantastic gem finely polished that gives honor to the metroidvania's genre. *Chef's kiss*

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this one came out of nowhere and ended up being one of my favorite metroidvania's in recent memory. In a genre that is stacked to the brim with certified classics I wouldn't go so far as to say this one's in the top 3, but it's at minimum top 10, easy. For a relatively lower profile release, I was shocked at how gorgeous this game is. If you have a high end gaming rig, this is easily one of the best looking games in the genre. The graphic fidelity did come at the cost of some stutters as well as odd texture and environmental pop in, but overall this one is a stunner. The overall aesthetic here I would describe as furry Final Fantasy 7.  The city the majority of the game takes place in reminds me a lot of Midgar, with it's haphazardly built slums and opulent entertainment districts. The game also bears more than a few thematic resemblances to FF7 as well, with the main character being a jaded former soldier reluctantly called back into action to aid a resistance group in fighting a tyrannical organization that is despoiling the planet. I don't usually comment on music quality, but I have to mention it here, as this game also has a really damn good soundtrack.Combat and exploration are both excellent as well. The movement here is just perfect, not too slippery, not too clingy, just right. Wall jumping and dashing through the environments is felt fluid and precise, and I never encountered a situation where the character felt out of sync with my inputs. Combat is simple on the surface, but the multiple weapons, special abilities, and pop up moves allow for some incredibly robust combos. My only complaint here is that you have almost no ranged options and are almost always up against dudes with guns. There is an upgrade to your dash that allows you to pass through enemies and projectiles, but it's withheld until the very end of the game. I really feel like this should have been the default, and it would have made a lot of the encounters with multiple gun users feel a bit more balanced. Overall this is a great game and 100% worth it at full price. While it won't dethrone something like Shovel Knight or Bloodstained, it's definitely up there with games like Shadow Complex and the Strider remake as some of the best of the genre. Unreservedly recommended to anyone who enjoys metroidvania's.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves WAAAY more hype than it has recieved. F.I.S.T doesn't really do anything super original as a platformer, but everything it does it does REALLY well. I had a blast playing through the game, inspite minor bugs and at times awkward localization transaltions. If you enjoy platformers, this is MUST play. Im glad I didnt wait for a sale and supported the devs at full price for this gem. Worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: FIST is a fantastic Metroidvania.  It follows all the classic tropes, sidescrolling, wall jumping, large interconnected map revealing goodness.   FIST takes place in a depressed, Steampunk world, that is being torn apart by a war between the Furtizens (anthropomorphic animals) and Robots.  Do not be put off, there is no odd "furry" stuff, I found the characters and the character designs to be creative and fun.  FIST brings a few top tier characteristics to the table.  The first, and one that is pretty obvious if you have seen screencaps/videos, is that FIST has stunning graphics.   The art is badass, and the engine is super advanced and modern, with support for heavy ray tracing.  All of the environments and characters and fur look terrific.  Another feather in FISTs cap is its combat systems.  You eventually unlock 3 main weapons, that are all interesting and fun.  The combat can be difficult, and your crazy juggles and combos and parries are all needed to survive.  It reminded me of a Platinum game at times, which is high praise coming from me.  FIST has all the requisite secret areas, and backtracking with new abilities to find hidden collectibles, and remains fun and challenging throughout, and lots of difficult bosses and sub bosses, to really test your mettle.  I really enjoyed all my time with FIST, it was never a chore, even when I was stuck on a tough room or boss.If there is one negative to FIST, is that it has a little technical jank.  The game would crash out pretty consistently every 30-60 minutes if ray tracing is on high, in addition to weird noise on the edge of the screen that you are moving towards.  Textures can load in a little slow, and the game can get choppy at times, even with vsync/gsync.  I do not think these issues are related to my setup, as I saw many similar complaints online.  These technical issues are the only mark against an instant classic.  I hope we see a sequel!9/10

I never once got irritated at the game.I would absolutely play more DLCs, and an "hard mode", or a boss rush mode.

I haven't finished it as I write this, but I can't find any negatives to it so far. Graphics are rock solid. For a platformer, its gorgeous. I like this better than Ori, and other games of its ilk. The mechanics are also solid in this with sufficient weapon variety. The Metroidvania elements to progress in the maps are pretty cleverly done too...nothing really seems contrived. The story is OK...while I can't bag it, it's pretty simplistic. Bunny boy is an old war veteran and tasked with taking down one of his fellow former ally soldiers who he thought was dead. He's not, and apparently he has bad intentions. As such Bunny-boy (Rayton), needs to talk some sense into him...through violence, and needs to ally with people who are less than reputable to do it. _childDocuments_.review: I am strongly recommending this game, with a few caveats that need attention.This game gets almost everything "right" and by that I mean the vast majority of the game is impressive as hell. The graphics/animations are well beyond what I expected in a metroidvania. The sound design was also exceptional, specifically the ambiance and sound effects which built both immersion and impact, respectively. The environments were detailed and beautiful. The story included cutscenes/cinematics which I wasn't expecting either, and added some depth to the characters and aesthetic.The abilities, while a bit vanilla (double jump, dash, wall climb) and predictable, were still fun to obtain and the process in which you do felt well-paced and definitely gave you incentive to backtrack, which you'll be doing a lot of.Speaking of which, navigating the map is a relatively easy feat, since main objectives are marked in or out of fog of war, and the paths are somewhat obvious. You won't be finding any wall chicken here, but there are some breakable entrances you might overlook. The mechanics are one of the areas where the game diverges from your standard metroidvania, but it's a good thing. You collect plants to turn in for rewards, eat noodles for temporary health pools, and there are a good handful of secrets scattered throughout the game that are entirely optional but could even open up new areas. The weapons, abilities, and items are diverse. Some are much less useful (imo) than others, but it still gives the player a little extra agency that often lacks in this genre.While almost everything about this game was enjoyable, the parts that weren't were, in my case, severe detriments; to the point that while I spent most of the game feeling a 8 or 9/10, the last few hours felt like a 5. If that sounds harsh, let me explain why.The controls can be clunky at the worst possible times. Namely, drinking a desperately needed potion. There is an animation lock/delay when trying to do so. If you're not perfectly still a half second or second before drinking the potion, it won't register the input. This meant death for me more often than not.  While most of the platforming felt responsive and smooth, switching weapons was also a pain. There is a mini-game where you are required to switch weapons mid-combo, and I simply gave up after a handful of attempts after the weapon swap wouldn't register.Navigating the map is simple, but tedious. This is a minor complaint, but since the game goes a lot harder on the platforming than most in the genre do, going back through a spike maze with double jumps and air dashes gets annoying on the fifth run because you finally got that new movement ability. This game also loves lasers, and Meatboy-style resets if you land on certain ones. The underwater areas, one in particular, I just flat out avoided at the expense of a few plant seeds because I just didn't want to deal with the teleporter location, traversing multiple areas, then swimming slowly through a lengthy area while hiding sporadically from a mechanic that is fun the first time and only the first time.Lastly, but possibly most importantly, the one aspect that infuriated me the most was the last hour or two of the game, as a whole. The last major dungeon is a total slog. The puzzles are boring and irritating at best. Without spoiling anything, the puzzle was a snooze fest but took a while to complete. They also added a lot of "let's just absolutely annoy the player to literal death" enemies that would snipe you as you were carrying a puzzle item, or prevent you from hitting a switch several times. It was an exercise in patience and tenacity, not enjoyment.But that area is nothing compared to the last 3 boss fights. I won't spoil anything, because I don't have to. The combat and boss fights in the game went from a comfortable challenge to a soulslike disaster very quickly. Regardless of the "get gud" lifers or people that just don't find games difficult in general, the difficulty scaling exploded. Until that point the scaling felt relatively natural and organic. You fought a boss that was maybe a 3/10 on the difficulty scale, then a few sections later a 4 or 5 tops. This went from 5 to 9 on the first of the three, then an 11, then a really strong desire to uninstall the game and never look back. Shame.The solution to this conundrum was listening to the players and adding in an Easy difficulty. Now, while I appreciate the devs doing this, here's what you ended up with:Easy: Too easy. The game is basically casual at this point. You'll rarely, if ever die, and bosses are a joke.Normal: Well balanced. Fun. Then basically go ♥♥♥♥ yourself for the last three bosses.Was that the right call? Probably not, but everyone should still play the game. I spent a lot of time on the negatives but it's because I am coming out of the game fresh and I felt blindsided. I want to both encourage other metroidvania fans this is a must-have, but also prepare y'all for the moment when the game suddenly decides to turn into a soulslike and maybe go ahead and get a replacement controller ready to order.

_childDocuments_.review: Where The Ascent is an exemplar of cyberpunk, F.I.S.T. is a prime exhibit of dieselpunk done right. With antropomorphic animals mixed in it, of all things. And it works nearly perfectly.  The game is metroidvania, featuring puzzles, exploration and fighting with combos. Abiliteis, comboes and gadgets are unlocked and upgraded as the strory progresses. Overall, movement and combat are very fluid and responsive, with the sole exception of weapon switching, which made me give up on advanced combo training. I played with a controller, as recommended.  The graphics and animations are gorgeous. The envinronment practically screams dieselpunk - there are factories, slums, military bases and neon lit streets, and it all looks like reimagined and more fantastic version of 1950s, with East Asian flair. On occations there are more natural areas, like caves, mines or snow covered mountains. The backgrounds have almost same insane level of details as in The Ascent. The characters are animals and it is fully acknowledged in story. They look great and they are excellently animated, especially in cutscenes.  I have played using original Chinese voices, which were good and added to the atmosphere. The music fits with the era that inspired dieselpunk - it is a selection of jazz that underscores the film noir feel of the story.  The story and dialogues are fairly interesting and I enjoyed them. As noted above, there is a heavy noir feel to them. Sometimes the translation is a bit clumsy and on a few occations the text did not fit into the dialogue window.  Overall this is an excellent and enjoyable game with a unique atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: I had an absolutely amazing time with this game. Incredibly polished gameplay with great platforming and movement mechanics as well as deep combat and combo systems. I found myself regularly pushing the limits of how I could combo a boss. I also love that this game has all the latest technologies in it, DLSS, RTX ray tracing, nvidia reflex and all. It's fun to see a great game also be well supported with cool cutting edge features. The game is hands down the most gorgeous metroidvania I've ever played, provided you have the hardware to max it out.Although I got the game for free this is a rare one where I'd actually buy it again were I not allowed to keep the copy after streaming/reviewing it. It's good enough to make me want it in my library and I would 100% return for any content updates or DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics, design, animations, weapons, movement, map / exploration, secrets - everything is great, a real treat for metroidvania fans like me. The voice acting is fun (I recommend the Chinese original with subtitles; nothing comes close to a badass rabbit with a deep Chinese voice). For me there's only one downside: the combat. I never really got into it. It's okay if you only fight one or two enemies, but the moment there are more the mechanics didn't really work for me. In my opinion it's a bad design decision to add parrying as a skill rather late in the game; I found it hard to integrate into the fights, especially those with many enemies. That's because there're a lot of combos in fighting which prevent the enemy from breaking free - but enemies also use combos and once you're hit you cannot recover but must endure the whole combo. So, if you miss the first parry you are locked into an animation and get a beating - rather frustrating. If you're fighting several enemies, I found it impossible to block on all sides; in the end I sometimes parried by accident, but I rarely used it on purpose. Even later in the game you get the ability to dash through enemies and attacks, which I found to be a lot more useful. So, I won most of the harder fights because I leveled up to the max and dashed a lot. Simply put: Other games do combat better. The biggest frustration was not being able to get a 100% because I was unable to complete the fighting challenges which earn you an item to open one last door, get one last skill, complete the map, and get the last poster. None of these are essential for finishing the game, but as any metroidvania addict knows, you don't want to stop before reaching a 100% ...But the fighting challenges require you to complete ridiculously complex combos, including several weapon changes in midair and what-not. I already failed the first advanced training (not for lack of trying) and after I learned there're also master challenges, I knew I wouldn't waste hours and hours in trying. I found the timing required for the combos simply too tight. Surely there are hardcore gamers who like this kind of challenge, I’d have preferred if this weren’t tied to completing the game a 100% but rather as an achievement for masochists.Despite the complaints: A beautiful game I had almost 30 hours of fun with and I can absolutely recommend it to fans of the genre.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game has stayed within my interest scope for quite some time. I've opened the page couple of times, read through reviews and postponed it to a "better discount - then we're talking. Maybe. Don't know. Should I get this?" shelf.Finally I've downloaded a demo, played a bit and decided that it's not that bad, so why not grab a copy? Should you get one too? Let's see...The game looks amazing: the characters, the backgrounds, all the small details and cut scenes. Visually it's gorgeous.Movement system is high tier too: once you unlock all the stuff that allows advanced navigation - the game really blooms.Abilities themselves are very well done and demand using all of them on a regular basis, which is a huge plus IMO, as recently I played too many metroidvanias bloated with different skills/abilities/features that are implemented just to be used once or twice and then vanish completely.Combat... Combat is: let's put it this way - not for all. It uses combo system, and personally, I never used any of those combos that are taught to you by your martial arts trainer. Simple ones are quite enough. Think of Guacamelee  style combat, yet more primitive and less diverse. Still well done and satisfying overall - yet I see where some people may find it non-perfect. Level design and backtracking - great, yet with some flaws. I still hope that I will get the ability to teleport between save spots in the endgame, as navigating around can be quite tedious. The world is full of puzzles, secrets and challenges all of which are fun to discover. True, some respawn logic in challenges and other minor details are not very well thought, but that's just a small issue along the way. The  that may turn people off is the developer's attempt to make the game more diverse by adding sections of gameplay that break out of the core game mechanics. I'm talking about stealth mission (there will be a level where you lose all your gear and will have to sneak through), some underwater madness (where the game starts to feel more like Eco the Dolphin), etc. And it's clearly a love/hate situation - either this will entertain you, or you will be completely turned off by it. Personally I found it frustrating first, yet now, looking back - that added to the overall experience and I think the game benefits from such sections. The music... Well, I can't say anything  felt close with my heart, so yeah, it's there and it's not bad. Matter of taste. (Though the starting city location tune... That's a weird melody choice) This is a great metroidvania with astonishing visuals, good movement/ability system and fun exploration.Some people may find it frustrating due to complex, yet not perfect combat system & random change of game pace in custom levels, such as stealth mission/underwater exploration, etc. Personally I think this is a great game and do recommend for all genre enjoyers! Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game does have a lot of PS2 energy, and I mean that in the nicest way. The characters all look nice, they have decent voice acting, and there's a lot of love put into the world. However. I reached a section where I rode slowly on an box for several minutes, not actually being challenged, but was forced to in order to recollect my gear after a Supposed-To-Lose-Fight. There were no enemies, no real challenge, and, let me emphasize, AN INCREDIBLY SLOW MOVING BOX I HAD TO RIDE. There are clear issues when the game wants to play unique animations during dialogue, with the occasional long pause between dialogue lines so that the fighting animation can load or something. Also, while the voice acting isn't bad, it suffers from a really awkward translation it feels like. Cicero, a character whose reveal is supposed to be a surprise, is mentioned earlier by another character as being someone you have to fight by your training Master. Your attacks all feel like they have slightly less range than they actually do and the fact that you can hang in the air and keep hitting without gravity applying feels strangely stiff? The longer I played, the more my interest petered out. Altogether, not the worst time I've ever had, but I don't want to play any more than I already have.

_childDocuments_.review: FIST is a Metroidvania with Spectacle fighter type combat. I like Metroidvanias and I like spectacle fighters, so I really enjoyed playing this game. I would've likely enjoyed this game a lot more if it took advantage of the spectacle fighter combat aspect better….. But more on that later.As I mentioned, FIST has spectacle fighter combat. So instead of simply spamming the attack button in something like Castlevania, you're using a mix of light attacks, heavy attacks, SP attacks, and switching between different weapons. SP attacks do lot of damage, but they take SP. You recover SP by doing regular attacks against enemies. So you're encouraged to master combos which incorporate both regular attacks and SP attacks, which is great.There's 3 different weapons in total, and there's a few hours in between as you get new weapons, so the game is nicely paced in this regard since you have a decent amount of time to master each weapon before you get the next one. Whenever I got a new weapon, I really enjoyed incorporating it into my combos, and it was really fun to master combos that used all 3 of the weapons! In addition to your main weapons, you also have 4 "sub-weapons", which cost EP to use. You can use these weapons to either heal, parry attacks, throw out a decoy, or shoot homing missiles. Out of all the Metroidvanias I've played, the offense aspect of FIST has to be one of the best I've experienced.While it would've been fun enough to do cool looking combos on enemies all day, the developers were also able to make the game challenging. Regular enemies are challenging through a decent amount of variety in what they can do such that you have to approach them in different ways:	• Some enemies have ranged weapons who'll be able to attack you before you can reach them, forcing you to dodge	• Some enemies can randomly disappear mid combo and attack you from above	• Some enemies have shields that can only be broken through certain attacks	• Some enemies are in the air and shooting at you from far away, forcing you to do some mid-air combos to reach them	• Some enemies "charge" at you with super armor, so if you try attacking them, they'll tank through it and hit you	• Some enemies can enter a "counter" stance where if you attack them in any way, they'll parry the attack and hit you backIn addition to having a decent amount of enemies, you're quite often going to be facing multiple enemies at the same time. Every so often, you'll enter "arenas" where waves of enemies will keep spawning, such that you can face 4 enemies at once. So combat definitely never feels like you are one-sidedly comboing enemies to death. If you were only facing one enemy, you could likely infinite combo them to death. However, since you're facing multiple enemies, you have to master dealing as much damage as possible in the shortest time possible so that you're never in one place for too long and can move onto the next enemy as fast as possible. So not only is the offense aspect of FIST really good, so is the defensive aspect.In regards to the bosses, they all offer a decent challenge. Bosses can basically be split into 2 types. "Humanoid" bosses can be juggled in the air every so often (they have super armor for a few attacks) while "Heavy" bosses can't be juggled in the air, but after doing enough damage to them they'll be vulnerable to a ground combo (or every so often they'll just stand around doing nothing, at which point you can go ham on them). Apart from these categories, bosses for the most part feel very distinct from each other and so whenever you face a boss, you have to master their moves and how to dodge them. While bosses are reused every so often, it's very rare. Most Spectacle Fighters are a series of combat encounters one after another with pretty much nothing else. FIST on the other hand is also a Metroidvania, which means there's a decent amount of platforming and exploration. The platforming is pretty decent, especially later on when you get the whip weapon and air dash at which point the mid-air platforming sections are really fun. The exploration also feels rewarding. The rewards are basically stat boosts to your HP, SP, and EP bars. While this is nothing new, it's particularly designed well in FIST since you HP, SP, EP bars are very tiny in the beginning. For example, your SP and EP bars start out at 2, so exploring and increasing these bars by 1 feels huge. Not only that, but you can find "data disks" by exploring, which allows you to learn new combat moves, which is always something to look forward to.While I found the non-combat sections of the game a decent way to change up the pace, one thing I really didn't like was that this game has a lot of underwater levels (emphasis on a LOT). I generally don't like water levels, but in this game it's even worse since when you're underwater, you can't do ANY combos anymore. Not only that, but the enemies you face are a lot more simple, needing only like one hit to take them down. I really wish all of the underwater levels were replaced with more land combat encounters, since I didn’t enjoy any of them.One last thing I'll mention about the combat isn't exactly a negative, but more like a missed opportunity. As I was playing the game, I felt that FIST was a great game, but it didn't quite reach the levels of something like Hollow Knight, where you really have to master the combat and bosses in order to succeed. Then near the end game, I reached a room with an "arcade machine". By interacting with the arcade machine, you could face bosses that you've previously fought all over again if you wanted. Not only that, but there were 3 "tournaments" where you faced 4 bosses in a row, with the last 2 bosses always being ones that couldn't be found in the game. These "hidden" bosses were basically Hollow Knight level bosses where they were really challenging and really required you to master them before you could beat them. I really wish these bosses were spread out in the game instead of all being saved as an optional thing at that absolute end of the game, since the difficulty curve would've been a lot better for it.There's a story, but it's fairly lackluster. You play as a rabbit who's in a town that's run by machines who are bad and you have to stop them. These machines are after something called a "spark" and if they get it, they'll be unstoppable which is really bad. The problem is that the game does not explain at all about WHY these machines are so bad. So while the story is really pushing me into caring about wanting to stop them, I really don't because I am never shown the machines doing anything particularly horrendous. If anything, I kind of find them funny since every so often the machines make jokes. They're kind of too "authoritarian", but that's about it. I also didn't care about the protagonist all that much, since his only goal seems to be to stop the machines, which is really generic. Since I didn't care about the antagonist nor the protagonist, I didn't find myself engaged with the story.Overall, I really enjoyed the gameplay of FIST. There's very few 2D spectacle fighters I've played, and after playing FIST, I wish there was more of them. Hopefully if I play some in the future, the developers will know better than to put underwater levels in their spectacle fighter :P

_childDocuments_.review: I'm quite liking this game more than I could ever expected, I haven't completely finished it but will update my review if the game changes much the further I go. So far it has a metroidvania style to it's level design like it was advertised but doesn't overdo it with constant backtrack aside from some collectables and a couple of objectives; gameplay is solid and there's enough enemy diversity not only on looks but how they play; different weapons each with it's own unique move set, not all seem to have a huge gameplay weight besides being a different move for the sake of diversity (not that this is bad quite the contrary)  but some are a must for certain enemies and the diversity in moveset allows for some room to juggle enemies for nice combos. The theme of the game is this animal world of bunnies, bears, racoons, rats and cats living in this dark city very similar to a sci fi China or even more similar to Midgar from Final Fantasy VII; it's executed well to match it's art direction with decent animations and graphics aside from some couple of corners with lower textures and a okish water. I totally recomend if you like this type of games, the price is quite fair for the product you are getting.UpdateJust beat it, my opinion remains largely the same, it's a awesome metroidvania style game! My only complain would be the weapon switch mid moves, I can't pass training challenges because of it, only thing keeping me from 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot, in good conscience, recommend paying money for this or any other video game published by Bilibili. The reason for this is that the publisher is extremely unethical. They fired an entire dev team (for NEON ECHO) without compensation just because their EARLY ACCESS game didn't make enough money... then proceeding to keep that early access game on the store despite it no longer being under development anymore. Prior to this, this was the most promising roguelite platformer under development.Update: I have now played this. In short this game is 30% cheaper than prince of persia the lost crown and it's basically prince of persia the lost crown but around 30% worse.The good about the game is exactly the same as the good with prince of persia the lost crown: large size, high end graphics, high end budget, voice acting, and so on. In addition it has a proper english translation despite being a non western gameThe bad things are also similar to those of prince of persia the lost crown but in addition it has the following issues:- very serious performance issues related to asset loading in two biomes, the hub biome and the underwater base biome.- 20% of voice acting is missing- The combat training is impossible, unlike prince of persia the lost crown. This also means it is impossible to obtain the final ultimate optional ability, which means it is impossible to defeat the penultimate boss on normal difficulty (but funnily enough the final boss is easier and is beatable on normal).- Unlike prince of persia the lost crown where it is possible to customize the game to your own playstyle with charms, there is no such option here and if you can't get used to DMC style combat then you are screwed.- This game has some of the worst backtracking I have ever seen in a metroidvania, it even goes out of its way to make it as bad as possible with the treasure chests that require a skeleton key, so even if you find it you still have to backtrack to it with a key later on (and these are usually really far away from warp points)On a neutral note, like all chinese video games this has bad writing but compared to all other chinese video games I've played this actually has the best writing and translation I've seen.Anyway I recommend just getting prince of persia the lost crown instead. You get what you paid for, especially if you buy that on the switch.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with modern visuals and quite nice tracks.Especialy the old town tune stayed with me for some time outside my plays.The zones are nicely made and a sight to look upon.There are some water areas. At first I thought: oh no. But they were quite enjoyable and now a favorite of mine.Also the game has a nice subtle way of showing what hazards will come.In small ways it tells what to expect next and to get prepared. I am a fan of these small things; Not everything has to be thrown at you with textboxes.Voice cast, story and characters are nice.Sometimes I wished for more explanations / more lore.The world is nice and I want to go deeper, but I think it could break the all around action driven vibe.Platforming can be challenging but stays all around fair.Backtracking is genre like needed but wasn´t as often as in other games.Stuning visuals and quite nice stylized zones made the exploration more a pleasure for me.Combat was a favorite of mine. I like to change my setup and playstyle a lot in difficult battles.Some bosses were easier for me with some weapons.It is satisfying to pull one of the bigger combos off o to get a bunch of parries in a row.Speaking of the bigger baddies: I had a blast. Every boss had some style or mechanic I liked.They were fun to figure out and a defeat wasn´t devastating. There is always a checkpoint near.The newly added Boss Rush is nice. It showed me what I have learned so far and that the first bosses are easier now.If to easy: switch on some or even all of the handicaps.Or see that there are even meaner versions of some of them.As hard as some bosses could be, I would wish me one or more harder difficulties.Just to spice it up a bit for the game outside the boss fights.Would I recommend?Yeah, go for it. I know I had a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: There's fun to be had here, but there are too many flaws. Easy mode makes it bearable but still irritating.The main issue is combat. The character feels like he came from a slower game. Combos have long wind-ups and are unreliable. Enemies often ignore attacks, with weighty hits treated like a light breeze. Meanwhile the main character is interrupted and thrown around by every attack, making combos a liability. It feels like the game is missing a strong deflect or shield option. The character is too slow to evade, but lacks the defence to deal with hits.Traversal suffers in a similar way. _childDocuments_.review: I picked this Metroidvania up on a recommendation, and the game largely lived up to it.The first thing that must be said is how gorgeous it is.  It's apparently the first/only game of some (indie?) Chinese studio, but the art easily feels AAA.  Of other indie Metroidvanias I've played, only Bloodstained comes close, but this goes above and beyond making its strictly 2-D gameplay feel like a planar slice of an immersive 3-D world.  In many places, interactible stage elements swoop in from foreground and background, and maps are crafted to give the feel of fully 3-d cities and rooms.  The only complaint I've got about this incredible scenery-fest is that on slower computers it definitely occasionally lags, and fuzzes in elements as it loads their low-detail meshes followed by their high-detail meshes.  Once or twice a day during my playtime, it would lock up entirely (<1 FPS) for a second or two, but as I played it usually settled down.It's worth a look for that alone, if you're more of an indie gamer looking for some eye candy in a genre not known for it.  Beyond that?  Pleasant but not a stand-out.  The difficulty curve was reasonable after some big early-game spikes; I took out most bosses on my first or second pass, with a few (including the final one) stomping me flat until I learned their patterns.  The basic enemies are dangerous in numbers, too, but the game is very forgiving -- you don't lose anything on death.  The automap is *exceptionally* friendly, marking many (but not all) collectibles and all unopened doors, so your backtracking is low-guesswork.  Quests are strictly go-here-fight-boss with a side order of acquire-collectibles, but the midgame has some branching story points keeping it from full linearity.  The story didn't particularly grab me (old grizzled war hero gets pulled back into his old life when bad guys intervene) but the English translation and the voice acting are solid.The gameplay is smooth but with some noticeable flaws.  Movement techniques are tight and pretty forgiving -- I appreciated that double-jump plus dash was sufficient to let you sequence break some areas -- but the late-game grapple has some counterintuitive auto-snapping (prioritizing targets below you sometimes??) and several of your moves have startup frames which can lead to false starts and failed activations.  (Also, I only discovered AFTER the final boss that you can continue to drink healing potions by keeping the trigger held down, instead of having to go through the startup animation each time.  That would have made several tough fights easier.)Similarly, the combat/combo system is deep and intricate -- but is both held back by poor controls (most of the sample combos you're shown in martial arts training switch mid-combo between your weapons, and the only way to cycle between your three weapons is L1 or L2, and if you hit the wrong trigger and cycle the wrong way, you're dead in the water).  Meanwhile, combat has a Souls-like pace of finding an opening for slow attacks which don't always stun-lock the enemy; most of the enemies have ranged attacks and you're almost entirely a melee character; and you don't even get an invulnerable dodge until the next-to-last level, so for most of the game you're relying on short strings of basic attacks in between madly jumping to avoid projectiles and dashing out of range of big enemy swings, greatly limiting the actual utility of the combo system.  You can lay down some serious hurt with your SP-consuming special attacks, though -- especially after upgrading them to more powerful versions with your in-game currency -- and it's always satisfying clearing a room by unleashing a special or two.I'll admit it, I largely played the game because furry, but I think there's plenty to like here beyond that.  I listed a lot of its rough edges above, but when I wasn't getting broken out of my experience by them, this was decently engrossing gameplay and a visual feast.

_childDocuments_.review: Six years have passed since the Machine Legion successfully invaded Torch City. The furizens (anthropomorphic citizens) left after this invasion live in constant fear. There is a resistance that thrives in the shadows, but for most they just want to be left alone, hopefully to live their lives the way that they can. In F.I.S.T: Forged in Shadow Torch, you will be taking on the role of Rayton, a former ace soldier who is pulled back into the conflict. You will not have to go it alone, however, you’re going to have a mechanical rig that starts with a very intimidating and painful metal fist. This is a Metroidvania type of game. It’s all about conquering different areas of the world, with the world being filled with platforms, obstacles, and enemies. There are of course hidden goodies throughout the game, as well as additional tools that you can use as you get further into the game. As you progress through the game you’ll also have the chance to spend currency on upgrading your moves to help better put the enemies out of their misery. I know that the storyline of the reluctant hero thrusted back into the spotlight to try to take on the world by himself is a very well worn theme, but I have to say that this game made it entertaining and interesting. I cared about the other characters in the game, I felt the pain of the main character, I felt as if the developers cared about the story. To be honest, the crowning achievement of any good story is that the player is left wanting more, and I indeed was left wanting to know “what happens next?”You’re going to end up with the fist, a drill, and a whip as your arsenal, and each has their own special talents to help with accessing sealed areas. They also give you different modes of attack be it with range, speed, or abilities. I did spend most of the game using the fist, but I will admit that there were certain parts of the game that relying on the fist alone will not equal success. There are some other limited use items that you’ll gain throughout the game, but to be honest I mostly had it on the carrot juice (think of it as health potions) so that when I screwed something up I didn’t immediately die. From start to finish this game took just under 11 hours and I have to say that most of the time it was jam packed with fast paced action. Sure there were a couple of areas that made me want to pull my hair out because I mistimed a jump, or I failed to get clear of an enemy when I was trying to heal so death came to meet me, but that was part of the game, and something that I learned from. There is some backtracking that you will have to do throughout the game, sometimes to continue the storyline, other times to go back and gain access to previous areas that you didn’t have the right skills to access, but for the most part you’re going to be revealing more and more of the world. There are a couple of “warp spots” but to be honest they kind of confused me and so I didn’t use them unless I was trying to get back to town.This is a solid game, I basically played this game non-stop from start to finish. I kept coming back for more, and that of course tells you that this is a game that you need to have in your collection. It also doesn’t hurt that the environment looks gorgeous throughout the game, even though you’re only truly side scrolling through the game, the background adds so much more life and depth to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: As Metroidvanias go I would say it's slightly above average?  7.5/10?  Most things are decent/good with nothing being overall excellent.The environments?  Good looking enough.  There's a lot of 2.5D effects in the game and they're generally used well.Characters look ok.  They're all some kind of animal and the fur effect looks kind of sketchy on medium settings.  The animations look quite good on the other hand.Music is passable.  Some tracks are catchy, many are forgettable.The combat system is a high point.  You have a few weapons at your disposal, with various special attacks that can easily combo together so the skill ceiling is a lot higher than just button mashing.  Bosses are pretty fun as a result.  Your damage output and damage sustained is rather high so you can end up dead quick, or take out a boss in one extended flurry of combos if you stagger them and don't miss.  The parry once unlocked has a forgiving window and is useful.  Your "MP bar" can be used for healing potions or various attack items, so you can choose a risk vs reward kind of situation.Map traversal feels good.  With your combination of wall jumps air dashes and double jumps you get around very quickly.  The pacing of the map expansion is ok, and secrets are split between "have to find them behind secret walls" and "Need an ability you don't have yet come back later."The story is mediocre.  You won't really care about what is going on.  The voice acting is shockingly decent, but the script translation/localization is quite bad.  The sentence structure is often stilted and you'll note characters suspiciously repeat themselves in slightly different ways a lot, a hallmark of bad localization.Worth playing?  For sure.  Price isn't bad either.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended! Personally my GOTY of 2021! The combat mechanics are really varied and fun to implement in actual gameplay. It has everything a good metroidvania should have, such as distinct areas, platforming, puzzles, character growth and so forth. The visuals such as character design, animation asset and environmental design are all beautiful! There's even a JOJO reference!For the life of me, I couldn't figure this out, but the game was almost always chugging or underperforming for me even with specs that should have been good enough to handle it without issue. Having said that, that's a personal issue and I won't let it affect my review.As much as I love the game, it's not perfect. The aforementioned features don't always reach their peak potential as most situations don't particularly lend themselves to using your full repertoire, there aren't a TON of reasons to return to an area after getting everything (or most of everything),  and the English localization is lacking in that it can be confusing at times and downright redundant. These may sound pretty bad, but the cons did not outdo the pros. I love it, but it could be better, like  most games.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... good, yeah! Not great, and I have my gripes, but, I enjoyed it! Beat-em-up style combat, which isn't my forte, but between the three different weapon types and a few subweapons (that I never really used much) you have a lot of options, the platforming feels pretty tight, the map is large but not overwhelming and most areas feel unique, the graphics are pretty well polished (though I had to turn some settings down to get this to run on my machine but whateverrrr)And I don't have any big nitpicks or issues, just... a lot of smaller ones. The game does look beautiful but it's kind of... samey, in its drab color palettes and mechanical fortresses, only a few areas stand apart and none of them are that striking. The weapons are all pretty good but it feels like each new one handily outclasses the previous one... and you get the drill like an hour and half into the game... and then don't get the whip until over halfway through, right before the end of act 2, so it doesn't feel like you get enough time to use it? There's also some pacing issues, namely a LOT of slow-moving elevators, platforms, unskippable cutscenes on boss retries, kind of sparse fast-travel points meaning backtracking can get annoying, in a lot of ways it just feels slow. Tack on a -ton- of reused enemies and bosses - the first "boss" you fight, uhh, prepare to see him a dozen more times, same with the ninja frogs - and  it did get a little exhausting by the end. Also, way too many water areas - one may have been fine but there's like, three or four water-heavy zones and a lot of them happen pretty close together too so it again gets, exhausting. The plot is a footnote but it feels... awkward, maybe as a result of the translation, but even then... sometimes stuff just -happens- and doesn't land with emotional impact, and the game kind of ends in a weirdly inconclusive location and eehhh I just wasn't that invested. Also, as a furry, the word "furtizen" hurts my soul.It's not that I have more problems than praises, just that what the game does right is... pretty standard and not particularly worth praising, it's all-around a good time, a strong 7/10, y'know, just, could be better too!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Beaten it and it's genuinely one of the best metroidvanias I've ever played. Absolutely worth it. Excellent really challenging boss fights and tough platforming sections. There's even a hidden fighting game mode if you want more combat scenarios. I wish there was an unlockable hard mode. There's only Easy and Normal. Beat it on normal and found it to be a fair challenge. Some tedious puzzles in the ancient ruins level and a little too much swimming, but a strong final boss fight. 8/10Haven't beaten it yet. This is more or less a first impressions. This game rules. Easily the best combat system I've experienced in a Metroidvania yet. Think Devil May Cry if it was a Metroidvania. There are a plethora of unlockable moves across all three equipable weapons that allow you to string together insane extended combos using classic techniques like juggling and weapon swaps mid-combo. It's extremely satisfying and fairly challenging. You gotta time your attacks and dodges just right. I would've really appreciated a style meter or combo meter to encourage more aggressive play, but that's just me. The game is gorgeous and runs smooth even at 4K with ray-tracing enabled. There is some stutter when loading into new areas unfortunately, but once you're in, there's no slowdown thankfully. Environments are highly detailed, atmospheric, and full of depth. The game isn't exactly linear, but you always know where you need to go and are rarely lost. You're encouraged to revisit areas and branch off the beaten path to unlock additional upgrades, items, and money. I prefer this approach, as I hate getting lost and having to backtrack constantly. Thankfully, backtracking isn't a chore thanks to the game's excellent movement controls and abilities. It's not quite as fluid or as fast as Metroid Dread, but you'll have no issue rapidly navigating through levels and possibly even sequence break the game unintentionally. If you're looking for a complex story with cryptic Soulslike storytelling, this is not that kind of game. The story is corny in its serious tone and it doesn't bother me. I found it amusing and enjoyed the voice acting featured here. I'm really enjoying this game so far.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a competent metroidvania, but there are far better ones out there. Get this for 10 dollars or less, I honestly think Dust, An Elysian Tail is a better anthropomorphic style game/ metroidvania.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid metroidvainia, it has some kinks, but what is there is enjoyable combat and great platforming that for the most part feel very fair.It does get a bit overboard toward the end. Combat gets a bit too spamy and some of the platforming loses what earlier sections did much better.A 80+ % run will take you about 16 hours to complete. Just enough.Special mention has to be given to the environments and how the world connects. This is often an issue in metroidvania games, but in FIST this is highest class. Might be the best I’ve ever seen. It really doesn’t feel like you’re playing a metroidvania game in the sense that the environments all make a logical world-building sense.For example, in a game like Indivisible (which is a game I really like) there will be so many parts, platforms and such that make gameplay sense, but no sense whatsoever in terms of the space and environment you are in. FIST does this extremely well, the environments are truly a treat to unfold.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game recently, here are my thoughts on it.- Gameplay 8/10Pretty original metroidvania in that aspect. It focuses heavily on melee combat, and the 3 weapons are really inventive and have a pretty good sense of weight / power. The platforming is solid and the fighting is pretty challenging in a good way. The combo system takes a little while to get used to ; commands are queued so it punishes mashing.- Art style 9/10The backgrounds are *gorgeous* and the machines' dieselpunk aesthetic works great as well. The Iron Legion design is really good, and while I wouldn't have chosen such a realistic style for the furry characters, it works. Well except for Lady Q, whose whole design is "I'M A GURL" with exaggerated curves and big anime eyes that look out of place. Also not sure why half the furry characters have a tail and the other half doesn't.- Sound design 6/10The soundtrack does the job. The voice lines get a bit repetitive after a while, and can someone get this poor rabbit some coffee please, he sounds like he's reading his grocery list.- Writing 3/10The big weak point of the game, it feels like they focused exclusively on gameplay and the story was added as an afterthought. Which is a shame, because the lore would have been so fun to explore.The characters and story are, unfortunately, pretty flat and cliché. You have the old disgruntled war hero, the fat comic relief bear, the old martial art sensei, the best friend turned traitor, literally Catwoman, and yes they're written exactly like you'd expect. Funnily enough, the most fleshed out and attaching character is an enemy NPC, the Legion's Head of Personnel.- Overall 7/10If you ignore the story, FIST is a great dieselpunk metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Definately one of the best platformer games I have ever played. Good story, graphics, mechanics, physics, and runs smooth. Should run on low end GPUs and high end hardware all the same. Running max settings at 60% usage on my 3090 w/o DLSS. Had RTX and DLSS but causes stuttering and frame drops. Turing on DLSS literally doubles FPS, but looks blurry and has no adjustment. DLSS on or off. That is all. I think it is running DLSS 1.0, therefore only worth it if you need it.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: A good metroidvania. It brings nothing new to the genre, but the setting and characters are great, the graphics and soundtrack are very good, the only bad point is a poor optimization which result into a heavy lag that makes some intense parts of the game (especially the boss fights) much more difficult (to the point they can become more frustrating that fun).Overall, a small 7 out of 10, which could be upgraded to a solid 7 or even a 8 if the optimization and lag issues are solved.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game design is backed up with solid combat and tight controls (and a pretty impressive sound track in my opinion) all help make this game stand among the top metroidvanias of all time. Upgrades are dolled out at a very sparing, even pace and feel well-earned. The characters and worldbuilding are a little sparse, but there is plenty of game to enjoy to keep you craving the next area until the very end of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth a play through. _childDocuments_.review: I finished this game in ~16 hours and got 100% completion.The game is a lot of fun from start to finish, the combos that you can pull off are so satisfying - or you can just power punch everything and still have lots of fun. I wouldn't say it was an easy game, but it wasn't that hard either. I think it could be kind of difficult at the start, while you're learning enemy moves and hit-box sizes, after that the game is smooth and rewarding. Boss fights are specially fun.Amazing graphics and scenery, really knowing how to create the atmosphere they wanted.The only weak point of this title is the story. Character motivations aren't solid nor interesting, the development of the story feels more like an excuse for making a playable universe rather than actually tell a story. I don't see this as a big problem, though. The mechanics and visuals compensate for the lack of good storytelling.A very satisfying and visually pleasing game. Don't expect a great story and just enjoy the mechanics and looks of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: System and Setup:Windows 10 64bitIntel Core i9 10900KNVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 SUPERLG 27inch 1440p 144hz monitor 27GN850-BThe game launches without trouble, although there were some unfortunate technical issues that brought down the experience. I can run the game maxxed at 120fps. Beyond that, the game starts to struggle to maintain its framerate.Notes:- The largest map I've ever seen in an Metroidvania. My first run took me around 20 hours, which feels absurd for a genre I usually associate with 10 hour playtimes. - A combat system based upon three main weapons that can be switched mid-combo. Fans of Guacamelee, or Character Action games will know what they're in for.- The game graphically looks nice, when it's behaving properly.- The English translation is often awkward to listen to. A native English speaker should've been hired to proofread and edit the script.- Poor optimization for PC. The loading stutter is a constant annoyance, and textures in the environment and Rayton himself will constantly flicker black seemingly at random.- The game doesn't have a mini map, which means that the player will have to constantly pull up the map screen to avoid becoming lost.- The game is nice enough to highlight locked chests and plant collectibles when you get near them, taking the frustration out of relocating them when you have the abilities and/or keys to get them. The game's map also tracks the percentage of an area of the game you've been to. However the game only tracks how much of an area you've seen and not if you've gotten all of the collectibles or upgrades from that part of the map. Posters are also not marked. This adds some annoyance to the game for completionists who don't want to have to use a guide or a video for help.- The ending was a little bit abrupt and I would've liked if there were at least one or two other scenes in the epilogue.Despite the game's flaws, FIST is a great Metroidvania game and fans of the genre shouldn't overlook it.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch

_childDocuments_.review: As a die hard fan of the metroidvania genre, I absolutely loved this game. Its fresh game play and inventive environmental elements reminds me a lot of how it felt to play Shadow Complex for the first time, more than a decade ago. Same engine from Unreal with many feature improvements applied over time. Highly recommend you try it if you're a lover of this games!!! The only minor complaint I have is that the  combo training challenges at high levels of difficulty can be insanely frustrating to pull off. I'd prefer if TiGames would remove the beginner, intermediate and master training challenges and give you the mystery shard after beating the three individual weapon challenges.While TiGames indicates the game is still being optimized on PC, it runs very well and only has a few minor hiccups from time to time with assets failing to load quickly enough. The hardware I used to run the game was the following at 1080p and max settings with motion blur set to the lowest option.

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvanias typically attempt to specialize in either movement or combat, and let the other be a secondary mechanic. FIST is the rare one that excels at both, and it's equally fluid whether you're juggling enemies in melee or dashing around between jumps. The map design is expansive and the game is beautiful though unfortunately even on a 2070 it chugs at times with crippling lag that requires a restart to fix. This primarily affects the hub area but there were times during underwater sections where I'd have to downgrade my graphics to minimum settings to get the game to run. The translation also isn't flawless, with odd disconnects between subtitles and spoken dialogue, to say nothing of the jarringly inconsistent quality of the voice acting. These are relatively minor quibbles though, and FIST is an incredibly solid game.

_childDocuments_.review: An all around decent metroidvania with fun game play, good graphics and nice atmosphere. The upgrades are meaningful and enjoyable and the exploration is quite fun. I played through 80% of the game on normal and had a good time, but the last part of the game goes berserk and I actually had to turn it to easy to finish. The final 2-3 boss fights are orders of magnitude harder than anything else in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me start by saying this is 100% worth it. Metroidvanias are my favorite genre of video games because their sense of progression is sooooo satisfying and F.I.S.T. nails it on the head. If you like Hollow Knight, you'll like this game.Combat is tight and challenging, music is on point, graphics and atmosphere are great and the story is....meh.The collectibles are always worth it making exploration very nice and the map is clear and concise.I do have 3 major complaints that I will list below if the person reading this cares.1: The fast travel systemHoly sh!t there needs to be like 2x more fast travel points. Like most metroidvanias, there is a ton of backtracking and this game does not make it easy to 100% most areas endgame when you have the proper abilities to go back and get everything. Most of the time, the only fast travel station is on the opposite side of the map as opposed to that tiny thing you missed earlier in game. 2: Huge expansions of underwater Need I say more? Underwater sections in video games are usually bad and this game is no exception. 3: The last ability you get *spoilers ahead*I hate writing spoilers in reviews but this boiled my blood and must be said. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've seen so far, F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch is a textbook metroidvania game with a very atmospheric steampunk/dieselpunk aesthetic. I have to say I was initially skeptical about the anthropomorphic characters (I mean, they are even called "furtizens"), but the story and dialogue are actually quite intriguing and have kept me playing this game for days, with no signs of me getting bored of it. As for the gameplay, the combat is smooth and responsive and there is plenty of exploration to be done and hidden areas to be found, just like I would expect from a good metroidvania. I have seen some criticisms towards the combo system in the game and in all honesty, I am beginning to see how all the combinations for the different weapons can become overwhelming and difficult to remember. I have mostly stuck with a couple of skills/combos so far and it has worked out OK though, so it doesn't seem like the game NEEDS you to remember all of these combo combinations.All in all, if you are a metroidvania or a steampunk enjoyer, F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch is a must-buy in my opinion. And again, don't let the furry characters dissuade you from the game! You'll get used to them pretty quickly.
