_childDocuments_.review: Don't take this pseudo JRPG in stride...I can safely say that Wolfstride is unlike any other game that I have ever played. Are there others like it out there on the market? Most assuredly. But none have as much thought or attention to detail put into them, if you ask me.I won't be providing any kinds of spoilers here, other than to say that this action-packed visual novel perfectly encapsulates the experience of playing an anime protagonist with a shadowy & tragic past. Everything from the visuals, to the exchanges of dialogue, to the story and setting and the relationships between the myriad of characters that comprise it all — it all coalesces into something akin to perfection.Even if you're not a fan of the various series that clearly inspired it ('Trigun', 'Cowboy Bebop', 'The Big O', 'Outlaw Star', 'Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann' and 'Cannon Busters' just to name a few), I'm still going to highly recommend this game. It's got everything you could ever want from one of its kind; heart, humor, action, suspense, drama, and big effing robot battles! (And who doesn't love big effing robot battles?)But perhaps the best thing of all is the value. This game is only 15$, when in reality it ought to be at least thrice that. God tier levels of work have been put into this thing. The voice actors do an outstanding job of propelling the narrative forward in ways that a lot of diehard otaku would say was impossible to do outside of Japan. The visuals make you feel like you're playing something produced by Madhouse or Studio Trigger, who have produced some of the most famous anime of any generation, past or present. And that soundtrack?! Oh, man. It's the icing on the proverbial cake!So, yes, I am going to recommend Wolfstride to everyone that I know. Raw Fury and OTA IMON have teamed up to deliver a must-have gaming experience. 5 out of 5 stars.Well, what're you waiting for, trash?! Get in that cockpit and punch Earth in the face!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. The vibes are immaculate, the main cast give me strong Cowboy Bebop vibes, and they all really grew on me with time. The battle system is fun, and it's incredibly satisfying seeing yourself get stronger. The art is just fantastic, too.It manages to be both funny and genuinely emotional, without those stepping on each others' toes, and while the main character can be very melodramatic, it's not like the game is unaware of that. (Thankfully not in the way that it gets constantly quipped about to the point of getting grating.)It's not perfect - the pacing - of upgrades most specifically, but in general - can feel a little wonky. Trying to get money and max friendships with people requires an excessive amount of minigame grinding. Our perspective character's long melodramatic rants about how awful he is can get a bit excessive, and even the chunky, satisfying main combat of the game can fall prey to you figuring out a dominant strategy, making it easier than it should probably be... but none of these things stopped me having a wonderful time. It's a game that I can definitely see not everyone completely vibing with, but it resonated with me, and completely sucked me in.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolfstride was basically love at first sight for me.  I love mecha, and it's tone and presentation press a lot of buttons for me.  I'd recommend to anyone, especially anime fans, because it plays like one at times.Gameplay is divided between walking around town doing various chores for mech parts, and occasional battles to put them to use.  I was playing Persona 5 Royal before I started, and while the structures are similar, Wolfstride is a little more concise, meaning I haven't been able to put it down.It isn't a perfect game.  There are supposed to lose fights, and minigames you can't win until you get upgrades later on, two things that always annoy me.  The story can also feel like it drags on, especially when characters start to repeat themselves over and over in soliloquies, which happens a few times toward the end.  The climax isn't very satisfying either,  the game alludes to  a big bad from pretty early on, but by the time they actually show up the fighting is done, and the focus of the story shifts from the stakes of the mech fighting in the real world, to one of the character exploring their own psyche and learning to forgive themselves.   Guess the structure isn't the only similarity to Persona.  There's even a pinrapple based social link system, now that I think about it, though the rewards feel a little lack-luster, most of them being things you can buy eventually anyway.  The rate at which you get pineapples is also abysmal, which leads to an absurd amount of grinding on minigames, which would've really put a damper on things if I didn't know how to use cheat engine and just give myself all the pineapples I could ever want.Wolfstride, though flawed at times, is the most fun I've had in a while, with a great cast of interesting characters.  Except for Peepoo, a deliberately annoying sidekick character.  His voice is like nails on a chalkboard, and he's a one trick pony who tries to say vulgar things but whose programming only lets him say 'PEEEEE.'  I skipped through most of his lines, and resent him being in the game.  Until he was introduced, I loved everything about it; and the game is still amazing around him, it just gets derailed for a little while when he shows up, and feels a little grating whenever he makes a lame, uh, 'joke.'If I seem hard on the game, it's because it was close to perfection for me, but that makes the few, minor flaws it has stand out much more.  It's still a solid 4/5, an 8-8.5/10,  I'm hoping for a sequel that goes a little more in depth, and actually explores some of the plot points it set up and then ignored.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has fun characters, nice music, and gorgeous sprites, so I can forgive it for being a little too entertained by poop jokes (seriously, cool it with those if you ever make a sequel). It's jarring, too, because this game does have some legitimately beautiful moments (e.g. the last LAST fight) and some jokes that felt like they earned a chuckle out of me, so this type of juvenile humor feels kind of forced and out of place when juxtaposed with the rest of the package.Ironically, this line of criticism doesn't apply to the character named PeePoo, who ended up being one of my favorite characters. You could tell the voice actor was just having so much fun with this character the whole way through.One part of this game that I really enjoyed was the way characters talk to each other. Every one has a nickname - Shade, for example, is also Shado, and Catman. Knife Leopard is Pineapples, Duque is Killer Hound, Zee is the Witch. A lot of times in stories this gets really annoying, but I feel that they did it in a very endearing way in this game.On the topic of voice actors - for this level of production, I was very pleasantly surprised by the entire cast's voice performances, with the exception of some lines sprinkled throughout that were clearly recorded out of context of the lines surrounding them. There are also quite a few typos, as other people have mentioned, and I wish that they would go back and fix those. That said, I definitely appreciated the moments where the actors adlibbed just a bit to make the characters sound more natural.It makes it even better, then, that all of these lines are accompanied by a myriad of beautifully-realized portraits, with all sorts of crazy and awesome expressions. Some larger, more intricate images are used in the more impactful moments of the game, which made me wish that there were some sort of built-in gallery for me to see them again later.There are all sorts of little things in this game that bugged me, including actual bugs. The biggest of which was a glitch which caused me to be completely unable to play the game. Luckily, support was very quick to get back to me on this issue, and I've published the fix I used to get past it in a community post. There were also a couple of smaller issues, like how the "money ticking" sound will sometimes start to loop infinitely. However, none of these issues were common enough for them to bog down my 25 hours with the game.There were some design decisions I wasn't a huge fan of, such as the way pineapples were done. This system did have some fun moments come out of it - such as a character telling you the pineapples made his heart stop, which teaches you the Cardiac Arrest Punch move for your mech - but I didn't feel rewarded for maxing out all of the characters. Even just making the pineapple god say something funny would've been nice; an achievement would've been appreciated as well.The arcade is another area I felt this. I was very excited to see the arcade grow as the weeks when on in the game, but I maxed out all of the upgrades in the first 3 days of discovering it. I kept coming back under the assumption that there would be more (the hint for the place says I can hire more people, but I never got that option), but there never was. These are very small things, obviously, but it's the type of thing where just a little bit more would have gone a long way.Finally: gameplay. This is the part of the game that I think is best enjoyed if you know what you're getting into. I'll just be blunt here: most of this game is waking up in the morning, walking to every NPC you know, talking to them, and maybe doing some side-jobs for money and other goodies.If you're hoping for mech battles galore right out the gate, you'll probably be a bit disappointed by the "slow start". There are lots of opportunities to play them to your heart's content later in the game, but the early game is all about getting the world and characters established. The mechs themselves are wonderfully brought to life, with gorgeous animations and punchy sound effects.In the end, Wolfstride is a very captivating story with really fun characters that are all unique and pretty well performed. If you let it, it can really pull you in with endearing character moments and hilarious mini-games .

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of heart and style, and the substance isn’t bad either.If you couldn’t tell, the game is in black and white, and that is an intentional stylistic choice. I would say that it would look a lot better in color, but fret not, there are a few twists and turns in terms of this design decision. And the game does a lot with its extremely limited color palette.The voice acting is very solid, pretty much every VA does a great job of portraying a single character, even some of the NPCs who don’t particularly matter to the overall story. This has a lot to do with the script, which makes each character distinct and unique, but the voice overs really hit this home. Wolfstride is an underdog story at its core, but there is other stuff happening in the background, and when it hits its story highs it hits them pretty hard. There is a really cool sequence about half way through the game that I wasn’t expecting, just fluff, and it is done in a really engaging way that makes you appreciate what the writers were doing with these characters.But I can’t say the entire script is perfect. Certain events happen with little explanation, some plot threads seemingly lead to nowhere, and certain characters have a tendency to either philosophize ad nauseam or go on melodramatic rants. One character in particular is written to be both incredibly annoying and lovable, and you may alternative between those extremes from scene to scene. I do believe some of the imperfections I mentioned are actually done on purpose. Wolfstride’s writing is quirky, so is the lore, to say the least. Overall though, the story is just rewarding enough to make the journey to the end worth it.You’re probably wondering about the gameplay though. The core mecha combat is really good, especially getting new parts and moves to customize your playstyle. To its credit the game gives you a lot of versatility in terms of how to approach each fight, and when you get your core together, you will feel like a badass. The problem is that it takes a looooong time to get there. The beginning is very slow and doesn’t have a lot of action, but once you’re reaching mid to late game, it’s almost nothing but a metal on metal, robot punching fight-fest. You will initially face off with some really basic, beat-up junkers, but gradually move on to some really powerful and very cool-looking opponents.There are also several minigames, and for the most part they are decently fun. The game doesn’t tell you this, but you won’t be getting high scores on those minigames until you progress further and unlock certain helper items. The main problem with Wolfstride though is that the world is kinda...empty. You’ll spend the majority of the game running in game-time through the same empty streets to talk to a few NPCs, grind some cash, and then do it again the next day. It’s not super daunting, but it does get old after you’ve been doing it for a while. There’s also some grinding involved with a certain mechanic, but if you wait until a little past the game’s mid-point, it becomes significantly less time consuming.Would I recommend this game? Oh yeah, overall I think it is pretty great. But try the free demo first if it is still available, see how you feel about it. For someone who likes giant robots and tactical combat there is plenty to love. Just remember to do what Foam Gun asks you to do. And talk to Barbara, she loves you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll edit this for a bit more detail later but for right now: Wolfstride is an absolute banger, The game's style alone would be enough to recommend it as an artistic indie game. The music, tone and art design are all stunning. The game wears plenty of hats and the DNA of a diverse group of sci fi elements are kicking around inside it.  Gurren Lagann, Pacific Rim and Cowboy Bebop are the clearest inspirations for the world and story, but the art design has that sleek, design-heavy stylistic flair to it that I associate with the likes of Persona or Dangan Ronpa. That's not to say there's nothing original in Wolfstride, it's a wildly creative endeavor. But it wears its inspirations on its sleeve and they come together in this bombastic, beautiful game.And it is a game. This is no walking simulator or glorified puzzle game. There's a lot of gameplay to be found in customizing your pair of cowboys (mecha and pilot both) and the combat is tactical and hits a good level of challenge where it's punishing but with a proper build and strategy few mistakes spell an instantly lost battle. I won't get into all the details of gameplay, particularly since at 5 hours of gameplay I am still unlocking new systems. Suffice it to say that underneath the flair and highly competent story and characters there is a genuinely interesting and play heavy RPG.The game's not precisely flawless. The indie heritage shows in a few rough edges UX-wise, mainly regarding the locations of certain menus and the travel times from location to location and the dialogue can be a bit unwieldy at times. There are also a minor handful of bugs I've run into but nothing gamebreaking and the developers have already begun to address the worst of them. Honestly, my biggest criticisms are largely nitpicks and not anything that I think would turn a player's experience of the game.In short,  the game's stunning. Zany, nostalgic without being unoriginal, and deeply engaging. Especially given its extremely generous pricing I can't recommend this one enough.  So give Wolfstride a shot, peopletrash. I didn't regret it and I'm confident anyone who's gotten far enough to read this review won't either.

_childDocuments_.review: rocks!What a game, what a wonderfully energic and stylish game.A funny/heartfelt/bombastic Visual Novel, bundled with a cool and competent turn-based combat.Explore the city, meet people and do odd jobs to scrap together enough money and parts to fix the mess of a mech you call "Cowboy" for the next big fight.Artstyle goes quite strong, good music and dialogue to boot and quite a lengthy game too for the asking price.Imagine the battlefield as a 7 squares line each mech occupying one space.The game builds around this concept by having abilities that can only target up to a certain range or over it, you can move, push your enemy, be pushed by them, buff yourself, use and recharge your ammo for special attacks and access a special move once a bar fills up.Your mech can be customized to fit multiple playstyles you may have in mind.When not in fights you’ll be doing some minigames to earn money for the upgrades and repairs you oh so desperately need for the next fight.A gangster with a heart of gold, a gruff canine mechanic, and a free spirited hunk wish to enter the mechfighting world tournament with their busted up, prototype of a mech......an incredible story ensues.In the early game the fights are sparce and far between, leaving much more space for the visual novel to set stakes and characters.Conversely in the late game is just a mad rush of a fight after the other with little time for the story and the little that there is while flashing out the world of the game a little ore is inconsequential for the characters and main narrative.Many things are left unexplained or narrative arc are opened and never closed or abruptly ended in a hurry to wrap things up.These are still minor complaints; I still thoroughly recommend this game because it deserve every ounce of praise.

_childDocuments_.review: To put it simply, Wolfstride is a ride. The steam page's own description puts it best when it describes itself as "an immature grown-up RPG". The art is obviously incredible and the game knows it. I've never seen a story's final act try to cram more crazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ into it and I mean that in the best way possible. While Wolfstride suffers at times from some slow pacing but the game had enough charm, style, and intrigue to keep me hooked and in the end it all paid off. Its influences shine through while still feeling like something totally original, albeit not without its flaws.             The Mech Battle system is unique and interesting enough to serve its purpose for fights but I didn't feel encouraged to swap around moves and parts often like the game has in mind as customization felt underwhelming at times. There were also a surprising amount of days with nothing special to do besides new dialogue for the characters. I do think the driving force of this game is the ride you get pulled along for with its cast but I think the surplus of days with nothing special going contributes to the game's pacing feeling a little weird at times, especially when there's inconsistencies about whether or not there's narration after the day. However, on the note of the cast, I'm not sure if I've ever seen an indie game with more character bulging out of its voice acting to the point I couldn't see any of the cast the same without it. Wolfstride's characters are its heart.                  With those flaws being said though, I think they're fairly easy to overlook once you get into the flow of the game. For an Indie debut I think Wolfstride is incredibly impressive and I'm a bit shocked to have not seen anyone online talking about it. I think OTA IMON has shown a lot of promise with this game and I'm excited to see and play more from them.

_childDocuments_.review: A Wonderful Mess in need of a lot of revisionWolfstride has great style, amazing voice work, a fun premise, and a lot of heart. For that I would prefer people support the creators.On the other hand there are a lot of issues:+Loads of dead time+Bugs that crash the game+Sluggish and mostly unimportant upgrade system+Pineapples to upgrade relationships which is more frustrating than enjoyable.I find the writing to be hit or miss. There are long monologues that go on WAY, WAY too long, especially at the end. I do love 'trash' and 'dog damn' though.Battles, once you get a rifle and a good punch, become meaningless except for the last few where you need to guard as well.Side-Jobs allow you to make so much money that you can just spam buy everything without looking and never care.Fights are won by destroying the torso, so you have no strategy--no enemy is a puzzle, just aim for the center.All of these issues could be addressed with adjustments: easier pineapple gain, better character interactions for social links (they're useless except for some items), more robust moves/tweaks, and damage reduction to the body is arms/head are active.There's so much to like, but a lot to improve. A great passion project that I would love to see be even better.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this I haven't finished it yet, but that's a foregone conclusion, I will finish it no doubt.The best way I would describe this gem to someone is if the movie Real Steel had a child with the anime Cowboy Bebop.  This game is a true gem its voice acting is very well done, the art is beautiful, even the basic pixel aspect is very nice.  Even the music is great and I don't usually pay much attention to the music in games but the chill jazz beats from certain screens get stuck in my soul lol.The only critiques I have for the game are small, and may be removed later when I finish the game depending on what late game has in store for me.  The critiques are this:1: too much grinding of "jobs" is necessary to acquire pineapples... unless I am mistaken you would need 147 pineapples to max out everyone's happiness in the game, so far I have only gotten maybe 20 from the story line, and I think 9 from the combat "battle pass" game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not big on mecha games tbh. Never have been. They tend to be rather...soulless to me. Mech battle after mech battle after mech battle with a story that's either a quick paragraph between menus or a relentless deluge of background details with no greater present story than "You want to be number one".Wolfstride...Wolfstride is different.Wolfstride is a game that at surface level, maintains the 'rags to riches' story I mentioned above, but uses it as a base to bring together a bunch of troubled characters and give them something to believe in again. And honestly, characters are where Wolfstride shines. Every single member of your team, every citizen of Rain City, hell every opponent you face on your rise to the top has a level of complexity and care put into them that makes you love, laugh with, laugh at or hate them effectively. Combined with the distinct artstyle of the world and solid soundtrack, it creates a world I wanted to truly absorb and enjoy as much as possible. Chatting with the crew in the hangar, grabbing a drink at the Midnight Rider, doing odd jobs at the Crapyard, they all make this place feel like a living world instead of a glorified menu.And the mech fights are nothing to sneeze at either. The anticipation between each fight is intense as you scramble to prepare your mech with the customisation system which strikes the perfect balance of being deep and complex enough that any playstyle can be used, but it's never so complicated that it feels overwhelming and intimidating. The fights are intimate, strategic and brutal. You're not chipping away at someone in a metal suit that moves like they're on the Moon going "pew pew pew" with a toy laser. You're getting in there, breaking through their defences and shoving a 10 ton fist RIGHT UP THEIR...chest. It feels cathartic and impactful, like a boxing match between two heavyweight champs. Just a relentless slugfest between two mechanical titans and I love it.Now I won't call it perfect. There are a lot of story moments that take 10 lines to say what could have been said in 2 and while the story itself is great, there are elements I wish were explored more relating to some of the side characters. And there IS a mechanic that I swear was trying to go for it, but it ended up just being a way to get some cool parts and bonuses for the gameplay, which is nice, but...man the potential was there. Also the game's not as funny as it thinks it is. The humour hits true in a good portion of the game, but there are moments where the comedy falls flat, 95% of the time due to one particular character who deserves to be punted into the sun.Those issues and some minor spelling and grammar errors aside, Wolfstride is an excellent time. An immersive, living, breathing world with some amazing characters and thrilling mech fights to be had that's just shy of being a bona-fide classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so this game isn't what you probably think it is.  It looks like a turn based mech combat game but it's not.  It has turn based mech battles, one on one arena matches, and they're fun.  The mechs look good and you can customize not only the mech equipment but the move list for your pilot.  You can make a bunch of different, and effective, builds.  That part of the game is great, and the black and white art looks nice.  If I were to rate the mech fights on their own?  Easily 8/10.  But that's the problem, the game isn't just about the mech fights.It's also full of tedious, repetitive tasks.  Loaded with rather poor writing and way, way too much dialogue.  There are several rather annoying characters with very annoying voice acting, one in particular that's just plain ridiculous - they were going for a character like Claptrap but they missed by a country mile.Then there are the minigames that are very boring and feel out of place.  There's also lots of pointless running around from one area to another.  The story is boring.  Too many cut scenes and voice overs that I can't seem to skip or speed up.  Just one thing after the next that's annoying, pointless, and/or tedious.There are glitches in certain parts of the game.  The display in the virtual combat arena starts to act up and you can't see where each mech is positioned, and that's pretty important.  I also managed to get stuck while walking from one area to another, no idea why, and I had to exit and re-start to fix it.The single biggest issue is that the first 3+ hours is annoying and boring.  You have to power through hours of boring story and annoyances in order to get to the mech battles and it's painful.  The first few hours should grab the player and make them want to play more.  If I hadn't read some forum posts that say that the game does get better I would have given up and that's a massive problem.Wolfstride is a beautiful, disjointed, and tedious mess that I wish I could recommend but I simply can't endorse a game that I have to force myself to play in order to get to the good parts.  8/10 for the mech combat and overall art/style but this is a 2/10 for the rest resulting in an average of 5/10 which is simply not good enough, folks.

Deciding to take part officially in the world-wide tournament of mechs, you claw and kick and drag you way through countless fights against all odds as the Player is slowly fed introspective bites and info on what might be really going on here. _childDocuments_.review: It's more of a gimmicky visual novel rather than a mech action, RPG game. And unfortunately, it's not a good kind of visual novel. It feels like at least 1/3rd of the game is missing with the way some of the side plots and the main story end. Dozens of new characters are introduced throughout the game, and the majority of them just end up disappearing or become irrelevant. Some of the locations like arcade, underground, and midnite rider also feel underutilized. The game has the oddest fast travel mechanic, which causes pointless backtracking between locations. This becomes even more evident when you are going around the map, trying to trigger new events.The soundtrack and the mech combat are ok, while the voice acting and the art style are top-notch. They Definitely make the game more bearable.It's a shame considering the game's world is honestly interesting. It's probably a case of the creators not knowing how to end a story. Wolfstride takes tons of Inspiration from Cowboy Bebop and Gurren Lagann, but all it learned from them was to be complex for the sake of being one.

_childDocuments_.review: I sunk 30 hours into this game, I 100%-ed it and unlocked every achievement. And yet, I cannot recommend this game in good faith. I'm gonna get heavy into spoilers in my review, so here's a short little tldr for those considering buying this gamePros: Incredible, if repetitive gameplayIncredible, if very repetitive musicIt's fully voice acted, and the VOs did an absolutely fantastic jobThe writing is incredibly hit or miss, but it hits a lot of the time and manages to be funny, charming, and gets you to care about (some of) the charactersThe art style is greatThe cons: Everything elseI realize that enjoying a story is subjective, but the contrivances are strange, almost nothing is explained, and when some are, you'll have wished they didn't even bother. Genuinely, don't play this game for the story. Watch the movie they ripped off instead! Redline is an incredible movie, one of my favorites, and so I was excited when the stories were eerily similar in the beginning. You can tell when they stopped plagiarizing and started writing for their own. Watch Redline and enjoy the gameplay. That's as much as you can get out of this game.Spoilers begin now:This is very obviously a character based game. There is an overarching plot, but it's there as set dressing and to provide motivation for the characters. The overarching story is confusing and kept insanely vague, so all you CAN do is focus on the characters. If you go in looking for character development, you'll find it in spades! Except for the main character, Shade. Shade starts out with Homestuck sunglasses and a chip on his shoulder, and from the getgo he has this "I'm too cool for all this" facade that is, at least I thought, intentionally grating. His friends provide enough buoyancy to offset his terrible vibe. The people around Shade grow and change and turn into legitimately better versions of themselves throughout the story, but Shade stays exactly the same the entire game. The other characters, and even Shade's own memories try to get him to improve himself but he resolutely refuses time and time again. Until finally you reach the ending, and you get a completely unearned 5 minute cutscene where he throws himself a pity party and then says he's changed, and then roll credits. The ending leaves such a bad taste in your mouth that it'll make you gag I swear. We even get a fire emblem type "Where are they now" type thing in the credits, and 1, we don't get to hear about the world at large, which is very strange considering the ending is the start of WW3, and we don't get to see what happens to our opponents, which is so disappointing. And in this “Where are they now”, Shade says that after this whole braveheart speech about how he's changed and he's better now, he says point blank that he's going to continue acting the exact same way. It’s such a gut punch.The second half of this game ruins the good will it establishes in the first 10 times over. 100 times over even. The story flies off the rails completely, none of your questions are answered, and it just keeps promising and promising that something interesting will happen, and it never does. At the end, a character we've never seen before shows real life footage of the American Military, makes some good points about the world that they live in, kills you, and is never mentioned before or again. He just kinda comes in, proves himself right unequivocally, and then the game is over. Who the hell is this guy? We never know. We never get answers to almost all of our questions. Who is GW? Vague hints and a big fat nothing burger. Why'd he kill himself gruesomely in front of his friends? No clue. Who is Godworm and why does he have a cult? Not only is that not answered, it's not even brought up. He paralyzes your best friend and you have no clue who this guy is, and then you have to read in between the lines and infer that he's somehow related to this universe's United Nations? Who blew up that oil tanker? NO CLUE? Why'd Shade make a deal with the devil? Because he felt weak I guess? What was the deal? THEY DON'T SAYAnd for the cherry on this sh*t cake, the big one we've all been waiting for, why is Shade in this mess to begin with? What exactly is the inciting incident of this story? Well I'm glad you asked, you see Shade's friend got shot, and Shade fired back, and f*cking missed, and just hit a random dude. That's the rock solid foundation this house of cards is built on. I swear to god I lost my mind when I found out this is what Shade had been whining about the whole game. Just a hollow vapid character, with a quirk that does not work, and with zero growth.It blew my mind that this was the direction they took the story. You feel like you missed something CONSTANTLY, but believe me, you didn't. It just doesn't connect, and doesn't make sense.There are a ton of smaller annoying things too, like the gameplay outside of the fights is grinding minigames or slowly running through an empty, way too big map to check if people have no dialogue or items for you, which 90% of the time is absolutely not. The difficulty is a joke. You have to stop yourself from killing your opponents on the first turn by ending your turn early if you want to hear the second round midfight dialogue. You have to intentionally handicap yourself to make this game have any semblance of difficulty (except for the penultimate mech fight, which is by far the best in the game).There are two characters who will be etched into my sh*t list for the rest of time, those being: Mary the niece of ZZ, who at first seems to be a genuinely interesting character until her writing turns batsh*t crazy and she becomes a "lol isn't she so random" type of character. She'll say literally anything, which makes her dialogue mean nothing. Genuinely "the narwhal bacons at midnight" type drivel. And then PeePoo, the robot that trains Knife, your pilot. Do you think the word Pee is funny? Well then you're in luck, as this character will say this a million f*cking times. You see he's comic relief, and his programming won't let him swear, so he says Pee instead of a swear. If you liked that, don't worry, that is his entire dialogue for the rest of the game, with some hackneyed "silence meatbag" trite garbage thrown in for good measure. Every single character besides Shade, Mary, and PeePoo are brilliant, vibrant characters that are brought down so far by association with these three bones hidden in this game's meal.This game is like a crossbreed between a siren and hydra. It draws you in with fun gameplay, cool mechanics, stellar voice acting, and incredible characters, and then suffocates you in bullsh*t. For every good joke there's 5 bad ones, for every fun fight there's an hour of tedium, for every genuinely sick character there's a gigantic segment of Shade wallowing in self pity, or PeePoo doing his tried and true one and only joke over and over and OVER AND OVER AND OVER. I cannot over-emphasize how f*cking sick I got of that one grating joke, sprinkled in between genuinely great writing, just enough sour the taste of the whole thing, it's that prevalent, and that annoying.And here we are, at the end of my inane ramblings. I wouldn't get so worked up about this if there wasn't something truly great hidden in here. It's just hidden pretty deep. This game truly had one of the worst endings I've ever seen. The entire game you're strung along with the promise of answers just around the corner, and in the end you're left with the answer to only one question, and it's so stupid you wish they didn't even bother giving it to you. This game is so close to being truly great, but it falls short in so many ways. Genuinely, as a retrosepective, I give this game a 2/10. If you asked me 10 hours in I would've given it a 8, maybe a 9. It falls off hard, and it never delivers on what it promises.If I had to describe this game in one word, it would be: Disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real mixed bag. Some great art, great music, decent voice acting, some interesting bot building/combat mechanics. There's a good sense of progression through earning currency and building up your bot and making design choices.Unfortunately, the writing for this game is miserable. The story is mostly just Cowboy Bebop as ordered from Wish™ or Temu™- a ragtag band of miscreants are broke and try to raise money. But the characters lack any sort of defining or interesting characteristics, they're all just generic anime tropes. You've got the mysterious broody guy, who isn't interesting enough to care about his mystery or why he's brooding, the energetic young femme type, who's an extremely poor fill-in for Radical Edward. The tough grumbling old man who just wants to get the job done. But they're all missing the uniqueness to their presentation and stories that makes those characters so good. And the addition to the crew is an absolutely intolerable robot, who's only gimmick is screaming PEE and POO and PEEPOO throughout every line of dialogue. I've played about 16 hours of this game, and that character alone made me start skipping the voice overs. And he talks A LOT. I've usually got a strong tolerance for 'annoying' characters, but this one in particular is so constantly present and annoying that it's made me stop playing the game. I've stopped playing for a couple of months to give it some space and see if I could come back to the game to finish it out, but honestly between the dry narrative that feels imitative of a pile of good anime without doing any work to make it unique or stand out, and "PEEPOOPEEPOO PEEEEEEEEEEE!!!!!" Defining what this game thinks humor is, I can't even bring myself back to barrel through it.A lot of heart here, a lot of good art, interesting mechanics, silly mini-games (even if the game design does lead to lot of aimless wandering)... Just having a completely generic story take up a lot of your gameplay time, and then bogged down by functionally a screaming child every other line of dialogue means that it's hard for me to recommend this to anyone over the age of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolfstride is the perfect game for a young male teenager, whose maybe struggling with depression, and isn't sure how to deal with it in a culture where men aren't as allowed to talk about feelings.  However I'm a trans female 20 year old, who has not, in fact, struggled with depression, or caring about my masculinity.Wolfstride is a mixture of minigames, interspersed with fun mech combat.  It has some of the best voice work in a video game since Night of the Full Moon or Hades, and a good story to go along with it too.  The biggest flaw, and what kind of spoiled the whole game for me, is it's Pineapple system, of giving people pineapples to advance your relationship with them.  So, wanting to complete all my relationships, I had to absolutely Grind SO MANY MINIGAMES, to get enough pineapples.  And I didn't even get anything good for getting them completed.  So, so long as you don't do what I did, you'll have a good time.That all said, I can't understate how important this game could be for a young guy trying to make sense of himself and his masculinity.  It's a game which very much addresses and discusses masculinity, what makes it appealing, why toxic masculinity can be harmful, and how to find a healthy way to be masculine.  It also talks about the unique ways depression and masculinity, which is refreshingly unique.  Again, most of these themes, don't speak to me ~specifically~ very much, but it's so easy to imagine someone who'd love this game.Altogether, Wolfstride is a fun game about mechs punching each other, the broken men who pilot them, going on goofy adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: You know when you play a game or watch a show and you can tell the people who worked on it loved making it? Yeah.As a fake persona fan (the real ones never play the damn games), this game does an awesome job of taking the daily task + turn based combat formula, putting it into a good redemption story and making the whole thing fun and exciting all the way through. It's short (for a jrpg), but I think that's the perfect length for this kind of story, it never felt dragged out or hastened. Every single voice actor did a phenomenal job, honestly, I'd say voice acting in Wolfstride is up there if not even better at times with voice acting in shows like FMAB, Baccano or Cowboy Bebop. Crude jokes really help, but even so, the game does do a good job of balancing being serious with stupid fun. Also, stupidly fun, the OST is an absolute jammer.The combat has some cool moments, though I do think it could be a bit more difficult at times, the big importance in this game is preparing the mech and the pilot instead of actually executing tactics, but some people do prefer it to be that way. The gameplay overall is pretty simple, as for me I like it, I really prefer focusing on the narrative, characters and story in the media, but if you're looking for a Tengen Toppa Titan Fall 2 then you'll be disappointed. Although I would still say that although the gameplay isn't revolutionary, the developers knew what they needed to get it to do and they did a solid job on it. Plus, simplistic gameplay works well for the slice of life type of world it achieves, at least for the most part.The Art style really makes this game work. The grayscale works for the tone, the characters are expressive, some cutscene shots are just so phenomenal I feel like I need to invest in a thesaurus so I could stop reusing the same words. If you like games with a focus on how they convey the story, like gameplay that isn't too complex or experimental but knows what it's doing, and some awesome music, artwork and voice acting to make the plot work even better than it already has, you're gonna have a good time with Wolfstride.I have been gifted this game by a friend, but I will definitely buy the OST and the Art collection, now that I have finished the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews often, but Wolfstride is, hard for me to describe. One the one hand it wants to be a visual novel lite, with rock'em sock'em robots thrown in. It has glaring issue that need to be buffed out, but from the discussion board it looks like mileage may vary. So I guess the good, Voice Acting is decent enough and the visuals do their part. There's a okay story in here, but sadly it is buried under the slow grind and pacing that it may turn a lot of people away.I want to add more positives, but so far that's about it. I will admit I haven't completed the game, but will do so. Once completed I'll come back to update if there's more to add. So there's a relationship system, that's fine and all, but it's increased through pineapples. Look I like pineapple and all, but if someone dumped as much pineapple as Shade does upon me I would get a restraining order on the man. To note, pineapples seem to be rare in the Wolfstride world and this dude is finding them left and right. I'd be questioning how he acquired them. Also, you get them out of a trash heap. Yes, there's Bounty's Hog Yard which is a trash yard. Shade is passing these out to people, the heck is wrong with this man. The big issue is pineapples are hard to get, but there are mini games that give them more than others. Which ties into the other issue I'll get into, but lets wrap up the relationship system. So each level you level up one of the many characters they'll give you useful items(sometimes). Though once you hit max level(level 7) that's it. I feel like the Persona games felt more rewarding, in Wolfstride it just end and is never brought up again. Like I just busted my butt to get you these rare fruits and once done that's it?So Pineapple god dude implores you and once done just throws you to the waste side. No thanks for helping spreading the magic of pineapple to the people. No reward from him once so ever. I like to tell this dude where to stick the pineapples. Anyway, the system become moot once each character is maxed out. Which I finish doing by like day 28. Which now we can talk briefly about the mini games.So certain locations have mini games and you can't get the highest rewards until you get certain items that help you do so. At least that what it should do, but the time and button sequence for the cat bathing game feels impossible to wash all 26 cats, even with the item upgrade you get. I'm sorry I don't use and Xbox controller and use a PS5, but it's kind of hard to press B when it's X on the PS5. Please have mutiple controller support. Yes, my memory suck and visual add would've help by having the button match the controller I'm using, but this is a personal issue. Though, the Dev could've made a little effort to have more then one controller supports for mapping.Then there's the BDSM bike mini game, now I couldn't even get more then just money from it. I couldn't get the first reward box even with all the upgrades. It's literately sitting a hair breath under the line for the first one. So unless there's more upgrades further down the road this mini game is also unable to get everything. The two that are by far the best are in Hog's Yard and with the upgrade very doable. Which I just focused on Junk hunt and Junk Mining for the time I was grinding for pineapples.Now here's the issue with the mini games, once you maxed out everyones level with pineapples, they become moot. Why? Because, you've gotten so much damn money you don't need to do them anymore. By this time I was take very little to no damage that even needing money to repair my bot became moot. I've bought or was given all the upgrade up to this point. Bought everything at Paradise Arcade. Bought Everything at the convenient store(with the rare exception it gets restocked for story purpose). I have over 150k+, why we need to do life risking robot battles again?So there's a VR game that allows you to have back to back robot battles and I got all the prizes at day 33. The only challenge I find completely RNG and unbalanced was Mongoose. Which will move into my next talking point, mech battles, but first, Fudge this fight. He literately gets like 3-4 attacks per turn, has an attack that can push you from one end to the other end of the arena squares, and undoes all your puny damage like you've done nothing at all. Oh, lets not forget the attack that allows him to speed from one end to the other after he knocks you back. How I beat him came down to sheer RNG and luck.So onto mech combat, you get AP(Action Points) and MP(Movement Points) the more MP you have over your opponent allows you to go first. So here's the balance issue I see, most of the opponents you fight have not only high damage with armor reduction, but it cost them as little as 1 AP to use. While most of you decent attack have high AP, High Ammo cost, poor range, cool downs, and crap damage. I'm sorry I'm barely do without moral boost with a 2AP, 2 Ammo, and cool down 40-60 damage and these guys are getting crazy attack that I don't see require any cool down and 1 AP for 45+. Maybe I suck at the combat system, but even when I do win I notice how garbage Knife Leopard's attack skills are. How in the heck has he managed anything. Even with all the skills bought up to the point I'm at(just now entering the underground), its been a slog. Not to mention you don't get enough recovery. I get maybe 1 recovery every other round, but my opponent has like 2-4 after just 1. How unbalanced is this? Like challenge is fine, but I feel so damn handicapped at times it makes me not want to complete the game. Yet, I expect the fights in the underground to be even more one-sided. I've read people complain it's, "Too easy and didn't even break a sweat." Well hold on there mister masochist who probably chews up and spits out Soul's games like they're childs play. Not ever gamer out there can be a dang perfect as you, okay. If you're so good why not tie one arm behind your back, blindfold yourself, and wear ear plugs. Maybe then games will sort of feel like a challenge. Seriously get tired of the, "Git Gud" attitude of people. I want to have fun playing a game, not be frustrated. If I want to deal with garbage I'll go outside and deal with real life.Anyway, sorry about that rant, but I know people on the internet will use that tired saying everytime someone has difficulty with a game. If the Dev makes another game like this I think having a challenge mode for those more interested in the story or heck, just having an issue beating a battle can change the difficulty. It's just sad to see game mechanics become moot. Area's at this point are empty and devoid of purpose, like the hospital. The location gets used once and it is never used again(to my current knowledge). The road that leads the hospital serves a little more purpose and there's a area you'll have cut scenes are and is used for the relationships, but beyond that; that's the only purpose it currently have. The Arcade is moot, which is sads as the Dev could've put possibly some mini games to win prizes, but it sole purpose, making money you don't need.The Crapyard(the S fell off) was cool, but ZZ generally loses her purpose, because you bought everything useful from her shop. Like, why do we need to get her every battle? Heck, I can't even pet the kitties, 26 cats and none pettable. Beyond an interesting story with helping her, I really having a hard time seeing why the main cast needs her. The general store has a Gacha machine, but beyond a box of information, no further interaction. Seriously, you put a Gacha machine in the game and I can't spend money on things? The heck is wrong with you. At least it give me some reason to come back to the general store over time. Anyway, guess I can't leave a though full review as I seem to hit a character limit for it. I hope the Dev fills in the world a little more in future games, the void and moot mechanics just leave things empty.

_childDocuments_.review: I try not to leave negative reviews. There's enough negativity to go around already. But after about 10 hours of Wolfstride, I think I'm ready to pack it in, and I'm really disappointed that I feel that way. I have a ridiculous amount of hours in BattleTech. And turn-based tactics games are my jam. You'd think a turn-based mech combat game would be perfect for me. And that's exactly what I thought I was getting when I played the Wolfstride demo. But the reality is that this game is more like a visual novel bloated with irritating characters, a needless story, and a collection of extraneous mini-games. It's almost as if the developers knew that there wasn't enough meat on the bones of the core gameplay and decided to punch it up with all kinds of other nonsense. The mech combat at the core of the game is solid, even if it gets extremely easy pretty quickly if you grind out expensive parts and pilot moves. And the visual style is exceptional. I have to give credit where it is due. But everything you're forced to engage with outside of the fights is just a slog, even if you attempt to skip every cutscene. 10 hours of entertainment for $15 is a pretty good deal, but considering the mech combat portion of the game was *maybe* a third of that, I can't recommend it. It's a real shame too. If there was more depth to the combat, and if it took center stage, the game could have been fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: The vibes of Wolfstride are immaculate, and there is some potentially delicious meat on the bones of its combat system, but the opening hours do a surprising amount to stop you from getting to the good part.The opening days of the game are extensive fetch quests, running along long empty roads to and from locations to characters that are an equal split of charming pastiches of classic anime characters, and some persistently unfunny characters that threaten to never stray from their 'bit'.There's a robot named 'Peepoo' with an intentionally screeching voice that replaces random words in their dialogue with 'pee' or 'poo' like a Smurf. They're also set up to be a persistent member of the main cast. This is probably 'the joke' of the character, but it's just not funny or pleasant, just loud.You do get a carrot dangled in front of you - introductory combats are fun and tactical and the next one feels like it's *just* around the corner, but there's more fetch quests and Peepoo to bear before you get there. I took a break from the game at the introduction of an Elite Four of characterful silhouettes that would have me Pokémon-playing, Tournament Arc-watching, No More Heroes-loving butt absolutely thrilled. But there was just no real guarantee that their writing would be any more engaging than Peepoo and I... just couldn't bring myself to come back to it.If you're an old-school anime fan with a taste for Rick & Morty or Family Guy at their more puerile moments you'll get along with Wolfstride solidly. I'd still recommend playing with the voice acting off.

_childDocuments_.review: "Wolfstride" is a RPG/Anime-Visual-Novel set in an alternative present where mech-fighting-sport is a thing. You take on the role of Dominic Shade - a former mobster - who got entangled in shady business and struggles with a ragtag cast of characters to get some cash and get even with their pasts. The game focuses heavily on storytelling and it delivers. The writing is consistent, sometimes good, even very good, but some jokes are hit and miss and things can drag into cringe-worthy territory (There are a LOT of pop-cultural references - to anime in general, "Cowboy Bepop" in particular, a lot of side notes to bands like "Ween" and "Beck" and serveral game franchises - some are implemented quite good, some not so well). The visual art and character design is top notch,  the pixel art still delivers, but is not that fleshed out in my opinion. Some places and scenes also feel empty and rushed, but the overall atmosphere manages to smooth this out. A big thumbs-up for the voice acting - almost everything is voiced and they did a great job! The game has a very slow pace in terms of gameplay: You socialize, prepare for the battles, are going places, talking to people and doing errands which are presented in mini-game-fashion (which can be offputting to some). There is also a lot of backtracking. The turn based mech-fights are fun, cinematic, original, strategic and intense, but the overall power progression and the balancing have a strange curve.Overall "Wolfstride" has its rough edges, but it is a quite unique experience and definetly a work of heart! A nice and hefty underdog package for everyone that likes a stylish piece of media!
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: Hold onto your pants because I have a review as usual my friends, so as usual I'll do my short version, Wolfstride is a game I heard was a slowburn and ya know what? It's half right, the gameplay takes a sec to get to the actual good parts and meat of the game itself but characters? Story? If you're a lover of these things you'll be eating out of this games hands like a half starved dog ready for a full course meal and a heavy petting session, as a whole it does it mostly right and has very few real issues, definitely nothing game breaking that's for sure dood.Okay ya'all here? Good so on the surface Wolfstride is a comedic RPG mecha battle game strewn with a few fun minigames here and there, some of which are hilarious but ironically as much as I came to enjoy the combat the game has a veeeery strong story element, the humour is on point but it also cuts deep, real deep and takes it to places even I didn't expect it to, it had me wanting more and it always delivered, lot's of fully voiced lines at that, very rare exceptions to that and quite the diverse cast I might add in terms of how they all sounded dood.So I talked about the story and I did it first which is rare for me, shows how much I appreciated it but now let's get onto the gameplay, you typically have an arena with varying amounts of space between you and the other mech, each panel can have + or - attacks on them and if you push them to the back you can deadlock them, allowing you to go to town on them in terms of damage but of course they too have this ability making it a real push of war at times doodEach mech has four key parts, the head, both arms and the chest, all of which can have an armour stat to decrease damage of incoming attacks and of which with the right attacks can shred that armour, arms account for damage but also your attacks in general so losing one will take away an attack you may have, head I believe accounts for AP this is what allows you to attack often and chest? Chest is your life blood, you get that destroyed? It's game over, off to the junkyard dood!Of course there's actually more parts than just those outside of combat and a variety of pieces you can equip to your mech, wanna be a long range specialist? Here's parts with more ammo and better ranged damage, wanna be a melee god? here's parts with more damage and armour, the games got ya covered, there are also parts to improve movement and AP so you can go back and forth around the field like nobodies business and push more than ever which helps because that costs two movement points dood.So about combat and why it's slow at the start, as the game progresses you learn more and more attacks and skills, both defensive and offensive, at the start? You uhhh are quite frankly pathetic and that's being extra nice, you're gonna be in for a rough ride, but between the shop, minigames and certain side things you can do you can qui-well in a reasonable time make your mech a God among mechs but here's the hitch, you keep unlocking things as you go along so it's hard to judge when the best time for that is, I grinded out a very specific item to get some super good stuff but honestly? I should have done some of it later when I had more attacks dood.That said the game is not all that hard of you get the right parts and play smart, the hardest thing to start is limitations but eventually you'll be able to make each fight seem almost too easy as long as you aren't dumb enough to try and be too fancy in your tactics, the game will definitely punish you for that and yet despite that it get's quite fun and tactical to play with some fun little visuals for the attacks dood.Bad things about the game? Let's see there's a lot of walking and that would be fine but the issue is you never know what may be new in an area or not, to the devs I suggest maybe markers in each area if something new is there to find or someone has something new to say, I always wanted to find all the things and not miss out on them but it meant a loooot of walking, by the way you usually go everywhere and the only things you may miss are jukebox discs, no achievement for that either, you're welcome lol and anything else is usually in such plain site you'll not miss it so feel free to concentrate on conversations or even events at times dood.Final words? This game is different and in a lot of good ways, both story wise and gameplay wise, the mechanics are surprisingly deep once you've unlocked everything and I'd love to see more games done like this, especially if they do one in the future with the end segment, that's as much of a spoil as you'll get from me on that ;) could they do more? What game can't do more? But what's here? Is a game I won't be forgetting anytime soon and I'd love to see the devs do more of these kinds of games, it doesn't even have to be mechs or the same world but as long as the storywriting is as good and they took on board all the good of the game I would play the heck out of a new game! (On that note in case the devs read a post game would be a good idea for all the new moves I never really got to use as much as I'd have liked for future games if you keep this formula) Thank you for reading and I hope you enjoy the game as much as I did dood! ^-^7

_childDocuments_.review: Wolfstride feels like it's an underrated gem, yet the reviews are very positive for it (this, of course, being another positive review to add to the pile).The gameplay is split into two parts: a No More Heroes-esk roam around the town and do odd jobs to get money to pay for mech parts and other items loop, and a turn based combat loop where each mech has (most of the time with a single-digit number of exceptions) four parts that allow the mech to do different kinds of offensive and/or defensive moves.What's kinda crazy is how the game melds 2d pixel art, really stylized non-2d art, and a (mostly) voice acted story with multiple characters (none of the voices are one person doing multiple voices from what I noticed).At first the story might not seem like it's worth seeing to the end, but it is.Oh, and choose the Black Door.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: When I came across this game, I had nothing to do, mentally hollow from my time in school and was just, overall in a bad mindset. Seeing the comments, about how it was too much walking, too much grinding, it made me, want to prove them wrong somehow, it was weird. I never heard of this game, never played much like it, but suddenly I wanted to defend it out of nowhere. But, I'm glad I did. I love this game to death, the stories are great, the dialouge is nice, all you need is pacing yourself to make sure you handle the story bit by bit.

The mech fights are very fun, beautifully animated, and sound so good.And hey, do yourself a favor: start stockpiling pineapples early. You'll thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: "What a piece of crap!"Story - absolutely fantasticArt direction - very goodEverything else - good to "wHy?"  As in: Why do the pineapple social links exist? Is it because Persona did it? Now is it? All it does is pad out playtime. Doesn't even give additional story content.  The previous point leads into the second one. Why are the minigames the only way to get half the damn pineapples or more? There are four of them and out of four of them only two are completed in reasonable time, making Hog your only helper on the grind. It still takes a stupid amount of time to complete, and you still have to pay attention the entire time. I wish I could just purchase pineapples 10k a pop.   And speaking of money, the aforementioned grind leaves you with heaps of cash so Why is arcade so damn pointless? You invest to get time-based income, but it is limited to 2k a day. Why??? You can make over 2k over 2 rounds of junk mining if you sell drops. So 2k are absolutely worthless.  Why do you need the pineapple grind if it ruins your monetary system, doesn't provide story content and demolishes story pacing for the completionists?   Mech combat is good, could be more dynamic, but the amount of changes that some fights provide is good enough.   Not nearly enough 1AP moves worth using, not enough moves that aren't a pain in the ass to set up, no melee armor breaking attacks which locks you into having to keep at least some gun attacks + reload.  Head is not worth going for most of the time.  Basement is disappointing despite providing the best parts, simply because it is so short and doesn't impact the story at all.  Also most mechs are missing one of their legs, and it would be fine if we were not able to see it, game devs don't need to draw things that the players can't see, but it is very clearly visible and distracting. Give Trinket and Killer their own game, it seems like what they were doing in the background was interesting enough.Recommended to everyone

_childDocuments_.review: This game has style, great music, a pretty interesting take on turn based combat, BUT my favorite part of this game was the fully voice acted Dialogue. Its a good time, especially for the price. But While I think it has some pretty high highs, there are some things I take issue with in this game. It's def not everyone.Main issues with the game are1. The economy is pretty much a joke since you can grind endlessly for money but there is not enough stuff to buy(also makes fights easy cause you can always get the best stuff if you grind for an hour or 2) 2. You have to walk around everywhere. Sometimes there is stuff to do besides Jobs to make money, but usually you just walk around for 8 screens for maybe some new Dialogue but no side quest progression. There being no fast travel is fine, but I wish there were markers that would tell you if things were happening at certain places. Kind of makes the game drag at times. and 3. SPOILERS:The story is kind of all over the place, and sometimes it feels like you didn't do something to get all the info you wanted on a topic. EX: There's a whole News Story about Oil and Alternative energy source found by russians. While its eluded too, the should be final boss (and best fight IMO) is instantly pushed to the side so this russian robot comes in and you cant even beat him.  For world building I guess? Regardless it put a sour taste in my mouth and may have ruined the game for me if It wasn't for the last story beat.

Storywise, it starts off strong and progressively gets worse as time goes on, but when I had already lost all hope, the plot turned things around at the last minute and gave me a candidate for best video game ending I have ever had the pleasure of witnessing.Also, the music is quite bangin' and the art is very stylish. _childDocuments_.name: Wolfstride

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty damn great, but horribly pacing in the beginning is basically catastrophic. Tip below to get past the beginnning then proper review.Tip: Just speedrun the first 10 days, do your tasks and all that and remember that the first 2 fights are plot fights instead of real ones, but just try and get to day 9 or 10 when the game opens up a lot more, cause that's when it starts to actually feel good instead of drag on, plus Junk Hunt gives plenty of money if you want to grind it, so don't worry at all about the biking minigame, and no from the start you can't make it to the end of the minigame.Note: I'm at end of act 3 of the game as of writing (having 24 hours in at that point isn't that showing of how long the game is. I just really liked the mech combat so did a ton of that, and did a lot of money grinding. That doesn't effect my discussion on the pacing though as most of my money grinding was after the first 10 days where the pacing is horrible)Now for the proper review: Art: Clearly its pretty incredible. Probably the best part of the game. It makes having to walk through many areas a lot better, and it definitely leaves a nice atmosphere. (but the game could still use fast travel past the inbetween streets)Characters: This is  so far to me the 2nd best part of the game. Early on the dialogue is pretty cringey with overreliance on basic swearing and toilet level humor. Especially the introduction of fifth member of the crew: , but with time the characters started to show more, and their personality really start to connect with you. There are side characters of clearly lesser importance but they can be fun and the main cast for the most part are really fun to hang out with and talk to. The game can also get really silly too, but when not using toilet level humor it can be really funny and charming.Music: It's pretty good I'd say. It may not always be my taste, but I can see people really liking it. I don't have the know how to go any deeper than that.Gameplay: Walking and Talking - it's pretty standard and alright. The biggest annoyance is that the character has a changing direction left or right bit of art that pauses instead of automatically taking them to the other direction. It just feels unnecessarily slow and is a bit annoying for the Junk Hunt mini game. The in-between streets while atmospheric and have some fun descriptions, can be grating to walk through after a while and no descriptions update. A fast travel would have been great after a few times through.Gameplay: Mech Combat - this part feels great. Sadly buying new parts doesn't give much aesthetic difference, but it's still quite fun seeing small changes when mixing and matching moves. You have only so many squares left or right to move your mech, and have to position yourself to correctly use your weapons and have as much bonus damage as possible, and leave your enemy with as little as possible. Good combinations, strategies, and some special items let you beat enemies definitely stronger than you from quite early in the story. From acts 2-3ish you can defeat even some of the stronger later game enemies if you plan and work through it right. Sometimes it can be annoying dealing with stuff you haven't seen before since there's nothing to prepare you for it other than just losing, but soon enough you've seen enough to prepare for fights ahead. I personally think of the fights are better thought of as puzzles with when you haven't bought a ton or gotten a ton of items, you may not have tons of wiggle room. and when fighting things above your intended level you definitely have to think it through. It's incredibly satisfying though to see a good plan come to fruition.Starting Pacing: Its utterly horrible. There's a reason that this game only has half of its people go through the first act, and that probably goes towards whoever structured the first 10 days or so. It feels very slow meeting everyone, the biking game when its the ONLY way to get money and you don't know how much stuff will cost later, and only slowly having more and more options of what to do around the city. Not to to even mention the 2nd fight of the game is also not one you're meant to win for basically no reason other than you didn't have the ability to buy upgrades to your mech, nor did you have the ability to helpfully get info on the mech and plan around what it could do. (BTW: Mech info when given to me is honestly pretty useless with how shallow it is. It gives you the barest idea on what's to come. Knowing their moves and maybe getting a round or two to see their opening movement from x or y position would actually make enemy info feel useful at all. Or even the first part of that at the very least.) It's like they thought people would be willing to sit through a persona intro length, without knowing how many people dislike their long intros already, and how those who do like it (like even me) know enough with previous games to know that what comes ahead is worth it. But for a new game like this? It practically kills it and it's pretty clear to see with the low rate of getting past chapter 1. Just speed past the first 10 or so days as fast as you can to get to the real good stuff.Once you're past that though you're past what I feel to be so far is the worst part of the game, and the great parts of it really start to show itself. This game is ABSOLUTELY worth it, but it really makes it hard to see it from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: Cant believe this isn't meta scored it deserves somewhere between 70 and 80. I prize this for the story line, characterisation and plot delivery. The art style and and turn based battle sequences are also very good, though ill avoid elaborating here for the sake of brevity. The main thing I want to mention is on the quality of the story and so on. The story revolves around misfit characters who have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up their lives and are now trapped in lively hood of scraping by, the main character shade has on openly troubled past that you're made aware pretty early on, and his past is given the proper attention it deserves. At first glance this game is humorous but underneath and especially when you get to the ending you realise that it covers very seriously the themes of suicide, life's hardship and the kind of general philosophical views that could be held by individuals contemplating suicide. The game will not have a dark and gloomy mood throughout most, so you will not realise this straight away. It will feel more like a faux-noir with slapstick and cheerful comedy. But that is precisely the brilliance of the game. The dialogue writing and the voice acting are both excellent and really pulls the whole thing together.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite interesting but unfortunately I can't recommend it. Pros:-Despite it being in black and white (for the most part) the characters are quite colorful. You get attached to them and want them to succeed.Cons:-The combat is poorly balanced. Even the final tournament was pretty easy-There's so many interesting plot points that could have been explored, but ultimately ends up going nowhere. This could have easily been avoided since there's a lot of "open" days throughout the game. Maybe they initially ran out of money and can correct this with DLC/updates.-The game relies to much on "and then things kinda happened" to push the main narrative along.-Due to a combination of the voice acting and writing, some of Shade's internal monologue is extremely pretentious and unnecessarily edgy. They went too hard on the tragic hero angle.-Why was the final mech fight with the Soviet even necessary? Previously the player had just fought the final boss that's been hyped up throughout the game. Then all of a sudden this guy shows up in an unwinnable fight. That's just bad story design.I know it seems like I listed a lot of Cons, and the game is definitely rough around the edges. It's still decently fun and very stylish. If you can get it on a deep sale then definitely go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is rather interesting, and if you are a fan of older styles of turned base combat with some giant robot flare, this is the game for you. The game itself is short, but packs in a lot of character development for the main cast. Though the combat is simple, some fights you do have to work out what moves is best in slot for the match up. (However, if you intend to do everything and get all that you can before the end of the main story, there is a way to cheese the fights, but I won't say how.) Simply put, this is an enjoyable game and I kind of would like to see more like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I learned of this game because I saw news that It'll come to the Switch. I purchased and binged the game since I got it. What I:-Loved is the non-pixelated art (like the mechs and character portraits). I have a bias to bold and thickly drawn art style. It's also noteworthy that almost all of the dialogue has good voice acting, which in my opinion, carried the game's narrative. Some dialogues are also funny, with some pop culture references added to the mix.-Likedis the combat. Though the animations tend to be repetitive at times.  The difficulty is a hit or miss IMO since I think I was able to focus in one style and it kinda carried me through the whole game. I only needed to upgrade parts if I find myself not being able to defeat enemies, so not much tactics were involved. I wish there were more animation and visual variety. -Hatedis that you needed to tediously walk ALL THE TIME if you want to go anywhere. In this game, you go through a menu to select a general area where you want to go, and walk 2 screens before you get to where you want. With the limited locations the game has, it's tedious to see the same scene time and time again, without anything happening. I don't see the reason why another menu was not used for it. While I don't pay attention to the story that much, the ending is kinda confusing as well.Summary:Game looks good with great ideas for it's game play. It's not the best game, but for the price I paid, I am satisfied. Should this get a sequel, it's probably a day-1 purchase for me. I totally agree with one of the reviews that said: “Wolfstride is an obvious labor of love that manages to be much more than the sum of its gameplay and presentation parts.”

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost: This game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocks. From it's aesthetic, to it's gameplay, to it's writing. Yes, there are some typos and grammatical errors in the text - That aside a lot of the writing doesn't feel forced,  and with it being 95% voiced,  this game proved to be an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gem.The story is great, from wacky moments - to /some/ cringe moments (Looking at the introduction to PeePoo) - to some genuinely unexpected twists and banging storytelling.If you have 15 dollars, buy this game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: To me, this is more of a Visual Novel than an RPG, and it's a fun ride if you're looking for a story. As the mech fights can devolve into a one-sided beatdown in your favor the moment you unlock some stuff. My biggest gripes are how time consuming traveling is, and how there's no indication for new dialogue in zones.If you're looking for an RPG experience, you're probably not going to find what you want here. But I truly feel the writing is what carries the experience, so if you're looking for a story, you might like what you get here.And for the love of God, don't try to unlock everything. The story is linear, grinding minigames for all the unlocks will not change the ending. Spending 1-2 minutes per minigame for a chance of getting an item to progress bonus unlocks is not worth your time when it doesn't affect the story.----I absolutely adore this game. I rock with the aesthetic, the writing is fun, and the voice acting really brought the script to life. To me, the game is more of a Visual Novel about mech fighting and the RPG is secondary to that. As in my playthrough, which had some early minigame grinding so I could see some unlocks, simply keeping your mech parts "up to date" and figuring out a rotation for combat resulted in the endgame fights being filler for the story.But of course, there are things that I didn't like. Like how there's no fast travel between the major zones, or anything that tells me that there's new dialog in an area (as I feel the writing is the big highlight of the game). When you're traveling around, a one-way trip is like this:1. Menu2. Area3. "Hallway"4. Arrive at your destination, NPC you're looking for might be on the complete other side of the areaSo if you're doing daily rounds to see if anybody has anything new to say, it takes a good couple minutes just running around. And at certain points, some characters either just repeat the same dialogue, or just have no dialogue whatsoever, making checking on them a waste of time. And in the endgame, if you're doing a certain side thing, it'll take you A LOT of walking just to repair your mech between fights.Also, the minigames are your primary source of Pineapples, which are used to improve your relations with certain characters, and unlock bonus items which make minigames easier, new moves, and parts. You honestly don't need to grind for too many, and I highly advise you don't. Either I can't figure out their drop rate, or my luck is just that bad.

_childDocuments_.review: This was genuinely a great game. Clearly influenced by Cowboy Bepop, FLCL, and Mecha anime. Shockingly great voice acting and extremely likable characters. The gameplay has its up and downs (the wandering around the city parts get repetitive ) with highlights being the mecha battles.The story kind of goes all over the place but that seems in keeping with how wacky everything is. Despite that, there is a central plot that deals with some serious issues that is genuinely touching.Overall a stellar game. I rarely have this much to say about games I play but this one really stood out.
