_childDocuments_.review: Aahh, Stray... The cat game everyone was waiting for!... I am going to keep this review like the game: Nice (not amazing!) and short.To start off, I enjoyed my time with it. In my opinion when it was over, it had just started overstaying its welcome, so the game's length is just perfect. I finished at around 7 hours with some achievement hunting but definitely not a completionist run.On the positive side, the game's of very high quality. With stylish visuals, great graphics, an awesome cyberpunk setting, interesting soundtrack and very good sound effects. It really is a charming project.On the neutral side, its story although interesting, is very cliche and predictable. There are some interesting touches throughout the story telling, but you really need to look for them, since almost all characters encountered are forgettable. I think that some of these aspects were done on purpose, and that's why I do not absolutely criticize the game for them. I just wish there were one or two interesting characters, since the basis with the cyberpunk setting is there. Also on the neutral side, the game's environments although very beautiful, feel a bit same-y and the grim-dark atmosphere gets a bit old. That being said, the environment fits the story perfectly, so I guess the story is to blame again.On the negative side now, I was very disappointed when I realized that the game is ALMOST a walking simulator. It is not a walking simulator, but the gameplay really is nothing interesting. Apart from some stealth-based areas and some light puzzle elements there is nothing more to it. The exploration aspect is too narrow, and the control over the cat's movement is very limited with Assassin's Creed inspired movement where every jump or interaction is a guaranteed success with a simple press of a button. I would love some cat platforming. And some combat... After about 3/4 of the game, I was really sick of JUST running around without much more to do. Granted, there are some extra buttons you can press, but they are nothing special and also feel very limited. I think this lack of real gameplay mechanics is due to the developers' focus on the cat part of the game. Ok, yeah, controlling a cat is interesting, cute etc etc, but still, some gameplay elements are needed in order to make Stray really shine!I loved everything about the game, mainly except for its gameplay. Or rather lack of. If the gameplay was meatier and less movement-limiting with some combat mechanics, Stray would have been amazing. Now it's just decent.6/10A recommended game for its interesting world and main protagonist but still, I don't think that anyone would really lose anything but skipping on this one. I hope a sequel will address my issues and prove to be a real masterpiece. Until then, I kind of feel disappointed with Stray.

_childDocuments_.review: Estimated 100% Completion time: 10-15 hours (Multiple playthroughs)Perhaps my favourite Indie game of the year so far. With this in mind, I have faith that Studio B12 will iron these small bugs out in time.While it would have been nice if the game was a tiny bit longer, what I got from the game I would describe as high quality, not only with the gameplay and controls, but the visual aesthetic and design of the world too.While I completed Stray, there were two playthroughs done, one at a leasurely pace, gathering all collectables, and one sub 2-hour speedrun. _childDocuments_.review: Still on the fence about the meow meow game? Cos hey it'll just be some gimmick for toxoplasmosis YouTubers and their catlady like-smashers, right? Cutesy meme crap that won't stack up against the chest-high wall of Proper Gaming?Hold up then, because you might well enjoy this one more than you'd think. I'm not gonna tell you Stray's perfect or anything adjacent. But there's more here than meets the tapetum lucidum.Cats' eyes glint like that when the light hits them because they've got a reflective layer at the back. It blurs the image a little but gives them a second bite at the light on its way back. Subtle and acute, yet somehow hazy, this shadowy trade-off seems emblematic of cats. The best way I can explain the bright heights Stray hits at its best is through chiaroscuro. This game:How can Stray be that good when there's so much wrong with it? These aren't things you can just hotfix out. The fundamentals of its gameplay are deeply flawed and there is a tentative lack of confidence to much of the game that maybe trudges along beside innovation. But Stray is also a fiercely intelligent game that develops timely and unorthodox themes with a subtle bravery that's worthy of its protagonist. Without rubbing your nose in its cleverness, Stray considers how humans, absent yet hauntingly present in its apocalyptic setting, remain entangled to the end with their environment, and asks what would be left of us without our companions and works on Earth. Cats emerge from the shadows as indivisible elements of who we were and will be, with a gentle suggestion: somehow, through all those terabytes of papyrus and digital video we devoted to them, we underestimated them all along.Stray is a game that finds hope in the utter desolation we're facing. It's a game that communicates remarkably complex ideas about co-evolution, mutual influence and the transmission of memory, and does that best when it's not using dialogue at all. It's a game with a cool reference to Another World on the Amiga, and it's even pretty damn fun in a nerve-shredding way towards the end.In conclusion, this game is important as hell and deserves to stand as an inspiration. Meow meow.

_childDocuments_.review: "Stray" is a captivating 3D platformer that blends elements of stealth and combat, where players control a cat navigating a world designed for everything but feline exploration. Divided into 12 chapters, the game alternates between linear platforming, action sequences, safe hub areas, light stealth, and combat segments. The simple yet serviceable plot revolves around an alley cat guided by a robot companion, B-12, through a city filled with decommissioned robots and menacing creatures. As players progress, they learn more about the world, its factions, and the quest to reunite with the protagonist's litter.The game's visual prowess, characterized by impressive graphics, textures, lighting, and atmospheric effects, is highlighted by the lifelike animation of the cat and expertly crafted environments. The city is moody and immersive, with hub areas offering vibrant visuals and a minimalistic HUD that adds to the overall appeal. Interactivity is a standout feature, with nearly every object in the environment being interactable, contributing to the believability of the game world.Despite visual excellence, the camera's proximity to the action and the intrusive interaction indicators slightly detract from the experience. The sound department falls short compared to the visuals, with unremarkable ambient music for most levels. However, the Slums area stands out with groovy tunes, showcasing the potential for music to enhance the gaming experience. Sound effects, particularly those associated with the cat and the environment, receive praise for their high fidelity.Stray's movement mechanics shine, offering fluid and natural controls that make exploration enjoyable. The game encourages finding routes through the world rather than relying on timing or precise jumps. The three hub areas—Slums, Antvillage, and Midtown—are rich in content, quests, characters, and exploration opportunities. Linear levels introduce new mechanics, but combat and stealth segments, while present, receive mixed reviews, with the latter feeling awkward due to limited tools and movement capabilities.The diegetic navigation system, relying on lighting and signs instead of traditional markers, enhances immersion. While the game's narrative is not its strongest suit, the overall experience is positive, reflected in its overwhelmingly positive rating on Steam. Stray's appeal lies in its next-gen graphics, the embodiment of a cat's perspective, engaging platforming, and well-crafted open areas. Despite occasional missteps in combat and stealth, the game's strengths, including great music in certain areas, make it a short yet replayable gem.

_childDocuments_.review: I too got tricked by the overwhelmingly positive rating, which i would have liked to award the game with, too - if it actually stuck to its strengths. This is a game that seems to be afraid of it's core ideas, and bafflingly, seems to completely abandon them in exchange for a smorgasbord of shallow story beats, one-dimensional dialogue, linear gameplay where characters just tell you to go somewhere, non-relatable, poorly written characters and jumping from mediocre gameplay system to gameplay system. Unlike the titular cat, it never seems to find its footing.When I started the game I fell in love with the quaint, simple atmosphere of being a cat together with its chosen family, just surviving in the wilderness. That the wilderness seemed to be post-apocalyptic was not relevant to the plot at all, and I believe it should have remained this way. It should not be relevant for a cat at all what the story of its surroundings is, since it cannot make sense of these human concepts and ultimately does not need to. It was the definition of a coherent in-universe "show don't tell", that captures a player's imagination but does not make the environment part of the story, which was focused on the cat itself and the struggles of everyday life. All of this was completely believable, too.But this lasts about 10 minutes. As soon as you get used to the tone, the setting, the artful indirect storytelling, some director decided to press the remix button and all of this gets thrown out of the window, together with your feline crew. The tone completely shifts and little by little, you are not the protagonist anymore. At some point, you are relegated to being a bystander, while your sidekick character gets the limelight. It is actually kind of funny how little trust the developers seemed to have in their own protagonist that its sidekick takes the center stage for the longer duration of the game. You are merely a vessel for it. Soon, every one of your actions will be dictated by this sidekick character and its own motivations, killing the agency and importance you feel as a player. You feel like a puppet with all of your carefully kindled motivation from the first 10 minutes of the game replaced with "go here, do that, because I want to".In games, narrative motivation is important. Games feel most powerful to me when the motivation of the player is shared with the main character. This game replaces the initial, powerful, emotional motivation to reunite with your crew with a player-focused, human motivation to understand the world and figure out the plot. Because it would not make sense for a cat to wonder about all of these things, they needed to insert a sidekick character. And it completely takes over. The core motivational concepts are so at odds with each other that it just left me confused and irritated.I could go on about the generic gameplay, but for players like myself, if the underlying motivation is not coherent, this tanks the experience unlike any bad gameplay system could.Maybe it dawned on them that they could not pull off a game that is solely focused on a believable cat experience and needed to introduce more conventional story elements that related to the human player. I would just have pulled the plug at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this little hit. Who knew gaming as a cat would be so refreshing, gaming mechanics lend so well to the control and overall feel of playing as a cat. _childDocuments_.review: Could have been a great game - instead it is a game with great sections, ruined by designers who decided they had to add some 'peril' to attract the sort of people who like to say "get good" to any criticism.The slum section is amazing, and could/should have been extended to include more puzzle solving/exploring, but apparently every modern game requires sections where button mashing is required to proceed, with literally seconds between the exact right move and death.The zurks sections are poorly implemented and almost unplayable on PC - with no consistency in what stops them from attacking, or how high they can jump when they decide to.No doubt there are gamers who are happy to play those sections because they are bored with  the slow pace of the rest of the game, or who like the challenge of beating an unfair set of rules.As an older gamer with poor touch sensitivity in my fingers, it just feels to me that the designers made a choice to deliberately ruin my experience at occasional points during the game, purely to shoehorn in something for the action fans (or perhaps the trailers).If it had been an action game and my cat had claws and could fight back, that might have been fun. Even better, if there had been a sneak/puzzle option OR a run and fight option, then everyone could have been pleased - instead it tries to be in parts a nice casual exploration/puzzle game, and in parts a fast paced 'action game' - and fails to stitch them together in any coherent way.Still enjoyable, but only worth getting on sale at £10-15 IMO unless you like the action bits and won't get bored with the slower pace of the good parts.

_childDocuments_.review: dfijgpifrwoqwkfojwfdjckqdmfvoinqdvuqwopnmcdokmvopkfnvmojpkvmcodfvmpfmvfsklmvmosjkvdfsajdsnfndjlnfjsnnmcnnwuiouwtjiopjfadpoiafkaopi...So, come on, shoo from the keyboard! I'm terribly sorry... What am I talking about? And yes, Stray!The action of Stray takes place in the distant future. While walking with his moustached companions, a stray red cat falls into the sewer and finds himself in an underground cyberpunk city where there have been no people for a long time.Humanity destroyed the planet's ecosystem and tried to hide in bunkers supplied with oxygen with the help of a new kind of plants that do not require the sun. But in vain. People died out, and only robots remained in their settlements, who built their own kind of society, where many consider the blue sky on old photographs to be fake.However, to arrange a real revolution in this underground world and return the sun to its inhabitants, one very brave cat is enough. And he will definitely need courage here: after all, the sewer is teeming with mutant parasites, devouring both flesh and metal with great speed.I'm sure Stray will disappoint many. For someone, it will be too simple. Too short for someone. For some, it's too quest-based (in the first hub, you'll have to sweat a little with mini—missions). And you won't find a deep cyberpunk plot here - after all, the main character is not some smoky detective with implants, but a red—haired cat.But the most important thing about Stray is how it is made with love. It's very hard not to get into it. I have no doubt that this quiet summer the game will become a hit, and the Annapurna Interactive publishing house will once again record a bright and original project in its portfolio.1. Perhaps this is the most feline game in history. The fluffy main character is made with great love.2. Amazing art design and music.3. Well-tested gameplay: the puzzles are logical and do not cause stupor, the locations are well readable, none of the mechanics are annoying or boring by the end.4. Excellent implementation of DualSense: the player feels the strumming of keys in the cat's teeth, the friction of wool and claws digging into carpets and curtains.5. Murrrrrrrr.1. There is not enough photomode, but at least the interface does not interfere with taking screenshots.2. Not all carpets can be torn and not all puddles can be drunk. Shhh, shhh.A game that is not a pity to spend time on and which will 100 percent appeal to all cat lovers.Rating 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: What a magnificent game, I highly recommend buying this and giving it a try. The cat was cute, the story was banging. If you are having doubts on whether to buy this or not stop because your doubts are ridiculous. You get to play as a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cat and roam around cyberpunk themed areas AS A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CAT. I'm not even talking about a humanoid cat or some special version of a cat I mean a full blown cat. What is there not to like? If you're saying "Obviously you get to play as a cat why are being so redundant." well my answer to you is this. You. Get. To. Play. As. A. Cat. That is all there is to it. Now on a serious note, I personally thought this game was very well made. Very well made graphics, well thought out story, and inventive ways to interact with the environment. It was a rather short game all things considered, but I think the length of the game was worth it considering the fact that they fleshed out the environment so widely. There were some minor glitches and some animations I wasn't too fond of, but all in all those didn't ruin the absolutely riveting experience of cat adventures that were to be had. It is a nice and simple game owing to the small amount of controls available and the not very complex mechanics. But I appreciate the simpleness of this as I see this as a well done story game with a focus on characters and the interactions leading to the grand finale. All in all I will most likely come back to play again and get all of the achievements and I believe as I have said that if you want to get this game you should do it.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray is in essence a cat simulator but with a full story packed in. You play as an unnamed ginger tabby (cat) that (within the first 5-10 minutes) gets separated from all your cat buddies after you fall into a large sewer drain. The over-arching story is just you trying to get back to the surface and mingle with your feline friends again.. As you continue your adventure you soon realise there is much more under the surface (literally and figuratively) than meets the eye. The whole gameplay experience was very relaxing and relatively easy to 100% (the one exception being the "" achievement which seems to require a lot more luck than skill to achieve). Overall though, my experience was brilliant, really hoping they make a sequel.8/10 Gameplay7/10 Story9/10 Graphics (I cranked them all to maximum)9/10 Performance8/10 Overall

_childDocuments_.review: It is with the most certainty I have ever had that I say this is the greatest game I have ever played in my life. The main character, of course, is the best I've ever played as. The other characters you meet along the way are all charming and excellently written. The world of Stray makes you feel like you are right inside it. It feels alive, with so many different characters all with their own personality, and entire swaths of this world to explore. The controls and movement are also the best I've ever had the pleasure of using, making me feel like a parkour professional as I leapt and bounded across this charmingly dystopian yet oddly hopeful universe. The ending made me openly weep, attracting the concerned attention of multiple family members. I cannot recommend this game enough, this review would be longer than the Bible if I tried to explain how much I love this game. I highly recommend you step into the paws of the little Outsider, and open the sky.

_childDocuments_.review: Hugged my puppy and teared up after playing this amazing masterpiece.Stray is an adventure game developed by BlueTwelve Studio and published by Annapurna Interactive.Gameplay: 9/10The best cat game I've ever played. The controls feel very fluent. There have been a small amount of bugs I encountered on my first playthrough, but nothing game changing/breaking like most Triple A games. You traverse whole cities and towns with nothing but your paws, a friend you meet in the game, and the most important feature in my opinion: the Meow button. The parkour in the game is pretty accurate, reminds me a lot of how Assassins Creed handles parkour, that's a good thing. You sneak, push things off and scratch furniture, like a normal cat, but the game actually rewards you for doing it, like turning on a switch by standing on it, scratching a clothrag down to open a drawer to reach a roof or ceiling. The game rewards you for exploration in the most cat-like methods possible. I also love the cute mechanics of scratching carpets, sleeping in beds, doing cat things, etc, there's definitely some boop-on-the-nose mechanics, and it brings out humour and joy.Visuals: 8/10Great looking game, most of the animations look realistic, and the environments are breathtaking and detailed.Story: 8.5/10From Wikipedia: "The story follows a stray cat who falls into a walled city populated by robots, machines, and mutant bacteria, and sets out to return to the surface with the help of a drone companion, B-12. The player traverses the game world by leaping across platforms and climbing up obstacles, and can interact with the environment to open new paths. Using B-12, they can store items found throughout the world and hack into technology to solve puzzles. Throughout the game, the player must evade the antagonistic Zurks and Sentinels, which attempt to kill them." A simple, yet effective story.Overall: 9/10Stray is a cute, fun and heartfelt story with the best cat gameplay I've ever experienced. Absolutely worth getting.

A game pad is REQUIRED. Mashing buttons is no fun for slow people like me. ESAD.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of cats, robots and dystopian scifi stories, I enjoyed this game greatly. The robot characters with their personalities and funny dialogue and all the details around the Walled City were enhancing. The story where the dark truth was revealed little by little kept me playing even through the parts where the bit clumsy gameplay and lack of savepoints made me repeat the same part a bit too many times. Overall the game was not too difficult nor too easy, but if you are looking for a good action game this is probably not the best match. But if you are looking for a cool and interesting story, well built atmosphere and a game where you can jump around as a cat (and do other random cat like stuff like dropping mugs, destroying sofas and just sleeping on random pillows), this is definitely worth using the 10 to 15 hours it will take to finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 4 hours in as of now. I'm bored. I was only interested in the concept of a game that lets me control something other than a human or vehicle. You control a cat, with very limited actions. You can use contextual prompts to jump on certain objects and you do so for the entirety of the game. Imagine playing Mirror's Edge but you installed a mod that lets you play as a cat. You will find that cats are vastly inferior to humans. I've seen people refer to open world action games as "Walking Simulators", well...this isn't open world or action and it is the best representation of a walking simulator I've ever found.I don't regret the purchase because 30 bucks is whatever, and I am certain I've spent far more on far worse products. That being said I will pay close attention and care to avoid purchasing from this developer in the future. There is nothing wrong with the game in and of itself. It is my opinion that the experience is dull, predictable and unengaging. This is the kind of game that you can watch someone else play and receive the same experience as having played it yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: What a profoundly whimsical protagonist!  What a beautifully poignant and meaningful setting!  What a wonderfully and intentionally haphazard yet utterly intriguing story!  Literally what can possibly be to complain about in a game with all these things going for it?Oh right, it is an adventure game, so it still kind of sucks to play at times.  Kitty controls just fine, honestly, even with the keyboard (and I have heard the game is easier with a controller); that is not the issue.  The issue is how I want to claw my eyes out when wandering past the same set of NPCs and buildings for the tenth time trying to remember which random hallway held the single hard-to-find element I need to access to get to the next segment of the game.The other issue is that the developers for some reason thought this largely stunning and wonderful adventure game needed some segments that objectively ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucked, so they decided to create the Zurks.  Actually, the Zurks being in the game, like basically everything else about the setting, is awesome, and I love them as story pieces.  I would love watching the movie adaptation of this game.  But I absolutely hated every second the game made me spend interacting with them.  At least 2 hours of my playtime has to be repeating the same three or four segments over and over again (or walking away from my computer to have a snack or something just to try to bring myself to be willing to face those segments again).  And the annoyance is not even linear; just when you think you have a handle on how to deal with the Zurks, the game throws a curveball and has the ones you previously got rid of respawn BEHIND YOU when you die and pop back up now in the middle of a room completely packed with enemies instead of totally cleared out.  Why did Annapurna Interactive hire a sadist to work on the cat game?  Was that just their way of giggling and knowing they were increasing the playtime of the game significantly through no actual storytelling effort?Whatever.  This game is still so great overall that I cannot possibly disingenuously give it a thumbs down, but just be aware that unless you get off on checkpoint-style games where you often have no defense against a horde of enemies that this game will not quite be the purely good-hearted exploration of whimsical themes that we all (or maybe just I???) expected.  But it is still extremely worth playing.  Just maybe consider watching a walkthrough if you are in danger of putting your keyboard through your monitor in rage.

_childDocuments_.review: Geniusyou play as a cat in a robot kowloon walled city, and its as engaging as it sounds. the design heavily relies on the familiarity of a cat. by using a realistic pet to ground the rest of the very alien, futuristic story in realism, it gives emotional impact you will struggle to find anywhere else. when the cat is in danger you feel intensely worried, and when its calm you feel calm. call it immersion, call it empathy. whatever it is the game manages to tell a story through emotion and text alone far better than anything else on the market.the gameplay complements the story and stands on its own. essentially imagine a platformer but with a cat (descriptive i know). the gameplay team clearly trusted the competence of the visual design team because it provides complete freedom to go anywhere, and yet the visual ques guide you seamlessly to where the story is at. you can spend 30 minutes in a segment or 5 hours and both will provide an equally enriching experience. a PC game that respects both your brain and your time is becoming increasingly harder to find and its a breath of fresh air to be able to trust that aspect of it. the movement is 3 dimensional and creates some fascinating puzzles. it rides the silver line of allowing my monkey brain to pick up on the clues but letting you feel like a genius for figuring it out. the enemies are intimidating and synergise with the puzzles well. its clear that this game was a team effort and every aspect feeds into the other.as i said with the emotional impact, the story has all the right calling cards of a great odessy. it has mystery, philisophical subjects to think about, relatability, good pacing and infrastructure for major plot points such as memory fragments. objects, paintings on walls, even the npc's themselves to reinforce the twists and turns. sounds insane coming from a game about a cat doesnt it?the game has doom eternal level optimisation. if your setup is from after 2010 you can play this at its full potential. no memory leaks, prominent glitches or crashes to speak of, though i believe the linear zone then free zone design of this game made its optimisation inevtiably goodwith money behind my words i can say that this game is well priced too and would highly reccomend buying it at full price. you wont get gameplay hours out of this like you would with a god of war or cyberpunk game, but thats ok because its not priced as such. for the money you spend its certainly the best in its league, and one of the top ten games ever for story and memorability.stray is a case study in a deeply layered game cloaked in simplicity. it will keep you invested from the start into the end and you will most likely struggle to put it down. innovation is an ugly process but when handled correctly it evidently creates true beauty. well played bluetwelve studio.

_childDocuments_.review: As with most of Annapurna's titles, a charming little game that works from a simple concept: You are a cat. Just an ordinary cat, albeit one with a vaunted intelligence that some owners like to attribute to their pets. And this works very well, possibly because through this simple platform you can experience the rich and immersive sci-fi/cyberpunk world that has been delightfully constructed and filled with small details (like two robots playing mahjong in a picturesque little ramshackle town deep in the underbelly of the game world). It's a bleak world without being too dark and serious, and the robotic denizens give a great sense of levity, in their interactions with each other and the protagonist, primarily through their pixelated facial expressions. And the game encourages you to stop and play, leaning into the concept of the cat protagonist - giving you the ability to bat things off of shelves, scratch carpets and doors, and even giving you a dedicated meow button that I admit I used far more than I should have.Typically the gameplay switches between platforming elements and simple puzzle solving, the different areas and challenges of the game are different enough to keep this feeling fresh throughout, and despite the simple concepts driving the game I felt like it was varied enough to keep me entertained throughout the duration of my playthrough.It's a short-ish game, so this is something to bear in mind. I took my time with my playthough, tried to find collectables, explored quite extensively, and at one point left my protagonist sleeping on a pillow while I went to get something to eat, and my overall playtime was just under 8 hours. This felt about right in terms of length - some games tend towards tedium if they're overstretched. I'm sure that at some point I'll revisit the game in the future, if nothing else just due to its atmosphere and the unique concept that it was built upon.All in all I would highly recommend this title. Especially if, like me, you enjoyed other Annapurna games.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray is a game whose idea is much better than the implementation. If you just see "cyberpunk" and "cats" and buy the game - like I did - you might be expecting something a bit more than than this is. This isn't Deus Ex seen through the eyes of a street kittie. This is more of a janky indie linear narrative that features elements of better games and doesn't really nail any of them.The controls are the first thing you'll notice sucking. For a cat, you move very clumsily. The things you are are allowed to jump on are very limited and only appear as jumpable on certain angles, which makes navigating an exercise in futzing around with the camera till the magical jump icon appears. So you think you're gonna get parkour, but it's parkour minus the joyous, free movement of Mirror's Edge.Then you think maybe you're gonna get a relaxing walking sim, which you do get for about 10 minutes, until suddenly you are chased by swarms of facehuggers that hatch from glowing eggs AND KILL YOU. Yes, this game features death mechanics and checkpoints. No difficulty slider as far as I can determine, so you just have to die and repeat and die and repeat until you eventually pick the path with the least aliens and make it to another checkpoint. Extremely frustrating. I almost rage quit a couple of times.Later in the game you pick up a weapon that allows you fight back, but that turns it into even more of a gross-out, ultra-violent splatter-fest than it already was. Weird. Then you clear the bugs and get the obligatory stealth game section, hiding or running from drones THAT KILL YOU. And because the controls are so twitchy, all of these die and repeat sections are far more irritating than they should be.Meanwhile the story is sweet but predictable. You're not walking around a heavily-populated cyberpunk city. It's just two or three neighborhoods in an empty post-apocalypse world with a handful of characters in each one. There are a couple of meaningless collectables, but mostly you're just following signs to fetch the next item and unlock the next door. There is no big reveal, no character arcs, you know exactly what is going to happen from the start.And probably if I'd read some of the reviews before blindly buying because "cats" and "cyberpunk" I would've had lower expectations. Or maybe not, since the reviews are mostly meme reviews that don't tell you anything about the actual game. It's not a bad game. It's fine. It's passable. But is it worth the price? There are cheaper indie games and cheaper classic GOTYs that provide a better story, better parkour, better stealth, better everything... except you don't get to be a cat. So unless you really, really want to be a cat, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to take the time to write a review about the game itself, rather than focus on the fact that the main character is a carnivorous quadruped stray cat (even though it is incredibly cool). Stray does something with the indie genre that makes it stand out from the rest of the genre's games. You, for one, play as a cat, and despite being a furry friend, you still retain the human element as you traverse through the game, for obvious reasons. The slummy landscape somehow appears beautiful to the player, and each and every corner is a puzzle waiting to be solved. What is this mysterious place, and how did it come to be this way? Stray has an artistic beauty that trumps even the most well-developed indie titles in the genre, and in conjunction with the fascinating story, the player may feel as though they are living through a heroic poem. You don't quite understand the need to open up the underground city, but you feel that it is the only thing you must do. Personally, this title is one of the few games I wish I could replay without having memory of ever playing it before. Try it out and you'll know what I mean.

_childDocuments_.review: Saying the word "cyberpunk" is already an effective way to get the internet to wet its collective pants, but these fools had to go and throw a cat into the premise as well.It should be said first that this game is an audio/visual triumph, which makes its tragically underwhelming aspects all the more apparent. Stray is absolutely worth playing, just understand that Stray isn’t as talented or inventive with its gameplay as it is with its presentation.And while we're addressing upfront biases, your overall attachment to cats will have a major effect on how you engage with the game. It's fair to say that being less of a cat-person reduced my investment in the story or whatever motives this indifferent protagonist has. Also, the realistically rendered cat behaviors weren’t as adorable as they needed to be to justify their consistent reuse.Surprisingly, there is a limited amount of novelty that comes with exploring the remains of human civilization from the perspective of a cat. Your comparative size doesn’t have much of a memorable effect on traversal beyond scenarios such as circumventing doors by hopping through windows instead. As for the challenge presented by the scale of the world, leaping around is more automated than Assassin’s Creed’s parkour. The controls are great, it just seems as if a lot of the fun and complexity has been taken out of the fantasy of being an agile cat with a tendency to get to places they shouldn’t be.Fetch quests and terribly generic stealth segments featuring inconsiderate checkpoints don’t belong in such an otherwise competent game. Compared to the effort that went into the presentation of Stray, these moments come across as creatively bankrupt bottom-of-the-barrel filler designed to meet a quota for the conventional gameplay that’s required to keep streamers awake.For as counterintuitively boring as it is to leap between boxes and outrun headcrabs in Stray, the ever-present atmosphere that accompanies you on your journey makes getting through the game completely worth it. The lighting that seeps over the desolate junkyard of a future highlights the chaotically intricate messes of trash, graffiti, and sludge in an expert fashion. In Stray, the mechanical life that's filled in for the absence of humans and animals is extremely well developed. The music that accompanies the locations you visit ranges from gorgeously immersive to exotically robotic, all within a superb variety of emotional contexts that adaptly reinforce the safety or danger of a given scene. The soundtrack can also be ridiculously catchy and there are a lot of strong uses of diegetic audio as well.Stray is an internally simple game with fantastic external attributes. Stray is at its best when it’s focused on being silent, eerie, and beautiful. Even though an abundance of dialogue and frustratingly game-y portions get in the way of what the game does best, I would by no means take back any of the time I spent with Stray.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty great game, with just a few flaws. I avoided looking into this game since I knew I was going to buy it and I was expecting a game where you played AS a cat rather than one where you just LOOK like a cat. It's kind of weird talking to people and doing normal puzzle game stuff as a creature that shouldn't rightly know how to do any of it. That's not one of the flaws, it's just funny to think about as you play. "Oh, you want me to take this key, go through this house and open the door for you from the other side? Buddy, I'm a cat. Freaking meow.".The main issue I had was the erratic auto-save. The game auto-saves on triggers which are sometimes often but other times are few and far between so you might want to quit but you're stuck playing until the game saves since there's no way to do so manually. In the Slums you can hold onto music sheets because giving one to the robot that wants them triggers an auto-save but the rest of the game can be problematic, especially Midtown. When I got to Midtown, I talked to a TON of people, I found a few memories, I did a quest to get an item and not once did it save. I wanted to quit the game but had to play another 30 minutes before finally triggering an auto-save. Kind of annoying.Other than that, though, everything is pretty great. The visuals, the cat animations, the music and the story are all really well done. The puzzles are all pretty simple and straight-forward, more like speed bumps than roadblocks, but that's fine. The game has a pretty chill atmosphere and rich environments so it's enough to just explore around. Overall, fantastic game. I enjoyed my time with it. Check it out if you love cats. >=3

_childDocuments_.review: I have two cats of my own so the general idea of a cat game, a brand new one nun the less, certainly intrigued me. I figured it would be a nice chill game away from my normal taste and a way to relate with my furry friends. Stray delivered that and so much more... The game so well executed what being a cat entails from splashing around in puddles to chasing around butterflies to even knocking things off tables. But beyond that, Stray delivers a story that is fresh, entertaining, and even a little sad. It's the perfect cocktail of serotonin and sadness that draws you in and keeps you longing for what there is to come in each and every adventure you partake in. I highly recommend you give this game a try whether your a cat owner yourself, or someone just looking to find something new to play, Although it wasn't what I initially portrayed the game to be, it was a pleasant surprise, one I definitely recommend experiencing yourself. Who knows, maybe you'll find yourself acquiring a furry friend of your own come the conclusion of the game. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: When I went into the game, all I really knew was you play as a cat and that there's robots. A game where you play as a cat is really all I needed to know to believe I'd enjoy it since I always absolutely love when games make the player character an animal. I loved the Spyro games, I loved Okami, I loved Twilight Princess, and as a kid I played any game I could find where that was the case.That being said, while I likely would have enjoyed the game for that alone since the controls feel pretty good and the experience was solid, the narrative elements really shine through as well. This game is instantly a favorite of mine. I don't usually achievement hunt for a game unless it's really special to me, but as soon as I completed the main story I turned around and set out to get it added to my perfect games list only because I wanted it to be clear I loved it so much.If you think even for a moment that playing as a kitty in a game may appeal to you, then absolutely get this whenever you can. I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray is a great adventure game, doubly so for cat lovers!  The animations are delightful, and both the story and gameplay make good use of cat behaviors and quirks.  Initially, I was wary of the extremely scripted controls but quickly came to love them as they allowed the cat to appear graceful and kept the difficulty low enough to be approachable to a wide audience.  The story is quite short but well-constructed; I enjoyed how the style and architecture of the different areas connected to the plot and worked to keep me invested all the way to the end.  I would highly recommend Stray as a fun weekend game to play on your couch - it is beautiful and immersive, but straightforward and short enough to complete in only a few sittings.Overall Rating: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Lost, alone and separated from family, a stray cat must untangle an ancient mystery to escape a long-forgotten cybercity and find the way home. Stray is a third-person cat adventure game set amidst the detailed neon-lit alleys of a decaying cybercity and the murky environments of its seedy underbelly.  See the world through the eyes of a stray and interact with the environment in playful ways. Stray is developed by BlueTwelve Studio, a small team from south of France mostly made of cats and a handful of humans.

name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story
detailed_description: Two best friends, one wild adventure. Join best friends Nunu and Willump on an adventure across the frozen wilds of the Freljord. Discover the unbreakable bond between boy and yeti as you traverse a land both beautiful and treacherous, making new allies (and enemies) on a journey of family, friendship, and magic. Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story is a single-player story adventure developed by Tequila Works. Dive headfirst into an immersive narrative set in the undiscovered reaches of the Freljord, where every snowy step brings you closer to the truth about Nunu and Willump’s past. FORGE AN UNBREAKABLE BOND Play as Nunu, a young boy searching for his mother with the help of his best friend, Willump. United by their endless imagination and shared love of snowball fights, the two will have to work together to navigate the Freljord, saving it—and each other—from the danger that lies within. UNLOCK AN EXTRAORDINARY WORLD Hike, climb, and sled your way across the Freljord, a frostbitten land full of harsh blizzards, ferocious wolves… and enchantment. Use your head to progress through the frozen landscape and uncover what secrets lie hidden beneath the ice. JOIN LEGENDARY CHAMPIONS Meet the powerful League of Legends champions of the Freljord, including Braum, Ornn, Volibear, and Lissandra—whose twisted magic threatens to bury the world in Dark Ice. Friendship finds a way in Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story.

_childDocuments_.review: (Never played League and didn't know freljord/nunu lore.)Great story and fun gameplay. It really gets the "Boy and Animal Companion/Imaginary Friend" trope right. Gameplay feels like a classic 3d platformer, with the visuals and general design multiple steps above in terms of polish.  Price is a little high considering it's only ~5-7hrs, but the polish, effort, and certainly the music are there. You're also able to replay it to get all the collectibles (as well as achievement hunt), which I'll probably do in a year or two when the story is less fresh. The VA for Nunu really made it work. I thought it was an adult woman at first, considering the quality of the VA and the amount of lines Nunu has. I will say when his voice cracks with emotion during some of the scenes you might as well stick my heart in an industrial blender. _childDocuments_.review: At its heart, Song of Nunu  is a joyous celebration of friendship between Willump (the Yeti) and the child Nunu (Notai clan).  Through thick and thin, the two unlikely companions have snowball competitions; play the flute and dance together; go on nail-biting sled rides and meet some amazing characters as they search for Nunu's mother in the icy realm of Freljord.  They support and encourage one another when the chips were down and bravely fought off ice wolves as a well-oiled team.  It was such a heartwarming and enjoyable romp to experience! Willump the yeti is such a goofball character who pulls funny faces, loves to eat berries and mushrooms and goes on strike when he's had enough.  You are able to hug him!   He becomes grumpy later in the game, but you soon find out why.  Willump is also a nifty dancer!  Who knew that yetis could dance?!Nunu is a young boy searching for his mother and the Heart of the Blue.  This is really a coming of age for him as he discovers what true courage is and how size really doesn't matter.  The downside of his character was that he talked too much and he had a really whiny voice which drove me nuts at times!The graphics in this game are really lovely and I often stopped and had a look around me.  I loved the blue ice theme throughout the game. The music was divine and was heavily flute based due to gameplay using the flute to open doors or activate slides.  Depending on the circumstances, the music emphasised the action taking place.Gameplay was platform heavy, but quite easy with some puzzle sequences.  There is combat involved and that can be frustrating for less dexterous people (more on that later).  There are cute little poros to find on each level and intricate murals to discover.  Most of the characters you meet are really well defined and believable and you have to battle a couple of them.  The most difficult part is remembering the flute notes you have to play and hitting the right keys in sequence.  This is a major part of Nunu's character as was throwing snowballs.Now, I am not the most dexterous of people, but I was delighted to see how accessible this game is for peeps like me.  In the accessibility section you can fiddle with things that make the battles easier whereby you don't lose life.  This god mode makes it easier on the sled sections too.  So for those who are hopeless at combat or have to play on keyboard like me,  this game is very forgiving in battles.I guess this is a game suitable for kids 8 and over.  The wolves and other characters are probably the scary part but there is no blood and gore.  Be aware that this is not a God of War game, but an enjoyable adventure of a boy and his friend.  Combat and gameplay are simple and can be repetitive at times....some reviewers found it boring. Most people completed this game in 5- 10 hours, but it is really not meant to be rushed through, but to savour every moment and explore every nook and cranny of this vast world.  Highly recommend..9/10  I'm heading back now to pick up my missing poros!

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed almost everything released by Tequila Works and was not let down by Song of Nunu. It has similar themes to RIME and GYLT.. a child who has suffered a loss embarks on a journey into a spirit-filled world to find answers. This game is more 'cartoonish' than RIME, with more animated cut scenes. Nunu is a small boy who is searching for his mother's spirit and a "Heart of Blue" magical item. He is accompanied by Willump - a blue comical Yeti with four arms (who knew... I assumed that Yetis were two-armed creatures!).Song of Nunu is best played with a controller. You are armed with snowballs to throw and a flute to play. I found the musical sections too hard to coordinate with the keyboard/mouse. You control Nunu directly and, at times, Willump (when he carries Nunu). The two work together to solve problems and overcome obstacles.The path is fairly linear and there is no time spent wandering, wondering what to do next. There are different areas/chapters to explore with some sub-quests that lead you to the main quest. No fluffy errands to run and almost no inventory to manage.... just a complicated landscape to navigate with many obstacles. The puzzle elements focus on how to use the environment and your powers to move along. The art is beautiful and the soundtrack is fantastic. The voice-overs are professionally done and fit the characters quite well.Although there is a good bit of platforming, it does not require precision and I missed very few jumps (which is unusual for me). Some sequences involve figuring out the timing of your actions and then executing your plan, with perfection. These situations usually took me a few tries to get things right. The combat was tough for me. Although this is not the focus of the game, there were enough assaults by wolves and magic creature to keep me on my toes. There is a boss fight at the end that, for me, was brutal. Achievements are fair. Once you have finished the game, you can return to individual chapters to find missed collectibles or complete unfinished tasks. This makes up for the single auto-save slot that does not allow you to go backwards while playing the first time through.I highly recommend this to those who enjoy a heart-warming adventure and don't mind working out puzzle timing and engaging with enemies. It is a wonderful adventure but a bit tough if your reflexes aren't quick and you aren't comfortable with attacking/evading under pressure.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been told that the heart is the strongest muscle, and by the gods does this game have a mighty heart! If you ever wondered what a “My Neighbor Totoro: Norse edition” would look like, this is pretty much spot on!Song of Nunu is a quirky puzzle platformer in the BanjoKazooie variety where you have 2 colorful main characters that work as a team to overcome the Freljordian wilderness in a quest to find the legendary heart of the blue. On their way they rescue poros, wrestle with wildlife and share a stew with a mustachioed gentleman of the highest order. This game is a pretty chill (hehu) and simple game and the story is lighthearted and genuinely cozy. Coming from a rerun of Dark Souls this game was like the antithesis of the soulslike formula that has become so popular and I actually loved it. The exploration was there, but minimal, the story melancholic and beautiful like an aurora and most importantly the characters are as they should be, larger than life! If you have lived under a rock for the past 15 years, and somehow missed the sensational show Arcane (Go watch it! Now!), you might realize that this game's story takes place on Runeterra, the world of League of Legends. However, having finished the game from start to finish I can gladly say that you need not bother with endless lore videos explaining the various factions and weird historical happenings, the game stands sturdy on its own legs and leads you into the Freljord and its inhabitants with a playfulness that is truly captivating. Also way to go to not turn Lissandra into a cardboard cutout saturday morning cartoon villain!Every now and then you come upon a game that really resonates with you and from now on I am really interested to see where this story goes! This game is easy, so do not expect a harsh and unfriendly freljordian dark souls to beat the life out of you. However what it lacks in bite it sure makes up for with heart, and if you have any love for a great and cozy story this is as good as it gets. Highly recommended, even if you can't stand the LOL from where it came!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute beautiful game to experience and play.  The colors and music just draw you in.  The relationship with Willump and Nunu is adorable. It was almost like when you finish watching a great series and you are almost part of the movie or equate this to a good novel that you wish would never end.

_childDocuments_.review: where do i even begin? this game was SO COOL (pun intended)!i have been waiting for this game ever since it was announced, nunu and willump are my favorites... despite not playing league of legends itself, i'm happy i got to experience their story. ^^anyway, onto reviewing it... it definitely is a quick game, someone could probably finish this within a day, i finished it for ten hours in the span of two days. so you might wanna think whether you want to buy it on full price or on sale based on the time you wanna get from the game, but there are achievements that may be missing so there's that to consider (depending on if you wanna collect it).the gameplay was simple, easy to understand and a casual gamer can easily get the hang of it (especially since the controls are slowly revealed to you and not just shoved into your face immediately). the puzzles were fun (in my opinion) and i didn't need to look up tutorials for any of it! there are some that you might get stumped at... but there just might be a third secret solution you haven't thought about...! ;)as much as i would love to talk about the art style and animation, i fear i had to run it on low graphics because of my laptop, however, it really suited the game and its story, befitting for the characters of nunu and willump.now, the soundtrack... definitely is one of the best parts of the game, i might be a little biased since i love fantasy music (and flutes). ever since i first heard nunu and willump's theme from league of legends, i've wanted to hear even more! and this game absolutely did not disappoint, i smile everytime i recognize their theme from the main game. :)also, i cried, like, twice! it was a bunch of little tears here and there, but it really warms your heart at the end. i also really LOVE the song choice for the ending, put a smile on my face immediately and sang the lyrics word for word. this game... I LOVE IT!!i wouldn't go as far as to say it's perfect, but it is in my heart! man, this is more of a rant than a review... but if reviews are meant to let you know what the product is like, this one works, either way... i had fun with the game! :Dhere's to hoping for a sequel!! i have a flute, which makes this even more fun.anyway, if you're even the slightest bit interested in the game... try it! if you do get it but don't like it... you can always refund, in fact, within the timeframe you can refund- i'm sure the game can be completed as long as you speedrun it. XDand that's all, i hope we see more of nunu and willump's adventures. :]

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I wanted to say: I loved this game.I play League of Legends since 2009 and despite my love-hate relationship with that game always I wanted something that tells me the story of the characters.Song of Nunu did just that. I know, arguements could be made that it's a childish game or it's just too straight forward and there is nothing at stake, but that is not what I wanted out of this game. I wanted a beautiful story with characters that I learnt to love due to League of Legends. And that it did achieve. The game isn't very challenging, but I don't think it was meant to be that. It gives you gameplay along with a beautiful story and a gorgeous world.I can't say for certain that you will enjoy this game if you haven't played League before, but I can only recommend this game.Sadly we won't be seeing games like this again since Riot Forge doesn't exist anymore because big companies are more focused on making the most amount money instead of putting their heart into a game.This game definitely gets a recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games where one wishes for something between thumb up and down. Very cute and just engaging enough that I'll probably play it through. But...as far as I can tell this was made for Nintendo Switch and then a half baked PC port put on Steam. Which is more than a bit cheeky with a 30 euro price tag.Particular annoyances, all of which seems to be symptoms of a poor port for PC/keyboard and mouse:1. No ultrawide resolutions, you have to edit a config file to not have a stretched image.2. Camera sensitivity comes maxed by default and is garbage, requires far too much movement of the mouse. Can be fixed by editing the config file. Changing from 100 to about 700 feels about right to me.3. Annoying camera that frequently locks in direction and/or changes FOV, presumably a cinematography thing, but mostly just irritating on something bigger than a Switch.Below are details for the config file fixes.File location: %localappdata%\SongOfNunu\Saved\Config\Windows\GameUserSettings.iniResolution, set to your preferred resolution (can force higher resolutions, but not ultrawide, you will have black bars on each side of the screen):LastUserConfirmedResolutionSizeX=3840LastUserConfirmedResolutionSizeY=1600DesiredScreenWidth=3840DesiredScreenHeight=1600LastUserConfirmedDesiredScreenWidth=3840LastUserConfirmedDesiredScreenHeight=1600Camera sentitivity:CameraSensitivity=700

_childDocuments_.review: Yup, Song of Nunu was great. A surprisingly cozy and enjoyable experience. The game's visuals have this charming simplicity that feels like stepping into a laid-back Disney movie. The characters are cute, and the overall design radiates a familiar, almost PS2 platform-ey atmosphere. Very easygoing gameplay – straightforward and doesn't overwhelm you with complex mechanics. It's the kind of game you can kick back and relax with, perfect for a casual gaming session. If you're into low-key, feel-good adventures, Song of Nunu should be right up your alley.I'd recommend playing through it all in a long sitting if you have the time some weekend. Wouldn't have wanted to split it up. 6 hours flew by.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute, visually impressive, and thoughtfully made game. Riot outdid themselves! All the attention to detail that's included really enhances the experience-- Willump and Nunu playing and bantering as you explore, the lowered POV from Nunu, Wilumps AI making it seem like he's genuinely there and with you. The gameplay consists of simple puzzles, easy platforming, and the occasional fighting which is not too violent/challenging. You meet various other Freljord characters and learn their lore along with your own. It's a good time.I love it and would definitely recommend buying even if you don't play League of Legends.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little game with an adorable protagonist and en even more adorable furry companion. Even if you aren't a League of Legends player (I am not), there is so much charm to enjoy here!While this is a solid recommend in my mind, I must temper expectations. Song of Nunu is not meant to be a complex, challenging game. It is meant to be a simple, laid-back game whose primary objective is to make you smile and root for Nunu (And this it does very well). The combat is pretty light with not too much variety in enemy types, however there is a pretty cool boss-fight at the end.The epilogue alludes to a potential sequel, but this unfortunately will never see the light of day. "Tequila Works" the developers of this wonderful game have been shut down by their parent company, "Riot Forge" as a part of massive layoffs at Riot. I hope these amazing devs have since found work in other studios. I wish we could have seen more games of this sort featuring the rich and varied lore of League of Legends characters, but alas, this does not seem to be on the cards.

_childDocuments_.review: Can confidently give Song of Nunu a well deserved 'Meh'. Stylistically it is what I expected from this studio, but I also think that it greatly misses the mark on target audience. Being the 'disney pixar' adaptation of the Freljord means it struggles to maintain the themes of the Lol universe, the overall tone is remarkable juvenile. There is a ton of hand holding throughout the entire game, and not much is left up to interpretation. Nunu himself is unfortunately portrayed as a very cringey and annoying kid. All of the other characters end up being remarkably one dimensional. I think Song of Nunu tries to be too many things at once and overall lacks a clear direction. The game doesn't give itself enough time to fully explore all that it is trying to offer in the way of telling a story in a densely lore rich universe. While you don't HAVE to be a league player to understand Song of Nunu, I don't think the game can really stand on its own. The 'wow' factor of this game depends a lot on knowing who the characters are. Apart from these issues, the controls and gameplay are clunky, the combat is satisfying briefly before it becomes a side note. Puzzles are beyond easy to solve. The game itself isn't long enough of an experience to warrant paying full price. All of that being said the game isn't terrible. It is a charming adventure filled with all of the positive things you can expect from an animated movie. Certainly worth picking up on sale and spending an afternoon/evening with. I think as long as this is approached with realistic expectations it can be a good time!
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare now a days to see a game committed to being fun. Most aim for mechanical depth, or stretching the limits of what the average computer can do. But Song Of Nunu is different. There is combat, but no skill tree or leveling system. There is stealth sections, but no advanced acrobatics or silent takedowns. Instead the game is focused on telling a genuinely heartwarming story set in an interesting world with love-able characters. It speaks to the perfection of the atmosphere that this game is the highest rated Riot forge game despite being the shortest. This game is fun, and you will have fun. It is simply a heartwarming tale of about a boy and his yeti.
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: An innocent lovely game which definetly worths a playthrough.  It is around 7 hours of gameplay with cutscenes to get to the end so the initial asking price looks a bit hefty. I'd recommend to wait for a sale if you not too keen to try it out right away. For any league lore fan it's a must play.Pros.-art style is awesome-characters are lovely, fluffy and full of life-children were in consideration, they can play this easily and happily-Cool puzzles because you use ice..-Cameo of fan favorite League champs-Snowball fight-Lovely lore setpieces-Willump MVP-Didn't really encounter any significant bugCon-Short, doesn't really have replay value-Combat feels a bit clunky sometimes-Some cutscenes have some wierd animation glitches-More enjoyable in short bursts than in long gaming session (Subjective ^-^)TL.DR: Good game I am recommending it, for league lore fans it's a must play!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just happy that League of Legends is branching out with its characters.Since I saw the announcement of this game, I have wanted it so badly. I was already aware of these characters even before their rework in League of Legends (they looked so ugly lmao). After they polished the old version, I loved what they did with them.The art style is one of the biggest ones for me. It's so pretty, like an actual story book or animation movie. Seeing Willump just do its own thing was very charming.I would've loved if it had a 2-player mode where player 1 could be Nunu and player 2 Willump to solve puzzles together, something like Cereza and the lost demon, but instead it focuses more on story telling, character interactions and cinematic than gameplay mechanics.It's a relaxing game where you just follow the road and see what happens. There is some combat here and there, but nothing too crazy.My minor gripes: I'm not a big fan of achievements in this type of game, and it holds your hand a bit too much sometimes, like you can't move the camera on your own.Like others have already pointed out, the game is rather short and a bit pricey, but can you put a price on hugging your best fluffy yeti friend? Jokes aside, I purchased for 20%, which I think was a more favorable price for me. It's really a personal preference, if you are able to afford it, of course.Length =/= Price - It's the experience that counts for me, and I couldn't be happier that I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Please brace yourselves because this is going to be a little long. To set the scene, I will state that this was right after my first League account got permanently suspended because of abusing an in-game bug when I was young and stupid. After losing my account, I felt that I no longer had any drive to play League despite it being one of my favorite games. I made a new League account because my friends encouraged me to do so, and I went through the long and arduous process of finding a new main for this account. I started playing a lot of Singed, thinking that he could be my calling, but deep inside, it didn't feel right. My friend Kraidden decided to tell me about his experience playing Nunu (this was back then before his rework). I laughed and thought that he looked funny and that I should give him a shot. I played and played him and felt like I was happy again because I had found a champion that was made for me.He gets reworked, and my joy for him only grows larger. I got to the point where I would even draw milestones for every 100k I accomplished with him (I still do this to this day). Everything about this champion brings me joy because I know that no matter what can be happening, seeing his interactions with his best friend is the purest and most beautiful thing in the entire world. Every skin he gets, I buy whenever it is released, and whenever I get a chance to get merchandise that could even somewhat relate to him, I don't even hesitate until Riot Forge announces that they would be making a game ON MY FAVORITE CHAMPION.I was ecstatic; there were no words to describe just how thrilled I was to experience Nunu and Willump without even touching League of Legends, and although I had to wait a long time to get the game because of delays, I do understand that they were for the better and that the finished product was everything I ever wanted and more. The day that the collector's edition got dropped, I remember taking a total of 5 minutes to complete my purchase and just count the days until the release.The game had absolutely everything; it has a great story, a great adventure, and even a greater friend that can accompany you along the way. I constantly found myself smiling at the interactions that the duo had with themselves and with other characters. This game just perfectly encapsulated what it is to have a friendship transcend to the point of brotherhood.I cannot recommend this game any more than I already have, and all that's left for me to do is to tell you to purchase it whenever you can and to have a blast."Every adventure is better with a friend!" (Willump noises) *laughs*

_childDocuments_.review: Song of Nunu is a great little game that brings the world of league to life in 3d for the first time. The story is well done, doesn't overstay its welcome, and the mechanics are tight and feel good. Willump is a great companion and feels natural in the world, I spent a lot of my time just watching him exist and interact with the world. There's also a dedicated hug button, so 10/10.If anyone knows Leagues lore, there will be a bunch of easter eggs however you will notice that there's some very simplified elements and versions of the over all lore the way the story is told, however it's not done poorly. It's comparable to telling League Lore as a children's story, which effectively is how the story is conveyed. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, just an observation.The game acts almost as a pilot project for future 3d League games and does progress Nunu and Willumps story and lore forward, in an effective manner.
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely beautiful and heartwarming game. Song of Nunu expands on the bits and pieces of lore we had gotten so far and does so spectacularly. The number of references to the bigger universe, the songs and melodies of both new and old and most importantly the themes of friendship and family at the core of its story are all presented wonderfully. I would strongly encourage anyone who is considering the game to give it a chance, it will undoubtedly warm your heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Song of Nunu is the latest in a series of spinoffs from the highly successful League of Legends. Like the rest, the goal is to expand the world and characters while also appealing to an entirely new audience. As you progress you’ll encounter a variety of puzzles. These are generally solved by either throwing snowballs at various environmental weak points, or through the use of Nunu’s flute.I would highly recommend playing this game on controller for a smoother experience especially with the camera. Even at max speed, the mouse movement for it is pretty bad. If you're looking to get all the achievements you are better off doing it in your first one b/c going back post game will require you to play the entire chapter until you reach the point where you need to perform the task. If you could select checkpoints within each chapter then it would be more ideal but that is not the case. A good tactic to max out their playtime. Would recommend but ideally if you can score it on sale like I did. If the game was open world such as Jedi Survivor then I may have a different opinion but who knows. Perhaps the next League Story.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun, the lore is interesting, and the relationship between the boy and his yeti is beautiful. It's a cozy romp through the snowfilled valleys and fjords of the Freljord, and you get to meet some interesting characters. The combat is... wel... it's there. It doesn't really add anything to the overall experience, other than reminding you the Freljord is a scary place at times, and something's not quite right. If you're looking for exciting combat encounters that will get your heart pumping, this is not it. But that's okay. The puzzles are mostly fun and interesting, although Nunu is a little trigger happy with his advices "I think we need to move that over there!" Yeah, that's great buddy, but you could've at least given me time to guess before you blurted out the answer. Some of the more intricate puzzles rely too heavily on precise timing and/or placement of the player character, so much so that I thought I had it wrong. You all know the feeling "but I'm doing the thing, why won't it open?!", and then you do it again and again and suddenly it works.The flute mechanic is nice, and a cool nod to Ocarina of Time, but Song of Nunu doesn't use it as much or as creatively as I hoped and expected. I was excited the first time I unlocked a "New Song Stansa", which turned out to not do anyting. It's just a piece of lore. Nice lore, but I expected some kind of new power up. The game also feels a tad too short.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ – PLAYSTYLE★★★★★ – ART★★★★★ – MUSIC/SOUNDS★★★★☆ – DOABLE ACHIEVEMENTSSong of Nunu: A League of Legends Story invites players into the rich universe of League of Legends, this time following the adventurous journey of Nunu and Willump. Even for those unfamiliar with League lore, this game offers a captivating narrative set in the Freljord, introducing familiar League characters and unraveling an emotionally engaging tale.As the young boy Nunu accompanied by the endearing yeti Willump, players explore, solve puzzles, engage in snowball fights, and uncover hidden collectibles. While the controls, especially on a controller, generally feel intuitive, occasional challenges with ledge interactions might arise. Or perhaps I just suck at catching onto the ledges...The visual presentation of the icy Freljord is stunning, boasting vibrant flora and fauna that breathe life into the otherwise frigid landscape. The attention to detail in character animation, especially with Nunu and Willump's expressions and interactions, adds depth to the emotional storytelling. Watching Willump's antics and the heartwarming ability to let them hug adds an endearing touch. The accompanying music, featuring familiar League themes, beautifully complements the gameplay.For achievement hunters, Song of Nunu is generous. Most achievements align with the story or collecting aspects of the game. The chapter selection post-completion assists in tracking collectibles, eliminating the need for a full replay, though completing entire chapters might still be necessary for missed objectives towards the end.Overall, Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story delivers a compelling adventure with a captivating narrative, breathtaking visuals, and a gameplay experience that resonates with both League enthusiasts and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Song of Nunu is a game that can be enjoyed by just about anyone, even by people who have little to no knowledge of League in general. _childDocuments_.review: So I finished the game and at all it's a really good game. LoL players will get an awesome experience and I think also non LoL players can have their fun, but I think tbh there are better ones(Kena for example). In this game there are many background informations about the lore which is awesome for LoL players but people who don' play LoL will sometimes miss the connection. Anyway:-Story: It's super nice to play another LoL adventure story and the duo of Nunu and Willump is really cool. Their interactions with each other(you can cuddle with Willump!), their talks and teamwork is nice to see and enjoyable. You also meet some other LoL characters which is also nice since I think some aren't needed for the main story but who cares. They don't drag the story and are a cool addition to the game. Also you get some nice background informations about the characters and find some easter eggs.  The end was kinda sobering- not in a bad way, I just expected a more completed "ending". The epilog after the credits opened up the possibilty for a continuation so we'll have to wait what RIOT will do with it. -Voice acting: I played it in german and I'm happy that they got all the VA of LoL for this game. Hope the other languages did that aswell. 10/10 for me.-Graphic: It's a simple graphic style, reminded me bit of Kena but it's not the same. I honstely wished it would have bit more detail. You can jump through some plants(no hitbox) but on the other hand the gras will move with you when you go through it. At all it's fine in my eyes, but bit more polishing on the details on some objects would have been better. I sometimes had frame drops- always only for not even a second, but more than 15 times, guess the game loaded something but it's not a Tlou or Red Dead Redempion which high quality graphics and texures so I can't really understand how that can happen. I also had some weird camera shifts of 90° which happened out of nowhere sometimes. Nothing game breaking but it takes you out of the game :/-World: The world is just awesome. You visit many different locations which all have their own charm. You visit ship graveyards, frozen battlefields, a garden out of icefigures, the Howling Abyss and much more. You can find Poro's, Elnukhs and Golems and play your flute whenever you want- you get an achievement when u play the flute for some Elnukhs. by the way sometimes taking a quick break lets Willump interact with the world. He does a painting, fishes, builds a little snow figures ect. so don't rush forward, you maybe skip that. The game has it's focus on the puzzles and they are really well made. Often you have to take out your flute and play different notes to solve them and I never felt bored by it. You can also take your flute out all the time and play your own melodies if you want. Sometimes you activate a song and I wished they would have been longer. All of them are over in like 10-20 seconds T_T. At all I'm happy that you do mich with that feature. The puzzles itself are not complicated but I think you will often hit your head, because you're such a dummy. Ah, there are also iceslides and damn are they fun. Would have been cooler you could slide on them with more speed but they did their part. -Fighting: Yes there is fighting, not that much but when it comes to battling some wolfes you have your fun. You can do combos of light and heave attacks- all with their own animations and I beg you: Please do a finisher move when you can. Besides the healing you get the finishing moves are just awesome. Think there are around 6(I maybe haven't seen all) and also the big wolfes have their own finisher so DO THEM DAMN IT! Sadly there are no real bossfights except the one in the final(and maybe some other midgame but it's not really a fight). There are also 3 snowball fights against Willump and I warn you, that guy "cheats" in the last one. Also Nunu's introductions to the snowball fights are cool. Kinda when you start a round of Tekken or some fighting game. Still the fighting isn't the main part.Conclusion: You get a cool experience and if you're into LoL and into the lore aswell you should really play this game. It's a good experience and you can see more of Braum, like hey, it's Braum(sadly no Poros with mustaches). For people who has nothing to do with LoL I would say don't. There are many other games which have a story, puzzles and fighting in it(like Kena). I finished the game with finding all secrets(finding lost Poros and paintings) in around 8 hours and with that I come to the biggest contra in my eyes: 30€ for that game is too much. 15€/20€ would fit this game with it's content much better. 30€ just isn't really justified.     7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Great short story in a style I can best describe as a combination of The Last Guardian and Brothers A Tale Of Two Sons, but set in the LoL Universe.
