_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, as an avid reader of most of the lore content Riot has put out and an especially big fan of the Freljord in particular so do note my bias, this is the game Riot Forge was made to put out.Very polished, very beautifully styled, very heartwarming.Song of Nunu delivered in every single way I could have ever wanted it to for exploring both the lore of Runeterra that we know and bringing new concepts and ideas to it. I could only hope for any subsequent Riot Forge game to even be HALF as good as this to make me happy.Every character you know from League of Legends is as accurate (in terms of their personality and actions) as they could be with the main duo Nunu & Willump looking absolutely perfect (this goes for most of the supporting cast of known characters too) but there IS something I'd like to delve into regarding the design choices for certain characters.Spoilers for Song of Nunu begin here:This game features two rather radically different designs from the source material belonging to the two brother demi-gods Ornn and Volibear. Ornn dons heavy armour and features body and hair almost entirely volcanic and akin to molten rock which is well in a way a departure from his typical look (very fluffy!) but I feel as if it helps heighten his connection to his forge and the look of Hearth-home itself in this game (VERY metal, VERY volcanic - it separates him from the typical look of the Freljord you see in this game and amplifies the feeling of meeting someone truly ancient, from a time now so far gone). The Volibear, then, is the one I personally found more interesting and (approaching the game) worrying at face value. This is my main and a BIG reason as to why I actually bought this game but I found myself concerned when I saw the music video featuring him in far different attire (attire at all, even) but I loved the way the game tied in this new and brutal look. The jagged bone spikes replacing his typical azure blue, the scars ripping across his shoulder and the horrid skull on the other, the fierce and fiery orange eyes plus the gnarly yellow teeth all link well to a Volibear who is waiting and regaining his power. He does not have the capacity to maintain full fur, the sense of divinity in his glowing runes and polished metal embellishings across his braids and partial remnants of armour stripped away without stripping him of his pride or fearsome bear look. It is a look, I believe, that sells the idea of a "weakened" Volibear far better than what we saw described in Silence of the Damned or with the "Thousand-Pierced Bear" (which is a design effectively reused for large Ursine in this game, I do not mind this).Thanks to everyone at Tequila Works and Riot Forge for producing, what is well in a way, my favourite glimpse into Runeterra we've ever been given.

_childDocuments_.review: A very heartwarming game, although a bit short for the price. I would recommend this game if you are interested in this universe, but I would suggest waiting for it to go on sale for $20-25 if you don't really care about the universe it takes place in.The game stays true to the Runeterra universe, and you can genuinely sense the developers' dedication to this game. This is evident in everything from the presentation, amusing achievements, captivating interactions between characters, varied Easter eggs for both hardcore fans and the general audience, and informative lore about the universe, among other things.The gameplay is straightforward, and the puzzles never take too long to figure out. The controls are manageable, although it's clear they were optimized with a controller in mind. Using a keyboard and mouse may lead to some frustrating situations during platforming, but it's nothing severe enough to make you rage-quit. Respawn times are quick, and you won't be set back too far from your original jump point.

_childDocuments_.review: Riot Forge is back at it again! And this time, they've teamed up with Tequila Works to develop and release Song of Nunu, a whimsical, puzzle-platformer with aspects of exploration along with a lovely, yet short story.I am an avid League of Legends player, mostly a support player, but I like to dabble in the other lanes sometimes! Unfortunately, I'm also  at League of Legends, so lots of champions go over my head. So when dabbling in jungle, it was tricky to pick the right champion to fill the role. Some champions are a bit too tricky, while some are incredibly boring. Enter Nunu and Willump.The duo was originally released in February 21st 2009, being one of the first champions to be added to the roster. Just like League before, all the visual and lore reworks, they had faces only a mother could love. But eventually, on August 29th 2018, they fully reworked and relaunched Nunu and Willump, completely redesigning the duo into what we know today. They are, without a doubt, one of the best champion reworks, in my opinion. Building a lovable duo that's full of child-like wonder and joy, while still being able to fit into the harsh province that is the Freljord. They are one of my favorite picks for the jungle, given their utility, crowd control and flexibility. Also, it's just fun to roll up a big snowball and go careening into an unsuspecting lane. Nunu and Willump is such an enjoyable jungler, I even have fun if I'm losing. TLDR; I love Nunu and Willump to death.Anyway, when Riot announced a game all about Nunu and Willump, I was ecstatic. I followed the development of Song of Nunu, rewatched the teaser clips over and over again. And finally, the game was released and...I didn't buy it. I didn't buy it until a few days ago, life just got in the way and I just didn't have time. And I am now regretting not buying it on launch day, because it was such a wonderful little game. I finished it in about four sessions and it was one of the most joyous experiences I have had playing a video game.    ❄️ - The style is stunning. It's unique and stylized enough to stand out among other games like it.❄️ - The story, while short, is full of enough whimsy, magic and heartbreak to keep you attached.❄️ - I very rarely experienced bugs or glitches. And any I did see didn't take away from the experience, or couldn't be solved by a simple "restart from last checkpoint."❄️ - League fans, rejoice! Not only is there Nunu and Willump, but also  ❄️ - Stellar voice acting, especially Nunu's voice actor. You can hear the genuine joy in his voice, along with the heartbreak when it matters. Not only that, a few characters' original voice actors reprise their roles.❄️ - The music, oh lord, the music. It's top notch.❄️ - This kind of relates to the last point, but when playing notes on Nunu's Svellsongur, there are notes that aren't even used, but the team still put them in, which adds a ton of possibilities to play random songs.❄️ - According to the teasers for the game, Tequila Works really wanted to capture the friendship between the Boy and his Yeti, and they nailed it. There are small little details, such as looking at each other when near one another, having a secret handshake celebration after a few puzzles and the hugs...oh god the hugs. You can hold a button while you're near Willump to give him a big ol' hug, and when on Willump, you can hold the same button to give him head scratches. It's canonical in the League of Legends lore that Willump is the best hugger in all of Runeterra, and they really showed that here.❄️ - While off Willump, he interacts with the environment by eating little critters, making snowmen, scratching his back against walls and rocks, smelling flowers or even flopping down for a little rest. It's a lovely little touch that gives makes the world feel like part of the story, and not just a background to walk around in.❄️ - The ending, and the credits song (despite the fact I have listened to said song well before this game's release) made me ugly cry. Not because I was sad, but because I was happy. Because I knew, at the end of the game, Nunu and Willump's bond was stronger than ever.   ❄️ - Sometimes I experienced tiny hiccups while Willump was running around where he stutters for a bit. While it doesn't take away from the experience, it was a bit jarring to see.❄️ - During your adventure, you will have three major snowball fights with Willump. For the life of me, I cannot beat Willump. I dodge the first snowball he throws, only for me to get hit by the second one. It really seems like the odds are stacked against me. Also, it feels like Willump has way too much health while he's literally chunking me. I get that it's supposed to be a challenge, given there's an achievement for winning all three fights, but it feels almost impossible.❄️ - There is no lock on feature, which would be so useful for said snowball fights, and fighting.❄️ - Jumps seem to be almost magnetized to what ever ledge I'm targeting, which can be finnicky in some spots, causing me to fall.❄️ - Some enemy attacks felt a bit bigger than the hit box, where I could've swore I dodge something, only to get hit.   Despite the few nitpicks I had with the game, I still enjoyed my experience, and will absolutely be playing this game again to get all the achievements. It really reminds me of the tie in video games some animated movies had where there's obviously a bit of jank and crust, but deep down, is a passion project, created by a passionate group of people. If you're looking for a short, heart-felt experience, I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When I talked to Riot Forge Creative Director Rowan Parker earlier this year, he made it clear the publisher wanted to do justice to your favorite champion. He acknowledged that Nunu and Willump isn't the most popular pick for your average League of Legend player, but I'm willing to bet you'll start to see more of the duo after Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story.That's because Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story is one of the most beautiful and captivating adventures I've played this year. In part, this is due to the stunning visual design by developer Tequila Works, but much of it is accredited to the wonderful relationship between Nunu and Willump, which is enough to warm even the Grinch's cold heart.ProsOutstanding Art DirectionSimple, Yet Fun Puzzle DesignNunu and Willump are a Charming DuoConsRemembering Flute Notes is a PainSome Frame Drops9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. Would definitely recommend the game, and will look into anything Tequila Works makes in the future as well!

_childDocuments_.review: Great if you're a fan of world building. However this game is solely for the story. Don't expect deep combat or a hard difficulty. You get this if you want to spend time with Nunu and Willump while crossing the tundra. Think, Ocarina of Time meets the Last Guardian sorta deal. focus on your music instruments to solve puzzles. Willump acting as your protector and extra hands. You tend to guide him to where he needs to go.  The most troublesome enemy is a plant that pushes you off cliff sides and the timing needed to pass it on some occasion. This is a game for the young and young at heart. Whole way through the focus on being wholesome is apparent, from the numerous snowball fights, to all the banter shared between the two. Controls are serviceable, and yea we could use a restart animation instead of cut to black on “death” but it does not denote the message of the game. At one point I felt bad for absolutely dominating Willump in the “ranked snowball” fight. So I threw the match and got rewarded with alt dialogue and a Wilump dance. Precious. Sometimes you gotta let your bro take a W.+ Wilump Lore+ Can snowball fight at any time+ Willump will fight back almost right way+ I got called out by Lissandra for snowball fighting during a crisis.+ Willump Sledding + We rolled Lissandra.+ Not a fan of Ice and Tundras but the environment was actually pleasant to explore.you get that feeling like when you map out springfield in the simpsons game. “Oh thats where this is in relation to this” - sometimes the plants…..you'll see.- could use more combat but I get that its a kid wandering the tundra, not a warrior looking for a fight- We talked about the void way too much and didn't have anyone show up.- What is volibear doing with his empty threats. - jump could be tighter, honestly needs like 1 or 2 more lines of code. Feels a bit lazily done.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: If you are not already interested in the league of legends lore and world I dont recommend this game.The exploration aspect of the game is poor, its mostly a linear game with a few secrets, there is no real exploring. There seem to be many paths but they seem to lead all to the same place.The puzzles are stupidly easy, most of wich i solved accidentaly in the first 20 seconds while trying to learn the rules.The controlls are stiff, jumping is weird and the latchinonto plataforms is inconsistent at best. You cant choose when you mount/dismount WIllump, the game does that automatically. While mounted the sprint feels like you are driving a truck, and bumping into things stuns you (which wouldnt be a problem if the detection wasnt as bad as it is) and it feels very slugish. While dismounted the controlls feel a bit better, but still nothing to write home about, and the climbing issues are still there.There is a forced stealth sectio later on in the game, as with any other its complete trash and unfun. the guard patroll routes are simpe and uninteresting with only 1 methond of ditracting all of them so you can go through the single pathforward.I will split combat into 2 parts, this one is about regular enemies. It is bad, repetivive and uninteresting, you can go by just by spaming light attack and the ocasional heavy to break defence, there are a total of 4 enemies: the wolf, the bigger wolf, the evil orb, and the fire/lava krugg, 3 of which need a "technique" to be defeated, the big wolft will sometimes block and you will need to use a heavy attack, the orbs need to be frozen and the killed and the krugg needs to be thrown snowballs and then doge its attack before it can be damaged. Looks like good variety, but you only fight like 3 kruggs and mainly regular wolfs and sometimes orbs.There are only 2 "True bosses", and they are by far the best part of the gameplay, one of which you dont even need to hit, they both play similar to a bullet hell. As with anything in the game its very easy regardless, I only managed to "die" once, and you dont even really die, you have a second chance to "revive" willump at full health.The plot is very simplistic and in my eyes nothing to write home about. The game starts with a low point for the character and then you are brought back to 3 days earlier to goe through the story beats that got you there. The game being tied to leagues IP is both one of its best things as well of its greatest weaknes (story wise), as it cannot kill, injure or change any major character in any significant way.Since everything should be cannon now I will assume this game is too. The expansion of the lore this game presents is perhaps the best part of it, it confirms some things as well as show other parts of the lore most people would never know unless they dive deep into the writen stories. And in the end it expands the personality of every major character as well as give other a purpose you cannot feel through only playing league.The sencond best thing about the game, te dialog is really good for themost part, there might be some instances where its not the best, but overall very good.This one is a mixed bag, I for one found it pretty good, while my brother didnt find it too amazing and even disliked some parts of it (like ornn). Overall i liked it.Its an middle of the road game, if it wasnt a riot forge game i wouldnt have even played it. I want in with the idea that I would be able to explore feljord but was left disapointed when it was basically linear. The boss fight where a high point in the gameplay, but happen very late in the story and i wish there where more of them. The stealth section was the low point of the game and almost made me not want to finish it, it happens on the last leg of the game so i was interested anough to see the final fight with  that i pushed through. In the end its a very easy game that is not very interesting in regard to the exploration, puzzles and plot, that combined with a combat that seemed like an afterthought and controlls that feels clunky throughout the game makes it not a recommendation for me. If you only want to know the story its better to watch someone play the game or just read it, but if you want to distract a kid with a somewhat decent experience this maybe a good option. That right there "Good game for a kid/non-gamer that like leagues lore" might be the point I am trying to make here.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very inoffensive and perhaps very nice to kids, or LoL fans, but as an adult who never played LoL it just didn't entertain me as much as I hoped based on the overwhelmingly positive reviews. The story is a bit cliche, it was all just ok; nothing was very surprising or emotionally touching. There were some random parts that could have been surprising, but were more like a parody on side quests in other games, I guess? It seems that the writers didn’t really think about things that well. For instance at a certain time a blind character is musing in front of a painting, about the content of the painting as if she had seen it. There were also some annoying plot conveniences like people not telling each other about certain important things (it’s vague as I say it now to avoid spoilers). The ending also came rather abrupt and was somewhat of an open ending. Even though the main baddy was defeated, there was still something important to do. After-credit scenes hint that this could be done in a next game. Still the ending was rather unsatisfying, and I literally said out loud ‘this is it?’The characters had the same problem. They were all just ok. The yeti was very cute tho, and Braum a hero friend was fun, the witch was ok as a baddy, but the kid was rather annoying as he kept talking all the time. Often he repeated what he just said 30 seconds ago. This really ruined some moments that perhaps could have been emotional. The little fuzzball side characters were also very cute and are a reason that maybe I will come back another time to this game, to give them all a cookie. The environments were also all just ok. They all had to have the theme of ice, which made them a bit monotonous. Still, you could see that they tried to make them a bit more varied (an icy volcano, a dungeon city in ice, an ice cave, and icy mountain, etc.), and this was well done, but there never was an environment that really mesmerized me. The gameplay consisted mostly of solving puzzles with the kid’s flute. By playing certain notes you can influence the environment which opens up a path to move on. This was done well, but was also not very challenging or interesting. The way to play the flute with a controller was done very well though, the characters of the notes to play, matched the layout of the controller very intuitively. It did make me feel very competent, as if I could really play this flute. There were also some fights that were an very needed distraction from the puzzles. Finally, there was a reasonably cleverly designed level that was mostly about stealth. The rest is mostly cut scenes. There are tons of long cutscenes in this game! All in all it was never too boring, or too frustrating, but also never really captivating.The music was ok and reminded me of Ori. All in all, the game was just ok, but it just left me feel unsatisfied. Perhaps if it is on sale, I can recommend you to pick it up. I also imagine if you want to play a videogame with young children, this game would be excellent. Graphics: 7/10Sound: 7.5/10Music: 7.5 /10Gameplay 6.5/10 Atmosphere: 5.5/10Value: 5.4/10In short, it is an ok game, but not great. Perhaps on sale I can recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I would love to recommend this game, I can't do it after working on some completion. Going back to redo areas is obnoxious for several reasons.  1. The chapters are long with few selections to pick from  2. A lot of dialogue can't be skipped  3. Picking a collectible doesn't always trigger a save. If you go back to menu before a save occurs, you have to re-do it.  4. Not all collectibles/achievements are listed for each section making them hard to track.  5. There's no power gain. Meaning it's just as slow the 15th time as the first.  6. Character movement is set in a lot of locations and even if you know what you are after, you cannot run through an area but have to painstakingly slow walk throughIf you only want a one-time play-through for the story and can find the game on sale, it could be worth picking up. Just be aware that you will spend a lot of frustrating time looking for completion if you're like me.

_childDocuments_.review: ‘Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story’ is a simple but lovely adventure experience, perfect for those looking for an accessible and simple game. In terms of performance, the game shines even on low-end hardware such as the Steam Deck, making it an excellent choice for portable play without compromising on quality.The gameplay gradually introduces new mechanics, from platforming to puzzles and collectibles, ensuring a smooth progression that keeps the player engaged. The art design is consistent with the League of Legends universe, with a non-realistic animation style and medium-low detail, resulting in an environment that is visually appealing without being overwhelming. The clear and straightforward narrative focuses on a simple goal that drives the entire plot, making it easy to follow and connect with the characters.For League of Legends veterans, the game offers subtle references to the franchise, but is accessible enough for those new to the universe. ‘Song of Nunu’ is a short and simple adventure, ideal for both fans of the series and new players looking for a light and immersive gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: League of Legends universe and stories have always amazed me. I may not be a big connoisseur of runeterra lore, but I've liked what I've seen and read so far. Song of Nunu is a very interesting story, I knew about the void but not much about the Freljord, it may not be the greatest game but it is fun to play, the best part of this game is the scenery, music and story, it really makes me want to play the other games of Riot Forge.What this game made good:- Great story and narrative.- Beautiful fantasy, characters, legends, scenery and music, the world feels magic.- The little details like animals wandering around, flowers blooming or emitting light when you walk next to them, Willump sculpting snow or playing around.- Dialogues, voice acting, character development.What this game could do better:- Art style is good but maybe terrain and characters could have some differences in shading, characters and moving creatures feel like they are made of the same material as the terrain.- Puzzle building, this game has few mechanics and they made a variety of puzzles with this mechanics in a way it does not feel very repetitive, but having more mechanics even if those are just used in a single chapter of the game makes games feel that you are not just doing the same thing over and over.- Puzzle elements, climbing walls and explosive fruits feel like they are not part of the scenery and they are just there so the player can solve puzzles or move forward through the world, I feel like these elements should blend with the landscape and have some hints to let the player know what to do, take for example GoW 2018 climbing spots and the elements you can interact with to solve puzzles.- More expressive characters more face expressions, gestures (Willump is okay he is playful, does different stuff while Nunu is exploring).

Landscapes and Art style are amazing and offer some unique nice views to gawk at.It also is a good introduction into the League of Legends universe and some of its characters.Finally its a perfect game for kids. The story follows a child and his friend, and they havea  great adventure together. My only complaint is, that its too short. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Received the game for free as part of a giveaway via the Official Riot Games OCE DiscordSong of Nunu: A League of Legends Story is a short but sweet game set in the League of Legends universe. Based in the Freljord, a snowy and inhospitable tundra, the story follows Nunu, a small child, and his trusty yeti companion Willump as they travel throughout the Freljord in search of an artifact called the "Heart of the Blue".While the game features combat, the main focus consists of environment puzzles that while short and sweet, aren't overly difficult and certainly never overstay their welcome. Due to the everchanging locations that the duo visit, there is enough variety and mechanics with the aforementioned puzzles to keep them interesting, such as moving around various creatures to reach new heights, or creating terrain with Ice Magic.On the other hand the combat in this game is a little on the basic side, and you know what, that's okay. Equipped with 2 combat buttons, a light attack and a heavy attack, as well as a ranged snowball that is mainly for utility, the combat feels overall really fluid and fun. You have the ability to chain attacks and juggle enemies and an execute mechanic to refill your health during combat.The main target audience for this game seems to be people who are at least somewhat familiar with the basics of Runeterra lore however I have it on good authority that even without it, you can still get a grasp of what is going on and enjoy the story as this is primarily a narrative driven game, the charismatic and interesting characters you meet bring life to an otherwise desolate wasteland.Overall I give the game a Solid 8/10, really only being held back by the duration of the game and overall difficulty being on the lower side. However if you aren't a seasoned gamer except a somewhat challenging and fun experience with an amazing narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Song of Nunu is a pretty good game, but it's fairly average too, unfortunately. The game's story is full of wonderful charm, with great voice acting the whole way through. The story and the music are definitely what to play the game for - they carry the game on its back by far. The gameplay is fine, but just serviceable - the combat is very simple and the platforming & puzzles are quite basic, minus one or two that did come across as confusing.The story is an entertaining times, and features plenty of cameos from other characters from League of Legends, and as always, Braum is a real highlight. I couldn't help but feel the game went a little too hard on having Nunu and Willump encounter all of Frejlord's legends in one adventure, but it was still neat to see the different portrayals of the different heroes. The environment design is a treasure too - the graphics of the game aren't anything too crazy, but the actual artwork and the creativity in the Freljord is terrific. Besides that, the story set pieces are also fun - there are some neat encounters along the journey that felt appropriately epic.Really, the only things holding me back from recommending this game more is that the 1) the game is really easy, 2) the gameplay itself is boring, and 3) $30 is a slightly steep price for a game that's 5-7 hours in length. There's not really much replayability unless you want to achievement hunt, too.Overall, I'd mostly recommend Song of Nunu, especially if you can get it on sale. It's a cute and wholesome adventure game that casual players would likely enjoy. For those looking for an experience they can really sink their teeth into, this one won't really be up your alley, but it can still be entertaining never the less.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun storytelling adventure game!A big plus right off the bat with the ps5 controller support on pc, everything works like a charm and they use ps5 controller icons. The gameplay is awesome. It keeps you engaged with events, cutscenes, combat, exploring, puzzles and more spoiler stuff, without ever getting "too much". There's no unnecessary walking or too much of the same combat. It's all balanced out very nicely and makes you want to keep playing. Even though it's not rewarding with levelling, looting, skilltrees etc, it's so incredibly engaging that you'll probably finish the main story in 1 or 2 playthroughs.Half storytelling happens when you're just exploring, when Nunu and Willump are exploring. There are no long annoying cutscenes and they are all skippable anyways. Though they are short and well executed I doubt people will skip them.The puzzles mechanics itself are easy, though it takes some time to get it right, the game changes it up slightly every time. No puzzle feels the same.The league of legends lore (why I bought this in the first place) goes in depth about the whole freljord and it's inhabitants. It's actually a really good story!The only downside is the length. It's not very long (+-7 main story, +-8 hours full completionist). I have been playing League for 12 years so I was gonna play this no matter what. But 30 euros for 8 hours might be steep for new people.Super bonus is the soundtrack. It is absolutely gorgeous. Changes well with the zones and environments, it helps set the scene exactly how sound is supposed to. Final verdict: It's a magical story in a magical setting with an amazing soundtrack. It's a fantastic game and I can only hope they make more of these lore stories in the future. They have enough material!

_childDocuments_.review: "Song of Nunu" is a story that focuses on League of Legends characters, Nunu & Willump. The story revolves around these two, their friendship, and their journey through adventures and hardships.Nunu is a small boy who seeks to find his missing mother, who seemingly "disappeared." Willump is a yeti, a magical and massive creature who became Nunu's best friend and protector. He is also the last yeti in Runeterra's universe. Together, they journey through the Freljord, seeking out Nunu's mother and dealing with challenges and making new friends along the way.The story solely focuses on their relationship, highlighting the theme of friendship, adventure, and the bond between them. The game encompasses different elements of adventure, puzzle-solving, and exploration.My time with the game was incredibly positive. Playing as these characters, and interacting with other inhabitants of Freljord, was captivating. The narration and music were exceptionally well-executed, making the storytelling more meaningful. As Nunu & Willump's story unfolds, you find yourself genuinely caring for them and their bond. The game introduces new mechanics thoughtfully, presenting well-crafted puzzles that require a moment of thinking and strategy. When puzzles do become complicated, Willump's subtle nudges are helpful without being overly directive.The bosses are great. I especially loved the end-boss fight, but for iconic "big" characters, I did feel they could have benefited from more screen time to develop their personalities further.The lore is great, it's easy to understand and go with the story. Having only a basic understanding of Nunu & Willump's backstory before playing, I was surprised to discover the depth of lore embedded within the characters, the environment, and the history of Runeterra. It has given me a greater appreciation for Riot's dedication to its lore and the way it allows room for expansion.The accessibility is great. As a hard of hearing person, I was able to follow the narration closely and understand where I was going or what I was supposed to do. The only drawback was the absence of subtitles during the end credits. There is a light-hearted conversation going on in the end-credits but there are no subtitles, and the overlapping music made it difficult for me to grasp the entire conversation.As someone who plays League of Legends and only casually reads Runeterra's lore, this game gave me great enjoyment and a deeper appreciation for the characters and the story. Kudos to Tequila Works for their meticulous and passionate effort in creating this game. I can see the love and passion that was put into the game, and I hope for other developers to follow the same suit in future Riot games.

_childDocuments_.review: The Nunu game boasts an exceptional musical score that greatly enhances the overall gaming experience. With a rating of 8.5 out of 10, it's clear that the music has left a lasting impression.From the moment you dive into the game, the music sets the tone and immerses you in the game's world. The composition is a perfect fit for the game's atmosphere, and it successfully enhances the emotions and engagement throughout the gameplay.What stands out most about the Nunu game's music is its ability to create a connection between the player and the in-game universe. The melodies, harmonies, and instrumentation are expertly chosen to draw players into the narrative, making every moment in the game feel significant.The music is diverse, with tracks that accompany different game settings and scenarios, and it adapts seamlessly to the changing dynamics of the gameplay. The soundtrack successfully matches the pacing of the story, building anticipation during intense moments and providing a comforting backdrop in quieter sections.                                                                         In summary, the music in the Nunu game is a standout feature that elevates the game to a new level. Its emotional depth, connection to the narrative, and ability to maintain engagement make it a key component of the game's success. With just a little more variety, it could easily reach a perfect score. Whether you're a gaming enthusiast or a music lover, the Nunu game's soundtrack is a compelling reason to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, I loved every second of it. It's a chill (pun intended) game that you would enjoy on a Sunday. Easy, pretty fast paced and with a beautiful environment this games makes it easy to be immersed in the chilly region of Frejlord. The combat is pretty fun, the puzzles are interesting and the story is the best aspect of it. The friendly graphics help build this wonderful world and it all feels just amazing. 10/10 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: coming in as LoL player and love Nunu beforehand, this is very chill adventure game. i think you will enjoy the scenery of the world of  freljord itself and all characters woven into this. it's very simple and not too complex with couple puzzle that actually couple time tackle me a bit but still manageable. overall a super fun simple game with great story!!

_childDocuments_.review: The story, art, graphics were really good. I loved the emotional aspects of the game and how it showed more of the lore surrounding nunu and willump and expanded on them. Now for the downsides, the gameplay was very lackluster, the same enemies and the same moves on repeat. It made it repetitive and boring. The camera angle was janky at times and had to reposition it made my character jump off the map a couple times. The stealth portion was also repetitive and made me just wish i'd get through it already. so overall if you want a good/fun story that explores the lore of LOL and has some very good emotional aspect to it that I very much enjoyed but gameplay wise there isn't much to say it was just repetitive after the first hour wasn'y really hooking me in . I still enjoyed the game but more on a story driven aspect vs gameplay wise.
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: It's an incredible game. Combat is really fun, the 'finisher' moves are cool, some are really funny. The dialogue in this game serves purpose too, its an interesting listen if you're into LoL lore and also it's just nice to listen to. The environment design, visuals, music literally everything feels so polished. I love the poros, so glad they're included!I love that this feels like a LoL game without having braindead team mates that /muteall in champ select then pick graves top.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Short and Sweet game thats actually canon to the lore. cool LoL lore story on Nunu & Willump and other Freljordian Champions. The atmosphere is really amazing as you get to explore Freljord and listen to the nice music it has to offer. Speaking of music, you also get to play songs with Nunu's flute that can harness the power of the Svellsongur. Playing music is often used as a means to solve puzzles and also in nice rest areas like campsites to lighten the mood. If you're looking for an amazing story you unfortunately won't find it here, but it does well for how short it's able to tell it. And as previously mentioned this is confirmed to be canon so this is a nice short story surrounding Nunu & Willump, Braum, and Lissandra. And one last little tidbit, there are some easter eggs to find for League fans so thats something fun to look out for :)Overall the game is a short and sweet tribute to Nunu & Willump and the rest of the Freljord and you will no doubt enjoy it if you like League of Legends lore, 3d platformers, or are just looking for a new story to get immersed in for a short while.
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: Great casual game for when you just want to chill and unwind. The lore, soundtrack, characters and everything else blend to create a perfect cosy vibe. A little too short for my taste, but the other things that I mentioned before made up for it. Looking forward to more lore games based on Runeterra!
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just amazing. _childDocuments_.review: While yes, I recommend this game - everyone and their mother here will tell you why its good. Let me be the one to tell you its faults.Controls:The controls at times feel a little wonky. It feels very much like it was made for a controller, not a keyboard and mouse. Because of the angle of most of the levels, I found myself zigzagging my way across platforms instead of just being able to walk straight. Sound:There are moments where the sound quality just randomly dips. Sometimes the voices sound like they were recorded with an Airpod. Gameplay:The levels were alright, if not repetitive. Go here, do this. Good, now go to the other side of the level and do it again. Good. Do it again.Puzzles & Level Design:For the most part, the music puzzles were a great addition. My main gripe are with two gameplay sections in particular - the Krug puzzles and the stealth missions.The Krugs move so impossibly slow that every time I saw one on my screen I let out an audible groan. Guiding them is such a chore. The stealth, though it only occurs minimally, is pretty mediocre. The guard detection was so finicky that getting past them felt more like trying to outsmart an AI than sneaking. Character Design: Willump, Braum, and Ornn were great. Everyone else... what happened? I hope you like Nunu's stupid gap tooth cause the camera will keep it center stage in every cut scene. Volibear - I mean what do I need to say that hasn't already been complained about. And Lissandra at the end just looks... wrong.Camera:Oh, God, the camera. The camera will force your perspective so many times you might forget where you are. You can barely move at times because the camera forces you to look at any random thing Riot decided to slap a proper noun onto. The forced perspective camera happens so often and is so intense that it became nauseating. Especially in a platforming-focused game, the camera made a lot of sections feel so amateur. And this might be just me, but when there are things to collect, forcing my camera into certain places makes me feel like I am missing parts of a level. But yeah cool game, give it a go, I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just eye-candy on top of pure wholesomeness wrapped like a Christmas present. The art, the music, the animations, the voice acting, the story; everything is working together to deliver you a blissful moment of joy in this ol' cold world, my friends. Please embark blindly on this journey and savor it.Let's remember that this is first and foremost a  game, so if you expect the smoothest jumping or dodging movements, it wouldn't be its strong suit. The animation lock can be annoying at times, but it's not a dealbreaker and you're not punished for it.For the completionists, there are various checkpoints and upon completion, you can go through the chapters again.The art as a whole is really what shines here. The characters are so endearing and the world is breathtakingly beautiful to explore. The music is a delight, and wonderfully implemented as a gameplay mechanic. The story cannot be talked about without delving into spoiler territory. Wait no longer and just play it.Being an UE5 game, it's suffering from shader issues that create some stutters, but there is a fix! All stutters were gone for me. Do I wish we didn't have to tweak on our ends to make the game a smooth experience? Absolutely! But does it make the game any less worth experiencing? No, on the contrary, it'd be a shame if it did; and the tweak doesn't take more than 5min.
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: & I despise Riot Games and the community they've created over the years. I despise Summoners Rift, I despise ARAM, and I despise anyone who associates themselves in any "meaningful" way with that game or the community these days. Regardless of how much I despise this poisonous and terrible experience with a company and their primary games like TFT, League, and Valorant.Song of Nunu takes a step away from all of that and is actually enjoyable. It is a good game. I've played some of their previous games. Mayhem, Convergence, Sylas, and King were all monotonous and uninteresting, regardless of how good their lore / narrative telling was. I just didn't like it and you can mostly chalk that up to my negative bias towards them. I feel that Riot Forge or at least Tequila Works understands how to create games that are quick and to the point, with good concepts and execution, as opposed to long drawn out games that are less palpable to the average gamer these days, who needs short bursts of content before they become bored. The game lasts about 5-6 hours and brought tears to my eyes. Hatred for the developers has clouded my vision, and toxicity has darkened my heart but this game was capable of reaching through to me and allowing me to immerse myself in the narrative and story of each and every character in this game. Showing many distinct sides of someone that I previously thought just had one. League of Legends offers a large world filled with lore and truly captivating story telling. Song of Nunu gets it properly. It's educational, entertaining, and, most importantly, entertaining. It's not the League of Toxicity.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was gorgeous. Another big win for Riot Forge, and tequila works for this awesome game. I loved this game and would recommend it to everyone who wants a casual story-driven game. (Around 7-8 hours of gameplay)

_childDocuments_.review: The story is awesome and many cute moments. You'll know what I mean when it happens. I am currently stuck on a ledge trying to make it to the the next, and cannot due to the angle change being in a dialogue scene as I'm climbing... I have tried for 20 minutes and switched from keyboard and mouse to controller to see if that helps.. nope. Just like League, I rage quit. Maybe skill issue, but I don't think so at this point. Combat is very very easy. I would recommend this game if you like casual, story-driven games. and if you are really into learning more League lore, this is great. _childDocuments_.review: CONTAINS A FEW MINOR SPOILERS. Amazing game. Like the little things like having snowball fights just randomly not apart of the story with Willump and also you can just go up and hug Willump is great. The story is amazing and the combat is surprisingly in-depth for how little you actually fight which is a nice surprise. A few immersion breaking things happen but they were because of game play reasons not the story mostly. On the most part the game flowed very well with 1 or 2 scenes giving me whiplash from how hard they went from happy to trouble but that was the only issues I had with the story and didn't make any real impact on my enjoyment of the game.I have Nunu as one of my most played champs in league and I am so happy to see a game about them come out as well as seeing the gods of the Freljord - Anivia which was surprising. On that I didn't like how Ornn was modelled and voiced in this same with Voli's model. But the Characterisation for Ornn was SPOT ON. He is my most played champ in League and Legends of Runeterra with 160k On LOL and 36k on LOR(which is similar amount of games played as league from memory due to how much less points you get in LOR). For people who love the Freljord and these champions this game is 100% worth it but for a normal person I would say it's overpriced for how short it is. $45AUD for 5-6 hours of story. I sat around a bit just looking at the environment. It would be about 5 hours 1 hours per chapter for most people I would imagine.but you should 100% either watch someone play it or buy it because you need to at least experience it in someway if you don't want to buy and play it.I only have 1 actual complaint about this game and it's the camera. I don't like having to fight the camera when doing parkour but it really want to shift and then if you are using your mouse to guide your character you end up jumping off the end. I am sure it's a lot less of an issue for controller but I wish it had taken just a bit more inspiration from Jedi: Fallen Order then it already has with the camera. The camera in that game doesn't take control unless it has no other choice and you almost never use the camera to help navigate parkour. I think that Willumps sprint being mouse steered and also A-D steered make it feel unwieldy.

_childDocuments_.review: Game was a wholesome experience for a place as grim as Runeterra is. Like the title implies, its a League of Legends Story Game, not a whole ton of meat in game play, but the interactions between Nunu and Willump were adorable. Cons:- I did have some issues with the music having strange cuts and the cut scenes feeling... robotic? - The voice-acting could def be better.    -You could tell the script was given a simple adjective of emotion plus the quote as the tone of the interactions felt they were stringed together rather than the context/scenario being told to the VA's before them voicing their lines. Lots of times Nunu starts bawling about him missing his mom then immediately goes to a determined "I got this" 2 seconds later. Even the god JB Blanc himself felt a bit off at times... Maybe i'm wrong but its fine.- Kinda short? Finished the game in 5.5 hours, and for a game that was $30, I was kinda expecting Ruined King levels of playtime. Convergence and Mageseeker were both 8-9 hoursish of gameplay, but for a game that was teased around the same time as Hextech Mayhem and Ruined King, while also being delayed, expected a bit more tbh. Pros- Expands lore of the Freljord which for me personally, I've craved for a bit, had all my favourite Freljordians in it too, so massive W.   - Many people didn't like Ornn and Voli's redesign, but I personally adored Ornn's new look. Makes him feel more "forge god" and less "grump dude". Braum gigachad. Lissandra is the only interesting part of the 3 sisters imo so I liked her lots. Nunu became mini Jesus at the end for Liss.- OST is a bop, lots of leit-motifs laying around where you'll do the soy face and you pointing how you can hear different champion themes. - There are some places in the game where you stand on a cliff or something and makes you realize how bad you wanna play the Runeterra MMO. Like just looking at the Freljord just felt nice. Seeing Ornn's Forge outside of his LoR Cards was sick and walking around the Citadel was pretty cool. Makes you realize the Freljord is more than just snow and ice- Just a wholesome game overall. Who doesn't like Nunu and Willump?

_childDocuments_.review: I currently can't finish the game because of a bug where you are stuck at the top of the hill and can't finish the story after the final, but I'm sure it will be fixed very soon. Anyway, here is my Review:Song of Nunu comes with a Pricetag of 30€ and I want to start with saying that I think it is completly worth the price. The Game itself is not a AAA title which is pretty obvious as soon as you start the game. No fancy menu, pretty simplistic  options and (for me) the giant bummer of max. full hd resolution. There was no way (yet) to change the game to run in 4k, which is pretty sadening for a game that releases 2023. But I'm pretty sure most of us playing this wont bother anyway, so this problem is not that big of a tragedy.Story 10/10You can tell that most of the work they've done with this game went into the story. For me it was very exciting to follow the story and I never felt bored with it. Very well doneCharacters 10/10Those that buy this game because they want to see some of the freljordian characters: YOU'LL GET THEM! Those who saw the trailers might have an idea, but be asured that you'll have very pleasent encounters. The characters are lore acurate, which is so nice to experience out of the perspective from Nunu and Willump. Worlddesign 10/10The World of Freljord itself is pretty much what you can expect from it: an icy, blueish world. But the artstyle they've chosen still makes it very welcoming and you're invited to freely roam the levels and explore the Freljord. I love what they have done here and I'm sad it's already over...Voiceacting 7/10Yes, it's nice they have voiced the game in so many languages. Yes, (in english) all the characters have all their original voiceactor. But: You're playing as Nunu&Willump. While Willumps groaning and moaning is always kinda wholseome and nice to listen to, Nunu himself can sometimes be quite nerve wracking. There will be passages in the game where you maybe take some time to enjoy the view or solve the puzzles and Nunu will be just keep talking. While you're processing at the awaited speed it will be no problem at all, but as sson as you're slower as the developers intendet you to be you will here 1-2 phrases from Nunu over and over and over again. I don't know why they did that and maybe I'm just nitpicking here, but for me that was very annoying sometimes. Near the end there was puzzle that took me some time to solve and I heard Nunu say the same phrase like a 100 times. Comming to that his voice is a high pitch kids voice, so... yeah. Gameplay 8/10Short: The Gameplay is very easy except for some parts where the developers out of nowhere crank up the difficulty, but it's never "undoable". Long: The Gameplay sometimes was quite repetitiv with you doing the same thing again and again to proceed thru the story, but sometimes they threw in new abilities or made you do things you can only do in exact that part of the game. I never felt bored, it was just too easy sometimes. But this doesn't have to be a bad thing when your main focus is to enjoy the world and the story. If you're playing the game because of that you'll have an easy time getting thru the story except for the few parts where it will be quite challening.I can realy recommend this game and think with ~8 hours playtime the price is fair for what you'll get. I don't know if I'll go for a second playthru just to collect the things I didn't manage to achieve like finding all the poros, but maybe in the future I will. For now you'll only have one savegame, you should keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story

_childDocuments_.review: In this single-player adventure, venture into the idyllic but treacherous world of the Freljord as Nunu, a young boy on a quest to find his lost mother. Unearth the secrets, myths, and legends buried deep in the frozen tundra alongside your best friend, a wise and playful yeti named Willump, and unfold an inspiring story one puzzle at a time.

name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX
detailed_description: The legendary Alex Kidd returns with Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX! Since his first appearance in 1986 with Alex Kidd in Miracle World, the iconic Alex Kidd makes his return to smash rocks, collect coins and tackle bosses once again in Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX! Return The Kingdom of Radaxian to its former glory and destroy the evil Janken the Great! Comprising of all levels from the original title as well as brand new levels which expand the lore of Alex Kidd, experience Miracle World like you’ve never seen it before with new animations, graphical detail and gameplay improvements. Relive legendary rock, paper scissors battles with Boss Rush Mode! As well as including all of the original classic boss fights, Boss Rush Mode will give you the chance to experience none-stop boss action! Transport straight into the classic with Retro Mode! Jump straight into the original classic with the press of a button with Retro Mode! At any point during gameplay, switch between the enhanced graphics and a recreation of the original art style! Feature Overview A Legend Reborn – Dive into a stunning recreation of Alex Kidd in Miracle World with striking new art and tighter, more fluid controls. New Modes – New modes such including ‘Classic Mode’ and ‘Boss Rush Mode’ will be available for players alongside the standard game. New Levels – Experience new levels which expand the lore of the original game. Alternative Boss Fights – New and improved boss fight mechanics with more intuitive combat. Classic Mode – Experience the original game with boss fights, dialogue, levels and functions the same as the original Master System version. New and remastered music - A wide array of reimagined music tracks as well as remastered tracks from the original classic game!

_childDocuments_.review: If you had a SEGA Master System before the new millennium, then Alex Kidd is no stranger to you.The acrobatic monkey child was a bit of SEGA's mascot next to Sonic BUT Alex Kidd in Miracle World was even built into certain versions of the Master System, especially in a series of the first generations of the console.Now the game is back with a finished remake as 'Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX'.In this video you can notice differences in graphics and world: Anyone who played the original Alex Kidd in Miracle World years ago knows all too well that it was a very challenging game. A lot of gamers have never even finished the game and this DX version is not a breeze either.The in-game shop where you could buy certain items or vehicles were and still are a good stimulation to try to reach the finish of the game again.The gameplay is still identically the same.If you are hit by an enemy, you are still instantly dead.Jumping is a precise job just like it used to be, especially since Alex Kidd always slips that little bit when landing a jump, but that's part of the job.Add to that that you barely have any lives and you know that reaching the end of the game is not for the faint of heart. (But pss, this is the PC, and there will be mods on the PC, but don't tell them)Not that there have been no quality of life changes, for example you now have faster access to your special items, although it is still not explained exactly what they do or how to use them, so you just have to use all the buttons once to discover it and yes, there's even an option to play with an infinite number of lives, quite surprising, and something we can give the devs extra thanks for.The only difference this mode makes is that you get certain achievements that you can't get.If you now lose all your lives, you can also continue playing from the last level you hit, although you will lose all your money.Fortunately, a save system has also been thought of to save your progress, so that you no longer have to make those one hellish routes through the game.The game works great on a steam deck too: If you play with the mode of infinite lives, you will quickly notice how quickly the game is finished,'back in the day' when the game was only built into the console, then you needed at least 2 days to get good enough to finish the game in 1 session.But now, if you've now completed the game, you can get started with the Boss Rush, in which you can hit all the bosses again, and the Classic Mode, which is a remake of the original on the Master System.Everything works and looks like it did all those years ago. So if you are looking for the original experience, you can also come here, pure nostalgia food.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? In the visual department, yes. The rest depends if you had a Sega Master System when you were a kid.The original Alex Kidd in Miracle World was released in 1986 for the Master System. It was later bundled with the console and so becoming very widely known, even beoming something like a mascot for Sega - until Sonic arrived in 1991. Alex Kidd was a fantastic platformer - for its time.  His primary skill is punching, which he can use to attack enemies, break certain types of rocks to open blocks, and access new areas and collect money. Alex can also jump like a monkey, but loses a life whenever he touches an enemy or other hazard. He can hold its breath for a very long time and dive like a fish, and there are some vehicles which are quite fun to use.The remaster comes with beautiful new graphics and a re-arranged soundtrack, but the same core gameplay as it was in 1986. Enemies do not notice you - they just run along their path, touch them, and you are dead. At the end of certain levels, you must face bosses in a game of jan-ken-pon (rock, paper, scissors). The enemies always chose in the same order, so you can easily memorize their turns to win. The levels are quite short, but the remake added a few new ones. The game is still not very long. The original was hard because there was no save option - you had to start anew after losing your lifes. The remake saves after each level. Be careful, though, if you select "New Game" at the beginning your progress is immediately deleted - you only have one save slot.I would have loved the game, if it wasn't for the slippery controls. Alex moves like he is running on ice. In a game were precision jumping is essential, this makes the game rather difficult and does take some time to get used to. I probably would have quit after the first level if the game didn't have the automatic save function.Replay Sega's first great platformer in modern (or the old) graphics. Highly recommended for everyone that grew up with Alex Kidd.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Got around 20-30 minutes into this and it just doesn't feel right at all. Played a lot of the original game back in the day and have regularly returned to it over the years. Something about the controls and collision detection feel terrible and left me not wanting to play it at all.There seems to be some issues with the framerate or frame pacing too, as it doesn't not feel smooth or consistent. what troubles me is that a lot of the overwhelmingly positive reviews don;t mention this at all. So do be wary before jumping in at full price for a piece of nostalgia, as it really doesn't hold up to the original in either mode you decide to try.I may try it again in the future once it's received some patches and is on deal. But right now, refunding and recommending avoiding it and playing the original game for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: A few days ago, I left a negative review for this game, citing terribly imprecise controls that resulted more often than not in cheap, artificial failures. It was one of the few times that I have been genuinely disappointed in a game.Since then, the developers have put out an update. There is now an option to turn off the sliding mechanic when Alex stops moving, allowing for a greater degree of control and ownership of one's mistakes. The trade-off is that certain parts of the game are now harder to access, since they relied on the sliding mechanic to reach them. However, the developers have wisely chosen to make this feature optional, as some players will be happy to slide.So, of course I jump back in. The idea that it had been improved was too good to pass up.I got a few levels in and Alex died a bunch of stupid, avoidable deaths, eventually leading to a game over screen. Every time, it was my fault, and it felt amazing.I have nothing but praise for game developers who take on criticism, with the aim to improve their product, and I will reward this by changing my review to a positive one. It's now mostly everything I could want in a remake.Well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: First of all:I'm a huge Alex Kidd fanboy (perhaps to be guessed by the avatar). I regularly play the Sega Ages version on the nintendo switch. On a good day, I can play through Alex Kidd in a good 20 minutes. (Record at 17mins). So I claim to know the game Alex Kidd in Miracle World very well and therefore to be able to assess how much the remake has captured the flair of the original...and the truth is: hardly at all. I had already bought the game for the Switch back then and was moderately enthusiastic...but now I bought it again for 3€ on steam because of the ccheap price and the controls update.I still find the new graphics very coherent. The choice of what Alex should munch on at the end of a level is great (Hamburger4Life) but that's where the fun ends. The controls are still spongy. When Alex jumps onto stones, the height is corrected again after his hit collision, which just feels awkward. The hit collision with enemies is a bad joke.The reset points after dying are completely pointless and unlike in the original game, where you continue where you die. Despite the “Control Update”, it is still not possible to jump out of the upper edge, which would be important in the castles or on the island, for example.The Ring-Ghost-Extralife Rotation is completely weird...most probably because due to the changes to the reset pointsIf you lose all your lives, you have the option to restart the level... but lose all your money...which makes the forest the final boss, for example...especially in combination with the spongy controls and the creepy final boss fight. (in the original you could by a continue for 400Gold)Helicoptercontrols are still way offThe new levels are meh...I have no idea what the makers of this reimagination tried to archieve...they took a game which has the (unfairly) reputation of being way to hard...and made it even harder...but with less fun...Yeah I get, that the boss fights (StoneScissorsPaper and the final bosses) are the weakest points of Alex Kidd, but the new Bossfights are not one bit more exciting...The new level feel completely out of place...would have been better they were making a few levels as epilogue and didn't touch the original level order...But the worst thing is still the physics (not even so much the controls) The physics feel so off, that it's almost another game...I would only recommend this game if you have nostalgic memories of this game, but haven't played it in 30years. And then for not more than 5€...
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: This remake of the original Alex Kidd game is as hard as it was back in the day, but now, with a lot more polish on the surface.The aesthetic is gorgeous. The characters look cartoony and lively, the lighting effects are beautiful, and the animation is so fun to watch.Interestingly enough, the game allows you to switch back to the old look of the game at the click of a button. It makes you appreciate just far we've come, and how much great work the devs put into creating an atmosphere and unique look to each level.The music is fun, although nothing to write home about. It had my head bopping, and it accompanied the levels well.Now the most important point: gameplay.Platforming and jumping feels totally fine. Unfortunately, because this is a faitfhul recreation of the game, it comes with a lot of the flaws the original game has too.I found that the level design in this game is a bit uninspired. Most of the level consists of breakable blocks, which includes obstacles, and some that contain powerups.Sometimes it can be fun trying to figure out the mini puzzle of which order to break the blocks to get some extra money in your pocket, however I found that after a while this quickly became a bit tedious.Your basic attack is very short ranged, so you need to go right up to each one, and there are just SO MANY BLOCKS TO BREAK!Obviously you can skip them if you'd like, but it's fun to collect stuff, and you do want to gather enough money to buy items later on in the game.Moving on to enemies, most of them die in one hit, although there are a few that take a bit more of a beating.You, however, will take one hit to die. And combine that with a short range melee attack, and sometimes unfair-feeling hitboxes, this can lead to a bit of frustration. There is still a lives system, and if you run out of them all, you will be put back at the beginning of the level. Thankfully, for those interested, you can enable infinite lives in the options, if you think the mechanic is outdated.Some levels begin with a shop, where you can purchase items, whose function you have absolutely no idea. They will be consumed upon use, so you have to just hope you used them in the right situation.These range from temporary invincibility, ranged attacks, or a small orb that deploys small Alex Kidds that march out, Lemming-style and hurt enemies they touch.I think they're fun and interesting, but the whole shop system feels a bit random. I just buy every single item at every single shop, and if it's a vehicle... The vehicle levels are awesome. However, if it's your first time playing a level, good luck keeping your vehicle alive for more than 5 seconds.On most of them, I would crash into a block or enemy that I didn't expect, only to be left stranded in a vehicle level, on foot. Which, can be a bit underwhelming.Finally, the boss levels.There are normal bosses, which are fun enough to figure out and defeat.There are however, also Rock, Paper, Scissors  bosses too.The first one was quite frustrating. Your fate is left to the Gods of RNG if you'll be coming out alive. Thankfully, the bosses do use the same "hand" every time you fight them, so you can memorize that and outsmart them, but it just feels like a waste of time.Later on you can get an upgrade that lets you see what they will play. and you just have to react fast enough to beat them.All that, is to say that I can't quite complain about a game's mechanics that came out in 1986. I am actually happy the devs kept it as annoying and frustrating as the original. (Although maybe some more quality of life changes like the infinite lives would have been nice as a toggleable option. Maybe a difficulty setting you can choose from the beginning).There are definitely platformers out there that have aged better, at least in my opinion, but I think this is still a fantastic remake. If you enjoyed the original, then I'd highly recommend picking this up. It's just a better version.And if you didn't play the original, then I'd say really give some gameplay a look. If I could give the game a neutral review, I would.I had mixed emotions throughout my playthrough, while some elements were frustrating, there was still enjoyment to be had in other areas. Overall, it's a decent game!

_childDocuments_.review: My mom would always tell me how growing up, she would play Alex Kidd on her Sega Master System when she was a lil' kid. Being the only game she had plus Astro Warriors, she grew very fondly of the game. Fast forward to 2017, my mom taught me all about the game from the Sega Ages version on Switch, how you can kill the octopus to get into a secret room and get a bunch of money, the crouch-sliding trick, the motorcycle, etc. And with this game being announced and releasing, we were both SUPER excited to get it and play it together taking turns once again. While my mom prefers to play on the Retro Visuals mode (And so do I, frankly), I have to say that the spritework is absolutely STELLAR, all the expressions and colors truly pop and catch the vibes of each level. The music in this game is catchy as the original, with the modern remixes being nice guitars. The new levels and music are very welcoming, truly expanding this game to be in my opinion the DEFINITIVE way to play this classic game.Theres even a bunch of stuff to do after playing and beating the game, and although the Boss Rush is a little barren bones and easy, the Classic mode and the advanced extras are truly a nice touch. I totally recommend this game to experience this classic in a modern age.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience at the moment of this review:- 3000+ hours in the original game- 28 hours played on DX 48 hours after his release++:- New graphics are magnificent.- Alex Kidd movements are nearly similar to the orignal and at the same time more dynamic. The best of the two worlds.- The original counts 17 levels, in this one you have 5 more and 1 completely remade. These news levels don't just bring more hours of gameplay they also bring new enemies and new environnements.- The capsule B (shield) item has been remade too. It's better now.- Bosses have been remade (more fun now and also more new content).- New modes: Boss rush (fun but quick), classic (i don't like it, just play the original game).- The infinite lives option shut the mouth of all the persons reviewing badly this game and telling he is too difficult. Go play Mario.--:- In the over way i found the hitboxes of some enemies really weird (like frogs). A patch would be great but it's manageable.- Only one save so if you press new game your save is erased (can be fixed copying you savestate in another file and the game is short).To conclude: Perfect symbiosis between keeping the old stuff we like and making new. 18/20

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible remake of this unappreciated gem from the old days.The obvious thing are the graphics, everything looks beautiful, plenty of attention to detail went into the new sprites, a lot more variety... the music is also great, many new tracks to replace the same main theme repeating pretty much every level. The game is still short, but this remake has a few new levels, and they are pretty decent. Could have been a few more, but at least the few we got are interesting and unique. We also get collectibles that have some cheeky references.Pretty much all of the classic level design and secrets were kept, even the questionable ones, but it also changes stuff, specially the bosses. Also what they did with the Jan-ken-pon fights is adorable, it doesn't allow you to skip the little jingle, which is a minor inconvenience when you lose the match, but it's still super charming. Also, there are A LOT of new sprites for the 8bit mode too, which is a very nice touch, definitively worth playing the game over again with the 8 bit mode.I'd say the only thing this really lacks is leaderboards, stuff like time attack and speedrun mode, maybe even one for most money collected, like the leaderboards on the Sega Ages port of the game... considering the game is short, giving more arcade-ish options like that would go a long way in incentivising replayability. Also, compared to the remake of Wonder Boy, I'd say that game has a better artstyle, but that's up to preference. I was worried I wouldn't enjoy the artstyle they went with for this, but it grew on me and I definitively enjoy it.To finish, it's a great remake, must-have if you are an Alex Kidd fan, and if you are new to it, give it a shot, it's definitively a unique blend of gameplay and level design that no other main platformer franchise has. If it's short length bother you, I'd say wait for a sale, but do still get it, it's worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: alex kidd in miracle world is one of my most nostalgic games from when i was a "kidd". i was psyched to hear when they announced this remaster. now i've played it a bit and its awesome. love the new pixel graphics, the comfort features and the infinite lives mode. and when i'm feeling really nostalgic i can switch to the original graphics/soundtrack at the click of a button. alex controls A LITTLE BIT more floaty i feel than in the original, which caused me to die once or twice because it deviated from my muscle memory.highly recommended for those that are nostalgic for this game, and those who enjoy really old school platformers. well done devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: Good News: It's Alex Kidd, just like you remember it, and now it looks and sounds just as you saw it in your mind's eye, the beautiful graphics could almost be called "nostalgia vision." (also, it has Wonderboy 3's gimmick that allows you to flip between new and original game).Bad News: It's Alex Kidd, with its frustrating, unfair gameplay, floaty jumps, and awful hitboxes.Silver lining: The devs introduced extra options (hit ALT in the options screen) to make things better: Infinite lives, non-floaty jumping, and better hitboxes.All in all, if you belong to the game's target demo (hardcore old Sega fans in their mid 40s), you'll love and cherish this piece of nostalgia (even if you get a guide with all the jan ken pon sequences and use infinite lives in the last stage, like I admittedly did).
_childDocuments_.name: Alex Kidd in Miracle World DX

_childDocuments_.review: While it looks great visually it didn't take long for me to notice that the smoother animations didn't account for the hit box of both the player character and enemies in turn giving the visual feedback that you're getting hit by nothing, for a game that kills you in one hit that kind of issue makes it instantly less fun for me I'm sure for people who enjoyed it in the past this is a real gemFor me coming in new to Alex Kidd i just can't recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: 90s-ass hitboxes and jumping physics, no wonder I couldn't get past the last level as a kid. And that was without being able to Continue at will like in this version!Why did I pay eight dollars for this masochism? I have now largely healed 30 year trauma. Any child that owned a Master System will know my pain. I now summarily and ceremoniously uninstall.Excellent remake though (with seamless transition between old and new graphics), and it holds serious nostalgic value for that and that alone, but otherwise, I'd hardly recommend this to anyone that values their sanity.Alex Kidd in Miracle World....more like Alex Kidd in '♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-ass Jumping Physics' World.
