_childDocuments_.review: Sumire, a young girl who is dealing with some issues, has recurring dreams about her recently passed away grandmother. She feels like her grandmother is trying to tell her something, but she isn’t sure what. She wakes up to visit the shrine of her grandmother when she hears a glass shattering sound. A little seed from a magical place that came through the window, laying there on the floor. A seed that will sprout a very special flower. A flower with only one simple wish, to have a perfect day as it will have to return to the place it came from when the sun set. So Sumire’s adventure, with the flower on her side, begins.The gameplay, a story driven adventure, mostly exists out of exploring and ticking off your ‘perfect day’ list. Which isn’t that hard as it’s part of the story. There are also small fetch side quests you can do, where you help humans, animals, a scarecrow and even a stone statue.All with a pinch of consequences, better known as karma. Your actions and choices will have a positive or negative effect. Just not as much as I hoped for as I’ll tell you in my final word.There is a fair amount of walking and running around but at one point you unlock fast travel.As a small extra bonus, one of the mini games that is a card game unlocks after your first play-through, ready to be revisited if you like. At least I’m fairly sure it wasn’t there when I started up for the first time.A tad magical and whimsical. From the water painted like art style to the colour pallet used. The depth of the game as you can walk back and forth along with the small curve of the globe. Or how the scenery changed. I liked all those little things and details.Beautiful. Each location has its unique theme that is very fitting. Relaxing or uplifting when needed and a bit catchy with moments.Controller or keyboard, your choice. I played with my xbox for pc controller and it was smooth and easy. Thumb stick to run around, B too run, Y to open your backpack and left/right bumper to scroll through it, A as action button. Which the game all explains as you put your first steps in the game.The movement was sometimes a tiny bit awkward but for me personally not that big of an issue and easily forgivable.The dialogue and story were sometimes a bit confusing, not sure if this is a me thing or…If you want all the achievements, then it can get repetitive as multiple playthroughs are required.It’s a short game that picks up on heavy topics such as grief, bullying, depression, divorce but also touching ones like love, new friendship, learning how to give grief a place, the choice to help others. Paired with underlying message(s). Message(s) of which I drew my ownconclusions as I believe it’s open for interpretation and everyone will draw their own thing out of it. Whether it be a form of comfort, a new view on things or a lesson/multiple lessons.I enjoyed my first playthrough and was satisfied with the ending I got, perhaps I should have left it at that.Of course me being me and being curious as can be I sped through another one. Trying to get worse karma and picking the most rotten answers/actions, which in all honestly really didn’t feel good, just to compare to the story and ending I just had of which I believed was mixed karma.There the game disappointed me a little as there wasn’t that much, just a tiny little bit, change in the overall story and no different ending. Maybe my karma still wasn’t horrible enough?But I’m willing to give it a, borderline -doubted a long time which way to swing-, thumbs up cause it was a nice experience to have gone through, one that I don’t regret in the end.Just be cautious if you pick it up and be aware you’re in for multiple plays if you want all the achievements.With love,Tchii

_childDocuments_.review: Well crap. I haven't been this emotionally ruined by a game since Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons. And, like that game, I loved every moment of it, but I will never play it again. You just can't have an experience like that twice. Running through again just to grab all the achievements would cheapen it.Sumire (the game, not the titular character) is proof that a story doesn't have to be 2deep4u to say some very profound things. Despite its absolutely gorgeous children's storybook visuals, it doesn't sugarcoat the uglier side of life: sometimes you have to go through fear and pain to see better times, some people are just awful no matter how nice you are to them, and once someone's gone, they're gone. Like all the best and truest stories, it is extremely bittersweet, equally tragic and hopeful. Just the way I like it.Sumire (the titular character, not the game) is wonderfully depicted, as are all the characters: even in spite of the relatively simple animations I couldn't help but feel her sadness. Especially considering that the relationship between my own parents is... yeah. Although perhaps even more painful than her overt sadness was Sumire trying to convince herself that she *wasn't* sad, although that does eventually turn around. If you want catharsis, you've come to the right place.And ultimately, this game serves as a good guide for getting over grief IRL: get out there, allow yourself to be vulnerable, help people out and make new connections. By making someone else's life better, you share in their happiness. There's no rule saying you can't be sad and happy at the same time.I hope you'll get as much out of this game as I did. It's definitely worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: What You Should Know Before Buying: Positives and NegativesPros:+Thought-provoking dialogue told through unpretentious conversations about big topics involving life, love, dreams, hope, and death+Captures the feeling of childlike wonder perfectly; nearly everything around you can be interacted with, and interacting with them spurs charming dialogue that builds up the characters and world+Puzzles reward you for paying attention to people and the environment+Soothing OST with incredible sound design (excellent-sounding reverb)+Hardly any loading screens in the entire gameCons:-There's not as much replay value as I'd like. I expected two different routes to the storyline depending on if you were kind or not, but the story largely remains the same with a few dialogue line changes. The ending is, however, fairly different depending on if you were kind or unkind-The storyline has some fantasy elements, and the amount of representation or explanation for these elements is very uneven. Even after experiencing both a good and bad day, I still felt there were some unanswered questions-The game is very short. My playtime reflects two playthroughs, one for a good day with near max completion of all help requests and one of a bad day. The map screen gives you the impression of the game being longer, but the final few areas are much shorter than the first half, making this impression false-One puzzle (involving the rabbit) was a bit obscure, in that I couldn't tell what actions could cause good consequences or if any action would be badAt the end of the day, you can ignore everything I said above and just know that when I took my first step outside in this game, the world felt like it opened up to me, and life could be better, richer, than I knew it before. For that feeling alone, this game is worth much more than it's asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: StorySumire tells the story of a little girl with a lot on her plate. You will follow her journey, make lots of small and big decisionsand you will witness how these decisions impact the people around her and herself.You can help those around her or focus on her goal alone. Will you seek revenge or go the path of forgiving?Will you be a helpful, kind-hearted spirit or isolate yourself and be self centered?Will you be able to face the darkness inside you? You basically need to button smash and this can lead to picking a decision you didn't want.The game autosaves after every decision, you can't make a save manually.MusicThe music really complements the game.It's soothing and compelling.And when necessary it gives you chills.It's not overpowering and really just fits.It supports the story-telling really well.I, for myself, am in love with the soundtrack.ArtThe animation definitly fits the narrativ.I liked how they went with a water color design.In my opinion it looks really nice.At times I cought myself just gazing at the backroundor just watched Sumire walking towards the screen. It's adorbale. VerdictEven with it's at times serious themes this game always found a way to make me smile and a First off you might not want to play it when you, yourself, are in a dark mindset. Otherwise:I suggest this game to everyone who likes deeper plot with dark sparks in it.But also tons of wholesame content when taking the good route. To people who want to play something simple and not too challanging. And to the ones who like to explore every inch and find every interaction. They are worth it. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing narrative experience with beautiful art style and soundtrack! Written well and the whole game has clearly been crafted by talented people and with great passion! A true hidden gem that I'm glad I bought with this year's accumulation of Steam Trading Card earnings.Sumire is an emotional story-driven 2.5D (?)  game that feels really Ghibli-esque in atmosphere. You play as a little girl with family troubles and embark on a magical journey to discover who you are as a person. There are many choices along the way that feel meaningful and impactful. As well as some minor choices that affect little things here and there. I've only played the game through once so I don't know exactly how much things would've changed if I had chosen differently in the more impactful choices, but I could see several things being completely different had I chosen otherwise.The story and narrative is written well, is loaded chock-full of emotion and keeps you hooked through the full journey. Everything from the settings to the characters are presented in a believable manner. This is especially important in a game, which tackles very heavy and deep philosophical and life issues. It's very easy to make them sound hollow or cheesy but this game makes me truly care and think about the topics that are explored. Gameplay consists mostly on normal story-driven adventure game stuff including talking to NPCs and exploring. While the game is basically a sidescrolling adventure, there's 3-dimensional depth. Though the towards/away from camera movement is often quite limited, it offers depth and a better sense of freedom and exploration than a flat 2D sidescroller would offer.Mostly you'll be traveling to left, finding points of interests, coins, sidequests or NPCs to talk to. Almost every character has an errand for you to run and you usually have at least 2 ways you can handle the request if you accept the fetch quest. Basically you can do it the nice way or some less nice way. This will affect your karma, which I will touch on a bit further down. In some cases you will not be able to complete the quest if you choose the naughty option.There are a couple of mini-games throughout the game and they are pretty cleverly tied to the narrative as the characters might converse while they are playing some mini-game. That adds to the mini-game experience and makes them more immersive in my opinion.As mentioned earlier, the game has a karma system, which is your typical Good/Evil point system. It's based on your choices. As far as I understood, the game did not require you to 100% good or evil as I was able to get an achievement for finishing the game with good karma. Despite getting bad karma at least 2 times. The evil choices were often faster solutions and seemed less of a hassle but you could choose to do things the correct way. Even if it is more troublesome.The graphics are a clever blend of 2D and 3D graphics, giving the game a unique style and depth. Paired with a vibrant watercolour painting art style and excellent art direction, There's a really great attention to detail throughout the game world. It has been crafted with much love and care, that is clear. You will see many beautiful areas and vistas along your journey. Animations are generally done really well. Though the main character's walk and run animations feel a bit off. Left and right direction animation especially. Weirdly the harder angle (towards/away from camera) angles worked better and were actually done rather well.usually these type of adventure games would use something like pixel graphics and the kinda 45 degree "top-down" angle (think RPG Maker games) and while I personally like those type of games, having the side angle with gorgeous watercolour art mixed with 3D elevates the experience and makes it look really stunning.Just simply beautiful music and soundscape. It's mostly acoustic guitars with some vocals here and there. Some more traditional japanese style music in the mix too. Every piece of music fits the scene or area it's being used and just enhances the experience tenfold. Can't find anything to complain other than maybe in few game sections the songs could've been longer and looped less.Sound effects are also on point. Fits the general style of the game perfectly.These are the kind of hidden indie gems I always hope to stumble upon. Exactly why I started the tradition of always finding one game to play on New Year's Eve that I can afford with just my steam trading card earnings for the year. It forces me to look at games I would probably normally miss. Anyone who likes well-written adventure games with a lot of heart and soul should give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of games like Ib and Yume Nikki (Dream Diary), for the setting and atmosphere. To be honest, I don't have the patience for story-heavy games anymore, but this game caught my eye and I decided to try the demo. I liked the setting and music. Couldn't stop thinking about it after the demo. So I bought it, knowing that it's only a few hours long.I was a little surprised by how much the game opens up after the demo, with more areas and side quests than I'd expected. Even some mini-games. I think this game has a good sense of world, despite its short length.There are lots of morality-based choices. For this kind of story-heavy game, I'd usually say "it would've been better as a movie/animation", but I think there are so many meaningful choices and interactive elements in this, that I feel it works better as a game.I played through the entire thing in one sitting. I'm not sure what kept me hooked, aside from the lovely music. Maybe it's because I strongly relate to many parts of the story. Or maybe because the characters are believable, interesting and well-written. Maybe it just appeals to me in all the right places.I generally avoid English localizations because they tend to be poor quality, so I played in Japanese. But I later discovered that this game originated from someone who visited Japan (ie. not a Japanese local), and that the developer team is roughly 50/50 Japanese and not. That's quite interesting. I think they did a good job.Overall, it was a nice experience and I enjoyed it. That probably means a lot coming from someone like me who can't stand 99% of modern games. Some parts were quite scary though, at a level that I think would probably traumatize children, so I'm not sure who the target audience is supposed to be.I think I'll probably replay it later just to experience the world again. But I don't think I can bring myself to pick the bad choices.Oh... one last thing. I almost didn't buy this because it advertises itself with review scores. When I'm trying to decide if I want to buy a game or not, the last thing I want to see plastered all over the game is vague numbers from random nobodies. Especially not at the end of the demo. I already finished the demo myself. I don't need review scores to tell me how to think.9/2021 edit: Still listening to the music months later. Really, really nice soundtrack. Also recently realized/remembered that Sumire is the same internet name a Japanese acquaintance used before they unexpectedly passed away in a tragic accident a few years back. So this game has added meaning for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Sumire is such a heartwarming game where we get to tag along with Sumire and her flower on a special journey that lasts just one day. And if you thought one day wasn't enough time for a game or in our busy lives, think again – this game is about to prove you wrong!Set in a charming Japanese countryside, you'll be right there with Sumire and her flower, striving to make this day absolutely perfect, just as we promised. With its stunning art style and captivating music, get ready for a rollercoaster of emotions – from happiness to anger, anger to sadness, sadness to fear... It's a complete emotional rollercoaster that we are going to be experiencing together with Sumire. During this single-day journey, you'll witness so many events that might seem a bit cheesy (like childhood crushes), or they might bring back painful memories from the past that you thought were locked away, or remind you of unfinished business that you might have left in the back of your mind. There are plenty of life events in this game that I'm sure many people can relate to, and loads of valuable life lessons to learn from it too.And on top of all the emotional journey, the game also treats us to several fun mini-games that are so well-made they could have been their own games! Sumire feels like a real hidden gem, and I absolutely recommend giving it a try if you're up for a journey filled with beautiful art, music, and life lessons.Who knows, maybe after playing this game, you'll realize that sometimes, all it takes to change our lives is just to have one perfect, courageous, and forgiving day ✨

_childDocuments_.review: Short, heartfelt, rather melancholy but with undertones of sweetness and hope - and hauntingly beautiful. These are some words that begin to describe Sumire. I wouldn't describe it as entertainment, exactly, so much as a work of art which evokes feelings in the person experiencing it.Pretentious? It may sound that way, but it can only be accurately called such if the description is not wholly accurate, yes? There is no pretense if something is actually art, actually emotional. Will it affect you? Who knows, your mileage may vary, but a lot of the themes are fairly universal so it seems likely. Do you currently need this experience? Quite possibly yes, quite possibly no. Decide for yourself.It won't be a super light experience, nor a constantly humorous one, and there is not a huge amount of gameplay besides exploring a vividly imagined world and getting to know the people and other beings who inhabit it. But if you're looking for something to make you feel things, give it a go.Lightly recommended for those who think it sounds like something they want to experience. Not so much for anyone who's already sad and/or lonely, though there is a fairly good (if slightly bittersweet) ending available - you probably won't get that if you do nasty things the whole game, so bear that in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Novel-like Interactive GameAbout 2h 8/108/10Sumire is a very short interactive novel-like game. There is not very much reading you need to do – it is fairly balanced between reading and exploration. To be honest I was a bit misled by the trailer: I thought it will be a puzzle game. However, the puzzles in this game are very simple. It’s more about talking to people and interacting with the environment.About the story: Sumire is a girl, who has lost everything.  She gets a chance to change her fate for the best or worse by doing the things she really wants to do for one day. Right, it’s basically the player’s choice how her life will play out in the future. A bit of a hard task… and in the end I chose to not finish the “worst ending”. Regarding the gameplay, you are just walking most of the time and interacting with NPCs – be it humans or animals.  There is some amount text to read in this game, but it’s not comparable to visual novels. Usually, it’s only a short dialogue between the main character and the NPC and it also depends on whether you choose to interact with the NPC or not. However, the dialogue is not skippable. The best you can do is set the text speed on the highest setting and spam “c”, but for me it still got a bit annoying (on my third playthrough). Plus, the game is kind of “forgiving” means you can’t get the bad ending if you have at least done one good deed. And no quick save options available either, so if you mess things up you have to replay the whole thing. Honestly, even though the whole not skippable part kind of annoyed me, I found the game to be overall enjoyable. It feels more like a “rough diamond” than a jewel though – the ideas were nice, but the delivery was a bit lacking. Sumire is in no way a bad game, but I felt something was missing. It felt like things were left undone, even though in the game they were “done”. I disliked also the impact of some of the things. It felt somehow like the world is black and white in this game:  All in all, I felt like multiple situations were “unsatisfying” and a bit childish. The whole game gives off a childish vibe like it is especially written for children because the solutions to the situations seem so simple (well, duh, Sumire is a kid though). I’d wish that the game had dealt with those situations more seriously though.All in all, while this game was enjoyable, it still gets an 8/10 from me because I was not satisfied with some parts of it. Lastly, my favourite part of the game:  I think this is a very valuable lesson for everyone out there because usually people tend to regret especially these things.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect this game to make me bawl my eyes out.The game doesn't even lay it on that thick with the emotions, but it tells it's story in such a believable and relatable way, it just hit me in the right places it seems.Sumire is a game about moving on and letting go of your anger, asking yourself what it means to be friends and deciding what you want your family to be.You play as the titular Sumire, a girl with a broken family and no friends, who suddenly finds a magic, talking flower one day.The Flower wants you to make it's day a special one, as it only gets to live for one day, in turn encouraging Sumire to take steps towards deciding on what she wants to do about all the loose ends she's left in her life.Will you make up with a past friend or will you hurt them like they did to you?These are the choices you will have to make and which will decide how Sumire's life will look like after the day is over.The gameplay is very simple, as it consists mainly of walking around the gorgeous town and it's various points of interest, meeting a bunch of cute animals and characters and helping them out with what troubles them if you want to.Even though this is pretty casual i did enjoy it a lot and with a short play time of 2-3 hours i think this is the perfect length to not get dull.A lot of praise also goes to the art of Sumire.I thought the game looked pretty okay in the screenshots here, but it looks so much better when playing in my opinion. The backgrounds are especially, gorgeous.The only thing standing out is some of the character animations looking a bit stiff, but that doesn't really detract from the overall pretty visuals.The soundtrack also is so much better than i would have expected.Each area has it's own theme and each is such a joy to listen to.I could just stand around admiring a new area and vibing to the music for a little while.All in all, i highly recommend you check out Sumire if you've got 2-3 hours to kill and enjoy emotional, story driven games.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much. I'm feeling very emotional right now having finished the game. I'm going through a difficult time in my life and my family is going through a difficult time, and this game has helped me to process and attend to my emotions, and helped me to bring a compassionate and gentle light on the dark and difficult situations I am going through. Oh, and I loved how this game explored darkness, anger, hatred, pain, fear. The game expressed something I experience - negative emotions, anger, darkness - without shaming it, and without making it easier, and it helped me to have compassion towards that while also seeing the way to heal.

_childDocuments_.review: Short but very sweet.  A touching game that really tugs at the heartstrings.  I finished it in around 5 hours, but it was the perfect amount of time to tell the story.With a talking flower at her side, it has a magical feel, yet deals with real world emotions of mourning, loss, grief, courage, and hope.  In a way that doesn't seem preachy.  Sumire is a young girl learning to navigate the world despite losing everything, and you may discover a little bit of your own magic along the way.There are a bunch of optional side quests that yield helpful rewards, and in certain places you have a choice whether to do good or ill.  Some may affect the outcome of the game (I haven't tried, I find it difficult to purposefully play Darkside, to use SW parlance) but it helps you empathize with Sumire.You also don't have more than one save slot so - just like life - you have to live with the consequences of your actions (unless you re-start from the beginning).I found everything about the game to be quite lovely, from the graphics where the background moves smoothly as you stay at the centre of the screen, to the vibrant, and sometimes gloomy characters who inhabit Sumire's world.  And Sumire herself, whose expressions changed depending on the situation.I highly recommend this game to anyone who is dealing with loss (you may cry a little, but in a good way), or simply wants to play a game with beautiful graphics and a heartfelt story.  ^-^

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think there is anything I can say about this game that has not already been said in other more eloquent reviews for this game. Frankly I just want to give this game one more thumbs up among the thousands more that it truly deserves. This is one of the most beautiful experiences I have had playing games in 2021. The look of the game is so lush and vibrant, it's like jumping into a watercolor painting that swirls endlessly around you. The soundtrack jumps from catchy and smile-inducing to solemn and introspective. The storyline is simple enough that anyone can follow it but deep enough to really awaken an emotion in anyone who ponders its themes. More important than anything, this game made me feel something real. That every day we live is a lifetime of opportunity. That you always need to say what you have in your heart because you never know when it will be too late. I care for Sumire, and I wish the best for that little girl. If you want something to sink into for a few hours, or just need a good cry, please buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent story, art, and music all coming together with great characterization that tells so much in such a short amount of time.  Was a bittersweet experience that I don't want to go into without revealing story elements, but if you're ok with that (and I get a kick out of that type of stuff) then I recommend trying it out.I don’t usually play visual novels, I don’t much like the walking simulators I’ve played, graphic adventures can keep my attention with the puzzles.  Sumire is very graphic-adventure lite, so it better have an amazing story to captivate me.  Well the story, the mood, the writing and dialog get a strong endorsement from me.  The music, just seems to fit, as if someone is reading the room and playing an instrument as you’re progressing, it’s not something I see in games much compared to some passive media where the scene and pacing is controlled.  To add to that, it’s very cohesive across tracks, flowing from one to another perfectly throughout the entire playthrough.Now getting into the story, I enjoyed it, I don’t want to alter someone’s expectations going into it, so I’ll leave it at that.  However, once I finished the game, I looked at my playtime of 2.7 hours and was surprised, I thought 4 hours had passed, it was so dense in delivery with character exposition.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, it's bittersweet, it's sad - but uplifting. A really moving story that might bring you to tears. Beautiful art and cutscenes with a dynamic soundtrack including some vocals that set a strong mood. Treat the price of admission like a movie ticket for a double feature film and you'll have no buyer's remorse if you're worried about the playtime. I think the game was the perfect length for what it was and the story it wanted to tell. The bonus card game is pretty fun too. The extra character interactions you get during it are nice. I'm so glad I found this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: An  absolutely lovely game about love, chances and about moving on. Love the artwork and music - breathtaking!  Trasnslation / writing? Could use a little more polish but it's a thoroughly lovely game with good premise. I care for the characters and the story. It's just beautiful1 Even the credits are wonderful, so warm-hearted. A game with a heart! Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Sumire is a beautiful game, and I mean that in every sense it’s possible to interpret that phrase. It looks wonderful, it sounds amazing, it tells a delightful story through some exquisitely written dialogue… and it will grab hold of your heartstrings and tug like there’s no tomorrow until you are an emotional wreck of a human being.I knew the game was going to be something special when I had the good fortune to try its demo in the Steam Game Festival back in February of 2021. And I was delighted to discover, upon playing the full version, that the final product not only met, but exceeded my expectations considerably. This game is an absolute work of art, and should be considered an absolute must-play if you have the slightest interest in narrative-centric games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: WoW..... It's been so long since i really played a great heart felt game that teaches about life when you become blind in your ever day tasks. The scenes are just pure beautiful, the text could be a little bit better but i knew what they were saying, The music is wonderful.For me i give this a 9/10. Just because of the art, the music but most importantly the impact it shows within about life. if you love 2D Adventure games with a great story line then i highly suggest it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review: Sumire is a short but beautiful game by its cute art, amazing ost and its touching story. The story is the main point of the game, they're many moment where you can make some mistake without realise it and you will sometimes feel guilty afterwards. Sumire was a memorable and unique experience and I recommend this game at everyone !
_childDocuments_.name: Sumire

_childDocuments_.review:
One Day, One Life. Embark on a mysterious journey to help Sumire achieve her deepest wishes, before the day ends and the sky turns to twilight. Sumire is an indie narrative adventure, featuring a one-day journey through a picturesque Japanese village. In this enchanted place, a disenchanted girl named Sumire meets a mischievous spirit who makes her a deal to fulfill her most desired wish.

name: Operation: Tango
detailed_description: FRIEND PASS About the Game Join our Discord Server NOTES: - This game is online co-op only and requires a microphone. - Thanks to the Friend Pass, any of your friends can play with you for free. - Cross-platform play enabled Operation: Tango is an espionage-themed cooperative adventure challenging you and a friend to complete dangerous missions across the globe in a high-tech near-future world. As an exclusive team of two, you and your partner will become AGENT and HACKER, working in tandem to bring a high-tech global menace to its knees. With only your voice to link you, teamwork is crucial, and communication is key! Now with a FREE CONTENT UPDATE - The Challenge mode introduces a new area to explore, new puzzles to solve, and new robots to hack. Game features: CO-OP PUZZLE SOLVING - Combine skill sets from different points of view to overcome challenges focused on communication, not difficulty. These missions cannot be completed alone. THRILLING ESPIONAGE - Investigate, hack and infiltrate while executing missions across the globe. Live out your ultimate “Hollywood” spy fantasy! HI-TECH TOOLS - Experience the visual splendor and technological advances of a hyper-connected world built around augmented reality. FRIENDLY BANTER - Constant communication makes for both heartfelt and hilarious moments. It’s all about sharing your voice. Multiplayer options: FRIEND PASS - If you own Operation: Tango, any of your friends can play with you for free. All they need to do is download the Operation: Tango Friend Pass on their platform of choice. It takes two to save the world, but it only takes one to pay for it. CROSS-PLATFORM PLAY - Operation: Tango can be played with a person who’s not playing on the same platform as you. It just works.

As fun as the core gameplay is, I can't really recommend a game that we can't finish because of serve issues.

_childDocuments_.review: SO FUN! Man what a great and well-executed concept. Had a fantastic time solving puzzles, racing timers, and cooperating to overcome some initially daunting challenges! Multiple times I found myself amazed at how interesting and different the missions were. I hope they add more, but in the meantime I'm looking forward to playing it again!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: They seem to have CORRECTED their regional pricing (increase of price in my currency) and I would say the amount offered is not polished nor does it have enough for the price requested. There are definitely better games out there for even less the price here. As of now, no new features, characters or missions available. The friend pass is great, but this being 2 player ONLY, it's required. Put the price back to what it was and maybe it's worth it if you have EXTRA cash lying around. If not, prioritize better games. No changes have been made regarding some features that can make it better, more interactive or more exciting as of yet.Loved the game, needs more missions. The devs had just pumped out the patches for the bugs as we were playing, so unfortunately we had to download the patch and restart the last mission. I think it's completely bug free as of now. It's great because your friend can play for free with the friend pass. It has so many puzzles so communication will be key in this game. Without the restarts maybe the game would be around 4 hours more or less in one playthrough. Maybe 6-7 if you play through it again with reversed roles. I would really appreciate it if they had extra missions that are perhaps free? These could be side missions not related to the main plot or some missions that help with intel gathering or recon.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well polished though short co-op game (it took my friend and I about four hours to complete the campaign once).  The challenge mode presumably gives it some more replay value though we haven't dove into that yet, and of course swapping roles and playing again would effectively double the play time.  The presentation/visual style is distinct and fun and the "hacking" has some very inventive mini games that avoid a lot of the stale and repetitive "hacking" simulation cliches that have pervaded gaming for decades now so kudos to the devs for being able to put a new spin on it.The fact that it has a friend pass means you don't have to talk someone else into buying it which is a great feature, though be aware a player using a friend pass won't unlock any achievements so if that's a big deal to them they should buy it.If you're looking for a co-op game with a different spin than just another shooter I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely fun coop game! Some glitchiness, but I didn't experience anything game-breaking in the two full playthroughs I completed. Despite some slight variation in puzzle solutions, there's not much replayability after you've completed the game with both roles. You  play again with a different person, but then it becomes an awkward situation where you're just staying silent while the other player figures out their side of the puzzle. I'd absolutely love to see more missions, either as free updates or DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Among asymmetrical co-op games in which two people with different roles attempt to work together, Operation Tango is by far the best implementation by far. Yes, as you'll read in other reviews as well, it is fairly short (2-3 hours), but make no mistake, these are quality hours.It's impossible to review this genre without referencing Keep Talking, so let's get it out of the way. This is the better game. Keep talking is fine, simple, and streamlined, but the variety of puzzles, challenges, and new ways you and a friend will have to communicate data, ideas, and other information keeps the game fresh throughout the entire 2-3 hours. In essence, Keep Talking is one very well designed level while Operation Tango is many well designed levels. The two roles are so vastly different that I found particular enjoyment when I watched another set of friends attempt the same puzzle but from the opposite side.Beyond that the artwork and world building are solid, making it a pleasant experience visually.I believe we'll continue to see evolution in the asymmetric co-op experience, but at the time of writing this and having played (to my knowledge) all the previous PC games with this mechanic, Operation: Tango is the current leader and a must play for anyone looking to be challenge their friendships in what ultimately amounts to a trust exercise taken to extreme limits.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun to play with your partner.  Some replay value repeating the missions in the other role (coupled with "OH, THAT'S WHY YOU WERE CONFUSED" when you see the other point of view)Would love to see more content and missions, though.  We finished the main story twice in around 7-8 hours with the second play through in the other role that went much faster. We found the visual style beautifully done, with great sound.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Such a big thumbs up for the developers, it's insanely fun and addicting.. It's just wayyy too short and you're expected to spend around 5 hours together in only 6 different levels, since they're really hard to complete, so without a good communication and a partner, it can easily turn into a couples nightmare video game..Me and my bf played it through and enjoyed it to the max, the puzzles and the story, bonus is the friends pass, so you don't have to spend 30€ for two copies to play it, it's 17€ for both so 8€ for each is a fair and understandable price.. You can play as both sides after your first playthrough so that can add up to the play time, it's just not gonna be as much fun since you will have an idea of what to do and it does not replaces the lack of content (more levels).. But yea, maybe I can't expect every game to be replayable many times with hundreds of hours of playtime..
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

That's the only thing. And please, if you learn anything from this game and manage to make another I'd be VERY interested in seeing what this studio can make.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those asymmetric co-op games where you should not see the other person's screen, and are meant to communicate clearly in order to make it through.The game does a great job at changing up the puzzles, so you're always doing something different and interesting. Sometimes some puzzles are recycled and built upon, but every level feels fresh for the most part.Both roles are equally fun and have moments to shine throughout.The game is quite short. We beat it in about 4 hours. The asking price is quite cheap to begin with though, which is good. I feel it's worth the asking price. There are some super memorable moments if you enjoy co-op games.Although we didn't find the game that difficult, the game comes with a hint system. At any point in time, you can both agree to see a hint for the puzzle you're working on. That's something I appreciated, as it eliminates the need for an external walkthrough. Overall though, we found the difficulty to be just right.We didn't run into any bugs throughout our playthrough, except the final level. It broke on us 3 times, and we were wondering if we were just missing something, or if it was glitched. Upon restarting the game, the issues were fixed every time. Still, frustrating.In the end, if you have a friend and enjoy games like Keep talking and nobody explodes,  Exorcise the Demons, or We were here, this is a strong recommendation! A super fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely great, I had 5 awesome hours with it with my friend, both roles are super fun, I hope they keep adding missions and new ways to play, maybe some more variation in the variables of the puzzle? it was a bit similar the second time around, but all around, excellent co-op experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, it's very fun, it's creative, it has memorable moments, and it's especially good when you want to put your communication skills to the test.But... I just had MAJOR issues.SPOILERS AHEAD:In my most recent playthrough with a friend, we managed to get softlocked TWICE.In the forth mission, where the agent has to open a gateway to let the hacker through, the "open" button loads really quickly before letting you actually opening the door.We failed, because my friend didn't know how quickly he fell, so we restarted, upon restarting, the Open button was stuck PERMANENTLY loading, so we couldn't open the door no matter how long we waited, we even tried killing ourselves again to try and fix it, but it didn't work. It was frustrating, because of how deep the point in the mission is, it just wasted time.In the final mission, where you go through a hotel to find the cords for the bomb, the game EXPLICITLY told me where the cords were, but the little screens didn't show us the cords, so we couldn't even get past the EASY part of the mission.I played this game multiple times and NEVER had these issues until last night and the time this review is up, which is heartbreaking because I LOVE this game to bits, but I can't in good conscious recommend a game that has these recent bugs.Until these bugs are fixed, I can't recommend a game, even if it is fantastic.But hey, maybe I'm alone here, you'll probably never have these issues come up, hence why I'm posting this as a positive review.Provided you don't have my experience, this is probably some of the most fun you'll have with a friend recently.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Quite fun asymmetric co-op game. If a little short... Only 6 missions, which is maybe 5 hours playtime, plus time trials mode postgame. One player plays the hacker, using computer UI. Occasionally you end up in first-person in a virtual world representation of the computer systems you're hacking.One player plays the agent, in first-person view, infiltrating places to execute missions.You can switch roles between every mission if you want to.Both players seek to gain info and gain access to the next area, and deal with emergencies that crop up. A voice call is required since you will be passing information back and forth constantly.(You do not have to buy two copies of the game.)The story and setting is this world where everyone is hooked into technology in a deep way, and the cybercrimes you have to stop are nuanced at first, growing to become outlandish. The game also pulls out absurd techno logic, like being able to download a physical EMP grenade that your partner sends to you over the net. It's all outlandish and absurd in a way that hit my partner's funny bone in the right way.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great and I had a blast playing it. The concept is straightforward; complete the task given to you. The difficult and fun bit is relaying information in a way that is fast and efficient and seeing what comes next. The levels also have a slight ability to replay them and have a different experience, as you can play them as hacker or agent. The only downside is that there are 6 levels and that's it. If they add more levels that would be great, and if not I feel that it would be wasted opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great game ! But my god is it short, only 6 missions is a real shame ! I played this game with my best friend and we had so much fun switching between the 2 characters every mission, we were very sad when we finished the game after only 4 hours of chill gameplay. If you want a fun, short, puzzle-solving thanks to communication game : I recommend you giving it a try If you're addicted to escape games, puzzle solving all night long, looking for clues and ways to get to the end goal : maybe this game is a bit of a waste of money

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is a great game to play with a friend or family member! The asymmetric aspect is interesting and makes communication an integral part of this game. I had a great time playing it and would definitely recommend it to others. However, it is a fairly short game. In the 3.6 hours I have played so far, I have gone through the game once, with a couple levels played again. I would love to see more content for Operation Tango, but it doesn't feel unfinished now.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: My review system works with a 10 point score. 0 = bad and 10 = good.I have 5 criteria on which I decide. Each can give 0 - 2 points.Below that I will explain my decisions.Operation Tango is the type of game this world needs far more of!Honestly, I haven't had this much fun playing a coop game with friends in a long while.Every level of the game has its unique and tricky puzzles which are perfectly in balance between not too easy to be boring but also not too hard to be frustrating. Also, the game actually makes you feel like the two people playing really depend on one another.The whole game has a toon-ish style which is perfectly matched with the graphics and sound design. Both give you a feeling like "The Incredibles" film. And the best thing is you can experience each level twice. Unlike other coop games, choosing one of the two characters really makes it a completely different experience.Story wise, the game is nothing special. But what the devs  did, they did good. It's funny, straight to the point, and it was all I needed.In my opinion, Operation Tango is a must-play for every coop lover, and I would gladly pay for more content. So grab a good friend, buy this game and enjoy a good time!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game but VERY short. 6 missions plus a challenge mode but there's some replayability since you can play each mission from either the Agent or the Hacker's perspective. _childDocuments_.review: This is really neat co-op game! My only gripe is I have weird bugs for some reason (cutscenes won't play for me, or game completely freezing). Otherwise, the gameplay is really cool, and def fun to play with friends :). You and your buddy take the role of a hacker or field agent and play the game through that perspective. I played through with the hacker for my first run.The hacker acts as a support for the field agent in carrying out missions, but sometimes as the hacker you fly or run around in a "Tron"/cyberspace type world. But on the whole the gameplay is really fun and engaging.I intend on doing another run as the field agent this time but, yeah, I definitely recommend this game! I got this with my Humble Monthly but, worth to pick up otherwise too IMO
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This will likely serve as more of a PSA than a review: Because purely in a gameplay sense, Operation Tango is definitely one of the highest quality "Hacker + Infiltrator" Coop games I've played. Lot of varying interactions required between players, minigame reuse is fairly rare, and each of the levels have wildly varying styles and objectives to them. The Hacker side has got to be the best visualization of the role in any game of this genre (Of which there are very few, to be fair) I've played. It's fast to navigate, completely changes depending on the context of each mission, and often goes as far as entering full first person control for some puzzles. It's a significant improvement over the usual 2D, lazily designed menu driven gameplay that the majority of games like this provide.But that's unfortunately where the praise ends, because we couldn't make it any further than Mission 3.The online for this game is utterly . My coop partner and I are in the same building, on the same local network. And yet from the moment we even started the tutorial, we were sitting at an average ping of 200ms. It fluctuated wildly throughout our entire experience, often spiking to highs of . The game was still somewhat playable, but desyncs in minigames became very irritating.But the final nail in the coffin was the full Disconnects for no reason. In only 80 minutes of play, we fully lost connection no less than 9 times. No fault with our internet or connection, the game just dropped us. The levels are generous with their checkpoints, but it was still frustrating getting instantly booted back to the menu constantly. And when four of those times were midway through a timed sequence of puzzles without checkpoints, we had to give it up.I can see a lot of positive reviews around, which shows that most were able to have a good experience. But we have Gigabit Ethernet throughout our house and decent internet: None of this is our own connection's fault. I can only expect that the developers only have a single set of servers in one region, and your experience will depend entirely on whether you're close to it or not. The Community Forums also have several topics from people suffering with ping issues.It's extremely disappointing, because from what we did play, the game is really fun and clearly well made. We were genuinely disappointed that we had to stop! But in the end we just couldn't play any further, the servers are inadequate.I'd say you could check the Demo to see how it'd perform, but it seems that the levels cause more network issues the further you go... Buy it cheap on sale, and be prepared to refund if you get a bad connection.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Tried the demo with a friend and we both really enjoyed it.We bought the game and played it start to finish non stop when it released today. Had a lot of fun, a few minor desync issues which were easily fixed with a restart. My PC bluescreened during play (not because of the game) and we were delighted to find that the game had saved a checkpoint very close to where we were in the level. This seems to be a consistent feature which is something I would like to see in more AAA games.All in all a great puzzle game for you and a friend! 10/10, would play again
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great execution of the asymmetric co-op.  Every task feels very rewarding when you manage to complete it.  Also loving the way the pricing structure works with being able to send a friend pass to someone so you can play with any friend you want without them needing to purchase a copy of the game themselves.  Simple yet cool visuals. 10/10 would 100% recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna say I recommend this game because it's a bunch of fun with a friend, and the two-sided gameplay works really well. The one downside is the length: in my playtime both my friend and I have both cleared 100% of the achievements in the game, including playing through as both roles.So yeah, players: if you think you'll enjoy the game, definitely recommended. It *seems* simple — and it teeechnically is — but the simplicity stacks up very fast.Buy this for yourself and your best friend, now.  Seriously.  Do it now.P.S.  Communication and knowing your teammate's style are key.P.P.S.  Dear, Clever Plays...  Thank you.  You deserve medals and playful condemnation for this creation.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent 2 player co-op game. You and your partner take on 2 asymmetric roles: Hacker and Field Agent. Hacker is mostly dealing with an informational interface and helping the Field Agent navigate obstacles. The Field Agent role primarily involves a first person view and moving around in the 3D world.Each task involves communicating information not available to the other in order to complete the puzzle. With several tasks requiring coordinated and timely actions, which are typically the most difficult. Tasks range from Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes type bomb defusal, to solving a maze or cross-referencing criminal information across different databases.Pros:- heavily communication based, no progression without teamwork, exactly how a co-op should be.- failure will reset the team back to the last checkpoint (no more than 1 minute of lost time)- on point old-school spy aesthetic- lovely visuals- 100% replayable as the other agentCons:- a little short (completed one role in ~5 hours)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great time with a friend. You both work together to solve a variety of puzzles, some shamelessly taken from other games. It was a blast the entire time! But, it is so short it only took me and my friend 3 hours to beat. At 20$ you could buy a more robust co-op game on the market. Granted only one player needs to buy it but I would say this game is worth 10$ for the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Game was pretty fun.My friend and I always enjoy playing these co-op only games (We were here, A Way Out, It Takes Two, Tick-Tock, etc) and this one was honestly really good, if only for a very short period of time.We were able to do a full playthrough as both characters for 100% in about 5 hours.There are a few bugs to be aware of which definitely extended this time and frustrated us the first go around.Specifically in mission 5 we noticed  of desync, and not ones that could be worked around. A puzzle where one us us had to control horizontal movement and the other vertical had the indicator in the completely wrong spot for one player, and on multiple occasions the code we had to input just registered as straight up wrong unless we closed to desktop.Luckily the missions do have checkpoints at points, so loading back in to try again when something like this happened wasn't really a hassle, just a minor annoyance.All around, definitely worth the price, more so if you choose to go halvsies with a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a light "Recommend" for me, because the game is honestly amazing and fun - but it's just so short, that it's genuinely hard to recommend the 20$ price tag on it. I'll be taking my second playthrough with a friend to complete the other "Half", but the game is pretty easy to complete in a single evening. You're going to have a few times where you might feel a lack of direction from the game - but that's part of the fun of doing these sorts of puzzle games. The communication needed is on point, and it's never too complex to the point of being unable to properly coordinate information to one another. Whenever a timer appears, you feel the pressure, but it's never too much to easily overcome, and the checkpoint system and retries make it genuinely forgiving. I wouldn't mind a challenge mode for achievements to complete each mission in an Ironman-style mode to do it in one try. I give it a recommend because even at 20$, it's still fun. I just wish it was longer, and getting hit with what felt like an advertisement for more games at the end felt a little bit frustrating learning there wasn't another set of missions. Both of us said, in unison, "That's it?" when we realised there wasn't more to come. You'll have fun when you're playing, and ultimately, that's going to leave you dissapointed at the end when there just isn't enough 'meat' to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you Clever Plays for the friend pass system. Other devs *please* take this approach going forward. I want to play your indie 2 player coop game, but convincing another player to buy a game just so they can play it with you is frequently a deal breaker. Operation Tango is good evening's worth of entertainment, but it is just that. The game is short, it took me about 45 mins per mission and there are 6 missions. There is no replay value here, it's a one and done deal. However, for your money, you are getting a fun, stylish asymmetric coop puzzle game, dense with variety and invention. The game throws a new mini puzzle at you every few seconds with minimal repetition. The focus is on keeping forward momentum going and minimising frustration, so the puzzles are relatively easy and checkpoints are plentiful. If Clever Plays continue this format with a sequel or DLC I will be back.

_childDocuments_.review: clocks in at about 6 hours of play (I see many others completed it in around 4 hours, so maybe we're just slow). There's a lot of great asymmetrical co-op fun to be had here, with one person playing the field agent, infiltrating and navigating various locations, and the other playing "the guy in the chair", hacking systems and databases and helping the agent get where she needs to be. As is typical of the genre, patience and communication are key.What's nice for a change is that the hacker role gets to do some limited first person action in the form of a virtual environment he has to navigate to achieve various goals. It's a nice change of pace from a strictly supportive role.Absolutely minor pet peeve: IP addresses that are out of valid ranges. They did  on this for the first half of the game that we actually commented on how refreshing it was, but then out of the blue all the ranges went wacky and into the high hundreds. Oh, well.There was also one puzzle in particular that didn't make a lot of logical sense, but we figured out the gist of it even if it seemed less puzzle and more arbitrary hunting. It was a little unimaginative, but again, that's a minor quibble in an otherwise high quality game.Overall,  is a fun entry that I can easily recommend. _childDocuments_.review: Some co-op games are about telling stories. Operation Tango is about solving puzzles. Each one beautifully veiled as a high-tech caper, where one player hides behind a computer terminal as a hacker, while the other infiltrates. Both have very different experiences and entry points, and are wholly dependent on the other’s skillset. Often, the challenge here is to correlate intel from two different points of views into something that makes sense. Like the hacker looking at a solitary PIN-code, but nowhere to punch it in until the other guy discovers a code panel. Information won’t always make sense to you alone, so sharing it will more often than not result in some collective -moments where all the disparate pieces suddenly click in place. In a way, it’s a game all about talking. Or at least one that highly encourages it, and recognizes how important dialogue is for cooperative play. The missions themselves are pretty compact and to the point, usually with a gimmick or theme running through them. One mission sees you identifying targets on a train based on the apps they’ve installed on their phone. Another might have you sneaking around, dodging flying sentries as you triangulate the position of a bomb. None of them feel derivative, or even like they emerged from a common blueprint. Highly recommended if you enjoy solving challenges with a friend, and love games like Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes.

_childDocuments_.review: A casual co-op puzzle game following a pair of agents on their quest to apprehend a cyber-criminal.In Operation: Tango, you and a partner take on the role of either Angel, a spy infiltrating various field locations, and Alistair, a hacker providing support through the use of various technology, respectively. You're given various missions, tasking you with snooping out locations and extracting intel without being caught. All missions are connected by a light story, which does a decent job at setting up a spy thriller setting, but is too vague and basic to be a driving force for playing.On every mission, each player is given distinct tasks, which build on one another and most of the time require teamwork to complete. Just like the missions overall, these activities are quite varied, providing an engaging experience throughout the game's runtime without much repetition. The main challenge of these tasks is found in understanding what has to be done and effectively communicating with each other, with things rarely becoming difficult to solve.Overall, Operation: Tango does a decent job at keeping both players busy throughout, which I very much appreciated. Given the very different natures of both characters' activities, the game also lends itself very well to being replayed with switched roles. Providing further replayability beyond this is a challenge mode, in which your given training missions much smaller in scope to those found in the main campaign. These challenge you with competing them in a set amount of time, making things a bit more tense and giving an opportunity for high score hunting.As for its presentation, Operation: Tango goes for rather cartoonish visuals, with flat textures, simple models and overall exaggerated features like proportions. Shading is used to great effect, with the game managing a good-looking and genuinely atmospheric look. Sound-wise, the game comes with some decent if not too memorable background music as well as similarly average sound design, both of which fit in well.In conclusion, I enjoyed my time with Operation: Tango. While it's not exceptional on any level, it provides a good co-op experience that's great fun with a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. Was really interested in it because of the premise of needing to cooperate with another person similar to A Way Out or It Takes Two but only needing one copy so its easy to get my friends to play with me. The game is definitely on the short side, me and a friend where able to complete one play through in roughly 3 hours making a bunch of mistakes on the way. That is only one time through as one of the characters so at the bare minimum, we plan to play again switching roles.I can definitely see this as a good game to play with someone you might want to introduce to gaming in a way that isn't too terribly overwhelming. _childDocuments_.review: Operation: Tango is an asymmetrical co-op game (similar to a game like We Were Here) where one player plays as an agent and the other as a hacker, and you must communicate with each other to progress through the game. I generally found the missions to be interesting and challenging, with parts of one or two missions being a bit unclear what you were supposed to do (even after having completed it as both the agent and hacker!). There are 6 missions and 10 challenges, with the missions taking about 6-7 hours to complete, and the challenges taking 3-4 hours to complete at the highest level. The game's overall aesthetic and UI is nice, and I enjoyed the music. I personally think the price is a little steep, though only one person needs to own the game (the other person can use a friend's pass to join) and 10 hours to complete the entire game is a decent amount of game time. Therefore, if you can get it on sale, I think it is worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright listen up folks. This game? This game right here? Think of it as Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes' next evolutionary step. This is a game of high intensity scenarios where you and a good friend are gonna scream, laugh, and bust your ass for hours. The game itself only needs one copy to be played which means send your pal 10 bucks, split that game 50/50 and get yo self some co-op spy action. The premise is you and your friend are two top tier spies, one a legendary hacker, the other a daredevil boots on the ground professional. You use your words (usually poorly) to try to solve a series of different puzzles in order to save the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ world. Is it cheesy? ♥♥♥♥ yeah, and that makes it all the more fun to roleplay and ♥♥♥♥ around in. There are plenty of parts you can just do something stupid and screw over your partner for a laugh, and others where your blood is pumping so fast you forget that you're supposed to be listening. It's short but I imagine there will be more content in the future and even if not I got 3.5 hours of gameplay out of just trying the hacker out. I assume knowing the tasks a little bit will make the next run through a bit shorter, but it probably ends up being about 5-6 hours with one of your best pals for a nice 50/50 split of $20, which to me is plenty worth it for the memories and the fun you're gonna have. _childDocuments_.review: DON'T WAIT TO BUY THIS GAME.I didn't think three hours could go by in the blink of an eye like it did. What drew me to this game first was the art style and the concept of having to communicate with another person but not being able to see what they are seeing. I bought the game but didn't have anyone to play it with for a long while until a good friend of mine said they'd be interested! We both stream on twitch, so we got together, went live and now have 3 hours of memories to go back and laugh at again. I was laughing so hard I was in stitches!! We anxiously tried to communicate with each other while facing countdowns to death. Can you communicate the exact time to simultaneously hit a button while under pressure? Or move the same object together from afar? What about describe how a shape looks so innately that they can pick the right one and clear that goal. So much to pay attention to, so much to describe, and the music is amazing to boot!We've only played through 4 missions so far, and I don't know how many are left, but I'm so excited to be able to play with them again and laugh that hard. 13/10 you should get this game!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the  not too long ago, I ended up developing a crave for more short co-op experiences. This brought me to  an asymmetrical co-op game where one person plays as an agent and the other plays as a hacker. It looked like an expanded version of  and that's essentially what it is, although it's far from perfect in execution.I like the style of this game quite a lot. The HUD design in particular is a highlight, as it's slick and it's very easy to keep track of what's going on. I also really like how the story of the game is presented in a comic book style, which really helps maintain the classic spy feel the game is going for. The environments and character designs aren't anything to write home about, but I still liked them well enough. More than anything though, this game succeeded in establishing the feel it was going for, and that was probably the most important part here.I had a ton of fun with this game. At the time of writing this, I've only played through the game as an agent, but I had a lot of fun with her. My friend, who played the hacker, also really enjoyed the game, so it seems that both characters are very fun to play either way. It's a fairly casual experience, and not one that's taken too seriously. You're given plenty of opportunities to screw your partner over and it made the game significantly funnier as a result. I found the puzzles, which make up the bulk of the game, pretty enjoyable overall, although I do think a couple towards the end were repetitive and presented in an overly-complex fashion despite having a simple solution. I found the game was at its best during the train mission where you had to identify a terrorist among the passengers () and the "heist" mission where you need to identify a suspect by cross-referencing information between you and your partner. There were a few points where I felt the agent was just a hacker-lite, and simply had to "hack" things on the ground, which I found slightly disappointing, but missions like the ones I mentioned were great examples of striking a balance between the two characters and giving each person time to shine through their distinct roles and the other missions were still pretty fun and unique in their own right. I think the big issue, however, are some of the technical issues we experienced in our playthrough. We ended up being softlocked multiple times during the playthrough, and we had to restart the game multiple times in order to fix them, and it was especially frustrating at certain points because we couldn't tell if it was part of the puzzle or an actual glitch. Thankfully, restarting the game didn't mean restarting the mission, and we were brought right back to where we were when reloading our game, which definitely made the issues a little more tolerable. Overall, the game was fun to play and did what it set out to do. It didn't really exceed expectations (outside of the train and heist missions), but it's still a good time either way and I was pretty happy with it.The story isn't anything to write home about. It's your typical "stop a terrorist and save the world" affair that doesn't really try to do anything unique with it, but I do appreciate that they let the story take a backseat for most of the game (only ever being brought up during brief dialogue bits or cutscenes in between missions), since the appeal of the game was just doing cool spy stuff with your friend. And occasionally deleting them from the system while they're trying to hack something.  If nothing else, it has charm, and it works for what it is.Again, just like the story, it's passable. There's absolutely nothing notable here, from the music, to the voice acting, to the sound design, but it never really got in the way of anything. I have nothing else to say here.Where I think  really falters, however, is in the content value, and that's mainly because this game is way too short. I finished it in a little over 4 hours, and that's considering the time I spent restarting the game and struggling through puzzles because I'm terrible at them. I normally don't mind shorter experiences, but there's so much potential in the gameplay loop they've created that only having six missions that take around 30 minutes (and upwards of 60 minutes for the last few missions) each was definitely a little disappointing. I hope the developers find time to add more levels, because I think there's still plenty of room for more content. It's not all bad, as there's definitely a little replay value in playing as the other character, though I'm unsure of the extent to how randomized puzzle solutions are. For $20, I think the price works if you and your friend split the price and each pay $10, but otherwise it might be safer to wait for a small discount for this one. At least you only need to purchase it once! That's a big plus no matter how you look at it.Overall, I enjoyed my time with  It's not an absolutely stellar experience, but I had a lot of fun navigating through different puzzles and timed situations, and it will definitely scratch your co-op game itch. There's a ton of potential in a sequel or DLC, if the folks at Clever Plays decide to go that route, but what's here is still a very fun and charming experience, even if it's a little too short and a little too buggy. - 7.5/10 - 8.5/10 - 7.0/10 - 6.0/10 - 6.0/10+ Charming art style+ HUD design looks great+ Very fun gameplay loop+ Only needs to be purchased once to play with a friend- Game-breaking technical issues- Extremely short- Agent feels  underutilized

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game for 4.5hrs of playtime (100% - pre-challenge update, see note below), I wish there were additional levels or more dynamic changes of challenges within a level to support more replay-ability. Due to the friendpass concept (which I hope other games adapt), I'm willing to argue that $10 per person for almost 5 hours of fun is worth it, but I would recommend waiting for a sale.This game has the same exact feel of Blackhat Cooperative (VR game), a hacker/infiltrator co-op style game, but has much nicer graphics (granted it doesnt support VR) and a more defined storyline. Once I did the storyline as one role my friend and I re-did the campaign in opposite roles, but the challenges are the same or have very minor changes that made it easy for us to breeze through a second run. Definitely some unique puzzles and interesting ways the hacker/infiltrator are linked together which I hope future updates or other games expand upon.EDIT: New content added that took about 2 hours to complete playing both sides (Challenge/Training Mode - 10 missions in total). It was nice to have a reason to come back and play again!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a fantastically unique concept that was also well executed. A co-op game that requires verbal communication skills to relay information and solve puzzles together from 2 completely different perspectives. The co-op aspect is enjoyable and collaborative. The puzzles are not overly complicated but still satisfying to complete through teamwork. The execution of the "spy" theme feels so right over voice that where you constantly bombard each other with fancy tech and spy terms like "mainframe", "decryption" and of course - my personal favorite: *LOUD KEYBOARD CLACKING HACKY NOISES*. The immersion into the "agent/hacker experience" is on point for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Having experience with many other asymmetrical co-op games, Operation Tango is just as good as genre hits like the We Were Here series, and maybe even better.A majority of the game is talking though puzzles with you co-op partner, while each of you only has half the information. The most appealing part of the game is the spy theme, where you'll defuse bombs, and evade guards. Timers put you on the clock, and they pressure the Hacker into sifting through the information faster to keep the Agent alive. Though there's no punishment for failing and the checkpoints are generous. If that sounds fun then the game is for you.Compared to We Were Here (the second one), the game is a similar length (3-4 hours), and has a similar complexity. None of the puzzles were harder than We Were Here, and there's a hint system in case you get stuck. I would have liked to see Operation Tango utilise the Agent role more, as it plays very similar to We Were Here's roles. You don't shoot anyone or platform about, and your never get tested on your movement skills, but that's not much of a downside and makes the game accessible to older, younger, and disabled gamers.The game was buggy at launch for about 6 hours which explains the inflated amount of negative reviews. When we experienced bugs and quit, the bug fixes were ready to download. The Devs had already updated them within 6 hours of launch.A sequel or more DLC would be greatly appreciated,.

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is a co-op puzzle game where you play as two spies, an Agent and a Hacker, who break into places and steal important things that danger humanity in some shape or form. The story is pretty straightforward. You start off with what seems to be a routine heist on a well-secured facility, but this then spirals into a more engaging story featuring various individuals who are involved in the overarching plot. The gameplay is pretty involved for a game of this length and utilizes its co-op-focused mechanics greatly. The Hacker and Agent both excel in their own areas, and the game makes sure that the gameplay of either option is unique even when playing the same mission. Some portions are entirely reliant on the Hacker, some on the Agent, and most of the time, it's a blend of both. It's a surprisingly seamless use of the co-op nature of the game, and it's really nice. Each level also introduces a different setting with different mechanics, so nothing ever feels too stale or repetitive. There are also enough levels to feel fulfilled with what the game has to offer while also not feeling like the game is overstaying its welcome. Unfortunately, this game has a few bugs that sometimes forces you to restart sections of a mission or the entire mission itself, so that is also something you should be aware of.The art and sound design is pretty standard. It isn't anything that stands out, but it isn't anything bad. Overall, this is a solid co-op game with fun mechanics that don't get too old and stay for just the right amount of time. I recommend giving this game a try, but only if you have a friend to play it with!

With a bit of simple math, 2 players, $10 each, roughly 3 hours each, and 10$ for 3 hours of a good game is a bit more reasonable, I've definitely paid more and gotten less with other titles.Original Review Below:[I'm gonna start this by saying this game is incredibly fun, has some complicated moments that require precision and critical thinking. I really enjoyed the game.It took me and a friend 2.5 hours to do the whole story and we messed about for probably 45 minutes. This game probably has about 2 to 3 hours of content. Now, Let me present my opinion about other titles and price, an average $60 title I expect to get 60 hours of gameplay out of at least, and I typically get more out of those titles, a 20$ title, should be at least 20 hours of content, so in my opinion the game is unfinished, you do 6 missions as either a hacker or an agent and because you've talked through the missions with eachother as you play, there's quite literally no incentive at the moment to go back and swap roles.I think this game would be better if it had something akin to the payday series, which is also a stealth based game series with many different play styles and objectives, at the moment its quite linear and short without any reason to continue playing the same missions over and over.Honestly, its a really good game, that has its challenging moments, but it just lacks content, i don't see it being worth $20 at the moment, pick it up on sale as you and a friend will enjoy it.]
