_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is one of the best co-op game ever! My brother and I recently embarked on this cooperative adventure, and we've been utterly hooked from the very start. The adrenaline rush of completing a mission together is simply unparalleled. One of the standout features of Operation Tango is its ingenious asymmetrical gameplay. As partners in crime-solving, my brother and I were forced to rely on each other's expertise and communication skills to progress through a series of challenging missions. The game's puzzles and challenges are wonderfully designed, while you're infiltrating a high-tech facility, hacking into secure systems, or defusing a bomb, you feel the enjoyment and tension at the same time. If you have a friend you should definitely try it.

On a second playthrough—even though most of the allure is gone since you know pretty much what to do from the start—it's still fun to go over the game again and get to see how the other side perceived things as you were going through it the first time around. The game didn't overstay its welcome at all even while going for 100% achievements, which isn't too hard and helps you maximize the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Asymmetrical games is a genre that hasn't been done much. This is an Asymmetrical Coop game and it proves how much potential these kinds of games have when done right.The way this game works is that two people are basically playing entirely different games (in terms of gameplay/interface). One person plays a first-person view and another plays a "hacker" role. Now saying that this games hacking system is unrealistic is a massive understatement. But it also proves that that's not a bad thing. It's actually really fun despite how comical it is. (And also the levels after the first one do provide a bit of a challenge if you arnet the best at explaining things or reacting to information quickly)Theres a free demo to check it out and see if you have anyone on your list who is also willing to play. It has the first level which is easy but still fun.Plus not only can people who bought the game play with demo users (essentially meaning only one person needs to buy the game), but so far it features crossplay! Havent gotten to use it yet since I dont have console friends but from what ive heared the devs are working hard to support this feature and its not just a PR stunt.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game, I would love if there was multiple story campaigns.But, I am also very disappointed, this game soft-locked, glitched and straight up crashed very very frequently, at least two-three times per mission. The soft-locking seemed to occur when I was playing as hacker and my co-op bud playing the spy lady would initiate a hack and you had to do those co-operative key unlocking sections. My screen would go black behind the mini game and when we had finished, I couldn't do anything and had to relaunch the game. The other big issue was huge, huge ping spikes, which doesn't make sense at all as I've never had issues with ping in any other games I've played, and certainly has never entered the thousands. I'm glad for the frequent checkpoints but it did still very much break my immersion and frustrate us to the point we had to take a break in the middle of a rather short game that would ordinarily take us one sitting to finish. Still very much liked the game. I just wish these game breaking bugs were fixed, especially when the game is 2-3 years old now and still not very functional.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Operation: Tango is a very unique coop experience. Fun new mechanics and riddles. Enjoyed it a lot! Nice graphics aswell! _childDocuments_.review: This game works perfectly on a Steam Deck! Since you need a second player (using the free Friend Pass), it means you need 2 PCs so most people will play with a friend online. For me, playing on the Deck meant that I could install the Friend Pass on my laptop and ask my non-gamer girlfriend to play with me! Gameplay is simple enough that she was able to understand everything by herself on her side of the game (that's kinda important because I absolutely did not want to see her screen). We played by the bonfire on a camping trip and had a lot of fun, the puzzles were reasonably difficult and we both think it was satisfying to beat them. 10/10Disclaimer: I got a copy of this game for review by the developer and it's not changing my opinion about the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Not a unique take in the co-op puzzle game genre, but many of the missions do have me and my partner at the edge of our seats, then taking a stale breath of relief after figuring it out. Some missions require a lot of patience, which is key here. While some co-op puzzle games put you on a timer, though this game does have a few, Operation: Tango is more of a take your time and learn the steps to figure things out. Really puts the whole agent-hacker dynamic into use.Very fun. I'd love to see more cases in the game, and if they come out as DLCs I would definitely buy them.

Cant wait to see more from this studio!Story: Classical Spy themed adventure. it may be on the shorter side but its DEFINETLY worth the asking price. _childDocuments_.review: This game bills itself as a coop puzzler, but it's more of a "coop minigames" game.  The difficulty in nearly all of the "puzzles" is not figuring out what you need to do or how to do it; rather, the difficulty is in actually executing what you need to do.That said, this is not a bad game at all. The art and sound design were , and the minigames were reasonably fun.  My brother and I had fun playing through it. There's about 3 hours of content, with a bit of replayability if you decide to switch sides and play again.Overall I think this is worth getting on sale, with the caveat that you should  go in expecting a puzzle game.

_childDocuments_.review: Its kind of like a cross between it takes two, and the we were here series.It's got a little bit of the technical and movement skills from it takes two, and its got a little bit of the puzzle aspects from we were here, mixed into a spy thriller in a technologically advanced society.It's a well polished, well rounded game where the devs set out to make an enjoyable game and have achieved in doing that.Other then that, it's not anything ground breaking.Oh, and you can break peoples ankles with a S P E E D Y cleaning bot, which is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun once you work out what the mission is asking you to do and what you need to do to help your partner, for this reason communication is the key to this game meaning you have to explicitly state what you see to your teammate so you can complete your objective. _childDocuments_.review: I felt the need to return to this review after completing the entirety of Operation Tango, but most of my opinion will stand - this game is not worth full price. On initial appearance and reviews I was very excited to play this with a close girl friend of mine. We both bought it without telling the other, but we didn't ask for a refund because we wanted to support the creators. It was also for a sale price, probably about $10 or so. This is a somewhat fair price, but I'd even go so far unfortunately to say The reason that premise is so unfortunately short is the story is laughable. Me and my friend tried really hard to understand the plot and story but it's pretty boring overall. On our first playthrough I was the Hacker and she played the Agent. We had a bit of fun and seriousness- that lasted at best an hour. The Hackers perspective can go from boring to aggravating, and the Agents is uninteresting and lackluster. We agreed that on both playthroughs the Agent had it worse since when you think of Agent you think of more action sequences or such. There were a few moments of stealth and absolutely 0 combat sequences, which was a slight let down to the already incredibly short game. The puzzles range from hand holding through an empty mall to drilling a golfball sized hole through your cranium. It took a third friend to help figure out some of them and they weren't there until the second playthrough meaning the first run around we just managed to squeak by. This game one full game completion is about three hours. There are 6 story missions to complete before you beat the game, and then unlock challenges for aftergame content. Most of the challenges were laughably easy, taking 2-4 tries to gold tier. They aren't meant to take long either so we spent perhaps a 1/2 hour to an hour on that. We both agreed the last mission is our least favorite, simply because it's the most nothing out of them all; says a lot considering it's the LAST mission. In this mission  After that we had 100% completed the game and uninstalled it immediately. My opinion has not changed- do not buy this game more than once, allow a friend with the friend pass. Don't get this game for more than $10 because it's laughably short and lacking. My cardinal rule is whatever price you buy the game for you should get double the time out of it. I barely have 9 hours and I 100% completed it, more upset then triumphant. I respect the company that made this, but I and my friend were left upset and disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Did a full playthrough the game. I really love puzzle games, especially challenging one. This game is unfortunately a miss for me. The game felt more like quick time event simulator where you have to tell your partner what to do. The puzzles feel trivial and offer little challenge. I would recommend this to children under twelve but unfortunately I'm not at that age anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to other co-op games that I have played, such as We Were Here or Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes, I really liked the fact that the puzzles were not one sided. There are two roles to play, agent and hacker. But unlike those other co-op games, both sides get to describe a puzzle to the other person, which makes the game feel a lot more "co-op" than other games. Not to mention the fact that you can replay levels with your roles swapped to get a different experience, which gives this short game some replayability. The game isn't super long, but for the price of admission, I thought that it was just long enough to not overstay it's welcome. The puzzles do end up getting slightly repetitive, but they do also keep getting more challenging so I didn't think that was a problem. If you have been looking for a co-op game to play with a friend, I would definitely recommend giving this one a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: One of those asymmetric information coop games like the Wish You Were Here series or The Past Within. Not based around escape rooms though, but more like 'Mission Impossible' style mechanics. One of you plays a hacker and the other an agent. You have to communicate relevant info to each other to help complete missions. The mechanics are pretty simple, but like always with these things, context is everything. Shouting random crap at each other under time pressure is always going to be a good time!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, its one of the best coop experiences I've played, an easy recommendation at full price even. That does, in part, from having free friend pass. Gameplay-wise this is an asymmetrical cooperative puzzle game that revolves around good communication and teamwork.  As one player explores the world as an agent, they are supported by the other players hacking skills.  Each player has half of the clues and half of the puzzles and you need to solve it, and only by sharing information can you make progress.It takes best the best parts of "Keep Talking and No one Explodes" and expands this into a far deeper and more rewarding experience.  There is a good combination of low stress puzzles and high stress timed panic modes. With each stage taking a new approach to things and introducing new puzzle elements... it never got old.It's a relatively short game, but I'd also say it didn't outstay its welcome. It had a good buildup, a good pace, and I felt the ending was absolutely satisfying. If, unlike me, you need more... they now have a series of challenge puzzles to master. _childDocuments_.review: While short, if you're thirsting for asymmetric co-op, it delivers. The price seems a little much for around 3 hours of content, but I think it's actually quite reasonable when you realize that your friend can play with you for free - it really only costs half as much, if you think about it like that.The game itself is somewhat of a mix of concepts in other co-op games - A mix of We Were Here and Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes.  Something I appreciated was that there was no penalty for failing other than moving back to the last checkpoint. While it's nice to be challenged, I'd rather not have spats with friends because of bad feelings over not understanding each other.I'm absolutely desperate for more content, honestly, and dearly hope there's DLC or other content down the line. There's a small storyline in this game that holds up on its own, but the game is really begging for additional 'episodes.'Being a co-op game that releases the same year as It Takes Two must be rough, but this one definitely carves out a niche for itself with gameplay I really would like to see more of, either within Operation Tango itself or just in the game genre in general.Final thoughts: Slightly pricy for the length of the game, but zero regrets on my purchase.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: The first four missions were fun - unfortunately in the fifth mission my friend encountered a black screen bug so we had to restart and continue. This apparently desynced the random number generators in the mission such that the password I found and the password he was supposed to put into the system was no longer the same, so we could either restart from the very beginning or just try the other 9999 different possible combinations. Fortunately we could skip to the final mission, but in that mission I got the black screen every time we messed up, and had to restart from the beginning every time. Eventually, we just gave up because it just wasn't very fun anymore.It's disappointing when these kinds of gamebreaking bugs stay in the game despite the game being out for 2 years - I probably wouldn't have bought the game knowing that after slightly more than 2 hours of fun the game would just stop working properly. It's a short game, but it's even shorter when you only get to play the first 4 missions, especially when the first mission is basically just a tutorial. A shame, but can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Both the hacker and the agent both feels like they're part of the game, so even if you're the hacker and thus a more supportive role, you STILL feel like you're actually part of what's going on, being able to manipulate stuff for the agent to progress.The stages are fairly short (if you know what you're doing, anyway - going through them blind, you'll probably look at about 40-60 minutes/stage due to the puzzles - time might vary, depending on how good you and your partner are at puzzles).You can and will fail puzzles multiple times. Thankfully, there are PLENTY of checkpoints, allowing you to easily continue the game from where you left off if you die.Cons:A bit short, with only 6 stages. I really hope they'll add more in the future as it's a really fun game.Some of the puzzles are more tedious than actually hard. Disclaimer: the following two things are bugs that I hope gets fixed. The first a minor annoyance at best, but still bad. The latter one is pretty annoying.For some reason, on stages 2-5 if you're playing as the Hacker, you can't see the end credits - the game just turns slightly dark and while you'll still hear the end credit sequence play out, you won't actually get to see it. Nothing game breaking, thankfully.The second bug is on stage 2. Slight spoilers ahead.As the agent, you have to avoid two drones but for some reason, the game will sometimes make you respawn inside one of the rooms where you're trying to hide from the drones, only to end up being instantly caught by the drone again, forcing yet ANOTHER reset. Other times, the drones will be somewhere else on the path, allowing you more free reign.Overall, I find the game very fun and I hope that they'll add more stages in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I spoke with my partner at length after completing the game in 2 sittings, and below will be the points we discussed. But for those looking for a short answer: Yes it's good fun, and we need more games like this.For the record, I played as the Hacker.It does need to be said; the game is short. Very short. Every level honestly felt like we just got the tutorial sample of what was possible, but it was over before we knew it. That doesn't mean the experience wasn't fun or worthwhile, but that we needed MORE with the tools we've now learnt to use. We were hoping to use all our new experience in less linear-based level design moving forward. Sadly, it was already the end.Don't stress too much about which character to play, as you'll both experience elements of each others default style in some form or another. The game revolves mostly around information gathering and sharing it clearly between each other to progress. This is mostly happening both ways throughout the game.We were a little confused at the decision for the theme of the story. We're supposed to be badass top agents, but the immersion wasn't really there as we're chaotically thrown into our levels with no real clue what's happening. In this casual and chaotic style of gameplay, it would've made more sense that we were like the worst agents on record, but everyone else was unavailable for some reason, and it was up to us screw ups to save the world. If you wanted a more badass tone, I personally would've preferred a proper planning phase before a mission starts, to get an understanding of what we'll be doing and to some degree, and how. The unexpected twists can still happen of course, but the cutscenes just lacked any real conveyance of how we're actually going to accomplish our task.This style of game is quite rare, and definitely worth the experience, but the point I want to make here is that this game just barely scratches the surface of whats possible for this genre. This game has great example of all the tools and creative ideas for puzzles and missions, but you'll rarely ever use a single mechanic twice. Which I mean, hats off to them for being unique and creative for every level. But imagining now using each of these mechanics, solving mysteries, and completing difficult objectives under more 'free-roam' environments...Let's just say this game represents the tip of the iceberg for what's possible in the future. I wish the developers all the best and would even go so far as to beg them for a sequel that's extensively deeper. Thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Possibly one of the best puzzle-solving co-op experiences you can have in the modern era, assuming you and your second agent are capable of sentient thought (you'd be surprised). There's about three hours of content per agent, meaning the worst critique I could level to this game is that there isn't more of it to digest.Visual presentation and art style are top notch, with a lot of clarity in User Interface elements. The visually distinct stages for the Agent and the well-polished interfaces for the Hacker have this cartoon-ish postmodern vibe that are all kept different over the course of play. My personal level, the Moving Train, is awesome to experience from either Hacker or Agent side, full of good twists and panic moments throughout the level's 20 minute long run time. The game has a lot of flair and passions put into it, from the polished light to the just-right sound effects really letting you experience the perspectives of the agents. A review should never say "It really makes you feel like X" (unless ironically) but this is one of the moments where I felt extreme gratification after finishing a level, like finally putting the pieces together in the detective sequence, or finally completing the ending of mission six with mere seconds between victory and obliteration.Not many puzzles or content are re-used, aside from the lock picking experiences which are kept consistent and expanded upon constantly. After playing both sides for myself, the difference in game play between the two agents is shocking; it makes other games of this principle look like they're slacking off by comparison. In Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, the other players besides the one tinkering with the bomb just get to read a manual for several minutes. In Operation Tango, that "Manual" Is a highly interactive second game that the Hacker is peeling through to get you openings or advantages. I'm baffled in hindsight that this isn't a more common idea.Since I got into this game on patch 1.01, I experienced an extremely minimal level of glitches. I played Cyberpunk 2077 on release and liked it; nothing this game can hit you with is even NEAR that. If you cannot stomach the idea of spending thirty Australian dollars on this short-but-ever-so-sweet experience, then you might want to wait until they either add more content or until the game goes on sale. I can say, personally that I'd rate this above games like Trine or even Portal 2's coop.

_childDocuments_.review: i've played a lot of co-op games before--this is easily one of the most intense and exciting. the puzzles are fun and both the agent and hacker play crucial roles in completing the missions. many times, there is information available only to one of the players, which they must relay to their partner in order to complete the mission. i found that the answer was clear most of the time, although some sections did have me resorting to looking up what i was supposed to do. overall, i think the puzzles were fair. no bugs found.the drawback is that the game gets you about 5-ish hours of gameplay--honestly not that much for the price. i would love to see DLCs or more content, but it doesn't look like it will happen. the storyline is simple and serves only to give context for your missions, and i enjoyed my time playing this game.

One of the best two-player co-op games I've played. I hope they add more missions because I really want to play more.

_childDocuments_.review: My partner and I are escape room weirdos who are always looking for co-op puzzlers. Operation Tango really nails collaborative, simultaneous puzzles that require working in tandem rather than asynchronously taking turns reading details and standing around.If you like games like Escape Simulator or the We Were Here franchise, pick this up.PS. The hacker role is basically everything I've ever wanted from a hacking component in a game. You fly through the internet, you hack the mainframe, it's all pixels and sh*t, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: 2 Player. Each Player controlls an agent. One agent is "in the Game" as a Human. The other one - the Hacker - operates as .. a hacker. Many Missions, many Problems to solve. So your communication-skills must be on point. It is so much fun and has elements like from "KEEP TALKING AND NOBODY EXPLODES" etc. Please. If this game gets new missions from time to time as an DLC, TAKE MY MONEY!!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Had no issues except for the first hotel part of the last heist, fsr the drone bit kept giving me blackscreens on failure, but on other than that very fun experience with my friend. We were excited enough to gold all the challenges which were relatively easy. The game being 17 euro's with friendpass feature is a godsend and i even got it on a summer sale and having completed it i can say that i would buy it fullprice.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast for some 2-player asynchronous puzzle solving. The roles are both very dynamic and the difficulty was just right for a moderate & experienced PC gamer duo. We had about 5 restarts which reloaded at an appropriate checkpoint. Graphics are polished, voice acting & soundtrack is solid, maps have the right level of detail, and the Friend Pass system is such an awesome move for a co-op game. Thanks, Clever Crew!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Fun asymmetrical coop with a light tone and appealing art style. Each of the 6 missions has distinct mechanics and is a joy to play. You'll get 2 solid playthroughs out of this as each character's perspective is very different. About 3 hours per playthrough. The challenges are kind of a pain as there are a lot of them and they remix the mechanics that are already in the game in more challenging ways and you have time pressure to get those elusive gold medals. Honestly the challenges seem more like a memorization thing since both players will need to remember the sequence to get a good time. Personally I did not enjoy the first challenge enough to continue but they do add more content; it's just a very different tone from the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, played with my partner we had lots of fun. I'm excited to see how the developers continue with this game! Communication is key, but you have to be accurate and fast, I'll never forget the laughter when I tried to describe the shape of a key "It's shaped like a. 9...a well endowed 9...with shoes" que hysterical laughter.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the 15-20 bucks! I played through this game with a friend and had a great experience with the puzzle solving. The multiplayer is incredibly well synced, and even leaves a bit of room for error in the event of slow internet or bad communication. The 'friend pass' is an excellent idea. Whoever came up with that needs a raise because that compelled me to buy even more. Only 15 bucks for a good two player experience? A steal.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: The six missions are elaborately designed and well made, but in the end they only take up two to three hours. Even with their DLC Challenges, it doesn't quite match up to the main story and knowing that there isn't much more makes the game experience less enjoyable. Being only a year old, I hope the game expands and adds more story missions. As it is now, it is NOT worth $20.00. It just feels like they made the gameplay long enough to pass the two hour return rule.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Nice idea in concept but the puzzles were unfun, the Minigames terrible and tedious. The main characters are everything but likeable and the main reason why one should not hack is not because security is bypassed, but because it is too much of a nuissance to bypass security.Oh and there were Network connection problems even though a stable connection present.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: If you and your friend enjoy solving puzzels and working together this is quite a fun game to play. The game got different varieties of puzzel solving so it won't get to repedetive wich in my opinion is really good. Still would recomment to get Operation Tango on a sale even though your friend gets it for free with the friend pass (Another W with this game). Limited content but recommended to play if you got someone close!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Wow wow wow, what do we have here? Quite the little gem. Let's begin with a hearty round of applause for the ethical concept of only requiring one player to own the game in order to delve into this mandatory co-op adventure. Somewhere, one of EA's shareholders just died of a heart attack from the imbalance of karma. More devs like this please and fewer triple A studios.Heroic financial decisions aside, the game itself is also really good. Many games have tried this kind of asynchronous experience before but few pull it off so well. It's not just about relaying information to each other but also about how to correlate that information and the unique experience/interaction with your environment. It's like "Keep Talking" if you could leave the room with the bomb and interact with other stuff while the other guy is plugged into the matrix. So whilst short (~4 hrs), you really can go back through as the other character and deal with an entirely different experience. Honestly, I had a great night playing this with one friend and I'm definitely going through it with another (and then back the second way with the first friend) for maximum enjoyment. I think I got my money's worth, the price point seems just about right. One minor glitch was literally patched while we were playing. I think we're onto a winner. If you have many friends that will likely play a free game with you, you're gonna get a lot of mileage out of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A short blast! Had so much fun with a friend playing it. Could be very nerve racking at times but overall hilarious encounters and unique fun gameplay as both spy, and hacker. Wish there were a lot more chapters; was very short. Beat the game in half a day. Hope you see more get added to the game. A very good purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This was really fun! It's not a super long game but I liked the gameplay and the visuals. There are parts where you might be susceptible to motion sickness, but it's mostly okay. It is also really great that the developers only require one copy of the game and your friend can just come in with a friend pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is a great co-op experience. Everything is set up for two players to play together. You can't even start the game alone, but thanks to the Friend Pass, it's enough if one of the two players buys the game.In effect, one player plays an agent and the other a hacker. Together you must stop the propagation of a dangerous virus (Covid 19?). You need to communicate successfully so that everyone can solve their tasks with the help of their partner. The tasks are very fun, exciting and sometimes even challenging. Especially in the missions where you are under time pressure, your brain is working at full speed. Nevertheless, all the tasks are, in my opinion, quite easy. My friend and I got through the game relatively quickly and played through the entire campaign (6 missions) in only 3 hours. Now we have switched roles so that everyone experiences the other perspective (after all the gameplay is completely different).The story itself is quite boring and stereotypical. There is also no real character development. But that's not half bad. I didn't buy this game to hear a good story, but because the co-op gameplay interested me a lot.The art style is also very appealing, the graphics are great, and the Secret Agent ambience is great. The soundtrack is also good.A great co-op experience that partly reminded me of "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes".
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing co-op game. Playing from both perspectives is really fun and it adds more replayability. These hacking mini games are definitely something I've never experienced before in a video game. In some instances it create these high tension and stressful moments. It requires flawless communication with your gaming buddy to complete the levels. It's awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A great experience you can share with somebody by only buying one copy, I love this format!Game is insanely fun and keeps you on your toes by switching things up from one mission to the next.The only bad thing about this is that the time spent playing is so fun you don't even notice that you've already reached the end of the game...
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Really great coop puzzle game. The price is really fair if you compare it to an escape room, for example, which this game is similar to, as it requires cooperation between players and quick thinking. Sadly, the game can't really be replayed, because missions are always the same, but hopefully the developers make more missions, as DLCs, or games with same characters, because of the greatly positive feedback they are getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with my friend (I bought the game, he used the friend pass). We both enjoyed it a lot, because our lack of communication skills let to us struggling a bit. The more of a chaotic duo you are, the harder the game is and the more fun the game is.  I played the hacker role, might try agent next time i play this game. The hacker role was a lot of fun because, while you don't get to move, you still feel relevant and cool. Most games would make it just a support role, but the hacker needs the agent and the agent needs the hacker. It is just a perfect balance.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a developer making a coop game, let me tell you that I decided to buy this game instead of skipping over it solely because it allowed for coop with a partner without them ALSO having to buy it.As for the game itself, very fun. Has a clean UI and visual style, a surprising variety of mini-games, and it uses the coop mechanics in an intelligent way. As of this review I have played through the first three missions and never felt like I was lost even with the variety of things you need to do as both hacker and agent. Would warmly recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, what if I don't get along with people, humm? You've got games like "Tale of two brothers" which revolves around Co-Op gameplay, but doesn't necessarily force you to have someone else playing your partner... And then you've got Operation Tango, in which you basically can't even launch the game without having someone on the other end.Operation Tango is an exclusively CO-OP game where you play as either an Agent or a Hacker, playing as one or the other entails going for specific objectives, like activating turrets with the hacker, or building a bridge and the agent is actually in place, doing the looting and the smashing (not the one you're thinking about). That's about it... Also, worth mentioning that the game is super short, so chances are if you don't have friends you'll do it by having another laptop.The only good thing about the game is that your partner doesn't have to own the game, they can log into your session by downloading the free demo of the game... That's pretty wholesome, so I was playing agent and hacker at the same time by switching frequently to my laptop and I hated every single second of it. That's why I'll rate "Operation Tango" a solid , I didn't have to buy it for my other account, but playing in two PCs was lame as hell. The game is like "Well, it sucks that you don't get along with other people and we don't care!", F YOU TOO, DEVS lol!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Played it all the way though with my boyfriend and my best friend and it had us completely enthralled all the way through. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE make more missions/ characters. I would play  so many more versions of this game even. That's honestly my biggest complaint. There just wasn't enough.fun graphicsawesome innovative play style
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Not sure if it has the same kind of replayability as Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, but I would definitely encourage everyone to play it at least once. Honestly, it's like an escape room, but with more full ambience.Hopes for the future:- DLC adventures (not sure if I'd pay $20 for another adventure like this, but definitely $10)- Make your own adventure (either a-la Mario Maker or mod support)- Jump support (I know it's not important, but when I couldn't jump I was sad)- More timed components. Once we were detected, it would have helped the thrill to know we're being chased.Update 2021:This is my vote for GOTY:Innovative Gameplay. And I am glad they did give us the new DLC for free.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all about clear communication.  If you want to challenge your ability to communicate with your partner in remarkable and complex ways, this could be the game for you.Computer/internet requirements: best to make it better than the minimum specs, because it laggy.The environments are very detailed, and this can be a blessing and a curse.  Checkpoints are generous.  Haven't figured out how to adjust the mouse sensitivity yet, and it's important in one section.  Generally, not a problem, but it can be.Good communication is absolutely key.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: We had a hilarious evening yelling at each other from opposite sides of our gaming room -- definitely a great evening or two of gaming for a couple or flatmates. Absolutely feels like a couch co-op, even though of course you need two computers to play. A couple of bugs requiring a quit and restart, but would recommend! I think we'll wait til we've forgotten the puzzles then switch characters and play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Truly great coop game!I played it with my girlfriend and we had a lot of fun with every mission.The devleopers have been inventive in how to best foster cooperation in different scenarios and situations.I highly recommend it and I would definitely play more levels if avaialble (the game lasted about 4 hours, unfortunately)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: With the world how it is, a game like this couldn't of come at a better time. A real cooperative experience that allows one of you to be a agent working a case, while the guy gets to be the guy in the chair typing away, and providing the agent critical information. This was absolutely everything I wanted it to be, being in lockdown, and wanting to play games with close friends I don't get to see, this was exactly what we wanted. If you liked Keep Talking and Nobody explodes, this is absolutely the next step down that line. I would love to see more content come out. With its pretty low price I'll definitely be buying this for friends. I hope to see oh so much more in this vein as I think it could really catch on!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Very good coop game, with interesting asymmetry regarding if you are playing agent (which has a lot more first person view and movement) or hacker (which has you more navigating interesting and varied computer user interfaces).  Therefore I would say there is an element of replayability.The puzzles you need to solve together are mostly a wide variety of mini games, and the goals are not always immediately apparent until you verbally communicate what you see to your partner. Then comes the playing of the mini-games:  Many are timed in some way and therefore require some reflexes or learning to communicate efficiently with your partner e.g. coming up with short hands for the things you must communicate verbally. However, in the first 3 chapters we've played so far, nothing impossibly hard after a few tries and figuring out the most efficient way to communicate.. The mini-games are challenging enough that it feels satisfying to complete, more so because of the required teamwork. The game has a groovy 60s spy movie esthetic and appropriate sound track. The technical aspects of the online co-op (including built-in voice communication) also works very smoothly and reliably.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Grab a close friend and you two will just lose yourselves in this game working together to breach the security systems. It was really fun playing as one role and then replaying the game through again to see what the other roles experience was like. Especially if you play as the cameras first, you'll be so surprised when you see how everything looked afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Game has a cool premise and I am interested in continuing to play the game, however there is a game-breaking bug that seems to keep my co-op partner and I from progressing in Mission 2. I cannot get into the Technology Center because booking the appointment does not change the message on the Technology Center door from "Your access to the Technology Center is by APPOINTMENT only" and the door does not open around the appointment time, whether that be 5:00 am or 5:30 am. We've tried fresh installs of the game (and in my case, a fresh OS install for an unrelated reason) and the issue still persists. I've also tried other things like verifying game files and nothing seems to correct the issue.I've seen posts from other players having this issue in the past. The game was released a year ago so I would have expected a bug like this to be fixed by now. If you do buy this game, hopefully you don't encounter the same bug. I can't recommend the game because I now just have one very expensive mission instead of a full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is a co-op spy experience done right!  There is all sorts of things happening and at the same time.  It requires focus and especially communication.  To many co-op games just let each person do their own thing at the same time, this makes you both do the same things at the same time and does it so well.  Playing as the agent and the hacker are both fun and different experiences.  Hopefully there's more content coming, but I'm definitely excited to see what else Clever Plays does in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively contained but ultimately fun game. Satisfyingly spaced out checkpoints allow for learning on the case. Graphically eye catching and aesthetically pleasing. Plus the Friend Pass helps lure in more friends to play with, granting more replay value for the budget-conscious. Greatly enjoyed, and hoping to see more from this developer in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I just 100 percented the game and it's really cool, among the best 2-player-asymmetric-coop I've played. Even if they copy 'keep talking and nobody explodes' in some parts, it's really well done and the asymmetry is felt throughout the entire game.Only complaint I'd have is that at some points it feels like they wasted some potential, but overall it's great price/enjoyment ratio.Do get it. Plus, only one of the players has to get the full version, the other can get the demo, but won't get the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the price of $20 given the current state.Cool concept and somewhat fun, but the game is so buggy beyond belief, and it's too short.Desyncs that make the mission impossible, drones that cannot be disabled, people showing up differently on the hacker's perspective and the agent's, the only solution is to restart the game and replay parts of the mission. Sometimes my friend cannot even join after this happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: We purchased the game while it was on sale, and at that price very worth it. Player 2 and I had a pretty good time! The puzzles didn't really get more challenging though, it seemed to really stay about the same difficulty and in that sense would liked to have seen a bit more. It made the last mission pretty meh feeling. It really excels in its art style! Graphically very well put together. If they were to release more missions, I would be very likely to purchase them. Fingers crossed for more adventures!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great co-op game with fun sometimes challenging gameplay and a cool story and graphics.The missions are fun as hacker as well as agent.You really have to be in contact with your partner and solve the riddles together.The only downsight is that there isn't much content. The missions take around 2-3 hours to solve and after that you can either switch roles and play them again or train yourselves in the training grounds area.I really hope that there will be more content in the future as this game has a lot of potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Some really fun mini-games and some a little annoying, but it is constantly changing and keeps you interested.  Kinda like a more polished "Keeping Talking and Nobody Explodes."  The spy aspect isn't much (so far, 5 missions in), you don't do a lot besides walk and interact with things, but the team communication is excellent.  So many roadblocks until someone explains just a little bit more of what they see on their screen and suddenly it all comes together.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this game is super fun. It keeps you on your toes and forces you to work together with the other player to figure out and solve the puzzles in the game. My only complaint is that the game is fairly short. (Although, at the time of writing this review, the game only came out 4 days ago so I am hoping for more content in the future.) I also do wish that more mechanics are added to the game as towards the end, the puzzles felt repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a barrel of laughs, Had a lot of fun, it's short but definitely worth $20 for two people, our completion playtime was around 3 hours, with 6 missions, loved every second of it, especially mission 4. Would highly recommend this, since it costs about the same price as a movie ticket and it's twice as fun. I really hope that the developer decides to make DLC or make more missions, would definitely pay more for more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is a hidden gem. I really recommend you play this with one of your friends and play both operators to get the most out of the game. I love that the challenges kept building on each other and making a foundation of gameplay that was fun but not repetitive. Some of the things had my friend and I stumped on what to do but the hint system really helped guide us without straight up giving us the answer. I love the goofy moments me and my friend got to share and I definitely recommend this to anyone who enjoys vastly different puzzles and challenges. It's fairly short but definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are less difficult than Lucasarts games. Allows for easy co-operation for two players. There were some parts that didn't make sense, so we did have to look at each other's screens. It's the mission where you're sliding through the Matrix. Then there's a puzzle where you have to "stack" each other's columns without triggering the alarm for the other. If there was a diagram for it, it would've been a lot easier to figure out. Other than that, we haven't experienced a lot of bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. Its a great cooperative puzzle solver. Very good if you want something casual to play with a friend. Its not without it's issues, First of all its very short, At the time of this review I've beaten this game 3 times, twice as the field agent and once as the hacker, and gotten gold on all the challenge maps, all within 10 hours of play time. So its a bit hard to recommend at the $20 price point. Aside from that, we also experienced a few network issues, and a game bug where the game was saying an access code was being reported as incorrect. It was fixed after we restarted the game but it had us confused for a little while. But other than that the game is great, it has beautiful minimalist graphics, fantastic lighting and level design  and a wide variety of puzzles that are fun to work through as a team. The puzzles tend to be pretty easy but progress is satisfying.Finally I have a few thoughts I'd like to tack on to the end of this review:Although its super short the two sides of the game play completely differently, so you have to play it through at least twice before you get the full experience. Second, if you have friends who want to play with you, they dont have to buy a copy. They can play free as long as a game owner gives them a lobby key, so in a way you're kind of buying a game for a friend as well.And finally, this game was made by an indie dev, I like to support this type of work, so I think that modifies my opinion of the price a bit. From a pure gameplay to dollar value comparison, $20 might be a bit much, but if youre looking for a coop game, its definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: An asymmetric cooperative game for 2 players, this has fun gameplay and a whimsical art style. Players take the role of either the hacker or the operative, each with unique minigames that require communication between players in order to complete successfully. The tutorialization is fairly poor, but the games are simple enough where the goal can be deduced and fail states tend to be generous. Overall, great fun for anyone looking for a low-stakes game to play with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun, my buddy and I had a blast going through some of the more stressful ones. Some segments are a bit too similar to Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes however. That's not a bad thing, but I felt like I was playing a reskinned version of that game some times. Also it is far too short for the price tag. Get it on a sale and have fun for three hours with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Neat collection of random mini games wrapped in cool spy aesthetics.Took us four hours to play through the six main missions once, looking forward to replay with the roles swapped, and there's also ten shorter (time) challenge levels. The puzzles and mini games are usually intuitive if you communicate well, there was only one that we couldn't figure out. There's also a hint option, never tried that though. (Completely forgot it existed, oops.) Quite a few puzzles require speed/timing though nothing suuuuper fast. Check points are also very generous, basically saving after every puzzle. Big thank you for that, devs!For the most part the mini games are literally just random puzzles and have no connection to the tech they represent irl. Although one thing that made me chuckle is  , The story didn't seem to be a large focus of the game, but it did do a great job of setting the vibe of the futuristic world it's set in. As are little details scattered about, like being able to read random emails and the beautiful art.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely must play for those who love some action and puzzle type games. This game depends on communication through the Voice Chat. Very interesting idea. Since you need to depend on other person to talk through some stuff (Hacker/Agent), sometimes hilarious moments are happening. Game by itself is not that hard, yet sometimes it does require creative thinking. As for the length of the game: It is not that long, yet good enough to play with someone. I do recommend this game (but buy on sale like I did. it's worth $10 but nothing more in my opinion).Did I had fun with my friend? Yes.Would I play it again with someone else as a Hacker (I played 1st time as Agent) - Possibly.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: If you like "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes", buying this is a no-brainer, otherwise, get this if you like teamplay. Depending on how fast you are with your partner, casual players will get about 4-5 hours out of this game. If you are a completionist that wants to play both sides and finish all gold medals, expect 9-10 hours. Playing both sides is well worth it, but maybe take a few weeks off of it after finishing the first run so that you forget most of the riddles at least partially.I desperately hope for either a sequel/prequel or another game with this concept. Loved every minute.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really quirky game that is, quite honestly, perfect for co-oping. The atmosphere and general game feel is exciting and fun. The game was not overly challenging, but definitely makes you work at a few things without being discouraging.   It was a very fun game even for somewhat novice gamers. I am greatly anticipating more possible missions in the future because I would love to continue playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great game to play with someone else! It was super fun to figure out what moves to make as each character. The challenges were actually challenging and it took a few tries to get gold on some. I would def recommend playing as both characters. Decent amount of playtime - took me 12 hours to finish the game and get all of the achievements: which gets you through all of the content.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Had errors going in that made it unplayable. Couldn't hit ESC on the first hacker level and people are reporting crashes and errors over all the missions. I would stay away from it personally. Also, I hear that it's 30 mins. a side (when working). So a total of an hour gameplay for $20 USD? No thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is too short rn to be worth $20 even with the friends pass. The game will probably only take you 2-4 hours based on how well you work with your partner (communication skills). The game is cool and fun but for a pc game that only lasts one evening $20 is a lot to ask. If you really want to play a CO-OP game with a friend then sure go ahead and buy it, but I would recommend It Takes Two as far as CO-OP games go.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game, play it with someone who won't judge you any differently for not being able to explain a shape correctly. I really just wish there was more, seems like a fun game for custom levels and mods too. Don't go in expecting a hacking simulator, I do wish there was a game like this that took a bit more inspiration from the real world, but it's a really unique two player co-op game that I had a lot of fun playing the whole time!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Lot's of fun to play with friends, great concept combining elements of We Were Here and Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes.     The hacker and the spy both get time guiding each other through the unique James-bond/Mission Impossible-esque puzzles. It's a short game without a massive difficulty curve that most teams will breeze through in <3 hours.  I enjoyed every second, but was disappointed it ended so quickly and felt there was more give. _childDocuments_.review: Coop game for two players in which one of you is a secret agent in the field and the other one a hacker supporting her from behind the scenes. It's reminiscent of games like the bomb defusing simulator "Keep talking and nobody explodes" in how it requires both of you to check the information and tools available to you to solve the tasks at hand together: So there is a corridor full of invisible lasers that the agent can't see, but the hacker with his camera access can? Sounds like he should tell her where to step to make it through safely. Other tasks include picking door locks, finding out the identity of a person of interest and hacking into highly secure servers. All in all, some tasks repeat, but you also constantly get new ones that differ from mission to mission, keeping the gameplay fresh and surprising.The game's difficulty is just right. It can be quite tricky in spots (especially those were you have to control the same moving dot together), but in the end, everything was doable.What I appreciated was that when we had a disconnect, the game allowed us to continue in the middle of the mission where we had left off. Another big plus: Only one of you needs to buy the game. The second player can use the free demo version as his "friend pass".

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I just played through this over the course of 4ish hours; a great little communication/teamwork game where you and a friend take on the roles of an Agent and Hacker respectively and solve puzzles, navigate networks and do espionage-flavoured things against a colourful comic book-esque art style backed by well fitting music. If you enjoyed We Were Here, this scratches a similar itch albeit coming from a more asymmetrical angleThe campaign consists of six Missions following your relatively typical spy-movie plot, typically tasking the Agent with on-site duties like slinking through security systems and sneaking into office computers to provide IPs, passwords and network details to the Hacker who then opens doors, manipulates elevators, and generally Trons about the place. Players can change characters between missions but we played through the whole thing in our roles and will probably go again to try out the other side in a year or two.Overall a punchy, stylish experience that doesn't overstay its welcome nor feel too thin for the $10 we paid - and, thanks to the friend pass, you only need one copy! I would wholly recommend this to any gaming couples looking for some silly fun.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE & WARNING: The first time I played through this, I was able to complete the game, but hit some obnoxious disconnect errors on the lock picking puzzles in later levels that necessitating switching who hosted the game and verifying the game files again. However, on my second playthrough, this workaround no longer seemed to fix it. As this may potentially render the game unplayable for some if the host-swap workaround doesn't work, I cannot in good conscience recommend it as a purchase even if I was able to complete it once. The rest of my review below still stands though.While I found O:T enjoyable, it was not what I was expecting, and I think it's important that a review makes this clear up front. This is an asymmetrical-information-based two-player puzzle game at its core, along the lines of the "We Were Here" games, or the Rusty Lake co-op puzzle games. It is strictly linear and the puzzles have strictly one resolution. With a very few exceptions, you are not exercising creativity or strategy here. You are solving puzzles with an espionage theme laid over them. The asymmetry comes in with one player playing the Agent, who handles physical infiltration and boots-on-the-ground tasks, and the other as a remotely located Hacker. The latter seems to have more to do. The Agent's role seems to mostly be just having eyes on providing the hacker with various numbers and IDs. But it's only a slight imbalance.There's no matchmaking as far as I know. If you want to play, you will have to find a partner out of game. At full price, at time of writing, that would put you and your partner out $20 each, which might be hard to justify for a game that's extremely short. You can complete the main story in under eight hours easily.There are some serious glitch problems as well. I encountered an error where initiating a collaborative lock-picking minigame would consistently crash the game. Switching who was hosting did alleviate it for some reason, FYI, but this bug has been known since last year with no apparent fix.The chief intended appeal of the game appears to be in orchestrating situations that force you and your partner to talk to each other like spy drama characters. It's definitely at its best when it has players shouting "I need an access point! Try ID 8675309!" at each other. There should be an achievement for resisting the urge to say "I'm in!" when playing the hacker, too. There's almost no story to speak of - it's not just so perfunctory you could jot it on a bar napkin, but much of what's there makes no sense. There are no real characters to speak of - only the mission-giver NPC ever even talks. But there is at least a good sense of visual flair in the design.I was expecting something more like a simulation game, where I can make strategic choices and collaborate on-the-fly with my partner. Instead it's a pretty relaxed affair, generally with no real time limits, simply teasing apart puzzles (some lifted outright from other games like Space Team, or Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes). But the puzzles are fun enough to still generally merit a recommendation from me, and there's a little replay value in switching characters for a second (invariably much shorter) playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Teamwork is the key! _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Played this through in one sitting with my partner through one of the roles, took about 3.5 hours to get through all six missions. We had fun, its just short enough for one sitting, but feels like there should be more than just the one "case." I'm not counting the challenge modes, as that isn't really our thing. I would say, as our first asymmetrical co-op game that this was a good start, Its forgiving enough when you mess up, but with enough difficulty to not feel like a complete cakewalk. Just because I was the "Hacker" role the whole time didn't mean I just clicked buttons, and just because my partner was the "Agent" role didn't mean all they did was run around and go where I told them to. There were a few points where we had to stop and talk it through since we think very differently (planning, directions, etc.) but the game allows for this with time and safe spots in almost every place. I only had one crash, and when we reconnected it brought right back to the end part of the level, so we didn't have to do the whole thing over again (thankfully). A lot of the puzzles have multiple iterations, so multiple playthroughs are viable (even though the story overall will be the same.)My biggest gripe is the time vs. price ratio, and what offsets it. My general rule is 50 cents/hour (I'm cheap, sorry) but since only one person needs a copy, I'd raise it to $1/hour. If you run through both sides like we plan to do, it'll probably equal out at 6-7 hours total, which at $20 is a fair ways short. I'm still recommending it, as on sale at around $10 I'd say its worth it to have a couple playthroughs with different folks and see how each of you thinks, and try again in a few months with roles swapped. I would absolutely look forward to any DLC for this, but as of writing this review its been two years, so I wouldn't hold out hope.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 6th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.An online co-op spy game. Operation: Tango is similar to the We Were Here series.  Two players try to complete spy missions in enemy territory.  One player will be a field operative, and the other plays a hacker, though both characters will have a variety of tasks that they will need to collaborate on to work their way through each mission.   The game requires online play but only needs one copy of the game and the expectation is the only communication between the players is verbal, with no way to see each other’s screens. Operation: Tango should be played by friends, random players won’t be as good for this.  But a bigger problem is that Operation: Tango is a single experience.  Once players get through the entire game, the same experience won’t be as special.  I forgot to record footage, and this is the second playthrough of the same level.  Even swapping characters didn’t change the experience.  There are only 6 missions and while there are ten additional challenges in a new free DLC, this isn’t the longest experience.   Pick this up if you have someone to play with, if you get the game, this is enjoyable, and with the right partner, it’s something else.  The reason I forgot to record the footage was that I was having an amazing time playing the game, but we also got through two out of the six original missions already, so, as I said, it’s not going to be that long. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal !! Yes... it is a short game. My buddy and I completed it in 5.4 hours. However, now we can replay it and swap characters. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Super short, but jam packed with brain twisting, spine tingling fun. Great game to play with someone you are great at communicating with, but probably super entertaining to play with someone you ARENT good at communicating with. I would love to see more criminals in the future, because this was an absolutely grand game. Like KTANE but on a Carmen SanDiego kick. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Tango is a co-op puzzle heist game that has you working with a friend to save the world from cyber terrorism. Playing through this game was a ton of fun. Each level is different and brings unique challenges to work through. Succeeding relies a lot on communication, and doing so effectively is surprisingly not easy. I feel like it was more than a game to play with a friend; it strengthened my relationship with the people close to me, and it's rare a game can do that. Since only one copy of the game is needed to play online co-op, this is an easy pick for gaming with anyone. Both roles are enjoyable in their own way, and neither felt better than the other. Overall, I loved this game and the memories I made while struggling through it, and I would easily recommend it to anyone looking for a good co-op challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This will be one of my first reviews but I feel I have to mention the excellence of this game. A brilliant asymmetrical co-op experience that insentivises clear communication in order to be the eyes for your other agent and deal with obstacles in your way.A unique introduction into the co-op genre that has many positives going for it. Such as affordable (£15) and with only one of the two needing to purchase my brother and I split the difference to play this game together.  It has great style. Unique puzzles and challenges that are evolving as you progress through the game. Every level offers different challenges and obstacles for Angel (Field Operative) and Alistair (Hacker) to navigate which means running through each mission is a blast.However, the game is not without its flaws. Namely that it is rather short, my brother and I managed to beat it in under 4 hours when I just played Angel and he played Alistair so if you are looking for an epic then this game will not be for you. Additionally, though there is story it is nothing special but simply serves a purpose for you to navigate to the next level. Finally, there is little character development between Angel and Alistair. It would have been lovely to hear the two communicate in some way in cutscenes or during downtime within the game, but I do understand the company is small and good VA is not cheap, therefore, I will not be too harsh with this criticism.Overall, I would highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking to play a styalistic and unique take on co-op that challenges your communication in fun and interesting ways. I do hope they release more content for this world, either with DLC, a sequel or a different game focussing on Angel or Alistair respectively. As I am intrigued by the setting this small dev team has conjured.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Short but very fun game! If you've played Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, this is very similar, except instead of it being about bombs (well...ONLY bombs) it's a start-to-finish spy game with missions in different parts of the world, and both players are in on the action, not simply reading instructions to the other player - and after each mission you can, like we did, switch roles and play the other character! Failures are forgivable and not frustrating, with quick return to action. Cross-play is a plus, and it's very smooth between the PC and PS5 versions.My only complaint is that the missions from start to finish were short - we finished it, with us swapping characters to see both sides of each mission, in under 10 hours. I REALLY want to see more!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Buy it, it's an exceptional co-op puzzle game. You don't even need two copies because of the friend pass, so actual price is 10 bucks if you split with a friend. Albeit a bit short, you'll have a lot of fun.Honestly, one of the best co-op puzzle games out there. It seems that half of its puzzles are the We Were Here type (i.e. lower intensity but slightly more complex) and the other half are Keep Talking and Nobody Explode's style (i.e. frantic, usually relying on some sort of "is X this?" and symbol matching puzzles). Of course, the range of puzzles is much more vast than I'm describing, but this is just a simplification to give you a taste of what to expect. None of them very hard, of course. All the puzzles are well paced, so you won't get bored with only doing one type.As for the game itself, it's clear that a lot of love and soul was poured into it. The artstyle and character design is unique, the settings are gorgeous (even the hacker ones!), and a lot of thought was put into what each character's role is. Simply put, you won't just be solving puzzles as a hacker and providing the clues as an agent. The two roles are often reversed during gameplay, with both the agent and the hacker serving as guides to the other.Honestly, its only fault is that it's too short! I need more! As it stands, it takes about 3 hours to complete the campaign with one character, and apparently 5.4 to completely finish the game. However, devs say DLC is (maybe) in the works. I honestly can't wait for more missions!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously brilliant.  It's short, yes.  But it's brilliant.  No word of a lie, I loved it so much I held off on reviewing so I could make it my review #200. I wanted this to be significant.This is a game about being spies.  One of you is an infiltrator, sneaking around in buildings and being subtle AF.  The other is a hacker, in the very spirit of being a netrunner in Cyberpunk 2020 or a William Gibson novel.On the surface, it looks like it follows the template laid out by an older game, Clandestine:  the spy, the hacker, the teamwork.  Except it's very extremely not that game.  That's like saying smoked salmon and buffing compound are the same thing because they look kinda dark red.  They're radically different.In Operation Tango, the game is really more about communications and problem solving.  In the midst of hacking a network, or infiltrating an office tower, or whathaveyou, somebody is going to get stymied by a lock, or a missing password, or something similar.  The other may have access to that very thing, but needs to go find it, and/or communicate to the partner how to find it.  Sometimes you can see what they're up to, but indirectly--a drone camera, some digital readout, etc.  From that frame of reference, you'll have to direct your partner.So this is very much a game about communication.  A partner is mandatory.  A partner you can communicate well with is mandatory.  Even still, failures will happen, but the game is extremely generous with its savepoints, very polite with failure messages, and extremely forgiving.  If communications aren't happening, luck and patience might see you through.But again, this isn't hard.  There's a bit of sneaking, "cyberspace" "hacking", bomb defusing, and so forth.  It totally nails the feel of being a movie spy, or a scifi hacker.  It's a game that brings you the *experience*.Now, it's a short game.  I played through the whole campaign as the hacker in four hours.  I might go back and play the campaign as the infiltrator.  Let's say another four hours.  But the thing is this:  My partner didn't buy a copy.  Only I did.  One person plays for free.  Effectively divide that price point in two, because both of you are paying for the price you see.  And that's a heck of a steal.This game is brilliant.  I have only one regret:  It's that I waited this long to play it.  I bought it pretty much on the day of release, and I sat on it for awhile, because that's what I do.This will be great fun to go through with my wife, as we've rigged up a picture-in-picture way of showing what she's doing on my own stream.  We'll surely give this a spin soon, again.  And if you made it here, you're my kind of person and I hope you pop in and say hello.  .Oh yeah.  And totally buy this game and get your buddy to grab the free coop partner download.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid co-op puzzling game. With the way it was setup and ended, I could easily see there being a sequel and even welcome it.  The game's cross-platform and friend pass eligible, so it's a viable option for many duos. Keep in mind that you'll need to own a copy of the game to earn achievements.Taking on the role of Agent or Hacker, your partner will assume whichever is left. Both roles offer entirely different experiences, which makes achievements tied to their respective roles not at all tiring since it's almost as if you're playing a completely different game.The game's pretty straight forward, so no guide was needed!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Take space team, combine it with keep talking and nobody explodes, then make it a two player game and you get Operation: Tango.The good: There seems to be a decent amount of "polish" to the game in terms of looks and sounds. The co-op gameplay is asymmetrical. Only one person needs the game (the other can use friends pass), which is a great system that works really well. Setting up a game over the internet is relatively painless.  The bad: The game's puzzles aren't particularly engaging. Basically they consist of one person explaining what needs to be done to another. This could be trying to describe some abstract symbol, passing on a string of numbers, giving instructions that the other person is missing, or working on interactive 2D puzzles together.The ugly: It's short, only 6 missions long. If you play both roles that extends the game time slightly.

_childDocuments_.review: An asymmetrical coop game that kills it. Honestly it manages to engage both the "guy in the chair" as well as the field agent in equal measures. Messaging from hacker to agent allows for some fun moments not to mention the agents emotes back at the camera. Absolutely hilarious.On top of that it manages to give relatively simple puzzles without being too easy but also time it just right so that you're always under a good amount of pressure without it being a serious detriment to the experience. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a handful of escape rooms played out as a separated-playspace co-op puzzler that applies a somewhat silly  narrative to sell all the arbitrary pattern-finding and code-breaking. Thankfully, there were only a few stressful time-sensitive scenarios, and even then the checkpoints were super forgiving. Despite the secret agent theming, the game is pretty light on stealth segments and mostly consists of asking your partner if there’s anything about an ‘x’ or ‘y’ code/symbol anywhere on their screen. However, when sneaking is required, having a second person on the cameras makes the process more interesting. The game is definitely at its weakest when it reuses or overuses the same mini-games, but this doesn’t happen too often and there are plenty of unique spy-esq scenarios to play through.Operation Tango is an overall satisfactory distraction. While it's not the most possible fun you can have with a dedicated two-player co-op game, it's about the right level of challenge and a good tool for practicing clear communication. Having a Friend Pass is a nice touch too.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really trying to think if I liked this game and honestly for the price point, I am not really feeling it. Very little replayability other than to do the other role, but once you understand what the other person sees or controls, the game loses a lot of difficulty and becomes a bit boring.The graphics are nice but again, the game is so short that I don't really feel the full power of the setting was utilized effectively. _childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the best co-op games you can get. The gameplay is amazing and requires timing, coordination, and using your brain. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Definitely play this if you like playing co-op with a friend.Operation Tango does a great job of capturing the feel of the spy movie tropes we've become accustomed to. The hacker manipulating the environment to help the agent reach an objective and ultimately escape the mission area.Some of the puzzles can get sufficiently tense, but you're never punished for failing a puzzle.  This might be the only shortcoming I can identify for the game.  Maybe allowing the players to select a difficulty which might give failing some more weight on higher difficulties.That being said, it doesn't detract from the joy of working together with a friend in a remote location that sees something completely different to yourself.I'd recommend this game over and over to anybody who has a friend who's up for starring in your own spy movie.In terms of playtime, we finished the game at around 3 hours and spent another 3 with reversed rolls.  Even though on the second playthrough you now know what the other player is seeing, it's still fun to see the whole picture after experiencing both parts.People expecting more replayability out of this game other than switching rolls once, have a skewed view of what this genre, and by extension, this game should be.It's meant to be played once from each viewpoint and having fun while doing so.As mentioned, definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango
