_childDocuments_.review: Now this is a cool game! :)  Finally something that does not involve killing hordes of enemies and pools of blood to wade through. Operation Tango is the perfect game for firends or partners who like to solve riddles. It relies on talking. A lot. The key to solving the puzzles is 50% communication, 30% brains and 20% trust.  Since some reviews critisized the price of this game in comparison to the play time, here is my 2 cents: Yes, the game is rather short. But keep in mind that this is (a) not a full price game and (b) you essentially get two copies of the game since only the host needs the full version. _childDocuments_.review: Operation: Tango is a phenomenal asymmetric co-op puzzle game. The premise (a spy and a hacker work together to stop Bad Mystery Man from blowing up the internet or something) is just enough to carry the game forward. It isn't original, there's no big "twist," and the puzzles make no sense in context. Which is good, because if Operation: Tango tried to be dramatic or realistic, it would be a mess. Instead it's just the best co-op game I've ever tried.I've played a few other asymmetric co-op puzzle games but this? This is something else. Your teammate has a completely different screen, with a completely different UI, and completely different controls. It isn't just about solving clever puzzles, it's also about finding a way to communicate to your ally what you need from them, without being able to explain where or how to find it. The game frequently takes full advantage of this...disadvantage, by making the spy avoid detection, hide from someone hunting them, and finish a long series of tasks before time runs out.You may have seen a complaint from other reviews that the game is too short. With only six missions and 3-5 hours of gameplay (if you only play it as one side), it can be played in an evening or two without much trouble. But here's the thing. Every mission in Tango is unique and memorable (especially the train mission, that one was incredible). It's a bit like Titanfall 2: I'll take a shorter campaign that was worth every minute than a long campaign of white-walled test chambers that I barely remember any of.Except O:T goes one VERY big step further and makes the game free for Player 2. ANY Player 2. You spend $20 (and $20 is a reasonable price, in my opinion), and you can play the game with anyone else, without them spending anything. It is an incredibly generous move by the developers.I very highly recommend Operation: Tango. It's great. Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I'm doing my due diligence to tell both the devs and gamers that this was a REALLY good time--I only wish there were more of it.This is possibly one of my favorite co-op games of this genre. While the solutions to the puzzles aren't terribly difficult in themselves, the bulk of the challenge and fun comes from your attempts to relay valuable information and convey nonsense symbols, sometimes in a timely manner. There's something so incredibly gratifying when you and your partner are trying to figure out exactly how to get something done, and then something clicks in your head--"wait, that thing you said? I actually need that. Oh, you need help getting into that room? I can help you with that."There were moments that felt like we were going through the escape rooms of the "We Were Here" series and others that had the same intensity as "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes". If you loved those games or just plain co op games, I think you'll find something to love in Operation: Tango.At the time of writing, my friend and I have put in 3.8 hours, having completed 1 run-through, and we plan on replaying the campaign again with the roles reversed. $20 bucks for 3.5 to 4 hours might sound a bit steep, but the devs were kind enough to offer a Friend Pass so you really only need one copy between 2 players.That being said, the devs have said they'd make more missions depending on the demand of the community. So I'll end this review by saying that this was a solid time and PLEASE MAKE MORE MISSIONS AND DLC!!![EDIT]: THEY ADDED FREE DLC!!!!!!!!!!!!10/10 experience. The agent x hacker fanfics practically write themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its similarities to others in the co-op genre, Operation: Tango is an incredibly unique spy game that gets so much right about its story, gameplay, and visual/audio prowess. With it being so short, it feels akin to a small basket of incredibly good, well-seasoned fries. You won’t be chewing away at it for long, but that time you do will feel oh so amazing. It definitely has its rough edges here and there (including a few game-breaking glitches), but other areas make up for it to some extent. If you and a friend are looking for an incredibly good experience akin to Hazelight’s titans of the genre, Operation: Tango has plenty of co-op excitement, hilarity, and nostalgia to go around.If you'd like to read the rest of this review and more like it, check out . Thank you to Clever Plays for providing a review copy.

There's even a SpaceTeam style game at one point that was funny.  It's a bit expensive for a game that only lasts 4 hours, but there are not a lot of good co-op games out there.  It Takes Two and the We Were Here series are my favorites, but is a solid entry in the category and worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game if you are looking for a puzzle co-op. Each players screens are different (Hacker and Spy) so trying to describe things to each other is the right amount of frustrating and fun. My friend and I had a hard time putting this game down. You get double game play if you wanna switch characters and for $13 and a free friend pass it's hard not to recommend. Just zelle a buddy 6 dollas and you get to be James Bond, hell yeahThe only issue we had was at one mission there you need to unlock a key by doing this dot box mini game. One player can move the dot up and down, the other player can move it left and right. Basically get the dot in the goal and don't hit the lines or you start over. It ranged from easy to moderate. The very last one was a pain in the ass to beat, it was stupid hard and you would have to be a 'total masochist' to want to keep pushing through it. Which apparently I am lmaooo but my friend is not.We even met in person and I controlled both sides on two laptops and it was still hard to beat. Sadly that feature did spoil the fun a bit at the time but I totally want to try again. I want to see the other missions. But I think there should be an option that lets you bypass certain challenges or just specifically take that one mini game level out. Other than that, I love the concept. I love the challenges and say it's a pretty decent game if you are into puzzles/co-op/spy themes/escape rooms/ or just pissing off your friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is essentially for you and one friend to play together. Only one person has to own it, while the other can install the free launcher for the game (found a bit lower on the store page from the purchase option), and I think that's pretty darn cool. This game is highly reminiscent of the "We Were Here" games, though it is a spy theme and felt more exciting to me. I also found the puzzles to be less vexing in this game, and I spent a lot more time communicating with my team mate to solve the puzzles in this game than just silently thinking up the solutions like I did in We Were Here.Another cool thing in this game which I liked much more than in the We Were Here games is that the two playable characters feel so different to play as, with one doing the more "physical" spy work in office buildings and public places, while the other deals with computer apps and providing remote guidance to the partner. I played through the game twice with my friend; with each of us switching roles after completing our first playthrough (and all of the challenge missions). I got every achievement and just had a really good time with the game. It's fairly short, but I had a lot more fun with this game than I did with so many other popular games. I highly recommend this game if you like some puzzles and have at least one good friend you like voice chatting and gaming with.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A great co-op puzzle game that puts your communication skill to the test. The puzzles are not hard, it comes down to whether or not you can effectively communicate with your partner. There are six missions total with quite a few optional challenges at the end. The main missions have a lot of checkpoints, so you aren't stuck replaying long sections when you fail.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This is a co-op puzzle game set in a futuristic stealth environment that is all about communication. Both players see different things and need to communicate with each other to complete tasks. It's fairly similar to the We Were Here series except it feels more like mini games for each puzzles rather than each player having a puzzle to solve. There's some funny moments you'll have as you get each other killed. The nice thing is only one person needs to buy the game. The other can download a free game pass and connect directly to their friends game. The puzzles aren't overly complicated, it feels more like We Were Here for beginners but there's still good fun to be had. It's a very niche genre without many options but this is a solid title in there.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A really great co-op game to play with a friend. _childDocuments_.review: Its so hard to find any co-op games like this one and I have to say as we really like the genre my mate and me had some fun playing the game, but some decisions by the devs/design choices make me not recommend this unfortunaly.First of all, the game isn't made for people who like a decent challenge or want to scratch their heads for a bit before they find a solution. If you don't know how to proceed you'll be asked to use a hint pretty much straight away. You can obviously choose not to use it, but it sets the direction for all puzzles. The only slight challenge in any puzzle was multi-tasking, so the game giving you multiple simplistic things to do and expecting you to maybe fail in one of them - and even that was very easy (and this is coming from somebody who thinks of himself as someone who isn't able to multitask very well). Many puzzles looked pretty cool and seemed like a nice idea in general, but were way too simple and accordingly rather disappointing and very short (lock-picking is a great example for this. A fun mechanic with way too easy solutions). If you fail at a task the game restarts right where you died, but any currently active "objective-timer" also gets reset. This a huge design error, because it took out any challenge of certain areas the moment we died for the first time as we gained additional time/rescources without having to start from the beginning. You can pretty much not loose/fail at all during these tasks (the overheating cooldown being reset in the shaft f.e. Its the only "challenging" aspect of this section, resetting it completely but allowing you to start where you died is beyond boring and eliminated all fun from this part).Also, the final chapter is pretty much taken 1:1 from "Keep talking and nobody explodes". Not because of the bomb defusing in general, but of the way the defusing works. "If a wire has this colour do this with that other wire, if not proceed to.. - How many batteries does the bomb have? - How many letters in the serial number?" I mean come on guys, this is so obvious and almost embarrassing.In addition, we both did not like the pricing and the way this game is sold on steam. Please hear me out: Do I think this game is worth around 8€ per player or maybe even just 5-6€ per player on sale? Yes I do, thats a more or less fair price. But here is the problem: My guess is at least 90% of all players buy this game knowing who they want to play it with. That means you talk to your buddy beforehand and ask him/her if he/she wants to play it with you. Then you might want to share the price, as you obviously get the more or less same experience and time out of it. It would be so much easier (and way more fair!) for each player to buy their own copy or a bundle of 2 copies if you want to gift it to your friend. In theory you could share the price for the game outside of steam or (like in my case) just buy it as a sort of "gift" for your mate. But my mate does not own the game, he isn't able to play this at all without me and he didn't get any achievements while he was playing with me as he played the free "Friend Pass Edition" of this game which is actually labeled a "demo". So I didn't really gift anything to him, I just spent too much money on an overpriced product and kinda let him play with me. Why on earth would you not make the pricing 10€ per copy and offer a bundle with 2 copies for lets say 16€, so 8€ each? This way both players would have the full game, you'd be encouraged to buy more than one copy because of the bundle-discount and you still wouldn't rip off solo-players or the ones that might want to play it with someone who already played the game. Because lets say my friend now tells someone else that he knows a nice co-op game and as you can experience the story from 2 different perspectives he might want to play it with another mate. But he doesn't own the game, he does not own anything. Now he has to convince this friend to spend 17€ on this title or spend that amount of money himself in order to play it again. And thats ridiculous and I'm very convinced the devs miss out on many sales because of their choice on how to sell copies and make half of their playerbase not own the game at all. Because as much as I think something between 6-9€ is more or less fair for this game, 16,99€ definitely isn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun, and really forces you to hone your communication skills. It involves a lot of cooperative logic puzzles. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a good co-op game to play with a friend or loved one, this game is perfect. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed my first play through with my brother, and I was very pleased. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, quick co-op adventure. The asymmetry of it makes for some very fun communication exercises. Honestly, it was a wonderful time, but it's also quite short - able to be 100% completed in just about 7 hours of playtime on a first play through, even with the free DLC Challenge levels. My partner and I enjoyed it very much, but the lack of content left us craving more after we'd done all the game had to offer.I do highly recommend it for a fun couple evenings of asymmetrical co-op goodness, but do be aware of how short the game actually is - It won't give a lot of replay value for your money if you're on a tight budget, but you'll deeply enjoy what it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Hell yeah, this game is really fun! I played it with my friend, and we had a lot of good laughs. However, panic attacks and anger issues may arise pretty soon. Communication with your friend is key. You can play as both an agent and a hacker. Each side offers a different perspective on the game. With six missions in total, you can switch roles with your partner, allowing you to experience the same mission from a different angle. Additionally, after completing the story, you can tackle challenges, which are really enjoyable. As always, I completed 100% of the achievements. See you in the next game, fellas!"
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: I had an absolute blast with Operation: Tango, so much so that I roped multiple friends into playing it again with me, despite the fact I knew exactly what I had to do in each level. Gameplay works off of telling each other what you have available to you and figuring out which elements of information you have that your partner needs to progress. There’s a degree of randomness in the execution of puzzles (i.e. the specific combinations to finish them change), but you’ll know exactly which puzzle type is coming next each time.Nothing’s overly challenging as long as both players are conveying all the information they have to their partner. Nothing requires particularly fast reflexes, though occasionally you’ll need to be calm under pressure. There're one or two puzzles that're a little obtuse as to what is required, though there's a hint system if you get stuck.Definitely feels a little short if you enjoy the concept a lot, but I think the developers smartly knew that there’s only so much that they could do with the premise while staying within their resources, and I think significantly more content could’ve led to the game outstaying its welcome or the quality dropping (I’d argue the last mission starts to show the ideas beginning to run thin).Overall, a well crafted game that comes with the kicker of the friend pass, which is a genius and commendable offering to help the game work without making the purchase burden too onerous.Incidentally, some sections are almost direct copies of game design from Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes so if you enjoyed Operation: Tango then it might be worth looking that up to extend your fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun! The game doesn't take itself too seriously, but offers fun coop missions, where one player is an agent (on the field) and another agent is a hacker, often logged to a computer system, or floating in cyberspace.You will have to work together to accomplish the goal of each mission. There are a couple of missions, and recently they have added a few special challenges, which are like small missions in a training facility.The game is not too difficult, it is rather accessible, and it's not really an action game. It is more of akin to the We were here games.A really cool feature is that, while the two players do need to have the game installed on their PC, one of the players can just install the Friend Pass version (free) if the other player owns the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: warning: This game is quite buggy. We played for 5 hours and had to reboot the game 3 or 4 times because it had softlocked us due to enemies being invincible, our info desyncing so we didn't have the correct codes to give each other, one of our screens went completely black, and another time one of the in-game buttons got glitched out and we could not progress at any of these scenarios. That is quite a bad rate of softlocks, but mostly these were minor inconveniences because the checkpoint system is quite generous and it did not take but a minute to get back where we were. If you are OK with anticipating these issues, I'd still recommend the game, as we had a lot of fun. We agreed that we would even recommend it to grandma.You can probably beat the main story (6 missions) in 3 to 5 hours. There is some element of randomization, so you could enjoy it just as much a second time through switching characters, as each one has an entirely different perspective. An extra game mode is unlocked after the main story which might tide you over for a couple more hours.Unique co-op game that has good style and good fun, and while you have a good variety in what you are doing, it is pretty limited. Would love to see more. But more importantly, would love to see more polish.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really cool, the gameplay brings to mind Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes a bit, but I feel OT is more immersive and engaging. The whole game has this tongue in cheek feel, playing off of numerous spy fiction tropes. The tone is pretty light, but that doesn't mean there isn't some tension; very nicely balanced, that.The game isn't particularly difficult, but that's not an issue - it's meant to be a fun, casual experience for two players, rather than a harrowing chore.For me the only downside is that the game is pretty short, although to be fair, that's as advertised. Hopefully there will be additional content available in the future, with new missions or campaigns to play through.All in all, I think it's really worth a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Together, my friend and I beat this in 3 hours-- not counting full achievements, but I'm sure we'll get around to that. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Pros - great art style and wonderful asymmetric coop gameplay.  Really makes you feel like you are taking part in spy missions.  Over all wonderful gameCons - Too short!  we want more missions!  DLC, 2nd game, anything!  Clever Plays did a fantastic job and I am looking forward to any more Operation: Tango I can get!
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A Nice Puzzle Coop game something you don't see much in the steam store besides A Way Out or It takes Two.It's very short (6 Missions you can complete in 3-4 hours)Replayability = You play twice once as a hacker and then switch up roles to see how the other side. Good Puzzles but a few are randomizedTimed Events are too long for example the scene with the train there wasn't really any pressure.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an incredibly wild ride, and I loved every moment of it! The intensity and pacing of the puzzles, particularly the train and dark web segments, kept me on the edge of my seat. I wish the game was longer, but I absolutely got my money's worth. I kinda feel like the game was presented as a 'chapter 1', and I sincerely hope there are future chapters / missions released as a DLC.Every puzzle gives all the contextual clues needed to solve the puzzle. I particularly enjoyed the learning mechanic for solving each puzzle. There's also a "soft guide" where you either can't go back or interact with with a station if you've completed all tasks related to it so you know the answers lie in progressing the mission. If you enjoy coop puzzle games then I absolutely recommend picking this game up.

_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, but buggy. DO NOT RECOMMEND in its current state.As much fun as this game is, my experience was ruined by a game ending bug on the last level, where my partner's controls for the bomb did not spawn properly and we were unable to complete the mission. After being stumped for a solid 15 minutes and becoming genuinely frustrated, we looked up a walkthrough only to find that our mission was bugged and we were missing controls on the bomb.This was after my partner's game had crashed early in mission 4 and we had to reset the game.Unfortunately, if you encounter a bug, you will be stumped for 15 minutes because of the nature of the game - because it's assymetrical, you'll assume one or the other of you is missing something, rather than the game being broken. It was fun, but leaves a bitter, genuinely frustrating taste if one of your missions ends in a bug.As such, I simply CANNOT recommend the game in its current state. So much hinges on the gameplay working, that when it doesn't work, it doesn't crash spectacularly, instead it's a slow steady burn of your enthusiasm and enjoyment until you look up a walkthrough and realize that your mission is bugged.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: We played many coop and split-screen games with my wife, so I can surely say this game is overhyped and, in general, bad.I DON'T recommend buying it for the full price.The majority of the "hacker" gameplay is absolutely boring and annoying, waiting for a real hacker on the ground to make the main part. The role of "hacker" itself is a joke. You, in this role, are a proficient hacker's secretary.QC left the development team after 4 chapters. So, from chapter 5, you should be ready to struggle. Want to finish level? No problem! Just restart the game in the next cases: - "wrong" pin code - your partner doesn't see the mission target - the game just freezes in the middle of "hacking" the mainframe- etc.The gameplay, in general, sounds and shows in trailers as fun, but nope. Almost all minigames are 90s-like puzzles, which are simple but annoying if you fail a coordination check with a friend and must repeat it.Don't buy this game for the full price, and don't buy two copies. Instead, use a friend pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Operation: Tango is an amazing cooperative game for two players where one plays as an agent and one as a hacker. _childDocuments_.review: It's so good! but it's way too short. The story is about half the length of what I'd hope for the price. There is a challenge mode which is nice. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome awesome awesome. I personally prefer the Agent side but hacker is still fun as well. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a great potential, but couple of things keep it from being great and frustration-free:- The game is really short for it's price. Main plot is 6 levels, "Challenge" set of levels is pretty boring. And it's so bad that devs has implemented "skip mission" button instead of fixing it. _childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Great co-op puzzle games. If you like the We Were Here games then you should have a good idea of what to expect. _childDocuments_.review: This is some of the Best fun Ive Had in a Long time, its a little short but for its cheap price of 1.86 on ggdeals its crazy how much we got out of this game, the cooparation required is not all that big, which makes it even more fun for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like us, we loved switching roles everytime, and both of them don't make you feel left out, a really worth while game you should check out

_childDocuments_.review: A really excellent but short game; two full playthroughs landed at about 5.5 hours. The co-op gameplay is great; none of the puzzles seemed overly difficult or easy.My only gripe is that some gameplay is heavily affected by high latency. With high lag, it was almost impossible to beat lock-picking and code-cracking mini games, which require coordination and timing. It was incredibly frustrating trying to make puzzles work when what was on screen for each of us was so massively different that it effectively didn't matter how we played.Overall: strong recommend. Great game, great co-op, fun premise, very stylish.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - the game is OK if you want to solve quite easy mostly abstract puzzles with someone else. Beyond that there's not a lot to write home about.I would give this a "maybe" if I could. It's OK. Asymmetric 2 player puzzle games are few and far between, and if you really need something to fill that gap this will fill it... But it's very just OK. The good:Everything works well multiplayer implementation wise. Voice chat isn't ideal but also not terrible if you don't have anything else. Puzzles are pretty varied, you do get some 'stepping up' from one puzzle to a more advanced version later, but it remains quite fresh through what I've seen.The fine:The visual design, music, characters, story, etc, are all thoroughly middle of the road. There's nothing particularly original or interesting about it though. The puzzles are generally very easy, although there were some interesting ideas here that I haven't seen before.The bad:The puzzle design is completely disconnected from what you are supposed to be doing, ESPECIALLY for the 'hacker' player. You are apparently hacking into servers and the like... But usually this involves some very cheezy l33t h4x0r "going into the matrix" nonsense where you have to navigate through virtual worlds. This is true to a lesser extend for the other player - you're doing tasks that don't really make sense outside of being a thin veil over what is quite obviously an abstract puzzle design. There is the barest of connections between what you are actually doing, and what the story/world is telling you.And the world itself... Is lifeless. Outside of a few moments there isn't really anything in the world that even moves. Characters on a train just sit there - even while you walk around "scanning" them or whatever.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun asynchronous 2 player co-op game, I do recommend it. Only 1 person has to buy it, the other person clicks on the free demo "Play Pass install." Both people can do that for free to get a taste of it, though in that case it just does the tutorial mission. It supports cross platform play too in case only 1 player has it on the PC. Some parts remind me a little like "Keep talking and nobody explodes." which is a good thing. Communication is key. Fairly short game, hope they come out with more cases or DLC or something. 8 hours was enough to play both sides for each of us, and to get 100% achievements (most of which you will get playing both sides anyways, and the few others are fun to get, not grindy). We liked it enough we are going to look for and play other async co op games.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, but very short. Did the co-op story with a friend in just under 3 hours. If we swap roles to do it again, 6 hours total, excluding challenge mode. The missions are fun overall, but generally speaking the agent has a lot less to do then the hacker in a lot of cases. The last level was also very confusing, and i think the devs know. When you ask for a hint, it gives you a multiple paragraph text box about how exactly that levels mechanic works, and even with it, i didn't full understand it.A good way to burn an afternoon or weekend, but not a game you can get 20+ hours out of.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Don't usually do a lot of reviews for games and especially a co-op for that matter! But here goes!First off! I was introduced about this game from a friend that has been bugging me about it for quite some time. After thinking real hard on it and we didn't have a game to play for the mean time! Sure! Why not! Let me go ahead and purchase Operation Tango! Now! The best feature I'll give this developer that me personally I haven't seen from any other is having your buddy install the "Friend Pass"! Which includes them installing the game on their end without paying out of pocket. Especially if that individual is a bit hesitant for trying it out. No biggie! We all have people that are a bit edgy nowadays for paying a full price game and not expecting what we're hoping for! I'll say this now! It was worth my $20!Second! As much as I adore my friend! Please for the sake of your sanity and theirs. Make sure they don't get highly too upset over the littlest things! Ha, ha, ha! Some areas of the game can be a bit frustrating and take a bit of thinking! At the same time know! The rewards you reap for each mission are very satisfying! Take it from me!Third! Communication is key in this game! Whether you're doing this over Discord (which we did), or VOIP in the game! There's no way you're going to bypass this without having a microphone on standby! You've been forewarned! I won't spoil any particular mission in this section, but I'll say the one we had to do together. It "really" took a lot of initiative from the both us to push through together without falling apart and rage quitting the game! We just kept on b***hing at each other until we finally got through! 😂We prevailed!Can't really say much about the graphics on the game! Since I was playing as the hacker and didn't really get to see what the Agent saw from her POV, but I'll probably give it around an 7.5/10! Granted! There were some areas as the hacker that looked impressive! At this point. I'm probably just too spoiled with the 4k graphics on some games (*cough* Series X *coughs)! Guess what know?! Sometimes the graphics don't make up for a good game! At the end of the day! It's the core of the game play mechanics that make up for what it is and, again, this game did just that!Now for the game play and keeping it brief! For me to play as the Hacker (hopefully I don't have to go in great lengths to explain what the role does) and supporting my fellow Agent! Oh man! I had a blast! Like I stated earlier above! There were definitely some frustrating moments when my friend screwed me over (Sorry Martin)! 😂 To me frankly it felt like a chore to keep him in line, but at the end of the day. Once we figured out how our roles played. Cake walk! Being zapped into the Matrix (Ceez moment btw)! Thanks for the fond memories, brother! Lol! Helping your teammate impersonate a Mission Impossible task etc.! I won't go into great detail, but you generally get the idea!Overall! If you're looking for a good, new co-op to sink your teeth into! Please! By all means! Try it out! You won't be disappointed! I wasn't! ;D
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast of a two player co-op game to play with a friend.Basically:- One player is boots-on-ground doing the dirty work (equally fun & challenging).- One player is in a futiristic, VR-ish computer terminal (remember Wade from Kim Possible? yeah.)The teamwork & communication required to enjoy this game makes it a stellar experience to enjoy.Many mini-games share uncanny resemblance to other pre-existing co-op puzzle games, but the storyline & art design gives Operation Tango an edge that makes it shine.8/10 Gladly paid full price for base game myself to enjoy with (different) friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the reviews complaining about playtime - I bought two copies 50% off each bc i didnt realize there's a friend pass. I *just* passed the 2 hour return limit and I'm not even mad about it. This is an extremely high-quality game that's an absolute joy to play. Gameplay is extremely varied and every level/moment is its own unique experience. It's clear they've sacrificed quantity for quality and diversity, and it paid off. I haven't yet reached the end of the base game, let alone the free content update, and if it ended right now I think I got my 20 dollars worth, especially considering how we could play the other side and it's a totally different style of gameplay. But would still recommend it if you have the blink $$. Game is honestly fun and it's literally making you and your friends to blame each other if you're not paying attention to any details. 8/10 would be 9-10/10 if the game is longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable two-player puzzle game with a focus on communication and cooperation, Operation Tango puts players into the shoes of two agents working together to save the world from a supervillain.The game is rather short; in fact, you can easily complete it within an afternoon if you're good at it, though it obviously depends on how good you are at solving the puzzles.The classic spy vibe is really charming, though the character designs are an interesting choice, but certainly easy to recognize, even in a crowd.The puzzles require communication via voice chat programs such as Discord or Teamspeak. In addition, only one player needs to pay to access the full game; player two is allowed to play the game using the Friends Pass. Woo!The gameplay itself differs depending on whether one plays the hacker or the agent.The agent has to move around the level and find specific information they can then give to the hacker, who then tries to use said information to help the agent reach their goal. As such, the hacker's gameplay mostly consists of using hacking tools to open doors and disable/warn the agent about surveillance cameras/drones, as well as providing information to allow the agent to proceed, whereas the agent's gameplay tends to contain a bit more navigating the level and solving more physical puzzles, which, of course, require information given by the hacker to solve.However, the game does its best to shake things up and make sure that no particular type of puzzle is used too much. In addition, it also has a decent difficulty curve, as later levels can be rather tricky if you don't already know the solution.The story is nothing too special; the protagonists are just trying to stop a bad guy who wants to cause global mayhem. You're tasked with finding said bad guy and bring him to justice. That's all I'll say without getting too much into it.The frequent changes in puzzle types do a successful job of keeping the game from getting stale and for the most part, the players have all the time in the world to figure out the solution. Sometimes, though, the game will put you on a time limit, forcing you to think fast and stay on your toes.From a technical point of view, I don't really remember experiencing any great issues with the game, which is commendable. Also, it has cross-play with other platforms, so you can send an invite code to your friend on, say, the PS4 version! As long as one of two players owns the game, nothing stops you from playing together!...aside from problems with the connection and paid online on consoles, perhaps.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A game that takes Clandestine, and turns it into a co-op puzzle game without sacrificing the intensity of a spy game (which is actually impressive since the spy doesn't have a gun).  There is at least a stage that highlights the role of the spy and a stage that highlights the role of a hacker/cracker where they truly shine, and makes you want to play both roles to experience the fun in their respective stages.Voice chat implemented in the game is appreciated as it's an absolute requirement, given how there are also stages where vision is impaired.  I actually dislike those puzzles as it's difficult to relay in real-time on how to progress when danger becomes a variable.  But then there's challenging time-based, yet fair puzzles where failing them offers a chance to continue progress by completing an emergency task, preventing disruption in gameplay and its intensity.It helps to have great sound design too, making everything seem more dramatic.  I highly recommend this game, especially with DLC that increases its replayability, given the overall short campaign.  Just remember that you can't play this game alone, but cross-platform multiplayer helps make this more accessible.  Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the kind of game you want a friend to have. It is absolutely amazing, and I hope they get DLC/free updates in the future. But as of now it took a friend and I about 5 hours to finish the game and get every achievement. That being said, if you know someone who has it, you can play with them for free which pretty much takes away the biggest issue with this game (the second being the occasional bug)
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: super fun co-op game.  they even have a friend pass (i have tried it) where your friend can play if they didn't even pay for it.The puzzles themselves aren't anything too crazy but when you add your friend as the person who gives you the hints to solving it, it either speeds it up or you never solve the puzzle.  You know your friends so expect pain.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing asynchronous two player co-op puzzle experience in the vein of We Were Here and Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes. The aesthetics are fun, and colorful. There is usually no need to panic, ticking clocks are rare and well placed. Only one player needs to buy the game, the other can use the free version, that is pretty cool. You can go through the main story in about 4-5 hours, and after that you have challenges. All the puzzle numbers/names/whatever are randomized, so there's even some replayability.I hope some sort of DLC, or a sequel, with a new story comes out because the campaign had lovely cutscenes and amazingly done visual storytelling. I'd love to see more of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: A short experience for two players (100% in less than 4.5 hours), Operation Tango involves verbal communication to solve puzzles similar to Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes or the We Were Here series. The Agent and Hacker levels are both quite different and both different kinds of fun, and is just the right mix of urgent timing and slower, more methodical approaches. Including a friend pass means you only need to purchase it once for two players to play, which is always a nice bonus. The only downside is the puzzles are not overly complicated so while it won't wrack your brain to solve what's in front of you, it's still a fun game that I'd recommend for an evening or two of play with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good. A bit short, but a decent experience for the money. However across the 3 hours it took me to complete the game, we ran into bugs about 5 times. Multiple times, after failing a step, resuming from a checkpoint wouldn't work. A button that we're supposed to press might not appear, or I just had a black screen and couldn't move. Quitting the session and resuming didn't always fix it either.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game kinda builds on the ideas of games like the “We Were Here” series. Take those sort of core concepts - intimate 2 player coop, puzzles that require information split between the two players - and put them in a futuristic setting with hackers and agents and you have kinda the base idea of what the game is. For “We Were Here” fans I think that’s probably already enough to sell you. The fact that it has a friend pass system is a nice plus. For people who tried the “We Were Here” games and didn’t like them, although I think this game sort of improves the formula, I’m not sure that it’s different enough that this will click for you when “We Were Here” didn’t. If you don’t know about “We Were Here” and just want a cool coop game that you and a friend can play, I think this is definitely worth a shot. And like I pointed out before, your friend doesn’t have to buy the game, if they download the friend pass they can join your game for free.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: As other comments already said, basically a storyversion of keep talking and nobody explodes with more kinds of puzzles and interactive parts for both sides. Also even though you'll know the story I think it has replayvalue because the actual puzzles are mostly randomized.In my eyes easily worth the money, even with it being a short game as of now. That's especially true when you consider that you can buy the game and play it with any of your friends because of the free friend pass. My girlfriend and I really hope for more missions and it would justify either a higher price for the basegame or something like a dlc/seasonpass.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth every penny of its £15.49 asking price. Especially when your friend can join you for free. I spent 3 hours testing my friendship with a good friend of mine and we made it out the other side relatively unscathed! The puzzles are fun and interesting, the storyline was relatively fun. There were moments of hysterical laughter, shouting at each other and utter confusion as to what we were meant to be doing. It took us 4 hours to stagger through this game with our incompetence and they were 4 hours well spent.Pros:Good puzzles (Except the tile path they can go jump off a cliff)Interesting but basic storylineReplayability as you go back to change perspectiveGood length (not too long or not too short as frustration mounts)ConsWill destroy some friendshipsControls aren't as tight as I would preferMore content for when you've completed the two perspectivesAll in all this was a really fun game and I would recommend it highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, although the game is quite short currently for the price, although the ending suggests more content coming later on. Completed the game completely as Hacker, planning on playing a second time as Agent later. Had 2 major bugs which were fixed via a restart of the mission, both on the last mission; Agent spawned outside of the map and the latter part of the mission did not allow me to interact with nodes as the Hacker.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game. Only $20 for roughly 6 hours of play time if you swap between hacker and agent, as there's 6 missions in total. Not a ton of replay value here, outside of who you choose to play, as the gameplay mechanics in place aren't too in-depth or extensive. This isn't a slight at the game, as it keeps it short, sweet and to the point. What little time is spent here isn't a waste. Think of it like this, I'd pay more at the movie theater for less time and enjoyment.This is more of a joint puzzle solving game than any focus on shooting or anything like that. Usually it boils down to you relying on one another tackling various hurdles with communication. At times it can be a bit hectic with multitasking, but overall an enjoyable experience. If you want more of an action experience with a similar premise, an underrated gem called Clandestine on Steam is more up your alley(though it's really jank). To this game's credit, there's a Friend's Pass which means only one person needs to purchase it. AND it's crossplay, which is super commendable. I can buy it on Steam while a friend joins me via PSN. Good job, devs. Neat game. Hope to see more games like this in the future, and/or hopefully future content for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

_childDocuments_.review: It takes two to save the world in this Asymmetrical Spy Thriller. Pair up with a friend as a special agent or elite hacker, and work together to bring a high-tech global menace to its knees.
_childDocuments_.name: Operation: Tango

name: Floodland
detailed_description: THE TEAM BEHIND Vile Monarch was founded in 2015 by Kacper Kwiatkowski and Grzegorz Mazur, both of whom worked on ‘This War of Mine’ – before starting a studio that created titles such Weedcraft Inc, Oh...Sir! and Growing Up, securing a number of awards. - Kacper Kwiatkowski and Grzegorz Mazur, founded Vile Monarch and worked on Floodland after being the co-creators of This War of Mine at 11 Bit Studios. - The art director, Konrad Czernik, had a lead position on Dying Light - Kuba Pałyska, our head of design was among the key staff of Hard West - Piotr Musiał, composed the soundtrack for Floodland, he is notoriously famous for his work on This War of Mine, Frostpunk and dozens of other games! - Other musical credits include Neil Haverty and Misha Bower of Bruce Peninsula! - Those are only some big shots that worked on Floodland but we also counted on the help of dozens of passionate gamedevs at Vile Monarch! The studio is now 80 persons strong, working on 3 different titles and continues to expand, with teams working in both Warsaw and Wrocław. About the Game Update 1.2 – NEW TIDE Floodland has been relaunched with a complete code overhaul fixing all major reported bugs, PLUS some awesome new content, leaving you with a new world ready to build! As well as core fixes, we’ve also introduced three new starting islands, bringing the total to four. These will randomly spawn when you start the game, making each experience different. As you progress through the resource tree you’ll also find a new building - the Mushroom Picker Hut is the perfect way to continue develop you food supply. There’s more! Law system updates, 10 new events, a new achievement on steam and 8 new clans all come to this game overhaul. Dive in and start building your post apocalyptic worlds! Unite Humanity - Shape Society The climate change was a catalyst for a succession of events that led to the destruction of our world; rising sea levels have inundated the coasts. Only you can help humanity survive by leading your band of survivors on a path to redemption. Starting with a lost bunch of survivors, you need to scavenge resources, rediscover technology and maintain the peace between differing factions as you strive to rebuild society. Explore and Exploit The world - as you know it - has gone, replaced by islands, swamps and isolated groups of survivors. Gathering scarce resources, you need to explore the world - island by island - helping those you can and dealing with those who do not share your vision of the future. Grow Your Colony There's more to a city than just people. Food, shelter, water, health, security - the list is long and varied. Technology to be researched along a branching Tech-Tree, buildings upgraded and specialists to train. It's down to you to make sure all these needs are fulfilled; a job made all the harder with limited resources, space and labour to complete these tasks. You Are the Law A society is only as good as its laws; it's up to you to define them. Will you usher in a new utopian age of equality or is your future a benign dictatorship? Not every group shares your vision and the choices you make can have a profound impact on the future of your settlement. A common goal will make your society more productive than one at loggerheads with itself; you need to define and choose your legal evolution and which route to follow on the Law-Tree but - as with all things - there are always consequences. Unlimited Playthroughs Each game is different; maps, events and make up of the world are randomly generated, allowing unique playthroughs every time.

short_description: A society survival game set in a world destroyed by climate change. Explore, scavenge and build a city to unite the clans. Conflicting cultures and limited resources mean you need to make tough choices; have you got what it takes to lead your people into a new era of humanity?

_childDocuments_.review: Start to end, this game (80% achievements) took me 4 hours. My first Frostpunk run was about 7 hours, and I felt like I didn't touch the surface with that one. You can read other reviews to see why this game isn't great, but I will add a few personal points of pain:- This is NOT early access, but feels like it should be. It's not finished.- The game loop becomes incredibly boring once you have a stable second island. - The same "events" happen over and over, in a row. This means you'll get shellfish issues 15 times in a row, then water issues 8 times in a row, then fish issues a few times, and back to shellfish issues.- The game looks pretty, but on my RTX 4090 (!) and i9 13900KF after the first two hours, lags on double or triple speed becomes jarring.- You will run out of resources. There are many non re-newable resources. There is plenty on the map to finish the story, but it means you are FORCED to use the SINGLE exploration boat to find more resources.- Sustainable food is so complex (as in amount of steps) that it's not worth it to set up. I didn't need a single bread bakery mushroom thing. You can get comfortably to the end without buidling any of these.- There are bugs with resources not being delivered or buildings not being built or upgraded. The solution is always to delete the building completely.Buy when 10 EUR or less, but don't expect a masterpiece. This is not worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough.At first, the reviews confused me. Mixed? This game is great! It's FUN. But one review said that the game consistently crashes. And I can confirm this. Towards the end of a run, there will be consistent crashes, usually just before the next autosave. I am unable to complete the story, because the game cannot handle its own complexity anymore. Keep in mind, I have a PC that handles triple-A games at highest graphic settings without any issues at all. This is an explicit software problem.I really want to recommend the game. Sure, there are some minor game design choices I take issue with (scrap metal can only be scavenged, advancing technology is NOT compatible with renewable sources, I have NOT found an island where I can use highest stage woodcutters without it depleting the forests, micromanaging the clans becomes irrelevant at some point, you can't swipe notifications away, etc.) but overall it's a great experience. As said; I had fun with this.But the crashes at endgame mean that I HAVE to start the game over, even though I'm close to beating the game. It means that if I try another run, I need to be aware that I'm not just playing against the environment, I'm playing against the software itself to BEAT the game, never mind complete it. Because if the map gets too big, if I have too many people, if too much is going on, it WILL crash.It's a tough decision, recommend or not? It's fun and I really enjoyed it! But I've decided that the crash at endgame is too serious an issue to ignore. As such, I cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I am not having the issues that others are having with the game being unplayable. My game runs just fine. There are a few occasional lags when trying to save, but no more than Civ 6 or other games do as well.However, the reason I don't recommend the game still is actually because I just did not enjoy it very much. I played for a while, and I really dislike controlling all 4 factions at the same time when their world views, etc., are constantly clashing. At the start of the game, you choose a group to control and make decisions for, so why choose between the 4 if I end up controlling all 4 eventually anyway? It's too much micromanagement, and I really dislike feeling like I am constantly behind / trying to catch up so that I can make everyone happy. I would recommend adding features such as:1) Population increases - such as access to clean water and stable food sources increasing population steadily over time2) Option to play as one faction and one faction only (random members of other factions do not just randomly join)3) There is a lot of multiplayer potential here, but perhaps I am a hopeful Civ player. TLDR: Game works, but just isn't very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: It's been over a year since my last review. I'm still alive! It takes a lot to encourage me to write a review these days; I almost didn't, but given the mixed views on this, I wanted to share my point of view. I've forgotten how to style a review nicely so you get a wall of text.If Frostpunk and This War of Mine had a baby, it would be Floodland. It's a post apocalyptic resource and colony management simulator. It's heavy on the micro management and excruciating on some of the detail, figuring out how to do it right and survive can be brutal and will take some time. Considering both Frostpunk and This War of Mine are in my top 10 favourite games, it's no wonder that I love Floodland too. There's so much to learn, so many mistakes to make - but very rewarding when you actually get that ah-ha moment of realizing you do know how to do something, until you're eventually one step ahead of the game.In my current game I'm still in crisis management mode at the moment, my colony is struggling, I've not got enough workers, I rescued an old lady who gave my settlement the plague and I've got clans of people who hate each other and I'm trying to get them to play nice before all out riots break out. There's a massive world to explore but to be honest, I'm still trying to manage my tiny little island. And it's fun for me. There's atmosphere and there's story and there's meaningful choices to agonize over.I did read quite a few of the negative reviews before playing and I think that going in to the game you do need to realize how brutal it is, how much reading of text and minute details, how much micro management and strategizing there is, and yes, how frustrating it can be too. Not everyone is going to find that fun. I've never sworn as much at a game as Frostpunk on hard mode, but that didn't mean it wasn't a good game. Perhaps it meant I wasn't a good enough gamer. But trying, and dying, is still a lot of fun. Floodlands strikes me as the same; a game that'll keep me swearing at it for quite a long time to come.I will say that there are currently some optimization problems. I know a lot of people are having crashes when I write this. The game runs pretty good for me until it gets to day 100 or so, then the saving gets longer and longer and eventually it starts crashing after a save game and I need to restart. If I run autosave (which you kinda want to do in a game like this) I tend to need to restart it once an hour just to keep it happy, but hopefully this gets fixed in future patches. Obviously I understand the frustration of people who've paid for a game they can't play, but I do feel it's a bit unfair to write negative reviews within the first few weeks of release purely about optimization, without seeing if there are prompt fixes.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoys Frostpunk, They are Billions, Rimworld etc, I was pretty hyped for this game, even after playing the demo. Unfortunately, it doesn't really lend itself to new players. The resources are finite, a la frostpunk, but it's easy to hit the resource wall in early game and be unable to progress. Restarted twice due to this. This would probably be less of an issue once you knew exactly how you wanted to progress in early game (Plastic into wood into rubble, wait I'm out of research points already, no more artifacts to be found on my island but no way to get points to research boats to go find more...)  But new players don't know the system well enough to plan for this, and it's frustrating to brute force your way into this knowledge through restarts. While misuse of resources will kill your settlement in Frostpunk or Rimworld, it's sort of a slow painful slide into death which gives you time to learn more than one thing before your next restart, so when you do actually restart it's exciting because 'I'm gonna do things WAYYY different this time....', and then you make significant progress each time.It's a shame, because the game has some really cool ideas, a great aesthetic, and could have been an excellent addition to my post-apocalypse-settlement-management games collection. But I just can't spend restart after restart pushing through stops which feel like frustrating softlocks to get to the enjoyment - which I'm sure is there! Just beyond my reach.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game abandoned with bugs and poor optimization never fixed.  Sadly, it could have been a good game.  Worth at best, $5.This game is barely beta quality. There are many game breaking bugs that have not been addressed in months. Limited gameplay, lack of direction, and an extensive lack of polish make this game pointless. Every game is literally just the same exact islands, but with their locations changed. Save your money, don't buy it.Some of the game breaking bugs I have run into:1) Saves getting stuck and failing to load. Doesn't happen all the time, but when it does, it sucks. I can get a lot done in a short amount of time, so I lose a lot of progress. Yes there is autosave, but if you don't mind your game locking up for a little bit every time it does it, maybe this will lessen the blow. I don't like having to redo crap, no matter how much.2) Quest line getting stuck because of over zealous requirement to bring electricity to every single person. I've electrified every building. Every, single, building. Which you have to do manually. Just why? Even double checking by deconstructing all habitats and replacing with new does absolutely nothing.3) Vanishing barges with people on them... I mean seriously?4) Banish that clan? Buggy as all hell. Sometimes they don't all leave, then you lose the option to banish them. Sometimes they leave, only to come back. Again, no option to banish them returns.5) Pathing and basic logic. Workers live too far away!! Even when there are four habitable buildings sitting empty right next to their workplace. Hampered even further by an overly limited range.6) Your pathfinder party even with no additional people and plenty of supplies, will just starve to death. Rare, but have had it happen twice in my last two playthroughs.7) Some buildings when you deconstruct them will get stuck at 100%, but not vanish. You have to reload the game for it to complete. There is no option to cancel the deconstruction or take any other method to remedy.8) Some buildings will not upgrade, they just sit at 0%, maybe reloading the game will get them to go, but faster to just destroy and rebuild. You can also just cancel the destruction and leave it.Limited Gameplay and Lack of Polish:1) The UI bogs down late game, many options are redundant. Tech screen and Build screen category order are inverted.2) Tech tree is an absolute mess.  Lacking extensively.3) Not all places can be connected. Even though you can climb and dive everywhere, your people can't do a lot of basic things. Like having rope bridges, for places where you can not build pathways or stilted platforms.4) Some buildings can be deconstructed, but some can not, for no reason at all.5) Can not remove renewable resources like Trees, etc.6) Fences can not be restored or deconstructed, but some you can build over?7) Housing is, an afterthought. The whole system was not well made.8) Pathways blending in with the ground making it hard to see where you have placed them. Then deconstructing them isn't always a sure thing.9) Vastly limited ranges on things that should not have limited ranges.10) Places that should have limited ranges, having no range indicator.11) Going from Medium to Large storage giving you barely any additional space.12) Reclaimed buildings having barely more capacity than your generic options, yet taking up a lot more ground space.13) Same islands, just in a different spot.  If you've played it once, that's it.  14) Notifications just fly off the screen.15) Game drags you away from what you are doing for certain quest/scenario events.I could probably go on and on, more than I already have. Why am I so upset with this game? Because I feel that it likely went on sale as a last ditch cash grab for a game that probably isn't getting fixed.  The last word from the devs was nearly 5 months ago.UPDATE 5/11/2023:  The long awaited update with all the fixes dropped yesterday!!  Updated the game. loaded it up and.... none of the previous saves will load.  Fine, expected this might happen.  Deleted all previous saves and started a new game.  Played around for a very short bit, saved the game and logged out.  Went to play the game today and it won't load the save.  Same as before.  Gets to about 95% and just hangs.  Again, same as before.  This team says you can send a save into their discord and maybe they can fix it for you, but with as often as this happens, this is ridiculous.  And with how they approach updates and "hotfixes", I am guessing it will be another 6 months before they throw out an attempt.  It's kind of funny though, because when I saw the release notes the part about the saves really stuck out.   Saving your progress and hoping to continue should not be a gamble.  Yet here we are.Update 4/27/24:  Havent't played this game in a long while, waiting on bug fixes that were promised and never delivered.  Game had potential, but it is clearly abandoned.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, I have playtested this game for two months as of writing and was able to witness how much work they put into polishing the really well working basic concept of the game.One of the easiest comparison as a game style is definitely Frostpunk, to give you a rough idea of what to expect. If you are not familiar with it: You manage a small settlement of people and grow it into a civilization. You will meet other clan members with different visions then your own, you have to do a lot of decisions which will upset everyone, and you can constantly optimize supply chains.I really love the artwork in the game, it continuously makes me excited to play more. The music is top notch and it has a great replay value for me.I can wholeheartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: This is game is beautiful and fun. Other reviews have it as very similar to Frostpunk, and I agree (which is great in my opinion.) However, I can't really recommend the game because of how often it crashes and loses all progress, without any noticeable reason as to why. It is incredibly frustrating, especially in a game where it can be very detailed with what you're doing from moment to moment. Even after the promised big update and for a couple of hotfixes and it's just as bad as it was. The specific issues regarding pathfinding camps and shacks not upgrading etc. do appear to be fixed, but each of these were either very annoying or completely halted all progress as they came up, and now that they shouldn't be an issue, there's still the crashing. So frustrating. I should be rage quitting a game like this because of the challenges, not because I just lost another 30 minutes of progress. (And regularly saving doesn't help, because oftentimes that's what triggers the crash). So disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: Summarized in 3 pointsGame is very poorly optimized. I would recommend 24GB RAM for a smooth experience. Till mid game it consumes more than 10GB RAM alone. Yes, we don't see that many games which are bottle necked by RAM.Play style mimics  by almost 99%. Go for Frostpunk for a smoother gameplay.The concept, design and music of the game is really nice. The game looks beautifully colorful. The gameplay is addictive. You wouldn't want to leave it if you enjoy city builders or survival or management. I continued playing it at 10-15 FPS towards the endgame.
_childDocuments_.name: Floodland

_childDocuments_.review: I´ve been playing for some time and grown a nice large settlement. Now, whenever I´m trying to save, the game crashes to desktop without saving. So, since I cannot save anymore, the game has become completely useless. This is a game-breaking and very severe bug. _childDocuments_.review: So I have a love/hate relationship with this game. You might see me put more hours into the game after I post this review because it scratches an itch I have for these types of games. It certainly brings a lot to the table as far as top down resource/strategy games go. I will start with the positives first..Pros:This game is gorgeous and has a beautiful art style and soundtrack. The music really sucks you into the game and time seems to fly by very fast whilst you are playing. The upgrading/research trees and UI are interesting and very well done. They can seem a bit overwhelming and difficult to understand at first but once you do, they work great. The buildings and mechanics involved around gathering resources and improving the lifestyle of your citizens are cool and interesting. Cons:The optimization and performance of this game is absolutely terrible. Even with the render distance turned down I still manage between 40 and 70 fps 6 hours into the game and I have a 4070 ti. This is after having several settlements on 3 separate islands. As far as progression through the game at this point I feel like I was only about halfway. There would be too much to manage and with the performance issues that I would get frustrated and start over. Also having multiple factions on the same settlement is extremely frustrating as no matter what you seem to do, they never get along and will progressively become more hostile with each other. As far as the laws you establish to try and help each of your factions (Some of them require you to establish certain laws) almost none of them will all agree on the same law and therefore causing more internal conflict than beneficial. I get that the devs made it this way as to seem more realistic, but it detracts from the fun by adding another layer to manage (A frustrating layer at that). Lastly, this game does crash from time to time and it can be annoying resetting some of your progress. It has blue screened my computer once. The devs have been inactive for some time so one could consider this game abandoned. If for some miracle they release a huge patch that fixes most of the performance problems and re-balances the game I will update my review.Conclusion:This game has immense potential and does have some fun mechanics, however I cannot recommend it due to the performance issues that makes everything pointless once you see the flaws. It is worth buying and trying out, but only on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely wasted occasion.The game is really nice, it's easy to pick up, charming, fast-paced, original, very enjoyable.Why can't I recommend it? Because the support is abysmal.It is incredibly unstable. I've been playing it for some days and never managed to go more than an hour, often less than half, without crashing. From a quick look to the reviews and discussions, it's a problem that has plagued the game since release, and the developers never managed to get it under control. This should already be unacceptable, but I decided to give the game the benefit of the doubt, since it's quick to crash but it's also very quick to launch again.However, after not even 10h of gameplay I've run into a game-breaking issue: the game crashes SYSTEMATICALLY on save. Auto save, quick save, manual save, it's impossible to save your game. For a game that can't exactly be finished in a single go - not just because of length, but mostly because of the continuous crashes, not being able to save means that the game is completely unplayable. It seems that the bug was introduced with the last hotfix in the middle of June, the devs asked for save games to help them investigate it immediately after, and since then there has been no news.Three months with no fix and not even news on a game-breaking bug are not acceptable in any form or shape and clearly denote scarce professionality and commitment from the development team.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. It's like.... really good. Although this comes with some MAJOR asterisks, I think this studio might be going places, so I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt. In fact I have a very personal reservation here, and yet I still believe this is fundamentally quite a good game.The core game is fairly pleasant. Some cool ideas around the core management experience. It has a pretty Disco-Elysium reminiscent art style, and a jaunty RimWorld-reminiscent music (some lyrics in the music too, which was actually nice and atmospheric).But what I almost gave the game a red rating for is the law tree. Some socio-political concepts were arbitrarily grouped into what which side might support. E.g. the more "leftist" (in all but name) clans are against any kind of policing. It rings of somebody having learned about some of these concepts from American TV shows and YouTube comments.And now the more personal gripe: as a gay man living in the developer's country - Poland, I am particularly dismayed by the inclusion of Same-sex marriage in that tree, at the end of one of the "liberal" paths. First of all, in my opinion, it has no business being there. It's a post-future-disaster setting, the depicted struggles should relate to community organisation, they don't need to litigate just a single minority issue (e.g. neither race nor gender got the same treatment). Then again in our country, lots of people believe gay marriage would cause floods, so even having the option in is some kind of progress, maybe an overcorrection by a studio with worldwide ambitions.So the fact I'm giving this a thumbs up, despite that huge, very personal reservation, speaks volumes. That I even found out this is a Polish studio, also responsible for some other titles I enjoyed, because I was waiting for information about a game breaking bug, eager to continue playing, rather than uninstalling it and moving to the rest of my games backlog is just another tangible proof of how much I'm enjoying the game.Twitter says a patch will drop soon. Hope it's the fix I'm waiting for!
