_childDocuments_.review: This game has not updated since this review came out, so don't expect anything mentioned in this review to be fixed.If you're really into building and management, I would avoid this game. It'll probably only cause head aches, but it's generally fine otherwise for other players who don't play for these aspects if you can ignore the lack of player-friendly tools and severe late-game performance issues. If you try to play it long-term like City Skylines or other in-depth building and management games, you will run out of things to do quickly. The game is shallow, but that's not a bad thing. It's just important to know what the game is before you get into it.Game has potential, but it's got some pretty annoying flaws in my opinion. Before the flaws, the positives. I like the setting. The level design and the islands are exactly what I wanted from a game about recovering from the collapse of the world. Aside from the below issues, the core mechanics of the game in general play fine. I have no complaints about the ideas the game works on. I love the scavenging aspect. Sending a team out to explore the ruins of an office complex feels really cool, and there's no shortage of loot they give you. I really like the laws tree and the fact that it gives you different ways to approach the game. I can't speak much on the story because I spent all of my time building and finishing the tech and law trees instead of progressing. The game is basically fully playable without progressing through the story. There aren't many hard roadblocks I've seen except for electricity, which really isn't needed. The art style is beautiful as well, and I really like the Disco Elysium-esque portraits.The factions can seem a bit copy-paste. The only unique thing about each faction is the story bits (the little paragraph about their backstory, their leader, and their icon), which don't affect the gameplay. So if you get two factions with the same oversimplified "political compass" leaning (ie. new world and liberty), they are functionally identical and have no unique interactions or decisions in my experience. There are different levels of leanings and extremes, but they only really affect how impactful an event is on their reputation with your main faction. It doesn't give them any different answers or change anything else from my experience. The system gives "political compass" vibes, but the depth of each faction's beliefs are just as 2-dimensional. There are a wide range of factions to find (more than you can select when you start a game), but this variation is kind of made irrelevant because any faction of the same leaning is functionally the same. The game even acknowledges this through random events where a smaller faction of the same leaning will get absorbed into a larger one, and there's nothing you can do about that. You can get some factions making some really silly choices, or having some really silly dislikes. For example, the Commune's leader went to the gym a lot prior to the end of the world and it's still a big part of her aesthetic, but the faction dislikes when you give them gyms. Because factions have to side with choices you make, the factions kind of feel like immature children with some of the decisions they are upset by because the choices you are posed with feel so minute sometimes. Ultimately though, I don't think it's too big of an issue, I would've liked to see more unique factions though.Firstly, the performance tanks hard once you get to filling the first island. It nearly crashes every time it autosaves when you get further into your run. During the day or when I'm deconstructing or building a lot, it becomes a slideshow. I don't think the game was meant for playing long-term on a save. I would recommend entirely avoiding building out with the floating platforms in any substantial amount.Second, there's a ton of bugs. Sometimes structures you place or find can't be deconstructed for some reason, or plans for a building stay despite construction being canceled, blocking you from building somewhere. Sometimes you cannot click on structures, particularly the floating platforms, and instead will click on another building somewhere off your cursor.The game moves resources by assigning workers to a storage building, and those workers go out and collect resources in range. The issue is, you can only assign a current priority. You can't designate anything beyond that, like prioritizing certain buildings. You can't blacklist anything from the queue making it virtually impossible to manage because the storage building's range will almost always cover an entire island, especially at higher upgrades. The daily +/- numbers next to each resource aren't to be trusted. They don't account for issues or bottlenecks with the above so it can be very misleading and it may tank your settlement if you don't catch it. There is no indication of how many resources you are consuming daily, only your net positive. There have been several times where I have been producing excess food or water, only to find that I can't build a supply and suddenly I have a crisis and fifty people die.There are too many resources and they will overflow from the top bar once you discover most of them. You have no control over which resources stay on the screen and which you push to the overflow menu, meaning you can accidentally ♥♥♥♥ yourself over if you didn't catch you're bleeding a resource.There's no mass-cancel or mass-deconstruction for anything besides paths, which makes it very annoying to rebuild, especially if you're using the floating platforms. Each item you order to deconstruct creates a particle effect on each that obliterates your game, at least on fast speed. There's not even a keybind for deconstructing or canceling. The floating platforms are a cool concept, but their execution leaves more to be desired. They hardly ever match the terrain they are placed next to, and you can't change their elevation. This means that sometimes you will build a section of floating platforms only to find some of them raised higher than others, blocking you from building anything in that area. The paths are very hard to see as well, as they often clip through the terrain they are placed on.You can't turn off certain notifications like in Stellaris for example. You will get pinged A LOT. If an issue isn't solved, you'll get a ping for it the next day. And you get a ping PER STRUCTURE. This issue is a detriment to the game's performance, I feel.Not the biggest issue, but when there's one tree stubbornly preventing you from using that space, it gets a bit frustrating. Or if you're not using a resource, you have to forfeit the space. For example, in my run I only used farms, mills, and bakeries as my food source, so mushrooms and fish were useless for me and only really took up space.

_childDocuments_.review: I've done two playthroughs and have really enjoyed it on the whole. Great visuals, music, and story. Now, some gripes: while lot of the bugginess mentioned in other reviews has been addressed in hotfixes over the last couple of weeks, there are two game-breaking bugs still happening to me: 1) I had an expedition party member starve and the expedition never returned to base -- so I lost the ability to do expeditions for the rest of the game; and 2) I sent some survivors from one district to another and the ferry just stopped on the way and never arrived. At the end of the game's main story, you have to provide electricity for all of your people. I got power to 180 of them with no problem, but the 20 people who were lost at sea counted against me, so I couldn't finish the quest, or the story.  Very frustrating.But check this game out, maybe after an update or two -- it has a very cool post-apocalyptic setting, interesting mechanics, and challenging survival gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun post-apocalyptic builder w/ classic resource management meeting the needs of different societies (clans).Lot's of research and civil options.  Could use a little more clues as to how to make respective clans increase happiness, and sometimes the result of a policy has the opposite effect that you think it should... but... ok.Need the ability to toggle recreation buildings - the gym and the art studio consume WAAAY too many resources... and the only option is to destroy the buildings.  I had two full time, fully manned, fully upgraded recycling centers producing paint and the art studio (a single one!) was constantly out of paint.  That needs to be fixed.  Definitely some frame rate issues as more of the map is revealed (being fixed).  And that auto-save... seems to take an increasingly long time to save which can disrupt game enjoyment and makes me wonder if a crash is incoming (it never crashed on me once).Could use better re-homing of citizens to optimize production, but later in the game there is a fully auto-mode for district management (I didn't like that mode, but it suggests the devs *could* auto-re-home ppl to better locations).Kind of grinds near end of the game (could use even more research unlocks at this point - like unlocking more scouting parties or increase their load capacity etc.).  I also think that for a game focused on the "event", there are a startling lack of events.  Come on guys, you teased us with the contaminated oil drums... we need more!.  Calamities.  Satellite debris falling on us.  Contaminated cruise ships being washed up.  Cemeteries releasing their bloated cargo causing plague.  Droughts or insect-collapse or soy bean fungus.  There are SO many stressors that could be added to the game to increase variety and re-playability.  I love the look and feel of the graphics and there are some surprise audio tracks that are quite delightful. Given the sheer number of negative comments, I was hesitate to play... but it is definitely worth the cost of admission and is a nice addition to my post-apo builder library!Some simple fixes for optimization of consumption vs. production rates are needed - but that is trivial.  The frame rate issue is being explored but isn't game breaking.  The slow reveal of the event was nice and simple and enjoyable.  A neat mashup of raft meets flotsam meets frostpunk.  Oh - and don't make me electrify EACH house... make some hotkeys guys.  That part annoyed me.(played over the course of a week, loading my saves each night w/o ever a problem).

_childDocuments_.review: It's disheartening to see so many people giving a thumbs down and appearing to just not understand how to play the game. My entire experience with Floodland so far has been a single playthrough of the demo, which is limited to a given number of days, and a single playthrough (meaning I beat the main story) of the released version. I didn't hit any specific soft-locks or death spirals. I hit a couple of issues that you'd expect to encounter in this type of game:- A large population (50) joins the settlement, so food and water are suddenly in short supply- An expedition brings back a severe virus that takes days to recover from - A specific food source runs out, so you have to adjust and build something more sustainable and varied- Having to research new tech to keep progressing (How is this an issue? What else would you expect?)I think the game is fantastic and it's disheartening to see people not "getting it" because I'm sure they'll convince the devs to change the formula, which will likely ruin it and just make it a clone of whatever other games people are comparing this to. Oh well. I got to have some fun before that at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the only time I'd recommend this game is if you played Frostpunk and really, REALLY needed to play a game that went in the exact opposite direction in terms of tone and mechanics. I was pretty impressed to see that in a world face ecological catastrophe (but only an aesthetic one,) every faction you can play approaches the situation with hope and a spirit of community. That optimism is charming, but it isn't enough to save the game from its flaws.There are people for whom micromanaging the clans across multiple settlements, waiting on scouting parties (which can only leave from one island) to arrive where you send them so that you can manually direct them to anything worth scavenging, and then balancing way too many resources while being unable to lock down where they're all disappearing to is exciting. I am not one of those people, so I found all of those tedious. Which is a shame, because that's the core of this game.But otherwise? Just play Frostpunk. Everything this game does, it does better. The art and optimism does not make up for all the things it does badly.

Haunting music, a little like country-and-western meets trance. Surprising you with songs when you hit a milestone in the story.The mechanics are smooth and reasonably intuitive, although there are a few cases (interactions of the various clans) where I ended up gritting my teeth and throwing solutions at problems. The tech trees (4 of them) make a certain amount of sense, and the occasional folk popping up to request laws, request old favourites (bread!) or just puzzle you (hey, we found this doll....) add to the sense of being a puzzled community leader. Downsides: it's slow. I spent quite a while playing it on highest speed so my one team of foragers could trek across the map, grab the stuff, trek back, get it processed through my tiny factories, and repeat. Taking a good week or so gametime, luckily about 1 min of play. I'm not sure if it's possible to play random maps. I hope so. I don't know if this game is ever getting upgrades; again, I hope so. As it is, this is a lovingly made work of art, and good fun for the first 15 hours or so. Beyond that, i suspect it gets a little repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite similar to Surviving the Aftermath.Sadly it is way worse than that game. (And i did not have a good oppinion of Surviving the Aftermath neither!) It has a lot of "visual effects" that actually do not add anything to the game beside draining resources. In Surviving the Aftermath you had a map where you could build your stuff and a world map, where districts were present and where you could loot, build outposts and the like.Here there is no world map, instead there are districts in the "build map". You need to unlock the technology to build districts, to build PATHS (which actually do not really matter), to explore, to be able to explore more thouroughly and such. By the time you get your third island(district) up and running you will notice that the game will start to slow down. Very noticeably. I had to turn off the autosave function as it is a known cause of crashing.(I myself experienced it 5 times.) By the time i reached the end game as to say, i often had to reissue commands as the game did not register them, the game quite often "hung" as in loading, so there are terrible performance issues. The technology menu seemed interesting, until it turned out that for some reason sometimes it does not want to expand, and you need to repeatedly click on it pull down and right and hope that this time you can finally unlock farms, as it will be visible.The game also overdoes micromanageing. Just the call it specializing.The two most important non-renewable resources are rubble and screws. You will be constantly on the lookout for them, and they will be the main reason for you to settle multiple islands. (So build an academy for each clan:P)There is a "clan" system introduced, which is basicly a form of different beliefs and customs for groups, but it is just annoying, and you are better off shipping everyone to their own island, as when the clans live under the same roof they usually just end up hating each other. Due to this a legislative system is also introcuded with buildings tied to them, and mutually exclusive laws. But basicly...it is just a bad ripoff from Frostpunk.I was quite excited for this game when i saw it first, but it failed to deliver quite hard. I bought it for 6 euros as it was on sale, and it was BARELY worth that price. The game is not really interesting, the gameplay is boring and repetitive, the story is way below average, and the performance issues are just terrible. Overall a 42/100.Edit: I played the game with a PC that is over the recommended system requirements. I managed to finish the game with medium settings. So basicly if you are below the recommended settings do not even try the game, as with even low settings you might experience constant crashes not letting you get past a certain point. Which you will most likely encounter after about 4-5 hours of gameplay.Edit2: The game has stopped receiving updates, so most of the issues that are there, including the terrible performance issues will persist. Currently the game for many will be therefore unplayable. (Even on the recommended computer.) I can only suggest not to buy this AT ALL.

_childDocuments_.review: So here's the thing. I'm giving it a thumbs up. But I gotta say, it's because they set out to do what they wanted to do.This is one of those difficult, lots of micromanaging, sometimes depressing kind of colony simulator games. A lot of decisions need to be made. A lot of micromanaging is involved. The game is unforgiving and punishing. It's not like other city sims or colony sims, this is almost like it's own genre of dark souls level difficulty colony simulator games. So if that turns you off and that wasn't what you were looking for. Then go ahead and back out now.But if you are used to games like this, love games like these and was hoping it'd be that type of colony sim game then congratulations you just found what you've been looking for ever since Frostpunk came out! Cuz this game is a lot like that.Setting up laws and policies, micromanaging your people to gather resources and streamline everything so it's most efficient. New clans who can join your clan and cause problems for you. Death around every corner and tons of detail and specifics for you to browse and lose yourself in.This game does that stuff almost perfectly with a few hiccups here and there. Which is why I gave it a thumbs up, because if this is what you were looking for, then this game will give it to you and I hope you enjoy it. if not though...definitely pass on this difficult game lol.The music here is fricken phenominal, I can't praise it enough. The graphics are okay I guess. The sound effects are appropriate. The game has tons of replayability and length along with tons of detail, dialogue and decisions you need to make which influence your society. Needless to say, it's pricetag is very appropriate.If you'd like a more in depth look at the game with gameplay then please check out the video on my YouTube Channel (Link Below). _childDocuments_.review: I first played this game as a demo during Steam's Next Fest sometime last year. I was hooked from that little teaser of content and had every intention of buying this game as soon as it was available. I believed this game would be something special and new, and I was very excited for it. After reading reviews and watching updates, I'm glad I didn't end up buying the game until recently, but I don't regret buying the game now and can absolutely recommend it to others.Altogether, the game is... good, but not great. I wouldn't have been satisfied to buy this for $60, but I think $30 or less on sale is very reasonable for the enjoyment I got out of the game. It still has bugs, there are some strange interface and progression choices I'm surprised haven't been edited considering how long the game has been out, and there are aspects that I feel needed more polish or were just plain not good and needed some fixing, but it was overall a fun and meaningful experience. The art and music was amazing and the devs absolutely nailed the ambiance and setting, the gameplay is novel, and the story and progression has a way of drawing you in and making you feel for the people you manage.Floodland felt different than any other survival/city-builder type game I've ever played (yes, including Frostpunk). The game has layers of challenge and often makes you prioritize one problem over another; are you dangerously low on food or water, is there an epidemic, is your main island too crowded, do you need more people, are there not enough jobs, do you need more research to learn to build something to fix a crisis, do you have to placate your people so they stop stealing resources because they hate eachother, or is it finally time to advance the story? There is a story that you are working to finish, but your path through the game is not linear. You are making the decisions on what to do next, not the game. I found myself wishing there was more pressure to continue the main story, as being allowed to take all these problems at my own pace with infinite time to spare took away some of the fun of the challenge, but at the same time this lack of a time limit or overarching threat of some kind made me focus on the people and actually made me feel the purpose of my role as the leader of the settlement. Balancing your people's needs and wants is the challenge here, not the secondary objective only there to put pressure on you, and Floodland executes this challenge frustratingly well.The game is as much a political sim as it is a city-builder. Your people are not so kind as to overcome their differences for the sake of the future; these are stubborn people that devoutly stick to their political beliefs and will do everything they can to convince you to follow their ideals. When you have clans in your settlement that are on complete opposite ends of the political axis it gets downright frustrating to try and figure out what laws you should pass, and if you decide you don't want to pass any extreme laws the clan leaders will pester you about it the whole game. Some clans staunchly believe that laws that only benefit you gameplay-wise are horrible and contrary to everything they believe in, and much like real life, there are laws that are meant to improve society or foster understanding between the people that clans will still argue over. This system by itself is immensely frustrating, but it serves to enhance the severity of every other crisis and makes the game feel different than other games in the same genre.The way Floodland presents its resources and exploration also felt novel to me. All the nonrenewable resources seem so plentiful in the beginning and there's so many ruins with an assortment of useful resources, so in my first few games this lulled me into complacency and I failed to set up a reliable renewable resource system before a crisis brought everything crashing down. Renewable resources are not infinite and seem to replenish so slow that they don't seem all that important in the beginning; why spend resources on slow income when you can just expand to a new island and take those resources now? Expanding your settlement has its own risks and isn't always viable, and many times in my attempts I found myself running out of food and water and unable to expand, thus collapsing everything. It was frustrating at first to restart, but very satisfying to learn how to be better next time.Floodland required some patience and learning for me, and it wasn't always fun, which might seem strange for a video game, but I always found myself excited to come back for more and felt proud to overcome the many problems it thew at me. Now, as for the negatives... I experienced pretty minor lag and only a few bugs up until ~23 hours, shortly before I actually finished a run. I thought at first all the crashes I had heard about were just others' computers not being very good, but I did eventually start experiencing problems. I had a bug that killed one of my earlier runs where 120 or more people suddenly decided they no longer wanted to work because I gave them autonomy and I was not going to manually reassign them one by one for the rest of the game. The game started crashing during auto and manual saves (though thankfully it successfully saved manually) and I started to experience lag more commonly with a settlement of ~370 people across four islands and a large portion of the map revealed. Considering the game that gives you infinite time, it would've been nice to try and explore all of the available map and invite every available person into the settlement, but it seems like the game can't handle very large settlements.Recreation made absolutely no sense. I simply never passed recreation laws, and the game never made this into an actual problem, it just bugged me about it the whole time. You expect me to place very large and rather expensive buildings, some of which use up vital resources on a daily basis, in a place close to as many houses as possible (but you're not necessarily supposed to cluster houses up, the game tells you over and over and over again to put houses near workplaces!), many of which individual clans hate and grow angry over their existence and the passing of the laws required to build them, to improve the relationship of clans? The solution to clans hating each other is segregating them, not recreation anyhow or anyway, which is really strange considering a major part of this game is about making these people get along despite their differences.There are no hotkeys for rapidly switching between buildings of the same type. When you have many houses you want to upgrade or provide electricity for, you have to click on each individual little house and click the upgrade button or the dropdown menu and then click again for electricity mode. I've never used hotkeys much but there are cases like these where it's borderline necessary to have something to speed the process up/make it easier.The notifications are terrible. It's hard to tell sometimes if something actually important is happening in the settlement because I'm constantly getting spammed with messages of "your people live too far from the workplace!" or "X buildings have no resources to gather in range!" or "X clans hate each other even more now!" Most of the game these notifications were complete redundant.You can't tear down some old buildings that take up vital space on your small islands despite having the resources to destroy other far more complex buildings. It's one thing to say the sunken ruins of stone and concrete that don't take up land space aren't necessary to destroy, but you can neither destroy nor re-purpose some collapsed wooden buildings fully on land? You can't tell me these people can blow up old gas stations but can't tear down a little old wood.

_childDocuments_.review: While I would love to recommend this game - I can't.The concept of a strategy game set in an ecological disaster post-apo was really enticing and was - for the first hours - really interesting.The whole concept of scarcity, sociology & politics alongside a deep and profund skill tree really talked to me. However, the game quickly becomes painful with the expansion. Not only very difficult to handle but really, really painful. Aside the regular crash when the map expand ; the concept of "exploration" quickly limits you to your small island and you have to send expeditions that requires micromanagement in addition to a lot of ressources ; taking you away from what the game should become overtime : macromanagement. Gone the foreseeing of the politics & research. You are suddenly stuck in gathering enough ressources (that are taken away from your main camp) to send an expedition that will take 6 days to move forward on the story, only to learn you need to do it 5 more times to have the chance to move a step further and finally set up a camp on the other side on the tiny river. The game is itself is full of amazing ideas - but the result is sadly underwhelming. I kinda want a Floodland 2 though... with all the improvements done.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to agree with most of the other bad reviews, unfortunately. I find the general gameplay quite enjoyable, there are some neat new details, but there's nothing groundbreaking new either. My biggest problem is the performance. I have a pretty powerful system, but I can see the framerate degradation in the game, even in the early stages. I start at a full 75 FPS (limited for my specific monitor) with a GPU load of about 75 to 80%. The more I expand the colony, the more the framerate drops, but the GPU load stays at about 80%. We're talking a solid 10 FPS loss per hour, so you won't get very far before hitting 25 FPS and below. To me, it looks like the game is very poorly optimized and it's a shame that the developers brag about what they've worked on before (like "this war of mine") and then release such obviously poor quality. Maybe there is a reason why they don't work on "this war of mine" anymore? ;)Update: Please also refer to the developers' update notes on the latest update (Nov 16, 2022), where you can read the following section:We also have a "low performance guide" for you:We'll be constantly optimizing the game in the following updates of which this is the 1st.In fairness, please don't expect miracles - if you have a low-end machine, play at lower resolution and reduce visual effects. Please check the suggested specs below.Our "Painterly" art style doesn't automatically mean it's "cheaper" performance-wise. There's plenty of detail, lighting and effects that will keep the GPU busy.The game's complexity also naturally means that the more buildings/people you have, the more power it demands, which is especially visible on fast forward (more calculations in a time frame).Interestingly, neither my CPU, GPU nor RAM are close to their limits. The game is complex? Sure, if you say so. Is that the problem? No, the problem is that developers are not able to effectively utilize the capacities of a system. There are indie games that are much more complex and offer better performance, and there are games with much more graphical detail that run much better. All I'm saying is that even if the statement sounds like you (the player) are the problem, you are not.Take care!

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting to see whether I would feel the pull to return to this game before writing a review and honestly I do not because this game feels more like a chore than deriving any sense of fun. I do enjoy resource-management sim games and was intrigued by the different philosophies of each faction and challenging choice-based research tree in a post-apocalyptic world, but this game goes too far in the need to manage resources, rival factions, penalties, etc without providing quality of life structures that would bolster the enjoyment of these things in the game. You're often left hitting a resource wall and waiting for replenishment or scouring for things (or unable to scout for things) and then when other factions start joining the communit(ies) and hating each other, there is no easy way to disentangle multiple groups from different jobs/tasks. This game thus becomes far too tedious a way to spend my time. When I logged in last and realized that the stack building I was tasked at finding was in the far corner of the map and that it would take several more hours of basically the same boring loop to get there, I logged out. There are better games in the genre out there that care more about their players.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the game overall, but there is definitely some room for improvement.1. I wish there was just a sandbox mode that didn't have a story line tied to it. Would be great to play a bit in that mode before jumping into the campaign. My reason for this is that the first time I started a campaign, I researched the wrong technologies and focused a lot of workforce on buildings that don't actually do much, like the shellfish station. 2. The randomness in the campaign is alright, but can really screw you over early on. For example - On my first run, the second clan I found was diametrically opposed to everything my first clan wanted. They pretty quickly became upset to the point where theft ruined me. I couldn't get the tech to separate them soon enough to avoid this.3. Storage for food & water seems to be a little low. It does add to difficulty, but makes it hard to adjust quick enough when you bring a 30 person clan in and need to have the wiggle room to incorporate them.4. Auto-saves are an issue in late game. Saving in general takes much longer than it should, and by the time you've expanded to several extra islands, it is taking several minutes to finish a save. I had to disable auto-save because of this.5. Performance in general should be improved. I'm running a 3080ti, 32gb ram & a i5-13600K, but have noticed drops happening. This shouldn't be the case on a game like this.6. Clan relationship mechanics are poorly explained and seem pretty nebulous. You can be absolutely ruined early game by happening to encounter a clan that isn't compatible with your first clan. The reasons why your clans lose relationship 'points' is also poorly explained. It might help to have some type of mechanic to spend resources to improve relations.All that said, I am enjoying the game. There are some unique mechanics that I like, and the game has the building blocks of something really neat. I just hope that the devs continue support for the game and expand on the base of what is here.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR 3/10 DONT BUY every run is practically the same. If you grow too much the game cannot handle it. (crashing, frame loss) Finite resources tedious to gather. Segregation is basically the only way to manage clans. Electricity addition later in the game feels lazy and tacked onPlayed on Ryzen 7 3800x - 32GB ram - Asus 1080 - dropped resolution too 720p -- played on second highest difficultyThe map is technically random, but really its just the same map with the islands shuffled around. The starting island is the same every time including the resources. Story events are pretty boring. Far enough in they are just people asking for policies that dont really do anything. The game seems to be incapable of handling more than 150-200 people, I got over 300 and it was a coin toss every day cycle if the game would crash. Finite resources are not hard to get but annoying to get. Need scrap? building often cost 400-600 some even more, you can either send a scouting party to take a raft to an area, gather material (they can only hold 750) then leave. and repeat that basically non stop to meet demand. The other way is too either set up a proper expansion near scrap piles usually only 3-4 piles worth about 250 each. after that they are gone. The third and most annoying but something you'll have too do is set up an expansion, ferry over some extra workers, gather the piles (which you can only do at a base and not with the scouting party) then once the piles are gone, dismantle the base and ferry your people back. Very annoying when you need thousands of scrap and rubble to progress with metal and concrete. Managing the different clans with differing world views seems interesting, until you learn that you'll be spending all of your time trying to build a glass tower just so they dont turn to crime and screw you entire economy. The only way i found to stop them from spiraling into chaos was too just give any clan with separate views their own district where that cant interact with another clan. As for the laws and policies, they are essentially pointless. any buffs they provide to make people get along are either too late to be useful or too minor to make a difference. All the other provide boring unnoticeable changes ie eat 10% more food, 25% lower chance for sickness to turn lethal.----------- ELECTRICITY... IS.... boring... very, very boring. minor spoiler ahead -----------You fix the power plant. good job. you can pretty much only use that power on that island, likely far from your main base, and chances are your island aren't close enough to one another too build a bridge that would connect them to make them one district.... So you need to build your own power plants. rather, a coal plant or a wind turbine... that's it..... turbines are very cost inefficient. So coal power it is. you can make an infinite amount of coal so you never need to worry about fuel. but scrap... remember that, the material that's super annoying to get. your going to need a ♥♥♥♥ ton of it too make metal too then make the coal plants.... Great, you've made the metal got the coal plants, now too put those electrons to work...... but hitting a toggle on all your building and giving them a 10%ish boost to its production..... good job. that's its... all doneOverall, this game feels like it fails to achieve any wins at anything its trying too be. too basic too be a city builder. really only one strategy, only emphasized by the map being the same. Not a very engaging story. (regardless of your opinion of climate change) any choice you do make is practically predetermined by your main clan worldview.DONT BUY, 3/10 i guess. there are far better games, probably on sale right now

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a thumbs-up, but I give it with some big caveats which I will list below. What this game has going for it is style, aesthetic and a basic concept. You get to build a city in a watery post-apocalypse, explore the ruins and build a thriving community. You are rewarded for utilizing what you find in the most efficient manner possible, and for planning ahead well. I had a good bit of fun with the early and mid game here, and if the devs support the game properly, it may yet realize its full potential. If you like city-builders and find the setting cool and interesting, it might be worth your money and time.Now for the big pro/con lists.The Good:- Unique "trashpunk" postapocalyptic setting, complete with creatively designed factions- Technological advancement from sticks and stones back to electricity is meaningful- Exploration feels rewarding and fun- Player freedom in terms of choosing your own path, creating synergiesThe Bad:- Inexplicably a very hardware-heavy game despite the smol indie studio feel- Poor optimization causes big framerate drops, saving the game takes forever and crashes can occur (optimization issues may yet be fixed by patches and hotfixes from the devs post launch)- Performance becomes even worse as you get more people and settle more islands- UI is very rudimentary and rough. Resource inventory is displayed in a single bar across the top of the screen, not grouped into structured categories- Warning messages are displayed for too many things unnecessarily- Exploration limited to only one 3-person-team being sent out at a time even in the late game- Lack of a diplomacy system or trading with AI controlled factions. It feels strange when no other groups of survivors are doing anything in this post-apocalypse- Seemingly strange balancing with resource production generally leaves the player very short of the materials needed- Late game seemingly consists of an extended grind for research and advanced resources which is tedious, especially with being limited to only 1 explorer team to go out and find stuff

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a reviewer but I'll do my best: Coming from the tiny windward island of Wai'tu kubuli, and seeing the amount of sarrgassum washing up on our shores from climate change... Knowing that we will some day end up under water with only our mountains surviving the fall... Being the only country on Earth known for its nature more than even our Native Kalinago people... It can go without saying I've been waiting for a game like this for a while. This is a refreshing, low-key mix of Tropico and that other game with the British frozen people (I'm lazy and don't wanna look the name up idc), except the tropes aren't Amerikan takes of our leaders and are more like down-to-earth representations of actual ideologies we come by on a day to day basis, jettisoned out into the nearish future, and given the task of surviving amongst each other. It makes this interfactional connection as important as resource management and gives you an evolving puzzle that changes from game to game (I failed badly twice so I would know despite not having beat it yet lol). What makes this game unique is its potential to give you a true choice in taking these ideologies and making the pressures a leader would face in making them work for everyone's "benefit", which you also decide despite there being a somewhat linear story for the faction you start with. The backstory is literally littered around the map, so if you plan on focusing on exploration, you will be in for a spicy treat. You'll find surprises you can't guess re: factions. I did lost over 30 pops to disease at one point, but I felt more ashamed than depressed (XCOM) or pissed (that frozen British people game). You could also just build a lot of farmland and grow a bunch of crops but that doesn't really mean much without money existing, and naturally occurring resources taking time to grow like IRL, making your infinite-growth dreams impossible (also like IRL). There are contradictions being heightened and conflict at every corner to be managed or to let happen for whatever end goal you please. It almost feels like an experiment. The art is beautiful. Watercolors and pseudo-caricatures fill a believable world that reminds me a lot of Disco Elysium. The music is heavily reactive to what's happening as you play. I'll probably come back to add more as I play but definitely get this game if you're even slightly curious about one very possible future we may be facing as a planet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels utterly held together by tape and string. The balancing is beyond backwards and nothing makes sense. I am sad that at this point I have played past the point of refund, so please take heed and avoid this game at all cost. I mean where do I even start? Everyone hates each other. Like to a unbelievable degree. You have to FORCE people of different "clans" to live together. How can the same people of the same settlement be different clans? No idea, but hey ignore that and suffer.  Shove them all into the same tents and public places and pray its enough to keep them from actively murdering each other. Probably wont. Research is just stupid and based off a resource you have to find. You know how humans just couldn't invent the wheel until they found the manual? Or how throughout history the majority of innovations came when we found a cool looking doodad and suddenly learned how to fish? Or how yelling at each other in a room sparked the idea of how to cook bread? No? Cause it didnt happen. Get rid of the dumb system and just let me actually research technologies. Get ready to collect some 1000 pieces of scrap to create one tent. Or cut down two entire forests to make a single dock. The resource requirements for buildings, like so many other things, is just terribly balanced. You will be staring at unbuilt projects for days on end despite having a fifth of your manpower collecting that one resource. Worst still is most, if not all, resource nodes collected by dedicated buildings are considered "renewable". This is a lie. Your tier one crappy wood cutting station can, and will, consume every tree around it within days. It will then be running on quarter efficiency as the game tries to "renew" these resources by offering you a pittance a day. I will literally have my stations running with one singular person in it and still have all resources consumed by noon. But hey, better get that building to tier three, how else can you keep up with demand right? Just everything, and I mean  feels so badly designed! It goes beyond annoying, this game is a rage game hiding as a normal city builder! You will be slowly pinpricked by nuisance after nuisance until your very sanity is in tatters. Until the devs tear this game apart and build it from the ground up again, just avoid. Not even worth getting on sale, which I did. I feel  for having played this game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundtrack, nice atmosphere and a pretty complex tech tree. It also has an interesting law system (which probably could be expanded/improved) and clan system. _childDocuments_.review: If you liked Frostpunk you're going to like this game too. Floodland is a climatic city-builder survival game with emphasis put into relationships between different factions in the community. This game does so many things well. Visual design is creative, soundtrack is relaxing and memorable and user interface is convenient. To progress through the game you have to complete quests, expand your settlement,  resolve disputes between factions, discover new technologies, make difficult desicions and many more. The gameplay is a pretty standard for the genre with no major innovations and it is not a bad thing. It is just a brilliant game setting idea paired with a great execution.However, the game is not flawless. If you are a type of player who permanently needs 60 FPS regardless of the game you play, you are going to have a hard time here. Once your village expands you can start feeling performance issues. My specs for the game were RTX2060 + Ryzen 5 2600 and at a later stage it was hard to keep even 20 FPS. This is not that big of a problem because it is a city builder after all but be warned. On the bright side, the game never crashed and I never encountered any game-breaking bugs. Creating paths and bridges feels very clunky though.All in all, despite performance issues, I can highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Halfway through the tech tree, the game really starts to open up. You have the space to segregate your clans on different islands. You have the buildings to meet all of your people's basic needs. You can plan out your economy by having different islands specialize in producing different commodities. You have the overarching goal of restarting the nuclear power plant to inspire you to move forward. I was compelled to reclaim civilization from the flooded wetlands.The early game is far too difficult and the tutorial doesn't do nearly a good enough job preparing you. I was overwhelmed by the walls of text describing lore before I could learn the basics. I was confused by too many NPCs telling me what to do. The game punishes mistakes it does not properly warn you about. Research fisheries before foragers? You'll only have raw food, everyone will get sick, start riots, and die. Invite another clan to your starter island? They riot, steal all of your food/water/supplies, and people will die. Upgrade your exploration camp into storage on an island without shallow water? They are stuck there forever because you can't build a pier. The law system feels pointless. At no point do any laws feel necessary to continue. Exploration is too tedious. Must be started from the radio tower, limited to 1 crew, which must be staffed from your starter island, and can only hold 750 resources. Electrification felt far too tedious. After the monumental effort to rebuild the power plant, I was not willing to relocate my entire population to that island, which would have destroyed my supply chains. So, I had to build a dozen small power stations for another monumental sum of resources. I wish it was easier to simply relay that power across the entire map. Also, manually selecting "electric mode" on every single building too far too much time. After around 100 days, the performance of the game degraded, substantially. In the late game, the game froze for several seconds every time I selected a building or reassigned 1 worker. Since rubble and scrap are non-renewable, I hit a wall in the late game. I wish the rebuilt factory, which produces some scrap, could indefinitely provide 120 scrap per day and there existed some quarry which, once rebuilt, could provide some amount of rubble per day, indefinitely.Some parts of the game were an absolute joy to play. However, there are a lot of quality of life improvements and optimizations needed to smooth out the game and make it an entirely fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo to death and counted down the days until this game released. It definitely scratches that civilization builder / survival game itch. The music is REALLY good, the art has a cool cell shaded look to it, and there's a definite feeling of progression as you sink time into the game.The devs are very active on their discord, open to feedback, bugs and suggestions. I reported a bug today and within a few hours a dev replied, acknowledged the issue, and said it was added to their to-do list for the upcoming patch. I definitely recommend speaking up on their discord if you like what you see here and believe in its potential.All that being said, the Mixed reviews are justified. The game does have quite a few bugs, although the crashing people have mentioned was fixed yesterday (I never crashed, personally). I've sent the devs copious notes in their feedback channel asking questions about features and design choices, why does this thing do this, this doesn't make sense, this was annoying to deal with, etc. It can get a little frustrating because these moments happen frequently.However, Floodlands definitely shows a lot of potential and for some reason has grabbed my attention and made me want to invest my time into it, which I normally don't do in games that I feel are not 100% ready. The game likely would've benefited from a few more months of testing and acting on player feedback, but I have no doubt it'll only improve with time.

_childDocuments_.review: Floodland does a number of things very, very well. It is incredibly atmospheric, nailing the visuals and aesthetics. The exploration system is fantastic. Game progression is mostly intuitive, aside from the occasional researches you can access before the resources required to make use of them. Some survival city builders intimidate you with complex district systems, but Floodland simplifies them with shared inventories.To compare this game to what I think is its closest rival, Frostpunk, Floodland attempts to expand on everything the predecessor did well. But there sits its downfall. The devs were way too ambitious with a game that doesn't flow well, attempts to accomplish way too much through the various law, tech, and diplomacy systems, and doesn't offer any level of in game support for your questions. Ultimately, Floodland would have benefited from a much smaller, scaled back version, where the devs and players could become familiar with the base mechanics, and rebalancing before advancing.

_childDocuments_.review: ----------------------Update 12.05.23:----------------------New Update, new clans. It runs also much smoother, especially the break during an autosave is noticeably shorter. But the update changes nothing about the issues with the late gameplay. So still can not really recommend this game, even though I´d like to.----------------------Update 15.12.22:----------------------So, we got a few patches, performance issues are gone, didn´t find any more (gamebreaking) bugs. Got a playthrough together because I was so lucky to get a map that where the important islands could be connected up to the powerplant.Longevity is still an issue - getting electricity to every housing requires a ridicoulus amount of resources, resarch points and micro management (click every house individually, yeah) and once you got this the game is over, roll credits. I got this done on normal difficulty in about ten hours for this playtrough. What comes next?----------------------Update 20.11.22:----------------------Still would not recommend to buy. The game has become much more playable, but still. There´s corrupted savegames (absolute no no), a memory leak, so you have to restart every hour or so, even with 32GB of Ram, the performance is not good considering the art style and complexity of the game and there are more issues with the core game mechanics...My main concern though is replayability / long term fun. I´m pretty much done after ~18 hours of playtime with a lot of restarts, reloads, corrupted saves etc. There´s only one scenario. No clue if additional will come. You have 4 start clans that change very little gameplay wise.I pretty much got the story done, but my map seed has the powerplant located at the top left. And on an island that you can´t connect to any other if my islands, so getting the power from there to the rest of the buildings is a no noWhen you set up generators, you have to set every building by hand to use electricity by hand. In my save we´re talking a couple dozen buildings, and well hitting the right one if you build tightly is complicated...If you can connect your islands together depends on your luck / map seed. If you´re unlucky and end of with a bunch of totally disconnected islands - tough luck. Connecting islands itself is not well implemented, figuring out if and where works requires you to drag the blueprint around and if you accidentally lift your lmb, it sets it. But you can´t delete it the same way, you have to click every single tile, delete it, repeat. Also dragging the blueprint around is only possible in a very limited grid and absolutely tanks your game performance. I mean come on, Dungeon Keeper II had this figured out!Keeping the clans together ends up at the end of the day by either connecting all districts and giving them plenty of all recreation buildings (and then they´ll still hate each other) or separating them completely on isolated islands - which sucks because each clan only has a limited amount of specializations but specialized workers are required to keep your eco runningWorking with isolated islands sucks because for some reasons it sometimes straight up doesn´t work. I couldn´t reproduce it, so nw clue how to get around it. Also the interface logic is backwards and it just takes ages to get people from island a to b. May be "correct" in the sense of people need time to get from a to b, but I don´t have to worry about this mechanic with a good map seed.Some sunken buildings can not be deconstructed, robbing you of a lot of resources. Same goes for searching them sometimes, also appears to be totally random. I also noticed that sometimes searching buildings does not count against your task limit and sometimes does.----------------------Original review:----------------------This game has a pacing and a balancing problem.Before we dive into the review: I´ve played a lot of Frostpunk and This War of Mine, not on the highest difficulty, but also not on the lowest one either.Problem #1: Pacing You always start from 0 (fine), need to research everything (fine) and are locked into missions that act as a secondary tutorial, even if you disabled the tutorial. The starting island is always the same, so you could massively accelerate the early start - but can´t because you only get a handful of research points for every mini mission, that you need to spend on the right things, else you lock yourself out of any further progressThe next thing is, you´re always short on people. So that means you can´t keep up researching and stockpiling and exploring new islands, because exploring requires people and resources. But exploring is mandatory to get to new non renewable resources and tokes which are the main way to enable research.Transitioning over to problem #2: BalanceWhile the base island is always the same, the stuff you find in abandoned houses is not (fine). Also many houses have a secondary storage layer that you need lockpicks for - which you can only find in houses in the beginning. So in some games you get a massive boost because you find enough lockpicks and in some you´re missing out until you get to explore more islands - which takes way longer because you don´t have the resources.Getting people requires you to explore - to know where to explore you should use the radiotower to know where you get new people - which requires another resource (fine), but not only does the radiotower like to reveal houses on the same island, or even on an already settled isalnd it also likes to show you a people pickup way to far away, on an island you can´t explore because it´s tech locked. This might also be a problem with the map seeding which would make it infinitely worse.And when you get enough people to get your eco up and running, the real trouble starts. The game has 4 factions, yours always get´s kinda along with 2 others and not at all with the 4th one - if you find the 4th one as first extra people you´re screwed. You desperately need them, but they don´t get along with your people, they will hate all decisions your people like and all laws your people like. But even with the 2 tribes you kinda get along it´s super frustrating because the relationship system is not explained at all. I had two games where I met the same tribe and did mostly the same thing, in the first one they hated me, in the second one we got along.All in all this game has interesting core mechanics, but for now I give it a break and wait for some patches. Also I´m kinda concerned for the longevity, Frostpunk started with clear communication that more scenarios would come, floodland seems to have only one and no mention that it´ll get more.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of positives and it could be a decent game but I doubt it will. I thought this was early-access but amazingly it isn't so I'll rate it accordingly. It's like reading a story on a bunch of soggy pages collected together and you aren't really sure whether they're all there. I suspect it's a story where the tribes all speak a different language and don't comprehend sign language. They're all as far apart as the Nazis are from Primrose Primary School. This needs a lot of word to make it playable.It's fun for a while. You get a small island and you need to move about and search out other little\tiny islands. Along the way you rescue people and add them to your workforce. They remain in their own tribe and everyone HATES everyone else. They aren't content that there are more people to do the work or that they now have a source of food, water and shelter. They just spend all their time antagonising each other until it breaks out into open hostility. You various options to placate them but the hostility goes up (very rapidly) It doesn't matter what law or decision you make, nothing seems to work. Even saving and retrying all the options doesn't help. You get a bonfire and a canteen that tells you things are looking up but it changes nothing however many of each you build.The small islands are pitted with trees and lamp posts that you can't quickly remove so you're hampered with your layout. The buildings aren't easily identified and the whole thing is an untidy mess of brown objects stuck on an island. Keeping people alive isn't a problem other than you keep them alive to be yet another loathsome person. The best outcome would be to let them all die. When you eventually reach that conclusion there really is no point in playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I took me 22 hours to finish it in normal difficulty. Pros: I really enjoyed the story which is very interesting and kept me playing longer. The design of the game is also fantastic. Overall, the game is not very hard or too technical and it didn't take me long to get a hang of it. Cons:Not very good graphics, I wish they were better. I experienced some performance issues once I reached a population of more than 100 though.. I have a RTX 3090 and a very good computer configuration, so I know for sure it was not me. Fortunately, I found a quick fix. I just saved the game, closed it, waited for a couple of minutes, and opened it again. I didn't have to do that very often. I just probably did it 2-3 times. Overall,I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the usual Post-Apocalyptic gameRather than dealing with a world destroyed by nuclear fire, Floodland deals with (obviously) a flooded worldYou control a small group of survivors who are looking for a new homeYou must send them out to scavenge materials and food items in order to surviveThere is also research to complete to unlock better and bigger buildings, ranging from simple homes to large buildings that harvest local resourcesThere is also an underlying story where your survivors are hunting for a power plant which will make life much easierI have only spent a few hours in the game, but I also spent some time with the demoThis game is definitely worth a look if you like lite-strategy games

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually one to notice the music of a game but this one I really liked it, especially how certain songs would play during specific story events/triggers which made it stand out a lot more. Also how most of the music was instrumental, the few times when I heard vocals I knew something important was going down.When it comes to Citybuilders the game is very much on the liner side which is something to keep in mind, but that's fine as instead of going for a more sandbox approach like some game, here they opted to focus more more on the narrative and storytelling where the gameplay was more of a tool to ferry you along that journey which I particularity enjoyed.As the game progressed and I got more people and buildings it did tank the performance of the game a fair bit, and every autosave would cause the game to lock up for 10 seconds, but aside from said performance issues I didn't notice any other kinds of bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 30 hours I lost pleasure in playing. The game is kind of frustrating in a bad way. As a management game player is almost always confused about how much he is earning and how much resources he needs, buildings don't show clear information on how much resources they consume to operate. Storages work as a kind of Stargates, so Players really don't need to manage distributions. Probably it's a good solution, to avoid using the game pathfinding mechanic that is kind of buggy. Clean concept is really not very engaging or great. All people in the game were once Americans, and now they are the Clans and they do not reintegrate, and they kind of don't want to leave together but they still do. It's really confusing … Politics and Influence concepts are not very thoughtful or useful. It isn't a Paradox level of development… I like the idea of places to gather that influence relations between people, but why can't people convert their views there? Game kind of want to show how relations between clans based on world views can be dynamic, at the same time don't even try to touch how people's world views can be dynamic, and assume they are constant. IMHO, in front of the Floodland there is a long way to be a good engaging game.

_childDocuments_.review: Floodland is an excellent management game with a soul, a strong ecological and political message and which offers real choices to guide your group of survivors.Unlike other survival management games, despite the difficulties you face such as finding a good balance between your population and your productions - especially of water and food - it offers a fairly positive message of solidarity and hope.The musical atmosphere is particularly pleasant (please go check the OST on YouTube, it's a delight !) and the design of the buildings, colorful and inspired by low tech, offers a particular character to your camps.I encountered a bug which was a little annoying - but not game breaking - regarding the expansion of residential buildings, but nothing insurmountable, and the devs are already working on it.The devs seem to be mindful to the messages posted on their Discord and seem to be preparing patches in the future, so I can't wait to see what they have in store for us to improve and enrich their work !

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful looking game, very easy on the eye to play. I like the mechanics of the game - the dependencies between tech tree branches is great and learning the clan interaction and island mechanics was enjoyable (takes a bit as the tutorial doesn't give much but all the stats are in the dashboards). I finished the campaign thinking I could do it better but not sure if I'm ready to play it again. The game isnt difficult once you understand its mechanics but it takes a long time to play; once you get your stockpiles up to weather the random events and you have your clans and districts sorted its just a slog to the final objective. In my playthrough it seemed there were a lot of laws, techs and buildings that simply weren't needed and were offered only to strengthen the specialisation aspect of the game (which I also didnt find necessary to win) - i.e. didnt provide depth to the experience.I might play one more time just to make sure the above is accurate, trick will be finding a whole weekend to do so! EDIT: played it once more on hard difficulty, had some early game panic but ended up reaffirming my initial view. At just 2 playthroughs before retiring it, I cant recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I would like to say that the Devs deserve an awful lot of credit, two hot fixes in 48 hours fixed 99% of all technical issues. This sure beats my expectations and the expectations set by other city building studios (*cough*Paradox*cough*). Still obsessed with the game, and I maintain at times it looks like an impressionist painting on the move, it's amazing. This title has an awful lot going for it, given the art style, direction and music. The Frostpunk comparison is a good one, albeit obvious. What I can point to as a difference is this seems a tad more hopeful(?), if that is the right word to chose. Many of the factions you chose to lead talk a lot about making a better, different society and it seems like the law tree and tech trees give you the options to back that up. It must be said that I've had some performance issues, from some infrequent crashes (usually while navigating the tech tree), and it doesn't always look it's best despite the fact that I have a 30's series card. If you have a tolerance for jank, I would still say dive in, as it seems like the Dev's are surely dedicated and more or less plugged in. It seems these guys have a better formula for a game like this compared to the offerings from Paradox and the like that are in a similar vein.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: My game is officially broken. I can't place exploration camps and customer support has given me zero help. They directed me to their Discord server which appears to be abandoned. Y'all need to fix these issues or stop selling a broken game.I really love this game. It's challenging, immersive, and I really like the themes. It's definitely the kind of thing I'm into and I'm excited that it exists. There are a number of things that are a little too frustrating, like inability to manage residents on a more involved manner (because it DOES matter who is doing what and where). Resource limitations means you're constantly struggling to keep up with needs for both survival and construction, and the high cost of building along with the very limited resources that do run out temporarily (so you have to constantly be moving people around - not fun) often means you need more manpower than you can support. You spend less time getting to explore because you're juggling a bunch of stuff that really shouldn't need to be juggled. It detracts from the story! I have other critiques, but ultimately, this could be such an amazing game with some tweaks and added/adjusted features. I'm disappointed because it seems like there hasn't been an update in a long time, which could mean they'be abandoned this fantastic game. PLEASE DON'T GIVE UP! IT'S SO GOOD!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Short intro about me: Generally enjoys all kinds of RTS, City Building, City simulations, Factory/Automation building, Strategie Games or anything related to civilization simulation or similar genres.Example games: Almost all Sidmeiers Civ games, Frostpunk, Rim World, Age of Empires 1-4, Cities Skylines, Factorio, Satisfactory, The wandering Village, Stardew Valley, Farthes Frontier, Dune: Spice Wars, Starbound , Terraria, Minecraft and so on and on i could name many more but you get the idea.So to keep it "short":If you understand and think about what the game is trying to be the game is a good, maybe even a great game. It has a variety of Clans(Civiliations) which are kind of unique in their own way, the bad thing is that the expirience system for the clans breaks the unique aspects. Im realising this is going to be a little more indepth than i was planning to write but ill let you guys know so i will structure it a litte better.Positive:1. For its price you get a amount of content. Msrp: 29,99€ (Available in sale for 22€-24€)2. I would guess to get all Archievements you would need 20 Hours the maximum at its current state, so if you buy this game in sale for 22-24€ and you want to get one hour of good gameplay per euro/dollar/whatever currency then i think 1.20€-1,40€ per gameplay hour is a fair and good price3. The Archievments are nice for completionists/ArchievmentHutner and are not stupid grinds and all of them are well balanced in terms of possibility of actually getting them without beeing to easy. (Currently got 21/28 with 11~ Hours of playtime, gotta say i took a look on them while playing and actively tried to do them)4. In my opinion the Musik is great and gives a good abience while playing. Around when the mid-game starts the musik kicks in really good and lets you sink into the game. Really gave me the feeling of managen my people and ressources in this dystopian setting5. Tech Trees are cool and Big, you get multiple categories like Exploration, Survival, Growth etc without beeing overly complex or to huge just for the sake of having a big Tech tree6. The Graphics have their own unique charm and style which i personally like7. Its hard to have unique buildings as this kind of genre obviously needs things which are very similar to other games in the genre but i felt like they still managed to make the buildings not feel like another XYZ Building from any other game.Negative:10. I first want to start with a negativ part as it feels this is responsible for 95%+ why i woulndt recommend this game. THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PERFORMANCE IS REALLY THAT BAD DONT LISTEN TO PEOPLE CURRENTLY STATING THAT ITS NOT TRUE!I have 16GB of RAM, RTX 2080, Intel i7 5820k, NVMe SSD with enough free space! I didnt specifically check my FPS Count because i never care if its 50fps, 70fps, 120fps or whatever as i mostly play above mentioned games. To be fair, my CPU is getting old, yes i know. but my overall setup including my CPU is still pretty decent. My specs are above the ones the developer recommends and once again yes, my CPU is getting old but still very close to the recommended specs. The first 1-2 the game is very playable and enjoyable but then every mouse move starts to lag a lot, saving takes up to 5 minutes sometimes, clicking on buttons (e.g. assigning people to work buildings) is so laggy that i sometimes have to do it 2-4 times till the action actually happend. Seriously, i can basically play any game and i never expirienced such bad performance. The archievment of finishing the Main story only have 5%~ of People. Im wondering why? Maybe because the performance gets so bad that most people dont want to bother with it? And yes, i dont have this one yet aswell because of the bad performance.In addition to that  when loading  a mid to late-game save is not possible, it will crash because of the bad performance. I could continou but i assume you get the point.11. Game Breaking bugs: For example when migrating people to other islands they sometimes just "get lost". With that i mean that when sending people to other islands they sometimes dissappear or be stuck and the Departure/Arrival tab and dont make any progress. There was a quest regarding giving all people a proper house but this was broken because of the stuck people migrating. I thought im gonna be smart and abandone the whole clan of 120 people but even doing that those people which have been stuck still have been there and i was unable to progress which basically forced me to give up on this playthrough. 12. Still many and other similar bugs like mentioned above, still feels like early access which i generally dont mind but then dont make a "Full official Release" when the game is in this state regarding bugs and especially the performance.13. Its hard to be innovative without failing, nevertheless there are some more smaler and more major game design issues. For example: beeing able to level up the individual skills/abilities of a clan by making them study in a research building to gain exp for this clan sounds really cool and like a great idea but the execution of this idea was done very poorly. To keep it short: Beeing able to make all clans have the ability any clan can quickly learn takes away the aspects of beeing really in need for other clans, at this point other clans only bring annoying micro managing problems without(!) giving you any benefits of dealing with this besides the basic improvements every clan has. The big problem is that those clan specific bonuses and increasing the level of the ability (e.g. fortitude or others) dont feel like they have any impact at all they are simply so small and weak. Currently the boring recommendation is to ignore any other clans and abandon them besides the one you started with and make all nomads join the same clan and make them learn the remaining abilities quickly, makes it much easier to keep an overview of which people to put into the buildings. Im tired of writing a review but im sure i covered most of the important things.Maybe one neutral point:14. The replayability of the game is pretty poor unless you give yourself different challenges e.g. finishing the main story with only one kind of clan but to do it with all of them. I personally like if there is a game you simply can play and enjoy and then be done with the content and be excited for a cool content update, free or even small dlcs (e.g. i bought all of the Northgard clans for 6€ each, those have cost me more than the actual base game just because its so good in my opinion)TLDR for Players;If you generally like this kind of game and genre you will get your money worth for sure. BUT ONLY BUY THE GAME ONCE THE PERFORMANCE HAS BEEN FIXED AND VERIFIED BUT INDEPENDENT PEOPLETLDR for the developers;I dont want to sound mean, im just trying to be honest. The game is really good and the design flaws are acceptable and its alright to improve and iterate even after EarlyAccess is done and the Release is Official now.BUT,seriously, in my opinion you should asap fix the performance and leave everything else on the side. Im not a game developer but im a Java developer and i know this takes money and especially time. And its not a fun job for the developers aswell to find and fix the bugs and "simply fix the performance" is much much easier than said. I know this sometimes takes a lot of trial and error to see what changes can have a positive effect, not everyone is a 100+ Years senior developer. Another BUT: take this serious, you saw with CD Project red how quickly reputation can vanish and how long it will take to fix and gain it again. Dont do the same mistake and put your priorities right.Seriously, just the best for you and im looking forward to enjoy this beautifull game again (more than just 1-2 hours before the session gets unplayable)Edit: cutting good parts because of character limitation here
