_childDocuments_.review: Floodland:~~~~~~~~ Well, here we are. Global warming . . . sorry, climate change . . . got the better of us, and the world is now flooded from one end to the other. Small pockets of land still remain here and there; believe it or not, small groups of people managed to survive the apocalyptic climate. After all, humankind is a tough species to get rid of. So, what would these survivors do to thrive again? Would they try to create new technologies, and with what, or would they search for pre-apocalyptic technologies or go back to basics from a million years ago? It’s probably a bit of all of the above. But what if you were the leader of these groups of survivors? What would you do? It’s time to get your hands on the (wet) deck in the post-apocalyptic game, Floodland!Floodland is a post-apocalypse survival strategy and colony simulation game developed by Vile Monarch and published by Ravenscourt on the 16th of November, 2022 on the Steam platform. As you start the game, you’ll be prompted to choose between four of the clans available for selection. All four clans have specific traits and worldviews. After selecting one, the way to the new world will depend on you alone. Your clan will have about twenty-plus people, and you’ll only see the land where you started from, while the rest of the map will be under a thick fog. You can select whether to follow the tutorial, but ultimately, the game is based on following tasks to move forward. Early in the game, you’ll realise that you’ll be micromanaging your community, but the question is, to what extent? The answer is obvious quite early on, and it will get worst when you welcome new clans on board. However, you must reclaim the radio tower beforehand, which will allow you to find out where people might be and where to find resources that you might need to build new buildings. Each expedition will need resources (food and water) for each day and a minimum of three people per expedition. There are specific items you need to find when you send out an expedition; some will be part of the task to move forward, but most of them are needed to increase your knowledge to unlock new technologies. And at one stage, you’ll have to start introducing laws for your community to follow. It is quite manageable when you have two or three clans to look after, but when the fourth one comes along (and by the way, you can choose whether or not you want to welcome any people or clans to your community), it becomes very tricky. The fact is that all the clans will start to make suggestions in regards to a new law. If you decide to ignore it, the clan’s unhappiness will rise, but if you do pass the law they suggest, the other clans might not be happy with it. So, it is really a catch twenty-two as far as I am concerned. It is manageable with two to three clans, but with four, it becomes a nightmare.In my third playthrough, which is my most successful so far, I reached the third chapter, which involves reaching and entering the industrial power plant. I got into the plant but now need to read the power blueprint and find who can read it in this flooding world. The big issue I have is the constant disagreement between the four clans; it never ends. I like the interface; it is easy to follow and use, which is a big bonus for these games. What I really like is how the world is presented. The pastel canvas style of graphics is just beautiful even though it portrays desperation and requires determination to explore the world further. A master stroke!Overall, the gameplay is fair, from the way you acquire new technology to how to get more resources in the world, and it makes good sense. For me, the only downside is the Law Tree as soon as you have more than three clans. It just becomes a finicky affair, and I find myself trying to deal with that rather than finding the answer to the tasks to finish a chapter. And you need to look at it because if you lose too many people, then you are heading to major problems.From time to time there are events during the gameplay, but I’ve only experienced a few of them so far. An epidemy, giant fish in your fishing ponds or an infestation in your shellfish farms, and that’s about it. Yes, it will affect food production and people’s moods, but that’s it. As the game works on days, people will die every now and then, but I can’t recall having any sort of birth rate. After 300 days of playing, I would have expected a little bundle of joy within my community, especially after signing off on a marriage between two people from different clans. Yes, you will be prompted to make decisions here and there as well on top of everything else.I enjoy the graphics and the soundtrack, which suit the game well. The interface is really good and easy to use. I quite like the game, but I did experience frequent crashes after loading a saved game.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great pastel style of graphics+	Great interface+	Quite fair until you acquire the third and fourth clan+	Good Law and Technology Trees+	Good replayability+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Crashing frequently after loading a saved game-	Micromanaging becomes a bit picky after acquiring the third or fourth clanFloodland is an interesting take on the survival strategy game. I enjoyed playing it, but it might not be for everyone.7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game, with plenty of character, and to a point creates a sense of limited resources and the need to marshal your people properly.  (In the end I found that having just enough people working at a job to keep the resources positive was needed to make sure every station had enough people)The biggest early struggle is the limited build space, hemmed in by things you can't deconstruct (yet), but the expedition system (and the very forgiving sharing between stockpiles on different islands) makes that feel less of a frustration.  I would like that there would be some way to provide better feedback on resource management, in that at some points it shows you have a net positive flow but that resource can be coming down to zero, or if you increase the intake of another resource it doesn't change the net negative change.The visual palette is unusual with it's choice of watercolours, but the painting of the different clans is more surreal than grounded.  Managing different clans feels awkward, in that with the limited build space, it's nearly impossible to naturally (without the Force Assimilation law) get clans to get along as there isn't much space for recreation buildings amongst the other needs of your community.Near the end game, diseases are nearly constant, where they were an occasional concern in the early game, making for an odd difficulty spike.I'm not sure how much replayability there is aside from starting with a different clan or a different difficulty, even if the maps are randomized, it doesn't feel like there are any outside pressures that would shape it otherwise.

The game delivered on many of those things and I am glad I chose to buy it on sale and put in the time that I did. However, and this is a big however, the game mechanics are still broken in some places -- the notification system is unhelpful at best when spending time perfecting resource management, which you'll do a lot of. Workers somehow find a way to work very far from home and that affects your overall yield. Even if I choose to overlook the minor annoyances and find a way to play the game to the very end, the game won't let me finish. The game quits while trying to save at the very end of the story and I have now given up on finishing the playthrough. That is the most I can put up with in terms of bugs. Final verdict: Wait till bugs are patched before you put in the time.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is interesting, and provide a new point of view of the survival genre. Unfortunately is plagued by some very annoying features, and few tips/tutorial on how to overcome them. For example, being a floodland game, it surprised me how nobody have a boat, up until mid game. Another one, having more clan sound like a good idea, but they will soon start fighting each other (with some people who doesn't want to live next to a park.... what's wrong with them?), unless you move them to an island for each other. making new island was very weird, and I carefully planned the resources for that, just to discover that storage magically share resources. After that I specialised each clan, and island, to a single task. Another point. I hated bit time that each clan have some "don't use this building" list. I'd rather have something like "preferred building", as for me it ended up that I constantly need to check what a clan DON't like, then to go back to building and remember that while expanding. Also, there should be a way to relocate people. If you don't like parks, don't go live nearby one, especially if other houses are available! Exploring is fun, but I soon end up having research team going up and down on the same spot to pick up resources. I wish there were a "get resources from this area until is empty" mode. Maybe even independently from the radio. I then tried to gather resources from big island by settling in there. just making a storage, few houses, and gather everything in range. and then.... again, making a pier to leave (which is surprisingly expensive for such a mandatory building). Making bridge is another mess. It's not really clear which island can be connected and which are not. ended up with half done bridges, and several unconnected areas. I wish collecting resources, especially in end game, would be easier, rather than the need to expand the base. And then I reached the final part of the game. Another not very clear instruction on how to proceed, and why, after all this effort on making a power plant working again, I need to build energy generator on each island. and then... the game crashed on saving. last 30 minutes lost. I think that would be it for me. I believe this game have very big potential; but need more tips/instructions, less annoying "why this is not allowed" situations; more exploration option (rather than 3 person per time), and better end game collecting feature,; and better method of improving/changing clan relationship. I'll be back after 2-3 update, let's see how it improve!

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting city-builder. Interesting take on the post-apo genre - much more colorful and hopeful than the usual brown-gray games.The exploration aspect is quite innovative. It reminds me a bit of hidden object games, as you try to scour the land looking for houses that store useful items. The mid game was the most interesting, where you try to coexist several clans with differing views. Eventually you develop your research and enact enough laws that that elements becomes easy to manage, and you concentrate more on expansion and city building.The biggest issues for me are the bugs - stuck expeditions, workers that seem to be stuck/gone. Upgrading houses doesn't seem to work now, I had to destroy and then rebuild them, losing resources. But developers are actively trying to fix the issues, and can manually fix your saves if needed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential, but not for $29.99 and it clearly needs more development. I do not feel it was ready to be released as there are still a significant amount of bugs.  I confirm the game took a long time to save (auto saves without warning), frequent pauses and lag, and game crashes. The recent hotfixes of the game resolved some of the long save times and lag but I still experience game crashes and other weird behavior. For example, the game seems to encounter significant issues the bigger the camp gets. The engine seems to have trouble managing all of the activities of the camp inhabitants.  At one point all of my inhabitants began starving for no reason, or they stopped production even though resources were available causing unhappiness (I found no reason for this in any of the game stats), the game seems to intentionally lead you to fail by placing the player in a position where they are completely unable to launch an expedition due to low resources that seem to be low for no reason resulting in game failure (even on the easy setting). Again, great game idea and it has a lot of potential, but I do not recommend it due to the significant amount of bugs, errors, and algorithm problems.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, but the performance issues are still really bad. I was able to complete the entire storyline, and honestly, I'm not sure if I'll play it again. The different faction bonuses are not unique enough to matter and if you play it right, you can easily have five factions which give you all the good bonuses anyway. The town building is fun, but everything seems out of balance. For example, trees are renewable resources, but you harvest trees much faster than they replenish. Logging Camps can have four or five people, but if you have more than one person, you harvest trees faster than they replenish. you get way more influence, the currency to enact laws, than you would ever need. The bonuses from some laws are so good, you will likely never take anything else. This cuts down on replayability, because I'm always going to take the good laws. So you would only take the other laws to make the game harder for yourself. Food and water was easy to get and maintain, if you explore smartly, you can keep up with non-renewable resources easily. I also had way more technology points than I needed, so the tech tree was a given. I didn't have to make hard choices in the tech tree, I just researched everything.It's still a fun game despite it's flaws. The soundtrack is beautiful and the game looks amazing. I wish the map had more variety between games, but it's really fun to explore the map and build your city.If you are having trouble with performance and long save times, you can save and quit the game and that helps a ton. The longer you play, the worse the performance gets.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I would definitely recommend this game, to the right person.At launch, there were some performance issues that made the game nearly unplayable due to memory-induced lag. This was resolved, so in reference to the other reviews which give a thumbs down over this, maybe give it another shot.PROS:- Choices have actual impact on the progression of the game. You are asked to make legislative and logistical choices which each of the 4+ clans have opinions on, based on a 2-axis sociocultural spectrum.- This game actually has things to say about the world, through bits of lore and artifacts hidden throughout the map.- Many resources are finite and must be managed carefully in order to put them to their best use. You aren't handheld in this game and making a misstep can have drastic consequences. This makes planning a much more important part of progression. For those who enjoy challenge in your survival colony sims, this is for you.CONS:- I personally enjoy a game I have to restart a few times to fully grasp, but I can't say it makes for a good feature. Games like EU4 make up for a steep learning curve by having dense content and far-reaching strategic consequences. There needs to be more content to delve through, perhaps alternative sites or map modes to apply the hard-fought strategy to.- While improvements have been made to performance, the graphics on this game can be surprisingly heavy compared to whats happening on-screen. Auto-saves (which I fully recommend you take full advantage of as I've had the game freeze up at least once) freeze the game up entirely, and the speed function tends to cause lag spikes later in the game when your settlement spans multiple districts.- A small thing: I would like more zoom. It would be nice to zoom in and watch the little folks doing their thing.SUGGESTIONS:- More content. More clans. More map variation. Just more. I enjoyed this game enough that I would definitely pay for DLC if only for more clans to interact with and balance.- A third axis for the belief system to go with the additional clans. Currently the Liberty/Unity, Old World/New World spectrum limits the diversity of the clans. You could expand on this with an Industrial/Agrarian axis or perhaps something based on religious practices. There's a lot of potential for diversity here.- Customization would be a nice QOL improvement. I would like to rename districts at the very least.- More control of worker placement- Keep working on this, the game is definitely worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Floodland is a beautiful, well-made (and best of all) COMPLETED game that is a perfect and more streamlined amalgamation of Frostpunk and Flotsam. That a game was delivered to release as a finished product is no small feat anymore as too many games seem to be stuck in EA purgatory with no end in sight (looking at you Flotsam).The game, set in a post-apocalyptic setting (that does not behave as a form of propaganda, by the way—but also, even if you believe Global Warming is false, what’s the harm in taking care of our planet?) possesses a unique artistry that appears fitting to a world greatly overwhelmed by water. The devs took especial care in the design and detail, making for an interesting and attractive play. It appears they also borrowed some great ideas from Frostpunk and Flotsam, as well, such as laws and pleasing the people from Frostpunk, and foggy environments that need exploration such as in Flotsam. There is an abundance to do, from resource management to relational management between different clans, to even research and upgrades that help improve your settlement as progression becomes more difficult and new threats and issues are encountered. Additionally, there is an actual, continuing campaign! that can largely be ignored until you are ready to progress, though it helps to follow along to improve your civilization. The few issues I have, however, are with clan management and the inordinate amount of memory the game eats as you progress through the game (saving eventually takes up to 30-45 seconds after playing for a few hours, and the game lags sometimes). Managing the different clans is a bit ridiculous--I appreciate that even in a post-apocalyptic world there would still be differing views, but their relational aggression and inability to work together seems unlikely given they are all facing extreme environments and difficult survival. I know shows like The Walking Dead portray the idea that the only remaining living survivors are almost all the seeming worst of humanity, but I actually think this is an improbable scenario: faced with extinction, I believe humanity would come together...or do I?  Given the current climate on climatic issues...maybe not?I still highly recommend trying Floodland if you enjoy resource/city management and survival games. Even at its full price tag I think it is well worth the purchase and play, just make sure you have freed up memory and a computer that can handle this behemoth of graphics.
